crucial_aspects: The fact that Australia was so far away and that I would probably not have a similar chance of staying there for an extended period after I finished my studies.
info_ease: Information was easy to obtain, although the host university office always took some time in replying to personal inquieries.
arrival_assistance: A couple of introductory sessions, which were very basic, non-social stuff that was for the most part unnecessary.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Took some steps, but you work yourself through.
registration_help: Emailing the host university, which took a while to respond.
registration_success: Registration was easy. Even after classes had started I shifted my courses around quite a bit, which was nice.
course_level: The course level was fairly easy I have to say. Considering they were master classes, I got through most of them with little effort.
teaching_comparison: It's similar, although there are much more students in classes and lectures.
courses_enrolled: Foreign Policy Analysis Foundations of Finance The Resort to Force Strategic Diplomacy
recommended_courses: All the courses were quite interesting. I would recommend the course Foreign Policy Analysis the most, as the professor was extremely engaging and knowledgable, and the weekly topics were interesting and time-relevant. Foundations of Finance was quite hard, as I had never completed a finance course before, but I wanted to challenge myself a bit, so I got what I was looking for. Also had a great professor. the other two courses were also recommendable.
unexpected_costs: Travelling the country was more expensive than anticipated, but obiously worth it.
cost_comparison: Beer was quite expensive if bought in supermarkets or liquor stores. Other alcohol in student bars was quite cheap during happy hours tho.
activities_available: Sports between the accommodation halls (football, australian rugby, volleyball). Also running club which hosts a iron-man style run at the end of the semster.
activities_recommended: Do a sport or attend a non-sport club to make new friends or for free meals/beers. I went to a few German society meetings and it was fun.
weekend_recommendations: Tasmania is great, but if you are there during winter the weather will be absolutely freezing. Otherwise, New Zealand is so worth it! East coast trip during the mid-sem break is also very popular among exchange students, but having your own car or renting one is very recommendable for all these destinations.
culture_adjustment: easy.
socializing_tips: Many Aussies at uni are quite young (18-21), as they start higher education right away and most do not persue a masters degree, because it is too expensive. As a master student, most of my classmates were from Asia and did not speak English well or sometime at all, so it was hard to make same aged Aussie friends for me. I got a job at the local irish pub tho, and got some more Aussie contact through that.
cultural_challenges: Very heavy Asian influence on campus, the supermarkets and restaurants on campus made it feel a bit like studying in Beijing at times lol.
culture_appreciated: The close and compact style of the university grounds, and the laid back atmosphere everyday.
top3_advice: I would not go to Canberra/ANU tbh. It is not by the beach and the weather there gets really cold. It was a good experience but I would not particularly recommend it, since there are other universities in cities that are much nicer (Sydney or Melbourne). Bring warm clothes if you do go there, but make it stuff you can leave behind, so you travel easier on your post-study travels.
most_rewarding: travelling after the semester had ended. New Zealand, East Coast, Vietnam.
greatest_challenge: The cold weather and the fact that I did not particularly fancy Canberra as a city.

crucial_aspects: I had a burning desire to come to Australia to experience the country, its culture, and the academic opportunities here, as I found the subjects offered here fascinating.
overall_comments: Absolutely the best decision I have made during my education. I have gotten everything out of it that I possibly could.
info_ease: I think it has been fine getting in touch with the university. They have been good at providing information along the way, responding to emails, and offering online meetings where we could ask our questions.
arrival_assistance: Mails, phone calls, online and offline meetings
arrival_comments: It has definitely been easier to get in touch with people once I arrived in Australia, as I lived on campus and the time zone difference was no longer an issue.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Absolutely the best decision I have made during my education. I have gotten everything out of it that I possibly could.
registration_process: Honestly, I can't remember, which probably means it was pretty straightforward.
registration_help: Mails, phone calls, meetings and that
registration_success: Unfortunately, they made quite a few changes to the courses I thought I was going to take, so I had to choose something else. However, I got into the courses I ended up selecting.
registration_advice: Stay updated on the courses through their website and keep an eye on any emails related to applying for courses and deadlines. The same course can be split into multiple sessions on different days/times, so you need to be quick to secure the session you prefer.
academics_comments: Absolutely the best decision I have made during my education. I have gotten everything out of it that I possibly could.
course_level: The level is comparable to Denmark, but the teaching methods are different, which can make it more challenging in some ways. There are ongoing tests, debates, assignments, presentations, etc., that all count toward your final grade.
teaching_comparison: Honestly, I prefer the teaching methods in Denmark. A lot of the "teaching" consisted of pre-recorded videos from the lecturer, and then we attended tutorial sessions, which I felt didn't go deep enough into the material. Otherwise, it was fine. It really depends on your lecturer and tutor, and it varies from course to course.
courses_enrolled: THOUGHT LEADERSHIP IN ORGANISATIONS ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND INNOVATION LEADING PEOPLE AND CHANGE MARKETING MANAGEMENT
recommended_courses: Whatever you prefer. Sometimes, the quality of a course depends on the lecturer/tutor, and that's something you can't control. However, there is the option to switch courses if you don't like it.
unexpected_costs: The food is more expensive. I had to purchase extra time for my travel insurance, which was quite costly. There are also some fees associated with living in the residential hall, which added to the overall costs.
cost_comparison: Food is more expensive
activities_available: All kinds. You can find it at their website
activities_recommended: There are many social opportunities at the residential halls and as part of being a student at the university. Both creative and sports-related activities. There are large and small associations, so there's something for every taste.
weekend_recommendations: Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve !! Black Mountain and the Botanical Gardens, which are right next to campus, the Parliament, Mount Ainslie, the museums, and Floriade.
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: ChatGPT They are very friendly and welcoming, but they tend to keep to themselves quite a bit. I think they're tired of making good friends who leave after just one semester, so it's all about charming your way into their circle anyway!
cultural_challenges: Learning to enjoy their version of a BBQ
culture_appreciated: The laid-back, chill attitude, friendliness, and approachability.
top3_advice: 1) Enjoy every second of it and take some walks around campus and in the botanical gardens – bring a cup of coffee or whatever you prefer! 2) Buy a disposable camera or something similar to capture some great moments. 3) There are many international students, just like you, who are excited about the upcoming semester, so everyone is very friendly and welcoming. Don't be afraid to approach new people and say hello! and... 4) GO TRAVEL IN YOUR BREAK. Don't let money stop you.
other_useful_info: 1) You won't see as many spiders and snakes as your friends will tease you about. That's only when you travel further north. That being said, they are in Canberra, but they tend to keep to themselves. 2) Be mindfull when packing. You don't need as much as you think. I arrived during winter and bought a cheap winter jacket from a thrift store, which I gave away. I also only brought 2 sweaters and pairs of pants, which I'm now lugging around here in the summer. There are also many thrift stations at the residential halls where you can find a free sweater or whatever you might need (including bedding and comforters), so take advantage of that and pack light.
most_rewarding: The friendships I made and the places I saw
greatest_challenge: Personally, I haven't had any major challenges during my stay. One of the hardest things, I think, has been meeting so many kind people and experiencing amazing places, only to leave them behind. That's probably been the most challenging part, but it just means that the experience has been great!
other_comments: Canberra's campus life is super charming. So if you come here, don't be upset about it. It may not be most people's top priority, but I'm so grateful I ended up in Canberra! In addition, the application process might seem annoying now, but it's all worth it. Once you're there, everything goes smoothly, and I can highly recommend it based on my own experience.

crucial_aspects: I wanted the destination to be further away from Denmark to get out of my comfort zone and also be able to travel to places I normally wouldn't go.
info_ease: I received a lot of information via email from the Global Programs team at The Australian National University. Before arrival they held a few zoom meetings and sent out powerpoints on what do before and after arrival and really made an effort to make sure that you didn't miss any information regarding visas, accommodation and also on how to physically get there in the smartest way.
arrival_assistance: They held in person presentations during orientation week where you could meet other exchange students and ask questions, etc. It was always possible to reach out to the Global Programs team during the stay and their response time was quick.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You had to submit an application to receive course codes to be able to sign up for the courses you wanted. There was a course catalogue for available courses. I found it slightly confusing because there were some 'prerequisites' for each course. For example to be able to take a specific law course, for some you need to have had an introduction course to Australian institutions which wasn't available during my semester. But when you submit the request for the course codes, you can submit documentation detailing that you have had a similar course back home which gives you the same requisites to take the course you want. For this documentation I submitted the course descriptions in English for KU courses I had previously taken. When I had received the course codes, I could register for the course on their ISIS portal. For some courses you have to sign up for tutorials and you should pay close attention to when that sign up opens, because the classes fill up quickly and you might not get the specific weekly time/date you want.
registration_help: The Global Programs team do send out very detailed guides on the registration process and checklists, so you should can on that.
registration_success: I registered for all the classes I wanted but I know that a lot of people were waitlisted for different courses.
registration_advice: If you want to drop or swap a course at the start of the semester, think about the fact that there may not be a lot of other courses with available spots or available tutorial classes - so check the availability for a course you want to swap to before your drop the courses you already have. It is your responsibility to make sure that you are registered for enough classes in order to not lose your visa.
course_level: Three of my courses were MA level and then it was a requirement by the host institution that I take a BA course on introductions to Australian law. Even though it was a BA course, however, I was graded as an MA student and during assignments I had to write more words. I think you can decide yourself if you wish to be in the BA or MA group but check with KU during your course approvals as they may have an opinion.
teaching_comparison: There were participation requirements for a lot of the courses. The grading was more spread out with like 10% for participation, 30% for a group presentation, 60% for a research essay or 50% for a research essay and 50% for a sit-in exam. There were some exam assignments during mid-term and some during the end of the semester. It varied between courses how much time the course convener spent lecturing and the amount of group work/active participation. Some of the courses had lectures and some only had seminars.
courses_enrolled: Foundations of Australian Law: it's an undergraduate class you are required to take during their semester 1/our spring term. There was a one hour lecture each week (which was also recorded and uploaded later) and a two hour tutorial like classic two hour seminars back home. The examination was a paper worth 50% that had to be submitted after the semester break and a 45% hand written 90 minute sit in exam at the end of the semester. The last 5% was class participation points. You were allowed two tutorial skips and then you also had a presentation to do where you had to visit an Australian Court and talk about it for 3 minutes in class. Chinese Law and Society: postgraduate course. We were around 170 people in the class which was a lot of people for a seminar class. There was a 3 hour seminar each week and a 3 hour pre-recorded lecture. The course convener was super nice and very well educated on the topic. He would usually spent the first half of the class lecturing and then the rest was group presentations. You had to do a group presentation with 3 other people which was worth 20% of your grade. For the group presentations, you need to be aware that the majority of the class participants are Chinese international students who sometimes will only speak in Chinese at the table even if you are also sitting there, so if you do not want to feel left out and want to be able to communicate with your group members, consider joining a group of Australian students. I signed up for the group presentations before the semester started. As there were so many students, the way the teacher did participation points was by making a survey you could join and register participation and do a little quiz each time - you did not actually have to say anything. You could also even join the survey if you for some reason were sick and couldn't be there if you left the tab open from the last time. The last part of the examination was a research essay worth 70%. It was a little bit difficult finding sources and the relevant legislation as some of the legislation isn't translated into English so keep this in mind. The teacher was very helpful in providing ways to find sources and even sent me some legislation that I didn't have access to. International Humanitarian Law: postgraduate course with one two-hour seminar a week. Great teacher. She sometimes did the seminar via zoom. The examination was 10% participation (you had to say stuff during class but didn't have to be there every time, I didn't really do that but still got an alright grade), 30% was a research proposal (you had to write a short proposal on what you wanted to write the subsequent research essay on). The 30% research proposal was handed in around 1,5 months into the semester and then the actual research essay worth 60% was handed in at the end of the semester. Information Technology Law: postgraduate and undergraduate course. There were no participation requirements for this class. 50% was a research essay that had to be submitted a bit after the semester break and then an online problem exam worth 50%. He did some of the seminars on zoom. It was one 3 hour seminar per week and he recorded the seminars and uploaded the recordings afterwards.
recommended_courses: If you want to do a bit of traveling during the week and would like as much flexibility as possible, I would recommend international humanitarian law and information technology law so you have the option of skipping some classes. Also, there were very nice classes with good teachers and interesting material. International Humanitarian Law is not very difficult when you have already had international law and IT law was a nice mix between intellectual property rights, cybercrime and AI.
unexpected_costs: I spent a lot of money on traveling each month while I was on exchange which I have not accounted for in the numbers above. I also did not really cook and mainly ate out or got takeaway, especially as I travelled a lot. I spent a lot on plane tickets and accommodation and activities. The above numbers would more likely reflect a normal month in Canberra.
cost_comparison: The food and especially coffee was less expensive compared to Copenhagen. You could get very cheap sushi rolls. Transport was not vert expensive either, especially if you travel to the Queensland state where all transport is 1 Australian dollar. I did not expect to have to pay 2000 DKK (a one time amount) for a mandatory overseas health insurance when I was already paying around 500 DKK pr month for a private Danish travel insurance. The cost of domestic flights can be surprisingly expensive sometimes, because the distances are a lot further than you think. It's a good idea to buy plane tickets early in advance.
activities_available: During orientation week, the university hosts a market day where all of the associations and clubs are available at their stands so you get an idea of what you can join.
activities_recommended: There were so many associations that offered different social activities.
weekend_recommendations: I took a lot of weekend trips to different places. You can easily take a three hour Murray's or Greyhound bus to Sydney. You can fly to Melbourne or Tasmania. There is a 2 week semester break where I went to New Zealand. After exams I did a 3 week roadtrip from Cairns to Byron Bay. I also took a trip to Fiji and a lot of people travelled to Bali or Western Australia during the break. You can try and plan the travels according to the weather as the temperatures are very different across australia. In Canberra, there were a lot of hiking opportunities and nice restaurants and historical buildings. I would recommend a visit to the Parliament, the High Court, the War memorial, Mount Ainslie, the Botanical Gardens, Mount Majura Vineyard or going to watch a rugby or AFL game. You can also take a two hour bus to Batemann's Bay or Wollongong by the ocean or rent a car and go to Jervis Bay, which is an old military base and has very nice water and sand.
culture_adjustment: It was a pretty easy adjustments as Australians in general are a more welcoming people. It took a while getting used to receiving so many questions about how my day had been at the supermarket.
socializing_tips: Join some clubs.
cultural_challenges: Students are a lot more willing to participate in class discussions so if you want to get some participations points, you need to make a bit of an effort.
culture_appreciated: The openness of Australian people.
top3_advice: Use your free time to travel. There is also a lot to see in Canberra even though the reputation is that it is boring and the university is great. It will be expensive, so apply for grants.
other_useful_info: For accommodation, make sure to look up the different housing options and do some thorough research. Apply for student housing in good time as well. For courses, make sure to sign up for tutorials when the opportunity opens (Australian time) as you might get waitlisted if you are not quick enough.
most_rewarding: Gaining more confidence by having to be very independent.
greatest_challenge: The few times I was feeling unwell were a bit tough so definitely important to surround yourselves with good people and have a good relationsship with your roommates, they really helped a lot.

crucial_aspects: Firstly, Australian National University was and is still a globally highly ranked university within my field (political science), which was one of the primary aspects in choosing my study destination. Secondly, ANU is located in an English-speak country, which was another deciding factor when considering the expected quality of learning at the university. Thirdly, ANU provides a student housing guarantee, which was another requirement when choosing my study destination, as many university cities face challenging housing crises.
info_ease: It was very easy (all things considered) to acquire the needed information upon arrival, as ANU have a very accessible and helpful administrative team. They replied quickly to my inquiries and were ready to find solutions to any problems I encountered.
arrival_assistance: Prior to arrival, it was possible to attend two online webinars at ANU to prepare for our exchange stay. Upon arrival, there was an Orientation Week, during which there were information sessions, stands, and various offers for exchange and international students especially.
arrival_comments: I encourage participation in O-week.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: When the registration period opens, you can register online for courses. It is a good idea to register when it opens to ensure a spot; however, it was not nearly as competitive as the last time I went on exchange. NB! You need a pre-approval from your home institution for all the courses you want to register for.
registration_help: There was an online guide which was very helpful. Email correspondence was also quick and somewhat efficient.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Do your research on courses in advance and have a list of alternative courses ready (with pre-approvals from the home institution), in case a course you want is dropped for the term.
course_level: The level of the courses varied somewhat, often according to the skills of the course convenor. However, I often found that the level at KU is higher than the level of classes internationally, and this was also the case for ANU.
teaching_comparison: A shorter syllabus than at KU and multiple assessment pieces throughout the semester. Participation was also graded in all classes.
courses_enrolled: 1) Australian Environmental Policy. 2) From Family to Family-State: Social Power in China. 3) Introduction to Humanitarian Action. 4) Revolution, Rebellion, Riot: Unruly Politics.
recommended_courses: I would recommend "Revolution, Rebellion, Riot: Unruly Politics" because the professor is incredible, the class sessions are taught in a deliberative way that promotes independent thought and co-learning, and the class comprises creative elements that are both fun and great for learning in a different way. I would also recommend "Australian Environmental Policy" as the professor is both nice and knowledgeable, and the course provides an alternative approach to public policy analysis and takes up some interesting (and often complex) cases of public policy whilst providing a great amount of background information on Australian history, politics, and culture.
unexpected_costs: I don't think i encountered any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: The visa was really expensive! While supermarket prices are comparable to Denmark, eating out is less expensive. Also note that there is a mandatory health insurance.
activities_available: Many different clubs, societies, and athletic activities. All can be found at the university website or Instagram.
activities_recommended: The self-defense short-course and boxing class at ANU sport was great fun and a great opportunity to learn.
weekend_recommendations: Canberra is a bit boring itself, but it is easy to take the bus to Sydney or the train to Melbourne. Otherwise rent a car and check out the nature surrounding Canberra or the coast.
culture_adjustment: Easy - unique Aussie culture but still a mix between British and American culture.
cultural_challenges: Kitchen cleaning habits in my dorm.
culture_appreciated: The Aussie openness, kindness, and laid-back approach.
top3_advice: 1) Apply for funding! 2) Live in an on-campus accommodation. 3) Participate in O-week.
other_useful_info: I opened an Australian bank account which was both easy and useful. And if you have a driver's license, I recommend bringing an international license or obtaining an official translation of your Danish license, so you can drive around Australia (beware the kangaroos and the wombats on the road though).
most_rewarding: The friendships, travels in incredible Australia (especially diving at the coral reefs), meeting the engaging academic opportunity, and general life on campus
greatest_challenge: The spiders (a lot do not really see them but I saw a lot...)

crucial_aspects: I had always dreamed of goint to Australia and this was just the perfect opportunity. It was also a plus that Australia is an English speaking country.
overall_comments: The academic opportunities were not that many but the personal growth and experience was worth it.
info_ease: Relatively easy most of the information was sent by email and the international department is pretty extensive. All crucial information was sent or easily accesible but there was some "good-to-know" information that you had to know to look for to get. You have to find your way to your recidence yourself.
arrival_assistance: The first week (o-week) had a bunch of information events and a mandatory information event for exchange students.
arrival_comments: It was a bit overwhelming having to find everything but as long as you turn up or look for it you get all the information and assistance you need.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: The academic opportunities were not that many but the personal growth and experience was worth it.
registration_process: You have to find the courses you want to take and then nominate them before getting an offer letter. If the courses have prerequisites you also have to prove that you meet those in your nomination. However it is possible (and as far as I heard relatively easy) to change courses after getting to the university by talking to the student admin.
registration_help: You are pretty much on your own when having to select courses but you can always contact the student admin, and it is possible to talk to student admin about changing or swapping courses as well.
registration_success: I got all my first priority courses.
registration_advice: Select the courses you want from the start but don't stress it because you have time to change them later.
academics_comments: The academic opportunities were not that many but the personal growth and experience was worth it.
course_level: I took one first year, two second year and one third year courses. I would say the level is just slightly below the level of courses at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: It was much the same although all lectures were recorded and one of my courses was a flipped classroom.
courses_enrolled: ASTR1003: Astronomy and Space BIOL2202: Experiments and Analysis in Biology PSYC2007: Biological Basis of Behaviour NEUR3112: Systems Neuroscience
recommended_courses: I would recommend taking a first year course in a topic that interests you as a "buffer" course you maybe put a bit less effort into. Having four courses at the same time is a lot of work if you are putting in max effort in all of them.
unexpected_costs: A room changing fee.
cost_comparison: Most were the same as expected.
activities_available: There were some smaller events by the student comittee.
activities_recommended: You can get free gym-classes through the student comittee those are a great opportunity to do sport and meet people.
weekend_recommendations: Get outside! If you are able go for hikes on the mountains.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy it's not that different from here.
socializing_tips: If living on campus mingle in the dinning hall people are generally very welcomming.
cultural_challenges: Perhaps just having to speak another language.
culture_appreciated: The people are generally very open, welcomming and laid back.
top3_advice: 1. Meeting new people is the real experience, live in a hall of in a share. 2. Get outside as often as you can. 3. Ask for help, it's there as long as you ask for it.
other_useful_info: Not anything I can think off at the moment.
most_rewarding: Hiking up a proper mountain and laughing in the dinning hall.
greatest_challenge: Having to share a space with other people and juggling four courses.

crucial_aspects: I wished to study a place, where they would offer different classes from what I am offered at home, but still classes that are relevant to my study.
overall_comments: I had an amazing experience in Istanbul. The city is very interesting, and I learned a lot. I also found some very good friends, which was great fun. I had perhaps expected more from the education, but I was very happy with what I got out of my exchange semester.
info_ease: It was easy with help from the Erasmus Office.
arrival_assistance: My buddy and Erasmus Office helped me with everything I needed. I got help with registration and visa etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had an amazing experience in Istanbul. The city is very interesting, and I learned a lot. I also found some very good friends, which was great fun. I had perhaps expected more from the education, but I was very happy with what I got out of my exchange semester.
registration_process: We had many papers to sign both for school and to get a residence permit. We fixed most of it within the first week – introduction week – with much help from our Erasmus buddies.
registration_help: The Erasmus Office and our individual buddies were of big help.
registration_success: I was luckily very successful in the end, but it took some time to get everything to fit.
registration_advice: Take the help that is offered. You will need it.
academics_comments: I had an amazing experience in Istanbul. The city is very interesting, and I learned a lot. I also found some very good friends, which was great fun. I had perhaps expected more from the education, but I was very happy with what I got out of my exchange semester.
course_level: We didn't have academic papers in the way, I am used to. Nor did we have to spend much time preparing for each class.
teaching_comparison: It was very similar with classroom-teaching and groupwork.
courses_enrolled: Persuasion, Digital Media Ethics, Photography, Brand Management and Understanding Social Behaviour.
recommended_courses: I would definitely recommend Digital Media Ethics, Photography and Brand Management.
unexpected_costs: We had to pay for a Turkish insurance in the very beginning that we weren't aware of. This was additional to our normal insurance.
cost_comparison: Food in the grocery stores were more expensive than expected. At least in normal grocery stores.
activities_available: I'm not quite sure.
activities_recommended: Join in on the Erasmus events. It is a great way to meet people.
weekend_recommendations: See the city – the mosques, the museums. Talk to people on the street and go to local places. You will learn a lot and meet a very open people.
culture_adjustment: It was easy more often than not. I felt safe, and I got very into the culture and cultural practices. It was extremely interesting.
socializing_tips: Don't be afraid to start a conversation. Turkish students are interested, and they will most likely also try to start a conversation with you.
cultural_challenges: Harrassment on the street.
culture_appreciated: The people and the food. They were very friendly, and the food is amazing.
top3_advice: Travel, take classes that you find interesting, learn some Turkish
other_useful_info: I can't think of any.
most_rewarding: Meeting so many lovely people and experiencing an interesting culture
greatest_challenge: Adapting to a new culture and new people.
other_comments: Nope :)

info_ease: Difficult. It was not easy to find the available courses or figure out how to fill out the documents.
arrival_assistance: The buddies at Bahcesehir University was ready to answer questions.
arrival_comments: I could have used a lot more help and information
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: There was a lot of paperwork, but except from that it was easy to get accepted.
registration_help: The buddies was ready to help
registration_success: I had to chose a lot of new courses because of the schedule and it took KU a long time to accept the new courses.
registration_advice: Be prepared to change your courses after arriving
course_level: The ECTS points varied from 5 to 7 points.
teaching_comparison: More creativity, less group work, different culture and different approach.
courses_enrolled: Persuasion, Photography, Digital Media Ethics, Brand Management, Understanding Social Behavior

unexpected_costs: Extra luggage for 150 dkk ESN activities, especially in the introduction week Payment for residence permit
cost_comparison: Food and traveling was less expensive. Data was more expensive.
activities_available: I found my activities elsewhere
activities_recommended: I recommend going on one of the trips, for example Cappadocia, it is a good opportunity to meet people.
weekend_recommendations: Traveling in the black sea area – trekking in the mountains and visit local families. Walking the Lycian road.

cultural_challenges: The language barrier and the catcalling in the streets (particularly the elder generation)
culture_appreciated: The welcoming warm people, amazing food, religion and history.

other_useful_info: Be openminded
most_rewarding: Getting friends from everywhere

crucial_aspects: At jeg kunne tage et sted hen, hvor at kulturen var meget anderledes og noget helt nyt ift. hvad jeg ikke har prøvet før. Jeg har længe gerne ville bo i Mellemøsten, og der er Tyrkiet og Istanbul et specielt sted, da byen skiller mellem Europa og Asian samtidig med at der er stor overvægt af mellemøstlig kultur blandet med meget vi også kender fra vestlig kultur i fx Danmark. Udover det er Istanbul Europas største by!
info_ease: Jeg synes klart, at der kunne være mere information omkring dét at rejse til Tyrkiet/Istanbul, da det ikke er medlem af EU og på den måde kan give en række andre udfordringer end hvis man rejser rundt i EU.
arrival_assistance: Universitet havde meldt ud forinden, at der ville være en introuge, hvor nogle tutorer kunne hjælpe med alt det praktiske papir arbejde ift. at søge opholdstilladelse, søge fag (dem man har skrevet på sin learning agreement er ikke nødvendigvis dem man får dernede), samtidig med at der også var nogle sociale aktiviteter. Her var man samlet med alle Erasmus+-studerende uanset uddannelse, så man kunne møde dem.
arrival_comments: Jeg var heldig at gå på et uni, hvor de rent faktisk hjalp med alt det praktiske (som ikke var en selvfølgelighed i Istanbul på andre universiteter). Dog synes jeg godt at de tutorer, der var, kunne være mere oplysende ift. processen og fortælle os hvad vi skal have af papirer (fx betale taxes), på immigration office osv.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Fungerede lidt ligesom når man registrerer sit udlandsophold på KU / Mobility Online. Lidt samme slags informationer og dokumenter men vær bare opmærksom på andre deadlines.
registration_help: En hold af Erasmus-hjælpere på mail, som svarede hurtigt!
registration_success: Jeg valgte nogle fag hjemmefra, som jeg synes lød gode og fik meritgodkendt dem + nogle flere. Det er godt at få forhåndsgodkendt flere point, måske 50-60 ects-point, fordi man ikke kan være sikker på at få præcis de fag man har skrevet i sin learning agreement. Jeg søgte først endeligt fag, da jeg sad i Istanbul i introugen, og det var ikke alle jeg kunne få, da de enten ikke var udbudt eller lå oven i hinanden. Hvert fag havde nogle forskellige tider, så man kan samle sine fag og have nogle fridage. Der er begrænset med pladser på hvert fag, men som erasmus studerende (ihvertfald på dette uni) havde man nogle fordele, hvor de altid fandt en plads til dig.
registration_advice: Få søgt forhåndsgodkendelse og skrevet under på din learning agreement hurtigst muligt! Der skal underskrives i to lande med forskellige deadlines, og KU holder sommerferie, når Istanbul havde deadlines, hvilke skabte lidt problemer for mig. Men alt skal nok løse sig i sidste ende, og lad vær med at gå i panik over hvilke fag du har valgt hjemmefra - det kan ændre sig.
course_level: Det var lavt niveau men også bare et anderledes skolesystem, hvilket var spændende at prøve. For mig gjorde det ikke noget at jeg ikke havde fag med særligt meget pensum eller nem undervisning, for jeg lærte alt muligt andet af mit ophold.
teaching_comparison: Det er meget forskelligt alt efter hvad man læser. Det kan både være store og små forelæsninger. Jeg havde meget praktisk/kreativ undervisning, som var i små hold.
courses_enrolled: Photography, Techincal skills in new media, Photojournalism, Digital Journalism, Introduction to new media
recommended_courses: Jeg vil bare anbefale at prøve nogle fag af, som kan lyde sjove, eller der kan give dig mere overskud i hverdagen i et nyt land. Vælg nogle fag ud fra du kan lave et godt skema, der er massere at vælge med. Til gengæld var førsteårs-fagene meget repeterende for mig, så overvej det.
unexpected_costs: Der skal gå noget betaling til en opholdtilladelse og ellers generelt bestilling af drikkevand osv osv.
cost_comparison: Alt var generelt rigtig billigt, da Tyrkiet er ramt hårdt af inflationen, samtidig med at det er billigere generelt sammenlignet med Danmark og især København. Det giver en kæmpe frihed og massere muligheder men vær opmærksom på ikke at gie udtryk for at alt er billigt hele tiden. For rigtig mange mennesker er det en kritisk tid, hvor det for dem er meget dyrt at leve.
activities_available: Der er alle former for begvnheder. Sport, fester, biografaftener osv osv
activities_recommended: Deltag hvis du gerne vil møde nye mennesker, men der skal nok komme massere af det, så ro på :)
weekend_recommendations: Der ligger nogle øer lige ude for Istanbul, hvor man kan bade og leve et lille ferieliv. Book en air bnb eller tag på dagstur derud og bad i havet og spis ud til vandet i solnedgang. Magisk oplevelse! Ellers udforsk byen, de gamle bydele eller rejs uden for Istanbul. Universitet arrangerer også ture!
culture_adjustment: Det var virkelig overvældende men fuldstændig fantastisk kultur. Alle er generelt mega søde og der er så mange virkelig skønne områder. Det er en god by til også at solo-spise og drikke kaffe alene, hvis man kan lide det. Det er en af de mest undervurderede byer, og et af det vildeste steder jeg har boet!
socializing_tips: Du kommer helt sikkert til at gå i klasse med mange lokale studerende, og der synes de sikkert også det er spændende, at du er der.
cultural_challenges: Der er mange kulturelle forskelle, samtidig med at der er stadig er meget vestlig kultur. Det hele er bare anderledes men du kommer til at vænne dig til det og synes det er helt fantastisk - selvom man også møder mange praktiske frustrationer og alt muligt mærkeligt hen ad vejen.
culture_appreciated: Det hele - menneskerne, maden, bylivet, deres måde at gå ud på.
top3_advice: Et skridt ad gangen, det hele skal nok gå selvom der er mange frustrationer. Lad vær med at være bange for, at du ikke får venner. Du kommer til at møde massere mennesker, både lokale studerende og andre internationale studerende. Vær nysgerrig og giv dig hen til the big city life og find nogle områder, hvor du elsker at chille!
other_useful_info: Vær opmærksom på at du skal søge opholdstilladelse, og der er en proces inden da, som forhåbentlig universitet hjælper med. Køb et simkort med det samme, Tyrkiet er først og fremmest uden for EU, så mange har ikke data der. Udover det skal du bruge et tyrkisk telefonnummer til rigtig mange ting. Dit simkort gælder kun i to måneder, da du ikke har opholdstilladelse, men enten hav is i maven og se om din opholdstilladelse kommer inden da - så kan du gå ned og købe et nyt. Ellers få (som jeg gjorde) en af dine tyrkiske venner til at købe et til dig - så udløber det ikke, og du kan bare fylde data på hver måned. Nogle fortæller dig at din telefon låser, hvis du ikke har opholdstilladelse, men det skete ikke for mig. Søg din opholdstilladelse med det samme, fordi processen kan tage flere måneder, og du må ikke rejse ud af landet under processen, hvis du ikke har dit tyrkiske ID.
most_rewarding: At prøve at bo i en ny virkelig vild by, hvor jeg havde så få forventninger hjemmefra. At opdage at man godt kan få nye venner i udlandet bare på andre måder end man er vant til. Kæmpe udfordring men også kæmpe eventyr!
greatest_challenge: At komme igennem alle de udfordringer hen ad vejen og opdage at det nok skal løse sig.
other_comments: Tag til Istanbul - det er et fantastisk sted!

The course we had about conservation science was very basic in my opinion and I did not feel as if I could gain much knowledge. The same was for the Research planning and communication course where the focus was on less important knowledge. However, there were also many interesting and good things about the courses and I could take home new knowledge. Especially learning about R-studio and ArcGIS was very interesting and well made.

unexpected_costs: Covid fees. To travel back into the UK tests had to be bought, which in the high phase of covid cost75 pound.
cost_comparison: Food generally was less expensive, especially compared with Denmark. I expected accommodation to be cheaper considering the small size of Bangor, but it turned out to be fairly expensive. Public Transport is very expensive in all of the UK.
activities_available: There are many societies, which fit your hobby perfectly. From every sport one can imagine to movie societies, game societies, cultural societies. Plus the short distance to Snowdonia National Park gives many hiking, climbing and biking opportunities.
activities_recommended: Going for many hikes in Snowdonia. It is for free and absolutely stunning.
weekend_recommendations: Again, Snowdonia. But also go for a holiday to the south of Wales, or see nearby cities such as Conwy, LLandudno (Great Orme), go to Aberfalls and visit the distillery, Betws-y-Coed or many more. But also Chester, Liverpool and Manchester are close by.
culture_adjustment: It was fairly easy to adjust to the culture. This comes however from a Germany person, where I feel like the culture in the UK is not far off.
socializing_tips: I felt that people were very welcoming and friendly and appreciated talking to me. That made socializing easy. Societies always have a day of socials, were they organise activities.
cultural_challenges: The drinking and going-out culture. Many of the society events evolve around drinking. But that is off course something no one is forced to participate.
culture_appreciated: The openness and friendliness of people. It made it easy to feel welcomed and included.
top3_advice: Come weather prepared, with rain and windproof shoe wear and jackets. Field trips can get wet. Don't be shy to approach staff and students, everyone is glad to help and talk to you. If in any way possible a car is available, it is helpful to get around, especially in Snowdonia.
other_useful_info: Winters can be long and rainy, so it is nice to plan trips with friends to keep up a good spirit. If you own them already, and like hiking, it is good to bring your gear.
most_rewarding: The people I met on the way turned out to be a great group if friends. Both in studies as well as in personal life.
greatest_challenge: As mentioned before I felt like the SUFONAMA second year at Bangor University was not well planned. That turned out to be very frustrating. Especially in the second semester, there were times where we had no courses, and no option to start our thesis, which left us with a long waiting period.
other_comments: Since I am a Erasmus Mundus Master student, my experience is not the traditional exchange experience. Further I feel that an exchange during the Bachelor year would be better, as most students in Bangor are Bachelor students. In my knowledge, the structure of SUFONAMA is to be changed. It is likely to be different in experiences of new students.

crucial_aspects: In my case, I selected Bangor University strictly from an academic point of view. One of my professors at University of Copenhagen had discussed an idea I had for my Master's thesis topic back in March 2022. During our discussions he had mentioned a professor that works at Bangor University that he had previously worked with, that would is specifically specialized in the topic I was researching. I had gotten in contact with this professor by April 2022 and they were more than willing to collaborate with me on my thesis as a supervisor (and they are now (still), officially supervising me on my thesis). Furthermore, Bangor University offered me the option to specialize in Conservation Science, which is the scientific division I am pursuing to work in once I graduate.
overall_comments: The overall university experience is great. Professors are very welcoming, understanding and down-to-earth. Furthermore, they're all very active in their scientific divisions and up to date with scientific literature, meaning we were constantly being thought up-to-date topics. The only downside, and the reason why I did not give a 10 rating, is that the overall course structure isn't very well defined and quite jagged. However, the university is aware of this and they are actively changing the module structure for next year's intake to make the study flow more consistent.
info_ease: I would give it a moderate rating. The university was very helpful in personal email exchanges to explain and give orientation upon arrival. However, there are some resources (such as an in-depth university campus map outlying the lecture halls) that are non-existent, so there was a lot of confusion in the first couple of weeks till everyone got used to where we needed to go.

crucial_aspects: For me, the most crucial aspect of choosing my study destination was the specialisation I would be granted based on the choice, as well as the provided courses.

arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance as I have not requested it.
arrival_comments: Even though I did not make use of it, it was very helpful of the university to provide incoming international students with transport from the airport.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Fortunately, I did not have to register for classes myself, it was done by the University. However, there is some paperwork to be filled out in order to proceed with the exchange which was more tiresome due to the lack of connection of Bangor University to Mobility Online.
registration_help: As I have not used any kind of help from the University, I do not know what kind of help was available. However, it was made clear to us who the course coordinators were and I am sure they would provide us with help if needed.
registration_success: I was not able to choose which classes I take, I had to follow the course plan. As such, I was registered automatically and did not have to worry about it.
registration_advice: I would definitely start the paperwork as early as possible as the communication between Universities can sometimes take some time.
course_level: Although the level of the courses was adequate to the degree level, the lecturers made sure that people from different backgrounds had the same understanding of the basics of the material as well.
teaching_comparison: As the course itself was smaller, it felt much more personal than at UCPH. Additionally, half of the assignments were not group assignments and therefore more individual feedback was provided. However, it was also less structured as every week had a different schedule, unlike at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Research Planning & Communications, Conservation Science, Agriculture & the Environment
recommended_courses: Conservation Science was a great module I can wholeheartedly recommend - not only does it cover a wide range of topics within animal and plant conservation, it also provides a lot of additional resources and topical examples.
unexpected_costs: Even if you have your own personal insurance/the European health card, when getting a student visa you must pay the insurance fee (which you can later get a refund for) of about 6000 dkk.
cost_comparison: The accommodation was more expensive than I expected - the prices are comparable with Copenhagen.
activities_available: There is a variety of societies available for students, from all the different disciplines - sports, music and theatre, research, volunteering, and more.
activities_recommended: There are so many student-led organisations that anybody can find something for themselves. I would definitely recommend going to Serendipity - a day at the University where all the organisations promote themselves.
weekend_recommendations: There are a lot of attractions for nature lovers - hiking trails, lakes, and wildlife reserves.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy to adjust - the University feels very welcoming and provides a lot of opportunities to bond with other students. However, there are definitely fewer socialising places in the traditional sense, such as clubs, than there are in Copenhagen.
socializing_tips: I would definitely check out the student organisations as almost all of them do weekly socials in pubs etc, which is a great opportunity to socialise with others.
cultural_challenges: I didn't think there were too many cultural differences - most of them came down to the language and slang not formerly known to me. I think one thing I noticed is that strangers are far more likely to approach you and that British people tend to be a little friendlier/louder than Copenhageners.
culture_appreciated: The locals were very welcoming.
top3_advice: Make sure you calculate your budget correctly, as it is very hard to find a job in Bangor. I would also start the paperwork and searching for accommodation as soon as possible. other_useful_info: Bring good hiking shoes and rainproof clothing! :) Umbrellas are useless here due to the wind.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of the experience was the people I got to meet - both locals and internationals. I also believe the study-life balance is well-kept.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge during the exchange was definitely the finances and budgeting.
other_comments: I definitely recommend Bangor University as an exchange destination!

Desuden var det vigtigt for mig at rejse til et universitet, der havde et højt akademisk niveau, hvilket man må sige Barnard College og Columbia University har. Desuden synes jeg at universitets placering i New York gav enormt god mening for de fag, jeg valgte.
info_ease: Vejlederne var meget svære at komme i kontakt med og kunne desværre kun svare på generelle spørgsmål. Så det var en smule svært at få svar på de spørgsmål man havde under rejsen.

Konceptet "Shopping Week" måtte gerne have været uddybet til vores afrejsemøde hos KU, da dette var en meget stressende og kaotisk oplevelse.

Desuden oplevede vi at KU ikke svarede på vores mails i den periode. Det var meget at navigere i, eftersom vores udvekslingsophold to en meget uventet drejning, da store dele af skolen lukkede ned. Det havde været dejligt med en guideline for, hvordan man skulle forholde sig.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Det var en meget lang proces. Først skulle man skrive en motiveret ansøgning og sende sine karakterer, samt sprogtest med, så skulle man vente ret lang tid på at få svar. Så skulle man i gang med sin VISA-ansøgning og i den proces skulle man få ens host institution til at lave et bank statement. Den del af processen var ret stressende. Dertil skulle man efterfølgende uploade en del dokumenter til Barnard, såsom ens vaccinationer mm.
registration_help: Det var meget svært at få svar på spørgsmål fra Barnard College, fordi der er så meget bureaukrati i Amerika. Ingen ville rigtig tage ansvar i telefonen.
registration_success: Det var okay. Men det var meget hårdt de første to uger, fordi du var nødt til at møde op til alle de timer, du gerne ville nå at prøve.
registration_advice: At søge på CUlpa omkring fagene og lærerne for at danne et overblik omkring, hvad tidligere studerende i de kurser har sagt.
course_level: Det var meget filmpraktiskefag på Undergraduate niveau.
teaching_comparison: Der er mange flere læsninger, som man skal bevise man har læst ved at lave et diskussionsafsnit man sender til læreren inden hver undervisningsgang. Desuden er der mange flere løbende opgaver end der er på KU, som alle sammen tæller med i din endelige karakter. Det føltes lidt som at gå på gymnasiet igen i forhold til deltagelse og så videre.

crucial_aspects: The city and school that I was going to study at and in. I wanted a place that could challenge me and expand my knowledge and understanding, and a destination rich on new experiences. I wanted to improve my english skills for my master degree as well, so it was important that it was an english speaking country.
info_ease: It was very hard. I felt alone in the proces and I was in distress with the visa, payment for the school and the sign up for classes where we were put last in line for registration which I found weird when we would only be able to participate in classes for one semester. I found the resources at my home university lackfull in regarding to the specific deal KU has with Barnard.
arrival_assistance: I studied at Barnard College in New York City where they had a welcoming program for international students called VISP and a resource at the school called Acces Barnard that introduced us to and helped us navigate a new university. Yet, not all times was this resource helpfull.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: There is a 14 days shopping period, were you try out classes, but all the students studying at the school has already signed up for classes, so you are put last in line and need to fight and try to convince the professors to give you a spot. This was very stressfull in a time where everything is new, so I think that we should be able register beforehand just as the other students. It is a little nervewrecking travelling to the other side of the world for your education not even knowing if you will be able to take classes that will be approved or even are relevant to your field of study.
registration_help: Counselors and deans were helpful, but the proces is just so bad that often they couldn't do anything about the fact that classes were full.
registration_success: I got classes that was relevant for me, but many of the classes I had looked at back home didn't have available spots when I got there which was a shame. Some of my classes weren't the ones I wanted and that was a big shame because I think I would have learned a lot from those.
registration_advice: Before going, ty to see if you can find the emails for the professors of the classes you want and then email them to tell them about your situation and see if you can get a spot on the waitlist or in the class. Often they are helpfull and this seemed like a normal procedure.
course_level: The level of the different courses varies a lot and I was taking both introductionary courses and graduate courses.
teaching_comparison: Different from back home, feels more like going to gymnasium where you have a big workload throughout the semester and has to do a lot of tests assignments and quizzes that you are graded for as well.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to architectural history Urban ecosystems Design futures: New York City Urban ecology and design
recommended_courses: Depends on what you study. I really enjoyed the professor of design futures; Ivan Munuera! and the professor in Urban ecosystems Elizabeth Cook. Urban ecology and design was also interesting with nice field trips
unexpected_costs: We needed to pay some extra money for the welcoming week and programme made for us during this time. Also the VISA for USA is very expensive and an extra travel insurance was needed.
cost_comparison: It is a very expensive city to live in in general so everything adds up when you go out with taxes and tips.
activities_available: All kinds of clubs and a gym.
activities_recommended: I didn't try out as many, but it was fun to go and watch the schools basketball games.
weekend_recommendations: Explore New York City, go upstate on a roadtrip
culture_adjustment: Yes, New York is such a nice (but also a little crazy) place
cultural_challenges: Hard to do group work in class.
culture_appreciated: Diversity and many experiences around every corner.
top3_advice: It will sort out with classes and enjoy the city as much as possible.
other_useful_info: Try to email professors beforehand.
most_rewarding: Living in a new environment and getting to know new people and a new way of studying.
greatest_challenge: All the stuff before the stay, planning, registration, etc.

activities_recommended: n/a

crucial_aspects: Location and the University's reputation
info_ease: Easy. There is one week of orientation for visiting and transfer students, so you are overloaded with information the first week. Not very useful, however, if you have any questions there are so many people who can answer them during this week.
arrival_assistance: We received the keys to our accomodation upon arrival, and could ask residential life any questions. Later that same day we had dinner with the International Students Services, who were also helpful to tell us about the orientation program. If anything, they give you too much info and too much assistance.
arrival_comments: Too time consuming to spend a week on orientation. They could have sent us a long document, and cut the program down to one day.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You can in december register ONLY for classes at Barnard. Around the 7th of January you can register for all classes, however most will be full, so you will have to jon to waitlist. You can join a max of 3 waitlists and 19 credits of classes in total. Join all the classes you may attend during shopping. Don't stress if you are number 50 on the waitlist, they move a lot during shopping. Everyone always ends up getting the classes they want, unless there are special restrictions. Tips: do your course search in vergil and focus onBarnard classes first, as you register for those first. Later look at Columbias. Register as soon as you can, mostly if there's a waitlist so you are higher up. Attend all your waitlisted classes, as they often take attendence, and you can talk to the professor about giving you priority.
registration_help: You have your own academic advisor that can help. You can contact the registrar for more technical issues.
registration_success: Got all the ones I wanted.
registration_advice: Talk to students about what classes or professors they liked. Look up your professors on culpa to see what students say. Attend as many classes as you can during shopping. Know that you can take basically any class offered at Columbia, even at the different grad schools, although you will need to contact professors directly about registering for classes level 5000+. They don't inform yoy about this beforehand, so I thought our options were limited based on Barnards website, but you can take any course you can find on Vergil basically. Try a class that is different from your field of study! They offer insanely many different courses, take advantage of that.
course_level: Two classes were third year undergrad, two were graduate or 4th year undergrad.
teaching_comparison: Much smaller lectures and professors are more available -more office hours etc., and students really take advantage of the OH. Instead of class style lessons with TA's like at UCPH, the TA's often offered either office hours or recitations, but they were more so based on questions from students or going over assignments than actually working through lecture material. A lot more work during the semester with graded assignments, graded participation and both a midterm and final exam.
courses_enrolled: Money and Banking (would not recommend with Tri Vi Dang) Finance and the Real Economy (Would recommend) Women and Health (would not recommend) Game Theory (would recommend as a substitute for micro 3)
recommended_courses: See above
unexpected_costs: Expect to pay Barnard 100.000 DKK in advance for housing, health insurance and meal plan. Further I spent around 8000 on my own insurance, and around 4.000 on flights in advance. Be aware of this, as it's a lot to pay all at once before leaving, so make sure you save up for that.
cost_comparison: Everything is more expensive than at home, but that was to be expected. I was mostly shoicked by how much Barnard charges for housing, insurance and meal plans and over there I was shocked by the insane prices of basic groceries. Eating and drinking out isn't that much more expensive than cph.
activities_available: There are many clubs and societies you can join. Your student ID also gives you access to many museums in and around NYC, which saves you a ton of money.
activities_recommended: Go to all the museums that are available to you for free!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! You can bring guests! While you are often let in for free, your guests will be let in on pay-as-you-wish, so they can literally give 1 dollar.
weekend_recommendations: Explore! Go out as much as you can, even if it's just a walk in a park or a coffee in a diner. I expected to visit other cities as well, but ended up feeling like 4 months in Manhattan wasn't enough, as there are do many places to visit. Also take advantage of how nice Columbia's campus is.
culture_adjustment: Relatively easy.
socializing_tips: They are very welcoming. If you want to make local friends it's super easy.
cultural_challenges: Americans are very different than danes, so probably people's behavior. Also the food in the dining halls was a bit hard to get used to.
culture_appreciated: How welcoming and warm Americans are
top3_advice: Be prepared for lots of paper work in advance, be prepared to pay around 150.000 DKK for the whole thing and please consider how the Trump administration is dealing with international students at the time of your visit and if you are willing to live with the stress of that.
other_useful_info: They shoud send you some sort of enrollment package after your enrollment is confirmed. This contains important deadlines about payment, signing up for classes, uploading vaccination documents, signing up for housing etc. They forgot to send it to us, so the three months before departure were extremely stressful, as we were constantly blindsided by short deadlines. So make sure you receive this enrollment package, if not ask for it.
most_rewarding: Living in NYC - 100% worth the struggle and the cost.
greatest_challenge: I stressed a lot about getting my courses pre-approved by UCPH because I couldn't get the syllabi for the classes until after I was enrolled in them, so that was a bit stressfull. Be prepared for the stress of that, and decide with yourself if you think it's worth it.
other_comments: If you are ocnsidering going to Barnard - do it! It's expensive and takes alot of time in preparation, but it's worth it!! However, be sure to check up on the US' policies for student visas, and be prepared for UCPH not helping you with anything. Connect with your fellow UCPH students before going, it's much easier if you help each others.

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte destinationen pga. universitetet for den række af specialiserede fag, som de udbød.
info_ease: Universitetets forskellige er meget behjælpelig med alle praktiske ting omkring visum, bolig, mealplan, valg af fag osv. idet de afholder løbende møder og er tilgængelige på mail i månederne op til. De har et helt kontor til at tage sig af deres visiting students
arrival_assistance: Den første uge er orientation, hvor man får overvældende mange informationer og mulighed for at møde de andre. Det største problem var næsten, at der var for meget information.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: KU var rigtig hjælpsomme til at starte med og gav de oplysninger man havde brug for. Koordinatoren var også hurtig til at svare på mails og man blev ikke overvældet af alt for mange informationer på en gang.
registration_help: Der er kontoret ISS for alle internationale studerende og så får man sin personal dean, som man holder møder med, som kan sparre med en omkring fag og det sociale.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag, som jeg ønskede. Der var et fag, som jeg var på venteliste på, men det kan betale sig at skrive til professorerne i forvejen og lade dem vide, hvorfor man er særligt interesseret, og at man kun har mulighed for at tage faget det ene semester. Jeg fandt dem meget imødekommende for at hjælpe.
registration_advice: Sæt tid af til det, og undersøg grundigt hvad du er interesseret i, så du får mest ud af det.
course_level: Niveauerne var forskellige, men grundlæggende højt til undervisningen, fordi der bliver forventet en anden form for deltagelse. Det var dog ikke svært at bestå. Jeg tog et fag, som både var for master, bachelor og phd-studerende, og der var niveauet højere, men der blev også differencieret mellem de forskellige niveauer, så der ikke blev stillet de samme forventninger. At have undervisning med andre typer af uddannelser løftede kun diskussionerne i klasselokalet.
teaching_comparison: Der er forventninger til at man deltager mere aktivt, og der skal afleveres mere i løbet af semestret. Læsemængden er også større. Til gengæld er de andre studerende grundlæggende mere aktive og derfor løftes niveauet. Der udbydes både kurser som er forelæsninger med tilhørende diskussionstimer, der undervises af PhD-studerende og så udbydes der seminarer, som er diskussionstunge og læsetunge fag, hvor man kun er maks 15 studerende.
courses_enrolled: British Portraiture, Identity and the Museum Pastel and the Enlightenment Land and Landscape
recommended_courses: Alle tre, hvis man finder europæisk kunsthistorie fra 1700-1800 tallet interessant.
unexpected_costs: Vær obs på at man bliver smidt ud af sin student housing, så snart semestret er slut, så forvent ekstra udgifter, hvis du ønsker at blive længere. Man skal også betale for orientation, visum, sprogtest mfl. små udgifter.
cost_comparison: Mad er i supermarkedet er dyrt, men man kan godt få det til at løbe rundt.
activities_available: Alt muligt: dans, kulturaftener mm. Benyttede det ikke.
activities_recommended: Brug byen
weekend_recommendations: Tag rundt i byen, se museer, gå rundt i forskellige kvarterer og spørg hvem end du møder, om de har gode anbefalinger.
culture_adjustment: Forholdsvis nemt. Columbia og Barnard har mange internationale studerende, så man blender nemt ind.
socializing_tips: Ræk ud til dem - de fleste er søde og vil gerne snakke, give anbefalinger eller mødes over en kaffe.
cultural_challenges: Maden kan være lidt op ad bakke...
culture_appreciated: Åbenheden og byens uendelige muligheder.
top3_advice: Sæt tid af til at forberede de prakstiske ting; Tag afsted, for du kommer ikke til at fortryde det; Nyd det mens du er der, det går alt for hurtigt.
other_useful_info: Barnard har høje krav til sprogtesten, og selvom de tager alt meget alvorligt, er det muligt at blive optaget, hvis man lige er et par point fra.
most_rewarding: Det faglige og sociale, hvis man kaster sig ud i det.
greatest_challenge: Maden

crucial_aspects: Jeg har altid drømt at komme til New York, og udforske byens kultur, teaterlandskab, mad og atmosfære.
info_ease: Det var ikke let, hverken fra KU's eller Barnard College's side. Man skal selv stå for at søge meget ift. en masse dokumentation, oplysninger mm.
arrival_assistance: Vi havde en velkomst middag hvor vi fik en del informationer om opstart osv. Den efterfølgende uge havde vi et introforløb hvor vi fik rigtig meget information om bolig, studieliv, regler på institutionen mm.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Jeg fandt flere forskellige hjemmesider som fremstod som deres kursus udvalg, men jeg var rimelig forvirret omrking hvilke kurser som var gjaldte eller ej. Det som jeg gjorde var: få en idé om de kurser jeg gerne vi søge, vær OBS på at de tidsmæssigt kan støbes sammen som et skoleskema(uden af de overlapper tidsmæssigt) og så sørg for at skrive til den mail der er tilknyttet kurset du er interesseret i! Da jeg skrev til de forskellige var der professore som gav mig bekræftelse på at jeg kunne få en plads på deres kursus når semestret startede, og andre professors gav besked på at kursus ikke kunne søges lige pt mm. En god regel er: hellere for mange kurser du er interesseret i end for lidt. Du skal min. have 12 credits for at tage et semester på Barnard.
registration_help: Jeg blev tilknyttet en "Dean" af Barnard, som er deres form for kursusvejleder. Jeg havde et zoom møde med vedkommende før og efter kursusansøgnignsprocessen, og det var en stor hjælp.
registration_success: Alle de kurser jeg søgte fik jeg plads på. Nogle kurser jeg havde interesse i valgte jeg fra til sidst, fordi jeg indså at jeg havde fået mig et skema med kurser der svarede til de 12 credits.
registration_advice: Gør dig en masse research på de forskellige kurser du kunne have interesse i og skriv kursets navn og nummer ned på en liste til dig selv. Og som sagt; hellere have for mange kurser på din liste, end for lidt. Du kan nemlig risikere at du ikke får dine favoritter.
course_level: Niveauet var højt, men jeg synes det var håndterbart.
teaching_comparison: Måden at studere på og deltage i undervisningen er meget anderledes for KU's måde. På Barnard bliver du bedømt på: aktiv deltagelse i undervisningen, en masse diskussions opslag på Canvas/mini opgaver i løbet af semestret og så de tager streng fravær og har du for meget fravær falder din endelige karakter.
courses_enrolled: ACTING I DANCE IN NEW YORK CITY DIRECTING I MOVING WITH THE VOICE BEGINNING YOGA
recommended_courses: Et særligt fedt kursus er DANCE IN NEW YORK CITY, fordi man arbejder med danskelandskabet i NYC, og gennem skolen skal ud og se en håndfuld danse performances betalt af skolen. Det er en unik mulighed for at se en masse performance i byen, og måske møde nogle stilarter eller steder som du ikke selv ville have opsøgt.
unexpected_costs: VISUM = i alt 2.874 DKK GEBYR ved betaling af husleje, mealplan, sundhedsforsikring = 12.947 DKK
cost_comparison: Sundhedsforsikringen tilknyttet Barnard var overraskende dyr. Der var ingen til få omkostningen for bøger og skolematerialer. Der var få "udflugter" jeg skulle på rundt omkring i byen, men 8 ud af 10 var betalt af skolen, så det var minimalt hvad vi selv skulle betale for.
activities_available: Der er ugeligt små pop-up events på Barnard og Columbias campus, hvor man kan komme til foredrag, lave krea ting, deltage i konkurrencer, deltage til middage mm.
activities_recommended: Deltag I Winning Wednesday i lobbyen i bygningen Diana på Barnard. Her kan du møde op og få små merch/legetøj/snack helt gratis, og få mulighed for at chatte med andre Barnard studerende. Hold gerne øje på din Barnard Mail, når du får sådan en, og skriv sjove events ned i din kalender! Alle disse er altså helt gratis, og en hyggelig mulighed for at få et pusterum fra studie ræs og opgaveskrivning.
weekend_recommendations: Tag til de forskellige boroughs i New York, besøg lokale anbefalede spisesteder/cafeer, tag ind og se Broadway Musicals, tag på jazz bar, løb en tur i parkerne, lav picnic i Central Park og generelt bare gå gå gå så meget som muligt! Pas på med at cykle i byen - de har altså ikke det samme smarte cykelsystem som i Danmark.
culture_adjustment: Det tog selvfølgelig lidt tilvænning, men jeg synes vi blev taget godt hånd om, og havde generelt det nemt ved at tilpasse mig den amerikanske kultur.
socializing_tips: Deltag til events, vær åben, nysgerrig og imødekommende, og tagg ud på solo trips - her ender du tit alligevel med at falde i snak med en ny lokal.
cultural_challenges: Mange af amerikanerne fra New York er meget travle folk, så du skal selv aktivt opsøge nye bekendskaber og vise din interesse og tid i at hænge ud og lære dem bedre at kende.
culture_appreciated: Deres åbenhed og deres snaksaglighed.

crucial_aspects: It had to be an academically high ranking univeristy while still be easy to get around in the city without a car.
overall_comments: It has been such a wonderful experience - the only reason why I do not give it 10 is because of the living situation. However, the university is bustling with life and such interesting people with all sorts of backgrounds.
info_ease: There was SO much information prior to and upon arrival. You get countless emails with a lot of redundant information. It takes a long time to find out what is actually necessary information for you to be updated on.
arrival_assistance: At American universities, they expect you to be coming straight out of your parents' house, so they pretty much give you all the assistance you need. Like ALL you need - at some point they went over what you should have in an emergency kit at home (like napkins and stuff)...
arrival_comments: I had all the help I needed and more if I would have liked.

registration_comments: It has been such a wonderful experience - the only reason why I do not give it 10 is because of the living situation. However, the university is bustling with life and such interesting people with all sorts of backgrounds.
registration_process: Exchange students are the last students to register for class. There are only a certain number of students that are entered into each class. However, in the US, they have a "shopping-period" - i.e. you have registered for a lot of classes and then drop the classes you don't like before the period is over. Thereby, if you waitlist for classes, spots are highly likely to open up even after the semester has begun. Additionally, the professors are very approachable and may let you in if you talk to them.
registration_help: There was an academic advisor available, but she was rather slow at responding.
registration_success: I was waitlisted for a lot of my classes in the beginning, but managed to get into all of them by the end of the registration period.
registration_advice: Book a meeting with the academic advisor to make sure you are aware of all the deadlines in regards to registration - there are a lot more than at KU.
academics_comments: It has been such a wonderful experience - the only reason why I do not give it 10 is because of the living situation. However, the university is bustling with life and such interesting people with all sorts of backgrounds.
course_level: They were very easy! In the US, people only do a few courses within their major and the rest covers other academic interests. Therefore, the average American student does not have a very thorough knowledge of their major at undergraduate level. All the economics courses I took turned out to be equivalent to a level 1-4th semester at KU. It even allowed me to do a total of 45 ECTS points - I would never have done that at KU!
teaching_comparison: It is a lot more interactive and taught in smaller classes. Participation goes towards your grade. It feels like being back in high school.
courses_enrolled: The Global Economy Economic History of Global Capitalism (approved as "Økonomisk Historie") Money & Banking China's Foreign Relations Advanced Poetry Writing Research Credit
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed pursuing my hobby at a professional level, which is why I took the course "Advanced Poetry Writing". Do take advantage of this - I am unfortunately not able to transfer these specific ECTS point back to KU because it is outside of my major, but the creative classes do not take up that much time. They have all sorts of creative classes: everything from pottery making to tap dancing and everything in between.
unexpected_costs: You pay for a mandatory health insurance when you are an exchange student. That's why the insurance costs I have listed are so high.
cost_comparison: Groceries are a lot more expensive in NYC than in Denmark.
activities_available: Literally anything you can think of.
activities_recommended: I joined a bible study through RUF. I enjoyed the academic approach to studying the bible. The people I met there were also some of the most sweet and welcoming people I have met throughout my stay.
weekend_recommendations: Go on the Staten Ferry Island - it is free and gives a beautiful view of the city from the river.
culture_adjustment: I have lived abroad before, so I found it relatively easy. The American culture is also very welcoming, so it is easy to find friends.
socializing_tips: Take advantage of how everybody has a meal plan, so it is easy to meet for meals.
cultural_challenges: In the beginning, I had a hard time adjusting to how the city could feel a bit unsafe at times. However, you learn that it is not unsafe; it is just the city that can look a bit odd at times.
culture_appreciated: The diversity of the student body - everybody has a different background than you, so you hear a lot of interesting stories!
top3_advice: If you are even considering it, GO! That's my only important thing:)
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: Academically, it has been super interesting to be exposed to economic examples that aren't Danish. Here, North and South America are in focus when examples are made. It has worked as a great source of inspiration for my studies.
greatest_challenge: Finding out where to get affordable groceries.
