crucial_aspects: I chose to study at the Complutense, because of the courses that were offered that I found very interesting and useful as well as the fact that I have wanted to be able to stay in the Spanish capital over a longer period of time and the semester abroad was the perfect opportunity to be able to live out that dream.
overall_comments: I am extremely satisfied overall with my study abroad experience in Madrid as well as thankful for what I have learned both academically and personally and for the people that have been part of making my exchange an unforgettable experience.
info_ease: Well, I would not say it was too difficult or too easy. The International Relations Office at the University was helpful with the general process, but getting to understand how exactly certain things work in an academic setting in Spain took some time in the beginning, but I view that as part of the learning process and never imagined that I would receive a piece of paper telling me everything I needed to know from day one. My experience was that if I sought out information either at the university office or among my Spanish peers, most of my questions would be answered.
arrival_assistance: Help from the International Relations Office to enroll me as an exchange student.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I am extremely satisfied overall with my study abroad experience in Madrid as well as thankful for what I have learned both academically and personally and for the people that have been part of making my exchange an unforgettable experience.
registration_process: Well, I was told by the UCM that as an Erasmus student, my registration process began with me trying out different classes and deciding which ones I liked. Therefore handing out a document to every individual professor getting their signature and then handing it all to the International Relations Office. Apparently, this was not all factual, as I was told by KU that I could only be enrolled in the courses where I had gotten a Forhåndsgodkendelse. After having realized this, I had to talk to KU about getting a revideret forhåndsgodkendelse. The only problem was that the deadline had exactly just passed even though I had only been at the uni for a few days. Luckily KU helped and we resolved it so that I could get the courses that I actually found interesting and not just the ones that I had selected at home in Denmark without having had a chance to be sure that the level was right for me as well as the content.
registration_help: I think I answer this above.
registration_success: I think I answer this above.
registration_advice: Talk to both of your Universities from the beginning and figure out whether the information you receive is the same or not. I did not receive the same information from the beginning which created a moment of stress for me in the registration process, but I am happy that it worked out.
academics_comments: I am extremely satisfied overall with my study abroad experience in Madrid as well as thankful for what I have learned both academically and personally and for the people that have been part of making my exchange an unforgettable experience.
course_level: The courses were just exactly to my liking. Additionally, the professors were very sympathetic which made me feel welcome as the only exchange student, which I was in 4/5 of my courses.
teaching_comparison: In most courses, there was less teacher-student interaction in the class. At KU and in Denmark in general we have a long tradition of valuing what students think about a certain topic and students get to be very much involved in the classroom conversation. Whereas in Spain, for the most part, it is much more a teacher monologue, and as a student you just sit back, listen, and take notes.
courses_enrolled: ESTRUCTURA Y SISTEMA MUNDIAL DE LA INFORMACIÓN (803634) HISTORIA DEL MUNDO ACTUAL (803582) OPINIÓN PÚBLICA (803614) PRAGMÁTICA Y DISCURSO EN EL PERIODISMO (803596) VARIEDADES DEL ESPAÑOL. EL ESPAÑOL DE AMÉRICA (802129)
recommended_courses: ESTRUCTURA Y SISTEMA MUNDIAL DE LA INFORMACIÓN (803634) I would recommend any future student with an interest in studying abroad at the Faculty of Infomation Sciences to enroll in this course. Sergio Principe is probably the most sympathetic and friendly teacher that I have ever had. He is extremely knowledgeable about current world affairs, politics, media theories, etc. He always teaches in an energetic matter which is why his classes are never boring. I have learned so incredibly much during his course.
unexpected_costs: Trips to other cities or abroad. Being on Erasmus you find yourself in a situation where you want to explore not only your study destination but also surrounding cities or even countries. I ended up going to places that I did not plan to go to.
cost_comparison: The cost of transportation in Madrid was way lower than I could have ever imagined. I pay only 8€ a month for my youth card which allows me to travel freely by bus, metro, and train in all of the Capital region, as far as Toledo. In Denmark the youth card cost close to 10 times as much, or 80€.
activities_available: The uni did offer certain conferences or excursions, but being very busy with my own private life, I did not pay too much attention to what was being offered.
activities_recommended: I answer this above.
weekend_recommendations: Depending on each one's interest, in the city of Madrid, there is an abundance of opportunities. Going to the Retiro Park with friends for a picnic, taking a swim in the public swimming pools on a hot day, strolling through the streets of the city center, and eating tapas at the bars or food markets. Madrid is a city where you really get to understand what living life means.
culture_adjustment: Quite easy as I have previously spent half a year living in Malaga, Andalucia where I learned about cultural barriers and was able to break them down.
socializing_tips: Do not be shy. Talk to them. Let them know that you are open to friendships. Do not expect everyone to come to you and do the talking. You have to do the work, at least in the beginning.
cultural_challenges: A classic of Spain is the siesta. Living a bit outside of the city center I have had to get used to not being able to go have a beverage or a tapas with friends at any time we wanted. We were all well aware of the siesta, but that doest not mean we like the idea that establishments are closed for multiple hours during the day. You change your habits a bit due to the environment where you find yourself.
culture_appreciated: The gastronomy, architecture, and laidbackness of the Spanish people.
top3_advice: First, look for accommodation as early as possible and research the neighborhoods and how far they are from uni. Madrid is a large city and the capital region has more inhabitants than our country of Denmark, so get used to longer distances and spending more time on transportation. Second, try to be as social as possible in the beginning. Both with your peers at uni as well as your roommates. The first impression you give to people is usually the one they remember the most. Also, join the events that Erasmus has to offer as well as other exchange student organizations such as City Life Madrid. By following my instructions you can be sure to meet like-minded people and make friendships. Third, focus on your studies. Studying abroad is not just fun, but a journey with its own challenges. Studying completely in Spanish is not easy and it takes time to get accustomed to it. Therefore go to your classes, hand in your papers, and try to absorb the language as much as you can in your free time. After one semester you will then see a big increase in your language skills.
other_useful_info: I think I already answer this.
most_rewarding: Being in a Spanish academic setting learning how to navigate a new system and also just the daily interactions with peers, strangers, and roommates while living abroad.
greatest_challenge: Besides certain academic challenges, I would say that living with 6 people for 5 months has been a challenge at times, both positively and negatively. However, it has been rather rewarding in terms of the friendships established and getting to know me while living under collective norms and rules compared to living by my own rules.

crucial_aspects: I have always dreamt of being a journalist, and Universidad Complutense de Madrid was the only partner university with the option to have journalistic subjects. Besides, I really like Madrid and I wanted to try to live here for some time.
info_ease: The international relations office at the faculty of information has been really helpful. When you arrive in a new country - and at a new university - sometimes it can be difficult to understand how exactly everything works, and there is a lot of information at the same time. The secretaries at the international relations office have been very welcoming and quick to respond.
arrival_assistance: Before the arrival, I received several emails from the internacional relations office with information about the arrival. The Friday before the semester began there was an information meeting for exchange students at the faculty of information about the matriculation process, but unfortunately I couldn't attend because of my exams at UCPH. There was also an information meeting for all Erasmus students at UCM, which was also very helpful. Apart from that, as mentioned before, the international relations office has been very helpful in all regards.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Before arrival, the international relations office sends you a couple of documents that must be filled in and signed upon arrival as a part of the matriculation process. You are responsible for putting together your own schedule, which means that already while you apply for "forhåndsgodkendelse" at UCPH you must check if the subjects overlap. If not, you have to apply for an updated "forhåndsgodkendelse" with new subjects which can delay the process a lot. Once you find out what subjects you are able to attend, you show up at class and get the professor from each subject to sign a document that approves your participation in the subject. Once all that is done, the international relations office can finish the matriculation process.
registration_help: As mentioned before, the internacional relations office has been really helpful.
registration_success: Luckily, I managed to sign up for all the subjects I wanted and that appeared in my "forhåndsgodkendelse", because I checked the schedule of each subject while I applied for the "forhåndsgodkendelse".
registration_advice: The most important thing is to read carefully all the emails and documents that you receive, fill in the documents in time and, as I mentioned before, take a look at the schedule of each subject while you apply for your "forhåndsgodkendelse".
course_level: The level has varied a lot from course to course, but generally it has been lower than at UCPH. Though, the work load has been quite high, since there are a lot of written assignments and presentations throughout the semester and because you have 5 different subjects at the same time.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching in Spain reminds me a bit of high school, because of all the (mandatory) written assignments and presentations throughout the semester and because they register attendance in class. There has been a lot of dialogue and interaction in class, at least in my subjects, which surprised me positively, but still there are a lot of memorizing. The lack of flexibility and perhaps self-determination has been a bit frustrating sometimes.
courses_enrolled: PRAGMÁTICA Y DISCURSO EN EL PERIODISMO - 803596 LINGÜÍSTICA Y ESTUDIOS CULTURALES - 805427 (faculty of filology) ESTRUCTURA Y SISTEMA MUNDIAL DE LA INFORMACIÓN - 803634 HISTORIA DEL PENSAMIENTO POLÍTICO CONTEMPORÁNEO - 803598 CIENCIA POLÍTICA Y RELACIONES INTERNACIONALES - 803581
recommended_courses: My favorite subject has been "pragmática y discurso en el periodismo" with the professor Raquel Taranilla García. It has been very "practical" because we got to write and analyse different journalistic texts from the news media, and I had the opportunity to make usage of cultural and linguistic knowledge. Raquel has been very friendly, helpful and willing to consider our situation as exchange students. She is definitely one of the best professors I have ever had.
unexpected_costs: Medicin in connection with illness.
cost_comparison: Especially public transportation has been way cheaper than I expected. As a student, you can use all public transportation in Madrid with a cost of 8 euros per month. Though, food in the supermarket has been more expensive than I expected (it is almost as expensive as in Denmark).
activities_available: Universidad Complutense offers a lot of different activities. There are a lot of sports facilities and teams, and the university collaborates with a variety of cultural institutions.
activities_recommended: I had a fitness membership through the university, where I could access fitness facilities and take different classes such as pilates and yoga. For me it was nice not having a fixed schedule as I would have had if I was a part of a football team or the like, because there are quiete a lot of written assignments, as I mentioned before.
weekend_recommendations: First of all, I would recommend exploring different neighborhoods in Madrid. Also, there are several nice places outside Madrid such as Toledo, Segovia and Alcalá de Henares. Madrid is very well-connected, and it's easy to take high-speed trains to other parts of Spain.
culture_adjustment: For me, it has been quite easy, since I already spoke Spanish when I arrived. Generally, the locals are very welcoming, open-minded and easy to talk to. They would often help you if you are in doubt of anything, invite you to social gatherings, etc.
socializing_tips: One of the things that made it easier for me to socialize with local students has been all the group work at the university. This allowed me to get to know the other students better. Apart from that, it is always a good idea to participate in cultural and athletic activities at the university.
cultural_challenges: Even though this is not only a cultural matter, I would say the age gap between me and the local students. Most Spanish students go directly from high school to university, which means they are really young and don't have a lot of experience.
culture_appreciated: I appreciated the mentality of the Spanish people. They are very social, talkative and open-minded, and they don't necessarily take things so seriously.
top3_advice: Be aware that the style of teaching is different compared with that of UCPH, be open-minded and try to interact as much as possible with the local students.
other_useful_info: No, nothing that I havn't mentioned already.
most_rewarding: To try to live in a new country and all the amazing people I met.
greatest_challenge: Getting use to a different style of teaching.

crucial_aspects: From the start I knew that I wanted to do my exchange in Spain, but I chose to do it in Madrid because I have a lot of connections there, plus its a big city with a lot of travel opportunities, you can easily take the train a couple of hours and go to other cities.
overall_comments: I love Madrid, it has been the coolest place to study, but the way they teach their clases has been a little difficult for me, because of the lack of dialogue in class between teacher and student, which is something that I've been used to in Copenhagen.
info_ease: I think it was very simple actually, they send you emails and information all the time, and once I got to the university everyone was helpful if I needed to know anything.
arrival_assistance: I didn't really need any assistance other than the first day when I needed to find the Erasmus office, or when I needed to find out how to print, but that was it.
arrival_comments: No
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I love Madrid, it has been the coolest place to study, but the way they teach their clases has been a little difficult for me, because of the lack of dialogue in class between teacher and student, which is something that I've been used to in Copenhagen.
registration_process: Once you get to your host institution they send you a lot of documents you have to sign, and you have to make your schedule by yourself, make sure that the courses don't overlap each other, and then you just show up to your chosen courses, you also have to get each teachers signatures to show that they have accepted your assistance in their classes. Once you have all the signatures you have to go to the Erasmus office and get the faculties stamp and get registrated.
registration_help: The Erasmus office helps you with everything you have to do.
registration_success: I was very successful, the only difficult thing was to make sure you don't overlap your courses.
registration_advice: There's a lot of paperwork, so be prepared to have a little patience.
academics_comments: I love Madrid, it has been the coolest place to study, but the way they teach their clases has been a little difficult for me, because of the lack of dialogue in class between teacher and student, which is something that I've been used to in Copenhagen.
course_level: The courses have different groups, some for first year students, second and so on, I mostly took courses for the first year students because I didn't know a whole lot about the subjects, other than I wanted and was interested in learning more.
teaching_comparison: I didn't like the way they teach that much, the clases was an hour and a half long without the usual 15 minutes of break that we get in UCPH, so it was hard to focus especially when the teachers just talk and talk the entire time, I missed a little more dialogue between student and teacher. Also, the fact that I chose first year courses also meant that the other student were very young and unserious in class, there wasn't a mutual student/teacher relationship of respect. In UCPH we are used to be treated as the adults we are, and the clases are much more respectful. In UCPH its your own responsibility to pass the courses, but its not mandatory to assist to the classes, in UCM you could suspend if you don't show up. Another thing was the amount of "homework" you get if you choose to do the "continuous evaluation".
courses_enrolled: I chose 4 courses in "La facultad de ciencias de la información", and one in "La Facultad de Filología" Facultad de ciencias de la información: - Pragmática y discurso en el Periodismo - Teoría de la Comunicación - Historia del Pensamiento Político Contemporáneo - Ciencia Política y Relaciones internacionales Facultad de Filología - Lingüística y Estudios Culturales
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed Teoría de la Comunicación and the way my teacher Fransisco Javier Malagon Terron, teaches his class. Also Pragmática y discurso en el Periodismo, Raquel Taranilla García, was my best Teacher during this exchange. Both of these courses were very instructive.
unexpected_costs: Unexpected sickness, medicine costs for example
cost_comparison: The transportation costs were less than I expected, if you are a student you can travel in all Madrid for 8 euros per month, all you want. Restaurants were more expensive than I expected
activities_available: With the campus card and your Erasmus card, you have access and offers to most social activities, outdoor pools and fitness centers, the campus also has a lot of different sports teams you can join if you wish.
activities_recommended: Definitely join the campus fitness or other sport teams, and take advantage of the offers they provide in museums and clubs as well.
weekend_recommendations: Travel out of Madrid, Toledo for example, as I said earlier, with the train from Madrid you can basically go everywhere so easily.
culture_adjustment: For me it was very easy because I have family and friends in Madrid already, so I've been here a lot. I love this city.
socializing_tips: Just be open, people are very open to do things together.
cultural_challenges: The healthcare system, it was very frustrating to go to the doctor, they take and eternity and I felt like they didn't take me seriously.
culture_appreciated: The atmosphere, Madrid just have a good vibe in general, the fact that people are so relaxed and social.
top3_advice: Be patient Take advantage of the offers you get with the campus card Sit in the front of the class, to make sure you are able to hear what the teacher is saying.
other_useful_info: Always ask your professors for help if there's anything you have doubts about, they are always ready to help
most_rewarding: Once you get used to the metro you feel like a local, and free to go anywhere. Also when you pass your courses obviously.
greatest_challenge: Medical attendance, but that's it.
other_comments: Enjoy and have fun in everything your doing during your exchange, time flies by so fast.

crucial_aspects: It was important for me to choose a university that is/was high ranked and recognized as international university ranking. Furthermore It was important for me that to choose an university that had high level in terms of language, culture and linguistic studies. In terms of location, it was important for me to choose a city that had a rich culture life to fulfill that objetive of the Erasmus exchange as a culture travel as well.
info_ease: I would say it was quite easy to find the relevant information on the Complutense webpage, and/or contacting the international office for philology if the needed information was not to be found on the webpage. Otherwise the information e-mails received told you most of what you needed to know related to deadlines, enrollment, choosing courses, etc.
arrival_assistance: I received assistance in the enrollment to the programe of students with disabilities to have the tools needed for my dyslexia. Furthermore I received assistance to get the Learning Agreement properly signed by the international office.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: 1) I had to make the learning agreement and get it signed by both sending and hosting institution. 2) I had to register myself as a student (and get accepted) in the enrollment page of Complutense. The information and link for this was sent by e-mail. You're not officially accepted at Complutense until this part in completed. 3) I had to make an Complutense e-mail to get access to Campus Virtual. The information for this is also sent to you by e-mail. 4) When the semester started, I had to make an enrollment with my informations and the information of each course chosen, and have it signed physically by the international office of philology.
registration_help: Most information you need, you can find on the university webpage and/or contacting the international office by e-mail.
registration_advice: 1) When choose the courses (already in the learning agreement) check the timeslots and weekdays for the courses you would like, and make a schedule to make sure that the courses do not overlap. 2) Look at more courses that the once you've chosen, the first 2 weeks you can change courses. Take advantage of this opportunity to try diferent courses the first week, and be open minded to a change because it's very likely that someone of the courses you've chosen is not what you expected.
course_level: The level of teaching and the content of the course/each class is very high with a lot of extra information than needed. In terms of spanish language and literature, the level in the classroom is very high both regarding to the texts you have to read, activities in the classroom and the assignments you have to make.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching in the classroom (in most classes) is similar to that what I experienced at UCPH. But, there is not room for question in the same way. Therefore, what you don't feel that you've learned properly, it is your responsibility to learn by your own or ask for a tutor meeting with your profesor. Furthermore, each course as fever ECTS which means that you have a lot more courses and more classes that all have a very high demand in assignments.
courses_enrolled: Retórica y crítica literaria Sociolingüística española Lingüística y estudios culturales Enseñanza de español como lengua extranjera El cuento hispanoamericano
recommended_courses: Lingüística y estudios culturales. The professor Viviane Martins has a different way of teaching than the majority of the professors, that both make the classroom comfortable for the students, but also by incorporating many assignments and presentations according to each subject. This also means that assignment demand is very high, be aware of this.
unexpected_costs: Since it is an intense and stressfull semester, in my case, my health was weaker than expected and I got frequently sick. Therefore the price for medicine was not something i encounter.
cost_comparison: The local transport is cheaper than expected. When you're less than 25, you can get a public transport card (for metro, trains and buses) for 8€ a month.
activities_available: There is a lot of different type of "fitness"-classes such as: Pilates, yoga, zumba, merengue, swimming etc. Sports activities in teams such as: football, rugby, tennis, etc. Cultural and creative activities such as: theatre, music, etc. Social activities was mostly organized by the group ESN UCM.
activities_recommended: I would recommend to to buy the sports-card from UCM (90€ for the whole semester), this gives you access to the university gym, and any sports class that you would like. Personally I took a lot of pilates classes. Highly recormended as they are in the middle of the day, so it is a nice break and renewing energy.
weekend_recommendations: Every sunday (and everyday during summer) there is social salsa and bachata dancing in front of the Ermita curch in the center of the city. Really fun and local experience. Furthermore, Madrid has endless cultural opportunities, especially theater, and as a student you often get discount so each play is quite cheap compared to going to the theater in Denmark.
culture_adjustment: Since I have already previously lived a year in Spain it was quite easy to easy to adjust.
socializing_tips: Take initiative, ask for their contact and talk with them in the classroom.
cultural_challenges: That the public system in terms of the doctor and getting medicine is not as effective as I was used to, so you have to both patient and bushy.
culture_appreciated: The extremely rich culture life of Madrid and the vibrant life on the streets.
top3_advice: 1) Be aware of a high demand of assignments in each course that are both time consuming and challenging on an academic level. Make an overview of the assignments you have to make in each course and start early in the semester, because there will not be time to do them all in the end of the semester. 2) Be aware of each professor has their individual way of using Campus Virtual, and for most courses there is not much information online. Furthermore, there is not an overview of the semester and its contents in terms of a semesterplan. Therefore it is also: 3) Extremely important to take a lot of notes in class, since most of the professor doesn't upload their powerpoint after the classes or does not use a powerpoint. In other words, your output of the class is mostly based on your notes. Therefore attendance in the classes is also very important. 4) Ask! Don't be to shy to ask fellow student, the international office, take advantage of the opportunity of getting individual tutoring by your professor.
other_useful_info: Be patient. Most of the information you need, you'll get throughout the semester. But if your in doubt, don't hold back from asking.
most_rewarding: My spanish has improved significantly both oral, written and reading.
greatest_challenge: The semester is short (4 months including exams), and very intens with a high demand of assignments.

crucial_aspects: The renomé of Universidad de Complutense combined with inspiration from other Erasmus students who have studied in Madrid
info_ease: Rather easy, given the size of Universidad Complutense it has been my experience that the inprocessing of new students works very well
arrival_assistance: There has been 2 in-processing events held at the university upon arrival.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process consist of two inprocessing events where you recieve relevant information. Afterwards students attend the Erasmus office where the Proof of Attendance is signed.
registration_help: The Erasmus office has been both helpful and available.
registration_success: I managed to get all the classes i wanted.
registration_advice: At Complutense the two first weeks of the semester is an opportunity to try out different classes. Take advantage of these two weeks although it may challenge some of the deadlines at your sending university.
course_level: The level of the classes has been high and requires a working knowledge both in spanish and preferably also a sound background knowledge of the subject matter i.e. literature, linguistics etc. Future students should consider how many different masters they take classes from as choosing courses from various masters may challenge both the social aspects as well as the students ability to cope with different teaching styles.
teaching_comparison: The teaching at Complutense is more unilateral and the distance between teacher and students seem further.
courses_enrolled: VARIACIÓN SOCIAL Y CAMBIO LINGÜÍSTICO CRISIS DEL REALISMO Y FUNDADORES DE LA NUEVA NARRATIVA EL PERSONAJE EN LA LITERATURA ESPAÑOLA CRÍTICA LITERARIA CONTEMPORÁNEA INTRODUCCIÓN A LA INVESTIGACIÓN EN LITERATURA MEDIEVAL Y DE LOS SIGLOS DE ORO
recommended_courses: I would recommend the courses; CRISIS DEL REALISMO Y FUNDADORES DE LA NUEVA NARRATIVA EL PERSONAJE EN LA LITERATURA ESPAÑOLA INVESTIGACIÓN EN LITERATURA MEDIEVAL Y DE LOS SIGLOS DE ORO I would recommend these for (1) the professors María Díez Yañez, Amelia de Paz Castro and Bethania Bethania Guerra de Lemos who have all been execellent and (2) because these courses are taught in the framework of the masters "spanish literature" and "latinamerican literature". The students at these two masters have been especially good in recieving Erasmus and incoroporating Erasmus-students in their social circles.
unexpected_costs: Two months deposit for apartment.
cost_comparison: Food, books, transport and have been less expensive than I expected.
activities_available: A broad range: from theater to football, Rugby, Padel, swimming and more.
activities_recommended: Any activiyt where you find like-minded people. I have heard that salsa classes have been a great succes for some students.
weekend_recommendations: Go to the movies and focus to explore Madrid instead of traveling far. There is plenty of opportunities to explore in the city of Madrid.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Spanish people are quite easy to connect with.
socializing_tips: Invite your classmates for coffee or "cañas" after class.
cultural_challenges: It has not been my experience that the cultural differences between Denmark and Spain are hard to gap.
culture_appreciated: The openness and the fact that Complutense students are very inclusive.
top3_advice: (1) Make sure to take courses where you like the teachers. It is a good idea to do some research on the teachers. Some of them participate in podcasts or can be found on youtube where they give or participate in academic presentations. (2) Try to limit yourself to ideally 2 or maximum 3 masters although other courses from other masters may seem interesting. (3) Make use of the possibility to try classes the first to weeks of the semester and choose your classes based on academic interest and the people in these classes. Nice fellow students go for a great opportunity to make new relations.
other_useful_info: A lot of the opportunities present themselves in WhattsApp groups and all students are part of them and for the most part very willing to include Erasmus students in them.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange has been the academic opportunities. The learning experience and the new connections i have made stem from choosing great courses, which lead to great people which lead to a great stay. That combined with the ful immersion in the spanish language.
greatest_challenge: Balancing commitments in Denmark with opportunities in Madrid while being away.

crucial_aspects: I study Spanish, so Spain made sense to improve my language skills.
info_ease: Very easy, there is a meeting with the Erasmus office, and they send you a lot of info e-mails as well.
arrival_assistance: I didn't need any.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: First you have two weeks to try classes, before regisering officially. You get all info you need on e-mail, and they also explain everything to you at the intro-meeting, so it was very easy. in the faculty of filology you need to have a C1 level of Spanish, and all info is in Spanish.
registration_help: Erasmus office was very helpful.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: Take advantage of the 2 weeks trial. I thought I knew which classes I wanted, but after I tried one, I decided to change for another.
course_level: The level is high, especially language wise. In facultad de filología you are expected to speak and understand Spanish at a high level upon arrival, and even then it was hard to follow sometimes.
teaching_comparison: It is very different. More high school like, with more exercises, and your are expected to participate and get evaluated on that in your grade. You are also expected to be physically present in most classes, which is different from UCPH.
courses_enrolled: - Heterogeneidad cultural y mestizaje - Crisis del realismo y fundadores de la nueva narrativa - Poesía de la postvanguardia y poetas contemporáneos
recommended_courses: - Crisis del realismo y fundadores de la nueva narrativa. Bethania is a great professor, and her class is very interesting. In general the community on the master Literatura Hispanoamericana is very sociable which is great as an exchange student.
unexpected_costs: The heating bill was very high as many buildings in Madrid are old and not insulated. But even included, in total my rent did not cross 5000 dkk
cost_comparison: Everything is cheaper that Denmark.
activities_available: Music, dance, sports, choir, volunteer work.
activities_recommended: I took dance lessons off campus, and met a lot of great local people that way.
weekend_recommendations: the villages north of Madrid like El Escorial, Segovia etc. You can take a bus or rent a car very cheap, and it takes no time to be in nature, mountains and beautiful small villages. Great sunday plan.
culture_adjustment: Spanyards are great people but speak very fast, interrupt a lot, and they don't slow down to include you in the conversation. So it was a bit tough in the beginning to feel included, but I believe I adapted quickly to the new circumstances.
socializing_tips: The Master in Literatura Hispanoamericana. If you study Spanish, take all of your courses the same place, so you see the same people in each class. It is worth it to get to know someone outside the Erasmus circle while yout here. You also have to actively look for it, and take initiative although it can be tough. It will be worth it.
cultural_challenges: Spanyards can be extremely direct and interrupt a lot. It can come across as rude for a dane, but it's really just a cultural difference.
culture_appreciated: The way everything is centered around being out in the city and socializing a lot.
top3_advice: Look for friendships in local communities. It is worth is. Don't be afraid to try again when you fail. You are here to learn, and in the end you will realize how far you've come. Don't worry that you feel shy or don't understand everything. Your energy, personality and abilities come across more than you think.
other_useful_info: Madrid is an amazing city, and I don't think anyone will regret going there. It is colder in the winter than you might think though, so bring warm clothes.
most_rewarding: All the amazing people I befriended.
greatest_challenge: Getting on the level of Spanish where I didn't feel lost in conversations ever. Understanding my Andaluz professor.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne til en stor by uden for Europa.
overall_comments: Jeg havde en rigtig god oplevelse, men Corona besværliggjorde processen.
info_ease: Der var en del ting at få styr på, men det var nemt at få svar, når jeg sendte e-mails og spurgte om hjælp.
arrival_assistance: Overordnet set fik jeg al nødvendig info tilsendt per mail. Da der var udfordringer med at tilmelde sig fag, blev det fikset for mig, da jeg skrev til koordinatoren for psykologi. Der var et internationalt kontor, men jeg brugte det kun til at tage på en organiseret byvandring. Det var dog en god måde at møde andre i samme situation.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Jeg havde en rigtig god oplevelse, men Corona besværliggjorde processen.
registration_process: De har et onlinesystem, hvor det er først-til-mølle, men det lykkedes mig at få plads på alle kurserne ved at skrive til koordinatoren. Det var jeg alligevel nødt til, for systemet giver ikke én mulighed for at registrere sig på kurser, der kræver, at man har taget andre fag tidligere, selvom Concordia har godkendt at man tager dem. Det er lidt mails frem og tilbage, men det hele lykkedes fint.
registration_help: Man får tilsendt en mail, hvor der står, hvordan man gør og hvem, man skal skrive til, hvis man har problemer.
registration_success: Der var et kursus jeg ikke kunne tage, fordi undervisningstiderne overlappede, men ellers lykkedes det.
registration_advice: Hav forberedt et par alternative kurser, hvis undervisningstiderne overlapper.
academics_comments: Jeg havde en rigtig god oplevelse, men Corona besværliggjorde processen.
course_level: Niveauet var en smule lavere end i København. Kravene var i hvert fald anderledes. Fokus var slet ikke i lige så høj grad på at reflektere kritisk over stoffet. Til gengæld var kravene højere ift. at huske en stor mænge information.
teaching_comparison: Der testes meget mere i løbet af semesteret. Mange små quizzes og afleveringer, som også tæller i mod den endelige karakter. På den måde bliver presset ikke så stort på den endelige eksamen, men man bliver også nødt til at være aktiv gennem hele semesteret. Derudover har underviserne meget at skulle have sagt om både indhold og struktur af kurserne, så kvaliteten afhænger meget af den enkelte underviser.
courses_enrolled: 310 Research Methods I 340 Fundamentals of Psychopathology 435 Developmental Psychopathology 441 Psychopathology: Schizophrenia and neurocognitive disorders
recommended_courses: Psychopathology: Schizophrenia and neurocognitive disorders var det fag, der gik mest i dybden, hvor de andre godt kunne virke lidt overfladiske. I Research methods I får man lov til at arbejde med en selvvalgt research proposal gennem hele semesteret, hvilket var meget lærerigt. Desværre er fokus meget ensidigt på eksperimentelle metoder.
unexpected_costs: Generelt brugte jeg mange penge, fordi man lever i en mellemting mellem at være ude at rejse og have en normal hverdag. Jeg sagde sjældent nej til noget pga. prisen og spiste meget mere ude end herhjemme. Jeg brugte også mange penge på at leje biler, fordi man skal bruge en bil, hvis man vil på tur de fleste steder.
cost_comparison: Dataplaner var overraskende dyre. Til gengæld er det billigere at spise ude. Der er gratis vegansk frokost på campus! På Loyola campus foregår det i "the Hive café".
activities_available: Der var mange muligheder. Tag til club fair i den første uge og snak med studerende, der har klubber om alt fra marinebiologi til "queer printing"
activities_recommended: "Concordia outdoors" tager på hike hver søndag. Det er en nem og billig måde at få set en masse natur. og hyggeligt! Jeg var også til nogle workshops med "Autodidacts Concordia Theatre". Det var sjovt og åbent for alle. Man behøver ikke binde sig til hele semesteret, men kan bare melde sig til, når det passer.
weekend_recommendations: Hvis du er afsted i efteråret, kan man se hvaler den første halvanden måned! Turen derud er også utrolig smuk, og man kan se Quebec City på vejen. Toronto og Niagara Falls er også et must. Og så er New York heller ikke langt væk, selvom jeg ikke kunne tage derhen pga corona. Vi lejede også en hytte en weekend og havde en hyggeligt tur sidst på opholdet. Om vinteren kan man stå på ski. Mont Royal, som er bjerget midt i byen er fantastisk hele året. Spis nogle gode bagels og se nogle ishockeykampe.
culture_adjustment: Det var ikke særligt udfordrende. Montréal er på mange måder en blanding af europæisk kultur, som man kender, og amerikansk kultur, som man kender fra film osv.
socializing_tips: Tag på vandreture og deltag i klubaktiviteter. Jeg var også til en froshaktivitet (deres svar på rus) de første dage. Det kan sagtens lade sig gøre, men andre udvekslingsstuderende er selvfølgelig nemmere at blive venner med, for de er i samme situation, som dig.
cultural_challenges: Jeg havde lidt svært ved at lære deres form for høflighed at kende. Det er mere almindeligt, at folk påpeger det, hvis man står i vejen eller larmer for meget. Loven er også anderledes, og bøderne kan være store, så der skal man lige snakke med canadierne.
culture_appreciated: Montréal er en meget international by, og canadierne sætter stor pris på diversitet. De har også et levende LGBT-miljø.
top3_advice: Vær ikke nervøs- det er nemt at møde mennesker. Tag på ture i weekenden, men stress heller ikke over det. Der er masser at opleve i Montréal. Man bliver testet meget på kurserne, så hold øje med, hvor meget de enkelte opgaver og quizzes tæller (nogen gange ender en quiz med kun at tælle 1,5% af din endelige karakter.) Tænk over hvor meget tid, du har lyst til at lægge i studierne.
other_useful_info: Man kan leje nogle af bøgerne brugt i Concordias boghandel. Der er et skjult drivhus øverst i en af bygningerne på downtown campus, hvor man kan studere. Hvis du bor i student residence, kan du risikere, at der INTET er, når du dukker op (fx ikke et bruseforhæg) Alt kan fås billigt i Dollarama. Bixi er lejecykler, der fungerer godt.
most_rewarding: Den frihed og selvfølelse, der følger med at tage alene ud i verden og opdage, at man kan bygge et liv op helt selv.
greatest_challenge: Al papirarbejdet før jeg kom afsted (særligt pga corona) og usikkerheden på, om det overhovedet ville lykkes. At skulle hjem igen.
other_comments: Tag afsted!

crucial_aspects: I kind of picked at random. It was important for me to study at an english-speaking university. I was intrigued by the large selection of elective courses.
info_ease: My exchange took place during the covid-lockdowns of winter 2021-22. I would not recommend that experience. The university was in large part because of that not able to provide a welcoming experience for me, but it was worsened as their material was oriented towards welcoming long-term international students starting their first year of studies. I was, however, able to figure everything out in the end.
arrival_assistance: Very little. I could read on their website and write emails. There was one virtual meetup for exchange students partway through the first month which allowed me to make some friends and from there we helped each other.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The course registration process is very different from the one in KU, and you will not be able to apply without first getting special permission, so just write directly to professors or program directors for access. This is not something they told me was possible, but I had no issues at all. Also don't be afraid to use the waiting list options as many students switch classes.
registration_help: Just talk to someone directly, hopefully the student services will be in person when you go :)
registration_success: I got amazing classes! Don't be afraid to ask for permission to take 400-level courses, as they were in my experience much more engaging and had way smaller classes which was incredible
registration_advice: As I wrote above ^
course_level: The level of courses varied wildly from course to course and subject to subject. At times, the very free and pick-your-own-path style of education in North America leads to frustrating repetitions and low baselines of common knowledge, but there is also way more interesting and niche courses to pick from.
teaching_comparison: Be aware that they teach differently, and I feel lucky to have had my first two years in Copenhagen. The students have in general never tried field work, and there was _a lot_ more writing than what I was used to.
courses_enrolled: ANTH 498-F - Special topics: Introduction to the Anthropocene ANTH 498-G - Special topics: Militarization in Oceania ANTH 343 - Media Ethnographies ANTH 302 - Art, Aesthetics, and Anthropology
recommended_courses: Pick specific courses ("narrow" focus). General courses can get kind of lost at times.
unexpected_costs: I was not able to get a refund of the insurance cost even though I was entitled to it as a Danish citizen. The issue is that the processing of the application (which was embarrasingly complex) took 90+ days while the deadline from the time I was able to start applying was way shorter. Maybe you can make it work. ALSO: Montreal still has issues with water lead contamination in certain places, make sure to find out if the place you stay has replaced their water pipes or you should probably buy a Brita water filter if you would prefer not to be exposed.
cost_comparison: The prices were more or less the same, I just ended up spending more money than what I am used to.
activities_available: A lot, I'm sure
activities_recommended: I went for a bouldering membership at Café Bloc. It's expensive, but fun and very social.
weekend_recommendations: Go ice skating in the winter. Enjoy all the public exhibitions and performances at Place des Art. Go to pop-up markets.
culture_adjustment: People are pretty friendly,,, It was easy for me to adjust. Just very hard to adjust to the cold weather and the baffling tendency of people to not use blanket but instead just crank up the heat - whats up with that?
socializing_tips: No just be social. Don't look at your phone if you have noone to talk to: Eventually someone will pity you and come up to you
cultural_challenges: It was a shock to learn about the intense battle between Francophone and Anglophone visions of the Province.
culture_appreciated: There's a lot. I saw a lot of light/projection-oriented art and installations while there which I loved. I just love the diversity and intensity of the city in general. Also I like that theres a lot of bars that brew their own beer.
top3_advice: Focus on making friends so you can hang out with someone daily – alienation and lonelyness are negative feedback loops. You don't have to do all the touristy things people talk about. Try and talk with the professors, they are extremely kind and nice in my experience.
most_rewarding: Meeting people
greatest_challenge: The lockdowns – my bank account

crucial_aspects: To me, it was important to go outside of Europe and preferably to an English-speaking country. Canada has always been at the top of my travel list, and I felt like it was the perfect opportunity to go there on exchange. I chose Montreal because of the location, what I'd read about Concordia University, and because I always wanted to learn some French
info_ease: It was a bit complicated. The university (and Canada in general) is not quite as technologically advanced as Denmark, so it required a lot of waiting hours at the International Students Office at uni, and going around the city to get everything in order. Also the way the university works is quite different from in Denmark. But they were extremely helpful at the offices, and a lot of the people I met in the beginning were either going through the same things in regards to arrival or had done it already, so we could help each other. But things like obtaining a student ID, metro card etcetera, was just generally more time consuming than what I was used to from Denmark. Also, finding information on Concordia University's website is not that logical.
arrival_assistance: The International Students Office were very helpful with requests, but it's not like you're offered it automatically. I did reach out to the student counsellors and whoever else I needed to talk to upon arrival.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The course registration really seems to me to be much more complicated than it needs to be. After your acceptance at the uni, you get a login for a MyConcordia page, where you can find and register for courses. You can read (very very short) descriptions of the courses in the course catalogue on the general website, and there it will say if there is some prerequisite to taking the course. A lot of them don't apply to exchange students though, depending on your program, but there are also more restrictions on courses that won't be stated in the course catalogue. Therefore, when you register for courses, it will sometimes tell you that it is unavailable to you, despite it not being full. Once you successfully register a Moodle page is going to become available, where you can see course materials etc.
registration_help: You can contact the particular departments or the International Students Office with questions. I contacted the departments quite a lot in the registration process to know why a course was unavailable to me. Sometimes, I couldn't take it because I was an exchange student, but a lot of the time it was simply because I didn't have the prerequisite normally required - but I could take it anyway. At the departments, they can either tell you why you can't register or open the registration to you. There is going to be a bit of waiting time for them to be reply though.
registration_success: I got some of the classes that were my first choice, but not all, because they were either full or unavailable. But in the end I wound up with some interesting classes.
registration_advice: Begin registering for courses early. That will give you time to sort out any registration issues, but also, many classes fill up pretty fast. So do it as early as possible.
course_level: The academic level is a lot lower than at UCPH, at least that was my experience. I found a lot of the coursework and reading to be closer to high school levels in Denmark. I also had way less readings than normally at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: At Concordia, your grade for the course is not entirely dependent on the final exam, like it is at UCPH. It normally only counts for 20-30% of your grade. The rest will be attendance, participation, tests, midterms and papers. However, I found that the in-class teaching style, for the most part, was pretty similar to that of UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Media Criticism, Propaganda, Contemporary News Media, Introduction to Contemporary Concerns in Women's Studies.
recommended_courses: I would recommend Media Criticism at the Communication and Journalism Institute, and Contemporary Concerns in Women's Studies at the Simone de Beauvoir Institute. Both were quite different in content than what I would have at UCPH, but in a very good way. I found them to be the most giving courses, and also the best structured ones. I recommend avoiding the online classes. I found them to be not very well structured, with very little help available, and also not that interesting. Classes are also a good way to meet people, so I really recommend prioritizing physical classes over online ones.
unexpected_costs: I was a bit surprised that everything costs money at Concordia - like student IDs, transcripts, some paperwork etc. It's not a large amount, like $13 for student ID and around $20 for the transcript, but still, nothing is free there. Also, tips are very much expected, not just at restaurants, but also hair salons, tattoo shops etc. You are expected to pay 15-20% in tips. Taxes are never included in the price listed, but added at the counter. Taxes vary depending on the item you buy, but are around 10-15%
cost_comparison: Public transportation is pretty cheap for students. You can get a card for half the normal price if you are a student, where you can ride unlimited. Buying groceries was more expensive than I thought it would be, and more expensive than in Denmark. However, eating out is pretty cheap compared to the cost of food at the grocery store, and Montreal has endless amazing restaurants where you can get really good food pretty cheap.
activities_available: Concordia has tons of clubs, sports, places you can volunteer, and just general activities you can participate in.
activities_recommended: I would really recommend to take part in the activities offered by the Concordia Ski & Snowboard club, and the Concordia Outdoors club. Both plan really fun events like skiing, weekend trips, hikes etc, that would be a bit hard to organize yourself and it is a great way to meet new people. I also volunteered at the student café, which was a fun way to meet new people as well.
weekend_recommendations: Montreal is a really amazing, and there are tons of things to do there, like go to museums, parks, explore the different neighborhoods etc. I also really recommend getting out of the city. Canada has so much amazing nature, and it is amazing to get out of the city to ski, hike, or explore in other ways. You really only need to leave the city borders to find amazing mountains, national parks, and some other nice cities are pretty easily accessible by bus or train, like New York, Toronto, Quebec City etcetera. It is also fun to rent a car and spend a weekend at a cabin.
culture_adjustment: I actually found it to be easier than I was expecting. Of course it is a challenge to move to a new country, and I'd never been to Canada before my exchange, so I didn't really know what to expect. But culturally, it was not that far away from other cultures I've seen or like the Danish culture.
socializing_tips: I actually mostly made friends with international students, but the local students I did make friends with were my roommates, and ones I met through activities at the university, like clubs and volunteering. Canadians are extremely friendly and chatty, so they are pretty open to new people.
cultural_challenges: I found the Canadian French pretty difficult, but it is absolutely not necessary to know French in Montreal, as everyone is at least bilingual. One of the things I found it hardest to adjust to was the climate, which has way colder, way more extreme weather than in Denmark. The winter lasts from October to April, and can have extreme temperatures and other weather occurrences I had never seen. But it was also very interesting living in that sort of climate.
culture_appreciated: I really appreciated how multicultural Montreal and Canada in general is. There are lots of people from all over the world there, and it is so interesting to meet people from so many different places. I also really appreciated how open, friendly and spontaneous people are there.
top3_advice: I would say that one of the best things Montreal has to offer in my opinion is the mix of cultures, so be sure to explore that. But also get out of the city to see some other parts of the country, which looks nothing like Denmark, and has so much to offer. It is a good idea to think in advance what you would want out of your stay, and what the best scenario would be, and then go for that - whether it is pursuing academic challenges, making a lot of friends, trying a lot of new things etcetera. But I will also say that, to me at least, my stay was nothing like I imagined it.
other_useful_info: Concordia offers language courses for international students (they don't give credit or is an actual university class). I'd recommend avoiding those, as they are pretty poorly organized and you don't get very much out of it.
most_rewarding: My new friends. I was very worried about how hard it would be to make new friends, but I found it pretty easy, as particularly international students are all in the same boat regarding the fact that they don't know anyone or anything there, and all just want to make the most of it.
greatest_challenge: I actually found the time difference to Denmark pretty challenging, which was a bit surprising. But I also found it challenging to work out the university systems and figuring out how everything worked.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go somewhere I hadn't been before.
info_ease: It took some time making sense of all of it, but generally it was pretty easy, and both KU and my host university were really helpful in giving out the information I needed beforehand.
arrival_assistance: Lots of email correspondence with my host university
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You get a student user account, add which courses you want to attend, get them approved, and then you're good to go. It's really easy and just a few clicks around on their website.
registration_help: Email, call, student center, etc.
registration_advice: Ask the International Students Office whenever you are confused about anything. They are super kind and helpful.
course_level: Less readings than at KU, but the readings are generally more varied and interesting, in my opinion.
teaching_comparison: Concordia is a lot more international and progressive than UCPH. Though you should be aware that most students in Canada start university at around 18 years old, so people are generally quite young in the classes. I was definitely one of the oldest and I'm only 22.
courses_enrolled: Marketing and Sociology courses focusing on racial relations and culture.
recommended_courses: Anything on Sociology
unexpected_costs: Thermal underwear, cause Canada is cold. I was NOT ready for -20 degrees Celsius.
cost_comparison: Dairy products are pretty expensive but restaurants are generally cheaper than in Denmark.
activities_available: So many different clubs, club events, social events, etc. Literally something happening every single week, it's amazing.
activities_recommended: Join the clubs! And if you're an ethnic minority, join one of the minority student unions. I had a lot of fun in the Black Student Union.
weekend_recommendations: I can definitely recommend going to Toronto for a few days if you ever have the opportunity. Don't go in the CN tower though. It's super expensive and not worth it.
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: Be yourself and be open
cultural_challenges: None, really
culture_appreciated: There is much more diversity in Montreal (and Canada in general) than in Denmark and people seem more culturally openminded. I really appreciated that, especially as a POC.
top3_advice: 1) Be prepared for really cold winters 2) Join as many clubs as possible (you don't have to go to all of their events, but if you join them, at least you'll know whenever something fun is happening) 3) Be prepared to study with people who are a lot younger than you
other_useful_info: Not really
most_rewarding: The friendships I made and all of the new perspectives I gained from the courses I took.
greatest_challenge: One of my teachers had a teaching style that relied very heavily on physical class attendance and note-sharing among students which can be annoying if you prefer doing most of the studying at home by yourself, but the courses are usually only one class per week, so although it was irritating, it was manageable.
other_comments: Remember to have fun!

crucial_aspects: That the university offered some courses that I found interesting, and that it was a country outside Europe.
overall_comments: I had the best time of my life. I've never been outside of Scandinavia so it was amazing to finally experience something else. Montréal is not a big culture shock compared to Denmark, and I very quickly felt at home.
info_ease: I spent alot of time preparing for my trip at home, and had some long e-mail correspondences with the University. Concordia also have a PDF guide for international students which was a big help.
arrival_assistance: I got an some e-mails, and besides that the university has a lot of happenings at the campus, where you can meet new people or ask other students about help.
arrival_comments: You have to actively reach out to people, no one was holding your hand.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had the best time of my life. I've never been outside of Scandinavia so it was amazing to finally experience something else. Montréal is not a big culture shock compared to Denmark, and I very quickly felt at home.
registration_process: You have to use the student hub website, they have a course planer that is very helpful. The problem is if you want to apply for a course with prerequisites, you have to write to the professor in charge of the program.
registration_help: They have a lot of help on their website, and don't hesitate with writing an e-mail to the ISO (INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS OFFICE) they answer e-mails fast.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Register as early as possible, then you will get the classes you want.
academics_comments: I had the best time of my life. I've never been outside of Scandinavia so it was amazing to finally experience something else. Montréal is not a big culture shock compared to Denmark, and I very quickly felt at home.
course_level: I did elective courses at Concordia, and the level was very different depending on the class.
teaching_comparison: You have to engage more actively in the classes, and do a lot more than just reading in books.
courses_enrolled: - BIOL 227 LAB STUDIES IN BIODIVERSITY - FRAN 211 FRENCH LANGUAGE: ELEMENTARY - PHIL 318 PHILOSOPHY OF BIOLOGY
recommended_courses: If you are into biology the lab course is very giving. You become very familiar with using a light compound microscope (something I feel like KU never tought me) and get to look at a lot of different organisms. Besides being in the lab you have to do three different surveys, which forces you to go out in nature and look for different organisms. I really enjoyed engaging with the outside nature as a part of my course.
unexpected_costs: Do keep in mind that taxes aren't always included in the price so things are typically more expensive than you expect.
cost_comparison: Public transport is way cheaper compared to DK, get an OPUS card and then you pay 220 CAD for four months, you can take metro and bus as much as you want.
activities_available: They offer movie nights, game nights, to go watch hockey games, yoga lessons and lots more.
activities_recommended: Montréal is a city that offers so many free events. My stay was in the winter and I was so worried that I would just stay inside most of the time, but the people in Montréal do many outdoor activities despite the cold. If you are here in the winter go to the lumiere festival, the nuit blanche (it's like culture night in Denmark) and igloo festival.
weekend_recommendations: I lived five minutes from place des arts where they have a skating rink, it is totally free if you have your own skates. I went there almost everyday in the morning where it opens, and there's only a few people. Go skate on the frozen river in parc la fontaine, discover Saint Laurent, go to Mont Royal and you have to experience tam tam in Parc du Mont-Royal if possible!
culture_adjustment: Very easy, people are so helpful and sweet.
socializing_tips: Say hi! Montréal is a very diverse city and people here are very outgoing compared to Denmark
cultural_challenges: Nothing
culture_appreciated: Their willingness to help out
top3_advice: 1. Apply for the quebec government health insurance (theres a guide on concordias website) 2. Go to the university in the beginning before classes start to participate in the happenings and meet new people. 3. Be open
other_useful_info: If you are not opening a bank account in Montréal you cannot pay for a phone subscription because they need an address. I was lucky I stayed at an airbnb in the beginning and the host was willing to pay for my subscription with her card and then I transferred the money to her. Fizz is very good.
most_rewarding: Meeting people from all over the world
greatest_challenge: Being on my own for the first time in my life in another country, but it was so fulfilling in the end.
other_comments: Live in the now, and enjoy the small things. As sad as it might be, you will meet people here that you might never see again, so enjoy the time you have with them as much as you can.

cultural_challenges: Not really anything.
culture_appreciated: The openness of people. I went so many places by my self and always ended up talking to somebody.
top3_advice: 1. Use the city and try everything at least once 2. Take advantage of the beautiful mountain in the middle of the city 3. Organize to meet up with the people you talk to. Everybody is so nice and wants to connect
other_useful_info: Bring warm clothes if you're doing a winter semester.
most_rewarding: Experiencing a new city and getting a new perspective of distance. So many people in Montreal are from around the world so you really get to know a lot of different cultures in one.
greatest_challenge: Wanting to go back :3

crucial_aspects: I wanted to study at a good school in a country far from home
info_ease: Easy
arrival_assistance: Had intro meetings with all the exchange students
arrival_comments: In terms of getting info and practical assistance the school did a great job. However, I think the social parts of the orientation were not always great. A lot of the orientation was with freshmen which did not always work well. It can be hard to make friends with 17/18-year old freshmen who have just begun college when you are a 22-year old exchange student who is only going to be in the US for a year. I would suggest doing more social events for all the exchange students or perhaps trying to get some juniors or seniors to host some orientation events or act as buddies/tutors for the incoming exchange students.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You had to preregister for courses before arriving at the school. The first week of school you could try out different courses and determine if you wanted to change some or stick with the ones you had preregistered for.
registration_help: You could call or email the school
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted
registration_advice: It feels stressfull in the beginning because you have to preregister before you are even at the school. During preregistration some courses might even be fully booked. However, it was my experience that in the end most courses became available and if they were not available you could email the professors and they were often times very helpful to accommodate your wishes.
course_level: It greatly varies. Some courses were easier than in Copenhagen others were similar to what I would expect in Copenhagen.
teaching_comparison: Less formal and mathematical, more about intuition. Tests and exams were spread out over the semester.
courses_enrolled: Financial Accounting, Fixed Income Securities and Derivatives, Financial Modelling, Public Finance, Intro to Game Theory and Strategic Thinking, Behavioral Economics
recommended_courses: Behavioral Economics, Intro to Game Theory and Strategic Thinking Both courses had great professors and were very interesting.
unexpected_costs: Most costs are known upfront if you live on campus
cost_comparison: Insurance and meal plan
activities_available: Anything you liked there was a club for it. From football to quidditch to political debates.
activities_recommended: I joined a football/soccer team which I enjoyed a lot. Great community and a great way to meet locals at the university.
weekend_recommendations: Lots of good hikes in the finger lakes area. See Niagara Falls. Go to NYC.
culture_adjustment: It took some time, but relatively easy.
socializing_tips: Join a club (academic or non-academic), in my experience that was definitely the best way to meet locals.
cultural_challenges: Took some time to adjust to campus life.
culture_appreciated: Everyone is very open and friendly. It is not weird to start a conversation with a complete stranger - even halfway through the semester.
top3_advice: 1. Join a club 2. Live on campus (preferably west campus) 3. Explore campus, don't just stay in the buildings where you have classes. Campus is so big and they have a cinema, bowling alleys, a gaming room and lots of other stuff. Even if you keep exploring for your full exchange you feel like you haven't seen everything
other_useful_info: Best ways to get to campus: Fly to ithaca (expensive) Fly to syracuse and take uber from there (approx 1hr.) (less expensive) Bus from NYC to Ithaca (ourbus or flixbus provide good service) (cheapest option)
most_rewarding: Making new friends and exploring a new country/culture
greatest_challenge: Being far away from home and trying to build a new daily life in a new country.

crucial_aspects: Nothing was particular crucial for me, but i knew i wanted to go somewhere further away than Europe.
info_ease: Easy
arrival_assistance: received plenty of assistance in form of an intro-day and several info mails etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Lidt usikker på hvad der menes, men alt i alt synes jeg det hele var super smooth. der er mange steps man skal igennem, men nemt.

registration_success: det var også rigtig nemt og overskueligt. Du har tid til at prøve kurser af før du er låst, hvilket er dejligt.
registration_advice: Undersøg kurserne grundigt inden så du ved hvilke du vil adde når de åbnes. De gode bliver hurtigt fyldt op.

overall_comments: Altså der var meget forskel i, hvordan udvekslingsstuderende generelt vurderede Cornell - det kommer SELVFØLGELIG an på hvad du værdisætter i sådan en udvekslingstur.
info_ease: Fint, de sender vist nogle dokumenter der hjælper dig med at finde rundt - bare fyr dem alle ind i chatgpt og så kan du spørge den i stedet for at læse 10 sider af pjat igennem.
arrival_assistance: Da jeg ankom fulgte jeg bare adressen jeg havde fået, fandt receptionen, som hvert hus har, og fik nøglerne. Dagen efter jeg ankom var der et orienteringsmøde, der gav rigeligt information om studiet og det praktiske (måske lidt for meget tbh) - men så var der ingen tvivl for den ængstelige studerende!
arrival_comments: Det vigtigeste ved orientation er at få venner! Du kan altid se studievejledernes powerpoint senere og spørge chatten - men de andre udvekslingsstuderende er lettest (og oftest sjovest) at blive venner med gennem turen. Du har kun et hvis antal gange du "skal" møde dem, så få nogle venner/vennegruppe og add dem på whatsapp eller noget.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Altså der var meget forskel i, hvordan udvekslingsstuderende generelt vurderede Cornell - det kommer SELVFØLGELIG an på hvad du værdisætter i sådan en udvekslingstur.
registration_process: Meget fint: her er cahttens respons, som jeg kan erklære mig enig med: "Kursustilmeldingen på Cornell foregik via portalen "Student Center" og "Class Roster". Jeg fik tildelt en specifik tilmeldingsperiode ("time ticket"), hvor jeg kunne tilmelde mig fag. Nogle kurser krævede godkendelse fra underviser eller havde adgangsbegrænsninger."
registration_help: Studievejleder - hun var fantastisk god til at hjælpe, og mange af de andre studievejledere havde skrevet op mod 100 mails med hende ;)
registration_success: Meget succesful synes jeg. Jeg fik dækket de fag jeg satte mig for at dække:) Dog krævede det en masse mails og afviste forhåndsgodkendelse, samt planlægning af mit eget skema på KU - altså fx kunne jeg ikke dække to af mine 4. semester fag, så jeg lavede noget magic med mit skema, sådan de blev udskiftet dem med valgfag, som var meget lette at finde forhåndsgodkendelser for.
registration_advice: Forhåndsgodkend for flere fag. Begynd at forhåndsgodkend så hurtigt som muligt - virkelig læs op på fagene, de fag der skal erstattes, og HVORNÅR fagene udbydes (spring/fall?). Holde styr på tilmeldingsperioden. Sæt god tid af til det.
academics_comments: Altså der var meget forskel i, hvordan udvekslingsstuderende generelt vurderede Cornell - det kommer SELVFØLGELIG an på hvad du værdisætter i sådan en udvekslingstur.
course_level: fra chatten: Kurserne på Cornell er opdelt efter et nummersystem, hvor de fire cifre indikerer niveauet: 1000–1999: Introduktionskurser på lavt bachelor-niveau (typisk 1. år) 2000–2999: Mellem-niveau bachelor-kurser (2. år) 3000–3999: Øvre bachelor-niveau (3.–4. år), ofte mere specialiserede 4000–4999: Avancerede bachelor-kurser, men kan også være åbne for graduate-studerende 5000+: Kurser målrettet graduate-studerende (kandidat og ph.d.-niveau)
teaching_comparison: minder mere om KU end det er anderledes fra KU - synes fx det er cirka samme niveau som KU (i hvertfald Psykologi). Rent interessant karaktergrundlag, f.eks. kunne det så sådan her ud: " Kurset blev bedømt ud fra en 100-pointsskala med følgende fordeling: Research paper: “Observing development in action” – 15% Tre skriftlige opgaver (Developmental niche, Babies in the wild, Parent kit) – 15% i alt (gennemsnit af de tre) 10 ugentlige quizzes – 15% i alt (laveste quizscore blev fratrukket) Preliminary Exam 1 – 15% Preliminary Exam 2 – 20% Final exam – 20% " Så meget anderledes arbejdsstruktur. Mere enkelt arbejde fremfor gruppe arbejde.
courses_enrolled: BIONB 4740 – Neural Dynamics of Learning CS 1133 – Short Course in Python (senere droppet ud) HD 2170 – Adolesc and Emerging Adulthood PE 1312 – Bass Fishing PE 1375 – Beginning Tae Kwon Do PLSCI 2010 – Magic Mushrooms, Mischievous Molds PSYCH 2090 – Developmental Psychology PSYCH 3150 – Obesity/Regulation/BodyWeight
recommended_courses: Selvfølgelig dem, som dækker dit semester på KU, men som du også kan se på mit skema, kan man tage alt muligt tilfældigt og sjovt, da man selv laver skemaet. Så fx forhåndsgodkendte jeg ikke for nogle af de følgende fag: PE 1312, PE 1375, PLSCI 2010 eller CS 1133. Det var bare fordi jeg havde ekstra tid, og gerne vil lære noget ekstra. Det må man selv vurdere om man har tid til: personligt vil jeg nok havde fået bedre karaktere på nogle af fagene hvis jeg havde skåret lidt ned. En ting jeg dog kan anbefale alle er at tage en eller flere PE classes - det er skide sjovt, og de har alle mulige forskellige, alt fra badminton til tree climbing. Det har dog nogle gange en lille fee inkluderet.
unexpected_costs: Obligatorisk studenteraktivitetsgebyr på 1500kr, plus ansøgningsprocessen for et visa, som vist kom op til 3000kr (fordelt i to udgifter). Plus mit housing kostede liiidt mere, da jeg boede alene uden roomate (prisen anslået er for dobbeltværelse)
cost_comparison: Bøger brugte jeg ikke penge på - kunne enten finde dem online, ellers var det bare research papers jeg fik tildelt online. Plus transport er gratis på campus, dog brugte man nogle gange penge på en uber, eller lavede en lille roadtrip tur, som kostede noget. Alt i alt kostede turen omkring 100k, men brugte omkring 15k ekstra på et roadtrip med mine udvekslingsvenner til sidst. Det bliver dyrt.
activities_available: Fitness centre, PE klasser, hundredvis af klubber, der laver alt muligt forskelligt, man kan også joine sports turneringer (fx joinede jeg en volleyball turnering med nogle venner, og det var skide sjov). Der var også nogle sjove holidays som st. patricks day, slope day, dragon day (spring perioden jeg var i)
activities_recommended: Stor anbefaling at leje en bil med nogle venner og tage til toronto, niagra falls, New York City eller noget andet. Hvis du har økonomisk overskud og nogle fine venner, så lej en bil og lav et roadtrip rundtomkring i USA i slutningen af semestret.
weekend_recommendations: vælge nogle af de ting jeg har listede lige før
culture_adjustment: I starten var det ret noiern, da jeg aldrig havde været i USA før, og det føltes som at være i en film hele tiden. Men altså man vender sig til det efter en uge eller to.
socializing_tips: Få et dobbeltværelse hvis du gerne vil forsikre mindst en ven. Jeg havde et værelse for mig selv, men det var inde i en større suite, med fællesrum og fællestoilet - blev gode venner med dem. Tal med mennesker i din klasse. De er ofte interesseret i at lære om exchange students. Bliv venner med de andre udvekslingsstuderende, ikke kun de danske!
