The international/exchange student community was amazing, the academic level was outstanding, the housing was great, and Stockholm is beautiful and very cool, so everything else would get a 10-mark.
course_level: The level is a little lower than at KU. You have MUCH more free time on exchange compared to at home. Furthermore, it's only failed, pass or pass with destination, which make all academics more chill. The exams are so nice, as they give you a lot of time so you don't have to stress and so you have the possibility to sit and think about your answers.
teaching_comparison: We had lectures, a few lab exercises, problem based learning (like SAU at SUND on Uni of Copenhagen, but where you are 6-8 students and TWO professors working together for 8 weeks - its really really cool and one of the best experiences academically), a few journal clubs, and only a few written assignments in "Cardiometabolics and infectious diseases".
courses_enrolled: BACH-Molecular medicine - oncology (15 ECTS) in English , End August - Beginning November BACH-Molecular medicine - cardiometabolic and infectious diseases (15 ECTS) in English , Beginning November - Mid January
recommended_courses: Both - I really, really loved "Oncology". It was amazing. We met patients, designed trials, had great lectures, and it was super well structured. "Cardiometabolics and infectious diseases" was super nice, and a very good deep introduction to some of the biggest killers worldwide. Both courses both revolved around molecular aspects but also more clinical than the courses I have had on SCIENCE and SUND in Copenhagen. I would really recommend you to take both courses.
unexpected_costs: None - everything is quite like in DK.
cost_comparison: Food is a bit more expensive in the supermarked. We ended up eating out a lot to get the full experience - remember Fika at least 4 times a week. Alcohol is SOOOO expensive (215 SEK for the cheapest bottle of alcohol). Traveling back and forth to CPH is super cheap by train if you plan 2 months ahead (like 150 DKK pr way). SAS has very convenient youth tickets too.
activities_available: Not much - our exchange coordinator (Giulia) was amazing to plan activities and dinners, but besides that the social part of Karolinska wasn't that impressive. The first day us 5 exchange people in my class found each other, and we had a blast for 5 months. They a friends for life <3
activities_recommended: Go to Tyresta national park. Go out eating a lot and live in a luxury bubble. Allow your self to spend extra money. Go to as many Christmas markets as possible. Go to Skansen Christmas market. Eat at 800 degrees, Greasy spoon, and Dino sushi. Watch a ballet in the opera. Go to the fotografiska museum and Vasa museum. Go to the cinema. Have the time of you life.
weekend_recommendations: Go out and see the beautiful nature. Take long walks. Find new places for Fika.
culture_adjustment: The local culture is quite like Denmark - except Fika, which is something we need to import to DK. It's very nice and easy.
socializing_tips: I drank a lot of coffees and invited people out that I met to socialize. Be outgoing and just ask if you meet a nice person if they want to hang out, go the the museum, or a coffee. That's the vibe and way to meet new friends. Furthermore, I also took lead on planning dinners in our common kitchen and signed up for hikes at the university. Go for it - you have nothing to loose.
cultural_challenges: The Swedes a very isolated, and actually don't truly like the Danish at first. You need to loosen them up, and then you'll found out that they are quite like us :))) KI don't offer language courses to Danish and Norwegian exchange students even though danish people don't understand people from Stockholm and vice versa.
culture_appreciated: Fika :-P And the lot of free time and Christmas vibe.
top3_advice: Be social and outgoing. Spend extra money on yourself. Eat lots of Fika (I recommend Lillebrors bageri, Stora bageriet, Kaffeverket and Pascal).
other_useful_info: Remember that's its hard to leave your best friends and family. You have used your whole life finding your friends in DK, so it takes time and energy to find new good friends in a new city. Use that time and energy. Make a nice vibe in your shared kitchen.
most_rewarding: The social experience with us 5 exchange student (2 danish and 3 dutch) and the academic experience.
greatest_challenge: To find out what really matters to you, when you have time to rethink you're everyday life in a new setting.
other_comments: Enjoy.

crucial_aspects: For me it was important that it wasn't too far away so family and friends could come visit. Also that the facilities seemes nice and that the possible courses I would be able to take sounded interesting.
info_ease: It was very easy. And the Exchange coordinater is very nice so even if some information was missing then it was easy to just contact her.
arrival_assistance: I didn't get any when I arrived because the move in at the acommodation was just by information on email.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was okay to figure out what to do. And as mentioned before the exchange coordinator, Giulia is veeery nice so it is always possible to contact her. But they needed to verify my identity with a copy of my passport that was signed by KU. But KU didn't understand what I needed when I contacted them so they send me around in the system to other people so that was a bit time consuming for something that shouldn't have been a problem. Just make sure to state what you need and ask if you can come by their office to have them make a copy and sign your passport.
registration_help: The exchange coordinator Giulia was helpfull from KI and their website also helps. And then Exchange coordinators from Ku also.
registration_success: I got exactly the ones I wanted. I followed their biomedicine 5th semester since I also went on exchange on my 5th semester
registration_advice: Just make sure to have all the right deadlines then it should be fine.
course_level: The levels were totally fine. Compared to Molecular Biomedicine on KU they were a bit lower I think but some parts of the courses were based on their previous courses which I didn't have. That made those parts a bit harder. They didn't really expect us to read anything so that was different than in KU (if you are someone who normally reads what is recommended)
teaching_comparison: Not a lot of reading just a bunch of lectures. And then one course was with a lot of assignments apart from the lectures. And in general there is a bit more mandatory classes.
courses_enrolled: Molecular Medicine - Oncology Molecular Medicine - Cardiometabolic and Infectious diseases
recommended_courses: I would really recommend the Oncology course. I'm really ineterested in Cancer and therefor it fit me perfectly and I really liked the course structure. The Cardiometabolic and Infectious diseases course was a bit all over the place and not structured very well. But is you are into the topic then I think the course would be good to choose anyways. During the course you get to make a research application which can be usefull in the future to have done before.
unexpected_costs: Nothing
cost_comparison: Nothing
activities_available: There is a free gym at both Solna campus (where I was) and Flemmingsberg campus. In the gym it is also possible to sign up for badminton, floorball, basket or other stuff and also just book courts yourself to play e.g. badminton. Medicinska Foreningen also held a bunch of parties. But those you have to pay for. I didn't really go to any but they had some cool dinner parties and them parties.
activities_recommended: Deffinately the sports activities at the gym.
weekend_recommendations: You should have a lot of Fika (coffee and a kardemomme bulle) and jsut hang out with friends. Do a bunch of shopping and go to the museums and in general just enjoy this beautiful city.
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: No it was a bit difficult since the iomedicine bachelor is international so only few swedish students were there. But it was nice to get to know people from all over the world.
cultural_challenges: Maybe the fact that rugbrød is very expensive here.
culture_appreciated: Definately all the kardemomme bulle they have here when they have Fika.
top3_advice: Apply for housing a soon a possoble so you have a higher chance of getting into The Residence (on campus). Maybe let your parents to drive you here since it's so close. Because then you can bring all your favorite things here. Take advatage of all the cool study spots on campus!
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Getting to know people from a lot of different countries.
greatest_challenge: To be away from family on the bad days

crucial_aspects: I chose this country taking into consideration the university reputation and quality of research. I always enjoyed the nordic countries and the cold weather so I decided that this country would be great for an Erasmus + internship.
info_ease: It was very easy! The international mobility department from the University of Copenhagen were super helpful and solved any doubt I had regarding the documents and insurance that I needed for this abroad stay.
arrival_assistance: The secretary from the department was the person in charge of making a batch so I could access the laboratory facilities and hospital building. Also the laboratory manager and all members from the department helped with anything that I needed.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: I didn't have to register for any courses because I was doing my master's thesis internship abroad. However, I had to do some courses about laboratory safety to be able to have a permit to work there. I had to fill up a form with my personal information and the name of the department I was working in to get a batch. Besides that, the laboratory manager provided me with a laboratory tour and safety precautions rules.
registration_help: The laboratory manager was in charge to make sure that everyone had their required documents ready. So after my arrival, she helped me signing up for the laboratory safety online courses and booking a time slot to get the working batch. Additionally, the secretary of the department also helped me with the paperwork.
registration_success: I didn't register for classes because I was working in a laboratory. The only documents that I needed for this Erasmus were the Erasmus contract and the insurance.
registration_advice: I would suggest to make sure to keep an eye to the deadlines for the paperwork so it is submitted on time.
course_level: I did the second year of my master's programme abroad which consisted in a master's thesis of 60 credits ECTS. After a 9 month internship, I had to submit a 50-70 pages report and present it in front of a commite at the University of Copenhagen.
teaching_comparison: Although I didn't need to attend any classes, there were some seminars from the department I was working in that were very interesting. Once a week, there were lunch seminars were one member presented her/his most recent work. Another day there were Journal Clubs where we reviewed and discussed recent papers published in our research field.
courses_enrolled: Master's thesis 30 ECTS
recommended_courses: I would really recommend doing the master's thesis abroad because it is a great opportunity to get to know how is research in another country and experience living abroad surrounded by a new culture.
unexpected_costs: I had to buy snow proof clothes and footwear because it snowed from November until mid-April.
cost_comparison: Food was more expensive than I expected in this country. However, public transport was cheaper than I thought!
activities_available: There were a lot of associations at the university ranging from sports clubs, dance groups, hiking club to science student associations. A part from that, students were invited to conferences and congresses that took place at the university.
activities_recommended: I would recommend going for hikes outside of the main city you are staying in to get to know the area in a different way. Also, I joined student gatherings that took place in the dorm such as international dinners, where each of us cooked a meal from our own country.
weekend_recommendations: Weekends are a great opportunity to visit the archipelago. So, we often took a boat to an island and spend the day walking around surrounded by nature. We also went bouldering, ice skating, hiking when there was nice weather. In case of rainy days, it was the perfect opportunity to cook and bake together with friends.
culture_adjustment: The country I visited was very near geographically to Denmark so I didn't encounter any differences. However, compared to my hometown, all the shops closed very early ( except for supermarkets) so you had to make sure to plan accordingly to avoid arriving to the shop and find it closed. At the same time, everyone spoke English fluently so communication was not a problem at all!
socializing_tips: I would recommend joining facebook groups such as " students in _________ ( your Erasmus destination)" , or focused in your favourite hobbie " Hiking around ______ ( name of your Erasmus destination)". However, while living in a student dorm, you constantly meet new people so don't be afraid! If you are taking classes at the university, you will meet local students during the lectures so suggest going for a coffee or eating together to chat and get to know each other.
cultural_challenges: Compared to my home country, people here spoke and behaved more quietly. For instance, I am used to speaking in the phone while I am in the bus or metro back at home. However, in this country public transport was a very quite environment! Also back at home, I am used to having pocket money while in my Erasmus destination, everyone paid everywhere by card ( there were even places that did not accept cash).
culture_appreciated: The work-live balance and the relax way they live. Having fika (coffee breaks in the afternoon) helped us to recharge batteries for the rest of the day! They appreciate a lot and take care of nature, it is very admirable!
top3_advice: I'd tell them to enjoy this learning and life experience a lot! It was an honour having been able to participate in an Erasmus in this country. It is an unique and incredible way to start working in a laboratory in a foreign university. The quality of research at this institution is amazing and you learn so many techniques, how to be independent and plan your own experiments. Don't worry about not knowing their native language, they speak English like a native. However, I would totally recommend learning some basics before arriving so you can say " hello, goodbye, thank you". It is a great way to start learning their culture!
other_useful_info: I would also suggest to plan all your experiments accordingly and dedicate some time for data analysis and writing the thesis! This way you will avoid last-minute issues and stress before the submission deadline.
most_rewarding: I feel I've learned so, so much!! It has reinforced the idea that I want to pursue a scientific career after my master's. Looking back, I feel so happy seeing all the techniques that I have learned, all the experiments that I've done. After a lot of hours of data analysis and writing, submitting and presenting the thesis were moments I will never forget!!
greatest_challenge: Sometimes some experiments don't go as planned and you don't understand why. However, after taking a little break, looking back at the protocols and speaking with your supervisor, you can find the mistakes and plan a new experiment! I learned not to be afraid of making mistakes, it is the way we learn!

crucial_aspects: Karolinska Institutet (KI) er et internationalt velanerkendt medicinsk universitet med stor fokus på forskning og uddannelse, og derfor tiltalte dette universitet mig. Derudover er Stockholm en by, som jeg længe gerne ville udforske. Ved at bo her i en periode oplever og udforsker man byen anderledes end ved udelukkende at besøge som turist. Man får nye rutiner, som passer ind i den kultur, som man indgår i. Derudover er Stockholm en perfekt kombination mellem storbyliv og natur, hvilket i høj grad tiltaler mig.
info_ease: Meget nemt. Karolinska Institutet er meget velorganiseret, og det er tydeligt at mærke, at de er vant til at have udvekslingsstuderende. Alt er koordineret og arrangeret, og der er masser af information og masser af hjælp at hente hele tiden. Derudover arrangerer de infomøde for alle udvekslingsstuderende inden start, hvor man dels for informationer om at studere der, og dels møder alle de andre studerende.
arrival_assistance: Jeg gjorde ikke brug af muligheden, men KI har pick-up service for alle.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Selve ansøgningen til KI var nemt. Man laver en prioriteringsliste over de fag, som man gerne vil have. På KI's hjemmeside kan man se, hvilke fag der er tilgængelige og hvornår, samt hvad de går ud på, og hvad der forventes af en.
registration_help: Både KU exchange og KI's internationale koordinatorer stod til rådighed og hjalp hurtigt, hvis der var nogle spørgsmål. Desuden er KI's hjemmeside meget oplysende, hvis man er i tvivl om noget.
registration_success: Jeg måtte gå på kompromis med tidspunkt for udvekslingsophold og rotationer, da der ikke var plads til mig på de hold, som jeg ønskede. Dog var jeg i kontakt med den internationale koordinator fra KI, som hjalp med et godt alternativ til mig. Jeg endte med at få de bedste måneder vejrmæssigt i Stockholm og nogle lærerige og spændende kliniske rotationer på trods af, at det var i andre specialer end jeg først have prioriteret.
registration_advice: Vær fleksibel og åbentsindet uanset om du får dine prioriteringer eller ej. Det er en kæmpe oplevelse uanset.
course_level: Jeg var afsted ifm. 11. semesters internationale perspektiv med klinik i udlandet, hvilket var meget passende. Der blev forventet noget af mig uden at det overskred mine grænser.
teaching_comparison: De kliniske rotationer var meget strukturerede og velorganiserede. Der blev forventet noget af dig, men du blev også i høj grad involveret og deltog i det daglige kliniske arbejde med udvikling af praktiske færdigheder også. Det er de bedste kliniske rotationer, jeg har haft gennem hele min studietid.
courses_enrolled: - Klinisk rotation i intern medicin (2 uger kardiologi, 1 uge hæmatologi, 1 uge gastroenterologi) - Klinisk rotation i oftalmologi (4 uger) - Klinisk rotation i almen kirurgi og urologi (4 uger)
recommended_courses: Jeg vil især fremhæve den kliniske rotation i oftalmologi, da vi igennem vores studietid på KU ikke har praktik/klinik i dette speciale, og det er et meget kort og introducerende kursus til faget. Jeg var på St. Eriks Ögonsjukhus, som er et stort oftalmologisk hospital med mange subspecialer indenfor øjensygdomme samt en stor øjenskadestue, hvor der er et stort flow af patienter fra en stor del af Sverige. Jeg udviklede både teoretiske og praktiske færdigheder, som jeg vil kunne bruge både i skadestuen og i almen praksis i mit fremtidige virke som læge, især som yngre læge i kbu.
unexpected_costs: Ingen.
cost_comparison: Den svenske krone var lav, mes jeg var der, hvorfor mange ting var billigere end herhjemme. Dog er der noget frugt/grønt, som er dyrere end i DK.
activities_available: - der er fitnesscenter på campus, som er gratis for studerende. - der var kaffe/kage hver torsdag eftermiddag på campus for at styrke det sociale - der blev holdt fester/arrangementer/ekskursioner for studerende løbende - international buddies, hvor man blev tilknyttet en svensk medicinstuderende, man kunne socialisere med, hvis man ville - intromøde for alle udvekslingsstuderende inden semesterstart
activities_recommended: Deltag i alt det, som kan passe ind i din hverdag og som møder dit sociale behov. Der er mange muligheder hele tiden, så stress ikke over, hvis du ikke kan deltage i det hele
weekend_recommendations: Udforske Stockholm og omkringliggende områder, så meget som muligt. Et must er at besøge den Svenske Skærgård på en sejltur og hoppe i vandet rundt omkring i byen, hvis vejret tillader det.
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Stockholm og København minder på mange måder om hinanden.
socializing_tips: Deltag i aktiviteter på campus.
cultural_challenges: Ingen.
culture_appreciated: At kulturen i store træk er den samme som i København.
top3_advice: - Kast dig ud i at snakke dansk/svensk og forbedre det nordiske samarbejde. Jeg kunne ikke noget særligt svensk inden, jeg tog afsted, men jeg blev tvunget til at lytte og tilegne mig sproget i nogen grad. Jeg havde en klar fordel på de kliniske rotationer sammenlignet med de andre udvekslingsstuderende fra andre lande, da jeg kunne forstå og tale med patienter og medarbejdere uden noget stor sproglig barriere. Jeg kunne altså indgå i hverdagen på en helt anden måde end de andre, da jeg ikke skulle have alt oversat. - KI går meget op i både det faglige og sociale, og du vinder altså på begge parametre - KI er velstruktureret og organiseret. De er vant til at have udvekslingstuderende. Der bliver forventet noget af dig, men du bliver både beriget fagligt, socialt og kulturelt, og det er en kæmpe oplevelse.
other_useful_info: Der bliver forventet, at du er der fuld tid og deltager. Desuden skulle jeg skrive case reports, holde logbog, lave præsentationer og deltage i små seminarer.
most_rewarding: At møde andre studerende fra alle mulige lande. Der var 50+ udvekslingstuderende, da jeg var afsted, og du bor i samme område med alle de andre, hvorfor der er rig mulighed for at lave noget sammen ved siden af studiet og i weekenderne.
greatest_challenge: At nå alt det, som jeg gerne ville. Tiden flyver afsted, og du har en fantastisk tid.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to find a host university that both had a high academic level, taught relevant classes in english and was in a city that i found interesting and would like to live in. All of this was applicable to Karolinska Institutet and Stockholm, which is why this ended up as my first priority when applying and why i was happy to accpet the spot when I was offered the spot here.
info_ease: KI was very good at guiding and welcoming new international students. We got plenty information before arriving and there was a whole week of welcome acitivities planned the week before the semester started. this included a wide range from both social activites to help with activating our student accounts and take picture for our student ID's.
arrival_assistance: As mentioned above there was a whole week of welcome activites and study fairs planned. It was always easy to find a faculty member or international coordinator to ask if need be, and KI was very good at having all nessicary information available online, either on their social media or on their webpage.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: There is an online application form you fill out on KI's version of mobility online. You have to create a seperate log in to use for their mobility online. Here you fill in your prefeered classes (you have to be aware that they offer limited options for classes when you go on exchange in the biomedicine programme) in a prioritised order and then you send them in though this online form. after they have oficially accpeted you, then you will recieve a letter of acceptance showing what classes you got. this letter is also nessicary to apply for housing through KI housing.
registration_help: There was a zoom-meeting with all incoming exchange students in the biomedicine programme before application deadlines with plenty options to ask questions about the process as well as the option to reach out to your individual international coordinatior.
registration_success: I got both the classes i wanted as my first priority.
registration_advice: make sure you study classes thoroughly beforehand to ensure its a good fit with what you want to learn and what your interest are. I did not have the best experience with the class in molecular medicine - cardiometabolic and infectious diseases, but i wanted to do the two 5th semester courses offered. In the future i would still have picked the oncology course offered on the 5th semester, but considered either doing a project or 3rd semeste courses for the remaining 15 credits of the semester.
course_level: both classes were fail/pass which means that the amount of details nessicary to remember to pass were way less than what I have been used to a UCPH. I did not find them more or as academically challenging as the classes i have had in Copenhagen, but i still enjoyed most lectures and seminars and i feel i gained new skills and knowledge from my exhange.
teaching_comparison: it is very similar with a combination of small group work and classroom sessions combined with lectures and seminars. There were more assignments and deadlines of papers that had to be handed in than i have been used to at UCPH, but the student-professor dynamic is very similar and very grounded in the scandinavian teaching-style.
courses_enrolled: Molecular medicine - Oncology Molecular medicine - cardiometabolic and infectious diseases
recommended_courses: Molecular medicine - oncology it was an extremly well planned and cohesive couse that offered a better introduction to the clinical aspects of biomedicine that we dont get with the courses we have in copehangen. At the same time, most professors and teachers were amazing educators and gave great lectures.
unexpected_costs: I did not have any unexpected costs during my exchange.
cost_comparison: groceries and lesiure activites like café visits were cheaper than expected, and cheaper than copenhagen. I expected my living-expenses to be comparable with Copenhagen, but i spend less on both rent and food in Stockholm. This might be due to the fact that the swedish Krone was fairly weak compared to the danish Krone while i was on exhcange
activities_available: There is a free gym available on the Solna campus that you can acess every day of the week. On top of this the student union plans different activites such as vollyball or badminton or yoga that you can sign up for and participate in for free if you want to. The different student union also plans parties and activities so keep an eye out on KI's social media and you will for sure find something to participate in!
activities_recommended: I participated in the Students Noble Night Cap, which is the official afterparty after the nobel ceremony planned and hosted by students. It was a lot of work and you have to be prepared to spend a lot of time on it, but it was a fun way to meet sudents from other programmes and universities in Stockholm, and you might even get the chance to meet a real noble lauerate! I would also definetly recommend that you buy a ticket for the lucia ball in december. It is a white tie event with music, dancing and a fancy dinner. Its a fun way to end your exchange year and a great excuse to get dressed up in a fancy dress or suit.
weekend_recommendations: Stockholm has a lot of amazing day-hikes all within a short bus ride from the city center, so i would definelty recommend that you travel out of the city center in the early fall while the weather is great to experience the beautifull nature. ESN Stockholm host som amazing hikes every other weekend in the summer and fall which is a good choice if you don't want to plan a trip on your own. If you have the time and money, then travel up north to swedish lapland and see northern lights, experience true winter darkness and wilderness in a way we can't really get back home in Denmark - i sadly didnt have time but many of my friends left for lapland-trips and they all loved it. Beware that it is quite expensive, but well worth it!
culture_adjustment: Since sweden is not that different from Denmark it wasn't a massive cultural shit to move to Stockholm. The biggest change came in meeting fellow international students who came from very different cultures from all over the world. This was especially clear when working in groups or preparing presentations, since not all were equally used to that type of teaching and to be in charge of own learning in that way.
cultural_challenges: At times the language barrier talking with other students who's english was not always as developed and who were not as used to working the independently could at times be challenging. You learn to have to communicate clearly and set boundaries to ensure that its a nice work-enviroment for everyone - which will definetly be a benefit long term.
culture_appreciated: fika! the mandatory almost daily coffe and cake/bun break, ensuring socialising and breaking down barriers between teacher and student, resident students and exchange students ect. It's a wonderfull tradition and something i will definetly bring home to Denmark.
top3_advice: Seize all opportunities that come to you consider doing a project and not just courses while at KI - they have amazing professors and reseachers and you get a chance to work directly with them. Stay on campus! it makes your life 100 times easier and you will get to participate in all on-campus activites a lot easier.
most_rewarding: Meeting students from other european countries and learning about other european cultures - i now have friends spread all over europe and the world.
greatest_challenge: At times it can feel quite lonely, and you need to put in a lot of effort to create the same sense of community and belonging that I had at UCPH. I definetly learned a lot about myself and my need for social interactions and close friendships that i hadn't realised before i left for exchange.

housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

crucial_aspects: Language was a crucial aspect for me, understanding the patients in their language.
info_ease: Easy enough, some of he information was hard to find than other.
arrival_assistance: I had a meeting with the host exchange coordinator, because I missed the introduction day there I could get answers to my questions, information about MRSA screening access and student cards.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: First you had to fill out an online application form, and send in your transcript of records and recommendation from your University along with a copy of your passport. After that you fill out the information in the host universities mobility-online where you then can select and prioritise courses.
registration_help: You can contact the Contact person/Exchange coordinator at the respective universities for help.
registration_success: The registering of courses was a prioritising system. I got my first two priorities of departments and after a dialogue with the exchange coordinator at the host university found a third course.
registration_advice: Be open minded, start collecting the documents early.
course_level: My exchange was exclusively clinical rotations. The level was matched to my knowledge.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style was similar to my university. The teaching was primarily case based and procedure training.
courses_enrolled: Clinical rotation in the emergency process - 2EE090 Clinical rotation in surgery 1 - 2EE036 Clinical rotation in surgery 2 - 2EE037
recommended_courses: I would highly recommend all of these courses. Since these were clinical rotations individual preference in specialties going to impact your view of it. The emergency rotation was interesting because of the Södersjukhuset had primarily acute specialists on staff instead of a representative of a specialties working in the emergency room, which gives a broad perspective that was interesting to see. The surgery courses was where really good for someone interested in surgery, with opportunities to participate in ward tasks and assistant surgery.
unexpected_costs: I had to buy two month cards for transportation the first month because I thought I was viable for the discounted, I was not.
cost_comparison: The housing cost do not include the rent of my apartment at home.
activities_available: There’s an open gym, outdoor tennis court, beach volleyball. Student club with events.
activities_recommended: I would recommend visiting the tourist places, the museums. It is a new city to explore
weekend_recommendations: I can recommend taking the ferry to health game or the train to Corona sailing in the archipelago. Some museums have free entry for students on certain days.
culture_adjustment: The culture is similar to my culture so it was not hard to adjust.
socializing_tips: Primarily got to know international exchange students, because I only had rotation with exchange students. so I have no tips.
cultural_challenges: I did not find any cultural differences challenging
culture_appreciated: I really appreciate the fika culture, And bringing leftovers for lunch.
top3_advice: I would tell them to start looking into exchange early, The whole process takes a while. I would recommend choosing housing with other people, and attending the introduction day and social events where everybody is looking for a friend, it can be challenging later on. I would recommend learning Swedish it makes the whole exchange better.
other_useful_info: I recommend arriving a few business days before your first day.there are a lot of practical things that need to be taken care of like getting access cards and student cards.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of the scene has been seeing that I am capable to adapt to new situations and settings, to work in a team of doctors and nurses. To have made new friends from all over the world, And connections for the future. It has given me the opportunity to see and live in a different culture.
greatest_challenge: The most challenging thing during this exchange has been managing my expectation of myself, to be OK with leaving the tourist activities to the weekend, because clinical rotations take a lot of energy especially in a new language. Not having been able to see everything I wanted here, just mean I have an excuse to come back.

crucial_aspects: The available courses and the reputation of the university
overall_comments: Absolutely incredibly experience
info_ease: Very easy. Almost everything had been sent the before arriving, and the little that hadn't was told to us in the intro days
arrival_assistance: In terms of residence at the university: none. However, everything was written in a mail which was highly informative and no problems arose. After that there were several intro days for new international students helping you be brought up to speed
arrival_comments: No comments. Basically flawless
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Absolutely incredibly experience
registration_process: Once you've arrived, i was are pre-registered to all your approved courses. i DID have to register for the exam as well but the lecturer made sure to mention and explain the process. You just log onto the website: "Ladok" (google: "Ladok KI"), click on your current course, and then "register". That's it. Very simple stuff
registration_help: I don't know, since it wasn't needed. Again, it was extremely easy
registration_success: No problems at all. I should stress that i did the biomedicine programme for 2nd year students and that comes as a package of courrses. In other words, if you want to have just a single course, that's not gonna be possible (as far as i'm aware anyhow). You have to go through all courses associated with the semester.
registration_advice: Doublecheck on canvas and ladok that you are registered once you recieve your login information
academics_comments: Absolutely incredibly experience
course_level: The level appropriate most of the time. You sometimes ran into the unfortunate situation of a researcher lecturing on something they've been working on for years, not really getting just how little we knew and how much they would need to slow down for people to grasp it.
teaching_comparison: A few big differences: For most courses, theres usually a new lecturer ever "subject"; e.g. a lecturer will teach you about T-cell for 3 hours and then you never see him again. This means you will meet A LOT of new lecturers as they will just constantly be introduced as leave. As one can imagine, there is quite a bit of varience here with some being great and others maybe being more suited for research. Secondly, your hours were you attend lectures will be longer. During most courses, i was there from 9-16 5 days a week. In theory, there is also no book associated with most courses (aside from neuroscience). I loathed this personally, but it is very much a preference thing, and you can make it work even if you don't show up to every lecture. Most thing aren't mandatory
courses_enrolled: Biostatistics Tissue biology Immunology and microbiology Neuroscience
recommended_courses: Neuroscience was excellent. Good pace, an actual book to follow, practical lab was informative.
unexpected_costs: Non that i remember
cost_comparison: Alcohol was more expensive than i imagined. Everything else was either akin to, or cheaper than in Denmark
activities_available: Too many to count, but I'll try: * Running * Bible studies * Gym * Tennis * A good deal of parties * More
activities_recommended: The Stockholm nobel light show in december was pretty good.
weekend_recommendations: Karolinska doesn't do any other holidays than summer and christmas. That aside, going up to see lapland during a weekend is recommended.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. To be entirely honest, basically everyone in my course and apartment was international, so it is not like a had a huge amount of interaction with Swedes and swedish culture unless i actively "chased" it.
socializing_tips: Go to events in the beginning. Then, start doing some activity routinely. This can be by joining a club, but even something as simple as a movie night can be great.
cultural_challenges: No drinking in public, alcohol can only be bought in government stores and they close at 14:00 during weekends
culture_appreciated: Individuality. People just mind their own business
top3_advice: * I cannot stress enough how much i would recommend getting an apartment on campus. Especially a shared 4-bedroom apartment. * As you know, social circles tend to form early. Lock in on being prosocial and active during the first month * Even if you don't have any holidays (christmas and summer aside), you can still make a lot happen during the weekends
other_useful_info: I feel like i've covered it... The library is open till 22, so use that when you are behind on your studies i guess?
most_rewarding: The people. I've met a bunch of people from pretty different background to my own, with whom i've had a great many good experiences. The social aspect really is special
greatest_challenge: Differences in teaching styles, meaning long days of complex lectures where i just wanted to read it in a book at my preffered hours. Maybe the darkness? But again, I'm danish so its not that different
other_comments: From what I've gathered, their research and internships are absolutely superb and probably where they really shine

crucial_aspects: It was in the countryside of England and had a lot of nature and the campus experience of living and studying on campus which provided fantastic social opportunities.
info_ease: It was fine.
arrival_assistance: I was picked up at the airport and showed my accommodation.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It worked very well and smooth I really liked the mobility portal.
registration_help: I had a Alexandra I could always call or email if I had any questions so that was nice.
registration_success: It went okay, they switched around some classes so I couldn't take them but I found some other ones.
registration_advice: Read through the information pages.
course_level: It was low compared to KU. The teachers were spending a lot of time on "bossing" around instead of teaching.
teaching_comparison: It reminded me of primary school teaching style
courses_enrolled: Advanced laboratory skills, infectious diseases and project and business planning
recommended_courses: project and business planning was okay
unexpected_costs: none
cost_comparison: food was way cheaper than DK
activities_available: There was a lot! I joined squash, cricket, tennis and aerial society. But I also tried badminton, karate, basketball and salsa.
activities_recommended: squash was really fun! cricket as well was something nice to experience when being in the UK.
weekend_recommendations: GO TO WALES!!
culture_adjustment: It was fairly okay
socializing_tips: Join societies and clubs.
cultural_challenges: The class room cultural differences. I felt like people were being very different which was interesting but I had to adjust.
culture_appreciated: The kindness of the British people, they were so so friendly and helpful.

other_useful_info: Enjoy the kindness of people and be open-minded towards them.

greatest_challenge: Learning to be more open and not judge a book by its cover.

crucial_aspects: I loved exploring GB and Ireland. They have some amazing hitten cities and national parks, which are very accessible.
overall_comments: My favorite part was traveling, the academic stuff wasn't that great.
info_ease: We had 2 orientation days, where we only got information of the University and campus and multiple tours.
arrival_assistance: The Global Opportunity department gave us a lot of information when we arrived.
arrival_comments: Volunteering students at Global Opportunity was so sweet and available throughout the semester as well for questions.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: My favorite part was traveling, the academic stuff wasn't that great.
registration_process: First I send a list of all the courses I found interesting. If found these courses on Keele's webpage, although there isn't a lot of information on the courses (If you compare them to KU). Then I was told to choose a top 4 of all the courses I wanted. Afterwards I was told a lot of the courses was not available in the spring semester, eventhough Keele Uni's website said it was. Then I got a list of what was available and I chose from that list. 2 weeks before arriving I got a lot more info on my courses. 1 week before arriving I was told I was enrolled at the courses.
registration_help: The Global Opportunity department was also in charge of registration of classes.
registration_success: I got all the classes I signed up for, but not the classes I originally wanted.
registration_advice: Make sure you get a list from Global opportunity of all the courses available to you from the start. It might safe some time. And be patient with them.
academics_comments: My favorite part was traveling, the academic stuff wasn't that great.
course_level: They were all level 7 courses, although not very academic when compared to UCPH.
teaching_comparison: It was more in-class participation and group work compared to UCPH. Furthermore, not many lectures.
courses_enrolled: LSC-40055 Infectious Diseases LSC-40033 Advanced Laboratory Techniques LSC-40030 Project Management and Business Planning
recommended_courses: I liked "Project Management and Business Planning" as I got to practice my English skills both literary and verbal with presentations and assignments. "Advanced Laboratory Techniques" is the easiest class I have ever taken.
unexpected_costs: I spend a lot on food, because my kitchen was so disgusting at Horwood Hall.
cost_comparison: Food is less expensive normally, but the Coop on campus is more expensive than normal supermarkets. The train tickets weren't that bad.
activities_available: Almost everything. Go check out clubs and societies on Keele's own webpage.
activities_recommended: I joined the squash and cricket. I loved it! There are so many clubs so I would recommend joining on of them, even though sports clubs are a bit more expensive.
weekend_recommendations: Go to Wales! The small towns by the sea are so charming and Snowdonia national park is so beautiful. Scottish highlands are also amazing, so rent a car a go expolore. Got to Ireland on saint Patrick's day... but don't go to Dublin (only Americans there)
culture_adjustment: People are more friendly, but it might seem a bit frightening and weird at first.
socializing_tips: Talk to the people in your class and join a sports club. The sports clubs also have a lot of socials which apparently are great and a good way to make friends.
cultural_challenges: Random people talking to you. The Northern English accent can be challenging to understand.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness.
top3_advice: Join a sports club. Go explore the country side/ Go on hikes. Go to Wales.
other_useful_info: The best housing is at Barnes. People at Keele University and other exchange students are typically around ages of 19-21.
most_rewarding: Making great international and local friends. Visition so much beautiful nature.
greatest_challenge: I wasn't to happy about my accommodation.

crucial_aspects: That it was a good university, preferably with a Korean Studies Department. I ended up choosing Dageu, because it was smaller than Seoul, so I thought there would be more opportunities, for instance to join school clubs and so on. (which ended up being true!)
info_ease: Not easy regarding the dorms. Information about the dorms were given out super late, and it was not easy to find the building.
arrival_assistance: There was an intro-day, where we were informed about many important things like courses, school events, school jackets, alien registration card, opening up a Korean bank account and so on. And they also sent us the power point after. So that was really helpful.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Upon arrival was fine, but for me personally, in the first week having to apply for Master courses, I felt helpless, because no information was given about that. Only through my Korean buddy was I able to figure out what I was supposed to do, and it was a lengthy and frankly very over-complicated process to apply for the Master courses. I had to email professors if I could be in their class, and at that point it was really late, but luckily two Professors got back to me and accepted within the 48 hours I had to apply (in the add/drop period, mind you). Then I had to fill out a form in Korean, and attach screenshots of the acceptance from the Professors.. BUT, for normal students on the undergraduate level, they just had to apply online, and it seemed fairly easy.
registration_help: My Korean buddy, and then emailing with the exchange coordinator. But she is extremely busy.
registration_success: I didn't get any of the classes I though, but I was actually very happy with the classes I ended up with.
registration_advice: I don't know, for Master's students, I guess email professors in advance and ask your buddy as soon as possible for help. For undergrads, definitely get up early and be ready for when the registration link opens, in order to get the classes you want. My roommate struggled a lot to figure out her schedule and get matching classes.
course_level: I took MA classes, as I am a MA student.
teaching_comparison: One class was very similiar, and the other was a bit different.
courses_enrolled: A9783-01 KOREAN HISTORY and A8432 TECHNICAL TRANSLATION AND CAT TRANSLATION
recommended_courses: For MA students, can definitely recommend both these courses A9783-01 KOREAN HISTORY and A8432 TECHNICAL TRANSLATION AND CAT TRANSLATION They were very giving.
unexpected_costs: Maybe school club fees? if you join a school club, there is a small fee, and if you want to go to their dinner parties and trips, you should set aside some money for that as well. Maybe for the trip to a cabin, it was like 300DKK?
cost_comparison: Doing laundry at the dorm was super cheap.
activities_available: I was in and English-club, and a volunteer club. My friend was in a women's football club, and there were also clubs like photography and astronomy etc.
activities_recommended: Joining a club, and the school fall festival! So many cool concerts for free, and opportunities to talk to Korean students.
weekend_recommendations: Apsan Mountain. And Suseong Lake. And downtown, Dongseong-ro.
culture_adjustment: Fine.
socializing_tips: Join the clubs. And fight against your own shyness, and start up conversations with the memebers of the clubs.
cultural_challenges: Nothing challenging.
culture_appreciated: Kindness and politeness.
top3_advice: The dorms have curfew and are up on a hill. Walking from the subway station will be really hard. Join the clubs. That's how I made Korean friends. Enjoy, the campus is stunning!
other_useful_info: The school also offers many free day trips to nearby cities, with cultural experiences and food.
most_rewarding: Meeting and socializing with so many Korean friends.
greatest_challenge: The registration process, haha. And not having a kitchen or a fridge.

crucial_aspects: New, interesting region - I could get knowledge about a new area that was relevant for my studies
overall_comments: It was very worth it. I gained new academic knowledge and got new academic competences and explored a new area ect.
info_ease: The institution was very helpfull.
arrival_assistance: The institution picked us up in a van.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: It was very worth it. I gained new academic knowledge and got new academic competences and explored a new area ect.
registration_process: I do not remember steps into details, anyhow, there was a lot of work, but it was made step-by-step and manageable, therefore it was not overwhelming.
registration_help: We could also ask the international staff and our professors, which was nice. Furthermore, meetings were arranged.
registration_success: I changed one of the classes. I liked my classes, though, especially two of them that were about politics.
registration_advice: If you follow the steps and the deadlines, everything should be fine, and as long as you do that, there is no need to to stress.
academics_comments: It was very worth it. I gained new academic knowledge and got new academic competences and explored a new area ect.
course_level: They start at university earlier, which means that there was some difference, you did gain knowledge, though, but if you want to have academic levels comparative to ours, you probably need to take some of the senior-bachelor courses or master courses.
teaching_comparison: As mentioned earlier, they use another system, the American one, so at some aspects you can't really compare them.
courses_enrolled: Central Asia in Global Politics, Foreign Politics of Kazakhstan, History of Kazakhstan
recommended_courses: Central Asia in Global Politics (master course, but both home and host University allowed us to take it)
unexpected_costs: Maybe that the sports were actually quite expensive. If you wanted to attend sport outside the uni. Because the ones at uni were for free, where for example they had a running club, for free, and a free gym
cost_comparison: I used taxies pretty much as they were easy and cheap, however, you could drive in busses and metroes (metroes I also did pretty much) for almost no money.
activities_available: Several arrangement. Parties and other. Language clubs ect.
activities_recommended: Running club if you like to run
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips!! Explore the culture, but also, the besides learning about culture and academics, the nature is impressing. Trips there are cheap, if you buy them at local places (of course choose the safe-ones that other people go on, that are actual companies)
culture_adjustment: Of course, another culture, but people were very friendly. Also, they seem quite open, so you open up yourself more
socializing_tips: Just be open. People do not really judge.
cultural_challenges: Maybe that in Denmark we have specific ways of doing things, so maybe that. However, I pretty fast got some good friends, so I didn't think about it to much.
culture_appreciated: That they were friendly and welcoming
top3_advice: Explore the area and have fun. And regarding more "serious": be aware that the air pollution is pretty bad, be aware that there is meat in most meals
other_useful_info: That you need to attend many of the classes - also, that staying on campus is a good way to socialize.
most_rewarding: I would actually say the people I met there. However, also some competences and academic confidence I due to mandatory presentations, especially due to a presentation in our master class.
greatest_challenge: That I had to addapt to the food and air, the first day, I got food posioned. After that it was fine.
other_comments: All the paper work for exchange were worth the experience!

crucial_aspects: That there would be opportunities to speak the language im studying, as well as the city/country being somewhere i've never been before.
info_ease: Quite easy.
arrival_assistance: I had a lot of assistance from the international office at my host uni - they were really extremely kind and helpful.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: I don't really remember, but I think it was alright (though quite a lot of paperwork and different locations that those had to be done at.) The International office was very helpful!
registration_help: The international office had students help us manage and help with potential language barriers.
registration_success: Some of the classes that looked like they would be offered (on the KIMEP website) weren't on the registration list, but I was happy with what I ended up with and I believe we were able to register courses before a lot of other students, meaning it was easier to get exactly what we wanted.
registration_advice: Have different options for classes ready, so that if something isnt offered, you have other options available.
course_level: I took 1 class that were a mix of BA and MA. I really liked it though!
teaching_comparison: Quite different! At my home uni its more of "here is the theory"/"here is what people in the field have done before" and then we have to use that information and apply it ourselves as well as a big focus on critical thinking, whereas KIMEP was more about learning things by heart/memorizing information. I was a bit disappointed in the intense use of AI at KIMEP uni. Some professors didn't use it, which was nice, but even if the professor didn't, almost all the students did, which made the presentations part of the year (towards the end, where we had to do presentations in almost all courses) really boring, cause it was so painfully obvious that 90% of all the presentations were made by AI.
courses_enrolled: Russian Speaking Practise, Intensive Russian, Kazakh Spirituality, Petropolitics, Emerging Powers
recommended_courses: Petropolitics! It was very interesting, and the teacher was my absolute favourite. He can go off on a tangent, but his stories are always very interesting and he is quite a funny (and very clever!!) man. I learned so much about oil, tax-systems and international politics in this course! All my russian-language courses were also really good!
unexpected_costs: Translitteration of passport from danish/english into russian. Kitchen utensils, duvet, pillow when moving in. Fitness membership.
cost_comparison: Transportation was way cheaper than I thought. Eating out was also quite cheap, even on a tight budget.
activities_available: A lot! And they send out e-mails as well as inform you in the beginning of the semester.
activities_recommended: Maybe a club! I didn't do that, but I used the free gym on campus, that all uni-students are welcome to use.
weekend_recommendations: Nature! (Hiking, horseback riding, skiing, ice skating, renting a car and driving further to see things like petroglyphs, the Great Steppe, lakes, Charyn Canyon etc). On national holidays there might be festivals or music playing, and KIMEP was located next to a big square that offen had concerts or events happening.
culture_adjustment: Alright! People are very nice and offen times interested in you if you are from a country far away. Not everyone speaks english, but people are still very nice and don't mind the language barrier too much.
socializing_tips: It can be a bit difficult, but try to just speak with people in your class or join clubs/sport teams while you are there!
cultural_challenges: Probably the bathroom/toilets and not being able to throw toiletpaper in the toilet. Other than that it was fine.
culture_appreciated: The people and how nice (most) people were. Also the architecture of the city as well as all the delicious food the city had to offer.
top3_advice: Be prepared for A LOT of AI use, and try to not fall into the trap of using it too much yourself. Be prepared for a lot of homework in your russian language classes! Remember to plan some of your weekends for longer travel (other cities or near-by countries) or/and events, since its easy to be tired and just stay in the part of the city that you already know.
other_useful_info: Not really.
most_rewarding: Seeing a new part of the world and meeting new people. I would recommend EVERYONE to try to visit Almaty/KZ (or generally Central Asia).
greatest_challenge: Probably getting my phone registered, but that was also a new thing, so the system around the registration were developing and changing. The international office were very helpful during this very long process tho!

crucial_aspects: The unique opportunity to live and be a part of society in Central Asia - a part of the world, that i didn't knew much about before my exchange stay. It seemed like a great chance to go on adventure, when KIMEP University in Almaty showed up on the list of friendship universities with University of Copenhagen, and I thought that I had to grab that chance.
info_ease: It was pretty easy, and KIMEP University definitely made a great effort to do everything they could to inform about everything. I never stood in a situation where i didn't knew what to do when i arrived or in my first days in Almaty.
arrival_assistance: KIMEP University provided transportation from the airport to the dormitory on campus, which was a great service, as it could be overwhelming to find way on your own, after arriving in a completely different country with different systems, valuta, language etc. KIMEP has a so-called International Office, that has been extremely helpfull. They have provided help whenever I needed it, and has when I arrived they helped me with logistics such as withdraw money, choose courses and get a Kazakh SIM-card.
arrival_comments: It has been a great help and security that KIMEP have the International Office, as they have students that provides help every day.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was really simple, even though I felt a little lost in the proces after getting accepted by KIMEP University. I contacted a study guide who calmed me, and told me that it would all succeed in the end - which she was right about. It is pretty easy to go through the registration process at KU, even though it can seem unmanageable while you're in the process.
registration_help: Study guides and the "Selvbetjening" on KUnet.
registration_success: I got all the classes that i wanted - 6/6. :-)
registration_advice: To relax when searching for registration before arrival in your exchange university - they are only interested in helping you, and it seems they often are able to get you into your first priorities when you arrive at the university.
course_level: Some of the courses has been really structured and theoretical, which i definitely like. These classes has learnt me a lot, and has a classic academic approach on teaching. Other courses has been unacademic and full of guesswork and undocumentated claims. Even though, these are also the courses that has provided me with the most new perspectives, as these professors seem to have a lot of opinions and attitudes. The level of my courses has variated a lot.
teaching_comparison: Here at KIMEP University the freedom is way less than at KU. At KIMEP there is a absence politic, which means that you will fail a course if you have been absent for more than six classes. Also, students are continuously being tested at KIMEP. This includes 2x mid-terms, presentations in class and quizzed. The pedagogical approach is about the same, as professors are not really personally involved in the students - still, you can always contact the professors if you need help or wants to inform them on anything.
courses_enrolled: Emerging Powers, Kazakh Spirituality, Terrorism and Security, Foreign Policy of Kazakhstan, Globalization and Diversity and History of Kazakhstan.
recommended_courses: Foreign Policy of Kazakhhstan!!! Really interesting, and a very unique approach on foreign policy. Classes are extremely entertaining and informative. History of Kazakhstan is always recommendable.
unexpected_costs: If you want to cook yourself in the kitchen, you need to buy all the kitchen tools and cleaning stuff yourself. It is not very expensive in Kazakhstan, but still it is good to know.
cost_comparison: Public transportation including taxis are really cheap, and the same are groceries.
activities_available: There are lots of clubs, including football, american football, basketball, table tennis, debate clubs, chess tournaments, music, movie nights.
activities_recommended: I would recommend everyone to participate in sports or debate/chess/music clubs. It is a great way into a community.
weekend_recommendations: Just to walk around Almaty, and to visit Medeu/Shymbulak in the mountains - it is only 25 minutes in taxi. In Alamty you can find lots of good and cheap restaurants, a great bazar and Arasan which is a popular sauna. Also, you should visit Astana if you want to experience a completely different, futuristic and cheap city. Kyrgyzstan is definitely worth a trip, but a weekend is not enough - I would recommend to visit in holidays. Uzbekistan is also great and really interesting.
culture_adjustment: Really easy - people are interested and open for foreigners.
socializing_tips: Just say hallo and all the rest will happen if you want it to. The Kazakhs are so friendly and curious.
cultural_challenges: Nothing was challenging, only interesting.
culture_appreciated: The openness and calmly behaviour that I have experienced in all of the Central Asian countries.
top3_advice: 1. All the practical stuff will be solved, even though it sometimes seems hopeless. KIMEP offers such a great service, and things will settle down when you arrive. 2. Be prepared that Kazakhstan doesn't have an embassy in Denmark, and vice versa. This means that you have to go to Stockholm to get your Kazakh visa. This can be a little challenging and frustrating if you dont know.
other_useful_info: KIMEP is extremely inspired by American universities when it comes to expression and culture, but still it provides you with great knowledge and insight in Central Asia. All classes are in English, and student life is full of great offers.
most_rewarding: The way I was welcomed by the Kazakh students and the university. This made the foundation for me to get to know people and the culture. Also, the fantastic travels was very rewarding. I have seen people and culture that I knew nothing about before.
greatest_challenge: That I sometimes missed Denmark. Things are very different over here. But only in a good way!
other_comments: I am extremely grateful that I had the opportunity to go on exchange. It has opened my eyes for Central Asia, and means that I have met many fantastic people and have had great experiences.

crucial_aspects: To live in a country where my target language is spoken.
info_ease: We got all the help we needed from the International Office at our host university.
arrival_assistance: We could always come by the International Office, text or email them for help.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: No issue.
registration_help: Help from the International Office
registration_success: We were able to registre before other students, which was a nice privilege.
registration_advice: To change classes, if one is not satisfied.
course_level: I do not think they calculate the ECTS points correctly considering the amount of work that is required. Only 5 points for a full class, is too few. But the level was accommodating.
teaching_comparison: American in the way that each professor has a lot of freedom in regards to how they do things. Fun to try.
courses_enrolled: Intensive Russian, Speaking Practice, Petropolitics, Ethics in International Affairs, Domestic Politics and Foreign Policy of the Russian Federation.
recommended_courses: The language courses are crucial for those who study language.
unexpected_costs: Being a copenhagener, one needs to get used to using taxis here often, as the city is very big. They are cheap though.
cost_comparison: Cost of living here is not expensive.
activities_available: Everything from book clubs to sport clubs. Very nice, that there is a free gym on campus.

crucial_aspects: London is such a big, international city which really appealed to me and I was sure that there was so much to see and do! Moreover, I was pretty sure the academic level would be more fitting than other destinations and I have family members living in the city.
overall_comments: It was everything I hoped for and I have made such good friends and really gotten to know the city.
info_ease: It was very easy as there was some introductory meetings and a lot of e-mails sent out from the university.
arrival_assistance: I received a lot of e-mails before arrival which also included invitations to introduction meetings where the uni gave a lot of information.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: It was everything I hoped for and I have made such good friends and really gotten to know the city.
registration_process: It took quite some time before the registrations opened because you had to fill out a looong document which a lot of priorities and had to check if the courses overlapped yourself - but as soon as the registrations opened it was easy as you just send the document by email. I got all the courses I wanted.
registration_help: You could write an e-mail to the university if you had any questions and they where very fast at replying.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wished for.
registration_advice: I would recommend to fill in the document with priorities in advance so you are ready to send it the second the registration opens.
academics_comments: It was everything I hoped for and I have made such good friends and really gotten to know the city.
course_level: I had level 7 courses which was the only level I could choose being a MA student. I found the level very similar to that of my home institution.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching is a bit different in England. My classes were shorter (1 hour lecture, 1 hour seminar), there were fewer people in the classes and the seminars are a lot more interactive than in Denmark.
courses_enrolled: 7AAON006 - Capitalism, liberalism and democracy 7AAON004 - Foreign Policies of the European Union 7AAON003 - European Identities and the EU 7AAON036 - The European Union & Global Capitalism
recommended_courses: I would really recommend the "European Identities and the EU" module as it was very interesting and the teacher Russell Foster good and funny. The class isn't that difficult but it is interesting. Also I really liked the Foreign Policies of the European Union.
unexpected_costs: It is a bit surprising how expensive London actually is. So the prices on food and so on were surprising and you just always end up using more money than you think.
cost_comparison: Museums are free which is really cool. Coffee is also cheaper than in Denmark. Groceries are pretty expensive (at least where I lived) and train rides are also expensive. I can recommend getting a National Railcard (I had the 16-25 years old one) where you get a discount on all the train tickets you buy and also you can connect it to your oyster card and get a discount for the tube and busses. It costs 30 pounds I think but you have really quickly saved that - especially if you plan on travelling around in the UK.
activities_available: There was a lot of lunches and social events (especially in the beginning) and then a lot of athletic activities.
activities_recommended: I would recommend going to a lot of events in the first weeks because a lot of exchange students did and I found a lot of friends there.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend going on trips around the UK: Bath, Bristol, Oxford, Cambridge, Cotswolds, Brighton, Canterbury, White Cliffs of Dover, Seven Sisters, Liverpool, Manchester. Also I went on a trip to Scotland for 8 days after uni was over which was amazing! Moreover, I can really recommend just exploring London. It is so big that you never really run out of areas or things to see. My favorite places are probably Hampstead (Hampstead Heath and Primrose Hill), Bermondsey, Shoreditch.
culture_adjustment: Very easy - the UK culture is not too different but still different enough that it is interesting.
socializing_tips: Attend the events in the first week and try to talk to people in classes. Or join a local sports club.
cultural_challenges: I think the most challenging was to figure out how things were done academically - but it was not that hard and the teachers were all really sweet and helpful.
culture_appreciated: I love the pub culture and just London and British people in general.
top3_advice: - Remember that the exams are transferred as passed or failed so don't stress too much about school. - Try to get accommodation that is pretty central as London is big and commuting very expensive. - If you are doubtful about anything academically go to the professor's office hours.
other_useful_info: I think I have covered the most important.
most_rewarding: That I have had more time than I normally have because I didn't have a job on the side so I have really just have half a year where I could explore, make friends and become much better at English :)
greatest_challenge: Figuring out the level academically and what was expected. My advice is: Try not to use too much time on it.

info_ease: It was quite challenging. I definitely feel that both KU and King's College are lacking proper and clear communication with their exchange students.
arrival_assistance: Many emails from the exchange-office at King's College and an introductory Zoom-meeting. And 1 hour "tea and greatings" with the other exchange students.
arrival_comments: They did nearly nothing to make it easier for us to meet other exchange students (or other students in general). One thing is simple orientation about the school and the general practical aspects of it. But another extremely important part of an exchange programme is the social aspect; meeting other students. And this was so disappointing. I attended one musical, where other exchange students were invited. And then I atteneded a 1 hour event where King's College just booked a room and then placed some cookies and tea. There was no host, no introduction - just 100 exchange students in one tiny room for an hour, trying to "network". And after this, there was nothing else. During my time, I made nearly no new friends (and I am extremely social), because we haden't gotten a proper introduction to anyone. I almost didn't see any exchange students (maybe except for a few Danes, that I knew beforehand).
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You get an email and then you follow the instructions. After being admitted, I had to pick 10 different courses we wanted to attend and then after (quite) a while I was placed in four courses. They were not all my first pick, but luckily I did get the two that were mandatory at KU.
registration_help: You can always write to King's College exchange-office.
registration_success: Got my two favorite and the other two were a but more random.
registration_advice: It can be frustrating but do your best and just send King's College an email if you have any question. I will be worth it in the end <3
course_level: I loved the courses! Academically King's College is great - or especially the classes I took. All great teachers/professors, who were very passionate about what they were teaching.
teaching_comparison: It was very different but great to try! We were often only between 7-15 in a classroom and participation was greatly encouraged. I am not normally fond of speaking in class, but this pushed me (in a comfortable way) and it made me gain a deeper insight in the litterature.
courses_enrolled: I attended: Authoritarianism, Global Power Europe, Comparative European Politics and Contemporary German Politics.
recommended_courses: I would recommend: - Authoritarianism: The professor is so knowledgeable and it was great to learn about other regimes than democratic - Global Power Europe: Tomas is amazing! I have never learned this much in such a short time. And he makes topics in the EU interesting :) - Comparative European Politics: This is much more basic and based on litterature that we have learned in DAK. However, it was nice to use my existing knowledge in the classroom, where debates were encouraged. This was not a very challenging course, but it was nice to feel much "at home" in a subject.
unexpected_costs: Restaurants are expensive (but good)! And public transport to outside of London is very expensive aswell.
cost_comparison: Housing: EXPENSIVE Public transport: more expensive Supermarket: less expensive
activities_available: Everything you can imagine.
activities_recommended: I attended the Running Club a few times - that was great
weekend_recommendations: Watch musicals! Eat as much Indian food as possible! Fun destinations - Seven Sisters (small hike, 2 hour train ride from London) - Bath (Roman Baths, 2 hour train ride from London) - Cardiff (Cute at Christmas, 2 hour train ride from London)

cultural_challenges: The quality of housing - the standard is horrible.
culture_appreciated: I loved the English people - they are so kind and welcoming! I loved London as a city - there is always something to do and something to eat! I loved that they took their academic career seriously - it really rubbed off on me!
top3_advice: - Choose accomodation - Be prepared to use quite a bit of money - but enjoy it and save up before! - Try to really engage in the courses and read the literature, it will make your experience much better at King's.

crucial_aspects: I chose London because of personal connections to the city, but also because King's College London is an excellent institution and has a great political science program. It was important to me that the exchange university offered courses that fit my academic profile and King's College did.
info_ease: Very easy. King's College has a very thoruough welcome week and program that offers both academic and social help. They consistently sent emails leading up to arrival.
arrival_assistance: You could get great assistance, if needed. The King's international office relugarly sent out information emails and encouraged students to get in touch, if they had questions.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was a little complicated. You are responsible for choosing courses at the right level (eg. Masters) and for ensuring that they don't overlap. If you're on a certain agreement, you also have to make sure that you fulfill the criteria of that agreement - I had to take 50% of my courses from certain departments for example.
registration_help: There was apowerpoint guide, but it was not very helpful.
registration_success: Fairly successful. I got two (our of four) of the classes that I really wanted and they offer enough different modules, that there were others that I also liked.
registration_advice: Make sure to register for courses on the day that registration opens, so you get the ones you want.
course_level: They were very similar to Copenhagen. The classes were smaller and had more reading for each seminar, so there was more material to go thorugh and you were expected to participate more than in Copenhagen. However, I think they are very comparable institutions.
teaching_comparison: It was similar, but King's required more student participation than Copenhagen. In my experience, it is more often lecture based teaching in Copenhagen and seminar based teaching in the UK.
courses_enrolled: - Religion and Politics in Western Societies - Foreign Policy Analysis - Contemporary Religious Movements - Postcolonial Political Economy
recommended_courses: I would recommend Religion and Politics in Western Societies. It was a great course and really highlighted how much religion still influences politics in the 'secular' west.
unexpected_costs: Nothing really - I had planned everything.
cost_comparison: Transportation was a lot more expensive that I was expecting! London now has the most expensive public transport....
activities_available: Everything you can imagine. Unfortunately the campus did not have space for everything and London is a very large city, so very often activities would take about an hour to get to.
activities_recommended: Join a sports society. They have social teams and it's a good way to make friends.
weekend_recommendations: All the classic tourist sites, the different parks, great shopping, and good train connections to other interesting places in the UK.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, Londoners are very used to different cultures and like meeting people from other places.
socializing_tips: Just be open and try to approach people first.
cultural_challenges: Maybe that so much socialising is centred around drinking here. Important to know that you can go to the pub without drinking alcohol - that's ok!
culture_appreciated: How open and genuinely interested people are in each other. And they're funny
top3_advice: 1. The academic level is high 2. London is huge so be prepared for a long commute in the morning 3. Have fun and make the most of it :)
other_useful_info: King's organise a lot of free talks with very interesting people - make the most of that while you're here!
most_rewarding: Living in London, I think. It's such a beautiful, hectic, cultural and fun city and I have felt very lucky to live here.
greatest_challenge: Living with housemates. No one lives in their own flats here, so you just have to get used to sharing your kitchen and bathroom with 'random' people. It can be challenging but also fun.
