registration_help: I didn't need any help with the process but I believe they both have a support email and number (which is a bit inconvenient with the time difference plus its expensive).
registration_success: I got all of the classes I wanted in the first round.
registration_advice: Follow the emails and 'just' do it step by step.
course_level: You can definitely feel that the university is one of the best in the world. In general are the students really hard working and academically strong. Their grading system is a bit different from ours which means only a few can get the best grade, however, I heard it is difficult to fail your courses.
teaching_comparison: You had less hours in general than back home but otherwise it was pretty similar. I had both lectures and tutorials but not any laboratory hours since I chose courses without.
courses_enrolled: Computational Thinking for Scientist, Organic Synthesis: The Disconnection Approach, Instrumental Analysis II
recommended_courses: I enjoyed computational thinking for scientist which was an introduction to Python. The course was really well put together and I learned a lot, so can definitely recommend that if you are looking to learn some programming. Organic Synthesis: The Disconnection Approach is also a good but difficult course if you are into organic chemistry. I found Instrumental Analysis II boring as it is mainly theoretical analytical chemistry.
unexpected_costs: Housing was way more expensive when you are living off campus compared to living on campus where a meal plan often is included as well.
cost_comparison: Groceries are very expensive in Singapore but it is affordable to eat out at hawker centers and on campus.
activities_available: They do have a wide variety of activities both for the local students and a few specific events for exchange students. However, they seem way less accessible when living off campus. For example is it not possible to join certain sport activities when living off campus. However I enjoyed water polo once pr week and they had an event in the beginning of the semester where you could check out available activities.
activities_recommended: If possible I would definitely recommend joining a sport.
weekend_recommendations: I really enjoyed traveling around the rest of south east asia and can definitely recommend that.
culture_adjustment: I found it quite easy as Singapore is a great city to live in. It is super easy to get around and everyone is super welcoming and helpful.
socializing_tips: Joining a sport or other activities/events.
cultural_challenges: N/A
culture_appreciated: The food is amazing in Singapore so would recommend being open minded and trying new things even though it might look unusual compared to what you are used to.
top3_advice: 1) Look for accommodation in a timely manner (also if you applied for on campus housing) 2) Try all the food 3) Travel!
other_useful_info: Even though I had a lot of fun traveling around South East Asia it was also rewarding to explore Singapore and using the amazing city it is.
most_rewarding: Exploring both the city and the rest of South East Asia.
greatest_challenge: The housing situation.

crucial_aspects: Det var vigtigt for mig at det var et engelsktalende land. Desuden så jeg Singapore som en mulighed for at afprøve min faglighed i en ny social og kulturel kontekst.
info_ease: Det var skidt fra KU's side. Fra National University of Singapores (NUS) side var virkelig nemt at finde information. Faktisk blev alt leveret til mailboksen lige før man skulle bruge den. De underrettede om deadlines der skulle overholdes og sendte 'how to' mindmaps i videoer om alt fra hvordan man søger kurser til hvordan man søger visum.
arrival_assistance: NUS anbefaler at man ankommer en uge før undervisningen starter. Her er der forskellige frivillige introduktionsforløb forberedt til alle udvekslingsstuderende.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Jeg husker ansøgningsprocessen som virkelig lang og at jeg hele tiden var bekymret for at have misset noget.
registration_help: NUS tog en meget i hånden. Det mindede en om deadlines og sendte fine guides. Det var jeg selv virkelig glad for de gjorde, da processen var meget lang og jeg hele tiden var bekymret for at have misse noget. Desuden svarer de på deres e-mails indenfor 24 timer. Så hvis der endelig er noget, kan man altid skrive til dem.
registration_success: Jeg kunne kun tage BA fag. Men udvalget var egentlig fint. Jeg endte med at få de kurser jeg ønskede mig.
registration_advice: Lad være at misse deadlines.
course_level: Niveauet var lavere end på KU. Der var næsten slet ikke noget pensum og man blev taget meget i hånden i undervisningen. Jeg tror bedst de kan sammenlignes med at gå i gymnasiet igen, dog med mere specialiseret undervisning.
teaching_comparison: Det var ret anderledes. Ikke så meget forelæsningerne, men hvordan man skulle lære og hvordan man blev bedømt, var anderledes. Der blev f.eks. målt fravær, hvilket havde betydning for end endelige karakter i kurset. Desuden var der en del opgaver undervejs i stedet for en eksamen til sidst (men dette varierer fra kursus til kursus).
courses_enrolled: Digital Ehtics and Data Privacy Public Health in Action Public Health Nutrition Introduction to Public Health Communication
recommended_courses: Public Health Nutrition synes jeg var ret sjovt. Man lærer en del om hvilke kost og ernæringsmæssige sundhedsproblemer der typisk er for forskellige alders-, socioøkonomiske og etniske grupper.
unexpected_costs: Jeg måtte købe en del mere til værelset end forventet, hvilket ikke var et problem, men det blev dyrere end forventet (også fordi alt er super dyrt i Singapore)
cost_comparison: Selvom mad er billigt (ca. 35 kr. per måltid på hawker-centre), så endte jeg med at bruge helt vildt mange penge på mad.
activities_available: Der er klubber virkelig mange forskellige klubber - både de mere traditionelle såsom fodbold, badminton, musik, brætspil osv., men der er også mange klubber man ikke lige ser på KU. F.eks. en dykkerklub og en klub der fodrede kattene på campus. Campus havde desuden alle tænkelige sportsfaciliteter, som man frit kunne bruge (nogle gange kostede det lidt. F.eks. kostede det 4 mennesker 5dkk at spille tennis).
activities_recommended: Bare deltag i alt du kan overskue. Jeg dyrkede selv alverdens forskellige sportsgrene, også en del jeg ikke havde prøvet før. Det var virkelig fedt hvordan campus lagde op til, at man var aktiv.
weekend_recommendations: Du kan nå at se det hele. Tag dig tiden til at få det gjort. Singapore er et virkelig fedt sted generelt - ikke kun ved marinaen.
culture_adjustment: Det var let på den måde, at Singapore i forvejen er meget multikulturelt, hvorfor man ikke føler sig som fremmed eller anderledes pga. kultur. Til gengæld er det virkelig svært at forstå Singlish, så det giver lidt af en barriere.
socializing_tips: Jeg faldt primært i snak med lokale studerende gennem min hall. Derfor er mit tip at ansøge om on campus housing. Desuden spillede jeg fodbold udenfor campus, hvilket gjorde at jeg fik en del venner som både var i arbejde, lokale studerende fra mit eget universitet og fra andre universiteter.
cultural_challenges: En udfordring var at begå sig i race-diskussioner – mest i faglige sammenhænge, men der var også ikke faglige sammenhænge. Der blev snakket en del om racer i mine studiegrupper i forbindelse med undervisningen, men også på mit fodboldhold. Det var aldrig en negativt ladet eller intent og ubehagelig samtale, men det var svært at følge med, da raceterminologien er så socialt defineret.
culture_appreciated: At alle bliver accepteret.
top3_advice: Nyd det.
other_useful_info: Medbring lange bukser. Der er virkelig koldt i forelæsningslokalerne.
most_rewarding: De mennesker jeg mødte.
greatest_challenge: At acceptere at jeg ikke kunne nå at deltage i alt jeg gerne ville.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville til et land der var engelsktalende, men hvor kulturen IKKE kun var vestlig præget. Derfor var Singapore en oplagt mulighed, da det er en mixture af mange forskellige kulturer fra øst og vest.
info_ease: Fra KU's side, synes jeg godt nok det var svært at få hjælp. Jeg skrev flere gange til dem uden at få hjælp og endte med at møde fysisk op (hvilket jeg ellers havde fået af vide at jeg ikke måtte) for at få svar. Fra National University of Singapores (NUS) side var det dog en helt anden sag. De var vildt gode til at sende e-mails hele tiden og underrettede om deadlines der skulle overholdes og særlig information, som jeg skulle være opmærksom på når jeg ankom.
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik ikke så meget assistance, men det var også fordi, at jeg kom dagen inden undervisningen startede. NUS anbefalede at man ankom en uge før undervisningen startede, fordi der var lidt forskellige introduktionsforløb. Disse var dog frivillige og jeg sprang dem over. Dog tror jeg det havde været en god ide at deltage i dem, da de andre udvekslingsstuderende virkede til at have fået meget ud af den assistance, som de havde fået.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Den var lang og med mange steps og derfor kan jeg ikke huske den præcis. Jeg har i nedenstående en guide til det (den er lavet en lille smule om siden jeg søgte, men overordnet er den det samme):
registration_help: NUS er meget gode og hurtige til at svare når man række ud til dem på deres mail. Det er rigtig godt!
registration_success: Jeg havde 7 fag jeg gerne ville have og fik 4 af dem, så jeg er godt tilfreds.
registration_advice: Hvis der er noget man ikke forstår så ræk ud til NUS. De er virkelig gode til at hjælp igennem med processen, der hvor det virker uoverskueligt.
course_level: Som FSV studerende kunne vi kun tage BA fag, så derfor var der en del, som jeg allerede vidste. Det var tydeligt, at de ikke selv har en BA som specialiserer sig i FSV, og derfor var det til tider også ret let (selv for en BA studerende på KU).
teaching_comparison: Det var meget anderledes. Man bliver bedømt meget mere under vejs med en masse afleveringer, test og bedømmelser af ens medstuderende og/eller underviser. Der var også mange flere fremlæggelser sammenlignet med på KU. På mange måder mindede det ret meget om at være tilbage i gymnasiet En anden stor forskel er at man hele tiden under semesterret bliver vurderet, og at alt hvad man laver tæller mod ens samlede karakter. Det kan godt være lidt belastende, at skulle være på hele tiden, men omvendt er det meget rart når man kommer til eksamensdagene, at selve prøverne kun tæller 40-60% af ens karakter.
courses_enrolled: Digital Ehtics and Data Privacy Systems and Policies to Improve Health Public Health Nutrition Introduction to Public Health Communication
recommended_courses: Jeg synes særligt at Systems and Policies to Improve Health var et godt fag. På mange måder mindede 'Sundhedsvæsenets struktur og funktion', som jeg havde på min BA, men dette var en en helt anden kontekst. Det gav mit et fedt indblik i, hvordan sundhedsvæsener er forskelligt opbygget og hvordan de har forskellige omfang og prioriteter. Derudover lærte jeg meget om, hvor meget sundhed som WHO anbefaler faktisk ofte ikke nødvendigvis passer ned i alle salags kulturer, men at anbefalingerne herimod bærer præg af at de er meget vestligt influeret.
unexpected_costs: Der er utroligt mange fede sportsfaciliteter til rådighed, så hvis man gerne vil bruge dem men ikke har taget udstyr med, så må man jo købe. Jeg endte bl.a. med at købe måde tøj og udstyr til fodbold, badminton og svømning.
cost_comparison: At købe mad ude er billigere end jeg troede, mens det er ret dyrt at handle ind selv. Derfor giver det ikke fra et økonomisk synspunkt nogen som helt mening at lave mad selv. Derudover er priserne ret meget som i Danmark.
activities_available: Der er klubber for alt hvad man kan forestille sig, som både kan være de mere traditionelle såsom fodbold, badminton, musik, acapella, brætspil osv., men der er også mange lidt spøjse klubber som er formet af de studerende. Fx var der en klub der tog rundt og fodrede katte på campus og en kirkeklub. Hvad angår faciliteter var de også i top. Der var alle tænkelige sportsfaciliteter på campus, som man (i dagstimerne) kunne bruge frit eller mod et symbolsk beløb (fx 5dkk). Stedet lagde op til en aktiv hverdag, hvilket der også var mange (inklusiv mig selv) der gjorde brug af
activities_recommended: Alt hvad man kan overskue. Det er en vildt fed mulighed for at møde andre mennesker. Jeg blev særligt glad for badmintonklubben.
weekend_recommendations: Singapore er på mange måder en kompakt by, hvor der er masser at se. Hvis man har en hel uge vil jeg tage ud af Singapore, men på weekender er der masser at lave. To gode bud er Chinatown og Gardens By the Bay, som jeg besøgte mange gange. Derudover har de mange parker og naturområder man kan gå mange ture i.
culture_adjustment: Der var både lette og svære elementer af at tilpasse sig til Singapore. Men det fede ved Singapore er, at de er så vant til at der kommer 'fremmede', så man bliver mødt med gode intentioner. Derudover omgås man rigtig mange andre udvekslingsstuderende, så det bliver hurtigt meget multikulturelt, hvor der er plads til alle Noget af det sværeste for mig har nok været at vænne sig til at spise varm mad 3 gange i døgnet, hvilket godt kan være ret kvalm hvis det er meget varmt udenfor.
socializing_tips: De lokale studenter jeg faldt i snak med var enten fra min collage eller gennem min undervisning. Der er rigtig mange som spiser frokost sammen, så det er altid let at spørge, om man skal tage en bid mad sammen. Det er nok den nemmeste måde at falde i snak med dem.
cultural_challenges: Jeg ved ikke om det var svært at lade være med, men en af de ting man skal være opmærksomme på er at det ikke er kutymen med kropskontakt – særligt med det modsatte køn. Jeg kom i en lidt akavet situation, hvor jeg en af de første uger, af ren dansk vane, kom til at kramme en af det modsatte køn da vi sagde farvel. Det er ikke rigtig noget man gør sig i i Singapore. Der skete ikke noget, men jeg snakkede med nogle lokale senere om det, som sagde at det gjorde de ikke i Singapore. Så for fremtiden stod den bare på vink når man siger både hej og farvel.
culture_appreciated: Jeg synes det var vildt fedt at samfundet er så multikulturelt at det virker som om alle er velkomne og imødekommende over for forskelligheder. Det kom bl.a. til udtryk ved at alle i landet fejre bådejul, nytår, kinesisk nytår, Eid, og andre mere eller mindre religiøse dage.
top3_advice: 1. Gør alt hvad du kan for at få on campus accommodation! Det sparer penge tid og giver mange muligheder 2. Meld dig ind i nogle af de mange grupper der er på Campus. Det er en fed måde at få nye venner 3. Vær åben mod at få dit vestlige verdenssyn udfordret. Det leder til vildt mange utroligt spændende samtaler. Bare sørg for at holde det respektfuldt.
other_useful_info: Selvom det er vildt varmt dernede så tag nogle bukser og trøjer med for alt indendørs foregår med en air conditioner som smækker temperaturen helt ned på 17-18 grader.
most_rewarding: Alle de mennesker fra vidt forskellige kulturer og med meget forskellige verdenssyn, som jeg fik lov til at blive venner med. Det har lært mig meget om, hvordan andre samfund fungerer og at vi måske ikke nødvendigvis altid er de bedste på alle parametre i vores lille del af verdenen.
greatest_challenge: Den største udfordring var at de har en meget anden måde at undervise på, hvorfor man skal vænne sig til den stil.

crucial_aspects: The availability of courses related to my field of studies. The new network, job, and academic opportunities are relations that the destination could offer for my future personal and professional carrier
overall_comments: I rated 8, because of course the exchange experience was great and gave me the opportunity to dive into a new culture, create new relations, and meet many great and interesting people. But the process was very difficult to carry out, and i didn't receive any guidance both from home and host university. In addition, most of the courses that i applied to weren't open to exchange students and this was notified only when i already applied for my exchange so i couldn't change my priorities.
info_ease: Not very easy, as we were told to have an orientation week (during the first week of august), but that was never held - so it make it very challenging to find all the information ie: finding classrooms, getting your way around campus, understanding how everything works.
arrival_assistance: emails from host university. some events, but very difficult to get a spot as we were a lot of exchangers.
arrival_comments: the orientation week did not take place
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I rated 8, because of course the exchange experience was great and gave me the opportunity to dive into a new culture, create new relations, and meet many great and interesting people. But the process was very difficult to carry out, and i didn't receive any guidance both from home and host university. In addition, most of the courses that i applied to weren't open to exchange students and this was notified only when i already applied for my exchange so i couldn't change my priorities.
registration_process: A list of courses open to exchange students is available. You can choose a minimum of 3 courses up to a maximum of 5. The 1000 to 4000 levels are bachelor's and the 5000 level is master's. You apply on the portal and for most courses you need to fill out a form to prove you are eligible for the course.
registration_help: course registration guide. and ask for help from other students.
registration_success: I was able to secure two courses I wanted ( out of 3) and for one I had to compromise. But I had to go through the registrar's office several times to secure master's level courses.
registration_advice: Look at the list of courses open for exchange students in advance, before applying to the host university. For master students, NUS is not ideal as the courses at the master level are not available, and you have to compromise with some undergrad courses.
academics_comments: I rated 8, because of course the exchange experience was great and gave me the opportunity to dive into a new culture, create new relations, and meet many great and interesting people. But the process was very difficult to carry out, and i didn't receive any guidance both from home and host university. In addition, most of the courses that i applied to weren't open to exchange students and this was notified only when i already applied for my exchange so i couldn't change my priorities.
course_level: The level of the courses was similar to KU, but the approach is very different. NUS use mostly continuous assessment as a way of assessing student, so you have a lot of hand-in, paper, and quizzes to carry out throughout the course - that can be challenging at first if you are not used to that.
teaching_comparison: NUS use mostly continuous assessment as a way of assessing student, so you have a lot of hand-in, paper, and quizzes to carry out throughout the course - that can be challenging at first if you are not used to that.
courses_enrolled: Majorities and minorities in SE Asia (BA) Food product development and packaging (BA) Global Food Policy and Sustainable Food System (MA)
recommended_courses: Majorities and minorities in SE Asia (BA) --> I would recommend this course if you want to have a better overview of SE Asia's culture and political situation. Is a seminar base course, meaning that the lecture is very brief and most of the class is a discussion on the readings you have to prepare at home Food product development and packaging (BA) --> I would recommend this course to undergrad students in food science as is a very nice hands-on course, where you get to develop a food product and packaging in collaboration start-up from scratch. (Include lab practice) Global Food Policy and Sustainable Food System (MA) I would recommend this course to master students interested in food policies and research methods in the field of food systems. Very nice course the one that was most related to my studies.
unexpected_costs: transportation
cost_comparison: food in hawker centers and the uni canteen is very cheap. food in supermarkets is quite expensive.
activities_available: any type of sports, and a lot of cultural events
activities_recommended: sports clubs, help you make friends with full-time students
weekend_recommendations: travel around Singapore and around SE asia
culture_adjustment: Yes
socializing_tips: be open and go talk to them
cultural_challenges: didn't find any
culture_appreciated: The food culture is very nice and diverse.
top3_advice: raincoat, flipflops, and mosquito repellent
other_useful_info: no
most_rewarding: The people i've met and the network that it allowed me to create. and the travels opportunities
greatest_challenge: Adjust to the commuting lifestyle of a metropolis like Singapore, at least 2 hours of subway rides per day :)))
other_comments: a bit challenging with the bureaucratic issues (application, course registration, visa), but DEFINITELY worth it! I would recommend it to anyone

crucial_aspects: Good academic record of university, nice climate, great travel opportunities.
info_ease: The information was easy to find and send well ahead of time. Only negative was that it was spread over a lot of emails.
arrival_assistance: None, an online walk through was made available to us.
arrival_comments: Missed some form of in person intro upon arrival.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Took place through their online portal, and was pretty self-explanatory. Emails with descriptions on how to fill out the different forms were provided.
registration_help: The university's exchange office was available for help over email if needed.
registration_success: It was very difficult to secure courses. Got my 1st, 3rd, and 7th priority out of 8 courses selected.
registration_advice: Start all the registration early as soon as information is provided to you, and check your email frequently as some of the deadlines are very short.
course_level: The math courses are in general harder than what I have had at KU, while the programming courses were at a comparable level.
teaching_comparison: A lot of content, and labs where the tutors just went through the problem sets. Not so much time to do exercises on your own with supervision.
courses_enrolled: Programming methodology 1 and 2 and introduction to business analytics.
recommended_courses: Really liked programing methodology 2 that dealt a lot with good code design.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Food is quite cheap when you eat out, but groceries are quite pricy
activities_available: Everything you can imagine
activities_recommended: Board game cafe and floor ball team
weekend_recommendations: Go to Malaysia, Japan or Korea
culture_adjustment: Very easy, everyone are friendly and speaks English well.
socializing_tips: Join one of the social clubs or sports clubs. Is a great way to meet local students.
cultural_challenges: NA
culture_appreciated: The food culture, and all the delicious food you can get very cheap at the hawker centers.
top3_advice: Get campus housing, choose a mix of hard and easier courses and join some form of club.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: I joined a board game club while I was there and made a lot of local friends by doing so. Consider getting a bike to explore the city.
greatest_challenge: Took some time to understand the Singlish they speak (Singapore slang).

crucial_aspects: That the university was of high standard, and that it was an interesting country where lots of people and cultures meet.
info_ease: Most but not all information was provided by UCPH. In general, this wasn't a problem.
arrival_assistance: Not much at all. We received information prior to going, but once we arrived, we had to figure most out ourselves.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You pick courses prior to going. Once you arrive, you book a time slot for vaccination registration and student card collection. This is very easy.
registration_help: Email correspondence with the host.
registration_success: I managed to get two thirds of the applied courses in the first round of application.
registration_advice: Be careful with choosing high level courses. High level courses are a lot more difficult and require a lot more work at the host than at UCPH.
course_level: Expect a course to be more difficult at the host than if you would choose it at UCPH. Eg. a 3rd year course at the host would be similar to a 2nd year course at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: A closer relationship to the lecturer. A bit more emphasis on assignments than lectures.
courses_enrolled: Calculus for Computing Introduction to Computational Biology Optimisation Algorithms
recommended_courses: Optimisation Algorithms was a very exciting course but also difficult. Choose this if you are familiar with Kattis and have a strong profile in Algorithms and Data Structures. You should be proficient in C++. Be careful with choosing this course. It caught me by surprise how difficult it was.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Dining out is less expensive eg. canteens.
activities_available: A lot of student clubs and you meet a lot of other people of different cultures in the classes.
activities_recommended: Hiking. There are a lot of cool places to hike eg. Sungei Buloh. Flights out are also cheap, which makes travel to nearby countries less expensive.
weekend_recommendations: Travel to other countries or explore the hiking opportunities.
culture_adjustment: It was fairly easy.
socializing_tips: Go and talk to whoever you think is interesting. Everyone is open minded and ready to go out.
cultural_challenges: The laws within the country are strict. Public transportation within the country is not available at night.
culture_appreciated: The culture of Hawker centers.
top3_advice: Make sure you have your insurance in order. Be careful when choosing courses. They are most likely more difficult than you think. At least for CS courses. Find accommodation early on and don't rely on the host to find you housing.
other_useful_info: The things mentioned above.
most_rewarding: All the people I met and friendships I have gotten. If you wish, you can form friendships with people from all over the world.
greatest_challenge: The academic part and the homesickness.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to an English spoken country outside of Europe. NUS is a highly ranked university in Asia with acknowledged and dedicated professors. Furthermore, I wanted to go to a place with higher temperatures than what we know of in Denmark. And most importantly, Singapore is a great place to travel from - you can easily buy cheap tickets to get to other destinations in Asia, also during the semester.
info_ease: It was easy to find the information you needed upon arrival. KU was very helpful to answer whatever questions you may have.
arrival_assistance: We got a lot of emails telling us what we needed to do, including making appointments for visa, module registration etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You get a lot of emails telling you what to do and what deadlines you should be aware of. In addition, the staff at NUS also responded quickly to emails.
registration_help: Email correspondance.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: I was really happy for only having three classes; 4 credits, 5 credits and 8 credits. Though one of the classes was really intensive, having only three courses made it possible for me to travel a lot during the semester.
teaching_comparison: They expect you to be prepared for classes, and participate in the discussions. There are many courses where you have to prepare at least one presentation for the class, and your participation in general is also a part of your final grade. However, I didn't have the feeling that the professors where cold calling students.
courses_enrolled: World Trade Law, 8 credits International Investment Law, 4 credits International Law and Asia, 5 credits
recommended_courses: I would recommend all my courses. WTL is really intensive, and the professor expects a lot from you. The workload is way more than what I have experienced in Copenhagen which is why I never did all the reading. If you just show up for class and familiarize yourself with the judgments, it will be okay but you should be aware that the reading is insane. International Investment Law is the best course I have ever had, including the professor. Even though the course was only for three weeks, the professor took time to learn all the students names and it was contagious from how passionated he was about the subject. It was a really interesting course! International Law and Asia was kind of boring, and you didn't have to show up to classes since the examination is a written assignment where you choose your own topic. Choosing this course makes it possible to travel some more.
unexpected_costs: I was hoping to get an on campus housing because that would have been much cheaper than having to rent a room. Alcohol was also really expensive.
cost_comparison: Buying groceries from supermarkets was really expensive which is why I almost didn't cook dinner. It was, however, possible to buy cheap food at hawker centre.
activities_available: All sports you can imagine like handball, football, tennis, volleyball, water polo crossfit, board games etc.
activities_recommended: I tried water polo, tennis and volleyball which was a success.
weekend_recommendations: Travel! You can easily buy cheap flight tickets going to Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia, South Korea etc., and it often does not take long to get to these places.
culture_adjustment: It was really easy. Singapore is a multicultural country where you can meet all kinds of cultures. Just be open minded and get involved in the different cultures.
socializing_tips: Join some different clubs and participate in the events that are arranged.
cultural_challenges: None.
top3_advice: 1. You have to look for housing in a good time, since you are not guaranteed to get offered on campus housing. 2. Lower your expectations of your own professionel performance. You just have to pass the courses so don't spend too much time on the reading. 3. Go travel. Asia is amazing! And as soon as you get out of Singapore everything is much cheaper.
most_rewarding: The possibility to travel to other countries during the semester.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville rigtig gerne langt væk og til et varmt sted. Jeg gad rigtig godt til Asien og Singapore var perfekt fordi de snakker engelsk.
info_ease: Jeg synes det var okay nemt. Der var dog slet ingen intro fra universitets side, så man skulle meget finde ud af det selv. Men da alt er på engelsk og ok overskueligt så fandt jeg ud af det.
arrival_assistance: Ingen. Jeg meldte mig til et buddy program, hvor man fik tildelt en lokal studerende som guide, men personen svarede mig aldrig.
arrival_comments: Jeg synes det var meget dårligt at der slet ikke var nogen intro for udvekslingsstuderende. Der var nogle få arrangementer, som var begrænset tilmelding så jeg nåede ikke at melde mig til nogen af dem. Vi kunne godt have fået bare en mail med nogle oplysninger.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Vi skulle søge fag ret sent og jeg havde søgt 8 muligheder med fik kun 2. Man skal have mindst 3 for at blive optaget. Dette gjorde at jeg skulle søge i en anden runde og derfor ikke kunne nå at søge 1. runde housing fordi jeg ikke var officielt optaget endnu.
registration_help: Jeg fik kun hjælp af de andre udvekslingstuderende som vi have en facebook gruppe med.
registration_success: Ikke særlig succesfuld. Jeg endte med kun at få et relevant fag for min uddannelse. Men er glad for de fag jeg endte med.
registration_advice: Der er ikke så meget at gøre hvis man ikke får de fag man vil. Så må man bare søge noget andet:)
course_level: Jeg havde 1 rigtigt computer science course som var level 3000. Det var lidt sværere end jeg troede men meget spændende. Var en blanding af emnerne fra AD (2. års bachelorkusus) og AAD (kandidat kursus). De lokale studerende var ret dygtige, så niveaut på opgaverne og eksaminerne var meget højt. Mine to andre fag var level 1000 og det var skønt. Jeg startede faktisk med at have et level 2000 matematik kursus om linear algenbra og det var så svært! Så det droppede jeg ud af og skiftede til Computational thinking for Scientists som basically var Python programmering for begyndere og det var meget hyggeligt.
teaching_comparison: Jeg synes faktisk det mindede meget om. Vi havde forelæsninger og øvelsestimer og ugentlig afleveringer. Lærerne opfordrer ikke til udenadslære, men at man skal tænke selv og problemløse på samme måde som i DK. Men de studerende er ret meget mere ambitiøse, så de lærer det udenad alligevel.
courses_enrolled: Design and Analysis of Algorithms Computational thinking for Scientists South Asia in Singapore
recommended_courses: South Asia in Singapore eller nogle af de andre kurser der omhandler Singapores historie og kultur. Kæmpe anbefaling og sjovt at lave noget andet end ens normale uddannelse.
unexpected_costs: Havde ikke forstillet mig at jeg skulle betale så meget i husleje. Det var ekstremt dyrt. Brugte en del penge på at rejse og opleve ting, men det have jeg forventet og prioritetet.
cost_comparison: Det er ret dyrt at købe ind i supermarkedet så jeg lavede faktisk slet ikke mad selv. Til gengæld er det billigt at spise på hawker centre og der er også god og billig mad på skolen. Fly-, bus- og bådbilletter til de omkringliggende lande er billige.
activities_available: Jeg gik til vandpolo fordi jeg ikke måtte gå til svømning fordi jeg ikke boede på et hall.
activities_recommended: Tag til sådan en sports og klubmesse der er i begyndelsen for så får du alt information om alle mulighederne.
weekend_recommendations: Hvis man ikke vil flyve så meget og passe lidt på miljøet:) så kan man tage bussen til Malyasia i et par timer eller båden til Indonesien, Men ellers er der bare mange dejlige lande omkring hvor man kan flyve til for under 1000 kr. Der er faktisk også ret mange ting at lave i Singapore når man nu har god tid til at udforske det.
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Singapore at er så multikulturelt at ingen kigger to gange på en i metroen fx. Det var virkelig fedt at man bare blendede så meget ind i forhold til andre asiatiske lande. Alt var på engelsk så det var også nemt at snakke med folk og forstå var der skete omkring en.
socializing_tips: De er super søde og vil gerne snakke.
cultural_challenges: Hmm ikke rigtig noget.
culture_appreciated: At der var plads til alle.
top3_advice: 1. Kom ud og oplev Singapore. Også bare gå nogle ture alene. 2. Du kommer nok til at have mere fritid end du er vant til fordi du ikke har lige så meget skole og mange venner og arbejde, så få en hobby 3. Hav en plan B hvis du ikke får on-campus housing
other_useful_info: Vær ikke bange for at prøve alt det forskellige mad der er på alle hawker centrene.
most_rewarding: Helt klart at have prøvet at leve i længere tid i et land så langt væk og få set en masse asiatisk kultur. Jeg var på 5 rejse undervejs og rejste videre i 2 måneder i Asien efter skolen sluttede og det var så skønt! Og at det var varmt hele tiden!
greatest_challenge: Jeg tog afsted uden at kende nogen som helst så var meget nervøs for det, men har fået nogle rigtig gode venner! Bare vær lidt mere åben end herhjemme
other_comments: Vil helt klart anbefale at tage afsted!

crucial_aspects: The courses offered and the reputation of the host university. And the oppertunity to live in a business hub such as Singapore.
info_ease: Slightly difficult - nothing out of the ordinary, but the many deadlines and a lot of different portals made me struggle a lot in the proces.
arrival_assistance: They were always very quick on e-mail and helped very confused exchange students A LOT.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: A lot of different portals and registration through different means.
registration_help: Email always and a lot of folders with additional information.
registration_success: Mostly successful.
registration_advice: Stay calm.
course_level: Very, very high! But easy to follow if you paid attention.
teaching_comparison: So interesting. A lot more interaction and discussions enabled by the fact that everyone showed up incredibly well prepared and the level of prestige of the professors.
courses_enrolled: Climate change law, energy arbitration, maritime law, international commercial arbitration
recommended_courses: All of them. Except maritime law if youre not very interested in ship collisions and general average calculations...
unexpected_costs: Additional fees for registrating at the university
cost_comparison: Food was very inexpensive, but you always, always eat out since noone ever really cooks in singapore so it adds up. Note the majority of your budget will go directly to travelling.
activities_available: A lot of clubs you could sign up for and i got very very into squash and sports facilities.
activities_recommended: Use all the sports options. There are clubs for it all and very lovely free gyms.
weekend_recommendations: All of south east asia - as much as possible. Especially Ha Jang Loop on motorbike in Vietnam and learning how to scooba dive (and then going to philipines, indonesia etc. for that)
culture_adjustment: Very easy!
socializing_tips: Join clubs and talk in class
cultural_challenges: none
culture_appreciated: Safety. Singapore is so safe. And the focus on academic excellence.
top3_advice: 1) Travel a lot, 2) pick courses you really care about cause it can really spearhead your career 3) make sure to live in dorms thats where you get the most friends
other_useful_info: Take weeks / months off afterwards for travelling.
most_rewarding: Travelling and friends.
greatest_challenge: A LOT of new people all at once. And a lot of "slef organised" exchange events by other exchange students, so stay on your feet and try to meet everyone in the first few weeks (that was stressful)

crucial_aspects: At det var en meget forskellig kultur fra Danmark, at de snakkede engelsk og at man kunne rejse mange forskellige steder hen
info_ease: Ret let: NUS sendte meget info på mail, med gode guides osv. Der var lidt forvirring omkring fag, men det var super let at finde ud af op til semesterstart
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik hurtigt et netværk af andre udvekslingsstuderende, og sammen fandt man ud af det hele med housing, semesterstart osv. Generelt var det ret let at finde ud af, da alt info på universitets hjemmeside var på engelsk. De sendte også massere af info på mail. Efter et par uger fik vi tildelt en 'buddy' fra universitetet. De var også søde til at hjælp, dog havde man ikke brug for så meget hjælp mere der, da man havde fundet ud af det meste. Der var også arrangeret et par events for udvekslingsstuderende og lokale lige da man kom, hvor man kunne få hjælp. De lokale man boede var også meget søde til at hjælpe, dog var mange af dem selv nye studerende
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Man søger nogle fag, når man søger ind på universitet. Her fik de fleste 3 eller 2 fag, nogle enkelte fik kun et enkelt. Resten af ens fag søger man først ved semesterstart i en runde to. I runde tre melder man sig til tutorials og kan igen droppe/søge nye fag.
registration_help: Jeg brugte den guide universitet sendte. Den var super, og det var let finde ud af.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag jeg ønskede
registration_advice: Man skal ikke stresse over, at man ikke får så mange fag i første omgang, da det er super fleksibelt med flere runder. Hvis man vil være sikker på at få fag i anden eller tredje runde, kan man også skrive til professorene, så spærrer de en plads til en. Generelt var det meget få der havde store problemer med at få de fag de gerne ville have.
course_level: Niveauet var ikke specielt højt: Der blev stillet færre krav til at man skulle tænke kreativt for at løse opgaver. De lokale læste ekstremt meget, men alligevel havde man ingen problemer med at følge med, og var meget på samme niveau.
teaching_comparison: Der var en del obligatoriske ting i løbet af semesteret: Midterms, afleveringer, tutorials og fremlæggelser ud over selve eksamen. Alle tingene talte en vis procentdel af den samlede karakter. Det var rimelig overskuelig, og også fedt, at man vidste at man var bestået sine fag inden den endelige eksamen. Det faglige var der noget mere fokus på resultat, samt matematikken noget mere simpel end man er vant til herhjemme.
courses_enrolled: Urban Economics, Financial Economics, Game Theory og International Trade
recommended_courses: Urban Economics; Man lærte rigtig meget om Singapore, og mange af hvordan dets institutioner er bygget op. Udover det var professoren virkelig dygtig
unexpected_costs: Jeg rejste en del (5 turer i løbet af semesteret), hvorfor min personal spending var høj.
cost_comparison: Mad var virkelig billigt! Derudover havde jeg mad på campus for 900 kr om måneden, som bestemt var billigt.
activities_available: Der var et mega bredt udvalg af klubber, sportsgrene og societies og derudover virkelig gode faciliteter. Der var et kæmpe sportscenter, flere pools på campus og fede gyms. Der var også en 'by' på campus med cafeer, butikker og food courts, hvor der var rigtig meget liv. Jeg kunne enten tage til interest groups via mit college, hvor jeg boede. Her var det meget hyggeligt og uforpligtende, og jeg var fx til klatring, DIY-workshops, fodbold og håndbold. Man kunne også være på universitetshold, hvor der var noget af det der var mere konkurrenceagtigt (fx fodbold), og man skulle forpligte sig til træning et par gange om ugen, men også mere hygge-ting, som var uforpligtende.
activities_recommended: Deltag i mange af de fede aktiviteter og vær med i en klub enten noget sport eller en interesse!
weekend_recommendations: Tag ud og rejs! Jeg rejste selv rigtig meget, og det var klart en stor del af min udveksling
culture_adjustment: Den lokale kultur var mere anderledes end jeg havde forestillet mig. Dog hjalp det rigtig meget at bo med lokale, samt at alle snakkede engelsk. Så selvom det var anderledes, var det rigtig sjovt at møde så meget nyt
socializing_tips: Bare vær åben! De lokale er rigtig imødekomne, og synes det virkelig sjovt at snakke med udvekslingsstuderende! Jeg synes helt sikkert det var lettest at connecte med dem jeg boede med frem for dem jeg havde fag med!
cultural_challenges: At de snakkede 'Singlish', hvilket godt kunne være lidt svært at forstå. Dem man boede på uni med var også ret unge (pigerne var 19 eller 20 år) og generelt ret umodne. De havde aldrig rigtigt prøvet at date, tage ud og var generelt meget skoleminded, hvorfor de ikke havde oplevet så meget udenfor Singapore. Derfor var de bare ret umodne, men de var rigtig søde
culture_appreciated: Drukkulturen var meget anderledes. Det var meget fedt at se en helt anden unikultur, hvor de fleste slet ikke drak. Men de hyggede sig stadig rigtig meget, og lavede mange andre fede ting. De gik fx. vildt meget op i deres foreninger og sportsgrene (og skole!!), så det var fedt, at se uni på den måde.
top3_advice: 1. Tag ud og rejs en masse! 2. Forsøg at få housing på campus og deltag i en masse foreninger 3. Selvom det er varmt bliver du glad for at pakke et par varme trøje og lange bukser: De er sindssygt glade for aircon, og næsten alt (shopping, restauranter, undervisning) foregår indenfor
other_useful_info: Du behøver ikke pakke reg
most_rewarding: Alle de rejser jeg kom på
greatest_challenge: Vejret: Varmen og fugtigheden var lidt svær at overkomme nogen gang. Selvom det selvfølgelig også var noget af det bedste at det var sp varmt!

crucial_aspects: To see and explore the world from a new perspective
info_ease: Quite difficult. Many things were unclear
arrival_assistance: None, as I recall
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Overall quite easy although there were a lot of things to have in mind and a lot of deadlines to remember.
registration_help: Only emails
registration_success: Not very succesful. I had to apply in the second round to secure my modules
registration_advice: It will all work out in the end, be patient and do not stress about it. Many of the other students only secured their final modules in the days leading up to semester start.
course_level: The level on the courses were satisfying and not too high
teaching_comparison: It was not as stressful to be in the lectures. But NUS also has way less class teaching so it is very much up to yourself to make sure that you are up to date with all the topics
courses_enrolled: LSM3210 Metabolism & Regulation, LSM3211 Fundamental Pharmacology, LSM3223 Immunology
recommended_courses: Immunology because the module was built up in a very good way and the teachers were amazing. Fundamental Pharmacology was difficult but very useful.
unexpected_costs: I think none
cost_comparison: Food is very cheap if you buy it from so-called hawker stalls (food courts) like 25 DKK for dinner. Alcohol is very expensive, so buy something from the airport
activities_available: There were all sorts of things available. Sports, DIY clubs, dancing and so many events.
activities_recommended: Try out new sports! Many of the local students also join sports which they have never played before. It is a fun way to meet new people and try out something new and fun
weekend_recommendations: Fly abroad. Singapore is a perfect destination to go explore the rest of Southeast Asia! Flights are not that expensive either.
culture_adjustment: It required some adjustment but was not that difficult.
socializing_tips: Join clubs and sports.
cultural_challenges: Maybe understanding some of the locals since they speak kind of "Singlish"
culture_appreciated: Laid back-relaxed mindset. I expected everything to be very harsh and punctual but it is a less stressful way of living compared to Europe.
top3_advice: It is going to be very hot and rains quite often but it is an amazing city to live in. The campus is a bit outside of the city but has everything a campus life needs.
other_useful_info: Campus has 3 pools - very nice! One of them is an infinity pool!
most_rewarding: Meeting new cultures and being able to take care of myself
greatest_challenge: Missing friends and family. The time difference was also challenging.

crucial_aspects: Going to Asia. Singapore is a perfect place to explore the surrounding countries as the flights are cheap and you can travel a lot.
info_ease: It was quite chaotic arriving in Singapore. There are a lot of formalities that you need to do within the first couple of weeks and everybody was stressing out about it. Be sure to check all the e-mails NUS send you, book appointments dates as soon as possible and be sure to show up :D
arrival_assistance: Not a lot. Only e-mails. There were different whatsapp groups with other exchange students that was helpful!
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: I can't haha. Very confusing and time consuming - they send you mails with reminders and guides of what to do though so just follow them
registration_help: Not much.
registration_success: I had no problems but met others who did not get the classes that they has chosen in their application.
registration_advice: Just be sure to apply for modules that are available for exchange students. When you apply for modules you can chose modules that you are not allowed for and won't get so you have to find the list of modules for exchange students on NUS website.
course_level: You can apply for 1, 2 and 3 year courses. I had some first year courses and all the people I was studying was quite young. If you want "easy" classes to pass and more time to travel and enjoy Singapore/Asia apply for "introduction" classes!
teaching_comparison: More focused on lectures and MCQ tests.
courses_enrolled: Plants and Society, Introduction to Psychology, Enviromental Politics and Ecology and environment
recommended_courses: Enviromental Politics was fun and engaging. Would not recommend the other courses.
unexpected_costs: Food is very cheap and good! A lot of foodstalls around campus for lunch and dinner:)
cost_comparison: Nightlife is EXPENSIVE
activities_available: NUS is big on social activities and sports - all students participate in something!
activities_recommended: Whatever you feel like:) I played a lot of football and climbing!
weekend_recommendations: Phillipines, South Korea, Indonesia!
culture_adjustment: Quite easy.
socializing_tips: People are very nice - talk with them:) A lot of whatsapp groups with events and socialising.
cultural_challenges: Not really anything.
culture_appreciated: HAWKER CENTERS!
top3_advice: Its very hot. You can travel all of Asia cheap and convenient!
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: Travelling.
greatest_challenge: Can be lonely at times:) Make sure to call home!

crucial_aspects: That it was a different culture to the European and that the academic level was good and the people spoke English
overall_comments: The best decision I have done at university level.
info_ease: Fairly easy. I have to do a bit of emails to KU staff concerning the need for an English test (don’t need one to go to Singapore from CPH)
arrival_assistance: The NUS is really really good to send emails in the whole process and answer extremely quickly to any questions I had. NUS law did also do a lunch for all law exchange students in the first week
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: The best decision I have done at university level.
registration_process: You apply and then you get an email that lets you pay for the whole stay and then a new email a few weeks up to the stay that explains the on site process.
registration_help: You can always write and emails to them and they have a office at pgpr
registration_success: Got 3 out of 4 classes
registration_advice: That you should take at least one intensive course because the semester is very intense, so you don’t have time to read up on everything if you have all exams at the end of the semester. Also read the material during the semester because the reading week is short before the exams in law at NUS.
academics_comments: The best decision I have done at university level.
course_level: There is some big gaps in the academic levels in the courses in NUS I did maritime law which was a really higely advanced course. I also did Singapore legal history which was very easy to follow and not that hard academically
teaching_comparison: On an overall level the teaching style is the same. What is different is that you can grade for your class participation that has and impact in the final grade. Normally 10%.
courses_enrolled: Maritime law Singapore legal history International water law Law of marine insurance
recommended_courses: Maritime law if the interest is there. Otherwise the legal history is a good course to get an overall understanding of Singapore history.
unexpected_costs: Not really any. See the answer for former students and you get a good picture of the overall costs. Grab in Singapore is expensive
cost_comparison: Food is cheap in the hawker center but beer is expensive. Transport is a bit expensive
activities_available: More or less anything you could imagine. NUS is really good at sending emails out to information students about upcoming events and activities.
activities_recommended: Do a sport and from there meet people. It is a nice way to meet new people
weekend_recommendations: Go travelling! Go around in south east Asia. It is really cheap and short destination to a lot of places.
culture_adjustment: Really easy. By upon to new things and food and you will be absolute fine.
socializing_tips: The NUS clubs and by approaching in between classes And so the buddy program NUS sets up
cultural_challenges: Not really any.
culture_appreciated: How friendly people are and nice.
top3_advice: Go travelling. By open to new things. Remember to enjoy it well you are there
other_useful_info: NUS is really strict and sends a lot of emails. However NUS is more strict on paper then in reality so don’t be to scared about the emails.
most_rewarding: The new view of the world I got.
greatest_challenge: Maritime law.

crucial_aspects: The use of english as the language of teaching and in society in general.
info_ease: Quite easy
arrival_assistance: There was quite a lot of information through mails, and many events for newcoming exchangers.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: When you get accepted by KU and register and apply, you are given a lot of step by step material that you are guided by. You first apply for getting accepted by the host university by choosing and applying to different courses that you would like to have. Acceptance of these courses depends on your grades, and the more popular courses (economy, architecture etc) will get filled by the people with the higest average. You have to apply for 8 courses, and to get accepted into the host university you have to get into at least 3 of the courses. It can be nerverecking since you dont know what your chances are - but remeber that whatever courses you are allocated when registering, you can always change when your have arrived. The first 2-3 weeks of the semester is kind of an introduction to the courses and you can change if it isn't something you like (based on availablity of other courses ofc.) But in general it seems more strict than it is even though the system is quite flexible.
registration_help: A lot of step by step guides and emails. Even online zoom seminars that guide you through the process. The website is also quite helpful.
registration_success: I was quite succesful and out of my top 4 choices I got into 3 of them.
registration_advice: Dont stress in choosing exactly the courses that you want in the registration and first application, you can always change your courses later if you are unsure if you like them or not. The forst couple of weeks there is a possibilty to switch your courses. So no stress. The system is more flexible than it seems.
course_level: I took level 3000 and level 1000 courses which is the same as third and first year BA courses respectively. Third year courses were the courses that were a part of my field (geography), and the other where introductionary courses to other fields of study that I found interesting (History and sociology)
teaching_comparison: Similar acedemic level, yet depending on field of study most grades are a mix of exams, participation, quizzes, mid-terms and assignments which means that the workload throughout the semester can be quite high (not neccesarily hard, just a lot to do all the time)
courses_enrolled: - Land below the winds: Introduction to Southeast Aisa - Nationbuilding in Malaysia and Singapore - Aquarian, Riprarian and Coastal Ecosystems - Cities and Regions: Planning for change
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed the introduction to southeast asia course since its a historical and cultural introduction to the region you will be living in (and probably also travel a lot in). And the proffesors a very good.
unexpected_costs: Visa applications
cost_comparison: Food in hawker centers and food courts are mostly cheaper than expected, but supermarkets are wuite expensive (same as in Denmark I would say). Transport is very cheap and drinks (coffes, teas and juices) are cheap. Everything else is quite expensive and you shouldn't expect stores and malls to be cheaper than in DK
activities_available: A lot. All kinds of sports, religious activites, games, music etc. The amount of clubs and groups seems unlimited.
activities_recommended: I enjoyed the many seminars that profs and students would organize - with evening lectures and workshops about a wide range of themes.
weekend_recommendations: I recomnend getting of campus - which sounds easy to do - but its so easy to just end up spending all your time on campus. Go out, the museums are free for students and parks are everywhere.
culture_adjustment: Quite easy since everything was in english.
socializing_tips: Singaporeans are BUSY. All the time. They dont sleep a lot, so expect people to be awake to quite late and always be busy with stuff (studying, clubs, groups etc) so they quickly end up only really socialising with people from thier groups and clubs. Remember that most also go home in the weekend to be with family, so socializing mostly happens throughout the weekdays
cultural_challenges: Singaporeans are really sweet in firsthand encounters but because they are so busy always its hard to get to know them.
culture_appreciated: The food and all the activities that there is around the city (cultural festivals, musuems etc)
top3_advice: 1) Remember it humid and hot outside, but inside its freezing because of the AC. 2) Dont stress with registration - it looks strict and hard but its quite flexible. Relax. 3) Enjoy the diversity of food and drinks (remember to include food in the budget eventhough you have mealplans)
other_useful_info: Even though the uni is asian and you might have some expectation of it being hard and competetive - its much more relaxed in reality, eventhough workload is a lot (but not necesarily hard)
most_rewarding: All the things I learned about Asia
greatest_challenge: The big workload and how to get into a healthy routine were school didn't take up most of my time.

crucial_aspects: When choosing where to study it was important to me that the education was in English as well as being a country with a distinctly different culture and history to that of Denmark. Personally, Singapore was the perfect fit for this as English is the main language spoken in most settings and the culture is heavily influenced by Asian values. Moreover Singapores geographical location makes it easy to travel to other countries doing the semester.
info_ease: Before arriving I had the general information I needed in order to check in to my accommodation. Generally, it is very easy to find information, but if they are very helpful over email.
arrival_assistance: I had the housing office help me with how to check in, which made the process very easy.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: When you apply for NUS you will simultaneously be applying for eight courses. You'll need around four courses to fulfill the requirements, and depending on the allocation process you will already have a spot on some of your courses. In the beginning of the semester you have the opportunity to apply for additional courses, change courses and appeal if you did not get the courses you wanted.
registration_help: They provide very good manuals which you can download on their website as to when you need to apply for your courses and when the appeal process begins and ends.
registration_success: I got three out of the four courses I wanted, after that, I just applied for other courses that did not interfere with my schedule. Due to limited spots, I had to appeal, which was a very easy process with staff guiding you through.
registration_advice: When registering i think it is a very good idea to look at the vacancy reports, that way you get an idea of how likely you will be in securing the courses.
course_level: The levels are indicated inthe thausands so three-thousand courses take more than two-thousand courses. Overall i did not find it particular harder than courses back home, there is just a bit more responsibility during the semester and not just at finals.
teaching_comparison: I had a lot of smaller seminar courses where we were only around twenty students in total which made it a bit more relaxed. Moreover, most courses have tutorials that can be helpful for discussions and understanding. The workload is very different from what I'm used to. At NUS there are different academic components throughout the year that count towards your final grade. This usually consists of group presentations and assignments.
courses_enrolled: I was enrolled in SC2220 Gender Studies, SC3203 Race and Ethnic Relations, SC2205 Sociology of Family, and SC3228 Senses and Society.
recommended_courses: I would recommend to enroll in the Gender Studies class as it is a broad topic that most people can follow. The tutorials are really interesting as they are discussion-based where everyone can participate. Moreover, there is no final exam for this course which makes the exam season less stressful.
unexpected_costs: I did not experience any unexpected costs during my stay, however it is nice to know that buses on campus are free.
cost_comparison: Eating out can be very cheap if you go to the right places! Eat at hawker centers and you can get a meal for 3-5SGD. Otherwise, food at restaurants and groceries can be pretty expensive.
activities_available: There is a very wide range of different clubs around campus and by the different halls. I recommend going to their CCA meetings in the beginning of the semester, there you can here all the different activities there are. I personally did NUS boxing and Raffles (my hall) swimming.
activities_recommended: I think doing most beginner sports here is really fun as it is a bit more chill and not too competitive. However, I do recommend finding out which teams are more competition-based or more for leisure.
weekend_recommendations: In the beginning I recommend just being a tourist in Singapore and going around the city. A lot of Singaporeans go to JB during the weekends as it is very cheap there. During the longer weekends i recommend going to places such as Malaysia, Indonesia or Hongkong. For longer breaks you can go to a wide range of other countries in Asia.
culture_adjustment: It was pretty easy. I do not feel that there are cultural differences that are hard to overcome.
socializing_tips: I recommend signing up for the NUS Buddy system if you want to get a Singaporean friend. I also recommend staying in a hall if you want a more submersive experience. Moreover, most locals are really nice and will be very welcoming to you. But I would say that generally, people hang out with other exchangers more than locals.
cultural_challenges: What I found most challenging is the very high surveillance there is. Of course, it can make you feel way more safe in the country, but it is also crazy to know that you are always being surveilanced.
culture_appreciated: I really appreciate how familiar the culture is in the sense that people are really welcoming and take you ‘in'. I think it depends on who you hang out with and where you end up living, but the people at my hall where very inviting.
top3_advice: NUS is known for being very hard, and it can be very hard, but you do not need to stress too much about it as you just need to pass. There will be more work throughout the semester but then the finals count for less. On-campus accommodation is a god sent for making friends and doing different club activities.
other_useful_info: NUS's website contains so much information and is extremely helpful in the beginning, so take a good look at it. When registering for courses at the beginning of the semester check when the exams are so they do not overlap and if they are very late in the semester.
most_rewarding: Definitely getting to know so many new people and making very good friends with people from all over the globe. And getting to travel around Asia with these newfound friends.
greatest_challenge: I think becoming at ease with the sense of homesickness you can experience can be hard at times, but there are also so many things going on that you can hardly keep up with people back home, which also can be challenging. Overall I do not think that there were any challenges too hard to overcome.

crucial_aspects: It was crucial that the stay was outside Europe for exploring new cultures. Singapore being an English-speaking country was also important. As was it important that the university itself was highly acknowledged worldwide.
overall_comments: I had a great stay. I met inspiring people that I today consider some of my best friends. I made a ton of new insides into the world. And I had some of my wildest travel experiences yet.
info_ease: It is quite easy. Everything will get send in mails in English and there will be plenty of time and second-chances given if you screw up the initial bureaucratic process. Also, they are very quick at responding to your emails.
arrival_assistance: No assistance.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

registration_help: An online tool. However, if you wanted additional assistance you could text the superviser and get really good help to match the courses.
registration_success: I was very successful. I got pretty much what I wanted and when I wanted it.
registration_advice: Perhaps registor for more courses than you want. You can easily drop in the beginning. And most of the courses are very dependent on the lector - some are old and boring. This way you have more options to choose from, when you finally want to settle on courses for the semester.
academics_comments: I had a great stay. I met inspiring people that I today consider some of my best friends. I made a ton of new insides into the world. And I had some of my wildest travel experiences yet.
course_level: I was only allowed to take Level 3000 courses. These are considered BA-level.
teaching_comparison: Tutorials are different from holdundervisning. Tutorials are mainly for testing the students. Not furthering understanding. Most courses have obligatory attendens.
courses_enrolled: Money and Banking Evolution of economic though and analysis ASEAN Economics Introduction to Game Theory
recommended_courses: Take the game theory course. It is closely related to the one at KU.
unexpected_costs: Getting a new passport.
cost_comparison: Food is cheap. Alcohol is expensive.
activities_available: Everything you can imagine. Not beachvolleyball however...
activities_recommended: The swimming hall, but go find out on your own! Try a lot.
weekend_recommendations: Malaysia. The jungle. Explore a lot.
culture_adjustment: Feel out the system of surveillance, but since everyone speaks English, then the culture shock is not that big.
socializing_tips: Do stuff before semesterstart. Live in a hall. Live on campus in general.
cultural_challenges: No, not really.
culture_appreciated: No criminality. You will feel very safe in Singapore. You can leave your computer or wallet wherever for however long. Nothing will be stolen.
top3_advice: Travel, but make sure you have a nice living in Singapore. Try food. Go clubbing at Ce La Vi.
other_useful_info: No, you gotta find out on your own. Everything will work out on its own.
most_rewarding: All the new things I know and have seen.
greatest_challenge: I don't know. I didn't have any great challenges. I felt alone a few times. Being far away from home can be hard sometimes.
other_comments: Singapore is a great place, because nature and amazing cultures are nearby. Singapore itself is also interesting to explore and understand. A very different country from anywhere in the world and especially Europe.

crucial_aspects: - Academics, especially wanting to improve my "legal english" and the specific courses offered - The national language is English - Wanting to experience an Asian country and a culture very different from my own
info_ease: All information was provided really.
arrival_assistance: There was a webinar before arrival, there were multiple e-mails and fliers about course registration, studentpass (visa) and housing.
arrival_comments: Some of the information was a little unclear, but overall it worked out well.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You start by requesting courses when you are registering at the university. At this time you usually get three courses, and if you need a fourth course, you will request this at the start of the semester. Then there is an appeals round if you for example didn't get enough courses or your exams overlap.
registration_help: I don't really remember, but I'm sure there was an e-mail adresse you could contact.
registration_success: Pretty satisfied
registration_advice: It takes a long time and you are responsible for making sure that your schedule works. However, NUSmods is helpful for this, as it has a "timetable" feature where you can add and remove courses. Also keep in mind that there are different examinations types - some a research papers, some are written sit in and some a written take home exams.
course_level: I think that the level of the classes varied a lot since they are elective courses.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style was quite similar to UCPH, as NUS also uses seminar classes. The professor would talk and ask questions and some times there would be student presentations.
courses_enrolled: Energy arbitration Singapore Legal History Public International Law Regulation of Digital Platforms (intensive course)
recommended_courses: Energy arbitration was an amazing course. The teachers are very competent and the topics were very interesting (at least to me). For an understanding of Singapore, I would really recommend Singapore Legal History. It was really nice to learn about Singapore's history. It was also nice to write a research paper as the final exam.
unexpected_costs: Dehumidifier
cost_comparison: Eating out at hawker centers or the canteens on campus is cheap, but buying groceries or going to a restaurant or for drinks is expensive.
activities_recommended: There is always a lot going on at NUS and with the other exchange students. Join whatever whatsapp groups suits your interest and then you can go the different events with other exchange students - ie. hiking group, sky diving group, travel group, off campus partying groups.
weekend_recommendations: You should definitely take a trip to Kuala Lumpur. If you are up for it a lot of students take an overnight bus (5 ish hours). Malaysia in general is very cheap. Going to Johor Bahru just on the other side of the border is also very popular. Singapore is generally ideal for traveling East Asia! Also most museums in Singapore are free for students, so you should take advantage of that!
culture_adjustment: It was not really an issue.
socializing_tips: I would say befriending the locals in your classes is the best way to go.
cultural_challenges: Singaporeans are generally reserved, so you have to make an effort to get to know them.
culture_appreciated: The many diverse cultures that make up Singapore. It was very interesting to experience how many different cultures lived harmoniously in Singapore.
top3_advice: Singapore is place with a lot of rules and laws, so make sure to be respectful of them.
other_useful_info: Downloade the apps: uNivUS, NUS NextBus, Telegram and Grab (basically Uber).
most_rewarding: I think the best part of exchange has been meeting other exchange students and Singaporean students! Getting to experience the unique culture in Singapore was also really great. Lastly, NUS has some truly amazing and accomplished teachers that are very passionate about their fields.
greatest_challenge: I think the biggest challenge for me was that the assessment was ongoing. This means that you are constantly evaluated for class participation and midterms. This was a big change from what I am used to back home.
other_comments: There were som challenges housing wise, but apart form that my stay in Singapore was amazing. I'm sure that anyone going will have an incredible experience! Going on exchange is a lot of work but so worth it:)

crucial_aspects: First and foremost, Singapore seemed as an exotic and interesting location, which is located in the middle of South East Asia with great oppourtunities to visit other interesting countries. Further, the university is ranked as Asia's best law school and one of the best law schools in the world, which was a big draw for me.

arrival_assistance: No assistance was required as the email sent out from the university contained everything needed.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

This process is explained in detail in the emails received from the university and the completition of the process is easy.
registration_help: Hotlines etc.
registration_success: I had to registrate for 4 classes and I was only successful in registering for two of my originally 4 requested courses. However, I was able to select my remaining two courses from a list of available courses, which was perfectly fine.
registration_advice: Follow the guidelines provided in the emails.
course_level: The level of the courses corresponded with 3rd year BA electives or MA electives. The level was perfectly fine and I did not find the courses to be more difficult than the ones offered at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: I found the teaching style to be overall similar to UCPH but also very dependent on the specific professor.
courses_enrolled: Law of Money and Central Banking, Competition Law, Principles of Financial Law, Law and Practice of Investment Management.
recommended_courses: I would heavily recommend the abovementioned first three courses as I learned a lot and the courses were very well taught and extremely interesting. However, I would stay clear of the latter course as it was a big dissapointment.
unexpected_costs: None.
cost_comparison: Public transport is very cheap and Grab (same as Uber) is available.
activities_available: Everything that you can think of.
activities_recommended: Engage in the social activities offered and sign up for any student clubs that you may find interesting.
weekend_recommendations: Travel all over South East Asia. Singapore has an amazing airport and you can easily and cheaply visit other nearby destinations during your weekends.
culture_adjustment: Easy.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: The openness and welcoming attitude.
top3_advice: 1) Make an effort in the beginning of the semester to meet other exchange students and try and form relationships to other exchange students as well as local students. 2) Travel as much as you can during and after the semester. 3) Have a good time and enjoy yourself during your exchange - and focus more on the social aspects rather than the academic aspects.

crucial_aspects: I always knew I wanted to go on exchange and had always thought I'd go to the US, but upon browsing through the partner agreements my home university had, I realized that I had never considered going to Asia and thought that was a shame as I perceive Asia to be "the future" with the changing world order etc. I choose Singapore as it works as a great bridge between the west and the east, and to this end thought there were great benefits to the main language being English.
info_ease: There was an administrative downside as I had to learn the system at NUS, but once I was able to look past all the different platforms and the overload of information, I really did feel that "my hand was held" the entire time upon arrival in terms of what I needed to get done/when to get it done/where to get it done. I suggest taking notes of what needs to be done though, because otherwise it really feels like information overload.
arrival_assistance: A lot of the assistance and information was online even when getting to my accommodation all I needed to do was download an app that worked as the key to my dorm.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: I was given a flowchart, but it was very administrative heavy.
registration_help: They did offer lots of services on campus!
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted!
registration_advice: Take notes of what you need to do/look at the flowchart, it is easy to overlook something also in terms of finishing the VISA process in person.
course_level: It is a different kind of law you learn. It is more doctrinal, which I think could have a lot to do with the differences between a civil law system and a common law one.
teaching_comparison: Depends a bit on the class, but I felt that participation was more normalized at NUS. The professors are very interested in hearing what you have to say/what options you hold, which was very refreshing and a lot more engaging.
courses_enrolled: Law and Democracy in East Asia Current Problems in International Law Human Rights in Asia Traditional Chinese Legal Thought
recommended_courses: I would honestly take a look at who's teaching the different courses and choose professors that are well-known/pioneers within their respective fields. I by chance ended up taking a class with Antony Anghie who's a great legal thinker within a specific school of international law, and that has hands-down been one of the highlights of my academic time - to be taught by someone to talented.
unexpected_costs: I by accident went to the doctor outside of NUS health clinic which was a huge mistake as I had to pay lot, which my insurance at the time didn't cover.
cost_comparison: Eating out (especially at hawker centers) and transportation was less expensive than I thought, but groceries were quite expensive!
activities_available: They had everything from barista clubs, astronomy club, student podcasts, different festivals etc.
activities_recommended: Sailing club or the outdoor adventure club!
weekend_recommendations: Travel, travel, travel! You can take a bus to Kuala Lumpur, JB or take relatively cheap flights to other Asian countries! I went to Malaysia (Langkawi and Kuala Lumpur), Thailand, Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, Vietnam and Indonesia (Bali). If you know you want to travel upon the end of the semester or throughout during the different holidays, I recommend saving some money before heading on exchange.
culture_adjustment: Super easy as it is quite westernized.
socializing_tips: Talk to people in class!
cultural_challenges: Maybe the fact that freedom of speech is less free.
culture_appreciated: The politeness, diversity, respect and food culture!
top3_advice: Find a way to strike the balance between academia and all the social and cultural opportunities you're going to have while on exchange. It is an amazing opportunity to learn things/courses you cannot otherwise learn back home (also seeing that Asia is a huge growing economy it is super useful to learn about from the inside), but at the same time there are also other important things about about on exchange in terms of personal growth and experiences.
other_useful_info: There is a larger emphasis on participation which might seem intimidating at first, but my experience is that whereas back home there is often a 'right or wrong' answer here it is more the professors looking for you to engage with them and share your opinions
most_rewarding: The connection I now feel to Singapore and all the places I got to travel to.
greatest_challenge: Not having more time. Time flew by and as I was really getting settled into everyday life and started knowing the city well/having favorite places throughout, I had to go back ):
other_comments: It is hands down one of the best things I've ever done in my life.
