institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: Crucial that the destination was close to Denmark, that it was a smaller city with nature close by, and that the culture was similar to Denmark. The academic level had to be the same or similar to UCPH. There had to be oppertunities to go hiking in the mountains for day or weekend trips.
info_ease: Easy. Both UCPH and the host institution (NTNU) provided sufficient information by mail upon arrival. NTNU had many guides on their homepage for exchange students.
arrival_assistance: None, but it was easy to get around in the city, and all necessary information about the intro-week and course registration was send to us by mail from NTNU.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Upon arrival to the host institution, exchange students are provided with a login to "Studentweb". From here it is relatively easy and intuitive to register for courses.
registration_help: You could write an email to the exchange office, but the whole course registration process is easy and mails are send to guide the students.
registration_success: A was able to register for all the courses I initially wanted.
registration_advice: None, it really is intuitive and easy. Just remember the date for last registration of courses, but this will also be send by mail from the host institution.
course_level: Courses were divided into Intermediate (BA level) and Second degree level (MA level).
teaching_comparison: Similar, with a lot of normal lectures and some, but not a lot, of group work. For some courses there were mandatory work, such as presentations of articles or midterm assignments, that needed to be passed in order to be eligable to take the exam.
courses_enrolled: MOL3000: Introduction to Molecular Medicine (MA level). MOL3023: Molecular Medical Bacteriology (MA level) TMMT4001: Sustainable Food Production (MA level) INTRO175: Introduction to Norway (BA level)
recommended_courses: MOL3023 was very interesting as it connected knowledge of bacteria to disease outbreak and surveillance, providing the clinical and medical aspect of infection with bacteria. Lectures were given on some selected bacteria such as streptococcus, staphylococcus, tuberculosis and E. Coli. The teaching consisted mainly of lectures and one midterm assignment in bioinformatics. But not to worry if you do not know anything of bioinformatics. The aim of the assignment was to become familiarized with the field, and I really learned a lot from it. MOL3000 was also really interesting with various subjects from the human genome, mutations and inherited disease to diabetes and some bioinformatics as well. The teaching consisted mainly of lectures and one mandatory presentation of an article within one of the subjects.
unexpected_costs: No unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: Generally, food was more expensive than in Denmark, but that was to be expected. A note to the costs; Internet was a part of my rent and I had no phone bill due to too much data being used. This is not the case for everyone. The expenses for trips was also more expensive in the first months, and less expensive from november when it got colder and exams were approaching.
activities_available: The university has a sports club called NTNUI. Here, students can sign up for all sorts of sports including swimming, badminton, kayak and soccer. Students can also sign up for SiT to be able to train at the gym. The students in Trondheim can become a member of Studentersamfundet, which is a large building where events and other festivities are held throughout the semester. ESN (Europen Student Network) is an organisation outside the university where exchange students can participate in events and come on trips during the semester.
activities_recommended: I would recommend that you sign up for some sports in NTNUI. If you are keen on hiking, Ski and Fjellsport arranges tours almost every weekend, with variyng difficulty. The destination depends on the trip coordinators, but they arrange hiking trips with tent or overnight in cabins owned by the university, ice skating trips, snowshoe trips and many other kind of tours. I would also recommend signing up for SiT.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend that you take some walks in the city to see the fortress (Kristianfestningen) and walk along the Ladestien, where there is also a nice little beach. Bymarka is a forrest very close to the city, where there are endless of hiking oppertunities for day-trips. It is very easy to get from the city and into the forrest. The highest top is 565 moh and provides great views over the city and to the mountains in the distance. In the fall semester, if you are lucky, snow will fall in late november/early december and you will be able to go cross country skiing. I would also recommend taking a ferry from Trondheim to Fosen for a day or weekend hike. For longer trips, I would recommend taking the train (or a car) down to Dovrefjell, rent a cabin and go on hikes. It might be advantageous to become member of DNT, as they own a lot of cabins all over Norway. It is also a good idea to plan a trip around some of these cabins, doing cabin-to-cabin hikes, where you really find yourself in the middle of nowhere in the mountains. ESN plans multiple trips during the semester, one going to Lofoten. I would definitely recommend going to Lofoten, but plan the trip yourself. It is easy taking the train from Trondheim to Bodø and from there a ferry to Lofoten (Moskenes or Svolvær). Rent a car in Bodø and take on the ferry. Go no later than september.
culture_adjustment: The culture is very similar to Denmark, so it was easy to adjust.
socializing_tips: Look for private accommodation with Norwegian students, and engage in activities provided by the university.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: Difficult to answer as the culture is so similar to Denmark.
top3_advice: Engage yourself in sports in NTNUI and events in at the university or in the city. Embrace the norwegian, take an oppertunity to learn more of the language. Take advantage of the nature and mountains being so close to the city.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Meeting a lot of other danish exchange students that had the same interests and wanted to go on hikes and tours together, and join different events in the city. Sharing great experiences together, and taking new friendships and memories back home with us.
greatest_challenge: Wanting to see and experience as much of the norwegian nature as possible, but not having enough time. It was a bit stressfull to have so many ideas for tours and wanting to go every weekend, but still remembering that we had courses to attend and exams to pass.
other_comments: Adjust your expectations before going abroad. Remember that Norway is not far away, and you can come back and do that trip you did not have time for at a later time. You may meet exchange students that are more interested in becoming involved in student organizations, or some that want to spend all their time exploring the mountains. Find out what it is that you want to gain from this experience and pursue it, but do not set your expectations unrealistically high. You do not want to end up being disappointed, or being stressed out about all the things you want to do before leaving again.

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: I chose NTNU because the courses sounded really interesting and relevant to what I study. I was also excited about the chance to experience Norwegian culture and everyday life. Plus, the nature in and around Trondheim really appealed to me. It's such a beautiful place to live and study.
info_ease: It was very easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. NTNU provided clear guidance.
arrival_assistance: I didn’t receive any specific assistance upon arrival, but the information provided beforehand was clear enough that I managed everything on my own without any issues.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: They have a dedicated website where you register and choose your courses. Everything was straightforward and well explained, so I didn’t have any problems.
registration_help: I didn’t need any help during the process, so I’m not entirely sure what kind of support was available. But everything was clear and easy to manage on my own.
registration_success: I was quite successful in registering for the classes I wanted. There was one course that wasn’t available, because they didn't have it anymore, but otherwise I got into all the courses I was interested in.
registration_advice: I didn’t run into any problems with registration, so I don’t have specific advice. But I’d recommend reading the instructions carefully and registering as early as possible to make sure you get the courses you want.
course_level: I took three bachelor’s level courses and one master’s level course. I found the bachelor’s courses a bit too easy, but they were still interesting. The master’s course, on the other hand, was more challenging and engaging. I really enjoyed it and felt like I learned a lot from it.
teaching_comparison: It's the same.
courses_enrolled: MOL3020 – Virology BI2045 – Sexual Selection and Communication BI2044 – Ethology BI2033 – Population Ecology
recommended_courses: Virology and Ethology
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Overall, things were less expensive than I expected. Prices were similar to those in Copenhagen, but because of the currency exchange rate, everyday expenses ended up being a bit cheaper for me
activities_available: They have a student sports association, NTNUI, which has over 60 different sports and activities. They also have cabins in nature that students can use for weekend trips, which is a great way to explore the area. And you can borrow gear for hiking, cross-country skiing, fishing, and more from Bumerang for free. There are also many student organizations and events throughout the year. NTNU hosts big cultural festivals like UKA and ISFiT, and there are plenty of student groups related to music, dance, theatre, and other interests. The Student Society is very active.
activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend hiking in the summer and cross-country skiing in the winter. The nature around Trondheim is absolutely beautiful and very different from what I'm used to in Denmark. It’s a great way to experience the Norwegian landscape
weekend_recommendations: The museums Storfossen (Large waterfall) Hiking in Bymarka Taking the tram The cafes and restaurants Take the train to Røros Take the train to Bodø
culture_adjustment: It was very easy to adjust to the local culture. The cultural differences were small, so I felt comfortable pretty quickly.
socializing_tips: I found it pretty easy to socialize through the courses. Group work and class discussions were a good way to get to know both local and other exchange students. Just being open and willing to talk during breaks or after class really helped. Joining student activities or events can also be a great way to meet people.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: I really appreciated everything about the culture. The strong connection to nature, the balance between work and free time, and the friendliness of the people in Trondheim all made a great impression on me. I also enjoyed that Trondheim is a very historical city. It gave me the chance to learn more about Norwegian history, which I found really interesting.
top3_advice: Get out into nature as much as you can. It’s incredibly easy and accessible in Trondheim. Whether it’s hiking, skiing, or just going for a walk. Explore the city. Trondheim has a lot to offer with its cozy cafés, interesting museums, and historical sites. Take time to enjoy what the city itself has to offer, not just the university. Pe prepared for the weather. Make sure to have good waterproof shoes.
other_useful_info: One thing that might be useful to know is that things are very well-organized at NTNU, so don’t stress too much. Most practical information is easy to find, and people are helpful if you need anything.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was getting to live in a completely new environment. I loved the nature, and it was great to meet both local and international students. It gave me new perspectives, both academically and personally, and I really grew from the experience.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge during my exchange was working in a group that didn’t function well. It was a bit difficult to manage expectations and communication, especially in a new academic setting. However, the teacher was very helpful and supportive, which made a big difference and helped me get through the situation.

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: Good academic opportunities, beautiful nature and not very far from home.
info_ease: It was very easy. We got a lot of emails all the time with necessary information. You had to keep track of it all, but it really helped. You could always just write an email to the university if you were in any doubt.
arrival_assistance: Assistance in form of an intro week.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You sign up for courses on Studentweb. You can sign up for as many as you want until 15th of September (in my case). If you aren't sure about your courses, it is better to have too many at this point. Afterwards, you can deregister from the courses you aren't going to take. I found it very easy.
registration_help: You could always text both the course coordinator and the exchange office at NTNU.
registration_success: Very successful.
registration_advice: If you are in doubt about 2 courses, register to both. You can always deregister, but you cannot register to a new one after the deadline.
course_level: BA course: Much details compared to it being a BA-course. But we could bring notes to the exam, so it was alright. MA courses: One had appropriate level for it being a MA-course, and the other was easy.
teaching_comparison: Very much the same. Lectures, group work, presentations...
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Neuroscience. Immunology. Pharmaceutical Innovation.
recommended_courses: I would actually recommend all of them. Although, there are some things to think about before choosing them. Neuroscience: A very good and thorough BA-course. Has a lot of details and is really not just an introductory course. Also, the lecturers were online - you never met the other people in the course. This might have changed, but for me, it was online. It was nice because then you could go on trips and then rewatch the lectures afterwards, but also sad because you didn't get to meet other people. Immunology: A MA-course. Very difficult with lots of details, but I actually learned a lot. Definitely a good course if you're interested in immunology. Pharmaceutical Innovation: A course describing the process from finding a drug to getting it approved to the market (going through preclinical tests and clinical trials). Mostly, it was very nice and very cool to get to know the process. Sometimes it was a bit challenging, because it's a MA-course on the pharmacy master, so they know a lot more about pharmaceuticals than us. But very nice with the overview.
unexpected_costs: Buying warmer clothes.
cost_comparison: Food is very expensive even though the Norwegian crown is low right now. Just be prepared. Clothes are less expensive, due to the Norwegian crown.
activities_available: Athletic: For sure Sit-training and NTNUI. Social activities: ESN Trondheim plans a lot all the time!! There are just a look of associations that you can join; I don't know all of them. But they'll tell you more about it in the introduction week.
activities_recommended: NTNUI classes: You get to be active and meet other students. Both Norwegian students and exchange students. Very cheap. NTNUI Koiene: They have cabins close to Trondheim that you can rent for 30 DKK. They usually are located in very nice surroundings. They have no electricity nor water, so be prepared for that. ESN Trondheim: They plan all your trips, so you don't have to yourself. You meet so many nice people!!
weekend_recommendations: Go to Bymarka. Take the ferry to Fosen. Try one of the NTNUI cabins. Go to Gløshaugen and watch over the city. Just walk around in the city, experience the atmosphere.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. The Norwegians are a lot like us.
socializing_tips: Live with them! They are much easier to talk with if they are forced to talk to you haha.
cultural_challenges: None, really.
culture_appreciated: The student environment.
top3_advice: Be open! Participate in as many social activities as you can! Speak with some Norwegian people.
other_useful_info: It is very dark in the winter. Bring D-vitamin :)
most_rewarding: Definitely all the trips and experiences I've had with people from all over the world. And getting to know my Norwegian roommates. It has been amazing!!
greatest_challenge: Missing home.

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: I was very interrested in the nature and environment in Norway, due to the love I have for nature and that I'm studying biology, which is applicable when you're out exploring. Also I am half Norwegian, so I wanted to explore the culture that I have always somewhat been seperated from.
overall_comments: Very good oportunity for self-exploring and development, meeting other cultures and people from all around the world. I've received many new friends. The teaching was quite a bit worse than in Denmark and on a lower level.
info_ease: It was alright, but sometimes it seemed like you required to do things that were actually not required. For example the "Proof of Attendance" document that was downloadable, was not required to be filled because we got a arrival and departure confirmation from our host university.
arrival_assistance: Not any.
arrival_comments: There were some problems with my courses because you had to register, before summer (because of limited space), which was before we even had acces to the NTNU systems, so I couldn't join the courses that I wanted. And also some teachers had stopped prior to my arrival, so there were just fewer courses overall. These factors led to the availability of Biology courses in Autumn/winter, being very limited.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Very good oportunity for self-exploring and development, meeting other cultures and people from all around the world. I've received many new friends. The teaching was quite a bit worse than in Denmark and on a lower level.
registration_process: Everything happened very easily, most happened through the KU system. The last application date was may 1st. You needed to included different files with information: Passport, Learning Agreement, Course descriptions (courses you were going to take on NTNU), Courses taken in spring (back on KU), Erasmus Grant Agreement and an additional from with information about emergency contacts and such. Everything was quite easy with the process being described to you as you go.
registration_help: You could always write either NTNU exchange og KU exchange if you had any questions. But again sometimes it was hard to find their mail if you couldn't remember it.
registration_success: As mentioned earlier, some classes required registering before we were even gived access to the NTNU systems, which was very annyoing, resulting in me having to choose 2 courses that I didn't find interresting or atleast not related to my bachelor. Also a teacher (or more) had stopped just before I arrived which resulted in fewer courses to choose between overall.
registration_advice: Expect a lower level of teaching compared to KU, and also research if you have to write specifically to the teachers of a given course.
academics_comments: Very good oportunity for self-exploring and development, meeting other cultures and people from all around the world. I've received many new friends. The teaching was quite a bit worse than in Denmark and on a lower level.
course_level: They were lower compared to KU, but still alright, as you also had to take 4 course on the same time compared to "blok struktur" on KU Biologi atleast.
teaching_comparison: Some things were the same: Some teachers were bright and you learned a lot, some were monotone and you received zero knowledge from their teaching. UCPH is better overall though, with the UCPH level being higher.
courses_enrolled: BI2043 - Biodiversity and Conservation Biology I BI2034 - Community Ecology and Eco Systems INTRO175 - Introduction to Norway NEVR2030 - Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience
recommended_courses: BI2034 - Community Ecology and Eco Systems. It started off with a fun and interresting field trip to Dovrefjell, where you learned a lot and you got close with your colleagues. And it was also the course I benefitted most from, as it was very relevant to my focus in biology: ecology.
unexpected_costs: I hurt my shoulder so I had to pay for a physiotherapist (Luckily i had traveling insurance that covered it, so make sure you have that). Different unplanned trips of experience(Trip to Lofoten, Surftrip and so on).
cost_comparison: Food was a bit more expensive compared to Denmark, but not much. Also I think my housing was rather cheap compared to what my friends paid.
activities_available: Almost any athletic activites you can think of. ESN (Exchange student network) hosted several Cultural and social activites such as different trips around Norway, although I didn't participate.
activities_recommended: Surf trip in Hoddevik with NTNUI Surf, mindblowing experience (Don't worry, you won't freeze), and its fun even as a beginner! A trip to lofoten, one of the most beautiful places I've ever seen in my whole life. Can be arranged fairly cheap by yourself (a group of friends recommended), for around 3500,- DKK for housing, rental of cars and food. Then It will cost more if you want different experiences up there.
weekend_recommendations: Go on hiking trips both in summer, autumn and winter! The nature is breathtaking, but remember to bring som good hiking boots. Surf trip, climbing (bouldering), Langrend and also Student samfundet is a big fun club for all students!
culture_adjustment: Norwegian culture is not far form the Danish, so it wasn't hard at all. Just a few language barriers and some things were done different.
socializing_tips: I was happy that KU gave us a list of other students going to the same destination, so you had someone to rely on in the beginning. Also going on different sport trips organised by NTNUI or ESN trips can get you some friends!
cultural_challenges: I don't think anything was that challenging.
culture_appreciated: The friendships I made, and the experiences in the Norwegian nature, which has revitalized my love and interrest for Biology. Also it was very fun to experience the Norwegian culture firsthand.
top3_advice: Contact the other students on the list that KU provides, so you have someone to hang with in the beginning at least. Don't be afraid to try out new sports or try something that sounds crazy, its gonna be fun either way! Save some money up or apply for different grants, so you don't have to worry about money while you're away.
other_useful_info: I can't think of any
most_rewarding: As mentioned, the experiences in the beautiful nature of Norway. Also meeting Norwegians from different parts of Norway, so you learned the different dialects of Norway.
greatest_challenge: Reading up for the exam for nearly 2 months, because there are 4 at the same time compared to block structure in KU in Denmark. Also the limited amount of sun in Trondheim (4,5 hours when it topped), also made the exam reading extra hard.

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne afsted med min kæreste, som ikke læser på KU. Skandinavien var et af de steder det var muligt og ret sikkert at vi begge kunne komme til. Vi valgte Trondheim, fordi det virkede som en fed studieby.
info_ease: Besværligt, men okay, endte med at finde ud af det hele.
arrival_assistance: modtog ikke noget
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Man tilmelder sig online.
registration_help: Man kunne skrive til en mail og spørge
registration_success: Jeg fik de kurser jeg ville, men eksamensdatoerne/undervisningen overlappede, så jeg endte med at skifte nogle kurser, hvilket jeg egentlig var glad for.
registration_advice: Find mange mulige kurser du kan tage og få forhåndsgodkendelser til dem, inden du tager derop. (jeg fik dog hurtigt svar på en ny forhåndsgodkendelse, jeg lavede efter semesteret var gået i gang, så det kan typisk lade sig gøre, selvom det måske ikke lige bliver plan A).
course_level: Fint level, nok ca det samme som på KU. Men jeg tror det kommer meget an på hvilke kurser man vælger!
teaching_comparison: Havde et online kursus, hvilket var pænt nederen, fordi så mødte jeg ikke nogen mennesker igennem det. Generelt havde jeg meget færre timer i Norge, det var mere selvstudie. Havde stortset kun forelæsninger, hvilket gjorde det svært at socialisere med medstuderende. Savnede helt klart nogle flere teoretiske undervisningstimer/opgavetimer og laboratoriearbejde (det havde jeg intet af), både for at få et socialt miljø, men også for at få et højere læringsudbytte.
courses_enrolled: Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience, 7,5 ECTS (online) Perspectives on Gender, 15 ECTS Genetics and Evolution, 7,5 ECTS
recommended_courses: Jeg brugte mine valgfrie 15 ECTS på Perspectives on Gender som er et humaniora kursus. Det var virkelig spændende, og gav en udfordring/frisk pust i og med at det er en anden måde at tænke på og studere på end i mit fag normalt (bioteknologi). Den kursusansvarlige er også vildt flink. Det er egentlig sat som et norsk kursus, men den kursusansvarlige er amerikansk og har engelske forelæsninger, og så havde jeg måske 2-3 forelæsninger på norsk og så 2-3 på dansk faktisk.
unexpected_costs: Nogle få ting vi skulle købe til lejligheden, selvom den var møbleret. Men man kan låne gratis møbler hos ReStore - stor anbefaling!
cost_comparison: dyrere: dagligvarer - mad, grøntsager. Billigere: nødder, fisk
activities_available: NTNUI er en (primært sports) forening for studerende og de har alt muligt man kan melde sig til, stor anbefaling! og man betaler kun 1 beløb for at være medlem og så har man adgang til fitnesscentre over hele byen og man kan melde sig ind i flere forskellige klubber som badminton, ultimate, dans, klatring, quiditch - you name it. Ville ønske vi havde et lignene koncept i KBH, det er virkelig fedt og billigt ift hvad man får for pengene. Så er der studentersamfundet (en slags studenterhus med mange barer og klubber osv), hvor der også arbejder mange frivillige og der bliver holdt fester, koncerter, quiz aftener, talks - alt muligt. Erasmus Social Network Trondheim (ESN) arrangerer events og ture for internationale studerende, tag til deres ting! Der er virkelig mange ting man kan melde sig til, det er bare det med at beslutte sig.
activities_recommended: Meld dig ind i en sportsforening eller noget andet frivilligt. Vi gik til Ultimate - det var rigtig hyggeligt.
weekend_recommendations: Tag til Dovrefjell og vær heldig at møde Moskus okser... Lofoten er vildt smukt, skal helt sikkert tilbage! Beseggen - mega flot vandrerute, ikke for de højdeskrække. Tag på en guidet glestjer tur fx Nigardsbreen. Stå på ski evt langrend ved Skistua (i Trondheim) Tag på hyttetur i en NTNUI Koine (typisk uden rindende vand eller elektricitet) Rockheim er et hyggeligt museum, hvis man godt kan lide musik historie. Tag til ESN arrangementer for at møde andre internationale studerende.
culture_adjustment: Nemt, nordmænd er danskere bare 2.0.
socializing_tips: meld dig som frivillig et sted, tag på studentersamfundet
cultural_challenges: Nordmænd er bare vildt trænede/i god form alle sammen. De er vildt gode til at stå på ski, har vandret i bjergene siden de var 2 år gamle. De er bare lidt mere hårdføre. Synes faktisk det var ret svært at forstå norsk... selv i Norge er Trondheim og Trøndelag kendt som en område med en dialekt der er svær at forstå - så bliv venner med folk fra sydnorge, de snakker nærmest dansk...
culture_appreciated: Naturen! Det var så smukt over det hele, de flotte bjerge osv. Sneen, de havde rigtig sne.
top3_advice: a) Meld dig til noget socialt heroppe, selve studiet/undervisningen ligger ikke op til så meget socialt. b) Nyd naturen! c) I eksamensperioden så skal man ankomme tidligt på dagen for at få pladser i bibliotekerne, sådan kl.8 eller tidligere...
other_useful_info: Nej
most_rewarding: At bo i et andet land (og en anden by), at opleve den norske natur og bo tæt på den.
greatest_challenge: Følte mig ensom til tider, og havde nogle helbredsmæssige komplikationer undervejs, hvilket ikke gjorde det nemmere. Og så egentlig selve planlægningen op til at skulle afsted, når man så var deroppe så gik tingene jo fint.
other_comments: Nyd det, jeg vil helt klart anbefale at tage til Trondheim! Det er en virkelig hyggelig by med en masse kultur og liv (barer, koncertsteder, cafeer, markeder, festivaler), tæt på naturen, ikke så turistet. Det er i den grad en studieby.

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: I looked for a city that would be close to nature, but still well connected and that had good student-opportunities. I was also looking for a university that had some of the course I thought of taking in Copenhagen.
info_ease: It was quite easy, there were some meetings designed for exchange students, and we also got most of the information by email.
arrival_assistance: We didn't receive any personal assistance per say. But we did attend a lot of different meetings and different welcome-to-Trondheim events that provide the needed assistance to get around town and figure out how the university works compared to UCPH.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You had to sign up for the class and the exam on a website called Studentweb. It was also possible to sign up/switch classes after you had signed up, until a specific date.
registration_help: If in need, you could talk with a studivejleder.
registration_success: I got all of the classes that I wanted to attend.
registration_advice: You will probably not end up with the exact list of classes that you decided upon at home. Take your time during the first month to find the ones that you think are interesting and also offer a good teaching schedule.
course_level: Most of my classes were of Intermediate level II.
teaching_comparison: NTNU only offers lectures - there is no aftermath during a group-classs-project or teaching in smaller groups. You will have to do a lot of self-studying.
courses_enrolled: Immunology - Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience - Medical Molecular Bacteriology - Psychological Disorders.
recommended_courses: I liked all of my courses, but most of all Immunology. The course was very fulfilled and it seemed a bit harder than the other courses that I had. The condensed introduction to Neuroscience class was actually online, which I though was a bit of a shame. But it was still quite interesting and the book that they advice is very good. The Molecular Medical Bacteriology was a bit confusing. We also had to do a bioinformatics exercise, which I didn't quite understand - but mostly because we did it on a platform that no students really knew how to use. The class focuses on sequencing methods and their use in the diagnosis of presence of bacteria. The psychological disorders course was in Norwegian, which was fine to understand. I though it was really interesting and I picked it even though it is not entirely related to my BA degree. I chose the course out of pure interest.
unexpected_costs: Some things were more expensive than in Denmark, but most of it is very similar. I went on a few more small trips than I at first had anticipated. But I'm very grateful that I did.
cost_comparison: Housing was a bit more expensive than expected. This was mostly because the rent becomes higher when you are only staying for 6 months. Most people only offer 1 year contracts.
activities_available: All sorts of activities are avalaible through the NTNUI (NTNU Idræt), the ESN (Erasmus Student Network) and a lot of other smaller clubs such as the Surfing-club, the Ski-club etc.
activities_recommended: Go on trips!!! And sign-up for some gym classes with your friends!.
weekend_recommendations: Go on a hike with some of your new friends :)
culture_adjustment: It was very easy (mostly because Denmark and Norway are quite similar).
socializing_tips: I unfortunately did not meet that many local students...
cultural_challenges: The currency of the norwegian crown being higher than the danish crown.
culture_appreciated: All Norwegian people seem to be sports-enthusiast that spend their free time in the outdoors.
top3_advice: Look at the course catalogue before hand, find some friends (show up at the introduction parties and welcome committees), and enjoy the nature!!!! And sign up for NTNUI it really gives you a great deal of opportunities for all kinds of sports!
other_useful_info: I do not think so.
most_rewarding: Meeting such great people in another country. Learning a different way of attending university and studying, than what I have been used to. I really really enjoyed being able to spend so much time outdoors and enjoying the beautiful nature of Norway. Put the "ja-hat" on!
greatest_challenge: Having to navigate in school studies, but also spending time with friends, experiencing new things everyday, keeping up with your sports, going on trips and calling home.
other_comments: No further comments

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: Aspects include course opportunities, language, nature experiences, and the country's culture.
info_ease: The assistance was great, and you were provided with all the necessary information.
arrival_assistance: There were some information meetings during the intro week, some info flyers, and detailed emails.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration seemed complicated at first since you have a lot of information to keep track of. But NTNU's own platform made it easy enough.
registration_help: Different contact mails/people, if needed.
registration_success: For me easy, but it was luck that since many had trouble switching around so their schedules and exams would not overlap. On the bright side, there were a lot of time to decide, so you could try out different classes before deciding.
registration_advice: You have a good time deciding, so don't stress.
course_level: The BA levels were perhaps a bit lower than expected but might be due to the fact that it was introduction courses. The MA level was harder than expected, but very giving.
teaching_comparison: The lectures were pretty much the same style. However, I experienced a lot fewer lecture-exercises, which is very common at KU and a nice way to work with the learning material.
courses_enrolled: 1. Introduction to Neuroscience (15 ECTS). 2. Immunology (7.5 ECTS). 3. Intorduction to molecular medicine (7.5 ECTS).
recommended_courses: Introduction to Neuroscience. This course was very big, but all lectures were online, making it very flexible (at the same time, the downside of the course), and the exam was easy to get through. Otherwise, Immunology was probably my favorite course with a supporting exercise classes and just overall interesting subjects.
unexpected_costs: Cost to nice outdoor clothes and shoes.
cost_comparison: Beer and alcohol were pretty expensive. Fish and mushrooms was less expensive than in Denmark
activities_available: A lot of social activities through Studentersamfundet, NTNUi (idræt), and ESN with opportunities both for nice trips in Norway, different sports clubs, or just social groups for almost everyone.
activities_recommended: A trip to Lofoten, either arranged privately or through ESN. Also, visit a koi through NTNUi which has small cabins you can visit.
weekend_recommendations: Again, visit Lofoten. Enjoy the city. Go on a hike in Bymarka or other places where you can find a small cabin to eat waffles.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, since the culture is vary like one in Denmark.
cultural_challenges: It was a challenge that people were so bad at taking the bus without blocking the whole bus and not making room for other people (when there were a lot of free space).
culture_appreciated: Their love for nature and active lifestyle.
top3_advice: 1. Bring good footwear, you will not regret it. 2. Remember to enjoy and travel the country. 3. Try to get a room and live with Norwegians. Otherwise, you won't get in contact with them that easy.
other_useful_info: Just do it.
most_rewarding: The overall experience. The people.
greatest_challenge: If it gets icy on the street.

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: That i felt it was a destination that offered a welcoming vibe towards exchange students, meaning that it was quite sure that you found some good communities to engage in
info_ease: It was quite easy. The home institution made sure that we knew what to prepere and NTNU also provided some extra information when we arrived.
arrival_assistance: During the first week we had "lectures" about the things we were responsible for getting in order ourselfs. And also different organisations told os about different opportunities to join different trips and communities. We had information meetings and get sent checklists - these were very helpfull
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You are responsible for signing up for classes and exams yourself. Therefore you have to check that exam dates don't overlap. This was a little difficult as the dates were visible quite late. Other than that it was okay easy.
registration_help: You could find good help at NTNU's website
registration_success: I got all the classes that I wished for.
registration_advice: Look at NTNU's webpage for help if you need it. It will probably be there.
course_level: I think the level was okay, maybe a little easier than what I usually experience in Copenhagen.
teaching_comparison: At NTNU, I didnt have classes where we had "øvelsestimer" which I've had in most of my courses at UCPH
courses_enrolled: FARM3003: Pharmaceutical Innovation INTRO175: Introduction to Norway MOL3014: Nanomedicine 1 MOL3023: Molecular Bacteriology
recommended_courses: I was very happy for the INTRO175 course as it was a nice way to get a broad understanding of Norway. It also had some good teachers.
unexpected_costs: Norway has a lot of beautiful sites that it really cool to experience. But taking trips can also be a little expensive. My advice is to try and plan some of them yourself (except if it's through NTNUI), as you often can do it cheaper that when signing up with an organisation.
cost_comparison: I had heard a lot about that food should be really expensive, but I actually didn't think it was a lot different from in DK.
activities_available: There's NTNUI who provides a group/community for pretty much every kind of sport/activity
activities_recommended: I joined the "NTNUI Topptur og Frikjøring group" who had training sessions every monday - this was really fun (and hard). I also joined the "NTNUI Surf Group" for a surftrip to Hoddevik in November, I can really recommend this!
weekend_recommendations: Go see all of Norways beautiful nature!
culture_adjustment: It was okay easy, I don't think it is much more different from in Denmark.
cultural_challenges: I actually can't come up with anything..
culture_appreciated: The many and easy opportunities for getting outdoor experiences!
top3_advice: 1: start as soon as possible to look for housing and get your exchange documents in order, it is nice to have this in order! 2: join every opportunity you get to go on trips and experiences, it is probably more cool than you would have thought 3: don't feel stressed or get fomo, you will reach everything
other_useful_info: Join NTNUI!
most_rewarding: The experiences I had with the other exchange students
greatest_challenge: To focus on school when there were so many nice people and things to do

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: It was important to me that the city was one I wanted to experience. That I had a sense of security, that there was a good study environment, and that I could get an Erasmus.
info_ease: I think the university I was going to attend gave good information. However, I think many things were unclear about mobility-online, OLA, etc. Difficult systems, and sometimes not so good instructions.
arrival_assistance: There was no direct assistance, but there was an introductory week for exchange students, where you had the opportunity to meet others and also received a lot of information.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It's a long and somewhat troublesome process. Fortunately, you can get help with registration, but I would definitely recommend that you sit down well in advance and look into it.
registration_help: You could write to them. It could take days for them to respond, which could be frustrating, so again, be out there well in advance and maybe ask someone who has been there before or is going there.
registration_success: It went well. I got all the subjects I wanted.
registration_advice: Be out in good time, familiarize yourself with things.
course_level: Since I'm on my bachelor's, I was only allowed to take equivalent courses for my bachelor's. I took four different subjects and although they were all the same level, they varied a lot in difficulty, etc.
teaching_comparison: Several of the subjects were very different, but it also depends on what degree you are taking. I am used to "classroom teaching", where you are expected to participate, do group work, etc. - there was really none of that here.
courses_enrolled: Childhood studies, Introduction to Norwegian history, personality psychology and social psychology
recommended_courses: I would recommend them all. But the psychology courses was difficult and challenging - but interesting!
unexpected_costs: You must be prepared for the fact that there will be a lot of expenses in the beginning, especially associations, memberships, etc.
cost_comparison: Many people think Norway is expensive, but it's actually not that expensive - very similar to Denmark. Transportation is much cheaper, shopping, fitness. On the other hand, food is a bit more expensive and restaurants are a bit more expensive - but not much more expensive than Denmark.
activities_available: The university had a lot of different associations. There is something for everyone. In general, the city is known for being a student city and there is a hugely good student life with lots of opportunities for different activities for students.
activities_recommended: Erasmus Student Network has a lot of cool trips. Their associations also have a lot of different things. They had some cool fitness centers with a lot of different fun teams, and then they have the Student Society, where everything happens (everything from concerts, music quizzes, lectures, etc.)
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips outside the city. There is a lot of beautiful nature to experience. Stay in a cabin, hike, ski, etc.
culture_adjustment: Since Norway and Denmark are very similar to each other, it was very easy to adjust.
socializing_tips: Associations through NTNUI and "Studentersamfundet"
cultural_challenges: Not anyone at all.
culture_appreciated: I found the Norwegians very welcoming, smiling and helpful. They are very active and "healthy", which I also found inspiring.
top3_advice: Spend your free time in the nature around you, spend a lot of time at the "Studentersamfundet", take advantage of the fact that it is a city with a lot of students - feel the student life.
other_useful_info: Not immediately, no.
most_rewarding: Not immediately, no.
greatest_challenge: I found the exam period tough. I'm not used to having four different exams, so it was challenging. I quickly got along with other students from my "home university", so I didn't find socializing, which can normally be difficult, so challenging.

culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: Maybe joining sports or other social activities/clubs.
cultural_challenges: That shops are closed on sundays, I kept forgetting.
culture_appreciated: The hiking.

most_rewarding: Making new friends and trying new things.
greatest_challenge: Keeping my calm and prioritising the experience over grades.

course_level: MOL3023 Molecular Medical Bacteriology (MA) MOL3005 Immunology (MA) KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses (BA) NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience (BA)
teaching_comparison: KLH3101 Obesity, got turned into a self study course due to low attendance (only 3 people were taking the course) which i haven't tried before at UCPH and NEVR2030 Neuroscience was entirely through zoom. otherwise my courses followed similar structure as UCPH

recommended_courses: MOL3023 Molecular Medical Bacteriology (MA) - Interesting course going through most common bacterial infections and bioinformatic methods of detection and sequencing. i chose this course for the bioinformatics MOL3005 Immunology (MA) - I really recommend this course. well structured and interresting KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses (BA) - A broad understanding of obesity and a visit to an obesity clinic where we got to scan our own bodies. sadly the course become self-study NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience (BA) - when it says introduction, it really is introduction. all lectures through zoom were recorded which gave a great amount of freedom for planning trips

Røros also has a very lovely christmas market you can visit in the start of december.

It still found it interesting but i belived i would have learnt more if there lectures was not selfstudy. MOL3000 Introduction to Molecular Medicine did not feel like a master course. We have learnt a lot of the meterial before or the new stuff is not on a higher level from what we already know. NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience is a bachelor course. We have already learnt parts of the curriculum of the course in the first two years of molbo. Dont be afraid of taking only master courses - the level is not different from what we already know.
teaching_comparison: Most courses just have lectures. In each course you often have to do either one presentation or hand in a paper. Some courses have class work as well.
courses_enrolled: NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses MOL3000 Introduction to Molecular Medicine MOL3005 Immunology
recommended_courses: MOL3005 Immunology was really interesting and good. KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses the course was really interesting. Was a bit sad that it became a self-study course so if there are more students that signs up for it i would really recomend it. NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience - is good if you want a course on the "easier" side but you still learn some. Also a good option to take it on 15 ECTS points instead of 7,5 to have one course less to focus on.
unexpected_costs: No unexpected costs but make sure you have a good insurance that will cover if there is any accidents
cost_comparison: Food and alcohol are more expensive than in denmark. I didnt spend any money on books because we could find them all online.
activities_available: A lot of different sports club. The ESN network also organize different social events. In generel Trondheim fells like a city made for the students so the student life there is really good and you have a lot of different opertunities.
activities_recommended: From the begining go on the cabintrips and so on. The time goes by super fast so try and join as much as you want form the begining. Get a membership card to samfundet - you do not need it for ESN.
weekend_recommendations: Go to lofoten if you have more time. There is also a lot of different places you can go nearby trondheim.
culture_adjustment: Same culture as in denmark so very easy.
socializing_tips: Just try and be open and go to the social events. It feels a bit eaiser to get to know other exchange studetns and local students.
cultural_challenges: No
culture_appreciated: They are really kind.
top3_advice: Make the most out of it from day one. Before you know it its december and you are going home again. Rember when you decide which courses you want also to look at the exams dates. A lot feels the same as in UCPH so dont stress about it and take it as a good thing so you can spend the energy on yorur courses, the people you meet and all the experience you are gonna get.
other_useful_info: The earlier you start looking for housing the cheaper i think you can get it but dont stress about it.
most_rewarding: The people i met.
greatest_challenge: Its hard to say goodbye to the place and the people you meet there when you go home again.

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: To come to a city, where I could study and be close to nature at the same time.
info_ease: A bit frustrating. NTNU, KU and Erasmus will send a lot of relevant but sometimes confusing information. Tip: Read the mails twice and create an inbox just for exchange emails so they don't get lost. You get a lot of links, usernames and codes that you need at different times
arrival_assistance: We got information emails, had a physical welcome meeting and a webpage called "NTNU GO" where there were some relevant information.
arrival_comments: NTNU really wants to inform you, but sometimes forgets the most basic information, such as "what is a FEIDE user, when do you get your email and where do you check your course information" because there is SO much to know. Give it time and be patient :)
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I found courses via the NTNU course catalogue. Here I encountered several challenges because NNTU had not stated which academic level the courses were for, so I had to apply for approval of courses in two rounds. NTNU has subsequently added the option to their course catalogue, so that you can apply for courses that suit your academic level. At the same time, it took a long time before I was told that I had been accepted into the courses (2 months), which is completely normal, so again: be patient.
registration_help: Email-support and sometimes you could find some information on NTNUs webpage, but it is big, deep and confusing with several dead ends.
registration_success: Very successfull, it got both courses that I had as top priorities.
registration_advice: Be patient, search for many different courses, consider the exam-form of the courses, as they can be a bit weird. You can also search for the course on »karakterweb.no«
course_level: I was a bit disappointed with the level. One of my subjects in particular (VL3000) moved at a very fundamental level of applying and understanding theories (such as constructivist vs. behaviorist conceptualizations) rather than discussing the theories against each other and how they can contribute to a greater understanding in interaction. It was at times far too basic, which was frustrating.
teaching_comparison: Mostly power-point lectures, sometimes with groupwork, most of the times not.
courses_enrolled: KULT3305 Teorier om kjønn, likhet og forskjell VL3000 Vilkår for læring i arbeidsliv og samfunn
recommended_courses: KULT3305 Teorier om kjønn, likhet og forskjell was great! It presented exciting and relevant theories and understandings of gender, body and inequality such as race and orientalism.
unexpected_costs: Many apartments are heated with electric radiators, and when it gets winter it can get a bit expensive if you live in an older wooden house like it did.
cost_comparison: Food and beverages = especially beer is expensive.
activities_available: Trondheim has some great student opportunities likes NTNUI (Sports organisation for students) and Studentersamfundet, which is an amazing building holding a lot of different events, parties, debates etc. The local campuses does also have organisations and student associations. Right next to the city is Bymarka, which is a lovely and peaceful forest area with lakes, hills and valleys, where you can hike, tent, go running in the summer and ski in the winter. There goes buses (18) and tram (Trikken) up there everyday.
activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend joining NTNUI. You can get a cheap membership as a half-year exchange student, where you have access to their training centers, and their various sub-organizations such as diving clubs, hiking groups. NTUI also owns several different cabins, which are located out in the mountains and forests around the city, which you as a member of NTNUI can rent very cheaply. I also recommend going to Bymarka, I have loved that area.
weekend_recommendations: Go to bymarka and see if you can finde the mooses. There are different cabins in Bymarka that sell coffee and waffles, which are incredibly cozy to go to in both summer and winter. I also recommend becoming a member of NTNUI, especially the cabin group called "Koiene" where you can go on hikes to the cabins mentioned. Here you can also join in on various volunteer activities where you help paint and work on the cabins together with other young people, and it's incredibly fun.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, but I am danish, and I understand swedish and norwegian easily and that gave me an advantage to adjust quickly.
socializing_tips: Do NOT join the ESN Group (Erasmus Student Network). Their activities (such as trips to Lofoten and various parties) are presented as "once-in-a-lifetime" opportunities, but it is expensive and here you are only with other exchange students, instead of meeting local young people. The same goes for apartments and the room rented through the university organization (called SIT) - if you want to meet locals, you have to live with them. Otherwise it becomes a small international exchange bubble.
cultural_challenges: Norwegians can be a little more reserved in their attitude towards new people. It's not that they don't like talking to strangers, but they just have to look someone over before they take them in. All shops, restaurants etc. close on Sundays, and it requires you to think ahead sometimes because nothing is open. The city can therefore also feel quite dead on Sundays if you don't make plans or enjoy a nice quiet day at home
culture_appreciated: The nature!
top3_advice: 1. Be patient with NTNU 2. Be open to the fact that your exchange may not go exactly as you planned, but that doesn't mean it wasn't a succes! 3. Set a flexible budget. Norway is expensive on the long run.
other_useful_info: NTNU can be a bit chaotic and confusing with their different student accounts and webpages – Be patient<3 It gets dark in november and december. Remember to get out and absorb some sun, when it is there.
most_rewarding: To go on trips and hike in the mountains and forests every week and to get local friends <3
greatest_challenge: Finding a good place to live.
other_comments: Do it! Go to Trondheim! :)

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte Trondheim, fordi jeg havde fået den anbefalet som studieby. Byen har en god størrelse (hvor man kan lære den godt og kende, og der er ting at opleve, men den er heller ikke kæmpestor), og byen ligger klods op ad skoven. Jeg vægtede højt at vælge en by, som ligger tæt på naturen.
info_ease: Synes der var overvældende meget information før afgang, men hvis man bare tager en ting af gangen, så går det fint. Man kan heldigvis få hjælp både gennem KU og NTNU og snakke med andre søde udvekslingsstuderende, som enten kan hjælpe eller er lige så forvirrede som én selv.
arrival_assistance: Der var en del infomøder for nye udvekslingsstuderende den første uges tid, og så får man et hav af mails med informationer og login-oplysninger, men jeg modtog ikke hjælp udover det. Den største hjælp var at tale med de udvekslingsstuderende, jeg boede med, fordi der var ting, de forstod, som jeg ikke gjorde og omvendt.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Jeg kan simpelthen ikke huske, hvor og hvordan man registrerede sig, der var så mange trin. Men jeg kan anbefale at komme til infomøder og, som nævnt, at snakke med andre udvekslingsstuderende:)
registration_help: Der er massere af hjælp at hente på NTNU. Tror der er et kontor, hvor man kan møde op og få hjælp og ellers kan man skrive dem en mail. Man skal ikke være bange for at spørge om hjælp.
registration_success: Jeg havde søgt 6 kurser gennem NTNU hjemmefra. 4 af dem blev accepteret. 2 gjorde ikke, fordi de enten krævede tidligere ansøgning (svært når man ikke kan søge tidligere som udvekslingsstuderende) eller ikke blev oprettet det semester. Men da jeg mødte op, viste det sig, at mange af fagene overlappede i skemaet, så jeg var nødt til at søge nye kurser. Enten med at udskifte alle pånær ét.
registration_advice: Du har sikkert hørt det før, men lad være med at gøre dig alt for umage med dit kursusvalg hjemmefra. Jeg lyttede ikke selv til det her råd, og følte hjemmefra, at jeg havde en god plan, men den gik så helt i vasken, da jeg dukkede op:) Uanset hvor grundigt, du læser kursusplanen og sikrer dig, at fagene ikke har overlap i skemaet osv osv, så sker der ændringer, før man starter, og pludselig bliver nogle af fagene ikke oprettet, skemaet bliver ændret, osv. Selvom det virker meget officielt, når man søger om forhåndsgodkendelse af kurser gennem KU og laver Learning Agreement og den slags, så kan det hele ændres, efter man er kommet frem. Så bare vælg nogle kurser nogenlunde indenfor dit fagområde og vent med at tage ordentligt stilling, til du starter på universitetet.
course_level: Jeg tog to bachelorkurser og to kandidatkurser. Jeg synes godt, at jeg kunne mærke forskel i niveauet, og generelt var bachelorkurserne en del lettere end kandidatkurserne.
teaching_comparison: Det varierede fra fag til fag, lidt ligesom det gør herhjemme. Nogle kurser (introduction to Norway fx) har udelukkende forelæsninger, intet gruppearbejde, ingen afleveringer og den slags. Mens mine øvrige fag havde gruppearbejde, fremlæggelser og nogle også et par afleveringer. Men generelt er de fleste undervisningsdage almindelige forelæsninger, som man er vant til det på KU, og så krydret med lidt gruppearbejde som skal munde ud i en aflevering eller fremlæggelse.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Norway (Intro175) - Natur, Miljø og Bærekraft (BI2081) - Resource Utilization in Food Systems (MATV4004) - Quantitative Analyses in Ecology and Evolution (BI3051)
recommended_courses: Natur, Miljø og Bærekraft var mit yndlingsfag. Jeg synes, det var dejligt at have et fag på norsk for at lære sproget bedre at kende og for at omgås en masse nordmænd. Jeg synes desuden at forelæsningerne var meget varierede med mange gæsteforelæsere og spændende indhold og at de faglige krav til gruppearbejdet ikke var særligt høje. Eneste minus var, at der var obligatorisk fremmøde til forelæsninger, og de tog fravær, hvilket føles meget folkeskoleagtigt. Jeg lærte meget af kurset Introduction to Norway. Forelæsningerne er møg-kedelige, men der er kun én hver anden uge (!!!! crazy). Lærebogen er tilgengæld rigtig spændende, og jeg synes, jeg lærte utrolig meget om Norges historie og Norge-Danmark relationen. Resource Utilization og Quantitative Analyses vil jeg ikke umiddelbart anbefale. Fine nok fag men ikke vildt godt strukturerede af forskellige årsager. Jeg ville ønske, at jeg havde taget et kursus om akvakultur. Det er et emne, der går igen i ALLE fag, fordi det er så vigtigt for den norske økonomi, og jeg ville ønske, at jeg vidste mere om det.
unexpected_costs: Ikke rigtig nogen. Priserne var som forventet.
cost_comparison: Kan virkelig anbefale at bruge bycyklerne. Vildt billigt! Tror jeg gav ca. 100 dkk for et semester (kunne bruge dem fra august til de lukkede ned for vinteren i midt/slut november). Det er dyrt at købe månedskort til bus, men det er det jo også herhjemme.
activities_available: Så mange gode muligheder for at melde sig i sportsklubber og hobbyklubber. NTNUI-hjemmesiden har en oversigt over alle de sportsklubber, der er. Desuden er Samfundet et nice studenterdrevet sted til fester, bingo, quizzer osv. SiT træningscenter er billigt for udvekslingsstuderende, jeg gav 1000 dkk for et halvt år.
activities_recommended: Jeg synes, det var nice, at fitnesscenteret (SiT) kun bruges af studerende, så alle er unge. Mange fede hold som step og cykling (man behøver ikke spinningsko for at kunne bruge cyklerne) og høvdingebold, haha. Synes det var nice at tage til træning med andre, jeg havde mødt. Desuden vil jeg anbefale Swing og Folkedans-klubben, hvor jeg gik til begynder Swing én gang om ugen. Rigtig hyggeligt og en god måde at møde en masse lokale på.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på hikes i Bymarka, besøg Korsvika strand, osv. Lad være med at stresse over at se hele Norge, mens du er afsted, du kan altid komme tilbage.
culture_adjustment: Nemt, men nordmændene forstår ikke dansk. Man skal vænne sig til at tilpasse sit sprog en del, for at de ikke begynder at tale engelsk til én:))
socializing_tips: Ligesom i Danmark er de fleste nordmænd kun interesseret i hinanden, og folk som bliver boende i længere tid end 5 måneder, så det kan godt være svært at blive venner med de lokale. Jeg synes Swing og Folkedans var en god indgang til at lære nogen nordmænd at kende, samt at have kurser på norsk, hvor selvsagt alle på kurset er nordmænd. Desuden kan datingapps gøre, at man kommer i snak med lidt flere lokale;) haha
cultural_challenges: Ingen rigtigt.
culture_appreciated: At folk generelt er mere ude i naturen.
top3_advice: Ikke at planlægge for nøje, hvilke fag man vil tage, når man kommer frem:)
other_useful_info: Nej
most_rewarding: At være meget mere udenfor
greatest_challenge: Eksamensperioden som starter i begyndelsen af november. Når man er vant til blokstruktur, så var det læææænge at gå og læse til eksamen. Synes det var super kedeligt at sidde indenfor i 6 timer hver dag og læse op.

institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
crucial_aspects: The university's good reputation and the surrounding nature
info_ease: Very easy
arrival_assistance: A lot of social events at the beginning.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You register online on kunet portable after you find your desired courses in the catalog.
registration_help: There was a lot of information on their website and you could contact their offices and the course coordinator for any specific question.
registration_success: Kinda succesful but a had two courses that they stopped providing so I had to find to new ones.
registration_advice: You can check grades on this link: https://grades.no/
course_level: Only master courses. I had one course: Asset Pricing and Portfolio Management which was taught very differently as to what I'm used to and it was an extremely hard exam. As an exchange student be cautious before picking this course.
teaching_comparison: A lot of self studying. Hardly any people were to the lectures compared to the one mandatory lecture. Also in the hard one mentioned earlier he just wrote down math on a piece of paper every lecture which had no assignment to it and therefore no lecture slides other than the math on paper.
courses_enrolled: FIN3009: Asset Pricing and Portfolio Management BFIN4015: Sustainable Finance SØK3540: Political economy FIN3010: Empirical methods in corporate finance
recommended_courses: FIN3010: Empirical methods in corporate finance BFIN4015: Sustainable Finance Great courses and the exam form is just you writing a big assignment which you can start whenever. This of course is great if you just want to enjoy the exchange. However the lecture were also very informative especially FIN3010: Empirical methods in corporate finance
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: NTNU is a big sport University. The had the best gyms I have ever experienced for very cheap.
activities_available: Every kind of sport you can think of. Go check out NTNUI and you will also get an opportunity to talk to them the first intro day.
activities_recommended: Hiking of course and skiing. Also go watch a Rosenborg football game.
weekend_recommendations: Mentioned above
culture_adjustment: Easy
socializing_tips: I mostly socialized with exchange students. But for local student co-living and different clubs are the best places to meet norwegian students.
cultural_challenges: no
culture_appreciated: It's very safe.
top3_advice: 1. Go hiking and try not to pick the same hikes 2. Some sort of club also if you have never tried the specific sport before 3. Try to focus on the social and pick courses that are not to hard. The hard courses are no joke at NTNU.
other_useful_info: All the apps you need ATB: Public Transport Blackboard: Same as absalon Studentbevis: Mobile studentcard (a lot of places only accept the app and not even the physical card) Mazemap: To get around on campus which at times is very confusing SIT: For fitness
most_rewarding: Meeting new people and being able to be in beautiful nature. Also I saw a lot of nothern lights.
greatest_challenge: Being "alone". I had not forced myself the first couple of days to be very social meet other people my stay would have been awful.
