recommended_courses: I recommend both to Korean studies students!! Diffusion of the K-wave is good if you have an interest or knowledge about Korean popular media
unexpected_costs: The national Korean health insurance was mandatory and a bit more expensive than I expected. You can opt out of it only if you can prove you have a health insurance from your home country that covers ALL THE SAME THINGS. !! it might not be accepted if it doesnt cover certain things. And if you are sick and go to the hospital, the fees are pretty expensive.
cost_comparison: hospital, insurance: more food, shopping: less
activities_available: There were many activities for the exchange students!! They were hosted by "HUG" the exchange student club where you can meet many Korean and non-korean students. There were sports, cultural, cooking, theatre, dinner, talent show etc.etc.
activities_recommended: Definitely join the HUG activities! And join from the beginning so you get to know people. If you start joining them too late it might feel like people are already close imo
weekend_recommendations: Hiking, cultural and traditional things, travel domestically
culture_adjustment: Since I study Korean culture, it wasn't that difficult
socializing_tips: Meet your buddy, join HUG activities
cultural_challenges: Consider that sometimes you might be in a place where no one speaks English. Elders are very respected and you should always make room for them. You might feel stared at sometimes, but i think people are mostly just curious :)
culture_appreciated: The respect between everyone, the love for food and sharing food, the Korean 정
top3_advice: Use all the opportunities you are given, like joining clubs and events Consider opening a bank account if you want to shop online etc Its a really great uni and a great location!!
other_useful_info: Maybe think about how you're gonna get a SIM-card/Korean phone number before you arrive so you're not stuck with no data right away (though the public wifi is good)
most_rewarding: Learning a lot of the language and trying new things, understanding the culture
greatest_challenge: Missing your family, friends and everything you are familiar with at home

crucial_aspects: Paris was the perfect destination for me both personally and academically. I study Modern Culture and I am therefore very interested in culture and the cultural offerings in Paris are abundant. Moreover, I was contemplating moving to Paris after my studies so my exchange also helped me make that descision.
overall_comments: All the uni admin stuff is difficult and there was not much help from KU's side. France is known for its bureaucracy which was also demonstrated.
info_ease: Just emailed the coordinator at Sorbonne Nouvelle
arrival_assistance: Lot's of information - maybe to much to keep track of.
arrival_comments: The coordinatrice answers really quickly
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: All the uni admin stuff is difficult and there was not much help from KU's side. France is known for its bureaucracy which was also demonstrated.
registration_process: You have to find the timetables for the classes and then register either online or in person. It's a mess so also just show up to all the classes you want to take and talk to the professor.
registration_help: Lot's of different admin branches to contact - there is also an Erasmus help desk in the Lobby all semester!!
registration_success: Got all of my classes.
registration_advice: Go to the Erasmus help desk
academics_comments: All the uni admin stuff is difficult and there was not much help from KU's side. France is known for its bureaucracy which was also demonstrated.
course_level: Liked my classes overall. Loved three of them but did not care for the other three. The classes are insanely specific and nothing like the generalised 15 ects classes at KU that doesn't really go into depth at all. These go very much, and some of them a bit too much, into depth. Dropped one of the specific erasmus classes intended to improve your french skills and knowledge of France, because the teacher did not want to teach and told us it would be student presentation the entire semester. VERY LAZY!
teaching_comparison: It was much more like folkeskole tbh. Boring classroom teaching, weird child/adult dynamic between professor and students - even at masters level. Kind of odd. Had an English teacher and his way of teaching was similar to KU, except that the students did not engage very much and were obviously used to adult/child dynamic from their other courses.
courses_enrolled: M7IC201 TD 01 Médiacultures, A7SL401 Dissident Bodies in Contemporary Art, A9SL203 Virginia Woolf - The Waves, C9MG007 Queer Studies : Identités, Sexualités, Représentations(ang), M9IC201 TD 01 Industrie et culture de la mode, A9SL401 Writing Shame
recommended_courses: Any class taught by Nick Rees-Roberts - he is a really good teacher and incredibly knowledgable in cultural, film, fashion, and gender studies.
unexpected_costs: None really
cost_comparison: Train was more expensive than expected - but I also only bike in Copenhagen. You can bike here but I would not dare to do it myself - have seen 3 bike accidents (car or scooter driving into cyclist) while here because they are not yet used to bikes.
activities_available: They had sports classes, lots of art stuff. Student based clubs and activities. No student bar though
activities_recommended: The film club was fun. Met a lot of people, watched good movies, they also had panel discussions with actors and filmmakers.
weekend_recommendations: Use the city - museums are free for under 26 yo.
culture_adjustment: Relatively easy.
socializing_tips: Talk to them in class
cultural_challenges: Language probably. A lot of people don't want to speak french with you because they can hear that you are not native and therefore assume that you don't understand it very well. At other times when you really don't understand some people will not try to speak english or simplify it for you. Very mixed bag really.
culture_appreciated: The art museums and the general focus on good art everywhere. Whether that be street art, graphic design, posters, architecture etc.
top3_advice: If in doubt email the Erasmus coordinatrice or ask at one of the help desks. Classroom culture is very weird. Students are either patronised or cruel towards each other when it comes to criticism after presentations (there will be a lot of those) and they do not know what constructive criticism is. You have to bring your own pen and paper to the exam - did not know you had to bring your own paper and the teacher was annoyed that they had to go get some for the exchange students.
other_useful_info: You will be able to take really nerdy specific classes, but the academic level is not very high - but that is nice because then you don't have to study to hard and have more time to have fun in Paris.
most_rewarding: All the friends I've made and the three classes I took that I was really interested in and wanted to take before my exchange as KU does not offer anything like them.
greatest_challenge: Language, all the bureaucracy.
other_comments: Download the app shotgun so you can see what events and parties are happening - you often need to book a ticket. Also if you book a ticket for a nightclub and arrive before 12 it's usually free (otherwise is can be very expensive) Make a google maps over places to see and go and add every time you walk past something that looks nice. Go on a croissant tour - there is a croissant tour video on youtube - fun way to explore the different arrondissements.

crucial_aspects: I chose Paris because I wanted to learn French, and Paris was the only city that I had the option of going to. I chose Sorbonne Nouvelle specifically because they had an agreement with my department at the university, which I took to mean that they were specialized in cultural studies.
info_ease: Sorbonne Nouvelle offered more information than the other Parisian universities that my housemates went to. They seemed to be more accustomed to welcoming foreign exchange students.
arrival_assistance: The Erasmus coordinator was nice and answered any e-mail quite quickly, which was definitely a help.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: In the first week, all the departments offered introductions to their courses and how to enroll in them. Every department had their own system, some used Google forms, others e-mail etc. As all the courses on bachelor level are 3 ECTS, it was a challenge to create a coherent schedule, as I had to take 10 different classes and make sure that they didn't overlap.
registration_help: The Erasmus coordinator was very helpful. Furthermore, the administration was nice.
registration_success: I got the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Remember that if you register for back-to-back classes, that also means that you will have back-to-back midterms and exams.
course_level: Many of my courses were at an academic level that was equivalent to Danish high school. At the same time, though, the workload was very big. So I had a lot of work, but low academic outcome, which was frustrating. On the other hand, I guess it was alright that the academic level wasn't so high, since I was taking most of my courses in French, which I don't speak fluently.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style was more authoritarian. Some of my professors were nice enough, but others treated us students as children, ex. by scolding us if our classmates didn't show up for class. In some of my classes, oral participation was more about guessing what the teacher was thinking than doing any actual academic work. I found this very strange, as they taught humanities as if there was one true answer to a question. Furthermore, it was evident that the other students were not trained at all in doing independant academic work, which makes sense, as this was not encouraged at all.
courses_enrolled: Feel good littérature et development personnel, Cultures savantes et pop, Langues imaginaires et fiction, Littérature et jeunesse, Philosophie et science humaine, Creation divine d'homme, Politique britannique, Récits de la diaspora vietnamienne, Méthodologie et francais universitaire, Princesses dans la fiction
recommended_courses: Langues imaginaires et fiction was very interesting, the professor was good, the academic level was somewhat equivalent to a course at University of Copenhagen. Philosphie et science humaine was a course specifically for Erasmus students, so the level was very nice and the professor very professional and kind. Politique britannique was good because my professor was very competent, and the French style of teaching matched this field of studies better, where there actually is one correct answer to a question.
unexpected_costs: Prices on groceries are very high here - even higher than in Denmark, which was a surprise to me. Also, stuff like insurance, additional stuff for my room (duvet etc.) was surprisingly expensive. Also, you just spend more money on exchange than you normally would, when you have guests or go on day-trips.
cost_comparison: Groceries. Also, the French train system is punctual, but extremely expensive (outside of the city).
activities_available: Both sports and cultural activities such as cheap cinema tickets, theatre etc.
activities_recommended: I went a lot to an event called "Lost in Frenchlation", which had nothing to do with the university, but was a really fun thing to do with other exchange students, as their concept is that they show French movies with English subtitles.
weekend_recommendations: Going on daytrips is really nice, but train tickets can be expensive. Most museums are free for students, so that's nice. Also, just taking walks in the different neighborhoods is something I wish I'd done more. Going to get good food.
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy. The culture isn't very different. I was frustrated, though, by the infrastructure of the city, that made me very dependent on the metro system.
socializing_tips: The French students at my university were much nicer than I had anticipated. But you have to speak French, since most of them aren't comfortable speaking English.
cultural_challenges: The style of teaching at the university. In Denmark, we students are treated as adults, and I feel that my Danish professors respect me. Here, it's very different.
culture_appreciated: People in public spaces were most of the time very kind and helpful. Also, Paris is a much more diverse city than Copenhagen, which is freeing and interesting.
top3_advice: See if you can avoid having to take 30 ECTS in France, since that will (at least at Sorbonne Nouvelle) mean that you have to take 10 classes, which is just too much. If you aren't comfortable in French, try to take a few classes in English - it boosts your confidence to have a least a few classes where you can express yourself freely. If you're planning on taking only English classes, you should try to learn some French anyways, since it's very difficult to live or travel in France without speaking a basic level of French.
other_useful_info: The professors try to tell you that attendance is mandatory, but it's not, really.
most_rewarding: Improving my French level (although this as also been a straining process). Also, I've gotten a renewed appreciation for my home university (University of Copenhagen).
greatest_challenge: Since I'm not fluent in French, I struggled with feeling out of place and a burden to the people I talked to. Also, I got really frustrated with my university, and I felt that I had too much work to enjoy my exchange.
other_comments: Going on exchange to France is way more work than you normally imagine for an exchange semester. So you should really think it through before you choose to go.

activities_recommended: The cinemas is so great in Paris. They are old and beautiful and show great oldschool movies. The parcs are great too! If you live in the Cité universitaire in Paris, then there are a lot of awesome sport facilities!
weekend_recommendations: We went on some different trips in France, Bordeaux, which was so nice! Definitly recommend that! I was we had went on more trips.
culture_adjustment: It required som energy to begin with, but then it was just fun and i made some nice friends.
cultural_challenges: The language and the tempo of the city.
culture_appreciated: My new freinds and the awesom sport activities in the Cité universitaire.
top3_advice: Its confusing Its okay It will be fun too
other_useful_info: The course schedule and process is great stressfull, and it feels stupid having 10 courses, but its just how it is, and i will be fun too.

crucial_aspects: Crucial in choosing this study destination was the opportunities to learn the french language as well as the opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of french cultural. I was also very drawn by the idea of learning within the prestigous and well respected academics facilities of the sorbonne
info_ease: How easy it was to find relevant information was very depending on what it was concerning. Copenhagen university were good at displayed the information in an accessible manner. It was very varying how easy it was to gain relevant information from Sorbonne University.
arrival_assistance: I was invited to a introduction meeting for exchange studies.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Have my university had given me the nomination, I had to send a formel application to my host university: my application consisted of a recommendation from a teacher, a letter of motivation, my grades and a b2 language test. I also had to write what subjects I was interested in taking. What follows were many differents bureaucratic processes: the learning agreement for example
registration_help: The help consisted in mails from Outgoing Exchange and Sorbonne varying in accessibility. One could write to the head secratary for exchange. She was usually very helpful
registration_success: Once I was at the institution, was where the actual registration began. I got all the classes I wanted
registration_advice: My main advice would be "Be patient". You WILL get registrate, even if the process is chaotic and long, as it is of the interest of the university that you do. My second advice would be to talk to people who have already as well as people who are going and are in the same situation as you.
course_level: I took courses in English as well as courses in English. I found the academic level of the courses in French to match the level at home. I found the academic level of the courses in English to be general a bit (som times quite a bit) lower, that what I was used to.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was very distinctly different from what I was used. It was a teaching approach, which was less open and dialogical that the general teaching approach at UCPH. The teaching approach, one could say, is more one-sided and very much based on a proces of the teaching saying stuff and the students writing exactly what they are saying down.
courses_enrolled: I took the following courses: 1. Méthod de la civilisation 2. Société britannique 3. Arts et Médias 4. Cultures sérielles 5. Perfectionnement expression orale en tandem anglais-français 6. Art français 7. Cinéma et philosophie 8. Langue française - avancé B2 9. Le melodrame 10. Les cinémas anticoloniaux et postcoloniaux
recommended_courses: I would warmly recommend future exchange to take the courses specifically intended the exchange students. Mine were the following: Art français Cinéma et philosophie Langue française - avancé B2
unexpected_costs: There were no unexpected costs
cost_comparison: I found the general cost of living to me very expensive.
activities_available: There were various activities offered by the host institution. Unfortunately, I was not good at seeking them and therefore I dont know what was offered.
activities_recommended: As I didnt myself go to these activities, I unfortunately do not have a lot to recommend in this regard.
weekend_recommendations: I would absolutely recommend students to go to some of the small towns outside of Paris: The town of Monet's house and the town of Van Gogh. Going to the cinema is surpringly cheap in Paris, so I would recommend that as well.
culture_adjustment: I found it to be rather difficult. However it helpful a lot, that there were many in the same situation
socializing_tips: I would recommend to seek various WhatsApp groups made for exchange students to connect.
cultural_challenges: I did not fin the cultural differences particularly challenging - the differences were mostly just fascinating
culture_appreciated: I found the big "flaneur culture" and the cultural of going to meseums and to the cinema to be a very fun cultural praxis to embrace and engage in.
top3_advice: I was say the following: 1. Make sure to taake as many of the subject specially made for exchange students as possible 2. In order to make the work load slightly more barrable, I would recommend taking courses in English 3. As the workload is so high (10 courses which means 10 midterm exams, 10 final exams and several presentations and papers to be made) one very quickly how to take on a very light attitude towards academic performance, as the workload makes very hard to do perfectly in every subject (especially if you want to explore the city).
other_useful_info: Embrace French Cafe Culture!
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of bettering my french and my knowledge of French culture, through the courses in French I took.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge differently was the big workload (10 courses which means 10 midterm exams, 10 final exams and several presentations and papers to be made). Back home we usually only take 2 courses.

crucial_aspects: I have always wanted to live in Paris, since I love culture and the arts and it has played a significant role in shaping the arts and humanities.
overall_comments: I had some complications with my host university about not getting the classes that I originally wanted but it worked out in the end.
info_ease: It was quite easy to finde the information needed, however the information came quite late. So I could not prepare very much beforehand.
arrival_assistance: There was an introduction and intro package to the exchange students. Otherwise I found all the information needed on the website and Sorbonne.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had some complications with my host university about not getting the classes that I originally wanted but it worked out in the end.
registration_process: It was quite easy to be registrated at my host university, and when registrating for classes we just got a google doc to fill out.
registration_help: The administration for the department helped with finding courses, however they mostly spoke french which was a bit difficult.
registration_success: I did not get the classes I wanted because there was a technical issue with my registration and all the classes I wanted was full. However the administration helped me find other courses
registration_advice: Make sure that you sign up the classes that you want properly and before the deadling, otherwise there might not be any spots left.
academics_comments: I had some complications with my host university about not getting the classes that I originally wanted but it worked out in the end.
course_level: I thought the courses were a bit easier than what I'm used to and there was not as much course work and reading during the semester.
teaching_comparison: It was less lecture and more seminar style classes, which I liked. However, they count class participation as part of your overall grade which I'm not used to.
courses_enrolled: Writing the living land (ecocritic perspective on 19th century british literature) Entangled Artefacts (global history and material culture class) Other Stories (experimental American literature from the 20th century)
recommended_courses: I would highly recommend 'Other Stories' as a class, it was my absolute favourite
unexpected_costs: I didn't experience any unexpected costs
cost_comparison: I think I spend more on food and going out than I had initially thought I would
activities_available: You could both join different sports, there was a cinema club and language club and probably many more.
activities_recommended: I didn't try any.
weekend_recommendations: I really enjoyed visiting some of Paris museums, because there are so many and a lot of them are free for European students under 26.
culture_adjustment: I think it was quite easy but it would definitely help if you spoke just a little bit french.
socializing_tips: Try talking to them in class or join one of the class. I found some of my friends in class settings.
cultural_challenges: I think it really helps you on a daily basis if you know just a little french because at restaurants, bakeries and supermarkets they much prefer french.
culture_appreciated: The food and going out culture in France is great and there is so much good food and relatively cheap everywhere.
top3_advice: Apply for a room at Fondation Danoise in Cité Universitaire because then you're guaranteed a social environment and friends while you're here.
other_useful_info: If you want a really cheap lunch you can eat lunch at their canteen (Crous) for 3,5 euros.
most_rewarding: For me the most rewarding experience was being able to live and enjoy Paris
greatest_challenge: I think the greatest challenge was the french bureaucracy and how you really have to keep coming back and write a lot of emails for them to do something for you sometimes.

crucial_aspects: A big city with a rich cultural life
info_ease: If you contact the administration you will get the help you need. Otherwise you probably wont be able to find the information
arrival_assistance: The administration was helpful but very busy, and hard to get in touch with.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You wish for courses online, and they put you in the ones with enough space. At first I only got 19 ects points, but after many discussions with the administration I managed to get 7 more.
registration_help: The administration tried to help but as I said - the demand was bigger than the supply so they were not able to help me that much.
registration_success: Not very succesful.
registration_advice: Be prepared to attend random classes that you didn't expect. You are very lucky if you get accepted in the classes you want.
course_level: The level was fine - a bit lower than my home uni, but nothing crazy.
teaching_comparison: Its much more like high school than UCPH. 50% of the overall assessment is oral participation, which is very different from UCPH, where the final academic product defines your grade.
courses_enrolled: Civilization Seminar 1 - A7SCV11S01 Civilization Seminar 5 - A7SCV15S01 Literature Seminar 1 - A7SLT11S01 The Telltale Image: Exploring the Limits of Representation - V7CAB12S01
recommended_courses: All the courses were fine if you're interested in those topics.
unexpected_costs: Nothing really.
cost_comparison: I thought groceries would be cheaper, but its basically the same as in Denmark. Restaurants are cheaper.
activities_available: Movie screenings, theater, sports, museum trips.
activities_recommended: Idk I didn't use them. But try them if you want to meet other students.
weekend_recommendations: Go out and eat, and try the many nice bars and cafés in Paris - the city is full of nice places. Also the independent cinemas and beautiful museums.
culture_adjustment: The language is difficult to learn . other than that is very easy.
socializing_tips: Apply for accommodation in Cité Universitaire - I really enjoyed living there and got plenty of friends, which is why I didn't participate much in social activities in uni.
cultural_challenges: The language.
culture_appreciated: Its normal to help each other and speak to each other when you're out and about.

other_useful_info: Not really.
most_rewarding: To experience living in a different country. It was a first for me, and an experience im very grateful for.
greatest_challenge: To balance uni and social life. You want to spend as much time as possible in the city, but being busy with exams are a part of the experience in my opinion.

crucial_aspects: Living in a metropole, learning the language, learning the academic culture, getting to know Paris, getting to know french culture.
info_ease: Overall, the information was ok, but at times it seemed unclear who was responsible for each domain in the administration causing a lot of futile emailing back and forth.
arrival_assistance: I received e-mails about important dates and then there was an online introductory meeting on how to do the course inscription.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was a bit tiresome because you had to read across several documents instead of just one when putting together your schedule. Also the relevant documents were not always easy to find on the website.
registration_help: Emails and an online meeting.
registration_success: Very succesful, I had all the courses I applied for and, I realize having received my transcript of records, even one I didn't apply for.
registration_advice: It's a messy experience but be indulgent and patient and all will be fine.
course_level: I took 5 third year courses. The academic level was similar to the one at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: To a great extent, lectures and seminars at Sorbonne are based on one-way communication from the professor. This has it's advantages as the academic ground covered this way becomes larger, but on the other hand it doesn't activate the students as much.
courses_enrolled: Littérature et cinéma Littérature classique et moderne Écrire et penser la fiction Patrimoine culturel de la France La peinture en Europe, 1650-1750
recommended_courses: I would recommend the first to courses (Littérature et cinéma and Littérature classique et moderne) the most because the professor who taught these courses were really good and really seemed to care if we understood the subject matter or not.
unexpected_costs: None really
cost_comparison: Local transportation was a bit expensive I think. Bakeries and small grocery stores are cheap.
activities_available: I went to the Parismus events a couple of times.
activities_recommended: I would recommend to do some kind of sport. I did a bit of bouldering which was a good way to get to talk to some new people.
weekend_recommendations: Do small trips in France. The train tickets are really cheap and the TGV-trains are so fast that you can get to almost any french city within a couple of hours.
culture_adjustment: At first even just finding out where to do your grocery shopping and what to eat for each meal was a bit exhausting, but you quickly get a routine and get tips from others.
socializing_tips: Most of them are open to talk if you take the initiative.
cultural_challenges: I often found french rules and administrative procedures overly bureaucratic.
culture_appreciated: The life and the buzz in the streets and in the bars, cafés and restaurants.
top3_advice: You have to figure out a fair amount of paper work to actually get to study, but just take it easy, you'll be fine.
other_useful_info: Remember that you're an exchange student and don't have to live up to quite the same standards as the french students and as back home. You'll learn a lot just by being there and by completing the courses.
most_rewarding: To become friends with some french speaking people and do small trips and soirées with them.
greatest_challenge: Not having a network of actual friends around you and relying a lot on superficial relations.

crucial_aspects: Even though languages usually aren't a problem, I knew that choosing France would be a helping hand, as I am already fluent in French. The quality and reputation of Sorbonne University was also something that I had in mind as it not only was a personal challenge to attend and learn with some of the best students in France at Sorbonne, but the program and courses that I could take in Sorbonne were also perfect for my personal developement. Hence why I chose Sorbonne University.
info_ease: Everything was sent by mail so there was no problem there, the first day where all erasmus meet is also a benediction as you get to socialise and gather information so I highly encourage this practice to continue!
arrival_assistance: Any assistance was available on contact with the coordinators, I had a meeting with my coordinators and other Erasmus staff to make sure I had all the documents and information.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: On the main site of KU you can find the form to apply, after a brief exchange of mails you apply via Mobility-Online, get your OLA and the pre-aproval and finally you are good to go!
registration_help: The coordinators where there to help.
registration_success: I was very succesfull, I managed to get all of the courses I wanted
registration_advice: Be sure to have all the papers and all the certifications you need very well kept and be tidy about the paperwork
course_level: The courses were on a very high level but it was manageable and accessible for anyone (any academic student)
teaching_comparison: The french learning system is very different from the danish one, but since i was raised in the french system, i didn't have trouble with the change. The french system is all about the theory and learning every detail by heart whereas the danish system is all about teamwork, hands-on experience and less about learning every detail, with a special focus on being able to understand and explain the subject.
courses_enrolled: Physiology, Neurology, Maths, Ecology and Evolution, Biochemistry, Genetics, Animal Biology
recommended_courses: The course that i liked the most was Physiology as the balance between hands on and theory was very good and I learned a lot from the course. It is a very hard course though.
unexpected_costs: I think I had done my research well so I was aware of all the costs
cost_comparison: In general france is less expensive than denmark, I found that electricty bills could be quite extensive, but since it is winter, it might be why it was more expensive than expected.
activities_available: Sports were available and the erasmus community where always trying to go to a club or other activities.
activities_recommended: sports on campus (fencing, cheer, karate, judo etc..)
weekend_recommendations: visiting france is always a good idea, in paris, museums, sights as trocadero, the eiffel tower, le marais, etoile and le 15ème in general are always worth going to
culture_adjustment: As i was born and raised in Paris, it was very easy
socializing_tips: Participating in the erasmus events are very helpful!
cultural_challenges: I think the fact that people are less open at first changes from denmark
culture_appreciated: Parisian coffee culture is a must try for newcomers
top3_advice: Don't be afraid to ask people and get to know them! Explore the city/country you are in! Enjoy the french culture and make sure you get the most out of the stay, whilst studying
other_useful_info: I think it is important for the student to get contact with people and join all the whatsapp groups
most_rewarding: Finishing the term was very rewarding
greatest_challenge: mid term exams where very stressfull as you have to find the level of where the exam level is

crucial_aspects: Wanted to use french in an academic setting and live in Paris.
info_ease: Very difficult. No information from Sorbonne until the semester had already begun. Copenhagen University was not of very much assistance. Felt very lost in the beginning. No idea how to sign up for classes, wasn't invited to any orientation for incoming exchange students. Didn't get any "Welcome to Sorbonne" mails, letters, anything. Wandered helplessly around the halls of the university the first days of the semester hoping to find information, but found none.
arrival_assistance: Had a meeting with a coordinator who gave me my student ID and briefly explained how I could choose courses.
arrival_comments: Had no orientation and received no information before the semester had already begun. Very stressful not to know what's expected of you. Started classes a week and half too late.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Course registration starts after classes start. So you can attend classes even if you haven't registred formally. It was very confusing, had to send lots of e-mails to different people and fill out forms on paper to register.
registration_help: Haha, not sure there was any.
registration_success: Ended up with different courses than I had planned beforehand, but all good with the ones I picked when I was in Paris.
registration_advice: Just know that registration happens in september. For the rest, french bureaucracy is an experience, but no way around it.
course_level: Had courses in both level L1, L2 and L3 (1st year, 2nd year, 3rd year). All were interesting and challenging.
teaching_comparison: Very different. No reading to do before classes, but sometimes homework assignments. The professor gives a lecture and you write down what they say. No discussions, and students aren't really asked to participate. More tests during the semester - usually 2 per course.
courses_enrolled: 1. Grammaire et histoire de la langue française 2. Linguistique diachronique 3. Linguistique française 4. Apprentissage de la programmation 5. Sociologie des migrations
recommended_courses: My favorite course was Linguistique diachronique, especially the TD with Géraldine Veysseyre, where we looked at how french has evolved from latin to old french to modern french.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: We weren't asked to buy any books, so no spending needed for university. Paris is expensive - going out, doing things... Lots of museums are free if you're under 25.
activities_available: Don't know
weekend_recommendations: Take daytrips og weekend trips with the train or TGV. You can get cheap tickets and there are so many beautiful cities worth visiting in France just a few hours from Paris. I visited Rouen with a friend and loved it.
culture_adjustment: I grew up in Paris, so I wasn't all new to the city.
socializing_tips: Perhaps ask them to show you something or explain something. People are sweet and helpful.
cultural_challenges: The rigidness of the bureaucracy is very frustrating when you're danish and used to everything being centralized and fairly easy to access and understand.
culture_appreciated: Parisians go out a lot to restaurants, bars, cafés. Meeting with friends on a "terrasse" for a drink or a coffee - lovely.
top3_advice: 1. Don't stress about registration before you get to Paris. It happens after courses start - that's all normal. You can attend lectures you think you want to sign up for. 2. Make sure to pick at least one course on L3 level, because they're usually taught on the old campus which is such a beautiful old building and the lecture halls are so impressive. Usually L1 and L2 will be at the other campuses. 3. If you're going on the 4EU+ program, they might not invite you to the Erasmus orientation. Maybe ask if they can include you or something. They considered this program to be different when I was there.
most_rewarding: Just being in Paris and going to classes at the old Sorbonne. Woah, what a life.
greatest_challenge: Figuring out all the administrative stuff was frustrating and took much longer than I thought. Didn't get my Erasmus Grant until november.

crucial_aspects: I work in the art world and my dream is to combine the studies of art history and French culture studies. Paris is a historical centrum, so I saw it as an incredible possibility to go and study in the center of it all. The courses offered at the Sorbonne fit my study plans perfectly. In Paris I could study the culture and then visit it after class. The language aspect was also very important; to improve my French as much as possible by living with a French host.
overall_comments: It was a hard puzzle to get all the classes/schedule set up. There was not much help with that. The courses were incredible, but the grading was very strict based on the fact that I am an Erasmus student. The classes were very hard to pass even though I worked so hard.
info_ease: It was hard I general to get information on scheduling and classes or cancelation of classes. Some teachers used the online platforms and some didn't. It was a solo project - but I made it work! Parismus worked very well.
arrival_assistance: I received a date to go and pick up my university card and one e-mail with a zoom introduction to the faculty. It took a lot of work to plan out the classes in the different locations (many different Sorbonne buildings around town). Mostly help from other erasmus students, and then by learning the French way over time. Every teacher introduced every class and the plan for the semester during the first week.
arrival_comments: Mentioned in boxes further up.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It was a hard puzzle to get all the classes/schedule set up. There was not much help with that. The courses were incredible, but the grading was very strict based on the fact that I am an Erasmus student. The classes were very hard to pass even though I worked so hard.
registration_process: One short introduction to all the erasmus/parismus events at the Sorbonne - where I also received my student id and got my arrival note signed. One zoom meeting about how to create your schedule and apply to classes. a great Walk-in meeting at the art history faculté to sign up for the right classes. Other classes was done through e-mail and in person in class when giving the e-mail address.
registration_help: Zoom meeting in the beginning. E-mails to the eramus coordinators.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted, but it was very difficult to create the schedule. The buildings are scattered all over the city, so it was a bit difficult to create before testing it out. I chose to take classes in two different facultés - if I would redo it, I would chose one over two. I struggled getting the right info and dates for assignments on multiples classes. It was just a very different system.
registration_advice: Chose one faculté. test out the distance between buildings first.
academics_comments: It was a hard puzzle to get all the classes/schedule set up. There was not much help with that. The courses were incredible, but the grading was very strict based on the fact that I am an Erasmus student. The classes were very hard to pass even though I worked so hard.
course_level: If I wasn't a student of French culture and language back home, I would have found it very hard to understand context. But I am and it was great to see how well my danish education prepared me in terms of culural and historic context. The courses at the literary departement were also very interesting, but I was lacking a lot of background knowledge expected in these courses - elements thought during past semesters. I had a hard time understanding the assignment form - the work we had to hand in was very different than the danish forms. Forms / formats that the French have been learning since le lycée.
teaching_comparison: I truly enjoy the way "TD/CM" work; the grand lectures followed by smaller classes with room for details. The way the courses are set up is very logical, chronological and made sense for me who grew up in Belgian schoolsystem. A lot of info, but it makes sense. It was clear and logic.
courses_enrolled: Littérature: L2LM13FR - LITTERATURE COMPAREE « Le thème du double » - 8ECTS L4LI12FR : HISTOIRE LITTERAIRE XIX et XX 4 ECTS points Les Arts de la Renaissance (XVe-XVIe siècle) Emmanuel Lurin L4AA08PG_Art moderne 1 La peinture en Europ (1650-1750) Michaël SZANTO L4AA09PG_ART MODERNE 2 L4AA43PG_ Concepts, théories et métodes de l'histoire de l'art 1CM
recommended_courses: The art history courses were incredible. The courses called : littérature comparée at Malesherbes in le thème du double
unexpected_costs: the expensive navigo card, the enormous work and failed attempt to get the CAF support. Cheap to eat as one person.
cost_comparison: Shopping in supermarket was less expensive - more possibilities. high rent and expensive navigo card. Amazing free acces to museums ass a student in Paris.
activities_available: Jobs trough studies. Shared uni coffeshops and friday-bars. many other groups and theme nights organized at uni.
activities_recommended: A lot of museums have free entrance for students and classes at Bozart. I recommend to go and participate and meet some erasmus students.
weekend_recommendations: Go and see some art. Walk around Paris. Join the Erasmus events during the daytime. Ask questions about the schools assignment forms ; they are very strict and different, other requirements.
culture_adjustment: I speak fluent French, so it was easy to live as a local.
socializing_tips: It was hard to meet locals. the classes are not connected, so every class has new students and no breaks to socialize. The students are very young, they usually don't take gap years + they already know each other from high school. It takes a lot of work to enter the French circles.
cultural_challenges: Paris is a very private and intense city - many people on the go. It can almost be to easy to be lonely in Paris. You have to follow the Parisian flow and walk very fast.
culture_appreciated: I enjoy the French culture and language very much. I like the politness and respect in dialogues with strangers. My favorite thing about France is the appreciation towards art and the history/ culture of their country. In France you don't question if art is important or not. The past and spoken words exists everywhere from metro stop names to presidential speeches.
top3_advice: Save up a good sum of money before going. Apply for legater. Do not only prioritize school over social life - socializing and having people around is very important.
other_useful_info: Practice the local language as much as possible. when handing in assignments; The format is more important than the content. The format is very strict and decides your whole grade. Have a good French/cultural historic overview before.
most_rewarding: The art courses and the city experience. The flow of the city - the fact that there's always something to do in Paris. Studying in the most beautiful places and historic buildings. Studying art in a place that celebrates it.
greatest_challenge: The grading of the papers. I worked hours and hours on them but received very low grades even though I speak fluent French. The format is more important than the content.
other_comments: More guidance in the beginning of the semester would have been good. Especially some help with finding all the course overviews etc.

crucial_aspects: Academic opportunities, living in Paris, studying in French
overall_comments: I had an overall great experience.
info_ease: Not very easy. Be aware that all of August is summer vacation in France, meaning that it's impossible to get in touch with anyone at the university. I didn't get my official acceptance letter or any information before I had already arrived in Paris in September.
arrival_assistance: Not a lot. In the beginning of the semester I got invited to a meeting with the Erasmus coordinator (for the 4EU+ programme which is not the same as regular Erasmus at Sorbonne which is good to know), who gave me my student ID and access to the Sorbonne sites. But you need to sign up for the classes you want yourself by contacting each institute.
arrival_comments: I had to find most information myself. But Sorbonne has students sitting outside campus helping out with everything for the first month, so they are good to ask about practical stuff (but not administrative).
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had an overall great experience.
registration_process: You need to contact the UFR (kind of like the administration of the institute) where you would like to take your classes and give them the number and name of the class and your student number. If you take classes at different institutes you need to contact each UFR (e.g. the UFR of Philosophy for philosophy classes, the UFR of Sociology for sociology classes).
registration_help: Not much, it's possible to find the course catalogues on the Sorbonne website if you search a little, but everyone at the UFR are pretty good at replying e-mails if you have questions. The UFR of Sociology also sent me the course catalogue and the schedule so I could see when each course was.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Be aware that Sorbonne has different campuses all over the city, so remember to check the transportation time if you take classes in different campuses the same day.
academics_comments: I had an overall great experience.
course_level: The level of the courses was pretty high. The ECTS credits for each course is not as many as they are at KU, meaning that you'll need to take a lot of courses.
teaching_comparison: At UCPH you need to spend a lot of time studying and working alone, and not a lot in class. At Sorbonne it's the opposite. Also you have exams both in the middle and in the end of the semester and not only in the end.
courses_enrolled: Sociologie de l'environnement Sociologie des migrations et diversités des sociétés européennes Sociologie du droit Sociologie des inégalités Apprentissage de la programmation Philosophie politique Grammaire et histoire de la langue française
recommended_courses: For sociology courses I would especially recommend sociologie des migrations and sociologie des inégalités. I also recommend philosophie politique at the philosophy department since it's very sociological and interesting as well, and as a bonus they have one of the oldest and prettiest classrooms at Sorbonne. Also apprentissage de la programmation is how to program in Python which can be useful for statistics. I wouldn't recommend grammaire et histoire de la langue française unless you're very interested in the technicalities of linguistics.
unexpected_costs: Nothing.
cost_comparison: Paris can be a really cheap city to live in if you're a student. Most museums free, cinema/concert/theater tickets are a lot cheaper, you can eat at the university cafeterias (Crous) for 1 euro, coffee and eating at restaurants is a lot cheaper and there's a lot of offers for students like free fruits and vegetables once a week. I also recommend getting a velib' card (city bikes) it's 3 euros a month, and then you can use bikes all over the city whenever you want. Also, you don't need to buy books since you can download everything once you get a library card or borrow physical copies at the Sorbonne library. I bought a few books because it was nice to be able to write notes in them but it's not necessary and even if you do, it's a lot cheaper than buying books in Denmark.
activities_available: Sorbonne has a million associations, I think there's something for everyone. They'll give you a little book with all of them listed in the beginning of the semester.
activities_recommended: I didn't have time to join any clubs at Sorbonne, so I don't have any specific recommendations. If you live in Cité Universitaire they also have a bunch of sports offers.
weekend_recommendations: There's a lot of cute sights and places not far from Paris by train, so I recommend travelling a bit around on weekends if you have time. Also Paris is a great city to live in since there's always something going on, so enjoy that there's always a new exhibition, concert or restaurant to check out! Or if you're new to Paris that it's a very pretty and old city with a lot of interesting sights and museums.
culture_adjustment: For me it was very easy since I already speak French and have lived in Paris before, so I already had a quite large network.
socializing_tips: Most people are nice even though they can seem reserved. Join in whenever there's a social activity and don't be afraid to ask your classmates about homework etc. A lot of classes have a WhatsApp group, so try to ask someone to add you, it can be very informative.
cultural_challenges: In some of my classes it was expected to write down everything the teacher said.
culture_appreciated: That culture is really appreciated, and that it's part of the culture to eat out a lot and going out for drinks and coffee during the everyday life.
top3_advice: 1. Don't worry too much about not getting informations the same time as your friends going on exchange to other places. You'll get all the information you need, even though it will probably be delayed. 2. Get a library card for the BIS (bibliothèque interuniversitaire sorbonne). It's a beautiful place to study and you have access to all the books you'll need online during the semester. 3. Enjoy Paris as much as you can.
other_useful_info: I think I've listed everything in my answers above.
most_rewarding: Studying at Sorbonne and improving my academic French and of course meeting a lot of really cool people.
greatest_challenge: Since you have a lot of courses you also have a lot of exams. But it's ok if you prioritize your time right.
