crucial_aspects: I wanted to experience how the legal world is in the US and be amongst American legal professors and students - I want to work internationally so I was also curious of the possibility of studying and working abroad
overall_comments: I had an amazing time and would 10/10 do it again.
info_ease: There is a lot of things to do in preparation for going on exchange but it was overall easy to find information. The university had an orientation day just for us exchange students to know our way around the university and understand everything that was important. They took really good care of us.
arrival_assistance: The Global Programs team in the school welcomed us and gave us all the relevant information and gave us a tour of the university and told us about each function of the different offices in the school so we always knew who to go to for further questions. We also got a mentor that we could write to and hang out with.
arrival_comments: Very satisfied. However, in the acceptance letter there were two orientation days - a Thursday and a Friday. But there were no activities on the Friday, so we had to organize ourselves which was fine, but it would have been nice that the university organized something for us - also with other students across the international program.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had an amazing time and would 10/10 do it again.
registration_process: They open the courses around 1 month before on the university platform and then you have to register. The courses register right away so you can see what book to buy and read for each course in Canvas. The registration process is good and works well. You can also see how many people are allowed in each courses and if there is a waitlist, you can keep an eye on where you are on the waitlist.
registration_help: Registar's Office was available or the Global Programs team.
registration_success: I was successful in getting what I wanted, but the biggest issue was the schedule of the courses. Most of the courses I wanted, was scheduled at the same time, so I had to make some sacrifices. I also didn't want to have classes after dark, because I didn't want to take the bus home in the night.
registration_advice: Make sure that the courses you want are actually being offered and check you are looking at the right semester (fall or spring) and then select them and have a look at the schedule. When the registration opens, then you have them ready to just press "register now".
academics_comments: I had an amazing time and would 10/10 do it again.
course_level: Some classes are harder than others and also depends on the professor and what they expect of you. The teachers who expect more are generally also the courses that you learn more from and work harder for. Any class with Professor Keith Hand is challenging but it's so worth it. I also had a practical course of negotiations which was less legal theory and more how to act strategic and use negotiation methods to become a good negotiator.
teaching_comparison: US is famous for socratic method (cold calling) so always be prepared because it's normal that the teacher ask you without you raising your hand. You learn to think on your feet and the more prepared you are, the more you can follow the class discussions. They also take attendance. DO NOT go on exchange in the US and expect a vacation - you will need to attend and prepare for most courses. Within the first two weeks you will know in what classes you don't have to prepare as much and which courses you need to be on your feet.
courses_enrolled: I had immigration law, environmental law, international business transactions and negotiations.
recommended_courses: International business transactions and negotiations - see above.
unexpected_costs: There is an administration fee of $700 that we suddenly had to pay in the first couple of weeks and you don't really know what it's for and why. But the university arranged a lot of trips for us (baseball games, barbeques, Alcatraz trip, Halloween party) so I have an idea that maybe the money was spend for this, because we didn't pay for these trips.
cost_comparison: Supermarket and housing is expensive. All things you buy in US does not have tax and tips included, so you have to get used to the price not being the final price. Some places in San Francisco are more relaxed about tipping and others are not. It's ok not to tip if you are getting a to-go coffee in my opinion.
activities_available: Legal lectures, Presidential Watch Party, hanging out in bars, emotional support dog, welcome party on the beach
activities_recommended: Depend on what you are interested in they have many guest lectures which are interesting
weekend_recommendations: Explore California - go to Yosemite, Oakland, Sausalito, Stanford University, Berkeley, Joshua Tree, drive to LA Explore San Francisco and all it's nice areas. I dance salsa in my freetime so I explore all the salsa parties around the city. Don't be afraid to go out alone and talk to locals. If you want to experience the LGBTQ+ area, go to Castro; it's a nice area in the day and also in the night. Valencia St is my favourite street!! Baker Beach is beautiful and walking to Lands End and seeing the Golden gate is amazing.
culture_adjustment: So easy. The students and Americans in general are so nice and open, so it was easy to fit in and bond.
socializing_tips: Make at least one friend in each course you have and then go for coffee with them or hang out in your space time. Don't be afraid to put yourself out there. I didn't focus so much on the other international students; I was more focused in bonding with the Americans as this is the point of exchange
cultural_challenges: All the American students are used to the cold-calling culture in the class so they always know how to keep calm and speak their mind. that's very different from the university culture here.
culture_appreciated: The openness and confidence when they speak
top3_advice: 1) Be prepared that you will spend a lot of money - I went without SU and I still managed to have a good time, but go with enough money, so you don't have to compromise yourself. 2) Be prepared that you have to pay 15,000 DKK in insurance to the university and it's hard to waive it. I have Tryg insurance and I got it waived after a lot of frustration and stress, but don't give up. 3) Choose courses that allow you the possibility to get an LLM (Master of law) and choose courses that are mandatory for the bar exam in the US in case you want to come back or work as an attorney in US
other_useful_info: You can borrow the books you need in the library for free for 3 hours at a time. I did not buy books at all, so it saved me a lot of money.
most_rewarding: That I went alone and loved it as much as I did. I made a home for myself and got to know a lot of people around the city. There was always somewhere to go and Americans are very sweet and open so there is always an opportunity for you to try something new and make friends. The university life was a big part of my experience as well. I loved going to class and never felt exhausted from school.
greatest_challenge: Getting into the legal language in English and following class, but once I found my technique, it was easy. If you are used to communicating in English, you will find it easy to adapt but it can be a bit challenging if you are not that used to speaking English.
other_comments: I went on exchange without SU so I had to find ways to save money in a lot of areas, but I was lucky to find someone to share a room with. Scholarships are not the easiest to get and I only got one scholarship of 10.000 DKK out of applying for more than 20. For anyone who wants to go, you need around 150.000-200.000 for the whole semester if you want to have financial freedom. You can do with less, but it's a once-in-a-lifetime experience, so you shouldn't compromise if you want to take weekend trips and buying that extra beer :)

crucial_aspects: Jeg ønskede at opleve USA og særligt Californien. Jeg overvejede både San Diego og San Francisco, men valget faldt på San Francisco, hvilket jeg efterfølgende var meget glad for.
overall_comments: Overordnet var det en virkelig god oplevelse. San Francisco er en spændende og ikonisk by, som efter nogle udfordrende år virker til at være på vej i en bedre retning. Universitetet tog meget godt imod os og støttede os gennem hele processen. Jeg udnyttede desuden opholdet til at rejse og til at se en del sport. Ulemper: Den primære årsag til, at jeg ikke vurderer opholdet højere, er, at universitetet kun har få udvekslingsstuderende, hvilket gør det sværere at opbygge et større socialt netværk. Vi var kun fem udvekslingsstuderende i alt. Der var dog omkring 20 internationale LL.M.-studerende, som vi lavede meget socialt med. Universitetet havde samtidig relativt få sociale aktiviteter, hvor man kunne møde lokale studerende. Der var eksempelvis ingen sportshold, og mange arrangementer havde et fagligt fokus. Der var dog en løbeklub. Mit råd er at deltage i sociale aktiviteter fra start, så man hurtigt lærer de andre udvekslings- og LL.M.-studerende at kende.
info_ease: Det kunne godt være forvirrende, fordi der er mange praktiske forhold at tage stilling til, og ikke alt er lige intuitivt. Universitetet er dog meget hjælpsomt, og man modtager løbende detaljerede mails om, hvad man skal gøre hvornår.
arrival_assistance: Vi havde en introduktionsdag med rundvisning på universitetet og gennemgang af alle relevante forhold. Derudover havde vi individuelle samtaler om fagvalg, hvor vi fik anbefalinger. Jeg endte eksempelvis med at skifte et fag efter samtalen.
arrival_comments: Jeg oplevede ikke at mangle information. Man modtager næsten for mange oplysninger. Det eneste, der ikke stod helt klart, var kravene vedrørende vacciner, forsikring og køb af bøger. Et godt tip er at finde sin egen internationale forsikring, da man kan spare mere end 10.000 kr. Universitetets egen forsikring er meget dyr, og danske forsikringer opfylder ikke kravene. Derudover kan man finde stort set alt pensum på universitetets bibliotek, så det er ikke nødvendigt at købe bøgerne. De er meget dyre, så i flere fag læste jeg blot bibliotekets eksemplar og sparede ca. 2.000 kr. pr. bog.

teaching_comparison: Der blev brugt meget tid på cases, og 10% af karakteren i de fleste fag er participation, så i de fleste fag forventes der aktiv deltagelse fra de studerende. Flere anvender også cold calling
courses_enrolled: – Intellectual Property Law Survey – Copyright Law – Entertainment Law – Climate Change Law
recommended_courses: Jeg kan klart anbefale IP Survey, som giver en god indflyvning til IP-retten i USA og minder meget om EU-tilgangen. Copyright Law var også rigtig godt, men mere dybdegående. Climate Change Law blev en positiv overraskelse. Jeg blev derimod aldrig glad for Entertainment Law, primært fordi underviseren ikke formåede at gøre stoffet interessant, og fordi faget ikke var særligt relevant for en dansk studerende. Hvis jeg kunne gøre det om, ville jeg have valgt AI Law.
unexpected_costs: Jeg var forberedt på det meste, men blev især overrasket over prisen på bøger og forsikring via universitetet. Der er heldigvis gode muligheder for at reducere disse udgifter betydeligt.
cost_comparison: San Francisco er generelt en dyr by, særligt når det kommer til husleje. Samlet set brugte jeg omkring 130.000 kr. inklusive alt. Jeg rejste meget, lavede sjældent mad selv og så en masse sport og koncerter, så det kan gøres billigere. Jeg modtog 50.000 kr. i legater.
activities_available: Løbeklub. Jeg hørte ikke om andre klubber som internationale studerende tilmeldte sig
activities_recommended: Jeg vil anbefale at udforske byen, som har utrolig meget at byde på. Find fx top 50-lister og arbejd dig igennem dem. Der findes også hjemmesider og Instagram-profiler, som viser lokale arrangementer; jeg oplevede fx udendørs filmvisninger, en gratis countryfestival, demonstrationer, Halloween og et stort julearrangement. På hverdagsplan købte jeg en brugt cykel, hvilket gav gode muligheder for at opleve byen. Jeg oprettede også en amerikansk bankkonto og meldte mig ind i Planet Fitness. Byen har desuden rigtig god mad, som bestemt er værd at udforske.
weekend_recommendations: Det er meget billigt at flyve indenrigs i USA. Jeg kan anbefale Los Angeles, San Diego og Las Vegas, som alle ligger relativt tæt på. Det er også oplagt at leje en bil og tage på road trip. Rejserne var et af højdepunkterne for mig, så jeg planlagde så mange ture som muligt. De andre internationale studerende er som regel meget interesserede i at tage med. Man kan også tage helt små og billige ture, fx til Berkeley eller nærliggende naturområder.
culture_adjustment: Jeg syntes, det var overraskende nemt at falde til i byen og kulturen. Folk var meget imødekommende. Jeg havde ingen problemer i den henseende. Det sværeste var afstanden til Danmark og at alle derhjemme sover store del af ens dag.
socializing_tips: Jeg talte lidt med lokale studerende fra mine fag, men det var generelt nemmere at socialisere med de andre internationale studerende.
cultural_challenges: Det sværeste var nok, at man ikke har samme tryghed som i Danmark. Vi blev fx bedt om altid at have pas og visum på os. Alt føles mere intenst, særligt med den aktuelle situation i USA. Jeg var glad for muligheden for at bo i USA, men det gjorde mig også endnu mere taknemmelig for Danmark.
culture_appreciated: Jeg var stor fan af amerikanernes åbenhed. Fra Danmark er man ikke vant til at folk snakker med hinanden på gaden, i supermarkedet eller i den offentlige transport, men det var hyggeligt, og de synes man er meget spændende som dansk udvekslingsstuderende.
top3_advice: Find selv en international forsikring og spar ca. 15.000 kr. Vær opsøgende, åben, og tag initiativ til sociale aktiviteter. Nyd byen og rejs rundt, når muligheden er der.
other_useful_info: Hvis man selv leder efter bolig, vil jeg anbefale at undersøge, hvilke områder der er bedst at bo i. Jeg fandt et farvekodet kort, som viste tryghedsniveau i de forskellige nabolag. Ud fra egen erfaring kan fx jeg anbefale Nob Hill og North Beach.
most_rewarding: Det mest givende var at flytte så langt væk fra alt det velkendte og opdage, at man faktisk kan opbygge et helt nyt liv på få måneder. Det gav et stort selvtillidsboost, og jeg lærte meget om mig selv.
greatest_challenge: I starten var det en udfordring ikke at kende særlig mange, men jeg fandt ud af, at jeg selv måtte opsøge fællesskaber ud over de fire andre udvekslingsstuderende.
other_comments: Jeg kan klart anbefale San Francisco.

crucial_aspects: I chose to apply for exchange outside of Europe, because I see the exchange program, as a unique opportunity to go abroad and experience everyday life in a place where it might otherwise be difficult to get the opportunity to settle down. I more specifically chose the U.S., because Ive always been curious about the U.S., and even more in the times we are in now. Moreover I wanted to go somewhere where English was the first language, as I saw it as the best prerequisite for improving my own academic English. Not least, Ive heard a lot of good stuff about San Francisco, and UC Law San Francisco offered a lot of courses, which I was interested in attending.
info_ease: UC Law San Francisco has been super helpful and welcoming. I was only a bit disappointed about their lack of information regarding how to waive the standard health care insurance, which is very expensive. I struggled to figure out how to waive it, and the university was not able to help me, but managed on my own hand. Moreover, I would have appreciated if the university would have told us, that all course books are available at their library. Some of the other exchange students had already bought expensive course books (which the university had strongly encouraged to do upon arrival) only to later find out that they could have managed without. Lastly, I would have appreciated the information that the visa has 1 month "grace period" after ending date. The university told me later, but by then I had already rescheduled my flight.
arrival_assistance: Everything else.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Students register through the universities portal Self Service, its quite easy, but be aware that putting courses in your calendar does not mean that you signed up for them, merely that you put them in your "shopping basket", so make sure that you did really sign up. However, the university is helpful, and helped me to get into all the courses that I wanted.
registration_help: The exchange cordinator
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Take advantage of the fact that you can "test" all courses in the intro week, to get a sense of the course and the professor, before making your final decision.
course_level: The level was moderate, but definitely manageable. It is worth noting, that the professor and the course often matters more than the mere credits in terms of workload.
teaching_comparison: Attendance and participation matters.
courses_enrolled: Climate Change Law Citizenship and Equality Comparative Constitutional Law Intellectual Property Survey
recommended_courses: Comparative Constitutional Law, because you get to compare different jurisdictions constitutional law, which is interesting and useful beyond the American context. Also I liked the professor -NAME REDACTED-. It is worth noting that the course focuses mostly on the human rights aspects of constitutional law, rather than institutional constitutional law. Intellectual Property Survey, because it gives a good introduction to intellectual property (copyright, trademark, patent and trade secrets) and the professor -NAME REDACTED- is fun.
unexpected_costs: Student fee (I think it was around 5,000 DKK)
cost_comparison: Going out for dinner can be more affordable, than back home in Denmark, however groceries are the same level, I would say.
activities_available: The host institution offered social activities for the exchange students together with the L.L.M. students, which has been super nice.
activities_recommended: Check out the "fun and cheap in San Francisco" website to see events happening in the city. There are always a lot of interesting cultural events going on and its a nice way to get to know the city. Go travel with some other exchange and L.L.M. students even if just for a day or a weekend trip, there is so many nice things to see in California.
weekend_recommendations: I enjoyed camping in the many national parks, which were incredible, and had a super nice trip down the coast to Los Angeles. Also Las Vegas was fun to visit.
culture_adjustment: Not too bad.
socializing_tips: Talk to the students in your courses they are super nice and welcoming and join some of the many clubs that the university has.
cultural_challenges: The "office hours" and the students relationship to their professors, which is very unlike the one we have to our teachers back home in Denmark.
culture_appreciated: Because San Francisco people are super welcoming and talkative I very rarely felt homesick
top3_advice: Do it!
other_useful_info: Not that I can think of
most_rewarding: The city, the people and the weather has been wonderful!
greatest_challenge: The academic culture
other_comments: I dont think so

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne prøve at leve tættere på naturen, og opleve hvordan stærke sollysforandringer påvirker kroppen.
info_ease: Lidt vanskeligt at finde ud af, hvornår det officiellt program startede for udvekslingsstuderende. Var der allerede d.10 august, men tror først jeg var på uni omkring d. 23 - og der var ikke et decideret lær hinanden at kende program, med mindre man havde meldt sig til længe før, hvilket jeg ikke havde forstået.
arrival_assistance: Ikke rigtig nogen, synes selv man skulle finde ud af meget. Fik nogle email med events jeg kunne deltage i. Deltog i et online møde, og i en vandretur samt en speeddate og quiz, hvor jeg mødte nogle andre udvekslingsstuderende.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Jeg tror vi fik en mail med nogle informationer, og var til et digitalt infomøde hvor de fortalte os om at lave et digitalt login, og at man kunne melde sig til nogle rundvisninger på universitetet.
registration_help: Til selve registreringen var der fin hjælp, det var mere ift. fag jeg synes hjælpen var ringe.
registration_success: I starten gik det fint, men jeg skulle lave nogle ændringer i fag undervejs, hvilket var helt vildt besværligt. Derudover var der et fag, som blev aflyst i sidste sekund, hvilket jeg kun fandt ud af fordi jeg selv opsøgte fagkoordinatoren, da jeg havde svært ved at tilmelde mig. Det var lige inden juleferie, så det var også stressende. Hun tog ikke telefonen, eller svarede på mine mails - prøvede endda at opsøge hende på kontoret, hvor der blot stod hun var hjemmearbejdende grundet corona, og at man kunne ringe eller skrive mails. Så alt i alt en ret skidt oplevelse, der har resulteret i at jeg må udskyde mit studie med et halvt år.
registration_advice: Hvis ikke du får svar for din fagkoordinator, så ring til nogle andre der har med udveksling eller lign. institut og brok dig over det.
course_level: Synes generelt niveauet var meget varierende. Havde A&O, som var 10 online forelæsningsrækker - og den eneste der var fysisk handlede om, hvordan man laver APA referencer. Så det var ret skidt, men Læringspsykologi og biologisk psykologi var ret fint niveau.
teaching_comparison: Kunne godt lide, når fagene indeholdt en blanding ml. traditionelle forelæsninger og workshops. Det gjorde det i biologisk og lidt i læringspsykologi, så har jeg også lavet mange præsentationer alene - hvilket var fedt at øve sig i.
courses_enrolled: Læringspsykologi Biologisk psykologi A&O
recommended_courses: Læringspsykologi Biologisk psykologi Cognitive science of aging
unexpected_costs: Det koster noget, hvis man gerne vil på tur. Var der med min kæreste, og vi havde bil med - så det kostede at køre rundt i den. Men man kan sagtens tage med bus rundt, eller på arrangerede ture - og ellers leje bil for en weekend, hvis man vil længere væk. Der er ikke mega god offentlig transport ud af byen nemlig.
cost_comparison: Mad er dyrt. Men var også forventligt, men man skal stadig vænne sig til det. Kan anbefale at skralde lidt, hvis man vil spare.
activities_available: Der er mega mange studie organisationer på universitetet, som man kan engagere sig i. Hvilket er fedt. Jeg var til strikkeklub hver anden uge, så var jeg på tur med fjellgruppen en enkelt gang, og en bålkveld. De arrangerer natur agtige ting hver tirsdag og weekend ture til rimelige priser. Ellers har jeg været på hyttetur med topptur (skigruppe) tull en enkelt gang. Hele året har jeg gået til ugentlig gratis morgenyoga i et træningscenter, der ligger lige ved siden af universitetet. Derudover var der hver tirsdag billig fællesmiddag i en kirke i byen, det var også meget hyggeligt. Jeg var også frivillig på Tromsø internationel filmfestival, hvilket var sjovt. Ja - generelt sker der noget, hver uge. Så det er bare at opsøge det.

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: Nature and the activities surrounding that.
overall_comments: Going on exchange was the best decision I ever made during law school.
info_ease: UiT has a very informative website, where you can find every piece of information you need. It might take some time, but the information is there.
arrival_assistance: You receive a lot of information during the Debut Week for International students, which I recommend you participate in. At least the social gatherings at first, not all the things during the debut week was that important, and if you meet a group of people that want to skip some of the information lectures that does have any important information, then just do that.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Going on exchange was the best decision I ever made during law school.
registration_process: The entire process tends to be very bureaucratic and takes a lot of time. You need to send a lot of documents and such back and forth from your home university and to the host university. Furthermore, the final approval for your stay might come a little late as was the course selection a bit late regarding when you leave for the exchange. But all is taken care of before you arrive.
registration_help: UiT's webpage.
registration_success: I got both the classes I had signed up for. Though, I initially thought I could take other classes, which were part of my decision to go I later found out those classes where only for a special program that exchange students couldn't take. Otherwise, the process of reregistering for classes was straightforward.
registration_advice: Be patient.
academics_comments: Going on exchange was the best decision I ever made during law school.
course_level: The level was a bit lower than at KU. Additionally, it did not feel like 15 ECTS point courses. The workload was smaller, and the courses are structured after a block structure. So, you only have classes and lectures in the courses for a certain number of weeks. The courses do not have classes during the entire semester. Though exams are still at the end of the semester.
teaching_comparison: Because the classes are way smaller and not as many students attend so it is very interactive. It is more personal in a way, and everyone can participate more. They do have questions for the classes, as we do at KU, that you need to prepare before class –depending on the course you take.
courses_enrolled: JUR-3050 General Law of the Sea and JUR-3626 International Criminal Law, Atrocity Crimes, and Transitional Justice
recommended_courses: JUR-3050 General Law of the Sea. It complements the surroundings of your stay, and you can draw a lot of connections. Furthermore, UiT has an entire department for like Law of the Sea, so they are very skilled in that legal field.
unexpected_costs: Because of the private housing situation I had to buy pillows, duvets and sheets.
cost_comparison: The books were a bit more expansive then first imagined. However, qua the Norwegian kroner being less worth than the Danish at the time of my exchange, you saved a lot when buying groceries etc. Furthermore, they had a lot of student discount in different places, which made it possible to do a lot of activities for example use the sauna, go to yoga classes, join the gym etc.
activities_available: There were a lot of different activities you could join. UiT were also very good at informing about every event held a school as well as in town. You received an email every other week with information regarding activities you could join. I for example enjoyed the knitting club for international students.
activities_recommended: If you enjoy knitting or want to learn, like I did, you should join that. Otherwise, join a gym or just participate in what you can. There is something for everyone.
weekend_recommendations: I truly recommend going hiking and exploring the nearby nature. This was a major aspect of my trip, and it made it very unforgettable. I enjoyed hiking during the summer and skiing during the winter. You can rent free gear through Turbu or pay for rent though Tromsø Outdoor. Either way, there is excellent opportunities for renting what you might need. The busses connect the entire island and takes you basically everywhere. See and explore the place every time you have the chance!
culture_adjustment: It was quite easy. You get a hang of the language quick, and the culture is not that different from what you are used to. Naturally, there are some differences, but generally everyone is just very friendly and welcoming. You kind of feel welcome from the moment you arrive.
socializing_tips: Try to find them during activities or other social gatherings where it is easier to meet them. You don't meet a lot during your classes, because it is primarily made up of international students. But otherwise just talk to them.
cultural_challenges: Nothing. There were no big challenges.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness and open mindedness. Everyone was so sweet and always wanted to help etc. Furthermore, I loved their approach to everyday life. Everything is centered around their life outside of works, which means they adapt their working hours to fit, what they want to do. You could meet locals on top of mountains at 12 on a Tuesday. This balance between work and private life, was very enlightening. They just have a more chill approach to life and especially work life balance.
top3_advice: 1. Enjoy the activities UiT has to offer 2. Explore nature 3. Adjust your expectations for the academic level (just a different way than at KU)
other_useful_info: UiT is extremely big, so familiarize yourself with the app MazeMap.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of the exchange was defiantly the experience of a chill everyday life. From the courses to your free time, everything is just less stressful. You get to really work with the courses and the textbooks, because there is not as much to read and work with, so you have the time to read everything. Furthermore, you do not have a lot of classes, so lots of time to explore the nature, which where an equally great experience.
greatest_challenge: There were not that many great challenges. You just have to adopt to a new way of life, but when you have landed and start to have routines you really fall into place.
other_comments: I highly recommend an exchange in Tromsø.

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: I choose The Arctic University in Tromsoe (UiT) because they had courses in Marine Biotechnology. I want to specialise in algae and a semester at UiT was a good opportunity to learn more about algae and marine organisms. UiT focus on marine sciences and collect samples from the deep sea of the Arctic which I found very interesting to work with. My exchange enabled me to come into contact with colleagues and professors that can help me with my thesis on algae.
info_ease: Almost all the information needed was on their website and they had a special page for exchange students or students coming from abroad. The course catalogue is also digitalized so the courses were easy to find but detailed information about the course schedules is not available. The course schedule depends on each professor and it can be quite difficult to avoid overlap in schedules. To get further information, I would recommend to mail the exchange student coordinators which usually answer quite fast.
arrival_assistance: The student coordinator, student housing committee, and students were all very welcoming and eager to help me upon my arrival. The student coordinator was always available and I could contact him with any minor problem I would get. The student housing committee were located close to campus, were open in office hours, and always responded mails quickly. The students were very welcoming and helpful both on- and off-campus.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: They had a webpage named studentweb where you register the courses you want to take. The courses are found in the course catalogue (google course catalogue UiT and you will find it). You have to activate your mail (FEIDE and UiT mail) before you can register for course but there is a very thorough guide whih they will send to your mail.
registration_help: Guides, mail addresses of course coordinators and the web page.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted and luckily I did not have to change them.
registration_advice: Select courses from a study like Marine Biotechnology so you don't risk that the courses are overlapping.
course_level: The level of the courses were equal or maybe a bit lower than the level at Copenhagen University. I felt like it was up to the individual how much work they would put into the classes and I think that was great.
teaching_comparison: I think it was very much the same as UCPH, there were both lectures, group work, and laboratory courses.
courses_enrolled: Marine Bioprospecting, Quantitative Microbial Biotechnology I, and Industrial Biotechnology
recommended_courses: I would recommend Marine Bioprospecting because you get to go on a real expedition and collect arctic samples. The courses focus on the arctic environment and you get to handle and process real arctic samples.
unexpected_costs: The Kraft subscription for exchange students is valid until December and you have to pay an extra fee if you want to go to the gym in the last weeks of your study
cost_comparison: Food is very expensive.
activities_available: I was part of Kraft which is the gym, it was really nice and they provided sauna and classes.
activities_recommended: I would recommend Kraft or pickleball because they are very social clubs. I would have liked to try the outdoor club but I did not have time unfortunately.
weekend_recommendations: Go do outdoor sports like hiking or trail running in the summer or autumn and skiing in the winter. Tromsoe is a really beautiful but there are also other places which are accessible with the bus that I also recommend to visit like sommeroeya,
culture_adjustment: I don't think there is such a large cultural difference and it was very easy to adjust.
socializing_tips: Norwegians are outdoor people so try to ask them if they want to go out hiking or ask for tips to do in Tromsoe and they will help you.
cultural_challenges: They eat very early like around 5 pm but it was not really a problem.
culture_appreciated: They are very happy and chill people and they like the outdoors which I appreciate.
top3_advice: Mail people if you have any doubts, go to a club, and go outdoors.
other_useful_info: The polar night can be quite difficult to handle and I recomment people to take vitamin D and go to UV lamp arrangements which is provided by the university.
most_rewarding: To study Marine biotechnology and meet colleagues which have the same interests.
greatest_challenge: The polar night which can change your day rhythm

registration_comments: Det var seriøst bare klasse alt i alt.

academics_comments: Det var seriøst bare klasse alt i alt.
course_level: Vil sige at niveauet måske var lidt lavere eller kravene lidt nemmere end i Dk, men det passede mig rigtig godt. Det er lidt hvad man gør det til.
teaching_comparison: Det var meget det samme.
courses_enrolled: SPL-1001 PLAN, KULTUR OG NÆRING SVF-2107 CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION (CCA) STV-1005 GLOBAL POLITIKK: INNFØRING I INTERNASJONALE OG TRANSNASJONALE RELASJONER
recommended_courses: SPL-1001 PLAN, KULTUR OG NÆRING: Sygt chill fag. Et førstesemesterfag på uddannelsen Samfundsplanlægning, som lidt er statskundskab/sociologi men i praksis. Det er spændende, men også nemt. Forelæsningerne er 20-40 min og online og så er der øvelsestimer 1 gang ugentligt i 2 timer. Jeg så forelæsningerne og kom et par gange til øvelsestimerne, men mest for det sociale. Der var en meget overskuelig skriftlig opgave i løbet af semestret, men ellers intet obligatorisk udover eksamen. Eksamen var en 1-uges hjemmeksamen som er meget overkommelig hvis man er vant til at skrive akademiske opgaver (op til 4000 ord på 1 uge). Jeg fik en god karakter for min, og havde ikke brugt særlig meget tid eller energi på den. STV-1005 GLOBAL POLITIKK: INNFØRING I INTERNASJONALE OG TRANSNASJONALE RELASJONER. Spændende fag med 2 timers forelæsning og 2 timers øvelsestime om ugen. God måde at møde lokale på. Det er et tredjesemesterfag for statskundskabere, men som sociologistuderende syntes jeg stadig det var spændende og til at finde ud af. Heller ikke sygt krævende og meget hvad man gjorde det til. Der var en meget overskuelig skriftlig opgave i løbet af semestret, men ellers intet obligatorisk udover eksamen. Eksamen var også meget overkommelig, man havde en uge til at skrive 2000 ord. Jeg anbefaler ikke SVF-2107 CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION (CCA). Faget var kedeligt, dårligt tilrettelagt og eksamen var hæslig:) Grundbogen var fra 2011, og det føltes virkelig tamt at læse noget der var så "gammelt" om klima.
unexpected_costs: Måtte købe mig et par vinterstøvler, fordi jeg ikke havde nogen i forvejen. Vinteren (som starter omkring oktober) er meget våd fordi det sner tidligt, men temperaturen er omkring -10 til 7 grader skiftevis.
cost_comparison: Kaffe var billigere end i Kbh:) Grøntsager var dyre. Alkohol var ekstremt dyrt. Kæmpe lifehack er at tage et par flasker spiritus med hjemmefra, fordi det kostede ca. 3 gange så meget som herhjemme!
activities_available: Vaffelfredag, åbne foredrag, filmaftener, burger nights. Derudover er der en studenteridrætsforening der hedder TSI hvor man billigt kan gå til alt slags sport.
activities_recommended: Studenteridræt. Vandreture (f.eks. Rødtinden, Natmålsfjellet, Tromsdalstinden, Store Blåmand, Sherpatrappen, Tromsøs geografiske midtpunkt. Brug f.eks. appen AllTrails, der ligger der rigtig mange gode trails. Se film i Verdensteatret, en gammel biograf der viser nye og gamle film, og næsten hver torsdag, fredag og lørdag har live-DJs. Gå i Sauna i PUST på havnen, hvor man booker en time for omkring 80 danske kroner. Klatre i Buldreterminalen. Live jam sessions på FINT cafe hver søndag aften. Hvis du er single, så gå på tinderdates lol, det er en ret klasse måde at møde lokale på:)
weekend_recommendations: Lej en bil gennem GetAround (privat biludlejning) og kør til et cool sted. F.eks. Lyngen Alperne hvor man kan gå til Blåisvatnet eller se en gletcher. Eller man kan tage til Lofoten (der er lidt langt tho) eller Senja (tættere på, sygt smukt!). Tag en endagstur til Bryggejenterne, en cute cafe en time med bud udenfor byen. Der kan man også gå til Natmålsfjellet. Jeg har hørt at det er overrated at tage til Nordkap, fordi der er langt og det i sig selv er ret kedeligt. Evt meld dig ind i DNT og få adgang til en masse billige hytter i Norge. F.eks. Majstua i Harstad!!
culture_adjustment: Ret nemt.
socializing_tips: Generelt er det ret nemt at socialisere med de lokale, fordi de fleste der studerer i Tromsø ikke er fra Tromsø, og derfor også selv er åbne overfor nye venner. Der er mange der kommer langvejsfra fra små byer i Norge og ikke har deres primære netværk her endnu. Her er nogle konkrete tips: - Studenteridræt - Hav norske kurser og snak med din sidemand (man må gerne skrive eksamen på dansk) - Bo på Panorama (det er den studentbolig der bor flest nordmænd på) - Prøv at snakke norsk selvom det føles akavet, de forstår dig vitterligt bedre sådan selvom det føles som om du paroderer dem. Se evt "Saving the fucking planet" på DR, hvis du vil øve dig på at forstå den nordnorske dialekt.
cultural_challenges: Ikke rigtig noget tbh. Norge og Dk minder meget om hinanden.
culture_appreciated: At det minder ret meget om Dk så det var nemt at adapte.
top3_advice: Nyd det!!! Tromsø er en sygt cool by!
other_useful_info: Der bor en del samere (et oprindeligt folk med deres egne sprog) i Tromsø og Nordnorge generelt, fordi det plejede at være deres land. Sæt dig evt lidt ind i det i forvejen. Omkring mørketiden: tag d-vitamin! Og selvom solen ikke står op i en periode, er der stadigvæk nogle lyse timer. Mørketiden er også farvernes tid; himlen er så smuk. Blåtime er også helt særligt, hvor alt lyser blåt. Og der er for det meste sne i mørketiden, hvilket gør det hele lysere. Nyd det, det er en meget unik oplevelse!
most_rewarding: Opleve den sygt flotte natur og lære søde mennesker at kende. Jeg havde det sygt hyggeligt og kedede mig sjældent.
greatest_challenge: Mørketiden på godt og ondt. Man skal virkelig vende sig til mørket, men det er virkelig det hele værd! Embrace det, drik en masse varme drikke, tag i biografen, gå ture i sneen, hæng ud med vennerne.
other_comments: Jeg vil anbefale hvalsafari og hundeslæde. Sidstnævnte bliver hurtigt fuldt booket tho, så book det tidligt hvis det er noget du vil.

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: For me, it was important that the destination had a strong focus on nature. I also thought a lot about the language, as I wanted to be able to communicate with the locals without them having to switch to another language.
info_ease: I felt there were many different documents to keep track of all the time, but this is not only the case for Tromsø.
arrival_assistance: We had a contact person, but he was responsible for all international students, which made it challenging for him to provide detailed assistance. This often resulted in very brief replies, and at times, it felt like he hadn't fully read the email before responding.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: I don't remember this part so good, but i just followed the process.
registration_help: I was able to fing alot of information on the UiT website, they had an email and when we arrived we could just drop in fore a personal meating
registration_success: I got almost all the classes I wanted, and the ones I didn't get were due to my sending institution. When exploring the classes, it's important to note that if you follow the link for international students, you won't be able to see the classes taught in Norwegian.
registration_advice: Don't panic about all the emails you receive from UiT. They send reminder emails to everyone, regardless of whether you've already submitted the requested document or not. That's why it's a good idea to keep track of what you've sent, so you don't get too confused when they follow up on something you've already handled.
course_level: The difficulty level of my courses varied greatly. I had one course where the main focus was reading scientific articles and presenting them, which was at a lower academic level compared to the University of Copenhagen. Then I had a pharmacology course where the teaching was on par with KU, but the exam was easier. Lastly, I took an immunology course, where the difficulty level was very similar to KU throughout the entire course. All of them 10 ECTS
teaching_comparison: It was very similar to what I'm used to at CPHU. We had lectures and practical sessions that were closely aligned with the lectures.
courses_enrolled: * Immunology * General pharmacology and toxicology * General and marine biotechnology
recommended_courses: Immunology was such a nice course and the teacher was very helpfull
unexpected_costs: I spent a lot of money during the first month to get settled. And more money on trips than expected.
cost_comparison: Trips were more, housing were less
activities_available: there where so many different.
activities_recommended: I will recogment to look at DNT youth. They organize trips to various cabins with other young people at really affordable prices.
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips and explore Northern Norway. Places like Senja, Lyngen, Lofoten, Harstad, and Alta are highly recommended. Additionally, it's possible to rent cross-country skis when the snow falls, which is also a must-try experience.
culture_adjustment: Norway was very similar to Denmark, so cute easy
socializing_tips: Live in student housing and talk to the locals in your classes.
cultural_challenges: not any
culture_appreciated: the love to the nature
top3_advice: - Bring all the outdoor gear you have at home. - Don't be embarrassed to try speaking Norwegian, even if it feels a bit outside your comfort zone. - If you enjoy a particular sport, join a local team or club—it's a great way to connect with the locals!
other_useful_info: If you're even slightly considering staying for two semesters instead of one, apply for it right away. It seems possible to withdraw the application later, but you cannot request an extension once you're already there. I knew several people who wanted to stay longer but couldn't because they hadn't applied in advance. This is a rule from KU.
most_rewarding: All the new people I've met and the amazing nature experiences I've had.
greatest_challenge: I am not sure

socializing_tips: Do as much of the host university's recommendation in the start and try as many different sports as possible
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The appreciation for nature and hiking

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: As a person who loved being outside, Svalbard provided an exciting place to combine geological education combined with lots of fieldwork in very hard and unexplored conditions and sites.
info_ease: Upon arrival, all the information we gathered was rather straightforward, so I didn't experience a lot of problem getting to know the systems and operations.
arrival_assistance: I didn't need a lot of assistance, but I got it from the student counseling or from the people in charge of helping the student, especially when it came to filling out relevant papers like proof of attendance.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: dont know
registration_help: The people at UNIS, was very helpful when it came to questions related to different stuff like exams, like filling out paper, but generally I didn't need that much help, so I can't really answer this question fully.
registration_success: Very successful
registration_advice: Since you can't directly apply to UNIS or if you want to get Erasmus, it's kind of a long process to get up there. You need to fill out a lot of documents and papers. It's worth it, but it can easily scare a lot of people away.
course_level: The courses sound very much like an introduction course, so it's from what I could learn from the teachers. The course just didn't only need, or couldn't only be attended by people who have already studied geology, but also people from other backgrounds. That's why it was pretty introductory. So I wouldn't say the level was very high, but I think it was pretty good. I have had experience with more difficult courses here in Copenhagen, but it was fun up there.
teaching_comparison: The education at Svalbard was very much dominated by fieldwork. We spent many hours and many days out doing fieldwork at different sites, where we combined with theory from the classroom, we went out to the location and saw them on the actual location and with our own eyes. My education in Copenhagen also, we had fieldwork included in it, but not as much and under different conditions.
courses_enrolled: AG214 (The Geological evolution of Svalbard) and Ag215 (Arctic Landforms and Processes)
recommended_courses: Since there's only two courses for Arctic Geology every semester, so it's difficult for me to tell about the other courses since I haven't had them. But I would definitely recommend the two I had while I was up there.
unexpected_costs: There wasn't really unexpected courses. Of course, the food and living standards up there are more expensive since it's so remote, but nothing that I didn't expect there to be.
cost_comparison: Fresh fruits and vegetables.
activities_available: Due to the conditions that the university was placed in and the location, there wasn't a lot of activities related to the university, but there were some small football and other social events in the town, but which was not related to the university.
activities_recommended: Since it's a very small town and there's not a lot of activities going on, but of course hiking around the area is really beautiful. There's also a sports center where you can play football, you can go to the gym, swimming, badminton, etc. So I would recommend that. And there's also some quiz evenings where you battle against other groups for a small prize.
weekend_recommendations: It very much depends on how much they prioritize their lessons or their homework. But else, go on a hike with your fellow students. Maybe go play football in the sports center or go do other activities. But there's not a lot, so you need to be pretty creative with what you think of doing.
culture_adjustment: Since it is part of Norway, the culture was very similar to Danish culture. That's why I didn't require a lot of getting used to their culture. But it is a small city that I lived in, so of course it is a bit more close neighborhood. So you start learning people relatively, or you start talking with people relatively quickly compared to in a big city.
socializing_tips: Don't only stay in your rooms, go out and join social activities such as playing football, or going to the quiz evening, or playing board games at the church. But you need to go outside your housing area because nothing really happens there.
cultural_challenges: No big cultural differences
culture_appreciated: Outdoor culture
top3_advice: A lover of the outside, be ready for hard conditions, small and tight and social classes.
other_useful_info: Nope
most_rewarding: I love the mixture of theoretical knowledge that we gained in the classroom, and then we saw and looked at the same theory, but in practice in the actual locations. But I also enjoyed the very laid-back attitude of a lot of the teachers that we have. It was very down-to-earth, and I think that it was a very good way of them, in a positive way, bonding to the class, that we, in many ways, respected them more, since they were very down-to-earth, and they could laugh with us, they could joke around with us, but also they are very knowledgeable, and we learned a lot of things from them.
greatest_challenge: All the paperwork that was needed to be filled out prior to me leaving Denmark
other_comments: no

info_ease: It was quite easy, though one needs to do their research on the university's website.
arrival_assistance: I received a lot of help from my roomies who were local, and two of them were guides in the orientation week for internationals. So I guess anyone can ask the guides about anything during the orientation week, they are all students at the university.
arrival_comments: Upon arrival everything was fine, but it could be nice to receive more assistance before the arrival.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Tromsø is a great place, no doubt about that. It is almost impossible not to consider to move there permanently, it is that amazing and unique.

academics_comments: Tromsø is a great place, no doubt about that. It is almost impossible not to consider to move there permanently, it is that amazing and unique.

greatest_challenge: To deal with the fact that it is over...

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: I was interested in the Geology of the Arctic and fieldwork in the Arctic. UNIS through UIT seemed to be one of the best options for this and it definitely lived up to the expectations I had of lots of field work and accompanying safety instructions on how to operate in the field. I was also excited to see the modern field equipment and data acquisition methods advertised at UNIS and I also received training in using drones for data acquisition in hard to traverse terrain. This all seemed relevant to the direction i wanted to go with my future studies and career.
overall_comments: It was a very welcoming community both of fellow students and of professors, i had many opportunities to join for fieldwork outside of the expected course work. I also made many friends i still keep contact with and intend to visit.
info_ease: UiT and UNIS provided a lot of information in advance of my arrival through various infosites and emails, the overall process was very smooth. When i did need more help, the staff was very helpful in providing it (this was mostly with administrative work regarding getting approval to rent rifles).
arrival_assistance: Assigned a room and delivered keys. Signatures to approve rifle renting. Introduction to the University Center and Town
arrival_comments: Since the town is quite small it was easy to navigate and get familiar with on your own/ with fellow new students.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: It was a very welcoming community both of fellow students and of professors, i had many opportunities to join for fieldwork outside of the expected course work. I also made many friends i still keep contact with and intend to visit.
registration_process: Apply to exchange to UiT through Copenhagen University's exchange program. Once accepted send in application to UiT through their søknadsweb site and upload documentation and select courses at UNIS. At the same time apply separately directly to UNIS through their søknadsweb site. They ask for similar documentation. Once approved by both institutions send the approval to the host institution. You also need Copenhagen University to pre-approve your courses.
registration_help: The E-mails received contained most of the information needed. Otherwise the information on UiT's website was helpful when i needed clarification on how to have my exchange approved. I did email the institution on one occasion when i was unsure and received good help. There was also a phone nr available, but i never used it.
registration_success: I was approved for the classes i wanted, it was a relatively smooth process to register.
registration_advice: Read the emails recieved from the various institutions carefully, they provide all the information needed to register correctly. If in doubt check the institutions website, UiT had a nice step by step guide for applying. Otherwise email or call if you are ever in doubt about your application.
academics_comments: It was a very welcoming community both of fellow students and of professors, i had many opportunities to join for fieldwork outside of the expected course work. I also made many friends i still keep contact with and intend to visit.
course_level: My 2 courses were The Geological Evolution of Svalbard and Arctic Landforms and Processes. Both were 15 ECTs giving a total of 30 ECTs for the semester. The level of the courses was very satisfactory. I felt academically challenged but never overwhelmed. Level was what i would expect of a bachelor's course.
teaching_comparison: Being in the Arctic, the institution took full advantage of this, with lots of fieldwork to experience the Arctic and see the geology at various sites. The in-class projects were also more independent, requiring us to plan fieldwork to sites up to 20km away from town. This gave a lots of opportunities for independent learning and preparing for more independent work. Overall there was a bigger emphasis on applying knowledge in the field than i am used to at UCPH
courses_enrolled: (At UNIS) AG - 214 Geological Evolution of Svalbard AG - 215 Arctic Landforms and Processes
recommended_courses: The choice is quite limited to these 2 aforementioned courses in the autumn semester if you are a geologist. There is also a geophysics courses at a bachelor level but i did not take these.
unexpected_costs: I underestimated the equipment required to do fieldwork in the arctic. I ended up spending an extra 3000DKK on good footwear and clothing.
cost_comparison: Food was more expensive but still affordable. You could borrow a lot of equipment from the university center, local community initiatives and student organizations so i saved on various kitchen equipment, books, field equipment, skis, etc.
activities_available: Directly with the institution i attended dance classes. Outside the institution i joined the local football club and got a gym membership. On my own and fellow students initiatives I went on several skiing, fishing and hiking trips.
activities_recommended: I was surprised at how fun dance classes were, i had never done it before. Otherwise hiking and fishing were my favorite.
weekend_recommendations: Weekends allow for longer multi-day hikes, there is a student cabin you can book or you can book a cabin through the local hunting and fishing club.
culture_adjustment: I already spoke Norwegian and English beforehand which helped as those were the main languages spoken. It is a very international town so you end up meeting a lot of other people who are just as foreign as you are. Speaking Norwegian was still an advantage for being included in the more Norwegian activities.
socializing_tips: Join for hikes and other activities outside of school. Most of your fellow students don't have family, friends or job or other obligations outside of schoolwork, so they are very available to join for activities.
cultural_challenges: There was nothing i found challenging culturally. It took a little time to get used to seeing firearms so frequently but at no point did it make me feel unsafe, they were handled with care.
culture_appreciated: Everyone was very open and caring, both locals and fellow exchange students. This was especially nice during the dark period when the sun didn't rise as you were more likely to become depressed, but the many chances to be social and various events led to this not being an issue for me.
top3_advice: Bring proper equipment to go hiking, you will be in the field no matter what study you come with (geology, biology, engineering etc.) and also to hike outside of school. Give new opportunities a chance, I was invited to join for lots of activities i never tried before and was pleasantly surprised by them. For me it was dance classes that i never tried before and i ended up enjoying it a lot and making lots of friends through it. Make lots of friends, you will have a lot of extra time due to not having obligations with family, friends and jobs from home and neither will your fellow students so people are extra friendly and have more time to be social.
other_useful_info: There are lots of local initiatives like "bruktikken" local charity shop where you can get clothes and various stuff for free. Check local billboards and talk to the locals they'll know all the various events going on in town.
most_rewarding: I made some friends for life and was academically challenged to do more independent work.
greatest_challenge: It was very physically demanding to go on fieldwork and going for hikes, especially carrying equipment and supplies in the rough terrain. You will be traveling a lot by foot during this exchange. This is at the same time felt very rewarding.
other_comments: I very much recommend taking an exchange at UNIS through UiT.

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: I'm not sure... It had to be financially feasible, so the Erasmus grant was a nice addition. But a crucial aspect was that everyday life had to include nature and adventure. You can get this in other places than Svalbard, but I felt I could always go to these other places. It's a unique opportunity to live on Svalbard for that period of time. Being a tourist for a few days is a whole other world than actually living there.
overall_comments: It was unreal. Again, this is the UNIS on Svalbard so I have no idea how it is at Tromsø. The overall study experience was amazing. However, it does require the person to take initiative. Not necessarily to make friends, but to go out on adventures. It can be hard, logistically, on Svalbard and sometimes you have to get creative. Seek help from the residents, like burrowing a car, find a boat to fix, take som (well-assessed) risks... You will go on some amazing field trips with the course (so much money pumped into this uni) so you will also get cool experiences without taking any initiative. Living and studying here is not for everyone. If you don't like the cold, hiking and being outside doing type 2&3 fun, it's not the place for you. I think you can find other places where the town/city and indoor life is a lot more fun and cozy.
info_ease: Very easy
arrival_assistance: A lot of assistance. It's such a small place and every student lives in the same accommodation. UNIS is very good at introducing you to the island.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: It was unreal. Again, this is the UNIS on Svalbard so I have no idea how it is at Tromsø. The overall study experience was amazing. However, it does require the person to take initiative. Not necessarily to make friends, but to go out on adventures. It can be hard, logistically, on Svalbard and sometimes you have to get creative. Seek help from the residents, like burrowing a car, find a boat to fix, take som (well-assessed) risks... You will go on some amazing field trips with the course (so much money pumped into this uni) so you will also get cool experiences without taking any initiative. Living and studying here is not for everyone. If you don't like the cold, hiking and being outside doing type 2&3 fun, it's not the place for you. I think you can find other places where the town/city and indoor life is a lot more fun and cozy.
registration_process: See above. In addition you use their own portal to apply for the UNIS courses. You send in some documents and information and they usually get back to you 2 weeks after the deadline.
registration_help: Not really a lot. A lot of emailing back and forth in which they are helpful.
registration_success: I got the courses I wanted (and the only ones available). AB-201: Arctic terrestrial biology AB-204: Arctic population ecology
registration_advice: Remember the deadlines and don't be afraid to email them.
academics_comments: It was unreal. Again, this is the UNIS on Svalbard so I have no idea how it is at Tromsø. The overall study experience was amazing. However, it does require the person to take initiative. Not necessarily to make friends, but to go out on adventures. It can be hard, logistically, on Svalbard and sometimes you have to get creative. Seek help from the residents, like burrowing a car, find a boat to fix, take som (well-assessed) risks... You will go on some amazing field trips with the course (so much money pumped into this uni) so you will also get cool experiences without taking any initiative. Living and studying here is not for everyone. If you don't like the cold, hiking and being outside doing type 2&3 fun, it's not the place for you. I think you can find other places where the town/city and indoor life is a lot more fun and cozy.
course_level: The level wasn't that hard. I would almost say it was easier than back at Copenhagen but that's also wrong as it's so different. I definelty prefer the UNIS way, but the exams are much harder at Copenhagen. At the same time the project and poster stuff I had never done back home so this scientific writing was hard for me.
teaching_comparison: Applied biology vs theoretical. That's UNIS' whole thing. The field work was amazing. We went to Ny-Ålesund (79 degrees) in a twin otter, for a week. This was an insane (and expensive for UNIS) trip. Saw lots of polar bears and Arctic foxes. There is also no big seminars. the teaching is VERY intimate. Small classroom style and you're even friends with the teacher. Very different from the boring teaching elsewhere.
courses_enrolled: AB-201: Arctic terrestrial biology AB-204: Arctic population ecology
recommended_courses: I am a marine biologist at heart, so the AB-201 could at times be boring. But it was actually more about the Arctic in general which was still cool. AB-204 is mostly marine biology ecology tbh.
unexpected_costs: Sooooo much gear. There's a lot of gear to buy if you don't already own it. Spikes for the shoes, sleeping mat, sleeping bag etc etc. There is however an organization called student equipment where you can burrow (free) a lot of the essentials. The 300 for transportation is because I rented a bike from the university. this is optional and lots of people didnt.
cost_comparison: Eggs were less expensive. I was surprised by how cheap everything is after all you heard about Svalbard and the Arctic. but I think that's because everything in Denmark is already so expensive. Snowscooters are cheaper than I expected.
activities_available: I didn't really participate in the clubs, but I know there is kayak-polo, indoor football, skiing/ ice hockey in the spring, and so on. I was part of the diving club which is pretty dead at the moment. I did dive however and that was cool. I'm planning to try to start the diving club again for both free diving and scuba diving. Then you have the nature and the cabins which of course is where it's at.
activities_recommended: Go out in nature and sleep in the cabins. Spend some money for a cruise to Pyramiden. hike to Grumant. If you can find a boat, then go to Barentsburg. Explore the mountains. If you have a camera, go out and find the Arctic fox and reindeer. The university also owns a student cabin. Very cozy. Got to the Nordenskjold cabin. Go to the mines. Early in the season, go whale watching. If you manage to burrow/buy a boat then go fishing and explore the fjords!
weekend_recommendations: Lots of knitting if that's your thing. Some small cafes. There's great concerts. There's really good restaurants (pricey). And then of course the friday gathering and afterparties at Elvesletta afterwards.
culture_adjustment: Culture wise it's mostly norwegian. Climate wise, it takes some time.
socializing_tips: There are no local students. Everyone are guests and therefore looking for friends.
cultural_challenges: Nothing really. Mostly just the abundance of knitting and love for hiking/nature is different from Denmark
culture_appreciated: Love for nature.
top3_advice: 1. Beware that the stay peaks early. As in all the cool activities and field works is in the first half of the stay. It gets totally dark by 12th of November but already around mid October it's pretty dark. This can take a mental toll on some people. There is still things to do but not as much. Mostly skiing and ice caving in November and December. 2. Be aware of the unique application method for these courses in contrary to other exchange places. Read above for more. 3. Look into buying a boat with a friend or something. it really is worth it! Also some people applied for grants and got a lot of money despite already having the Erasmus. might be worth looking into.
other_useful_info: I think I've covered all of it in the above answers.
most_rewarding: The animals and nature.
greatest_challenge: Balancing school with social/outdoor life.

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: The location. For me, the most important was going to a place with beautiful nature. But also going to af city with af nice student environment.
overall_comments: It's is not a cliché that exchange will be one of the most amazing experiences of your life:) You really learn something about yourself.
info_ease: Sometimes a bit confusing, but it was doable.
arrival_assistance: There was an introduction week at the university, which was very nice and helpful.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It's is not a cliché that exchange will be one of the most amazing experiences of your life:) You really learn something about yourself.
registration_process: You just had to fill out a formular
registration_help: Not that much. The Exchange coordinator at UiT is not that good. But you can find your faculty/institute leader or something like that and they are very helpful!
registration_success: I wanted to take some very interesting master courses, but unfortunately, thats is no longer allowed at UiT if you are a bachelors student... However, of the bachelor-courses that I applied for, I got all the courses I wanted, and even managed to change later on, when I discovered a Norwegian course that i would rather have.
registration_advice: Find your institute leader and text them if you have questions about joining a specific course. They will help you.
academics_comments: It's is not a cliché that exchange will be one of the most amazing experiences of your life:) You really learn something about yourself.
course_level: Way easier than in Copenhagen and way less expectations at the exam.
teaching_comparison: Mainly lectures, very few theoretical exercise classes, if any, which is quite a shame. Laboratory exercises though. However, theres only very few at the lectures, so there's opportunities to ask the lecturer.
courses_enrolled: BIO-1103 Botanikk BIO-2504 Fish physiology BIO-2009 Nordlige biologiske ressurser (eller evt. Biologiske ressurser i nord) Det er det samme.
recommended_courses: Nordlige biologiske ressourcer! Det er et lidt skørt fag, men man kommer på en fantastisk ekskursion til Alta og får lov at prøve nogle ret særlige ting og kommer på et kortere marint togt på et forskningsskib. Det handler om norsk forvaltning af naturen, og man lærer en masse om hvordan norge forholder sig til naturen og hvilke ressurser der er. Et veldig bra kurs! Botanikk er lige som Organismers Diversitet på KU biologi bachelor ift. alger og planter. Bare mindre dybdegående... Så ikke om arktiske planter, men dejligt at have et fag man lidt havde haft i forvejen.
unexpected_costs: Food is expensive... And if you like being outdoors you might end up buying a lot of nice outdoor equipment;) Problems with landlord...
cost_comparison: Food was more expensive. Beers extremely expensive. Public transportation was very cheap if you bought the monthly pass for young adults on Svipper. And the Tromsø zone is very big so you can go really far without having to buy extra. And very cheap to go on trips - become member of DNT and you can book beds in lovely huts for nearly no money!
activities_available: A lot! Choir, a lot of sports, Waffle-friday... Gardening, knitting...
activities_recommended: The Choir was very nice - and a lovely way to meet both locals and other exchange students. TSI - the student sports association. Theres a lot of different sports activities.
weekend_recommendations: Go as much as you can to the mountains! Kvaløya, Senja, Sommarøy. Go to the Lyngen Alps!!! The DNT-hut system is an amazing way to explore the nature if you are not to much into camping in a tent. Go climbing and swimming.
culture_adjustment: Very easy! Helps a lot being Danish and able to understand Norwegian.
socializing_tips: Join events and actively engage with them. They might not come and talk to you by themselves.
cultural_challenges: They eat dinner very early, so all social arrangement starts when you would normally have dinner...
culture_appreciated: The respect and use of the nature
top3_advice: - You will never regret going on a trip to the fjell! - Don't be afraid to ask other people if they want to join you doing something; they are just like you looking for someone to hang out with! - Be active! Don't wait for others to ask you, but do the things you want to do! Be the one that plans the trip, and reach out for others. - Don't be to disappointed with your courses; they might not be as you had hoped, but see it as an opportunity to go and enjoy Northen Norway even more!
other_useful_info: Get a Norwegian phone number and a TURBO (BUA) account! Then you can rent outdoor-equipment for free! Tents, sleeping bags, skiis, snowshoes... Bring your hiking boots! And a good backpack, sleeping bag and mat if you want to go camping a lot. It is annoying to coordinate going to turbo all the time.
most_rewarding: Experiencing how you can live and shape your life in a completely different way than you are used to! You get so many new hobbys and friends instantly that you might never want to leave again.
greatest_challenge: It is quite demanding that theres is always so much to do and you feel like you have to make the most out of everything. So remember that it is okay to say no and have a chill day at home, even though the sun is shining:)
other_comments: Tromsø is extreme, yes, but in an amazing way. Don't fear the darkness and the cold, you will have such an amazing time skiing and watching the everlasting sunset and northern lights that you won't notice. However, if I had not loved being active, hiking and in the mountains, Tromsø is a small city and you might be bored after some months. For me, the mountains compensated for everything bad, but it might be different for you:)

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
crucial_aspects: Wanting to experience life in the Arctic, especially midnight sun and polar night and all the snow and how people live with all that! And obviously also the mountains and fjords and nature overall :)
info_ease: Quite easy, a lot of information is given beforehand and if you don't know something you can always ask or send an email, everyone is really willing to help
arrival_assistance: Debut week gave information on important topics like registering in Norway, living with snow/darkness but also sports and other free time activities. But I think if you don't go to the orientation week it can be a bit difficult, although there are some emails sent out too. That week is also a great way to meet people so would definitely recommend arriving early enough
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You just look at the list of courses and then add that to your UiT application, really easy. There's a specific catalogue for courses that are open to exchange students. Although one of the courses I got approved was also not from the list so it's definitely possible to take other courses but probably depends per case
registration_help: The course catalogue and you could also just email any of the lecturers and the department or the mobility office, if you had some specific questions. They're happy to help
registration_success: Very successful!
registration_advice: The scheduling is pretty weird as every department/faculty has their own and they can overlap easily. Even though the semester started mid August, one of my courses didn't start until mid September so make sure to check the calendar. I was really busy in October for example because one of my courses was already ending so we had our project due and then two exams but the other course also had some deadlines at the same time.
course_level: Very similar to KU
teaching_comparison: I think the quality of teaching is pretty good. Also a lot of group work and projects which was fun. A lot more readings though
courses_enrolled: SPL-3014 Arctic Cities Field Course SVF-2107 Climate Change Adaptation
recommended_courses: Would recommend both! Arctic Cities especially is really cool because it's very applied and you learn a lot about Tromsø as a city and meet a lot of planners from the municipality. But you also get some really cool knowledge on cities in the Arctic overall and the region of Northern Norway. As the name suggests lots of field trips. Climate Change Adaptation was interesting too, also pretty applied and very focused on the Arctic and Norway. If you don't have any or only little knowledge about climate change I'd definitely recommend it, otherwise a lot of it will be repetition as it is an introductory course to climate change and only Bachelor's level
unexpected_costs: Nothing really
cost_comparison: Fruit and veg more expensive, otherwise pretty similar to Denmark. Alcohol also more expensive
activities_available: There's a student sports organization that offers pretty much any sport imaginable and there's also a gym on campus. Every other Friday there's free waffles. A good number of clubs like board game clubs, knitting, etc. Also a lot of conferences that are usually open to students too. ESN does a lot of events as well
activities_recommended: Tromsø is a very active and dynamic city, there's so many events and things happening that you can go to! Pubquizzes (highly recommend the one at Storgata Camping every Tuesday), karaoke nights, comedy nights, cinemas, small festivals and concerts, swimming pool, saunas. Also check Facebook for more specific events like flea markets or some shows
weekend_recommendations: Hiking!! As much as possible before the snow comes, the nature is just ABSOLUTELY breathtaking. Would also recommend sailing and camping (no need to bring tent or sleeping bag as you can rent that for free at Turbo). When the snow is there, I'd definitely say cross country skiing, it's pretty easy to pick up and SO easily accessible as there are tracks all over the island and on Kvaløya (again equipment can be rented at Turbo or bought for very cheap at Rebell, a big second hand store). Also lots of nice trips from Tromsø like Sommarøy, anything on Kvaløya, some glacial lakes and glaciers (Lyngen Alps), Senja, and of course cabins all over. For some trips you need to rent a car but it's pretty easy and the journey is already kind of the destination, as you're just driving with breathtaking and never-ending views of mountains and fjords
culture_adjustment: It's not that different compared to Denmark so very easy, the biggest difference was just that people are a lot more outdoorsy
socializing_tips: Sports and other social clubs
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The focus on nature and being outdoors
top3_advice: Go outside as much as you can, the seasons change so quickly and the semester will be over before you know it... Remember to start taking your vitamins early so you don't get depressed when the sun doesn't rise anymore. Consider applying for two semesters right away if you can because you might want to stay longer once you get there and realize how amazing it is! :) Bonus: if you have the time, take the train instead of the plane, the views on the way there are amazing!! Also pretty easy to go from Copenhagen, you just transfer in Stockholm and then take the night train to Narvik and from there a bus to Tromsø. But might want to plan an extra day as backup as the nighttrain isn't that reliable and delays are common
other_useful_info: Just reach out to people if something isn't working out and you will probably have a solution to your problem very quickly
most_rewarding: Honestly the nature with all its outdoor activities and living in the Arctic. Also seeing the northern lights everywhere, even from my room, was pretty cool!
greatest_challenge: Leaving :(
other_comments: I honestly didn't find the darkness that bad. You just kind of adjust to a new rhythm/routine as it gets dark so early that it's totally normal to still do things in the afternoon, like skiing or studying, otherwise your day would only be a couple hours long. Even during polar night it's not pitch black outside 24/7 but it does get lighter for a few hours every day. I was luckily done with my courses pretty early so I had more time to focus on friends and social activities and didn't have to study for exams in the darkness, then it would've been a very different story probably... The snow also reflects a lot of the darkness, so it always seems lighter than it actually is, especially on cloudy days, and on cloudless days you usually have northern lights! :)

institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
