At the end of the stay, you will most likely have visited way more places in Mexico than the average Mexican - most Mexicans don't even get to visit another state in their life. In this way, it is very priviliged to get a chance to have 5 months to explore this hugely rich cultural place.
registration_process: Quite easy, but a bit annoyingly bureaucratic. You had to both fill out a form and send a list of your choices to the coordinator.
registration_help: You can always ask the international office.
registration_success: I got every single one I wanted - I got a feeling that they were very flexible with helping you, and that you shouldn't worry too much about not getting your courses.
registration_advice: Don't worry too much about it.
academics_comments: Mexico really is an absolutely amazing country! So incredibly rich in culture.. The food, the beautiful colored buildings, walking around in a pastel heaven sipping on a fresh juice smoothie. Mexico is amazing. Understanding the diversity of this country has been one of most rewarding experiences of my stay. At the end of the stay, you will most likely have visited way more places in Mexico than the average Mexican - most Mexicans don't even get to visit another state in their life. In this way, it is very priviliged to get a chance to have 5 months to explore this hugely rich cultural place.
course_level: I had master's courses in Spanish even though I don't speak Spanish. It is not as fun, of course, to sit in class, but since many readings are in English, I still have learned a lot from writing my assignments, which my teachers agreed for me to do in English.
teaching_comparison: As mentioned before, very few class hours but a lot of time consuming assignments - at least one pr course pr week.
courses_enrolled: Governance and Political Theory Global Political Economy Regional Studies International Studies and Institutions
recommended_courses: Global Political Economy was really interesting, and the professors slides are in English, which made it way easier for me to follow his class. Regional Studies have an unproportional big workload, so I wouldn't recommend that course unless you want to study all your wake hours your last weeks of your exchange.
unexpected_costs: Mobile data is expensive I would recommend that you buy a subscribtion from the beginning on instead of ordering new data all the time from Telcel like I did - this way is flexible and telcel is a stable network, but it is way too expensive.
cost_comparison: Regular groceries in the supermarkets are not that much cheaper than in Denmark. Oats are more expensive, milk is the same, eggs only a bit cheaper. Eating out at every meal will almost cost you the same as cooking home-cooked meals.
activities_available: A lot of different things! Photography, dance and music classes, sports.
activities_recommended: I took ballet three times a week from 8-9 am. I didn't show up to most classes, as it simply was too early for me to get a good nights sleep if I didn't want to go to bed early most days. If I could do it all over, I would focus more on learning the dances of Latin America and maybe sign up for salsa in Cholula instead of at UDLAP.
weekend_recommendations: I went to the north, where there really was nothing to see. On the other hand, it was fascinating to escape the tourists routes and really meet the real Mexico, and in that way, it is one of the experiences I remember the most clearly. Travelling with some of the international housing and travel companies are cheap and accesable ways to get around and seeing a lot in a few days, but the bus rides are very exhausting, and there is often a lot of focus on drinking.
culture_adjustment: Not hard at all. Mexicans are very nice. I found it harder to adjust to the culture of many of the international students, who would be quite young and focus mostly on cheating on their partners back home and drinking. Cholula is a place where party is big, so you kind of need to make up your mind if you want to take part of that whole international party scene and mostly hang out with internationals, or try to seek out a bit more local experiences.
socializing_tips: Just meet them at parties. There are a lot of really really cool locals whom it is nice to befriend.
cultural_challenges: many people talk about the male "machismo" but I want to shout out that almost all Mexican men I was introduced to were very respectful and progressive - with a few exceptions. Men can be very insisting here, and walking in the streets outside of Cholula, you shouldn't let your guard down completely. Being in Mexico City alone as a woman was a big eye-opener to the constant sexism and unsafety facing women in Mexico. I went to the women's march on 8 March, and we were told to write down telephone numbers on our skin in case it got violent and something happened to us. Kidnappings also happens here, even in Cholula, so even though I didn't feel too unsafe in this little town, you still need to be careful. A french exhange student got kidnapped and had her nose broken last semester.
culture_appreciated: I mostly appreciated the diversity of the culture of the different states in Mexico. The richness of the different foods, costumes, costoms, beliefs - it is just overwhelming how much there is to do, learn and see here!
top3_advice: You are never going to see rugbrød during your 5 months here. Yesterday, I dreamt that a Mexican friend gave me rugbrød as a surprise present. Embrace it though, you will soon be home again. Bring: a good book. There are very few options for finding English speaking books, so buy your lonely planet - Mexico beforehand or buy it in Amazon. Also something surprising; the fashion is so different in Mexico, so don't except to buy your summer wardrobe while you are here - bring clothes you like with you from back home. I got one of my bras ruined while it was being washed, and it took me two months to find a reasonably pretty bra without padding here in Mexico. Padding is big here, and most clothes are fast fashion made of plastic materials - and not even that cheap either! So bring; - clothes you like (clubbing clothes too, as you will most likely go out a lot) - rugbrød - a warm sweater, as the weather changes a lot. You don't need your heavy leather boots or leather jacket though - I would think more in layers when I was packing.
other_useful_info: The stay at UDLAP is a bit like a prison sometimes. You have to show your ID card when you enter and exit campus, when you want to enter the library and even when you want to buy lunch! Security is such a big thing in Mexico, and since UDLAP is a private university, parents expect high leves of security. Also; except that the Mexicans you will meet at UDLAP will come from the very priviliged parts of Mexican society. They are still lovely all of them though!
most_rewarding: The richness of the culture.
greatest_challenge: The international students being quite young and wanting to party like in Danish high schools. But for sure you can choose a different kind of stay if this doesn't appeal to you. And if it does; enjoy!

crucial_aspects: That Spanish is the national language in the country of destination. In this way I was able to practice the language, both for personal reasons and for future career possibilities.
overall_comments: I enjoy more the way of studying in the University of Copenhagen, therefore not 10. It
info_ease: It was fairly easy to find the necessary information as both the host university and my home university send various e-mails with information e.g. about how to get to the university in Mexico, how to change a course or when and where exchange-meetings would be held.
arrival_assistance: I received written help via the host university's mail system, orally in the internacional office on campus as well as advice from other students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I enjoy more the way of studying in the University of Copenhagen, therefore not 10. It
registration_process: To gain 30 ECTS points I had to choose five courses. Initially it was a bit difficult finding all the necessary information about what courses was available during the spring semester. After choosing some courses and getting them accepted by the host university, one of the courses I had chosen was declined by my home university with the explanation that the course did not qualify as bachelor level. Therefore, I had to change one course. I wanted to change to a course taught in Spanish, but as I did not have a high enough score in the language test, initially it was not possible to take courses in Spanish. After talking with the internacional office at the host university, and changing courses twice I was allowed to change to a course taught in Spanish.
registration_help: Oral (inn person and via telephone) and written.
registration_success: It was successful as I got help from the international office at the host university changing some courses after the deadline of registration.
registration_advice: Do it within the deadline and if you are in doubt about something rather ask the host university twice. The people working at the internacional office are really helpful and want to make things work for the students.
academics_comments: I enjoy more the way of studying in the University of Copenhagen, therefore not 10. It
course_level: I had five courses, the level of some of the courses was fairly high. For instance the course of philosophy was fairly difficult. Two of my courses were on the other hand fairly easy academically, in the way that we did not go into depths with the material of the course. With that said I would still say that I have learned new things; in some cases more superficially.
teaching_comparison: It was quite a different fro the way of teaching at UCPH. I some ways it felt more as if being in high school in the way that you would get points for making your home work or coming to class. The students had more home work than at UCPH that you had to hand in every weak for the teacher to see that the students were participating in the course. At UCPH the students, at a higher degree, have the responsibility for their own attendance and how much they learn.
courses_enrolled: Humanistic thought (philosophy) Communication and Globalisation Bilinguisme Translation Practices Introduction to Translation
recommended_courses: I would recommend the two courses regarding translation, as the teacher was structured and held interesting clases. Furthermore, it is interesting if one is interested in the field of translation and linguistics.
unexpected_costs: Going on trips to visit different places in Mexico.
cost_comparison: Food was less expensive than in Denmark. In general it was cheaper to live in Mexico than in Denmark. Some cafes in the host town in Mexico had prices comparable to Denmark.
activities_available: Different celebrations such as internacional women's day, valentines day, sports installations such as a gym, a swimming pool, or football fields, different on-campus food markets, a library, seminars and cultural events such as art exhibitions or theater shows (though I did not attend the latter).
activities_recommended: Swimming in the pool, go to art exhibitions or fairs in the center of the university. Outside of campus explore small cafés, join a sports team, go to Climbing Club ´Moonrock Boulders´, by groceries and the mercado central. These are ways of engaging in the life of the town, maybe feeling more at home and finding hidden gems.
weekend_recommendations: Explore Cholula and Puebla, visit other regions of Mexico.
culture_adjustment: Overall it was fairly easy to adjust to the culture. As there where many exchange students in the town I lived, the culture was also affected by the presence of foreigners. Furthermore, local students where happy to help explain how something works, e.g. how to buy a sim card for your phone, which stores have the best prices or if some parts of the town are unsafe to walk in.
socializing_tips: Initiate conversations during or after clases, maybe asking for students´ contact information or asking if they would be interested drinking a coffee with you one day or if they can help you with practical information. My experience is that the local students are open and want to help and socialise.
cultural_challenges: Machisme
culture_appreciated: The people in Mexico are in general all quite open and helpful, also towards strangers. I really enjoyed the food as well. There are colours everywhere.
top3_advice: - Do not stress, people are helpful and will aid if you have any doubts about anything. - The way of studying and teaching is different from that of Copenhagen University. Of course this depends on the courses, but you might have a lot of homework all the time. - The teachers are open to help you if you want to move a deadline or have any doubts about anything.
other_useful_info: If you are living off-campus it might be nice to rent or buy a bike to get around the town faster and easier. There is a facebook page called something like ´venta y renta en UDLAP´ where students at the university sell used things. Here one might find things that one needs less expensive e.g. books, a bike, clothes, blankets etc. Even though you get recommended not walking alone at night, I did not feel unsafe walking alone at dark. The only thing is that you have to be vary of the street dogs. The dogs might be a bit aggressive at night, but during the day they do no harm.
most_rewarding: Meeting people from around the world, both local Mexicans and other exchange students was very rewarding and gave me other points of view of the world. Furthermore, understanding how the everyday life works in the town, and learning more Spanish was rewarding.
greatest_challenge: balance school work with activities in my spare time.

crucial_aspects: I chose my destination based on an interest in the local culture and society. It was not my first visit, yet I knew that Mexican culture attracted me since I had already visited the country once before.
overall_comments: In all seriousness, it was one of the best experiences of my life. However, it is crucial to keep in mind that an exchange stay is what you make of it.
info_ease: Mostly, this was fairly easy and the information was accessible.
arrival_assistance: UDLAP had arranged an 'International Buddies' program to help those arriving in the airport get safely to Puebla. This created a sense of comfort and was very helpful.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: In all seriousness, it was one of the best experiences of my life. However, it is crucial to keep in mind that an exchange stay is what you make of it.
registration_process: You have to use an online portal, yet finding your courses and registering for them is somewhat confusing.
registration_help: You can contact the international office physically or by email and they will be very willing to help you.
registration_success: It happened but did not have to be so confusing.
registration_advice: Ask for course descriptions at UDLAP in good time before you apply for your KU pre-approval of courses. If you study at the Master's level, you will have to contact the international office when registering courses for the second trimester.
academics_comments: In all seriousness, it was one of the best experiences of my life. However, it is crucial to keep in mind that an exchange stay is what you make of it.
course_level: Most were very insightful and the level was fitting, not too hard nor easy.
teaching_comparison: Much more group work. Less formal teaching setting. Less individual assignments. Softer deadlines. Lesser burden of work which I thoroughly enjoyed. Some semesters at KU, especially at the bachelor's level has an absolutely absurd work burden (2. semester in particular).
courses_enrolled: Business Economics. International Strategic Management. International Business. Company Talent and Culture.
recommended_courses: Business Economics was pretty difficult as far as the math goes but the teacher was awesome. If you wish to really improve your knowledge on business you should choose 'International Strategic Management' since the teacher of this course Francois Duhamel is extremely knowledgeable. The rest are fine. Company Talent and Culture has a Swedish teacher who is also really nice.
unexpected_costs: Food at restaurants are much cheaper than in Denmark, yet supermarket prices are almost the same. European products such as deoderant, etc. are more expensive. I was scammed by my housing organization out of 10.000 pesos. Public transport is much cheaper than Uber. You will find that you spend more on trips, etc. so that your monthly expenses will probably be higher than what you are used to from home even though you might think that the contrary is true given that you are in Latin America. Nevertheless, travelling in Mexico is still significantly cheaper than in many other locations.
cost_comparison: European products are more expensive than at home. Public transport has a reasonable price. Museums are free with student ID.
activities_available: The UDLAP_informa email will bombard you with activities that you can partake in. I participated in a 'represent your country' activity which was fun.
activities_recommended: Make as many friends as you can early on, this will help you later.
weekend_recommendations: Go to Puebla, Veracruz, Oaxaca, CDMX and wherever else you feel comfortable. Close to Puebla avoid Guerrero and Michoacan due to safety.
culture_adjustment: Mexicans are extremely inviting, friendly and open to foreigners. Their hospitality can be amazing such as when me and my friends were invited to a children's birthday party in CDMX with a family we randomly met.
socializing_tips: Make friends in class, your Mexican classmates will be open to hang out with you.
cultural_challenges: The lack of timeliness can be frustrating at times. Mexican time is much more relaxed than what we have in Denmark which is closer to German time. You cannot expect people to show at the time that you have indicated. There are wild dogs everywhere, which can also be annoying yet mostly they will not do anything to you.
culture_appreciated: The loving of fun and the hospitality. Mexicans truly know how to enjoy life (this will be very refreshing for you as a Dane).
top3_advice: 1) Do it. 2) It will be awesome! 3) Bring warm clothes for the winter-time, especially for when you have to sleep since Mexican houses do not have heating.
other_useful_info: Cholula and Puebla is truly a great place to live. San Andrés and the downtown of Puebla are amazing locations. You live in the center of the country, which gives you good opportunities to travel around. Make friends so that you have someone to explore with.
most_rewarding: The social part. My international friends, travelling around the country with them and also the Mexican friends I made. It was also very fun for me to date Mexican girls as this gave me the opportunity to practice my Spanish and get an insight into the customs and ways of living of the locals.
greatest_challenge: Figuring out which of the many sweet girls I wanted to make my girlfriend ;) It can be rough to be away from home if you get sick or something similiar that sucks happens to you.
other_comments: It is awesome, you should certainly go!

crucial_aspects: Da jeg lige var blevet student, rejste jeg rundt med rygsæk i mellemamerika og var derfor inspireret til at bo i et mellemamerikansk land, da jeg allerede følte at jeg havde tilknytning til Mexico, idet jeg allerede havde besøgt landet før og havde haft en god oplevelse. Desuden var det vigtigt for mig at studere udenfor Europa (og som ikke var et primært engelsk-talende land) derfor var jeg meget glad for at opleve hvordan KU havde samarbejde med UDLAP på nogen af de førende universiteter i mellemamerika
overall_comments: Jeg er virkelig glad for at jeg tog afsted. Jeg vil sige at det klart, for mit vedkommende har været en mere kulturel udveksling end en daglig udveksling. Jeg fik meget fornemmelsen af at være til gene for dem - så jeg var faktisk virkelig frustreret og ked af det de første dage fordi jeg oplevede en helt utrolig uprofessionel og uhøflig tilgang fra personalet ved det internationale kontor (specifikt omkring at skulle ændre fag, fx. fordi DE havde annonceret fag på engelsk og så mødte man op og så var faget på spansk - og så ville de ikke lade mig skifte til et nyt fag selvom jeg ikke var godkendt til at tage fag på spansk. Så vær OBS på det og sig det med det samme der er det mindste. Vores koordinator hjemme fra KU har virkelig været en stjerne i den proces. Det hele skal nok løse sig til sidst - men de er virkelig nogen skrankepaver. Så de første uger var faktisk lidt tough ift. personalet og finde ro i at man kunne få alle de fag, man var godkendt til. Synes det var dybt kritisabelt den måde de tilgik det på (vi var over 30 elever i samme situation, så mit var ikke et enestående tilfælde). Så skift fag, sig det højt og hold fast. Efter alt det er landet, skal man heldigvis ikke have mere at gøre med de internationale kontor. Pudsigt de er så stride når de får nye internationale studerende hvert halve år.
arrival_assistance: Vitterligt ingen brugbar hjælp fra det internationale kontor. De andre udvekslingsstuderende, mexikanerne og KU-koordinatoren er den bedste hjælp.
arrival_comments: Jeg tror min kommentar ovenfor forklarer hvorfor jeg er utilfreds.

registration_success: Jeg fik 3 af de kurser jeg havde ønsket mig på forhånd (6 ECTS point pr. kursus) og så endte jeg med 2 jeg ikke havde ønsket, men var nødsaget til at vælge fordi de jeg oprindelige havde valgt var hhv på spansk og ikke engelsk og det andet var ikke blevet oprettet. De 2 andre fag jeg fik blev dog også forhåndsgodkendt af KU efter jeg kom frem - så alt gik fint-
registration_advice: Vælg alle de fag der er interessante gennem portalen, mærk efter når du er fremme om de er noget for dig, hvis der er det mindste problem så lad det internationale kontor vide det med det samme - og hold på din ret til at vælge om. Husk at den stressende fase med fag og forhåndsgodkendelse derhjemme kun er midlertidig.
academics_comments: Jeg er virkelig glad for at jeg tog afsted. Jeg vil sige at det klart, for mit vedkommende har været en mere kulturel udveksling end en daglig udveksling. Da jeg synes at det bliver klart meget hurtigt hvor højt fagligt niveau KU tilbyder os som studerende - og hvor (lav) niveauet er på andre top-universiteter i sammenligning.
course_level: Undervisningsniveauet var generelt ikke så højt, hvilket både kunne være befriende og frustrerende. Dog syntes jeg også at det afhang meget af hvilket professor man blev undervist af - hvilket var overraskende at der var så stor forskel. Jeg vil personligt anbefale fag med Viviana Ramirez og Richard Guy Emmerson, som var de undervisere jeg havde der levede op til dansk undervisningsniveau.
teaching_comparison: Som nævnt ovenfor er det meget meget gymnasiepræget. Du skal lave ugentlige afleveringer til nærmest alle fag (eller fremlæggelser) - men fordi undervisning niveauet er meget overskueligt så gør det ikke så meget. Karakterer er givet ud fra forskellige parametre (aktiv deltagelse, fremmøde, afleveringer, præstation ved fremlæggelser) så på den måde ligner det meget den danske gymnasiestruktur. Jeg føler det både har sine fordele og ulemper - jeg tror måske jeg blev lidt "mæt" af det til sidst. Jeg havde også kun 2 fag hvor der var en større afsluttende eksamen - derfor så betyder din deltagelse og dine afleveringer gennem semesteret r meget for din karakter (om du består), da du ikke kan vente til sidst på semesteret med at lave en mega god opgave og så bestå. Man skal lægge lige effort hele tiden. Men grundet niveauet er det altså meget overkommeligt. Karakterene går fra 0-10 og alt over 7.5 er bestået.
courses_enrolled: Public policies, Communication Globalization & History of International Relations, Sociolingusitics, Social and Political Theory
recommended_courses: Af disse var Public Policies og History of international relations mine favoritter - de andre var også fine, men væsentlig lavere niveau. Jeg ville anbefale de ovenstående pga underviserne som bare var knalddygtige og engagerende. Det var sådan nogle fag hvor jeg havde lyst til at gøre mig umage. Public Policies i særdeleshed var fedt fordi det er et fag alle de mexicanske studerende skal have i løbet af deres studietid og derfor var det for mig også en klassesammenhæng hvor jeg fik mulighed for at bonde med nogen lokale som blev blandt mine gode venner resten af semesteret. Desuden, så giver faget indsigt i mexicansk politik og lovgivning og sociale strukturerer hvilket jeg syntes var virkelig spændende - særligt når man kommer udfra og ikke ved så meget om de forskellige dynamikker i landet og de forskellige stater.
unexpected_costs: Jeg havde faktisk ikke nogen uforudsete udgifter i forbindelse med mit ophold. Jeg har skrevet 1500 DKK til mad, og det er måske i virkeligheden kun halvdelen jeg har brugt. Ift. danske priser kan du cirka dividere med 3 ift. hvad det koster. Så du kan leve virkelig billigt, hvis du også aktivt taget på det lokale marked i stedet for at tage i supermarked - og hvis du køber lokale vare istedet for europæiske importerede ting. Det er også virkelig billig at spise i UDLAP's kantine. Sådan 17 DKK for et måltid cirka. Det "uforudsete" jeg brugte penge på var klart de ture jeg to på i weekenden med Cholula Capital eller selv arrangerede
cost_comparison: Frugt er virkelig billigt (ananas, papaya, vandmelon, banan mv.) så det fik jeg hver meget med yogurt - omvendt var ost og "godt brød" ret dyrt. M4en man ændre hurtigt sine spise vaner, hvis det er det man ønsker.
activities_available: Hov jeg har vidst allerede besvaret noget af dette ovenfor. Jeg kan tilføje at universitetet har sit eget amerikanske-fodbold hold og baskethold. Det er virkelig sjovt at tage til kampene (der koster det symbolske beløb af 2 kilo bønner). Det er både en virkelig sjov og fed stemning og nærmest ligesom man ser det i amerikanske film med cheerleaders. Der er også koncerter flere gange om ugen for et symbolsk beløb! Tjek tit din UDLAP mail for at holde dig opdateret. Kan også anbefale at få lokale venner - de er virkelig søde til at tage en med til forskellige events man måske har overset!
activities_recommended: Jeg ville anbefale at melde sig ind i nogen af studenterforeningerne for at møde andre uden for dit housingselskab og for at få lokale venner. Det endte med virkelig at blive en af de allerstørste gaver for mig.
weekend_recommendations: Der er ofte second-hand markeder i Cholula hvor du kan få lækre vintage ting til en god pris! Desuden vil jeg sige rejs så meget som dit fravær kan holde til. Tag en tur til Atlixco (30 min væk), Hike Malinche (bjerg der ligger i Cholula), Tag en weekend tur til en af de omkringliggende stater med bus. ADO busserne er af høj standard og kører nærmest alle steder hen. Ellers så er flybilletterne indenfor mexico også relativt billige. Min egen favorit var Chiapas (besøgte San Cristobal de las Casas, Palenque, Tuxtla) - Det er virkelig et helt andet Mexico hvor der er mange flere indignous people og folk der ikke taler spansk. Virkelig spændende og stort at opleve. Brug en weekend i smukke Mexico City - der er altid noget at opleve"!! Hold øje med om der er nogen af dine yndlingsartister der spiller i mexico mens du er der! Både Paul Mccartney, Niall Horan og Travis Scott spillede mens jeg var der (og til virkelig god pris) Kan også anbefale Puerto Vallerta og Sayulita som er nogen af de mest queer-friendly steder i hele mexico!!
culture_adjustment: Jeg synes den første måned var en smule tough fordi man lige skulle finde sig til rette, finde sine folk og akklimatisere. Efter da syntes jeg det gik rigtig fint. Overordnet synes jeg det var relativt nemt - de andre udvekslingsstuderende er i samme positions som dig, Mexico er et relativt veludviklet land og hvis du kan bare lidt spansk på forhånd (eller prøver at lære det dernede) så skal det hele nok gå.
socializing_tips: Jeg vil sige: Lave det første move. "Hej må jeg sidde ved siden af dig" eller "Hej jeg er lige kommet, jeg kender ingen - hvor er det gode sted af drikke kaffe i byen?" De er klart mere generte end os - altså ift. at de ikke nødvendigvis henvender sig til dig, fordi de tror at vi helst bare vil være sammen med andre udvekslingsstuderende. Efter at det er blevet afkræftet mellem jer - så er de virkelig gæstfrie og søde og meget åbne. Ja, eller meld dig ind i en forening.
cultural_challenges: Jeg tror ikke jeg syntes at der var nogen der var overordnet markant anderledes. Det er et ret progressivt universitetet at gå på - men man kan godt fornemme at de fleste er ret katolske. Så det kan godt komme til at fylde lidt i flere samtaler.
culture_appreciated: Deres venlighed, åbenhed og ligefremhed. Jeg blev inviteret til både "de dødes dag" af min mexicanske veninde og fik lov til at opleve den tradition helt tæt på og endte med at fejre jul med en anden mexicansk ven. Så åbenheden, ærligheden og gæstfriheden kan virkelig noget.
top3_advice: Forbered dig godt hjemmefra (ift praktiske ting både med KU-ting, men også hvad du skal have med for at føle dig glad og godt tilpad) Vær åben, men ikke naiv (Tag i mod de muligheder, tur og venskaber der byder sig - tiden går som at blinke med øjnene. Mexico er dog Mexico så mærk efter om du føler dig tryg) Husk at det også er OK at synes det er overvældende og svært.
other_useful_info: Jeg tror at jeg har udfoldet mine tanker og følelser omkring udveksling. Det har været en fornøjelse for mig, og jeg synes at jeg er blevet meget klogere på mig selv og på Mexico. Jeg er endda inspireret til at tage i praktik i Mexico på min kandidat, fordi jeg bare synes at landet og menneskene er så skønne her.
most_rewarding: At jeg fik nye venskaber fra hele verden som jeg ved at jeg kommer til at møde igen i fremtiden.
greatest_challenge: Ensomheden i starten. Jeg syntes det var svært at finde ud af hvad jeg havde lyst til, hvem skulle være mine venner - men efter den første måned og alt stress og flyvene tanker havde lagt sig - så blev det hele godt

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne bo i et land der adskiller sig markant fra Danmark kulturelt såvel som sprogligt. Yderligere har jeg altid været fascineret af syd- og Mellemamerika.
overall_comments: Mit udvekslingsophold var fuldstændig fantastisk. Det var mere end jeg turde håbe på og jeg kan kun anbefale at man vælger at studere på UDLAP i Cholula.
info_ease: Det var ikke super gennemskueligt at finde kurser på UDLAP, man satser mest bare på at de kurser som ligger på deres hjemmeside også bliver oprettet når man selv skal afsted, hvilket mange af dem ikke gør. Jeg fik først mit endelige kursusprogram da jeg var i Mexico og havde startet på mine fag, og krydsede bare fingre for at mit fakultet (SUND) ville godkende alle mine fag.
arrival_assistance: Udvekslingskoordinatoren fra UDLAP stod i CDMX lufthavn og tog imod de studerende der landede og ledte os hen til den bus vi skulle tage for at komme til Cholula, hvilket var meget betrygende, selvom det er ret nemt selv at finde vej til og fra hovedstaden. Der var 2 dages orientation på UDLAP, hvor man kunne blive vist rundt i byen og på campus.
arrival_comments: Hele introforløbet på UDLAP var ret forvirrende og nogle af de kurser som jeg havde valgt blev ikke oprettet og nogle var på spansk, selvom der stod i kursusbeskrivelsen at de skulle foregå på engelsk.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Mit udvekslingsophold var fuldstændig fantastisk. Det var mere end jeg turde håbe på og jeg kan kun anbefale at man vælger at studere på UDLAP i Cholula.
registration_process: Man får tilsendt en word-fil med de kurser man kan vælge (dog er denne liste af fag fra året før, så det er ikke garanteret at man kan få lov at vælge de samme fag igen, hvis kurset ikke bliver udbudt)
registration_help: Udvekslingskoordinatoren var meget presset da hun stod alene med alle udvekslingsstuderende, så jeg vil anbefale at få hjælp fra de andre studerende.
registration_success: Jeg fik de fleste af de kurser som jeg ønskede mig, men mange af dem blev ikke oprettet. Der var ikke så mange relevante fag for min studieretning, Folkesundhsedvidenskab, men jeg fik en indsigt i Internationale Relationer som også var meget spændende.
registration_advice: Jeg kan varmt anbefale kurset Human Rights med Prof. Samuel Stone. Han er en fantastisk underviser, og det har været et af mine yndlingsfag igennem hele min uddannelse (også herhjemme). Yderligere nød jeg virkelig Public Policies med Vivianna Ramirez - meget dygtigt underviser.
academics_comments: Mit udvekslingsophold var fuldstændig fantastisk. Det var mere end jeg turde håbe på og jeg kan kun anbefale at man vælger at studere på UDLAP i Cholula.
course_level: Jeg er/var selv kandidatstuderende da jeg tog derhen men der blev ikke udbudt nogle MA-fag som var relevant for mig derfor tog jeg 5 BA fag i stedet for 4 MA-fag.
teaching_comparison: Se mit svar ovenfor.
courses_enrolled: Public Policies Human Rights Theory of International Relations History of International Relations Communication and Globalization (lad endelig være med at tage dette fag - underviseren er ikke dygtigt og det er på ingen måde universitetsniveau)
recommended_courses: Som skrevet ovenfor, Human Rights med Prof. Stone og Public Policies med Prof. Ramirez.
unexpected_costs: Transport var dyrere end jeg havde forventet, hvis man tager lange busture rundt i landet. Feks. en bus til Puerto Escondido koster omkring 400 DKK. Men lokal transport med collectivos er meget billig, f.eks. fra busstoppestedet tættest på Cholula (Paseo Destino eller CAPU) koster det omkring 50 pesos. Yderligere var jeg også overrasket over hvor dyrt det er at have 5G. Man kan købe simkortet Telcel, hvor man skal tanke op med 5G hver gang man løber tør - man kan maksimalt køber 8GB per gang, som koster 500 pesos.
cost_comparison: Mad, husleje og tøj. Der er virkelig mange fede genbrugs butikker og loppemarkeder i Mexico generelt og hver 4 uge er der et kæmpe loppemarked i Cholula med en masse fedt tøj! :)
activities_available: UDLAP har mange smukke faciliteter (man kan tydelig mærke at det er et privat universitet, hvor der går rigtig mange velhavende mexicanere). De har en pool, store fodboldbaner, amerikanske fodboldbaner, volley og basket hal, atletik baner osv. Derudover er de også kendte for deres kunstprogrammer, hvor de udstiller kunst fra de studerende, har koncerter og danseopvisninger.
activities_recommended: Det hele. Orienter dig på campus og snak med de mexicanske studerende - de er enormt søde og vil meget gerne vise deres campus, by og land.
weekend_recommendations: Nyd først og fremmest Cholula - det er en enormt hyggelig by med rigtig mange lækre restauranter, cafeer (de har surdejsbrød, god kaffe og lækkert bagværk), og rigtig meget lækkert street-food. Jeg var selv de følgende steder imens jeg var i Mexico, hvor jeg tog afsted med en gruppe venner: - Chiapas (smukkeste stat som ligger sydligst i Mexico ved grænsen til Guatemala) i 6 dage - Oaxaca (kyststat med kendt surferstrand (Puerto Escondido) og Oaxaca City som er Mexicos kulturelle epicenter med helt vildt mange lækre restauranter, både lokal mad men også michelin stjerne restauranter. - Taxco (en by som er bygget oven på en sølv mine, så man kan købe sølv smykker for næsten ingen penge) - CDMX (Mexico City self. Der skal man tage hen - jeg tror jeg var i byen 6 gange i alt. Min alletiders yndlings storby. Fantastisk mad, museer, gallerier, street-food, tøjbutikker, loppemarkeder, klubber og barer.) - Yucatan og Quintana Roo (smukke strande, pyramider og dykkersteder) - Guanajuato (en flot stat, især hovedstanden som også hedder Guanajuato med underjordiske tunneller som er fyldt med markeder)
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Mexicanerne er enormt åbne og varme og helt vildt gavmilde. De tager imod en med åbne arme og man føler jeg meget hurtig tryg i deres land, specielt i Cholula.
socializing_tips: Vær nysgerrig på deres land og kultur - de vil meget gerne dele den med dig.
cultural_challenges: Ikke nogen.
culture_appreciated: Deres måde at være på, deres mad og farverige kunst og tøj. Det er som at bo i et land med et skønhedsfilter på - alle mure er malet i de skønneste farver og deres mad smager fantastisk.
top3_advice: Tag afsted. Du har ikke lyst til at komme hjem igen.
other_useful_info: Tag endelig kontakt til mig - jeg har en masse gode tips, råd og anbefalinger. Der står at de ikke anbefaler at man skriver sig navn på, men hvis du har nogen spørgsmål så hedder jeg Emma Vejlgaard og læser folkesundhedsvidenskab. :)
most_rewarding: Det hele tror jeg - alle de mennesker jeg mødte og alle de ture jeg tog på.
greatest_challenge: At vænne sig til at bo i et land som ikke taler dansk eller engelsk.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to a spanish speaking country so i could improve and use my spanish but also be able to take my academic courses in english as my spanish is not good enough for university level.
overall_comments: Mexico is a great destination for a semester abroad, I had an unforgettable experience.
info_ease: fairly easy
arrival_assistance: if you arrive on the recommended day of the university there will be university staff at the airport to help you find the right bus to cholula. the first 3 days at the university where orientation days where we got most of the information we needed
arrival_comments: the orientation was good but the assistance was not. The international student coordinator was rude and not very helpful and it was difficult to change courses.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Mexico is a great destination for a semester abroad, I had an unforgettable experience.
registration_process: the platform for the registration process was easy to use but they had several issuses with it and so uploading the documents and getting them accepted was difficult. they extended the deadline several times because of the issues.
registration_help: there is a whatsapp group for all incoming students where there is a lot of information, but people also ask a lot of questions and it can be hard to navigate. I also emailed the international coordinator alot and she was very helpful however she quit before we arrived and the new coordinator was very rude.
registration_success: I got most of the courses i wanted except of the spanish ones i applied for. when I arrived we were told we could potentially change courses and ask about avaliability. whoever when I ask about the beginner spanish courses the coordinator questioned if ihad past the spanish placement test and told me that the course was full. I found out later talking to people whohad the course that the class was only half full.
registration_advice: be patient and dont be afraid to email and ask questions. the information is not great so you have to ask for a lot of additional information which is easy enough to get if you ask.
academics_comments: Mexico is a great destination for a semester abroad, I had an unforgettable experience.
course_level: I had a few different course levels some were first year courses and others third year. I would say that the general level of the courses are lower than at KU. So if you are looking to be challenged academically UDLAP might not be the place for you.
teaching_comparison: it much more like gymnasiet, there is a lot of group projects and presentations, hand in assignments, homework that has to be done and uploaded, and attendence. the clases are small and most of the lessons are a seminar style rather than a lecture but if also depends on the teacher.
courses_enrolled: TEORÍA POLÍTICA Y SOCIAL I TEORÍA DE LAS RELACIONES INTERNACIONALES DERECHOS HUMANOS HISTORIA DE LAS RELACIONES INTERNACIONALES COMUNICACIÓN Y GLOBALIZACIÓN
recommended_courses: DERECHOS HUMANOS with Samuel Stone was an amazing course, he is a great and passionet teacher and the course covers some really interesting topics both internatinal and mexican.
unexpected_costs: not really any
cost_comparison: housing is cheap and so is eating out, grocceries are not as cheap as you might expect but still cheaper than in denmark.
activities_available: there where several activities provided both by the university and the clubs, like movie nights, or womens rights talks, sports matches and lanugage groups. the university also had bigger celebartions like on independence day with activities, dance and food trucks.
activities_recommended: use the sports facilities and go to the football matches, and the bonfire nights with revolución violeta
weekend_recommendations: go on trips around mexico, it is very easy to get around by bus to most parts of the country and there are soo many beautiful cities and nature. I would definately recommend going to Chiapas to see the palenque ruins and San Cristobal althought it is a longer trip. Closer to cholula I recommend hiking La Malinche, its amazing or staying in a cabin close to the volcano popo that you can see form cholula.
culture_adjustment: very easy, it helps to know basic spanish enough to order and be polite, traffic is a bit more caotic so be careful when walking or biking.
socializing_tips: a good way to talk to the people in your classes is to do group projects together and go from there. most of them are very helpful and sweet and will invite you to parties and such. be good at asking for instagrams and whatsapp this a good way to make contact with the local students and show them that you are interested in getting to know them. Also inviting them to the international student events.
cultural_challenges: Time and being punctual is a bit different here so dont be too stressed when meeting people or going to things on time other than class.
culture_appreciated: people are very open, helpful and friendly
top3_advice: enjoy the city and the university and its social life travel as much as you can during your stay dont stress to much about the courses
other_useful_info: exams nearly all fall in the same week so dont make too many plans the last week of the semester
most_rewarding: just being in mexico and creating and everyday life in cholula and at the university while also getting to visit amazing places on the weekends
greatest_challenge: keeping up with school work, not because the level is difficult but because there are a lot of assignments and deadlines to keep track of and different teachers will use different platforms.
other_comments: generally I think UDLAP is a great university and cholula is a wonderful city to live in and i would definatly recommend going

crucial_aspects: That I could have courses taught in both english and spanish as well as a general interest in the culture of Mexico and Latin America.
info_ease: It was easy.
arrival_assistance: There was a trip to the city of Puebla, and other practical information during the first days before the semester started.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was really difficult to register courses, as they had to match courses that i would otherwise have had on my own campus, so they had to be accepted by my own uni. On the website on UDLAP there's no syllabuses and not a lot of information about the courses, so it took a while to get everything accepted.
registration_help: They have an international office that you can send e-mails to for help and questions. The reply time was quite long sometimes though.
registration_success: I got the 4/5 of the courses i applied for. then i had to change 1.
registration_advice: Start in good time so you dont get stressed with everything in the end. The preparation for going on an exchange is a long process with many practical things to get in order before.
course_level: I think that the level of the courses was as expected.
teaching_comparison: It was in general the same style of teaching, with a lot of interaction and inclusion of the students in the classroom.
courses_enrolled: LIO3022 - Pragmatica LPT2042 Sistemas politicos comparados LRI2022- History of International Relations LRI3052 - CONTEMPORARY LATIN AMERICA LRP2032 - Comunicacion y Globalizacion
recommended_courses: My favorite two courses were sistemas politicos comparados and history of international relations. They are both available in english and international relations also in spanish. I really liked them because of the topic.
unexpected_costs: None.
cost_comparison: Nothing.
activities_available: There are sports clubs and a nice gym. Honestly i didn't really use any of the social activites at the uni.
activities_recommended: Fiestaaa
weekend_recommendations: Travel! It's a beautiful country with amazing people and culture.
culture_adjustment: Of course it's always a bit of a culture shock arriving to a place so different than what you're used to at home. But for me i quickly got used to it and grew to like it more and more.
socializing_tips: Talk to people that you have classes with. Everyone at uni speaks good english, but if you can speak a bit of spanish it's an amazing way to connect to people as well.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The people, the food, the music
top3_advice: Find a nice place to live, i would definetly recommend staying outside of campus, but of course everyone is different. Learn just a bit of spanish before, it will make your life there much easier and more fun. The bureacracy in Mexico is slow, even in universities, so start your paperwork early.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: The friendships and people that i met, and the cultural insight i got. It's different living in a country for 5 months than just travelling, you really get a different feeling of how people are and live.
greatest_challenge: Having 4 final exams in 4 days..

crucial_aspects: I was interested in the culture of Central and North America
info_ease: Quite easy
arrival_assistance: At the orientation, you are sufficiently filled in on courses and registration - There are plenty of other exchange students, so it is easy to set up groups to figure out stuff
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Easy to figure out; They publish the relevant course lists quite late in the process though. Other than that there are people to help you with everything.
registration_help: There are a few "incoming coordinators" that help you with everything from course registration to printing copies of your passport for the internationals office - in that sense it was quite easy. The orientation tells you everything you need to know.
registration_success: Pretty succesful; I enrolled in four out five first priorities.
registration_advice: Take it easy - you can handle most problems that may occur, when you get to UDLAP.
course_level: 3 of my courses were way to easy to be Uni level. 2 of them were more challenging.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching resembles Gymnasium in DK - There is a lot of homework compared to back home, a lot of assignments and a limited amount of absence. Most of the work is relatively easy compared to my education back home though.
courses_enrolled: History of International Relations, Humanist thought, Sociolinguistics, Psychotherapy and Communication and Globalization.
recommended_courses: Humanist Thought was a great philosophical course ! I would recommend taking any courses that is taught by Francisco Iracheta; All in all a great instructor, a very inspiring guy.
unexpected_costs: ADO busses for travelling - i travelled almost every week, which was one of my main priorities, and the busses are nice and safe, but a bit expensive.
cost_comparison: Most things are quite cheap; ADO busses to get around in the country can be a bit expensive
activities_available: Dancing, music, singing and sports.
activities_recommended: I knew a few people who took salsa lessons, which they were very impressed by
weekend_recommendations: Travel as much as you can ! Oaxaca, Chiapas, CDMX !
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy
socializing_tips: Go to the local dancing clubs to learn salsa, do the sunday flee markets, do sports at campus
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The holidays ... Day of the dead, independence day, new years
top3_advice: Stay somewhere off campus
other_useful_info: In my opinion, don't listen to people who tell you Mexico is not safe; As long as you use common sense, everything will be fine - The mexicans are a great, welcoming and chill people
most_rewarding: The friends i made
greatest_challenge: I dont feel like i had any
other_comments: No

crucial_aspects: Crucial for choosing my study destination were language and culture. I wanted to improve my language skills in Spanish. I also wanted to learn more about different cultures and was particularly interested in the Latin American continent. I wanted to take advantage of learning from a different, non-Scandinavian academic environment, as both Bachelor and Master I studied in Scandinavia.
overall_comments: I very much enjoyed my study abroad experience. I learned a lot of new skills and met people from around the world. I am very grateful for this opportunity.
info_ease: Some information was quite accessible, other information was difficult to gather. There, it helped that was in contact with other students from KU who went to the same exchange University. More information was available for Bachelor students, Master students were often not in the same information channels and neglected.
arrival_assistance: The International Office was always accessible, however, usually did not follow up on my requests for information.
arrival_comments: A lot of information was accessible for Bachelor students, Master students were not granted the same access to information. Yet, there were guided tours, which were nice and helpful. But, there was not mentor programme or so organized from the University.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I very much enjoyed my study abroad experience. I learned a lot of new skills and met people from around the world. I am very grateful for this opportunity.
registration_process: There is a portal for the incoming students. Some functions were difficult to access. Later, we had to register for different courses, which was not very easy either.
registration_help: There international office was helpful at times.
registration_success: I was able to register to all the courses I wanted. However, some interesting courses were offered on Saturdays.
registration_advice: It was difficult to find out the course syllabus. Even upon request for more information it was difficult.
academics_comments: I very much enjoyed my study abroad experience. I learned a lot of new skills and met people from around the world. I am very grateful for this opportunity.
course_level: I took courses at Masters level. Some courses content was repeatition of courses I had during my Bachelors.
teaching_comparison: At UDLAP, there was mandatory attendance and classes at Masters levels were taught in the hybrid format. The class size was much smaller. There were usually weekly assignments.
courses_enrolled: International Studies and Institutions, Trade Agreements in Emerging Economies, Regional Studies and Global Political Economy.
recommended_courses: International Studies and Institutions and Global Political Economy.
unexpected_costs: Most of my budget I spent on travelling and exploring
cost_comparison: Food was very affordable
activities_available: All kinds of Sports activities, dancing, and social events.
activities_recommended: Salsa classes and using the free sports facilties.
weekend_recommendations: Travels as much as possible! There are many things you can learn during it. There are many affordable travel opportunities during the weekends.
culture_adjustment: Mexican society is very welcoming and open. It was fairly easy to adapt. However, many things work very different compared to Denmark, which one has to get used to first, such as security.
socializing_tips: There are many organization such as "cholula capital" which organize many social events for international students. This made it very easy to get to know international and local students.
cultural_challenges: There were few cultural differences, such as security, or student life. In Denmark, it is much freer, whereas it is much more regulated in Mexico. Additionally, UDLAP is a very expensive privat University which reflects the inequalities of the country. This is very different to the University life in Denmark.
culture_appreciated: The welcoming nature and openness of all Mexicans, which I very much appreciate.
top3_advice: I would recommend the students to be open for new experiences, adventures, learn Spanish and travel as much as possible.
other_useful_info: I would recommend making use of the organizations that host events for international students. They were very helpful and a place to meet lots of people.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part was to meet many new people and improve my Spanish.
greatest_challenge: It was challenging experience University in Spanish and navigate every day challenges.
other_comments: Enjoy!

crucial_aspects: Jeg studerer indianske sprog og kulturer, så ville gerne til det område jeg har studeret
info_ease: Nogenlunde, men det man ikke får at vide inden finder man ud af når man ankommer. Ingen grund til at stresse over det
arrival_assistance: Jeg blev modtaget i lufthavnen af en medarbejder fra UDLAP som hjalp med at komme på den rigtige bus til Puebla
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Kursuskataloget hos UDLAP er meget uoverskueligt og jeg fik valgt nogle forkerte ting, men man kan vælge om i introugen
registration_help: Ikke meget, der er langsomme svar på mails. Men igen, i introugen er der masser af hjælp og man kan lægge hele sin kursusplan om.
registration_success: Jeg fik de kurser jeg gerne ville have
registration_advice: Undlad at vælge kurser i weekenden og endda om fredagen, så du har forlænget weekend og bedre mulighed for at rejse rundt
course_level: Gymnasieniveau, vil jeg sige.
teaching_comparison: Mange lektier, strenge med fravær og deltagelse i undervisningen. Men niveauet er lavere end uni i DK, så man klare det sagtens.
courses_enrolled: Sociolinguistics, theory of international relations, history of international relations, artistical investigation og Cultura Mexicana (spansk kursus)
recommended_courses: Sociolinguistics var fantastisk, hyggeligt og lærerigt. Cultura Mexicana er super til at blive bedre til spansk!
unexpected_costs: Det koster en del at rejse rundt i weekenderne hele tiden. Det løber op i sidste ende, men er det hele værd.
cost_comparison: Det er semi-dyrt at købe SIM-kort og fylde det på med data. Brugte flere penge på det end mit CBB abonnement hjemme i Danmark
activities_available: Fitnesscenter, udendørs pool, running track, tennisbaner osv. Alt sammen gratis!
activities_recommended: Kulturelle aktiviteter på campus. Nogle gange er der danse, forestillinger, koncerter, "horror-runs" til halloween og meget mere.
weekend_recommendations: Rejs rundt i Mexico og se andre stater, de er vidt forskellige alle sammen! I Puebla er der også meget at se og vulkaner at bestige! Til hvis man vil på tur uden overnatninger.
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Vær opmærksom på drikkepenge-kulturen, ikke kun i restauranter.
socializing_tips: Dem skal man nok komme til at snakke med, bare vær social, tal med folk på uni, på gaden, i byen, i butikkerne, til fester osv. De lokale er meget åbne!
cultural_challenges: Uønsket mandlig opmærksomhed, når man er kvinde. Man vænner sig til det, men det er selvfølgelig super irriterende.
culture_appreciated: Musikken, glæden, maden, festlighederne osv. Hver dag er en fest! Selv apotekerne spiller reggaeton til dagligt! Nyd det
top3_advice: - udnyt UDLAPs faciliteter som fitness, pool osv, men også deres billige kantine gode bibliotek - Det kan være ligeså billigt at spise ude som at spise hjemme, men det bliver fedtet og usundt med tiden. Udnyt frugt og grønt markederne!! - Lav alle de små lektier du får for i løbet ugen, så du har weekenden fri. Der kommer mange ting man gerne vil lave i weekenden, om det er at rejse, tage til det lokale genbrugsmarked, bestige en vulkan, you name it. Alle de andre udvekslingsstuderende laver en masse fede ting i weekenden, og det ville være synd at gå glip at det pga. lektier
other_useful_info: Eksamenerne varierer meget fra kursus til kursus. De er nemme nok, men de er læreren der bestemmer hvordan lektier, opgaver og eksamen ser ud. Og niveauet er sådan at du kan vælge et kursus i noget du ikke aner noget om. Det gjorde jeg. Så udnyt det og vælg nogle spændende kurser du måske ikke ville vælge herhjemme.
most_rewarding: De mennesker man møder fra verden over. Venskaber for livet:)
greatest_challenge: Savnet til dansk bagværk. Heldigvis er Cholula lidt gentrificeret og man kan sagtens finde godt bagværk (og surdejsbrød!) her, men det måler sig ikke rigtig med dansk kvalitet. Det er også svært med tidsforskellen til Danmark, ift. at finde tid til at tale med familie og venner derhjemme.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to learn Spanish and at the same time I saw an exchange semester as an opportunity to try to live in a country that was significantly different from Denmark.
overall_comments: I have had a fantastic experience, however, the way of being a student at a Mexican university is very different from what I know from home. I found it to be less challenging, more led by professors and less characterized by self-study, which can of course be both an advantage and a disadvantage, however I prefer the "danish" way.
info_ease: I found it very hard to find information about the courses, which was stressfull to me when planning. However I know now that I was able to change courses during the first week of classes and therefore I wouldn't have had to stress about it :-)
arrival_assistance: Tania, the exchange coordinator from UDLAP was waiting for me at the airport in order to make sure that I was able to find the bus and arrive safely to Puebla. I also visited her office several times for help with my visa, where the university prolonged my visa (it was only valid for 3 months and I needed 6) and furthermore the international office at UDLAP helped with changing courses etc.
arrival_comments: Especially super helpful that they fixed my visa problems and were waiting at the airport to help.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I have had a fantastic experience, however, the way of being a student at a Mexican university is very different from what I know from home. I found it to be less challenging, more led by professors and less characterized by self-study, which can of course be both an advantage and a disadvantage, however I prefer the "danish" way.
registration_process: preregistration and then a possibility to change courses during the first week of classes.
registration_help: Going to the international office at the university or writing them an email
registration_success: Almost got all the classes I wanted
registration_advice: if you want to learn or improve your Spanish, I really recommend taking the spanish test in order to be able to take classes in spanish, I took some beginner level classes and I learned a lot!!
academics_comments: I have had a fantastic experience, however, the way of being a student at a Mexican university is very different from what I know from home. I found it to be less challenging, more led by professors and less characterized by self-study, which can of course be both an advantage and a disadvantage, however I prefer the "danish" way.
course_level: I found it easy to follow along the courses even though I took classes that differed from what I am used to back home. Not all my classes were challenging, but I still enjoyed them.
teaching_comparison: Grades are given depending on assignments during the semester, final exams, participation and attendance. In that way it is very different from back home. I found it weird that the professor took attendance, since I am used to being at university because I want to learn, however it wasn't a problem , but reminded me a little of going to gymnasium instead of uni.
courses_enrolled: Cultura Mexicana (in Spanish) Sociolingustics Artistic investigation History of International Relations Social and Political Theory II
recommended_courses: I really recommend taking the course Cultura Mexicana (in Spanish) and also the other spanish beginner course called Lengua y Communication. I only enrolled in the first mentioned since I thought my level was too low (I had practiced some Duolingo and could order a coffee and that was almost it), but I regretted not taking both because I really learned a lot and would have loved to have both. I really enjoyed the teaching by -NAME REDACTED- (who taught History of International Relations). His methods are more similar to how my professors at UCPH teach and I found him very inspiring. Sociolingustics was interesting if you want to learn more about languages and how they interact/are in contact, it was a very chill class but I enjoyed it a lot.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Busses are a little expensive compared to how cheap traveling in general is in Mexico, however they are really comfortable and safe and a great way to experience the country
activities_available: There were a lot of events arranged such as Mexican folk dancing, celebrations of "dia de muertos" and other national holidays and also football matches etc. Make sure to join them! the university uses many funds on this and it is a great way to experience Mexican culture.
activities_recommended: Go watch Mexican folk dancing, celebrations of "dia de muertos" and other events at the big auditorium. You get an email when there is something coming up, some are free and others cost around 30 dkk-100 dkk.
weekend_recommendations: Take as many trips as possible. I made sure to have Fridays off from classes and in that way I was able to go away for more than just two days.
culture_adjustment: I found it extremely hard in the first two days / half week. Everything seems so different than Denmark: the sounds, the houses, the food, the language etc. I missed my friends, family and boyfriend, however it turned around quickly and I met a lot of other exchange students, that also had the same experience as me. Now, I am super happy that I fought through the hard part in the beginning.
socializing_tips: Mexican people are some of the nicest and most welcoming people I have ever met and all the other exchange students were exited to meet new people too. My best advice is to attend a lot of things with other students, arrange trips etc, but also remember to take some time off. I usually relax when I am with other people, but I experienced that being with people that I didnt know very well didnt necessarily give me more energy even though I liked spending time with them. And if you want to skip an event, it is completely okay, people rarely remember if you went to all of the parties, trips, game nights etc <33
cultural_challenges: Mexico is a very loud country! I was woken up every morning by roosters and fireworks from the nearby church. Remember to bring earplugs.
culture_appreciated: The people are extremely welcoming and warm. Everyone always greets eachother and Mexicans really want to help if you are lost or need any help. The food is amazing too, and then I was overwhelmed by all festivities and richness of culture. Mexicans are really good at celebrating and it is amazing to experience things such as dia de muertos, Independence Day, Posadas (in Christmas time) and other things!
top3_advice: Learn Spanish! Not many Mexicans outside the bigger cities speak English, but they are really nice and helpful when they hear that you try to learn and speak their language. Try to meet Mexican people, since they are extremely hospitable and welcoming. You will have so many great experiences if invited by a Mexican to something. Pack lightly if you like vintage/second hand clothes - there are both flea markets and great second hand shops in Cholula. I bought a lot and had to carry two big suitcases home, since I had brought too much from home too.
other_useful_info: Go to UDLAP and Mexico if you want to experience the country, the culture and the nature. I have learned more schoolwise at UCPH, so dont go if you only want to go to classes and afterwards sit in your room and study :-D
most_rewarding: Learning to live alone in a country very different from Denmark and experiencing the richness of Mexico and how lovely people in Mexico are.
greatest_challenge: The first week, settling in a new country where you dont know the language and where everything seems different. But give it time and tell yourself it is okay to feel homesick. It is really worth it
other_comments: Take some spanish courses outside the university! it is super cheap and you learn a lot

crucial_aspects: Salamanca is a historical university city, and I was seeking an academic challenge. I also wanted to stay in a smaller city, since it's easier to get to know others in a smaller city. I have friends, who study at the University of Salamanca, and they've spoken positively about the city, which encouraged me to apply for my Erasmus.
overall_comments: It was lovely! I don't regret my decision at all.
info_ease: Somewhat easy. There are quite a lot of international students in Salamanca, and my coordinator was very helpful and always answered my questions whenever needed.
arrival_assistance: Mainly from my coordinator, Alejandro Lozano. He helped me answering the questions I had, and helped me change the subjects that I had to change.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It was lovely! I don't regret my decision at all.
registration_process: I had to do the matriculation, after I had recevied my Online Learning Agreement. The matriculation took part mainly online, and I then had to go and get my student ID (which I never received, as they failed to inform me how to get it).
registration_help: Mainly help from my coordinator.
registration_success: Quite successful, as my coordinator helped me finding the courses I'd wanted tot take.
registration_advice: Don't hesitate to reach out and ask questions! The coordinators are more than happy to assist you.
academics_comments: It was lovely! I don't regret my decision at all.
course_level: I had four courses in the 4th year, and one in the second year. The level was somewhat high but quite different from Denmark.
teaching_comparison: In Denmark, the professors expect the students to participate in class, and ask critical questions, while in Spain, it's much more about memorizing everything in class, and not asking nearly as many questions. It's more about looking at a PowerPoint, and writing down everything.
courses_enrolled: Theory of Art, Image Aesthetics, Political Philosophy, Cultural Philosophy, History and Tipology of Religions
recommended_courses: I'd highly recommend Political Philosophy and Cultural Philosophy, as those subjects are fairly more doable than others. The professors are also very open towards Erasmus Students.
unexpected_costs: Personally, I didn't encounter anything
cost_comparison: Most things were cheaper than expected since Spain is a more affordable country than Denmark.
activities_available: There were some presentations and sports activities. I didn't participate in any
activities_recommended: N/A
weekend_recommendations: I'd highly recommend doing the excursions that are offered by the different Erasmus organizations. I went on five trips; one to a nearby village, one to Portugal, one to Seville, one to a hiking area, and one to Bilbao and San Sebastián. It's an excellent opportunity to bond with other international students.
culture_adjustment: It was pretty tricky in some ways. The Spanish culture is very different from the Danish one, and Spaniards aren't the most social ones when it comes to foreign students.
socializing_tips: Maybe try to join a sports club, where local students are playing. Some local students are more open than others, so definitely try to do some group work with them. Some local students volunteer in different Erasmus organizations and are easier to bond with.
cultural_challenges: Definitely that Spaniards aren't very keen on befriending international students. Most of my friends, myself included, had very few local friends.
culture_appreciated: Definitely the siesta culture! Having a break in the afternoon is very well-needed, especially when the courses are quite heavy. And I loved the food as well, as well as the outdoor culture.
top3_advice: 1) Consider how you want to live (student dorm, shared apartment...). 2) Have several subjects in mind. 3) It's okay to fail an exam, in most cases you can repeat the exam.
other_useful_info: Don't be afraid to ask questions, the professors and coordinators are there to help you.
most_rewarding: Experiencing growth, both personally and academically!
greatest_challenge: Overcoming cultural boundaries, for sure.

crucial_aspects: The classes I could take were the most important, as well as the language the classes were in.
info_ease: It was very easy, the Erasmus office was always replying very fast.
arrival_assistance: I got help from a friend who had studied there the semester before, and then I met some Erasmus organisations, and also got a lot of help from the Erasmus office at the host university itself.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I had to go physically to their erasmus office, and fill out some paperwork, but it was very simple and I only had to go one time.
registration_help: The erasmus office at the university
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted and didn't have to change during the semester.
registration_advice: To ask all the questions you may have, the erasmus office are very sweet and take their time to help you.
course_level: I chose courses that were in the last year of their bachelor (4th year of university), because of this the courses requiered that you had studied beforehand, and I noticed this level both in the teachers as well as the students who shared a knowledge and compassion of the topics studied. The level fitted quite perfectly for me.
teaching_comparison: They give you much more homework and assignments that you have to do, and in most of my classes you also had to participate actively in class to be able to get a good grade.
courses_enrolled: Ética y Teoría Feminista Pensamiento Filosófico II Estética de las Creaciones Literarias Historia de la Filosofía Española e Iberoamericana Literaturas Europeas Contemporáneas
recommended_courses: Literaturas Europeas Contemporáneas was an especially international class, because we were mostly exchange students. However, one of my favorite courses was Ética and Teoría Feminista, where we were only two exchange students, however, the teacher was very nice to include us and it was especially an interesting class because I got to compare feminism in spain and latinamerica vs. my own country.
unexpected_costs: I did not encounter any unexpected costs, however I did choose to go travelling, which also adds to the budget.
cost_comparison: I found out that my housing was quite expensive compared to what the spanish students were paying
activities_available: We were never introduced to the different activities available, so you had to go out and find it yourself I took a painting course directed by one of the student organisations.
activities_recommended: The painting course was a really fun way to meet other exchange students
weekend_recommendations: There are a lot of places close by where you can go hiking. Apart from that, the train to Madrid is really cheap, so it's easy to go on a daytrip to Madrid or continue from there to other places.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy for me, since I've been living in Spain before. The students were very open to include me in their activities.
socializing_tips: Be open and ask quesitons. Most students at the university of Salamanca actually come from different parts in Spain, this means they are usually more open to talk to exchange students as well.
cultural_challenges: Getting used to the spanish timetable, especially since Salamanca is a smaller city all the shops and restaurants close in the middle of the day during siesta.
culture_appreciated: There were a lot of festivities where all of the city joined in. Especially the classical guitar music is something I enjoyed very much.
top3_advice: 1. To prioritize studying during the semester, otherwise you won't have enough time to study for the exams. 2. Take time to search for activities, they might be hard to see at first but there's actually a lot of student sports etc. 3. Make some spanish friends, you'll get better at the language and they might help you if you need notes or other help for the studies.
other_useful_info: In general they requiere a lot to get a good grade, so it's a good tactic to study persistently all through the semester so you don't drown in studies at the end. That said, don't forget to enjoy the Erasmus life!
most_rewarding: I have definitely learned a lot in my classes and I have become much more independent in my studies. This is a maturity I will bring with me.
greatest_challenge: For personal reasons I felt a bit lonely in the beginning of my stay, however, I was lucky to find some very good friends later on. I would say it's good to try and make as many friends as possible especially in the beginning.

crucial_aspects: I could choose between Madrid, Cáceres, Barcelona or Salamanca. I went with the place that i already hadn't been to and which wasn't a metropolitan big city. That is, i went with Salamanca. Moreover, I like to explore new places without looking into them beforehand and so I thought Salamanca would be a fun experience in that regard since it is more or less unknown to the common man outside of Spain. Also i got to study philosophy which i had gotten a taste for up until that point, considering it was a requirement for going there, and so i thought 'Let's goooo'. Why not. Let's try something new. What is the worst that could happen?
overall_comments: The spanish system of education is what i would call in my common tongue a "rodebutik". Would not recommend going there for educational purposes since the bureaucracy is what sailors in time past memorial called drowning 'like going home'.
info_ease: I don't recall there being any special information that i needed to know upon getting there. That being said, it as quite easy finding my way as long as one can ask for directions and so forth so there is that.
arrival_assistance: I don't recall there being any assitance at all.
arrival_comments: There is basically none, but that is fine. I expected it and found my own way.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: The spanish system of education is what i would call in my common tongue a "rodebutik". Would not recommend going there for educational purposes since the bureaucracy is what sailors in time past memorial called drowning 'like going home'.
registration_process: It is like the last time i went on exchange with erasmus. There is a lot of unnecessary bureaucracy going back and forth between institutions, signing, expressing that 'yes, i comply to the rules' and so forth. So i knew what i was going into.
registration_help: I don't recall there being any. Although, there might have been some available, but as i recall it i think it was more catered towards students of bachelors degrees.
registration_success: I was successfull, although, and i thought this being there for the first weeks getting a feeling for the classes, there is no way that i would be able to choose any other classes, since the registration process for getting the classes approved is incredibly cumbersome and slow. The option is obviously there, but before getting through with the process of actually getting them registered so that one can get access to the host university's webpage before being halfway through the semester is just not a realistic proposition.
registration_advice: Choose carefully the classes that you want to pick because there is no time to change them one you get there. The system is simply too rigid. And make sure also that you make sure your classes are within a certain timeframe one from the other during the day. That is, don't choose classes in the morning and in the afternoon on the same day.
academics_comments: The spanish system of education is what i would call in my common tongue a "rodebutik". Would not recommend going there for educational purposes since the bureaucracy is what sailors in time past memorial called drowning 'like going home'.
course_level: Competent teachers obviously, but the overall level of the academic programme was brought down by a cumbersome rigid system that is impossible to follow. That is, the programme is chaoticly put together, or at least so was the ones i chose. For an example, i had 6 small courses at 3 ECTS each, those courses each were then SUBDIVIDED into smaller sessions, for an example directed by 3 different teachers over several weeks intermingled with other courses. This ended up in me actually missing an exam because i was handed a portfolio document not knowing it was an actual exam that needed to be handed in since the course and the examination document had diferent titles.
teaching_comparison: Veyr different since every teacher has his own style. Some used the intranet for giving out homework, other only in hand. Some used the chalkboard for teaching, some just taught with a monologue and others used PP as well.
courses_enrolled: -Textos de Historia de la Filosofía IV (ES PAÑOLA E IBEROAMERICANA -Pensamiento Filosófico y Científico Es pañol -Historia de la Estética y de la Teoría de las Artes -Metodología: Problemas, Métodos y Líneas de Investigación en Historia de la Filosofía -Filosofía del Lenguaje I -Filosofía de la Ciencia: Nuevas Dimen sione -Metodología de la Ciencia: Ciencias Natu rales, Semióticas y Humanas -Historia de la Filosofía Moderna y Con temporánea
recommended_courses: "Filosofía del Lenguaje I", although i would only recommend it if the student has a passion for linguistics with an aptitude for mathematics as well (of which i didn't). The teacher is great and the subject very interesting if you were to dive into subjects beyond the grammar of languages. "Historia de la Estética y de la Teoría de las Artes". Interesting subject that for our part delved into the philosophy behind how art and aesthetics is/could be perceived. Good teacher as well, although a little finecky and controlling at times. "-Historia de la Filosofía Moderna y Contemporánea", had a good selection of teachers that all seemed quite competent and engaging in each their own subject. Interesting chats.
unexpected_costs: housing was more expensive than anticipated
cost_comparison: housing was more expensive, food was less expensive. Also going out for eating is many times a better deal than buying groceries in the supermarket.
activities_available: There were quite a bit, but the majority from what i could see were for bachelor students.
