crucial_aspects: A good receiving university, good weather, receiving country culture in general.
info_ease: Nova SBE assisted well in providing sufficient information upon arrival. However, the bidding system for choosing courses before arrival was difficult to navigate as an exchange student.
arrival_assistance: Folders with general information, presentations and a good introduction to the university.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You have a profile at a bidding platform. This platform has all the courses with descriptions, timetables, exam dates etc. And then it is up to you to make sure that you choose courses that do not overlap - both in terms of classes and exam times. After you have decided on courses, you use your bidding points to "bid" on each course. If there is great demand and few spots in a course, students will be allocated seats in accordance to how many points they have allocated relative to each other. So, as an exchange student it is difficult to know which courses are "popular" (and therefore would be wise to allocate many points to) and what courses you can get with few (or even zero) points. I would advice to look at the available spots as the main indicator for how many points to allocate. There are two bidding rounds. So, if you bid points on some courses in the first round and you do not get a spot in these courses, your points will be given back to you for you to use in the second round of bidding.
registration_help: The International Mobility Office was very good a providing guides/online introductions and answering e-mails to assist with questions. But, as mentioned before, this was also necessary due to the pretty complex system you need to navigate in when your courses.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Spend a decent amount of time reading courses descriptions before bidding on courses. While this gives an idea of the content of each course, be aware that these descriptions are not always very good at describing the relative difficulty of the courses. As such local students will "try out" courses the first couple of weeks of the semester and change if they do not like the course. This option is not available to exchange students, and therefore you are "stuck" with the course you have been allocated to once the classes start. I took "Introduction to Machine Learning" as a course. The description of the course was relatively sparse, and once the classes started we observed many local students drop out as the teacher explained that this was an extremely demanding course with a high workload. However, as this point we as exchange students were fixed to the course. We spent many, many hours on this course, and it would have been nice if it had been stated in the course description how high the workload was, compared to other courses.
course_level: The courses varied greatly in difficulty. I think I have both had the easiest course and one of the most difficult courses (Introduction to Machine Learning --> NOT an introduction, if you ask me :)) ) of my university studies at NOVA on this exchange. In general, though, the courses are much easier than at UCPH. The masters courses do also have a much smaller syllabus than we are used to at UCPH, since most of them are only 3,5 ECTS credits. As such, you should expect to have quite a lot of courses (I had 8 courses).
teaching_comparison: Smaller classrooms, maximum of 70 students. Closer relationship to your professor. They expect more classroom participation. Many more presentations in the classes. Grades are often a type of average between in-class presentations during the semester, hand-in's, and the final exam. The final exam typically weighs 50% of the final grade.
courses_enrolled: Economics of Health and Health Care Environmental Policy Economics of Health Systems Financial Crises in History International Migration Impact Investments Entrepreneurship Introduction to Machine Learning
recommended_courses: Financial Crises in History was pretty fun. It was nice to learn about what happened in past financial crises, and to dive into the general characteristics/recurrent topics that they have in common. Economics of Health and Health Care was good as well. The professor was really nice, easily my favorite professor of this exchange. International Migration was cool. The professor is pretty well-known for her contributions to this field of research and it was one of the most academic/research based courses I took.
unexpected_costs: Be ready to spend quite a lot of money on events and trips. In general it is quite cheap to travel, eat and sleep when going on trips, but it still took up the majority of my spending here. Travel costs are by far the greatest expense of the exchange, but Portugal has so many beautiful places to visit so I wouldn't hesitate to spend some savings here ;))
cost_comparison: Housing was more expensive than expected. Car rentals were way cheaper (!!). It was cheap to eat out at restaurants, but we did it relatively often so it was quite a big expense as well. Make sure to bring some savings in addition to the Erasmus grant and SU.
activities_available: The Nova Student Union was very good at inviting us/including us in all of the events offered to local students. This was everything from parties, paintball games, sunset bars etc.
activities_recommended: Go travel!!! Porto, Nazaré, Peniche, Erriceira and many more places in the North. Lagos, Sagres and many more places in the South. You can also get very cheap tickets to Madeira or the Azores if you go out of season (maybe €40 for a plane ticket).
weekend_recommendations: Join the social events organized by the student union.
culture_adjustment: Not a problem. Very chill and open culture.
cultural_challenges: Not any, really.
culture_appreciated: They are very open to international students, workers, etc. Pretty quickly you don't feel like a visitor, but just as another international living and having their day-to-day life in Lisbon.
top3_advice: Allocate most of your money to housing, travels, and eating out. Housing was more expensive than expected, whilst travel and restaurants just offer so much more for your money compared to Denmark, so you have to make the most of this!
other_useful_info: The courses have quite a lot of group work. This can be annoying since you spend quite a lot of time preparing presentations etc. with other students. Do not expect that you can just put in minimal effort, since you will often be placed in group work with local students and their grade will depend on your performance as well. So, even though the difficulty is not too bad, be prepared to spend some time at school anyway (because you have to sit with other students for group work).
most_rewarding: To experiencing the Portuguese culture and be given the opportunity to truly adapt and have your day-to-day life in these beautiful surroundings.
greatest_challenge: It was a bit annoying to spend so many hours studying and preparing presentations in groups. I expected to be able to go surf between lectures, and while that was possible sometimes, I often found myself with obligations to do some group work after or in-between lectures.

registration_process: It was so confusing. They had a lot of confusing and contradictory information on the different platforms (website and sharepoint documents). They changed the ECTS points on the courses from 7,5 to 7, but it only said so sometimes. The enrollment was very stressful, and because I needed some specific courses to be able to obtain 30 ECTS it was crucial for me that the website worked, but it didn't. Sometimes some courses weren't showing. My friend and I also applied for the exact same courses at the exact same time, but he ended up getting completely different courses than me - random courses that he couldn't use, so we have spend so many hours at the student counsil trying to fix this, but they were no help. After around 1,5 months we finally fixed the problem by getting our home university to contact the professor at Nova, that had the course he couldn't enroll in (because it wasn't showing on the website in the post-enrollment period), and he luckily ended up getting the course. But we had to come up with this solution ourselves. I think if it was me this happened to, I would have wished that I would just have stayed home in Denmark, which sound very dramatic, but it was so stressful.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to stay in Europe because of the Erasmus grant, and I thought Lisbon was the most “exotic” destination Europe has to offer. The warm climate, with summer lasting until November, was very appealing. Additionally, I really wanted to learn how to surf. I chose my destination primarily based on the lifestyle and activities available rather than academic opportunities.
info_ease: It was easy. As long as you remember to check your email, you will receive all the necessary information from both KU and NOVA.
arrival_assistance: I did not need any assistance upon arrival. However, NOVA had an Erasmus Student Center help desk where students could get support with study-related questions, for example if they experienced issues with course registration.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: NOVA divides course registration into two rounds. In the first round, registration is not first-come, first-served. Students submit their course preferences, and places are assigned randomly. I was fortunate to receive almost all of my preferred courses in this round, although some students only received a few. The second round is first-come, first-served. NOVA sends an email in advance with information about when registration opens, and it is important to be ready at that time. I did not get my remaining courses immediately, but persistence helped, as places continued to open up. The second round was open for approximately two to three days.
registration_help: There was limited formal assistance available. Most of the helpful information came from earlier Erasmus students who shared their experiences. I was concerned about not getting the courses I wanted and contacted NOVA by email. However, there was not much they could do, and the only option was to register during the second registration round. In the end, everything worked out, and I was able to enroll in all of my courses.
registration_success: I was able to register for all of my preferred classes. Almost everyone I know also ended up getting the courses they wanted.
registration_advice: Do not give up during the second registration round. Check the registration page frequently, as spots may open up during the two to three days of the registration period.
course_level: Most courses were below the academic level at UCPH. Only Advanced Microeconomics was equivalent to the level we are familiar with from home.
teaching_comparison: Lectures were much smaller, typically with around 30 students per lecture. Practical classes were also different, as students did not work independently on exercises. Instead, the instructor went through examples. There was more structured and mandatory activity, such as class presentations, which made the teaching style feel more similar to a Danish high school than to UCPH. However, the atmosphere was relaxed, and attendance was generally not registered, except for tests or presentations.
courses_enrolled: Advanced Microeconomics, 7 ECTS (pre-approved as Micro III) Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History, 3.5 ECTS (pre-approved as Economic History together with Economic History) Economic History, 3.5 ECTS (pre-approved as Economic History together with Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History) Development Economics, 7 ECTS (pre-approved as Development Economics) International Trade, 7 ECTS (pre-approved as International Economics) Ethics, 3.5 ECTS (taken to fulfill the 30 ECTS requirement)
recommended_courses: I would highly recommend Advanced Microeconomics! I have generally not enjoyed microeconomics courses in Denmark, but the professor teaching this course at NOVA (Paulo) was excellent. The course is pre-approved as Micro III (Game Theory), but it covers material from Micro I, Micro II, and Micro III. The academic level is comparable to UCPH, and the lectures are very well structured, with clear and intuitive examples that made the material easier to understand. I also enjoyed the two history courses, Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History and Economic History. Both courses must be taken together in order to receive approval as Økonomisk Historie. Although I did not attend many lectures, I found the course readings very interesting, especially for students with an interest in history.
unexpected_costs: did not encounter any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: pretty much as I expected.
activities_available: NOVA has a fitness center on campus, although I did not personally use it. Also, the student club Mindspace organized activities such as yoga and pilates classes held at the beach for approximately 3–6 euros per session. There is also a surf school called Lisbon Surf Camp located at Carcavelos beach, about a 15-minute walk from the university if you follow the beach. While it is not officially part of NOVA, they offer special deals for Erasmus and NOVA students. For around 50 euros per month, students can get four surf lessons and eight equipment rentals, which is very affordable. The staff was extremely welcoming, and they also organized a surf trip to southern Portugal in November, which was a great experience.
activities_recommended: Go on weekend trips with friends and surf:) Watch the sunset from one of the many miradouros (viewpoints) in the city.
weekend_recommendations: If you surf, Ericeira and Peniche are great destinations, and I would strongly recommend joining the surf trip organized by Lisbon Surf Camp. If you have travel insurance through a credit card, it is often possible to rent a car for as little as around 5 euros per day, which makes road trips with friends very accessible. Beyond surfing, there are many other experiences to enjoy. A weekend trip to Madeira for hiking is highly recommended, as the nature is absolutely stunning. Porto is also easy to visit from Lisbon by FlixBus. And go to Sintra and beach Ursa. Also, a trip to Nazaré to see the world’s largest waves (often over 20 meters) and the surfers riding them is a must.
culture_adjustment: very easy:)
socializing_tips: I mostly socialized with other Danish students, as NOVA has a large international student population. At the master’s level, almost half of the students are non-Portuguese, which means that many social activities naturally take place in international groups rather than with local students.
cultural_challenges: none:)
culture_appreciated: The great weather and the amazing food (especially fish and other seafood).
top3_advice: Academically, the workload is manageable, so I would encourage students to prioritize making the most of their exchange experience. Take advantage of opportunities to travel, surf, and enjoy life outside the classroom, even if that occasionally means missing lectures.
other_useful_info: I think, I covered the most:)
most_rewarding: Having a lot of fun with great people. Lisbon is amazing!
greatest_challenge: no challenges:)

crucial_aspects: I wanted something within Europe to be able to finans my study abroad. I wanted somewhere with a different culture and different nature.
overall_comments: I loved studying abroad in Portugal! It is a very great country to spent a semester.
info_ease: I did not have a lot of issues with the information needed prior to my arrival. There was some confusion about classes and if my credits could transfer. They posted the classes for the semester late, so I had trouble checking the classes and so on until very close to my arrival.
arrival_assistance: NOVA hosted a welcome week where they introduced us to the basics we needed.
arrival_comments: We had trouble with the OLA. NOVA did not have access to the official website to sign it, and there was a lot of back and forth to get it signed the proper way. This was a little exhausting, however all the staff we talked to in person were all very helpful. The exam schedeule and the schedeule for midterms should be posted before the semester starts at NOVA, I would recommend to check these before planning any trips - as most midterms and finals are obligatory.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I loved studying abroad in Portugal! It is a very great country to spent a semester.
registration_process: See comment above.
registration_help: I think they had an email you could contact, however I did not need it.
registration_success: I got all classes but one - which luckily were all the obligatory ones, then I just had to choose an elective in the second round. I got Economic History, Micro 3 and Public Economics transferred as obligatory classes in Denmark, which was great.
registration_advice: Check the excel sheet with classes at KU that has previously been accepted. Search for information on the schools website and make a groupchat with other people going to the same destination - they might have found documents that you haven't:)
academics_comments: I loved studying abroad in Portugal! It is a very great country to spent a semester.
course_level: Some of the courses were easier than the ones at KU and some were the same level. I think the biggest difficulty is to understand the different learning methods used at NOVA. Overall the academic burden was smaller than what I am used to - but this might be due to the fact that all my classes were pass/fail based and that I had much more time (no student job).
teaching_comparison: We were taught in much smaller classrooms with fewer students resulting in a more intimate classroom. We both had practical and theoretical classes, however I found that they seemed less different than in KU. We did not have time to solve assignments and so on in the practical classes, it was mostly the teacher solving exercises as a lecture. Public economics and Advanced Microeconomics were similar to the teaching style at KU for the Economics Bachelor. Other classes were more discussion based and way more empirical than theoretical, which in my opinion was a nice change.
courses_enrolled: Advanced Microeconomics (7 ECTS) Public Economics (7 ECTS) Economic History (3,5 ECTS) Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History (3,5 ECTS) Seminar in European Economics (7 ECTS) Law in Business and Economics (3,5 ECTS)
recommended_courses: Seminar in European Economics !!! This was by far my favorite class. The class was discussion based, and the professor was really good. It was nice to experience a more empirical approach to teaching and learn how to apply economic theory to the world. You do have to write a free assignment over the time of the course, however I did not find the workload to be too bad, as long as you start in advance. Make sure to be in a group with people with the same ambition level as you. The workload was probably equivalent to one of the assignments in "Økonomi i samfundet".
unexpected_costs: To get the Navigante card you need to pay some fees. All the Erasmus events cost money. Many cafés and restaurants in Lisbon are very turist oriented, so the prices were higher than I expected, however everything is still cheaper in Lisbon than in Copenhagen.
cost_comparison: Coffee at the local cafés is only around 1-2 euro.
activities_available: NOVA had everything. Surf, Yoga, festivals, tennis etc. I was very impressed about the offers that NOVA had. There were a lot of different clubs like the surf club, sports club, student union (arranging parties etc), mindspace, several consulting clubs, green club and many others.
activities_recommended: I recommend attending the events hosted by Mindspace.
weekend_recommendations: Explore the country!! Madeira!!!, Ericeira!!, Porto, South Coast, Serra de Estrella.
culture_adjustment: This was pretty easy. Portugal is an easy country to be a guest. People are friendly and helpfull - much more than the Danes.
socializing_tips: Sign up for the activities in the intro week in time! Join the surf club (https://www.lisbonsurfcamp.com/) and reach out to other students before you go.
cultural_challenges: The biggest cultural challenges was that the public transportation is unreliable and that in Portugal things are less organized - "you can't control the sea, but you can learn how to surf" is the mantra.
culture_appreciated: The laissez-faire and openness.
top3_advice: 1. Double check the housing situation - you might not get the perfect place, but remember that it is only for a short amount of time. Do not let it scare you away from going abroad, but be aware of the fact that it is difficult to find good housing, and that you might need to make compromises. 2. Make sure to plan you trips early - time is going to run by so fast, and you should make sure to take advantage of the ability to explore the beautiful country. 3. Remember to bring a good rain jacket and a warm sweater + sweats to wear inside. Portugal is great and sunny most of the year. However in the winter it gets surprisingly cold out of nowhere. The houses are not built for bad weather and are difficult to warm up resulting in the need for big sweaters indoor during winter.
other_useful_info: See above.
most_rewarding: I loved my semester abroad. I loved exploring a new country and making the most of the different daily-life by using the outdoors way more than I do back home.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was the homesickness - missing my family and friends back home. However did this not outweigh all the great great things I experienced!

crucial_aspects: For at få det fantastiske vejr i Lissabon, gode muligheder for surfing og opleve sydeuropæisk kultur.
info_ease: Det sværeste var at få fat i de rigtige kursusbeskrivelser til forhåndsgodkendelsen. Derudover var kommunikationen fra skolen udemærket og de praktiske informationen fik vi, før vi kom.
arrival_assistance: Fik hjælp til at få underskrevet online learning agreement. Systemet virkede ikke for skolen, så det skulle gøre manuelt. Det nemmeste er klart at få den underskrevet i hånde og scannet ind efterfølgende. Forhåbentligt virker det til næste semester
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Vi skulle tilmelde os online gennem en portal også blev kurserne tildelt tilfældigt. Det var også først her man kunne se de kursusbeskrivelser som var gældende. Efterfølgende var der en Add and Drop periode, hvor man kunne skifte kurser eller vælge andre kurser, hvis man ikke fik det man ønskede.
registration_help: På Sharepoint, som man får adgang til inden kursusregistreringen, var det muligt at se skemaer og eksamensperiode før vi ønskede.
registration_success: Jeg var så heldig at få alle mine kurser, som jeg havde ønsket. Generelt fik alle næsten de kurser, som de havde ønsket.
registration_advice: Kan klart anbefales at planlægge lidt ud fra at få en fridag. Jeg lykkedes med fredag fri, hvilket gav gode muligheder for at lave noget i weekenderne uden at skippe for meget af undervisningen.
course_level: Jeg havde tre kurser i mikroøkonomi, hvor det matematisk niveau ikke var super højt, men der var mere fokus på intuitionen i opgaverne, så når der var styr på det, så var det meget overkommeligt.
teaching_comparison: Forelæsningerne var mindre end på KU og det er ingen mikrofon på, så sid tættere på for at kunne høre, da Portugiserne kommer for sent og det er ret forstyrrende. Holdundervisningen foregår anderledes, hvor en underviser gennemgår opgaver og man regner ikke selv, men noterer og ser hvordan det skal løses. Derefter bliver der ikke sendt vejledende løsning ud, så man skal være til undervisningen for at få svar på opgavesættet. Lidt en sjov opsætning. Derudover kører de 80 minutters forelæsninger uden pause også har man 10 min til næste starter, så lidt en anden struktur end på KU.
courses_enrolled: Advanced Microeconomics( Mikro III - 7 ECTS), Public Economics (P-fag - 7 ECTS), Industrial Organization(P-fag - 7 ECTS), Economic History (Økonomisk historie - 3,5 ECTS), Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History(Økonomiske historie - 3,5 ECTS), Human Behavior and Decision Making(Fyldefag til at få 30 ECTS i alt - 3,5 ECTS).
recommended_courses: De to historie fag som udgør økonomisk historie var meget spændende, var mindre teoretiske og med orienteret mod nyere verdenshistorie med et økonomisk perspektiv. Advanced Microeconomics var også godt, en god forelæser. Human Behavior and Decision Making var også super spændende og giver nye vinkler på klassisk økonomisk tænkning, som vi bliver undervist i på bacheloren i København.
unexpected_costs: Vi spiste den del ude, meget billigere end i København på lokale restauranter, men det løber bare op i længden.
cost_comparison: Drikkevarer i byen og på restauranter var billigere end jeg regnede med. Billeje er også meget billigt. Det kan betale sig at anskaffe et kreditkort, fordi det er krav for at kunne leje uden biludlejningens dyre forsikring. Kantinen på skolen er også billig, tre retters frokost for 4€. Bolig var dog dyrere end jeg regnede med, jeg tror de fleste jeg kender har betalt mellem 500-700€ om måneden.
activities_available: Skolen tilbød mange forskellige aktiviteter, som man kunne deltage i. I introugen har de et event med alle de forskellige klubber. Der er mulighed for det hele. Vi fik tennistræning gennem skolens sportsklub. Derudover havde de surfklub og en yoga klub. Der var også en masse foreninger med faglig interesse, som holdte forskellige event. Man kan finde en liste her https://www.novasu.pt.
activities_recommended: Vi tilmeldte os surfing gennem en af de lokale surfklubber på stranden. Det var super sjovt og man kunne købe et måneds abonnement med lektioner og leje af surfboard ret billigt. Derudover kan man finde mange forskellige aktiviteter på stranden ved skolen.
weekend_recommendations: Rejse rundt i Portugal, der er så mange dejlige steder. Det er nemt med billeje, men også med Flexbus, hvis man gerne vil til Porto eller Algarve. Cascais og Sintra, som ligger tæt på Lissabon er også gode dagsture, hvor man kan tage toget ud. Ericeria, Peniche og Nazare er også tæt på, hvis man er interesseret i surfing. Maderia eller Azorerne kan også anbefales.
culture_adjustment: Jeg ankom to uger før skolen startede, hvilket gav god tid til praktiske ting og falde på plads. Kan klart anbefales for at vænne sig til at tingene går lidt langsommere og ikke er ligeså effektivt, som derhjemme. Ellers er det relativt nemt at navigere rundt i byen og de fleste steder man kommer forstår og snakker de engelsk.
socializing_tips: Skolen er meget international, så der er mange studerende fra andre lande i Europa, især Tyskland. Hvis man gerne vil møde lokale ville foreninger og klubber være oplagt. Hvis man gerne vil møde mange fra andre lande, så er laver Erasmus også en masse aktiviteter.
cultural_challenges: Det mest udfordrende var at skolens anderledes struktur med lange forelæsninger uden pauser.
culture_appreciated: Meget imødekommende og snaksaglige portugisere. De lokale restauranter er geniale.
top3_advice: Vejret er virkelig vidunderligt og sammen med skolens placering gør det udvekslingen meget solrig og byder på strand. crucial_aspects: I had multiple ideas about which kind of exchange experience I wanted. Initially I wanted to a more ‘ambitious’ experience and considered universities in the US. However I also sensed a need to have a break from academic pressure. Thus I allowed myself to pick a less demanding destination in the end. I had a curiosity about surfing and wanted to experience some place warm. This left me deciding between Australia and Portugal. Ultimately I decided on Lisbon over Australia due to two main reasons. 1: it was economically attractive, as the cost of living are affordable and I was guaranteed the Erasmus stipend. 2: Lisbon allowed me to be relatively close to Denmark which made visits from my girlfriend possible during the stay.
info_ease: Information was relatively easy to access. I had a lot of information prior to arriving from having read the student reports on Mobility Online from earlier years. The school also sends plenty of mails.
arrival_assistance: We were offered to be connected to a local student who could assist us with questions of the school, social activities or what else one might need to get settled. However, many of us did not feel the need for this kind of help.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You register for courses in an online system. Be aware of the deadline days associated with this, as the courses have limited spots and are distributed as first come first serve. There seemed to be plenty of spots for courses like microeconomics III, Industrial Organisation, Public Economics, Economic History. However the smaller courses of 3.5 ECTS you will need to reach 31.5 ECTS in total (28 ECTS is not allowed by KU) were associated with a lot of competition. It was the case that some students had to pick between either Ethics or European Law if they were slow with the registration process.
registration_help: Emailing to student council at NOVA and a student office.
registration_success: I was able to get the exact courses that I wanted to as I was aware of when the registration opened.
registration_advice: Be aware of the deadlines and be ready to pick your courses at the time that registration opens. Also be aware of the time zone difference.
course_level: The courses are divided into 3.5 ECTS and 7 ECTS courses. The 3.5 ECTS courses only has lectures and no practical classes. The courses which are 3.5 ECTS begin either at the start of September or in the middle of October. Thus the semester is split into two sections (T1/T2) regarding the 3.5 ECTS courses. Thus you can consider if you want to have more classes in T1 or T2. I decided to have more classes in T1, which allowed me to have fewer exams at the end of the semester. The academic level was definitely below the level at KU. I would say that microeconomics III was less demanding that micro I back home. Of course new subjects were introduced which were sometimes demanding, but the math always remained relatively simple. For example we did not need to use Lagrange to solve equations and such.
teaching_comparison: It is quite a bit different. There are lectures and practical classes (holdundervisning) like at KU. However for most of the classes the lectures are way smaller in terms of students attending. Half my lectures would have no more than 40 students attending. The practical classes are a lot like back home. There are midterms in almost all classes. However there are almost no written assignments. There might also be oral presentations. The final grade is calculated by combining academical performance at different points throughout the semester. For example in microeconomics iii the final grade is calculated about as follows: FG = 0.6*final exam + 0.25*midterm exam + 0.15*multiple choice assignments. Exams for the economical exams are done with pen and paper.
courses_enrolled: Advanced Microeconomics, Economic History, Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History, Industrial Organization, Global Business Environment, Human Behaviour and Decision Making
recommended_courses: I recommend taking the mandatory courses microeconomics III and Economic History. Economic History will be approved by combining the two 3.5 ECTS courses’ Introduction to modern and contemporary history’ with ‘Economic History’. The courses are quite well taught I would say and also easier than back home. Economic history is very much a history class and quite different to the way it is taught at KU. Based solely on my personal (academical) interests I would recommend Industrial Organisation which is a Prioriteret valgfag back home. If you are more ambitious and don’t mind having a more demanding class, then I also think Introduction to programming is a fruitful course. I would not recommend the course Global Business Environment. This course was, to me, very unorganised and way too ambitious. However, the exam is VERY easy. Supposedly no one has failed the exam for the last couple of years.
unexpected_costs: Travel costs should be expected. I had expected this from home, but it was a bigger expense than I had imagined.
cost_comparison: It costs about 2/3 of the price to eat out compared to back home if you want the same quality. Thus you could have a fancy dinner with a glass of wine for about 40-50 euro per person or a very simple dinner with a beer for 15 euro. Groceries are a bit cheaper. Transport is super cheap. Monthly unlimited public transport for 40 eur and a 15 min uber ride costs maybe 6 euro.
activities_available: There was a bunch of different clubs/associations that one could participate in. A few of my friends actually ended up doing that. You are also able to sign up for different sports very cheaply through NOVA. I played tennis twice a week for 40 euro a month. It is also very cheap to rent tennis courts.
activities_recommended: I would recommend surfing, tennis, padel and using the social activities arranged by NOVA.
weekend_recommendations: Do whatever you feel like. There are plenty of options and you can do almost all the things you can back home, just with new friends. I recommend visiting Porto, Madeira and Ericeira.
culture_adjustment: I think it was quite easy. The locals are very friendly and most speak fluent English. Also Lisbon has become quite an international city making it easy for foreigners to settle in. To be honest I did not engage very much the local culture however. I ended up making good danish friends and spending all my time with them.
socializing_tips: I can only base my tips on the experience of friends that succeeded with local friendships. They did so by engaging in the social clubs/associations at NOVA which have many local students or by connecting to the local student that was offered through the school.
cultural_challenges: The language is quite difficult, but if you don’t have ambitions of learning to speak Portuguese then you will have no problem. English is plenty sufficient to have a great exchange in Lisbon
culture_appreciated: The openness and laidbackness that I experienced from the local people.
top3_advice: Consider what kind of exchange you would like. For our semester it was very convenient to create a strong social group of danish people which I loved to be honest. However, I had hoped prior to the exchange hoped that I would engage myself more with local people and a mix of different nationalities. So if that is something you want, I would recommend being aware of this and pursue socialising on your own as well. Be aware of the day when signing up for courses open. Find housing early, as the options become significantly more expensive and limited the closer you get. Most people decide to stay in Lisbon and commute about an hour to school every day. This decisions seems to be something that almost everyone is very satisfied with. However, if you plan on surfing a lot, partying less and don’t suffer from FOMO, it might be worth it to stay close to the school. You can even stay ‘at the school’ as student housing is offered on campus. This way you will have less commuting day to day and will mostly need to commute into Lisbon, when attending social activities there.
other_useful_info: I would recommend to arrive a few days (or weeks) before the official welcoming day if possible. This time can be used to settle into the apartment before everything starts at once. I arrived two weeks before and had myself a bit of vacation in Lisbon. In these days I recommend acquiring the monthly transport card that you will be using every day for transport to university. It costs 40 euros a month and gives access to all public transport in and around Lisbon. The easiest way in my experience to get this is to go to the ticket office by the metro station ‘Marques de Pombal’. Be aware that is you are 22 (might be 23) years old or younger it is free if you apply for a local tax number as well.. There will be social activities on the first welcome day, which are quickly ‘sold out’. So if you have an ambition of meeting others NOVA students early through social activities, you should read your mail closely in the week prior and sign up.
most_rewarding: Catching loads of waves, creating memories and new friendships and catching a break from a demanding lifestyle back home
greatest_challenge: Listening to myself and declining an invitation to a social activity once in a while. Also being economically responsible, as the lifestyle gets quite laid back and the people around you most likely don’t care very much about limiting their expenses.

crucial_aspects: I have been to Barcelona a couple of times before and I really love the city. The fact that it is a big international city but also surrounded by nature and the sea was definitely important to me. Furthermore I really wanted to go to a Spanish speaking country to refresh my Spanish, and even though they mostly speak Catalan in Barcelona, I have definitely improved my Spanish.
overall_comments: The experience as a whole has been absolutely amazing!!! The administrative things around the university was a little slow, but everything worked out fine, so it was not a major thing.
info_ease: I managed to find everything I needed, but you have to keep up yourself and make sure that you have everything under control about the necessary documents and everything. But if you do that, it was definitely manageable.

housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: The experience as a whole has been absolutely amazing!!! The administrative things around the university was a little slow, but everything worked out fine, so it was not a major thing.
registration_process: After I received my pre approval I had to fill out a form for the host university, but everything is done by email, so it took a while, as I had to wait for them to reply. It was also a bit hard to figure out the language of the courses (but apparently if it says partly English, partly Spanish, it will be in Spanish - and the same with Catalan). I also had to get a signature at the administration office, which is not open that many hours a week, which was a bit annoying.
registration_help: If you seem desperate enough in your emails, they are okay at replying (somewhat quickly), and helping you figuring everything out.
registration_success: One of the classes I wanted was unfortunately cancelled that semester, but beside that, I got the classes I wanted in the first place. However, when I found out that one course was fully in Spanish, they told me that the class I wanted to change to was full (even though it didn't seem like it from what I heard from other students in the class). If I had been more persistent, I might have been able to switch, but that was a bit annoying (but I guess fair, as the class had already started).
registration_advice: Be aware about the language of the class! And be persistent with your emails to them - if you seem desperate enough, they will answer!
academics_comments: The experience as a whole has been absolutely amazing!!! The administrative things around the university was a little slow, but everything worked out fine, so it was not a major thing.
course_level: In general it seems like the expected level at the exams and assignments has been a bit lower, but during the classes the level was okay. Some of my classes here, were partly similar to classes I already had at UCPH, but the level was still okay.
teaching_comparison: The style of the classes were pretty similar (the teacher presented the content of the class and then we participated in some discussions). The classes were a bit smaller, which was nice. They did more continuous assessment than I'm used to from UCPH (weekly quizzes, assignments, presentations), which was actually quite nice, as your whole grade doesn't come down to one exam. However the amount of assignments I had to write, was a bot overwhelming (but maybe mostly because I did them last minute...).
courses_enrolled: Socio-Political Marketing (10 ECTS) European Integration (10 ECTS) Polítiques Migratòries i Integració Social / Migration and Integration Policies (10 ECTS)
recommended_courses: The Socio-Political Marketing class was really interesting and it was divided in five parts, so we had a lot of different professors which was cool. That also meant that we got to work in different ways, which was also nice.
unexpected_costs: I spilled coffee in my computer, which was a bit unexpected and expensive to fix, but otherwise nothing really :-)
cost_comparison: A little bit more expensive to do grocery shopping than I expected, but on the other hand it's quite cheap to go out for dinner and drinks/coffee.
activities_available: As I lived in the city center and UAB was 50 minutes away, I didn't really look for activities at the uni, so I actually don't know.
activities_recommended: It was not really connected to the host university, but ESN do a lot of activities and the app Erasmus Barcelona is also good to have (they also do trips and stuff).
weekend_recommendations: Montserrat, all the museums in Barcelona, some of the beaches outside of Barcelona (Castelldefels, Sitges, Vilanova, etc.), go on some hiking trips in the areas around Barcelona. I know a lot of students went on weekend trips to Valencia, Mallorca, Menorca, etc. which is supposed to be really nice (and cheap).
culture_adjustment: It was surprisingly easy to fall into the Spanish chill vibe (which I don't think is necessarily a good thing), but the Catalan people are in general hard to get close with (they're quite closed and mostly keeps to themselves).
socializing_tips: To be honest I didn't really socialize that much with local students myself - all of my courses were mostly with other exchange students, and I lived with other exchange students, so it was difficult to get in touch with the locals.
cultural_challenges: I think mostly that fact that everything works slower here than in Denmark, but otherwise I easily felt like Barcelona was my home.
culture_appreciated: The food is really nice and the architecture of the city!
top3_advice: 1) Be persistent with your emails when you have to figure out the enrollment and the registration in courses - sound desperate if necessary; 2) If possible, do your work during the semester, so you can enjoy your last time here (especially if it's summer; 3) Don't freak out if everything seems a bit unorganized - it's gonna fall into place!
other_useful_info: It is a bit outside the city, but the train ride there is really nice :)
most_rewarding: Meeting amazing people from all over the world and really being on my own and out of my comfort zone! I have learned so much and I've had some of the best experiences here!
greatest_challenge: Fighting a bit with my landlord about stuff in the apartment and maybe figuring everything out at the university (but these have been minor things and it hasn't really bothered me that much)
other_comments: Barcelona is truly an amazing city to be an exchange student in!!! So many international students, many different areas in the city, the beach, the nature around Barcelona and the restaurants and bars :-D

crucial_aspects: I wanted to improve my Spanish and was abroad last year which was an incredible experience as well.
info_ease: It was quite easy, even though some of the IT systems used for applying for exchange are very confusing. There are many different websites (from UCPH, service4mobility and the receiving institution) which can be very confusing at times
arrival_assistance: I talked to the Intercanvis Lletres in my faculty (humanities) and to the International Student Office
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was a bit difficult because UAB doesn't sign the OLA in the digital system, which means you have to download the pdf and send it manually to them. I didn't realize this until very late, so I ended up getting my Erasmus rant quite late into my exchange.
registration_help: You can contact Intercanvis Lletres
registration_success: I ended up getting the classes I wanted
registration_advice: Remember to send the OLA manually on mail after having received the signature from your sending institution. Go to all the classes that you chose the first week to find out if they fit your schedule and if you like the teacher, exam method, work load etc. If not, try out alternative classes and decide as fast as possible which ones to follow, preferably in the first couple of weeks so you don't miss to much. Be aware of the period of changing enrollment that UAB has (you'll be informed about this on the Introduction day, so show up for that).
course_level: The level of courses is a bit more difficult because of the "language barrier", I had all my courses in Spanish which was fine but sometimes a bit harder to follow compared to back home. Also I experienced the work load as way bigger than in UCPH. In UAB, a course of 6 ECTS points will have as much or more reading, more exams etc. than a course of 15 ECTS points in the UCPH, and in addition to that everything is in Spanish. Last year on exchange I did 5 courses of 6 ECTS points which was very busy and in exam periods quite stressfull. This year I did 3 courses of 6 ECTS points and my bachelor thesis at the same time, which I wouldn't recommend (I've ended up prolonging my bachelor thesis). 3 courses of 6 ECTS points is busy as well but would have been perfect for me.
teaching_comparison: The style of learning and teaching is different, the exams are often without any help so it's mostly about remembering all the stuff by heart and writing it down as fast as possible in the exam. Most classes consist of the teacher speaking to the students for 1,5 hour, most of the time with very little or no student participation at all. In my experience, the best way to prepare for the exams was to attend all the classes and try to write down what the teacher says in the class, as some teachers don't use powerpoints or don't upload them to Campus virtual after class. When studying for the exams I would go through all my notes and try to memorize it. The website Wuolah is also very helpful, as students from the exact same courses as you upload their notes in there.
courses_enrolled: 100023 Literatura Española 106348 Comentario de Textos Literarios 106347 Literatura Española desde el siglo de las luces hasta las Vanguardias
recommended_courses: I would recommend 106348 Comentario de Textos Literarios because the teacher I had (Lucia) was very nice, used powerpoints in her classes and didn't do memorizing exams. Instead she did an exam in the end of the semester in which you had to analyze an extract from a text. The course is less theoretical and more practical (meaning you learn how to write a literary commentary), and it doesn't have as many "in-class" exams, instead you have to hand in a couple of papers during the semester. I would also to some extent recommend 100023 Literatura Española as I liked the teacher (Rebecca), but there is a lot of reading to do in this subject (you have to read the first part of the Quijote, a novel and some theater plays) which can be challenging if Spanish is not your native language. If you do choose this subject I'd recommend to start reading the obligatory readings when you start the course basically, so that it doesn't get too stressfull in the end.
unexpected_costs: None that I remember
cost_comparison: Transportation was less expensive that I expected. If you get the T-mobilitat joven card you can travel anywhere in Barcelona (and outside as well to some extent) with bus, train, metro etc. for approx 45 euros for 3 months.
activities_available: I didn't participate in any activities outside of the academic ones in my university
activities_recommended: Not sure but you can definitely get information about this in the Introduction day and on the website of the uni.
weekend_recommendations: Enjoy the city (and the nature around it), it has endless opportunities to offer. Take the train down or up the coast to the smaller villages. Go to other Spanish cities with public transportation or rent a car.
culture_adjustment: I didn't have any challenges adjusting
cultural_challenges: I didn't really find any of the differences challenging
culture_appreciated: The openness, especially if you speak Spanish, the food, the music, the nightlife, just the city in general.
top3_advice: Live in the city center, not on campus. If you only have 3 courses, try to schedule them so that you don't have to go to the uni every day of the week (you can schedule it so that you only have to go 2 or 3 days a week) if you live in the city center. It's a 40 minutes train ride from Plaza Catalunya, so you could end up spending a lot of time on transportation. ENJOY it, don't stress it too much (even if you fail a course, it's all going to work out in the end) and speak as much Spanish as possible.

other_comments: For future mobility preparation, there should be some kind of offer if not compulsory session in which the outgoing students should be prepared better to tackle challenges related to intercultural learning. During my exchange, I have unfortunately encountered many fellow Danish students that did not quite understood the essence of studying and living abroad, resulting in them blaming their lack of understanding on their surroundings among other things that in reality should be a responsibility of their own to understand and solve. I have obviously followed the recent trend of a decreasing percentage of Danish students deciding to not do student mobility in which I really hope that KU will do everything in their powers to turn around that pattern as that and the seemingly 'bad' experiences that I have observed students express will only have negative consequences for the international recognition of KU.

overall_comments: Den eneste grund til jeg ikke giver 10 er fordi det faglige var ret kedeligt, men det fyldte ikke særlig meget.
info_ease: Det var ret nemt.
arrival_assistance: Ingen. Havde fået det meste på mail før jeg ankom.

housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Den eneste grund til jeg ikke giver 10 er fordi det faglige var ret kedeligt, men det fyldte ikke særlig meget.
registration_process: Man får et login på mail og skal uploade sit pas, sygesikring og andre oplysninger.
registration_help: Man kan ringe eller skrive på mail. Jeg synes de svarede rimelig hurtigt.

registration_advice: Husk at checke eksamensdatoer (midterm og final) og tidspunkter for undervisning så det ikke overlapper.

recommended_courses: De var alle ret kedelige og nemme, men en nem måde at få overstået fag på og det var rart ikke at være presset af uni.

activities_recommended: Jeg gjorde ikke brug af det.
weekend_recommendations: Gå ud og spis, gå ture i byen, rejs til Marrakech, tag på stranden, tag toget til de nærliggende byer osv.
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Spaniere er søde og imødekommende.

cultural_challenges: Intet.
culture_appreciated: Gå-ud kulturen. Der er caféer, restauranter og barer alle vegne.
top3_advice: Vær åben. Tal med andre udvekslingsstuderende. Brug byen.
other_useful_info: Det tager noget tid at føle sig tilpas et nyt sted. Der sker mange nye ting i starten som man godt kan blive overvældet af, men det er det hele værd at tage på udveksling.
most_rewarding: At få en pause fra uni herhjemme. Hvis man er skoletræt så tag hertil. Det gør en kæmpe forskel at man kun skal bestå fagene og at ens karakterer ikke bliver overført.
greatest_challenge: Snakke engelsk hele tiden, men det vænner man sig hurtigt til.
other_comments: Tag afsted! Lad dig ikke skræmme af togturen til uni. Den er hyggelig, og det er ikke nødvendigt at møde hver dag, selvom man ofte har undervisning hver dag.

info_ease: UAB har været gode til at svare på mails, så det gjorde det hele meget nemt.
arrival_assistance: Man modtog en masse information inden vi ankom, så der var ikke behov for særlig meget hjælp udover det. Derudover kunne man søge en "mentor". Jeg brugte min til at vise mig rundt på campus og hvis man havde andre spørgsmål, som andre lokale studerende er bedre til at svare på.

teaching_comparison: Det er meget gymnasieagtigt, hvor man sidder i et klasselokale, og hvor underviseren gennemgår slides (som man kender det fra KU).

recommended_courses: Vil anbefale alle pånær Microeconomics III, da det minder meget om mikro 2

cost_comparison: Billigere end Danmark - og ca hvad jeg havde regnet med.
activities_available: Klubber, fitness og mentor-ordninger.
activities_recommended: Tag på en masse udflugter. Vi var bl.a. i Marrakech og tog på længere udflugter i Spanien.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på udflugter og nyd byen.

most_rewarding: Forelske mig i by og møde verdens bedste venner
greatest_challenge: Ved det ikke.

crucial_aspects: The most important thing for me was to go to a place where I could practice my oral skills in German. Furthermore I had already lived a year in Munich and wanted to live somewhere else than in South Germany.
info_ease: I got most of the information I needed from the Erasmus-coordinator at Hamborg University and then I searched a lot on the university's homepage. But sometimes it was a bit difficult to find all the relevant information.
arrival_assistance: I got mails from the Erasmus-coordinator.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Some weeks before the semester started I got access to a website where I could see all the courses. Then I had to write an email to each professor and ask if it was possible to join their class and then later on I would get officially registred for the class in an online system.
registration_help: I could contact the Erasmus-office (but they were often very busy) and then I had a 'buddy' who already studied at the university, but she was new in Hamborg, so she didn't really know that much about it either.
registration_success: Very successful, I got almost all of the courses I wanted - there were only a few I didn't get because there was overlap in the schedules. But overall it was very successful.
registration_advice: In Hamborg you had the possibility of trying out different classes for the first week of the semester, and I would highly recommend you to just try out a loot of different classes if you also have that possibility. Also I will recommend that you talk with your professors about exams and ECTS-points pretty early (as soon as you know which courses you are taking) because you need to be sure that you can get the right amount of ECTS-points and that often depends on which type of exam you need to do. So just talk with your professors right away.
course_level: I think the level was very appropriate - I got challenged and learned a lot but without feeling totally overwhelmed. I had a good combination of seminars which were quite challenging and where I had to prepare well and the some introducing lectures which were easier.
teaching_comparison: The relation between professors and students was a bit more formal but otherwise the style was pretty similar. We had both lectures and seminars. What I really liked was that there was always room and time for discussions in the seminars and generally discussion was a bigger part of the courses as what I've experienced at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Der Erwerb von Deutsch als Zweit- und Fremdsprache, Einführung in sprachwissenschaftliche Theorien, Genus und Geschlecht, Einführung in das Studium der Neueren deutschen Literatur, Postmigrantische Narrative and Medien, Film und Kultur. Film- und Medientheorien.
recommended_courses: I can highly recommend the courses Genus und Geschlecht (a linguistic course) and Postmigrantische Narrative (a literature course). The professors were really committed and we read a lot of very interesting texts and the themes were just very relevant and exciting.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Groceries were a bit more expensive than I thought (close to Danish prices) but beer, chocolate and candy was very cheap and it was also less expensive to go out and eat as it is in Denmark.
activities_available: There was a broad selection of sport activities you could join and it was also pretty cheap. That was really cool. There was also a lot of social events for Erasmus-students like bike trips, parties and stuff like that.
activities_recommended: I thought the sport activities were a great and easy way of meeting other student - also student who were not on exchange but lived there permanently.
weekend_recommendations: Explore the city a lot, go for long walks and visit museums and the cultural institution. I also wished that I had traveled a bit more to other cities nearby so I would also recommend that.
culture_adjustment: I think it was quite easy. The differences were not that many and I quickly adjusted.
socializing_tips: The sport activities are a great opportunity of meeting local students and I would also recommend to live with Germans because that is probably the easiest way to get to know locals. Otherwise I can recommend the app 'Bumble' where you can get new friends and often local students who are new in the city use this app, so that is also a good way of getting in contact with locals.
cultural_challenges: Maybe the bureaucratic stuff - Germany can be a little old school on that matter, but it was not that big a problem.
culture_appreciated: The people I met were all very open minded and friendly and were just inviting me to go a long ti different social activities and I really appreciated that. Then I also had the feeling that Germans are very spontaneous and would just ask "do want to go for a beer" or "should we go to the cinema tonight" instead of always planning ahead and I found that very refreshing and nice.
top3_advice: Don't stress to much about the paperwork, enjoy Sternschanze and all the other cool places in Hamborg and just try out different courses the first week of the semester and then choose the ones you found most interesting.
other_useful_info: I think the buddy program was a very good initiative and I recommend signing up for that.
most_rewarding: I improved my verbal skills a lot and during my exchange I got a lot more comfortable talking German which was really nice. On a personal level it was also a very rewarding experience - you learn a lot about yourself when you move alone to a new city and a new country and I think you grow a lot from that.
greatest_challenge: At times it was a bit lonely being on exchange but I think is almost inevitable not to feel lonely some of the time and I always found comfort in calling somebody from home or talking to my roommates, so it was not as bad as I had feared before going on exchange.
other_comments: I'm really happy that I went on exchange and I can only encourage all students to go!

arrival_assistance: I recieved some information from the Erasmus office and there was a meeting. But still had to do a lot of stuff independently.

weekend_recommendations: Luneburg and Lubeck

socializing_tips: Talk to people in class
cultural_challenges: Nothing

other_useful_info: For a room, try calling Studierendewerk Hamburg.

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte universitetet, fordi det havde fag, som interesserede mig og var relevante for min karriere, og fordi at jeg elsker de romanske sprog som f.eks. fransk og spansk. Jeg ville have foretrækket et fransk universitet, men ingen af dem, jeg fandt, havde fag, som var vedkommende for min fremtid.
overall_comments: 98% af alle folk, jeg så, tågede rundt med mundkurve både udendørs og indendørs, så jeg så meget få nye ansigter. Heldigvis blev steriliseringskanylen aldrig et universitetskrav, som det har været i Danmark. Der er meget få indvandrere i gadebilledet, modsat i Danmark, hvor de er over det hele. Med det sagt stjæles der ofte ting, hvis man lader sin taske eller telefon stå et sted i blot et øjeblik. Selv hvis man er på stranden og kigger væk i et halvt minut eller lukke øjnene kommer professionelle tyve og tager dine ting lige så diskret; så hold fast på dine ejendele og medbring kun de ting, du behøver, når du går udenfor. De spanske piger er smukke, ligesom deres sprog. Ikke alle er brunhårede; der er flere blondiner og rødhårede, end man tror. Man skal dog længere op nordpå, hvis man gerne vil have flere af den slags! Og ja, jeg forveksler dem ikke blot med alle de tyske og hollandske udvekslingsstuderende. Det er altid sommer i Spanien; vinterjakke er fuldkommen unødvendigt året rundt. Der er aldrig sne. I august og september er det umuligt at ligge med dyne på. De fleste lejligheder har ingen indbygget varme, så folk bruger varmekanoner om vinteren; men når man er mange folk i en lejlighed, så kan sikringen ofte springe, hvis alle har sine varmekanoner tændt på samme tid. Derfor skal man være indbyrdes enige om at tænde eller slukke for disse meget strømkrævende apparater. Nogle lejligheder døjer med myrer og kakerlakker. Myrerne klares nemt med nogle fæller. Kakerlakker kan også for det meste klares med fæller, men vær forberedt på at dræbe dem med din sko, da du ikke ønsker, at de store mødre flygter og laver unger et andet sted. Hvis du er pige, så få drenge i lejligheden til at hjælpe dig. Alting er billigt, fordi den spanske moms er 21%. I Danmark bliver vi berøvet med 25%. Der er stor forskel på kvartererne i byen; nogle områder har pæne, nydelige bygninger og gader, medens andre områder har halvforfaldne huse uden vinduer, hvor folk rent faktisk lever. Den gamle bydel er vidunderligt smuk, ligesom alle gamle byer i Europa er de smukkeste i verden. Vandet indeholder klor og bør ikke drikkes; det ville svare til at drikke vand fra en svømmepøl. Man kan købe store vanddunke af rent vand på helt op til otte liter for en euro eller deromkring i Mercadona, SuperCOR og andre forretninger. Jeg anbefaler mærket Cortes, som smager renest. Forretningerne har lukket om søndagen undtagen enkelte døgnforretninger som f.eks. SuperCOR og visse restauranter. Det er næsten umuligt at planlægge en rejse med den spanske offentlige transport, medmindre man benytter Google Kort; Googles tjeneste er de fakto KONGEN af at planlægge rejse i Spanien. Billetter købes på stationerne i automaterne, som er nemme at betjene.

Også i bunden er "Plano 2D," som viser kortet over Vera Campus, som er navnet på campusset i Valencia, modsat det i Gandía.

registration_help: De internationale koordinatorer i KU og UPV er meget hjælpsomme. Man kan nemt skrive til dem og få svar.
registration_success: Jeg kom ind på mine kurser, men jeg valgte kun spansktalende kurser; de udvekslingsstuderende, som valgte engelsktalende kurser, blev i mange tilfælde flyttet til spanske hold, fordi de engelske hold var fyldte.
registration_advice: Sørg for at gå i gang i god tid med at forberede dig, da det internationale kontor i UPV holder lukket i august. Sørg især for at få sprogcertifikat og "learning agreement" på plads inden august. Der var en del udvekslingsstuderende, som havde en lidt sen start på sine kurser eller havde andet bøvl, fordi der var mange ting at ordne, som de ikke havde ordnet inden august.
academics_comments: 98% af alle folk, jeg så, tågede rundt med mundkurve både udendørs og indendørs, så jeg så meget få nye ansigter. Heldigvis blev steriliseringskanylen aldrig et universitetskrav, som det har været i Danmark. Der er meget få indvandrere i gadebilledet, modsat i Danmark, hvor de er over det hele. Med det sagt stjæles der ofte ting, hvis man lader sin taske eller telefon stå et sted i blot et øjeblik. Selv hvis man er på stranden og kigger væk i et halvt minut eller lukke øjnene kommer professionelle tyve og tager dine ting lige så diskret; så hold fast på dine ejendele og medbring kun de ting, du behøver, når du går udenfor. De spanske piger er smukke, ligesom deres sprog. Ikke alle er brunhårede; der er flere blondiner og rødhårede, end man tror. Man skal dog længere op nordpå, hvis man gerne vil have flere af den slags! Og ja, jeg forveksler dem ikke blot med alle de tyske og hollandske udvekslingsstuderende. Det er altid sommer i Spanien; vinterjakke er fuldkommen unødvendigt året rundt. Der er aldrig sne. I august og september er det umuligt at ligge med dyne på. De fleste lejligheder har ingen indbygget varme, så folk bruger varmekanoner om vinteren; men når man er mange folk i en lejlighed, så kan sikringen ofte springe, hvis alle har sine varmekanoner tændt på samme tid. Derfor skal man være indbyrdes enige om at tænde eller slukke for disse meget strømkrævende apparater. Nogle lejligheder døjer med myrer og kakerlakker. Myrerne klares nemt med nogle fæller. Kakerlakker kan også for det meste klares med fæller, men vær forberedt på at dræbe dem med din sko, da du ikke ønsker, at de store mødre flygter og laver unger et andet sted. Hvis du er pige, så få drenge i lejligheden til at hjælpe dig. Alting er billigt, fordi den spanske moms er 21%. I Danmark bliver vi berøvet med 25%. Der er stor forskel på kvartererne i byen; nogle områder har pæne, nydelige bygninger og gader, medens andre områder har halvforfaldne huse uden vinduer, hvor folk rent faktisk lever. Den gamle bydel er vidunderligt smuk, ligesom alle gamle byer i Europa er de smukkeste i verden. Vandet indeholder klor og bør ikke drikkes; det ville svare til at drikke vand fra en svømmepøl. Man kan købe store vanddunke af rent vand på helt op til otte liter for en euro eller deromkring i Mercadona, SuperCOR og andre forretninger. Jeg anbefaler mærket Cortes, som smager renest. Forretningerne har lukket om søndagen undtagen enkelte døgnforretninger som f.eks. SuperCOR og visse restauranter. Det er næsten umuligt at planlægge en rejse med den spanske offentlige transport, medmindre man benytter Google Kort; Googles tjeneste er de fakto KONGEN af at planlægge rejse i Spanien. Billetter købes på stationerne i automaterne, som er nemme at betjene.
course_level: Det er til at have med at gøre. I DIKU har man allerede lært de fleste ting i de første to år, som gør, at man kan tage de fleste bachelorkurser i UPV.
teaching_comparison: Underviserne benytter løbende evaluering i alle fag. Ellers er det meget ligesom man kender det i andre universiteter med afleveringer eller projektarbejde samt nogle prøver i teori.
courses_enrolled: 11576 Introduction to Computer Security 11584 Real-Time and Embedded Systems 11591 Introduction to Interactive Computer Graphics Systems 11592 Techniques, tools and applications of artificial intelligence 11606 Security in networks and computer systems
recommended_courses: Jeg anbefaler kurserne 11584 og 11591. Kursus 11584 handler om at lære programmeringssproget Ada og lave små projekter i det. Det er et meget velskabt og ordentligt sprog, der kan bruges til at udvikle meget sikre programmer; f.eks. bruges det i fly, tog og satellitter. Flere udviklere bør lære det. Kursus 11591 handler om at lave et lille videospil fra bunden med 3D-grafik. Der bruges ikke Unity, Unreal, Godot osv. til at hjælpe dig; du laver alt fuldkommen selv med OpenGL. Det er meget nyttigt at lære om 3D-koordinater, 3D-transformationer og OpenGL, især hvis man vil udvikle videospil.
unexpected_costs: Når man køber billetter til offentlig transport, betaler man først gang for et lille papkort, der indeholder billetterne; det svarer til et slags Rejsekort. Hvert transportselskab har sine egne kort; f.eks. et kort til Metro Valencia, et kort til Renfe (det spanske DSB), osv. Man kan fylde kortene op med nye billetter ved automaterne på stationerne.
cost_comparison: Alting er billigere pga. den spanske moms på 21% modsat den danske moms på 25%.
activities_available: Der er mange sportsfaciliteter på UPV, f.eks. svømmehal, tennis- og badmintonbaner, fodboldbaner og volleyball-bane. Der arrangeres også regelmæssigt fællesaktiviteter for studerende.
activities_recommended: Fællesaktiviteterne. Der fortælles om dem i orienteringsmødet og i velkomstdagen.
weekend_recommendations: Se den gamle bydel. Der er masser af gammel arkitektur, gamle tårne og flotte kirker. Der er også mange gode parker, som alle er et besøg værd.
culture_adjustment: Det var nemt nok. De spanske folk er flinke.
socializing_tips: Tag ud og spis eller drik en øl sammen.
cultural_challenges: Nogle gange manglede jeg et ord på spansk, men det gik som regel, hvis jeg omformulerede min sætning. Derudover er spanierne meget regelrette og var meget glade for at "minde mig om" at tage mundkurv på.
culture_appreciated: Spanierene værner meget om sit sprog og sin kultur på samme måde som franskmændene gør det. De oversætter altid gloser til sig eget sprog med meget få undtagelser i stedet for at bare direkte smække engelske ord ind i sine sætninger som danskerne gør det. I stedet for at lade sig amerikanisere vedligeholder spanierne sin egen kultur (musik, film osv.), importerer fra andre spansktalende lande eller eksporterer til de lande.
top3_advice: 1. Sørg for at have så mange ting på plads som muligt inden august, så det er lettere for dig i september. 2. Deltag i det intensive spanskkursus i Gandía. Mine bedste minder fra Spanien er fra mit ophold dernede. 3. Begynd meget tidligt med at lære spansk. Tro ikke, at hvis blot du kan tale engelsk, så går det nok alt sammen. Det her er ikke Holland.
other_useful_info: Jeg kan varmt anbefale bogen "Poco a poco" til at lære spansk. Man læser kapitlerne højt, så udtalen øves, og bagefter laver man nogle øvelser. Bogen består af 40 kapitler, så med et kapitel om dagen kan man komme igennem den på lidt over en måned. Bogen er fra 1922, men den er stadig meget nyttig i dag.
most_rewarding: Oplevelsen af Valencia og den faglige læring.
greatest_challenge: Nogle gange manglede jeg et ord på spansk.
other_comments: Tag ned til Valencia, ¡mi amigo! Det er en smuk by. Det er det hele værd. Den eneste grund til, at jeg har givet oplevelsen af min tur bedømmelsen 8 og ikke 10, er, at det var voldsomt irriterende at se alle folk gå rundt med de åndssvage, anonymiserende mundbleer. Hvis ikke der nogensinde var coronapsykose og krav om det såkaldte "coronapas" i restauranterne, havde jeg givet min oplevelse af Valencia et afgjort 10.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go south, to a more exotic country with a different culture than what I am used to. Also, I wanted to learn Spanish.
info_ease: Fairly easy. My host university provided a lot of information in advance.
arrival_assistance: I had a mentor, but I did not get to meet him, even if he was available. Also my facutly was really helpful. So if I wanted more assistance than I had, I am sure I would get it.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Registrating for courses was a bit of a hard time. I was provided a website way before applying for courses, and this did not fully align with the courses that I could actually registrate for. A factor could be that it was not intuitive if a course would be rolling my particular semester there or not. We had to sign up for the courses before, not knowing if we would actually get them. Since there is mandatory attendance at UPV, we would also have to choose groups, which became full very quickly. It was first serve, first come. And the date for signing up for courses was not obvious, and talking to some other students, they could already sign up for groups before this sign up date. In other words, it was a bit messy. But when I got there, and got to talking to the administration, when one of the courses I really wanted to take was full, they still let me in on the course. Also, changing courses and signing off courses was very okay. They were helpful.
registration_help: International office at my faculty. Helpful people.
registration_success: I got all the courses that I wanted in the end.
registration_advice: Be up to date with all the dates, especially when signing up to groups. This is what lets you in on the course. And knowing exactly how your timetable will be, in order to sign up for groups accordingly. The more sure of the timetable from get go, the easier the process will be (I think).
course_level: Of all six courses, 3 of them were master courses and the rest was bachelor courses.
teaching_comparison: Somewhat different. No books, fairly more practical than UCPH, which I really liked. Lectures and seminars were mandatory for most of them. Important information given at lectures/seminars was not announced. you just had to be in class or get that information by asking lecturer or peer afterwards. Also, having evening school was interesting. Had several days in which I only had classes from 18-21:30 for instance.
courses_enrolled: Data Science, MA E-learning and Social Networks, MA IT Project and Planning, MA Intelligent Systems, BA Databases and Information Systems, BA Spanish A2, BA
recommended_courses: It depends on what one is interested in, but I really recommend having the Spanish class, of your level. Also, IT Project and Planning was in Spanish, which made me learn some Spanish and connect with international people! Also, Intelligent systems, if you are into AI.
unexpected_costs: None really.
cost_comparison: Everything was less expensive, for sure. Public transport was free. UPV provided free gyms, rent of tennis courts, padel courts, and so on. So many good privileges!
activities_available: Everything you could think of, from my interests at least. I did not miss anything.
activities_recommended: Signing up to a sportsteam. Its free and you get to meet new people.
weekend_recommendations: Enjoy the beach, renting a car (very cheap) and go outside of Valencia to discover btoh North and South Spain. Eeating out is so cheap, tapas bars (and other cuisines) can be found literally everywhere. The city is vibrant with a lot of sightseeing opportunities as well.
culture_adjustment: Soso. It was a fun adjustment with evening school and late dinners.
cultural_challenges: Spanish people are not as open as you would think, but that might be explained with their lack of English skills. Talking to them in Spanish was hard, because they speak fast. Other than that, they are loud but that is okay.
culture_appreciated: The music, the food and siesta. Having midday off. The beaches and beautiful sites and old buildings.
top3_advice: Learn some spanish and engage in the Spanish culture. It so beautiful. There are a lot of organizations, both non-profit and profit, who arranges a whole load of social event throughout the entire semester. We are talking basically every day of the week, there will be something. Do not feel the pressure to do it all in the Welcome Month. There are tons of possibilities later if you are having some hard time adjusting. Also, enjoy, take on day at a time, and talk to your professors if anything is not going the way you want, study-wise. They are really really nice, and they will find a way to help you pass.
other_useful_info: No, not that I can think of. But they can contact me per mail, if any specific questions :)
most_rewarding: Moving there by myself, and having to come out of my comfortzone a lot, gave me a lot of personal growth. So cliche, but not less true.
greatest_challenge: A natural catastrophe hitting the city, making the society close down a bit. And uni was remote-only for two months.

most_rewarding: Meeting a lot of new people.

crucial_aspects: Kurserne der blev tilbudt på universitetet, og muligheden for at leve og studere i Frankrig, heraf forbedre mine franske sprogfærdigheder. Selve destinationen og de lokale forhold var mindre vigtige
overall_comments: Hvis det faglige niveau på universitetet var højere, så ville min oplevelse have været i top. Til gengæld trækker de mennesker jeg mødte under mit ophold helt vildt op på den samlede oplevelse, men det er også individuelt
info_ease: Det var ikke helt så nemt, da universitetet ikke har et kursuskatalog man nemt kan tilgå fra deres hjemmeside, så det handlede om at danne sig et overblik over de uddannelse, der interesserede en, og så håbe at man kunne finde et tilhørende kursuskatalog. Frue Briand, der sidder på det internationale kontor i Nice, ville sende nogle mails ud før afrejse der angik de første to uger inden at undervisningen startede. Det var en hjælp, men det var sjældent man fik svar tilbage, hvis man havde et specifikt spørgsmål til hende
arrival_assistance: Primært fra frue Briand ved det internationale kontor, som man kunne møde op ved for at svar på sine spørgsmål. Jeg blev også medlem af en Whatsapp-gruppe med andre udvekslingsstuderende, men de var i mit tilfælde ikke til meget hjælp
arrival_comments: Der var helt klart nogle udfordringer i kommunikation, da den kun foregik én vej. Dertil så bliver de første to uger inden undervisningen brugt til at registrere en til de kurser man agter at tage. I mit tilfælde havde frue Briand ikke set min mail, så det var først to uger efter at undervisningen startede, at jeg formelt blev registreret på mine kurser
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Hvis det faglige niveau på universitetet var højere, så ville min oplevelse have været i top. Til gengæld trækker de mennesker jeg mødte under mit ophold helt vildt op på den samlede oplevelse, men det er også individuelt

registration_help: Frue Briand fra kontoret, men hun fortalte mig ikke at jeg skulle en mail til underviserne. Det fortalte en anden udvekslingsstuderende
