crucial_aspects: Det var helt afgørende for mig at komme på udveksling i et fransksproget land, eftersom jeg læser en bachelorgrad i Fransk sprog og kultur. Dertil kom et stærkt ønske om at kunne gennemføre udvekslingsopholdet på et parisisk universitet, da jeg boede i Paris i forvejen (her har jeg boet siden et praktikophold i foråret 2021), og jeg var interesseret i at forlænge mit ophold og få så stort et fransksprogligt udbytte som muligt.
overall_comments: Jeg har været meget glad for undervisningen og for mit akademiske og sproglige udbytte af opholdet. Men jeg er blevet mødt af en lang række administrative udfordringer, både før og under opholdet, og de har udgjort en betragtelig stressfaktor. De administrative udfordringer omfatter mangelfuld og utilstrækkelig information, og de har både involveret mit hjemuniversitet (Københavns Universitet) og mit værtsuniversitet (Université de Paris-Diderot). Jeg vil løbende udfolde de administrative udfordringer i nedenstående punkter. For der var mange af dem.
info_ease: Det var tæt på umuligt at få den information, jeg havde brug for. Så snart KU havde givet mig besked om, at jeg havde fået min udvekslingsplads på Université de Paris-Diderot, skrev jeg til sidstnævntes kontor for "Mobilité d'études Erasmus+". Her spurgte jeg bl.a. til, om jeg kunne se en form for oversigt over, hvilke kurser jeg kunne tilmelde mig som udvekslingsstuderende, og om der var andet, jeg skulle være opmærksom på. Jeg skrev flere mails over en periode på flere uger, men modtog ikke svar, kun et autosvar om, at min mail var modtaget. Jeg måtte derfor selv på jagt efter en form for brouchure/studieordning for kurserne på det fakultet, jeg havde fået en udvekslingsplads på (for at kunne sende anmodning om forhåndsgodkendelse til KU) og måtte bruge temmelig mange timer på det. Hjemmesiden var langt fra intuitiv, og jeg havde ikke en eneste kontaktperson, der kunne hjælpe mig. Efter utallige søgninger fandt jeg et dokument, der lignede en kursusoversigt, og med afsæt i den kunne jeg sende min ansøgning om forhåndsgodkendelse af sted. Heldigvis var der ikke mange ændringer at foretage senere, men jeg blev til gengæld klar over, at brochuren rummede fejlagtig information om en eksamensform, og at jeg havde fået forhåndsgodkendt et kursus, der ikke egnede sig til udvekslingsstuderende. En fejl, der udviklede sig relativt dramatisk i løbet af semestret, og som kunne have været undgået, hvis universitetet havde responderet på min – rimelige og retfærdige – anmodning om at se en form for kursuskatalog. Efter jeg havde modtaget min forhåndsgodkendelse af KU, begyndte arbejdet med at udfylde min Online Learning Agreement. Jeg fik kontakt til min Erasmus-koordinator på KU, som var hurtig til at underskrive – men som ikke kunne hjælpe mig med, hvem min kontaktperson på Université de Paris var. Herefter begyndte en proces, som jeg vil tillade mig at kalde et administrativt mareridt. I to måneder ringede og skrev jeg til samtlige mailadresser, jeg kunne finde i Université de Paris-Diderots studieadministration. Der var intet svar. Jeg var i løbende kontakt med min Erasmus-koordinator på KU, men hjælpen her var beskeden. Hun sendte mig løbende flere mailadresser på administrationsfolk på Université de Paris, som hun havde i sit arkiv, men hun var ikke villig til at hjælpe mig yderligere. Hun opfordrede mig sågar til at "tage ud på universitetet og virke lidt ked af det”. En opfordring, jeg følte både grænseoverskridende og helt urimelig. Jeg havde trods alt fået en udviklingsplads på helt almindelige vilkår. Kunne det virkelig være rigtigt, at jeg skulle kæmpe en så indædt kamp for at få kontakt til et universitet, som KU havde haft en årelang udvekslingsaftale med? Havde jeg ikke boet i Paris i forvejen, havde dette jo aldrig været noget, man havde bedt en studerende om at tage ansvar for. Jeg indvilligede, tog ud på universitetet og talte med tre personer i administrationen. Ingen kunne hjælpe mig, men henviste blot til den mail, som jeg allerede havde skrevet til fem gange. I min research efter den rette ansvarlige på det parisiske universitetet erfarede jeg desuden, at jeg skulle sende en særskilt anmodning om udvekslingsplads til Université de Paris' eget interne system (MoveON) for officielt at få bekræftet min plads (et såkaldt “Lettre d'acceptation”). Denne anmodning kunne dog ikke afsluttes, før min Learning Agreement var underskrevet af begge universiteter, og jeg gik således i (særdeles stressende) uvished fra oktober 2021 og flere måneder frem. Jeg vidste ganske enkelt ikke, om pladsen var min, og om jeg nogensinde ville få kontakt til den ansvarlige, eller om jeg var nødt til at opgive, opsige min lejlighed i Paris og tage hjem til Danmark med få ugers varsel. Da situationen spidsede til, luftede jeg endnu en gang min frustration og nervøsitet for min Erasmus-koordinator på KU, der – ikke særligt beroligede – ytrede, at "vi må håbe, at du kan blive genindskrevet på de kurser, du skulle have haft på KU, hvis det ikke lykkes med Université de Paris“. Jeg følte mig fortabt og dybt, dybt uretfærdigt behandlet. Først i starten af december (to måneder efter at jeg havde sendt de første mails), modtog jeg respons fra en i studieadministrationen hos Université de Paris, Jan Douat. Jan Douat videresendte dog blot min henvendelse til den mail for "Mobilité d'études Erasmus+”-kontoret, jeg både havde skrevet og ringet til et utal af gange. Jeg forklarede min situation til Jan Douat og insisterede (med hjælp fra en fransktalende veninde) på, at han måtte kunne hjælpe mig med at komme i mål med en underskrift af min Learning Agreement og med min oprettelse i universitets interne system MoveON. Efter en længere mailkorrespondance, hvor Jan Douat bl.a. afviste, at man på Université de Paris kunne underskrive en Learning Agreement (hvilket viste sig at være helt forkert), tog en ny administrativ person, Fabien Vaugarny, over. Han kunne – OMSIDER – oplyse mig om, hvem min Erasmus-koordinator på Université de Paris var (jeg kunne dog kun få et navn og måtte selv google mig til en mailadresse. Jeg fik ikke oplyst telefonnummer, selvom jeg bad om det). Jeg skrev straks en mail til Erasmus-koordinatoren på Université de Pars og ventede og ventede og ventede. Jeg modtog hverken svar eller underskrift, og hele processen gik endnu en gang i stå. Jeg skrev igen til Fabien Vaugarny, skitserede endnu en gang min håbløse situation og mit ønske om at finde en løsning, inden alle gik på juleferie. Han indviligede til sidst i, at jeg, helt ekstraordinært, kunne få lov til at uploade min Learning Agreement uden underskrift fra min Erasmus-koordinator på Université de Paris, så jeg kunne oprette mig endegyldigt i systemet MoveON og modtage mit Lettre d'acceptation (indskrivningsbrev). Det skete d. 15. december 2021, ca. to måneder efter at jeg havde sendt de første mails. Denne lange og kringlede beretning taler for sig selv. Det var et helt absurd bøvlet forløb at få fat i de nødvendige informationer, og jeg har været meget skuffet, både over Université de Paris, men også over KU. Jeg kan ikke begribe, at der ikke var mere hjælp at få; at det ene og alene var mit problem, at mit værtsuniversitet ikke besvarede helt basale spørgsmål om administrative forhold, og at KU ikke kunne tage over og kommunikere “fra administration til administration”. Jeg befandt mig i en lang periode i en temmelig stresset tilstand af uvished, som, jeg mener, var fuldstændig unødvendig og urimelig. Og var det ikke, fordi jeg i forvejen boede i Frankrig og havde franske venner omkring mig, der kunne hjælpe mig med at forfatte høflige, men bestemte, mails til Jan Douat og Fabien Vaugarny, er jeg ikke sikker på, at min situation var blevet taget alvorligt. Jeg ønsker ikke et lignende forløb for nogen anden udvekslingsstuderende; det var opslidende og udmattende og slet ikke i orden.
arrival_assistance: Efter juleferien forsøgte jeg på ny at få fat i den underskrift, jeg fortsat manglede, men jeg modtog fortsat ikke svar på mine mails. Jeg måtte derfor vente til den første introdag på Université de Paris d. 17. januar 2022, hvor jeg mødte Fabien Vaugarny, der kunne fortælle mig, at jeg skulle indstille mig på en forsinket kursusindskrivning. Mit studiekort og studienummer (som skulle bruges til kursusindskrivning) var endnu ikke bestilt, fordi jeg ikke havde leveret en Learning Agreement med underskrift fra begge parter – en underskrift, som jeg jo ihærdigt havde forsøgt at skaffe i månedsvis, og som Université de Paris nu gav mig ansvaret for ikke at have fået i hus. Jeg måtte forklare min situation igenigenigen, og heldigvis kunne en ansvarlig for Eramus-kontoret, Addy Serna, få min Erasmus-koordinator i Paris til at underskrive samme dag, og mit studiekort kunne blive bestilt. Det var imidlertid med en forsinkelse på et par uger, og jeg var således nødt til at gå til de første undervisningstimer og forelæsninger uden officielt at være tilmeldt kurserne og dermed uden at have adgang til de studerendes intranet Moodle, hvor alle tekster og anden info lå tilgængelig. Den øvrige information til de to introdage d. 17. og 18. januar 2022 var udmærket; universitetet havde arrangeret forskellige atelierer, der oplyste om universitets historie, campus-indretning, oplysninger om sports- og kulturaktiviteter for studerende, restaurantrabatter m.v.
arrival_comments: Til de føromtalte introdage blev det oplyst, at kontoret for “Relations Internationales/Mobilité d'études Erasmus+” var under en form for omrokering/omorganisering af personale, og der ville derfor være ganske få træffetider de første to uger. Det var en temmelig uheldig timing og kunne muligvis også forklare en del af årsagen til, at jeg havde haft så svært ved at få kontakt i månederne op til. Fabien Vaugarny indrømmede, at afdelingen “havde haft lidt problemer med deres mail, men at man nu havde fundet en løsning”. Det forklarede dog ikke, hvorfor alle de andre 10-12 mailadresser, jeg havde skrevet til i løbet af det sene efterår 2021, ikke var mundet ud i dialog og hjælp.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Jeg har været meget glad for undervisningen og for mit akademiske og sproglige udbytte af opholdet. Men jeg er blevet mødt af en lang række administrative udfordringer, både før og under opholdet, og de har udgjort en betragtelig stressfaktor. De administrative udfordringer omfatter mangelfuld og utilstrækkelig information, og de har både involveret mit hjemuniversitet (Københavns Universitet) og mit værtsuniversitet (Université de Paris-Diderot). Jeg vil løbende udfolde de administrative udfordringer i nedenstående punkter. For der var mange af dem.
registration_process: Al indskrivning foregik pr. mail. Jeg skulle således skrive en mail til hver af de to ansvarlige for kursusindskrivning med en liste over mine forhåndsgodkendte kurser og oplyse mit navn og studienummer. På trods af en lang mailkorrespondance, hvor jeg udførligt noterede listen over de kurser, jeg ønskede at følge, var der alligevel fejl i en af mine kursustilmeldinger, og jeg gik således forgæves til en række aflyste forelæsninger og missede flere informationer pr. mail. Først i sidste halvdel af semestret erkendte og rettede den kursusansvarlige fejlen. En af underviserne underviste på distancen, selv om langt de fleste coronarestriktioner var ophævet, og alle andre undervisere underviste fysisk. Den omtalte underviser var ansvarlig for to af de kurser, jeg var tilmeldt, og “undervisningen” foregik ved, at han sendte skriftligt undervisningsmateriale pr. mail. Først et par uger inde i semestret opdagede jeg, at han havde, ved den ene kursus-tilmelding, havde tilføjet mig til en forkert mail-liste, og jeg derfor modtog de forkerte dokumenter. Det var først i samtalen med en medstuderende, at jeg blev opmærksom på fejlen, og underviseren var flere uger om at rette den og sende mig materialet til undervisningsgange, jeg var gået glip af. Med andre ord kom jeg mange uger bagud i dette kursus, der i øvrigt viste sig at være blandt de mest krævende. Den øvrige kursusindskrivning gik nogenlunde glat; de to ansvarlige var begge hurtige til at besvare mine spørgsmål, og jeg fik (næsten) alle mine kursusønsker opfyldt.
registration_help: Der var ikke yderligere hjælp at hente, og min situation blev yderligere kompliceret af, at jeg fik ny Erasmus-koordinator på Université de Paris kort efter semesterstart. Da jeg blev nødt til at justere min forhåndsgodkendelse og derfor oprette en ny Learning Agreement, noterede jeg min nye Erasmus-koordinators oplysninger, men han modtog tilsyneladende ikke nogen mail eller online formular, og en ny administrativ udfordring opstod. Vi fandt heldigvis relativt hurtigt en løsning.
registration_success: Jeg kunne heldigvis få plads på næsten alle de kurser, jeg havde fået forhåndsgodkendt, og der var således ganske lidt administrativt arbejde i KU-regi; KU var hurtig til at godkende mine justeringer. Til gengæld var det ikke helt let at få min nye Erasmus-koordinator til at underskrive den nye Learning Agreement som omtalt i ovenstående punkt.
registration_advice: 1. Vær opmærksom på, at al kursusindskrivning foregår pr. mail. 2. Vær opmærksom på, at man kan komme til at koordinere kursusindskrivning med flere, der er ansvarlige for forskellige afdelinger (første, anden og tredje årgang på bachelorniveau). 3. Vær opmærksom på, at man ikke nødvendigvis regne med, at de eksamensformer, der står beskrevet i brochuren/studieordningen holder stik. Jeg udfolder min egen erfaring med denne udfordring under punktet “Please elaborate on the level of courses”.
academics_comments: Jeg har været meget glad for undervisningen og for mit akademiske og sproglige udbytte af opholdet. Men jeg er blevet mødt af en lang række administrative udfordringer, både før og under opholdet, og de har udgjort en betragtelig stressfaktor. De administrative udfordringer omfatter mangelfuld og utilstrækkelig information, og de har både involveret mit hjemuniversitet (Københavns Universitet) og mit værtsuniversitet (Université de Paris-Diderot). Jeg vil løbende udfolde de administrative udfordringer i nedenstående punkter. For der var mange af dem.
course_level: I oversigten fra KU om adgangskrav og praktisk info om den specifikke udvekslingsaftale med Université de Paris-Diderot stod der, at man skulle have niveau B1 (på European Language Level-skalaen, dvs. DELF B1). Jeg tog Erasmus' egen sprogtest (OLS), som viste, at jeg havde C1 og dermed burde have et rigeligt tilstrækkeligt niveau til at følge kurserne. I praksis var det dog langt fra alle undervisere, der tog hensyn til, at jeg var udvekslingsstuderende, og at fransk ikke var mit modersmål. Det var forventet, at jeg afleverede samme type afleveringer (i omfang og udformning) som de modersmålstalende, og det var ikke alle undervisere, der tog højde for, at jeg ikke kendte det franske uddannelsessystem indefra; at jeg fx ikke kendte de skriftlige, akademiske opgaveformater, som de øvrige studerende var skolet i. Jeg kunne godt lide udfordringerne, gik til opgaverne med krum hals og sugede til mig som en svamp. Men i et af kurserne, Esthétique 3, blev udfordringerne for store (og uforudsigelige). Esthétique 3 var det kursus, som jeg har nævnt i et af de tidligere punkter; som viste sig ikke at være helt egnet til en udvekslingsstuderende, og som havde et helt andet eksamensformat, end det var oplyst i kursusbeskrivelsen. Jeg fik, som tidligere nævnt, ingen respons, da jeg spurgte den parisiske studieadministration om hjælp til at finde og vurdere relevante kurser som udvekslingsstuderende, så jeg måtte selv vurdere, hvad der gav mening (og hvad der kunne forhåndsgodkendes af KU). Jeg valgte at tilmelde mig Esthétique 3, dels fordi kursusbeskrivelsen appellerede til mig, dels fordi kursets eksamensform virkede overkommelig for mig. Det stod beskrevet, at halvdelen af eksamenskarakteren bestod af et mundtligt oplæg (baseret på en skriftlig opgave) i løbet af semestret, og at anden halvdel af karakteren bestod af en “un examen terminal écrit”, dvs. en skriftlig stedprøve i hånden og uden hjælpemidler. Jeg vidste, at faget ville være svært, men vurderede, at en god præstation til det mundtlige oplæg ville kunne give mig lidt karakter-elastik til den skriftlige prøve, og jeg dermed kunne opnå en samlet bestået karakter. Da jeg mødte op til kurset, spurgte jeg underviseren, hvordan det mundtlige oplæg skulle udformes, og hun fortalte, at hun havde ændret eksamensformatet, og at jeg i stedet skulle til en “Contrôle sur place”, en tre timer lang skriftlig prøve, i hånden og uden hjælpemidler, som ville udgøre halvdelen af min karakter. Prøven lå allerede i starten af marts, og jeg havde således sparsom erfaring fra den franske universitetsverden, da prøven skulle finde sted. Jeg forsøgte at forhandle lidt med underviseren; forklarede at jeg var udvekslingsstuderende, at jeg følte mig meget usikker på formatet, og spurgte om jeg kunne få ekstra tid. Underviseren var ikke indstillet på at give mig særbehandling, selvom denne prøveform var langt mere krævende end et forberedt oplæg, og selvom underviseren indrømmede, at det eksamensformat, jeg kunne læse i kursusbeskrivelsen, var et helt andet. Dertil kom, at Esthétique 3 byggede oven på en kursusrække (Esthétique 1 + 2), som jeg af gode grunde ikke havde fulgt. Jeg havde ikke som sådan problemer med at følge kursets indhold og temaer, men det var tydeligt, at de andre studerende var skolet i en særlig måde at analysere æstetik-filosofiske tekster. Med andre ord var det min oplevelse, at kurset ikke henvendte sig til udvekslingsstuderende; det krævede en forhåndsviden og -erfaring med et særligt opgaveformat, som var vanskeligt at læse sig til. Med den nye eksamensform in mente vurderede jeg, at det ville blive svært for mig at bestå kurset. Derfor kontaktede jeg en underviser på Fransk sprog og kultur på KU, som, jeg vidste, havde hjulpet en af mine medstuderende fra KU, da hun fik problemer med at bestå et kursus på et parisisk udvekslingsophold i foråret 2021. Min underviser beroligede mig og forklarede, at jeg ville kunne skrive en afløsningsopgave under hans vejledning, såfremt jeg skulle dumpe Esthétique-kurset. Min underviser vidste imidlertid ikke, at jeg var på udveksling med forhåndsgodkendte fag, der skulle svare til kurserne på 4. semester af bachelorgraden i Fransk sprog og kultur (jeg var med andre ord på udveksling med grundfag). Jeg var ikke selv klar over, at der gjaldt andre regler for mig end for studerende, der er på udveksling med deres tilvalgsfag; det var jeg på intet tidspunkt blevet oplyst om. Men det erfarede jeg, da jeg oplyste min individuelle aftale med fransk-underviseren for Engerom-studievejledningen. D. 17. marts skrev en studievejleder til mig: “Det er lidt mere kompliceret, når du er afsted på dit grundfag. Hvis du dumper bare ét fag dernede til f.eks. 4 ECTS, skal du hjem og bestå en eksamen til 15 ECTS herhjemme”. Det var en information, jeg meget gerne ville have haft tidligere i forløbet. Den fejlagtige oplysning om eksamensformen i kursusbeskrivelsen til Esthétique fik nu langt mere vidtrækkende (og uoverskuelige) konsekvenser. Eftersom mit udvekslingssemester i Paris var det sidste, jeg manglede, inden jeg skulle starte på min kandidat i efteråret 2022, var det vigtigt for mig at få vished om, at jeg kunne bestå de point, jeg måtte dumpe i Paris, i KU-regi. Førnævnte studievejleder beroligede mig; forsikrede mig om, at jeg ville kunne tilmelde mig reeksamen “uden at have fulgt kurset herhjemme. Der må du selv vurdere om det ville være muligt for dig at bestå.” Jeg dumpede, ganske som jeg havde forudset og frygtet, den første deleksamen i Esthétique-kurset i marts, og derfor søgte jeg yderligere oplysninger om, hvordan jeg kunne tilmelde mig reeksamen i det 15 ECTS-kursus, jeg skulle have haft hjemme på KU, hvis ikke jeg var taget på udveksling. Denne gang kontaktede jeg Engeroms studieadministration, der kunne berette om andre regler end dem, studievejledningen tidligere havde oplyst. Jeg både skrev og talte med en studiesekretær fra Engeroms studieadministration, der, i modsætning til instituttets studievejledning, afviste, at jeg kunne tilmelde mig reeksamen i det omtalte 15 ECTS-kursus. Det kunne ikke lade sig gøre uden at have været indskrevet på kurset, og jeg skulle derfor vente til foråret 2023 for at kunne indskrive mig og gå til eksamen den følgende sommer. Denne udmelding var en stor mavepuster. Jeg var vred og forvirret over at få så mange modsatrettede informationer og mente ikke, det kunne være rimeligt, at jeg så sent i semestret skulle orientere mig efter helt nye regler om reeksamination. Jeg var IKKE interesseret i at skulle vente et helt år på at måtte starte på min kandidat — fordi et 4 points-kursus i Paris af åbenlyse årsager ikke stillede rimelige krav til mig som udvekslingsstuderende. Jeg kontaktede derfor studienævnet og sendte en ansøgning om dispensation til at tilmelde mig reeksamen i det omtalte KU-15 points-kursus, selvom jeg ikke havde fulgt kurset i løbet af semestret. Endnu en administrativ opgave, der tog tid og fokus fra opgaver og forberedelser til min undervisning på universitetet. Studienævnet viste sig forstående og imødekom min ansøgning. Med vished om dispensation og en mulig udvej, kunne jeg færdiggøre mit semester med mere ro i sindet. Når jeg redegør for det her forløb, er det for at gøre opmærksom på, at der var en vis inkongruens mellem det fransksproglige niveau, der, ifølge KU, officielt var adgangsgivende til at læse et semester på Université de Paris-Diderot, og det niveau, der i praksis skulle til for at kunne gennemføre svære skriftlige (og uforudsigelige) eksamensformer. Dertil kom den manglende information fra KU's side. Havde man fortalt mig fra begyndelsen, at jeg, ved at tage på udveksling med mine grundfag, var tvunget til at bestå samtlige eksaminer i Paris, er jeg ikke sikker på, at jeg havde valgt et udvekslingsophold. Jeg vidste, at det ville blive en stor mundfuld for mig at læse på et parisisk universitet. Men det massive mentale pres, der fulgte med KU's skiftende meldinger om reeksamensregler, gjorde i perioder opholdet til en FOR stor mundfuld. Jeg var alvorligt bekymret for ikke at få lov til at starte på min kandidat i efteråret 2022, og den bekymring påvirkede mange uger af mit ophold.
teaching_comparison: Undervisningen adskilte sig på flere måder fra undervisningen på KU. Undervisningen var generelt meget underviserstyret, der var ganske lidt interaktion med de studerende; ganske lidt gruppearbejde og få oplæg fra studerende. Desuden skulle jeg vænne mig til at skrive både afleveringer og eksaminer i hånden. Det kræver en anden skrivestrategi, at man ikke kan rykke rundt på afsnit, men er bundet af den disposition, man indleder med at skrive. Undervisningen adskilte sig også ved, at der var meget af den! For at opnå det nødvendige antal ECTS-points, måtte jeg følge hele syv kurser. Det satte høje krav til min omstillingsparathed; der var mange forskellige undervisningsformer og undervisere at forholde sig til, og nogle var, som antydet, mere imødekommende end andre. Endelig vil jeg også knytte en kommentar til den “magt”, underviserne havde (og sommetider udøvede): For det første vidner mit eksempel fra Esthétique 3-kurset om, at den enkelte underviser – tilsyneladende – havde mandat til at ændre eksamensformatet, hvis han/hun ville. For det andet oplevede jeg til en af mine eksaminer, at underviseren (som skulle afvikle og holde opsyn under vores eksamen) kom over en time for sent. Han var fanget i et forsinket tog og informerede løbende de studerende over mail; her truede han også de studerende med en dumpekarakter, hvis de skulle finde på at forlade lokalet – selvom vi sad, nervøse og anspændte, og ikke anede, hvornår (og om) eksamenen reelt ville finde sted. Da underviseren kom, afviste han at give os ekstra tid i den anden ende; vi fik således 1 time og 45 minutter til en eksamen, der skulle have varet 3 timer. Det var en presset tidsramme for de studerende – og en særdeles presset tidsramme for os, der var udvekslingsstuderende. Selvsamme underviser (der sendte undervisningsmateriale pr. mail i løbet af hele semestret), havde i øvrigt også givet de studerende mangelfuldt materiale frem til eksamenen. Halvt inde i semestret sendte han ikke længere materiale og feedback på vores opgaver; han undskyldte sig med, at han var ramt af corona og kunne ikke give os nogen tidshorisont for, hvornår undervisningen blev genoptaget. Vi modtog den sidste halvdel af undervisningsmaterialet hhv. en uge og tre dage før vores eksaminer. Det var langt fra ideelt. En gruppe studerende gik sammen og forfattede en klage til administrationen (om både manglende undervisning og forsinket eksamen), men det fik tilsyneladende ikke nogen konsekvenser. Ovenstående episoder gav et indtryk af, at underviserne var magtfuldkomne; at de kunne gøre, hvad der passede dem, og at de studerende ikke kunne henvise til objektive og universelt gældende rettigheder, hverken i studieordninger/kursusbeskrivelser eller ved at kontakte administrationen. Historien var heldigvis en anden for størstedelen af mine undervisere, men jeg mener alligevel, at undtagelserne er værd at nævne. Endelig vil jeg gøre opmærksom på det faktum, at Université de Paris-Diderot ikke gjorde brug af ekstern censur (i hvert fald ikke afdelingen for Lettres, Arts et Cinéma, hvor jeg var indskrevet). Det var således underviserne selv, der evaluerede egne studerende. Eksamensbesvarelserne var godt nok anonymiserede med en lille flap papir nedover navn og studienummer, men som udvekslingsstuderende føltes det ikke som et entydigt trygt og retfærdigt evaluerings-/bedømmelsessystem.
courses_enrolled: Esthétique 3 (4 ECTS), Lecture de la poésie (5 ECTS), Lecture du conte (3 ECTS), Histoire littéraire 2 (3 ECTS), Ateliers pour l'oral (4 ECTS), Lecture de textes philosophiques (4 ECTS), Techniques d'expression 2 (4 ECTS).
recommended_courses: Som franskstuderende er kurserne Ateliers pour l'oral og Techniques d'expression 2 særligt interessante. Det er to kurser, der beskæftiger sig med hhv. mundtlig og skriftlig kommunikation/sprogfærdighed på fransk. Begge undervisere tog hensyn til min situation som udvekslingsstuderende og var gode til at inddrage mig. Det var på alle måder berigende og lærerige kurser, og jeg kan kun opfordre andre franskstuderende med interesse for sproglige registre, situationstilpasset kommunikation, retorik, præsentationsteknik og skriftlig sprogfærdighed til at følge samme kurser.
unexpected_costs: Kontingent for at synge med i universitetskor, udstyr til min bolig.
cost_comparison: Bøger er meget billige i Frankrig, og da vi ikke skulle betale for kompendier i universitetsregi, var udgifterne til undervisningsmaterialer både få og små. Til gengæld er offentlig transport i Paris relativt dyr, men det er næsten en nødvendighed at investere i et månedligt metrokort, hvis man ikke bor i nærheden af universitetet og i øvrigt gerne vil udforske byen; det bliver hurtigt en omstændelig affære at cykle, men det kan godt lade sig gøre.
activities_available: Der var både sportsaktiviteter, teater- og koncertoplevelser, restaurantrabatter m.v. Alle tilbud og aktiviteter var samlet på Université de Paris' portal “La BOX”; her kunne man løbende orientere sig i igangværende forløb og enkeltbegivenheder.
activities_recommended: Jeg søgte optagelse i O.C.U.P. (L'Orchestre et Chœur des Universités de Paris), som er et universitetskor og -orkester, der samler amatørmusikere på tværs af alle universiteter i Paris. Vi havde en ugentlig korprøve på Sorbonne og en månedlig søndagskorprøve ved Panthéon, og så sang vi fire store koncerter i løbet af foråret. Det var ubetinget den bedste beslutning, jeg tog uden for universitetet; jeg fik mange gode venner og bekendte i koret, det var i det hele taget en fantastisk måde at møde nye mennesker. Jeg kan varmt anbefale, at andre studerende med interesse for (og gerne erfaring med) klassisk kormusik søger ind!
weekend_recommendations: Paris er så rig en by; der er så mange muséer, historiske bygninger, parker, gallerier, caféer, restauranter, barer og butikker at udforske. Kender man ikke Paris i forvejen, bør man absolut udforske centrum (1.-6. arrondissement), men der gemmer sig også meget guld uden for de allermest centrale arrondissementer. I det 11. arrondissement bugner det med lokale (gode og billige) restauranter, og i det 19. arrondissement kan man eksempelvis besøge parken Buttes-Chaumont, som er en af Paris' allerstørste og -sjoveste. Vil man uden for Paris, kan jeg anbefale en tur til Bretagne; i byer som Rennes og Dinan kan man opleve betagende bindingsværkshuse, og man kan måske lige nå at runde Mont Saint-Michel, en fantastisk tidevandsø ved Normandiet. Ønsker man at opleve Alsace, kan man fx tage til Strasbourg (ca. to timers hurtigtogtur fra Paris) og spise sauerkraut og drikke Riesling. Strasbourg er en charmerende by med mange fine museer og en smuk katedral og naturligvis særlig interessant, hvis man interesserer sig for EU-politik og Europarådet.
culture_adjustment: Jeg var i den lykkelige situation, at jeg havde boet i Paris i et år, inden mit udvekslingsophold begyndte. Derfor havde jeg allerede haft god tid til at tilpasse mig den franske kultur, og jeg var hjulpet af at bo sammen med to franske kvinder. Frankrig er berygtet for sit “paperasse” (bureaukratisk papirarbejde), og i mange tilfælde er der hold i rygterne. Men — generelt møder man mange hjælpsomme mennesker, og som dansker er man hjulpet af at være EU-borger; så går det hele mere glat. Og så taler mange i øvrigt engelsk, særligt de unge. Så på universitetet kan man relativt hurtigt finde sig til rette blandt sine medstuderende, også selvom ens franskkompetencer ikke altid måtte række.
socializing_tips: Udnyt universitetets tilbud om både sports- og kulturaktiviter, og søg evt. bolig i en såkaldt “colocation” (bofællesskab).
cultural_challenges: Selvom man føler sig relativt flydende på fransk, kan de være svært at begå sig i de mange forskellige registre og høflighedsformer, fx i mailkorrespondancer med universitetsundervisere og administrative medarbejdere. Det kan være godt at alliere sig med et par modersmålstalende og få dem til at læse ens mails, indtil man har lært formatet at kende og ved, hvordan man kommunikerer med franske autoriteter. Jeg skulle også vænne mig til undervisningssituationen; at være Des med underviseren og dus med sine medstuderende. Og så er de franske studerende meget unge, og det gav et lidt andet undervisningsmiljø, end jeg er vant til fra KU.
culture_appreciated: Jeg har værdsat, at teater, musik og litteratur er så tilgængeligt og billigt; at jeg kan købe en roman til 3 €, at foreningslivet er så rigt og arrangerer gratis koncerter, at der er studierabat til muséer osv. Paris er i det hele taget en meget studievenlig by; dels fordi der er så mange studerende i byen, dels fordi de mange kultur-, mad- og sportstilbud, jeg ville bruge hjemme i København, er lige så tilgængelige (og i mange tilfælde billigere) i Paris.
top3_advice: 1. Man bør væbne sig med tålmodighed og være indstillet på at skulle være meget insisterende og stædig for at blive taget alvorligt. Jeg har været meget skuffet over måden, jeg blev behandlet af kontoret for “Relations Internationales/Mobilité d'études Erasmus+” på Université de Paris-Diderot. 2. Man bør have en god kontakt med den enkelte underviser; gøre opmærksom på, at man er udvekslingsstuderende, og aftale i god tid, om man fx må medbringe ordbøger og få ekstra tid til eksaminerne. Ikke alle undervisere tager hensyn til de udvekslingsstuderende, og man kan ikke forvente at få særbehandling. 3. Man kan med fordel tilmelde sig universitetets Buddy-ordning, hvor man bliver “matchet” med en lokal studerende, der kan hjælpe med alle former for spørgsmål, både i og uden for universitetsregi.
other_useful_info: Universitetet har et helt genialt bibliotek, der er så stort, at man (næsten) altid kan være sikker på at finde en plads. Generelt er universitetets faciliteter fine, men lokalerne (og især toiletterne) er meget slidte og ikke altid rene og pæne. Universitets campusområde er spredt over hele byen, og jeg ved, at det var en udfordring for nogle af de andre udvekslingsstuderende. Jeg selv havde kun undervisning på campusafdelingen Grands Moulins i det 13. arrondissement og undgik derfor overlappende undervisning forskellige steder i byen. Men ønsker man undervisning på forskellige fakulteter, kan man fordel (prøve at) få kontakt til administrationen og søge oplysning om, hvordan et evt. skema ser ud for de kurser, man ønsker.
most_rewarding: Et stort fransksprogligt udbytte, generelt spændende og vedkommende undervisning, lærerige opgaver, fantastiske korprøver og koncertoplevelser med føromtalte universitetskor O.C.U.P. og gode franske venner, som jeg absolut agter at holde kontakten med.
greatest_challenge: Jeg har svært ved at udpege én udfordring, der var den største. Alle de administrative udfordringer, jeg løbende har udfoldet i ovenstående punkter, besværliggjorde mit ophold og gjorde mig stresset og ked af det i flere perioder. Jeg håber, at denne evaluering bliver læst, og at de administrative udfordringer, jeg har skitseret, bliver taget alvorligt. Jeg håber inderligt, at min(e) administrationshistorie(r) er enestående, og at andre får et mere gnidningsfrit forløb, end det jeg har haft.

crucial_aspects: For a long time I've been interested in trying to live in Paris, since I love France and especially Paris. Furthermore, I would like France to be part of a major part of my future career, which was probably the most important aspect of my decision to spend a semester in Paris as an Erasmus student.
overall_comments: While there was major differences from UCPH as far as the methods of teaching, for me the most important part of the semester was without a doubt the social aspect. I had received many "warnings" from other students I had contacted in connection with my considerations of studying in Paris, and other travel reports that mentioned the French students being very cold, the teaching system being too rigid and overall bad experiences. It made me a bit hesitative about spending a semester in Paris, however I knew that it had been my dream, and that I had to try it for myself and make my own experiences. Upon arrival and throughout the semester, I've made countless friends, French as well as other Erasmus students from Italy, Belgium, and more. I don't doubt that I will stay in contact with the friends I've made in Paris, since we connected very easily and we had lots of fun experiences on and off campus.
info_ease: There was an information meeting in the end of august before classes started, where all the Erasmus students met each other and were shown around on the campus by French students afterwards. During this meeting, pretty much all concerns and questions I had were answered throughout the day. Overall, it was quite easy to find the information I needed upon arrival.
arrival_assistance: There was a coordinator in charge of handling questions from international students throughout the whole semester. This person was present at the information meeting and made sure that all the Erasmus students felt at home and were not confused. Although I wasn't in really in a position where I needed much assistance, it was possible to get this if necessary.
arrival_comments: It was nice to get shown around by the French students afterwards who were extremely open and welcoming.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_process: I was automatically registered in the courses that I had chosen in my Learning Agreement. Throughout the first couple of weeks I changed 1 course which was extremely easy, I just updated the Learning Agreement and sent it to UCPH and UPC. Thereafter, I was registered in the new course.
registration_help: The Erasmus Coordinator from UPC was (mostly) very helpful, although it sometimes took a very long time for her to answer compared to UCPH. I rarely had questions, so instead of e-mailing her, I just went to her office on campus.
registration_advice: Talk directly to the Erasmus-coordinator if you have questions and otherwise just remember to have a Learning Agreement containing the courses you want to follow. The last date to change the Learning Agreement was October 15th, so if you are in doubt, try the different courses.
academics_comments: While there was major differences from UCPH as far as the methods of teaching, for me the most important part of the semester was without a doubt the social aspect. I had received many "warnings" from other students I had contacted in connection with my considerations of studying in Paris, and other travel reports that mentioned the French students being very cold, the teaching system being too rigid and overall bad experiences. It made me a bit hesitative about spending a semester in Paris, however I knew that it had been my dream, and that I had to try it for myself and make my own experiences. Upon arrival and throughout the semester, I've made countless friends, French as well as other Erasmus students from Italy, Belgium, and more. I don't doubt that I will stay in contact with the friends I've made in Paris, since we connected very easily and we had lots of fun experiences on and off campus.
course_level: Other than the fact that legal French is of course quite different than everyday French, the content of the courses was on a surprisingly high level. The best example I have of this, is the course "Introduction au marché intérieur européen", a M1 course of 3,5 ECTS. In this course, we were taught pretty much the same as in the 2nd year BA-course "EU-ret" on UCPH. However, the course also contained EU-competition law (including EU-merger control) and EU-state aid regulation. In my view, this tendency was also the case throughout the other courses I followed. In addition to the difficulty of the courses, if you ask me, 30 ECTS in UPC is not equivalent to 30 ECTS in UCPH. It was not possible to take a master's course with more than 3,5 ECTS, which motivated me to take some licence (bachelor's) courses of 6 ECTS. Their grading-system is also fundamentally different. In certain courses, obtaining a 10/20, which is necessary to pass the course, is not at all an easy task, and I witnessed many of my fellow French students fail courses, since they (contrary to at UCPH) need an average grade of 10/20 out of all the courses they've taken throughout the semester in order to pass. My impression was that it depends on the professor, and if this person is easier on the Erasmus students. There is definitely courses where this is the case, but also the opposite. Important note : The level of French (grammar etc.) in the classes is incredibly high, so I would at least say that you should be very, very comfortable in everyday French. In my case, I was required to take a DELF B2 test from home which cost around 1300DKK.
teaching_comparison: It is important to note that the courses of 6 ECTS were TD courses, comparable to "seminartimer" at UCPH, thus both lectures and smaller classes. Presence and homework for these courses was not mandatory, and I didn't make homework for any of the 3 TD-courses I had, since this would require incredible amounts of time. As mentioned, I prioritized the social aspects of my exchange semester and didn't always meet up to all my classes. I would however say that one of the most interesting/bizarre experiences was the TD-classes. The amount of respect (fear) from the French students towards the TD-professor was something I have never experienced, probably since their grades depended on their performance in the TD-classes (not the case for Erasmus-students). This sometimes lead to small clashes between me and one professor since she didn't know the rules for Erasmus students were different. At least I found that the teaching style and institutional differences herein between Denmark and France are incredibly noticeable, but not necessarily negatively. The exams varied a lot, as I had both oral exams, written exams and a multiple choice.
courses_enrolled: Introduction générale au droit (6 ECTS), Introduction au droit constitutionnel (6 ECTS), Droit civil des contrats (6 ECTS), Droit de l'environnement (3,5 ECTS), Droit du marché intérieur européen (3,5 ECTS), Droit des sociétés commerciales (3,5 ECTS) and Histoire du droit des affaires et des relations sociales (3,5 ECTS) - in total 32 ECTS
recommended_courses: Since the system for TD courses is different and more lenient for Erasmus students, I would definitely recommend taking these in order to minimize the necessary amount of courses (and exams). Nevertheless, if you're interested in corporate law, I can highly recommend "Droit des sociétés commerciales" since this course thoroughly covers almost everything relevant as regards commercial company law in France.
unexpected_costs: Eating out can become very costly, and even though there are is an incredible amount of delicious cheap foods (banh mi and falafel especially), most of the bistros/brasseries are not very cheap.
cost_comparison: Books and travel. I highly recommend renting a Swapfiets which costs 19 euros a month and takes you all over Paris. My travel expenses were higher due to sometimes taking the metro.
activities_available: Many different associations, although I think these were in general for the French students.
activities_recommended: Go to the museums, drink lots of wine, eat lots of cheese, experience the parks, the bars, the nightlife and the shops. Since Paris is undoubtedly the greatest city in the world for "la kiffance", this is what I enjoyed doing the most. Live life !
weekend_recommendations: I went to Normandy and Marseille on weekend trips, and especially Marseille is one of the most beautiful cities I've seen in Europe. The people there were unbelievably nice and open - I highly recommend going see some French cities and regions outside of Paris in the weekends.
culture_adjustment: Extremely easy. As long as you're open and actively trying to make friends with the students on campus, from your classes etc., it is very smooth. Even if French isn't your mother tongue, French students are not at all (at least regarding this) judgy. People are very friendly, however I would imagine that it is quite difficult making friends if you are not actively trying to speak to the local students. Even if you are nervous about your French, be brave and everything will be alright.
socializing_tips: Don't be afraid, the local students were (almost) all extremely nice and friendly. Speak to the French students that show the Erasmus students around on campus, and you will quickly know many people on campus. Also, just saying hi and having conversations with the people next to you during the lectures was great for me.
cultural_challenges: Since it is quite a prestigeous university, the French students were super focused on their grades, which is not necessarily a cultural difference from UCPH, but it is nice to know. The waiters can often be rude.
culture_appreciated: I love the openness of French people as they were always open to share notes, talk, eat lunch, hang out etc. This is the main reason that I wouldn't have chosen any other university looking back now.
top3_advice: 1. Be prepared to work (the exam period was horrible hahah), 2. Always be open, 3. Enjoy as much as you can of Europe's cultural capital.
other_useful_info: Applying for grants (legater) is extremely recommended. In my case, it drastically changed my exchange semester, as I had so much more financial freedom. Although it takes time, there is so many grants to apply for, and also French-specific grants as well.
most_rewarding: The friends I've made along the way and all that I've learned thanks to the courses. Additionally, just the experience of living in Paris is something that cannot be described.
greatest_challenge: Probably the exam period. 7 exams that were all extremely difficult made for a long and difficult exam period, even worse than at UCPH in my experience. However, the public libraries (especially la BnF) are easily accessible and incredibly beautiful.
other_comments: Never be scared to ask for help from anyone, in my view it helps much more than I would have known

crucial_aspects: I wanted ti improve my French. Also, I wanted the opportunity to live and study in Paris because of all the cultural offers the city has.
overall_comments: Paris is an absolutely amazing city, and alone the chance to live here for four months made my experience amazing. The academic experience was at Dauphine was OK, but UCPH has a much higher academic standard.
info_ease: The administration at Dauphine is very chaotic. All international students I spoke to had some kind of problem which needed to be solved out administratively upon arrival, and that created a lot of chaos and line in front of the international office. So honestly, it was not very easy.
arrival_assistance: There is an international office responsible for all the international students. I had to go there 3-4 times to solve out everything upon arrival. The staff at the international office give rather contradicting information, and they do not have the capacity to handle all the international students.
arrival_comments: France is generally very chaotic when it comes to administrational stuff. Take it as an authentic experience. It will all work out in the end.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Paris is an absolutely amazing city, and alone the chance to live here for four months made my experience amazing. The academic experience was at Dauphine was OK, but UCPH has a much higher academic standard.
registration_process: You apply to Dauphine through a link they send you. That proces was very easy. The course registration is more difficult. You chose courses also through a link they sent you, but a lot of courses time class, and the options for master courses in political or social science are not many. You can also change by going ditectly to the international office when you arrive
registration_help: You can send an email to the international office before arrival, but they will most likely not respond. The easiest is to go there yourself when you arrive. As almost everyone have to change courses, it creates huge lines in front of the international office. I once waited in line for 1,5 hours.
registration_success: Not very succesful. I had problems finding relevant courses that were not time clashing. I ended up changing everything when I arrived, and I ended up taking a course in Finance to get it all to add up. In general, they do not offer so many master courses - especially not for political science students. You therefore have to take what you can get.
registration_advice: The courses are worth 3 or 6 ECTS, but the work load on the 3 ECTS-courses are sometimes the same as 6 ECTS-courses. Therefore, I would recommend to try to take as many 6 ECTS-courses as possible.
academics_comments: Paris is an absolutely amazing city, and alone the chance to live here for four months made my experience amazing. The academic experience was at Dauphine was OK, but UCPH has a much higher academic standard.
course_level: The courses meant only for international students are not very good. The courses also open to French students at the actual master programmes are way better, but also more difficult. But in general, I think that UCPH has a higher academic level.
teaching_comparison: It requires more participation in class. Often, your final grade is also based on assignments that you hand in throughout the semester.
courses_enrolled: International Finance (3 ECTS) International Politice (3 ECTS) Management of Information Systems (6 ECTS) Global Media (6 ECTS) Industrial Organization (6 ECTS) Global Climate Politics: Comparative EU-US Perspectives (6 ECTS)
recommended_courses: Global Climate Politics was good. International Finance was very difficult, but I really learned a lot.
unexpected_costs: Going out! I ended up spending more money on going out than I had planned. There are so many good restaurants to chose from, and often social gatherings are centered around going out.
cost_comparison: I don't know, I think in general prices are close to the Danish. Bakeries are a bit cheaper.
activities_available: There are a lot of Erasmus events. It is a good way to meet people. And also, they had a welcoming week, which was unstructured, but a good way to meet people. They have an option to do sports as well. They have a lot of different student clubs as well.
activities_recommended: Go to the Erasmus events (especially in the beginning) if you want to meet other international students. I went to a few, it was fun. Otherwise, I didn't use the non-academic options at school.
weekend_recommendations: Visit museums. Use the cultural offers in the city. Go to restaurants. Go out. Go to Versaille. Explore and enjoy the city, the options are so many!
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: If you know some French you are better off.
cultural_challenges: Not really any.
culture_appreciated: The social lifestyle.
top3_advice: 1) Prepare for a chaotic start 2) You have to take many courses as they are only worth 3 or 6 ECTS 3) The level of the courses and the work load really depends on whether you take courses from the actual master programmes or not
other_useful_info: You can take free French lessons without getting ECTS if you talk to the course administration or the French teacher.
most_rewarding: The social aspect. And getting to know Paris.
greatest_challenge: The administrational stuff in the beginning.
other_comments: Just enjoy Paris! I can't say hat enough times.

crucial_aspects: I chose UCC primarily based on the courses I could choose as well as the student life. I liked that UCC has so many clubs and societies and the student life seemed very active.
info_ease: The student office was very helpfull, but a bit slow. But I figured out everything I needed to know.
arrival_assistance: They had arranged transfer from the airport, tours of the campus and a fair to join the clubs and societies.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You apply for courses before arriving and wait for approval. You have to make your own time table and make sure that none of your courses are overlapping. If you do not get the approval you need to register again and hope to be accepted for the new courses.
registration_help: The International Student Office was very helpfull.
registration_success: I was rejected for a lot of courses because of the reduced capacity, but I ended up getting courses I wanted. I had to write the professors for a few courses to prove that I was qualified to take their courses.
registration_advice: I would recommend to have a few extra courses to apply for, if you get rejected. And know that you might have to reach out the the professors.
course_level: The level was generally high.
teaching_comparison: There was only lectures and laboratory work, so you are a lot more independent. The syllabus is not a clear so you have to find literature on your own sometimes. But most professors were really helpfull, if you didn't understand something. They have a lo of "continuous assessment", so you have to be prepared to do a lot of tests all the time.
courses_enrolled: "Introduction to Neuroscience, the Brain and Behaviour" "Advanced Inorganic Chemistry Part 1" "Advanced Analytical Chemistry Part 1" "Western Music, Culture and Media" "Structural and Experimental Biochemistry" "Advanced Research Methodology in Neuroscience"
recommended_courses: "Advanced Analytical Chemistry Part 1" was really interesting and fun. They focused a lot on the application and gave a lot of useful tips on careers. "Advanced Research Methodology in Neuroscience" gave a lot of knowledge on conducting an experiment and how to work as a researcher.
unexpected_costs: My phone bill was very expensive the last month, because my phone company (3) raised the prices after being abroad for over 2 months.
cost_comparison: Public transportation is not too expensive. Also restaurants are a lot cheaper than in Denmark.
activities_available: There are a lot of clubs and societies to join. There is a huge selection, so everyone can find something they like.
activities_recommended: Taking trips around Ireland, hiking.
weekend_recommendations: Definitely hike. The mountaineering club has some nice trips, but you can easily plan them your self as well.
culture_adjustment: The Irish are so friendly, so it was very easy.
socializing_tips: Be open, and go out
cultural_challenges: In Ireland they party during the week and go home on weekends. Otherwise it's not too different.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness.
top3_advice: There is a lot of test, so definitely keep up with studying all the time. Take trips and see the country, it's so beautiful. Join clubs and societies, there are so many and they do fun events all the time.
other_useful_info: Go to all the lectures and do extra reading. There is so much help to find, if things are difficult.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people and learning to study in a diffrent way.
greatest_challenge: Balancing having fun and exploring a new city with studying. You want to have fun all the time, because there is so much to do, but sometimes you need to spend the weekend at the library.

crucial_aspects: The country were native english, so I would be able to understand the lectures to the fullest and make friends, that was not only other international students, but be a part of the everyday life by not having a language gap. The selection of courses at the university were also crucial.
info_ease: Pretty easy. There was always the opportunity to write an email to the exchange office at KU or UCC, who would replied quickly and guide you to the information you were seeking.
arrival_assistance: Emails from the hosting university, two orientation days, guided tour at the university.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: I got an email from my host institution, where I had to send my grades, and fill a form. Then later in the progress I send my wishes for courses and the acceptance from my home institution of the classes I wanted to take. Upon arrival I signed up for the classes.
registration_help: Email to Erasmus coordinator, student center, learning center, professors.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted, so very succesful.
registration_advice: Go for the classes you want to explore. Exchange is about both the social, the new culture, the classes, so even if the class disappoints, you will still learn a lot from it.
course_level: I had classes on all 3 levels; 1st year, 2nd year and 3rd year classes. The level was high academic english in the 2nd and 3rd year classes, where the 1st year classes was really high level in understanding academic theories in the culture you are in.
teaching_comparison: The host institution more lectures than seminars, where at UCPH I am use to seminars, discussion groups and interacting with the teacher a lot. There was less of that at my host institution, but there was still a lot of answering question and still having a debate with the teacher and fellow students.
courses_enrolled: 'Social Analysis', 'Contemporary Criminological Theory', 'Political Sociology', and 'Family, Gender, Sexualities'
recommended_courses: 'Social Analysis' was super interesting, as it combined the everyday life and practice in Ireland with some of the bigger sociological theories from Marx, Foucault, Weber, Bourdieu, etc. Very interesting to get the irish point of view through this course. 'Family, Gender, Sexualities' were also a great course, as it was very interactive between students and teacher and a lot of different people were in the class from a lot of different countries (still mainly irish people, but definitely a more diverse class).
unexpected_costs: Traveling and social meetings. I spend a lot of money traviling around in my host country, on tourist attraction, busses, trains. Besides that there was meeting with friends, which then often included buying food in town and not cooking yourself, drinking coffee while studying, etc. Laundry cost 30 DKK and drying 15 DKK.
cost_comparison: Laundry and drying was a lot more expensive than I expected. Drinks were a lot more expensive. Housing was so much more expensive than expected. Busses were super cheap (5 DKK for students).
activities_available: Everything. Swimmingpool with steam room and sauna, three different kinds of gyms (cardio, strength, etc.), climbing wall for mountaineering, sports arena to play badminton, football, handball, squash, yoga. Outdoor athletic stadium, football fields, literally everything.
activities_recommended: Mountaineering club (climbing wall activities), trampolining (with personal coached that helps you), the swimming pool and the gym, be a part of the international group in Cork (they arranged meetings, and where most people met each other).
weekend_recommendations: Go to new citys like Galway, Dublin, Belfast and explore, spend the money you will not regret it. Take the bus to beaches in Cork County, do the touristy things in Cork, because they are super nice. Go to the national parks, the nature is spectacular.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. The most friendly people on earth.
socializing_tips: Do not hold back or be afraid that you have an accent that sounds wierd, they do not care, they are interested in you and why you chose to come to their city.
cultural_challenges: They drive on the left side of the street.
culture_appreciated: The openness, and kind-hearted people.
top3_advice: Explore the nature, it is so beautiful. Be open towards anyone you meet. Just go say hi to knew people, I promise they will not find it wierd.
other_useful_info: Use the library for studying, it is a very good atmosphere to get into writing mode.
most_rewarding: The friendships I gained.
greatest_challenge: The expenses.

arrival_assistance: I didn't really receive any, other than an introduction to the Erasmus program and the university
housing_how: I found housing on my own

teaching_comparison: It was kind of the same.

activities_available: All kinds of sport clubs and societies. I think over a 100 in total, so lots of opportunities to meet new people.
activities_recommended: I played a lot af handball and went to matches with the team i Dublin which were very cool. I also joined Harry Potter society and Feminism society, but didn't have much time to engage with it as i had a lot of assignments.
weekend_recommendations: Take it easy and explore the city and surroundings on the weekends, and then go on a bigger trip once in a while. If you can, rent a car at least once as it is the best way to see Ireland, especially West Cork and Kerry which are incredible places.
culture_adjustment: Easy
socializing_tips: Be open and ask what places they would recommend you to go to, and they might invite you along for a beer one day.
cultural_challenges: Its hard to say. Personally, I thought a lot of the Irish college students were a little superficial and immature, but maybe thats because of the age difference (they were mostly around 20 and I 24).
culture_appreciated: The Irish are in general very sweet and helpful.
top3_advice: Go alone, live in a student accommodation (even though it is expensive, it's worth it because it's easier being social) and join as much stuff as you can at the beginning. Since the stay is kind of short, you want to make friends early. Also, a lot of assignments will hit you after a couple of months, and you won't have as much time to make friends then.
other_useful_info: Don't think so.
most_rewarding: Being able to experience living in an other country.
greatest_challenge: To complete all of the assignments and to be social at the same time.
other_comments: No

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to a place where they speak English in order to make the study easier for myself. I also chose the destination because I thought that the courses in the university sounded really interesting and relevant for my education.
info_ease: I think it was fairly easy. The host university was good at sending out information on what to do next. And the website for the host university also had a lot of information.
arrival_assistance: In the beginning of my stay I was invited to several orientation meetings where they told us about the social life at the university and the academics and life as an exchange student.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The host university sent out quite detailed descriptions on how to register. You would register for the courses you wanted. Later you would have to check that the timetable for the various courses matched up and you would maybe have to change some of your courses to make it work. You would also be given some time to try out your chosen courses and then have the opportunity to change them.
registration_help: There were people at the host university that you could ask for help if you had questions about the registration. For example I was a bbit confused about the timetables, and they helped me with that.
registration_success: I ended up only being able to take one of the courses that I was originally planning on taking, since the courses change and some get canceled, and some of them did not match up with their different timetables. However, I ended up really liking all of my courses!
registration_advice: I think I would just say to check your mails regularly for updates and guides to register and to ask for help if you are unsure of something or try to find the answers at the host university's website.
course_level: I think that because it was in English for me it automatically made it a bit more difficult to understand certain things in the courses. However, I do not think that it was so difficult that I could not follow, and generally, I feel like the level was about the same as at the University of Copenhagen. I feel like there was perhaps a bit less reading per week compared to what I am used to, but at the same time there were also more assignments (I had two courses that were worth 10 ECTS which each contained two assignments or an assignment and a presentation, and then two courses that were 5 ECTS points and each consisted of one assignment). The assignments were generally between 2500-3000 words. I feel like I had a lot of free time in the beginning of the semester, and then later on I ended up being a bit stressed about studying for and doing all of the assignments. Therefore I would say that it is a good idea to make sure to read up on some of the texts in each subject as you go along and think of what you might want to do in your assigments, so that you do not get too stressed in the end.
teaching_comparison: I think the style of teaching was somewhat similar to that of UCPH. However, my courses were lecturers in which it was possible to ask questions but other than that it was mostly the lecturer talking. I did not have any group work or something like that.
courses_enrolled: Aspects of Irish Folklore (5 ECTS) which is about beliefs and customs in Ireland which I really liked! I also took the courses Sociology of Memory, Trauma & Collective Denial (10 ECTS) which was also quite interesting. I also took the course Race, Ethnicity, Migration and Nationalism (10 ECTS) which I also liked. And then I had a course called Sexuality and Society (5 ECTS), and I enjoyed this course as well.
recommended_courses: I liked all of my courses and would recommend them to others. I feel some of the courses were somehow connected to each other and also that they each provided me with new insights that I feel I could use in my own studies.
unexpected_costs: I think that living in my destination was generally quite expensive. I definitely ended up spending more money on beer than I had expected
cost_comparison: I think that everything was maybe a bit more expensive than what I had imagined
activities_available: There were clubs which consisted of different sports. There were also societies which consisted of many different kinds of interests that people could join. And there were various happenings at campus for students to get engaged in
activities_recommended: Unfortunately, I ended up not making so much use of the opportunities of clubs and societies, but I think that they are probably a good way to meet people. I was also told that it is a good way to meet more of the Irish students instead of mainly other exchange students.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend looking into opportunities of going on different day trips and also setting aside maybe some weekends to explore other parts of the country. I did this several times and these experiences were some of the highlights of my exchange
culture_adjustment: I don't think it was too hard, but of course, some things were different from what I am used to
socializing_tips: I would recommend joining some clubs and societies and generally just going around the city and checking out what it has to offer.
cultural_challenges: I don't think there was really anything that was very challenging in terms of the cultural differences. But of course it could sometimes be a bit challenging having to speak English all of the time. I was also sometimes a bit confused by the Irish accent
culture_appreciated: I think that people were generally friendly and I really enjoyed meeting up at some of the local pubs with the people I met
top3_advice: Be open to meeting people:) You could for example try to join some clubs and societies and different kinds of groups for exchange students. Make use of the opportunities that the university and the city offers and explore it. Just see it as an opportunity to meet many different people from other cultures, to improve your English and in general learn more, both academically but also about yourself!
other_useful_info: Make sure to check your emails daily and to make use of the facilities offered at the university.
most_rewarding: I thought it was pretty scary in the beginning because I was going to travel alone and live in a country where I don't know anyone, but it feels great that I have done it and know that it is something that I can do. I am also really happy that I got to see more of the country and experience the culture more and get to share it with other people. And I also feel like it has made speaking English feel a bit more natural to me.
greatest_challenge: It was especially challenging in the beginning when I had to meet a lot of people, and it was even more challenging to do in English. But I also feel like it has been good for me to experience. And people were very nice and just as nervous and eager to meet other people!

crucial_aspects: English language courses, access to faculties other than my own course of study, university-assisted housing
overall_comments: UCC did wonderful in making my Erasmus stay as smooth and easy as possible, although I do think that their claim to "assist with housing" is false. They do not provide housing or any guarantee of housing, they provide *help* with *finding* housing, which I found to be very different. I think mainly the unexpected housing crisis in Ireland might have something to do with this, and it definitely influenced my stay and experience in general, because I ended up in a shitty room with shared bathroom and kitchen, paying double what I'd do in Copenhagen for my own studio apartment, fully renovated, complete bath and kitchen.
info_ease: Easy! UCC is good at communication and really spelling things out for everyone.
arrival_assistance: I didn't need any extraordinary assistance.
arrival_comments: None
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: UCC did wonderful in making my Erasmus stay as smooth and easy as possible, although I do think that their claim to "assist with housing" is false.
