crucial_aspects: Ville gerne have at det var en europæisk by.
info_ease: Rimelig nemt. UvA var nemme at få fat i og de sendte e-mails undervejs med den vigtigste information.
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik ikke rigtig nogen assistance, men det var fordi jeg ankom efter intro-dagene.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Det var en fin proces. De er gode til at sende reminder-e-mails med deadlines osv. som man skal huske.
registration_help: Man kunne nemt række ud til enten exchange-kontoret eller til min department - Economics and Business Economics.
registration_success: Jeg havde lidt svært ved at vælge fag, da UvA ikke udbød nogle af de prioriterede valgfag, som jeg egentlig ville have haft på KU, hvis jeg havde været hjemme på 5. semester. Jeg endte med at vælge valgfag i stedet.
registration_advice: At kigge i UvA's course catalogue i forhold til at vælge fag.
course_level: Mine fag var ret forskellige i niveau. Jeg synes nogle af dem var for svære, og nogle af dem passende. Generelt er niveauet ret højt på UvA, så jeg har læst ret meget mens jeg har været afsted. Jeg uddyber længere nede...
teaching_comparison: Forelæserne på UvA gik ikke rigtig op i at vi fik pauser, som de ellers virkelig respekterer her på KU, i hvert fald som jeg oplever det. Selve undervisningen på UvA var meget forskellig fra fag til fag - nogle holdtimer var obligatoriske og nogle ikke. Nogle fag havde fremlæggelser, andre ikke.
courses_enrolled: Money and Banking, Environmental Economics, International Trade and Investment, Behavioral Economics og Finance 1 for Business.
recommended_courses: Jeg kan ikke anbefale Money and Banking eller Finance 1 for Business. Begge fag har midterms, hvilket jeg syntes var alt for krævende, nu hvor UvA også har blokstruktur. Det vil sige, at man allerede går til midterm efter 3-4 uger af at have haft faget, og hvis man ikke består den, så er det svært at bestå den endelige eksamen. Det er også lidt hardcore, når man i forvejen er i gang med at falde til, allerede at skulle forholde sig til eksamen. Så jeg kan generelt anbefale at vælge fag, der ikke har midterms. Environmental Economics var rigtig fint, men handlede ikke om makroøkonomiske modeller med klimaeffekter, som jeg lidt havde regnet med. Det handlede mere om at gennemgå studier, fremlægge om dem og lære derigennem. Ingen midterm. Behavioral Economics var fedt. Rigtig engageret forelæser, der gjorde det spændende. Man skulle lave et eksperiment til holdundervisningen med en gruppe og så fremlægge resultater derfra. Det var virkelig fedt. Ingen midterm.
unexpected_costs: Ikke rigtig nogle faktisk.
cost_comparison: Supermarkedet er i hvert fald billigere end i Danmark, så det var en god ting. Det samme hvis man skal købe kaffe eller andet. Generelt billigere.
activities_available: Jeg var på basket-holdet på USC, som foregik i Science Park. Det var mega fedt. Det kostede dog cirka 1500-2000 DKK for et semester. Man skulle melde sig til 'try-outs' hvilket jeg fandt på deres Instagram.
activities_recommended: Kan helt klart anbefale de sportsaktiviteter der foregår i Science Park. De har alle mulige slags sport - der er vidst også et fitness center.
weekend_recommendations: Tag til Jordaan, tag til de Pijp og om sommeren er der også særligt fedt i Øst.
culture_adjustment: Synes det var ret smooth - der er ikke så stor en kulturel forskel, og hollændere er generelt temmelig tjekkede, ligesom i DK.
socializing_tips: Jeg snakkede ikke med så mange lokale, da jeg ikke havde fag med dem, så det var svært at komme i kontakt.
cultural_challenges: Synes ikke rigtig at der var nogle kulturelle forskelle, der var udfordrende.
culture_appreciated: At hollændere er super direkte - det er ret nice. At de er tjekkede. At der er cykel-kultur.
top3_advice: - Kan ikke anbefale at vælge fag med midterms - så skal man i hvert fald lige være forberedt på det. Forbered dig generelt på at skulle læse ok meget. - Meld dig til student-housing-lotteriet, og hvis du så får en plads, så vælg Prinsengracht, hvor jeg boede. Fantastisk lokation og sted! - Vær' med til introdagene/ugerne. Det var jeg ikke, og ville ønske jeg havde været. - Og kan anbefale at blive i Amsterdam alle 3 blokke, altså også i blok 3 i januar. Jeg havde nemlig planlagt at tage hjem til jul, men endte med at blive i januar også.
other_useful_info: Nej.
most_rewarding: Har fået nogle dejlige venner. Og det var bare rart at blive sat lidt ud af KU-konteksten og opleve noget nyt.
greatest_challenge: Nok nogle af de svære fag, som jeg havde valgt.

crucial_aspects: Amsterdam er en by, som har enormt meget at byde på udover det akademiske ved UvA både gastronomisk og kulturelt samt er musikscenen dernede enorm og uudtømmelig.
info_ease: Det var enormt nemt, da der blev afholdt en "introdag" for udvekslingsstuderende med diverse vigtige informationer. Samt modtog man løbende mails med informationer, som var nyttige, fra universitetet. Har man spørgsmål kan man kontakte deres kontor for udveksling, som er enormt behjælpsomme.
arrival_assistance: Modtog ingen.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Universitet oplyser dig om, hvilke kurser man kan tage og deres hjemmeside, som er målrettet til udvekslingsstuderende er enormt informationsrig ift. hvilke kurser, der er tilgængelige. Selve registreringen foregår i en portal, der hedder GLASS, og den var super brugervenlig med drag & drop menu, mv.
registration_help: Man kunne kontakte studievejledningen eller kontoret for udveksling under hele processen.
registration_success: Jeg fik de kurser, som jeg ønskede mig.
registration_advice: Undersøg de tilgængelige kurser i god tid og indhent en forhåndsgodkendelse inden, at du skal registrere dig til kurserne. Jeg skulle ændrer min forhåndsgodkendelse hos UvA, da UvA ikke tilbød kurserne, som jeg havde fået godkendt, og det var problemfrit for mig ift. de kurser, som der blev tilbudt. Meritdatabasen fra KU (https://kumerit.carve.dk/) er super god at orientere sig i, da man her kan se, hvilke kurser der tidl. er blevet givet merit for.
course_level: Det var tilsvarende KU, og underviserne gjorde meget ud af at understrege, at de ikke gjorde forskel på udvekslingsstuderende og de øvrige studerende. Min fornemmelse er, at det ikke uden videre er nemt at komme igennem eksamenerne, hvis man ikke ligger en eller anden form for indsats i løbet af semesteret. Kravene til de studerende er tsva. KU, dog er læsebyrden fra dag til dag lidt større.
teaching_comparison: Meget lig undervisningen på kandidatuddannelsen med enkelte forelæsninger på de store kurser og holdundervisning.
courses_enrolled: Comparative Law, Consumer Rights in the Single Digital Market, Advanced Private Law in Context, International Trade Law og International Investment Law.
recommended_courses: Jeg vil navnlig anbefale Comparative Law, da underviseren, Klaas Eller, er enormt engageret i undervisningen, dygtig og gerne vil have, at de studerende forstår kurset samt lykkes i faget. Eksamenen bestod delvist af en opgave skrevet i grupper samt en skriftlig stedprøve, hvor der skulle skrives essays. Derudover vil jeg slå et slag for International Investment Law, da underviseren, Stephan Schill, er enormt dygtig og vidende. Faget omhandler primært ICSID voldgiftsret og vil nok tiltalte dem, som er interesseret i proces- og voldgiftsret. Eksamenen var open book og var en klassisk "fact pattern"-eksamenen og var en hjemmeprøve. Eksamenen i Advanced Private Law var en skriftlig stedprøve og bestod af to essays, og var closed book. Eksamenen i International Trade Law var en skriftlig stedprøve og bestod af en fact pattern del og en essay del. Eksamenen var open book. Eksamenen i Consumer rights in the Single Digital Market bestod delvist af en skriftlig hjemprøve, hvor man over nogle dage skulle udarbejde et domsnotat over en EU-dom, og en skriftlig aflevering, som blev udarbejdet i grupper. Dette fag var klart det mest barmhjertige ift. arbejdsbyrde, såfremt man har lidt forudgående viden om EU-ret og om EU-domme.
unexpected_costs: Ikke umiddelbart nogle ikke-forventede omkostninger, men jeg vil bare understrege, at det er enormt worth it at få fingrene i en cykel, da det gør livet i Amsterdam 100 gange lettere.
cost_comparison: Generelt vil jeg sige, at madvarer (både dagligvare og restaurantbesøg) er lidt billigere end i Danmark. Som en tommelfingerregel kan det siges, at priserne er tilsvarende eller lavere end i Danmark.
activities_available: Der en forening, som hedder UsC, der er tilknyttet Uva, hvilken tilbyder diverse sportsaktiviteter. Det er klart herigennem, at man kan få det billigste fitnessabonnement i Amsterdam som studerende. Nogle af udvekslingsstuderende, navnlig de yngre, var enormt glade for ESN arrangementerne. Jeg selv deltog i et enkelt, hvilket var udmærket, men det var ikke noget for mig.
activities_recommended: Jeg vil generelt anbefale at udnytte de mange kulturelle og musiktilbud byen har at tilbyde. Der er enormt mange gode venues, særligt for elektronisk musik. Derudover er der mange flotte museer. Udforsk byen - den har enormt meget at byde på. Jeg vil anbefale at deltage i orienteringsmødet for udvekslingsstuderende for at møde de øvrige udvekslingsstuderende fra de andre lande. Her fandt jeg selv de mennesker, som jeg var mest sammen med i løbet af semesteret og blev gode venner med. Derudover var jeg heldig i comparative law at blive tildelt en gruppe, som jeg også kunne med socialt.
weekend_recommendations: Centraal er i sig selv enormt charmerende med sine kanaler og hyggelige gader, men jeg vil klart anbefale at tage lidt ud for centrum og udforske De Pijp (masser af vintagebutikker, barer og spisesteder), Bilderdijkstraat (enormt mange gode spisesteder) og gå en tur i Vondelpark.
culture_adjustment: Meget lig DK. Alle taler engelsk, og det er meget nemt at bo der, selvom man ikke taler hollandsk.
socializing_tips: Tal med folk til undervisning. Der er mange studerende, som ikke er hollændere, og som tager hele deres uddannelse i Amsterdam. Generelt har min oplevelse været at folk er enormt åbne og imødekommende.
cultural_challenges: Vær forberedt på at hollændere er meget direkte og ærlige (haha). Deres cykelkultur er meget lig den københavnske, men trodsalt lidt anderledes i den forstand, at det hele er lidt mere kaotisk, og folk cykler generelt lidt gnarly.
top3_advice: Husk at være opmærksom på sprogkravet - særligt som kandidatstuderende!!! Forvent ikke at du uden videre kan lade vær med at læse hele semesteret og ikke dukke op til undervisning og bestå. Ha' det sjovt og udnyt musikscenen i byen. Kontakt studieinformationen hvis du er i tvivl, de er enormt søde og behjælpelige.
other_useful_info: Husk sprogkravet og kontakt UvA administration for at høre, om du imødekomme deres undtagelse for sprogtest, hvis du har haft Engelsk A i gym, eller har taget det kursus på KU, der hedder Legal English.
most_rewarding: Enormt dejlig by, udforsk den og se så meget af den som muligt - den har så meget at byde på. Derudover var det enormt givende, at fagene bliver overført som bestået/ikke-bestået til det danske karakterudskrift, da man på den måde kunne parkere karakterræset på bagsædet og reelt forsøge at forstå og lære faget og ikke blot tænke på få den bedst mulige karakter.
greatest_challenge: Det var en omstilling at skulle skrive engelsk på et forholdsvist højt engelsk niveau, men øvelse gør mester, og det var blot et mindre "bump på vejen". Derudover kunne man til tider føle sig lidt ensom - særligt i starten, da man ikke kender så mange.
other_comments: Tag afsted og nyd det.

FBI fandt og anholdt ham hurtigt, men det var en voldsom trussel at modtage information om. - Universitetet modtog to telefoniske trusler i løbet af den samme dag. - To studerende blev forsøgt frarøvet deres værdigenstande på campus af en mand med et skydevåben. - En kvindelig studerende blev overfaldet af en mand, der fulgte efter hende i bil i nærheden af Campus Rec. Hun slap fri og stak af. - En kvindelig studerende oplevede en seksuelt krænkelse, da en fremmed mand fulgte efter hende og overfaldt hende og befølte hende i skridtet på vej hjem fra campus.

crucial_aspects: As someone studying biology, the beautiful, unique and different nature was very interesting and important for me. It was also important that I could choose meaningful courses within subjects that interest me.
info_ease: It was easy. The university was very helpful and communicated clearly.
arrival_assistance: None. However, if I had lived in a student accommodation, I would have been picked in the airport and been brought to my accommodation free of charge.
arrival_comments: I was a bit confused about what the orientation week was going to consist of, as there was only one official international orientation day arranged by the university. The main activities besides that were organized by an international student organization and was super fun and brought a lot of new connections. However, I did not know about most of the activities until shortly before they happened.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: They had a platform that you need to register through. Got an e-mail with instructions. You can drop/change courses until two weeks (I think) into the semester, which is nice because it gives you the chance of trying out the class. Was working fine, but took a while to get familiar with the platform and understand how the process works.
registration_help: E-mailing the international office. When being here physically, you can drop by their Student Hubs for help (long lines in beginning of semester though!).
registration_success: I wanted to pick a few master courses (I'm a bachelor student), and they were quite strict about that. Couldn't just sign up for them. It was a long process. I had to e-mail the course coordinator and explain my situation and convince them that I had the academic skills to take the course. In the end, it worked out with one of the master courses, so that was nice (however I actually ended up dropping that one but oh well).
registration_advice: Look at the type of assessments the courses have. It matters quite a lot for how stressful the semester feels and it's very different from course to course. Some don't have exams (yay!) and only do assessments through quizzes, reports etc. Some have more big assignments than others. So definitely something to consider!
course_level: Appropiate.
teaching_comparison: Different with all the different types of assessments throughout the semester. I wasn't used to that, so that was a bit stressful to navigate, especially in the beginning.
courses_enrolled: BIOSCI 394 BIOSCI 334 MARINE 303
recommended_courses: BIOSCI 394 is super nice. It had two cool field trips, the lecturers were really sweet aaaaand it did not have a final exam!! BIOSCI 334 is also a very interesting course for people interested in marine biology. Very interesting topics! I learned a lot and enjoyed the lectures. top3_advice: 1. Consider what type of experience you want when deciding where to live. Do you want are more authentic, local experience? Consider living in a shared flat with people that seem nice! Do you want a more "socially safe", international experience? Live on campus. 2. Consider what is important for you regarding your courses and read about the course assessments. I know exchange students that had way more free time than me and no exams because they prioritized that. I could have done that too, but that would have meant that I had to choose some courses I was not as passionate about. So it's something to think about. 3. crucial_aspects: The combination of academic opportunities along with possibilities for travel, exploration, and recreational activities. It is a unique opportunity to live a routine-based life in a whole other country, and in doing so, be liable for economic support through scholarships, your home university, and welfare support (SU). I consider any well-timed opportunity for cultural, experiential, and existential enrichment a worthwhile endeavor; thus, there was no other option but to go on an exchange, given the fact that life is small, fragile, and unfortunately short. That is my reasoning for going on an exchange. It should be noted that I will also be spending time traveling the country after the academic exchange. Another vital matter to me is that after my graduation, I should have specialized not only in Sociology as a broad academic field of theoretical expertise, but also in certain aspects of sociology, and thus, the courses mattered a lot to me. By finding a partner university that offers subjects within my field og interest, I am focusing on a career path that overlaps with my personal inclinations. These are the prospects of my motivation.

Well, I wanted to apply for psychological courses to specialize in that direction, but alas, KU Uni did not allow me to take late BA psychology courses, and Auckland did not allow me to take MA psychology courses, so I had to settle for a Pute Sociology degree. It was alright, haha. However, I find it absolutely ridiculous on KU's part that you're not allowed to take BA courses towards your master's degree, and I see the argument that the difficulty and knowledge learned in these do not meet the standards and expectations of MA academia to be absurd. MA students are grown adults who choose to specialize in ways that are personally motivating to them. By not allowing cross-studies, regardless of level, we are collectively creating SILO thinking, demeaning students' ability to make meaningful and sound choices in their careers, as well as limiting cooperation and creative thinking between institutions. Bonkers? We have sacrificed our trust in human creativity, resolve and potentials by putting our faith in standardized bureaucracy to dampen our fear of cynic behaviour that does not exist.

Maintaining colonist power inequities. It (Moari culture) is, however, very available for tourists, nice :)
top3_advice: The most enriching part of this journey had been staying after my studies to travel the country. Just fucking awesome. You have a unique opportunity to experience things you'd treasure forever! I made a distribution of 50/50. 50 percent uni, 50 percent travelling, and it worked wonders :)) 2. Get a friend with a car or buy a car. NZ is accessible, but only by car, as there is far and wide between the epic spots! Join one or several clubs; they often organize transportation to distinctly awesome places! :)) 3. GO TO FIJIIIIIII. Many essential things were communicated at an individual meeting in the office of the university the first week of arrival, but essential things, such as it being mandatory to book an appointment for this meeting and logging your arrival within a certain amount of time, were things I didn't know when I arrived and only found out gradually or by coincidence. registration_process: I went to a meeting at the office of the university the first week of being in Barcelona to log my arrival. After that university started and we had two weeks to try out different courses before choosing our final ones. The week after the try out period being over I went to another meeting at the office of the university where the courses where officially approved (if you have courses outside of your own faculty you have to get them approved by the faculty your taking them at before this meeting). After that I went to another part of the university where my matriculation was completed which gave me access to the virtual campus and provided me with a university email. It was only after the last meeting that I had access to all material and my courses at the university.

Therefore, I had to choose one course in catalan and two courses outside of my own field which were both interesting and challenging.
registration_advice: Don't be afraid of picking classes outside of your own field or faculty, and if you really think a course would be interesting, but it's in catalan, then take it anyways. If you know some spanish, you can pick up on a lot of the catalan after a little bit.
course_level: A bit lower level than in the ones I had in Copenhagen
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching took place in class rooms rather than lecture halls which I was used to from home. We didn't have classes with tutors like in Copenhagen, but instead each course had practical classes assigned to them apart from the normal lectures

unexpected_costs: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs as such

activities_available: I know that you could pay a fee that gave you access to a wide range of sports activities by the university, but I only heard about it through friends and too late to apply to it myself. Since I was there during corona there weren't any social activities arranged by the university
activities_recommended: I didn't participate in non-academic activities arranged by the university. I used the app Meet Up a couple of times and then I became part of some Whatsapp groups for the faculty where people would occasionally meet up and share information
weekend_recommendations: Go to Costa Brava, Montserrat, hike around Montseny, go to Valencia and the Pyrenees and take advantage of all the cultural offers that a vibrant city like Barcelona has to offer. academics_comments: Barcelona is a beautiful, warm and lively city for an Erasmus student. However, the academic level is not that challenging (compared to Denmark), which gives you more space to experience the city. You meet so many other students from many other countries, which gives you the opportunity to expand your international network.
course_level: The courses at UB are way more flexible
teaching_comparison: Way different- At UB you have to make student presentations, project/hand-in papers during the semester where all got evaluated continuously. For example, a project can count for 30 pct. of the final grade and a hand-in paper for 20 pct., where the in-class exam counts for 50 pct.
courses_enrolled: 1. Public Economics I: Political Economy 2. Economic Geography 3. International Trade 4. Intertemporal Decision-Making and Temporal Preferences 5. Public Policy Analysis and Evaluation 6. Welfare Economics I: Education and Social Policies - 5 ECTS each
recommended_courses: Based on all six enrolled classes, I will recommend to future exchange students to take: 1. Economic Geography 2. International Trade 3. Public Economics I: Political Economy - because they include interesting reading papers and hand-in papers to work on, and the content in each of the three classes is new and relevant that can be used in the future for e.g. bachelor projects and master theses. Actually, I am going to use the theories in "Economic Geography" for my theses.
unexpected_costs: I don't really met unexpected costs
cost_comparison: Nothing
activities_available: Running- the so-called "uni run".
activities_recommended: The Erasmus group in Barcelona makes a lot of trips both in and out of Barcelona, where they give you the opportunity to see other sides of Catalunya. Also, I can recommend to join salsa or bachata classes (It is very funny and you also meet new friends there).
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips to the cities around Barcelona (for example Costa Brava, Girona, Tarragona and Sitges)
culture_adjustment: Very easy, the citizens are very open and kind.
socializing_tips: Go on bars, get enrolled in Spanish language classes, or start on dance classes.
cultural_challenges: Everything! (in a good way)- the weather is good, the food tastes delicious, and the citizens are so festive.
culture_appreciated: The pollution...
top3_advice: 1. Be your self and don't be scared to not meet new friends (they are already there and waiting for you) 2. Make time to also experience the city by your self (Barcelona is so special when you have it by your own at a local tapasbar or at the park) 3. Be careful with your personal belongings (there are many pickpockets)
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Personal development, indescribably good memories and long-lasting friendships
greatest_challenge: The first week: when everything is so new for you.
other_comments: No :-)

crucial_aspects: The warm climate, the city, the study environment. I checked online for the courses that were available, and I found that they lined up well with what I wanted.
info_ease: There was a bit confusion initially due to covid as to whether the classes were going to be held online or in person. But we got a mail send with the information and how to enroll. The information that was available online concerning housing and so on was fine, although most were in spanish or catalan.
arrival_assistance: I went to the international office when I arrived and they provided me with the steps on how to enroll. I had to change some courses so the process took a bit longer than it should have.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: After you have signed your learning agreement etc. you go to the international office where they enroll you oficially, so you can enter the online campus site and have access to your courses there. I found it a bit confusing as to the rules on what classes you could take, but I think I was also a special case, as the course i was enrolled in had classes provided by different universities. I had to change my classes, so the final registration took some time.
registration_help: You can communicate by mail and otherwise you can go to the international office where they can help you.
registration_success: Not so succesful initially, as there were some that overlapped schedule-wise, and some that were provided by other universities. But I ended up finding some classes I really liked, though.
registration_advice: If you enroll in the CCiL course, be sure that you are allowed to take the classes (as it is interdiciplary and covered by multiple universities), and thouroughly check the schedules for classes online.
course_level: It varied a lot. As the course was interdiciplinary (philosophy, psychology, linguistics), some classes had to provide some introductionary material to the subjects we were covering. Others I found to be pretty specialized in one field, so there were more expectations on sudent knowledge. Overall, I think the classes and teachers struck a fine balance.
teaching_comparison: It was much the same, were students are expected to intervene with questions. For some classes, the first half were devoted to a presentation of the subject while the second part were more open to discussion. Other classes had more of a "teacher teaches" style. I think one difference may be that UCPH is more keen on 'activating the students', where some time in class is devoted to group work or small discussions with your side partner. That was not really a thing here.
courses_enrolled: The Nature of language, Action, perception and consciuosness, Developing language and cognition, Interdisciplary application of linguistics, Language and cognition.
recommended_courses: It really depends on what you what and how much work you want to put in. For me, as a philosophy student, I actually found the psychology classes I took to be really interesting and with much up-to-date science and experiments, although I had to familirize myself with a lot of concepts and methods that I had not really been introduced to before. (Action, perception and consciuosness, Developing language and cognition) 'Interdisciplinary application of linguistics' provided a very good introduction to some topics in biolinguistics, and the teacher was very open to discuss and present topics the students wanted covered.
unexpected_costs: As I had to stay in a hostel the first couple weeks, that made food and and accomodation a bit more expensive than I expected. I also lost my wallet the first week, so that was also problematic.
cost_comparison: Generally I think I expected things to be more expensive. Food and groceries (and eggs especially) are pretty cheap, although some specific products (some dairy, fish) can be more expensive than in Denmark. Going and eating out is also pretty cheap, so overall I would say the prices are around 75 % of what they are in Denmark.
activities_available: I didnt participate much in activities that were offered by the university, but I guess they host some debates and other social activities.
activities_recommended: Going on hikes in the nature sorrounding Barcelona. Going to some of the small seasite towns. Or just going to the beach in the afternoon.
weekend_recommendations: Visiting some of the nearby towns - like Sitges or Tarragona - is a great day experience.
culture_adjustment: It was pretty easy - it is more easygoing than Denmark. The hardest thing is the eating schedules.
socializing_tips: There are some Whatsapp groups where a lot of activities is hosted. Also just going to the library or hanging around Campus you will generally meet people.
cultural_challenges: Not any.
culture_appreciated: The people are generally very nice and easy to chat with. The weather is great and the culture is very outgoing. You can go to a cafe at all times of the day.
top3_advice: 1. Be sure that you have the relevant information regarding registering courses and availability - preferably before you leave. 2. Make sure to be part of the Whatsapp groups - a lot of great activities are posted there. 3. For housing - a site like Idealista is great, but make sure you don't get caught with some of the very expensive options offered by housing firms.
other_useful_info: Generally, communicating in english is fine, but some information is only available in spanish or catalan - so there can be a language mixup sometimes.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people and exploring some subjects I hadn't touched before.
greatest_challenge: Finding a place to stay.

housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: The international office was very helpful and replied quickly to my mails.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: I advice you to contact the international office if you run into problems.

greatest_challenge: Maybe finding the right balance between studies and social life.

crucial_aspects: Relevant Master courses at uni, and a city full of culture and life
info_ease: Pretty easy. It was possible to get help via e-mail with pretty fast responses, or you could go to the international office
arrival_assistance: There was a welcome seminar at the university, with presentations from the Erasmus coordinators and the students responsible for events etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: At the presentation seminar you received a paper with your pre-approved courses, and then you had some weeks to attend (check out) the courses and make sure that the time table was good, and then you could go to the international office and be registrated to the courses
registration_help: You could make appointments at the IO or write an email. The teachers were also happy to help and suggest other courses or send you the material until the registration went through
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted
registration_advice: Don't stress if you have to change some courses, they are used to it
course_level: A little different levels in the different courses. A lot of them were only 3 ETCS, and therefore quite short - It seemed to me that the expectations did not always match the number of credits.
teaching_comparison: Not too different. In Barcelona they also liked to involve the students with questions and discussion
courses_enrolled: Bases Teóricas y Metodológicas de la Enseñanza de ELE a Inmigrantes, Refugiados y Niños y Adolescentes Recursos Lingüísticos Digitales para la Enseñanza del Español como LE/L2 Anàlisi i Disseny d'Unitats Didàctiques Metodología de la Investigación en Español como LE/L2 Los Discursos Profesionales en el Ámbito del Español como LE/L2 Sociolingüística de l'Espanyol Lingüística Romànica
recommended_courses: Bases Teóricas y Metodológicas de la Enseñanza de ELE a Inmigrantes, Refugiados y Niños y Adolescentes - because it gave some good examples on how to teach different groups. Kind teacher
unexpected_costs: My phone got stolen, had to buy a new
cost_comparison: Coffee, beer, wine etc. was much cheaper than in Denmark
activities_available: Erasmus Barcelona offers a lot of activities, there are things to do every day if you want to. Beer pong tournaments and free entry to clubs are a hit, but also museum trips, beach volley and trips to nearby attractions and other cities are available
activities_recommended: The welcome dinner in the first week, and generally many of the activities in the two welcome weeks, to meet people. Volley is also a great way to talk to new people
weekend_recommendations: Montserrat is beautiful for a hike. The city Sitges near Barcelona is great for a beach day - charming and less busy
culture_adjustment: The people are very kind, which makes it easy
socializing_tips: Not really, just be open and not afraid to ask for help, that is an easy way to start a conversation - fx if they can show you the library
cultural_challenges: The structure of the lessons meant there there were no breaks during class, and rarely people stuck around to wait for another class. This made it difficult to make contact, since everybody went out after class
culture_appreciated: The tempo. They talk fast, but they are not in a rush otherwise. In the cafes, the supermarket etc. everything is more slow and relaxed.
top3_advice: It is likely that not all your courses are very relevant (if they are 3 ECTS you'll need a lot of different courses), and it is okay to lose motivation sometimes. If you should fail something, it is not the end of the world. Remember that you are on exchange for more that academic purposes - get out and experience something - it doesn't have to be something big, it can just be a walk in the neighborhood or finding a new icecream place to try. It is normal to miss home even though you are having the time of your life
other_useful_info: Not that I can think of
most_rewarding: Improved language skills and many cultural experiences - food in particular
greatest_challenge: Some courses requiered some former knowledge that I didn't have, since I only took the second semester on the Master - this made it a bit difficult to follow sometimes
other_comments: Don't be afraid to ask the teachers for help

crucial_aspects: That they spoke spanish down here, because I really wanted to improve my spanish. The weather was also a factor, and that you have the beach very close. I love also doing a lot of sports, playing football, padel tennis, tennis and so forth and I knew that these sports are being played a lot in Spain and thereby of course Barcelona as well.
info_ease: It was fairly medium I would say. When you first found the course catalogue it was okay, and then also I would add that the incoming coordinator was very good at answering your questions both over phone and email, she speaks englise quite well also.
arrival_assistance: When I arrived it was very easy. You just go the university's international office and they sort you out with everything and also a week later, there is a big day for all the exchange students where you get to meet each other and ask questions there as well and so forth.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was very easy. There was an online portal where you just chose your desired destinations and found some courses that the university offered and yeah, quite easy.
registration_help: Not much really. There was a seminar regarding this, but you didn't really need that much help I would say.
registration_success: 100% successful, so that was nice.
registration_advice: I would say that you find the schedules and the exam dates ahead of time, so maybe in an ideal world I would have organized my subjects so that I could travel home a week before.
course_level: The level of the courses is relatively lower compared to the University of Copenhagen. It is easier to pass the courses also because there is continuous evalutation and the required level of math is very low. What challenged was that for two courses I had to make research proposals based on exisisting scholarly articles, which is something I hadn't done before.
teaching_comparison: It's very different. The classes are way smaller and there is large focus on scholarly articles and writing reports about this. Also we had to make a lot of presentations which is something I never did at my home university, and as i said, the research proposals.
courses_enrolled: Economic Growth, Game Theory, Macroeconometrics, Microeconometrics, Empirical Approach to Economic Growth, Welfare Economics
recommended_courses: I quite liked game theory, also because it was the only course with proper math and it challenged. Also the welfare economics is very different from back home and gave different perspectives to what I am used to.
unexpected_costs: I though I could use the EU data through my danish supplier, but i couldn't after three months. A speeding ticket from a rental car :))
cost_comparison: The public is really good and very cheap, it's 20 euros a month for all the public transport, it even takes you to the airport and to the small beaches outside the city.
activities_available: There is both padel tennis and tennis offered through UB sports, it was 40 euros for 12 group classes and it was really fun social and cheap.
activities_recommended: I would recommend the app 'Celebreak' if you're into football. You can play all over Barcelona with other people and it's a really nice way to meet new folks and just play. Also hiking trips in northern catalunya, such as Mont Rebei and a trip to Costa Brava to cliff jump and chill out.
weekend_recommendations: Just chill up in Gracia and if you go to the beach, for god's sake dont go to Barceloneta but go to Platja de Bogatell.
culture_adjustment: It was fairly easy for me. I love the laid-back culture of no stress, eating late and stuff like this so.
socializing_tips: Yea, as I said, the 'Celebreak' app and the tennis classes. Otherwise just keep an open mind, there are a lot internationals down here, and everyone wants to make friends, so just don't be scared of starting a conversation.
cultural_challenges: Nothing really.
culture_appreciated: The "manana-manana" vibe, and the vibe that you meet late and there is no pressure on getting absolutely hammered when you go out as in Denmark, you can just chill have a few beers and then also be ready for the next day and I enjoyed that.
top3_advice: The academic level is lower. The class 'Economic Growth' can be taken as a seminar. Can't think of a third.
other_useful_info: Not really.
most_rewarding: The new people, the time for sports and exercise, the hiking trips, the laid-backness, the opportunity to not stress around with job and school and have so much more free-time, so that you can say yes to anything.
greatest_challenge: Probably missing my girl.

course_level: The level of courses was a bit disappointing as some of the courses touched upon topics that was reviewed in courses on the bachelor.
teaching_comparison: This was rather different. We got to do referee reports, research proposals and a lot of oral presentations. This differs from the form of teaching in Denmark which was interesting to try.
courses_enrolled: I took the following courses during my exchange: - Microeconometrics (2,5 ECTS) - Macroeconometrics (2,5 ECTS) - International Trade (5 ECTS) - Economic Geography (5 ECTS) - Empirical Approach to Economic Growth (5 ECTS) - Economic Growth I (5 ECTS) - Welfare Economics: Education and social policies (5 ECTS)
recommended_courses: Economic growth was really interesting. I found international trade and welfare economics interesting as well. The other courses was also interesting but some of the parts was already covered in other courses that I have completed on my bachelors degree in Denmark.
unexpected_costs: Unexpected costs such as transportations costs (to/from the airport), culture attractions. Also the apartment ended up being really expensive to live in.
cost_comparison: In general, the cost of food and groceries were cheaper in Barcelona relative to Denmark. On the other hand, it was expensive to explore the culture and visit attractions.
activities_available: A lot of sports at UB sports. I applied for tennis lessons twice a week. This was very good and not too expensive.
activities_recommended: Apply for some sports that you find interesting. I met some good friends from sports.
weekend_recommendations: Do some weekend trips. From Barcelona, we went to costa brava (sunny-vacation), cal barbut (hiking trip), mont rebei (hiking trip) and Girona (old city).
culture_adjustment: It was rather easy. The society in Barcelona is quite international so the locals speak both spanish/catalan and often also English.
socializing_tips: Participate in debates in class, in the breaks etc.
cultural_challenges: The students at UB were from all over the world. The challenging part was the communication. The majority speaks English, but the accents are really different. This resulted in lack of understanding of some of the teachers and also other students and hence participation in debates some times.
culture_appreciated: The diversity of people from all over the world. I found it so interesting to speak with people from middel america, Polen, russia, france and Finland at the same time and discuss society structures, politics and economics.
top3_advice: Enjoy every single day and be the best version of yourself.
other_useful_info: Be in good time with applying for financial support, findings apartments etc.
most_rewarding: It is difficult to pick. I enjoyed every moment from trips to everyday life and everything in between.
greatest_challenge: To get to know everything at a time both new people/social circle, courses and the whole city you live in.
other_comments: No.

crucial_aspects: Since Universitat de Barcelona is a top university in Spain (and nr. 1 in Catalunya), I had big expectations for its academic opportunities. This was well met, as I found the classes, professors and co-students to be of high quality. Therefore, I learned how social economics works in a southern European country, which has been through huge financial crisis'. Otherwise, I chose Barcelona because of its cultural differences from Denmark. I wanted to learn the Catalan culture is significant for the people living in Barcelona, making my stay very local.
overall_comments: The study abroad lived well up to my expectations, as I learned a lot about the culture, economy and myself.
info_ease: Upon arrival, it was very difficult getting he right information. It took a long time for the UB to confirm the starting dates of my classes, since I am on the masters degree. For bachelor students it is easier. The communication could have been separated between bachelors and masters students.
arrival_assistance: The Erasmus office was easy to contact, and was good at answering relevant questions.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: The study abroad lived well up to my expectations, as I learned a lot about the culture, economy and myself.
registration_process: We met at the Erasmus Office and got everything fixed in short time, i.e. registration for courses etc.
registration_help: Phone, E-mail and personal help in person.
registration_advice: Signing up for courses in the Master's degree is no problem. The classes are very small and never filled up, why registrering for courses was not a problem.
academics_comments: The study abroad lived well up to my expectations, as I learned a lot about the culture, economy and myself.
course_level: The level of courses differs a lot. Some are quite hard, i.e. the macroeconomic courses, however the econometric courses are of low level compared to Denmark.
teaching_comparison: There are a lot of presentations at UB, which is really great, since at UCPH there are none. Otherwise the teaching style is more one-sided at UB, and lacks some student interaction/exercise classes.
courses_enrolled: Economic geography, Empirical approach to economic growth, Macroeconometrics, Microeconometrics, Welfare economics, Economic growth I, International trade.
recommended_courses: Economic growth I was a tough but rich in learning. I can recommend that.

activities_recommended: None, I didn't attend to any.

culture_adjustment: Very easy. You have to get used to the different "eating periods", where every meal is moved two hours ahead.
socializing_tips: Use Celebreak app to play football with randoms and meat friends. Go to local bars and reggeaton dancing clubs to meet young locals who also like to go out. Be openminded.
cultural_challenges: The local's can be tough against turists, and they might think you are a turist until you prove them wrong. Why, sometimes it is hard to get local friends/student friends.
culture_appreciated: The relaxed vibe.
top3_advice: Be social in the beginning, as you will create a strong bond to those friends you meet from the beginning. Don't be affraid to talk with the professors/offices when you are in doubt about anything, they are very helpful. Come to classes, as it is one of the places where you can meet new friends.
other_useful_info: If you are in doubt, call the Erasmus office at the host university in stead of corresponding over E-mail, which can be quite difficult.
most_rewarding: How easy it is to get friends, whether they are danish, swedish, catalan or anything. Culture meets in Barcelona.
greatest_challenge: Getting local friends.

crucial_aspects: As a Master's student in Economics, I chose the University of Barcelona as my study destination because of its strong reputation in the field of economics, as well as the availability of programs that aligned with my interests. Additionally, I was attracted to the location of the university in the vibrant city of Barcelona, which offered unique cultural and professional opportunities.
overall_comments: Although I really enjoyed my exchange experience in Barcelona, the workload was more challenging than expected due to the need to complete six courses in only three months to achieve the necessary credits. While the pace was demanding, I appreciated the opportunity to immerse myself in my studies and found the experience to be valuable overall.
info_ease: One challenge I encountered during my exchange experience in Barcelona was the difficulty in finding information due to the fact that some of the information resources were only available in Catalan without a translation. This made it more challenging to navigate some administrative processes, but I found that seeking out assistance from university staff and local resources was helpful in overcoming this obstacle.
arrival_assistance: We attended a intro presentation on the university. It was mainly directed towards students on the bachelor. It could have been nice with a more thorough intro to the masters program.
arrival_comments: They honestly seemed a bit confused and the response time was quite slow. It was also very challenging to obtain information on grading and the exams.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_process: We had to print a lot of document beforehand. This includes insurance document, passport documents and so on. When we were there we also had to select the courses we wanted to take.
registration_help: We were able to ask the staff questions, but they did not really know much about the master that we took
registration_success: Successful I guess
registration_advice: If you are able to, write the university beforehand and see if you can get more information on the specific classes than what you can find online.
academics_comments: Although I really enjoyed my exchange experience in Barcelona, the workload was more challenging than expected due to the need to complete six courses in only three months to achieve the necessary credits. While the pace was demanding, I appreciated the opportunity to immerse myself in my studies and found the experience to be valuable overall.
course_level: I would say that the level of the courses was for some of the courses a bit below but with larger workload and for other of the courses the same level as my home institution or a bit above. It differs a lot for both institutions, so it is difficult to compare.
teaching_comparison: The classes at the University of Barcelona differs in a way that I really appreciated by having more intimate class sizes, which allowed for more discussion and participation among students. With fewer students in each class, there was more opportunity for engagement and interaction, which made the learning experience more engaging and dynamic. Also the teachers were more welcoming to discussions after class and had open office hours were we often went by to get guidance and help with assignments.
courses_enrolled: Governments and markets cooperative decision making and social choice Economic growth II Urban and regional economics Econometric methods of urban and regional econommics Political economy
recommended_courses: cooperative decision making and social choice - which is a course in game theory. If one enjoys micro economics this class is really interesting and the teacher is extremely good at teaching it.
unexpected_costs: none
cost_comparison: I do not think any items were more or less expensive. But it is smart to by a three months metro ticket to begin with or else metro expenses can be high - however, this is nothing compared to Copenhagen.
activities_available: I don't know, because I did not do any of them. I think there were some sports activities but with the amount of school hours we had, this would not have been possible to participate in.
activities_recommended: Did not do any so I cannot recommend anything.
weekend_recommendations: Go on erasmus trips. They have some to different cities and also some sunday trips were you go on hikes or go sailing.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy for me to adjust to the local culture during my exchange experience in Barcelona. I found the city and its people to be welcoming and friendly, and I appreciated the opportunity to immerse myself in a new culture and way of life.
socializing_tips: Erasmus events are an excellent way to get to know other students on exchange and meet new people while studying abroad. They provide opportunities to socialize and engage with others from diverse backgrounds. It is a bit more difficult to get to know local students but one way is by doing projects with people from your classes and invite them about for drinks and beers after.
cultural_challenges: No not really - as a said before, I find the people in Barcelona really welcoming. However, if you are a person which likes to arrive on time, you might find it difficult to adjust to "spanish time".
culture_appreciated: I particularly appreciated the local culture and cuisine. I loved exploring the city's vibrant food scene, trying new dishes like paella and tapas, and experiencing the social aspect of eating together with friends. Additionally, I enjoyed learning about the city's rich cultural history through visiting museums, attending cultural events, and exploring architectural landmarks such as the Gothic Quarter. I also do like the chill mentally of the people of Barcelona
top3_advice: 1. Embrace the local culture - Barcelona has a unique and vibrant culture that is different from what you may be used to in Denmark. Try to immerse yourself in the local culture by learning the language, trying new foods, and attending cultural events. You will have a much richer experience if you embrace the city's unique identity. 2. Make an effort to meet people- Studying abroad is an incredible opportunity to meet people from all over the world. Don't be afraid to introduce yourself to other exchange students and locals, and take advantage of opportunities to participate in social events and activities organized by Erasmus. 3. Stay organized and plan ahead - It's important to stay organized, keep track of deadlines when you have a lot of courses BUT remember to enjoy the city at the same time.
other_useful_info: Yes, I would probably recommend not taking as many courses as I did or spread it out over a longer period
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was living in the vibrant city of Barcelona. I enjoyed immersing myself in the local culture, exploring the city's many sights and attractions, and meeting people from all over the world. The experience challenged me to step outside of my comfort zone and broaden my perspective, and I came away with a newfound appreciation for the diversity and richness of the world around us
greatest_challenge: living with friends. We lived in a quite small apartment and in periods during exams and so on, it could be a bit difficult not to have your own space however it was also a great experience to live with friends and I would do it again.
other_comments: no

crucial_aspects: I picked Barcelona specifically because of the city and the culture. I love Spain and wanted somewhere with nice weather, potential for a good social life and a place to practice my spanish.
overall_comments: The school was very different from back home and not the best in my opinion, but the city, the vibe, the social life, the people, the food, the weather and the nightlife was all fantastic!
info_ease: I think going on exchange in general takes a bit of effort and requires a lot of time with figuring stuff out. On top of that, Universitat de Barcelona is very old school with a lot of stuff still not being digitalized. The Spanish culture is always a bit late and laid back, so you had to do a lot on your own to get the necessary information.
arrival_assistance: We had a check in at school and it worked ok. Of course there is always a bit of chaos moving to a new place and a new university, but everything worked out and there were people who could help you if you needed it.
arrival_comments: A bit late at giving information and not always too organized, but everything worked out fine.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: The school was very different from back home and not the best in my opinion, but the city, the vibe, the social life, the people, the food, the weather and the nightlife was all fantastic!
registration_process: You get a HUGE course catalog with available courses and then you have to pick courses that are relevant for you and get them approved by KU (Home university). Then some time in July/August, Universitat de Barcelona open for a link, where you have to be ready to get the courses you want. You have to spend a lot of time to be ready for this because you need to make sure that neither the classes or the exams overlaps with some of the other courses you choose.
registration_help: I had to take quite a lot of time to apply for the courses but there were both some people at my home university and UB that could help me. The only problem was that a lot of these people were on holiday for a lot of the summer, so it could take some time to get an answer.
registration_success: I didn't get the classes I initially wanted because some of the lectures overlapped but I got the classes that I wanted which didn't overlap.
registration_advice: Do stuff in good time because it can be a bit difficult to get help in the middle of the summer when people are on holiday. Don't be too stressed about if everything doesn't go to plane or what not - everything will work out.
academics_comments: The school was very different from back home and not the best in my opinion, but the city, the vibe, the social life, the people, the food, the weather and the nightlife was all fantastic!
course_level: Differed a lot. In general I would say it was a bit lower level than back home.
teaching_comparison: Very different from back home. It was a lot more like high school (gymnasium) where you had to, or were strongly incentivized to participate in class, do weekly/monthly assignments and participate in smaller exams or group projects throughout the semester. Besides from that, the school is very old school - exams are still written exams with pen and paper. The thing I found the most frustrating was the huge difference in level and structure from course to course. Some of the courses were super duper easy (pretty much everyone could get a top grade without even trying) and some other courses were very tough with a huge syllabus and required a lot of studying. The structure was pretty much up to the individual teacher in how they wanted to structure the lectures/classes and how they wanted to examine the students. I found this a bit frustrating, especially in the exam period, because you had to adapt to a lot of different exam structures and every exam had different requirements to pass.
courses_enrolled: -Game Theory for Business (merit for Micro III) - it was super easy. -Corporate Finance - very big syllabus but very interesting. -International Economics -Strategic Management - very easy but I did not like it. -World Economic History
recommended_courses: I would recommend International Economics it was really interesting and we had a very good professor. I would also recommend corporate finance even though it required a lot of studying.
unexpected_costs: If you really want to enjoy your life, the city and the surrounding cities/nature you will probably end up spending a lot of money, so have that in mind.
cost_comparison: - Museums, parks, trips etc. were more expensive than I expected. - Housing was a bit more expensive than I expected - pretty much the same as in Denmark - Food was a little bit more expensive than I expected compared to other parts of Spain that I have travelled a lot. You can feel that Barcelona is a big city and the prices are therefore also a big higher. - Drinks is super cheap. At a restaurant/bar you can normally get a beer/soda at around 2-3 euros.
activities_available: They had a lot of different culture/language activities as well as a lot of sports activities. I signed up for a spanish class which I got at a very favorable price (180 euros for 4 x 1,5 hour classes a week for 10 weeks = 60 hours. This was a lot cheaper than private classes and I got to do it with other exchange students at the same Spanish level as me). Furthermore, I signed up for padel tennis classes which were held at the school sports campus together with other students. It cost 90 euros for 16 hours of padel classes (which is extremely cheap for padel). The school had a sports campus only 10 minutes walk from my campus where you could get an annual membership for around 100 euros and then freely use the gym, swimming pool, football pitches, padel courts, tennis courts etc.
activities_recommended: I recommend the spanish classes and the sports activities.
weekend_recommendations: Explore Barcelona and the surrounding nature. Go to museums, parks etc. Go to the beach when the weather is good. Explore and find the nicest bars and restaurants (there are a lot). Go to the bars and clubs at night. You will have an amazing time in Barca! I also recommend doing either one-day trips to the cities nearby - I went to Sitges, Lloret del Mar and Montserrat and can recommend it. Finally, I strongly recommend to go visit other parts and cities of Spain. Specifically I will recommend Valencia, Sevilla and San Sebastian - they are some of the most cozy places I have been to. There is quite a lot of cheap and relatively fast options with public transport in Spain.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. I love the culture and the vibe of the city - felt home from the start.
socializing_tips: I very highly recommend living with other students/young people. I lived in an apartment with 12 other young people from all over the world and it was the best decision! Because I found a lot of friends at my apartment and I got to know a few people from my classes as well, I didn't feel the big need to go to a lot of Erasmus events, but these events and trips that is organized every week is a very good way to meet friends and get to know a lot of other exchange students.
cultural_challenges: In Spain it can be difficult with the language because they are not always very good at English, but I didn't see it as a huge problem. I only speak a very basic level of Spanish and therefore of course you miss out on some interaction with the local population, but I actually found that a lot of the local students wanted to practice their English and interact with foreign students.
culture_appreciated: Pretty much everything. I love their laid back attitude and the way they just chill on the street, in bars and restaurants all night. I love the language and the food as well. Don't settle for mediocre turistic tapas that you will find in other parts of Spain. Barcelona has some incredible and yet affordable restaurants and tapas bars.
top3_advice: - Live with other students/young people - it is the easiest way to get to know people and make friends. If not, then make an effort to go to Erasmus events or approach people in class. All the exchange students are in similar situations and everybody is very open and nice and wants to make friends. Nobody goes on exchange and then don't want to meet new people. - Be open minded about school - it is going to be very different from back home, and the application process might be a bit slow and tough, but everything will work out. - Go explore the city and the surrounding area in the weekends and on your day off - there is loads to see and enjoy!
other_useful_info: - Use idealista to find accommodation. - I would recommend learning just some basic Spanish before coming here - it just makes everything much more interesting and easy, and the locals really appreciate when you just try to speak Spanish.
most_rewarding: The experiences and the friends that I got. I would not change my experience for anything. I can highly recommend going!
greatest_challenge: - Trying to be as open-minded as possible with meeting new people from all over the world and learning about their cultures.
other_comments: Enjoy!

crucial_aspects: Mainly a destination with different culture and a different academic structure to try something new and different from what i was used to.
info_ease: Generally quite easy to know where go or where to write them.
arrival_assistance: Received most of the assistance when i had to get enrolled to all the courses.
arrival_comments: It did take them a long time getting me enrolled which entailed that I missed some of the first lectures in some courses. Furthermore, I wasn't able to get one of the courses i wanted as it had changed to only be offered another semester, which I was not able to see anywhere beforehand.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: At first it was quite difficult as the course list I was able to find through UCPH was only for bachelor students which I only find out after the host university rejected my pre-approval.
registration_help: The general guide to the registration was plenty elaborate and when calling the they were very helpful. They only problem was that it was quite difficult to connect the information from UCPH with the host university.
registration_success: My registration for classes where quite difficult as I needed very specific courses at two different master, however, I ended up with most of the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: My best advice would be to start early and write both the host university and the receiving university as you will ensure that you do everything correctly and can save a lot of time from possible misunderstandings.
course_level: It did have courses on two different masters but the level varies greatly between all courses and the workload was also disproportionate for some of the courses compared to ECTS points.
teaching_comparison: Very different as most classes were only around 10 people and we did not really have any lectures but rather just classes. Also there was much greater focus on assignments and attendance which accounted for most of your grades compared to UCPH where the all of the grade is decided at the final exam.
courses_enrolled: Multinational Accounting, Multinational Financial Management, Economic Growth II, Governments and Markets, Cooperative decision making and social choice, Political Economy, Cooperation and strategy in finance and insurance
recommended_courses: Cooperative decision making and social choice, Political Economy, and Economic Growth II. Those were the courses where I actually felt that I learned something valuable and where the work load was more appropriate although it seems a little difficult in the beginning.
unexpected_costs: Did have to buy covers and a pillow and so on the first month as it wasn't a part of the room I'f rented.
cost_comparison: Generally eating out is way cheaper and most of the time i bought food instead of making it myself.
activities_available: I mainly saw athletic activities promoted by the host university but through Erasmus there was a lot of cultural and social activities as well.
activities_recommended: Definitely playing a lot of padel and otherwise attend as many of the Erasmus trips and events.
weekend_recommendations: Erasmus does some trips in the weekend that I'd really recommend.
culture_adjustment: Took a little while to get adjusted but after a few days walking around in the city you'll be more confident.
cultural_challenges: More homeless people and low-level crime such as pick-pockets which is not that normal in Copenhagen.
culture_appreciated: More relaxed and later dinner times made it feel like i got more out of the day.
top3_advice: Participate more in classes as it counts for a lot of your grade. Focus more on your assignments and don't worry too much about the exams as they are not as difficult as they are at UCPH.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Getting to experience a new culture and a new academic structure.
greatest_challenge: I was unfortunately very sick at most of my stay and the health care system in Spain is not as effecient.

crucial_aspects: I was told that the University Of Barcelona was a good University, and it was also a good opportunity to explore the spanish culture along with the Catalan culture in an aspect of cultural differences.
info_ease: It was very easy to find information. In the beginning it was a little hard to understand how it all worked at the University, because it's different from Copenhagen both in the way of teaching which I find to be a little more practical in Barcelona and also the differences in exams.
arrival_assistance: We had an introduction one of the first days where information was provided, and we also had a person we could tall to when we needed information on a specific subject. This came in very handy from time to time.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process was easy. In the introduction days we had the opportunity to change the courses if we didn't like the ones we had chosen. This was possible within the first 3 weeks. Registration office helped us find the right courses and schedule to make it all fit together. From there you had your personal ID number and access to the virtual campus where most of the material and stuff could be found from the classes. Also we were given a student card.
registration_help: We had a person who worked with all of the erramos students who was available both by e-mail and during office hours.
registration_success: I got all the clases I wanted.
registration_advice: Be present in the intro days because this is where a lot of information is given.
course_level: The level of the courses was very mixed in my experience. All of the clases had 6 ECTS each. But some clases were very heavy compared to others. Both in the material that you had to read and also the final exam. Overall the level was very aline with the level from the home university, but since everything is in a foreign language this can be a little overwhelming, especially in the beginning of the courses.
teaching_comparison: I find the teaching to be a little more practical at UB because there are different ways to pass. Doing all the practical stuff during the semester gives you points that gives you the opportunity to pass the exam without having to attend one single exam at the end of the semester. I also find that the teaching in some ways at least in my classes was with a hint of philosophy. Overall the teaching was very effective and gave me the tools I needed for the exams.
courses_enrolled: Spanish sociolinguistics. Introduction to linguistics. Culture and Communication. Semiotics of Communication. Text production in Spanish.
recommended_courses: All of them were interesting in their own way but I find Culture and Communication to be the most interesting because of all the different aspects the course had to it which was culture, communication, globalization, journalism. Also Semiotics of Communication was exiting because it was a new way of leaning about communication especially within the media field.
unexpected_costs: In my flat because of the inflation gas, electricity, water was a little unexpected. Because these bills were high which was around 750 DKK extra each month.
cost_comparison: Grocery shopping was not a little more expensive then I expected, but this was because of the inflation. Transportation was also a little expensive. Housing is more or less the same, but going for a coffee was cheap. Around 10 DKK for a cup of coffee in a café.
activities_available: There was a lot of cultural activities outside of school, both in meeting and the eramus students who arranged a lot of activities around the city. This was clubbing, sightseeing and other activities to explore both the culture and meet new people. The whole experience was very vibrant.
activities_recommended: The Erasmus activities gives you a lot of social connections which is very nice outside of school. Usually there is made a group in WhatsApp in the intro days where activities are published.
weekend_recommendations: Explore the city. The city is so big and has a lot to offer. In the summer the weather gives you the opportunity to live the beach life and travel to other parts of Catalonia or Spain.
culture_adjustment: It was easy the Catalan/spanish people are very friendly and even though your Spanish is not perfect they really try to help you express yourself. This way it was very easy to talk to people because you feel very welcomed by the locals.
socializing_tips: In my classes the majority were locals. Start a conversation and be a part of the group work in class this opens the door and shows that you are interested in meeting them.
cultural_challenges: One thing that was a little hard was that the local students in my classes sometimes spoke in Catalan. Also sometimes with the teacher even though I chose the classes in Spanish. So sometimes I missed some questions because of this, you are allowed to ask if they can translate into spanish but since a lot of students do it, it feels weird to ask all the time. But mostly the questions were answered by the teacher in Spanish.
culture_appreciated: I liked the diversity in the culture and the food. It was a magical experience to explore spanish and Catalan culture in a mix. Because Barcelona is a big city you have everything. If you go outside of the city you will find towns where the Catalan culture and language are very dominant. This was exiting to see.
top3_advice: 1: Make sure your housing is comfortable for you 2: Attend the intro days and classes. 3: Socialize with the locals and the other Erasmus students.
other_useful_info: Make sure that you really understand how the exams work from the beginning. Because in Barcelona and Spain in general the exams are very different from Denmark, the point system and grades are different as well. Take your time to understand what is important for you to pass the exams, because the point system starts within the first couple of week if you attend the practical work in class and it will have an influence on your final grade.
most_rewarding: The whole experience of going abroad. The culture, the people and especially the language. When you are in a country where the language you are studying is spoken it gives you the opportunity to really utilize it and make it better. So for me the most rewarding thing was the evolvement of my spoken language.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was to understand how the whole system of the university and how it worked. This is why it's super important to attend the intro days and ask questions if you have any. Don't be shy to ask because you will benefit from it in the end. It's not fun to reach the end of the semester and find out that there are things you are unsure of.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to improve my Spanish, so selecting a Spanish-speaking country was essential.

arrival_assistance: The Erasmus coordinator was very helpful in guiding us when we had difficulties. They also organized a welcome event for the Erasmus students where they explained all the necessary information.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: We had an Erasmus coordinator, Oscar, who was very helpful. I changed courses several times before getting completely settled, and he was very helpful throughout these processes.
registration_help: As explained above.

recommended_courses: I would recommend "Sociolingüística del español." This course is very exciting if you are interested in the Spanish-speaking world and the differences between various dialects. The teacher is very engaged and inclusive. She paid a lot of attention to the exchange students and wanted to hear our thoughts and opinions. Additionally, the course "El Procés de Producció Audiovisual" was very different and exciting! Not many exchange students choose this subject, and you get paired in groups for a short film project. This provided a great opportunity to make Catalan friends and speak Spanish more.
unexpected_costs: My personal spending was a lot higher than in Denmark because of all the different things I wanted to experience. This included various activities, tips, and visiting different Spanish cities etc.
cost_comparison: Eating in restaurants and buying groceries were significant expenses. The drinks were very cheap, but the food at restaurants was more or less at Danish prices, only a bit cheaper.
activities_available: Everything! You can do whatever sport or activity you like. The app "Meetup" is very good for all sorts of events and activities, including free ones.
activities_recommended: Dancing! There is a huge dancing environment in Barcelona, especially for salsa and bachata.

culture_adjustment: Not as much as I expected. Barcelona is an international city, with 20-30% of the population in the city center being foreigners. However, choosing subjects at the university that were not common for exchange students and getting paired in groups helped me a lot!
cultural_challenges: It's a bit hard to get into the local environment as an exchange student if you don't speak the language perfectly, especially since many prefer speaking in Catalan.
culture_appreciated: My experience was that they are very spontaneous. They eat dinner very late, so the city is always full of life and people until very late at night.
top3_advice: Make sure to get Spanish-speaking roommates. I lived with two people from Denmark, which hindered my improvement in speaking Spanish a lot! Prioritize an apartment close to or in the city center; it is definitely worth the extra money. Investigate different courses and ask the teachers or Erasmus coordinator for help.
other_useful_info: Not that I can think of right now..
most_rewarding: Living in a different city and experiencing its culture is a completely different experience compared to being a tourist.

info_ease: It was still quite messy unfortunately and not always so transparent as to where to find the necessary information.
arrival_assistance: We had a very brief introduction meeting, but it didn´t include any new information if you had read the welcome email, so I was a bit disappointed by that. It must be said though, that the local coordinators were very welcoming and tried their best to answer questions if you came to them.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: The coordinators from the international office for incoming students.
