housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Jeg ville gerne udelukkende have kurser på norsk og på deres mere praktiske del af psykologiuddannelsen (i Bergen er psykologiuddannelsen delt op i to spor, hvor den ene del er overvejende teoretisk og forskningsrettet og den anden del er praktisk og med en masse færdighedsøvelser og forskning relateret til den faktiske terapi). Jeg tog kun kurser på den praktiske del og fik god hjælp til dette af Toril Salen.
registration_help: Studievejledningen og Toril Salen var meget behjælpelige.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de kurser, som jeg gerne ville have.
registration_advice: Læs de forskellige beskrivelser af kurserne igennem og overvej, om du gerne vil have en mere teoretisk eller praktisk-orienteret undervisning. Og spørg studievejledningen om hjælp, hvis du får behov.
course_level: Niveauet føltes passende i forhold til KU.
teaching_comparison: På mine kurser var der skiftende undervisere, som selv både forskede og var praktiserende psykologer ved siden af og mange var meget passionerede omkring deres felt. Og deres tilgang til lærerollen og dynamikken med eleverne er meget det samme som i Danmark - afslappet og i øjenhøjde.
courses_enrolled: Psykologisk kartlegging Psykologisk behandling 1 Psykologisk behandling 3 Vitskapsteoretiske perspektiv og etikk i klinisk praksis
recommended_courses: Jeg vil anbefale alle fire kurser. Psykologisk kartlegging centrerede sig om, hvordan man i begyndelsen af et terapeutisk forløb kortlægger, hvilke områder der bør tages højde for i forløbet med den specifikke klient, hvilke metoder der er mest passende og lign. Psykologisk behandling 1 og 3 havde undervisning i et væld af forskellige psykologiske emner, såsom parterapi, behandling af depression, udførelse af gruppeterapi, behandling af personlighedsforstyrrelser, traumatiserede flygtinge og en masse andet. Og der var helt konkrete bud til, hvordan man bedst muligt behandler de forskellige problemstillinger. Derudover var der også undervisning i mere grundlæggende psykologfærdigheder, såsom hvordan man skaber og opretholder en god terapeutisk alliance. I vitskapsteroretiske perspektiv og etikk var der en masse overvejelser om forskellige etiske og moralske dilemmaer, som alle som psykologer kan støde ind i - og derefter undervisning i, hvordan man kunne sikre sig, at man som psykolog agerer så etisk korrekt som muligt.
unexpected_costs: Mad var en del dyrere end i Danmark, og jeg brugte generelt flere penge på mad og råvarer end normalt.
cost_comparison: Øl er dyrere end i DK og råvarer (særligt grønsager) er dyrere. Men man kan spise en masse lækker fisk, for det er markant billigere end i DK.
activities_available: Jeg tror, at der var en masse fine tilbud, som jeg dog ikke gjorde så meget brug af. Der var bl.a. en masse guidede naturture, klatreture og lign.
activities_recommended: Jeg vil anbefale, at man særligt i starten er socialt åben og opsøgende, så man får nogle venner at lave hyggelige ting med.
weekend_recommendations: Jeg vil anbefale, at man tager en masse på tur i de syv fjelde rundt omkring Bergen. Man kan enten gå dertil eller tage bus. Løvstakken, Fløyen, Ulriken, Stoltzekleiven osv er alle meget fine. Og stisystemerne er gode og meget brugte af nordmænd, så man føler sig ikke utryg, selv hvis man vandrer alene. Og ellers er der også et fint kulturelt og socialt liv i Bergen. Der er mange oplæsninger og arrangementer på Litteraturhuset og Kulturhuset bl.a.
culture_adjustment: Det var overraskende nemt, fordi nordmænd og danskere har en så ensartet social omgangsmåde.
socializing_tips: Det var svært at få venner på kurserne, fordi man går med et hold, som har fulgt hinanden i 3 eller 4 år, og nordmænd er ligeså introverte som danskere. Men folk er generelt høflige og åbne.
cultural_challenges: Ikke umiddelbart noget.
culture_appreciated: Det var rigtig sjovt at opleve 17 maj, som er en big deal særligt i Bergen. Og nordmænd har en ligeså tør og lidt sarkastisk humor som danskerne, så det var hyggeligt at falde ind i.
top3_advice: Vær socialt åben og opsøgende i starten af dit ophold, så du får skabt dig et netværk. Accepter, at du nok ikke får størstedelen af dine sociale behov opfyldt gennem kurserne. Nyd den smukke natur og det lidt langsommere tempo i Bergen.
most_rewarding: Oplevelsen i sin helhed - både spændende faglig læring, nye venner, at stå helt på egne ben i et nyt land. Og naturen.
greatest_challenge: At navigere i alt det nye. Man får nye omgivelser, nyt undervisningssprog, nye daglige relationer osv. Det var rigtig godt at gå nogle gode ture alene rundt på Nordnes og på fjeldene for at mindske overvældelsen lidt.

crucial_aspects: Primary it was the nature, and an Erasmus was perfect. I wanted to experience the life next to the fjords and also see how it is to live in a more northern country than Denmark. I loved to see how technology is evolved in Norway. It was also interesting how the courses are different to Denmark and how its they teach the subjects differently. I chose Bergen because I always wanted to visit it.
info_ease: The University of Bergen gave a perfect experience for a student. It provided me with an accommodation, where I had honestly the easiest experience of finding an apartment/ room. The University helped with EVERYTHING. Also with helping to get into the Norwegian culture and how to find friends with volunteering or clubs at the University. It was the perfect place to go anytime and the employees were always really helpful. The introduction week helped to find friends, I enjoyed during my whole Erasmus time.
arrival_assistance: I had a responsible person which helped me with all the organizational stuff for the Erasmus. And also I received help in the introduction courses, where they gave you an overview of how to apply for courses or how to live in Bergen /Norway in general. They did an excellent job in making you feel like home, or in making you feel welcomed by everyone.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: I had to register from a course catalog in Soknabsweb and they provided me with a detailed description of the procedure
registration_help: You could ask the responsible Erasmus person, and you receive an email with the details. There is also the website.
registration_success: It was good, just some of the classes where overlapping so it was complicated to attend the one I wanted to take.
registration_advice: Be aware that a lot of the courses overlap. And if you are not sure about anything just ask!! and apply very soon for the Norwegian course, the deadline ends early.
course_level: Introduction. to Cognitive Science of BA ( 1 year), Natural Resource Management ( MA 1. year), Software Specification (MA 1. year ) each of them have 10 ECTS
teaching_comparison: Yes and no. The Cognitive Science course it is similar, but the Natural Resource Management course was a only online course and the Software Specification course was like a small UCPH Master course, and my favourite one.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Cognitive Science, Natural Resource Management, Software Specification
recommended_courses: Just take the Norwegian Intro course/ or the language course, I would have love to take it. But all the courses at UIB are good quality.
unexpected_costs: The travels and the high supermarket prices, be aware that Norway is really expensive when you consider basics like vegetables.
cost_comparison: The groceries were more expensive and the alcohol. Going out is similar to Copenhagen ( except alcohol ) and also going to a coffee is similar to Copenhagen prices. The rent is less expensive then in Denmark.
activities_available: I went to yoga, afrobeat, swimming and to the gym. I helped in Kvarteret( a student cafe from Bergen ) and I went to the social activities of the faculty of informatics.
activities_recommended: Volunteering and sports are good ideas. I would recommend a Damen gym membership and volunteering at one of the many student clubs in Bergen.
weekend_recommendations: I recommend to hike one of the 7 mountains, go to Bryggen, take cruise tour and try the whale salami. Bergen is rainy so take the raincoat. But the city is absolutely worth a visit and it's absolutely beautiful. Hiking on one mountain is a must for a Norwegian experience.
culture_adjustment: The Norwegians are a little reserved like the danish people, but with the help of the introduction week it was doable to create a connection with Norwegians. The University helped us to arrive and guided us through the first couple of weeks, so I never felt really alone in the things I had to do. The international office helped with the documents and the student advisor could help with any type of questions. The University taught us in the beginning some thing about the Norwegian culture and made us aware of the differences.
socializing_tips: Attend the social clubs, in informatics they do a lot of social events and just talk to them. They will gladly help you with anything. It is hard to find a Norwegian friend, but just ask them to drink a beer and they would love to hang out with you. A drunk Norwegian can become your best friend. It takes time and I was happy to find one Norwegian friend, but this is not normal so don't put so much pressure, be nice, try to ask them if they join you for a hike or a beer and you will be fine. When you hike with a Norwegian be aware that they hike very fast.
cultural_challenges: To Danes there are not so many cultural differences. Finding Norwegian friends is a little challenging.
culture_appreciated: I like a lot the hiking culture and that if you find a Norwegian friend they are very funny and always interesting to be around.
top3_advice: Take a rain jacket, try to get to know a person from Bergen and you will fall in love with bergen
other_useful_info: Check the Norwegian course early!! and Take a lot for the Rain. Don't miss the introduction week, because there you meet a lot of nice people, that can be your friends. And please just ask anyone at the University if you have questions, because they are really helpful.
most_rewarding: My friends and also to have the experience to live in a norwegian city, which I would have never dreamed about. I loved every day, because I also learned so much about myself in this experience
greatest_challenge: Dealing with the 1 hour more of darkness, and the rain and being far away from my friends was hard. But after 2 months I had very good friends in Bergen and they made the rain and the darkness beautiful and they helped me to enjoy the city more.

crucial_aspects: Bergen is in Norway, a crucial country in the green transition, I wanted to see in first person how Norwegians deal with their "Norwegian paradox". I always loved the nature in Norway and always wanted to try moving here to live: I wanted to have a grasp of its culture. Additionally, UiB is famous for its oceanography department, a field I'm deeply interested in. Lastly, they grant international students accommodation, which helps take off the most stressful part about moving abroad
info_ease: Very easy, the university website is well-organized and the process to apply was very easy (even for the accommodation). Everyone was also very quick at replying to emails, which is crucial when you don't understand something on the webpages
arrival_assistance: I don't think I received much assistance, but it wasn't needed.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: As an Erasmus student, you are given access to most of the courses just by applying for them on the "student web" webpage. You can always withdraw for exams and it's very easy also to enroll in different courses. One of the easiest processes I've encountered in my academic experience in three different universities!
registration_help: Quick replies from the secretary and the detailed description of the courses
registration_advice: Just register for all the courses you might want to follow, start following them in the first week, and then withdraw from those you don't feel like taking. It's the easiest and most effective way!
course_level: I took an introductory course in oceanography, but it gave me all the info I think I'll need in my career; no previous knowledge is strictly required. The MA course was at an MA level, you really need to have a good grasp of the mathematical tools you learn in the Bachelor's. I also took a course addressed both to Master's and Bachelor's students. I have to say that being a Master's student helped me a lot: my experience was very valuable in that course and made it way easier in the various assignments. But again, the course was accessible to Bachelor's students as well
teaching_comparison: Way better. My experience at UCPH has been strange; I felt left alone for most of my studies. Here, the professor is very present and really makes you feel understood. Also, the mandatory assignments during the semester made it easier to study for the exams in the end: I didn't really have important and valuable assignments during the semester at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: MAT253 - Fluid Mechanics GEOF236 - Chemical Oceanography SDG207 - Energy Transition
recommended_courses: SDG207. Great course, it is very well-managed and gives you a ton of info.
unexpected_costs: The food is really expensive here. Cooking at home is way more expensive than in Denmark
cost_comparison: Vegetables and fruits. But in general the groceries
activities_available: The gym is very cheap, and there a lot of students organizations you can join
activities_recommended: Depends on their interests, I really don't know
weekend_recommendations: Go hiking, as much as you can. Find some friends to go with and you'll enjoy your stay in Norway so much!
culture_adjustment: Very easy, Norwegians are always welcoming and the social rules are easy to apply.
socializing_tips: Join the student organizations.
cultural_challenges: The fact that they rely on planned events to socialize with each other
culture_appreciated: Their willingness to talk to international students! Everyone speaks English and they want to know from you a lot of stuff! Very easy to talk with Norwegians!
top3_advice: The vibes are similar to the Danish ones. Go hiking. Try to find a scoail flat
other_useful_info: Not that I've already said
most_rewarding: The great feedback from professors and the bonds with A LOT of international students I made here.
greatest_challenge: I was enrolled in some courses that required more study than my flatmates. It was kinda hard to keep pace with my studies while at the same time being social.

På KU læser jeg sociologi, og det var et antroprologifag, men følte sagtens man kunne følge med, og bruge en del sociologisk viden. De andre fag var lidt mere bibbob. Klimafortællinger havde nogle gode undervisningsgange, men var ellers ret usammenhængende. Og det om displacement var også fint, men også lidt ustruktureret og vi læste primært forskellige artikler.
unexpected_costs: Jeg er ikke helt sikker på talene, men ved jeg, at jeg har brugt flere penge, end jeg forventede. Jeg endte fx med at bruge mange penge om måneden på at tage på hytteture (DNT), hvor både transport og overnatning kostede lidt. Det kan heldigvis godt gøres ret billigt, da man kan låne mange ting gratis i noget som hedder BUA.
cost_comparison: Mad var mega dyrt, men det er det jo også i DK. Alt alkohold var også seriøst dyrt. En fadøl på 40 cl. kostede de fleste steder mindst 70 Dkk, og man kunne ikke finde en vin i vin monopolet til mindre end 80 dkk. På nogle barer kunne man godt finde noget lidt billigere med studierabat (fx Folk og Røvere).
activities_available: Der var lige hvad hjertet begærer. Alt fra kor, vandre, aviser, klatring, dans osv.
activities_recommended: Jeg var rigtig glad for at klatre i Laksevåg, hvor man hver tirsdag og torsdag kunne købe morgenmad derude - det var bare max hygge! Jeg var virkelig også glad for at tage på en masse vandreturer, både i alle de skønne fjelde rundt om byen, men også på overnatningsturer i DNT hytter. På de turer kunne man virkelig mærke, hvorfor det var fedt at være i Norge! Jeg var også til mange filmvisninger på bibloteket, som viste gratis film hver mandag. Ellers gør man jo bare ting som derhjemme; hænge ud med sine venner, lave skole og måske feste (Rommet er en kæmpe anbefaling).
weekend_recommendations: Helt klart vandre en tur i et af Byfjellene, og evt tage en tur i Sauna, og slutte aftenen af med at danse på Rommet.
culture_adjustment: En af fordelene ved Norge, er at det var så relativt nemt at føle sig hjemme, fordi hverdagen i høj grad ligner den i Danmark. Så ville sige meget nemt.
socializing_tips: Jeg endte med at få nogle norske venner i klatrehallen, og blev rigtig gode veninder med en jeg mødte til et intromøde til avisen STOF. Jeg kom godt nok ikke med i avisen, men fik en veninde, som endte med at tage med og en anden dansker med i hendes norske vennegruppe. Så mit råd er nok bare, at tage til nogle sociale ting og snak med nordmændene - folk var ret åbne og interresserede. Jeg mødte fx også en random til et loppemarked, som inviterede mig med i hendes kor.
culture_appreciated: Måske kulturen for at gå så meget på tur.
top3_advice: Har lyst til at være lidt cliche og skrive nyd det! Jeg synes selv det var ret udfordrene i starten og noieren at være helt alene i en ny by, men det blev så hurtigt mega fedt. Alle udvekslingstuderende (især fra DK) skulle jo også selv ud og få nye venner, så man var meget i det sammen!
most_rewarding: Alle de nye bekendtskaber jeg fik; både danskere og nordmænd. Meget smukt at nogle vil bruge så meget energi på en, når man kun er der for 4 måneder. Og så helt klart alle naturoplevelserne.
greatest_challenge: Måske savnet jeg havde til derhjemme i starten, men jeg var også meget nervøs for at tage afsted.

registration_help: Studentsenteret og infosenter på fakultetet man er tilmeldt.
registration_success: Jeg fik de fag jeg havde skrevet mig op til.
registration_advice: Hold øje med skemaet for fagene, nogle af dem varer kun 5 uger og er mere intensive, det kan være fedt at fordele dem lidt ud over semesteret. Man behøves ikke at stresse så meget over det før man er ankommet da fristen for tilmeldelse først er 1. september, medmindre man skal have lukkede/restricted fag. academics_comments: Kulturelt og socialt var det 10, men fagligt var min oplevelse ikke ligeså god
course_level: det var generelt ikke ligeså højt som derhjemme, men de fag som er tilgængelige for udvekslingsstuderende er heller ikke særligt avancerede, anbefaler at tage kurser på norsk!
teaching_comparison: det var forskelligt fra fag til fag. nogle var gode til at engagere og aktivere de studerende og skiftede mellem forelæsning og seminar. andre var mere bare en to timers forelæsning uden nogen engagering af studerende.
courses_enrolled: KLIMA200, KUVI105, SANT285-13.
recommended_courses: Jeg var meget glad for KUVI105 hvor underviseren var meget engageret og undervisningen var varierende og spændende. SANT285-13 var interessant ift. emnet og teksterne, men undervisningen var ikke så engagerende, mere bare forelæsning.
unexpected_costs: Ingen
cost_comparison: Alt er lidt dyrere end i DK, særligt øl og vin. Det er dyrt at gå ud og spise og købe ind i supermarkedet er generelt også lidt dyrere.
activities_available: Alt hvad man kan forestille sig findes der en klub for. Tag på student fair i starten af semesteret og se hvad du vil melde dig ind i. Min største anbefaling er også at melde sig ind i DNT. Her har de både aktiviteter/ture man kan tilmelde sig fx kajaktur, sejltur, vandretur osv. og så får man med medlemsskab halv pris på overnatning i alle DNT-hytter som ligger rundt omkring i hele Norge. Der er en masse fede hytter og mega fede og godt afmærkede ruter hvis man tager offenligt eller bil nogle timer væk fra Bergen. De fineste oplevelser jeg havde under mit ophold var helt sikkert vandreture og overnatning i DNT-hytterne.
activities_recommended: Jeg klatrede meget under mit ophold. Først med UiB's klub BTSI, hvor jeg mødte en nordmand som jeg forsatte at klatre sammen med. Anbefaler klatresenteret Laksevåg og at melde sig ind i BTSI der også arrangerer udendørs klatring.
weekend_recommendations: At tage på vandretur. Både i byfjeldene, hyttetur længere væk eller med bus ud til Sotra og de andre øer udenfor byen hvor det er fedt at vandre ved kysten. Tag evt. Skyss båden op langs kysten, det er mega billigt da zone A strækker sig udover et kæmpe område, også på havet. Tag ud og klatre! Når det er dårligt vejr så tag på museum. Universitetsmuseet er gratis for studerende, men der er mange andre gode. Byen har så mange kulturelle tilbud også. Tag på Rommet, følg med i hvilke arrangementer der sker. Spillestedet Østre er fedt og der er mange hyggelige caféer rundt omkring. Generelt er det nemt at følge med i hvad der sker i byen fordi den ikke er så stor. Saunaen Laugeren er også en kæmpe anbefaling når det bliver koldt.
culture_adjustment: Jeg oplevede at det var utrolig nemt. Hvis man er nysgerrig lærer man nemt at kommunikerer på tværs af sprogene og selve kulturen er ret lig den danske.
socializing_tips: Meld dig ind i klubber så du kan møde folk gennem aktiviteter. Nordmænd er ligesom danskere ofte lidt reserveret i offentligheden.
cultural_challenges: Ikke rigtigt noget.
culture_appreciated: Åbenhed og et meget tættere forhold til naturen.
top3_advice: Lær nogle nordmænd at kende! Meld dig ind i en klub. Studiet er ikke ligeså tidskrævende som hjemme, så der er masser af tid til at socialisere og taget på tur. Find et sted at bo i byen, vil ikke anbefale Fantoft.
other_useful_info: Nej
most_rewarding: Fik nogle meget tætte venskaber med en masse søde nordmænd som jeg helt sikkert skal besøge igen. Bergen er en skøn by at have forbindelser til. Havde de mest fantastiske ture i fjeldene.
greatest_challenge: At skulle hjem igen haha!

crucial_aspects: Exciting and relevant electives for my academic interests, the nature around the city, a low language barrier, and the destination not being far away
info_ease: Relatively easy
arrival_assistance: There was an intro week, however I missed it, because information about this and the courses arrived quite late, so I was not informed the semester would begin a month earlier than in my own country.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was easy to get an overview of courses available to exchange students in English. However not easy to find which courses in Norwegian you can apply for before the deadline for ola.
registration_help: There was a long list of courses and generally good communication with the host institution over outlook. The university website also had boxes to check off and pages with reminders to do as an exchange student.
registration_success: I got the classes I applied for.
registration_advice: Find out more about what courses you are able to apply for in Norwegian as well, if you believe you are able to follow along.
course_level: I took a theoretical course in digital culture at humanities and a methodological course on computational text analysis in linguistics. In Copenhagen, I study a master in social data science. Both were master level at 15 ects points.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching varied a lot between the two courses I took in Bergen. The theoretical course was much more active and discussion-based than that of UCPH, and more comparable to seminars in form. We also had to hand in weekly essays discussing self chosen topics with the reading of the week. I found it was a very good course form for following and learning the syllabus throughout the semester. For the course in computational linguistics, I was more disappointed with the teaching style, as it was much less involved, even though we had to code in R, which several students did not have experience in (it was not required). From UCPH, I have had good experience with learning a method and a programming language simultaneously, where we e.g. were given weekly coding challenges, which in my opinion works very well. Both courses had very little attendance. I had preferred a bit more classes a week.
courses_enrolled: LING310 25H / Datalingvistiske modellar og bruksområde DIKULT302 25H / Key Theories of Digital Culture
recommended_courses: DIKULT302 25H / Key Theories of Digital Culture It was a great course for discussing and thinking about how to use theory in practice, especially if you (as I did) wanted to also brainstorm about your master thesis topic.
unexpected_costs: Generally Norway is not that much more expensive than Denmark, with exceptions of specific items such as alcohol or cheese (and for some reason cucumber). But the Norwegian krone was also quite low during my exchange, which was an advantage as a Dane. The housing is expensive, and the transport is not cheap either. Not many people bike, as the city is very hilly, so you will have to get accustomed to walking and taking public transport. If you want to go on nature trips around Bergen and Norway in general, this can also quickly become expensive with the trains. However, it is possible to make it cheaper, and the city’s public transport by bus covers a very large area.
cost_comparison: Alcohol was expensive, but that was expected. Remember to ask for student discount everywhere, it is widely used in Bergen. The supermarket prices were less expensive than I thought.
activities_available: There are many activities available for students in Bergen, both as a part of UIB and outside of it. There are often concerts and art exhibitions, very cool events and cute cafes! I also volunteered at a concert place called Hulen, which I would really recommend if you like live music and want to practice your Norwegian. Athletically, there are also many sports and outdoor associations, so keep a look out for that. I became a member in one of the student gyms, which also gave access to a swimming pool, I would also recommend that. I heard a lot of people found places to climb as well. There are also student cafes and bars, I spent time at Ad Fontes, where there is free coffee, tea, and water of course. Overall, a very active student city.
activities_recommended: Engage in some of the student associations there are, people are quite welcoming. Maybe become a volunteer at one of the student bars or sports clubs.
weekend_recommendations: Go for hikes in the nearby mountains, you can see very beautiful nature on a short amount of time. There are apps such as UT, where you can see the difficulty levels of the routes. Also try to plan weekend trips in good time and get in touch with other exchange students and Norwegians. There are cabins to rent through DNT.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, quite similar to danish culture. The language is a bit more tricky, because of the dialect, but it’s possible!!
socializing_tips: Engage in student associations.
cultural_challenges: As I did not live in housing afforded by the host institution, I found it challenging to meet new people. I heard many of the other exchange students met each other there.
culture_appreciated: The great connection to nature and the language is amazing
top3_advice: Try to find space in your calendar to join weekend trips to the mountains, even if you do not have much experience with hiking. And take initiative.
other_useful_info: Go to the cold plunge and sauna.
most_rewarding: Finding out what I wanted to write my master thesis on, creating a stable weekly routine, and experiencing beautiful hikes.
greatest_challenge: Meeting people when you don’t live in student housing.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to Norway because I wanted to be closer to wild nature and I wanted to try living in a more calm study environment than Copenhagen. The University of Bergen had some really interesting courses for me to take, and the nature looked amazing, which is why I ended up choosing Bergen for my 1.st priority.
overall_comments: I had a wonderful experience living in Bergen. The courses were interesting, truly beautiful nature was in my back yard, and people are welcoming and helpful at the university.
info_ease: It was a bit tricky to get the hang of where to get information, but it was quite easy once I got to know the campus, and where to look for it. It was easy to find e-mails of the people you could write if you had questions, and finding the information center on campus was quite easy as well. The website for my courses and information about where to find classrooms were easily accessible as it was designed the same as the one used by the university of Copenhagen.
arrival_assistance: I got emails with information on where to go get my student ID and where to find my classes, and it was easy to find the student information center, if i needed more assistance or guidance.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had a wonderful experience living in Bergen. The courses were interesting, truly beautiful nature was in my back yard, and people are welcoming and helpful at the university.
registration_process: I went to the information center, upon my arrival, and they registered me online
registration_help: There were staff at the information center who helped, and you could also write or call the information center, if you needed more information
registration_success: I chose the classes online, and was lucky as I got all my 1.st priorities
registration_advice: I recommend reading the emails you receive thoroughly and ask at the student center if you need additional help
academics_comments: I had a wonderful experience living in Bergen. The courses were interesting, truly beautiful nature was in my back yard, and people are welcoming and helpful at the university.
course_level: I took MA courses with BA-students who took the class at a BA-level, which meant there was an additional workload to the MA-programme, but this was specified, and it was easy to find information about.
teaching_comparison: I have not before tried taking MA-level classes with BA-students studying the same class at a BA-level, but it worked quite well, and it was clear what skillset you should have once the class was finished. I had more exams than I have had at UCPH at MA-level courses, and this was a bit overwhelming in the beginning, but I adjusted quickly.
courses_enrolled: EU and EEA Institutional Law and Policymaking Comparative European Institutional Law Human Rights and Welfare Policies.
recommended_courses: For law students who are interested in EU and EEA law and International law, the courses i took was very interesting. You learn about the different organs and actors and the strengthes and weaknesses of these. I would highly recommend Comparative European Institutional Law, this is a class where you reflect about the strengthes and weaknesses in national constitutions, and why it works/does not work in their specific countries, which I thought was very interesting.
unexpected_costs: I needed a good winter jacket, and good winter boots and more practical clothing during this exchange than i thought. You should have a good set of rain clothes, gloves and a beanie, and stiff like that.
cost_comparison: Some groceries are more expensive than in Denmark, but it is more or less the same.
activities_available: Sammen provides opportunities for fitness and sports of various kind, and the University also provides different types of sports.
activities_recommended: There are quiznights every week around campus and I would recommend going to those, also to meet other students and local students. I would recommend signing up for a sporting activity of some kind, also to get to know other students and to get a little study break.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend going on hikes! There are many cabins you can rent, and beautiful day hikes to do in Bergen. I would recommend the app UT to check out hiking routes.
culture_adjustment: It was easy. Norwegians and Danes are quite alike, and a bit reserved, but if you talk to people at events usually they are very welcoming.
socializing_tips: I would recommend signing up for local activities like quizzes, social events etc. These are easily found on posters at campus, or ESN instagram sites, and on facebook.
cultural_challenges: I did not really find any cultural differences challenging as such
culture_appreciated: I felt a very strong urge to go explore the nature. This was wonderful, the Norwegians go for day hikes and smaller hikes every week, and it was inspiring and I would recommend going on walks and hikes in the Fjell at least once a week.
top3_advice: I would recommend going to explore the nature! It is truly amazing Join some sort of social community, there are many, and you will get to meet a lot if nice people Take advantage of the opportunities to do the various kinds of sport, like climbing, ice skating, swimming and winter bathing.
other_useful_info: Do not be afraid to ask for guidance and help. Teachers and university staff are very nice and helpful.
most_rewarding: I got to experience a different kind of being taught, and to work and study with people from different countries and hear their perspectives on the studies we were doing. I learned a lot about people, study-methods, laws of different countries and it was very rewarding for me. I also connected to nature in a whole new way, and that was really amazing.
greatest_challenge: For me it was quite scary to be in a new country and being without my support system back home, but I learned to ask for help, and to jump into this experience with an open mind.

crucial_aspects: Most of all, the surrounding nature was of great importance - to have opportunities to travel and explore beyond where I would study. Also the culture, aesthetic architecture, and people of the country attracted me to choose my destination.
overall_comments: Fantoft studenthousing in Bergen, appears to have two different accommodations: One where you live in a shared flat with one roommate, but a big kitchen and living room with 15 other flatmates. The second is where you live with one roommate in a very small bunker bed, with one small kitchen and table in that same room (referred to as 'the prison' by the fantoft students). I was put in the second accommodation, which to me and to many others, has unfortunately been a quite disappointing experience. I personally think the very tiny constellation and only being two people can be very challenging for many. I therefore recommend that the 16-person accommodation is the most ideal investment, based on my experience.

info_ease: Very easy, the UiBs website has a very pedagodical guide that I used prior to and during my arrival.
arrival_assistance: Not really that much. The UiB administration was very helpfull if there was any questions.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: To be honest I do not even really remember the process, which just speaks to the simplicity.
registration_help: The UiBstreet, studentweb (internal systems) and the UiB website all gave plenty of information. And if I was ever in any doubt the administration was quick to respond to mails.
registration_success: Somewhat succsesful. I didn't get two courses I wanted to eroll in but that was due to very valid reasons. The one was reserved for first year biologist student and was not offered for exchange. The second was a sub-courses mangled in a larger masters track, so it made sense they couldn't offer it to me. I gpt all other courses I applied for.
registration_advice: Keep order in all the important mails you get, and save links to webpages you need to access later. It can quickly turn confusing.
course_level: The level was similar to what I am used to in UCPH. However, I have a block structure and even though the courses spanned a whole semester, they felt very much just like a slightly longer block. That is to say that prehaps the levels was not that hard.
teaching_comparison: Very refreshing and creative. I can't, of course, speak on the behalf of all courses but the ones I had applied a variety of teaching styles. Lectures, excurtions, poster sessions, gruops work and presentations where some of the methods.
courses_enrolled: BIO203 - Introduction to aquaculture BIO201 - From individual to ecosystem BIO250 - Palaeoecology
recommended_courses: Palaeoecology was a great course with a subject matter not discussed much in the basic curriculum at UCPH. The course included both an excurstion with field work, lab work and a poster session. Great course, the only caveat is that it is only held every other year.
unexpected_costs: I tried to buy a bike twice, and they both got stolen within the week I got them... so yeah, don't buy a bike. Other than that you might buy some extra hiking gear if you don't already have it. Also, If you want to workout the sammen GYms are great and quite cheap, but you have to pay for the whole semester up front (around 1000dkk).
cost_comparison: Genereally I think that the food prices are exaggereated. On avarage I belive the price of groceries are around 10-20% more expensive, but it really depends on what you buy. I recommend using the "eTilbudsavis" for scouting out deals. The Rema1000 app is also a must, but it should be noted that it is regionlocked and needs a Norwegian number to work. This can be a bit tricky but the special deals you unlock are definetly worth it. Also try not to eat out to much, but if you do byVENN are good for deals.
activities_available: There are many activities happening in Bergen all the time. It is a very dynamic city, especially if you volenteer e.g. Spire, Hulen, are the ecco festival. Honestly I mostly just went hiking every weekend.
activities_recommended: Hiking, the nature is breathtaking. Otherwise refer to my answer to previos question.
weekend_recommendations: I can not overstate just how amazing the nature is. Try to maximize your time in nature. use the "UT" app to get the locations of cabins and trails.
culture_adjustment: As a dansih person there is hardly any difference between our cultures, it honestly almost felt like going to a different region in Denmark.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: Learning the language was a fun challenge.
top3_advice: -Find your own accomodation, preferably with Norwegian people. -Maximize hiking, get a memberhip with DNT (Den Norske Tursitforening) that makes cabins a whole lot cheaper. - Don't get a bike, they will be stolen. Trust.
other_useful_info: When planning hikes public transportation can proce tricky over the weekends. If possible shift the trips to enable transportation on weekdays. Otherwise renting cars are pretty affordable if you are multiple that shares. Hyre is a great service get the Hyre pass if renting often this saves a lot of money (If you swith your location in the app to norway you get the pass cheaper only 99 NOK).
most_rewarding: The experiences I got outdoors. Especially on my solo trips, they were truly eyeopening. But also trips with friends, going for morning swims in mountain lakes and making food with storm kitchens next to waterfalls.
greatest_challenge: Honestly back home I can find it hard to balance my sudy load, which has lead to something akin to burnout in the past. It took some geting used to to prioritize the culture, nature and people a bit more than back home. But definetly wort it, and remeber that your grades won't get transferred;)

socializing_tips: I think that joining an association or soe social activity is probably the easiest way to get into contact with local students
cultural_challenges: I didn't really have any big challenging cultural differences.
culture_appreciated: I really appreciate the Norwegian language, and the nature. It is also a very active country where hiking and the gym is a bit part of a lot of peoples daily life.
top3_advice: Even though it is important to study, don't forget to have fun and have a lot of new experiences and trips. For me, living in a shared flat, even though it was a shared room was a great part of the exchange, you get so close with the other people that you live with. The university has very good facilities for studying. Try out the different faculties' libraries and study spots. The social sciences library was open 24 hours if you have a student card during the exam season
other_useful_info: Sammen is very helpful or a lot of aspects of life as a student in Bergen. It is not only housing but also the cafeterias at the Uni, many gyms, help to go to the doctor and the dentist and so on.
most_rewarding: The connections you make with other people. Living together with other people becoming friends while being away from your normal life creates a special bond.
greatest_challenge: Prioritising your studies while also having an active and social daily life, going out with friends, going on hikes and trips.

crucial_aspects: To be honest, it was random, but I had in mind that I wanted to choose a country that I normally would not travel to. However, I really chose it well as nature is insanely beautiful and I was shocked that this was in Europe. You can both swim in lakes and go skiing during the exchange.
info_ease: The University of Bern sends you everything you will need to know. They have a thorough introduction programme, where you can join a zoom call and ask questions. They send you information from accommodation possibilities to vintage bicycle shops.
arrival_assistance: The introduction week at the campus was fun and good. They give a lot of information about everything and you have the possibility to meet all the other exchange students, which in my case was a lot.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: KSL and ILLIAS were quite difficult to understand in the beginning, but during introduction week they give you an information sheet on how to register for different courses.
registration_help: You could ask by email, zoom call (intro) or use the given information sheet about registering.
registration_success: I registered quite earlier than everyone else just to be sure, but I got in every class. The good thing was that a lot of my fellow exchange students and swiss students could pick and choose what class to attend during the first few of the semester. They changed courses just by writing an email to the professor, so there is a lot of flexibility here.
registration_advice: I checked the exam dates and the attendance date, which were so important. I made a weekly schedule and made sure that I had time during the exams to study, because the academic level is quite high, so you need to study and attend in order to pass. And I specifically choose not to have a writing/sit-in exam - only projects or presentations!
course_level: The level of my courses was quite high. Higher than the level of courses I have taken at my home university.
teaching_comparison: The courses I took didn't have a lot of students attending. In one of my courses, we were only four, so the professor will expect you to work hard. I didn't attend all my classes, because of overlap and because I sometimes wanted to hike/have fun instead. But I took my assignments seriously and worked effectively when needed.
courses_enrolled: 1. Empirical Macroeconomics II 2. Quantitative Macroeconomics 3. Spatial Methods using Python for Economists 4. Environmental Econometrics 5. Labour Economics 6. Banking Theory
recommended_courses: These are the ones I will recommend if you are planning on not dying during the semester: Spatial Methods using Python for Economists (group project), Environmental Econometrics (only assignments), and Banking theory (one nice midterm and group exam). Don't take quantitive macroeconomics if you are not good in loops and more advanced stuff (Value function iteration) in Matlab (this one killed me every week, and also all the other students). Even though I received the best grade in Empirical Macro II I would not recommend it if you are not planning on working hard (and everything is mostly in coding, and Matlab), but the professor is nice and helpful (Luca Benati). I didn't know Matlab before attending, but I think it is something you can learn fast if you have some experience in coding.
unexpected_costs: You should expect Switzerland to be expensive. However, if you do your research on half-fare cards and stuff like that transportation will get so much cheaper. The prices above are the maximum that I would use, so you can either use less or more. But I spend most of my money on train tickets for hiking and going around Switzerland, which I really recommend because it is so beautiful!

other_comments: I did not think I would enjoy this exchange so much. I fell in love with Switzerland and the mountains. To be honest, I have seen a lot of different nature in the world, but nothing compares to Switzerland, because there are always transportation and hiking possibilities. No matter what hike we chose it was always incredibly beautiful.

crucial_aspects: I had been in Switzerland three times before my departure, why I was in love with Switzerland even before. And now I love Switzerland even more. The three times I was there before, it was only on vacation, why I didn't have time to explore the whole country. Therefore, I wanted to have more time in Switzerland to explore the whole country. Switzerland is very unique in every aspect. Sometimes you don't believe that it is a part of Europe. The fact that it is so different from the other counties in Europe is one of the main reasons why I chose Switzerland. A lot of the counties in Europe are so similar to Denmark, why going on an exchange doesn't change that much. However, the situation is different with Switzerland. Everything is turned upside down in Switzerland. The system is different. The people are different. There are 4 main languages and English is not one of them. The University is different. The nature is unique and different. The food is unique and different. Everything is different, which makes it interesting.
overall_comments: I will give the study abroad 9/10, because I will leave some space for some improvements. It could have been made a little bit easier in terms of paperwork and/or moving exams to Denmark, for instance. The experience was 10/10, but some pratical things were a bit stressful, why the overall rate is 9/10.
info_ease: The University of Bern sends you all the information you need by email. There is a lot of information you receive, and they require that you read everything before your arrival. It's very pratical information about the introduction week, how to register to courses, how to change courses etc etc. Furthermore, there is a zoom meeting, where they are going through all the information step by step. It's also possible to ask questions there.
arrival_assistance: There is an introduction week, where they provide you with all the information you need. However, it's just pratical information, which you knew before if you read the information you received by email roughly. However, they are well organized and very helpful. And if you need any further information or help, they are always free and ready to help at their office.
arrival_comments: Very professional.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I will give the study abroad 9/10, because I will leave some space for some improvements. It could have been made a little bit easier in terms of paperwork and/or moving exams to Denmark, for instance. The experience was 10/10, but some pratical things were a bit stressful, why the overall rate is 9/10.
registration_process: They use to systems. One system is a webside called KSL. In KSL you can read about all the courses in Switzerland, register to courses, deregister from courses, receive grades etc. The other system is Illias, which is where you can see the courses you have registered for. Illias is very similar to absalon, which is used a lot in Denmark. This is the platform where you can see your chosen courses.
registration_help: The University is always ready to help if you have any kind of questions. This can be given through zoom or email if before arrival, or you can ask in the office at your stay there. Above that, there is always a lot of other people in the same situation, which are ready to help if you have any questions are your stay.
registration_success: I read about all the courses at the University of Bern quite early. Therefore I had a good idea which courses I wanted to participate in. However, the University of Bern offers students to change courses throughout the semester, why I changed some courses along the way. This is not recommended, but it's easy to change courses if you want throughout the semester.
registration_advice: I would recommend to check the structure of the courses. As an exchange student you want to have time to do other things (apart from studying) as well. I would check (for instance) if there is any required tasks you need to do, what time of the day the lecture is (make sure not to have some at the same time), when the exams are (they are quite close in Bern), how the exam is (written/oral/presentation) etc etc. Thereafter, I would choose the courses that fits best your preferences.
academics_comments: I will give the study abroad 9/10, because I will leave some space for some improvements. It could have been made a little bit easier in terms of paperwork and/or moving exams to Denmark, for instance. The experience was 10/10, but some pratical things were a bit stressful, why the overall rate is 9/10.
course_level: The level of the courses where quite similar to the level of the University of Copenhagen. However, most of the courses are only 4.5 ECTS compared to 7.5 ECTS at the University of Copenhagen, why you need to take more course to achieve 30 ECTS.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was quite similar to that of UCPH. The structure was the same.
courses_enrolled: 1. Banking theory (4.5 ECTS) 2. Combinatorial Optimization (4.5 ECTS) 3. Macroeconomics II (4.5 ECTS) 4. Mathematical Methods in Economics (4.5 ECTS) 5. Microeconomics II (4.5 ECTS) 6. Organization Behavior (4.5 ECTS) 7. Organization Economics (4.5 ECTS)
recommended_courses: I would recommend Banking theory, Macroeconomics II (if you liked macroeconomics III at KU), Microeconomics II, Organizational Economics and Organizational Behavior. You might notice that this is all course with pen and paper math only. If you like pen and paper math, I would recommend this. There is no required taks you need to pass during this courses, only the exam, which is an written exam at the end of the semester. Banking theory might have some midterm exam, which was not the case during my stay. Organizational Behavior is not math, but rather how people behave, which is very interesting, and the exam is an multiple choice exam at the end of the semester.
unexpected_costs: Switzerland is very expensive, that should not come as an surprise. However, I was surprised about how expensive the local transportation and car parking was. I had a car with me, and the parking was so high that I was not able to use the car inside the city (Sometimes I did, but not every day). Therefore I bought a monthly train travel card, which gave me free access to travel inside an area around Bern (via busses, metros, trains etc). However, I had to pay around 2.100 DKK for this travel card every month. Therefore, I would say that transportation cost is expensive in Switzerland. However, I think it's possible to get it much cheaper than I did. I bought all zones, since I lived 30min. away from Bern., and I did not use the half-fare opportunity, which is recommended by everybody.
cost_comparison: I think the local supermarkets (like. Coop, Migros and more) were less expensive that I expected. The reason is that I expected everything to be extremely expensive before departure. However, the big supermarkets produce food/items for some fair prices. On the other side, is it very expensive to go out for shopping, eating on restaurants, cafés etc.
activities_available: There are so many different cultural, athletic and social activities available that it's impossible to write them all down. There are more than 100 different sport activities plus a lot of cultural and athletic activities going on all the time, it's absolutely breathtaking. It's actually easier for me to say what is not there, because everything else it there. Therefore I would say that the only thing that I missed was some place to play paddle tennis and a bigger climbing hall. Otherwise I think you can do everything else there.
activities_recommended: There are so many beautiful things to do in Switzerland. Hiking, skiing, visit different cities/places (so many beautiful places), visit the parlament, visit some chokolade production, visit some cheese production, visit some vine production, swim in Aare etc etc. There are so many different opportunities.
weekend_recommendations: Travel around Switzerland. There are so many beautiful places. For example explore and visit the cities Bern, Zurich, Geneve, Lausanne and all small beautiful places around Bern (for example Grindewald, Murren, Wengen, Interlaken, Oeschinensee etc.)
culture_adjustment: It was very easy. The people are very helpful and easy going. They are very similar to Danes.
socializing_tips: Just go ahead and ask a lot of questions. They are very nice to talk to, and very helpful.
cultural_challenges: I did not find any cultural differences particularly challenging. The only thing that was a bit challenging was to understand 4 different languages. However, it was just a positive challenge to try to understand the people there.
culture_appreciated: The way the people treat each other was the part that I appreciated the most. I think the people are so nice to each other there. If you have a question, they don't just answer the question, they also follow up upon the question. You can feel the love from the people there. They are very welcoming, interested in you and helpful. That was my experience. For me, it felt like a culture where people were helping each other all the time. They didn't seem so stressed, but rather more smiling and taking their time to help others.
top3_advice: Be social and open (Participate in sports, hiking, skiing etc.), enjoy the semester (don't think too much about grades etc.), try to learn a new (local) language (it's fun).
other_useful_info: Just enjoy your stay, ask a lot of questions and meet a lot of interesting people along the way.
most_rewarding: The sports program, meeting new people, learning new language, hiking and visiting new places.
greatest_challenge: The exams and learning a new language.

crucial_aspects: I chose Switzerland as my study destination because of several crucial aspects: Firstly, the multicultural environment of Switzerland, with its four official languages and diverse population, intrigued me. I was eager to immerse myself in such a rich cultural tapestry, believing it would provide a unique learning experience and foster my cultural understanding and global perspectives. Moreover, Switzerland's high quality of life, excellent healthcare, safety standards, and overall standard of living were appealing factors. The opportunity to live and study in a country known for its exceptional quality of life was something I valued greatly. Furthermore, Switzerland's breathtaking natural beauty, including the Swiss Alps, pristine lakes, and picturesque towns, offered ample opportunities for outdoor recreation and exploration. I was drawn to the idea of studying in a country renowned for its natural landscapes and outdoor activities.
info_ease: I fairly easy found my way around the country and to my accommodation to uni etc. Even though I was surprised that the grocery stores closed already at 7pm!! I ended up buying my first dinner at the local gas station instead. Be aware that much communication is in german!! You need a translator...
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance
arrival_comments: Whenever I reached out to the university, they were always really helpful and quickly provided help.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Applying fo subjects is KSL was easy and intuitive. You just go to the course you want to enroll in and apply for participation. Be aware of deadlines and openings for applicaitons.
registration_help: You could always reach out to an advisor designated to you field of study.
registration_success: I successfully registered in all classes that i desired to participate in.
registration_advice: Don't worry if you don't find the right subjects in the first go - the uni offers you to change subjects within the first week or two of the semester.
course_level: Economics field: I copenhagen the level of theory is much higher than in Bern. I found myself having an easier time wrapping my head around econometric theory than my peers. However, they seem to be very strong when it comes to application of theories. It was really nice to experience this difference. The level was in general 'right-on' for me.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching is nice. In general the students the students are not that active in class. However the professors I had were very relaxed and classes were in general comfortable spaces to be in.
courses_enrolled: Real estate economics Regional and urban economics Environmental econometrics Seminar: economics of biodiversity Valuation of environmental goods
recommended_courses: Real estate economics Regional and urban economics Are nice courses applying microeconomic theory on an actual market. I haven't had courses like this at home so I really enjoyed this.
unexpected_costs: none
cost_comparison: Little bit less expensive than anticipated., But expensive in general
activities_available: A lot of sport activities. I participated in Pilates and Fitness.
activities_recommended: I would recommend going to the jazz club in the old town. This is a really cozy experience.
weekend_recommendations: Go hiking in the beautiful swiss mountains!!
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: Be outgoing towards the swiss when participating in classes with mostly swiss students
cultural_challenges: The language. I did not speak german, and they are not everyone good with English
culture_appreciated: Touch with ´nature , empathizing sports in everyday life
top3_advice: - Don't live at studentlodge bumpliz if you want to live in a clean place where you feel at home - Go to the mountains often - make sure you are financially covered
other_useful_info: participate in language courses if you want to learn german and have an easier time in the country
most_rewarding: Being in touch with nature
greatest_challenge: Being away from my girlfriend for a semester

crucial_aspects: - Feeling like there would not be that much of a change in the every day life in regards to culture and how things work. - The opportunities to do other things and explore when not studying.
info_ease: Medium. If you make an effort it is not that hard, but you have to do a lot of research yourself to be sure you have all the necessary information.
arrival_assistance: We had a mandatory introduction week for all international students where we got information about the most important things.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You have to fill in a personal information, upload a photo and sign some documents.
registration_help: It was always possible to write an email to the responsible person at the international office at the host university.
registration_success: Very succesful. I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Do not wait until the last minute in case any problems occur.
course_level: The level of the courses is ok, and all the subjects are recognizable from what is learned at KU. However, the work load is way heavier than at KU, especially when being a master student, we are not used to making assignment and having exercise classes anymore.
teaching_comparison: Very small classes with few people, working on school computers in programming courses, exercise classes is just the teaching assistant giving all the answers.
courses_enrolled: Resource Economics, Organizational Economics, Mathematical Methods in Economics, Empirical Macroeconomics II, Environmental Econometrics, Banking Theory.
recommended_courses: Depends on what you want. The ones at 4.5 credits usually does not require that much trough the semester, but even at 4.5 credits the exams are tough. The ones at 6 credits have many assignments that takes a lot of time trough the semester, but typically no exams and instead a term paper to hand in.

crucial_aspects: Jeg vidste jeg gerne ville til England at studere, så jeg gjorde en stor dyd ud af at undersøge hvilke universiteter der var rangeret højt i statskundskabs institut. Derudover ville jeg gerne til en storby og så fandt jeg Birmingham særligt tiltrækkende da det også er en by der er kendt for dets multikulturalitet.
info_ease: UoB gør alle informationsprocesser meget nemt tilgængelige.
arrival_assistance: Der er opsat et velkomsttelt hele den første måned, hvor der er mulighed for at komme og stille diverse spørgsmål. Derudover har du mulighed for at besøge det internationale team på universitetet hele semesteret igennem, hvis der er det mindste og sidst er de altid tilgængelige på mailen med hurtige svar.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Det foregår i et stort velkomststelt for internationalle studerende hvor du kan få alle dokumenter underskrevet på en gang, samtidig med at du får udleveret dit studiekort. Nemt og effektivt.
registration_help: Alt den hjælp du kan forestille dig. De har et stort team af ansatte der altid er tilgængelig både fysisk på campus og online på mail.
registration_success: Jeg fik desværre kun tildelt én ud af de tre fag jeg havde anmodet om.
registration_advice: Dobbelttjek når du undersøger fag at de bliver udbudt på det semester du skal afsted på. Videre vil jeg anbefale at finde flere fag der forhåndsgodkendes inden du tager afsted, skulle der opstå problemer med tildelingen af fag på udvekslingsuniversitetet.
course_level: Niveauet svarer meget til min erfaring med fagene på KU.
teaching_comparison: Undervisningsstilen er meget lig på Københavns Universitet, forstået på den måde at den ugentlig undervisning i hvert fag består af en forelæsning og en holdundervisning. Den eneste substantielle forskel er at holdundervisning varer én time i stedet for to. Derudover er undervisningen i begge henseender langt mere interaktiv end på KU.
courses_enrolled: Comparative Politics Global Governance Economic Perspectives on Development
recommended_courses: Jeg vil klart anbefale 'Economic Perspectives on Development' da den fungerer som en rigtig god efterfølger til at have haft mikro- og makroøkonomi. Det giver spændende og indsigtsfulde perspektiver på hvordan den økonomiske eurocentrime multidimensionelt har haft og stadig har afgørende implikationer for økonomisk udvikling i udviklingslande.
unexpected_costs: Jeg har ikke oplevet nogle uventede udgifter. Modsat var jeg positivt overrasket over at alt pensum er online, så der skal ikke bruges nogen penge på bøger.
cost_comparison: Når du kommer hjemme fra Danmark vil du opleve at de fleste ting er relativt billigere. Jeg vil dog sige at offentlig transport var billigere end jeg forventede, så det vil jeg klart anbefale at gøre brug af. Dog hvis det ønske at opleve de omliggende dele af UK, vil jeg anbefale at planlægge ture i god tid, da togpriser godt kan være meget dyre hvis de bestilles de lige op til at de skal benyttes.
activities_available: UoB tilbyder mere end 500 forskellige societies man kan tilmelde sig og være en del af, så der er noget for en hver smag og det er klart noget jeg vil anbefale at melde sig ind i, da det er en god og nem måde at måde nye mennesker.
activities_recommended: Gå på opdagelse i Birmingham. Det kan udefra opleves som en by man kan nå at se på et par dage, men der findes mange små spændende områder går man bare 5-10 minutter ud fra centrum shoppinggaden. Rigtig fede områder er: Chinatwon, Gay Village, Digbeth og ikke mindst kanalområdet omkring Brindley Place.
weekend_recommendations: Tag en masse ture rundt i UK til de omliggende byer: London, Manchester, Liverpool, Brighton mm. De fleste steder kan man nemt komme til med busture på 1-2 timer.
culture_adjustment: Det er altid lidt skørt at flytte til et andet land, men jeg ville give det et par uger også vil du føle at du er faldet godt ind. Universitetscampuset er som en by i sig selv hvor der er rig mulighed for at møde en masse mennesker, både britiske og internationale studerende.
socializing_tips: Vær åben og snak med så mange som muligt! Ikke vær genert. Det er min opfattelse af de britiske studerende godt selv kan være en smule generte, men de er meget snaksaglige så snart der bliver åbnet for en samtale.
cultural_challenges: Der var ikke nogle dele af kulturen jeg fandt udfordrende.
culture_appreciated: Det multikulturelle befolkning. Det er fedt at være omgivet af en masse forskellige slags mennesker, der ikke nødvendigvis ligner eller lever på samme måde som en selv. Man bliver på en fed måde opmærksom på hvor meget alle ligner hinanden i Danmark.
top3_advice: - Gør brug af alle de sociale initiativer der bliver stillet til rådighed på universitetet. - Prioriter at lav dit uniarbejde i hverdagene og dagstimerne, så du kan tage nogle fede weekendture rundt i UK - Vær åben og nysgerrig på menneskerne omkring dig. Det er altid spændende at få internationalle venner og ikke mindst lære nogle lokale at kende, da det altid er dem der kender de gode steder.
other_useful_info: Nyd det og hold fast i at der skal være god balance mellem hvor meget tid du bruger på uniarbejde og hvor meget fritid du giver dig selv. Derudover skal du ikke stresse over pludselig at skulle skrive eksamnier på akademisk engelsk, også i dette henseende er der mulighed for at få hjælp, råd og vejledning af både underviserer og din personlige tutor. Gør endelig brug af dette!
most_rewarding: Jeg synes det var rigtig fedt at bo udenfor campus i et houseshare med fem andre unge mennesker. Satte meget pris på at have mit uni-liv på campus og stadig have mulighed for at kunne tage hjem til min private base. Derudover gør det at du lærer nogle mennesker som højst sandsynligt laver noget helt andet end dig, hvilket altid er sjovt. Mine roomies er klart blevet nogle venner jeg kommer til at holde kontakten med.
greatest_challenge: Det er klart at der er mere uniarbejde i forhold til hjemme på KU, så det kunne i perioder godt være lidt en udfordring at finde ud af at finde en sund arbejds/privatlivs balance.

registration_process: Processen var fin og meget lige til, men man fik sit ”letter of acceptance” forholdsvis sent.

registration_advice: Deltag i de møde UoB holder og hold dig opdateret. Jeg stressede meget over at jeg fik mit ”letter of acceptance” ret sent, men det er normalt og det skal nok ordne sig.

Jeg var heller ikke fan af eksamensformen ift. andre fag. Law, Justice and Ethics: Dette er et første års fag, hvilket jeg var meget glad for at have, da de andre to fag fyldte meget. Det er et hyggeligt fag med en rolig eksamensform.

Derudover var flere af mine venner medlem af fx: Tennis, fodbold, basketball, art society, hiking society, theater society og meget andet.

most_rewarding: For mig var det klart at blive bedre til engelsk og møde en masse søde mennesker, som man fik nogle fede oplevelser med. At bo på en samlet campus var virkelig en fed oplevelse og noget jeg vil anbefale alle at prøve, da det er så langt fra et studieliv på KU.
greatest_challenge: Det krævede lidt ekstra arbejde, at alt undervisning var på engelsk.
other_comments: Jeg var virkelig glad for mit udviklingsforhold på UoB og kan varmt anbefale det til alle. Hvis du har nogle spørgsmål, ift. et udvekslingsophold på UoB, er du velkommen til at kontakte mig; cml553@alumni.ku.dk

cost_comparison: As an Erasmus student you can get a TPER card which gives access to the bus in Bologna and costs 10 euro for your whole erasmus semester, very cheap! activities_available: As a part of ESN there was volleyball and basketball every saturday. I heard it was fun. Other than that a football tournament during the semester. But in the ESN whatsapp groups it was easy organizing some activities.
activities_recommended: There is a lot going on in Bologna. It is a student city and a lot of events are happening all the time. I was at a wine festival in Bologna, and there are music and concerts going on as well. Follow bologna_parvenza on instagram, they put up a "what is going on in Bologna" every weekend and sometimes in the weekdays.
weekend_recommendations: Bologna is quite central and from Bologna you can visit some parts of Italy. I had some friends who had cars here and I enjoyed very much to go on few trips around Bologna. I highly recommend to go hiking Via degli Dei, which is a hiking route from Bologna to Firenze of 130 km. You can do it by tent with some other people. Parco di villa Ghigi is a really nice spot up in the hills above Bologna, takes one hour to walk there. Not many people go there, but you have an amazing overview over the city and a quiet park. I loved going there on weekends.
culture_adjustment: It was quite easy I think. I loved going for a cappucino and a cornetto in the mornings at a "bar" for 2.5 euro and to just eat pasta daily.
socializing_tips: In the beginning I just wrote a Facebook post in one of the Erasmus groups if anyone wanted to go for a coffee or a beer, and a lot of people answered and we went for a coffee. Other than that in the ESN groups to begin with a lot of people are writing if anyone wants to go for something, and then you can just join. Everyone is on the same level to begin with so people are very keen to go meet people, and then groups slowly formed.
cultural_challenges: I found it difficult to be able to speak italian as I mostly just met other Erasmus students which I regret a bit, I would have wanted to live with some italians if I had to do it again.
culture_appreciated: The italian people in Bologna are very friendly, and aperitivo is cool.
top3_advice: Be open towards other people, try to figure out what is going on in the city, as there are so many things happening all the time.
other_useful_info: I think I've covered it pretty well above.
most_rewarding: 1 euro espressos and being able to live in the Italian culture for a semester.
greatest_challenge: I think most people would answer here; finding housing.

crucial_aspects: To be half a year in Italy.
info_ease: The website of University of Bologna seemed at first site to be pretty organized. However, I still found it quiet hard to find the correct information about which courses were available in the spring and also general information on incoming exhange. As an exchange students I could have taken an Italian language course for free, but since I received no information about the course, I unfortunately missed the deadline for registration.
arrival_assistance: The university provided sufficient help if I needed it - you just need to email them :) It was pretty easy to contact the international mobility office at the University by mail. Also, the professors were very helpful and will answer you by mail if you have any questions about the curriculum of the courses, timetables etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Usually you will get the courses you want, which is really nice. The thing is, that you are actually free to change courses until you have registered for the exam. So if you feel unsatisfied with a course, you can easily swap to another (If you do this, I would still recommend to do it in the beginning of the course, otherwise you will probably miss some important learning)
registration_help: On most of the courses you can find information on unibo.it. On the website, it's a bit hard to see if the courses are available in the spring or autumn. To find this information, you probably have to go to the website of the specific program. Also be aware that even though the topic of the course is in English on the website, it may still be in Italian.
registration_success: Unfortunately, a lot of the courses I wanted were held on the same time. However, when I finally found the courses that fitted my study plan, I got all of the courses I wanted! :)
registration_advice: I would recommend not to start too earlier to figure out which courses you want to take. Because as most thing in Italy, the sufficient information will first be uploaded very late.
course_level: The level of the courses was a bit too easy for MA students. There are usually not a lot of readings, which is uncommon for a UCPH student like me. Instead, there are more classes during the week, which is very nice, because you then see your class mates very often (which is a very good way to find new friends!)
teaching_comparison: The students play a more active role during classes. There are a lot of discussions between teacher and students, and a lot of student presentations as well.
courses_enrolled: WOMEN'S MOVEMENTS WORLDWIDE - I MOVIMENTI DELLE DONNE NEL MONDO (6 ECTS) HISTORY OF GLOBALIZATION AND CRIME (8 ECTS) POWER RELATIONS AND VICTIMIZATION PROCESSES (8 ECTS) SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND ECONOMIC INEQUALITY (8 ECTS)
recommended_courses: If you are interested in criminology, Università di Bologna provides very interesting courses. I had two criminological courses. First was called "History of Globalization and Crime" where the teacher gave an introduction in sociological theories on the topic, and applied it on cases related to globalization. Second course was "Power Relations and Victimization Processes", which focused primarily on theories about victimization, including victims of criminal actions, but also victims of more broader societal issues and transitional processes. I will also recommend the course "Social Stratification and Economic Inequality" if you are interested in a more "core" sociological topic. Here the focus is mostly on quantitative studies on social inequality, and you also get the opportunity to work with quantitative analyses in R as a part of the exam, which I enjoyed a lot.
unexpected_costs: I unfortunately had some troubles with the flights both when arriving and leaving Bologna, because of a cancelled flight and strike, so I had to buy double flight tickets.
cost_comparison: Food and alkohol are veeeery cheap, which is very nice, but it also makes you buy more :))
activities_available: Parties, dinners, trips to other Italian cities etc.
activities_recommended: Tandem! A lot of Italian young people would love to do language exchange, where you improve your Italian and they improve their English. I also did a lot of bouldering at Up Urban Climbing, where there was a small community of really nice Italian guys. Otherwise I will just recommend to explore Bologna's amazing cuisine and vibrant atmosphere.
weekend_recommendations: There are a great train system from Naples and up. So from Bologna, you can very easily go to Milan (1 hour), Florence (40 min), Rome (2 hour) and Naples (3 hours) by train.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, Italian people are some of the most friendly I know.
socializing_tips: Go to all of your classes! It's a very easy way to get friends, and we usually went out for a gelato or a spritz after class.
cultural_challenges: You have to get use to people being late for meet ups :) And to eat a 9 in the evening!
culture_appreciated: The friendliness, the pace and - of course - the food!
top3_advice: Shorts A fan Wine glass
other_useful_info: I would recommend you to try and learn italian! I kind of regret that I didn't put a bigger effort in learning the language.
most_rewarding: To enjoy Bologna
greatest_challenge: The language barrier (but you will figure it out any way)
other_comments: Enjoy and remember "when in rome" :)

arrival_assistance: There was a zoom check-in meeting which was helpful. Other than that, I had to figure it out for myself.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: You were able to ask questions during the meeting.

unexpected_costs: Overweight luggage on the way home...

activities_available: I didn't really check it out because there was so much else to do. But I think there are Erasmus facebook groups with activities, karaoke nights, and trips to Venice etc.
activities_recommended: Use the very good train connections and check out other cities nearby (Milan, Florence, Rome, Naples). And go out at night - people are very open and easy to talk to.
