culture_adjustment: Very easy. The italian lifestyle is easy to enjoy.
socializing_tips: We found it pretty easy to talk to people in class - that is where we made most of our friends. We also became regulars at a few cafes and bars where people were very welcoming.
cultural_challenges: You can't expect everything to be scheduled and people to be on time. But generally, the teachers and everyone else don't expect you to be either.
culture_appreciated: People being very welcoming - and very social. You live your life outside and people go out a lot which is a lot of fun.
top3_advice: Check out restaurants, bars, and don't be afraid to talk to strangers when going out. Talk to people in your class. Take the train to other cities - it is very easy.
other_useful_info: Get a bike (I bought one on Facebook Marketplace). Also: If you go there in february, don't expect it to be 25 degrees and sunny...
most_rewarding: The culture, food, and the social experience.
greatest_challenge: The administrative processes take time. And it isn't always clear what the exam guidelines are (I was told that I couldn't take my exam online, but in the end 12 other people did for instance).
other_comments: Great city! Go for the cultural experience - not the academic one. But I would definitely reccomend it!!!

crucial_aspects: My desire to experience living in Italy, as I have always been very fond of the country and the culture.
info_ease: Quite easy, no real issues
arrival_assistance: None really
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You need to update your study plan with the courses you want to follow, wait for it to get approved and register for the exams when they become available.
registration_help: Whenever I was in doubt, I just asked other students.
registration_success: I had to change 3 of them, one because it wasn't taught in english, another because it was held in the next semester instead, and the third because I decided to attend a different class.
registration_advice: Notice the relevant information of the courses (teaching language, semester, etc.), look for the official course programmes when they are released, and remember to update your study plan with the courses you want to follow.
course_level: It felt the same as in Denmark.
teaching_comparison: It was pretty similar with maybe a little greater focus on active class participation.
courses_enrolled: 1. History of Economic Thought 2. Risk Management 3. Political Economy in Macroeconomics 4. International Monetary Economics 5. Machine Learning for Economists
recommended_courses: Well, Professor Bajo in Risk Management was a very good and engaging professor, and the book in History of Economic Thought was very interesting (although be wary if it is still held online only)
unexpected_costs: None really (maybe the high service fees for the housing websites, but not really unexpected, per se)
cost_comparison: Milk and fruit were more expensive than anticipated! On the flip side, public transportation isn't really necessary as the city is very compact and walkable.
activities_available: Not completely sure, but there's a gym (quite pricey though) and a swimming pool at least.
activities_recommended: Take advantage of Bologna's central location to visit the rest of the country, hang out in the streets and bars in the evenings, and find some people to play sports with.
weekend_recommendations: Go and see San Luca (a monastery in the hills), wander the hills of Bologna, go on daytrips and weekendtrips to the rest of the country (especially places like Napoli, Rome, Torino, Verona, Cinque Terre and San Marino).
culture_adjustment: Very easy. I'm used to being a little late and eating quite late, so the adjustment wasn't that big for me.
socializing_tips: Learn a little italian, and when speaking english, talk a little slower and make them comfortable so that they are not so shy about speaking english themselves.
cultural_challenges: The language barrier was still the main issue. I was somewhat negatively surprised by how limited their english were/is (and my expectations weren't particularly high). It seems like no italians +35 speak a word of english, and the younger ones are mostly either too shy to speak it or are at a quite basic level. However, it is not an issue, you can easily get by. Besides, there are a ton of international students.
culture_appreciated: The food, the landscapes, the architecture, the history.
top3_advice: 1. Start your housing-search a few months in advance and find a place not too far out of the centro storico 2. Learn a little italian (it makes it easier to shop and travel) 3. Attend events, socialize with your housemates and be yourself.
other_useful_info: I think I have covered most aspects.
most_rewarding: Visiting and exploring all the beautiful cities and places that Italy has to offer, mingling with the locals and the international students.
greatest_challenge: Probably when the Danish and Italian authorities lowered the validity of the green pass/coronapas, which created some difficulties.
other_comments: Bologna is not a big city, but it is very cozy, walkable and nice place to live. Also, it has great travel connections to the rest of country and it has a huge student population.

crucial_aspects: The possibility to study at the University of Bologna, to live in Italy for a while and soak up the Italian culture & learn the Italian language. Especially the courses from the MA Psychology of Wellbeing and Social Inclusivity and Mediation since I want to combine Psychology and Film in my future career.
overall_comments: I was impressed by my professors and their way of teaching.

I had a lot of calls with Unibo and KU to make sure everyone was on the same page because I received a lot of contrary information.

academics_comments: I was impressed by my professors and their way of teaching.

recommended_courses: Humanitarian Communication was one of the best courses I have ever had - it is incredibly important to learn about it because it focuses on contemporary and prospective societal challenges and how we should talk about them.

cost_comparison: Coffee less expensive Food and housing more expensive

weekend_recommendations: Take the trains and go to the cities close to Bologna, a lot of places are very close and it is cheap to travel by train.

socializing_tips: Join sports classes, go to bars and cafés to meet new people, go to the library to study - you will always see similar faces.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: The welcoming and friendly attitude from the Italians, the eating and enjoyment culture. They also appreciate it a lot if you know some phrases in Italian and they see you want to learn them.
top3_advice: - Look for accomondation very early - Choose courses also from different departments than your own - Be open and ready for new learnings, new friendships and new opportunites
other_useful_info: Sometimes things seem a bit messy and chaotic but relax and take it easy.
most_rewarding: The knowledge I gained from the courses.
greatest_challenge: In the beginning to know that you do not have to be part of everything and to know that the right people will come to you at the right time.

crucial_aspects: Most crucially for me was an interesting city/culture, that I could get an insight into and immerse myself in.

arrival_assistance: I received the possibility to be connected with another student, though this program never came through. I was checked in virtually (Corona) and I was giving all the information I needed to start.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: The Erasmus desk was helpfull in changing courses.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Try out different classes, you don't have to commit before hand!

activities_recommended: Take italian lessons, you patience will be rewarded!
weekend_recommendations: Travel around italy, trains are cheap and quick! You can get to rome in 2 hours using the speedtrain from bologna. Run or bike in the hills!
culture_adjustment: Very
socializing_tips: Sport clubs or studen clubs. A lot of politics in bologna, easy to meet other italien students if you get involved
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The food, and drinks!
top3_advice: Things are more relaxed at Bologna University in regards to deadlines, adapt to the Italien way by knowing that everything will get done, it'll just take some time.
other_useful_info: Read about bologna, the cuisine and the region and you will be rewarded when finding nice restaurant and cities to visit on the weekend.
most_rewarding: Learning and immersing myself in italian culture.
greatest_challenge: The differences in how things a done administratively between bologna and copenhagen.

crucial_aspects: I have always been fascinated by Italy and the Italian culture so for me it was a personal preference already from the beginning. But I knew also that Bologna had the oldest university in the world and that, I think, was a clearly upside because the university was big and culturally important as well. Furthermore I found it appealing that Bologna isn't that big of a city - I wanted to get to know the city I was supposed to live in and find my own way of living there and that was a easier achieved if the city wasn't to big.
info_ease: There wasn't so much information upon arrival - I attended an online meeting with people from UNIBO and that was good but I still had a lot of questions regarding deadlines for a lot of things that turned out to be without any concerns but when everything is new and you have to fit into a new system it would be helpful to have even more information to stick to. But UNIBO was great at helping out when you yourself reached out.
arrival_assistance: Not enough.
arrival_comments: There is a lot of information and things to deal with during the mobility and especially when you have arrived. You have to choose your courses after your arrival and that can be a little stressful but don't worry, you have time to change the courses almost through the whole exchange period. The leaning agreement can be signed again, so I would recommend to get it resigned when you are completely sure of the courses but of course before you return to Denmark - the Erasmus Grant cannot be granted to you if you don't have the learning agreement signed before your return to Denmark.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I applied for a second round spot and it was very easy to send the application. The only thing that would have been appreciative for was a little bit more structure and information from the point when I got accepted. There were information letters that the students from first round received that I didn't but had to ask for information myself.
registration_help: Both the administration on KU and the KU-UCPH abroad have been nice.
registration_success: I was succesful. I even got registred for a class that normally has student limit from a specific course of education - I didn't knew this limit when I registred but UNIBO told be and said that I was welcome to ask the administration for a spot in the class and I got that.
registration_advice: It is a little difficult to get a overview of the many different classes. Be aware of the location because UNIBO has many location also far outside of Bologna. Then the next thing is to type down the different class schedules so you make sure that the classes don't overlap. I experienced that they changed the time schedule after having registred to the classes but then you just make a new study plan on your personal unibody site and change your learning agreement. Therefore I would recommend to get the final learning agreement signed when you are certain in your classes.
course_level: I took 5 classes at 6 ECTS points each. Some classes matched this amount of points but some classes were way more time-consuming than 6 points I think.
teaching_comparison: the classes I had was quit similar in teaching style. I study art history in Copenhagen.
courses_enrolled: History of Italian Cinema Italian Culture Exhibition, New Media and Performance Art Art Law in a Digital Age Feminist Critique
recommended_courses: All of them
unexpected_costs: You can live quite cheap but you eat out a lot so in the end it would be the same amount of costs as in Denmark.
cost_comparison: The housing
activities_available: There are a lot activities that you register to but for the sports you need a medical certificate with you from your doctor in Denmark, so if you want to do sport on Campus make sure you bring that to Bologna. You can read about it on UNIBO's website.
activities_recommended: I didn't join the trips myself but I know a lot of people who attended the different trips and excursions for the incoming exchange students - if I was supposed to go again I would attend at least a couple of them.
weekend_recommendations: Walk around the city and look up on all the beautiful buildings, go visit the many nice museums and galleries, do aperativo and go for a run in Giardina Marguerit.
culture_adjustment: Easy
socializing_tips: Go out for an aperativo or just chat with the locals in class. Be open-minded.
cultural_challenges: The language - I took a language course before arrival which turned out to be a good solution.
culture_appreciated: Everything! Their leaned back way of living, the art, the food.
top3_advice: Structure your mobility period before and after arrival so you have a good overview on the deadlines and information you need to provide. After that enjoy and do yourself the favor of going on train trips around the different parts of Italy. The country has so much to offer and then you hopefully feel the great feeling when you return to Bologna - this city is amazing and that you realize when you compare it with other Italian cities. It made me appreciate Bologna even more and made me feel at home in the city as well.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: The people, the culture, the academic classes. I'm very satisfied.
greatest_challenge: The language.

course_level: The level of the courses was much like at KU. Some of them more easy than others (like at KU).
teaching_comparison: It depends from course to course. But in general it is more engaging than at KU. Students actually ask questions and the teacher wants you to do that. One of the courses was very much like a proper seminar with discussions and texts for each lecture.
courses_enrolled: Public Economics, Advanced Topics in Liquidity Management in the Post Crisis Era, History of Economic Thought, Computer Programming, Advanced Interest Rate Models and Markets.
recommended_courses: All of the listed courses! Public economics: You go from basic knowledge from Micro II and Macro III and then read top academic papers. Very nice professor! Adv. Liquidity management: Finally a course on actual monetary policy! This is lacking so much at polit. You learn how ECB conducts MP! And how the baking sector absorbs and amplifies shocks in connection to the central bank and real economy. Best course in my life. Professor is so nice. The curriculum even included this year's nobel price winners paper (before the winner was announced). History: Very good professor and quite demanding course. Lots of readings due to discussion of papers each lecture. But very nice and a feeling of a proper seminar. Very academic. Not just 3 hour closed book exam. Programming: You should not know python before this course! It starts from the very basics. So you would be bored if you knew it already. It was good for beginners and still demanding. It was good that I already knew som Matlab from the SVAR course a KU. Adv. interest models. Extremely difficult course. Continuous time finance with a physicists as professor. This is like the courses at mat.øk . If you want to understand everything you need to have "mål og integralteori" from mat.øk and some previous introducing continuous finance courses. It is not enough to have attended e.g Fin 1 and from mat.øk and financial theory and models from polit. However, I had only attended those courses and I still completed with highest score as I was in a very good group for the exam and I spend a lot of time. In the end the exam is about pricing instruments so you need to apply the theory which saved me although there still was a proof in the exam which the group could do together. The professor is probably the most competent man on the planet for this course so a very good course if you want to be "quant" after your studies (or just understand what they are doing).
unexpected_costs: None.
cost_comparison: I had dinner maybe four times a week at restaurants which are extremely cheap compared to Denmark. Groceries are the same price as in DK.
activities_available: None
activities_recommended: Travel with train is so easy. Bologna is really well placed for this!!! Go wherever you want. You can also fly easily to southern Italy as the airport is 7 (yes seven) minutes away from the city center in train. Eat a lot of food! It is soooo good. Bologna is the food center of Italy.
weekend_recommendations: Eat, eat and eat. Bologna is called the "fat city" for a purpose!
culture_adjustment: Took a few days to get used to the crazy traffic. But then it is easy. They are very open minded.
socializing_tips: Drink apperitivos and go to parties. They love to just drink outside and squares.
cultural_challenges: The trafic is f****d! Be very carefull if you rent a car and when just walking around. The city is not made for biking so take care when you bike.
culture_appreciated: Italians are lovely and the food is fantastic
top3_advice: Find housing in advance (10 months before), travel, eat.

crucial_aspects: The aspects that were of primary concern to me were the following: 1) Opportunity to improve my Italian 2) High level of education at host university 3) Academic tradition for nurturing the humanities at the host university As the oldest university in the western world (founded 1088), University of Bologna satisfied the above three aspects. The university has long cultivated the humanities, offering a wide range of courses within the arts and humanties. Furthermore, University of Bologna is known as one of the best universities in Italy, as they pride themselves of upholding a high academic level for longer than any other university in the Western world. Needless to say Bologna offered me the opportunity to take all my lectures in Italian so that I could improve my English language skills. The language school that is connected with the university also offered Italian courses with an intensive course placed right before the beginning of the semester, which was ideal for preparing me for my exchange. For me it was also an advantage for the University of Bologna that Bologna primarily is a university city. Unlike universities in Rome, Milan or other Italian metropoles, in which the university is just one institution out of countless, the university in Bologna is the most important institution of the city: it is both a pride and a priority of the city.
info_ease: It was extremely easy to find the necessary information. The website of the University of Bologna provides all the information that is needed.
arrival_assistance: I do not remember needing any assistance upon arrival.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: On the website of the university there is a page dedicated to exchange students. Through the website it is possible to book an appointment for what they call a "check-in". The check-in happens online with verification of ID. After check-in has been completed, the student receives a QR-code to print a student card at machines on campus.
registration_help: There is an international desk available, which can be contacted in person or by email (they usual respond within 24 hours)
registration_success: I was successful in registering for all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: It is not rocket science; be on top of things and do what is expected of you.
course_level: Because I wanted to study Italian literature in Italian, I choose courses that all included Italian texts. The challenge of the courses were not so much the course material but the fact that I am studying a subject for which I did not know the context upon arrival: Italian students obviously have some familiarity with Italian literature and history from their time at Liceo (high school). I had to gain this information in my free time by reading books on Italian literary history while also learning the language during the semester. In sum I would say that the level of the courses reflects the level at my own university in Denmark – it was only my choice to immerse myself in Italian that made the courses incredibly difficult.
teaching_comparison: As already mentioned, the Italians only teach my lecturing (at least in the humanities). Each course consists of 60 hours of lecturing. On the one hand the student receives an incredible about of information to internalize during a semester, information which it is necessary to learn, since the exams are all oral. On the other the student does not develop the ability to think for herself, because the only requirement of the students is to learn exactly what the professor has said in lectures. In Copenhagen, the student has the opportunity to engage in a conversation with other students and professors in the seminars. Whereas the style of teaching in Italy is a monologue, the style at Copenhagen University is a dialogue. I certainly prefer the latter mode of teaching. Long live the Humboldt brothers who developed the seminar mode of teaching a few centuries ago in Berlin!
courses_enrolled: Contemporary Italian Literature ("Occasione" of Eugenio Montale; "Alcyone" of D'Annunzio) Italian Literature 1 (10 canti of Dante; 10 novellas from Boccaccio's "Decameron"; Tarchetti's "Fosca"; "La divina commedia" di Pasolini; "Il primo dio" by Emanuel Carnevale)
recommended_courses: I highly recommend taking the three courses on Italian literature: Italian Literature 1 Italian Literature 2 Contemporary Italian Literature There is no better place in the world to study Italian literature than in Italy. Why waste your time with pseudo-courses taught in English in which you get a brief introduction to Italian literature when you can get the real deal? Be aware though that it is immensely time consuming to follow courses in Italian if you have never studied Italian literature before!
unexpected_costs: I mostly battled with inflation. Be aware that cheaper accommodation is available than what I chose; yet rents are constantly increasing in Bologna. Landlords typically add between 10 and 20 euros to the rent every six months.
cost_comparison: All items in supermarkets were about 10 % more expensive than I had expected. This was due to the severity of the inflation.
activities_available: N/A
activities_recommended: N/A
weekend_recommendations: I recommend that they learn Italian, e.g. through sports activities or by following language classes at the university (I did the latter!). During my stay I met too many Erasmus students who could not even order a spritz in Italian. :-(
culture_adjustment: I already knew Italy fairly well as I have many Italian friends and been on holiday in the country several times. Nevertheless it is always stressful to move to a new country. It is a challenge.
socializing_tips: It was very difficult for me to localize with local students. The problems is that the universities offer activities specifically for erasmus students; at these activities you do not meet local students. At my courses it was also difficult to meet local students because lectures were 90 minutes without a break. In other words, there were no breaks that gave me the opportunity to socialize. I did meet some students, but it was challenging. Also, they tended not to invite me for anything; I had to seek the opportunities myself. It was tough. I recommend that exchange students install the application "tandem" on their phones in order to find Italian tandem partners; I met some Italians by using the application and got to know an Italian PhD student whom I met every week to practice my Italian.
cultural_challenges: The health care system is a challenge; I could not go to see a GP even with my private insurance, because the GPs do not offer a booking system that you can enter. In other words, legally I should be able to see a GP here; how to do it, I still have not figured out.
culture_appreciated: The Italian life style... Nothing better than a cup of coffee in the centre of beautiful Bologna!
top3_advice: 1) Learn the language! The university offers you a course for free! You can take an intensive course that takes place in the two weeks preceding the start of the semester. And if possible, have a B2 Italian before arrival. It makes your stay much more rewarding! 2) Take courses in Italian. Even if you do not understand anything, why would you be in Italy to take a course in English? Then you might as well study in Dublin, where they speak a much better English! 3) Go to your lectures; too many Erasmus students on my course neglected the lectures; each course offers you 60 hours of spoken Italian. Who would want to miss this opportunity for learning the language?!
other_useful_info: Consider taking two semesters abroad instead of one. None of the Erasmus students I knew wanted to go back after a single semester: they had just settled when they had to go back. What a shame!
most_rewarding: The ability to sustain academic discussions for 40 minutes at my exams. For my first exam I was really nervous; at my second exam a professor told me to take as much time as I needed to express myself; this suggestion really helped. I am really proud that I managed to achieve a level of Italian in which I could complete five oral exams.
greatest_challenge: I chose to follow three courses on Italian literature. ALL the reading, both secondary and primary, was in Italian. I have never spent so much time on a single course in my life! The language barrier was therefore by far the biggest challenge. I recommend that students begin to learn the language well in advance before they begin their courses in Italy.
other_comments: I am grateful that University of Copenhagen do not write the grades that I achieved in Italy on my Danish transcript. It encouraged me to seek out courses that were taught in Italian, because I knew that a bad grade (owing to my lack of abilities in the Italian language!) would not be recorded on my transcript. Though I managed 3 top grades out of 5 exams, I also had a black-out at one exam, which resulted in a grade way below my usual level. The black out was entirely due to the language barrier; it would have been awful to have an unusually low grade on my transcript when this grade reflected more my capabilities in Italian than my knowledge of the subject. If the grades would be written on the transcript, I would obviously be more likely to choose courses in English than in Italian because that would play to my advantage. I would however add that I hope that Copenhagen University encourage their students to take courses in Italian! It is very challenging but a very rewarding experience!

crucial_aspects: Both culture and academics were important to my choice. I chose unibo in part because they had some very exciting electives, including some that were not available at my home university. The reason I decided to go in the fall semester was also that the largest range of electives were available at this time. More important than this however, is the fact that Bologna is a beautiful and historic city. Especially inside the old city walls, it is just old renaissance palaces, archways with terrazzo flooring, cozy plazas and a ton of gingko bilobas. Immideately to the south of the old city walls is also some potential very nice walks into more old architecture and nature. Bologna is also not a very large city, which makes it feel not to overwhelming. It is a very unique and beautiful city, with very nice people.
info_ease: It wasn't super obvious. There was no information that you couldn't get, but you had to search a bunch of different places. You can setup these office visits with guides who are super helpful, but it's also kind of a hassle. In general, I think it was satisfactory, but it took way longer than necessary.
arrival_assistance: Not really a lot. Again, there are these helpdesk meetings you can setup, which you also need to do in order to "check in" at the university so you can get your student card. But like, the student card you gotta find out which campus near you has a student card vending machine, and then just go there and print it out.
arrival_comments: While I think a lot could have been done to improve information for incoming students, and reply times are sometimes very slow, once you get a hold of someone, they are very helpful and polite.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You have to have this online learning agreement to receive your erasmus grant. When it's approved you automatically get signed up to the final exams for the courses. Then you just gotta find the relevant courses in "virtuale" and sign up for them there too, and then you're pretty much done. Very easy, super simple, barely any work.
registration_help: I mean the process of actually signing up for the courses was very simple, but again, getting the OLA in order took ages, because unibo had some very very long reply times.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted! A few of them were a bit crowded, but the lecturers are very flexible with moving rooms if necessary, and they are great at squeezing in all the exchange students they can manage.
registration_advice: Request a preliminary course catalogue from unibo as early as you can, and get a sense of which courses you would like to take. It can be a lot to dig through, but the search function is really helpful. Once the full course catalogue for your stay is released, start working on your OLA and having it approved as soon as possible, because, as mentioned, they can take very long to reply.
course_level: In general I found the courses to be slightly lower level than the ones at my home uni. However there is much room to read extracurricular and additional materials, and the lecturers are happy to discuss their subjects of interests.
teaching_comparison: It was very similar. One very nice thing though was that the classes were often smaller, and so there was a bit more time for each student. Also, there seems to be more of a culture of active participation in the classes, which is really nice, even if you don't feel comfortable participating to that degree yourself.
courses_enrolled: Advanced Behavioral Economics, Advanced Panel Data Methods, Information Economics, Machine Learning for Economists, Structural Macroeconometrics.
recommended_courses: I thought all of the courses were great. I would probably recommend the ones where you write a final project. The feedback you get is great and detailed, and you will often also get the opportunity to defend it with a presentation. It is a very good learning experience.
unexpected_costs: I thought there was gonna be a cheap public transportation card for all exchange students. However this was discontinued from the fall semester and onwards.
cost_comparison: I knew housing was gonna be expensive, and it still turned out to be more expensive than I thought.
activities_available: I was unaware of any, except for one party for erasmus students. However, I think I might just not have been informed about them.
activities_recommended: If you enjoy running I think the city is great for that :) Also the walk from Porta Saragozza to Basilica di San Luca is great.
weekend_recommendations: You can take a short trip to some of the nearby cities like Modena, or go a bit further and stay for a weekend in Milano or Firenze.
culture_adjustment: It was fairly easy to adjust to the culture. One small challenge was that my italian isn't great, and many of the locals don't speak a lot of english. However they are eager to help you understand their italian and to understand your english.
socializing_tips: The local students are super friendly and welcoming! Even if you're a bit shy, they'll take an interest in you and talk to you and make sure that you feel welcomed to the uni/class.
cultural_challenges: There weren't really any that I found too challenging.
culture_appreciated: Price of coffee and food in general. Also quality of coffee and food in general.
top3_advice: Make sure to start to take care of administrative stuff that unibo has to reply to/confirm early, because they can take very long to reply. Start looking for housing early, potentially with other people, and maybe even with someone who is going in the semester after you, so you can get a good deal on a longer rental contract. Go out to eat a lot. There are so many great and cozy places, and it is really not expensive.
other_useful_info: If you don't want to spend a long time looking for expensive housing, check out the student hotel. A few of my friends stayed there. Very social and pretty close to campus, but also maybe a bit too social and like with party vibes every night.
most_rewarding: It was very fulfilling to experience that despite all of the things I was nervous about and the language barrier, I was still able to live a pretty comfortable life and like establish a routine in a completely different country. The challenges and mental hurdles I found out I was able to overcome.
greatest_challenge: Loneliness to be honest. Being so far away from friends and family and partner, and no matter how many friends you make at the host institution
other_comments: Via Saragozza, 3a, 40123 Bologna, 3rd Wave Espresso. Best coffee I have ever had, and I have had plenty. Really nice staff and regular costumers. Very local. The shop next door has a dog that sometimes slips out of the door and goes around and gets pets and scraps from the customers at 3rd wave.

crucial_aspects: I wanted a historically and culturally rich destination, and Bologna fit that description perfectly. It was superbly located in the middle of Italy in one of the country's most interesting regions. I had, however, also heard good things about the university and was obviously aware of its position as the oldest university in Europe.
info_ease: Fairly easy, although a bit confusing. They sent me quite a lot of information on email, but it was a bit overwhelming to figure out the right order to do things. I guess that's more or less an inevitable part of it, so I was not too frustrated by it.
arrival_assistance: I got some e-mails about check in, where to go to get my student card etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Once I figured out which platform to use it was fairly simple. But the courses are not always public until very late in the process so a bit of patience was required for that. My absolute biggest issue with this process was the fact that I HAD to choose at least one course from a department that I really wasn't too interested in. For some reason I had been assigned to this department and they didn't have a lot of English courses of any relevance to my studies. I ended up finding something, which then turned out to be the worst course I've had in my life, but that's another story ...
registration_help: I emailed both professors and people at the exchange student desk who were quite helpful
registration_success: I got everything I wanted but had to change things up a few times because of scheduling issues.
registration_advice: Just ask for help when you need it. Otherwise it will be quite confusing.
course_level: Almost all of my courses were on MA level, but I could easily follow them without difficulty. I would say that the level is generally lower than in Copenhagen, but the exam period is so intense because you have so many smaller courses.
teaching_comparison: Fairly similar. Some classes you would just sit and listen for two hours straight, but some professors were also interested in involving the students more, which I found great. I guess it all depends on the professor, just like it does here.
courses_enrolled: Visual Communication Literature and Visual Culture Introduction to Italian Culture Cultural Economics Italian Pop Cultures
recommended_courses: Visual Communication was fantastic and easily had the best teacher I've had not only in Bologna, but probably during all my time in university. I highly recommend this course. It was relevant, up to date, inclusive and had a great mix of theoretical and practical learning. Italian Pop Cultures was also super interesting and I learned a lot in that course.
unexpected_costs: Nothing of note, really. I just spent a lot more money on traveling, events, concerts, football games etc. than I expected.
cost_comparison: Housing was easily the most surprising part, as I had expected to pay around 3500 kr pr month. But food, drinks etc. are generally quite cheap down there.
activities_available: I'm sure there were opportunities, but I did not make much of an effort to look into that. There was so much else to do constantly.
activities_recommended: In the city of Bologna, I would recommend reading up on what's happening in terms of events etc. There is literally some sort of festival happening every weekend. I watched quite a lot of films as well (they have an excellent cinematheque), I went to some of the museums, checked out all of the churches multiple times, saw Bologna FC 3 or 4 times (highly recommend, even if you're not a big football fan). You will neeeever be bored in Bologna!
weekend_recommendations: The region of Emilia-Romagna is full of incredible cities that can ALL be recommended: Modena, Parma, Cesena, Ferrara, Ravenna etc. I traveled a lot during the weekends, mostly just on one-day trips, where I watched a football game and saw a new city. It was so much fun and can be pretty cheap. The train connections are great from Bologna, and Flixbus has super cheap connections to popular destinations like Venezia, Firenze and Milano. I would also recommend going to the beach or visiting some nature, as Bologna is a bit intense and very "city-like".
culture_adjustment: Pretty straightforward, I think. I came for the cultural aspect so naturally I wanted to experience that as much as possible. People are kind and open in Bologna.
socializing_tips: Not really, as I met very few local students. I did, however, meet loads of wonderful exchange students like myself through the Erasmus Student Network. It's a must that you sign up for this when you get there, they do tonnes of events every week and it's a great way to meet other people.
cultural_challenges: Honestly probably just that a lot of stuff closes down for siesta and during Sundays/Mondays. Just be aware of that, and it won't be an issue at all. Just takes a little bit of getting used to.
culture_appreciated: The spontaneity of Italian people is so cool. They just get out there and do stuff. I really enjoyed that you could go for a cheap Aperol Spritz on a random Tuesday night without having to get absolutely plastered. I really found myself appreciating small things so much more down there.
top3_advice: - Get out there and explore. Get lost in the city, find hidden gems and cool spots and just enjoy yourself. - Don't worry too much about money. It will ruin the experience if you do. Obviously, make sure you aren't running entirely out but you can always earn it again, when you come back. I'm just saying that you shouldn't say no or hold back because you don't want to spend too much money. This is a once in a lifetime experience, and if not now, then when? - It's okay to have a night by yourself at home as well! I did that many times, because you cannot be social every single day. Try to find a balance and don't worry about missing out on anything. There'll be so many opportunities during your semester.
other_useful_info: I don't think so.
most_rewarding: That I got to eat great food, be in a beautiful city, meet fantastic people while studying. It's an experience I will never forget, and I'm SO happy I did it.
greatest_challenge: Finding the balance between studies and experiences. I had a hard time with this, especially in the beginning as I wanted to see and do so much all the time. Take your time and remember that you are also there to study :) And don't wait too long before you begin writing your exams. I did that and had a very hectic April/May/June.

crucial_aspects: Før opholdet var jeg meget interesseret i at komme til Italien pga. kulturen, menneskerne og maden.
overall_comments: Jeg valgte flere fag som ikke lå direkte i forlængelse af mit eget studie, så jeg har lært en masse nyt. Byen og universitetet er fyldt med udvekslingsstuderende, så der er altid en god stemning i Bologna og masser af muligheder for at møde nye mennesker fra hele verden.
info_ease: De er ikke gavmilde med informationer før opholdet starter. Jeg skulle lede meget selv til at starte med og selv finde mennesker som kunne hjælpe mig med at checke-in på universitetet osv. Min Erasmus-koordinator i Bologna kontaktede mig aldrig tilbage, men det kan godt lade sig gøre på anden vis! Spørg dig frem, for du er helt sikkert ikke den eneste.
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik et powerpoint show med alle informationer, men jeg fik det først efter jeg havde checket-in og undervisningen var gået i gang. Men jeg har haft rigtig god dialog med professorerne, som er gode til at svare på mails, hvis man har spørgsmål eller brug for hjælp.
arrival_comments: Man skal kæmpe sig lidt for meget til at få de nødvendige informationer. Jeg var heldig, at jeg kunne bruge en anden koordinator end den jeg fik tildelt idet vedkommede aldrig vendte tilbage på mine henvendelser. Jo hurtigere du checker ind på universitetet, jo nemmere er det at vælge fag, få studiekort og få en studieplan på plads.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Jeg valgte flere fag som ikke lå direkte i forlængelse af mit eget studie, så jeg har lært en masse nyt. Byen og universitetet er fyldt med udvekslingsstuderende, så der er altid en god stemning i Bologna og masser af muligheder for at møde nye mennesker fra hele verden.
registration_process: I starten skal du checke-in på universitetet. Jeg gjorde det igennem et zoom-opkald, hvor jeg viste mit ID og relevante dokumenter. Herefter kan du printe dit studiekort og oprette en studieplan og dermed vælge de fag, som du gerne vil have. Det kan gøres løbende og er først bindende, når du tilmelder dig til eksamen. Studieplanen og forhåndsgodkendelsen fra KU skal bare ende med at matche hinanden.
registration_help: Jeg fik tildelt en koordinator før jeg tog afsted, men vedkommende svarede mig ikke i løbet af hele semestret. Så jeg var heldig, at jeg kunne bruge mine roomies koordinator i stedet. Men spørg og skriv rundt, mit indtryk er, at der er altid nogle, der gerne vil hjælpe - det kan bare tage lidt tid at få svar.
registration_success: De første to uger gik med at prøve fag af og vælge imellem dem. Det var ikke alle fag, som jeg havde valgt hjemmefra, som blev udbudt. Men Bologna tilbyder mange spændende fag, så jeg prøvede mig bare frem og gik til flere forskellige fag, før jeg endelig valgte. Det kan man sagtens! Jeg endte med de fag, som jeg gerne ville have, men i starten var der lidt klassisk italiensk kaos og bureaukrati. Jeg mødte op til et fag et par gange, men som viste sig at have en max grænse for antallet af Erasmus-studerende. Det var kun Erasmus-studerende, som havde fået godkendt faget lang tid i forvejen, som måtte deltage i kurset. Så vær opmærksom på om fagene har begrænsninger ift. faglighed eller niveau. Det står oftest i kursuskataloget. Når det er sagt, så er det meget nemt at rette løbende i sin studieplan og få godkendt reviderede forhåndsgodkendelser.
registration_advice: Tjek kursuskataloget ud hjemmefra. Hvis faget blev udbudt samme semester året før, så er der god sandsynlighed for, at det bliver det igen. I Bologna skal du selv have overblik og lave dit eget skema, så vær opmærksom på om diverse fag overlapper. Man kan se fagenes tider inde i kursuskataloget. Brug tiden i starten til at prøve forskellige fag af og se, hvad der er mest spændende. Vær også opmærksom på selve opbygningen af fagene, og hvornår de slutter. Mine fag lå i blok, så mine fag havde forholdsvist få undervisningsgange før en ny blok startede. Så tag heller ikke en beslutning alt for sent.
academics_comments: Jeg valgte flere fag som ikke lå direkte i forlængelse af mit eget studie, så jeg har lært en masse nyt. Byen og universitetet er fyldt med udvekslingsstuderende, så der er altid en god stemning i Bologna og masser af muligheder for at møde nye mennesker fra hele verden.
course_level: Generelt er niveauet lavere end på KU. Jeg valgte dog flere helt nye fag for mig, så på den måde er det en god mulighed for at blive udfordret på ens faglige niveau.
teaching_comparison: Jeg havde meget klassisk holdundervisning, som ligner meget det samme som herhjemme dog med mere dialog mellem de studerende og underviseren.
courses_enrolled: ACCOUNTING IN THE ARTS AND CULTURAL SECTOR ARTS LAW IN THE DIGITAL AGE BUSINESS STRATEGY AND INNOVATION IN CULTURAL INDUSTRIES HISTORY OF ITALIAN CINEMA LABORATORY OF MANAGEMENT OF MUSIC AND NEW MEDIA LABORATORY OF MANAGEMENT OF THE FILM INDUSTRY
recommended_courses: Jeg kan især anbefale LABORATORY OF MANAGEMENT OF THE FILM INDUSTRY. Underviseren var en independent producer fløjet direkte ind fra Hollywood. Vi skulle lære at være filmproducere og lære om, hvordan man finansierer film. Vi skulle lave vores egen pitch til et filmprojekt, som vi arbejdede på undervejs i kurset. Til eksamen skulle vi udføre vores egen pitch og vise, hvordan vi ville finansiere projekterne. I klassen agerede vi marketplace, og vi skulle så vurdere, hvilke film vi skulle købe og sætte i produktion. Det var et kort og intenst forløb, men det hele værd. Meget learning by doing.
unexpected_costs: Kun overvægt i lufthavnen, men sådan er det når man gerne vil have lokal parmesan, olie og andet godt med hjem :)
cost_comparison: Jeg var meget ude og spise. Man kan sagtens bruge færre penge på mad! Kaffe og drinks er billigt. Vi boede meget centralt, så jeg gik til alt - men man kan sagtens cykle eller tage bussen. Jeg brugte mest transport penge på at tage på ture rundt i Italien.
activities_available: Der er en sportsklub gennem universitetet, men da vi undersøgte det skulle man have en lægeerklæring for at være med. Ellers skal man selv opsøge hvor der er mulighed for at dyrke sport. Jeg kendte flere som lejede paddel eller tennisbaner.
activities_recommended: Tag ud og brug byen. Der er studerende alle steder, og folk er meget venlige og imødekommende. Bologna er smuk og man kan gå til alt.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på ture med tog/bus fra Bologna. Jeg endte med at have besøgt Verona, Firenze, Modena, Parma, Venedig, Siena, Milano og Rom inden jeg tog hjem. Tog er hurtigt og billigt i Italien.
culture_adjustment: Det var på ingen måde svært. Jeg har rejst meget i Italien før, men man tilpasser sig hurtigt kulturen og tempoet.
socializing_tips: Snak med sidemanden til undervisningen. Enten er vedkommende Eramus-studerende eller italiener og kender byen! Tag ud på en bar omkring universitet. Italienere er generelt meget imødekommende og søde.
cultural_challenges: Tingene går helt automatisk lidt langsommere i Italien (undtagen toget), men det har også sin charme. Og så er der nogle gange nogle sprogbarrierer, men der er ikke noget som kropssprog ikke kan hjælpe med :) Jeg gik en måned på sprogskole inden jeg tog afsted, og det var en anden god måde at lære kulturen endnu bedre at kende! Der er også mulighed for at gå til italiensk i Bologna med en engelsk-talende underviser.
culture_appreciated: At opleve hvordan italienere er passionerede omkring deres egen kultur. Jeg nød maden, stemningen, konceptet aperitivo, det langsomme tempo og italieneres imødekommenhed og hjælpsomhed. Og så kan man komme til næsten alle steder i Italien på forholdsvist kort tid. Der kan DSB ikke lege med :)
top3_advice: 1. Find bolig i god tid, undersøg kursuskataloget hjemmefra og prøv nogle fag af i starten inden du beslutter dig 2. Spis ude, nyd byen og tag på ture for at få den italienske kultur helt ind under huden 3. Lad dig ikke skræmme af mundtlige eksamener med udenadslære eller skriftlige eksamener i hånden på papir - det viser sig, at der ikke skal så meget til at bestå, som man går og tror
other_useful_info: Vi fandt vores lejlighed gennem portalen roomlessrent.com
most_rewarding: Ny viden, nye venner fra hele verden og masser af italiensk mad og kultur. Bologna er mega rar og hyggelig at bo i.
greatest_challenge: At finde bolig og eksamener med udenadslære - men det hele skal nok gå!
other_comments: Tag afsted!

crucial_aspects: Multiple aspects were crucial for my choice of Bologna as my exchange destination. First of all, University of Bologna is one of the oldest universities in the world and has a very positive reputation. This historical aspect made it interesting for me to visit the university. The faculty of economics also have several connections to my home university which ensured for me that the academic level was of a high standard. Moreover, the culture in Bologna, especially in terms of food and wine, of course was very attracting to me.
overall_comments: A wonderful city with many students. The city center is full of life any day of the week. The university is great. I can only recommend going to Bologna.
info_ease: I had no problems finding the necessary information. The website of the university is very informative.
arrival_assistance: I did not recieve any assistance
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: A wonderful city with many students. The city center is full of life any day of the week. The university is great. I can only recommend going to Bologna.
registration_process: Upon arrival I booked a Teams-meeting with the university, who registrered my arrival and provided me with the necessary information.
registration_help: Information about correct registration in courses, exams etc
registration_success: I was registrered in all classes that I wanted
registration_advice: At least at the faculty of economics one should not worry about getting the courses they want.
academics_comments: A wonderful city with many students. The city center is full of life any day of the week. The university is great. I can only recommend going to Bologna.
course_level: The level is very high and almost the same level as the University of Copehagen
teaching_comparison: We had some mandatory student presentations in some of the courses. Besides this the style of teaching was very similar
courses_enrolled: Advanced Behavioral Economics, Financial Market Regulation, Structural Macroeconometrics, Public Economics and Advanced Time Series Econometrics
recommended_courses: Structural Macroeconometrics was a very good course with a great professor. The course has a good balance between the theoretical part and applied part of econometrics.
unexpected_costs: The opening of the apartment I was supposed to move into upon arrival was postponed by 3 weeks
cost_comparison: Housing. As told earlier this is the only thing to be aware of if going on exhcange in Bologna. Housing is difficult to find and is more expensive than expected. However, look outside the city center and buy a bike upon arrival or use the bus. It is easy getting around in city
activities_available: A lot of different clubs for different sports. However, easier to arrange matches with people yourself.
activities_recommended: I did not make use of any of these. I found my own connections by going out in the city center and meeting up with some of the many international students
weekend_recommendations: Visit other cities in Italy. Going around by train is cheap and fast. Also some cheap flights to Sicilia is available from Bologna.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. No problems since the city and the university is very international
socializing_tips: Just go out and be open to new friendships. Ask some of your classmates if they want to go out and grab a beer
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The restaurant culture. The restaurants are fully booked every weekend with localsl. The atmosphere at all restaurants are great.
top3_advice: Make sure to leave space in your budget to eat out, visit other italian cities and start looking for housing in well advance
other_useful_info: Not besides what already told
most_rewarding: The many great experiences in the evenings and during trips which created friendships for life.

crucial_aspects: Well, I really liked the Italian culture beforehand, so I wanted to do my exchange in Italy. Also, I had never visited Bologna so it made a lot of sense to go there. Additionally, being located in the middle of Northern Italy, Bologna is a great point of departure for exploring. And then of course the food, the drinks, the football...
info_ease: It was all right. You can find most information on the website, and if in doubt, you are assigned an instructor who will help you. The bureaucracy of the university is a whole lot more loose in Italy, which you will have to get accustomed to.
arrival_assistance: I received a few mails from both KU and the university of Bologna with guidance which was sufficient.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process is pretty much just getting your courses pre-approved at Bologna University, just as you have to do it at KU.
registration_help: I found information on the website and then contacted my instructor.
registration_success: I was quite satisfied. Some of the classes I wanted were scheduled at the same time, so obviously I could not follow both. But other than that it was just fine.
registration_advice: If in doubt, contact your instructor. Besides, look at the website for information.
course_level: Even though I was a BA student, most of the classes I followed were second degree programs. But I did not think about it much. I did not find the classes particularity difficult.
teaching_comparison: The classes contained much fewer students at Bologna University compared to KU. Therefore, there was much more interaction among the students during the lessons opposed to merely a professor giving a lecture. At Bologna University in general, the professors appreciate active participation.
courses_enrolled: Humanitarian Communication Web Society and Globalization Urban Studies and Climate Change Visualizing the Italian Society
recommended_courses: Humanitarian Communication was definitely my favorite of the four. I will recommend everybody to follow that course. Urban Studies and Climate Change and Visualizing the Italian Society are pretty easy to get by, but not well taught either. Web Society and Globalization is quite interesting, but, for me, yield of the class was too narrow.
unexpected_costs: I did not encounter any unexpected cost, but it is quite expensive being on exchange as you want to use money all the time - whether on food, on drinks, on clothes, on experiences...
cost_comparison: Going to restaurants is a lot cheaper compared to Denmark. Much of the time, it is not more expensive to eat out than cooking food yourself.
activities_available: I did not participate in these, but there are a group of 'Erasmus tutors' who plan a lot of activities.
activities_recommended: I did not participate in these.
weekend_recommendations: Travel around Northern Italy. Go to Venice, Florence, Milano... Also, just have a good and easy time in Bologna - the city is very laid back.
culture_adjustment: It was all right. I was told beforehand that most Italians are reluctant to speak English, but this is not true.
socializing_tips: Many of the classes at the university include group work. Here, the professors appreciate when local students and exchange students work together, and I think it is a good opportunity to getting to know the locals.
cultural_challenges: I missed rye bread a lot. Also, they eat dinner very late in the evening, which is hard getting accustomed to.
culture_appreciated: I was surprised by Italians' openness. Everyone down in Bologna is very kind. Also, 1/4 of the population are university students. Therefore, there are a lot of young people - and they very modern and cool as well!
top3_advice: Get accommodation beforehand - and as early as possible If you have the time, explore other parts of Italy is well - Bologna's location is key Go to local places and act like a local 8)
other_useful_info: The professors might get a little mad if you call them by their name instead of calling them 'professor'.
most_rewarding: Being away from family and friends for a long time - in a good way.
greatest_challenge: Again, being away from family and friends, and, as such, being forced to seek new relations and make new habits

crucial_aspects: One of the important aspects for choosing Bologna as an exchange destination was that it had a great student life and good university vibes. It is a really nice city with a lot of students and student life in general in Bologna is really great.
overall_comments: My overall experience in Bologna was really great, it is a lovely city and general student life in the city is really good. The downside is that housing is quite expensive due to high demand and it can be a bit difficult to find a room. Furthermore, if you are on your bachelors (at least in economics) the amount of courses (in my experience) provided in english was a little limited.
info_ease: When I arrived in Italy it was a little bit difficult to find information and coordinate with the university regarding courses, attendance etc. But in the end it all worked out. The Italians are generally not as organized and fixed on deadlines and formality regarding course registration etc. as i'm used to in Denmark. But in the end it all works out, but patience can be important in the beginning.
arrival_assistance: You can go to the student desk, but in general it was a bit difficult to find information in the beginning, however it all worked out fine.
arrival_comments: In the beginning it was difficult to find information on courses etc., and the system for registration at the university was way too crowded so it took some time before I even officially got registered at my courses. But again everything worked out, and once your registered the UNIBO app is very good for information.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: My overall experience in Bologna was really great, it is a lovely city and general student life in the city is really good. The downside is that housing is quite expensive due to high demand and it can be a bit difficult to find a room. Furthermore, if you are on your bachelors (at least in economics) the amount of courses (in my experience) provided in english was a little limited.
registration_process: You had to register for your courses online and do a online check in at the University before you were originally registered. The problem was that check in was only open a few days a week at specific hours and it was very difficult to get through due to high demand / server problems. It seemed like they did not have the capacity to register everybody in the beginning. So the first weeks was a bit chaotic because of this I think.
registration_help: You could write professors of your courses and they were quite good at responding.
registration_success: Fine
registration_advice: Take it chill. The registration process can be a bit frustrating if your used to very organized systems, but it will work out in the end.
academics_comments: My overall experience in Bologna was really great, it is a lovely city and general student life in the city is really good. The downside is that housing is quite expensive due to high demand and it can be a bit difficult to find a room. Furthermore, if you are on your bachelors (at least in economics) the amount of courses (in my experience) provided in english was a little limited.
course_level: Course level was a little bit easier compared to what I am used to, but when you are on exchange it is quite nice. Also I think it depends on what courses you take, I also had one course which was quite difficult.
teaching_comparison: More lecture focused, where I am more used to exercise classes, which i prefer.
courses_enrolled: Public Finance and Public Policy, Corporate Finance, Introduction to Behavioral Economics, Industrial Organization.
recommended_courses: Introduction to Behavioral Economics and Industrial Organization were very interesting courses and well organized.
cost_comparison: Housing was more expensive than expected.
activities_available: I did not attend anything "through" the university but arranged stuff by my self with other exchange students. Trips, football, padel tennis, food, drinks etc.
activities_recommended: Going out to eat and enjoy the good Italian food. Go out on bars and enjoy the cheap espresso and approach the Italian lifestyle with siesta and aperitif
weekend_recommendations: Go on a lot of trips around Italy. Bologna is very well connected with a lot of cities around Italy. You can easily go to a lot of the Italian cities in North Italy like Verona, Venedig, Lake Como, Lake Garda, Firenze, Rome. Go visit some nature, a vineyard and maybe the dolomites. Take a trip to South Italy which is easily accecable with the train to Napoli which only take 3,5 hours.
culture_adjustment: Quite easy, the Italian culture is easy to adjust to and they speak english very well in Bologna, also there is a lot of other exchange students.
socializing_tips: Go out and enjoy the city, you will find a lot of other exchange students.
cultural_challenges: Nothing really.
culture_appreciated: The more laidback lifestyle, siesta, coffee and aperitif. Going out to eat way more often etc.
top3_advice: Don't stress about the practical paperwork etc. it will work out. Go and enjoy the city and think about the courses you take.
other_useful_info: no
most_rewarding: Meeting a lot of really nice people. Getting 3 months more of summer. Learning (some) Italian. Getting to travel around Italy a lot and eat a lot of good food.
greatest_challenge: I dont know.

crucial_aspects: The proximity of Italy's art history. Studying history, I see no better place than Bologna. I wanted to be at the physical location of the subject matter in my studies.
info_ease: A little difficult, but I survived through communication with other Erasmus-students who were equally confused.
arrival_assistance: Not much. You were left to yourself in terms of finding accommodation in which Bologna is absolutely impossible. I spent the first month from September 3rd to October 15th on looking for a place to sleep. The initial assistance was a video-check in with a few informations on how to operate the IT-systems. They helped.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Online check in with proof of flight ticket. Firstly you had to register online at AlmaRM and you had to fill out a study plan in accordance to your pre approved courses.
registration_help: A supporting e-mail for incoming students on the faculty of humanities. They replied quickly.
registration_success: Completely succesful after a few tries.
registration_advice: Ask other incoming exchange students and write the mobility assistance e-mail.
course_level: The art history of medieval and early modern art was of such high level, that I am now crucially inspired to learn everything about those subjects. Absolutely high level.
teaching_comparison: Way less Foucault and meta-talk that the North in their perpetual americanization has become so fond of. Instead, In Italy you approach the subjects more in the "ad fontes"-way, where you go directly to the source material of history and do not spend most of the time making methodological discussions. In some courses the teaching was a bit more relaxed and easy to process than in UCPH, but it highly depends on which course we are talking.
courses_enrolled: Early modern art history medieval and early renaissance art a survey of early modern italian and European architecture history of Italian cinema rome and the universal
recommended_courses: Early modern art history medieval and early renaissance art a survey of early modern italian and European architecture
unexpected_costs: nothing
cost_comparison: All met my expectations.
activities_available: Sport facilities out of town with tennis and swimming. Concerts and parties.
activities_recommended: Travel around at see the beauty of northern Italy. Go to concerts. I was annoyed by all the Erasmus-events because it felt like a summer camp for mindless cattle, but I think people in general liked them.
weekend_recommendations: See the Pinacoteca, the tomb of San Domenico, go to Modena, Parma, Firenze, Rome and see all of Italy's art!
culture_adjustment: Easy and nice. I tried to learn a bit of Italian and understand a fair amount now. The culture is more relaxed and pleasant than that of Denmark.
socializing_tips: Go to bars, smile, and talk.
cultural_challenges: Nothing.
culture_appreciated: The social usage of the city, the food, the coffee, the aperitivi.
top3_advice: Get your housing well in advance, and be very careful of scammers! appreciate the rich history of the area. Stay hydrated. They eat a lot of salt.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: The beauty of art in Italy, the learning of 2000-years' art history and falling in love with an italian woman.
greatest_challenge: The initial housing problem.
other_comments: Enjoy. It's a wonderful life if we can find it.
