crucial_aspects: To consider not just where I want to visit, but where I want to live and study. Consider how you want to spend your time and if the destination allows that. Consider your finances before going - some places are more expensive than others.
info_ease: I would say the Italian attitude to administration is a bit different than in Denmark, and therefore it took some "administrative days" to figure out everything.
arrival_assistance: I talked a lot to my fellow exchange goers, and also received some information about courses from the international coordinator.
arrival_comments: Honestly, it was difficult to figure out which courses i could attend.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Make sure you are accepted at UCPH first, but also get a confirmation from Bologna University. Then read the available information about checking in and picking courses. Check which courses you are allowed to have. Fill out the learning agreement and the study plan.
registration_help: I got questions answered by the International Coordinator.
registration_success: There wasn't room for me at one of the courses I wanted, and had to apply for a new approval from the home and host university. Other than that, I could attend the courses of my choice. In Bologna we could change the courses freely before registrering for the exam. But make sure the courses you end up with are approved.
registration_advice: Check courses early, and make sure there is room for you to take the course.
course_level: The level depends a lot on which courses you take. It is possible to take courses with a level similar to in Copenhagen, but also to take very easy courses.
teaching_comparison: More rote learning in general, less critical thinking.
courses_enrolled: Lifestyles and Health Outcomes, Health Systems, Introduction to Financial Derivatives and Hedging, International Economics, International Finance.
recommended_courses: International Economics and International Finance were interesting mostly because they were held with an Italian Master programme, meaning it was not only exchange students following the course.
unexpected_costs: Nothing unexpected. But it was a bit more expensive than i imagined. Going out for dinner (in a cheap place) was almost cheaper than cooking yourself.
cost_comparison: Grocery shopping was more expensive than imagined. It makes sense, therefore, to exploit that restaurants and bars are cheap.
activities_available: Honestly, i don't know. But remember that it was somewhat cumbersome to attend sports, since you needed a doctors approval. But didn't look into it more than that.
activities_recommended: Attending a language course could be a nice idea for some. Personally, it took up too much time for it to be a priority of mine, but i know people who benefitted from it.
weekend_recommendations: Go to other Italian cities by train. Really easy, and a nice way to explore Italian culture other than the student vibe in Bologna.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Pasta, wine, spritz and going out alot was a nice way for us to settle in and feeling welcome.
socializing_tips: Try to go out for dinner, coffee etc. alone. It is way easier to meet people alone or in small groups.
cultural_challenges: Sometimes Italians are a bit "much". They speak loudly, don't let you through and are always certain that they are right. So you get to practice your confidence.
culture_appreciated: People are very open in general, which makes it easy to make friends. Also the tradition of aperitivo and 'La Dolce Vita' vibes in general were just as I imagined it.
top3_advice: Check courses early and find accommodation before going. Prioritize aperitivo and money spend at restaurants. Be there for as long as you can! I went earlier, which meant I knew the city and some people before uni started, which was perfect to make you feel at home.
other_useful_info: Administrative stuff will be slow. Be patient. Write e-mails to people when needed. Use other exchange students for ranting.
most_rewarding: The people! The food! The vibe of going slow and not knowing exactly how you spend your money and time.
greatest_challenge: Finding out everything by yourself! But realizing that everything works out is very rewarding.

crucial_aspects: First and foremost due to my interest in Italian culture and architecture. Secondly, the University of Bologna is the oldest in Europe and due to the large number of students in Bologna, the city is also very politically active. I found this intriguing both personally and academically.
info_ease: When I first came to Bologna, there was a check-in for exchange students where I spoke to an employee from the university. It was good and informative. However, generally speaking, I will say that the university system, e.g. course schedules, class locations, exam info, has sometimes been lacking and difficult to see through, especially for exchange students who are not assisted very well in this regard.
arrival_assistance: As mentioned above, there was a brief phone conversation during the "Check-in". That was mostly about the Learning Agreement, how to fill out you study plan and where to print your university ID-cards (which is good), but not so informative of the day-to-day university life, how to enroll and attend classes etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: As previously mentioned, it was difficult to actually enroll for the courses and getting access to the course resources/schedule/readings etc. Even though my courses where accepted and on my learning agreement, it seemed as if no one knew I was attending them. I didn't receive any information or access to the course's online resources beforehand, which made the beginning a bit uncertain. Other than that, the registration process prior to arriving in Bologna was also very time consuming and frustrating. It seemed as if KU and UNIBO's systems didn't work together which caused me a lot of trouble in terms of getting my Learning Agreement accepted and signed. There was no issues with registration (my acceptance to UNIBO) but I wish there would have been a physical/online info meeting provided by the university close to the semester start, that I could have attended before going to Bologna.
registration_help: At UNIBO there was an exchange student help desk. I only used their email services, and I'm actually not sure if there is a physical office you can go to.
registration_success: Late in the process I found out that I had been accepted to the department of Language and Literature, so I had to redo my Learning Agreement because of a demand to take at least one course that is taught at that department.
registration_advice: Use the "Going abroad" help desks at KU for any questions you might have, and call the host university (if it's possible) if you have any trouble with registering. You can get extremely lost in emails, forms and different platforms, so I would highly recommend human contact when sorting out your exchange.
course_level: I had the opportunity to take elective MA-courses even though I'm a BA student. So I did both, but a difference in difficulty was not noticeable.
teaching_comparison: Less group work and seminars, more lectures. Bigger focus on historical events and the state of 'real life' and less emphasis on theory. A more relaxed attitude towards exams and, thus, less information about exams. No "studieordning" for the courses as we have at UCPH, meaning less structure and more room for the professor and the students to shape the teaching underway.
courses_enrolled: Women's Movements Worldwide Introduction to Italian Culture Gender Studies Global Diasporas. Cultures, Identities and Politics. Semiotics of Conflict
recommended_courses: Global Diasporas and Semiotics of Conflict were both relevant, better-structured classes with really interesting and modern theory.
unexpected_costs: No costs were unexpected. But living costs in general were higher than I anticipated.
cost_comparison: Food was more expensive.
activities_available: There is all kinds of things going on. Different sport teams, student organisations, political activism, readings and seminars (for example I went to a seminar with Judith Butler who visited the university). You just have to seek the events and ask around if there's something you wish to participate in.
activities_recommended: Whatever you're into. I really liked the political talks and demos, and some of the free seminars you can attend as a student.
weekend_recommendations: Visit restaurants (restaurants with traditional food in Bologna is generally cheap and good). Take the train and go on small trips. Get out of the city or seek green spaces to clear your mind.
culture_adjustment: I would say it's not difficult if you're genuinely interested in understanding and adjusting to the culture.
cultural_challenges: The daily rhytm (Siesta from about 13-16).
culture_appreciated: The socialness and food culture.
top3_advice: Make a budget and try to keep it. Be patient with the university system and have faith that your classes, exams etc. will work out well. Come with an open mindset and seize new opportunities when they occur.
other_useful_info: If you wish to do the Italian classes that are provided by the university, you must do a language placement test beforehand.
most_rewarding: Getting to know a new culture on a deeper level, making international friends and just living abroad in general.
greatest_challenge: University bureaucracy.

crucial_aspects: I chose Bologna because I wanted to go to Italy and experience the culture and thought that doing so in a "smaller" city would be better.
info_ease: Easy, the University of Bologna is not super helpful, but they have the necessary information written online.
arrival_assistance: Not much, I used the university's website
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I arrived early and hence had no problem checking in, which is done through an online platform were you videochat with a coordinator. I know others had some trouble, because of limited capacity each day, and therefore had to try multiple times before succeeding.
registration_help: Required information was available on the website and through mails sent to me.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted, no problems at all.
registration_advice: Either arrive early, or don't stress. I don't think it matters when you do, you will still get checked in from your day of arrival, but I'm not entirely sure.
course_level: In general, I found the courses to be easier than in Copenhagen. The exams I did were focused on the slides presented and were more tuned toward remembering the material.
teaching_comparison: Very similar. Lectures are often three hours though.
courses_enrolled: Asset Management and Transition Risk Climate Macroeconomics and Finance Introduction to Financial Derivatives and Hedging Machine Learning for Economists Market Microstructure and Algorithmic Trading
recommended_courses: I found "Asset Management and Transition Risk", "Climate Macroeconomics and Finance" and "Introduction to Financial Derivatives and Hedging" to be fairly straightforward. The lectures are not particularly good, but I found this to be a general thing. As for "Machine Learning for Economists" and "Market Microstructure and Algorithmic Trading" both require some work to pass and when I did them I needed to hand in a group project in the end, which is nice since you get to work with either local students or other exchange students but also requires to put up some work.
unexpected_costs: Not any. I used more money on eating out than I initially thought I would.
cost_comparison: Travelling in Italy, especially accommodation was more expensive than I thought it would be.
activities_available: Not sure of all, but at least some sports clubs were available.
activities_recommended: Can't recommend any, since I haven't tried them.
weekend_recommendations: Travel around in Italy. High-speed trains are really good in Italy and can be cheap if you order in well enough in advance. Also, Flixbus is very cheap and fairly reliable. Other than that Bologna is a really nice city to spend time in. Be sure to check out the hills south of the city for hikes in green surroundings and nice views.
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: I did courses with group work, through which I met some local students.
cultural_challenges: Not any really. Though Italians do have almost "religious" traditions about their food, but they immediately know you're not Italian, and most of the time just joke about it.
culture_appreciated: Definitely the food and the more laid-back attitude towards life. Also, the whole culture around going out and being outside in cafees with friends is really cool, even in the winter.
top3_advice: Make sure you bring enough money to go out and enjoy the city's restaurants and cafes, as well as traveling. Don't do courses that take up too much of your time. Focus on enjoying life. Find your accommodation well in advance. I found accommodation to be more important than I thought I would.
other_useful_info: No, not other than what is already mentioned.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people and the experience of living in another country with a different culture.
greatest_challenge: Didn't have any major challenges. Perhaps prioritizing what to spend my money on :p

crucial_aspects: The culture, the climate and the university.
overall_comments: I enjoyed the study abroad very much, however the level of education was lower than expected and much lower then CPH.
info_ease: it was a very well organized systems in terms of course catalogue, but assistance with everything else was difficult to get a hold on and contact person didnt take a lot of responsiblity, they sent you to the next office and so on - problem with organisation and help desk in generall.
arrival_assistance: I recieved a welcome mail and a guide to check in.
arrival_comments: The check in process was essay, however I was a bit strange to do everything through Zoom.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I enjoyed the study abroad very much, however the level of education was lower than expected and much lower then CPH.
registration_process: The registration process was run through bolognas internal site ALMA RM, where I made a profil and recieved mails with the process from Bologna. I was also at a welcome day with information regarding the courses in end of january, before I started the semester a few weeks later.
registration_help: I was provided with an mail of the exchange cordinator and the university has a site in the internal platfrom where there is Zoom office hours for contacting the exchange student help desk.
registration_success: It was nicely arranged in terms of the course catalgoue, however I had a lot of challenges beacuse I had to do my Learning agreement over many times, because a few courses weren't avalible in the end, for example one course of 3 Credits said on the site that the language was in English, however it was in Italian and beacuse of this I had to find a lot of other courses to make the "math" go up for the 30 credits.
registration_advice: Check up on you new university mail, start early and accept that there are many exchange students in bologna so be patient.
academics_comments: I enjoyed the study abroad very much, however the level of education was lower than expected and much lower then CPH.
course_level: I have found that the academic standards at the University of Bologna are somewhat lower than I expected. However, the quality of education varies significantly across different subjects. I was surprised to encounter some courses where the academic level and the instructors' proficiency in English were disappointingly low.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style at the University of Bologna was more traditional compared to the University of Copenhagen. However, in some aspects, such as preparation and the amount of reading required for each class, it was quite similar to what I experienced at Copenhagen. The biggest difference I noticed was the variation in teaching methods and academic levels across different courses. At Copenhagen, the level of difficulty is more consistent, and the teaching methods within my field are more aligned across different subjects and instructors.
courses_enrolled: 1. Semiotics of Memory 2. Cultural Mangements of Events. 3. History of Mass Communication 4. Italian Pop Culture
recommended_courses: I found the course "Semiotics of Memory" particularly fascinating, especially for those interested in language and modern history. The instructor was highly skilled, and the course offered valuable insights into Italian culture through discussions on cultural heritage. Another intriguing course was "Italian Pop Culture." The instructor's expertise made it engaging, and topics such as the North-South divide in Italy, along with analyses of Italian culture through film and music, provided a theoretical understanding of Italian culture. These subjects were compelling and enriched my appreciation of the complexities of Italian society.
unexpected_costs: There weren't any unexpected cost I encountered, however the prices at the supermarcet was more expensive then excepted.
cost_comparison: It was less expensive to drink cofee at cafes then expected but more expensive to by groceries.
activities_available: There were different cultural events avalible such as a talk from Judith Butler, however the spaces was a general problem – they dont have enough tickets for sutdents, chairs a courses, and bathrooms.
activities_recommended: I would reccomend to go to cultural events such as the film festival in june, however I experienced that many of the non academic activites were from the city itself and not the university.
weekend_recommendations: I recommend going to resturants, going hiking in some of the parks nearby, going to musueums (most of them are free of charge for students) and going for long walks in the beautiful old streets.
culture_adjustment: Initially, the language barrier posed a significant challenge for me. Navigating daily life, from simple conversations to understanding signs and instructions, was quite demanding. This made the early stages of my time in Italy somewhat overwhelming. However, this challenge also presented an opportunity. I was motivated to learn some Italian, which turned out to be incredibly rewarding. Not only did it help me navigate everyday situations more effectively, but it also enriched my overall experience in Italy. Learning the language allowed me to better understand and appreciate the culture, communicate with locals, and integrate more seamlessly into daily life.
socializing_tips: As my Italian improved, I found it easier to make friends and and enjoy the local culture. This progress was gratifying and made my time in Italy more enjoyable and fulfilling. Additionally, the effort I put into learning Italian was appreciated by the people I interacted with, fostering a more supportive and inclusive environment - learn a little bit of italian must be my main tip.
cultural_challenges: Lanaguage barrier as mentioned above.
culture_appreciated: I love the Italians' relaxed approach to life and their ability to go out and enjoy themselves instead of staying at home. This cultural trait has been a refreshing change for me. The emphasis on socializing, spending time with friends and family, and savoring the simple pleasures of life, like a leisurely meal or a stroll through the city, has been inspiring. It has taught me the value of balancing work and relaxation, and I have come to appreciate the joy of living in the moment and embracing a more laid-back lifestyle.
top3_advice: Start Early in Finding Accommodation: Housing in Bologna can be competitive, so begin your search well in advance. This will give you more options and a better chance of securing a place that suits your needs and budget. Consider reaching out to student housing services, exploring online platforms, and connecting with current students for recommendations. Learn Some Italian: Even a basic understanding of Italian will greatly enhance your experience. It will help you navigate daily life, communicate with locals, and integrate more fully into the culture. Taking some language classes before you arrive or during your stay can make a significant difference. Be Prepared for Changes and Flexibility: Academic schedules and course offerings can change, and things may not always go as planned. Embrace this flexibility and be ready to adapt. This mindset will help you make the most of unexpected opportunities and handle any challenges that arise with a positive attitude.
other_useful_info: Make sure you are placed in the correct academic institute that aligns with your study direction at home. This can significantly impact the courses available to you and ensure that they complement your academic goals. Checking this beforehand will help you select relevant and beneficial courses that support your degree requirements.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding aspect was the boost in confidence I gained from adapting and meeting new people and learning new systems, a new language, and studying in a different way, yet I was able to adapt and still achieve both academic and personal goals
greatest_challenge: My biggest challenge was feeling lonely at the beginning, not knowing anyone in a new place. It takes courage to meet new people, and it's not always easy, but it's rewarding. Building new relationships takes time and effort, but putting yourself out there gradually pays off in creating meaningful connections.

crucial_aspects: The University of Bologna is one of the best in Europe. The cultural experiences in Italy are fantastic and getting to enjoy that for many months was a great motivator.
info_ease: Relatively easy. UCPH made it fairly easy to understand, though the University of Bologna website and student services could really do with a bit of an upgrade since getting any information out of them is a very long process that rarely yields any fruit.
arrival_assistance: I was able to very quickly verify my having arrived via web call with the university and the instructions on how to get my student ID card that same day were incredibly quick. This made it very easy to get everything sorted out.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was very easy. You simply show your passport, plane ticket (or other mode of arrival), and your Erasmus letter on an online video chat with the university international student office and they get you set up on the spot. You then receive an email with the information to get your student ID card from a machine in one of several locations throughout the city so it is very convenient.
registration_help: The UCPH office was very helpful when it came to figuring things out on the Danish end. It was less helpful in Italy, but that is likely because they get an intensive amount of Erasmus students and they have less budget and administrative capacity. So long as you come early and plan ahead I would say that most people will be fine, but it is not as seamless an experience as in Denmark.
registration_success: Very successful. I had to change schedules a few times to ensure that the OLA could be approved by both Bologna and Copenhagen, but at the end of the day it was fine since I was still able to find classes that were to my liking and that both universities would approve.
registration_advice: I would recommend that they come early, plan ahead, and ensure that they have a conversation with UCPH ahead of time about how OLA might work with them and at other institutions. Try to call Bologna ahead of time to get an over the phone explanation of how the system works since you are not likely to get a response or anything via email unless it is one of those mass sent emails which does have information but sometimes they raise more questions than they answer.
course_level: I had to take one 10 ECTS BA course because it fell under the category required by Bologna to take given the deal they have with UCPH as the credits had to fall under economics and management. The rest I was able to sort out in one way or another to get 16 ECTS under what they wanted and then another 16 ECTS of what I wanted so that the contract was split 50-50 and they would sign off on it. It is a big annoying since UCPH signed off on all the courses that I wanted and pre-approved them, but the problem was with Bologna's system and requirements that I do what they wanted to study here citing an agreement with UCPH.
teaching_comparison: Bologna has a more traditional lecture system like in both universities around the world with only one professor instead of the two professor model with course seminars in my program at UCPH. I FAR in a way prefer the way that Bologna does things since it is just more old school and what I prefer as I feel that the classes are more meaningful and there is far less fluff in the materials and no pointless group exercises that do not bring me any sort of value.
courses_enrolled: 1. History and international Relations of The Middle East 2. Politics of European Institutions 3. Global Connections: A Long-Term History 4. Central Banking and Monetary Policy
recommended_courses: I recommend that they take half of their credits as required by the University of Bologna and the other half just take whatever they want that they can get pre-approval one. It is a pretty relaxed atmosphere down here so you have a ton of options in English and even other languages.
unexpected_costs: Having to pay an agency to help me find a place since it is impossible to find a place. That was a cost of €250 euros which was very expensive, but it is one of the only ways to help you find a cheap place in Bologna.
cost_comparison: Everything here is far less expensive than in Denmark with the same if not greater quality. So the cost of living is definitely a lot lower which makes it more budget friendly for students. The housing is still expensive by Italian standards and especially given the EU Erasmus grant, but it is still more affordable than in Denmark.
activities_available: Tons of things from politics to reading to history to science. I do not tend to go to stuff like that, but they are there for those that like them.
activities_recommended: Everything the city has to offer in terms of culture and culinary experiences. Bologna is a fantastic city and I highly recommend it to everyone. It is a town where you can make a ton of university friends or just relax on your own and enjoy la dolce vita. It is really up to you.
weekend_recommendations: There is a ton of historical things to see in the Emilia-Romagna region where Bologna is located. Cities like Modena, Parma, Ferrara, and Rimini are in the region and they are fantastic cities which beautiful architecture and histories. There is the Adriatic Sea by Rimini, and you can take a day trip to San Marino which is a country completely surrounded by Italy. Milan, Venice, Padua, and Florence are also fairly close to Bologna and easy to see in a day. And while Rome is further away you can get very cheap tickets on a bus to go see the city.
culture_adjustment: Extremely easy. Italians are a very welcoming people and it is a very loving culture.
cultural_challenges: None. I loved it here and it was far easier to get used to here than Denmark.
culture_appreciated: The hospitality. The food. The warmth and friendliness of the people. And their openmindness.
top3_advice: 1. Come early to find a place 2. Keep an open mind as the culture is different from Denmark 3. Relax and enjoy it a bit more. Do not stress as much as you would in other places. Try to let the feeling carry you since the bureaucracy is a lot to handle, but you need to take it in strides.
other_useful_info: NA
most_rewarding: Being able to live in a place like Italy for so many months and being able to enjoy its culture in a way that I might never again get to do in my life given work and responsibilities is a memory that I will cherish forever. It was not so much the classes but everything surrounding my time living in Italy that has made it one of the most memorable experiences of my life.
greatest_challenge: Sort out housing (please refer to above)
other_comments: I encourage everyone who wants to do Erasmus to consider Italy, and Bologna in particular. You will love it here.

crucial_aspects: My wish was to go someplace different from where I usually attend the university - in Denmark. I think that the culture in the South of Europe is very different from ours - so I wanted to explore something new. Also, Bologna is very much a student city and the medium size of the city was also appealing to me. And of course the weather also drew me there.
info_ease: It was alright - especially since I could talk to a lot of other Erasmus students, and we could help each other.
arrival_assistance: I don't think that I received any assistance - perhaps some e-mails!
arrival_comments: It was very confusing - having to get to know a whole new system - but you figure it out along the way!
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process is very relaxed in Bologna - you registrate during the fall, and you get the opportunity of trying out different courses before signing up for them.
registration_help: I think that there was a student desk. Mostly, I just scrolled around on the main websites for the university - those are helpful.
registration_success: Succesful!
registration_advice: Don't stress about not having everything in order in good time - Italy is not that organized, so deal with things as they come.
course_level: The difficulty of the courses depended very much of the professor. A MA course is not necessarily more difficult than a BA course - but can be. Overall, more easy than in Denmark - but you still need to put in effort to get through the courses.
teaching_comparison: We had a lot of lectures and no class teaching. I like the style in Denmark more, but it was a lot of fun to try out something different.
courses_enrolled: BA course: Philosophy of Law 9 credits BA course: Comparative Constitutionalism 9 credits MA course: Corporate Law 6 credits MA course: International and Transnational Civil Litigation 6 credits
recommended_courses: Philosophy of Law and Comparative Constitutionalism. Great teachers. Interesting courses! The exam type in Comparative Constitutionalism was very nice - I kind of enjoyed writing those papers on very interesting topics even though I stressed about it. Notice that Philosophy of Law requires more effort - it is an oral exam, and you need to know your stuff if you want to obtain a good grade.
unexpected_costs: When I arrived, I had to buy a duvet, sheets, etc.
cost_comparison: Food and drinks are cheap! Put some money aside for making trips also.
activities_available: Language courses. My roomies did choir. But mostly you don't do activities that the university arrange - people mostly attend activities that the Erasmus network organizes!
activities_recommended: I did not attend any activities as such at the university. But I attended a lot of social activities with the Erasmus network - can recommend!
weekend_recommendations: First of all, get to know the city. It is a great city with a lot of great restaurants and bars. Make sure to go to San Luca, and do hiking in the surrounding areas! Also, do trips! I can really recommend Napoli, Verona, Lucca, and Firenze.
culture_adjustment: I found it quite easy - italian people are very welcoming. One advice would be to try and learn the language.
socializing_tips: The most easy one would be to live with italian people. Other tips: Take courses with italian students. Make conversation in the streets at aperitivo time or in bars.
cultural_challenges: In Denmark, we have a lot of structure. They don't have that in Italy. Can be both an advantage and a challenge. Also, the way things work in the university is very different - you have to get used to that.
culture_appreciated: A lot of life in the city at all times of the day and at any time of the year. The Italian people have a great spirit, and you should definitely spend much time just hanging with your friends for an Aperol in the afternoon and going to restaurants at night. Also, so much culture and history to explore in this country.
top3_advice: 1. Search for housing in good time. 2. Arrive a bit before the courses at the university begins - so that you have time to get to know and explore the city and meet new people in advance. 3. Do not stress about not having things in order - in Italy things take time and be prepared that some things will be delayed.
other_useful_info: Try to study a bit during the semester so that you won't be too stressed when the exams get close.
most_rewarding: Meeting new friends from all around Europe. Exploring a new culture - Bologna is an amazing city to live in and has that Italian vibe. Exploring the country - there are endless opportunities on going on different trips.
greatest_challenge: It was challenging having the courses in English - I was not used to that, but I like this challenge and gained a lot from it. Also, I think I should have taken a bit more time to be by myself - it is exhausting to settle in a new city not knowing anyone.

info_ease: Unibo has a great site for general information. Google 'unibo onlime mobility' and you can find a lot. Finding faculty specific information was difficult.

registration_process: At Unibo you register for exams, not courses. You register for the exams a few week before they take place. In order to register for the exam you have to put the courses in the study plan. Only those courses in the course catalog that have a published time table are available for registration. Unibo post these time tables rather late, so it can be difficult to start early. For the Learning Agreement there are different rules according to faculty that dictate which courses you are allowed to take.
registration_help: You can contact your faculties incoming student desk via email. In my experience they were slow in supply.
registration_success: It was a difficult process but in the end we found a solution so i could take the courses i wanted.
registration_advice: Contact your specific faculty ahead of time and ask if there are specific rules for that faculty. For example bachelor/undergraduate econ student are not allowed to take master/graduate courses - this rule does not apply to other faculties, that i know of.
academics_comments: Go go go
course_level: In general the level is lower than at UCPH, but can vary from course to course. It is easier to get a high grade than at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: They use slides like we are use to. In none of my courses did we have assigment during the duration of the course. But i know that in many courses student must do a presentation during the course as part of the final grade. The information on grading and exam style can be found in the course catalog. Some courses last from september to december with exam either in december or january Some courses last from september to october with exam in october Some courses last from november to december with exam in december/january
courses_enrolled: Intro to python for economists (6 ECTS, graduate course) International finance (6 ECTS, graduate course) International Economics (6 ECTS, graduate course) Health economics and policies in low and middel income countries (6 ECTS, graduate course) Public economics (8 ECTS, undergraduate course)

unexpected_costs: Fees from my housing company, because i did not read my contract correctly
cost_comparison: drinks were less expensive than in Denmark. Groceries were not as inexpensive as expected.
activities_available: A lot of people used ESN Bologna, who organized a lot of fun things for exchange students. Follow them on instagram.
activities_recommended: Travel. Bologna is perfectly placed to visit a lot of the great italian cities. Modena, Parma, Ravenna, Ferrara, Siena, Verona, Venice, Rome, Rimini
weekend_recommendations: See the sites.

socializing_tips: Get a drink at Piazza Verdi - there are always a lot of students. And the italians are super friendly
cultural_challenges: Not all italians speak english. They can be very stubborn
culture_appreciated: Their friendliness and generosity
top3_advice: Enjoy the city - don't worry too much about school. Walk around a lot and get to know every street take it easy - everything works out in the end
other_useful_info: Learn a little italian - it is fun and the people will be more sympathetic towards you if you show interest and try.
most_rewarding: The friends i got and the way that Bologna feels like home now.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne til udlandet og læse for at prøve at bo i et andet land og opleve en anden kultur, og siden jeg havde boet i Italien før dette ophold, så ville jeg også gerne forbedre mit italienske sprogniveau og prøve at læse der. Jeg havde også akademiske interesse for øje, såsom at læse om Dante i landet han er fra, og prøve at have tilvalg, der passede til den italienske kultur og det akademiske miljø.
info_ease: Ret svært - Mobilitetskontoret hos Bologna svarede aldrig på ens henvendelser, og generelt var der ret dårligt kommunikation. Jeg måtte vente af flere omgange om morgenen på zoom for at få fat i min koordinator, og indtil da anede jeg ingenting. Informationen var ikke rigtigt givet på forhånd, jeg måtte selv opsøge den.
arrival_assistance: De holdte et zoom møde inden mobiliteten startede, men det var ret generelt og vagt. Da vi ankom skulle vi tjekke ind, men åbningen for dette var så kort at de fleste slet ikke nåede igennem. Det tog mig tre forsøg på tre dage for at komme igennem, og jeg måtte få mast nogle spørgsmål ind her, fordi kontoret for internationale studerende næsten aldrig havde åbent.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Besværlig. Man skal lave en studieplan, men det er faktisk lidt bøvlet at regne ud hvordan, fordi Bologna har rigtigt mange forskellige studenterportaler. Først skulle man checke ind, så sørge for at få printet sit studiekort, hvilket var nemt nok, og så kunne man udfylde sin studieplan. Men man kunne ikke udfylde den før man havde tjekket ind, hvilket betød jeg endte med at udfylde min plan meget kort før kurserne begyndte.
registration_help: Jeg fik fat i min koordinator på zoom, men kontoret svarer ikke på e-mails. Det virker til de er meget overvældet i den periode hvor alle udvekslingseleverne ankommer.
registration_success: Det lykkedes fint, når jeg først var inde i systemet kunne jeg finde mine fag på deres kodenummer.
registration_advice: Sørg for at checke ind hurtigst muligt og udfyld din studieplan hurtigst muligt. Det er egentligt ikke svært at gøre, da du i princippet kan møde op til de fleste fag selvom du ikke er tilmeldt, så du skal ikke have styr på det hele på en gang.
course_level: Jeg fik på en eller anden måde indtrykket af, at jeg kun kunne tage fag på bachelor-niveau. Alle andre Erasmus elever jeg mødte, der var på deres Bachelor to Master fag på engelsk. Jeg endte med 75% af mine fag var på italiensk, og det gjorde det akademiske arbejde noget tungere end det nok behøvede at være. Jeg bestod og fik også fine karakterer, men det lykkedes også mest fordi jeg kunne lidt italiensk før og også tog et italiensk kursus mens jeg var der.
teaching_comparison: Det er meget forskelligt fra professor til professor. Ofte er det noget kaotisk. Nogle brugte powerpoints, hvilket hjalp, men en af mine undervisere snakkede bare frit. Det er ret anderledes end i København hvor strukturen er noget mere stringent, og hvor det også er nemmere at finde ud af hvad man skal læse hvornår osv.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Italian Culture, Cinema e Letteratura, Letteratura e Critica Dantesca og Letteratura Italiana Contemporanea
recommended_courses: Introduction to Italian Culture er lavet til Erasmus studerende, så det er ret ligetil og formidlet meget overkommeligt. De andre fag er svære, hvis ikke man har noget italiensk i rygsækken.
unexpected_costs: Ikke andre end at huslejen var urimeligt dyr.
cost_comparison: Huslejen - Jeg endte med at bo på et kollegie udenfor byen, der var privatejet. Huslejen var latterligt dyr, men det var det eneste jeg havde tilbage - jeg har hørt om mange der tog hjem fordi det var umuligt at finde et sted at bo. Jeg kan ikke understrege nok at boligsituationen i Bologna er meget slem, og man skal være ude i rigtig god tid og gravende for at finde noget. Det kan lykkedes, kender mange det lykkedes for, men det gjorde det ikke for mig.
activities_available: Jeg tror ikke det var forbundet med universitetet direkte, men der er nogle store organisationer såsom ESN og IC, der arrangerer turer og begivenheder for Erasmus studerende. Det kan varmt anbefales, det er ofte virkeligt sjovt og man møder mange andre elever. Det er ikke alle arrangementer der er lige gode, men der er nogle barer og foreninger der samarbejder med dem.
activities_recommended: Tag med på turene som ESN og IC holder, for her kan man møde folk. Der er skiture og dagsrejser rundt omkring i Italien, og de er rimeligt prissat. Ellers vil jeg sige man skal prøve at komme lidt omkring i nærområdet, der er så mange byer tæt på Bologna der er værd at se. Om sommeren kan man tage på stranden og om vinteren på skiferie.
weekend_recommendations: Der er virkeligt mange gode barer og restauranter i Bologna, hvilket nok næppe er en overraskelse. Piazza Verdi der ligger ved universitetet er lidt et samlingspunkt for studerende. Der er også mange klubber hvis man er til den slags. Ellers i ferierne rejste jeg selv til andre byer eller lignende.
culture_adjustment: Til tider svært ift. sprogforskelle og undervisningsformer, men for det meste rimeligt ligetil. Der er mange ting ved selve skolesystemet der er anderledes, men synes hurtigt man får en god hverdag i Italien.
cultural_challenges: Måske mest undervisningen og karaktersystemet. Timerne ligger helt anderledes på dagen og man læser slet ikke forberedelsesting som man gør i Danmark. Derudover er universitet spredt for alle vinde, så jeg endte med at løbe fra time til time. Men kulturelle forskelle ellers ikke rigtigt, man skal bare nyde tilværelsen har et andet tempo.
culture_appreciated: Det sociale i Italien er skønt, og self. det kulturelle. Man ender ofte med en apperitivo efter skole eller lignende, og så er der meget meget hyggeligt og smukt. Bologna specifikt har et meget ungt miljø fordi det er en studieby, så man føler sig ikke helt på bar bund.
top3_advice: Hold hovedet koldt, gør dit bedste og nyd det.
other_useful_info: Tror jeg har fået uddybet det meste ovenfor.
most_rewarding: Jeg har fået venner for livet og virkeligt også erfaret at blive mere hårdfør. Når man står i et andet land og skal få tingene til at hænge sammen selv så lærer man at kaste sig ud i det.
greatest_challenge: Eksaminerne var ekstremt svære fordi de var på italiensk. Og det kan være helt utroligt hårdt. Alt er anderledes, ens familie og venner er langt væk, og man aner ikke hvordan tingene fungerer. Det kræver lidt koldt vand i blodet. Og så erfarede jeg selv at jeg var meget bekymret og lidt små ensom i begyndelsen, men så snart man begynder at møde andre studerende og får nye oplevelser bliver det virkeligt skønt.

In Bologna, I would take a course in FICO Eataly World, where theres both wine tastings, pasta courses, mortadella courses etc. which is a nice experience. I would also recommend go hiking. Mountains are just outside Bologna and are very beautiful for watching sunsets and picnics, and the famous Via Degli Dei (rout of Gods) is a hike from the center of Bologna to Florence (so a 4-7 day hiking trip). Finally, take the time to stand in line to eat at "Sfoglia Rina", it is very very good pasta.
culture_adjustment: It was fine. Italy is not that different, however not all Italians outside of the university understand or speak English, so knowing some basic phrases is very nice. Further, Italians are not very strict about times, so they're often late by 10-60 minutes, so this is something I should get used to.
socializing_tips: I would definitely take some italian courses, Babbel is a great platform to do so, even though it cost a bit, I think it is worth it. Italians love when other people try to learn their language and are happy to help! I would also sign up for the social stuff through the Erasmus network to get to know people.
cultural_challenges: The only big difference is the language. It is very difficult to socialize with the locals, and they're not always so good at switching to english, when international people are around. This could sometimes make me feel a bit lonely. However, I did not take any courses at the university, so this experience is solely from the research group I was in.
culture_appreciated: I really enjoyed the aperitivo concept of grapping a drink or beer after work/school. The entire city does this, which means that from 16-18 there's people siting outside at every bar having a drink. It is just a very nice energy and atmosphere in the city and I really enjoyed this concept instead of going directly home every day.
top3_advice: I would definitely take Italian courses before going! It just give a way better understanding. I would also seek help to find a place to live. If possible, go there yourself to make sure to avoid scammers. If you know someone in Bologna, or somebody who speaks Italian, make them help you, as not everybody understand English.
other_useful_info: I think most of it has already been mentioned.
most_rewarding: I really enjoyed living in Bologna, and it was very rewarding to try to live abroad in general, but I also think Bologna is perfect for this. I also tried to live with roomies which I have never done before, and I think this was a very great experience.
greatest_challenge: It was very mentally challenging to be social. As I didn't take any courses but only did my master's thesis in a research group, I was surrounded by the same people all the time. academics_comments: I would rate my overall study abroad experience in Bologna as highly positive. It was an enriching opportunity that allowed me to grow academically, culturally, and personally. I faced some challenges, such as adapting to a new education system and cultural differences, but these experiences helped me become more independent and adaptable. Overall, it was a transformative experience that I would highly recommend to others.
course_level: The level of courses at the University of Bologna was generally high, aligning with the expectations of an established institution. As a law student, I found the courses to be challenging and intellectually stimulating, with a focus on both foundational principles and more specialized topics in law. The level of difficulty varied depending on the professor and the subject, but overall, the academic rigor was consistent.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style at the University of Bologna was quite different from what I experienced at the University of Copenhagen. At my home university, I was used to a more interactive, seminar-based approach with a lot of group discussions, presentations, and student participation. In contrast, the teaching style at Bologna leaned more towards traditional lectures; more old style. However, the professors at Bologna were approachable, and there were some courses that included practical case studies or debates, which made the experience more engaging. Overall, I found the Bologna teaching style to be more formal and lecture-oriented, while my home university had a more collaborative and discussion-based approach.

recommended_courses: I would especially recommend the courses European Legal History to future exchange students. European Legal History offers a unique perspective on the development of European legal systems with a very qualified professor.

cost_comparison: I was surprised to find that groceries, especially fresh produce and local specialties like cheese and olive oil, were more expensive than I anticipated in Bologna. On the other hand, eating out at casual restaurants or pizzerias was generally less expensive than I expected, especially in comparison to prices in Copenhagen. Public transportation costs were also reasonable, but I was surprised by the higher upfront cost of setting up utilities and housing deposits. Overall, the cost of living in Bologna was manageable, but certain everyday items did take me by surprise.
activities_available: The University of Bologna offered a variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities. The Erasmus Student Network organized events like city tours, parties, and cultural outings, while sports facilities provided options for football, and running.
activities_recommended: I would recommend exploring Bologna’s local attractions and engaging with the city’s vibrant cultural scene. Additionally, exploring the authentic Italian cuisine in local trattorias provides a immersive experience.
weekend_recommendations: I recommend visiting nearby cities and exploring Italy’s rich culture on weekends. Cities like Modena, Parma, and Padova are just a short train ride away and offer amazing art, architecture, and history.
culture_adjustment: Adjusting to the local culture in Bologna was relatively easy, as Italians are generally welcoming and proud of their culture. The slower pace of life and focus on socializing over meals was a pleasant change and allowed me to connect with locals more deeply. While there were a few cultural differences, such as the more formal approach to some social interactions, the friendly atmosphere made it easy to adapt. Learning a bit of Italian also helped with everyday communication and deepened my cultural immersion. Overall, it was an enriching experience, and I felt comfortable adjusting to Bologna’s lifestyle.
socializing_tips: To socialize with local students in Bologna, I recommend starting by attending university events or social gatherings, as these are great opportunities to meet people in a casual setting. Joining student clubs or sports teams is another excellent way to make connections.
cultural_challenges: One cultural difference I found challenging was the slower pace of life in Italy, especially when it came to service in restaurants and shops. Things tend to move at a more relaxed speed, which can feel frustrating at first if you're used to a faster pace. Another adjustment was the more formal approach to social interactions in certain situations, such as addressing people by their titles or using formal language.
culture_appreciated: I most appreciated the Italian focus on food, where meals are not just about eating but also about socializing and enjoying the moment. The sense of community and the importance placed on family and friendships also stood out to me, creating a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Lastly, the rich history and cultural heritage of Bologna itself, with its beautiful architecture and vibrant student life, made the experience truly special.
top3_advice: Start your housing search early. Embrace the local culture. Be flexible with academics, since the teaching style may be more lecture-based and formal than what you're used to.
other_useful_info: Yes! One important tip is to familiarize yourself with the Italian bureaucracy early on. Bologna is a student-friendly city, but be mindful of the busy academic periods, as the city can get crowded, and accommodations can - as mentioned - be hard to find.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was immersing myself in Italian culture, both academically and socially, and trying to live abroad for 5 month.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was adjusting to the slower pace of life, especially when it came to bureaucracy and service, which took longer than I was used to.

crucial_aspects: Bologna is a great city for studying. It is a young city and like Aarhus in size. Moreover, the train connections to cities like Milan, Florence, Naples, Rome and many more are good, which means, that there are many cultural opportunities nearby.
info_ease: The websites concerning exchange information and courses are not always intuitive, but once you get to know them, you will know, where to find the information, you need. University of Bologna also have an e-mail for incoming students, but the answer time might vary.
arrival_assistance: I received a couple of e-mails on, how to check-in and get a study-ID.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The semester begins in the middle of September, and the courses are published in the beginning of July. I would recommend to be a bit flexible, since some of the courses are of limited capacity and may be full. The university sends an e-mail to your UniBo-mail with a website, where you fill in your course wishes. This all has to add up with your pre-approvals from University of Copenhagen. It can be a confusing process, but University of Bologna are not very strict with the deadline of your course choice, since you have to register for the exam and not the course in the end.
registration_help: University of Bologna has an e-mail and a physical office, which can help.
registration_success: I was succesfull overall. However, I am a bachelor student, and it is important to notice, that University of Bologna do not allow bachelor students to attend master courses.
registration_advice: I would suggest to take a look at the courses from last year, since it offers more time for both deciding and getting pre-approvals. The courses did not change that much.
course_level: University of Bologna does not allow bachelor students to attend master courses.
teaching_comparison: Both University of Copenhagen and University of Bologna have classical lectures. However, University of Copenhagen also offers weekly exercise classes, which University of Bologna only does one or two times per semester and close to the exams.
courses_enrolled: Applied Political Sociology (8 ECTS) Industrial Organization (9 ECTS) Monetary Economics: Theory of Money and Liquidity (4 ECTS) Principles of Management (9 ECTS)
recommended_courses: Industrial Organization was very interesting to me regarding competition, and I would really recommend it. Also Applied Political Sociology was a good course with critical perspectives on data and its origin.
unexpected_costs: Transportation was a bit more expensive than expected, when visiting other Italian cities.
cost_comparison: Food in both supermarkets and restaurants is a lot cheaper than in Copenhagen.
activities_available: The university has a department similar to KU Studenteridræt with many different activities. They also host different kinds of events. The Erasmus Network in Bologna also hosts different events and trips.
activities_recommended: I went to the Italian language course, which was a great opportunity to both meet other international student and learn more about both culture and language.
weekend_recommendations: I really enjoyed going on trips to other Italian cities. By train, most of the larger cities are reachable in around 3 or 4 hours. Also, hiking is a great activity for the weekends.
culture_adjustment: It was quite easy. Of course it is a different language and environment, but the basics of the culture are not relatively far from the Danish.
socializing_tips: There are many cozy cafes and libraries, where many both local and international students go, so I would go there.
cultural_challenges: The university hours are a bit different, which means, that classes usually do not start at 8 in the morning, and that it is not abnormal with classes ending at 7 or 9 in the evening.
culture_appreciated: I appreciated the calmness and non-stressfullness of the culture and the amazing food.
top3_advice: Be in good time with planning, but not too good. You will not regret going on exchange, since it is great. Prioritize eating out.
other_useful_info: Around 1 or 2 days per month, classes were cancelled because of bad weather (often rain). They find online solutions or similar, but be prepared for changes.
most_rewarding: It is a big privilege to be able to experience another city than your hometown from the inside or as close to the inside as possible. It creates a lot of perspective on both the world and your own country. Also a great privilege to feel at home in another city.
greatest_challenge: Some of the paperworks did create challenges at some points.

crucial_aspects: I have traveled to Italy with my family loads of times and have always loved the Italian culture. I have also always wanted to try and live abroad for a period or to travel for a long period. When I got the chance to go on exchange, a stay in Bologna was the perfect choice.
info_ease: I received good information on the check in process of the university in terms of the practical stuff, but not so much in terms of the teaching stuff.
arrival_assistance: I received assistance with checking in online and with signing up for courses at the university.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You were enrolled in courses through registering them in your OLA. The university then reviewed your OLA and signed you up for the courses, if they were available. We had issues with a lot of our wanted courses being filled up, but luckily we were able to get enrolled either ways. We also changed a course a week in to the semester, which wasn't a problem.
registration_help: Online office hours and assistance through e-mail was available. This help was needed, as we initially had loads of problems with being able to attend the needed classes.
registration_success: In the end, I got all the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: Start applying for your courses through your OLA in very good time. In case some of your desired courses are deemed filled up, contact the responsible contact person and plead/argue for attending the course anyway - this worked for us at least.
course_level: The level of the courses were below the level of courses at KU.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was quite similar. I only had lectures and no exercise classes, which is in contrast to at KU. Most of the lectures were with digital slides, like at KU. The exams were different, as they were all held with pen and paper and nothing else.
courses_enrolled: Corporate Finance Economics of Financial Intermediation Industrial Organization Public Finance and Public Policy
recommended_courses: I would specifically recommend Economics of Financial Intermediation. The lecturer was one of the best I've ever had, as she was very engaging and obviously very, very interested in her field. The course was also a great introduction to financial markets and financial products.
unexpected_costs: I do not think I encountered any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: Going out to restaurants was less expensive than expected.
activities_available: ESN Bologna hosted lots of different events and trips, but I only participated in a few of them.
activities_recommended: I would probably recommend going to more of the ESN events and trips to meet more exchange students.
weekend_recommendations: I would REALLY recommend going on trips to different parts of Italy via train. I went to Lerici, Rome, Parma, Modena and Milan - and thoroughly enjoyed all of the trips!
culture_adjustment: It was very easy. People were very friendly and welcoming - and a lot of people wanted to speak Italian with you.
socializing_tips: I unfortunately did not succeed in socializing that much with local students, but I would definitely recommend doing so if possible.
cultural_challenges: At first I found it challenging with the much slower pace of things compared to Denmark, but gradually you get used to it - and begin enjoying it.
culture_appreciated: The love for food and for enjoying life.
top3_advice: Eat lots of good food, go to Bologna FC soccer games and visit San Luca
other_useful_info: Start applying for courses in good time. Be aware that the exam sessions are carried out very casually compared to at KU, so try not to get stressed out if the teacher shouws up too late and the whole exam is delayed.
most_rewarding: Challenging myself to live away from my friends and family for 5 months.
greatest_challenge: Dealing with feeling homesick.

crucial_aspects: I chose Bologna because I have family in Italy. I have lived in Denmark my entire life, but I thought it would be interesting to experience Italian culture in a different way than just as a tourist. With my program at the University of Copenhagen, I only had two options in Italy: Bologna and Milan. I chose Bologna because it is a smaller city, where I felt I could have the most authentic experience.
info_ease: I think it has been difficult to navigate both from the University of Copenhagen's side and from the University of Bologna. There is a lot of information, various emails, and very little communication between the two universities. I have missed having clearer communication from both sides.
arrival_assistance: I haven't really received any assistance as such. I registered my arrival through a somewhat complicated online system, where it was only possible to proceed at specific times. I think it would have worked better if I could have shown up in person. All I had to do was show my flight ticket, receive some brief information, and then I could ask questions.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I registered my arrival through a somewhat complicated online system, where it was only possible to proceed at specific times. I think it would have worked better if I could have shown up in person. All I had to do was show my flight ticket, receive some brief information, and then I could ask questions.
registration_help: Only online help was available. We tried to get in touch with different people at various offices in Bologna, but found it very difficult. They all referred us to the online help desk.
registration_success: We have been very confused about the courses. We were informed very late that we had to take at least 50% of our courses in humanities, as that is the faculty we are affiliated with in Copenhagen. On the other hand, it was easier to change courses in Bologna than in Copenhagen. In fact, we could change courses up until November. This was because some courses did not require physical attendance or only started in mid-November. Furthermore, the process of getting courses approved (pre-approval) at KU and the Online Learning Agreement is quite complicated. Each time we changed a course, the process had to start over, which was very frustrating.
registration_advice: I would advise other prospective exchange students to choose courses based on their own faculty and to get as many courses pre-approved as possible in advance – to avoid having to go through the lengthy process later.
course_level: The level in Bologna was not very high in my courses, but the teaching was enjoyable, and it also provided an opportunity to learn more about Italian culture.
teaching_comparison: The teachers were a bit slower and somewhat lazier compared to what I experience at KU.
courses_enrolled: Applied Political Sociology Introduction to Italian Culture Visualizing the Italian Society Education Systems and Politics Social Studies of Science and Technology
recommended_courses: Visualizing the Italian Society – It was fun to watch older Italian films and have them combined with some history. The teacher's English was poor, but it was manageable. Education Systems and Politics – Very interesting, especially if you're studying sociology. Social Studies of Science and Technology – Very similar to a course one could take in Denmark. The instructor was skilled, and the exercises and assignments were well-designed.
unexpected_costs: Bologna is a great city with many restaurants and other things you can spend money on – so it turned out to be a more expensive experience than expected.
cost_comparison: None
activities_available: ESN Bologna
activities_recommended: Explore the city on foot.
weekend_recommendations: Visit the San Luca Church – very beautiful. Wine tasting.
culture_adjustment: Bologna is a city known for its university, so many exchange students automatically come here, especially for the English-taught courses I was enrolled in. Therefore, I found it quite easy to adapt.
socializing_tips: Go to Via Del Pratello and have a drink and a chat with the local students Be in the city before all of the other exchange students arrive
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The language The food The people
top3_advice: Don't stress about the courses and the system there – everything will work out in the end, and the university is willing to help. Choose courses with exams that don't require you to return to Bologna if you fail. Make sure to sort out your housing situation in good time.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: I definitely think the most rewarding part was experiencing the Italian culture up close.
greatest_challenge: The biggest challenge was probably that I lived very close to my roommates. We were four people in a very small apartment, and it can be demanding to make that work. Additionally, I also felt there were significant challenges with their entire system and the communication with the people from the university who were supposed to help us. However, in the end, there was a solution to it.

overall_comments: Jeg vil anbefale alle at tage til Bologna University, men må desværre også tydeliggøre at den bureaukratiske proces har været utrolig forvirrende og til tider dybt frustrerende. Det kan være svært at finde hjælp på værtsuniversitetet, og KU har også haft svært ved at hjælpe.

arrival_comments: Jeg blev misvejledt, ingen kontorer kunne hjælpe mig og den mail jeg blev henvist til, havde 3 ugers ventetid på svar
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Jeg vil anbefale alle at tage til Bologna University, men må desværre også tydeliggøre at den bureaukratiske proces har været utrolig forvirrende og til tider dybt frustrerende. Det kan være svært at finde hjælp på værtsuniversitetet, og KU har også haft svært ved at hjælpe.
registration_process: Kurserne der udbydes, bliver først offentliggjort få uger før skolestart. Derfor kan det være svært at forberede sit skema, og man kommer hurtigt til at skulle lave sin "online learning agreement" mange mange gange - her skal man være opmærksom på at få den godkendt inden deadline ift Erasmus! Det kan nemlig godt være en lang proces. Man skal checke ind online ved UniBo og dette system er ofte overfyldt, så hvis du kommer til Bologna tidligere end skolestart, så sørg for at checke ind så hurtigt som muligt!
registration_help: Unibo har en officiel mail for udvekslingsstuderende, som kan være behjælpelig. Det største problem er deres svartider.
registration_success: Reglerne for hvilke kurser, jeg måtte/skulle tage blev hele tiden lavet om, og der var ikke klarhed om aftalen mellem de to universiteter, så det endte med at være en langsommelig og bøvlet proces, hvor jeg nær mistede håbet, men det lykkedes til sidst. Forbered dig på at bruge rigtig meget tid og energi på at få styr på kurserne - særligt hvis du læser sociologi, da deres exchange-agreement er med antropologi, hvilket er et humanistisk fag i Italien. Desuden var der stor uenig om hvorvidt bachelor-studerende måtte tage kandidat-fag, og det var også lidt af et cirkus.
registration_advice: Tålmodighed og gåpåmod - hvis du vil have hjælp, skal du gøre dig umage for at finde det.
academics_comments: Jeg vil anbefale alle at tage til Bologna University, men må desværre også tydeliggøre at den bureaukratiske proces har været utrolig forvirrende og til tider dybt frustrerende. Det kan være svært at finde hjælp på værtsuniversitetet, og KU har også haft svært ved at hjælpe.
course_level: Der er meget stor forskel alt efter hvilke fag man tager. Jeg tog både master fag som lå langt under det BA-niveau jeg var vant til fra KU, men oplevede også kurser, som var lige så krævende, akademiske og avancerede som jeg forestiller mig MA-fag er på KU. På det måde kan du selv vælge hvor meget du vil udfordres.
teaching_comparison: Meget kurser kræver at du er fysisk tilstede minimum 75% af undervisningsgangene. Der er få forelæsninger, og undervisningen lægger generelt mere op til samtale. Eksaminerne kan man ofte vælge mellem forskellige datoer, og hvis du ønsker det, kan du også ofte vælge en mundtlig eksamen i stedet for en skriftlig.
courses_enrolled: Humanitarian communication, urban studies and climate change, web society and globalization, criminology of the borders
recommended_courses: Criminology of the borders var mit absolut yndlingsfag! Det var klart det mest krævende og havde den tungeste læse-byrde, men det var utrolig spændende og lærerigt!
unexpected_costs: Bolig var en del dyrere end jeg først havde regnet med, og der skal oftest betales stort "agency fee" til dem der hjælper med at finde din bolig.
cost_comparison: Du skal lidt udenfor byen for at finde billige supermarkeder, ellers bliver det hurtigt dyrt at handle.
activities_available: Der er mange forskellige muligheder for sport gennem universitetet. Her skal du være opmærksom på, at det kræver en italiensk lægeerklæring, som er ret dyr.
activities_recommended: Jeg var selv en del af to løbeklubber (gratis), som jeg fandt på instagram, et dansehold gennem universitetet, en hiking-gruppe jeg fandt på Whatsapp (også gratis), og tog et tegnekursus som jeg fandt på internettet - der er rigtig mange muligheder for at dyrke sine hobbyer!
weekend_recommendations: Norditalien (og italien generelt) byder på rigtig mange fantastiske byer, der er lette at nå til med deres toge eller flex busser - så der er mange gode muligheder for både weekends- og dagsture.
culture_adjustment: Let. Det er dog en kæmpe fordel at lære lidt italiensk - både af respekt for dem og fordi det kan være svært at begå sig uden (men ikke umuligt)
socializing_tips: Tal med dine medstuderende - det er klart på universitetet det er lettest at finde italienske studerende! Eller hvis du tilmelder dig fritidsaktivitetsgrupper.
cultural_challenges: Sproget - det engelsk niveau er ikke særlig højt. Derudover logistikken ved deres universitetsprocess.
culture_appreciated: Deres fantastiske madkultur!
top3_advice: 1) NYD DET! 2) Processen i starten kan føles lang og tung, men det skal nok lykkes i sidste ende. 3) Det giver virkelig pote, hvis man kan ligge lidt af sin stolthed fra sig, og bare turde gribe chancen for at tale med fremmede mennesker - der er mange, der gerne vil have nye venner.
other_useful_info: Spørg om hjælp så mange steder du kan, og forbered dig på, at du bliver sendt videre til nogle andre, som forhåbentlig kan hjælpe dig.
most_rewarding: Akademisk udbytte, tid til hobbyer og internationale venner der forhåbentlig varer resten af livet.
greatest_challenge: At sætte sig ind i et nyt universitet
