crucial_aspects: I wanted somewhere culturally not too far from Denmark, as well as somewhere with great nature and especially mountains.
info_ease: I found it quite easy to find the needed information through KU, and later on UBC's own website.
arrival_assistance: I didn't receive any personal assistance, but most things had been sorted from home, and once at campus it was quite easy to figure out what to do.
arrival_comments: I didn't need any specific assistance, but it seemed to be quite easy to get in touch with someone if you needed help.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: When accepted to study at UBC you first have to fill out a list of 10 possible courses, but this is not your final courses. Once the registration opens, you find all of the courses online and can manually change some of them if needed.
registration_help: You were able to write the UBC student services, which was super helpful.
registration_success: I got all of the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: Not a lot is written in the course description, so remember that during the add-and-drop phase in the first 2 weeks of the semester, you are allowed to switch courses if they turn out to be different than expected! Your exchange is supposed to be 4 nice months, so a great tip is to not choose courses that take up way too much time.
course_level: The level of the courses were generally lower when compared to my courses at KU. I took mainly 300 level courses, which was okay, but definitely easier than what I am used to. As a third year bachelor student, I believe 400 courses are academically more suiting (but I found it really nice that I didn't have to focus too much on school)
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching is quite different from Denmark, since it resembles our gymnasium quite a lot. For some courses it is mandatory to show up to class, there are quite a lot of assignments, and you are being graded throughout the entire semester. This is often seen by the final exam counting between 30 and 50% of your final grade, whilst the rest is determined based on assignments, participation etc. This was a little stressfull throughout the semester, and I didn't feel nearly as independent as a normally do, but once we reached the finals, it was really nice that you didn't have to study a lot to get an okay grade.
courses_enrolled: BIOL 364 Comparative Cardiovascular, Respiratory and Osmoregulatory Physiology BIOL 260 Fundamentals of Physiology BIOL 335 Molecular Genetics BIOL 336 Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology. This is not a classic molecular biomedicine course, but I have been missing some more evolution at KU, so it was really nice being able to do it at UBC. Also, the teacher Wayne was such a great and charismatic teacher.
unexpected_costs: It was really expensive to do grocery shopping. Phone plan is also expensive in Canada Expect to use a lot of money on traveling, the area around Vancouver is amazing!
cost_comparison: It was a little less expensive going out to eat in Vancouver compared to Denmark
activities_available: Almost everything! UBC rec has a lot of different clubs, involving different sports, languages, clubs related to specific studies as well as a surf club and an outdoor club.
activities_recommended: Use the aquatic center and sports facilities (badminton, volley, basket) on campus - they are free! The Varsity Outdoor Club also offers some amazing trips
weekend_recommendations: Get out of Vancouver, and especially out of Campus. You are surrounded by the most amazing mountains, so use them as much as possible - for skiing, hiking or just going for a drive. It is possible to get around by bus, but definitely easier if you have or know someone with a car. Go to Vancouver Island and spend some time - Tofino is an amazing little surf-town.
culture_adjustment: Canada is not very far from Denmark culturally so I didn't find it difficult to adjust.
socializing_tips: Use your time in classes if possible!
cultural_challenges: Nothing was particularly challenging, but you have to get used to tipping when paying for anything, and the very polite lifestyle of the Canadians - they line up very nicely at the bus-stops, so don't just get in front of everybody.
culture_appreciated: The canadians are very friendly and easygoing, and I always felt really safe, and certain that someone would help me if needed.
top3_advice: Remember to enjoy your time - do not spend too much time and energy on school, there is so much else to experience! Remember, that life back home goes on as usual. You don't miss out on a lot, so you can just as well focus on yourself and your time in Canada, when you come home, most things are as they were when you left. Say yes to any opportunity you are giving. 4 months passes by incredibly fast, so do as much as possible when you can
other_useful_info: If you like skiing, remember to buy a season pass for Whistler well in advance, a lot of money is saved!
most_rewarding: Being able to fully commit to a different lifestyle for a few months. When on exchange, you don't need to focus on anything besides yourself, and you have so much time to just do whatever you want without any great commitments. Also, I feel super grateful for all of the friends I got in Canada!
greatest_challenge: It does take quite a lot of courage and planning when going abroad for such a long period, and there are definitely a lot of boring days where you miss everything back home

crucial_aspects: Jeg vidste jeg ville til Canada pga. flere faktorer: 1) den smukke natur og muligheden for at stå på ski 2) det var et engelsktalende land, så nemt at kommunikere med folk i landet. 3) Jeg vidste at canadiere var helt vildt søde og imødekommende mennesker og så self. også 4) det var et anerkendt universitet, hvor der var mulighed for god undervisning.
overall_comments: Over alt forventning. Helt fantastisk oplevelse. Selvom corona skabte meget usikkerhed inden afrejse, var der stort set ingen problemer i løbet af opholdet. Og både landet, menneskerne og universitetet var så fantastisk. Vil anbefale alle at tage på udveksling på UBC.
info_ease: Jeg husker umiddelbart ikke de store problemer, så snart jeg fik adgang til KU-mailen. Forbered dig på at der er de sædvanlige KU-problemer, såsom web-mailen. Man kan kun få adgang til webmailen (og dermed alt det nødvendige information og tilmeldelses-links) via sikkerhedskoden der sendes til ens mobil. Mit danske abonnement virkede ikke i Canada, og mit nye canadiske nummer modtog aldrig sikkerhes-koderne. Så det var egentlig det system - og manglende mulighed for hjælp fra KU når ens telefon ikke modtog sms'er - der udgjorde det størte problem ift. at få den nødvendige information.
arrival_assistance: Man fik mange mails om hvad man skulle huske, samt zoom-møder, hvor de gennemgik det vigtigste. Det var en stor hjælp.
arrival_comments: Har ingen klager til host-institutionen UBC. Men havde heller ikke den store brug for hjælp fra deres side.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Over alt forventning. Helt fantastisk oplevelse. Selvom corona skabte meget usikkerhed inden afrejse, var der stort set ingen problemer i løbet af opholdet. Og både landet, menneskerne og universitetet var så fantastisk. Vil anbefale alle at tage på udveksling på UBC.
registration_process: KU hjælper med det meste. Og så er der en add og drop-periode hvor man til- og fravælge fag ok nemt via sin UBC-bruger.
registration_help: Massere af informationssider. Jeg google ting som "register couse at ubc" og så kom den rette side frem.
registration_success: Jeg fik ikke de fag, jeg troede, jeg skulle have hjemmefra, da de kun var til forårssemesteret og jeg var på efterår. Men da jeg ankom og fandt ud af hvilke fag der var at vælge imellem, fik jeg næsten alle dem jeg ønskede - undtaget et meget populært.
registration_advice: Læs og genlæs de informationer man får tilsendt. Og team op med en eller to der skal samme sted tidligt i processen, så I er flere om at huske deadlines og finde rundt i systemet.
academics_comments: Over alt forventning. Helt fantastisk oplevelse. Selvom corona skabte meget usikkerhed inden afrejse, var der stort set ingen problemer i løbet af opholdet. Og både landet, menneskerne og universitetet var så fantastisk. Vil anbefale alle at tage på udveksling på UBC.
course_level: Jeg tog kun 300-level courses. De var semi-nemme, og engang imellem udfordrende. Man ville uden problemer kunne tage 400-level (hvilket nok også ville gøre det mere interessant, til gengæld også kræve mere arbejde). Og jeg ville ikke gå under 300, for så tror jeg man vil kede sig.
teaching_comparison: Der er mere engagement fra de studerendes side. Man deltager mere i forelæsningerne (hvis man har lyst). Så er der mere "udenadslære" (dog med hjælpemidler til prøverne pga corona), og små test og skriftlige opgaver i løbet af semesteret. Det gør også eksamensperioden nemmere at komme igennem, fordi man har høstet point i løbet af året.
courses_enrolled: Gender Relations Sociology of Development and Underdevelopment Crime and Society
recommended_courses: Gender Relations og alt med Craig som underviser. Det var det mest spændende fag, med den mest engagerede og inspirerende underviser jeg overhoved har haft på studiet.
unexpected_costs: Jeg rejste mere end jeg havde troet jeg ville. Så det var ret dyrt - men worth it. Og så var det tæt på umuligt at leve billigt. Jeg havde det billigste mobilabonnement på 230 kr. pr mdr., boede billigt for 4500 kr. pr mdr., og lavede madpakker og den billigste aftensmad jeg kunne. Men indkøb er dyrt i Vancouver. Selv de billige supermarkeder kostede det samme som Irma og Meny.
cost_comparison: Indkøb er dyrere end i Danmark. At købe mad ude er en anelse billigere - men ikke meget. Det er generelt bare dyrt at skulle leve i Vancouver... Men WORTH!
activities_available: Alt. Man kunne være med i hockey-klubben, quiditch-klubben, fodboldklubben, skiklubben, strikkeklubben, ølsmagning- og bryggeri-klubben osv. Alle udvalg man kunne forestille sig fandtes der, og det var nemt at blive medlem.
activities_recommended: Ski og vandring. Det var højdepunkterne fra hele opholdet!
weekend_recommendations: Tag ud i bjergene og vandre så længe det er muligt. Og når skilifterne åbner, tag på ski. Vancovuer er en skøn by, men det er omgivelserne der gør det til et fantastisk sted.
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Vancouver er som en amerikansk by der er blevet europæ-ficeret. Alle er åbne og imødekommende. Men forbedred dig på, at alle vil small-talke - både i busserne, køerne og på caféerne.
socializing_tips: Meld dig ind i flere klubber, hvis du vil tale med de lokale studerende. Ellers ender man hurtigt bare med de andre udvekslingsstuderende som jeg gjorde. Men det var nu også fedt, så ingen skam i det!
cultural_challenges: Faktisk ikke rigtig noget. De er nemme at omgås og tale med. Der er flere hjemløse i Vancouver end man er van til i Danmark, og de henvender sig mere til en. Men når man opdager de alle er søde og rare, så tænker man ikke så meget over det.
culture_appreciated: Deres imødekommenhed og deres brug af omgivelserne. De er alle sammen optagede af enten vandring, klatring, ski/snowboard eller diverse vandsports.
top3_advice: 1) GØR DET, det er det smukkeste, skønneste og sjoveste sted man kunne vælge. 2) Spar op, for det er også sindssygt dyrt at leve godt derovre. 3) Tag med på alle de vandreture, teltture, skiture, kanoture osv. som du kan.
other_useful_info: Vær klar på at bruge mange penge, have meget transporttid, og leve med en masse regn. Og så kan man altså google sig til det meste derfra, når KU eller UBC er lidt besværlige at hive informationer ud af.
most_rewarding: At opleve så meget skønt - at stå på ski, være i nationalparker, rejse til varme steder i læseferien, møde gæstfrie canadiere, og få en masse nye udvekslingsvenner.
greatest_challenge: At finde et sted at bo lige da jeg ankom. Det tog lidt at ankomst-glæden, så undgå det ved at finde et sted inden.
other_comments: Acceptér at du måske ikke bliver bff's med canadiere, men at de andre udvekslingsstuderende har ligeså meget at byde på.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne til Vancouver, da det var en god mulighed for at komme til et naturskønt område i et engelsktalende land uden for Europa. Derudover lød UBC som et spændende universitet.
info_ease: UBC har generelt været gode til at give information om ansøgningsprocessen, og de Go Global har hurtigt hjulpet ved tvivlsspørgsmål. Allard Law har en lidt anderledes ansøgningsprocedure end resten af UBC, men der gøres opmærksom herpå, og de har en udmærket guide på deres hjemmeside.
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik ikke hjælp i forbindelse med ankomsten.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Man skal registrere fagene online på SSC af to omgange. Det er en god idé at være tidligt ude, så man er sikker på at få fagene, da pladserne opfyldes efter et først-til-mølle-princip. Man kan gemme fag, man er interesseret i på en "Worklist", så man blot skal trykke på en knap, når registreringen åbner. Jeg havde ingen problemer med at få de fag, jeg var interesseret i.
registration_help: UBC plejer at være gode til at svare på spørgsmål.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle fag, jeg var interesseret i, og formåede også at bytte til et andet fag inden udløb af prøveperioden. Populære fag vil selvsagt blive fyldt hurtigere end mere obskure fag.
registration_advice: Gør jer klar i god tid, så I kan registrere hurtigt, når registreringen åbner; det gør alle andre. Husk, at det er let at bytte fag inden for de første to uger af semesteret, hvis ikke det var det rigtige. Det klares online.
course_level: Niveauet og kravene kommer meget an på underviseren i de enkelte fag. Generelt synes læsemængde og niveau at svare meget til fagene på KU.
teaching_comparison: Umiddelbart meget lig KU. Det kommer dog an på, om man vælger "Lecture" eller "Seminar". Jeg havde kun "Seminars". Underviseren har også selv meget indflydelse på undervisningsmetoden. Jeg havde valgt et seminar, hvor kun få deltog, hvilket betød at det i højere grad var en tretimers samtale mellem de deltagende end undervisning med professoren, der underviser, og de studerende, der lytter.
courses_enrolled: Freedom of Expression E-Commerce Law Japanese Law Comparative Law Natural Law
recommended_courses: Natural Law var meget intenst og arbejdskrævende men også meget spændende; jeg vil kun anbefale det, hvis man er klar på at deltage aktivt og virkelig læse grundigt op. Comparative Law giver et godt indblik i forskelle mellem civil law og common law og giver en bedre forståelse forskellige retstraditioner. Læsningen i faget er ikke klassisk juridisk, så man skal være forberedt på at læse lidt let økonomi, retshistorie og komparativ ret. Jeg er meget glad for at have haft det. Freedom of Expression, Japanese Law og E-Commerce Law er meget brede fag, der måske ikke går så meget i dybden med de enkelte områder. Til gengæld giver de et godt overblik over godt alt i canadisk (og andre staters) ret, der kunne tænkes at være relevante for områderne.
unexpected_costs: Maden (også dagligvarer) er dyr. Derudover tror jeg at de fleste har en tendens til at spise lidt mere ude, når de er på udveksling, så man skal være forberedt på, at man nok bruger lidt flere penge derovre. Hvis du står på ski, og har tænkt dig at gøre det mere end tre dage, så køb et Epic Pass til Whistler hjemmefra. De kan ikke købes, når sæsonen er i gang, og de er langt billigere end at betale for dagspas, der i højsæsonen godt kan komme over 200 CAD. Overvej at købe en bil; lidt dyrt men virkelig det hele værd.
cost_comparison: Ingenting.
activities_available: Meget begrænset grundet corona. Dog nogle arrangementer senere på semesteret.
activities_recommended: Kom ud i naturen.
weekend_recommendations: Tag til Whistler, Vancouver Island (Tofino), Sunshine Coast, Bannf og Jasper (når sæsonen passer)
culture_adjustment: Kulturen er på mange måder ikke ulig den danske. De canadiske studerende (og roommates) er dog generelt lidt yngre end de danske. Det var bedre på Allard, da folk har taget deres undergrads der.
socializing_tips: Bare vær åben, og sørg selv for at tage kontakt til dem.
cultural_challenges: Kan ikke umiddelbart komme i tanke om nogne.
culture_appreciated: Venligheden (særligt uden for Vancouver).
top3_advice: Sørg for at komme væk fra campus, også i hverdagene. Brug weekender på at komme væk fra Vancouver, hvad enten det er ski, ture længere væk eller hikes. Overvej at købe en bil; offentlig transport er ikke verdens bedste.
other_useful_info: Ikke umiddelbart.
most_rewarding: Vancouver ligger perfekt ift. naturoplevelser og skisport, så det har været et fantastisk sted at være.
greatest_challenge: Kan ikke umiddelbart komme i tanke om noget.

crucial_aspects: The host university needed to be decent. The course selection had to suit me somewhat. The surrounding area needed to be decent, and it needed to be an English-speaking country.
overall_comments: It would be an 9 or 10/10 were it not for Covid. The hassle with the study permit, travel restrictions, cancelled events etc. due to Covid sucked. But it's quite telling when I still feel like I got an 8/10 experience, even with those problems. Exchange was awesome!!
info_ease: Regarding UBC, it was easy enough. Regarding Covid, it was a pain. I spent many, many hours looking into restrictions, calling hotlines etc. Especially regarding travel restrictions and quarantine at arrival in Canada.
arrival_assistance: I didn't get assistance, but Go Global is there for exchange students. You can just drop into their office.
arrival_comments: Help was there if needed.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: It would be an 9 or 10/10 were it not for Covid. The hassle with the study permit, travel restrictions, cancelled events etc. due to Covid sucked. But it's quite telling when I still feel like I got an 8/10 experience, even with those problems. Exchange was awesome!!
registration_process: You browsed the course catalogue for 10 courses you wanted. This was submitted to Go Global as a priority list of 10, and they applied for you. This is because, as exchange students, we are not fully in the system and they thus need to apply for us. For some courses, Go Global could not register for you, and you had to consult the course teachers once the term started. You had until 14 days into the term to get the courses you wanted, where you could also drop out of the courses you wanted with no consequences.
registration_help: Go Global could offer a lot of assistance.
registration_success: I got all I wanted.
registration_advice: Start browsing the course catalogue early. Plan your week regarding sections - it's e.g. a pain to have a single lecture at 16 when your day otherwise ended at 11. As an extension of that, make sure that combinations of different courses don't result in big conflicts. It would e.g. suck to have two lectures at the same time.
academics_comments: It would be an 9 or 10/10 were it not for Covid. The hassle with the study permit, travel restrictions, cancelled events etc. due to Covid sucked. But it's quite telling when I still feel like I got an 8/10 experience, even with those problems. Exchange was awesome!!
course_level: They were generally easier than UCPH courses, at least the courses I had. But it generally depends on the course and the teacher - I had friends in Engineering that struggled with their courses.
teaching_comparison: The lectures are really short - about 45 minutes. You also have to be on top of the course throughout the semester, as there are quizzes, assignments etc. throughout the course that actually factor into your final grade. It's not just all about the final exam.
courses_enrolled: BIOL421: Plant-Microbe Interactions MICB301: Microbial Ecophysiology MICB405: Bioinformatics
recommended_courses: BIOL421 was great if you're into plant biology and research methods. The teachers are great, especially Jim Kronstad. And the course is easy too.
unexpected_costs: Buying all the stuff for the dorm. Both kitchen equipment and bedding. But the kitchen stuff isn't that bad if you can split with your flatmates.
cost_comparison: Groceries are more expensive. Alcohol is a LOT more expensive - which is especially bad news as a Dane. Sugary stuff was much cheaper, and eating out was a bit less expensive than Copenhagen.
activities_available: A LOT of things. A huge variety of clubs within whatever hobby, sports games to come watch (tickets being free for students), drop-in sessions for skating, swimming etc. It really was a great selection, and the facilities are excellent.
activities_recommended: Go to the sports games, and join a club or two!
weekend_recommendations: Sightsee and hike! And in the mid-term break, try to go somewhere else in North America - e.g. Hawaii or Toronto.
culture_adjustment: Easy.
socializing_tips: Don't be afraid to ask questions - in most cases, it leads into good conversation. Just initiate!
cultural_challenges: The tipping culture. It was just an odd thing you always needed to think about - how much to tip, whether to tip, where to tip...
culture_appreciated: The friendliness towards strangers, and how open people were for talk.
top3_advice: 1: Go to the campus events, e.g. sports games! 2: Invest in or bring hiking boots - experience the nature! 3: Eat out a lot!
other_useful_info: If you don't get on-campus housing, try to find something in Kitsilano. A lot of students live in basement suites, which are subletted by the house owners. Try finding a few other people to share a suite with.
most_rewarding: Growing as a person. I had to talk to a lot of people I didn't know, which is outside of my comfort zone. I feel like I'm more "worldly" too, in part because I met so many exchange students from across the world, in part because I learned about Canadian/North American culture.
greatest_challenge: Settling in and taking care of a lot of small things. Finding a mobile plan, buying kitchen equipment for the dorm, learning how course grading works...
other_comments: If you have any doubts about going: don't. Trust me - it's worth the money, it's worth the hassle, and it's worth missing courses at UCPH. It's a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity and experience. I will never regret doing it, and I'm positive you won't either.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go somewhere with beautiful nature as well as vibrant city vibes, and Vancouver had everything!
info_ease: It was fairly easy, Go Global was good at keeping me updated.
arrival_assistance: No.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You can do "course shopping" the first couple of weeks, which is really helpful in case you end up in a course that you aren't fond of. Courses were very limited at the time due to Covid, but if I wrote an email to the professors, they were very helpful with getting me into the course.
registration_success: I was succesful and got the courses I needed in the end.
registration_advice: Don't be afraid to try a lot of different courses in the beginning, so you end up taking the courses that you like the most. I found that every course really differed in quality depending on the instructors, so it's a good idea to try it out before you are locked into a course. Also, look at the course material/syllabus beforehand and see what kind of examination they do in the specific course - this really varies as well, and might impact how stressed you will be during exams!
course_level: The courses were not very challenging, but required more work along the way (i.e. graded assignments, midterms, participation...). But I found that it was easy to keep up.
teaching_comparison: It was more like high school because you had to hand in smaller assignments along the way and you were graded for participation (but this is not the case in all of the courses). Also, it was more individualistic than at UCPH, and there were a lot of class discussions.
courses_enrolled: POLI 333A "Issues in Comparative Politics" POLI 366 "International Political Economy" SOCI 312 "Gender Relations" GRSJ 300 "Intersectional Approaches to Thinking Gender"
recommended_courses: I would HIGHLY recommend SOCI312 "Gender Relations". It is the best course I have ever taken during my university years. Our instructor, Craig Meadows, is incredible, funny and extremely critical. I would recommend all courses with Craig Meadows.
unexpected_costs: Covid tests for travel purposes (they are between $90 - $250 depending on what type of test and place).
cost_comparison: Groceries were more expensive than I expected.
activities_available: I was a part of VOC which is the UBC outdoor assocation, and they do many trips every weekend in nature that you can join. You can also rent equipment (for free - but with a deposit) which is super useful. I went on some of the most amazing hikes here. I was also a part of the Ski & Board Club, that hosted a really great Whistler Opening weekend. Would highly recommend!
activities_recommended: VOC (Varsity Outdoor Club) and Ski & Board Club.
weekend_recommendations: I bought a car with some other friends and we did trips every weekend. I would really recommend doing this! I can recommend Banff/Jasper, Gariabldi, Whistler, Vancouver Island, Mount Frosty (Especially in the last weekend of september), Hawaii, San Francisco, Unnecessary Mountain (yes, that's what it's called...)
culture_adjustment: Very easy! People are super nice and friendly.
socializing_tips: Say yes to all invitations in the first few weeks. I found that these weeks were imperative for the people I have become close friends with today. This is the time when everyone is looking for new friends. And join in on some VOC hikes.
cultural_challenges: There are ques to everything...
culture_appreciated: How friendly Canadians are, the amazing nature and all the possibilities for great adventures in British Columbia. Campus is also really beautiful.
top3_advice: 1) Buy a Whistler Season pass and go skiing/boarding as often as possible. 2) Get a car or an EVO membership so you have easy access to the outdoors and the beautiful nature around Vancouver. Just do as many trips as you can in general! 3) Allard Hall Library (Law building) is best for studying, there are mountain views!
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: The amazing people, the incredible nature and the beautiful city.
greatest_challenge: Covid-19 restrictions on the application process and flights.

crucial_aspects: Naturen og områderne omkring Vancouver, samt ski-mulighederne og især Whistler
info_ease: Husker det som ret nemt
arrival_assistance: De afholdte noget kaldet "imagine day", som var en slags intro-dag for alle udvekslingsstuderende, hvor man fik en rundvisning på campus i grupper. Her fik man både mødt mange af de andre og havde mulighed for at stille spørgsmål osv.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Man var blevet tilmeldt nogle af de fag man havde søgt hjemmefra og da semesteret startede var de første 2 uger "add and drop period", så man havde tid til at prøve forskellige fag af før man skulle vælge endeligt.
registration_help: Underviserne var klar til at svare på spørgsmål man skulle have til fagene - og ellers studievejledningen.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag jeg søgte.
registration_advice: På portalen kan man også se hvor mange pladser hvert fag har tilbage, men mange professorer er ret fleksible, så hvis der er et fyldt fag man virkelig gerne vil tage, vil jeg anbefale at forsøge at skrive til underviseren - så kan de ofte presse en ind.
course_level: Det var virkelig forskelligt fra fag til fag - tror underviseren har virkelig meget kontrol over hvordan de vil køre kurserne. Så nogle fag var udelukkende lærebøger og multiple choice quizzer, mens andre var primær tekster, teori og essays.
teaching_comparison: Det er meget forskelligt fra KU. Det varierer selfølgelig meget mellem fagene, men generelt oplevede jeg at man lavede flere mindre opgaver/quizzer/prøver i løbet af semesteret fremfor en stor til sidst. Det betød så også at nogle fag næsten var beståede før man nåede til afsluttende eksamen/slet ikke havde en afsluttende eksamen, men blot gav karakter ud fra det man havde afleveret løbende.
courses_enrolled: SOCI 312 - Gender Relations SOCI 301 - Sociology of Development and Underdevelopment SOCI 220 - Sociology of Indigenous Peoples CONS 210 - Visualizing Climate Change
recommended_courses: Helt sikkert Gender Relations! Craig der underviser er virkelig fantastisk - både til at forlæse og generelt til at skabe et virkelig godt rum for diskussion. Det var et fag, der altid var spændende at komme til og som altid satte en masse tanker igang! Vi var 5 danskere der alle havde faget og vi kom nærmest altid til at snakke videre om teksterne eller diskussionen udenfor undervisningen også. Til gengæld vil jeg nok ikke anbefale Sociology of Development and Underdevelopment. Undervisningsformen var næsten udelukkende bygget op omkring udenadslære og multiple-choice quizzer, hvor underviseren praktisk talt udleverede svarene i undervisningen - så meget uinspirerende undervisningsform. De to sidste fag jeg havde var begge virkelig spændende, men ikke specielt akademisk udfordrende - så hvis man er interesseret i at lære mere om klima og/eller Canadas oprindelige befolkninger vil jeg helt sikkert anbefale dem. I Sociology of Indigenous Peoples var der virkelig mange spændende undervisningsmaterialer at dykke ned i og i klimafaget havde vi nogle super spændende gæsteforlæsere. Men begge fag er nemme at komme igennem.
unexpected_costs: Nok ikke uventede udgifter, men jeg brugte en stor del af mine penge på ture rundt i BC samt på skileje og sæsonpas til Whistler
cost_comparison: Dagligvarer er dyrere end i Danmark desværre, mens det er billigere at købe take-away/spise ude
activities_available: Tror at der findes en klub for alt hvad man kunne drømme om på UBC!
activities_recommended: Skiklubben! Det koster kun 20CAD at melde sig ind og så holder de fester i løbet af semesteret samt selvfølgelig skiture. På efterårssemesteret er der "condo-cram" turen, hvor skiklubben tager til Whistler i åbningsweekenden og senere på sæsonen er der flere ture planlagt
weekend_recommendations: Vancouver Island, dagsture og hikes omkring Vancouver, Banff og Jasper, ski i Whistler
culture_adjustment: Super nemt - Canadierne er super søde!
socializing_tips: Prøv at få snakket med dem du sidder med til forelæsninger (hvis ikke de snakker med dig først!) eller måske vælge fag hvor der indgår gruppearbejde/-opgaver
cultural_challenges: Ikke rigtigt nogen
culture_appreciated: At de er så imødekommende og åbne
top3_advice: Kom ud og brug naturen så meget du kan (især når vejret er godt!), brug klubberne på UBC og begynd at lede efter bolig i god tid (hvis du vil undgå stress før studiestart).
other_useful_info: Mange boliger både på campus og udenfor er meget sparsomt møbleret, med fx helt tomme køkkener - en tur i Value Village fremfor fx IKEA kan spare dig mange penge:)
most_rewarding: Alle oplevelserne! At bo i Vancouver med bjerge, skove og hav lige udenfor. Det var også fedt at få lidt mere selvtillid ift. at skrive større opgaver alene - det er ikke det man gør mest af på sociologi i København, så det var godt at prøve
greatest_challenge: Man skulle vænne sig til at have afleveringer osv løbende gennem hele semesteret samt en travl periode omkring midtterms i oktober/november.

crucial_aspects: The defining factor in choosing my study destination (Vancouver, Canada) was a mix between academic opportunities and the possibility to explore a beautiful country and nature. I have definitely not been disappointed. British Columbia has offered some of the most amazing cultural and natural experiences I have ever had. From surfing on Vancouver Island, hiking in the mountains around Vancouver and Banff/Jasper to skiing in Whistler and Big White, I have had the experience of a lifetime. Moreover, the University of British Columbia offers a great academic program from an international perspective. I have made many new good friends both from Denmark and from around the world.
overall_comments: Fantastic experience. I would recommend everyone to attend UBC. The nature is amazing and the academic level is reasonable ie you still have time to do a lot other than just study.
info_ease: Very easy - GoGlobal, UBC and UCPH provide you with the necessary information. However, I would recommend researching information on insurance etc. on your own time. I was only covered by iMED which is mandatory as a student at UBC. This is sufficient if you only stay within British Columbia. However, I was very unsure if this was the case and if it was necessary to have insurance besides iMED. This can be necessary if you want to go skiing after the end of the semester, and it is often mandatory to make a private insurance agreement BEFORE departing for Canada. I would recommend you to make such an agreement before departing for Canada - but only with covering after the end of the iMED period. Alternatively, I think it is possible to extend iMED for the period in question.
arrival_assistance: I received some general information via e-mail. It is pretty straightforward. There is also a lot of information on the webpage of UBC.
arrival_comments: Make use of the many different possibilities offered by UBC. For instance, you can join a team - football, volleyball etc. Moreover, there are free recreational facilities, for instance for swimming, basketball, badminton etc.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Fantastic experience. I would recommend everyone to attend UBC. The nature is amazing and the academic level is reasonable ie you still have time to do a lot other than just study.
registration_process: You make an ordered list of priorities for courses. Be prepared not to get your first priorities. I am a graduate student, however, I could only attend undergraduate courses. Therefore, the academic level was significantly lower than what I was used to from UCPH. Upon arrival, I am told it is possible to attend graduate-level courses if you contact the individual professors. The only difficult thing about the process is to get course descriptions in order to get merit at UCPH. These are not publicly available. You have to contact the individual professors - and not all of them respond. However, you can be lucky that UCPH has already accepted the course as available for merit transfer. Therefore, I would recommend writing to UCPH first with your preferred courses and ask if UCPH has already accepted some of the courses, befrore you contact the professors at UBC.
registration_help: E-mails from UBC explain the process very carefully.
registration_success: Pretty unsuccessful - got a mix of the classes I wanted and didn't want. However, I ended up dropping some of my unwanted courses at the end of the registration period. For instance, I got a course in Political Economics which I was really happy about.
registration_advice: Contact UCPH with a list of your preferred courses and ask if they are already accepted for transferring credits. The professors at UBC don't always send you a course description upon request.
academics_comments: Fantastic experience. I would recommend everyone to attend UBC. The nature is amazing and the academic level is reasonable ie you still have time to do a lot other than just study.
course_level: The course level was not very high. However, there is a big gap in difficulty between 300 and 400 courses. 400 courses are pretty demanding. For instance, International Trade (ECON455) and Economics of Renewable resources (ECON472) were pretty difficult and interesting. However, be prepared that the biggest part of your work should be focused on the assignments and the midterms. The final exam counts for around 25-40% of your final grade. By that point, if you have done well on the assignments/midterms/term paper you could already have passed the class before the final exam. This could be important seeing that grades are only transferred as passed/not passed to UCPH with passed being >50%. Moreover, for many students at UBC, there is a "finals week" where all your exams are placed. Therefore, there are lower expectations for students at the final exam. To this end, it should be noted that difficult exams are "curved", such that you receive additional points if the overall score of the class is low. This is different from UCPH. I personally think that UBC is more interested in keeping a high score for their students, seeing that they depend on tuition.
teaching_comparison: I had a lot of courses where attendance was graded. This was pretty weird - I prefer the teaching style at UCPH. However, I liked the way that assignments count towards the final grade. This creates an incentive to follow the course closely - and takes pressure off the final exam.
courses_enrolled: Economics of Renewable Ressources (Econ 472) International Trade (Econ 455) Economics of Technological Change (Econ 339) International Political Economy (Poli 366)
recommended_courses: International Trade (Econ 455) and Economics of Renewable Ressources (Econ 472). Both are demanding but interesting. I cannot recommend Econ 339. The professor had a very irritating teaching style with an overemphasis on being pedagogical.
unexpected_costs: Food is expensive. I also had a pretty large budget, so I prioritized eating out several times a week. Moreover, every chance I got, we traveled out of Vancouver. This entails several extra costs for transportation, food and gear (especially skiing!).
cost_comparison: Food is expensive. Moreover, if you wan't to experience the country I would recommend buying a car. I bought one with two friends for +-20000 in total (4000 dollars). If your car does not break (as ours did :-)) then the resell value should be pretty close to the original price of the car.
activities_available: I joined a soccer team - an invaluable experience. Made a lot of new great friends.
activities_recommended: Join a team of some sort. There are a lot of possibilites.
weekend_recommendations: Hike in the mountains, visit Banff/Jasper, go to Whistler, surf in Tofino, visit Victoria. We also made a road trip to California.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Vancouver is pretty European in mindset. There are surprisingly many Asians. I would guess that there are more Chinese students than native canadians.
socializing_tips: Join clubs and link up with the other students from UCPH. We had a great group of 12 people from UCPH with whom I traveled a lot with.
cultural_challenges: Not any
culture_appreciated: The friendliness and respect. Be prepared to chat to people in grocery stores.
top3_advice: 1) Go explore the crazy nature of Canada, 2) Buy a car, 3) Be extrovert - see if you can join some of the Whatsapp groups for exchange students.
other_useful_info: Have a Canadian credit card if you want to stay at a hotel on Vancouver Island! Danish credit cards does not work. You can create a credit card at a bank such as RBC or CIBC.
most_rewarding: The nature experiences. I have been on the greatest hikes, road trips, and skiing trips.
greatest_challenge: Balancing school with all the opportunities outside school.
other_comments: I would 1000% recommend UBC to anyone. Experience of a lifetime.

socializing_tips: You don't have much time to chat during classes so ask them if they want to meet outsite of school ! Also if you live on campus then talk to people in the common rooms or join a club!
cultural_challenges: I thiI think that the teaching style and the general culture around stusying at a university was really diifferent and therefore a bit difficult to adjust to when you are used to another academic culture.

crucial_aspects: Good creative writing and anthropology programs and great natural surroundings.
info_ease: I think it was quite easy. There were introduction activities and helpful front desk services all around.
arrival_assistance: I was attached to a "buddy," who helped my get settled in my classes. Other exchange students helped out as well.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: To register for courses you list as many courses as you wish and they will assign you to five or so. The first two weeks of term you then have the opportunity to move around a bit. I ended up doing three courses instead of five as this was the demand from my home university.
registration_help: Not a lot of help during this process, but I didn't look for it either.
registration_success: I got into all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Try out as many courses as possible, but do as few at a time as you can - the workload is quite heavy at UBC.
course_level: I did mainly 300-level anthropology courses (my major) and one 200-level creative writing course. I liked them all, and found the level not too challenging. I could have taken 400-level instead no problem. The lower level courses will "baby" you more and give you many assignments to keep track of your work. The upper level courses have more freedom, but are obviously more complex as well.
teaching_comparison: Less participatory lectures, no seminars in my courses. I enjoyed the teaching style of all my profs, but they definitely didn't demand as much in-class participation or discussion as courses at UCPH. Also, they require more assignments during the term, which keeps you on top of things.
courses_enrolled: ANTH341 -Anthropology of Museums, Heritage and Memory, ANTH378- Anthropology of Media, CRWR205 - Introduction to Writing Creative Non-Fiction.
recommended_courses: I enjoyed all my courses, but mainly recommend CRWR205. UCPH doesn't offer courses in CRWR and it's a great way to develop your English language skills while you are here. The prof is amazing and engaging. I never missed a class. ANTH341 is interesting while being in Canada as it gives you some insight to Canadian history and indigenous politics. The prof is a little shy though, but I enjoyed her lectures none the less. ANTH378 was a classic and really good ANTH course, non-anth students could take it as well.
unexpected_costs: Food! So expensive to go grocery shopping. Also, if you want to go on many trips it will be expensive. Whistler/skiing in general is super pricy.
cost_comparison: Housing was slightly more than I anticipated for on campus housing, but similar or better than many other places in the city. Food was so, so expensive. Also, no cheap coffee on campus.
activities_available: So many clubs and societies available. Joined the surf-club and yoga-club, but I'm sad I didn't join the Varsity Outdoor Club (VOC) - old society at UBC that arranges all sorts of hiking, climbing, skiing etc. trips.
activities_recommended: Go on surf trips to Tofino and ski trips to Whistler. Join the VOC! The yoga club has lots of classes on campus and is quite cheap. Also take advantage of the aquatic center with a morning swim every once in a while.
weekend_recommendations: Go on as many.trips.as.possible. Don't hold back. Go hiking, skiing, surfing. Don't expect to much of Vancouver (it's called Raincouver and the No-Fun City). Nightlife is non-existent and everything is expensive. Take the trips.
culture_adjustment: Quite easy, similar to home. Canadians are adventurous and kind!
socializing_tips: Join VOC, Surf Club and other societies. And talk to people in your courses! Not just the exchange students. People are really nice, so don't be too shy.
cultural_challenges: Not really anything. Maybe the politeness - I felt quite rude in comparison.
culture_appreciated: Kindness, adventure, language. People really love and take advantage of the mountains.
top3_advice: Don't expect too much from the city, go on as many trips as possible and make the first move to get friends!
other_useful_info: Be prepared for food to be expensive. Be organized and take trips to cheaper super markets. Make the most of your stay, it goes by pretty fast.
most_rewarding: Ski season! And all of the sweet international students I got to meet.
greatest_challenge: It was expensive and I didn't enjoy the city. It got cold, grey and wet in the winter and before ski season starts it can be quite depressing. Workload on courses was heavier than what I'm used to at UCPH, although it wasn't more difficult.

crucial_aspects: I wanted a host university with English as the main language.
info_ease: Easy. UBC provided plenty of information on their website and as part of the exchange program.
arrival_assistance: Because of covid must information was online. We had an introduction to the university and how to thrive as a student on the canvas platform. We were also put into exchange groups on the week of arrival and got a tour guide.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was pretty messy because of covid - I was suppose to go on exchange in 2020 but ended up going in 2021, so I had to register for courses twice, but this is of course not UBC's fault. However - you need to make a priority list of 10 courses, which can be quite hard.
registration_help: I didn't really use the help provided, so I am not sure..
registration_success: I got all my first priorities.
registration_advice: Be sure to see if the courses you want to sign up for are running during the term you are on exchange - most of them only run during the fall or spring.
course_level: I took 300-level classes because I was in my 3rd year. But it is possible to take all kind of levels.
teaching_comparison: The style of teachings were very different in each of my course. The biggest difference is that in the Canadian school system they divide their exams into many pieces, which meant that I had two midterms during my term and one final exam in each course. This made me more stressed in the beginning but during my finals I has more time.
courses_enrolled: PHIL 332A Environmental Ethics SOCI 301 Sociology of Development SOCI 310 Canadian Society
recommended_courses: I really loved Environmental Ethics! It was challenging since I am used to studying anthropology but it was really interesting to learn how to argue in philosophy. The course very strait forward in it structure which made it easy to know what to suspect. And the topics were just very interesting - everything from First Nation perspectives on the environments to ecofeminism and climate change. The main goal was to discuss the moral problems arising in the context of human relationships to nature and to non-human living things.
unexpected_costs: I went on quite a few trips, when we had to rent cars, pay for gas etc. I also did a lot of skiing where I had to rent skies, boots etc.
cost_comparison: Groceries on campus was really expensive, but I you take a bus foe 15 minutes to the nearest No Frills you can save a looot of money.
activities_available: There is about 300 clubs that you can sign up for. There is also a recreation center with a gym, swimming facilities, dance classes, yoga classes, and martial arts - there is a free week to try out the classes and then you can sign up for a semester or 2.
activities_recommended: Go skiing in Whistler!! Buy a season pass (for students) and ski from november-april! You can rent skies and boots in Sports Junkies in Vancouver.
weekend_recommendations: During the summer: There are plenty of hikes to do in the area. Sign up for evo cars and rent them easily. Go to Vancouver Island and Tofino to surf. During winter: Whistler for skiing. In Vancouver there's plenty of cinemas and restaurants to explore.
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: Sign up for some of the clubs or try to find some study partners in your classes.
cultural_challenges: To say "How are you" all the time:)
culture_appreciated: The friendly and kindness of Canadians!
top3_advice: 1. Prepare what you want to see before you go to Canada! Otherwise you'll stress about it the first week which is a waste of time! 2. Get a approval of your drivers license from your home country (traffikstyrelsen) so that you can rent evo cars. 3. Spent as much time in nature as possible!
other_useful_info: Figure out what your priorities should be and what you want to spent most time on: school, making new connections, exploring nature, skiing, volunteering, working etc.
most_rewarding: The academically part was definitely most rewarding: learning to navigate in another educational system, being challenged on my academical knowledge, and forced out of my comfort zone.
greatest_challenge: Being away from my home and friends for that long was quite challenging.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go somewhere English speaking with a nice climate and beautiful surroundings
overall_comments: I would definitely recommend Vancouver and UBC to anyone going on exchange, it is a great campus and a beautiful city!
info_ease: The go global office was only available to contact through zoom in the beginning of the term, but it was still relatively easy to get answers to any questions.
arrival_assistance: I got help changing my course registrations.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I would definitely recommend Vancouver and UBC to anyone going on exchange, it is a great campus and a beautiful city!
registration_process: I filled out a list of 10 courses a long time before the term started, and I was then registered in some of them. It is possible to add and drop courses two weeks into the term, so it is pretty easy to get the courses you want.
registration_help: The go global office handled my course changes after the term started, which was nice. That way I was sure I was doing it right.
registration_success: I pretty much got the courses I wanted, I changed them a little around after I tried the courses I was registered for initially.
registration_advice: Try the courses out and make sure to change them if you feel like it. Some courses have crazy workloads for no real reason, and it's not worth spending all your time on exchange doing endless assignments.
academics_comments: I would definitely recommend Vancouver and UBC to anyone going on exchange, it is a great campus and a beautiful city!
course_level: I took one 300 level and two 400 level courses, and the level was about the same as I would expect at KU.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was very different in the different courses. In general there are more little homework assignments during the term, and especially in the smaller courses (<50 students) some participation was expected and graded.
courses_enrolled: MICB 325 Analysis of Microbial Genes and Genomes MICB 418 Industrial Microbiology and Biotechnology MICB 425 Microbial Ecological Genomics
recommended_courses: I would recommend all the courses, basically. 325 and 418 overlapped a bit with courses I had taken at home, so they were on the easier side. They were both more lecture-based with homework questions through the term. 425 had a more philosophical take on ecological microbiology and then transitioned to a more practical data science approach and had a group project in the end.
unexpected_costs: The dorm I was offered was very expensive
cost_comparison: Food in supermarkets was very expensive, eating out was pretty cheap (especially sushi, hehe). Staying in hotels was very expensive, which made it very expensive to stay in the Vancouver area after the term ended.
activities_available: A lot of athletic opportunities, and many of them were free or cheap for students. Things like the aquatic centre, the recreation centre (sports, dance and yoga classes, fitness etc.) and many other facilities were fun to explore.
activities_recommended: The hot tub in the aquatic centre, and the museums on campus are free to students.
weekend_recommendations: Go on hikes, there are many opportunities around north and west vancouver that are accessible with bus. Also exploring some of the more quiet neighbourhoods in vancouver, like the west side or burnaby.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy, vancouver is a very international city, so people are very used to many different cultures being mixed
socializing_tips: Come when there isn't a pandemic lol
cultural_challenges: Not really anything
culture_appreciated: People are very nice and polite, and open to talking to new people
top3_advice: The spring term ends really early, so you can travel for a month after the term and still have a full summer back home if you want. Vancouver is maybe even more gorgeous in real life than in pictures, and the weather is way better there than in all other places in Canada. Although a rainjacket and some waterproof shoes are essential.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Having an everyday life in a different city so far from home and meeting lots of new friends.
greatest_challenge: The term overlapped with the KU term in the beginning, which made the workload in the first month pretty hard. Also it can be a bit hard to talk to people at home due to the nine hour time difference.
other_comments: No

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgt UBC af tre grund: 1) jeg ville til et engelsk talende universitet, 2) jeg synes fagene på afdelingen Gender, Race, Sexuality & Social Justice lød mega spændende og 3) jeg drømte om at bruge min fritid udendørs og her er mulighederne uendelige i Canada
overall_comments: Jeg kan virkelig anbefale UBC og Vancouver, jeg havde et fuldstændig fantastiske ophold.
info_ease: Jeg synes UBC var rigtig god til at støtte udvekslingsstuderende i deres ankomst - de er også vandt til at få rigtig mange, tror der startede 5-600 på det semester jeg gik der.
arrival_assistance: Der blev afholdt forskellige arrangementer, både social og praktiske som skulle gøre det nemmere for de udveklsingsstuderende. Jeg deltog ikke i de sociale, og de af mine venner der gjorde var ikke vildt begejstret fordi arrangementerne på mange måder henvendte sig til et lidt yngre publikum (17-19 årige), hvor at de fleste andre danske udvekslingsstuderende jeg mødte var omkring 25 år. Men de praktiske arrangementer var rigtig givende! UBC har også en afdeling, som specifikt er der for at støtte de udvekslingsstuderende og dem kunne man altid hive fat i.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Jeg kan virkelig anbefale UBC og Vancouver, jeg havde et fuldstændig fantastiske ophold.
registration_process: Jeg husker ikke processen præcis, men UBC's afdeling for udvekslingsstuderende var gode til at hjælpe her.
registration_help: Afdelingen for udvekslingsstuderende, man kunne booke møder med dem og de afholdte også et par webinar inden registreringen blev åbnet.
registration_success: Jeg fik 3 ud af 4 og endte med at finde et udmærket sidste kursus. Her var add/drop perioden rigtig god, så jeg kunne teste et par af mine backups af.
registration_advice: Brug add/drop perioden. Og så vil jeg anbefale level 300 eller 400 fag, fordi folk ofte er lidt ældre her, niveauet er en smule højere, men der er også markant mindre obligatorisk arbejde i løbet af semesteret. Desuden havde mine fag på level 300+ ingen afsluttende eksaminer hvilket var ret nice.
academics_comments: Jeg kan virkelig anbefale UBC og Vancouver, jeg havde et fuldstændig fantastiske ophold.
course_level: Niveauet er ikke lige så højt som på KU, men tilgengæld er der flere obligatoriske afleveringer, test og deltagelse som er en del af ens bedømmelse i sidste ende. Således bliver undervisningen lidt som på gymnasiet i mine øjne. Men slap af når du er der, nyd Canada og så skal alt nok gå.
teaching_comparison: Det minder meget om KU, udover at seminar undervisning var præget af en gymnasie-agtig deltagelse, hvor studerende nogle gange sagde ting for at få point for deltagelse, men hvor deres bidrag enten var tæt på direkte gentagelse af hvad underviseren lige havde sagt.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Creative Writing Youth Activism & Social Justice Intersectional Approaches to Thinking Gender Contemporary Anthropological Theories
recommended_courses: Jeg var mega glad for Intersectional Approaches to Thinking Gender, og kan virkelig anbefale det kursus. Underviseren Bishop var kompetent og skabt et accessible læringmiljø. De tilføjede en masse perspektiver på køn, som jeg aldrig havde overvejet. Desuden var det ret sjovt at have Introduction to Creative Writing, det var lidt et hygge fag for mit vedkommende, men hvor jeg stadig fik en masse ud af det, som jeg kan bruge i min videre uddannelse. Contemporary Anthropological Theories var mit backup-fag, da jeg ikke fik faget Gender, Family and National states. Faget var fint og supplerede på mange måder faghistorie rigtig fint. Der var meget læsning, bl.a. læste vi 3 monografier i løbet af semesteret. Youth Activism & Social Justice var også meget lærerigt. Det var kunne på level 200 og derfor var undervisningen en smule gymnasie-agtig.
unexpected_costs: Jeg oplevede ikke nogle uforudsigelige udgifter, men mit budget blev sprunget lidt af spas, ture og andre sjove ting som jeg lavede med mine venner
cost_comparison: Mad var dyrt - det var lidt billigere en københavn at spise ude, men det var virkelig dyrt at handle i supermarkedet.
activities_available: Alt - og det er ikke en underdrivelse. Jeg tror dog at nogle af klubberne kunne være svære at få adgang til som udvekslingsstuderende, fordi de krævede minimum et års tilmelding
activities_recommended: Ud i naturen! Du er i Beautiful British Columbia. Der er så mange fede hikes omkring Vancouver. Jeg var på langrend for først gang hvilket var grinern. Jeg var ude og surfe. Jeg var ude og fiske. Grib mulighederne og hav ja-hatten på.
weekend_recommendations: Det er et must at tage til Banff og Jasper. Vancouver Island er også helt vildt smuk. Du skal gå Panorama Ridge!
culture_adjustment: Det var virkelig nemt synes jeg. Canadierne er vildt søde og jeg oplevede ikke nogle definerende kulturforskelle på universitetet
socializing_tips: Ræk ud. Canadierne er virkelig søde og er også rigtig gode til at smalltalke med den de sidder ved siden af til undervisningen - embrace it!
cultural_challenges: Jeg oplevede ikke de store kulturelle forskelle. På universitetet var det primært den lidt store aldersforskel som nogle gange kunne overraske.
culture_appreciated: Canadiere er så venlige! Men landet har også en mørk historie og jeg vil virkelig opfordre dig til at søge viden omkring hvad der er foregået.
top3_advice: Hav det grinern! Lad vær med at stress over det akademiske og grib alle de muligheder for sjove oplevelser du får - de er mindst lige så meget værd som om du lige får læst teksterne til i morgen.
other_useful_info: Ikke lige hvad jeg kan komme i tanke om.
most_rewarding: Er blevet markant bedre til akademisk og samtale engelsk, jeg har fået nogle fantastiske nye venner og haft en masse vilde oplevelser.
greatest_challenge: Det er super skræmmende at ankomme alene til at fremmede land og skulle finde ud af al ting selv - hvordan får man et telefonnr? Hvordan finder man et sted at bo? Hvordan får man en tid til lægen? osv osv. Men det skal nok gå alt sammen, alliere dig med andre udvekslingsstuderende og tro på dig selv (og man må godt ringe til familie og venner hjemme i Danmark og græde lidt, når alt bliver lidt for meget)
other_comments: Random, men en praktisk ting: jeg kan anbefale at bruge en tjeneste som fx Wise (der findes også andre, men det var lige den jeg brugt), hvor du kan få et visa-kort og nemt og billigt veksle mellem forskellige valutaer, samt fx overføre husleje.

crucial_aspects: I chose University of British Columbia because I wanted to go somewhere out of Europe and with a lot of nature. Canada is a extremely beautiful country and when you live in Vancouver the nature is very easy to access.
info_ease: I was easy enough to find information, but you shouldn't expect someone to just offer it to you, I lot of th things you have to find on your own.
arrival_assistance: When you are on exchange at UBC you are connected to their Go Global-program which helps exchange students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: Go Global
registration_success: I am very happy with the courses I ended up in. I ended up dropping some of the courses I initially thought I wanted to follow because the material was different than I expected but then found other interesting courses.
registration_advice: Look at courses from home. Sign up for more classes than you need and try them up when you get here. Sign up fro classes that you can't have at home.
