course_level: 300 courses are waaaaayy too easy, think 1'st semester. 400 classes is a massive jump think about appropriate for 5th semester at home, but with a "heavier" workload in that you have at least 2 midterms and 1 exam in every class, meaning you end up with 4 classes having essentially 12 exams. So 400 aren't more difficult, just the level you're used to, but with a different workload.
teaching_comparison: Pretty similar, no "hold timer" though at least not in anyway that resembles back home, so very individual learning, essentially only lectures.
recommended_courses: 333 was great, amazing professor, don't touch 345 with a 10 foot pole, the professor is the worst I've ever had. 355 was also good. 371 was very boring and by far the easiest class, which is saying something.
unexpected_costs: Not really any
cost_comparison: Food is pretty expensive to make yourself, takeout and restaurants are considerably cheaper than back home, so you end up spending a lot on food, especially if you want anything remotely healthy since the quality in general isn't that great unless you go to special stores.
activities_available: All kinds, there are like a thousand clubs, if you have an interest, there is a club for it, but some of them are pretty niche, and it isn't as chill as one might think, the people who are in these clubs make their hobbies a fundament part of their personality. If you imagine the surf club they live up to all the stereotypes that you have, and the outdoor club as well. All the clubs are very stereotypical of what you think, they live up to their image in an almost comical sense.
activities_recommended: As I said, the surf trip to tofino, the outdoor club's very week activities and also their "rock" part which is a rock climbing getaway, very fun.
weekend_recommendations: If you are going in the 5th semester as most people probably are, PACK your September and early October with stuff, don't ever have a weekend free, because the sun and good weather disappears fast, and when it's gone it's gone. I highly recommend going to the Campbell river to see grizzly bears and the salmon run which happens in the end of September start of October every year, it's sick. Go to panorama ridge, and again go in September or early October, just hike as much as possible, once the weather is bad, you won't be getting out, it will be too cold to do any longer hikes, so really really take advantage of of the first month and a half, stuff it with as many activities as possible.
culture_adjustment: very easy, although they don't have a party culture at all, if you want to have fun nightlife Vancouver is NOT for you, that place is ass concerning the night life scene, and everybody knows it. If you ask the locals what they do they will consistently answer "nothing" because there genuinly isn't anything.
socializing_tips: you have to join a club and preferably multiple it's a must especially if you don't get on campus housing, and even if you do you need to be lucky with the people living with you.
cultural_challenges: none
culture_appreciated: none.
top3_advice: Get on campus housing, join a club, go outside as much as possible, if you spend a single weekend not hiking the first month and a half you're wasting your time, because it's only an option in the beginning.
other_useful_info: no
most_rewarding: the travels I went on, I went to San Fran, Seattle and New York ,that was fun. lot of people go to Banff but I had been already, but again you can only go to Banff and those places before the 20th of October basically where after that it's over.
greatest_challenge: Finding people older than 18 and who were worth hanging out with.

crucial_aspects: English speaking country, and that the nature was different than i DK, and that it was accessible.
info_ease: It was somewhat easy, mainly because of the other danish exchange student. We helped each other out a lot
arrival_assistance: I didn't receive any upon arrival, but I did get assistance a few weeks into the semester, in changing my courses, so that it fitted my academic profile more.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Very confusing. But as soon as spoke to a person from go global irl, he made it a lot easier for me. Just had trouble finding the office on campus... big campus
registration_help: In-person and over mail, although through mail it is always more complicated and takes a lot longer than it has to.
registration_success: Not very. I ended up with some quite strange courses, that doesn't really fit into my profile as much as I wanted, but it was the only available ones.
registration_advice: Depending on the expectations and requirements from their home uni, I would say that the courses you are going to take on exchange, don't expect them to fit completely in with your academic profile. See the course more as extra, that may feed in to more hobby-based interest. Although you can get lucky, especially if you don't study something in humanities or arts... typical
course_level: Tbh I am a bit disappointed in the level of the courses... Seeing as UBC is in the top 50th universities in the world, I was really disappointed in some of my courses. I didn't expect to make myself dumber for a final paper, because I wasn't allowed to be critical of a theory, but only convey the key elements of the theory. On a 400 level course!! That was surprising, and not in a good way...
teaching_comparison: It is very strange actually. In KU the settings are much more informal. I call my prof. by their first names, and they see us as peers more than students, but I don't know that much, if anything about their personal lives. Whereas at UBC, the framework is very formal, in addressing the prof. by their last names, and being seen a lot more like a student rather than a peer, but I know a lot more of private information about my profs. there. Very strange and kind of difficult to navigate.
courses_enrolled: ARTH_V/VISA_V 479 001 2025W1 Performance Actions and Approaches PHIL_V 416A A_001 2025W1 Topics in 19th-Century Philosophy SOCI_V 414 101 2025W1 Feminist Theory THTR_V 443A A_001 2025W1 Women in Theatre and Film
recommended_courses: If you are in to performance art, I would highly recommend Performance Actions and Approaches with prof. Camille Georgeson-Usher. It was by far my favorite courses of my exchange. In comparison to the other courses, she didn't mind us calling her Camille, and she saw us as peers more than students. And i addition, she is doing a lot of practical and curatorial work also, so you really get hands on knowledge, and it is all very up-to-date, and she is just a really good communicator
unexpected_costs: I don't think I have any. Maybe like car rentals or ferry ticktes. But otherwise none.
cost_comparison: Less expensive was the groceries, gas prices, uber, dining out More expensive buying alcohol
activities_available: There were a lot. Some times a bit to much, so it got confusing... I think I would have participated more, if I had lived on campus...
activities_recommended: Joining the outdoor club, cause they have rentals like tents an such. But otherwise I don't know.
weekend_recommendations: Vancouver Island - Campell River was really nice! Also rent a car and drive up to Whistler and Squamish, and do some hikes and sleep in the car - just make sure it is a place that is legal! Also highly recommend taking a longer trip to Banff! We rented a camper van and drove around Banff for four days. Was magical! Do it sooner rather than later, so it dosn't get to cold to sleep in the car. Also really liked Seattle, but that trip kind a depends on the situation in the u.s., but really cool city - only four hours with bus from Van
culture_adjustment: Somewhat easy. Like the cheap prices a Tim Hortons, and just in general the prices on service and dining out - really nice! Hard to adjust to the bars and so closing a 2 a.m., and all the locals just going home to sleep after... Even at like house parties, they close around midnight maybe if you are lucky at 1 a.m., and people just go home to sleep - disappointing.
socializing_tips: It's hard. Everybody is really busy and stressed, because they take so many courses and extra points ans such. Much easier to socializing with the other exchange students. A bit sad though. Byt doing group-work with local students in class, is a way to talk with them a bit more and a little bit informal.
cultural_challenges: People going home so early. And the very big portions of groceries - very difficult to just buy like a single banana, or one coke - you have to buy the whole thing.
culture_appreciated: That everybody is just really kind. Even if they say that the Canadians in Vancouver is more closed off, they are much more welcoming and friendly, than any place in Europe.
top3_advice: Go enjoy the nice weather quickly! Go in weekend-trips in the beginning - do all the hikes as soon as possible! It is true, when the rain comes it doesn't stop... It rains more than DK... Also don't spend money on whale-safari! It is really expensive, and really bad for the whales! Just take the boat to Vancouver Island or Bowen Island or such
other_useful_info: Don't stress about your grade that much. You only need 50% and that is really easy to attain.
most_rewarding: Cliché, but I would say the people I met. I made some really good connections and friendships that I am very fond off. Also, enjoying the nature! Banff is some of the most beautiful nature I have ever seen.
greatest_challenge: Finances... It is very expensive going on exchange. And you are in constant limbo as to spending money on trips and such, but also needing money for practical stuff... Very difficult

crucial_aspects: To experience North American college-culture and then the nature in British Columbia!
info_ease: I would say it was fairly easy. The GoGlobal office is very good at helping incoming students. Just make sure to also look into things yourself and go to the introdays and so on.
arrival_assistance: A general introday for exchangestudents.
arrival_comments: Seriously do not hesitate to reach out to Go Global they are very helpful.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: For grad-students. Send email to professer teaching the course you wish where you introduce yourself and clarify why you are eligible to take the course. Wait for their reply. Then forward the email to the department offering the course, and then the faculty for grad-studies. And then Go Global. There is also a whole bunch of course registration for EVERYONE beforehand by GoGlobal, which does not really matter when you need grad courses.
registration_help: GoGlobal and then reaching out to the professors and departments. Also I showed up at the math departments office in the first week because they had not replied to my emails.
registration_success: I got 2/3 of the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: If you are a grad student - do email the relevant professorts before the term starts so that you can get enrolled fast. Everyone are very busy in the first weeks of class, so you get the best help beforehand.
course_level: So I had one exceptionally easy introductory statistics course (545A+B), which I picked cause I knew it would be easy. And then 2 very hard math courses - the prerequisites they listed were not quite explicit enough, so my background was a bit insufficient. Both of them were only assignment/take home exams and they were still hard work. It is possible to do it, just don't expect the level 500 math courses to be a lower workload than graduate math courses at KU :)
teaching_comparison: Fairly similar honestly. A bit more discussion-based, but not by much.
courses_enrolled: STAT545A+B Exploratory Data Analysis, MATH503 Discrete Mathematics and MATH516 Partial Differential Equations.
recommended_courses: Both math courses were good and very interesting. And the professors were excellent. I was just struggling because my background is in probability and not so much functional analysis and algebra :)
unexpected_costs: Grocery shopping is very expensive (go to NO FRILLS or T&T. And the housing comes without ANYTHING.
cost_comparison: Food. 50DKK for organic yoghurt... And then you can go eat out for 75DKK, which makes no sense
activities_available: There are so many things. Calender parties, weird social events with student housing and also sometimes faculty-specific things I think. You can also do sports - swimming, yoga, pilates jiujitsu and what not. Just sign up!!!
activities_recommended: VOC (Varsity Outdoor Club) a very nice community and great for giving you inspiration for what trips could be nice. And the UBC-filmsociety. You pay 5 dollars ONCE and then they screen 4 movies every week in a small actual cinema. And they have some nice niche stuff. And use the libraries there. They have both course-books but also A LOT of fiction.
weekend_recommendations: Go to Squamish and Whistler for hiking and skiing! And to Vancouver Island! Also a trip to Seattle is worth it.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. But I was also mainly close to other exchange students.
socializing_tips: Talk to the people in your classes! Most Canadians are fairly open. And join some of the VOC-trips.
cultural_challenges: None in particular. It is more normal to small-talk with strangers.
culture_appreciated: Small-talking with strangers is very cute when you are an exchange-student feeling lonely. Also Canadians are nice. But Vancouverites are less so than other Canadians.
top3_advice: Just stay on top of the administrative things cause they are not that bad, and try to not have courses that you absolutely NEED to take. Be flexible, then it will be very easy.
other_useful_info: Not really.
most_rewarding: Being in such a beatiful place and experiencing the whole college-culture. It is crazy.
greatest_challenge: Being away from friends and family.

crucial_aspects: I really like Canada as a country, the people are friendly and nice - had travelled here before - but hadn't been on the West Coast yet. Heard good things about Vancouver as a city and metropole with amazing opportunities in terms of exploring beautiful nature and outdoor activities. And then I chose UBC because of it's good reputation.
info_ease: I think it was fairly straight forward. I must admit that I have a good friend who was also on abroad at UBC the semester before me, so I had some sort of a hotline connection to her, where I could ask her stuff I wasn't sure about, which helped me quite a lot.
arrival_assistance: Nothing in particular really. But I'll also emphasize that going to Vancouver on exchange is probably one of the smallest culture shocks or changes one can experience, if deciding to study somewhere outside of EU. We had a intro-day at UBC, which provided information and a tour around Campus but besides that I figured things out myself.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was step-by-step pretty straight forward. One step at a time, nothing complex. Just check KU-mail regularly and then everything is streamlined. The proces was transparent and made sense all the way through.
registration_help: Guess help was available if wanted. If something isn't done correctly in the process, then they people at UBC are good at writing to you about what needs to be corrected.
registration_success: Successful. Got the courses I applied for. Didn't do the exchange for the courses though. I found something that sounded interesting. But fair to say it isn't perfectly related to my study at KU. But that's the beauty of going on exchange.
registration_advice: Use this site, and make sure that the courses you apply for correlate with the Faculty that you are enrolled in:
course_level: Somewhat easy to be fair. I bit difficult because I'm not used to delve into e.g. anthropological academics, but it's also 200-level courses which maybe explains the level. I think it was okay. Wasn't here in Vancouver to drown in school stuff :) But the courses were interesting and learned a lot from them!
teaching_comparison: Pretty much the same, but slightly more weekly submissions, lecture notes and stuff like that to make sure that you are following along the pensum. Some courses do attendance. Either explicitly or implicitly by having in-class activities you have to submit, and you can only do them if you are there physically.
courses_enrolled: ANTH_V 217 001 Culture and Communication ENST_V 211 101 The State of the Earth SOCI_V 260 101 Work and Society SOCI_V 280 101 Data and Society
recommended_courses: ENST_V 211 101 The State of the Earth: It's like geography, but in an interesting way. SOCI_V 260 101 Work and Society: Learned about work and how that has changed through history and also varies between countries and that. SOCI_V 280 101 Data and Society: A lot about AI and automation which is somewhat diffuse, but relevant to learn about it
unexpected_costs: I will just say that's extremely difficult to budget an exchange, and some months where expensive because of weekend trips basically every weekend. Bank account is bleeding, but social and cultural capital is levelling up (Bourdieu).
cost_comparison: Groceries are less expensive than expected.
activities_available: All sorts. So many clubs. Some would say too many.
activities_recommended: The VOC (Varsity Outdoor Club). I did some hikes with them. They were amazing and meet people through that activity that I eventually did weekend trips with on own hand.
weekend_recommendations: Everything :) No for real, get outside. Nature stuff like the following. Garibaldi, Panorama Ridge, Joffre Lakes, Cypress, Grouse and Crown Mountain. Vancouver Island: Tofino, Ucluelet, 5040 Peak, Campbell River, Sooke, Victoria Banff: Sentinel Pass, Moraine Lake, Plain of Six Glaciers, Johnston Canyon Go to Seattle, Olympic and Mt Rainier National Park
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: In every class, see if you can find someone to talk with. They are all friendly and interested in you and your life back home.
cultural_challenges: None. Took me a week to accept the premise of tipping 15-20% at restaurants and places like that.
culture_appreciated: How open and talkative Canadians are.
top3_advice: Life here is expensive, but not as expensive as in CPH. Only more expensive because you do more stuff than back home. Bring some Gore-Tex. It rains quite a lot, but on Sunny days, Vancouver is amazingggg. So get here early (a few weeks before school starts maybe) to enjoy the weather in August, if starting september. Canada is multicultural. It's fascinating to hear stories and origins of fellow students, and make sure to spend some time getting to understand Vancouver, the Indigenous people. It's interesting.
other_useful_info: If you don't get housing on-campus, then Downtown Vancouver is maybe not the perfection option to go with. I really liked it, but if I had to choose a place to live now that I have been here for some amount of time, I'd say either Kitsilano or Mt. Pleasant are good options as well. Though Downtown is also nice, but maybe a bit to central. Like living in K in Copenhagen or sum'tin.
most_rewarding: The hikes and trips with people.
greatest_challenge: To accept the fact that it's not possible to do everything you want to do. We have 24 hours a day, and need time to recharge sometimes. Be proactive and do stuff, but also chill and enjoy the fact that you live abroad and life is good, no matter if you do many things or not.
other_comments: Yolo

crucial_aspects: The nature, the academic level and reputation, the courses available and their fit with my mandatory bachelor courses.
overall_comments: Didn't get on-campus housing and first apartment (airbnb) was really bad and uncomfortable. Second apartment was really good but only minus was that it was far away from campus (10km). It was a great experience except from my housing situation.
info_ease: Very easy and accessible.
arrival_assistance: Didn't get any assistance exept from information on exchange student orientation days.
arrival_comments: Very easy! The exchange office at UBC is great, very proactive and always physically at campus to help you immediately.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Didn't get on-campus housing and first apartment (airbnb) was really bad and uncomfortable. Second apartment was really good but only minus was that it was far away from campus (10km). It was a great experience except from my housing situation.

registration_help: UBC exchange office was very kind and helpful, that really made the experience better!

registration_advice: Relax to begin with and wait for free spots at filled courses when the term starts.
academics_comments: Didn't get on-campus housing and first apartment (airbnb) was really bad and uncomfortable. Second apartment was really good but only minus was that it was far away from campus (10km). It was a great experience except from my housing situation.
course_level: 3rd and 4 year courses equivalent to 3rd year courses on UCPH.
teaching_comparison: More physical learning at UCPH with valuable exercise classes, but actually pretty similar.
courses_enrolled: Econ 421 - Introductory game theory and applications Econ 455 - International trade Phil 369 - Philosophy of Science Econ 333 - Economic history (...)
recommended_courses: Phil 369 was very hard compared to UCPH but was really interesting too, and the small classes provided great circumstances for finding Canadian friends. Econ 333: Great teacher (Mario) and very exciting material - every class was a pleasure, and the readings was worth reading.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Housing was more expensive as we got a bad house in the beginning and had to get something more expensive afterwards to get it quickly. On campus housing is very cheap though.
activities_available: All of them.
activities_recommended: Join the outdoor club - it's great! Also try something new, that is really where you meet new friends.
weekend_recommendations: The mountains north of Vancouver, Whistler in the Winther, Banff (moraine lake). San Fransisco is also great (but expensive).
culture_adjustment: Very easy, it's pretty similar to DK just a litte more open, outgoing and doesn't drink as much.
socializing_tips: Seek clubs or courses which are not filled with exchange students. Get out of your comfort zone and take the first step, most Canadian people love to socialize;)
cultural_challenges: Tipping culture, but its easy to get used to.
culture_appreciated: The openess to be different and the courage to be unlike everybody else. Its very multicultural, that's very cool and one of the most valuable experiences.
top3_advice: See a bear, join a club doing something you are not (yet) good at, don't do it all - do all the most important things.
other_useful_info: There is a lot of midterm exams counting toward your final grade which can be hard if you choose tough courses but also make the final exam easier.
most_rewarding: Making a friendgroup with Canadian students and bouldering (a lot) with one of them + my roomate.
greatest_challenge: Too establish a life away from home, friends and family, and also to get over difficulties with housing while participating in a lot of activities at the same time.
other_comments: no

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne til et sted hvor jeg talte sproget, så jeg nemmere kunne lære lokale at kende og have flere valg ift. tilbudte kurser. Derudover ville jeg gerne opleve naturen omkring Vancouver med både fantastisk smuk kyst og bjerglandskab. Jeg havde også hørt godt om Vancouver som by, der er meget international og multikulturel, hvilket gør det nemt at falde til som udvekslingsstuderende. Og Canadierne er meget gæstfri og søde som folk.
overall_comments: Vancouver er fantastisk. Det eneste der rigtig gør det svært at være her er huslejeprisen, og bøvlet med bolig. Og så skal man være forberedt på rimelig meget regn (også ift. Danmark). Men det hele bliver opvejet af hvor smukt her er. Et semester er slet ikke nok til at opleve det hele.
info_ease: Det var super nemt og UBC og GoGlobal er generelt meget hjælpsomme og svarer langt hurtigere end KU.
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik hjælp fra GoGlobal til kursusregistrering og forskellige administrative ting med underskrifter. De holdt også nogle velkomstseminarer både fysisk og online inden man kom. Vi fik også mange mails med meget brugbar information.
arrival_comments: Ift. det akademiske fik vi næsten for meget information, men jeg kunne godt have brugt mere orientering der hjalp med at socialisere med andre udvekslingsstuderende i starten.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

Danmark). Men det hele bliver opvejet af hvor smukt her er. Et semester er slet ikke nok til at opleve det hele.
registration_process: Man finder kurserne på ubc's hjemmeside og kan så sammensætte et skema på Workday (ala ku.net). Så søgte vi 10 kurser, der ikke måtte overlappe skemamæssigt. Jeg fik 6 af dem, selvom man kun skal bruge fire. Kan anbefale at starte med for mange kurser da man kan droppe ud af dem man synes er mindst interessante de første 2 uger. Det er også relativt nemt at skifte/tilføje nye kurser de første to uger, selv hvis det først ligner at de er fyldte - der kan sagtens åbne nye pladser op når andre skifter. Det gælder bare om at holde øje løbende. Her er det canadiske system ret fleksibelt.
registration_help: GoGlobal og fakultetet var meget hjælpsomme hvis man kontaktede dem, og der blev holdt flere onlineseminarer der forklarede alt + sendt en masse info per email.
registration_success: Jeg fik de kurser jeg ville have. Der var dog nogle af de mindre faglige og "sjovere" kurser der var sværere at få.
registration_advice: Lav en masse research hjemmefra, men stress ikke hvis du ikke får dine topprioriteter i første omgang - du kan stadig nå at ændre kurser når du kommer. Søg på kurserne og professorerne på Rate my Professor. Find mere information om kurserne ved at google kurset og "syllabus" eller skriv direkte til professoren. Vælg nogle fag der ikke har en eksamen (kun opgaver) så du har fritid i eksamensperioderne. Især midterm-perioden er fed at kunne rejse i i stedet for at læse op hele tiden. UBC har også en karakterstatistik side hvis du går op i det - generelt er der dog meget få der dumper kurser derovre, og som ku-studerende er man jo pass-fail.

Danmark). Men det hele bliver opvejet af hvor smukt her er. Et semester er slet ikke nok til at opleve det hele.
course_level: Jeg tog 2 level 400 kurser som var virkelig spændende og jeg lærte en masse. Og så tog jeg to level 300 kurser der også var spændende, men hvor niveauet var væsentligt lavere. Vil dog ikke anbefale at tage 4 level 400 kurser hvis du har lyst til at lavet andet på udveksling end at læse. Hvis du har økonomisk baggrund fra DK og tager økonomikurser på UBC er det meget anderledes, da der sjældent er (svær) matematik i deres kurser her. Til gengæld kan der være meget læsning og fokus på teoretisk forståelse.
teaching_comparison: Forelæsningerne mindede meget om dem derhjemme, men jeg havde ingen øvelsestimer/holdtimer på UBC. Det kan man godt finde enkelte kurser der har, men det er ikke så udbredt som på KU. Det savnede jeg klart, men da der var mindre matematik var det heller ikke så nødvendigt.
courses_enrolled: GEOG_342 - Post- and Anti Colonial Geographies ECON_335 - Fertility, Family and Human Migration ECON_485 - Political Economy FRE_490 - Impact Evaluation Analytics (muligvis skrevet på hjemmesiden som Current Issues in Food and Resource Economics - der har vist været en fejl med navnet i flere år)
recommended_courses: GEOG_342 - Post- and Anti Colonial Geographies - Et meget spændende perspektiv på blandt andet degrowth og klimagæld (samt mange andre issues) med en virkelig dygtig og engageret professor (Priti). Ingen midterm eller eksamen og en masse små quizzes du nemt får point for - nemt at bestå. Ingen mødepligt. ECON_335 - Fertility, Family and Human Migration - Meget spændende artikler/readings og spændende fag/perspektiv på økonomi generelt. Dog ret lavt niveau. Der er både eksamen og midterm, men de er ikke så svære igen. Fianl project er en Poster (+ mindre afleveringer) lavet i gruppe som tæller 40% af karakteren - så nemt at bestå. Gruppearbejdet er godt til at møde andre - især lokale. ECON_485 - Political Economy - Vildt spændende og udfordrende fag med meget læsning. Claudio er virkelig en god forelæser. Hvis du vil lære om korruption, demokrati/autokrati, hvorfor stater er rige/fattige er dette et vildt fedt kursus. Men det går hen over mange forskellige emner og ikke i dybden med dem. Der er ingen mødepligt men quizzes + participation tæller samlet 30%. FRE_490 - Impact Evaluation Analytics Et virkelig fedt fag med en fantastisk og engageret professor Sean. Det er et lille hold hvor der bliver brugt meget tid på gruppearbejde og diskussion i undervisningen, og næsten ingen tid på traditionel forelæsning. Mange af de canadiske studerende kender hinanden og Sean, og det skaber en virkelig fed dynamik i undervisningen. Der er virkelig meget gruppearbejde og ingen eksamener, og det er super nemt at lære nogle lokale at kende i faget. Fokus er på evaluering af udviklingsprojekter, men logikken kan overføres til al slags projektarbejde. Det er fedt at faget er meget hands on. Det er også fuldstændig umuligt at dumpe hvis du bare engagerer dig minimalt.
unexpected_costs: Huslejen er dyr, ellers bare rejser og en masse restaurantbesøg. Forsikring var også lidt dyrere end jeg havde regnet med. (De tal jeg har skrevet er omtrente beløb jeg ikke er helt sikker på - men regn med at det bliver virkelig dyrt.)
cost_comparison: Husleje + rejser og ski var dyrere. Restaurant og bar er lidt billigere end i København. Offentlig transport er meget billigt. Der er et obligatorisk rejsepas man skal købe gennem UBC, som jeg tror var knap 800 kr. for semestret og dækker hele Metro Vancouver. Cykler kan fås meget billigt på Facebook Marketplace (mange til ca. 500 kr.)
activities_available: Der er helt vildt mange klubber at vælge imellem - uanset hvad du er til kan du finde det. Der er fx vildt mange sportsklubber, outdorrklub, surfklub, bageklubber, en filmklub med næsten gratis biograf og endda en Skandinavisk klub...
activities_recommended: Jeg var UBC's Varsity Outdoor Club der har mange vandreture, muligheder for klatring, camping, kajakture mv. Vær dog opmærksom på at det er en klub for de avancerede outdoor-typer og ikke den gennemsnitlige vandreglade dansker. De fleste af os fra KU var kun på "begynder" turene, eller dem lige over. Du kan også leje grej gratis gennem klubben. Skiklubben er god at være med i hvis du vil kunne leje ski og støvler gratis. Der er en skitur til Whistler i efteråret, men der er rift om pladserne. De holder også et par fester, men jeg syntes ikke de var specielt gode. Jeg var også med i Agronomy Garden der er en fælles køkkenhave der mødes en gang om ugen. Det er en meget chill måde at møde nogle lokale, da der næsten ikke er nogle udvekslingsstuderende.
weekend_recommendations: Stå på ski, tag ud at vandre. Tag til Seattle, til Vancouver Island - og op i bjergene. Inden semestret var jeg i Rocky Mountains og tog en roadtrip fra Calgary gennem en masse af nationalparkerne der, til Vancouver Island og sluttede i Vancouver. Det kan virkelig anbefales at nå at se noget af naturen mens det er sommer! Man kan også nå at se meget i September og Oktober, men derefter er det svært at tage mange steder hen, da det bliver for koldt i bjergene og regner hele tiden ved kysten.
culture_adjustment: Nemt, canadierne er meget gæstfri og der er virkelig mange internationale både på UBC og i Vancouver generelt.
socializing_tips: Klubber og vær social i undervisningen - men det er svært rigtigt at blive tæt med dem. Gør en aktiv indsats og prøv evt at finde nogle lokale at bo med.
cultural_challenges: Ingen af betydning. Var lidt træt af at tax og tips ikke er inkluderet i prisen nogle steder.
culture_appreciated: Venligheden og åbenheden. Hvor stor en del af folks liv det er at være aktive og tage ud i naturen.
top3_advice: Tag ud i naturen, spis en masse lækker mad, engager dig på uni.
other_useful_info: Ikke umiddelbart.
most_rewarding: Alle oplevelserne uden for uni. Men også de spændende og anderledes fag man kunne få.
greatest_challenge: At være her alene i starten og vejret i November og December. Det regner meget mere end man forventer - ca dobbelt så meget som i København.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ønskede et sted, som var en del anderledes end Danmark. Hvor der var natur, og hvor man kunne lave nogle ting/ tage på ture som ikke mindede om det man kan omkring Danmark.
overall_comments: Jeg elskede Canada, Vancouver og UBC!
info_ease: Rimelig nemt. Dog havde jeg en del problemer med godkendelse af fag fra KU's side. UBC var virkelig gode og hurtige til at svare på mail. De har virkelig styr på tingene, i forhold til udveksling.
arrival_assistance: UBC afholder hvert år, for de nye studerende, en introdag. Her møder man en masse andre studerende som også er på udveksling, fra hele verden. Man føler sig taget rigtig godt om, og meget tryg.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Jeg elskede Canada, Vancouver og UBC!
registration_process: Det var nemt. Der var en deadline et par dage inde i semestret.
registration_help: Der er en masse kontorer, og andre ansatte på skolen som var enormt søde til at hjælpe.
registration_success: Meget! Jeg fik alle de hold/ kurser jeg gerne ville. Bortset fra Europæisk Politik, som er et obligatorisk kursus på 5. semester på Statskundskab. UBC tilbød bare ikke kurset, det specifikke semester jeg var afsted. Ellers var det rimelig okay, at få plads og få godkendt alt. Jeg valgte også, hjemmefra at kontakte en professor på UBC i forhold til Pensumplanen som man skal bruge til sin forhåndsgodkendelse, og han svarede virkelig hurtigt. Hvilket er en tendens der er på alle kontorerene på UBC. De er meget hurtige til at svare.
registration_advice: Hver ude i god tid. Og lav alt forarbejdet hjemmefra.
academics_comments: Jeg elskede Canada, Vancouver og UBC!
course_level: Jeg tog kurser på forskellige niveauer. Men vil klart anbefale, at tage kurser på level 300. De er meget mere interessante og folk er mere på bølgelængde med hvad vi er i Danmark.
teaching_comparison: Det hele foregår i hånden. Det skulle man lige vende sig til. Og der er meget mere udenadslæren, men ikke særlig meget teori eller kritisk tænkning. Så på den måde føles det nemmere end det er i Danmark.
courses_enrolled: POLI_V 220 - Introduction to Political Systems Around the World POLI_V 304 - British Columbia Government and Politics POLI_V 312 - Threats to Contemporary Democracies POLI_V 341 - Contemporary Political Theory
recommended_courses: POLI_V 341 - Contemporary Political Theory. Jeg elskede det her kursus og professoren. Det var det fedeste og mest geniale kursus. Mega interessant. Kæmpe anbefaling, hvis man godt kan lide Politisk Teori eller bare nyder en virkelig god underviser der fanger alle sine elever.
unexpected_costs: Alt det man skal købe til sit værelse på skolen overraskede mig lidt. Især at køkkenerne ikke har noget overhovedet.
cost_comparison: At spise ude er virkelig billigt i forhold til København. Det er virkelig lækkert. Især deres sushi.
activities_available: UBC er et kæmpe campus som tilbyder alle former for klubber, grupper osv. Tror man kan alt på campus.
activities_recommended: Der er klubber til alle interesser. Og en af de første dage i semestret, er der en kæmpe 'Club-fair', hvor man kan møde alle klubberne.
weekend_recommendations: Kæmpe anbefaling, at tage til Banff. Det er en nationalpark der ligger i Alberta. Det er noget af det smukkeste jeg nogensinde har set. Jeg var der i Oktober, i omkring 4 hele dage. Vi lejede en Van, hvor vi campede og kørte rundt i parken. Det var helt fantastisk. Man kan enten køre dertil fra Vancouver, eller flyve til Calgary. Vi fandt nogle billige billetter og fløj. Ellers at stå på ski er også helt fantastisk. Vi var en gruppe der holdte jul i en lille hytte, i en by lidt nordpå, der hedder Nelson. Det var virkelig magisk og en kæmpe anbefaling.
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. De snakker engelsk.
cultural_challenges: Ikke rigtig noget. De er meget europæiske.
culture_appreciated: Den måde de bruger naturen på. Regn eller sne, de er altid udenfor. De er aktive og elsker at lave ting i naturen.
top3_advice: Tag på en masse ture, hike og være i naturen, og husk en regnjakke. (Det regner enormt meget)
other_useful_info: Husk en regnjakke! Vancouver ligger midt i en storslået tempererede regnskov, med gigantiske træer og har et meget rigt dyreliv. Sug så meget af deres udendørs kultur til dig!
most_rewarding: De venner jeg har fået! Det er virkelig uvurderligt.

crucial_aspects: Vancouver is a city located in close proximity to some of the most beautiful natural areas in the world. Mountains and temperate rainforests surround the region and are easily accessible compared to Copenhagen. Moreover, the province of British Columbia is a major global supplier of wood, which is why UBC possesses some of the most advanced forestry expertise.
info_ease: I would think that it always is a confusing time whenever one moves to a different country. However, i thought that the process was quite easy, based on the circumstances of being abroad. I was lucky enough to have accomodation through the campus, so i already knew when the dorm let me move in. Then it was just a matter of showing up at the designated time. UBC sends out plenty information, way to much in my opnion. If you succesfully get through the application i would say you are more than capable of finding your way once you arrive.
arrival_assistance: My dorm had a designated move-in day, so I knew when to arrive. I had volunteered to help on that day, which allowed me to move in a day earlier. The work was really easy. I mostly directed people and traffic along with a few others. Even though I didn’t know my way around campus, it was simple, trust me. I also got the chance to meet some other people during move-in, which was a nice way to start life at the dorm. Plus, I received a $20 CAD gift card for the campus food halls.
arrival_comments: Workday sucks, it just does. I had trouble with it because I am a graduate student, which meant I needed approval from individual lecturers to be admitted to the courses. It all worked out in the end, but it was quite stressful having only a few weeks before the semester started and not knowing whether I had secured the courses I wanted. If possible, avoid graduate courses for this reason unless you know you have access to multiple faculties and therefore a wide range of courses to apply to. It worked out for me and for others, but be cautious. I had to choose graduate courses, so I did not have a choice. Besides that the different intro videos gave an insight into some of the essentials. I don't think it's necessary to watch them while they are being streamed though. You get the same information out of scrolling through the slides. You just need to know which documents you need before entering Canada (ex. eta). You get acces to a canvas course where all that information is available.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You get login information to workday, and navigate their platform. When you plan for courses make sure they're available for that term.
registration_help: I was able to contact the Faculty of Forestry, they were quite helpful, but sometimes they took a long time to answer. Go Global were also helpful, but they took forever to answer... Write everything in the first email you send to them.
registration_success: I got everything i wanted, but there is an add/drop period where you have time to get other courses, if the once you got initially isn't to your liking. Here you'll be able to add courses if others have dropped them and a spot has become available.
registration_advice: Choose undergrad courses.
course_level: I thought the courses were appropriate in how hard they were, some where however too easy. Forestry is however different in Canada, the nature is different and the issues they're facing are different. Therefore i wouldn't be too worried about picking 200, 300 or 400 level courses, as long as you've touched on the topics that is underlying for the course.
teaching_comparison: The grad courses were very down to earth, just as in Copenhagen. Distance between the lecturerer and students weren't big. The undergrad courses felt more like big highschool classes. I weren't allowed to take notes on my computer, because my lecturer felt young students couldn't administer it...
courses_enrolled: FRST 547 - Forestry in BC FRST 593 - Climate Adaption in Socio-Ecological Systems FRST 509 - Advanced Biometrics
recommended_courses: Read above. But... FRST 547 - Forestry in BC (Easy/moderate) FRST 593 - Climate Adaption in Socio-Ecological Systems (EEEEEASY) FRST 509 - Advanced Biometrics (moderate/hard)
unexpected_costs: I went on a lot of trips. They were expensive. You can do it on a way tighter budget, but i got carried away.
cost_comparison: Groceries were expensive, alcohol as well. Eating out was a bit cheaper.
activities_available: All the clubs, use them. There is so many i can't list them all. The outdoor club is really popular, so you have to be really quick about getting on their trips. It's first come first serve, so look at their available trips often, they update them frequently.
activities_recommended: Go to Whistler, Seattle and Vancouver Island.
weekend_recommendations: Download Alltrails, a good app for looking up trails. Browse it and pick some beautiful areas. Many times you'll have to rent a car. Do that through Evo or Turo!
culture_adjustment: Easy, Canadians are very easy going.
socializing_tips: Just go to club events. The surf trips were really fun. The same as with the outdoor clubs trips.
cultural_challenges: None really.
culture_appreciated: Their outdoor culture!
top3_advice: Use the weekends for trips! Use the clubs. Socialize early.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: Looking at all the beautiful nature areas. I had the chance of going to: Vancouver Island (4x), Interior BC, Whistler, Mount Rainier, Olympic National park, Yosemite, Yellowstone, Sequoia national park, Joshua Tree and many more.
greatest_challenge: The application process, and getting the courses.

crucial_aspects: UBC has an excellent reputation as being one of the top universities in Canada. I wanted to go somewhere with a high academic level. Furthermore, the university is know for its many social opportunities. UBC has hundreds of social clubs where you can dive into every interest imaginable. I also love doing outdoor activities, and Vancouver is arguably the best destination in the world for this. With its close proximity to both the ocean and the mountains, Vancouver provides easy acces to activities such as hiking, camping, rock climbing, mountain biking, skiing, kayaking, diving, whale watching etc.
overall_comments: I had an excellent experience during my exchange. Classes were great, teachers were professional, the other students were open and fun to hang out with and the city and the surrounding area was amazing. The only reason that I don't rate it 10/10 is because I had to compromise a bit on the courses that I took. I still had some really good courses, but many of the courses that I originally wanted to take, were not available.
info_ease: I found it quite easy. Everyone was really helpful, and a lot of information is already provided via email. They also have an orientation day before the classes start.
arrival_assistance: GoGlobal assisted me when I had trouble with my courses. I ended up changing two of my courses during the first two weeks, and the staff were really helpful with finding the right courses for me.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I had an excellent experience during my exchange. Classes were great, teachers were professional, the other students were open and fun to hang out with and the city and the surrounding area was amazing. The only reason that I don't rate it 10/10 is because I had to compromise a bit on the courses that I took. I still had some really good courses, but many of the courses that I originally wanted to take, were not available.
registration_process: First, you have to send an application to UCPH. Once it's approved, you also have to apply at UBC. Once that's approved as well, you have to apply for pre approval of courses (regardless of whether you have decided on your courses). You then apply for your courses. If you receive an Erasmus grant, there are a few extra steps, including filling out an Online Learning Agreement, which has to be signed by the Erasmus responsible at both universities.
registration_help: A few online guides are available for help as well as email reminders.
registration_success: I succeeded in registering for the classes that I wanted. However, I also found out that not all the classes that are featured on their website are available.
registration_advice: Just know that it's time consuming. And that you aren't guaranteed to get the classes that you want.
academics_comments: I had an excellent experience during my exchange. Classes were great, teachers were professional, the other students were open and fun to hang out with and the city and the surrounding area was amazing. The only reason that I don't rate it 10/10 is because I had to compromise a bit on the courses that I took. I still had some really good courses, but many of the courses that I originally wanted to take, were not available.
course_level: There are 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500 level courses, depending on what year you're on. As BA exchange students, we can take anything from 100-400 level courses. There is a noticable difference between the different levels. However, in general, I found the level to be the same as, or easier, than at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: Like at UCPH, the classes were often divided into lectures and discussions/lab. In general, there were more projects to do at UBC, such as assignments and presentations. My classes also included noticably more field work, like learning about plants while walking around the forest. One difference, that I personally found to be brilliant at UBC, was the fact that the course grade isn't determined by a single exam. Instead, the course grade is based on quizzes, assignments, presentations, midterm exams, final exams etc. that all count a little towards the final grade. This makes it much less stressful and removes a lot of the pressure during exam season.
courses_enrolled: 1. Introduction to Conservation 2. Forest Ecology 3. Atmospheric Environments 4. Issues in Genomics and the Environment
recommended_courses: My two favorite courses were Forest Ecology and Introduction to Conservation. I liked Forest Ecology because it included a lot of field work in the forest. The course also included many interesting and relevant topics, such as climate change, forest management and forest fires. Introduction to Conservation was especially interesting because it included many different approaches to nature conservation, both historically, politically and scientifically. It gave some new perspectives on this very relevant topic and allowed me to reflect on the state of our world.
unexpected_costs: A mandatory health insurance (iMED) at UBC of approx. 1700 dkk. This was on top of my already paid travel insurance of 2800 dkk. There is also a 250 dkk housing application when applying for on campus housing. You also have to get used to Canadian taxes. The prices that you see are always before taxes are added, which can be up to 12 % extra.
cost_comparison: Take away food was much less expensive than anticipated. On the other hand, groceries were more expensive.
activities_available: There is an abundance of social clubs to join. Personally, I was in the outdoor club (VOC), diving club (Aqua Society) and chess club. All of which have my highest recommendations. On top of that, the university offers free access to the aquatic centre as well as free badminton, basketball, table tennis and much more. You can also get a very cheap fitness membership. You can also watch hockey/football games for free and participate in various arranged activities throughout the semester, such as the Day of the Longboat, which is a boat race for students.
activities_recommended: All the things mentioned above.
weekend_recommendations: - Banff National Park - it's far away but incredibly beautiful and worth the trip. - Vancouver Island - Whistler - Local mountains - Local ski resorts - Downtown Vancouver - Whale watching - Hockey games
culture_adjustment: The culture is not totally different from European culture, so I found it quite easy.
socializing_tips: Join student clubs, attend events and just be open in general.
cultural_challenges: In Downtown Vancouver (1 hour from campus), there is a lot of drug addicts and homeless people. Seeing how they live their lives came as a bit of a shock.
culture_appreciated: Canadians are very open and the environment was very inclusive. They also put a lot of effort into acknowledging the lands of their indigenous ancestors, which I found interesting. I liked the fact that UBC and Vancouver in general holds a blend of many different cultures. Only a handful of the people I met were born and raised in the city. There were many people from other parts of Canada, Europe and especially Asia.
top3_advice: 1. You couldn't pick a better destination for exchange. You can do anything here. 2. It's not the cheapest destination. Especially groceries and housing can be a big expense in Vancouver. 3. Make sure to take advantage of all the opportunities that are presented to you
other_useful_info: Don't hold back. It's an experience of a lifetime.
most_rewarding: All the incredible experiences, enjoying the beautiful Canadian nature and meeting amazing people from around the world that I am still in contact with.
greatest_challenge: Navigating between academic responsibilities and social opportunities, as I found it difficult to find the time for alle the social events and travel experiences that I wanted to pursue while also managing my schoolwork. Fortunately, it all worked out just fine in the end.
other_comments: Just do it!

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to a country that had beautiful nature. Vancouver had this, plus a university that I had heard much about. And I always wanted to visit Canada. Going on exchange, there were also a bit of comfort in going to a country that spoke English.
info_ease: Stuff like that is always a bit confusing, but I found it overall easy enough to find the information that I needed upon arrival.
arrival_assistance: I went to the information meetings and imagine day, but other than that nothing, as I did not need it.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I registred before arriving and ended up switching out two of my classes after arrival. It was easy enough.
registration_help: There was help available on campus for exchange students, but I didn't need it.
registration_success: Before arriving, I got all the classes that I wanted, but when switching to different classes a lot of them were filled up.
registration_advice: I really enjoyed the weeks at the beginning of the term where you could try all the classes you wanted before deciding. I ended up switching two of my courses for something else after coming to 1-3 classes in the first weeks and finding out that it wasn't for me. I really recommend doing this, as you get a sense of the profs teaching style and hear more about exams and expectations + attendance.
course_level: Coming from Denmark, I found the academic level a bit too low. Some of the classes were really interesting, but some were a bit "ruined" by the papers we had to do. Instead of making critical papers and using the theory we had read, it became very "summary-based" papers, where the prof just wanted to make sure that we had read the texts for that week, instead of actually wanting us to learn. In this way, it didn't feel like a university-level course. Of course, this was very nice for an exchange student, as I didn't need to stress about keeping up.
teaching_comparison: The profs had a more pedagogical approach. This was in some instances nice, as they really led us through the semester, but it didn't feel very academic. At UCPH your relationship with your profs tend to feel a bit more like academic peers, which I really like.
courses_enrolled: Feminist theory Special Topics in Gender, Race, and Sexuality Topics in 19th-Century Philosophy Gender and Nation: Women's State in Modern Central, Eastern and Northern European literatures and Cultures
recommended_courses: "Special Topics in Gender, Race, and Sexuality" with Dr. Alifa Bandali was a really great course! Dr. Bandali is a really great teacher and the theory we used was really interesting.
unexpected_costs: The compass card, but it turned out to be really nice to have. Other than that, I used most of my money on travel.
cost_comparison: Groceries were pretty cheep. Housing was the most expensive.
activities_available: Everything was available at UBC.
activities_recommended: I heard the the surf-club or the outdoor-club were really good.
weekend_recommendations: Visit Whistler and Vancouver Island. There are a lot to do very close to the city and renting a car is pretty cheap. I went on a lot of hiking trips.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Canadians are very kind.
cultural_challenges: Nothing.
culture_appreciated: The kindsness and openness of the Canadians.
top3_advice: - Be aware of the housing situation. You may not get on-campus housing, but there are a lot on facebook looking for roommates (+ airbnb). But it is expensive. - The nature is amazing. Go on as many trips as possible! - Try out different classes at the beginning, and be aware of the different expectations of exams and attendece that the profs have. I found it very nice to have a few courses where attendance were not a thing, as it gave me the possibility to travel more.
other_useful_info: There is a lot of school work (papers, mid-terms, class facilitations etc.).
most_rewarding: Getting to travel so much to the most beautiful places.
greatest_challenge: There were a lot of school work, so I had to adjust a bit.

crucial_aspects: I chose to stay at UBC for my exchange because I really wanted to experience Canada and the nature in the area surrounding Vancouver. UBC was also a good university with many interesting and relevant courses since I wanted to use my time on exchange to learn more about climate policy and forest conservation.
overall_comments: The only negative part of the experience was the administrative and practical aspect of getting courses to work out.
info_ease: I did not experience any problems in regards to this.
arrival_assistance: Assistance was provided, but I found no need for it.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: The only negative part of the experience was the administrative and practical aspect of getting courses to work out.
registration_process: I received an email from UBC where I could register for courses and rate them from 1-10. However, I did not end up getting any of my first choices but after writing back and forth with KU I made it work.
registration_help: I wrote a lot with the international office at UBC and at KU.
registration_success: European politics was not on the course list for the term I travelled to UBC because the professor was on research leave and this created a lot of problems during the months leading up to my arrival at UBC. Overall, I was happy where I ended up but I cannot stress enough how arduous the process leading up to my arrival was.
registration_advice: UBC is way more flexible regarding courses than KU so this is by far where I would focus my energy.
academics_comments: The only negative part of the experience was the administrative and practical aspect of getting courses to work out.
course_level: I took one 200 level course and the rest were level 300 (third year).
teaching_comparison: Way more hands on with more assignments, midterms and participation. I really enjoyed this way of learning and it allowed the final grade to be made up of different assignments instead of the final exam constituting 100pct. of the grade.
courses_enrolled: POLI_V 351 (001) Environmental Politics and Policy POLI_V 220A (001) Introduction to Political Systems Around the World - INTR COMP POLTCS GEOG_V 310 / ENST 310 Environment and Sustainability
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed the different courses on environmental politics and sustainability. The ENST 310 course was online but really well structured with a very supportive and educational professor. I would definitely recommend this course!
unexpected_costs: I had to buy new bedding for my room and getting a data plan in Canada is just generally really expensive compared to other countries. I ended up buying an esim but I would probably recommend also getting a Canadian phone number in case you need to rent a car and/or Airbnb.
cost_comparison: Groceries are expensive in Canada but compared to Copenhagen going out for dinner is more affordable. Public transport is cheap compared to Copenhagen because UBC has an arrangement with compass card where you get a deal as a student.
activities_available: Lot of sports events and homecoming games. UBC is massive and there is a club for everything - even a Scandinavia club if you get homesick.
activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend going to the homecoming games just for the experience. This was a lot of fun!
weekend_recommendations: Go on weekend trips to the nearby islands, hike up the mountains, go whale watching, take the ferry and you might just get lucky and see whales here too, walk through their large forests near campus, walk along the shore surrounding UBC and so on and so on... the nature is beautiful and definitely worth prioritizing.
culture_adjustment: It was not so bad. Everyone is super friendly and will always want to help both on and off campus. It was mostly the different currency and tipping culture I needed to settle into.
socializing_tips: It is really helpful to choose shared housing where you live with others. This was a very positive experience for me. And it is really great to just ask people around you if they want toy join you for a weekend trip. Everyone is there to have fun and see Vancouver and being the one to take initiative allows you to meet new people. The varsity outdoor club also arranges plenty of hikes so be sure to sign up!:)
cultural_challenges: For the most part it was an easy culture to fit into.
culture_appreciated: Peoples outgoing and friendly way of being was a big part of how quickly I settled in. Canadians are generally very friendly and understanding the language breaks down a lot of barriers when moving to a new part of the world.
top3_advice: Try to get student housing on campus - this was a huge plus for me (and honestly a good price compared to options off campus). Bring good hiking boots! And honestly communicate with UCPH over email so you have the correspondence in print so you can refer back to earlier answers and agreements at a later time since the process of getting admitted to courses is pretty long and it can be really constructive to have your agreements written down officially since you are communicating with multiple universities and offices at the same time.
other_useful_info: When you make it through the process of getting admitted to courses the exchange experience is amazing and completely worth it!
most_rewarding: Seeing the nature and getting to live in a part of the world I have wanted to see all my life.
greatest_challenge: Having a long time of mingling and getting to know other people without having my old social group from home around. Although this was also a big plus and it allowed me to meet some of the nicest people.

crucial_aspects: First of all I wanted to go somewhere where I spoke the language. Therefore, I considered English and German speaking countries. I also wanted to go to a country that is safe and not too unfamiliar - so I applied to universities in Canada, Switzerland, Germany, and Scotland. The University of British Columbia seemed like the best option in Canada for me. UBC is a great academic institution with massive facilities, it has a beautiful modern campus right next to the Sea, it is in the big city of Vancouver - but by itself, which makes it even safer than the city. The campus life here is completely different to University of Copenhagen, since everything at UBC is in one place. You naturally to meet students that study completely different things to yourself, which is so fun. At UCPH I mostly spend time with students that study the same thing as me, and I'm very happy to have close friends that I spend a lot of time with there, but it is different at UBC. Since the students at UBC are always mixed up they have a lot of friends, however they don't have that many close friends, this makes it a good place to study abroad since people are very open and used to making new friends, so if you're open yourself it is super easy to make friends here. UBC also has a lot of clubs and campus activities. I myself became a member of the Varsity Outdoor Club, which was great fun. I went on a lot of trips in the weekends with other students who enjoy getting out and exploring nature. The club has some super advanced trips, but I mostly did beginner friendly ones. Becoming a member also means that you can rent gear for free. If you're not a hiker, skier, or snowshoer there are also 300+ other clubs you could join, and I'd highly recommend taking a look at the ones you find interesting, since the people running the clubs are always very passionate and love when potential new members show interest - so don't be shy! As I mentioned they also have a lot of campus activities, the UBC Thunderbirds have sports teams in Hockey, American Football, Basketball, and much more. As a student it's free to go to these games and if you bring along some friends it can definitely be a fun experience. The only thing I was worried about when coming here was the long distance away from home, but I honestly haven't felt it at all.
info_ease: It was quite easy. I was just sent emails with what I had to do.
arrival_assistance: I recieved help finding my room once I arrived in residence, and the first few days there was a big introduction to studying at UBC, where all exchange students were also shown around campus to get familiar with it, which also meant we met many other exchangers so to make new friends. We were also introduced to all the clubs and so on, so I felt very welcomed.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You had to tell Go Global what you wanted to be registered for and then they would do it for you. It could be a pain if you wanted to take very popular courses since they were not that fast. Also if you wanted a graduate course the process was a bit more complicated where you might even have to write the professor an email yourself. So the process wasn't ideal, however they explained everything very well in great detail, so you just had to follow their instructions, and they were also good at answering any questions.
registration_help: Go Global helps all the exchangers get their desired courses. However they can't guarentee anything, so you have to find backup courses, if you didn't get the ones that you wanted the most.
registration_success: I had some that I initially wanted, that were only offered in the second term so I couldn't get those, but of the ones that actually got offered in the first term, I got the 5 I wanted the most, and then dropped one so that I only had 4 courses, which is what I needed to get 30 ECTS.
registration_advice: Just keep up to date on the courses they are offering, check what they offered last year, and follow the instructions of Go Global. You might have to submit your pre-approval to UCPH before you're actually registered for courses, so just add as many courses as you can. I even registered twice, just for extra security.
course_level: I'm a in my third and final year of my BA at UCPH. At UBC it is common to go work right after your Undergrad and not do a Masters. It is also a 4 year Undergrad, since they start 1 year earlier at uni than we do in Denmark. At UBC I took 300 and 400 level courses, which are made for 3rd and 4th year students. This made a lot of sense. The level of 4th year courses at UBC was similar to 3rd year courses at UCPH and the 3rd year courses at UBC was about the same as 2nd year courses at UCPH, so it matched quite well. And taking some courses that were a bit easier was nice, since I had more time to explore British Columbia.
teaching_comparison: I study physics at home and took physics courses at UBC. Usually we have a lot of tutorials at home here we didn't have any tutorials, we still had problems to do, but you had to do them more on your own, which was nice for me since it made my schedule more flexible.
courses_enrolled: PHYS 407 Introduction to General Relativity, PHYS 400 Introduction to Elementary Particles, PHYS 315 Quantum Physics of Materials, and PHYS 312 Introduction to Mathematical Physics
recommended_courses: PHYS 315 was very nice as an exchange student, since the course was very easy to get a good grade in, but I still felt like I learned alot. If you want a challenge then PHYS 400 is a good one, since it is an undergrad/grad course, so the class is small, the level is high, and there is sooo much material.
unexpected_costs: There were no costs I didn't expect.
cost_comparison: Most items are less expensive some are the same price, however tax is not included in the price you see when buying.
activities_available: Over 300+ clubs + loads of on campus activities aranged by the university, the housing, or one of the clubs.
activities_recommended: VOC - Go on hikes. You can plan your own trips, but going with the VOC is so nice, since someone will have planned the trip for you, and they are often experienced, so it's almost guarenteed that it will be a success.
weekend_recommendations: If the weather isn't great you can go to a Whitecaps game, it isn't as expensive as you'd expect. You can also watch the Canucks, but that is more expensive. There are loads of fun museums around campus that are free as a UBC student. And then go on trips, Vancouver Island is very nice. Banff and Jasper isn't very far either. There are also loads of beautiful hikes near Vancouver.
culture_adjustment: It is very international, so not difficult at all.
socializing_tips: Go to all the activities and clubs that you find somewhat interesting.
cultural_challenges: Not really any.
culture_appreciated: How open a lot of people are when you first meet them.
top3_advice: Apply for housing and have backup plans. Look at what you want to do before you get there - find a few objectives you wanna conquer. Be open and talk to people about their passions.
other_useful_info: Nah, you're good.
most_rewarding: The people I met and the experiences I had - especially in nature.
greatest_challenge: Overcoming the barrier of asking people to do stuff, but also doing stuff by yourself.

crucial_aspects: That it was far away, so I could try to live in another culture. Therefore I choose North America, where Vancouver did not disappoint. It is an amazing city, and the University is equally amazing. That was another aspect of my motivation, to try a semester at a top-50 University in the world, and UBC did not disappoint in this manner.
info_ease: The UBC team for international students are very helpful, which made it way easier. They provided me with the useful information, and whenever I had any questions, I just asked them for help, and they helped me every time. UBC is an awesome choice, if you are afraid you will not know all the needed stuff before arrival, because their team can help you out easily.
arrival_assistance: I got invited to an information meeting for international students, where I meet the team physically, and they provided me and other students with all the information needed. They also gave me physical documents with information on.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Before I got there I had to wish for 10 courses, where I got 6 of them. I only needed 4, so I had to drop 2. During the first two weeks of classes you can swap between courses with empty spaces, so it is a good idea to try different classes during these weeks, so you end up with courses you enjoy the most.
registration_help: The international office was very helpful, and the professors are as well.
registration_success: I got most of the classes I wanted, but there were many classes with empty spaces I could have taken that seemed interesting, so overall it was easy to be succesful here,
registration_advice: Try something different during the first two weeks, where you can change courses. Talk with the professors and TA's about what to expect. They are there to help you!
course_level: The level of the courses is quite similar to the level of the courses on UCPH. They do focus on different aspects though. In Political Science, UCPH focuses a lot on methodology and theories. where UBC focuses more on a specific empirical phenomenon.
teaching_comparison: It is very different. It is only professors who teach, and most courses have attendance as a part of your grade. The grade is determined by many different aspects, including midterms, attendance and the final exam, among many things. Most of the exams and midterms are written in hand.
courses_enrolled: POLI321 - Chinese Politics and Development POLI369B - Politics of Outer Space POLI370A - Negotiations POLI370D - Civil Wars
recommended_courses: I liked all my courses, but I would really suggest POLI369B - Politics of Outer Space and POLI370A - Negotiations, as they are very different from what you can get at UCPH. I looked forward to all most every lecture in these courses.
unexpected_costs: I had planned in detail, so did not get any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: Eating out was less expensive, but in general Vancouver is very, very expensive, so use some time to apply for grants!
activities_available: Many - I played in the Intramurals, where I played soccer, I joined the film society. and the gym facilities was very good!
activities_recommended: Join a free-agent team for the intramurals, in whatever sport you like the most!
weekend_recommendations: So many things to do! Most people ski, hike or enjoy the beautiful nature, or watch sports such as the Whitecaps or the Cannucks
culture_adjustment: Quite easy - put on an open mind and you will be good.
socializing_tips: Live on campus! And don't be afraid to talk to people after classes.
cultural_challenges: People from North America is sometimes a bit superficial, so you need to make an effort.
culture_appreciated: The way that they care about many different sports
top3_advice: Live on campus, be open to meet canadian people, join a team for intramurals
other_useful_info: No :D
most_rewarding: To learn new things about myself, study in a different environment, and experience the amazing canadian nature!
greatest_challenge: To meet new people - but it went well anyway!

crucial_aspects: Geografiske årsager samt værtsuniversitetets fagudbud.
overall_comments: Jeg har været utroligt glad for at studere i Caen, havde det udelukkende været det faglige og kulturelle udbytte samt oplevelsen, jeg vurderede have karakteren været betydeligt højere. Men alt det administrative især før men også under og efter har været en kæphest.
info_ease: Da jeg skulle være af sted i et helt år, savnede jeg dybdegående information. F.eks. at man ved udrejse i over 6 mdr. ikke er dækket af den danske sygesikring. Det ville være elskværdigt at informere om dette samt vejlede studerende i, hvad værtslandet kan tilbyde af alternativer.
arrival_assistance: Diverse møder for Erasmusstuderende på universitetet i Caen, som var meget velorganiserede.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Jeg har været utroligt glad for at studere i Caen, havde det udelukkende været det faglige og kulturelle udbytte samt oplevelsen, jeg vurderede have karakteren været betydeligt højere. Men alt det administrative især før men også under og efter har været en kæphest.
registration_process: Først melder man sig til kurser via en online portal. Dernæst håber man på, at det er muligt at lægge et skema ud fra de valgte kurser. Er det ikke tilfældet, så må man i gang med blyant og papir og opliste ens vigtigste kurser, finde ud af hvornår på ugen der er timer og så se, om man kan tælle til 30 ECTS uden overlappende moduler. Det er en hjernevrider og du står med den selv. Derudover er kursusbeskrivelserne meget svære at finde, så man kan sende dem til KU til forhåndsgodkendelse, som kan tage meget lang tid. Når man har valgt sine kurser, går man på kontoret for det pågældende institut i åbningstid udenfor lange frokostpauser og meddeler sekretæren sine valg. Det kan være mange skridt, trapper og banken på døren. Men en trøst er, at alle de franske studerende er i samme båd, så der er nogen at snakke med når man står i kø.
registration_help: Man kunne spørge alle, samt skrive mails. Måske stod der også ting og sager på hjemmesiden, men informationen der er ikke altid opdateret. Det nemmeste er helt klart at troppe op, og så holde godt fast i de håndskrevne post-its man får med navne, mail og telefonnumre på hvem man kan kontakte i forskellige situationer.
registration_success: I sidste ende, fik jeg flettet to gode semestre sammen, med fag som alle behagede mig. 2. semester var naturligvis betydeligt lettere end første, da jeg kendte til processen.
registration_advice: Trop op på kontorerne. Spørg, spørg, spørg. Folk er søde og behjælpelige.
academics_comments: Jeg har været utroligt glad for at studere i Caen, havde det udelukkende været det faglige og kulturelle udbytte samt oplevelsen, jeg vurderede have karakteren været betydeligt højere. Men alt det administrative især før men også under og efter har været en kæphest.
course_level: Jeg var på en fransk litteraturvidenskabelig Bachelor på både 1. året og 2. året. Førsteårskurserne var til den lette side, men brede og interessante. Med de få timers litteratur man har haft på bacheloren i Fransk Sprog og kultur, så er det muligt at klare sig udemærket. 2. året tilbød betydeligt mere specifikke kurser, mere dybdegående og mere krævende. Jeg nød at have vekslingen mellem de to, da meget fra 2. års kurserne byggede ovenpå metoder tillært på 1. året. Derudover havde jeg litteraturfag på nordiske sprogs 3. år samt engelsk på 3. år. Begge dele meget, meget let. Engelsk havde et skræmmende lavt niveau med en dødelig stilhed i holdundervisningen, men interessante forelæsninger.
teaching_comparison: Der var en blanding af forelæsninger (Cours Magistraux CM) og holdundervisning (Travaux dirigées TD). Forelæsningerne var til tider med power points, til tider uden. Nogen gange blev disse power points lagt ud på universitetsplatformen, nogen gange ikke. Så det var bare om at tage egne noter. Det som hed TD, var som oftest meget som forelæsninger, blot i mindre klasser med mulighed for at stille spørgsmål og uden powerpoints. Der er man hensat til egne noter.
courses_enrolled: Fransk : Litterature comparée, poésie romantique, compléments culturels, histoire du roman, éco-poésie, littérature séculaire, le roman du moyen-âges au XVIIIe Engelsk: english picture books, english litterature Shakespeare and Oscar Wilde Nordisk: Litteratur fra færøerne og grønland, autofiktion og øko-poesi Latin
recommended_courses: Alle kurserne om fransk litteratur interesserede mig. Især TD'erne, som man sagtens kunne følge uden CM. De er mere dybdegående, hvorimod le compléments culturels blot er wikipediaagtige.

cost_comparison: Mad købt på marked er billigt og af høj kvalitet. Restaurationer og caféer er generelt billigere end i Danmark.

weekend_recommendations: Cotentinhalvøen, cidergårde, de omkringliggende byer, som kan nås med bus, blablacar eller tog.
culture_adjustment: Det sværeste er madkulturen, der er noget anderledes end den danske rytme.
socializing_tips: Bare spørg dem om hjælp med opgaver osv. alle er vildt hjælpsomme og nysgerrige på at du kommer fra et andet land. undgå Erasmusgrupper, da de lokale godt kan blive lidt generte, hvis de skal tale engelsk. Prøv på fransk, de bliver imponerede og glade.
cultural_challenges: Den umyndiggørende tilgang til de studerende fra visse underviseres side. Franskmændenes tilbøjelighed til altid at brokke sig samt den samfundsmæssige mistillid og den administrative træghed og uigennemsigtighed.
culture_appreciated: Markedskulturen, gode lokale råvarer til billig penge. Foreningslivet, som i alle samfundslag er stærkt og bredt. Det smukke sprog og den litterære kultur, alle læser og vil gerne snakke om læsning. Derudover at det er helt cool at medbringe sin madpakke på en café og drikke en kop kaffe og læse i en bog.
top3_advice: GØR det. Men søg det franske. Det er et valg man skal tage inden man tager af sted, vil jeg have en lokal oplevelse med total immersion i værtskulturen eller vil jeg have en international Erasmusoplevelse, hvor du bliver bedre til norsk, engelsk og tysk, men ikke nøsvendigvis til fransk.
other_useful_info: Sørg for at få dine klassekammeraters nummer, alle de unge er på WhatsApp, og er gode til at svare og dele noter. Derudover er det hyggeligt at sige hej til et kendt ansigt i et amfiteater med 70 andre studerende.
most_rewarding: Helt klart undervisningen og det lokalmiljø, jeg faldt ind i.
greatest_challenge: Jeg synes forhåndsgodkendelse var dødes pølse. Det franske system med meget små eller ikke eksisterende kursusbeskrivelser spiller ikke sammen med KU's krav til detaljerede fagbeskrivelser. Derudover ALT det administartive omkring opholdet. other_comments: Der er ikke kultur for studiegrupper i Frankrig, så måske man kan finde en enkelt læsemakker eller ven. Måske en anden udvekslingsstuderende, med hvem du også kan diskutere de store studie kulturforskelle der er mellem nord og sydeuropa.
