recommended_courses: Avoid Math 128A at all costs. You'll get much more out of numerical analysis at KU and you'll still have your sanity afterwards. Stat 153 was incredibly good, I highly recommend that to anyone interested. The professor was very committed to teaching us and making us understand the topics, and the homework, while long, was very good as it added additional understanding of the topics taught. Math 105 was also very good and has the added benefit of being a smaller course where you can really get to know the professor. He is very interested in the subjects and going to his office was very rewarding. It was also participation based *chefs kiss*. Stat 33b, if you want to learn R, is very good. I did not anticipate going from thinking so little of R to thinking so highly of it. Goes to show that a good teacher can completely change your perspective of a topic or programming language.
unexpected_costs: It was not unexpected, but Americans and their insurance.
cost_comparison: I did not anticipate housing being that expensive. I know some that paid 35.000 DKK for a two bedroom apartment. Ouch.
activities_available: Almost everything you could think of. For clubs they had sports, gaming, consulting, coding, charity, painting, etc.
activities_recommended: Berkeley als has something called a DeCal which I wish I knew before I chose courses. They are courses started by students with the counselling of a professor. I put these under non-academic as some of the deCals included "introduction to tea", "Introduction to Poker", "The Nature of Pixar Films", and the all time favorite: "Learn to Play the Sather Tower Bells", where you learn to play the bells of the Sather Tower in the middle of the campus. Check out https://decal.berkeley.edu/courses for more.
weekend_recommendations: Go hiking, climbing, sailing or something else. California is all about the nature and being outside, and if you're danish, you're not gonna get that at home, so use the nature while you can!
culture_adjustment: Being danish, there really isn't that big of a difference. Americans are much more open, and if you ever talk to one on the street it is not uncommon to be invited to dinner or to join their communist activist group (actually happened). Once you get used to the openness of the locals, everything is easy enough to get used to.
socializing_tips: Go to the bars or to the club fair! Talk to other students in class, or meet people in the dining halls. Just talk to other students, its incredible how easy it is to find friends that way.
cultural_challenges: Guns and safety. We had a 45 min introduction to safety in the area where we were told to always watch our surroundings as muggings, even downtown in populated areas were not uncommon. Always walk in groups and avoid suspicious people. They had a campus police station, which came in handy quite a lot as there was at least a mugging or an assault a week. In terms of guns, some americans hated them, some loved them. But the fact that most people shrugged at a local school shooting because they were so common what unfathomable to me. Get used to the guns, especially when travelling outside a major city.
culture_appreciated: The openness of the americans were amazing. Americans are always friendly (Unless they're from NYC).
top3_advice: Take breaks and use them to enjoy the nature, do not concern yourself with the food quality, and try to talk to as many people as possible!
other_useful_info: I would recommend finding a place to live before arriving. And if/when you feel homesick, know that it is okay. We all feel it, and it is natural to miss home after such a long period away. Remind yourself of it when you get back home.
most_rewarding: The experience of studying at such a major institution was amazing.
greatest_challenge: The academical pressure at the university is difficult to handle. A lot of students end up doing nothing but school work for 14-15 weeks straight due to the pressure to perform. Homesickness as well, especially because they don't have adequate rye bread and greek yoghurt is subpar.

crucial_aspects: I knew I wanted to go to California because I love it there. I chose UCSD because of the classes and the beautiful campus and also the location and weather.
info_ease: It was really difficult to get to know the ucsd different sites and systems
arrival_assistance: ISPO did some welcoming camps and made themselves available to assist us with questions
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Find the classes you want, see if they are active for the quarter, when the registration opens you can choose up to 12 units and there after you can choose more and drop classes.
registration_help: It was quite confusing for me and ended up writing both student counseling and the professors and ended up with the right amount of classes
registration_success: I got the classes I needed and had some classes because I had to have 12 units
registration_advice: Do your research before the registration opens, be ready when it does, ask for help, write the professors sooner rather than later.
course_level: The level of the classes were appropriate, not too difficult but very interesting and very capable professors!
teaching_comparison: Even thought some lectures are with a lot of people, you feel closer to the program, course material and professor. There's a lot more tests, quizzes and assignments than at UCPH
courses_enrolled: 1. quarter: social psychology, popular culture, sexuality and sexual identities 2. quarter: psychology of human sexuality, qualitative interviewing, philosophy and feminism
recommended_courses: social psychology, sexuality and sexual identities, psychology of human sexuality
unexpected_costs: Bought a car and car insurance
cost_comparison: School books and materials were less expensive. Grocery shopping and rent was a lot more expensive that expected.
activities_available: Everything, all kinds of sport and crafts and other community building groups and clubs
activities_recommended: Dont know
weekend_recommendations: A lot of beautiful hikes, beaches, wine country, nice areas in and around SD, go to a baseball game, surf camp
culture_adjustment: Lived with two american guys which definitly made it easier, spend a lot of time with them and their friends
socializing_tips: No...
cultural_challenges: Not really.
culture_appreciated: People are really kind and interested, a lot of amazing food and diversity
top3_advice: 1. Its very expensive, so make sure you have the money (but so worth it!) 2. Highly recommend living off campus (near the beaches) 3. Explore and experience, you will pass your classes so make sure to also do something else than school
other_useful_info: na
most_rewarding: The social life, friends I got here!
greatest_challenge: Money, very expensive to live in SD
other_comments: na

crucial_aspects: I wanted to experience the westcoast of USA and heard that California was a good place to study - both in social and academical aspects. I knew people who had visited UCSB, why i chose it as my first priority.
info_ease: It was alright, helped a lot(!) that Simone made sure we were added to a group chat with others attending UCSB
arrival_assistance: Not really any, but could contact Simone with problems, which was good
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Had very little information about it prior to starting
registration_help: Didn't use any
registration_success: Not very. We had limited options and they were not that good at communicating to us, that pre-reqs were required
registration_advice: Remember to get pre-reqs before registration pass!
course_level: Depends on what you choose. Some undergrads were quite easy, some were challenging
teaching_comparison: More free and less assignments
courses_enrolled: Public Finance, Monetary Economics, International Finance
recommended_courses: Topics in Applied Economics, Monetary Economics and International Finance. All had a decent level with the first-mentioned being the hardest. All very useful and reminded me of courses I would enjoy to enroll at KU
unexpected_costs: none
cost_comparison: High food costs
activities_available: Tennis courts, surfing, fitness
activities_recommended: Tennis, surfing - just using the facilities available
weekend_recommendations: Travel along the West Coast
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: Join Excursion Club and party at Del Playa. Preferably live with locals
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: Free-spirits and open minds
top3_advice: Be open to everything - it will not be fun if you purely spend time on the library
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Living in Isla Vista - a small community of students who socialize and study at the same pace as you
greatest_challenge: To find housing

crucial_aspects: Especially, the cultural differences and experience of the US were crucial.
info_ease: It was super easy. UCPH were helpful before the arrival and a few weeks before arrival, I got in contact with people from UCSB, who were extremely helpful.
arrival_assistance: I had some assistance with class registration and sports.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was not easy. First of all, American students are prioritized before exchange students. Secondly, the supply of economic courses are limited due to the need for prerequisites, which I spent a lot of time convincing the institution that my courses at UCPH had covered the demanded prereqs. If classes are full, it is common to crash classes. This means that you register as waitlisted and follow the class in the hope of getting a free spot.
registration_help: The professors were understanding and tried to help.
registration_success: Difficult to say. I wanted some other classes, but they were filled up before I even read about them.
registration_advice: Get in contact with EAP department and professors as soon as possible.
course_level: Undergrad were pretty straight when attending the master at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: Despite smaller class rooms it was close to being the same. Biggest difference was a more fast-paced structure with quarters and midterms.
courses_enrolled: Behavioral Finance Environmental Economics Monetary Economics Adv. Mathematical Finance International Finance
recommended_courses: Adv. Mathematical Finance International Finance
unexpected_costs: Rising inflation and exchange rate USD/DKK.
cost_comparison: Food were more expensive in Isla Vista.
activities_available: Intramural Soccer was a great part of my exchange. Easiest way to be a part of this is through network. Befriend some american and ask them about intramural activities.
activities_recommended: Soccer and partying in the backyards with the people in IV.
weekend_recommendations: Travel the western coast. The nature is beautiful. Especially Yosemite National Park.
culture_adjustment: Kind of easy. Just be yourself and integrate that into the american culture.
socializing_tips: Live with them. Get a spot with american students.
cultural_challenges: The biggest difference was the fact that I was on exchange and every was just another ordinary day in their life. So local students don't have the same incentives to travel and experience. Or even go to the beach.
culture_appreciated: The laid back and casual California vibe.
top3_advice: 1) Find a housing spot with local students. But remember, first is not always best, so explore some different housing possibilities and get a place close to the beach. 2) Travel. 3) Socialize. Makes the experience way better.
other_useful_info: N/A
most_rewarding: Great friendship and memories. The life in America is truly amazing and different to living in Copenhagen.
greatest_challenge: Home sickness. Missing the closest people at home.

crucial_aspects: Berkeley is known for having one of the best economics departments in the world. Acces to courses taught by world-renowned professors drew me to Berkeley.
overall_comments: Would recommend anyone going on exchange.
info_ease: At first it's a little confusing getting to know all the different Berkeley websites and such, but you'll get a hang of it.
arrival_assistance: Unfortunately orientation was online - even though courses were taught in-person just a couple weeks later - which was rather boring. But the information that was conveyed was fine. There's a lot of focus on alcohol and drug abuse and mental health, and they tell you how to tackle that regarding to yourself or friends.
arrival_comments: I think i was unlucky with my orientation leaders.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Would recommend anyone going on exchange.
registration_process: I picked out the courses I was interested in from the course website. Remember to check how full they are, and whether you can expect to get a spot by the time your course registration opens. I think seniors and athletes get to pick courses first, so popular courses can be filled up before you even get to register. Then you go to calcentral (their kunet) and register in the middle of the night when it opens.
registration_help: They had guides online
registration_success: Some classes I was originally interested in were already full by the time my registration opened. But there are so many great courses to choose from, so finding replacements wasn't difficult.
registration_advice: Wake up in the middle of the night for it - courses fill up fast! Have the courses ready in your shopping cart, so that you only have to click 1 button when registration opens.
academics_comments: Would recommend anyone going on exchange.
course_level: Some courses were easier than what I was used to from UCPH but others more difficult.
teaching_comparison: It was more relaxed than at UCPH. Classes were generally smaller, and there was more interaction with professors.
courses_enrolled: 143 - Econometrics: Advanced Methods and Applications (with Bryan Graham) 134 - MACROECONOMIC POLICY FROM THE GREAT DEPRESSION TO TODAY 191 - Topics in Economic Research (seminar with David Card) 171 - Development Economics (with Ben Faber)
recommended_courses: All of them really. 143 was amazing! One of the best courses I've taken in my lives. 134 was not very technical, but extremely interesting. 171 was amazing as well. It introduced a wide variety of topics in development economics. 191 was just a seminar, but they had very interesting guest lecturers come in and talk about their research.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Everything in Berkeley was more expensive than I expected - it's more expensive than Copenhagen.
activities_available: Berkeley has clubs, but they're a little difficult to figure out as an international student.
activities_recommended: Go to sporting events and experience the schools spirit.
weekend_recommendations: Go to SF, Las Vegas, Sonoma or Napa, Monterrey, Carmel by the Sea, Oakland, Yosemite. There's lots to see around the Bay Area.
culture_adjustment: Easy.
cultural_challenges: Maybe drug use - seems more common in the US than what I'm used to.
culture_appreciated: People are generally more outgoing and willing to help each other than I typically feel like Danish people are.
top3_advice: Go on lots of trips and explore California.
most_rewarding: The courses were awesome. The opportunities for taking trips was great.
greatest_challenge: Midterm season can be overwhelming, but hang in there.

crucial_aspects: Hvor jeg havde de bedste uddannelsesmuligheder indenfor film
overall_comments: UCLA er et stort og fedt universitet med mange muligheder og tilbud samt god undervisning, I hvertfald på Film Major
info_ease: Det var for det meste nemt at finde information. KU's infomationsmøder inden opholdet var en stor hjælp.
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik mailspåmindelser om at melde min ankomst mm. som var vigtigt. Derudover fik jeg invitationer til velkomstmøder mm. Det var et obligatorisk onlinemøde som jeg deltog i.
arrival_comments: Jeg kunne godt have tænkt mig en introduktion til campus arealerne, hvordan parkering, fitness mm. fungerede. Det helt lavpraktiske.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: UCLA er et stort og fedt universitet med mange muligheder og tilbud samt god undervisning, I hvertfald på Film Major
registration_process: Det fungerer online på deres hjemmeside. Du kan finde informationer om alle kursuser og bladre online, tilføje dem til en "course planner", så du kan danne dig et overblik over, hvordan dit skema kommer til at se ud, og hvorvidt fag ligger oveni hinanden. Der er en tilmeldingsperiode og det er godt at være hurtig, da nogle fag kan være populære. Ligesom KU er der også en eftertilmeldingsperiode.
registration_help: Der var en påmindelsesemail om tilmeldingsperioden.
registration_success: Jeg tog alle de kursuser som jeg ønskede, indenfor de rammer jeg havde. Som udvekslingsstuderende på Film Major er der nogle kursuser, som man ikke må tage.
registration_advice: Hvis du ikke er glad for et fag eller en lærer, så skift til noget andet. Undervisningen starter en uge eller to før anden tilmeldingsperiode slutter, så man kan nå at skifte, hvis man kan mærke, at man har valgt forkert. Jeg fandt fx. et litteratur og film fag under italienske studier, som jeg blev rigtig glad for, fremfor at tage et Film Minor fag, som jeg kunne mærke var helt forkert valgt til mig.
academics_comments: UCLA er et stort og fedt universitet med mange muligheder og tilbud samt god undervisning, I hvertfald på Film Major
course_level: Jeg kunne kun tage Undergraduate kursuser, Nogle kursuser var lette, men da der var mange løbende opgaver, så kan man selv gøre stille sig sværere opgaver og tilpasse det til ens niveau. Derudover får man meget praktisk erfaring.
teaching_comparison: Mere praktisk undervisning, hvor der ofte var mindre ugentlige opgaver. Opgaverne var ikke for store men passede godt som supplement til forelæsningerne. Der var generelt også mere fokus på elevinddragelse i undervisningen og meget mindre læsning. Man kan godt sige at den enorme mængde læsning på KU var erstattet med praktiske opgaver eller små blogindlæg, som man skulle skrive om et emne.
courses_enrolled: FILM & TV DIRECTING (FILM MINOR) FILM&TV DEVELOPMENT (FILM MINOR) INTRO SCREENWRITING (FILM MINOR) DIGITAL CINEMA (FILM MINOR) LITERATURE & FILM (ITALIAN STUDIES) DESIGN ASSIGNMENT - PD ASST. (FILM MAJOR) INTRODUCTORY PSYCH (PSYCHOLOGY)
recommended_courses: FILM & TV DIRECTING FILM&TV DEVELOPMENT INTRO SCREENWRITING DIGITAL CINEMA LITERATURE & FILM (ITALIAN STUDIES) DESIGN ASSIGNMENT - PD ASST.
unexpected_costs: bilforsikring er meget dyrt, hvis du ikke har Californisk kørekort.
cost_comparison: UCLA's sundhedsforsikring er meget dyr, jeg valgte ISO som er billigere men besværlig. Derudover havde jeg en dansk rejseforsikring.
activities_available: stortest alt hvad hjertet begærer..
activities_recommended: udnyt det gratis fitness center og fx. pilates/yoga hold. At gå til yoga et sted ude i byen koster ca 1000 kr om mdr. På UCLA betaler du kun $45 for at benytte dig af tilbuddet pr quarter.
weekend_recommendations: Kom ud af byen. Tag på camping/glamping. Der er mange gode hiking steder. Hvis du kan så tag til San Fransisco. Det er en fed by og helt anderledes fra LA. Det kan være dejligt med en by, hvor man rent faktisk kan gå rundt til restauranter og ikke skal have bil eller anden transport. Godt sted at tage hen, hvis du har Europa hjemve.
culture_adjustment: rimelig nemt. USA og især Californien er "lavet" af immigranter, der er meget multikulturelt. Stortset alle er oprindeligt fra et andet sted. Det er en helt normal "conversation starter" at spørge "where are you from?" når man hører en accent.
socializing_tips: Hold dig ikke tilbage, alle vil gerne snakke med dig, hænge med dig osv, hvis du har lyst. Amerikanere er ikke generte, som danskere kan være, de behøver fx. ikke alkohol eller en fest... Du kan bare snakke med dem på gangen fx. på vej ind i undervisningslokalet og I kan tage en kaffe sammen bagefter eller senere.
cultural_challenges: Mange amerikanere vil rigtig gerne alt muligt, men de er ikke altid så gode til at følge en aftale til dørs, så man skal bare blive ved, hvis man gerne vil have en aftale. Madkulturen er helt væk, jeg handlede primært i Whole Foods for at få frisk økologisk mad/grønt, men det er ikke billigt.
culture_appreciated: At man nemt kommer i snak med fremmede og bliver mødt med nysgerrighed og begejstring.
top3_advice: Det er dyrere end du tror Brug dine professorer Du vil ikke fortryde det
other_useful_info: Køb en brugt bil. Det er generelt 100 gange sjovere at have bil i LA end ikke at have en. Hvis du er filmstuderende så tilmeld dig som produktionsassistent på en graduate filmproduktion. Det er sjovt, lærerrigt, du møder en masse filmfolk, der er ved at blive færdige, og du kan tilmed få credits for det.
most_rewarding: Undervisningen. Karrieremuligheder.
greatest_challenge: social samvær, da der var online undervisning i de første to måneder og jeg havde svært ved at finde nogen ligesindede. At hjælpe til på en filmproduktion gjorde at jeg fandt nogle.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to visit the US. The whether, nature and culture of California seemed great. From there I chose to go with Berkeley based on the academics.
overall_comments: Be ready to apply for a lot of grants - it is surprisingly expensive in and around Berkeley.
info_ease: Realy easy - but I lived in the International House, which made it all very easy. With regards to classes we got loads of information in the beginning of the semester - otherwise ask you fellow students.
arrival_assistance: Digital information from UC Berkeley - due to covid it was online though, which wasn't great (and we still had to pay for it).
arrival_comments: No.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Be ready to apply for a lot of grants - it is surprisingly expensive in and around Berkeley.
registration_process: We had several application rounds for the courses - but some courses had massive waiting lists. For some courses (most not in your major or grad-courses) you have to write the professor.
registration_help: Don't know - figured it out in the portal (Cal-central).
registration_success: Did not get 1 of those I wanted.
registration_advice: Do it early - but don't panic. A lot of people drop classes in the first weeks of the semester.
academics_comments: Be ready to apply for a lot of grants - it is surprisingly expensive in and around Berkeley.
course_level: I took 5 undergraduate courses.
teaching_comparison: More free writing and oral parts. More discussion of what you think and way more articles (less theoretical than back home).
courses_enrolled: ECON 135 The History of Economic Growth ECON 191 Topics in Economic Research POLSCI 179 Colloquium in Political Science STAT 33A Introduction to Programming in R UGBA 128 Strategic Cost Management
recommended_courses: POLSCI 179 Colloquium in Political Science is perfect if you need one more unit. It is a series of lectures from guest speakers (on e.g. Voluntary euthanasia, American politics, prison, climate, labor and wages) once a week and then a "for-fun" exam on your phone in the end of the semester. Extremely interesting but not a lot of work. Topics were alright as well - not too much work and you get to experience the "best of ECON faculty".
unexpected_costs: Travelling around was a bit more expensive than expected. Spend more on the bars than expected as well ;-).
cost_comparison: Housing were very expensive. (My housing of 13000 DKK a month in I-house were with food).
activities_available: All kinds - from every sport imagineable to a Harry Potter or block chain club.
activities_recommended: I did not attend any - I think 1 semester were too short a stay for me to get involved.
weekend_recommendations: Spend time in SF, to see the nature parks nearby (Yosemite, Tahoe etc.). GO TO VEGAS on a weekend (nummer på en promoter som fik os gratis ind på et par vilde klubber +19125315148). Kør route 1, men behøves ikke fortsætte efter Santa Barbera - LA er kedelig.
culture_adjustment: Easy in I-House - a lot of europeans.
socializing_tips: Dining hall in I-house - in general I think your housing is important - try the coops if you are ready for something a bit different.
cultural_challenges: Nothing comes to mind - maybe having a (young) roomate.
culture_appreciated: Sports and parties.
top3_advice: Find good housing, go for the grants and don't choose to many hard courses. You will need time to adjust and socialize (and travel).
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: The social life in I-house - meeting new friends.
greatest_challenge: Don't know.
other_comments: NO.

crucial_aspects: It had to be a first-class university. I did not care what city the university was located in.
info_ease: Very easy.
arrival_assistance: I received assistance from the people I lived with.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: They opened up registration for courses on different dates. I was able to register at a later date than others, so I could not get some of the courses that I wanted. They were already full.
registration_help: The university provided online guidance, which was very helpful.
registration_success: Very successful, but I needed to go out of my way to get the courses that I wanted.
registration_advice: Do not hesitate to email professors in advance to ask for a spot at their course.
course_level: The level ware upper-division but they were very easy.
teaching_comparison: They are focused on learning facts and specific phrases. Not critical thinking.
courses_enrolled: Clinical Psychological Laboratory, Introduction to Health Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Historical Studies in Existentialism: Nietzsche, Philosophy of Psychology, Research Methods.

unexpected_costs: I used a lot of money on trips I went on.
cost_comparison: Transportation was very expensive
activities_available: Everything you could think of. They had all sport facilities and different types of social organizations
activities_recommended: Do some sports at a club.
weekend_recommendations: Go to Grand Canyon and Las Vegas.
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: Just be outgoing.
cultural_challenges: There were none.
culture_appreciated: Their openness and talkativeness.
top3_advice: Do not expect much academically and spend some time with actual Americans and not just other international students.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: The friends I made.
greatest_challenge: Doing a long-distance relationship.

crucial_aspects: Opportunities in Santa Barbara as the 5th best public university in the US. Their TMP (Technology Management Program) especially caught my interest, and as exchange students we have full access to this Business oriented department which is very rare.
info_ease: Decently easy
arrival_assistance: Not really any
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Most is online. The main thing is you order an access card online that you have to pick up at campus. It is quite easy.
registration_help: Email to counselors
registration_success: Very, but it was hard sometimes. Make sure to get pre approval from host university to take courses good time in advance.
registration_advice: Get approved for courses weeks before the enrollment pass opens up.
course_level: Very different structure than at UCPH. Lots of obligatory stuff. But in general it is easier to do well than it is at UCPH. You more or less just have to show up and turn in mandatory stuff to do well.
teaching_comparison: TMP and PSTAT courses were much more interactive and professors really care. A much closer connection with the lecturer. ECON courses were big lectures were you just sat and listenede for 90 minutes and then went on your way.
courses_enrolled: ECON 135 Monetary Economics ECON 181 International Finance TMP 122 Entrepreneurship TMP 127 Managing Technology Organizations TMP 240 Business Strategy & Leadership PSTAT 194FM Financial Market Risk & Modeling
recommended_courses: TMP 122 Entrepreneurship TMP 127 Managing Technology Organizations TMP 240 Business Strategy & Leadership PSTAT 194FM Financial Market Risk & Modeling They were all great courses that you cannot get at UCPH.
unexpected_costs: Mandatory student insurance. I recommend to waive with SHIP.
cost_comparison: Travelling was expensive, really expensive. But I would not have missed it for anything.
activities_available: Free gym. Cheap excursion club with lots of tours and free surf boards.
activities_recommended: Travel, becuase california is awesome!
weekend_recommendations: Travel! And go to some crazy isla ista parties!
culture_adjustment: Quite easy. At UCSB people are very welcoming and nice. Also, exchange students are much more normal in the US, so people are more accostumed to accommodate them.
socializing_tips: Go up and say hi.
cultural_challenges: No being allowed to drink in public, and all the civil restrictions in general.
culture_appreciated: The "hiking" mindset of so many people. Everyone goes in hikes all the time and it is great!
top3_advice: Start looking for housing early, and write all rental agencies to see if they have any vacancies where you can do a 6 month rental. Take TMP courses, as you get so many more friends in those courses and learn much more. Go out and travel.
other_useful_info: Be ready to pay a lot in rent and share a room with 2-3-4 strangers.
most_rewarding: Meeting so many inspiring people and travelling to see so much amazing nature.
greatest_challenge: All the bureaucracy

crucial_aspects: Interesting location in a nice country with good academics.
info_ease: Decently easy. A lot of work had to be done.
arrival_assistance: Not much.
arrival_comments: Terrible. Had a mandatory program which was online and cost $250 dollars and did not provide any useful information.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Not much except choosing courses and picking up IDs. They have some mandatory online courses/tests which are quite boring.
registration_help: Mostly online ressources.
registration_success: Very. Registration opens around october/november, be prepared and ready. If you dont get the courses you want sign up for the waitlist and be ready to swap during the first two weeks.
registration_advice: Do your research early and register in October and November as courses get filled up but most have space then. Use the first couple weeks to figure out which classes your really want, and often space opens in all courses if you're on the waitlist.
course_level: Undergraduate courses are quite easy, graduate courses are difficult. A balance is nice. In general classes are very good. Take a DeCal course as well, and be ready for the sign up at the start of the semester.
teaching_comparison: More empirical and interactive. Office hours are nice. Very passionate and engaged professors.
courses_enrolled: ECON 230B - Public Economics , ECON 134 Macro Economic Policy from The Great Depression Until Today, Econ 133 Inequality and Growth, Econ 115 World Economy in the 20th Century.
recommended_courses: Honestly i really enjoyed all my courses. Especially 230B with Saez. 133 With Zucman is also really interesting.
unexpected_costs: I tried to waive the insurance with Gouda but was denied mid semester and forced enrolled with a fee of $1888 dollars. Housing was in general super expensive. Surprisingly books for class where almost all free.
cost_comparison: Food was very expensive and hard to grocery shop so difficult to cook for yourself.
activities_available: Decals for learning new things. Sports clubs for most. Intramural sports as well.
activities_recommended: Play some tennis. Perhaps join some intramural sports. Hike around the firetrails.
weekend_recommendations: SF. Firetrails. Yosemite. Big Sur. Hearst Castle.
culture_adjustment: Yes. Very easy.
socializing_tips: Little difficult. They're mostly 17-22. Perhaps rush a frat / live in a coop / join some sports league. Decals are good for this as well.
cultural_challenges: Most locals 'had their own life' so a little difficult to get in contact wtih them.
culture_appreciated: Hospitality and openess.
top3_advice: Search and apply for courses and especially scholarships (Legater) in very good time! Its really worth it. Housing live at I-house (And apply in good time as its first come first serve) if you want easy mingling and living with other exchange students, Co-ops if you want to meet locals who like to party and do drugs, Off campus through facebook sites otherwise. SHIP is very difficult to waive with danish insurance companies. If you wanna waive do it through something like ISO.
other_useful_info: Enjoy Berkeley and SF. Its a nice place and academics are top notch. Participate and attend. Meet people. Enjoy the sunsets from up the firetrails. Go on trips to the national parks and hike.
most_rewarding: Incredible professors. Beautiful country.
greatest_challenge: Getting everything in order before going. Finding good housing.
other_comments: Enjoy!

crucial_aspects: I wanted to try and live in the United States and experience the culture and american way of life. A state I was particularly attracted to was California, due to the many iconic cities such as San Fransisco and Los Angeles as well as its beautiful nature and weather.
info_ease: Information was fairly accessible, however it is important to read the emails that are sent from the university. Despite them being numerous and many superfluous, some of them do contain very important information and oversight of these could lead to trouble and heartache down the road.
arrival_assistance: Before arrival we were given the opportunity to be put into small groups with other exchange students. This meant that from the very early stages of the exchange stay you could connect with people, who were in a similar situation as yourself and face the challenges and complications an exchange stay inherently has together. Furthermore, several exchange student events took place at the start of the exchange stay. where socializing was possible. Staff were also - in general - relatively quick and thorough in responding to any questions or problems you had both by email and in person. However, this naturally varied between staff and faculty members.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: A month or so prior to the beginning of the quarter you choose your courses. The registration process consists of 3 registration periods. In the first period you can choose two courses and in the second and third period 1 additional course. As an exchange student it is very important to be cleared of any prerequisites a course may have before registration begins. This is done by reaching out to your assigned EAP (Exchange Abroad Program) helper. Unfortunately, course descriptions are very vague and in order to get more information on any given course you have to personally contact professors for the course syllabus, which was a hassle.
registration_help: The help wasn't the best with respect to course enrollment. You were to some degree left to a type of trial and error process, in which you contacted different university faculty and staff members. This could definitely be improved.
registration_success: I was very fortunate and got enrolled in all the classes I wanted. Whether this is luck, my particular major or a general outcome is hard to tell. My impression, however, was that the other exchange students also got most of their chosen courses, but not always - sometimes classes were filled early.
registration_advice: Be prerequisite cleared in good time before the first registration pass begins! Use your first registration pass for the subjects that are most important / have highest demand (check prior years).
course_level: The academic level was a lot lower and less sophisticated. The econ major had very little math and was a lot less challenging than at home. However, this did vary a lot between courses. Some were very easy courses with no homework and a few multiple choice tests, some unfortunately had more "pseudo" type homework that took time to do, but didn't provide much to any academic improvement. Luckily, others were more challenging and stimulating with well put together homeworks and good curriculum. The easy courses did have the benefit of giving one more time for traveling the country and partake in social activities. The moral of the story is therefore to pick courses wisely and to taper them to your particular wants and desires.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching is a lot more like in a Danish gymnasium. Homework, presentations, tests or quizzes and participation in class during throughout quarter often count toward your final grade.
courses_enrolled: -Monetary Economics (ECON 135) -International Finance (ECON 181) -Introduction to Game Theory (ECON 171) -Philosophy of Economics (PHIL 147) -Introduction to Data Science 1 (CMPSC 5A) - Financial Market Risk and Modelling (PSTAT 194FM)
recommended_courses: My prefered courses were PSTAT 194FM, CMPSC 5A and ECON 171. These were the courses where I felt I learned something useful and new. The finance course gave a good overview of financial markets as a whole and different types of financial instruments and the risks involved. The CMPSC 5A was a good introductory course to programming and doing data analysis in Python, where you got quite familiar with the programming language. Finally, Econ 171 was a more challenging and stimulating course with a lot more math, which to me made it quite enjoyable.
unexpected_costs: Insurance was a huge unexpected cost. I purchased a travel insurance that lived up to the university insurance requirements but I was unable to get it waived. This meant that I had to use their UCSHIP insurance, which cost 15000 DKK and be double insured.
cost_comparison: Things unfortunately tended to be more expensive than I was expecting especially food and rent.
activities_available: As a part of campus there is a free recreational center available to all students. It has a gym, climbing area, pool as well as tennis, squash, american football and soccer fields/courts. There is also an excursion club administrated by students. As a member you can paddle board, surf and go on weekend trips.
activities_recommended: I would recommend getting a membership in the excursion club. I would also recommend spending some time in Downtown Santa Barbara. There are plenty of cool and exiting things to do including museum trips, an old franciscan church, whale watching, clubbing and eating out. There are also some cool hot spring and hikes in Montecito.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend trips to San Fransisco, Los Angeles, Yosemite or/and Sequoia.
culture_adjustment: It was relatively easy, since I understood the language and was accustomed to american culture through movies, news and social media. There were a few ways of greeting people and some slang that may took a short while to get used to, but other than that it wasn't too challenging.
socializing_tips: Americans are very friendly and extroverted. They are in general very easy to chat with.
cultural_challenges: There are very many homeless people in California, who are in very bad condition and often mentally ill. This was quite saddening.
culture_appreciated: I loved the civil extroversion of Americans. I think we danes can learn from it. I also loved visiting the culturally rich cities of LA and San Fransisco.
top3_advice: 1. Even though an exchange stay may be a daunting idea and your are met with challenges and problems, have faith it all will turn out alright - It usually does :) 2. Be open minded and try new things. 3. Be mindful of appreciating the exchange experience in the present moment - it wont last forever.
other_useful_info: Get a bycicle. The walking distances are quite long.
most_rewarding: I loved all the traveling and the countless new impressions, experiences and people. As a whole it was an invaluable experience.
greatest_challenge: At times missing home, friends and family. However, this wasn't too frequent an occurrence and by no means debilitating in any manor.
other_comments: Have fun!

crucial_aspects: I always wanted to experience the US and I have heard good things about University of California.
overall_comments: I can really recommend Santa Barbara. Especially if you are interested in learning to surf, hiking and other outdoor activities. Nature is always close to you. You can go for a run on the beach before class and sit at the library with view over the ocean.
info_ease: It was fine. I received an e-mail with information from the advisor at USCB just before I arrived and one more after arriving. If I needed more information, it was possible to call the advisor or write an e-mail.
arrival_assistance: I was assigned to two different groups one with two other international students also arriving the same time as me and another group with American students from UCSB who are going on exchange to Denmark the following semester. It was very helpful to have other people to discuss things with and learn from. Otherwise, as I mentioned before it was possible to call or send an email to the office or advisor of UCSB Education Abroad Program.
arrival_comments: It is easy to find information or clarify any concerns.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I can really recommend Santa Barbara. Especially if you are interested in learning to surf, hiking and other outdoor activities. Nature is always close to you. You can go for a run on the beach before class and sit at the library with view over the ocean.
registration_process: You sign up for classes at their website called GOLD. At the website you can find information about when you can sign up. At that time be prepared for which classes you want to take. Be aware that some classes fill up quickly. Make sure that the classes don't overlap in the weekly schedule and the exam week. All the information about the classes you can find if you look up UCSB course catalog on google and then search for courses by subject area. If the class have prerequisites, you can email the department that offers the class to get a sign up code. Therefor look up in good time which classes you wish for (make sure to have a plan b), if any prerequisites e-mail the department and be ready by the time you have your sign up timeslot.
registration_help: If you write to the department, they will help you.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted. I did experience that in the first week of class I changed my mind and wanted another course. This made everything a little difficult. I could just have signed up for four classes and tried them all out and sign off on one of them.
registration_advice: Be prepared for the sign up timeslot with prerequisites, plan B and consider adding an extra course in case you don't like one of the classes you have chosen.
academics_comments: I can really recommend Santa Barbara. Especially if you are interested in learning to surf, hiking and other outdoor activities. Nature is always close to you. You can go for a run on the beach before class and sit at the library with view over the ocean.
course_level: I was happy with my classes. I chose only undergraduate classes, but the upper division of undergraduate classes. The classes have numbers and classes with numbers higher than 100 are for higher level. Some were not so challenging, but then I had more time to go experience Santa Barbara.
teaching_comparison: There was no time for doing assignments or homework problem in class. It is expected of you to do it at home. I found it much more fun and rewarding to sit together with one or two other students after class and go over the homework together. I will therefor recommend finding a friend in each class.
courses_enrolled: Biophysics and Biomolecular Materials Introduction to Scientific Computation Geophysical Time-Series Analysis Geophysics Geophysics (Seismology) Global Warming
recommended_courses: Depending on your area of interest all the classes I took, I really liked. My favorite was the Geophysical Time-Series Analysis. If You take this class, you can become very good at Fourier Transformation. I also really liked the Global Warming course. Not that much heavy physics or mathematics in the class, but a lot of interesting point on global warming and a good professor.
unexpected_costs: It costed more than I expected to establish myself with towels and sheets and so on.
cost_comparison: Housing was very expensive. It took up most of my budget.
activities_available: There are a lot of things happening at UCSB. You must find them yourself. For example, they have choirs and they did a musical. You can also try and join their soccer team. I joined the Excursion club which cost about 30 dollars for three months. Here you can borrow their surf boards, kayaks, wet suits, climbing equipment and a whole lot of other stuff. They also arrange field trips each week to go skiing, hiking or paint the sunset.
activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend joining the Excursion club.
weekend_recommendations: Find some good friends you feel comfortable with and arrange a weekend trip to San Francisco, Los Angeles or similar. It is easy enough to rent a car. California is a big place with a lot of things to see.
culture_adjustment: It was all fine. I arrived a couple of days before and lived at a hotel. I got to know some of the other exchange students from Denmark and we met up to go explore a bit of Santa Barbara before the school started. After that I can only recommend talking to as many people as you can. Generally, I find that most of the people you will meet are friendly and wants to talk.
socializing_tips: It really helped me bonding with people in my classes. Starting the conversation with homework and then go to parties together or drink smoothies from Blenders (if it is still there – It is really good) or something else. There are also lot of eateries nearby campus which is fun to try with some locals.
cultural_challenges: It was not so much any cultural differences that was challenging. It was much more being able to small talk in English that was challenging for me, but after a while I got over it. The best solution to that is to just leap into it and talk to everyone you meet.
culture_appreciated: People are very friendly and open. Most people loved to talk even though we did not know each other yet. In that way it made it easy to get in touch with new people.
top3_advice: Make friends with people in your classes. It will help you with both the studies and the social life. Join clubs and go on trips. It is a great possibility to experience another culture and environment. Prepare as much as you can from home, so you can relax and enjoy this great experience. It goes by so fast.
other_useful_info: The buss was free for students at UCSB, which was nice and made it easy to go downtown. I bought a used bike which I was really happy about and I sold it just before I left.
most_rewarding: The people I met in class. I found friends in my field of interest whom I still talk to.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge for my exchange was finding housing. I will recommend starting early by joining facebook group for UCSB housing and looking at campus housing website.
other_comments: Remember to enjoy the experience it is a great and one-of-a-kind experience. Another tip: It is nice to have mobile connection from the beginning. I used MintMobile. With that you can download an electronic sim card before arriving in California.

crucial_aspects: I had dreamed of visiting California, and Los Angeles in particular, for a long time. Being in a city and close to the entertainment industry and being able to take courses in film at UCLA were also motivating factors for me
overall_comments: Unfortunately, Covid-19 restrictions played a role in my exchange experience since the first half of my programme was almost entirely online.
info_ease: As far as I remember, we received emails from UCLA and UCEAP Reciprocity before and after arrival with instructions. However, there wasn't one single official in-person orientation or event for exchange/international students who had just arrived, which was something I would have liked to have. Some things I had to find out on my own
arrival_assistance: Received emails from UCLA and UCEAP Reciprocity
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Unfortunately, Covid-19 restrictions played a role in my exchange experience since the first half of my programme was almost entirely online.
registration_process: UCLA has different enrollment 'passes' on MyUCLA which is determined by factors such as your college year/level or your major – make sure you check the specific requirements for each of the classes you're interested in taking before enrollment starts, and make sure to enroll as soon as possible! Some courses are more popular than others – I was lucky that I got all my desired courses but it's better to be prepared in advance, especially if you're looking at specific courses you really want to enroll in.
registration_help: I received emails from UCLA regarding enrollment and enrollment passtimes (when enrollment starts), and you can log onto MyUCLA and explore courses and add them to your 'Class Planner' to visualize how your weekly schedule could look before enrollment starts.
registration_success: Before arrival, I was hoping to be able to enroll in some practical/studio courses within a particular major. Unfortunately, some majors have restrictions on specific types of classes if you're in another major, which restricted my enrollment. Fortunately, I was able to enroll in all the other courses I was interested in (including lower-level/more theoretical courses within said major)
registration_advice: Make a list of all courses you're interested in, try to see how they fit into your schedule, make sure you read the requirements/prerequisites on the Schedule of Classes or MyUCLA for each class you're interested in, and make sure to check your emails and your MyUCLA account to see which enrollment passtime you can enroll in – and enroll as soon as enrollment starts to be safe
academics_comments: Unfortunately, Covid-19 restrictions played a role in my exchange experience since the first half of my programme was almost entirely online.
course_level: I took courses with numbers between 20 and around 124 – the lower numbers indicate introductory courses, and the higher numbers indicate mid-level or upper-level courses. Overall, personally, I didn't find the general level to be too difficult, but again, this can depend whether you're taking introductory, upper-division courses or masters' courses
teaching_comparison: Some of my courses consisted of a weekly lecture and no discussion seminars, while another course I took had two lectures a week and one discussion section a week. This section differed from my seminars at UCPH, however, in that it mostly consisted of my TA briefly going over some points from the lectures instead of being based on mainly group discussions and classroom 'activation'. I found it a bit difficult at times not having a combination of lectures and discussions with other students, which also made it a bit more difficult meeting new people in/around class. Furthermore, I took a practical in-person course which had little theory which was a nice contrast to more theoretical courses.
courses_enrolled: Beginning Martial Arts (Dance/Worlds Arts & Cultures major), Evolutionary Psychology (Anthropology), Introduction to American Indian Studies (American Indian Studies), Experimental Film, Digital Cinematography, Film Editing – Overview of History, Technique, and Practice (Film/Television)
recommended_courses: Experimental Film was quite fascinating and inspiring. Evolutionary Psychology was very interesting, but also a bit challenging if you haven't taking an introductory course in evolution or aren't a biology/psychology/anthropology major. I'd recommend Introduction to American Indian Studies as well!
unexpected_costs: Most weekly meals at the Co-op were included in the price of rent – I did buy extra groceries in addition to this but wouldn't strictly be needed most of the time. Extra/unexpected costs would include uber, uber eats, going out, getting film (photos) developed, cultural events such as movie tickets, museums, restaurants... I also went on a roadtrip with some friends which included car rental, meals, and hotels/airbnbs
cost_comparison: Many things were around the same price as in Denmark. Some food, movie tickets, public transportation were a bit cheaper
activities_available: Many! There's a whole page (UCLA Rec) with hundreds of different clubs/activities such as sports, creative clubs, societies etc.
activities_recommended: Would recommend signing up for something you're interested in or interested in trying! I signed up for the archery club where I met some nice people – they also arranged meetups and activities outside practice
weekend_recommendations: See all the tourist sites, the beach, Hollywood, DTLA... There's so much to explore and LA is a huge area. I went to Santa Barbara for the weekend while I was there which was really nice – would also recommend going around California or the neighboring states if possible! There are many beautiful national parks in and around California that are amazing to see in-person. I also enjoyed spending time along the coast, in Santa Monica, Venice, Malibu, and going hiking in the hills.
culture_adjustment: In general it was pretty easy
socializing_tips: Try signing up for clubs and activities and talk to people in your classes and at your dorm/the co-op (if you live here)
cultural_challenges: Many undergraduate students are a bit younger than UCPH students
culture_appreciated: Many opportunities for activities and different events, and people can seem pretty open in general
top3_advice: Save money (and try to apply for scholarships/legater!) before you go – there are so many things, activities and cool places to visit that you'd want to experience if possible
other_useful_info: Look at other UCPH students' evalutations on this page, talk to other UCPH students who are planning on going to UC or your specific UC campus, look at which courses each UC campus have and which ones you're especially interested in enrolling in – but do also prioritize which city/place you would like to live in as this can play a big role in which environment you have a chance to explore daily – as well as which type of environment (city, beach town, closer to nature...) you might thrive in and enjoy!
most_rewarding: Getting to live in Los Angeles and explore the city/area, going on a road trip to California and neighboring states and seeing some very different and fascinating places, landscapes, and nature, meeting new people, and becoming more independent
greatest_challenge: Covid-19 restrictions on campus and in my dorm the first half of my programme made it harder to meet new people, which was especially challenging in the beginning where you don't necessarily know anyone upon arrival. Hopefully, this might not be the case after 2022, however! It was also challenging at times trying to balance everything in daily life yourself.
other_comments: If you're interested in going on exchange and it's a possibility for you, I very much recommend it! It's really cool getting to live in another country for a longer period of time in contrast to a shorter vacation, and it makes you understand aspects of the local culture(s) and daily life more, puts your life in Denmark into perspective, and provides many social and cultural opportunities and experiences.

crucial_aspects: I am a really big fan of the US and the culture and wanted to experience it in a different way which can only be truly acheived by living in the country. I also wanted to improve my English and get more comfortable with it since I'm gonna use that for the rest of my working life. I was also really curious how they teach stuff in the US. They definitely managed to make in more tangible and interesting than in Denmark. This is because it's not as theoretical as in Denmark which is really nice in my opinion. I also wanted to develop as a person. I think putting myself out in a situation where I have to live in a new country where I don't know anyone is a really good way to develop as a person. I definitely have developed socially which is an important aspect in both my personal life, but also my working life. Nevertheless, I didn't chose the university based on the courses and if I could go back I would probably have chosen something more relevant to my studies. This is because it is a big gap now that I have to write my Master's Thesis that I haven't worked in the field for almost a year. Also because I did a lot of school work in the US and then it would have been better to do some school work which would have benefited me more.

crucial_aspects: At bo i LA/Cali og studere på et fedt campus som UCLA.
info_ease: Det var ikke det nemmeste i verden. Især fagtilmelding var lidt af en jungle, og deres system er meget anderledes end vores. Man skal være forberedt på, at fag bliver hurtigt fyldt, og fordi man ikke bliver registreret som en major i sit fag, så har man ikke førsteprioritet. Det er en del af deres system, at man kan skifte fag de første to uger, hvilket kan føles lidt uoverskueligt, men omvendt gør det også, at du kan komme til undervisning og snakke med professoren, hvis du ikke har fået plads på faget og nogle gange lader de dig tage det selvom det er fyldt.
arrival_assistance: Ikke specielt meget. Den bedste hjælp får du fra de andre udvekslingsstuderende. Der er også en udvekslingskoordinator på UCLA, som man kan skrive til. Det var jeg ikke selv opmærksom på, men eftersigende var han god til at svare hurtigt og hjælpe.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Efter du har gennnemgået KU's registreringsproces skal du gøre noget lignende, men langt mere omfattende, på UCEAP's hjemmeside. De skal have alverdens oplysninger om dig, og du skal vist nok også skrive et kort statement og derudover søge de tre universiteter du ønsker i prioriteret rækkefølge. Derefter venter du på svar i et par måneder. Du får så at vide hvilket universitet du er kommet på og skal ind og udfylde nogle oplysninger, så de kan sende dig din DS-2019. Det er dog ikke altid, at du får de oplysninger du skal bruge for at kunne logge ind på MyUCLA med det samme, så du går lidt og venter på, at får dit UID (id-nummer), så du kan få det gjort.
registration_help: Programkoordinatoren Simone kan hjælpe en del, men det er primært i processen omkring udfyldelsen af oplysninger på UCEAP og processen med visum. Efter du har fået dit campus og skal anvende deres hjemmeside til fx at få udfyldt oplysninger så de kan sende din DS-2019, giver det bedre mening at skrive til deres hjælpeservice.
registration_success: Relativt succesful. Som nævnt har man ikke førsteprioritet, når man skal registrere. Det betyder, at vi først kan enrolle i anden runde, og der kan man risikere at fag allerede er fyldt op. Man gør sig selv en tjeneste ved at have lavet den brugt deres class planner på forhånd, så man hurtigt kan tilgå de fag du vil have, når tilmeldingen åbner. Så kan man også nemt følge med i, om de er ved at blive fyldt op, og man kan se hvornår de ligger, så man ikke kommer til at tilmelde sig fag, som overlapper. Vi havde ikke på forhånd fået at vide, at vi ikke kunne enrolle i første runde, og det var lidt stramt at stå op kl. 4 om morgenen for at sidde klar, når det åbnede, for at konstatere at tilmeldingen stadig var låst. Underligt nok, så kunne de økonomistuderende fra KU godt enrolle i første runde, det var kun os på stats, der ikke kunne.
registration_advice: Det er bøvlet, men det skal nok løse sig. Du kan stadig nå at ændre dine fag de første to uger af studiet, og nogle professorer vil godt lade dig tage faget, selvom det er fyldt op. Du kan også skrive en mail til dem og få en bestem kode, så du kan tilmelde dig tidligere end du burde. Det er der mange der siger nej til, men hvis du skriver du er stakkels udvekslingsstuderende, så er der nogen som forbarmer sig. De er generelt hurtige til at svare. Jeg tilmeldte mig faktisk 6 fag på mit andet quarter, og så tog jeg til alle undervisningerne de første to uger, hvorefter jeg bestemte mig for, hvilke 3 jeg ville droppe. Det kan være en god taktik, hvis man orker det.
course_level: Til den lave side. Jeg tog mange kurser om amerikansk politik, hvor jeg selvsagt var mere på udebane end de andre, hvilket udlignede det lidt. Men de er ikke vant til at skrive akademisk, og det er meget tydeligt i fag, hvor man skal aflevere længere opgaver, at man er ret langt foran dem på det parameter.
teaching_comparison: Det kommer meget an på faget. Nogle kurser er det forelæsninger meget som ved KU, mens det på andre kurser er meget mere dynamisk. En forskel er, at mange kurser inkludere holdundervisning, hvor man får karakter baseret på aktiv deltagelse, som medregnes i den endelige karakter.
courses_enrolled: National Institutions - The Presidency Political Parties and American Democracy American Political Development: Institutional Development Political Economy of Climate Change Political Economy of Development Special Topics in Metode and Models: Randomised Trials for Social Change
recommended_courses: Jeg synes egentlig alle var gode på hver sin måde på nær The Presidency faget, som var ret tørt. Ikke et vildt dårligt fag, men ret kedeligt. Man kan lidt sige det samme om American Political Development, men jeg fandt det lidt mere interessant og det var noget jeg vidste mindre om på forhånd. Men begge to var meget historisk orienterede. Political Parties faget køres af John Zaller, som jo er en stor kanon i politologien, hvilket er meget fedt. Han er dog lidt gammel og forvirret, så det kunne godt blive lidt kaotisk en gang i mellem. Meget af pensum var også lidt random, men overordnet en fin indføring i amerikansk politik. De to Political Economy fag var rigtig gode og kørte snorlige. Development havde mange overlap med DAK3 i første halvdel, men blev derefter langt mere detaljerede omkring handel, ulandsbistand og verdensøkonomien i nyere tid. Climate Change var virkelig spændende og det vil jeg virkelig anbefale. Det kombinerer en masse forskellig statskundskabsdiscipliner og ser på klimaforandringer og den manglende politiske ageren både fra et politisk teori, IP, nationalt politik og økonomisk teori perspektiv. Og professoren er god og meget engageret. Metodefaget var super kaotisk, og det vil jeg ikke anbefale. Der var nogle spændende tekster ind i mellem og professoren var virkelig på forskningsfronten når det kom til at bruge eksperimenter til at teste effekten humanitær hjælp i udviklingslande, hvilket var fedt. Men som sagt var det super kaotisk og ustruktureret og der var rigtig meget gruppearbejde, som folk var ekstremt useriøse omkring.
unexpected_costs: Primært inflationen og den stigende dollar.
cost_comparison: Housing og mad var meget billigere end forventet pga. UCHA. Men hvis du bor på campus ville du nok opleve det modsatte.
activities_available: Fuldstændigt vanvittige faciliteter. Pools, tennisbaner, fodboldbaner, løbebane, gym, beachvolley, squash, klatrevæg og meget mere. Alverdens klubber, som jeg dog ikke selv var en del af. Alt er gratis.
activities_recommended: Jeg brugte sportsfaciliteterne, og jeg vil især anbefale deres tennistræning. Det koster 30 dollars pr. quarter og så får man professionel tennistræning en gang om ugen. Du kan også få træning i alt muligt andet for en rigtig god pris. De bliver dog hurtigt udfyldt, så man skal sidde klar når det åbner, hvilket det gør et par uger inden quarteret starter. Du kan finde det ved at søge på UCLA Recreation. Man får også en mail om det.
weekend_recommendations: Få set de klassiske LA ting de første par uger: Getty Center, Griffith Park, Walk of Fame etc. Derefter weekendture til Las Vegas, Grand Canyon, Yosemite, SF, Santa Barbara, San Diego, Death Valley og meget mere alt efter økonomien. Meget kan kombineres i en weekendtur, hvis man lejer en bil og laver et roadtrip. Især hvis man sørger for at have fri mandag og fredag. Og så Cancun eller Hawaii i spring break, hvis man er der i foråret.
culture_adjustment: Ret nemt. Der var mange europæere, hvor jeg boede og amerikanerne er også nemme nok at snakke med.
socializing_tips: Sport og klubber og ellers er det meget betinget af hvor du bor.
cultural_challenges: Jeg ved ikke om man kan kalde det kulturelt, men der var et par års aldersforskel i gennemsnit. Det er nok den største forskel.
culture_appreciated: Åbenheden og venligheden.
top3_advice: Rejse på mange weekendture, brug sportsfaciliteterne, kommuniker meget med de andre KU studerende, der skal på UCLA omkring alt det praktiske. Det kan være ret uoverskueligt med alt det man skal have styr på, og man kan godt komme til at overse noget. Hvis man kan spørge andre om det, så kan man nemmere dække hinandens blinde vinkler. Og så en fjerde ting: UCHA - ekstremt billigt, fint nok sted at bo, hvis du ikke har noget imod at dele værelse med andre (hvilket du alligevel skal on-campus eller i en lejlighed, medmindre du er millionær), meget tæt på campus og nem måde at møde nye mennesker på.
other_useful_info: Det kan godt betale sig at købe en bil, hvis du regner med at tage på mange ture. Det gør det så meget nemmere at komme rundt i LA, og en tur til fx. Santa Monica går fra at være en halvdagstur, til noget man lige kan gøre, hvis man keder sig.
most_rewarding: Møde en masse nye mennesker på UCHA. Både fra Danmark, USA og rundt om i Europa.
greatest_challenge: Bureaukratiet ifbm. visum, fagtilmelding og ansøgningprocessen. Legatsøgning var også lidt en orker.
other_comments: Start tidligt med legatsøgning. Man kan virkelig få mange penge, hvis man er grundig og det gør det muligt at rejse langt mere.

info_ease: It was not specifically easy, I fell like it could have been made clearer especially considering that everybody is doing the same thing. Also we had to go through undergraduate introduction which was unecessary.
arrival_assistance: Email´s with some introduction, a 3 day introduction course before start, but most of the 3 day introduction course was for undergraduates and irellevant for us.
arrival_comments: I feel like you could make it much clearer and focus on internation and transfer students more.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You find the coruse on the Cal dashboard, sign up to a course and either get on a waitlist or an error message. Then as the final deadline approaches you will get into the courses and hopefully all of them will be turned from waitlisted to enrolled.
registration_help: You can write proffesors or advisors
registration_success: I got all of them, even those that were very unlikely by writing to the professors
registration_advice: Be calm, do not mind being on the waitlist, and write proffesors or advisros if in doubt.

recommended_courses: All of those I took, they give a nice overview of specialized courses we do not have on KU and gives you basic knowledge in neurobiology and immunology. if you are interested in that.

cost_comparison: Food and housing was incredibly expensive
activities_available: all kinds of clubs, fitness and socail gatherings
activities_recommended: Go travel, rent a car with the other danish students
weekend_recommendations: Go travel, rent a car with the other danish students
culture_adjustment: Very easy, no problems at all
socializing_tips: Just talk with them, go to gatherings etc. They are incredibly social
cultural_challenges: All the homeless people
culture_appreciated: How friendly and open everybody were
top3_advice: Have a lot of money, talk and engage with people who are american, do not stress about all the midterms just read through and remmeber the slides and do show up!
