greatest_challenge: Homeless people and expenses

crucial_aspects: Exploring a new educational culture, but first of all to get an adventure far away from Denmark.
info_ease: Regarding visa and needed documents I used a lot of time to find the correct information. The visa process changes over years, wherefore I also sometimes got some wrong/outdated information.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance when arriving at the destination.
arrival_comments: I did not attend the orientation events, wherefore it is hard to answer.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process is online, and you can see all steps + there is online assistance.
registration_help: Online assistance.
registration_success: I was successfully registered in the classes I wanted. The only problem for me was acceptance from KU, since it took student administration in Copenhagen so long to finally accept my courses that I no longer had the opportunity to change classes at UCSD. Luckily KU accepted the courses, but I would have been in a really bad situation if not.
registration_advice: Just do as the steps says online, it all makes perfectly sense.
course_level: The courses are overall at the same level as at KU, however the exams are a lot easier.
teaching_comparison: Some of the courses were a lot smaller than at KU, with more conversation during the classes.
courses_enrolled: Topics of Macroeconomics, Monetary Economics, Economics of Education, Behavioral Economics, Economics of Modern Israel
recommended_courses: All of them. Especially Monetary Economics, Economics of Education and Behavioral Economics was super interesting and the courses have really taught me a lot.
unexpected_costs: Taxes and tips
cost_comparison: Everything was more expensive than expected, expect when going to Mexico for spring break:)
activities_available: So many sport games, student organisations, etc. were available. When entering campus you are told about all the opportunities, and it is so easy to go there.
activities_recommended: Check out the student organisations. There is a app showing all possibile. I went with UCSD hiking, it was super cool.
weekend_recommendations: Rent a car for the whole period, it will make it so much easier to explore San Diego County, California and go to trips in Las Vegas, Grand Canyon, Zion National Park, etc.
culture_adjustment: It was super easy, since the American culture is somewhat close to the Danish.
socializing_tips: Go out in Pacific Beach, all students go there.
cultural_challenges: Not really any.
culture_appreciated: That Americans are so outgoing. It makes it so much easier to socialize with locals.
top3_advice: 1. Have a large savings 2. Live off campus, at either Mission- or Pacific Beach 3. Be open minded
other_useful_info: Find Facebook-groups for students in San Diego.
most_rewarding: Living off campus at the beach, living the beach life with a lot of other international students.
greatest_challenge: Money

crucial_aspects: Living in California, opportunity to study at a renowned university.
info_ease: UC Irvine are great at providing assistance and information, and the international team is very quick to respond to any inquiries. Much better than UCPH.
arrival_assistance: There were events that assisted both in making friends and in formalities. I had no issues whatsoever with getting set up and ready for studying over there.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: They have a system called webreg, which they will tell you about, it is not complicated.
registration_help: International Center is there for you to answer all the questions you may have.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted except one. For some courses they require specific merits, of which some can be certain basic 1st year courses that you have not taken (ex. basic level academic writing) and they are not flexible with these requirements, so be aware this may make it difficult for you to register for a class that you should be considered fit to take.
registration_advice: Just be on the lookout for registration requirements.
course_level: I was there as a masters student, but I could only take bachelor level courses because of the exchange agreement. Hence, the courses were much easier than they would have been in UCPH. Bachelor level courses in UC are also a lot easier than bachelor level courses in UCPH.
teaching_comparison: More interaction with the professors, the professors had more freedom in designing their own classes and style of teaching. More tests throughout the course.
courses_enrolled: UC Irvine has quarter structure, so I took three quarters, corresponding to two semesters. In my first quarter I took: Liberalism & Conservatism, Political Participation, and Just War: Revisited. My second quarter: Modern Political Theory, Capitalism and its Critics, and Enlightenment Legacy.
recommended_courses: Any course with prof. Steven Bilakovics or prof. Daniel Brunstetter.
unexpected_costs: There are some fees that the uni needs you to pay. For each course you take they charge you an administration fee of a few dollars. They also charge you to give you your official transcript after completing your exchange.
cost_comparison: Everything is more expensive than you think, especially groceries and housing.
activities_available: Many clubs do events in everything you can imagine.
activities_recommended: Surfing! Visiting LA! Doing road trips to national parks!
weekend_recommendations: See above. Go out in Newport Beach.
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy.
socializing_tips: It will come naturally, don't worry.
cultural_challenges: Americans are welcoming and the other exchange students are also looking for friends, so don't worry.
culture_appreciated: Americans are so much more open toward strangers, and they are more willing to go out and do stuff together.
top3_advice: It is worth all the administrative trouble! It won't be summer temperatures all year round. There is no life in Irvine, but don't worry, you will have plenty of things to do around the area once you get settled.
other_useful_info: Transportation may seem hopeless in the US without a car, but you will find ways to get around, even if you don't buy a car.
most_rewarding: Making great new friends and living the California lifestyle.
greatest_challenge: To remain in contact with friends and family at home.

crucial_aspects: UCSD has an institute for oceanography (Scripps Institute of Oceanography) which is an interest of mine and they are very good at climate studies. Also a great location neat the ocean with good study environments.
overall_comments: Amazing place but very expensive.
info_ease: UCPH gave a very good overall guideline on how to get a visa and what needed to be done before going abroad. However, there were a lot of documents which needed to be sorted and many processes to go through in order to get a visa, health insurences and other requirements for the university. There was a lot of uncertainty regarding housing and the process of getting campus housing was long and a bit confusing but worked out in the end. All the information needed to organize the exchange was a bit stressfull.
arrival_assistance: I did not recieve any special assistance but it felt like it was available if needed.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Amazing place but very expensive.
registration_process: I had to make a general motivational application to get into the UC system where I had choose my preferences of universities and relevant courses. When I got accepted at UCSD I had to apply for the DS2019 to get my visa. Then I had to choose my courses.
registration_help: There was a guide on how to apply for each step. I also had some questions which I asked the student service who helped me.
registration_success: I was very succesful in registering for the classes I wanted and even though I did not have all the prerequisits for the classes I could ask for permition by the professers to get a spot.
registration_advice: I would recommend that you plan everything in good time inadvance and that you sort out your prerequisits before going. It was a bit stressfull to learn a new registration system but if you take your time it will definetly work out in the end.
academics_comments: Amazing place but very expensive.
course_level: Very high level in general and the classes used more applied math and physics than what we are used to at geography at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: There were more assigments and test, but other than that it was simulair to UCPH with discussions and presentations. They also used teacher assistants for all classes who were very hepfull.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Physical Oceanography, Physical Basis of Global Warming, Analysis of Oceanographic and Atmospheric Data.
recommended_courses: Analysis of Oceanographic and Atmospheric Data really improved my coding skills and gave taught me much about data analysis but it was VERY demanting and requires many hours of investment and struggle but in the end it was the class I learned most from and the one I perfomed best in since it was the most interesting class. I can recommend it if you are interested in earth systems, climate change and data analysis and statistics and dont mind putting in some time learning how to code. I did not have any coding experience but managed anyways by investing a lot of time. I can also recommend Introduction to physical oceanography which gives a good understanding of the physics in the oceans.
unexpected_costs: The food was very expensive.
cost_comparison: Food and travels.
activities_available: Most sports were available. There was a nice gym, climbing center, a very nice outdoor pool, tennis courts and much more.
activities_recommended: I can recommend the climbing club. It is great community and does not require any skill level.
weekend_recommendations: Go climbing with the locals in the nearby mountains or go surfing at La Jolla. There is also many good hikes nearby but it requires a car (or friends with cars...).
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Nice and easygoing, friendly people and a great community for international students.
socializing_tips: Join a club on campus.
cultural_challenges: Most people at campus are living away from home for the first time and they are not used to manage everything in the household by them selves; cleaning, cooking etc.
culture_appreciated: The outdoor life and use of nature was great but you had to seek it. There are so many things to do if you seek it. I also realy appriciate a bagel and coffe on the way to class every morning :)
top3_advice: Plan everything well in advance. Dont stress to much about classes. Remember to enjoy your stay by going on trips - there is a great acces to nature and activities.
other_useful_info: California is very car based so I would recommend buying a car to get around. Maybe you can share it with some friends. I did not have one so I relied much on my friends.
most_rewarding: Passing harder classes was very rewarding and also experiencing some amazing nature.
greatest_challenge: It was challenging adapting to a more mathematical and physical approach in the classes but also very rewarding.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to experience a different country and a different culture as far away from Denmark as possible while still being able to understand the language. It was also crucial that the university was a good academic university.
info_ease: It was all quite easy.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance when I arrived.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: To be honest, I do not recall how the registration proces was. As far as I recall it was fairly easy.
registration_help: I believe all necessary information was available on the website
registration_success: I got the classes I wanted, but I could have used more information on how registration works beforehand, as it was quite stressing scheduling classes.
registration_advice: Relax more regarding the registration. Look for the courses you might want, talk to people who know the courses to figure out if they are good, and do not be too concerned with waitlists. Usually people on waitlists get to enroll.
course_level: It was quite different. The academic level was not as high, but there was much more material to cover, so in that sense it was difficult but in a different way.
teaching_comparison: As stated above it was quite different. More quantity and less quality I would say.
courses_enrolled: CS61A STAT33B STAT151A STAT154
recommended_courses: CS61A, in general look for CS courses if you are into data science and computer science.
unexpected_costs: I did not encounter any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: In general the prices on food was much higher than I expected. Books and transport were cheaper than expected.
activities_available: Basically anything you can imagine.
activities_recommended: Play chess, play Tennis, go swimming
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend Yosemite, Lake Tahoe, Big Sur, Highway 1, Hawaii and Utah national parks.
culture_adjustment: Quite easy.
socializing_tips: Join clubs, engage in social activities, play sports, engage with your class mates.
cultural_challenges: People are much more open, and you have to get used to superficial talks with strangers.
culture_appreciated: That people are open. That people dare to take themselves serious. The way everything seems huge and more adventurous.
top3_advice: If you just take a small step at a time in the end all the planning works out. Apply for I-House or a coop. Even though the coops look very shitty, they are actually very nice. Enrolling in courses is very different. You should prepare for not being settled on courses until the second, third or even fourth week, so it can be tough. Try the different courses, see what you like, talk to the professor about enrolment if you are unsure, and just try to enroll. Do not be afraid of waitlists. When the semester begins the waitlist goes very fast, and almost everyone end up with the courses they want. If there is a course you would like to take, and you find a similar course in the computer science department, enroll in the one in the CS department.
other_useful_info: Use the resources available online and reach out to the contact person at KU.
most_rewarding: The friends I have made.
greatest_challenge: Balancing academics and exploring the country.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go on exchange for a full academic year, which left me with few options, among them University of California, Berkeley. After having looked at my options I decided to choose Berkeley for my reasons: - Highly rated academic school - I have family nearby - Interesting history - I've never been to the US
overall_comments: Go for two semesters, not one and apply for housing at the BSC system the moment you consider going to Berkeley. I really loved my stay and I would recommend anyone to go, and if possible in any way I would encourage people to go for a full year rather than only spending one semester abroad. The second semester was by far the best, because I already had established a connections with people, settled in the area and I received new, unforeseen opportunities.
info_ease: I must admit I don't remember, so I guess everything was OK
arrival_assistance: There is a mandatory, expensive Golden Bear Orientation (GBO) which is a huge event for all new students. It is kind of a mess logistically and I've heard some people manage to waive the attendance. I met some people during GBO but did not stay in contact with any of them during the school year.
arrival_comments: People are extremely helpful but the first days have way too many events. I would recommend going to everyting, but also taking your own time walking aimlessly around campus and entering random buildings on your own to get your own perspective of the university. That is how I found the Student Musical Activities Center
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Go for two semesters, not one and apply for housing at the BSC system the moment you consider going to Berkeley. I really loved my stay and I would recommend anyone to go, and if possible in any way I would encourage people to go for a full year rather than only spending one semester abroad. The second semester was by far the best, because I already had established a connections with people, settled in the area and I received new, unforeseen opportunities.
registration_process: It is relatively competitve to get the calsses you want, but it's all about playing the long game. Many people drop classes during the first two weeks and I have rarely met people who waited until the end of the deadline and still hadn't got what they wanted/needed. In the summer you have to choose classes and during the first 2-4 weeks you can drop classes. That is very helpful in making decisions about what is the most interesting. I actuall ylike thiss system better than the KU system, because there is way more flexibility.
registration_help: I don't know of any
registration_success: I got into all the classes I wanted. I took a Chinese class which had different recommendations than the rest, but I ended up talking to the instructor directly and then they allowed me to join the class.
registration_advice: Find classes you want, go to the lectures in the beginning and just keep your place on the wait list and you will get in (except for really tiny music production classes).
academics_comments: Go for two semesters, not one and apply for housing at the BSC system the moment you consider going to Berkeley. I really loved my stay and I would recommend anyone to go, and if possible in any way I would encourage people to go for a full year rather than only spending one semester abroad. The second semester was by far the best, because I already had established a connections with people, settled in the area and I received new, unforeseen opportunities.
course_level: I only took 100- level classes in statistics and they where much more applied than the equvalent are at Copenhagen University, but they ave way more exercises. I think the general consesus among exchange students is that there is way more evaluation during the semester and that you almost don't need to study for the exam because the final is only 30%. People say they are super busy at all times. I had a course load of 15 units the first semester and 13 units the second semester, and I still had plenty of time to play music, go for runs and enjoy the weekends. Be prepared to do many assignments and get used to just doing them, then you can keep your evenings of.
teaching_comparison: Way more tests and midterms, more concrete tasks. The exercises are less useful, since the TA useful just shows the solutions rather than letting yourself figure stuff out.
courses_enrolled: STAT 135 Concepts of statistics (4 units) - brilliant, but tough, class. A bit like MStat and StatMet. I had 10 assignments, 4 quizzes, 1 midterm and 1 final STAT 133 Concepts of computing with data (3 units) - Very easy, great for getting to know R, would maybe not prioritize again PHILOS 128 Philosphy of Science (4 units) - A substitute for Videnskabsteori. It was very different from VT, but was very interesting and it is actually pretty great to be challenged in a different way of writing and thinking ENE RES 160 CLIMATE JUSTICE (4 units)- super important class! It is mostly a general introduction the the term Justice and the consequences of climate changes.
recommended_courses: I would recommend people to do classes that are not possible at KU! Remeber that you are here to learn something different that people back home, spend time taking classes in humanities ENE RES 160 CLIMATE JUSTICE CS61A
unexpected_costs: Car insurance and parking was very expensive. Food is way more expensive than in Denmark! In addition the school has many extra fees I had never heard of (approx 3500 DKK) at the beginning of the semester
cost_comparison: Nothing.
activities_available: Many things, especially consulting and dance clubs
activities_recommended: I was part of the SMA (Student music activities) and played in the UC Bigband and World Music Ensemble (WME). WME was great if you want a more spiritual discussion of music.
weekend_recommendations: Go for runs in the hill! The stonewall panorama trial is amazing, Yosemite overrated. Go to all the cool performances, lectures and conferences on campus.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy. People don't drink as much alchol which is actually pretty nice. On the other hand you will hear al ot about other substances. I think it's very important to get a more nuanced look and Danish alcohol culture! In addition most students and Berkeley are 18-22, so you may feel slightly old at times
socializing_tips: Live in a coop. People a young but amazing
cultural_challenges: Nothing. It was amazing
culture_appreciated: The cultural diverisity and access to other types of music and philosphies. Remember to get non-exchange friends and get to know "local" life in the US. Europe will also be there when you come back from exchange.
top3_advice: - Apply for living at a coop this moment coop.bsc (seriously). You can end up spending way more time and eneryg living at a shittier place if you don't-
other_useful_info: Don't forget that this is a once in a life time opportunity and immerse yourself in the culture. Don't spend too much time alone watching movies, but remember to take care of yourself when needed. Most people around you are in the same boat (moving far away from home to a new school), join a club and prioritize people over school work!
most_rewarding: Experiencing so much diversity
greatest_challenge: Accepting that it would be over

crucial_aspects: There were so many. First of all, the good reputation of UC Berkeley and its program in Environmental Economics and Policy, a field which few universities offer enough courses in. Secondly, I have family in the Bay Area. Third, the nature in California and neighbouring states is incredible. Fourth, the US is a very diverse place, and the Bay Area in particular is quite progressive and interesting culturally.
overall_comments: I loved my time at UCB!
info_ease: Pretty straightforward. The CalCentral portal tells you everything you need to know.
arrival_assistance: There was international student orientation and then the Golden Bear Orientation during the first couple days which gives students every opportunity to have all their questions answered and a chance to meet fellow students, both American and internationals.
arrival_comments: It was kind of fun (depends a lot on your orientation leaders) but also too expensive and a lot of the information was actually unnecessary.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I loved my time at UCB!
registration_process: I don't remember so it must have been very easy.
registration_help: The international student office is always there to help if you need it. UCB generally has a lot of student resources.
registration_success: Successful, although I didn't get a music class I wanted. Be prepared to change your schedule last minute and be patient. At UCB you can drop classes until the third week of the semester, so sometimes spots in classes that are initially full open up at the start of the semester.
registration_advice: Go with the flow, find information on CalCentral and ask for help from international student office or fellow students if you need it.
academics_comments: I loved my time at UCB!
course_level: It was an appropriate level, I think. Not necessarily higher academic level than at KU, but there is so much to choose from and it's much easier to mix and match courses at UCB than at KU.
teaching_comparison: There are maybe less lecture and lab hours (especially if you're a Science student at KU) but more small assignments, so you have to stay on top of those. The grades are usually based on many different aspects (e.g., attendance, homework, midterm, final exam), so don't expect to get good grades if you only prioritize the final exam (which you can get away with at KU).
courses_enrolled: International Environmental Economics (ENVECON C132) CLIMATE JUSTICE (ENERES C160) Philosophy of Science (PHILOS 128) Foundations of Data Science (DATA C8)
recommended_courses: If you want to get an introduction to python, do one of the introductory data science or computer science courses at UCB, they're all generally really good and well-structured. All my courses were good except ENVECON 162, which was bad not because of the material but because of the professor.
unexpected_costs: Just be prepared for 'the land of the fee'. Remember, sales taxes are never included on the price tag but added when you pay.
cost_comparison: GBO was unexpectedly expensive.
activities_available: ALL KINDS OF CLUBS: sports, music, politics, magazines, radio, film, major-specific, gender, origami, outdoor, ethnic groups, furry club, (academic) sororities and fraternities, food clubs, you name it.
activities_recommended: Do what you like, there's something for everyone. I love singing, so I joined an a capella group, where I made my best friends at UCB.
weekend_recommendations: See the redwoods in Marin, go on trips (you can rent free kayaks at the marina, for example).
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy. Never got used to the water tasting like chlorine though.
socializing_tips: JOIN A CLUB or live in a co op or both, ideally.
cultural_challenges: The substance culture (ketamine, cocaine, mdma, alcohol, vapes, weed, etc.). People in Berkeley are not heavy drinkers like in Denmark but rather use a lot of other different types of substances. However, most Berkeley students are very open to talk about substances and are generally more vocal about consent than in Denmark.
culture_appreciated: The openness and focus on inclusivity (especially in the co ops)
top3_advice: 1) live in the co ops 2) join a club 3) apply for funding (legater)
other_useful_info: I've said it all already
most_rewarding: Making friends!
greatest_challenge: Getting funding, until I got it.
other_comments: Nope.

crucial_aspects: 1. Location: I love the Bay Area and the fact that the campus is just 40 minutes away from San Francisco. 2. Academics: I had heard many good things about the professors at Berkeley.
info_ease: Pretty straight forward. Just read the emails and you will be guided through orientation easily.
arrival_assistance: No assistance needed.
arrival_comments: The orientation (Golden Bear Orientation, GBO) had both positive and negative aspects. Positive: You are put into a random group with other exchange and transfer students (transfer students are students that change university half way through their undergraduate studies), so you get to meet many new people. This is one of your best chances to make american friends. Negative: Many of the activities were boring and I skipped 2/4 days of the orientation, as did most other students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You do it online through Calcentral.
registration_help: There were advisors that could help you.
registration_success: I got all except 1 class. Some are pretty difficult to get into because exchange students can only register some time after the actual students at Berkeley.
registration_advice: Be prepared and ready at the deadline so you can get as many courses as possible.
course_level: I took high level undergraduate courses, which is from 100-199. I think every BA exchange student at UCPH should have an easy time following these courses.
teaching_comparison: More interactive - so better in my opinion.
courses_enrolled: MCELLBI 149 - The Human Genome (3 units) INTEGBI 134L - Practical Genomics (4 units) NUSCTX 110 - Toxicology - Last time this course was taught. (4 units) MCELLBI 198 - DeCal Neuroscience 101 (2 units)
recommended_courses: Can highly recommend Practical Genomics for students in Life Sciences. Professor Peter Sudmant is an awesome teacher. At least go read the description of the course. If you want something easy, take DeCal courses. They are taught by other undergraduate (bachelor) students and are ungraded. Note that you can first sign up for the courses a couple of weeks before the semester starts. It is really easy to get recommendations from your professors if you want - literally just email them and ask. Many of them will give you recommendations even though you are not active in classes.
unexpected_costs: Sim cards is surprisingly expensive.
cost_comparison: It's pretty expensive to eat out at restaurants. You should give about 18% in tip if you are eating at a restaurant (but 0% if you are ordering take away). You also have to tip in a lot of other instances (e.g. at bars), so look it up so you don't tip too much.
activities_available: I mostly went to frat parties, college football and basketball games. You can buy a season pass to all home football and basketball games for 125$.
activities_recommended: I especially recommend going to the Berkeley vs Stanford football game.
weekend_recommendations: Yosemite Roadtrip on highway 1 to LA (although the city of LA sucks, the drive on highway 1 is amazing) Go see redwood forrests Enjoy SF, it's an amazing city - although there are many homeless people smoking crack downtown.
culture_adjustment: Easy.
socializing_tips: Live with Americans roommates by renting a room or live in a co-op (not many americans in the International house, obviously). Talk to as many during the orientation (GBO mentioned above). The transfer students are americans that are transferring to Berkeley and thus they also don't know anyone. Just talk to random people - americans are very friendly and forward.
cultural_challenges: called my professors by their first name in the start.
culture_appreciated: The very forward american attitude makes it easy to talk to people. Also the students of Berkeley are very diverse, so you learn a lot about other cultures.
top3_advice: 1. Make the most of your academic experience. Go to office hours and talk to the professors. 2. Go on trips. Even if you have a lot to do, you can go on day trips to SF or go hiking just north of Golden Gate. 3. Look for accommodation and stipends early.
other_useful_info: Be good at applying for stipends. I got all my cost covered.
most_rewarding: Being apart of another culture.
greatest_challenge: There was a lot to think about in the start: Socialising, academics, practical information, housing, etc.
other_comments: There are some staff from Copenhagen that you can ask questions about the exchange stay, but they are pretty useless and can't answer many questions. So be ready to do some research of how to get visa, housing etc.

crucial_aspects: Surfing and meeting new people.
overall_comments: The surfing community on campus is very cool and welcoming. The people taught me to surf. We even planned surf trips up and down the coast (even going to Mexico).
info_ease: Upon arrival the campus was very organized for incoming students. Even applying for courses was easy.
arrival_assistance: They have a student service for exchange students that helped us. They even offered free SIM cards and a good discount on a cheap monthly plan.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: The surfing community on campus is very cool and welcoming. The people taught me to surf. We even planned surf trips up and down the coast (even going to Mexico).
registration_process: Pretty cool they had an add-and-drop period going into the semester where you could go to a couple of extra courses to see if you found them interesting and a couple of weeks in you could drop those you did not want to attend.
registration_help: It was a pretty simple process. If you had trouble you could contact the administration but also go directly to the professors.
registration_success: I think I got all but one course.
registration_advice: Make sure to have some electives as it makes it easier and you are able to pick some fun courses and try to find some friends you can register with.
academics_comments: The surfing community on campus is very cool and welcoming. The people taught me to surf. We even planned surf trips up and down the coast (even going to Mexico).
course_level: Around the same academic level as in Copenhagen (maybe even a bit lower) but with an insane inflation in the grades. People were sad with getting a B.
teaching_comparison: They implemented and stuck to streaming and recording the lectures. Way better! The students also had more influence on the lectures and syllabus.
courses_enrolled: Game Theory Economic Development Economics of the Environment
recommended_courses: All of them but the game theory was really good
unexpected_costs: Everything was just more expensive than expected.
cost_comparison: Everything more expensive.
activities_available: They had literally everything.
activities_recommended: I joined the surf club. Highly recommended.
weekend_recommendations: Drive up and down the coast. Go to Mexico and eat tacos, Drive up the coast on highway 101 and see the small surf villages of Encinitas etc. We also did road trips to Grand Canyon and Yosemite.
culture_adjustment: It was okay but the food was a big change.
socializing_tips: Join the social and athletic clubs and just speak to people in your classes and where you live.
cultural_challenges: Transportation and food.
culture_appreciated: Surfing and welcoming.
top3_advice: Appreciate the ocean, the weather and don't be afraid to say yes.
other_useful_info: Go surfing.
most_rewarding: The surfing and the people.
greatest_challenge: The money

crucial_aspects: I would like to be better at English, why the destination being an English speaking country was important. Furthermore, I choose California as my destination due to its unique cultural features and the possibility to go exploring nature in and around the West Coast.
info_ease: Relatively easy. However, the visa application can sometimes be a little bit troublesome and there is in general a lot of information to process, why it can feel a little overwhelming at times.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance other than pre-approval of new courses.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You registered for courses at the beginning of each quarter and you then had a couple of weeks to make your final decision. Some courses were really packed, why you could not always get what you wanted.
registration_help: I did not get any help. I asked some fellow students.
registration_success: I missed a couple on the first quarter, which created some trouble.
registration_advice: be flexible and have some alternatives ready in case you do not get your first pick.
course_level: It was relatively easy. Some courses were relatively hard to understand 100%, but it was still easy to get a high grade.
teaching_comparison: I liked it, because the classes are smaller and the professor knows you.
courses_enrolled: Economics of Education, Monetary Economics, Topics in Macroeconomics, Behavioral Economics, Industrial organization and firm strategy, and Economics of Modern Israel.
recommended_courses: Behavioral economics because its a fun subject. Also, the professor in Monetary economics is really good.
unexpected_costs: Transportation and living expenses were a bigger cost than expected
cost_comparison: None.
activities_available: Almost all kinds of sports; basketball, soccer, football, swimming, gym, etc.
activities_recommended: None.
weekend_recommendations: The nature on the west coast and the beaches in California.
culture_adjustment: Easy enough.
socializing_tips: Just make contact. They are interested in getting to know you as well.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: Their openness.
top3_advice: 1) Be aware of the high living expenses 2) make clear if you want to stay inside or outside of campus 3) the academic level is not the highest.
other_useful_info: Campus is not especially social compared to other institutions in California.
most_rewarding: The cultural experiences.
greatest_challenge: Living closely together with seven people who I had never met before.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to either a warm place or a "known" place, preferably somewhere I could experience the "college culture".
info_ease: Pretty hard, the university was not great at telling us when and what was happening. There was a lot of fear mongering into making sure we did all the mandatory stuff, but everything else was not really talked about.
arrival_assistance: A two day introduction which was mostly a tour around campus and them telling us to do mandatory stuff. Didnt really meet the other internationals.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You had to register yourself and there was a one or two week grace period.
registration_help: Nothing, i got help from other students. The UCD website is a mess.
registration_success: Somewhat. Unfortunately a lot of the classes i wanted were not online in the quarters i was abroard.
registration_advice: Be ready to take courses you didnt exactly intend on getting.
course_level: mostly 0-99 and 100-199 level courses
teaching_comparison: Much more hands on and the examination is very different.
courses_enrolled: Electrical engeneering, Intro to AI, Intro to ML, Chemical engineering and beginners philosophy
recommended_courses: Intro to ML and AI
unexpected_costs: Davis requires a bike. Also a bunch of trips everywhere
cost_comparison: Housing + food is crazy expensive
activities_available: A lot of different ones, didnt really try them though
activities_recommended: The ARC is very nice. Also go hiking to Yosemite and Lake Tahoe
weekend_recommendations: SF, Yosemite, Lake Tahoe, LA, Las Vegas in that order
culture_adjustment: Not very different from Denmark, so pretty easy
socializing_tips: It's not really possible. You spend almost all your time with the other internationals.
cultural_challenges: It feels like the US and especially Cali is very divided, so sometimes people got offended.
culture_appreciated: People are usually very friendly and forthcoming.
top3_advice: Get housing early, Get a big, Socialize Socialize Socialize
other_useful_info: Aknowledge that UCD is not recognized as a tier 1 university and just have fun
most_rewarding: Meeting the other internationals that i now have contact with being back home
greatest_challenge: Having a girlfriend back home. It was very hard.

crucial_aspects: UCSD is the third highest ranked university in the US in Biological Sciences, which is my field. The possibility for me to dive further into immunological and neurological diseases was a huge motivation for me. Aside from the academic opportunities I was drawn by the surroundings in San Diego (e.g., climate) and the ability to socialize through my hobby (volleyball).
info_ease: UCSD uses a bunch of different platforms that weren't that easy to navigate through. Course selection was fairly easy, but especially housing information was difficult.
arrival_assistance: Introduction from Resident Advisors in the International House.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Webportal where students had time slots to register for courses. First time slot to register one course, second time slot to register a second course and afterwards everybody could register for their remaining course credits. As an international student I had to apply for pre-approval for all courses as I didn't take the required courses for the upper level courses I took. For some courses the pre-approval was pending for a long time. The course catalogue available didn't reflect the courses offered in each quarter.
registration_help: Online video tutorial and contact information to faculties and professors.
registration_success: For the most part I got the courses I wanted, but I didn't get the courses I had planned from home, as not all courses were offered in every quarter.
registration_advice: Apply for pre-approval as early as possible and do it for all courses you even consider a little bit. Be prepared to register for different courses than you expected, as not all courses are offered in every quarter.
course_level: As I didn't take the required courses for my upper level courses at my host institution, I had to adapt to the course material in the beginning of the courses. Some of my courses overlapped quite a bit with my previous courses, and some didn't at all. For these I had to work harder to keep up, but throughout the course I did well.
teaching_comparison: At UCSD all courses had written exams with primarily short answers and multiple choice questions. This made it easier to study for exams than at UCPH, but in my opinion this allowed for memorization rather than understanding. All my courses had attendance, assignments and midterms throughout the course that contributed to the final grade. This forced me to be more active throughout the course than is necessary at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Human Physiology I + II Immunology Neuroanatomy and Physiology Diseases of the Nervous System Neurostress and Mental Disorders
recommended_courses: Neurostress and Mental Disorders: forced me to think more about how to structure scientific experiments in neurobiology labs. Diseases of the Nervous System: introduction to 15 of the most relevant diseases of the nervous system. Immunology: a great go-through of the entire immunological system and how this related to the nervous system and patophysiology.
unexpected_costs: Fees to acquire a visa - around 5000 DKK. Fee to pay rent (from Danish bank account) - around 3% (= 300 DKK per month).
cost_comparison: Rent and groceries were especially more expensive than I expected.
activities_available: Sports clubs, all sorts of clubs and fraternities were available for students. The associations were present throughout the quarter on the main square of campus.
activities_recommended: Commit to a sports club - this makes for great socializing with Americans (primarily) that you will stick together with throughout the quarter. I played at the Club Volleyball Team and got a lot of friendships through that - a group I had social events with and that I traveled to different other universities in California with.
weekend_recommendations: As much as possible. For me nature sights was most unique and worth of watching.
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy in an academic sense. I felt that most students were younger and more immature than college students in Denmark, which showed in their habits.
socializing_tips: Find a club so it's the same group of people you keep seeing.
cultural_challenges: Adjusting to the different course structure, where you have to make a bigger effort throughout the whole course.
culture_appreciated: Rallying behind the university's students (e.g., sports teams).
top3_advice: Commit to a club so you develop relationships instead of only fleeting interactions. Experience the culture and surroundings of the university, but know that the academics is the reason to go away. No matter how you end up living, know that Americans and other nationalities live completely different than Danes - even though you think it "should" be a Western civilized country.
other_useful_info: Most things will be more expensive than you imagine. Get as much information beforehand as possible, but know that you'll be surprised by a bunch of additional fees.

crucial_aspects: It was decisive for my choice of destination that it had to be outside Europe as I wanted to experience a completely different culture and challenge myself. In addition, I chose California because of the good range of sociology courses and, of course, because of the good weather and vibes.
overall_comments: I had a fantastic exchange stay with a lot of cool experiences both in terms of study, social and unique experiences. There are really good opportunities to try some exciting courses within many different areas of interest. I found that it was a different way of studying with less homework and more small take home exams that you don't have to be nervous about. It gave room to enjoy the time outside the lectures.
info_ease: There were some good information meetings about what to do before departure. However, there were many time-consuming processes, so I would recommend that you start applying for a visa etc. as early as possible. In addition, it is a good idea to talk to others who are going on an exchange or have been, if you are in doubt about something. Upon arrival, I recommend being accompanied by other exchange students and finding the office associated with exchange students on campus so you know where to go if you have questions.
arrival_assistance: I was accompanied by five other Danes who were going on exchange at the same university. We had all been given a room in the international house on campus where there were resident assistants who you could ask for advice. Otherwise, a lot of information and experiences were exchanged with the other international students.
arrival_comments: There were a lot of new things to get used to and a lot of information at once, but I didn't experience any problems with not getting enough information.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I had a fantastic exchange stay with a lot of cool experiences both in terms of study, social and unique experiences. There are really good opportunities to try some exciting courses within many different areas of interest. I found that it was a different way of studying with less homework and more small take home exams that you don't have to be nervous about. It gave room to enjoy the time outside the lectures.
registration_process: I found the most important information at reciprocity.uceap.universityofcalifornia.edu. It is well described there what must be done upon arrival. I recommend attending KU's information meetings as this is where the most important information and deadlines are presented.
registration_help: Both contact with the exchange supervisor and emails to the University of California were useful for clarifying questions.
registration_success: Unfortunately, not all the courses I had hoped to attend were offered in the two quarters I was on exchange. Therefore, I had to find some alternatives, but it was not difficult to find other exciting courses. However, I had to be a little creative with which courses to choose.
registration_advice: The most important thing is to start early so that you have time to clarify questions that arise along the way. It is a good idea to apply for courses as soon as you have the opportunity to get a place before they are all taken. In addition, it is a good idea to reserve an appointment at the embassy early to get a student visa in time.
academics_comments: I had a fantastic exchange stay with a lot of cool experiences both in terms of study, social and unique experiences. There are really good opportunities to try some exciting courses within many different areas of interest. I found that it was a different way of studying with less homework and more small take home exams that you don't have to be nervous about. It gave room to enjoy the time outside the lectures.
course_level: I think the level was not as high as in Denmark, so it wasn't difficult to keep up. However, I still thought there were interesting courses.
teaching_comparison: There were both midterms and exams, which meant that you had tests approximately every two months. However, these tests were not that difficult as the subjects in question had just been dealt with in the lessons. I mainly had lectures in large lecture rooms and not so much group teaching in smaller groups.
courses_enrolled: I was away for 1 semester corresponding to 2 quarters in California. In the first quarter I had the courses: Crime and Society, Predicting the Future and Genetics and Society. In the second quarter I had the courses: Climate and Civilization and Humans are Cultural Animals
recommended_courses: I loved the course Crime and Society because it is within my primary area of interest, the professor was phenomenal and the themes and guest lectures were really exciting. Predicting the Future was also a really exciting and different course about how we try to predict the future in different ways, from computer algorithms to Tarot cards. Genetics and Society was also a very interesting course on the social effects of the “genetic revolution”: eugenics, genetic discrimination, and stratification.
unexpected_costs: I bought a car with three other students. It was an old car so there were some unforeseen costs associated with it. Also traveling around California is expensive but so worth it!
cost_comparison: Housing was way more expensive than I had thought. Fitness on campus, transportation by bus and train was free for students. Food was more expensive than I expected.
activities_available: There were many good events to take part in. In addition, there were multiple sports matches which were nice to go to.
activities_recommended: There were many events in international house which were fun to participate in. It is especially nice to participate in many activities at the beginning to get to know people.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend going around the city and seeing the different areas, going to the beach and to other big cities and national parks in California.
culture_adjustment: There were some things that were very different from Denmark, but you get used to that quickly. There was nothing that was really challenging. I experienced that it can be difficult to get a close relationship with the Americans.
socializing_tips: They are generally very open and welcoming, so it is easy to get to talk to new people. However, I did not get to create long-term relationships with Americans as I was mostly with exchange students.
cultural_challenges: There were not really any cultural differences that I found challenging.
culture_appreciated: The culture and food was very inspired by the Mexican since it was close to the border. In addition, there was a lot of diversity, which was exciting and, of course, good weather and happy people.
top3_advice: Spend as much time as possible socializing, experiencing all the amazing places in California and try surfing.
other_useful_info: Check if the Duolingo language tests are still accepted at UC San Diego. It is much cheaper and easier than the alternatives. Seek a waiver for the expensive health insurance offered by the university. I can recommend ISO International Student Health Insurance which costs half as much.
most_rewarding: All the experiences I had along the way. It is so rewarding and at the same time you get to challenge yourself in a really cool way.
greatest_challenge: That you had to deal with things yourself. You are so far away from home and you have to cope with the challenges you encounter and that makes you really strong and independent.
other_comments: Just do it. You will not regret it!!!

academics_comments: It was amazing! Only drawback is that the estimated costs of living in San Diego provided by the University of California were grossly underestimated
course_level: I took uppper devision undergraduate courses for 4th year students.
teaching_comparison: You are expected to learn mainly from lectures - not from textbooks or notes. This means that taking good notes is essential because you often cannot find the course content in writing. Also theoretical exercises at UCSD were different. At UCPH, the students work on problems at the exercises, and the TA helps the students individually and answers questions. At UCSD, the TA goes through the problems on the board as if he/she were giving a lecture.
courses_enrolled: Biological Physics Spacecraft Guidance and Navigation Aerodynamics Physical Basis of Global Warming
recommended_courses: Biological Physics. An amazing course with an exciting final project structured as a regular research project. Interesting topic as well, and excellent professor! Aerodynamics. A very good introduction to a topic that we do not teach at UCPH. Very useful for geoscientific and industrial applications. Very good lecture notes Quantum Physics III. Just a well-structured quantum physics course. Unlike many other courses, the professor in this course provides a set of extensive notes covering all of the course contents. This is good because topics in advanced quantum mechanics are not covered coherently in a single textbook, so the notes are very good for future reference as well.
unexpected_costs: Mandatory health insurance even though my travel insurance includes health insurance
cost_comparison: Food and housing were more expensive than expected. Public transportation was free for students. Eating out (restaurants etc) and material things was cheaper than expected. Sports facilities were free for students
activities_available: I could never list all clubs, activities and societies available to students at UCSD. If you can imagine something, UCSD for sure has it. I personally took part in: - Sunday Supper for all the international students - Surfing events - Dia de los Muertos - 5km exercise run - Member of the local rowing club, and took part in several competitions - Surfing
activities_recommended: Surfing. You have to surf with a location like that! Try some of the sport/athletic offerings from the university Sunday supper is great Try making a big deal out of the American an South American activities like Dia de los Muertos, St. Patrick's Day, Thanksgiving, etc
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips to some of the surrounding national paks and monuments Go to the city Chill and enjoy the beach Use the sports facilities
culture_adjustment: It was relatively easy - Americans are very welcoming
socializing_tips: Remember to try to meet local students. You can do this by joinging clubs, sports teams, etc. Many exchange students make the mistake of only hanging out with other exchange students
cultural_challenges: I was surprised with the division and racism in the American society. That fact that people primarily prefer to hang out with others from their own ethnic group created a division that I had never imagined. In the beginning, I found it challenging to adjust to the fact that there are certain things that I as a white man cannot do or say without appearing racist. This includes things that would be non-controversial in Denmark.
culture_appreciated: The general openness of Americans is great. They are welcoming, and they appreciate new ideas and thoughts. It is generally a very positive environment.
top3_advice: You're in for a good time! Remember to get the most out of your stay by socializing with the local students and community and exploring the area and the city. Academics are important, but remember to leave some time to have fun! Be prepared for your stay to become more expensive than planned

crucial_aspects: Exploring a new country and university life, as well as academic opportunities
info_ease: Fairly easy. The university had an extensive arrival and orientation schedule.
arrival_assistance: E-mails from the university and info sessions
arrival_comments: Everything besides selecting courses was pretty easy
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Before you leave, you have to be ready online at a certain time, and after you arrive the classes you selected online are not guaranteed. You have to "try out" classes, swop them around and e-mail professors a lot. You make your own schedule, so it can be difficult to make the time tables of different classes fit into one schedule.
registration_help: Student administration in terms of your overall schedule. But when it comes to the individual courses (e.g. if there's one you really want), just email the professors directly.
registration_success: Pretty successful. You just have to be prepared to not get enrolled in every single course you expected/wanted. Be open to take a course in something different, simply because it's the only way to make your time schedule fit. Also Bcourses are nice and fun if you just need an extra ECTS-point or two.
registration_advice: Don't wait until last minute. Email professors and tell them how much you want to be in their course (even if it seems strange). Be open to try other courses than you expected.
course_level: Hard but not too hard. More niche-oriented than at UCPH which is super nice and fun. Amazing and super intelligent professors.
teaching_comparison: Berkeley demands a lot more reading (every day for every class) than what I'm used to. Also you "have" to speak up in classes. Generally there's a lot more active learning, tasks, assignments, presentations quizzes etc. (all counts in your final grade) than at UCPH, where we're more responsible for our own learning.
courses_enrolled: Documentary Style, Theorizing the American Film Musical, Japanese Auteurs and Beginner's Guide to the Universe
recommended_courses: I had the pleasure of being taught by Dolores McElroy in Theorizing the American Film Musical. I would recommend any course she teaches, as she is the best professor I've ever had.
unexpected_costs: A lot of fees in regards to visa, applications, orientation etc.
cost_comparison: Phone plans are a lot more expensive than in Denmark. Also housing is incredibly expensive, but that was expected. Public transportation to and from campus was free with a Clipper Card though.
activities_available: Basically anything you can think of.
activities_recommended: I was part of Berkeleys Cinematic Arts Club which was nice. People are sweet and the films they make are ambitious.
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips! Yosemite, Los Angeles etc. There's a lot of nice cities and hiking opportunites nearby.
culture_adjustment: Not bad. The US is of course culturally different from Denmark, but not too different. I got along with pople fairly easily.
socializing_tips: Join a club, show up for events, talk to people in your classes. I made some of my best friends in classes, which was unexpected.
cultural_challenges: Specifically at Berkeley, students are very ambitious and study a lot. But you kind of get used to it.
culture_appreciated: The openness of the people. Everyone is super sweet and welcoming. Americans make friends very fast :)
top3_advice: 1. Be prepared to spend A LOT on housing and life in general (and to have a roommate, like in your bedroom). 2. Ask students at UCPH who has previously been on exchange at Berkeley for help. 3. Make the most of your time culturally and socially - the culture of studying all the time can make you think you have to do that as well, but you'll do fine.
other_useful_info: Look up Facebook-pages for housing and join the UCPH California group too. Ask the people in there for help.
most_rewarding: Meeting new friends (both international and locals) and experiencing such a high level of education.
greatest_challenge: Financial problems (I managed because of scholarships - be sure to apply!)

crucial_aspects: For mig var det vigtigste at opleve en anderledes kultur og udvikle mig personligt. Det akademiske aspekt spillede selvfølgelig også en rolle, som STEM studerende, især datalogi delen af min uddannelse (Datalogi-Økonomi), er Californien (Silicon Valley) et af de mest førende steder. For mig personligt går jeg meget op i skateboarding, hvor Californien er oprindelsesstedet for dette og jeg har derfor altid drømt om at komme derover. Jeg kom ind i Santa Cruz, som også var min topprioritet, fordi jeg havde hørt om deres surfer/skater miljø og ydermere er det et fantastisk smukt sted, især campus, som ligger oppe i Santa Cruz mountains og rangerer som et af de smukkeste campusser på jorden.
overall_comments: Personligt fik jeg indfriede alt hvad jeg kunne ønske mig. Jeg kunne eventuelt godt have været mere ambitiøs på det akademiske område, men det kommer også med en pris. Det vil sige mindre tid til at udforske områderne og prøve ting af, men jeg kunne nok godt have sigtet lidt højere. Jeg havde også en frygt for at kurserne ville være for svære, det er samtidigt meget svært at sammenligne de kurser de tilbyder derover med de kurser man har taget på KU, men her har jeg fået den indsigt at kurser der minder om kurserne på KU er på stort set samme niveau, når det kommer til datalogi kurser er der en mere praktisk tilgang til tingene, men generelt er der ikke noget at være bange for med hensyn til sværhedsgraden, så længe kursusbeskrivelsen ser ud til at være overskuelig for dig.
info_ease: Der bliver holdt orienteringsmøder med de ansatte, som har med internationale studerende at gøre, samt møder med de personer som har med det specifikke college du bliver tilknyttet (Hvis du bor på campus), så du får rigeligt med information og samtidigt information omkring hvor du kan finde mere information. Det burde ikke være noget problem, de ting du skal vide får du at vide og yderligere information kan du spørge dig til.
arrival_assistance: Jeg boede på campus, så som det første skal man flytte ind. Jeg flyttede ind i Fall quarter, dette er starten af det akademiske år, så alle studerende der bor på campus flytter ind. Dvs. det er en stor indflytningsdag hvor man blot følger instruktioner for at få nøgler osv. Nogen dage senere er der møder for de internationale studerende hvor man får alt den fornødne information. Deres kurser bruger Canvas som online portal, så dette er ligesom på KU og her kan du finde den nødvendige information i forhold til kursus start osv.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Personligt fik jeg indfriede alt hvad jeg kunne ønske mig. Jeg kunne eventuelt godt have været mere ambitiøs på det akademiske område, men det kommer også med en pris. Det vil sige mindre tid til at udforske områderne og prøve ting af, men jeg kunne nok godt have sigtet lidt højere. Jeg havde også en frygt for at kurserne ville være for svære, det er samtidigt meget svært at sammenligne de kurser de tilbyder derover med de kurser man har taget på KU, men her har jeg fået den indsigt at kurser der minder om kurserne på KU er på stort set samme niveau, når det kommer til datalogi kurser er der en mere praktisk tilgang til tingene, men generelt er der ikke noget at være bange for med hensyn til sværhedsgraden, så længe kursusbeskrivelsen ser ud til at være overskuelig for dig.
registration_process: registreringsprocessen for kurser foregår før du kommer til campus/USA online, det var lidt rodet at finde rundt i her. Det kan være svært at vurdere niveauet på de forskellige kurser. Du har også på forhånd fået forhåndsgodkendt nogle kurser som du godt kunne tænke dig at tage udfra deres kursuskatalog, men det kan meget nemt være at disse kurser ikke længere bliver tilbudt eller kurserne du godt kunne tænke dig foregår i et andet quarter eller kurserne allerede er fuldt optaget, så vær klar på at kigge efter alternative muligheder. KU er heldigvis fleksible i forhold til at ændring af kurser, da det er klart at man ikke nødvendigvis kan tage de kurser man havde kigget på forinden. Det foregår sådan at man logger ind på deres online portal og finder de kurser du gerne vil tage. Du ligger disse kurser i en indkøbsvogn og så kan du "enroll" i disse kurser. Det lyder nemt nok, men forinden skal du have overført merit for de kurser du har taget i Danmark, dette skulle vist nok gerne ske automatisk, men for mit vedkommende var det ikke sket, her anbefaler jeg du kontakter en vejleder på det fakultet du er tilknyttet (dette er den major du har valgt, for mig var det Economics) og så kan de overføre meritten for dig. Hvis du ikke har de "prerequisites" det kræver at tage et kursus, som er meget muligt, da vi ikke nødvendigvis har præcis de samme kurser, som de har i USA, så kan det kræve en godkendelseskode for at kunne enroll i et kursus. Her fandt jeg senere hen ud af at den bedste måde at få disse godkendelseskoder er at kontakte ISSS (International Student & Scholar Services) og så er de meget hjælpsomme med at få det til at lykkedes ellers skal du kontakte den konkrete professor som tilbyder kurset og så er det ham der bestemmer om du kan tage det eller ej.
registration_help: De enkelte fakulteter har vejledere, som holdte zoom-møder hvor man kan komme ind og få svar på stort set alt ting, disse er meget nyttige, hvis du føler dig fortvivlet. Yderligere kan du kontakte ISSS (International Student & Scholar Services), som er et organ for internationale studerende og de kan også hjælpe dig.
registration_success: Ikke særlig succesfuld, jeg var kun i stand til at tage et enkelt af de kurser, som jeg på forhånd havde tænkt mig at tage. Jeg tror dog hvis jeg havde vidst at jeg kunne få godkendelseskoder fra ISSS at jeg kunne have taget et par stykker mere af de kurser, som jeg gerne ville tage, men de fleste af kurserne var simpelhent ikke mulige at tage.
registration_advice: Vær klar på at det ikke er muligt at tage de kurser du gerne vil have. På Santa Cruz vil jeg anbefale at kontakte ISSS, hvis der er et kursus du gerne vil tage, men det kræver en godkendelseskode for at enroll
academics_comments: Personligt fik jeg indfriede alt hvad jeg kunne ønske mig. Jeg kunne eventuelt godt have været mere ambitiøs på det akademiske område, men det kommer også med en pris. Det vil sige mindre tid til at udforske områderne og prøve ting af, men jeg kunne nok godt have sigtet lidt højere. Jeg havde også en frygt for at kurserne ville være for svære, det er samtidigt meget svært at sammenligne de kurser de tilbyder derover med de kurser man har taget på KU, men her har jeg fået den indsigt at kurser der minder om kurserne på KU er på stort set samme niveau, når det kommer til datalogi kurser er der en mere praktisk tilgang til tingene, men generelt er der ikke noget at være bange for med hensyn til sværhedsgraden, så længe kursusbeskrivelsen ser ud til at være overskuelig for dig.
course_level: Jeg tog nok kurser der var lidt under det niveau jeg burde at tage, da jeg var lidt nervøs for at få for svære kurser og ikke have tid til at opleve ting udenfor studiet, men min generelle opfattelse er at niveauet på kurserne er meget ens med de kurser der er på KU. Man skal være klar over deres system er lidt anderledes, for eksempel har man som regel 3 kurser per quarter (et quarter er 10 uger), her har man som regel to major kurser (det er kurser der har med din uddannelsesretning at gøre - for mig Datalogi & Økonomi) og så et enkelt GE (General Education) dette er et fag som kan være hvad som helst, de er som regel mærket som GE fag og er generelt nemmere fag. Ydermere er der nogen major fag, er kurser som de der tager den major skal tage, disse er som regel lidt tungere, og så er der electives, som er fag de specifikke majors kan vælge at tage, disse er som regel lidt mere specifikke og måske lidt nemmere.
teaching_comparison: Undervisningen foregår generelt på nogenlunde samme måde som i København, man har forelæsninger og øvelsestimer. Jeg vil dog sige øvelsestimerne er som regel mere en gennemgang af de øvelser der er blevet givet i løbet af en uge og ikke timer hvor man sidder og laver øvelser.
courses_enrolled: Advanced Quantitative Methods - 2022 Fall Quarter Introduction to Networking and the Internet - 2022 Fall Quarter Introduction to Probability Theory - 2022 Fall Quarter Environmental Economics - 2023 Winter Quarter Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms - 2023 Winter Quarter Popular Music in the United States - 2023 Winter Quarter
recommended_courses: Som en GE kan jeg anbefale at tage Introduction to Networking and the Internet, hvis du gerne vil have en introduktion til hvordan internettet og networking helt generelt fungere på et meget praktisk niveau, professoren Rick Graziani er super dygtigt og gør forelæsningerne meget spændende. Dette er et kursus, som alle kan tage uanset hvilken major du er på. Hvis du er datalogi studerende kan jeg anbefale Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms, dette er måske lidt for nemt når du allerede har taget Data Strukturer & Algoritmer på KU, da mange af emnerne overlapper, men hvis du godt kunne tænke dig en mere praktisk tilgang til emnet er dette et super kursus, som består af 90% programmering. Dette kursus giver dig lyst til at udforske meget mere indenfor programmering og lærer dig også at programmere i C++.
unexpected_costs: Hvis du bor på campus, så kan du ikke bo der henover winter break, sådan cirka 3 uger, dette er en god mulighed for at rejse rundt i USA, men man skal lige være klar over det, da det hurtigt bliver dyrt at rejse rundt i Amerika, især hvis ikke du kan bo hos venner eller familie noget af tiden. Der var også 200 dollars omkostninger til sådan noget international visitors fee + international exchange orientation, som ikke var blevet gjort helt klart, så det kom lidt som en overraskelse.
cost_comparison: Jeg rejste til USA lige i det inflationen virkelig tog fart, så det var lidt svært for mig at vurdere hvor dyre ting var ift. Danmark, men generelt var madvarer væsentligt dyrere end jeg havde forestillet mig, mindst lige så dyrt som her hjemme og nogen ting væsentligt dyrere.
activities_available: Der er masser af muligheder for at være aktiv indenfor både kulturelle klubber og sports klubber. I starten af Fall quarter er der et stort event hvor alle skolens klubber stiller op, hvor du kan melde dig ind. Mange af sports klubberne er mere seriøse hvor der kan være f.eks. optagelsesprøver osv., men der er også bogklubber, religiøse klubber osv. Jeg vil anbefale at holde øje med UCSC athletics and recreation, som tilbyder alverdens sports muligheder for alle. Her kan du tilmelde dig begynder surfer hold, begynder sejle hold, enkelt stående hiking ture osv. Hvis du søger på UCSC athletics and recreation kan du finde alle deres tilbud. Du skal være opmærksom på at mange af deres hold bliver fyldt meget hurtigt, dvs. du skal sidde klar den dag tilbuddene bliver udbudt, da f.eks. surfer holdet bliver fyldt stort set med det samme.
activities_recommended: Det kommer selvfølgelig an på hvad du godt kan lide at lave, men jeg vil anbefale at du tager ud på noget hiking om det er igennem UCSC athletics and recreation eller om det er ture du selv planlægger, så er dette en super god måde at opleve noget Californiens helt unikke natur. Der er mange national parks, som alle er meget fantastiske. Der er endda "Henry Cowell State Park" lige nord for campus, som har 2000 år gamle redwood trees, dette er helt klart et besøg værd, da det også ligger så tæt på.
weekend_recommendations: Som sagt er der en masse national parks (Yosemite, Death Valley, Pinnacles, Grand Canyon etc.) som jeg vil anbefale at besøge. Generelt er naturen helt fantastisk. Derudover synes man burde udforske hele Bay Area, hvor du kan opleve Silicon Valley, bruge tid i San Jose, San Francisco osv. Ydermere kan du tage en Greyhound bus (6-7 timer - du kan køre om natten og være der om morgen) eller flyve til Los Angeles, hvis du er interesseret i at se Hollywood, The Getty Museum, Venice Beach osv.. Ift. Los Angeles så er det værd at vide, at det tager ret lang tid at komme rundt i byen hvis du ikke har en bil, så hvis du ikke har så meget tid og gerne vil se en masse kan det anbefales at leje en bil.
culture_adjustment: Jeg boede på ILC (International Living Center) hvor det var meget nemt at tilpasse sig, da der var en masse ligesindede udveksling studerende, dette var en af de helt store fordele ved at bo lige netop der. Du skal blot være åben overfor en masse nye indtryk og bare tage det ind. Overordnet vil langt de fleste dig det godt og er meget venlige.
cultural_challenges: Vi er jo i Danmark relativt amerikaniseret, så mange ting er ikke så overraskende, men bilkulturen er en helt anden, man kører simpelthen i bil alle steder og så er alkohols kulturen lidt mindre aggressiv end i Danmark, men der er masser af natteliv, hvis det er det du er interesseret i.
culture_appreciated: Amerikanerne er generelt mere åbne overfor fremmede, dvs. du let kan falde i snak med en tilfældig amerikaner på en bustur eller hvor du nu møder dem. Dette syntes jeg var meget fedt.
top3_advice: 1) Der kan være mange stress faktorer i hele forløbet op til at rejse derover, her skal du bare række ud efter hjælp og ikke være nervøs for at spørge vejledere osv., da alle meget gerne vil hjælpe og du er helt sikkert ikke den eneste der er i tvivl om diverse ting. 2) Når du er kommet til Santa Cruz skal du bare nyde det så meget som muligt og forsøg at tvinge dig selv til at opleve/lave ting så ofte som muligt, fordi du falder hurtigt ind i rutine med skole osv. og lige pludseligt er dit udvekslingsophold overstået 3) Meld dig ind i nogen af de utallige klubber, der er programmerings klubber, bog klubber, sports klubber osv. Du kan også melde dig ind i PE (Physical Education) klasser hvis du godt kunne tænke dig at lære f.eks. tennis eller kampsport - dette foregår det samme sted hvor du tilmelder dig kurser (MyUCSC)
other_useful_info: Californien og i særdeleshed Santa Cruz er et af de dyreste steder at bo i verden, så det skal man lige være forberedt på. Det betyder ikke at man ikke sagtens kan leve derover på et budget og stadig have en fantastisk oplevelse.
most_rewarding: For mig som Datalogi-Økonomi studerende var det meget givende ift. datalogien, man mærker virkeligt at man er tæt på Silicon Valley, at der er meget konkurrence når det kommer til Computer Science, som er det langt størstedelen af de studerende læser. Der er en særlig fornemmelse af at det er derover den ypperste udvikling foregår.
greatest_challenge: Finde kurser som jeg havde mulighed for at tage, som ville være akademisk udfordrerne men også give tid til at lave alt muligt andet end at studere - Jeg endte med at tage kurser, som var lidt for nemme, men ikke desto mindre har de givet mig noget lærerigt alle sammen.
