course_level: I took one 3rd year sociology course, which had amazing lectures, great curriculum and interesting class discussions. The course papers were interesting, inspiring and quite challenging. I took one 2nd year contemporary health issues course, which has interesting lectures and curriculum, but very poorly facilitated group discussions. The course assignments were also interesting and challenging. The third course was at the nursing faculty. This course was a bit trivial in the beginning, fx. a whole lecture on the fight or flight mechanism as one would explain it to 1st year high schoolers. But the course got better and more interesting after a couple of weeks. The course assignments were not very difficult, but still demanded a bit of work ofc.
teaching_comparison: Same divide between lectures and classes. But the classes were mainly discussions rather than teacher presentation or group work. Also, some classes were taught by professors, not student instructors, which was very inspiring.
courses_enrolled: Contemporary Feminist Issues Contemporary Issues in Health and Wellbeing Mental Health: Life Sciences and Nursing Care 2
recommended_courses: Contemporary Feminist Issues - This was extremely interesting and very well managed! Give it a go definitely :) Contemporary Issues in Health and Wellbeing. I liked this course, although it was not as great managed and facilitated.
unexpected_costs: The above amounts are by no means precise. I did try to monitor my spending once during my exchange, but honestly I didn't go to Scotland to spend my time budgetting. I went out a lot to enjoy the city and the nature, so I spent quite a bit on food and weekend trips. But I had to fill in the above, so you can disregard most of it, although my rent really was 3250 kr, which is very cheap for Edinburgh! Also the travel insurance amount is correct.
cost_comparison: I didn't expect to pay for hiking association membership and gym membership, but I am glad I did. Also weekend trips were a tad more expensive than anticipated. But honestly, don't go with a group trip, did it once, and not worth it. Just find a group of friends, rent a car or catch a train, book an airbnb and enjoy the highlands or borderlands :) Food was not too expensive.
activities_available: Everything you can imagine. I did hiking, choir, lindy hop, tango, blues and ceilidh dancing. There is also a student gym (Pleasance) with equipment and classes, but you pay for your membership. They also have an indoor swimming pool.
activities_recommended: Hiking, choir, lindy hop, tango, blues and ceilidh dancing.
weekend_recommendations: Go to the highlands (west)! Inverness, Loch Ness, Loch Lomond, Cairngorms national park, Isle of skye etc. Also, heard the borderlands are nice and the cities in the east. Didn't have time to visit those.
culture_adjustment: Extremely easy.
socializing_tips: Join the societies from UoE and Erasmus Student Network (ESN). Both have lots of events in the intro week. There are not that many Scottish ppl at UoE, as this university is more expensive than the other two universities in the city. So UoE is mainly full of English ppl and exchange/foreign students.
cultural_challenges: None. Just that the traffic was on the other side of the street.
culture_appreciated: The ceilidh! Scottish folk dancing - so much fun and very easy to learn. Most of the societies have a ceilidh [Kayli] dance it once or twice a year :D
top3_advice: 1. Have a LOT of preapprovals ready from KU. This means you have to look in the exchange student course finder on the UoE website a good while before the exchange starts. 2. Start looking for accommodation early and try to see if you know someone who knows someone in Edinburgh, who might be able to help. 3. Join the university societies and enjoy your time with all the other lovely students! This is also a great place to meet people with whom you can travel Scotland and visit the highlands :D
other_useful_info: Get a railcard if you expect to travel a lot in Scotland. Glasgow is only 50 min away by express train and worth a visit! And many more cities :)
most_rewarding: All the dancing communities I became a part of :D I meet amazing students from all over the world and became good friends with many of them. They will be with me even if the exchange is over :) Also going to the highlands with my group of exchange student friends!
greatest_challenge: Having time to do all the stuff I wanted to do. Seeing the highlands, Edinburgh, other cities, studying, working, being a climate activist. Pretty packed 4 months heh..
other_comments: Enjoy if you go! I had a great time, despite initial stress with course registration and a crammed exam period. You'll meet great people from all over the world and have lots of amazing ppl to visit later :D

crucial_aspects: Good university within the culture and art department with a large variety of different courses. But in general I choose University of Edinburgh because I wanted to explore and live in Scotland because of my Scottish herritage.
info_ease: I found the CAHSS office within University of Edinburgh quite helpful, and they were quick answering questions and doubts upon arrival.
arrival_assistance: I only received assistance through mail correspondance with CAHSS.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: There was a thorough video guide on University of Edinburghs website showing you have to register at the university. Still, it was a bit confusing. A lot of steps were necessary in order to fully matriculate, having to be done on different platforms.
registration_help: Video guide and CAHSS office per mail.
registration_success: I was quite lucky and in the end ended up with courses that I had wished for.
registration_advice: Don't worry! You will be registered one way or another.
course_level: I had two third year level courses and one first year level courses. The difference was quite big, but it was out of interest that I have chosen all of them. In general I think the level of courses at University of Edinburgh is quite high and the teachers are talented.
teaching_comparison: I found the style of teaching and the expectations of the written papers more conservative and restricted as opposed to UCPH. It was more a question of saying or writing what you know instead of analysing and discussing what might be.
courses_enrolled: Sinners, Saints and Seers: Scottish, Irish and English Art from 600-900 Sustainable Sculpture Practice Films on Film
recommended_courses: I would recommend going for courses at ECA (Edinburgh College of Art). It is a beautiful building with lots of interesting courses within art, art history and architecture.
unexpected_costs: All the events and trips the university arrange! Some are good, but it's not for free.
cost_comparison: Going out having a beer or a coffee were more expensive than expected.
activities_available: University of Edinburgh has a lot of societies, whether you are into theatre, sports, music, beer, pole dancing etc. It does cost something to be a member of these societies which is also an extra cost one should have in mind.
activities_recommended: Going to The Jazz bar, where the Edinburgh Jazz Society (students) play (and it's free!). In general go to pubs and hear folk music.
weekend_recommendations: The Highlands, Glasgow, Loch Lomond.
culture_adjustment: I found it quite easy. I'm part Scottish, so for me it was like coming home, even though I haven't lived in Scotland before.
socializing_tips: Go outside academic/university activities! Most of the students are international students like yourself, so if one wants to talk to local people, go to Leith or somewhere outside campus.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: The open-hearted, open-minded, straight forward, kind and funny Scottish people!
top3_advice: Very few actual Scotts attend University of Edinburgh (so bear this in mind, you will meet mostly international students), the country and culture is absolutely beautiful, stay away from Buckfast.
other_useful_info: Edinburgh is a good size for being on exchange for only half a year, and the nature surrounding it makes a magical city.
most_rewarding: To get to live in Scotland.
greatest_challenge: Meeting new people and having the energy to do all the stuff you wanted to do. Going on exchange can be quite challenging in itself; a new educational system to learn, new expectations, new courses, new city and new surroundings.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to an English-speaking country to improve my English but also to a place with a great university and lots of history and culture.
info_ease: The university is pretty good at taking care of their arriving international students. Most things are compiled on MyEd/Learn (their intranet) for easy access, and if not, the visiting student office are super helpful, and you also get a personal tutor assigned that can assist you with questions.
arrival_assistance: I got most information from emails before my stay and from flyers/information posted on the LEARN site. Also I just emailed the visiting student office or asked someone else - lots of people are in the same boat, so you can almost always find someone who can help you.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You pick the courses you want and prioritise them 1-5 and they give you what they can. I got all of my first 3 priorities but changed one of them later.
registration_help: The visiting student office and your personal tutor can assist you with courses and course changes.
registration_success: I got all of the classes I wanted, even the 4th level course and a high-demand course I didn't expect to get into.
registration_advice: It's fairly straight forward, but be sure to check out the courses outside your field, there are many interesting ones. I didn't take any courses in my own field during my stay abroad.
course_level: As mentioned above, most subject-specific courses (such as sociology, political science, literature of the ones I wanted to do) require you to have completed 2 years of studies in that subject to have the fundamentals down. This makes it difficult to take courses on your level. I found most of my courses very easy since they were 1st year courses which was both nice since I could focus on other things but also a shame since I wasn't challenged too much academically.
teaching_comparison: There are almost no teaching hours which I generally don't like. For each course, there was 1 hour lecture, 1 hour tutorial (in class session, usually 5-10 people with a tutor/instructor). The tutorials were the most interesting since you could discuss with your classmates and to practical excersices, but it is not a lot of teaching and a lot of self-study.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Queer Studies History of the Scandinavian Novel Sociology 1B: The sociological imagination: Private troubles, public problems
recommended_courses: I surprisingly found my sociology course very interesting. It taught me different ways to approach a lot of things.
unexpected_costs: Travelling is insanely expensive in Scotland. We did many day tours out into the country (e.g. we went to Glasgow, Stirling, St. Andrews, Inverness and more), but trains are VERY expensive (I can recommend getting a Railcard from trainline.co.uk if you expect to travel a lot by train, it is really worth it), busses as well. I wish I had saved up more money for the longer trips like Isle of Skye, Glencoe etc. where I didn't get to go simply because it was too expensive and very hard when you don't have a car.
cost_comparison: Coffee is much cheaper in Edinburgh..... pricing for everything else is more or less the same. Going out, however, is very expensive. They don't have bodegas the same way that we do; a pint costs what a pint costs, the cheapest ones are usually 4 pounds with student discounts. So if you like to go out, be prepared to spend some money.
activities_available: There are societies for almost everything, and it is amazing. During the welcome week, most societies have intro classes, meetings and other free stuff you can attend to see exactly what society fits you. I really do encourage you to go check them out, it is very worth it!
activities_recommended: Join a society! Even if it's a weird one. Try something new. I got into pole dancing while I was away, and it was so much fun and a great way to both exercise and meet new people.
weekend_recommendations: Travel! Go see Scotland. Edinburgh is amazing in itself, but you quickly realise it is very small. Plan ahead for some day trips - there are plenty of places where you can get with coach or train in an hour or two from Edinburgh, and it's a great way to spend your weekend.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy. There are so many international people in Edinburgh as well so you can find a bit of everything.
socializing_tips: Go to classes, talk to people you work with, ask them to have a cup of coffee or study together. It's really awkward, yes, but they are most likely not from here as well. Edinburgh has many international students.
cultural_challenges: None that I can think of.
culture_appreciated: The accents <3
top3_advice: Plan ahead for your weekends/holidays and take advantage of the fact that you have so much beautiful nature close, don't stress too hard about university (it's in a different language, so everything feels different and harder probably), and please please please don't do like me. Bring a fricking raincoat.
other_useful_info: I really do recommend getting housing with likeminded flatmates. My flatmates were all 10-15 years older than me, and although they were lovely, and we had some great times, we didn't have much in common in terms of how we spent our time.
most_rewarding: Travelling around Scotland.
greatest_challenge: Meeting people since Scotland was still in hard lockdown when I arrived.

crucial_aspects: I was important to me that I new the language. I also wanted it to be a place with a good study environment and outgoing people. Lastly, I've just always really wanted to live in the UK for a bit, and this seemed like a great opportunity.
info_ease: I found it to be a bit difficult, but it all worked out.
arrival_assistance: I used my flatmates, who were also on exchange like me. And also, the university provided a personal tutor, who I had a zoom call with in the beginning to make sure I knew everything. She was available to me throughout my entire stay.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I had a mandatory meeting with a personal tutor, and had to go and be signed in on campus. There probably was more stuff, but I've forgotten what it was.
registration_help: A personal tutor could help me.
registration_success: Unfortunately, a lot of the courses I wanted when I applied for the first time wasn't available, because I had to postpone the stay one semester due to covid. But I still got some interesting courses, and it was very easy to apply and change within the first few weeks.
registration_advice: Talk to your personal tutor if you need help.
course_level: I thought the academic level of the courses was a bit lower than in Denmark. However, the tutorials offered more opportunity to have discussions within the class.
teaching_comparison: It was very different. The lectures and tutorials were only 50 minutes. In UCPH, I'm used to 2-3 hours of lectures and tutorials. However, the tutorial classes in Edinburgh were with less people, which made it more okay to want something explained again or have good discussions with fellow students and teachers. In Edinburgh, there were also tutorial tasks you had to do, which was very involving compared to only reading articles as preparation for class.
courses_enrolled: Topics in Popular Music Scottish Studies 1A: Conceptualising Scotland What's Up Doc? Introducing Animation Studies
recommended_courses: Topics in Popular Music
unexpected_costs: Don't know.
cost_comparison: The apartment was a bit expensive compared to Denmark, when thinking of the condition the apartment was in. Pints and drinks were less expensive than expected. Also, museums were mostly all free.
activities_available: There is a lot of societies, so it is easy to be social and find stuff to do.
activities_recommended: I joined the film society with film screenings and quiz nights. There was also a whisky society, which I joined a couple of times. A lot of my friends were also a part of the hillwalking society.
weekend_recommendations: 1) Glasgow is a very nice city to visit, and not that far away. 2) Edinburgh Filmhouse and Cameo are two very cute cinemas showing great films. Also Dominion Cinema in Morningside is a cinema designed like first class on a plane. There are stewardesses and you sit in couches. 3) King's Theatre and Edinburgh Playhouse are great places to see shows and concerts 4) Go to a rugby game 5) The Golf Tavern is a great pub with a view over Arthur's Seat 6) Arthur's Seat 7) Panda and Sons is a cosy (and expensive) cocktail bar that looks like a barbershop on the outside, but behind a bookshelf is a cosy bar with great drinks 8) Stockbridge is a cute part of the city with vintage shops and cafes and a great viewpoint 9) Pub Quizzes (Queen's Arms is a nice pub in new town, and The Southsider has a long hard quiz close to the university) 10) Morningside has a lot of cute places to have a coffee
culture_adjustment: Very easy, because we could speak the language.
socializing_tips: Join societies.
cultural_challenges: Can't think of any.
culture_appreciated: They are very open and good at small-talking. The culture around the pub and pub quizzes is really nice.
top3_advice: 1) If you don't know anyone, then join a society, because you don't necessarily spend a lot of time with people from your class 2) The academic level in humanities is a bit lower than in Denmark 3) Edinburgh is a great mix of culture and nature, and with a lot of people from around the world. Most of the Scots are in Glasgow.
other_useful_info: Don't think so.
most_rewarding: The friendships and the fact that there was so many things to do there.
greatest_challenge: Don't know.

crucial_aspects: An English speaking country A well-rated university A city I would like to explore and become familiar with its culture
overall_comments: If you get the chance to go abroad with Erasmus+ do it!!
info_ease: It was quite easy. The University of Edinburgh sent all necessary information to my email with guidance upon arrival, on how to change courses, get registered with a personal tutor and how to attend events etc.
arrival_assistance: CAHSS helped with changing my courses
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: If you get the chance to go abroad with Erasmus+ do it!!
registration_process: Arriving in Edinburgh you would have to pick up your student card at the main library, fill out upon arrival and proof of attendance form which CAHHS needs to sign, and then have a short meeting with your personal tutor. Everything is explained through emails you will receive from Edinburgh University and else, CAHHS is the one's to contact.
registration_help: CAHHS is really helpful!
registration_success: I got 2 out of three of the classes I wanted after CAHHS helped me switch.
registration_advice: Read thoroughly through the emails, and if you have any questions, contact CAHHS or your personal tutor.
academics_comments: If you get the chance to go abroad with Erasmus+ do it!!
course_level: I took one first-year undergraduate class in History which was all pre-recorded lectures and the level of the Cours was quite fitting. I had two other third-year courses in ECA and the level of both courses was also fitting, sometimes challenging, but I learned a lot and the classes were very well structured.
teaching_comparison: At the University of Edinburgh, the classes I had in person were based on a lecture from the teacher, but they also incorporated discussions and exercises to change it up. I had one tutorial class per week in my History course which was really helpful to discuss and get to understand the content of the week's lectures.
courses_enrolled: Sinner, Saint and Seers: Scottish, Irish and English Art from 600-900. Orientalism and Visual Culture. The History of Edinburgh: From Din Eydin to Festival City.
recommended_courses: If you would like to get to know something about the history of Edinburgh, the History course is a good starting point as you get to know the city, buildings, and areas through the lectures and then apply the knowledge when walking around. The two art courses are really good. I knew about Orientalism before coming to Edinburgh, but my teacher used different artists and aspects which helped broaden my knowledge and interest in the matter. Sinner, Saints, and Seers is a cool course if you like looking at illuminated manuscripts, medieval treasures, and stone crosses and have an interest for Christian, Roman and Celtic religion, traditions and how it all influence the insular world!
unexpected_costs: As you are on an exchange, you would (and should) explore the country you are living in. Eventbrite and the University of Edinburgh made a lot of trips to the highlands etc which is really worth going on!!
cost_comparison: All busses in Edinburgh costs 1,8GBP which is quite good. Coffee is a bit less expensive than in Copenhagen.
activities_available: Everything!! There's a society for everything, a sports club, and activities - just search for it!
activities_recommended: Sign up for the Pleasance Gym - its a standard gym, but you can also do classes, play squash and go bouldering or go to the swimming pool! Play tennis in the Meadows, a court is 10GBP and you can be as many people as you like.
weekend_recommendations: Go to the highlands - you can't be in Scotland without..! Go to the markets - Saturday in Grassmarket and Leith, Sunday in Stockbridge. Explore the city by foot - everything in Edinburgh is in walking distance and the best way to get around is by walking! Go to the beach in Portobello or North Berwick. Climb Arthurs Seat and the Craigs. Go second-hand shopping - Edinburgh has the best ones!!! Take a day-hiking trip to the Pentlands - the bus leaves from Edinburgh. Eat your way through the city and get some pints!
culture_adjustment: Very easy as the culture is close to the Danish
socializing_tips: Go to as many events at the beginning of the year as you can through the university, go to a pup or get yourself a local coffee bar and talk to the people working!
cultural_challenges: Scotland is known for their pup culture, be prepared to drink a lot of pints and get "heavy steaming"!
culture_appreciated: The kindness and easy going vibe.
top3_advice: 1. It all seems like too much effort at the beginning with paperwork and getting to know the university and people, but it is all worth it in the end! 2. CAHHS and your personal tutor is your best friend - use them if you have any questions! 3. Check the format of your course exam before applying for it - some courses have a lot of course work and others a more end-exam based.
other_useful_info: Get to know the different campuses - Edinburgh University is huge and is spread all over the city!
most_rewarding: Learning about a new culture, meeting lovely people and exploring the country.
greatest_challenge: Finding a solid group of people to hang out with and adapting to writing in English.
other_comments: GO FOR IT!!

crucial_aspects: A culture I wanted to explore and access to nature. Because of Covid, I did not want to be at a destination very far away if the situation should change. I also wanted to improve my English skills.
info_ease: The receiving university did a good job informing me of everything I needed to know.
arrival_assistance: Everybody is assigned a personal tutor that you meet within the first weeks. I needed some help changing a course and that was solved quickly. I didn´t need more help during the semester, but it was nice to know who to reach out to if I needed help with anything.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I remember it as you send a request list, they check if you can take the courses, and send an answer with your courses. It was very easy. Just check the course requirements before requesting a course.
registration_help: The Visiting Student Office via email.
registration_success: I was only registered for courses that I wanted.
registration_advice: Check requirements. The course searching site is working fine and is easy to use.
course_level: The level of courses was appropriate.
teaching_comparison: The university has tutorial classes where you discuss topics from lectures in smaller groups, often with a Ph.D. student as a tutor. I liked this but unfortunately in my courses, not a lot of students showed up for these.
courses_enrolled: Dynamics of Language and Power, Linguistics and English Language 1B, Scottish Studies 1B: Creating Scotland
recommended_courses: I liked the Scottish Studies course because I was introduced to many different aspects of Scottish culture.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: I don't know.
activities_available: The university offers a lot. I joined the fitness center (which has many different classes and a lot of equipment), the futsal club (football), and the book club.
activities_recommended: Just try something, anything. They have so many different options and in the first weeks, many societies host socials where you just show up and see who they are and what they offer.
weekend_recommendations: Hikes. Take the bus to the Pentlands or even travel to the Highlands. Isle of Skye is also amazing. And go see lots of castles and ruins, there are quite a few around Edinburgh. Jupiter Artland was also fun. I went to the Lake District in England and to Pembrokeshire in Wales, and can definitely recommend both for hiking if you're looking for longer trips.
culture_adjustment: It was quite easy, but I think it's important to get yourself out there in the first weeks and meet some like-minded people to share experiences with.
socializing_tips: Join societies or clubs. Go to their socials at the beginning of the semester.
cultural_challenges: I don't really know.
culture_appreciated: People are friendly and down-to-earth. Good humor, mostly. It doesn't feel like a busy place, which was very nice.
top3_advice: Join something and meet people through something you like or just try something new. Be very social at the beginning of the semester and relax with good friends later :D Enjoy your city.
other_useful_info: Don't know.
most_rewarding: The people. And also, that I've proven to myself that I am able to travel somewhere alone and make it wotk there. That is something I'm definitely bringing with me.
greatest_challenge: Maybe, being exhausted from meeting so many different people, but that is also one of the best things :DD

crucial_aspects: I wanted to find university in an English-speaking country, with courses that matched my interests.
overall_comments: I would give a higher rating if it wasn't for the Covid restrictions on in-person teaching.
info_ease: Easy except for the fact that the abundance of information could make it difficult to find exactly what I was looking for.
arrival_assistance: I was sent some very helpful guides and reminders via email, and in any case, I knew that I could reach out to the visiting student office.
arrival_comments: I know that several welcome events took place during the first weeks, but I did not participate.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I would give a higher rating if it wasn't for the Covid restrictions on in-person teaching.
registration_process: There's a pretty straight-forward online survey, that guides you through dropping or adding courses.
registration_help: You can always email the visiting student office, it might just take a few days to get a response.
registration_success: I changed my courses a few times, because I was hoping for a spot to open up on a specific course that I wanted, which unfortunately didn't happen. In the end, I had to make a change at the very last minute, and had to choose a course that I didn't really want.
registration_advice: There's not a lot of spaces for exchange students on most courses, but I would recommend contacting the course organizers, as some will have a waiting list.
academics_comments: I would give a higher rating if it wasn't for the Covid restrictions on in-person teaching.
course_level: The courses I took happened to be intended for 1st or 2nd year students, which meant that they weren't too challenging - they weren't easy either, but I didn't feel out of depths.
teaching_comparison: Very similar - we had weekly online lectures, and would then discuss the material in small tutorial groups.
courses_enrolled: Understanding Gender in the Contemporary World Introduction to Social Anthropology Scottish Literature 2a
recommended_courses: There's a few courses on Scotland, and Scottish literature and culture, which are aimed specifically at exchange students - might be a good place to meet people as well.
unexpected_costs: I had to book a Covid test to take after arrival, which was 68 pounds.
cost_comparison: Cafes, coffee shops etc were cheaper than I expected, especially the ones around campus. I also saved some money by getting most of my course materials from the university library.
activities_available: There's hundreds of societies to choose from, there'll be something for anyone.
activities_recommended: I didn't actually join any, so I wouldn't know.
weekend_recommendations: If you get the chance to travel around Scotland, I recommend taking the train up to Inverness and going from there - there's plenty of bus tours available which take you around to see the most beautiful sights.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy, I don't think Scottish culture is all that different from Danish.
socializing_tips: I would think that societies are the best place to meet like-minded people.
cultural_challenges: Nothing except for how overly polite some people are, it almost made me uncomfortable.
culture_appreciated: Again, people are very polite, and most of time it's really nice.
top3_advice: 1. Use the campus! The library is a great place to study, and the student association has several amazing cafes, bars etc. 2. Reach out and connect with your teachers and lecturers - they're always really cool about it. 3. Don't just stay in the most central areas of the city. I recommend taking a walk around Stockbridge, Morningside or Leith.
other_useful_info: The university is really committed to ending period poverty, so you can get free period products anywhere on campus.
most_rewarding: I felt so so privileged to be taught at such a prestigious institution and it definitely boosted my confidence in my own academic capabilities that I was able to do well in my courses.
greatest_challenge: There's an overwhelming amount of information, deadlines and documents to keep track off, so you really need to stay organized and keep a detailed diary.

crucial_aspects: The courses available and being able to understand and speak the language of the destination.

unexpected_costs: Beer.

I would recommend to sign up for these things as quickly as possible, through the Student Association webpage, because lots of the events sell out fast. socializing_tips: Societies!
cultural_challenges: Can't think of any

registration_success: I første omgang fik jeg ingen af de fag, jeg havde ansøgt. Jeg blev ved med at søge fagene i de to uger, hvor der var eftertilmelding (de to første uger af semesteret) og på næstsidste dag i tilmeldingsperioden fik jeg så 1 af de fag jeg gerne ville have. Så jeg var ikke særligt succesfuld, men til sidst var jeg bare lykkelig for i det mindste at få et af mine ønsker.
registration_advice: Når der står at et kursus er 'high demand' på UoEs kursushjemmeside, så betyder det at der er utroligt få pladser. Først efter at jeg var kommet ind på universitet og skulle til at søge fag (i sommerferien) fandt jeg ud af at 'få pladser' faktisk betød at der var 1 plads til udvekslingsstuderende på det fag jeg gerne ville have. Og den plads var allerede blevet taget. Så man skal (desværre!!) være klar på at man ikke får alle de fag, man gerne vil. Og jeg vil også virkelig anbefale at være klar ved computeren, når kursustilmeldingen går i gang. Det er først til mølle og man kan sende så mange tilmeldinger, som man vil, så man skal bare sende løs fra starten af - så er man først i køen, hvis nogen springer fra. Fordi de tager fra bunken af ansøgninger løbende, så skal man altså blive ved og ved med at søge, for at ens ansøgning ligger i toppen af bunken, når der bliver en plads ledig på et kursus. Det er et forfærdeligt system.
academics_comments: Jeg var meget heldig med at møde nogle søde mennesker, som jeg blev venner med. Det betød virkelig meget for min tid i Edinburgh. Jeg havde også et fag, feministisk filosofi, som gjorde studie-delen virkelig god, fordi det var et rigtig spændende fag. Opholdet var dog ret kort (3 måneder) og det var meget intenst - både med skole, arbejde, familiebesøg og socialliv, så hvis jeg kunne ønske noget anderledes, ville det være at have bedre tid, både i hverdagen (ift studiemængden) og også opholdets længde, så jeg havde bedre tid til at opleve byen og bare være der.
course_level: To af mine fag var introduktionskurser til studier, som var nye for mig: Antropologi og arkitekturhistorie. Så der var niveauet 1. års / introduktionsniveau. Men der var stadig høje krav til afleveringer og læsning, vil jeg sige. Mit sidste fag var et 3. års filosofifag.
teaching_comparison: Undervisningsopbygningen lignede ret meget den på KU med en kombination af forelæsninger og seminarer på alle kurser. Seminarene var dog kun 50 minutter lange og i små hold, ca. 10-12 personer, og det fungerede virkelig godt. Jeg deltog meget mere mundtligt fordi holdene var mindre, og rummet derfor også blev tryggere at snakke i. Det var også rart med kortere tid, fordi det gjorde undervisningen meget fokuseret og man ikke gik derfra helt udkørt.
courses_enrolled: Architectural History 1A: Introduction to World Architecture Feminist Philosophy Introduction to Social Anthropology
recommended_courses: Feminist Philosophy var virkelig godt. Vores underviser Filipa Melo Lopes er ekstremt dygtig, både fagligt, formidlingsmæssigt og til at engagere sine studerende. Hvis det er muligt at få et fag med hende, så skal man gøre det!
unexpected_costs: Jeg havde slet ikke regnet med så dyr en husleje (£825 pr måned), og det var også kun muligt for mig at bo der fordi jeg havde sparet lidt op inden udveksling, og så fordi jeg fik Erasmus-stipendie oveni SU'en. Jeg takkede ja til det boligtilbud, dels fordi lejligheden var virkelig nice, med søde roomies som også var internationale studerende og med en central beliggenhed, men også fordi jeg var ret desperat efter at finde et sted at bo, og det var vigtigt for mig at have et rart hjem at trække mig tilbage til. Og det fik jeg virkelig. Men det var alt alt for dyrt for mig. Jeg brugte også penge på at rejse (både i Skotland men også til og fra DK et par gange), men det er selvfølgelig ikke en nødvendig udgift for alle.
cost_comparison: Priserne minder om de danske, vil jeg sige.
activities_available: Alt muligt. Fordi de studerende er ret spredt på uddannelsen (fordi hver enkelt vælger sine egne fag, frem for at følge et program med det samme hold i 2 år som på KU), så mødes man til gengæld i de forskellige societies. Og dem er der mange af, og de laver mange spændende arrangementer.
activities_recommended: Oplægsaftener og pubcrawls, fordi det både er spændende og hyggeligt.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på en vandretur - enten til Højlandet (man kan tage bus til Arrochar fx, det er nemt) eller til Pentland Hills, som ligger en kort bustur syd for byen. Der er også et Hiking society, som arrangerer ture. Tag til Glasgow - det er super billigt med bus (man kan være heldig at finde en afgang til så lidt som £1) og der kører busser mellem Glasgow og Edinburgh hele døgnet. Der er så mange dejlige ting at lave i Edinburgh - gode barer, butikker (fx Lighthouse boghandel), natur, mad. Jeg boede lige ved siden af Calton Hill, så der gik jeg ofte op - det er ret unikt at have sådan et udkigspunkt til rådighed altid, og det sted savner jeg. Så der kan jeg anbefale at sidde og kigge ud over byen.
culture_adjustment: Ret nemt, den britiske/skotske kultur er ikke så fjern fra den danske.
socializing_tips: De venner jeg fik, mødte jeg i introugen til arrangementer for Erasmusstuderende, så vi var stort set alle udvekslingsstuderende i min vennekreds. Så ingen af os var lokale, men jeg vil helt klart anbefale at tage til introarrangementer for at møde andre unge studerende.
cultural_challenges: Sprogbarrieren kan være udfordrende. Ikke fordi det er svært at tale og forstå engelsk, men det kan være frustrerende ikke at kunne udtrykke sig præcist som man gerne vil på et andet sprog. Det oplevede jeg nok mest med mine venner - at jeg ikke altid kunne vise min personlighed som jeg gerne ville, eller at jeg ikke kunne bruge præcist dét danske ord, som ville beskrive min følelse eller tanke bedst - det var nogle gange frustrerende.
culture_appreciated: Jeg synes det er en meget varm og velkommende by - folk vil gerne snakke, når man møder hinanden på en bar eller lignende. Meget mere åben tilgang end i Danmark.
top3_advice: Edinburgh er en virkelig dejlig by - tag derhen! Søg fag så snart de bliver tilgængelige, og bliv ved med at søge, hvis der er et fag du meget gerne vil have. Selvom Freshers Week kan være overvældende, så tag til nogle arrangementer der. Det var der jeg mødte mine venner og det er jeg så evigt taknemmelig for at jeg gjorde. Det er jo held om man lige møder nogen, men introugen er i hvert fald et rigtig godt sted at prøve.
other_useful_info: Niveauet på University of Edinburgh er højt, så man har travlt mens man er der, synes jeg. Men det er fedt, at det er så stort et universitet, der summer virkelig af liv og der er mange forskellige mennesker. Ift filosofi er universitetet mest rettet mod analytisk filosofi. Og så har de fag som feminisme, socialepistemologi og dekolonialisme, som jeg personligt synes er enormt spændende.
most_rewarding: Faget feministisk filosofi, mine venner, at være i byen og tage på ture ud af byen, få besøg af venner og familie, der var mange gode ting :)
greatest_challenge: At nå alt det, jeg gerne ville.
other_comments: Brug ESN - Erasmus Student Network. Det er en god måde at møde andre udvekslingsstuderende på og til at få hjælp til at falde på plads som udvekslingsstuderende.

crucial_aspects: I did not have any "crucial" aspects in choosing my destination. However I found it important that the courses I was going to attend were courses that I would actually enjoy. After reading about UoE's (many) interesting courses I just became more certain that UoE was the right choice.
overall_comments: I do believe that it is important to do some research about the accommodation opportunities in your exchange country when you are choosing a destination. My overall experience would have been a lot better if my accommodation, apartment (private leased), had been better. Coming from Copenhagen where a lot of the apartments are modern and renovated, I found it difficult to live in an apartment with mold, mouse and drafts. The apartment did not function as my "safe" space and a place were I could relax after a long day.
info_ease: Do your research from home and you will be fine. The UoE were very helpful in many ways! Great communication and they are doing their best in taking good care of their students.
arrival_assistance: I did not need any crucial assistance when I arrived. I was also lucky to have co-students from UCPH with me so we helped each other.
arrival_comments: I did not need any "important" assistance but I know that the UoE is very helpful if you need any help.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I do believe that it is important to do some research about the accommodation opportunities in your exchange country when you are choosing a destination. My overall experience would have been a lot better if my accommodation, apartment (private leased), had been better. Coming from Copenhagen where a lot of the apartments are modern and renovated, I found it difficult to live in an apartment with mold, mouse and drafts. The apartment did not function as my "safe" space and a place were I could relax after a long day.
registration_process: I had to send my boarding pass upon arriving to prove I were present at the host country.
registration_help: The CAHSS Visiting Student Office is very helpful if you need any help!
registration_success: Very successful as I was accepted for the courses I had applied for.
registration_advice: If you are in doubt just ask your host university - write an email, book an appointment. They are helpful and do only wish the best for their exchange students.

My overall experience would have been a lot better if my accommodation, apartment (private leased), had been better. Coming from Copenhagen where a lot of the apartments are modern and renovated, I found it difficult to live in an apartment with mold, mouse and drafts. The apartment did not function as my "safe" space and a place were I could relax after a long day.
course_level: The level was suitable for someone which mother tongue is not English. Challenging, but not too difficult.
teaching_comparison: Compared to UCPH the lectures were recorded 👌. I also had the opportunity to attend seminars to discuss texts and the lectures.
courses_enrolled: Social Anthropology 1B Anthropology Matters Evidence, Politics and Policy Data Literacy
recommended_courses: It depends on what you are interested in. Read the course catalogue as UoE has a lot of great courses!
unexpected_costs: I do not think I encountered any unexpected costs but it is important to have a saving in case you face any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: I think the food was a bit expensive compared to Denmark
activities_available: I know there were a lot of social activities available for students.
activities_recommended: I did not anticipate in any but I would recommend doing it if need a social group with same interests.
weekend_recommendations: Explore the city and the highlands.
culture_adjustment: Denmark is ahead in many aspects and I found the difficult that a lot of the way things are done in Scotland are done differently.
socializing_tips: Come to the seminars
cultural_challenges: I did not find any cultural differences to be challenging. The culture is different and that is an experience.
culture_appreciated: I appreciated how kind, helpful and open the scottish people are compared to people in Copenhagen.
top3_advice: 1. Do your research about the destination especially the housing (and of course the university)! 2. Have a saving so you can have fun in the weekends as the Erasmus grant will not get you far 🥴 3. Be prepared for better online opportunities
other_useful_info: Have fun!
most_rewarding: That what I thought I could not handle, I managed!
greatest_challenge: The personal challenges I have faced but in a good way. While the exchange may not have been the best, I have learned a lot and appreciate things in a completely different way now.
other_comments: DO IT! ❤️

crucial_aspects: At kunne tale sproget samt at opleve Storbritannien.
info_ease: Det var okay - men der var mange informationsmeddelelser, som var lidt svære at holde styr på.
arrival_assistance: Ingen.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: En lang række mails, skemaer og undersider på hjemmesider, der skulle udfyldes. Inden for psykologi var det svært at få plads på kurser. Fik man ikke plads, kunne man udfylde en formular og så få svar en uge senere på, om man kom ind på et andet kursus, eller om der var kommet en plads. Det var en enormt dårlig måde at gøre det på. Det var rent held, om man fik en plads, fordi de lige tjekkede ens ansøgning, når en anden var hoppet fra. Der var ikke ventelister eller lignende.
registration_help: Jeg synes, at registreringesprocessen var under al kritik. Ud over at være meget langstrakt og med utallige mails/skemaer og lignende var der meget lidt hjælp at hente fra udvekslingskontoret på UoE. De var meget søde, men var grundet corona hjemsendt UDEN TELEFONER. Hvordan det kan lade sig gøre er mig en gåde. Men det betød, at man kun kunne få fat i dem via mail, som de typisk svarede på omkring 10-14 dage senere. Jeg skulle have plads på et specifikt kursus og skrev frem og tilbage med dem i tre måneder. Hver gang fik jeg svar fra en ny person og der gik 1-2 uger mellem svar på mine mails. Efter tre måneder fandt de så ud af, at der vist alligevel var en venteliste, som jeg så blev skrevet på. Da jeg så - en uge før semesterstart - blev tildelt en personal tutor (en akademisk medarbejder, som man er tilknyttet - viste det sig, at min var leder af psykologiuddannelsen. Han kunne slet ikke forstå, at jeg ikke havde fået plads på kurset, da det er et førsteårskursus med flere hundrede pladser. Han foretog ét opkald, og så var jeg inde. Altså må udvekslingskontoret end ikke have forsøgt at ringe til det psykologiske institut for lige at høre ad. Summa summarum: man skal virkelig holde sig til og ikke tage et nej for et nej.
registration_success: Se ovenfor
registration_advice: Se ovenfor
course_level: Jeg må indrømme, at jeg var meget skuffet over undervisningen. Niveauet var egentlig højt, og underviserne akademisk dygtige, men de fleste ret dårlige til at lære fra sig. Jeg havde intet gruppearbejde og én holdtime á 50 minutter hver uge i hvert fag. På den tid kunne man intet nå. Samtidig turde folk ikke rigtig at sige noget, og vi havde ikke plenumdiskussioner, men mere bare spørgsmål-svar. Derfor udviklede de fleste holdtimer sig bare til mini-forelæsninger. I alt var der meget selvstudie.
teaching_comparison: Se ovenfor
courses_enrolled: Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience: Infancy, Psychology 1B, Human Resource Management 2
recommended_courses: På Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience: Infancy havde jeg klart de bedste undervisere. Uheldigvis var det online grundet corona, men Dr. Hugh Rabagliati formidlede virkelig godt. Dog var niveauet højt, og det tog en del kræfter at følge med i kurset.
unexpected_costs: Ikke rigtig noget.
cost_comparison: Ingen.
activities_available: Mange klubber inden for stort set alt.
activities_recommended: Kom til alle intro-arrangementer - også selvom du er selv og det er skræmmende. Alle er i samme båd, og man falder i snak med folk.
weekend_recommendations: Højlandet er fantastisk og Glasgow er helt sikkert en oplevelse værd. Et pro-tip er, at der er studierabat på Festival Theatre og King's Theatre i Edinburgh. Hvis du møder op i billetkontoret efter kl. 12:00, kan du få billet til en forestilling samme aften for 10 pund på nogle af de bedste pladser i teatret. Det er virkelig værd at se forestillinger, også selvom man ikke lige kender dem. Storbritannien har en rig underholdningskultur, og især musicals synes jeg, var meget underholdende.
culture_adjustment: Det var forholdsvist nemt. Skotterne er enormt søde og meget høflige.
socializing_tips: Som ovenfor: kom til intro-arrangementerne.
cultural_challenges: Bureaukrati lever i bedste velgående i Storbritannien. Man skal gå kommandovejen og det kan tage laaaang tid. Et eksempel: jeg ville sørge for, at min kæreste fik et bibliotekskort, så hun kunne komme med ind. Først skulle jeg ansøge på nettet, så fik hun en mail med ting, hun skulle udfylde. Så fik vi at vide, at vi skulle møde op i receptionen. De fortalte os så, at nu skulle hun gå ind og booke en tid til at få kortet udleveret. Det gjorde vi så, og kunne 5 timer senere gå hen til en anden skranke og hente kortet (som i øvrigt ligger lige ved siden af receptionen - og i øvrigt var det lørdag, så der var nærmest ingen gæster).
culture_appreciated: Skotternes gæstfrihed og høflighed er fantastisk.
top3_advice: Hæng i og vær ikke bange for at ringe/skrive og presse på, hvis du skal bruge et svar på noget. Vær ikke bange for at møde op til ting - alle er i samme båd og vil gerne lære andre at kende. Kom ud af Edinburgh og besøg resten af Skotland/Storbritannien.
other_useful_info: Intet andet.
most_rewarding: At opleve den britiske kultur og lære at være selv. Det, jeg tager med hjem, er, at man godt kan tage til en koncert alene eller i det hele taget klare sig uden, at have sine venner/kæreste/familie med sig hele tiden.
greatest_challenge: Samtidig var den største udfordring også at være alene. Der er dage, hvor der ikke sker noget, og man sidder helt selv. Der skal man huske, at det hele nok skal gå og at det er okay at ringe hjem.

crucial_aspects: The fact that the general language is English was important to me since it makes it much easier to get to know the locals at the university, chat with people and be integrated in your local communities. I have heard a lot about Edinburgh from friends and family, and they all recommended the city as well as the university. I wanted to experience some of the beautiful nature in the highlands surrounding the city, and it was important to me that it was easily accessible. Furthermore, previous exchange students had had good experiences at the university, and I was looking forward to study at a high ranking institution like The University of Edinburgh.
info_ease: The university was very good at keeping one updated by mail, and they were quick to answer emails sent to them. Just make sure to check your email often, then you'll be guided through all the practical things you'll need to organize before going. However, one piece of information which was difficult to find, was an overview of all the courses exchange students were able to participate in. But if you look up http://www.drps.ed.ac.uk, which can be difficult to find through the official website, the details about the course are provided.
arrival_assistance: You are assigned with a personal academic tutor, who is an academic member of staff who will help you, if you have any academic questions throughout the semester. The university arranged several small events, where international students could meet each other, such as picnics and parties.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Once I knew the webiste with all the courses the university provided, I found the enrollement pretty easy. Although the univerisity first knows what courses they provide in the first learning week, so you're only certain of what courses you are enrolled in when you arrive. I had contact with the Visiting Student Office by mail before i knew what courses I would apply for, but they were very helpful and quick to answer.
registration_help: As mentioned above the Visiting Student Office was there to help me, and by mailing back and forth during a period, they helped me to apply for the courses. I also attended to an online session about the application process provided by the university, where a lot of beneficial information was provided and I had the opportunity the live chat with the staff.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted to apply for. The main problem for me was that the possibility to find courses which could replace the one's I had at my home university was limited.
registration_advice: Don't be afraid to ask for help and email the visiting student office - the staff are there to help you. I was a bit hesitant to contact them at first, but you shouldn't be. And go to the information session, where you'll get an impression of what the city and university is like.
course_level: The level was lower, since the courses generally covered more subjects than in Copenhagen, which meant that I didn't go as much into depth with each subject as I'm used to.
teaching_comparison: The teaching was less teacher-led and more dependent on the students and their discussion.
courses_enrolled: - Philosophy of Science 1 - Contemporary Issues in Health and Wellbeing - Psychological Perspectives on Health and Care These courses covered Clinical Psychology and Scientific Design and PhiloSophy of Science on Copenhagen University.
recommended_courses: Philosophy of Science 1 is great if you are into philosophy or want to know more about it. It was by far the best structured course I had, and it covered a lot of interesting topics.
unexpected_costs: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs but make sure to have money for eating out and going out, and for travelling if you want to go on road trips in the Highlands or similar things.
cost_comparison: Groceries were much cheaper than I expected, while the prices at restaurants were the same.
activities_available: The student societies provide a huge amount of activities for students at the university. I was part of a hillwalking society, mountaineering society and a trail runner society, but there are societies for almost everything you can imagine. Most of the societies are described on the university's website.
activities_recommended: Join the hillwalking club if you want to go to walk some hills in the Highlands. It's great fun, you'll see some stunning nature and meet other students.
weekend_recommendations: Some of the places I went to and was happy to see were Glasgow, Isle of Skye, Glencoe, Inverness and Loch Lomond. There is lots of very beautiful nature once you go a bit north!
culture_adjustment: They can be very hard to understand at first, since their dialect is so strong. But you will get used to it pretty quickly. In general, I didn't find it hard to adjust to the local culture, and even though there are many differences between Scotland and Denmark, it is overall easy to chat with them and get to know them.
socializing_tips: I think one of the best ways to get to know them, is by joining some student societies. Many of them are both having weekly events and arranging trips on the weekends.
cultural_challenges: Understanding their language!
culture_appreciated: The folk music at the pubs. I recommend going to some of the small pubs where people are a bit older, since they often have a lot of great music and a nice atmosphere. But the Scots are also very talkative and open, so it is much easier to chat with them compared to the Danes.
top3_advice: 1. Join a student society 2. Bring warm clothes, rainwear and hiking boots. The Scottish weather is hard to predict. 3. The application process can be long and difficult, but in the end, it will be worth it!
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Joining the student societies, exploring the Highlands and Scottish nature, meeting international students from both Europe and the rest of the world, to be in a beautiful and historically rich city, to be integrated into the local communities.
greatest_challenge: The exam period was tough with many exams following each other and with little time to do them. But all of them were finished before Christmas, so you have a long holiday in the winter if you go abroad in the autumn.

crucial_aspects: I chose Edinburgh because I had family who previously attended the University, some of whom were still living in the city. They had very positive things to say about the academic environment and city alike.
overall_comments: 10 socially, but maybe a 6 academically. That's why I chose 8.
info_ease: The University website is very accessible and covers pretty much every aspect of moving to the city.
arrival_assistance: None.
arrival_comments: 5, because I was satisfied with whatever information was available on the website. I didn't need any assistance upon arrival, but I had the impression that it was available through student services if need be.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: 10 socially, but maybe a 6 academically. That's why I chose 8.
registration_process: The online portal for course registration is arguably even more intuitive than the one UCPH uses. So you'll find no problem navigating it.
registration_help: There was no need for help, but the academic support seems well-equipped to handle any questions etc.
registration_success: I was eventually succesful. However, there was some initial confusion as to whether I could participate in postgraduate courses and be assessed for my work in them. Once that cleared up, I could choose the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: Don't worry too much about it.
academics_comments: 10 socially, but maybe a 6 academically. That's why I chose 8.
course_level: Evaluating the level of the courses is difficult for a number of reasons. 1) You (or at least I did) spend more time studying, because you don't have a part-time job on the side. Overall, this means you're better prepared than you are in Denmark. At the same time, this is also expected from the lecturers, who expect more from you in terms of reflections before class. 2) The academic level is probably somewhat lower (if you visit at the end of your master's, like I did), but the exam format is quite different from what you're used to (essay-style short format). 3) Unless you're a native speaker, the language takes some time getting used to. Debating academic papers in English is just different than what I was used to (even though I had taken English courses in DK).
teaching_comparison: In some cases, it was more engaging than what I have experienced in Denmark. Here, we could spend 20 minutes discussing a single paper or chapter of a book where everyone had a chance to contribute and reflect on the paper. I liked that.
courses_enrolled: 1. Computational Text Analysis 2. International Political Economy 3. Comparative Analysis of Social and Public Policy
recommended_courses: If you're into R, Natural Language Processing, sentiment analysis, machine learning etc., I would definitely recommend Computational Text Analysis. On the contrary, don't choose Comparative Analysis of Social and Public Policy - it does not cover anything you do not know from the pol.sci. bachelor's at KU.
unexpected_costs: The main unexpected cost was probably a 5500 DKK deposit for the room in the apartment.
cost_comparison: Going out can be quite expensive if you're not solely frequenting student bars. Beers are probably 55 DKK and most venues take an entrance fee of approx 8-10 GBP.
activities_available: All kinds.
activities_recommended: Hiking is probably the biggest one. Go experience nature that we do not have in Denmark!
weekend_recommendations: Travel to the country-side. The highlands are absolutely phenomenal, and the opportunities for traveling on a budget are quite good. It is a truly stunning country nature-wise. Also, see Glasgow - it's very different but also well worth a visit.
culture_adjustment: Very easy as there's almost no language barrier and people are very friendly.
socializing_tips: Not really, people are very welcoming and warm. You'll find no problem fitting in, I'm sure.
cultural_challenges: Half eight means 8.30 and not 7.30, like it would in Danish. Remember that.
culture_appreciated: Scots are more open and less reserved than Danes. That is a very charming trait and you'll find yourself striking up conversations with strangers all the time.
top3_advice: 1. Enjoy it, because time flies past. 2. Remember good shoes - you'll be walking around A LOT. 3. Bring a rain jacket.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: The people. It is a massive gift to meet people that give new perspectives on things you assumed were universal truths.
greatest_challenge: Not spending too much money, I think. Remember to apply for as many scholarships as you can!
other_comments: Don't worry too much about all the planning. It'll take care of itself as you go along. Whether it's Edinburgh or somewhere else, just GO! We are in such a position of privilege to be able to bring SU and Erasmus grants to travel, so please capitalise on that.

crucial_aspects: since I study european ethnology, I wanted to explore a culture with a rich history as well as an interesting social culture. above that it was crucial that the university had great options for subjects and classes. Edinburgh university had all of the above, and the city/country also seemed welcoming for international students, and a great environment for studying abroad. another thing was the climate, Scotland is not too different from Denmark, so I know it would feel more homelike, and I would really enjoy exploring.
info_ease: it was very difficult, there was so many things from Erasmus coordinators that was wrong, and a lot of wrong emails and so on. above that I didn't get accommodation, so I had to figure that out last minute. also the university is spread out around the city, and the system is different there. so not very easy.
arrival_assistance: no assisant.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I had to find the courses I was interested in, then get them accepted at my home institution. after that I applied on Edinburgh universities website, were you register your classes and as an international student, were you put all your personal information as well as your record . I had gotten a confirmation mail from host uni were it said what needed to do to registrer. Then I could choose diffrent classes that I wanted, and I registered for a lot of them, and then I got a confirmation of which classes I was accepted to.
registration_help: you could contact the host institution, even though they were quite slow at answering, there was also a handbook that we got sent the last minute from the Erasmus coordintator in copenhagen.
registration_success: I got most of the classes I wanted
registration_advice: be certain of dates and deadlines, make sure you ask for help by writing emails to your host institution if you are uncertain. talk to other people that are going to exchange, and do it together.
course_level: the level of the courses was quite similar to home, but I seemed a but easier when I was there. to clarity, there was a lot of new students whom are around 18-19 years old, so the courses had a great structure and the teachers were very involved, and there were tutorials every week that you could go to and discuss the subjects. all in all the university of Edinburgh was 10 times more structured than copenhagen uni, and it was a lot more clear what the learning outcomes of the classes were, and what you should learn for each lesson. therefore it seemed easier, even though the material of the courses was about the same level as back home. but I will admit that because I didn't feel the same pressure as I do back home, the level of the courses felt less overwhelming and difficult.
teaching_comparison: A lot more structure, since covid was still active when I arrived, all of my lessons were prerecorded. and their website "learn" is the same as Copenhagens "abalon" but just a lot better. the teachers would use learn a lot more, and they were very clear on what had to be learned at so on. the students openions were taking a lot more into the teaching, and I was surprised at how they used what the students had to say a lot more. so all in all a great style of teaching, were they included the students more, made sure everyone understood what had to happen by making clear learning outcomes for each week. it made me realize how much copenhagen uni needs an update on abalone and their website, and they could definitely learn from Edinburgh university.
courses_enrolled: Object of desires Idenitty and experience in health social anthropology 1b
recommended_courses: i absolutly adored my identity and experience in health course. We were a lot of students from diffrent backgrounds, some very nursing students and others from anthropology. it was such a fresh course, that really dived in to current issues of health and the health system, with a fresh view. and the structure was so great, and really easy to figure out.
unexpected_costs: that I had to pay 2 months of rent and I had one day, so be sure if you move that you have emergency cash. also the social events at the beginning of the year for exchange students really takes a toll on the wallet, if you want to be social and meet other people.
cost_comparison: the food was in general a bit cheaper, and nothing was really more expensive.
activities_available: diffrent clubs both athletic and cultural.
activities_recommended: go out on trips, and join the group chat of Erasmus exchange students.
weekend_recommendations: just make some friends, and hang out with them, don put too much pressure on having to see everything all the time, remember to enjoy the city and were you are. but I would recommend nature trips on the weekends.
culture_adjustment: okay easy, I got some great friends and we figured out the diffrent social things together.
socializing_tips: be yourself, go out a lot and just meet other peoples friends.
cultural_challenges: hmm, not rellay any.
culture_appreciated: how sweet and open everyone is over there. so eye opening how we are and act in copenhagen.
top3_advice: prepare for housing and unexpected fees there. go to the library and study with your friends, and get outside. make sure to find some good friends the first 3 weeks and eat a lot of fish and chips.
other_useful_info: make sure to ask for help, study the map of where your classes are in the city, and just make sure to walk around a lot and get to know the area. and be prepared for unexpected things that will happen, and dont panic if they do, it will get sorted out
most_rewarding: my amazing friends that I got there, I didn't know I could become so close to people in such a short amount of time. and seeing my own culture with new eyes, and bringing back som Scottish good energy and happiness to people of copenhagen.
greatest_challenge: housing. absolutely terrible to figure out, but that is part of the adventure.
other_comments: be social, have fun and dont care about what others think, find a good spot in the city that you like, and visit that when you can.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne på udveksling et sted med et godt og anerkendt universitet, hvor jeg kunne styrke mine engelsk kompetencer, få nogle relevante og spændende fag og samtidig blive udfordret både kulturelt og sprogligt. Derudover ville jeg gerne til en stor, men samtidig overskuelig by med et stort udvalg af diverse kulturtilbud, byliv og smuk natur tæt på. Derfor endte jeg med at vælge Edinburgh, som levede fuldt ud op til mine forventninger - og mere til.
overall_comments: Jeg har haft et skønt ophold! Det eneste jeg har kunne sætte en finger på, er at mit ophold har været en smule præget af corona, hvilket man skal have i mente, når man læser min vurdering. Dog tog jeg afsted med to andre fra mit studie, så ift. det sociale (som ellers var en smule påvirket af corona), fik vi det bedste ud af det og havde stor glæde af hinanden.
info_ease: Super fint. University of Edinburgh (UoE) har mange ansatte til at hjælpe udvekslingsstuderende, så hvis man var i tvivl om noget kunne man altid sende dem en mail, og de svarede altid hurtigt tilbage.
arrival_assistance: Hver udvekslingsstuderende får en personlig tutor, som man kan spørge alt om mellem himmel og jord. Jeg blev taget rigtig godt i hånden, og havde egentlig ikke brug for alt den hjælp, de tilbød, men det var betryggende, at de var gode til at hjælpe og være til rådighed. Det samme gælder det kontor, som er knyttet specifikt til udvekslingsstuderende.
arrival_comments: Se ovenstående.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Jeg har haft et skønt ophold! Det eneste jeg har kunne sætte en finger på, er at mit ophold har været en smule præget af corona, hvilket man skal have i mente, når man læser min vurdering. Dog tog jeg afsted med to andre fra mit studie, så ift. det sociale (som ellers var en smule påvirket af corona), fik vi det bedste ud af det og havde stor glæde af hinanden.
registration_process: Havde ingen problemer. Var til en online præsentation/spørgerunde inden tilmelding, hvor man blev taget godt i hånden ift., hvordan man tilmelder sig, hvilke deadlines der er vigtige, ting man skal huske osv osv. Mener jeg fandt frem til det på UoEs hjemmeside. Det var meget behjælpeligt, og ellers er de gode og hurtige til at svare på mails, hvis man har spørgsmål.
registration_help: UoE har en helt afdeling kun for udvekslingsstuderende, så der er altid masser af hjælp af hente, personer man kan skrive til osv. Derudover får man som sagt sin personal tutor, når man ankommer til Edinburgh, som gladeligt hjælper med ting fra a-z. Der bliver også oprettet diverse Facebookgrupper for de studerende.
registration_success: Det var en smule forvirrende. Jeg fandt sent ud af, at det kun er nogle bestemte kurser, der er åbne for udvekslingsstuderende, så det er vigtigt at finde den fane på UoEs hjemmeside, der har et kursuskatalog for netop udvekslingsstuderende. Her er det også vigtigt, når du søger efter fag på den side, at vælge det rigtige semester. Herefter kan du browse alle mulige fag, som du kan tilmelde dig. Dog er der mange fag, der har særlige krav, eller som der er særlig høj efterspørgsel på. Sidstnævnte er ofte de fag, man vil finde relevant ift. film og medier, så hav dette i mente, når du søger, og hav et par ekstra fag i baghånden, hvis du ikke får dine første prioriteter til en start. Intet skåret ud i sten, før du officielt set starter, da man har tre uger til at hoppe til og fra fag. I den process kan man udfylde en formular, hvor du har mulighed for potentielt at øge dine chancer for at få et bestemt fag, hvis du ikke fik det du ønskede til at starte med. Så gå ikke i panik i første omgang :)
registration_advice: Ha' is i maven og skriv til kontoret eller din personal tutor, hvis du er i tvivl om, hvordan du skifter eller søger nye fag.
academics_comments: Jeg har haft et skønt ophold! Det eneste jeg har kunne sætte en finger på, er at mit ophold har været en smule præget af corona, hvilket man skal have i mente, når man læser min vurdering. Dog tog jeg afsted med to andre fra mit studie, så ift. det sociale (som ellers var en smule påvirket af corona), fik vi det bedste ud af det og havde stor glæde af hinanden.
course_level: Niveauet er lidt lavere end man er vant til, fordi man oftest tager førsteårsfag som udvekslingsstuderende, men det er ikke givet på forhånd. Det er til gengæld meget fint, hvis man vil prøve kræfter med fag fra et andet fakultet end humaniora. Arbejdsbyrden er mere jævnt fordelt, hvilket man lige skal vænne sig til, fordi eksamen typisk er delt op i to (så man har en form for midtterm eksamen og en endelig eksamen). Ved de mere "kreative" fag kan man godt komme ud for, at en del af ens eksamen er en portfolio, hvor man skal lave nogle mindre opgaver eller en form for gruppearbejde, præsentation eller lign. De fleste eksaminer er vistnok skriftlige essays, og der skal meget til, før man ikke består, så man kan lidt selv vælge, hvor meget man vil udfordre sig selv og lægge i det. Læsningen var også ganske fin - nogle tekster sværere end andre, men ca. samme niveau som man er vant til, vil jeg sige (og det afhænger self også af det enkelte fag). Her er det også generelt, hvad man gør det til, og hvor meget man forventer af en selv.
teaching_comparison: Lidt alla det man er vant til. Jeg havde kun gode erfaringer med mine undervisere, synes de var meget pædagogiske og hjælpsomme, hvis man var i tvivl om noget. I nogle fag har man kun en enkel underviser, men det er også rimelig normalt, at man er flere undervisere om et enkelt fag, hvilket jeg ikke var så vant til fra KU, men det fungerede også fint.
courses_enrolled: - Music 1A: Psychology of Music (MUSI08069) - Sociology 1B: The Sociological Imagination: Private Troubles, Public Problems (SCIL08005) - Films on Film (DESI08129)
recommended_courses: Vil anbefale alle de fag, jeg havde. Musikpsykologi var lidt af et sats, og uden at være særlig musikalsk begavet, var det vildt interessant og niveauet var klart til at følge med på. Det var helt sikkert det fag, der overraskede allermest positivt, underviseren var fuldstændig genial, og jeg blev virkelig klogere på, hvor stor en rolle musik spiller for mennesker og samfundet. Kæmpe anbefaling! Sociologi-faget var også vildt spændende, og beskæftigede sig med universelle emner såsom ulighed, race, socio-økonomisk klasseinddeling og køn. Dygtige undervisere og virkelig interessant og relevant stof uanset, hvilken uddannelse man kommer fra. Nok en af de fag, jeg lærte allermest af. Filmfaget var overraskende nok det sværeste fag alt i alt (mest pga. det sproglige og til tider svære læsestof), men stadig overkommeligt - særligt når man er FM'er. Fik heller ikke indtrykket af, at det var et førsteårsfag. Der var filmvisninger hver uge, ingen tutorials og en god underviser. Det handlede primært om, hvordan det at lave film kommer til udtryk i film (så meget meta-agtigt).
unexpected_costs: Har ikke rigtig overblik over, hvor meget jeg brugte på mad og fornøjelser - alt afhænger af, hvor du handler, hvad du vil opleve og hvor mange ture, du tager på - f.eks. til højlandet, andre storbyer osv. Jeg manglede absolut intet, og kunne klart have sparet mere, end hvad jeg gjorde.
cost_comparison: Mad var måske en smule dyrere end forventet. Afhænger self af, hvad du bor tæt på. Vi boede tæt på en Coop, hvor priserne var rimelig almindelige ligesom i DK, og en Waitrose, som kan sammenlignes lidt med Irma, som givet er til den dyre side. Lidl er til gengæld vanvittig billigt. Off. transport er ca. samme priser som i DK, alkohol og restaurantbesøg er generelt en smule billigere. Husleje er dyrt, og kan formodentlig gøres lidt billigere end det, jeg endte med at betale. Et godt tip er, at Edinburgh har rigtig gode genbrugsforretninger, hvis man vil spare lidt på tøjbudgettet.
activities_available: Der findes et link til en side, hvor man kan se alle former for societies. Derudover har UoE en app, hvor der popper alverdens begivenheder op, og der er som regel nogle fester og sammenkomster i løbet af semesteret - både for alle, men også nogle forbeholdt udvekslingsstuderende.
activities_recommended: Læs ovenstående.
weekend_recommendations: Mine favoritsteder i Edinburgh var Blackford Hill, bydelene Newington, Stockbridge, Haymarket og Bruntsfield, kunstmuseerne (nærmest alle museer er gratis!), studiecafeen/baren Library Bar, Bennet's bar, Paradise Palms, The Meadows og Dr. Neil's Garden. Hvad angår bylivet anbefaler jeg Mash House og Sneaky Pete's. Man bliver nødt til (!!!) at tage til højlandet, Isle of Skye og Inverness. Glasgow er også dejlig nemt at komme til og er også en helt vidunderlig by med mange kulturelle tilbud og et godt byliv:) Vi tog også til Nordirland og Irland, mens vi boede i Edi - kæmpe kæmpe anbefaling også!
culture_adjustment: Super fint. Skotterne er nogle af de sødeste mennesker, jeg har mødt. Meget åbne, chatty og imødekommende.
socializing_tips: Edinburgh er en meget international by, så nogle gange var det faktisk svært opstøve skottere (desværre) - de fleste mødte vi i byen. Og ellers er der også mange søde udvekslingsstuderende! Vil også klart anbefale at joine et society eller to.
cultural_challenges: Ikke noget. Dog er man på universitetet typisk lige et par år eller tre yngre, end man typisk er, når man starter på uni i DK, hvilket var noget, jeg bed mærke i, men som slet ikke er altafgørende. Bare godt at vide:)
culture_appreciated: Den skotske accent (!!!), pubs, fish n chips, dyrkelsen af naturen - og så er skottere bare virkelig søde og imødekommende.
top3_advice: 1) Start med at søg bolig asap 2) Tilmeld dig minimum et society 3) Tag på så mange skønne weekendture, du kan!
other_useful_info: Tror jeg er kommet ind på det meste:)
most_rewarding: Det sproglige og det at finde ud af, hvor vanvittig undervurderet Skotland og skotterne er på så mange punkter!
greatest_challenge: Udover at finde bolig, nok det sproglige, men intet uoverkommeligt, særligt fordi man er i båd med så mange andre udvekslingsstuderende. Opfatter det nærmest ikke som en udfordring, nu hvor jeg kigger tilbage på det samlet set. Nok mest en bekymring i starten.
other_comments: TAG TIL SKOTLAND, du vil ikke fortryde det hihi
