crucial_aspects: I wanted to do an exchange abroad because I wanted to live in another country and meet new people. I chose Edinburgh because I had heard it was a very student friendly city, and because I thought it had a great mix of nature, culture and history.
info_ease: It was fairly easy. The university provides a good introduction for when you arrive.
arrival_assistance: The university created a little online assignment where they give you a lot of information. You have to read and complete the assignment in order to be fully matriculated. The university also gives you a personal tutor. You meet with them in the first weeks and they can answer any questions you may have.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: When you apply you have to wish for the courses you want. They're not final so you can change later if you're not satisfied.
registration_help: The exchange team were there via email if you had any questions and were good at answering more general enquiries.
registration_success: Not very successful. I wanted some courses for year 2 or 3, however these are often in high demand, so I ended up with some introductory courses.
registration_advice: Don't be hesitant in changing your courses if you're not satisfied.
course_level: Lectures and tutorials are only an hour long, so I would say that you engage with the subjects in a more shallow way than at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style is a mixture of lectures and tutorials. In tutorials you are 10-15 people. Often tutorials is one big group discussion about a specific reading. I think this differs from UCPH where you often work and discuss in smaller groups.
courses_enrolled: - Empires (SCAN08010) - Sociology 1B: The Sociological Imagination: Private Troubles, Public Problems (SCIL08005) - Language and Communication in Health and Society (SHSS08005)
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed the course Language and Communication. The course is a part of a social work degree. Therefore, it has both theoretical and practical elements. In the first part of the course we looked at different theories to analyze health communication such as discourse analysis. The second part of the course we practiced how to be a good and empathetic listener in a client-professional setting.
unexpected_costs: I don't think I had any.
cost_comparison: Most museums and galleries in Scotland are free.
activities_available: The university has a lot of different student societies that you can join.
activities_recommended: I really loved the hiking society. They do weekend trips as well, so it was a really great way to see other parts of Scotland.
weekend_recommendations: I really loved Aisle of Arran. It is a little island close to Glasgow.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy.
socializing_tips: I was mostly with the other international students. However, I think the easiest way is to join one of the societies.
cultural_challenges: I don't think there were any I found particularly challenging.
culture_appreciated: People are very open and friendly. I'd also recommend going to one of the Cèilidh dances.
top3_advice: 1. Join the whatsapp groups. I found most of my friends this way. 2. Start looking for an accommodation early to avoid unnecessary stress. 3. Use your weekends to travel and see Scotland - it's so lovely!
other_useful_info: I don't think so.
most_rewarding: Meeting so many lovely people and making memories with them.
greatest_challenge: Remaining motivated to do the academic work while receiving lectures online and dealing with strikes.
other_comments: No.

teaching_comparison: Similiarly to KU there are both lectures and smaller classes for discussion. I did find that the discussion classes was still more like a lecture than at KU. There are not as much of a culture for being critical about texts or theories - Its more about learning by heart.
courses_enrolled: Ethical Values and Challenges in Care Introduction to Cognitive Science Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience - Childhood
recommended_courses: Ethical Values and Challenges in Care was very interesting. It is centered around the ethics and issues you are faced with as as a professional working with people who need care. I took the course as an elective and the class consisted of nurses and students in various fields in social sciences. There was a lot of discussion and examples from real life. The person running the course, Sally Brown, was incredible at teaching. Developmental Cogntive Neuroscience was also interesting, it was centered on both normal and atypical cognition and brain development in children. A bit too sciency and biological for my taste. I did however include some classes regarding how aspects such as low socioeconomic status, abuse and neglect affects children, both cognitively, socially and behavioraly, which was really interesting and more relevant the interests I have in psychology. Introduction to Cogntive Science I would not recommend - the level and content was very mixed. Quite suprisingly a part of the course was about programming/Python, which was difficult and the connecting to psychology was hard to see. A part of the course was an introduction to philosophy of science, which seemed very introductory and unnecessary.
unexpected_costs: If you want to join societies in cost extra. would not say that there was any expenses that I was suprised with - Maybe that the room was so expensive. I also know many other exchange student paying loads more than me, some up to 9000DKK a month.
cost_comparison: Food and drinks was a bit less expensive than in Copenhagen - However, the inflation is of course also present in UK and prices were higher than usual.
activities_available: There is loads of societies to join at UoE: various sport societies, wine society, film society, choir etc. There is a fair in the beginning of the week were you can hear about the different activities.
activities_recommended: I joined the hillwalking society which I would recommend! They have weekend trips every other weekend to various places around Scotland.
weekend_recommendations: It is fairly easy to go to nice nature areas. There are busses going to the Pentlands, which have good easy hikes. It takes less than an hour to get there. Google 'hikes/daytrips' around edinburgh, there are plenty. There is many beautifull gardens/nature reserves to visit - look at the National Trust of Scotlands sites. Glasgow is also only a one hour train drive away, and is also a nice city.
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy. British/scottish culture is not that different from danish. Many people living in Edinburgh are also foreigners. I however have mostly spend time with a group of other danes also on exchange.
socializing_tips: Good question. In some aspects I wish I had tried harder to get local friends, but it just did not happen for me. I think societies is a very good way to talk to different people.
cultural_challenges: It found it a little difficult that people at uni are way younger than me. I am already a bit older than students at KU on the bachelor, but at UoE they are even younger. Therefore it did not make so much sense for me trying to become friends with people in my classes, since most of them are 5-7 years younger than me.
culture_appreciated: People are very friendly and warm. I really like the pub culture, it is so cozy going to a pub and having a pint:) I love the aesthetic of edinburgh, very old school hoghwarts-ish. I think it is very easy to feel at home there. I could see myself living there again.
top3_advice: Edinburgh is an amazing city for exchange, the vibe and feeling is so cozy and nice. There are a lot of strenuous admin stuff before going (getting courses registered, finding a place to stay etc) but once you are there it is worth it.
other_useful_info: Start looking for a place to stay early, there is a lot of FB groups to join. If you are able to, maybe go for a weekend a month or so before to visit flats.
most_rewarding: It was nice to experience living somewhere else for a long enough time for it to feel like your home. I found a good community with other danish exchange students, who were all lovely.
greatest_challenge: It can be difficult to have to be social a lot with people you dont know. I found it challenging to find a good balance between taking the alone time I needed while also pushing myself to get the most out of the experience. I think this has a lot to do with what type of person you are - Im fairly introverted, and having this temperament can be challenging during exchange. But a good learning experience also! And I would recommend fellow introverts to go on exchange aswell.
other_comments: I really recommend going to Edinburgh.

crucial_aspects: Firstly, I felt a strong connection to the destination having travelled there on numerous occasions, and it felt familiar and safe. Secondly, I had an extremely good impression of my host university. The courses matched my interests very well and I knew other students who had a great experience with the University of Edinburgh. Although I was very set on this university from the beginning, I felt that all of my needs were met - personally and academically.
overall_comments: Such a great and progressive university with so many opportunities outside of academia. There were many groups and societies to join with all kinds of special interests.
info_ease: Fairly easy. The study abroad team at my host university were consistent with check up emails and events to make sure everything was done correctly. Very kind reception and understanding to the fact that you are a new visiting student.
arrival_assistance: The visiting students team held an online meeting to go through the steps of matriculation. What to do and check up, how to do it, so i felt looked after in this process.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Such a great and progressive university with so many opportunities outside of academia. There were many groups and societies to join with all kinds of special interests.
registration_process: Registration was part of the matriculation process, in which there are four steps as I recall. These steps must be completed in order to be accepted into the host institution. It is register as student, complete international checkin, confirm attendance (which the visiting students team will help you do) and pay tuition fees (not applicable to erasmus exchange)
registration_help: The visiting students team at my host university made sure to do regular checkups and reminders and they held an online event where attendance was confirmed and explained the other steps. They are easy and quick to contact in case you need help. You are also assigned one 'personal tutor' who will be your contact during the exchange.
registration_success: Fairly succesful. I did my exchange on my 4th semester, which unfortunately meant that I did not have the prerequisites for quite a few courses. And I did a subject specific exchange, which meant there were some limitations in choosing courses. However, I did end up with the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: Do not worry about unintentionally missing steps, the visiting students team are with you every step of the way and are very helpful. However, do note down deadlines, so you have an overview of when to do what. Get to know the specifics of your exchange, as well as the prerequisites for the courses, so you know which courses you are eligible for - that could have saved me some time in choosing my courses.
academics_comments: Such a great and progressive university with so many opportunities outside of academia. There were many groups and societies to join with all kinds of special interests.
course_level: Level is definitely doable. I did not feel too stressed or felt that I was behind. I chose year 2 courses which matched very well with the level I was at. I know you can choose year 1 courses which are less demanding. But I would say that the level is not very different from what I was used to, and I never felt that at assignment or exam was too difficult to tackle.
teaching_comparison: More or less same format with lectures and seminars. However, the seminar classes were quite small with only 10-12 students and shorter, typically lasting just one hour - so, speaking up was quite easy.
courses_enrolled: English in Time and Space Songs, Swords, Rebel and Revivals: Modern Celtic Literature in Translation Literary Studies: English Literature post 1789
recommended_courses: University of Edinburgh offers many courses with a focus on Scottish language, literature, history and culture, so I would definitely recommend doing something that relates to the country. It's a fun way to learn about the place you are visiting, and you feel even more connected to it.
unexpected_costs: Housing was a little more expensive that I first expected/hoped for. But the cost of living is lower than in DK, so it was manageable.
cost_comparison: Grocery shopping was generally cheaper than back home, so you can live on a budget. I only had to buy books for one course, so that was helpful. Materials from other courses were all online. Some societies require a fee for membership, but not all.
activities_available: Countless possibilities. During introduction week, they do taster sessions for all the clubs/societies and there are truly too many to count. No doubt you will find something that you will find fun/interesting.
activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend joining a club/society. It's a great way to meet new friends with similar interests as yourself. I joined an equestrian club (which was quite expensive, but very fun), and met some great people there.
weekend_recommendations: Edinburgh is a very walkable city (low cost on transport), so stroll around during the weekends. Many museums are free, so that's another great option. Some societies also do day trips to the countryside/highlands for a low price and that's a great way to get out of the city.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Scotland is not too different from Denmark. Very safe place and sociable people.
socializing_tips: Join societies, that is by far the easiest way. And there are so many places around campus to meet up, study, have coffee together.
cultural_challenges: Not any.
culture_appreciated: There is so much pride in the Scottish history that you can feel all over the city. The Scots definitely cherish their culture and that is very easy to see when you walk around Edinburgh. You can almost always hear a bagpipe playing and the pubs and bars are always full of people.
top3_advice: 1. Don't worry too much about the academic level - some things are challenging, but it's perfectly doable. And they want you to feel comfortable and do well on the courses. 2. Join a society! 3. Take time to explore the city - Edinburgh is magical, and there are so many places to see and the Scottish culture will definitely get under your skin.
other_useful_info: Spend some time checking the prerequisites for the courses - that can be a bit challenging. Try to find accommodation in the city centre. Edinburgh is a quite small city and very walkable, and you will save money on transport. University of Edinburgh is very inclusive and progressive and they definitely try to meet your needs.
most_rewarding: Meeting people that will hopefully stay in my life for many years. Trying to live abroad and manage the exchange on my own also strengthened my self confidence. I definitely feel more brave and optimistic about my personal and academic future. While the whole experience might seem scary at first, you will feel more self assured when you complete the exchange.
greatest_challenge: Of course having the whole semester in front of you is quite frightening, but to be honest I never struggled that much. I think my greatest worry was if I did well enough in my assignments and try to get a sense of what was expected of me - but that turned out just fine. Also putting yourself out there socially can be intimidating, as you are taken out of your usual setting.
other_comments: I warmly recommend University of Edinburgh. I had an absolutely amazing experience and would never be without it. I have learned so much about myself and what I want to do with my education. Living and studying abroad has been incredibly rewarding for me and has made me feel more self assured personally and academically.

crucial_aspects: The University of Edinburgh is ranked as one of the best universities in the UK and the world and therefore was a perfect choice for an academic challenge because of its well-known reputation. Further, I've talked to former exchange students who recommended the university because of its way of welcoming exchange students. The university is known for hosting many international students so there is plenty of opportunity to make international connections. Last, I wanted to explore Scottish nature and culture (which didn't disappoint).
overall_comments: My study abroad experience was overall good. However, some of my courses did not live up to my expectations.
info_ease: It was pretty easy but the University of Edinburgh has a tendency to send an overwhelming amount of emails which inflict more harm than good.
arrival_assistance: I received emails concerning my arrival and what to remember. Further, I was assigned a personal student advisor.
arrival_comments: Sometimes an overwhelming amount of information from the university.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: My study abroad experience was overall good. However, some of my courses did not live up to my expectations.
registration_process: I had to fill out an online application. The process was fairly easy but slow.
registration_help: I could always write an email to the university if I needed help.
registration_success: I was not successful since I only got one of the courses I wanted. However, I did change my preferences 1 1/2 months after my original registration, hence the new courses I wanted were already full. It was therefore my own fault.
registration_advice: Be sure of which courses you want and apply for them as soon as possible. There is limited space in most year 2 and 3 courses of around 30 people, so the courses fill out quickly.
academics_comments: My study abroad experience was overall good. However, some of my courses did not live up to my expectations.
course_level: The amount of obligatory reading was more than I expected in all the courses. However, the level was as I expected taking into account that some of my courses were year 3 (and therefore more demanding) and others year 1.
teaching_comparison: The seminars are in some ways similar to UCPH. They consist of a class which then discusses the topic of the day. One of my year 3 courses called Gifts in Context was mostly taught through an abstract debate of the obligatory reading, so it was pretty difficult to follow the topic sometimes. It was rare you came out with any answers since it was more about reflection and discussion. Moreover, both my year 3 courses did not use any PowerPoint at all, which we usually do at UCPH Further, the structure of the lectures is also similar to UCHP's lectures. However, my lectures were only online but that was a decision of the course organisation for that specific course. One also has to be aware that if the course is a year 1 course, it is mostly lectures and a few tutorials (similar to seminars) where you discuss the lecture in more depth.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to global crime and justice (year 1) Contemporary Issues in Competition Law and the Single Market (year 3) Gifts in Context (year 3)
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed Contemporary Issues in Competition Law and the Single Market since it is also usable in Denmark because of the EU rules.
unexpected_costs: I did not encounter any unexpected cost.
cost_comparison: In general, Scotland is around 10% cheaper compared to the prices in Denmark. Therefore, grocery shopping, eating out, etc. was less expensive than I expected.
activities_available: The university offers a range of cultural/social societies. For example, the university has a harry potter society, a whisky society, an anime and animations society, a bad film society, the Erasmus society etc. Besides the societies, the university also has plenty of sports clubs + a gym for university staff and students.
activities_recommended: I would recommend joining the Erasmus Society since they arrange trips to other parts of Scotland. This is a great way to explore Scotland since you just have to show up and enjoy the trip. Moreover, it is a great way to meet other exchange students.
weekend_recommendations: As described above, I would recommend buying Erasmus trips. They offer both day trips and 2 to 3 days trips. By doing that, you are sure to see the most popular spots in Scotland such as the Highlands. Further, I would recommend arranging your own day trips to Scottish cities such as Glasgow, Aberdeen, and so on. You can also take the train and bus to multiple cities in the two national parks, so I would recommend exploring the parks and going on some hiking trips.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy since the culture is similar to the culture Copenhagen.
socializing_tips: I would join a society or a sports club since it otherwise can be hard to socialize with local students.
cultural_challenges: There as not particularly challenging differences.
culture_appreciated: I especially enjoyed the pub culture in Scotland since almost all pubs offer both a meal and drinks. I have enjoyed many beers with my friends at different pubs during my exchange. I also appreciated how friendly and helpful the Scottish people in general are. I also appreciated the fact that most museums were free so it was easy to explore the cities on a low budget. A little tip is also that tap water is free, so always ask for tap water at restaurants, cafes, and so on.
top3_advice: 1. Remember to explore outside the city. Scotland has amazing nature! 2. Try out the local pub culture and some pub quizzes. 3. Don't be afraid to challenge yourself. Go to events where you don't know anyone - maybe you'll find a new friend.
other_useful_info: Consider making a list of activities and trips you want to do before you arrive. Time goes by fast, and before you know it, the semester is over. By making a list, you are sure to have an overview of everything you want to explore.
most_rewarding: Definitely getting to know all the wonderful international people. It was amazing learning about different cultures and also developing friendships with people from all around the world.
greatest_challenge: There were not any specific challenging circumstances, but overall moving to another country without knowing anyone can be challenging and difficult - but also very rewarding if you hang in there.

crucial_aspects: I visited Edinburgh when I was fourteen and I knew then that I wanted to come back to live there. The exchange programme was an excellent opportunity to do just that.
overall_comments: I though a semester abroad was over-hyped, but it was truly an intense and amazing learning experience.
info_ease: Very easily. The university has an excellent system, and are very good at informing students. As long as you keep up with your school e-mail, you're good to go.
arrival_assistance: Not applicable.
arrival_comments: No additional comments.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I though a semester abroad was over-hyped, but it was truly an intense and amazing learning experience.
registration_process: I had to do an immigration check, where they checked a potential visa (not applicable for me), passport and that I was correctly enrolled.
registration_help: Easily available advice place and accesible staff at the university.
registration_success: Very succesful, I got enrolled in all four classes I applied for originally.
registration_advice: Don't stress about it too much, as long as you keep up with your e-mail it is very easy and they are very available to help.
academics_comments: I though a semester abroad was over-hyped, but it was truly an intense and amazing learning experience.
course_level: Third-year BA courses, on the same level as I would have taken in my home institution.
teaching_comparison: Similar, but with much more written work, which was a welcome change.
courses_enrolled: Critical Practice: Criticism Critical Practice: Poetry Modernism and Empire Scottish Emigrant Traditions
recommended_courses: Pick what sounds interesting. From personal experience, I would recommend Modernism and Empire.
unexpected_costs: Rent was more expensive than I expected. You'll want to save up for fun activities too, to not miss out.
cost_comparison: Rent was more expensive than expected. I didn't travel as much.
activities_available: Many many different types of sports and clubs. Diving, archery, normal sports, film club, Taylor Swift club etc.
activities_recommended: Definitely the Bad Film Club. Hold a screening of a bad film every monday, the newsletters are always hilarious.
weekend_recommendations: Walk around! There is so much to see in Edinburgh. Take a day trip to St. Andrews.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, I feel at home in Edinburgh.
socializing_tips: I talked almost exclusively with othe rexchange students.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: It is slightly more diverse than Denmark, which is, to me, always a liberating feeling and environment.
top3_advice: Have fun, save up, don't stress about the academic aspects too much, you're not there to sit in your room for ten hours a day.
other_useful_info: Use all their resources. They want to help but you have to initiate contact.
most_rewarding: Going abroad and meeting new people. Changing my environment to a place where no one knows me and I can be the newest version of myself.
greatest_challenge: Being far away from family and friends from back home during hard times.
other_comments: GO! You won't regret it

crucial_aspects: Close to home, courses available, academic reputation of the University.
info_ease: UoE made it easy with information before and upon arrival.
arrival_assistance: Lived in student accommodation so i had RAs, I also had my personal tutor for any academic assistance, and there were many people to contact if i had troubles with anything.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Very easy, they gave you a flyer to follow.
registration_help: There was an online meeting that guided you before I submitted my application.
registration_success: Succesfull and I had my personal tutor afterwards who helped me switch between courses.
registration_advice: Just follow the instructions.
course_level: The level was really good. Comparable to UCPH, but courses were more compressed since the semester is shorter.
teaching_comparison: It was very comparable with the lectures, however there was more coursework and their classroom teaching was in much smaller groups at around 10 persons.
courses_enrolled: Mechanisms of Brain Development 3 Immunology 3 Introduction to Social Anthropology
recommended_courses: Mechanisms of Brain Development 3 Immunology 3 Introduction to Social Anthropology They were all recommendable, very interesting subjects in all three courses.
unexpected_costs: We had a lot of extra costs for our housing with kitchen utensils and room features. We had ordered a university kit from home but the quality was very bad (knifes and pans) and it did not arrive on time so we had to by duvets and sheets ourselves anyway.
cost_comparison: I did expect it to be less expensive to go out. It was also more expensive because you often go out a lot when you are abroad compared to home. I used around 1500 dkk per month on going out with people for coffee, food and drinks. I had all texts provided online, so no expenses on that. If you are under 21 you can apply for a free scots card, which give you transportation with busses for free.
activities_available: Many societies, almost one for everyone.
activities_recommended: I did not join any of the societies but i would definitely do it if i went again. There is for example a scandinavian society or societies that arrange diffrent activities.
weekend_recommendations: Go to isle of skye! There is a company that arrange student tours from Edinburgh and Glasgows, these are better price options and you have other students as your travel companions.
culture_adjustment: Easy.
socializing_tips: UoE is not very local. almost only international students.
cultural_challenges: none.
culture_appreciated: The Scottish people are very friendly, you can easily ask policeofficers, bus drivers or anybody else for help.
top3_advice: Remember to enjoy it. Use the first weeks when it is still warm to go on tours into the highlands, the last weeks gets more stressed academically. Remember to use some of the many nice study spaces at the university, that helped me a lot.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: The extremely beautiful country and Edinburgh is simply stunning. I also liked my courses that really challenged me and was some of the most interesting i have had so far.
greatest_challenge: Hard to study without the people that are normally part of your study group .
other_comments: no.

crucial_aspects: That it was not too far away from home, and that it was a good University in a nice city
info_ease: Overall the information during the whole process has been quite difficult to get in my opinion
arrival_assistance: Only the opportunity to mail a contact person, but with quite slow response because they were very busy during the start of the semester.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: First you have to do all the paperwork with Learning Agreement and so on (which was a bit difficult at the University of Edinburgh, because they don't have the online system, so you have to do everything manually). When arriving in Edinburgh you have to book an appointment to show that you have arrived - this part is very easy and fast. Furthermore, you have to register for your classes. You can change between classes for the first two weeks and have the opportunities to try different classes and change classes. Though I would not recommend doing that because a lot of the classes gets filled up quite fast.
registration_help: We got a contact person that we could send emails when having any questions.
registration_success: For me I had a lot of troubles registering to classes because most of the classes I wanted was already full.
registration_advice: Apply for the courses you want as quick as possible, and have patience because the respondence time is quite slow since they have a lot of students to answer.
course_level: Most of my courses were 3 year BA courses
teaching_comparison: Much the same, but a bit more interaction between students and teacher in our tutorial classes (probably because we were only around 8-10 people in each tutorial class).
courses_enrolled: The Anthropology of Energy in the Global South The Anthropology of Health and Healing Scandinavian Civilisation A: Vikings, Sagas and the Road to Enlightenment
recommended_courses: The Anthropology of Health and Healing : because we read a lot of great texts. Also the lessons with Alexander Edmonds were very good. Scandinavian Civilisation A: Vikings, Sagas and the Road to Enlightenment : a very interesting course seeing Scandinavia from another perspective. The teacher expects quite a lot from you which is both motivating but sometimes a bit stressfull if you have a busy week.
unexpected_costs: Only that the rent was much higher than I expected
cost_comparison: Food is a bit cheaper than in Denmark - especially when eating out. The money I spend on food also reflects that I ate out a lot.
activities_available: All kinds of different societies - A LOT of different opportunities.
activities_recommended: I was in the Scandinavian Society which was nice! And also the Hill Walking club is a great way of getting on trips to the Scottish highlands.
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips! Scotland really has a lot of beautiful nature. If you have the possibility I would recommend to rent a car and go by you self or with the Hill Walking club instead of going with the ESN trips.
culture_adjustment: Very easy - very similar to Denmark in my opinion.
cultural_challenges: People living at my accommodation place were very young and shy(?) so not much interaction from them. I felt a bit old, but it wasn't a problem.
culture_appreciated: The kindness from everyone on the street etc.
top3_advice: 1. If you want accommodation through the University keep calling them eventhough it feels very uncomfortable to be that pushy. 2. Do not stress too much about keeping up with school work and remember to just enjoy the whole experience. 3. Find a hobby, society or club
other_useful_info: Not really
most_rewarding: Trying to live away from home without a network and being more on my own.
greatest_challenge: I would say the same as written above: establishing a network a place that is completely new to you.

crucial_aspects: To find a good university, nice city, nice nature for hikes
info_ease: Pretty easy. Nice to go to an English speaking country, and I quickly met a lot of exchange students so we could help each other out. UoE is very aware of their students' well-being.
arrival_assistance: UoE has a Visiting Student Advisor who reaches out to you individually and you have to attend a zoom meeting where you are informed. All introduction activities can be found on an app.
arrival_comments: Most introduction activities were targeted freshers, so I did not find it necessary to stress about attending them
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: We had to meet up at an office at Old College and get our arrival registrated by showing passport and flight tickets. we also had to meet up at another office and get registrated. we got the information on mail and booked time for both.
registration_help: Visiting Student Advisor! You can always write to him/her and you get a personal advisor. I didn't really use it, but I know many people did successfully.
registration_success: Very! I didn't get everything I applied for, but ended up with something I enjoyed even more.
registration_advice: Read (and organize) your mails - you'll get a lot!
course_level: Lectures were similar to KU, tutorials were an easier level. I've been told that it's very easy to pass your exams when they're essays, but I haven't had feedback yet, so I don't know about that
teaching_comparison: Very similar! Lectures were the same. Tutorials were smaller groups.
courses_enrolled: Culture and Power Anthropology of Health and Healing War and Peace: Anthropological Perspectives
recommended_courses: All of them, but especially Culture and Power!
unexpected_costs: I joined The Hillwalking Club, were we went on weekend trips. Each trip was £50 and really worth it!
cost_comparison: Accommodation was so much more expensive than expected! Transportation! I walked everywhere. Only if I took the bus outside the city and it was still quite cheap. I did although go on roadtrips and likewise which isn't calculated above, but that was also an acceptable price.
activities_available: Clubs and societies. Lots and lots and well informed at your arrival
activities_recommended: Hillwalking Club!! Perfect and easy way to experience the incredible nature!
weekend_recommendations: Other than the club I went on several weekend trips. Go on a roadtrip (we went for 5 days), go t oGlasgow (maybe for a concert) or other cities. A small country with a lot to offer!
culture_adjustment: Very easy! Many international students and very European milleau.
socializing_tips: People are very outgoing, so literally just reach out and you will be rewarded :)
cultural_challenges: The pedestrian crossing turns green both ways at the same time. More seriously, people are pretty young when starting university there, so most of my neighbors were 18 years
culture_appreciated: Their love for dogs and cozy cafes - and how you often find both the same place
top3_advice: - Go hiking / see nature - Call student accommodation early if you apply there - Bring room for lots of nice 2nd hand shopping
other_useful_info: Shout out to university fitness center. They put their logo on everything, including weight plates. I payed £100 for one semester of fitness AND bouldering/roped climbing. Very nice climbing staff.
most_rewarding: Meeting nice people and going nice places
greatest_challenge: Finding time for everything. It's a big plus that the semester is quite short cause I needed a lot of time to relax after coming home.
other_comments: Look up the location of your classes. I had 10 minutes between two classes and a 14 minute walk - but I managed, so not your biggest worries.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to choose something that weren't too far from home, and accessible in case I needed to go home in case of emergency. Preferably a country where they spoke a language familiar to me. A university that offered courses which I found interesting. The city seemed interesting to me.
overall_comments: Accommodation was difficult and complicated - could have been more help and organization from the university's side.
info_ease: Not VERY easy, but I feel like when you sat down and took time to look for the information it was there to find. Eventhough the paperwork was stressful. In the end I figured everything out.
arrival_assistance: Was offered a meeting with my personal tutor, which was great help.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Accommodation was difficult and complicated - could have been more help and organization from the university's side.
registration_process: All online. Had to show up with my boarding pass at the university, was fast and worked well, always someone ready to help. registration for courses was complicated
registration_help: Emails, personal tutors etc..
registration_success: pretty succesfull, there were a lot of misinformation about what courses we were allowed to take, and it was a bug job getting all the courses to fit into a correct timetable. A lot of help from the personal tutor tho, and in the end I was satisfies with all my courses. they were fun!
registration_advice: have lots of different options as to which courses you are interested in
academics_comments: Accommodation was difficult and complicated - could have been more help and organization from the university's side.
course_level: I think the level of courses was quite suitable

courses_enrolled: Immunology 3 Mechanisms of Brain Development 3 Introduction to Social Anthropology
recommended_courses: All of my courses were great I enjoyed them a lot
unexpected_costs: Damage to tooth which was covered by the insurance. Thank god!
cost_comparison: buscard and sports were more expensive than expected.
activities_available: All kinds of sports and societies. A lot of different events during freshers week.
activities_recommended: Sports was a fun way to meet other people
weekend_recommendations: Highlands were amazing!
culture_adjustment: I don't feel like we met that many local people. All the people living with us were also new to the city, but I fit right in
socializing_tips: Just get yourself out there, everyone was very nice and welcomming
cultural_challenges: That people drive on the other side of the road
culture_appreciated: People were very friendly in general
top3_advice: Keep your head high! It's gonna feel a little lonely and hopeless at times, but overall you're gonna be okay. Dont be afraid to ask for help
other_useful_info: Dont expect anything, embrace everything with open arms

greatest_challenge: Practicalities

crucial_aspects: I decided to study abroad for various reasons, but the biggest one was to improve my second language, make international friends, and open up new academic possibilities. I wanted to be in a diverse environment that would help me connect with people from around the world. I looked for top-notch schools with specialized programs and resources to support my academic growth. It was also important for me to have opportunities for post-study work and internships to gain practical experience. My goal was to have an amazing and enriching experience that would help me grow personally, professionally, and culturally.
info_ease: It was pretty easy, but I am glad that I came here with my friend so we could help each other out.
arrival_assistance: I don't recall getting any assistance when arriving
arrival_comments: I think the things you must do before, during, and after the exchange is very confusing and it takes up a lot of time and energy.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I asked other exchange students, where to go and then it was all fine. There is just a lot to do and find out at the beginning of the semester.
registration_help: I had a student adviser I could ask for help.
registration_success: It was fine. I tried to change one of my courses, but all the other courses I wished for, were unfortunately fully booked.
registration_advice: Talk to fellow exchange students or maybe friends who already have been on exchange
course_level: I went on an undergraduate programe
teaching_comparison: It is different but also fun to try something a lot different. It is more active participation and the best difference was that they put in a lot of work to give a lot of feedback on assignments.
courses_enrolled: Working and relating: developing your people skills Language and Communication in Health and Society Innovation and healthcare
recommended_courses: Working and relating: developing your people skills The teachers were great and I had a big learning outcome, which I can use in my future studies
unexpected_costs: In order to get the full experience I think it is important to travel around in the country you study in. Therefore traveling and small trips were an unexpected cost.
cost_comparison: Housing is extremely expensive in Edinburgh.
activities_available: All kinds. You could choose between 90 different societies, for a small amount of money. And I also joined the student gym, where they also provide a lot of different activities.
activities_recommended: I would defiantly recommend people to join some of the societies and the gym
weekend_recommendations: Buy tickets for the day trips even though it is expensive. It is absolutely worth it.
culture_adjustment: It was fine.
socializing_tips: Agin join the societies and also the events Erasmus is hosting. That was how I met all of my friends.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The slow living, I feel like everyone here is never in a rush which is nice. I also love that most of the people in Edinburgh are students and it just gives a nice vibe.
top3_advice: Go to the Erasmus events in the beginning in order to meet other exchange students. Be open-minded when meeting people from all over the world. Say yes to all the opportunities that come across. Time flies on exchange so you better get the most out of it.
other_useful_info: If you are unsure of your courses use time on exploring other courses and maybe go to other courses in the beginning and then reach out to your contact person in Edinburgh
most_rewarding: Improving English. Getting friends from all over the world. And getting to have another home in a different country.
greatest_challenge: For me, it was that even though I got a lot of new sweet friends, it isn't as many as I have at home so I had a lot of time alone. But I learned to enjoy the alone time which is also another rewarding thing about exchange.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to experience both the urban, and cultural life in the city but I also wanted to have the opportunity to have to experience an outdoor lifestyle by having easy access to nature.
info_ease: There were a lot of emails about the first days - both about social events and practical stuff from the University
arrival_assistance: I was assigned a supervisor from the international student office who I was invited to contact if I had any questions.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It difficult for me to remember all detail about the process. In the online form, you had to provide information about passed exams, approval of subjects from your home university. You also had to write a motivated application, etc.
registration_help: As mentioned earlier we had a supervisor from the international student office who we could email and book a meeting with.
registration_success: I had a lot of problems getting relevant courses as I was not on a subject-specific study abroad. I couldn't get enrolled in any of the landscape architecture courses as I was told that these were full. I ended up getting an email to one of the teachers at the relevant courses and we organized an unofficial meeting. She ended up pulling some strings so that I could get enrolled in the relevant courses. Overall it was a quite frustrating process as I chose to go to Edinburgh because one can study Landscape architecture.
registration_advice: If one struggles to get the write courses before getting to the country it is easier to wait till you get there. Usually every thing falls into place.
course_level: The courses were too easy but I also took courses on first year
teaching_comparison: It is quite the same: a combination of coursework, fieldwork, studio work, tutorials, pinups, and critics.
courses_enrolled: Landscape Architecture Theory 1B Landscape Architecture Design 1B Landscape Architecture Technique 1
recommended_courses: Landscape Architecture Design 1B It is a very interesting course where you work on a site outside Edinburgh. It is very interesting to design for an environment different from Denmark
unexpected_costs: I had to buy all my kitchen items for the accommodation
cost_comparison: I didn't use public transport as much as I expected. The city is not that by and you can walk the most of it
activities_available: There were a lot of cultural, athletic and social societies you cold join
activities_recommended: West-African dance, and the hillwalking society.
weekend_recommendations: Go to a Ceilidh event - its the best
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Skotland is not very different from Denmark. In many ways, we share humor, values, political approaches, and so on.
socializing_tips: I went to a ceilidh event and met a group of Scottish people they invited into a group chat of locals and they all became my friends. Remember that it's not only the exchange student events you should go to. Try to do something outside what the university is offering.

crucial_aspects: When choosing my exchange destination I took several things into account. First of all I wanted to go somewhere I hadn't visited, followed by a University with courses taught in English, but most importantly a destination where I could go into the mountains and/or nature and hike!! A combination of all these lead me to choose Edinburgh, Scotland. Which in my opinion is a perfect destination for exchange as it combines cute city with good nightlife, a good university and in beautiful surroundings!
overall_comments: I highly recommend to study abroad (even though admin stuff sucks). I especially recommend Edinburgh for nature- and pint-loving people!
info_ease: Easy. The University of Edinburgh platforms for students are easy to comprehend and they send many different informative emails.
arrival_assistance: Upon arrival I received a personal tutor, whom I could ask for help throughout my entire exchange. My tutor reached out to me already before semester start, which was nice, as I had problems with my courses. He assisted me (in-person) with solving the problems and was always quick by email as well. As I was in the School of Biological Science, I am not sure if the other schools had the same system with tutors. But there was a lot of informative meetings in the beginning of the semester as well!
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I highly recommend to study abroad (even though admin stuff sucks). I especially recommend Edinburgh for nature- and pint-loving people!
registration_process: Registration for courses starts when applying for Edinburgh. It can be a bit difficult to figure out which courses one can apply for and not, but there is a lot of available webpages through Uni website.
registration_help: Many different web tools including course descriptions and course timetable browser
registration_success: Well, it is common that they change the timetable up until semester start, so all my three courses were overlapping! This was of course a shame, but my tutor helped me finding new courses that did not overlap (also by using the course timetable browser, available through Uni Edinburgh).
registration_advice: Remember to double check that your courses are not overlapping by using the Course Timetable Browser https://browser.ted.is.ed.ac.uk/
academics_comments: I highly recommend to study abroad (even though admin stuff sucks). I especially recommend Edinburgh for nature- and pint-loving people!
course_level: I had two level 9 courses (Year 3) and one level 11 course (Year 4). The level was a bit lower than what I am used to at CPH, otherwise great.
teaching_comparison: No group work. All assignments were individual. Lectures were shorter and fewer. Lab work was not as independent compared to CPH.
courses_enrolled: Molecular & Synthetic Plant Biology 3 Molecular Microbiology 3 Bioinformatics 1
recommended_courses: I would definitely recommend Molecular & Synthetic Plant Biology 3!! Small course, enthusiastic professors and students, a lot of help, fun lab work. Great if you like plants! This was no doubt my favorite course.
unexpected_costs: My bike needed repair a few times :) I also went to the highlands quite a lot, so a lot of transportation.
cost_comparison: Rent was more expensive (but it was catered so food was included). Local public transportation is cheap
activities_available: So many. So many different clubs, socials, activities, societies. I was a part of the Uni Hillwalking Club, Fitness, Kickboxing and Feminist Society.
activities_recommended: Definitely the hillwalking club. If you like bouldering as well, join the mountaineering club and the bouldering in the Pleasance fitness center. I would also recommend the Fungi Society. There is a lot of societies for bands as well (music).
weekend_recommendations: The highlands! Explore all the great Munroes (mountains) of Scotland, go to Ceilidh (folk dance), dance in general, drink pints, explore Edinburgh, go to Glasgow or Manchester. Visit all the cute small book shops. Go to Arthurs Seat, Dean Village, Stockbridge, the Pentlands, Morningside.
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: Join societies.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The scots are very welcoming and kind! And funny.
top3_advice: Bring good footwear (walking boots) Join a society / club Use the University libraries (especially Law and Nucleus library)
other_useful_info: Admin sucks, but you'll survive
most_rewarding: Walking in the mountains and forests with friends.
greatest_challenge: In the beginning when you miss your friends! And of course exams.
other_comments: Go go go

crucial_aspects: I've always wanted to go to Edinburgh to study as it's a really lovely city and campus. I also wanted to go to an English speaking country

crucial_aspects: I wanted to study in an English speaking country and in a big city with public transportation and cultural offers.
overall_comments: I was really nervous before going to Edinburgh but I'm really glad I did it and despite also being a challenging experience, I ended up having a really good time and enjoying my stay. Edinburgh is a really great city and the University of Edinburgh is a great place to study.
info_ease: The staff at the Visiting Student Office was really helpful and good at keeping you updated on the exchange and studying process. If you had any questions, the Visiting Student Office was always happy to help.
arrival_assistance: The first week of the semester was a welcome week, where you had the opportunity to get to know the different offers at the university and get involved in the different societies. There aren't many mandatory events, so it's up to you to seek out the information. Also most of the social events for the Erasmus Society is ticketed and sell out somewhat quickly, so I would recommend buying tickets to these beforehand. Although, I didn't participate in many of the welcome week events, I still felt like I had all the information I needed by just staying updated on the Facebook page for visiting students, the university's website etc. I would recommend downloading the university app to get an overview of the events during the welcome week.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I was really nervous before going to Edinburgh but I'm really glad I did it and despite also being a challenging experience, I ended up having a really good time and enjoying my stay. Edinburgh is a really great city and the University of Edinburgh is a great place to study.
registration_process: The course registration itself was pretty straightforward and the University of Edinburgh guides you through the process. I think it's first come, first served so I recommend sending your application off as soon as possible and be aware of any restrictions from UCPH and the University of Edinburgh by reading the pre-requisites for the courses.
registration_help: Yes, the course finder at the university of Edinburgh website, guides and the visiting student office.
registration_success: I got the courses however do beware of timetable clashes. Also, I only got my final timetable two weeks into the semester, so I missed the first week of some of my courses but in the end it wasn't really a problem.
registration_advice: I found the registration for courses pretty straightforward and the University of Edinburgh was good at making me aware of course requirements such as how to sign-up for art and design courses. Obviously, take the courses you find interesting but I do recommend reading up on the lecture hours and assessments of the courses you're interested in as I know some visiting students ended up with an overwhelming amount of uni work.
academics_comments: I was really nervous before going to Edinburgh but I'm really glad I did it and despite also being a challenging experience, I ended up having a really good time and enjoying my stay. Edinburgh is a really great city and the University of Edinburgh is a great place to study.
course_level: I only ended up taking first and second year courses, so my fellow students were quite young. However, most of courses weren't related to my major at UCPH, so I didn't mind it being at a "lower level" as everything was quite new to me. I think the workload was around the same as UCPH, maybe a bit less and as I had two days off every week where I didn't have any lectures or seminars which I don't have at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: I had lectures which were pretty similar to the lectures at UCPH, but most courses also had seminars which were discussion based and quite different from the teaching I'm used to. At first, the seminars were a bit intimidating as they required a lot of active participating and speaking, but they are quite useful for asking questions and going more in-depth with the course work and all my teachers were really nice and helpful which made it a bit easier.
courses_enrolled: Topics in Popular Music What's Up Doc? Introducing Animation Studies Creating Edinburgh: The Interdisciplinary City
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed all of my courses. If you want to try something different and want to explore and learn about Edinburgh while studying, I recommend Creating Edinburgh.
unexpected_costs: The cost of living in Edinburgh is about the same as Copenhagen, however I did find most things a bit cheaper in Edinburgh like groceries and rent. Also, if you live in the city then Edinburgh is a pretty walkable city and you don't really need a monthly bus pass. Also, coffee is a lot of cheaper which was a pleasant surprise.
cost_comparison: See answer above.
activities_available: There are so many societies at the University of Edinburgh, so there are plenty of opportunities for being social and meeting people.
activities_recommended: I recommend ESN, the scandi society and the board game society.
weekend_recommendations: I recommend going on trips with ESN and ISTours as these are for visiting students and are somewhat affordable. Scotland is beautiful. I didn't go myself but I heard really good things about Isle of Skye. Also Glasgow is great and very easy to get to by bus or train.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy. Edinburgh is not that different from Copenhagen and the Scots are really friendly and polite.
socializing_tips: I personally didn't socialize much the local students as I mainly spent my time with other visiting students, but you can definitely meet local students by getting involved in the societies.
cultural_challenges: Everyone is really polite, so you will constantly be saying thank you, excuse me and please and you have to queue for the bus and say thank you to the bus driver when you exit.
culture_appreciated: Edinburgh is a really pretty city and Scotland is so picturesque.
top3_advice: A bit cliche but: Relax - I was really nervous about everything, but it all worked out and everyone I met was really nice. Don't spend all your time studying - Obviously, you're there to study but try to also find time to enjoy Edinburgh and explore Scotland.
other_useful_info: If you have any questions or is struggling, just reach out to the University of Edinburgh as they have so many offers and is always eager to help. Also, it can get really windy and cold in Scotland so bring warm clothes.
most_rewarding: Getting to live in Edinburgh. I really loved it.
greatest_challenge: Feeling a bit lonely at times and not knowing anybody, but I still had a great time.
other_comments: No :))

crucial_aspects: It was crucial that it was an English-speaking country so that I was able to communicate eaily with people in and outside class while still being challenged on an English academic level. Furthermore, it was an advantage that it was possible to get the erasmus grant when studying in Edinburgh as it helped a bit economically.
info_ease: It was as easy as it could possibly be I would say - the University itself was good at offering information through e-mail communication and so, and offering assistance if worried or in doubt.
arrival_assistance: I recieved the possibility of joining a zoom(or so)-meeting with a little presentation about and introduction to University life with a possibility of questions. Also, there were several welcoming events which you could join via an app on your phone such as 'get to know each other' and a 'showing around campus' that was a bit helpful when arriving at a place where you have never been before.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration itself was easy because I just had to either participate in a welcoming online call or show up at the counter of the receiving student office. After that, I just had to show up to classes in which we were registrated every time with signature.
registration_help: The office for recieving students at my college (College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences) were always helpful with answering e-mails or you could show up in person after booking a meeting even though they were quite busy and you might have to wait a week or so for an answer.
registration_success: There was a lot of things that was difficult to find out through the online registration before arriving in Edinburgh and took a lot of time. I didn't even know my classes before arriving and starting at the University and couldn't recieve many of my first priorities courses, but as soon as it was finalized (after a period where everyone needs to be in contact with the same people who have to contorl your choice of classes) everything was fine and easy - although it was frustrating within the first two weeks.
registration_advice: Be patient, you might not have an overview ready for all of your classes before arriving but you will figure it out eventually and people are always very helpful although they are busy.
course_level: It was a mix of levels that i recieved though my courses. Some where first year classes which was interesting because I chose different causes than what I knew from home and practiced my academic English a lot, even though the level was a bit below where I am in my studies. Others were very challenging academically which I learned a lot from and were very happy to be a part of.
teaching_comparison: The two institutions have a lot in common - for example very intersting, skilled professors. But there was a bit more mixing of class types with both big lectures (where the professor is the only one speaking), smaller seminars where it is a lot of discussion between professor and students and lastly tutorials that are even smaller groups of students with becoming-professors. Also, the classes were often only one hour long which made it a bit more superficial but also more dynamic in the everyday school life.

recommended_courses: Scottish Literature 2B and Poetry, Politics and Place were especially giving.

cost_comparison: Food and living (drinks) were a bit mroe expensive than expected.

activities_recommended: Film society, hill hiking society and the Pleasence Sport Complex
weekend_recommendations: Go to the Scottish Highlands (it is amazing) and take some trips to Glasgow by bus.

socializing_tips: Join a society or two, maybe find a private housing to live in with other students (that was helpful for me).
cultural_challenges: Nothing in particular.
culture_appreciated: The kindness, the welcoming attitude and a bit less stress than in Copenhagen.
top3_advice: Join a society, go to the Scottish Highlands (and Glasgow) and use the unviersity's spaces for studying/reading/doing assesments/drinking with your friends.

crucial_aspects: a high academic level at the university the university had an international outlook (e.g. embraced and included international students)
info_ease: Very easy
arrival_assistance: was connected to a member of staff at the university (who e.g. did an introduction for the new students in his group)
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You could pick up to 10 courses from their couse catalogue and sent them in to the university ranked(check the prerequisites!). You then got put into three (or the amount needed to make a total of 30 ECTS) and when the semester started there was a two week period where you could request courses changes if needed
registration_help: A course catalogue with descriptions and time tables of all the available courses + an email you could write to if one needed help (I didn't use this)
registration_success: Mostly successful – there were two courses that I would have liked more to have gotten into but they were filled when I requested a change. Overall, I ended up being very happy with the courses I had though
registration_advice: Keep your expectations low – but if there is a course you really won't you might have to be insistent on e.g. sending in requests for a course change; there are changes all the time over the two week period
course_level: I ended up having to take 1st- and 2nd-year courses only (I'm studying Danish so my pre-requisites to courses were limited and therefore limited the number of courses available to me) but generally I found the level lower than I'm used to. At the same time, I found that you could easily self-adjust the level e.g. through recommended extra reading and the teachers were very open to giving you extra material etc.
teaching_comparison: The number of hours in a week was about the same but was (instead of two- or three hours long) all limited to 50 minutes of teaching and therefore more spread out throughout the week, e.g having two lectures of one hour each on two different days, instead of one two hour lecture. Also, I had so-called 'tutorials' where a small group of students (8-10) sat down with a teacher each week to discuss the week's reading and topic. This was very rewarding
courses_enrolled: Morality and Value Scottish Literature 2A Migration, Diaspora, exile: the politics of representation
recommended_courses: if you are a humanities student, take a course at the Scottish Studies Institute (e.g. Scottish literature or Scottish studies)
unexpected_costs: If you want to join a university sports team (or other students' associations), this will easily become very expensive (often you will need a gym membership in addition to the cost to the association itself)
cost_comparison: I spent very little money on course books/materials as almost all them were available online
activities_available: All sorts (I don't have the overview) – but I was personally part of the Badminton club with weekly training
activities_recommended: A sports team is fun – also lots of the associations arrange events open to all students throughout the semester
weekend_recommendations: explore the many nature areas near the city – also, the Highlands are beautiful but can be harder to get to (there are lots of tours though, e.g. through the Erasmus Student Organization)
culture_adjustment: It is a very international university and city in general so it is easy to meet other international students for example but harder to find and meet 'true Scots' – also, I found it quite difficult to connect to other students outside of my courses (e.g. no Friday-bars as I'm used to back home)
cultural_challenges: Nothing was particularly hard but I did have to practice saying 'please' and 'thank you' much more often than I'm used to
culture_appreciated: I enjoyed the pub culture and how willing students were to talk in both the lectures and in classes in general
top3_advice: It might seem like everyone is having the most fun all the time (going out, making so many new friends etc.) but remember to listen to yourself and rest when you need to; a night in with your roommates can be just as fun and memorable as a night out Be open to talking to anyone and don't be afraid to strike up a conversation; there are so many interesting and different people in the world Try to be realistic about what's possible: there are so many possibilities available to you and it's impossible to do everything, try to find a balance between socialising and studying, striking up new friendships and calling your friends back home (I know it's hard to don't beat yourself up if it doesn't succeed all the times)
other_useful_info: it's impossible to do all the things available to you so try to pick a couple of the ones you find the most interesting (e.g. a student organization) and cultivate these
most_rewarding: you get to really push yourself and your boundaries and I found a whole new level of independence and here through self-confidence
greatest_challenge: while life living abroad can be really intense and full of new people and new experiences, it can also be quite lonely and I felt at times cut off from my friends and family back home; it can be challenging trying to both establish new relations and keeping up with you loved ones back home Having people visit is really nice but can also be time-consuming and make you miss home so much more so try to find a balance that fit your needs

overall_comments: I have had a wonderful stay overall and would highly recommend anyone to study abroad in Edinburgh if they are given the change. That said, it is an expensive city (country) to live in and the heating bills were shockingly high which meant we couldn't afford having heat on during the cold periods. In terms of the actual studies, I had hoped for more teachings since I only had 6 hours a week for 10 weeks. In Copenhagen I am used to 8 hours for 14 weeks and, considering the money other students pay to study here, I believe you'd be in your good right to expect more.
