crucial_aspects: One of the most important aspects for me was the language and academic opportunities. I am personally very interested in further studying or working abroad someday, why it seemed like an exceptional opportunity to go to England. Likewise, I wanted to be able to experience a different approach to the academics and I wanted to expand my social network.
info_ease: The Erasmus team at Kent were very helpful with most issues, questions or inquiries. They were also fairly quick to respond to emails, although it could take a little longer at times. However, some things were not stated explicitly anywhere, so you had to spend some time to search for some things on Kent's website. The majority of information is also available of KU's website. The only thing that was a bit unsure, was the information concerning covid, particularly the covid-rules for arrival.
arrival_assistance: None. This should have been better and more organised.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: The registration process took some time because you needed approval of several documents, which took time. Both KU and Kent were pleasant to be in contact with during this process. You may discover a lot of useful information on 'Udlandsrejser' on KU's website. Further, don't hesitate to contact the Erasmus team at Kent as they will help to guide you through the process as well.
registration_help: Email - KU and Kent. And information on both their websites.
registration_success: Three of my four modules were approved. The Erasmus Teams sent me a list of available modules from which I could select the last one.
registration_advice: Don't hesitate to contact the Erasmus team or KU. They will gladly help you.
course_level: Personally, I thought it was the same level as in KU - maybe a little easier. But I should also note, that I am fluent in English. I heard that some fellow exchange students found the language a little challenging. I had four seminars and four lectures each week. The seminars and lectures are only an hour long, so it is shorter than at KU.
teaching_comparison: Because the seminars were shorter, there was less time to discuss and go over the material. So it was up to you to read most of it on beforehand. The professors, on the other hand, expect you to have completed the readings and to participate in the seminars. Another difference was the exams. They vary from module to module, but I had a lot of essays which was different from the 4 hour exams we have at KU.
courses_enrolled: Law and International Development Environmental Law International Human Rights in Context Privacy, Data Protection and Cybersecurity
recommended_courses: Privacy, Data Protection and Cybersecurity was by far my favourite module. It is very relevant and is something that keeps transforming as the world develops. I also have a personal interest in this area, why I found it even more interesting. All the other courses were also decent and the professors were competent. However, International Law and Development was not very law oriented.
unexpected_costs: Nothing. Just be aware that public transport in England is quite expensive.
cost_comparison: It was what I expected. In general less expensive than Denmark. The accommodation was quite expensive, but it is possible to get a cheaper place on campus.
activities_available: University of Kent has a lot of societies. Don't be afraid to join them! They are very sociable and you meet a lot of new people!
activities_recommended: Societies!
weekend_recommendations: It is easy to travel a lot of places from Kent as there is a train station a coach station near by. It is about 50 minutes from London, which is definitely worth a trip. Otherwise, I would recommend exploring the Kent area (by the coast), Brighton, Cambridge or Oxford.
culture_adjustment: I have relatives in England and know the country and culture quite well. So I found fit quite easy to adjust.
socializing_tips: Join societies - this is definitely the place to meet people. Otherwise, talk and socialise with you flatmates (if you live on campus) and reach out to other international/exchange students.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness.
top3_advice: Be open-minded Don't be afraid to approach people Be positive
other_useful_info: Some students, especially first-year students, will be likely be younger than you. However, don't be put off by this. The majority of them are incredibly friendly, and suddenly age doesn't seem to matter.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people, learning a lot of new things about myself and gaining new knowledge.
greatest_challenge: Balancing the work-load and social life. And dealing with a messy kitchen at times.

crucial_aspects: The possibilities to build a social life in the host country (possibilities for joining societies, for sharing accommodation with others, etc.). That I was able to speak the language (english), so that it was easier for me to "get around" The courses available - that there were at least some of them I found interesting
info_ease: There was a lot of information available, but it was a bit difficult to keep track of everything, because there was actually so much information. But it was definitely possible to figure out.
arrival_assistance: I collected my key to my accommodation at the reception and was directed to my house. We had gotten some e-mails about different social events in the beginning of terms (both in person and online) which I attended, but otherwise I was pretty much "left to myself", and had to go out and meet people etc.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: The course registration process was a bit frustrating because we were told VERY late in the process which courses we could choose between, and we had not been told that we were supposed to wait to find courses available. So I looked at courses from the very beginning, and in the end I could only choose between maybe 12 courses out of all of them. So I had spent a lot of time choosing courses I was very exited about only to find out that they weren't available for exchange students that are only here for one term. Once the courses available were published, the process of choosing them was very easy.
registration_help: I could write on e-mail to the host university's "Erasmus-employees", and they could help me most of the time.
registration_success: There was only one of the courses that I finally chose that was not available/already full out of 4. I could choose another one instead.
registration_advice: I would advice you to ask the host university early on in the process, which courses will be available for just you (as an exchange student staying for maybe only one term), since this puts some restrictions on which courses you can choose between. Remember also to look at which term (autumn or spring) the course is available in, and for how long the course is taking place (some take place over both terms, which might make it impossible for you to choose it).
course_level: The level of courses was the same as in Copenhagen, but because of the different teaching style there were other expectations of you.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was different from that of UCPH. The classes were only 50 minutes long, so there wasn't much teaching. I think it was a bit short for class discussions etc. And the seminars were a lot of talking very briefly about the subject - not a review of the syllabus as we (often) do in Denmark. There were always a "seminar sheet" which you had to prepare for class containing some questions to discuss in class. But otherwise it was very brief (since there was also only 50 minutes).
courses_enrolled: Environmental Law Critical and Legal Reasoning Privacy, Data Protection and Cybersecurity Law Law and International Development
recommended_courses: I would recommend the course "Privacy, Data Protection and Cybersecurity Law" - a really cool course that surprised me a lot. The topics were really interesting and had a lot of ethical dilemmas to discuss in class.
unexpected_costs: You had to buy plates, cutlery, pans, pots etc. in the beginning, since the house was empty
cost_comparison: It was almost the same as in Denmark, maybe a little cheaper.
activities_available: There was a lot of societies you could join. There was singing, dancing, sports, academic interests etc. There were "global hangouts" for people from different cultures to meet each other.
activities_recommended: I would recommend joining any society - they do social stuff each week and there is a lot of people who study different things than yourself, and you find both exchange students and local students there.
weekend_recommendations: Go to some of the cities around Canterbury (Dover, Whitstable etc.) or to London or Cambridge which is also close by (1-2 hours away). Go to the city or to the woods nearby campus for a walk.
culture_adjustment: It was okay. But there are differences between England and Denmark, of course.
socializing_tips: Live with other students, join societies (!), join different groups on social media for exchange students or other groups of people.
cultural_challenges: Not anything really challenging.
culture_appreciated: There was a lot of parties and people were very social and a lot of fun.
top3_advice: Be open to getting to know people, join all the social events you can manage. Try not to have any specific expectations because things will often be different than exactly how you imagined it. Ask all the questions you need - there is a lot of help to get both from students who already know the place when you get there and from the administration and student-help.
other_useful_info: Canterbury is not a big city. But on the other hand, you get to live on campus and experience that. University of Kent is very multinational and there are people from really all around the world (both taking their whole degree or being there as exchange students), which I think was really great to experience.
most_rewarding: Of course the social part - you meet people from all around the world and spent a lot of time with them and go to parties and on trips etc. I have become much more confident in speaking in English.
greatest_challenge: It is always a bit challenging to go to a new country, live in a new place, study in a different language etc. all at once and without any family/friends from home nearby - it is possible to get a feeling that it is all a bit much/overwhelming. I also had some challenges understanding the way the exams/assessments work because it was different from the exams I have taken in Denmark. But as time went, I understood more and more what was expected of me. But it was difficult some of the time, I think.

weekend_recommendations: The whole of UK. If it wasn't for the weather the UK would be a very exotic place with its beaches, cliffs and nature in general. Further, the cities are the more American-like than any other cities in EU, such as London and Liverpool. Also visit Scotland, the treasure of UK. Very diverse country in terms of its cities. Go to Kent to see the UK you see in BBC News and in Harry Potter, of these small houses with small gardens and ugly cars.
culture_adjustment: UK is very much DK like, except the UK being more talkative, openminded and respectful. be ready for people talking to you at unexpected times.
socializing_tips: Join societies in aim to find mind a like people.
cultural_challenges: saying please at random times. Saying thank you to the bus driver was very weird for me.
culture_appreciated: The talkativenesses, the open-mindedness.
top3_advice: UK is expensive. Be mindfull of the fact you have to be openminded to meeting new people, even if they might not necessarily look like the typical people you hang out with back at home.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: being exposed to the talkativeness of UK.
greatest_challenge: Using the word please when ordering food.

crucial_aspects: Both academic opportunities, career opportunities, personal connection to the destination and explore new cultures meant a lot to me. Most important it was to study more music business related courses as these don't exist at university level in Denmark.
overall_comments: I enjoyed my time and stayed in London with family which was very important to me.
info_ease: It was a bit difficult but I let people know that I was new and their student coordinator Francoise was a big help
arrival_assistance: Student coordinators (Francoise was a big help to me)
arrival_comments: There was one intro meeting - besides that I had to let the teacher know I was and exchange student because I didn't know anything about their grading systemt, online systems (moodle) and so on.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I enjoyed my time and stayed in London with family which was very important to me.
registration_process: Very easy, it was just personal information that you had to fill out.
registration_help: Their student coordinators will help you with everything!
registration_success: Semi. The one I signed up for clashed with another course of mine but I luckily just found another one!
registration_advice: Patience. You might get tour timetable the same week as classes start.
academics_comments: I enjoyed my time and stayed in London with family which was very important to me.
course_level: I think the course were very easy which helped as I didn't know much about the subjects.
teaching_comparison: Easier to understand and less stressfull. I think sometimes, loads of people experience burnouts at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: - Sex Gender and Performance - Music Journalism, PRESS and PR - Music Marketing
recommended_courses: If in the music aspect, definitely - Music Journalism, PRESS and PR - Music Marketing. Or courses with Ben Horner who is an amazing teacher
unexpected_costs: I didn't have any unexpected costs and I lived off campus, but I do think that housing is more expensive than Denmark but food is cheaper.
cost_comparison: Train tickets were more expensive than I thought but luckily I lived for free with family. Food and eating out is less expensive than in Denmark.
activities_available: Sports, fitness and social gatherings. Like yoga with dogs
activities_recommended: Meet up with other danish people or meet up with people that have the same activity of preference as you
weekend_recommendations: London! Or the costs like Bath, Cornwall, Brighton and so on
culture_adjustment: Very easy as I do have family there. I can though be very tiring to talk english all the time but if you are lucky there will be other exchange students as well.
socializing_tips: Just go out and meet people. Others might be in the same boat as you.
cultural_challenges: Nothing else than that people in university in the uk are much younger than the average age in denmark.
culture_appreciated: the pubs!
top3_advice: Make an effort in getting to know people on and off campus Go explore elsewhere than Kent Let people know that you are an exchange student and that you are new.
other_useful_info: You don't have to stay or live in Kent. Try to get out of Canterbury as it is easy to just hang around campus. The UK is huge so make your stay worth the time.
most_rewarding: Getting to study courses that wasn't available in Denmark!
greatest_challenge: The transport. I lived in London and it was 4-5 hours travel but luckily only twice a week. It was expensive but I was productive on my train ride.
other_comments: GO!

crucial_aspects: I chose my study destination because of the courses at the host university and because of its location.
overall_comments: I really enjoyed my stay abroad. It was very enriching personally and academically.
info_ease: It was easy.
arrival_assistance: I attended a welcome event for international students. I received help by email concerning my courses and my student accommodation.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I really enjoyed my stay abroad. It was very enriching personally and academically.
registration_process: In the beginning it was a bit difficult to find the information, but after a while I got to know the system and I was pleased that the international administrative team was helpful and easy to get in touch with.
registration_help: Email with international administrators, on location help around the arrival time.
registration_success: I did not get the classes I planned from the beginning, but the classes I did register for turned out to be very interesting.
registration_advice: Take your time in the application phase to look into the details about courses, prerequisites etc.
academics_comments: I really enjoyed my stay abroad. It was very enriching personally and academically.
course_level: The level varied a lot. In some courses the level was low, but in others it was high and very inspiring.
teaching_comparison: We had less time in class/lectures in the UK. Classes were very short, but the teaching style was similar to that of UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Biodiversity WCON 3050 Migration and belonging SOCI755 Geography of development and the global south GEOG5007 Environmental Politics SOCI5250
recommended_courses: Environmental Politics and Migrantion and Belonging. Both courses were taught by very engaged professors and I learned a lot from them.
unexpected_costs: More expensive transportation than expected, cooking utilities, pillow/duvet
cost_comparison: Transportation
activities_available: A lot of different societies to enroll in. Not very political, but a lot of different hobbies (sports, cultural activities etc.)
activities_recommended: Free membership of Kent Sport for students living on campus
weekend_recommendations: Go to neirby villages, to the coast, to London, enjoy the hiking possibilities of UK
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: I mostly socialized with other international students, but student societies/clubs are good for any type of socializing. Be open!
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The diversity of people in the UK
top3_advice: Enjoy the green areas around campus. Enjoy sport facilities. Be curious about the university's progressive past - it still lives in the cracks.
other_useful_info: There is a wonderful garden that you can volunteer in. Living on campus comes with good facilities. Trains to London are expensive but it is worth the price to get to know London a bit
most_rewarding: Meeting wonderful new friends for life. Becoming a part of a new radical film club. Finding peace in my own company. Enjoying green areas around campus and finding local, sustainable options when grocery shopping.
greatest_challenge: Social uncertainty in the beginning, but it settled quickly.

crucial_aspects: I had always dreamed of studying in England because of a fascination with the country, its culture and its customs. I specifically chose Canterbury to see new areas of England, including some beautiful nature spots. Moreover, the university had a lot of different interesting law modules to choose from.
info_ease: It was very easy and I had no issues with it
arrival_assistance: There were plenty of information sent on e-mail, a reception, as well as different apps you could use
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was all quick and easy and happened online via an email
registration_help: As mentioned, there is a reception for all the dorms and all relevant emails are listed.
registration_success: They had made a mistake with letting me register for two classes that were overlapping so I had to change one of my modules but that process itself was easy and manageable
registration_advice: As mentioned, I would make sure that the dorm house is suitable to you. I would also make an effort with finding friends and joining all the many social events right away.
course_level: I thought the level was a lot lower than I am used to in Copenhagen.
teaching_comparison: Again, it was not as "concrete" as I am used to and involved a lot of discussions of people's personal opinions (not based on law). I would have liked it to be more to-the-point and factual.
courses_enrolled: 1) Privacy and Data Protection Law (LAWS9210), and 2) Commercial Credit (LAWS9070)
recommended_courses: I can only recommend the Privacy and Data Protection Law (LAWS9210). It was the one that gave the biggest academic outcome.
unexpected_costs: Because I struggled with the gas stove in the dorm kitchen, I did order and buy already-made food more than anticipated
cost_comparison: The dorm is a little expensive for what you get. Everything else was less expensive than expected.
activities_available: There were a myriad of clubs and activities to choose from - rugby, dancing of various kinds, swimming, tennis, french etc etc
activities_recommended: My biggest recommendation is to join as many of the welcome week social activities as possible. That is where I found almost all of my friends for the entire stay. Joining a society is of course also a great idea.
weekend_recommendations: I recommend taking trips to the following places: 1) Rye, 2) Dover, 3) Folkestone, 4) Whistable, 5) Seven Sisters Cliffs, 6) London, and 7) Bath.
culture_adjustment: It was easy as it is pretty similar to the Danish culture. However, I did miss some of the food from back home.
socializing_tips: Be yourself, be positive and open, and show your curiosity for them! Ask them questions about themselves
cultural_challenges: Mostly the food
culture_appreciated: The extrovertedness, humor, and politeness
top3_advice: 1) Make sure to attend as many events in the welcome week as possible, 2) Make sure that the accommodation is suitable to you, 3) Make sure to sign up for classes that you think you will actually find interesting and useful
other_useful_info: No, I don't think so.
most_rewarding: It was the wonderful people I met
greatest_challenge: Lack of proper and nutritious food and my flatmates not sharing my cleaning standard

crucial_aspects: My options were limited, but the bettering of my English speaking capabilities was a priority for me
info_ease: Pretty easy. The incoming exchanges team at Kent are really super
arrival_assistance: Again, the incoming exchanges team are really quick to reply and give solid advice and help
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was pretty intuitive. The module selection thing is a bit janky, but overall it's pretty good. The system seemed surprisingly up-to-date
registration_help: Again, I have to give kudos to the incoming exchanges team at Kent - they helped me with just about everything
registration_success: They had some issues with certain courses not being formed, as they had a professor leave right before semester start, so that was a bit disappointing, but it is no fault of theirs really. Overall, I was relatively succesful
registration_advice: When in doubt, as the incoming exchanges team
course_level: The level was fine, but i would defer to my answer to the overall academic level.
teaching_comparison: It was relatively similar, but I would say that the teachers felt less qualified in certain aspects of the teaching. Still, they were really nice and relatively competent.
courses_enrolled: Commercial Credit, Policing, and International Cultural Heritage Law
recommended_courses: Commercial Credit. It was pretty elementary but the teaching featured a lot of discussion which was pretty nice.
unexpected_costs: Not really any. The figures above do not accurately account for things such as social spending, as I would not include that as "other fees" given that they will vary heavily depending on the student in question.
cost_comparison: Not really any. Prices in the UK are comparable to Denmark, although everything is generally a little cheaper in the UK.
activities_available: All kinds of sports, clubs for just about everything, and they had societies for pretty much all nationalities where student not of said nationality could participate anyways. E.g., I went to several events with both the French and Spanish societies.
activities_recommended: Get involved with the nationality-based societies, as they generally have the most stuff planned.
weekend_recommendations: Go to London or any of the academic cities, e.g., Cambridge and Oxford, as the nightlife is great there. If you enjoy a beer, do partake in British pub culture, as that truly is a national treasure.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. The UK is not dissimilar to Denmark in terms of culture.
socializing_tips: Just get out there - people are really nice! Do go to the speedfriending event in the first week - it's an easy opening, as some of the local students participate as well
cultural_challenges: None really. It was just a bit annoying that people always say "how are you?" even when passing each other, but I was aware of that before I went there.
culture_appreciated: I thoroughly enjoyed pub culture
top3_advice: 1. Do not go for academic purposes. 2. Go to local pubs - even on weekdays for a couple at least. 3. Socialise with the locals and not just the other exchanges - this would also include the students doing a full master's
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: The cultural aspects, though centered around drinking (much like Danish culture), and language proficiency.
greatest_challenge: I had some unfortunate encounters with some of the other exchange students

crucial_aspects: Det var vigtigt for mig at opsøge et sted, hvor der var et internationalt miljø, interessante og relevante fag, en masse naturoplevelser i nærheden, tæt på en by og gode transportmuligheder.
info_ease: Universitetet og tutorerne var gode til at vejlede de studerende til at finde information angående ens Erasmus-ophold, universitetets infrastruktur og studiemiljøet. På den anden side er det Østrigske skolesystem ret indviklet og bureaukratisk, hvilket gjorde det svært at søge informationer uden hjælp fra de lokale.
arrival_assistance: Jeg modtog en studiemappe med diverse dokumenter og kort over universitetet. Derudover blev jeg oprettet på universitetets intranet, hvor informationer om mine fag lå. Desværre var mange af oplysningerne og informationerne kun på tysk.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Der var alt for mange mails som man skulle forholde sig til
registration_help: Mailadresser til mine kontaktpersoner på institut für kulturwissenschaft på universiteter, og whatsapp-grupper med tutorerne
registration_success: Selve registreringen på intranettet var ikke svært, og jeg tilmeldte mig de hold som jeg havde udvalgt. Desværre var der ikke så mange relevante fag for etnologi der foregik på engelsk
registration_advice: Man skal være sikker på at de ects point som fagene indeholder er af relevant karakter. Jeg tilmeldte mig introfagene i starten af mit ophold, hvilket man ville modtage ét ects point for men det kunne ikke godtages af KU. Derfor var jeg nødt til at rokere mine fag.
course_level: Jeg havde nogle fag på BA niveau og få andre på MA niveau. Der var ikke den største akademiske forskel.
teaching_comparison: Jeg synes at undervisningen på Klagenfurt Universitet var mere overfladisk end på KU. Derudover var meget af undervisningen på tværs af fag bygget op på 50% teoretisk/metodisk/faghistorisk grundlag og 50% var studerende præsentationer. På den ene side var det spændende at arbejde med præsentationer da de ledte op til diskussioner men på den anden side følte jeg ikke at den undervisningen var dybdegående nok til at jeg følte mig helt sikker i, hvordan jeg skulle strukturere og lede mine præsentationer og diskussioner. Derudover virkede det til at undervisernes forventninger til de studerende ikke var af samme niveau som på KU
courses_enrolled: 140.034/22S Sociology: Business and Society 551.321/22S Early Thesis Forum: Culture 551.336/22S Advanced Topics in Literature and Culture Studies: Hitting the Floor? - Filmic Representations of Queer and Alternative Masculinities in Sports 170.050/22S NGOs and Visual Communication 120.397/22S Rethinking borders in the age of migration: education, conflict and post-conflict case-studies
recommended_courses: NGOs and Visual Communication. Jeg synes dette fag var super spændende og givende, hvis man gerne vil have en teoretisk indsigt i NGOer
unexpected_costs: Intet
cost_comparison: Intet
activities_available: Sportsklubber og foreninger, queer-foreninger, haveforeninger, sprogkurser
activities_recommended: Udnyt at du bor så centralt i Europa! Rejs til Slovenien, Italien, Kroatien og rundt i Østrig. Det er super billigt og super nice. Derudover er der den smukke Wörthersee som jeg benyttede mig af i alle de varme måneder
weekend_recommendations: Wörthersee, Vandreture i Kärnten og weekendture til Ljubljana
culture_adjustment: Jeg synes ikke der var de store kulturelle forskelle mellem Østrig og Danmark. Klagenfurt er en lille by, og folk virkede måske af denne årsag mere venlige. På den anden side skulle jeg vende mig til at det var et mere konservativt sted at opholde mig end det jeg er vant til fra København.
socializing_tips: Tag på MacMullens bar.
cultural_challenges: Den østrigske konservatisme.
culture_appreciated: De er super høflige og ydmyge
top3_advice: 1.Vær forberedt på en lang ansøgningsproces og konstant mailkorrospondence mellem dig og universitetet 2. Der er ikke en særlig god kommunikation mellem KU og Klagenfurt Universitet 3. Du kommer til at bo i et af de smukkeste områder i Europa
other_useful_info: Ha' en god kontakt med studievejledningen
most_rewarding: Mine venskaber, rejser og naturoplevelser
greatest_challenge: At rejse tilbage til Danmark

crucial_aspects: Jeg ønskede at være i et land der grænsede tæt op af andre. Jeg fandt det interesant om man kunne se hvordan de forskellige kulturer flød sammen. Derudover befandt universitetet sig i et meget naturskønt område, hvilket jeg synes var tiltrækkende da jeg er meget ude i naturen og nyde den.
overall_comments: Selve opholdet har været rigtig fint. Der har været nogle problemer med kommunikation mellem mit hjemmeuniversitet og udvekslingsuniversitetet, der har gjort det til tider meget besværligt.
info_ease: Klagenfurt universitet havde lavet et hæfte med alt information, dette fik jeg dog først udleveret 4 dage før min afrejse. Det var derfor en smule besværligt at indskaffe alt nødvendig information. man skal forberede sig på, at Østrig er et meget bureaukratisk land, så der kommer til at gå nogle timer med dokument udfyldning, kommune besøg og diverse andet. Klagenfurt universitet sender en masse mails, det kan være lidt overskueligt at holde styr på, og de sender nogle gange også mails forkert og sender mails som ikke vedkommer en selv. Hvis man kan holde styr på de mails er de rigtige gode og giver en masse information.
arrival_assistance: Første skoledag kom man hen på skolen og fik udleveret et dokument, som man skal benytte sig til dokumentere sin fysiske tilstedeværelse (som man skal have sendt inden til universitetet). Her blev jeg mødt af nogle af medarbejderne fra det internationale kontor. Der kunne man stille spørgsmål, hvis man havde nogle.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Selve opholdet har været rigtig fint. Der har været nogle problemer med kommunikation mellem mit hjemmeuniversitet og udvekslingsuniversitetet, der har gjort det til tider meget besværligt.
registration_process: Da vi ankom modtag vi vores studiekort. Det gik umiddelbart ganske glidningsfrit.
registration_help: Der er flere kontorer der er villige til hjælpe, eller bliver du også tildelt en buddygroup, hvor du kan spørge de andre / en der allerede går på universitetet om hjælp,
registration_success: Deres system med at registere for kurser er lidt bøvlet. Du skal betale nogle penge før du kan registrere dig, men du kan ikke betale de penge før du har registreret dig. Jeg kontaktede det internationale kontor og de fixede det for mig. Husk at holde øje med hvornår de åbner for tilmeldning. Deres kursuskatalog kommer oftest ret sent. Jeg kiggede på de gamle kursuskataloger og blev inspireret af dem, det var dog ikke alle kurser jeg ønsker der blev oprettet.
registration_advice: Hold øje med kursuskataloget. Deres kurser på engelsk er rigtig fine og alle snakker engelsk der er til at forstå.
academics_comments: Selve opholdet har været rigtig fint. Der har været nogle problemer med kommunikation mellem mit hjemmeuniversitet og udvekslingsuniversitetet, der har gjort det til tider meget besværligt.
course_level: Jeg havde både BA og MA kurser. Jeg synes ikke at det akademiske niveau var højere end KU. Du skal forberede dig på, at deres kurser har lave ECTS point og du derfor nok kommer til at gå mere i skole end du er vant til hjemmefra. Der er dog ikke den tungeste læsebyrde og det hele foregår ret stille og roligt, så alle kan følge med.
teaching_comparison: Jeg havde ret små fag hvor der ikke var så mange indskrevne. Det var meget dialog baseret undervisning, hvor der forventes at du byder ind og hvor du typisk holder et oplæg i hver af dine fag.
courses_enrolled: SE PF 8.3 Rethinking borders in the age of migration: education, conflict and post-conflict case-studies (120.397) SE NGOs and Visual Communication (170.050) SE Sociology: Business and Society (140.034) AG Early Thesis Forum: Culture (551.321) SE Advanced Topics in Literature and Culture Studies: Hitting the Floor? - Filmic Representations of Queer and Alternative Masculinities in Sports (551.336)
recommended_courses: Jeg kan klart anbefale de kurser jeg har taget. De var rigtig fine planlagte og undervisning var både lærerig og i godt selskab med underviseren.
unexpected_costs: Ikke nogen
cost_comparison: Huslejen var meget lavere end forventet.
activities_available: Klagenfurt Universitet går meget op i sport og de har et tilknyttet fitness, som du kan købe et billigt medlemskab hos. Derudover har de et stort katalog med forskellige sports hold du kan gå på. Der er også mange muligheder for at finde forskellige WhatsApp grupper med f.eks. hiking eller andet. Der er flere steder at gå i byen - det er meget a la A-bar stemning de steder.
activities_recommended: Tag ud og oplev naturen. Brug Østrigs placering som en rejsemulighed. Jeg rejste meget rundt - til både Kroatien, Slovakiet, Italien, Slovenien og flere steder i Østrig. Der er mange muligheder med Flixbus som er rigtig billige.
weekend_recommendations: Rejs!
culture_adjustment: Meget. Jge følte ikke det store kulturelle chok og tilpassede mig hurtigt til hverdagen.
socializing_tips: Tag ud og drik kaffe, brug de loade områder, tag på universitetet og læs.
cultural_challenges: Ingen.
culture_appreciated: Deres hjælpsomhed og velkommenlighed.
top3_advice: Spar penge sammen, husk at more dig og brug ikke alt din tid på skolearbejde, snak i timerne, det får du sindsygt meget ud af.
other_useful_info: Nej
most_rewarding: At få en masse nye venner og bekendtskaber
greatest_challenge: At komme igennem alt dokumentation og kommunikere med to universiteter på samme tid.
other_comments: Nej.

info_ease: Very easy
arrival_assistance: I was allocated a German buddy who helped me with everything from local guidance to logistics and administrative errands. A very good experience
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

registration_success: Fully
registration_advice: Don't stress too much about it, it will be resolved on the spot
academics_comments: I truly emnjoyed my stay there, I had indeed a wonderful time. However, German beuraucracy, lack of digitlisation, poor housing situation as well as the administrative procedure at KU brings down the average experience.
course_level: Think they were at the right level. Just the right amount of difficulty and challenging and developing in other ways than at KU
teaching_comparison: Smaller groups, more interactive, more active participation, more presentations and more discussions
courses_enrolled: JUR-16170 International law in practice SLI-21100 GO-Konstanz German intensive A2.1 INT-10770 Regional policy in the European Union: Policies, institutions and public INT-10830 Terrorism and Law POL-31590 The political consequences of technological change POL-31610 Workplace ties: The role of social relationships in organizations

cost_comparison: Food and housing less expensive. Travelling more expensive
activities_available: Opera, theatre, orchestra, karaoke, skiing, snowshoe-hiking, normal hiking, trips to surrounding places in the alps
activities_recommended: Karaoke, cultural ticket and sport facilities were great fun! And get around and explore the alps and the lake! Take a biketrip around the lake! Get a Deutschland-ticket and travel around in Germany. And use the Interrail-pass provided by Erasmus sustainable travel
weekend_recommendations: Take a trip around the lake! Or rent a car and drive to Liechtenstein!
culture_adjustment: Think the poor digitisation and the lack of wifi and card payment was the hardest part.
socializing_tips: Sign up for the buddy-programme. Get involved in local sports clubs, choirs or workplaces
cultural_challenges: The lack of digital services.
culture_appreciated: Christmas markets, carnival, other outdoor activites. And overall more chill with alcohol
top3_advice: Sign up for the buddy programme! Participate in GO Konstanz! Be ready to bring cash and to print a lot of stuff
other_useful_info: Nothing that I can come up with
most_rewarding: All the people I met and all the places I've seen

crucial_aspects: Good opportunities for learning Russian. The opportunity to (academically) learn more about a country/culture, which I had little previous knowlegde about.
info_ease: I found the host university's course system rather confusing, which was made worse by the fact that there were being made changes to the system, when I arrived. This made it difficult to find a course combination, which could actually work. Contact information was reasonably accessible.
arrival_assistance: I (and some of the others travelling from Denmark) spoke with department and exchange coordinators and attended an Erasmus intro meeting.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Many courses were, which were applied for in the spring, were no longer available. Other courses, which had been approved over the summer, had conflicting schedules. Some course schedules were also changed/decided in the first lessons. This meant that I (and the other students from Denmark) basically had to start from the beginning. This was very frustrating, because our OLA's had to be changed multiple times in the spring, before they were approved, which no seems wholly meaningless.
registration_help: Department coordinators, who responded very quickly during the registration weeks.
registration_success: Many courses were not an option. Also, the process was so frustrating that at the end, it was more important (to me) that the registration got done, than which courses I would have.
registration_advice: Spend as little time as possible on the OLA in the spring. It is almost completely useless. Look at some courses over the summer, but don't put in too much effort, before you arrive.
course_level: The academic level of the courses was very low. Compared to Danish standards it was like gymnasiet/(high school). The exception was the Russian courses, which had very good quality.
teaching_comparison: There were different teaching styles in the Russian courses, but I would rank both on the same level as UCPH. However, the other courses did not compare to UCPH in terms of academic level, and often seemed like opinion and basic knowlegde rather than the product of academic study.
courses_enrolled: Russian as Foreign 3rd level (B1) Part 1 Russian as foreign language (Level A2 1) Media Representation, Ethics, Memory and the Holocaust Historical Narratives in Propaganda: Cases studies of Russia and Ukraine Environment and Sustainable Development in the Baltic Sea Region International Media Law A History of Latvian Culture: 20th Century
recommended_courses: Russian as Foreign 3rd level (B1) Part 1 (good quality teaching) Russian as foreign language (Level A2 1) (good quality teaching (especially for getting grammar into your spoken language))
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Transport was much less expensive.
activities_available: I would simply say that there was something for everyone.
activities_recommended: I would suggest participating in speed-friending or similar events, because being part of one or more groups of Erasmus students will be very good for having further non-academic experiences during the exchange.
weekend_recommendations: The are museums, cinemas, cultural events, other nearby towns, relatively nearby beaches if the weather allows for it, Tallinn and Vilnius are also possible weekend destinations.
culture_adjustment: It was ok. There are some cultural differences in terms of communication at the university (both regarding exams as mentioned above but also regarding the death of one of our educators during the semester, which has never been officially communicated).
socializing_tips: I mainly ended up socialising with Erasmus students
cultural_challenges: There are some cultural differences in terms of communication at the university (both regarding exams as mentioned above but also regarding the death of one of our educators during the semester, which has never been officially communicated).
culture_appreciated: I particularly enjoyed the culinary experiences, the nature, and some museums.
top3_advice: Don't spend a lot of time on the courses for the OLA, before registration week. Focus on the cultural and social opportunities, while you are abroad.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: The cultural and social experiences.
greatest_challenge: Communication regarding exams.

crucial_aspects: It was relevant for my regional studies due to the region and the language options, and I was motivated to see this regions political, societal and geographical climate.
info_ease: Not that easy, it was unclear how to access some certain information, especially within the universoty itself sometimes, but it did not ruin the experience though. I felt the erasmus community info was more clear and reachable.
arrival_assistance: administation at uni, erasmus network
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: it was comprehensible mostly, but some practical things were unclear, so I had to call several times.
registration_help: certain admin. for exchange, asking former students who were abroad the year before.
registration_success: not great, almost all of them were removed, so I had to choose random ones that had to make sense for my studies back home
registration_advice: Research in advance and dont be afraid to ask for help! and ask a former student who was abroad from the same course as yourself,
course_level: I hope it makes sense when I say that the academic approach here was more "quantity over quality" in the sense that each course only had max 6 ECTS comapred to back home which offeered 15 ECTS per one course. teaching_comparison: More authoritative and stricter and more traditional. Less group work, innovation and interaction, and more old-school ways of teaching. More repetition though, which actually worked better.

cost_comparison: Exp: Certain grocery items like nuts, fruits etc. Some restaurant/cafe visits Some beauty products Beauty service like hairdressers etc Less exp: Second-hand Clothes Prepared food at the grocers Fish Meat like beef and poultry Public transport monthly card Cinema visits (due to student discount)
activities_available: Many fun erasmus events arranged by the erasmus network - local, athletic and social Local events like folk-dancing, cultural events Good downtown activities like bars etc Museums, churches, exhibits Amazing theatre productions!! like ballet and opera etc
activities_recommended: Attend ESN events - great for meeting new people, getting friends and networking Attend local events like exhibits, local festivals and celebrations - to come closer with the culture Museums and important historical/memorial places Cinemas and theatres - be close to local and cherished art
weekend_recommendations: Attend ESN events - great for meeting new people, getting friends and networking Attend local events like exhibits, local festivals and celebrations - to come closer with the culture Museums and important historical/memorial places Cinemas and theatres - be close to local and cherished art ALSO VISIT national parks and nature nearby Go to other cities or towns nearby to not only see the capital and main cities

greatest_challenge: remaining calm under stressful situations, dealing with anxiety, trying to stay happy/positive during really grey and cold days, dealing with unfamiliar situations and not knowing what to do, finding a balance between academic and social life and also self-relaxation, getting used to a different academic system

It was also important, that I would be able to understand the language in what they would be teaching. I also contacted the university early on to hear about their module offers, as I had questions to what the possibilities were regarding master modules and also just guidance. They were very kind, and helped as much as they could remotely.

I had hoped to have more face-to-face teaching and possibilities to engage with students from England. I also had an annoying experience with the student service. At least I had the opportunity to meet a lot of great people, both locals and other international students! These will definitely be there for life!

Also, it would have helped to have had the meeting for erasmus students at the beginning of the first week, instead of in the end. Then, we could have been guided to the vital parts of the freshers week at out parent school.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: It has been great to experience something else. The situation with Covid-19 has been inconvenient anyway, even though we hoped for it to be different this year. registration_process: You wish for modules worth more credits than you can have. Then they assess whether or not you are qualified for these modules, and enroll you in all modules they think you qualify for. Before semesterstart, you will have to either enroll in more modules in order to have enough credits or deregister for some modules - perhaps some of them are at the same time.
registration_help: A module catalogue and the student service at my parent school-
registration_success: I got registered in all modules I wanted, even though not all first priorities.
registration_advice: Make your research on avaliable modules and be open-minded, as you will have to choose from last years module catalogue. Also, be aware of what modules you get enrolled in, so you can change or deselect or select more modules if needed.
academics_comments: It has been great to experience something else. The situation with Covid-19 has been inconvenient anyway, even though we hoped for it to be different this year. I had hoped to have more face-to-face teaching and possibilities to engage with students from England. I also had an annoying experience with the student service. At least I had the opportunity to meet a lot of great people, both locals and other international students! These will definitely be there for life!
course_level: It varies a lot. The two modules in which had to work hardest was a master module and level 1 module. I would say the level 1 module was not proportional for it's level, otherwise it should have been worth more credits.
teaching_comparison: It's hard to tell, as I didn't get to have much teaching due to corona. I had one in-person seminar, one in-person lecture and one online lecture. They used self-studies more than at UCPH. The style of teaching is somewhat similar.
courses_enrolled: Programming for the Web Traditional Alcoholic Beverages Glacial Landforms and Processes Creating Alternative Futures GIS and Environment
recommended_courses: Creating Alternative Futures is highly recommended, as you engage in a critical discussion of society, and think about alternatives in a world of change. This is about socialism, civil empowerment and structures of power and how to change them. GIS and Environment is great for practising your GIS-skills and develop your knowledge on physical geography and mapping. These are really good modules, where you gain in-depth knowledge on the topic.
unexpected_costs: The socities at uni have different prices for memberships
cost_comparison: You just end up spending a lot of money on being with new friends and buying a bit of stuff for you to bring back.
activities_available: Everything...
activities_recommended: Darts! It's a lot of fun and the society is festive and everyone loves to drink a pint while playing. This is an authentic experience, and do yourself a favour and play in a tournament! It's truly one of my best memories, especially the bus drive home. It was just english chants and songs all the way.
weekend_recommendations: Go hikinh in the countryside. Also visit some major cities, Liverpool and Manchester are not far away, and York is a great place with a lot of history. Especially at christmas!
culture_adjustment: Quite easy.
socializing_tips: Dart society!
cultural_challenges: They party culture.. English people can behave really rude when drunk.
culture_appreciated: They are very polite.
top3_advice: Involve yourself in a society, participate in the icebreaker activities before the semester starts and get there early.
other_useful_info: All lectures and seminars end before christmas. Plan early what you want to do for christmas and new year's, a lot of people want to stay, but everyone is afraid no one is there, so make arrangements early on before people buy tickets home.
most_rewarding: Meeting locals and learning about cultures through other international students.
greatest_challenge: I had a lot of assements due within the same 3 weeks, which made it hard to actually gain in-depth knowledge. I just had to make it through.
other_comments: Go on exchange! It is such a good experience, and you learn a lot about yourself when you are challenged to establish in a foreign country.

I did not use any of them. You are also given a parent school and a personal tutor through them. That person is also their to help you.
arrival_comments: It was okay once I reach out. But there was a strick while I was their which affacted a lot of things. When I was in dought with some stuff about choosing modules or other things I just email or called Study Abord Office and they put me in contact who I should speak to. Or I simpel ask the teacher/lecture of the curtain module. They were all really helpfull once you asked,
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: I remember it as fine.
registration_help: You can find most on the University of Leeds webpage. But they also send you emails of 'Preparing to Study at the University of Leeds' with to-do lists, specfic deadlines etc. so just pay attention to your email.
registration_success: Not that successful as I was appling for some popular modules/classes outside my academic discipline. And when their is a lot of applicants they tent to choose student within the discipline.
registration_advice: I would give the advice if you really want specific classes to really make an effort in the motivation letter when you are doing the registering at University of Leeds. They really read it and choose you for the specific classes because of that. And if you do not get choosen for your first choices of classes it is okay. courses_enrolled: Religion in Modern Africa Sociology of Religion Academic English English Through Interpersonal Communication
recommended_courses: Choose want ever seems interessting and fun. And do not be afaird of the langague level you get use to it.
unexpected_costs: How much I use to travel on public transport
cost_comparison: The food and groceries are a bit expersive when you look at the quality of food. I choose to cook a lot to save money and not eat out as much as my friends did. Also the housing. It is more expersive then Copenhagen.
activities_available: Everything! Leeds has alot of Student Social Societies. Everything from any kind of sport to any time of culturel and social soceity, music, social, teacter, non-alcohol societies ect. ect. ect. They also have a gym on campus. And if you live around campus in a university accommodation it is for free to train there.
activities_recommended: Look at the Leeds University Union webpage and just sign up to all the Social Societies that you find interessting. It is the best way to find new friends especially British onces. And look for Student Activities and go to them. It is really the best way to get friends. Look for GO OUT GET ACTIVE. They arrange trips and the walking onces are really fun and a good for you to go to the national parks for a day trip.
weekend_recommendations: Go to the national parks such as Yorkshire Dales and Lake District. It is fun to get a break from the city and see the mountains. Manchester is really close and cheap to travel to if you are interessed.
culture_adjustment: Really easy. First of all because you are just around students from everywhere. Some for a one semester exhange, some for a whole degree, some are local Britis, some are international. Second of all if is different from Denmark, but still Western Europe so not that different again.
socializing_tips: Be a memeber of Social Societies and participate in Student Activites! The more is better, especially in the start of the semester. You don't know which ones really fit you, so just turn up to alot of them in the start and then you can always be less active if you get too busy or they are not the once for you. Social Societies in Leeds don't demand alot. You just participate in the Social events the committee have arrange for the Society
cultural_challenges: English people talk alot, and you have to remember to answer politely all the time.
culture_appreciated: How open and polite English people are :)
top3_advice: Be patient with the registering processes at UCPH and at University of Leeds. There is alot of things to do and read etc. etc. but once you get through them it is okay. And send emails if you are in dought.
other_useful_info: I think I have expressed them already.
most_rewarding: That you really are being pussed in your English langauge skills and you really develop alot. You will be surprice at how much you actually are able to do and preform in academics.
greatest_challenge: Managing schools and exsams and really get on the other sides of them. And managing to have a life abord in an English speaking country.
other_comments: No

crucial_aspects: I really enjoy travelling. Meeting new people and learning about their cultures and how different cultures is represented in the personality of individuals from around the world is very exciting. This was one of the main reasons for my interest in leaving Denmark for half a year.
info_ease: It was fairly easy! University of Leeds has a very elaborate webpage that assists in most aspects. Any circumstances, questions, etc., that requires further help, can easily and quickly be dealt with per email correspondence with the lovely staff.
arrival_assistance: First of all, they made sure that I swiftly got to Leeds from Manchester Airport. They had arranged a bus transport for all the international students arriving. Furthermore, they gave each of us the opportunity to apply for further covid assistance including a start food-package and information on how to order food and goods to be delivered.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was done online. The process was easy, but getting your student ID might take you longer than one might expect. A friend of mine did the registration a month before me, but got his student ID several weeks after me. If you want your student ID faster than what their usual delivery time, head down to the student office in the Marjorie and Arnold Ziff Building.
registration_help: The staff is always available per email, so if you have any questions, do not hesitate to reach out to them. I believe they would be able to assist with almost everything imaginable, and even if they cannot, they will make sure to help you getting the contact information on any other helpful sources.
registration_success: It was successful in the sense that I ended up having the modules I wanted, but they allow you to change modules two weeks into classes.
registration_advice: Be careful of changing too many modules once classes have started! I did the mistake of changing half of my modules, and thus was behind from the beginning. I was not able to catch up in the end - some might be, but I had other priorities for my stay.
course_level: The level of courses vary a lot! I had modules that was very difficult, and I had modules where I did not even participate because it was basic. It really depends on what year of the programme the module is offered (i.e., 1-year modules, 2-year modules, 3-year modules).
teaching_comparison: First, the lectures and seminars are shorter! They require more self-study compared to UCPH. Most lectures were online, and all seminars were at campus. Seminars were useful if you came prepared.
courses_enrolled: Advanced Finance Financial Mathematics: Risk Programming for the Web Statistical Methods Traditional Alcoholic Beverages Economic Controversies
recommended_courses: I would recommend any students to do the Traditional Alcoholic Beverages. It is a fairly easy but very interesting module allowing you to put in more energy on other modules. In addition, I recommend any persons from any backgrounds to do the Programming for the Web. You learn the basic foundation of programming, and you will use two of the most common languages (Python and Javascript). It is a tough module, so make sure to have a couple of "easy" modules on the side. And make sure not to have 6 modules in total! I also want to recommend Advanced Finance to anyone with a economic/financial background.
unexpected_costs: Depending on how social you are, extra costs can run op. That is, if you attend the pubs often, if you fancy daytrips out of leeds, if you go to football games, etc.
cost_comparison: I did not really have to buy any books, which was a surprise to me.
activities_available: There is an endless list of social clubs and societies that students can join. Furthermore, the city in general is characterised by the immense amount of students and activities. Staying in is really difficult!
activities_recommended: Seize the opportunities! Join any society of interest! Attend the fresher's events in the beginning! This is probably the best means to meeting new people and kickstarting your social life in Leeds. I recommend attending the fruity events in the beginning! They are usually crowded, drinks are cheap, and you will get to know a lot of people!
weekend_recommendations: Go for daytrips! You should visit cities such as York, Manchester, Liverpool, Newcastle, and even London! We went to London for a weekend trip, and later to celebrate New Years Eve.

For mig var destinationen ikke det der var det vigtigste. Jeg vidste bare jeg ville på udveksling og møde en masse nye mennesker og udfordre mig selv. Så jeg kiggede på hvor man var sikret accomodation og hvor der var Erasmus legat. Jeg endte så med ikke at få en plads inden for EU, men i sidste ende gjorde det ikke så meget.
info_ease: Det var rigtig nemt at få den information man skulle bruge. Både på campus og på ens kollegie var folk virkelig gode til at hjælpe. Selve University of Leeds' hjemmeside var også god at finde information på.
arrival_assistance: University of Leeds var virkelig gode til at tage hånd om en når man ankom. Der var folk fra universitet der tog i mod en i lufthavnen og man kunne booke gratis transport til campus. Det skal man huske at gøre hjemmefra, hvilket jeg ikke havde fået gjort, men de fandt en plads til mig på bussen alligevel.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Det var super nemt at registrere sig som elev på universitet. Det er bare vigtig man holder øje med sin mail og har styr på deadlines, så man ikke misser noget.
registration_help: Man får tilsendt 3 nyhedsbreve, inden man skal afsted hvor man får forklaret alt.
registration_success: Det var forholdvist nemt at tilmelde sig mine fag. Jeg havde dog en lidt mærkeligt oplevelse, hvor jeg havde skrevet en mail til en kursusansvarlig med nogle spørgsmål til et kursus jeg gerne ville tilmelde mig. Jeg finder så senere ud at jeg er blevet tilmeldt kurset uden at have lavet en egentlig ansøgning og uden at få besked fra underviseren. Jeg ville anbefale at man er ude i god tid med at tilmelde sig sine kurser, da man kan risikere de bliver fyldt op. Det oplevede jeg med nogle kurser, men studievejlederen for engelsk var rigtig god til at hjælpe med at tilmelde mig nogle af de kurser der stadig var ledige.
registration_advice: Når man går i gang med at finde sine kurser, ville jeg anbefale at man bruger tid på grundigt at undersøge de fag man er interesseret i. Jeg skulle erstatte tilvalgsfag, så jeg havde mange forskellige valgmuligheder. Det tog rigtig lang tid at kigge alle kurser igennem da jeg gerne ville være sikker på jeg havde undersøgt alle mine muligheder. Så jeg ville helt klart anbefale man går i gang i god tid. Og at man holder siger opdateret med om man kigger i det opdateret kursuskatalog:)
course_level: Generelt synes jeg det faglige niveau ligger under det man er vant til fra KU. Jeg havde kurser fra 1., 2. og 3. årgang og synes ikke der var en stor forskel på det faglige niveau. Jeg ville ikke anbefale University of Leeds hvis man tager på udveksling for at udfordre sig selv fagligt.
teaching_comparison: I forhold til KU er der i mindre grad fokus på teori og metode på University of Leeds.
courses_enrolled: * Laguage in Society * Modern Fictions in English: Conflict, Liminality, Translation * Interactional Linquistics
recommended_courses: Jeg ville helt klart anbefale kurset interactional linquistic med Professor Leeandert Pluug. Det er et fag jeg også har arbejdet med på KU men det var virkelig spændende virkelig at kunne gå i dybden med CA. Det er helt klart også noget man kan tage med sig i sine videre studier. Mr. Pluug er også en super underviser der er virkelig god til at videreformidle stoffet.
unexpected_costs: Jeg var meget overrasket over hvor mange ting man skal købe til sit kollegieværelse. Man skal købe alle køkkenredskaber, service osv.
cost_comparison: Offentlig transport er koster det samme som herhjemme. Det er også virkelig dyrt at tage toget, så hvis man planlægger at tage på nogle ture rundt i landet, ville jeg helt klart anbefale at købe sine togbilletter i god tid. Det er en del billigere at tage bussen, det tager dog bare meget længere tid.
activities_available: Universitet er også gode til at holde forskellige events. De forskellige kollegier holder også nogle gange forskellige arrangementer.
activities_recommended: Jeg ville anbefale at tage til Drag Bingo! Det er mega sjovt og man vinder nice præmier:)
weekend_recommendations: Jeg ville helt klart anbefale at tage en tur til York. Det er en virkelig smuk middelalder by, med nice sightseeing. Jeg ville også anbefale at tage ud og hike ved Yorkshire Dales.
culture_adjustment: Det var nemt at tilpasse sig kulturen i Leeds. Menneskerne er virkelig søde og imødekommende.
cultural_challenges: Det var ikke rigtig nogle udfordringer i forhold til kulturelle forskelle.
culture_appreciated: Jeg synes det hjalp rigtig meget at det var et engelsk talende land.
top3_advice: 1. Overvej at hæve dit budget i forhold til accomodation. Det gør meget ved ens helhedsoplevelse at man bor et sted man synes er rart (og tæt på campus). 2. Vær åben overfor at møde nye mennesker og vær klar på at det er super hårdt i startet at skulle være så social hele tiden (som introvert kan det især være svært). Men også husk på at det er okay at sige nej til at tage med til ting. 3. Søg legater! Det kan virkelig gøre en forskel at have den ekstra finansielle støtte især hvis man skal til England. Der er virkelig mange man kan søge så gå i gang i god tid.
other_useful_info: Hvis du kan, så undgå at bo på Lupton Residences.
most_rewarding: Det var helt klart det at udfordre mig selv og flytte til et nyt land alene uden at kende nogle. Det var virkelig givende at møde så mange nye mennesker fra så mange forskellige kulturer og danne nye venskaber.
greatest_challenge: Det er virkelig meget arbejde at forberede opholdet. Man skal have styr på alle deadlines og man skal også lave meget research.

crucial_aspects: It was crucial for my choice to study af University of Leeds that the academic opportunities were of the highest standard and within a field of study and interest which could not be fulfilled by studying electives in Denmark or at University of Copenhagen.
info_ease: The university made it quite easy to gain access to the relevant information about my first week in Leeds. Some information about schedules were a bit more complicated, but the administration at the university was very welcoming and helped answer every question.
arrival_assistance: I was picked up, alongside some other international students at the Manchester Airport. They driver drove us straight to our accommodation. It was great as it both saved us time and trouble with public transport and suitcases. I arrived at a Saturday, so my accommodations office was unfortunately closed, which made it a bit more difficult to move in. The first week I had an introduction and meeting with our tutor at my school (I was connected to two schools, so I ended up attending only one orientation), which made sure I understood the academic system and some of the challenges most commonly faced by international students.
arrival_comments: Orientation happened after the first classes, so some of the information would have been great to have before, but it worked nonetheless very well.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: As I had a bachelors in social science I was eligible for studying at different schools, which I could choose from. At Leeds you apply for 'discovery modules' - also known as electives, and then you can write why you are qualified for this specific course, if the course is not within your assigned school (as a postgrad in Sociology, I could study all electives connected to the School of Sociology and Social Policy, but I was also accepted into electives at School of Political Science and School of Philosophy), as I had relevant prerequisite course before applying.
registration_help: The administration was available over email or call, and the answering time was very short compared to my home institution.
registration_success: I got into the classes that I wanted - I got accepted into more classes than I had time for, so I had to prioritise them.
registration_advice: I would advice future students to seek out what other courses other Schools have than necessarily the one you are connected to via your home institution. Some of the most interesting and thought provoking courses I had was completely different than what I would 'normally' study.
course_level: In the postgraduate program in Sociology and the host university, there were no available courses for me to take so I did undergrad electives in sociology, criminology, and political theory. I found the academic level adequate, yet the culture of teaching is less theoretical and more historical than what I am used to. The reading were of a good level and the theoretical discussion in the tutorials were of a good academic level.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching is very different than Copenhagen. It is much more dialogue based and less 'using this theoretical stance one could argue this or that' and much more your personal engagement, understanding and opinion about theories. This was both fun, challenging and sometimes frustrating. I loved the amount of tutorials or "øvelsestimer" we had at Leeds - engaging and preparing for discussions with the actual professor was very rewarding and adding to my understanding of both the theories and the subject. I loved the use of open office hours to engage with the assignments and the work I was doing throughout the semester. The examinations were also, for my schools, theoretical essays, which for me was very different from the more empirical and methodological approach at Institute of Sociology. at UCPH
courses_enrolled: State Crime and Immorality - Crimes of the Powerful. Global Terrorism and Violence. Reimagining Politics - Gender, Race, and Popular Culture.
recommended_courses: I would really recommend the courses "State Crime and Immorality" and "Reimagining Politics" as they both helped develop a more nuanced and critical view of modern society and institutions. I really enjoyed the course "Global terrorism and Violence", but I know that this is purely of a professional interest in democracy and political violence.
unexpected_costs: While I knew that exchange would cost, I spend more money on travels around the UK, going on day trips, going to social activities and eating out than I would normally do - everyday is filled with activities or opportunities. I do not regret a pound spend.
cost_comparison: When getting a railcard (DO IT) public transportation on the trains around the UK was far less expensive than I imagined. Going out to eat or for drinks is less expensive than in Copenhagen and a lot of social activities are either cheap or free. I did not expect housing to be as expensive as it was - Leeds especially is an expensive city to live in, but overall there is a housing crisis in the UK. Many of the everyday expenses are overall the same as in Denmark - groceries and necessities. There are money you can save by buying budget brands.
activities_available: Anything you can imagine. I was a part of the surf society, kickboxing, book club and knitting club. I attended activities at the debate club, went weekly to a jazz club, was at culture nights, took jewellery making classes and pottery painting with other students. The bars around and on campus have football screenings, pub quizzes, folk music nights and so much more.
activities_recommended: I really recommend joining a few societies (there is a sign up fee, which can vary from £5 to £30, and while this can seem a lot, there is often a 'social' or activity once a week). It is a great way of meeting both other internationals but especially other British people - they can seem quite shy in class until you meet them outside class and they are suddenly the chattiest.
weekend_recommendations: Living in the North and in West Yorkshire you have the perfect location for experiencing some of the most beautiful natural landscapes, hiking routes and scenery in England. It is also perfect for going around the North, into Scotland or even down south to London, Bristol, Oxford or the like. I really recommend all the hiking routes around as well as the cutest British villages around Leeds - they are straight out of a Barnaby episode. Cities such as Harrogate, Harewood, York, and Hebden Bridge are absolutely stunning (and with a rail cars between €2-10 to go by train.) Pack a pair of good walking boots and hike around the Moors of the Peak- and Lake Districts, walk alongside the cutest sheep you'll ever see and finish up in a tea house with a cuppa of Yorkshire Tea and a scone.
culture_adjustment: Once you accept that the Northern English accent is just rubbish, you'll get on grand. The people in Yorkshire are so sweet and polite it is almost 'scary' in the beginning. Soon you'll learn to always greet other in shops and chatting up people in the queue. The university and the community of other internationals made the adjustment easy for me, and the university does focus a lot on events for internationals exactly to make sure we process any culture shock.
socializing_tips: Join the societies, chat up people in the bar and go where the locals go. Northerners are great at being hospitable and never once was I rejected when I asked "Do you guys mind if I join?".
cultural_challenges: The food was a big challenge for me as a Dane and bread-lover. The quality of food in the supermarkets and at the bakeries took some getting used to. The culture for eating quick and ready made food was a surprise and the amount of sugar and crisps certainly added a one or two pounds of the hips. Leeds is a student city with many bars and pubs so I did find that drinking (or at least going out, wether you drink or not) was a part of socialising in the beginning. The famous "Otley Run" is a 17-bar-long pub-crawl dressed up in costumes - and you don't just do it once. So seeing Mario and Luigi on a Saturday afternoon running around campus or the surrounding are not uncommon - but quite funny.
culture_appreciated: I loved the mentality and friendliness of the people in Leeds, both the students, faculty or just the people you meet in the train or in the grocery store. As a Dane, the chattiness was in the beginning quite strange, but I have come to love it and I try to incorporate it in my life in Copenhagen now.
top3_advice: - Sometimes you have to invite yourself along - it people will definitely not mind you doing so - Everyone is very young. Most people are in their very early twenties and that can cause some frustrations if you are 25 and have lived on our own. - Take this as an opportunity to engage with your professor in 1:1 - use your tutorials and office hours to really understand and maybe learn even more than in the classrooms.
other_useful_info: The 'local' students take their education quite seriously and for many it is a privilege to be there (and an expensive one!). So respect that when you are there and respect the campus.
most_rewarding: Pushing myself to go out and learn new interests and parts of myself - and doing it 'on my own'. Discovering how social and spontanious I can be, engaging in new hobbies and of course, meeting to many new and different people while making great friends.
greatest_challenge: Balancing having fun, learning new thins and also resting and having down time on your own. Realising not all new people are going to be your friend but pushing yourself to engage with the people you really like.
