crucial_aspects: I have a personal relationship with Germany, and the university I chose had courses taught in English which was essential for me.
info_ease: The mobility online system was quite difficult to navigate in, but the websites of my home university and exchange university was helpful.
arrival_assistance: I got a buddy from the buddy program at University of Mannheim, who helped me in the beginning.
arrival_comments: We were told to be available one full week for introduction purposes, however there was less introduction from the university than expected.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: We had to send an email to the faculty in order to apply for courses, by prioritizing them. There was a list specifically for exchange students with the relevant ECTS-credits.
registration_help: The exchange coordinator from the university.
registration_success: Very successful.
registration_advice: Don't hesitate to contact your coordinator if you have any questions.
course_level: The level was fit for master courses.
teaching_comparison: In most classes, there was a lot of talking/presentation by the teacher and no student involvement, which is very different from UCPH. It made the lectures very long and hard to take part in. I did however get used to it over time. But in one of my classes it was the opposite, and the teacher was very good at creating a safe teaching environment where students would and could participate.

recommended_courses: International business transactions. The teacher was excellent, and the course was very difficult but interesting. Also a very nice experience at the examination.
cost_comparison: The washing and drying at the student housing was quite expensive, but food was a lot less expensive than expected.
culture_adjustment: Quite easy. Germans are way more out-going than Danish people, which was helpful in the adjustment proces.
socializing_tips: Use the many ESN-Visum events to meet both local and exchange students - and your buddy.
top3_advice: Be open, go on trips (use the trains), be patient with the paper work.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people and cultures, getting to experience law from a different point of view, and taking courses not available at UCPH.
greatest_challenge: Adapting to the language and feeling homesick.

activities_recommended: Depending on your field of study the university has good contacts with the local businesses and provides a lot of, guest lectures, forums and conferences for different subjects e.g. competition policy
weekend_recommendations: Mannheim is very well located for travel esp. by train. I highly recommend going to Heidelberg, Frankfurt, Munich, Paris, Stuttgart, Freiburg, Schwartzwald, Nürnberg and Berlin.
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: Be very outgoing and engaged in the first weeks of the semester, participate in as many events as you can! Also take part in the buddy programme.
cultural_challenges: The polite way of addressing strangers e.g. addressing professors by title and last name
culture_appreciated: Germans are very outgoing and festive. I loved the events taking place not only in and around the university but also the city of Mannheim and the surrounding cities. Don't miss out on going to Oktoberfest/Frühlingsfest it is probably the most german thing you'll ever experience
top3_advice: Most important tips:
other_useful_info: Don't be scared of going to Mannheim because of it's reputation. The city may not be the most amazing one, but that has its advantages. Acommodation is cheap and not difficult to find. Everything is close by. Travelling by train or bus is very convenient. The city is not crowded by turists and eating out is easy and cheap.
most_rewarding: Experiencing the south-german culture, meeting new people from all over the world and proably most importantly of all realising that living and working outside of Denmark is not difficult or hard.
greatest_challenge: Settling in at the beginning of the semester. It was harder than expected having to learn everything from scratch e.g.: Getting around the city and campus, finding friends, adapting to local rules and regulation (municipality and university) etc. But even though it was a big challenge it was also fun and exciting.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to improve my German and travel in a climate friendly manner. Furthermore, previous exchange students had written in their reports that the administration at the university in Mannheim was great, which was important to me, because I did not want to stress over administrative issues (unfortunately this was not my experience).
overall_comments: The score is not that high, because I was a bit unlucky and experienced some extraordinary challenges and events in the city and at the university. However, I also had many good experiences and most exchange students have a great time in Mannheim.
info_ease: Quite easy - the university provides detailed guides.
arrival_assistance: My buddy (a student) and contact information on the international office at the university
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: The score is not that high, because I was a bit unlucky and experienced some extraordinary challenges and events in the city and at the university. However, I also had many good experiences and most exchange students have a great time in Mannheim.
registration_process: Registration for the intranet and enrollment was easy - the university gives you thorough guidance. Registering for courses is another story, though... We had to "pre-register" before the exchange and then register officially later. For the final registration the IT system was down for most of the registration period and the faculty had changed the course schedules completely without notice, meaning that multiple of my courses were suddenly overlapping. The faculty was unreachable (by mail, phone and in person), when I tried to solve the problem.
registration_help: Guides and personel (in principle)
registration_success: Not very successful - 2/5 of my courses I was "forced" to take due to schedulling issue
registration_advice: 1) make sure to check that none of your courses overlap both when pre-registering and for the final registration. Be prepared that the schedule might change even after you have made sure that everything works out. 2) get more courses pre-approved than you need, so you can adjust to changing schedules.
academics_comments: The score is not that high, because I was a bit unlucky and experienced some extraordinary challenges and events in the city and at the university. However, I also had many good experiences and most exchange students have a great time in Mannheim.
course_level: The level is lower than at UCPH and you do not have to prepare much, because the curriculum is the PowerPoint slides that are used in class.
teaching_comparison: It is similar - the professor will do a presentation and sometimes the students will do small cases/exercises. However, there are no mock exams and previous exams are often not made available to students.
courses_enrolled: Advocacy Skills (6 ETCS - oral exam), International Civil and Commercial Litigation (8 ECTS - 2 hour take-at-home exam), International Sale of Goods (6 ECTS - 1 hour written exam), International Trade Law (6 ETCS - 1 hour written exam), Law & Economics (& ETCS - 1 hour written exam).
recommended_courses: Advocacy skills: the professor is entertaining and the course provides useful insights on how basic communication techniques can improve your legal practice. The exam is quite relaxed. Law & Economics: an interesting course that gives you a sense of how the law and legal issues are analysed from an economic point of view. You have to put some work into it, though, because you have to know all the economic theories by heart at the exam. DO NOT TAKE INTENATIONAL TRADE LAW: it was a chaotic and pointless presentation of cases from a local law firm. The lawyers, who were teaching, answered the questions for the class themselves, because none of the students understood what the point was.
unexpected_costs: A semester fee around 900 DKK
cost_comparison: Living costs in Germany are lower than in Copenhagen and you get student discounts more often.
activities_available: The ESN VISUM makes a lot of events for exchange students and there are many student-driven clubs. Furthermore, a gym membership is relatively cheap and there are different sports teams/classes offered.
activities_recommended: Events by ESN VISUM Mannheim, because it is a great way to meet people and it is fun. I also recommend the International Summer/Winter Academy (an intensive German course offered by the university). You have to pay for it, but you meet exchange students from alle over the world and you get time to settle in to life in Mannheim, before the semester starts.
weekend_recommendations: Heidelberg, when it is sunny - it is prettier than Mannheim and a nice get-away. Smaller cities, such as Worms, Speyer and Schwetzingen are also worth a visit. If you get the chance to go to Faschingskarneval in Cologne or Oktober-/Frühlingsfest in Stuttgart, you should go - it is a lot of fun. You will get plenty of opportunities to travel across Germany and Europe, because many exchange students from e.g. the US, Asia and Australia want to see as much of Europe as possible and Mannheim is a great starting point due to its central location.
culture_adjustment: Relatively easy, but remember to have cash and do not expect IT systems to live up to Danish standards.
socializing_tips: Find a WG room or join a student club/sports team
cultural_challenges: Social and economic differences are more obvious than in Denmark, so there are more people living on/wandering around the streets and crime is a bigger issue than back home. I got catcalled way more than in Copenhagen and had some unpleasant experiences, so I had to think more about how I got home at night than I normally do.
culture_appreciated: (most) Sounthern German people are warm-hearted and like to small talk. People can afford going to cafes and restaurants and do it often.
top3_advice: 1) Join ESN VISUM events and the International Summer or Winter Academy 2) The courses are not as demanding as at home, but even if you study throughout the semester, the exams might be challenging because they are conducted very differently from what we are used to 3) You will not have that much control over which courses and exams you end up taking.
other_useful_info: Bring and old-fashioned wrist-watch because there are no clocks in the examination rooms
most_rewarding: Improving my German and experiencing living in another country
greatest_challenge: Administrative issues throughout the semester, exams and safety.

crucial_aspects: Semestertiming og mulige fag.
info_ease: Ved ankomst var jeg blevet gjort bekendt med al relevant information. Vær dog opmærksom på de 100 euro i semestergebyr, det hørte jeg først om 3 måneder før jeg tog afsted.
arrival_assistance: Der var introseminarer, rundtur og events fra den lokale ESN-afdeling.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Universitetet i Mannheim hjælper dig gennem processen, og du får alt information i god tid. Det kan virke en anelse uoverskueligt, men det er rimelig overkommeligt.
registration_help: Du bliver giver en meget grundig guide og tjekliste.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle mine 1. prioriteter.
registration_advice: Lad være med at stresse over det. Mannheims universitet er noget mere chill og fleksible end KU.
course_level: Generelt er underviserne engagerede, men niveauet er noget lavere end KU. Derudover er særligt andre udvekslingsstuderende meget uengagerede, så barren er lav.

cultural_challenges: De ansatte i supermarkeder tager deres job rimelig seriøst, så være klar på at pakke din pose hurtigt.
culture_appreciated: De mennesker jeg har mødt har været søde og imødekommende.
top3_advice: Tjek eksamensformer. De mundtlige eksamener foregår sammen med 2-3 andre studerende, og du risikere at få en skriftlige eksamen hvor formen blyant og papir. Accepter at starten er overvældende. Du kan altid gå i en introvert hi med netflix og wolt når først du har fået venner. Rejs! Mannheim er en ufattelig grim by med meget lidt natur, så for at undgå depression bør du tage en tur til Heidelberg eller en af de andre nærliggende byer. Deutsche Bahn giver DSB kamp til stregen ift. forsinkelser men du må tage det som en oplevelse.
other_useful_info: Modsat KUA er universitetet ret flot, så brug bibliotekerne til din eksamenslæsning.
most_rewarding: Det har været en rar pause fra stress og jag. Der er sjældent noget at forberede eller læse før undervisningen, så der er massere af fritid til at rejse i.
greatest_challenge: De første to uger. Der sker meget og det sker hele tiden. Efter min opfattelse går folk meget hurtigt i sociale grupper, og dem der hverken boede på kollegie eller deltog i de fleste aktiviteter røg ud af fællesskaberne.
other_comments: Pray for en plads på Studierendenwerks kollegier.

overall_comments: En oplevelse for livet, kan kun anbefale
info_ease: Lidt svært,må skrive rundt til nogle forskellige fra deres uni

housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: En oplevelse for livet, kan kun anbefale
registration_process: Mannheim Universität gjorde det nemt og overskueligt. registration_success: Fik alt hvad jeg ønslet mig
registration_advice: Bare søg, havde vitterligt ingen vanskeligheder (bortset fra KU)
academics_comments: En oplevelse for livet, kan kun anbefale
course_level: Niveauet fra delvist på samme niveau som KU og delvist lidt lavere synes jeg. Men det var ikke så meget i sværhedsgraden, men mere at fagene var kortere og der deraf var mindre at holde styr på, hvilket gjorde det nemmere. Lærte derfor stadigvæk en masse, det var bare mere overskueligt end det plejer at være, hvilket naturligvis er godt.
teaching_comparison: Det var sgu fint nok, man er lidt mere personlig med sin underviser dernede, da det også er dem der giver dig karektere og semseterprøverne er ikke anonyme, så sørg for at vær på god fod med dem. Ellers var det sgu meget ligesom i Danmark, bortset fra man ikke har lektier som sådan, og fik ingen bøger (jeg havde en, men det var i mit tyske fag) - alt hvad du lærer foregå i undervisningen og gennem deres plancer/powerpoints. Fravær kan derfor varmt frarådes, fordi du kan oprigtig ikke "bare læse op derhjemme".
courses_enrolled: Næh det rager ikike alle. Jeg kan fortælle at tre var på engelsk og et var på tysk
unexpected_costs: Altså mange af de her udgifter har jeg slet ikke tænkt over. Aner ikke hvad jeg brugte om måneden på mad eller nogle af de andre. Gudskelov var det ikke så dyrt så jeg gik og tænkte over alt det her fis. Huslejen er dog nøjagtig, men det skal bemærkes at ALLE jeg mødte dernede betalte mere end mig, nogle sågar to gange så meget. Det er altså umiddelbart usandsynligt at du kan få en tilsvarende lav husleje, men jeg krydser da finger for dig! :) Bare vær klar på det sagtens kan være dyrere Prisen bøger er prisen på den enkelte bog som var krævet i mit tyske fag.
cost_comparison: ved ikke, dôner er billigt
activities_available: Mannheim har en smule selv man kan gå og se, derudover Ishocky Stadion (Mannheim Adler), Fodboldanlægget (Mannheim Waldhof) og ellers er der alle de omkringliggende byer. Heidelberg især, samt en masse andre. Ludwigshafen må du dog aldrig tage til, det er bare en stor ghetto - og det er ikke mine ord, det er de lokales ord. Men alle andre byer end Ludwigshafen er stort set værd at besøge, man kan også tage over grænsen til Frankrig, det gjorde vi et par gange.
weekend_recommendations: Julemarked til jul også, men ellers find selv ud af det. Det er også en vinfestival vi besøgte i Dünnheim? Kan ikke huske navnet, men der køre en sporvogn diretkte fra Mannheim, endestoppet er der hvor den foregik.
culture_adjustment: Nemt, det bare Tyskland.
socializing_tips: Tag til mange af de der EUCM begivenheder, især i begyndelsen, det er altafgørende!!! Jeg er selv til tider lidt indadvendt, men jeg vidste også godt at det vigtig at komme ud og møde folk så man har nogle kontaker og venner. Jeg mødte tre gutter den første fredag i første uge, og de gutter (jeg mødte mange andre senere igennem begivenheder og fællesvenner) endte med at blive mine tætteste og vi hang ud sammen alle 5 måneder. De blev mine bedste venner dernede og vi har også aftalt at mødes igen her efter semestret er slut, det kræver dog planlægning da de kommer fra forskellige lande. Jeg siger bare det her for at understrege at husk at mød nogle mennesker, fordi ellers kan de blive meget ensomt! Så heller få nogle gode venner, måske for livet, som jeg, frem for at være for ængstlig og ikke turde tale med nogen eller komme ud Hvis jeg kan, kan alle.
cultural_challenges: Stort set intet rugbrød, hvilket jeg synes var overraskende. Og ja de har heller ikke salatpizza og de faattede ikke hvad pepperoni pizza var, så hvis du skal have fråder mad så bare køb döner. Kan varmt anbefales Selamin i Mannheim, den ligger på Dönerstrasse som vi kaldte den, vejen har oprigtig ikke et navn, men når du finder den er du ikke tvivl. 50% af alle butikker på vejen er döner forretninger
culture_appreciated: Pølser, øl, döner
top3_advice: 1: MØD FOLK I BEGYNDELSE! 2: HUSK AT BESØGE TING, det er ikke officielt en ferie, men ærlig talt hvis det ikke var for at have det sjovt hvorfor så overhovedet rejse derned i første omgang? Husk at se lidt forskelligt osv. 3: Have gode penge med, man kan som udangspunkt jo ikke tjene penge mens man er væk, så hav en god sjat sparet op. Og nej EU legattet er ikke nok, spar op selv også.
other_useful_info: 99% af alle veje i Innestadt (indre by) har ikke navne, da men i stedet har givet hussamlingerne navne, som C3, G7, B2 osv. Du lærer det hurtigt det er meget smart, men det er derfor adresserne kan virker underlig da de blot kan være "C3, 21864 Mannheim"
most_rewarding: Alle menneskerne, uden at være tåkrummende så har det oprigtig været en oplevelse for livet, er meget glad for det! Mødte folk fra hele verden og også nogle danskere som jeg også blev rigtig gode venner med. Har grint så meget jeg burde sagsusme have en six pack efterhånden, kan kun anbefale at tage afsted!

cost_comparison: Housing was more expensive than expected
activities_available: Heaps of social clubs and activities were available for the students at the university. We were introduced to all of them during the intro of the semester, which was very nice! I joined different kinds of clubs, which I highly recommend because it made it way more easy to get new friends - both other exchange students and other locals too.
activities_recommended: I joined the surf club, the diving club, the mountaineering club, and the dance club. I highly recommend the surf club. The committee was so nice and I got to know so many new people at the parties at Tikki House. The surf camp itself was also so much fun!
weekend_recommendations: Experience Melbourne - the city is amazing! During the holidays I traveled around Australia. The country is amazing to travel in and there are so many incredible things to see and places to visit!
culture_adjustment: It was quite easy. Everyone is so nice and friendly and easy to talk to. I felt very much at home in the city already from the beginning!
socializing_tips: Join the social clubs! It is definitely the best way to get to know local students. People in Australia are so friendly and welcoming, so they are easy to talk to and make you feel a part of the community.
cultural_challenges: No cultural differences were particularly challenging. Of course, there are cultural differences, but I was curious and wanted to get to know all those differences. I think it is a part of being on exchange, so I just enjoyed getting to know them.
culture_appreciated: The way of living in Australia. The way people think and meet each other. It is very inspiring and I want to take it with me home.
top3_advice: 1. Make it easy for yourself when choosing the subjects! 2. Find housing with roommates so you don't get to live by yourself. 3. Join the social clubs so you get invited to house parties and get to know local students.
other_useful_info: Find housing close to the university. The location of Unimelb Parkville is very good, so if you get to live close by, you know that you live in a good location close to all the good places and things of the city.
most_rewarding: I am forever thankful for this experience. It was very special to get a close connection to Melbourne itself and share the experience with all the wonderful people I met during the semester.
greatest_challenge: Be aware that you are far away from home from all your friends and your family. You are going to live a separate life with only new people, which can feel a bit lonely sometimes. Even though I had the time of my life in Australia, I was surprised at how rarely I was in contact with people at home. I talked to a lot of my exchange friends about this during the semester, and they all felt the same. So it is a common thing being on exchange, which is nice to know beforehand.
other_comments: Enjoy the time of your life!

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to an English speaking country and particularly liked Melbourne when i travelled around Australia some years ago. Good university with interesting subjects also important
overall_comments: Incredibly happy with everything, genuinely had such a good time while i also achieved my academic goals
info_ease: Fairly unproblematic, good orientation program organised by the university for all exchange students
arrival_assistance: The orientation program provided all the information i needed, no further assistance required
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Incredibly happy with everything, genuinely had such a good time while i also achieved my academic goals
registration_process: All happened online in the student portal. Straightforward and simple to figure out. Changing subjects close to the beginning of semester start was completely unproblematic
registration_help: Stop 1 is the student service that can help with all questions related to university admin. They are very helpful, but can be a bit difficult to get an appointment with as they are very busy, especially around registration period
registration_success: Completely, was accepting into all of them
registration_advice: Arrive having chosen some subjects from home, but don't be too bothered about whether you have chosen the right ones. You have plenty of time to change your mind once you arrive
academics_comments: Incredibly happy with everything, genuinely had such a good time while i also achieved my academic goals
course_level: I did three second year courses and one first year course. In hindsight probably could have gone for more advanced courses, but they were all interesting, and covered topics i hadn't been taught back home
teaching_comparison: More centered around lectures, with everything needed for the exams covered in lectures. There was not much need for further independent reading. Practical classes where the knowledge from lectures was applied was somewhat reminiscent of the style of teaching in the Danish gymnasie. The whole grading structure is different to UCPH. Each subject has its own marking structure, but typically you get marks throughout the course that all count towards your final grade. For example in one of my subjects there was a weekly quiz, the results of which counted for 20% of the final grade. Exams usually only count for about 50% of the grade, with the rest being based on assignments, presentations or quizzes done throughout the semester
courses_enrolled: Wonders of the Weather Dangerous Earth Economic Tools for the Environment Past Climates: Icehouse to Greenhouse
recommended_courses: Economic Tools for the Environment was very enjoyable and interesting as well. It is based around valuing nature and biodiversity and coming up with economic cases and methods to protect them. The style of teaching is quite independent and students are encouraged to take an active interest and role in the subject.
unexpected_costs: Nothing unexpected as such
cost_comparison: Public transport is a tricky one to define. Trams are the primary way of getting around the city, and every trip costs 4,60 dollars (20-25 kroner) no matter if it takes 2 minutes or 2 hours. This means the value for money changes dramatically depending on how far you have to travel. However, at no point during my stay here did i meet a ticket inspector on a tram. Make of that what you will In terms of travelling around the country, domestic plane tickets were surprisingly expensive but nothing that breaks the budget if you have set aside money specifically for this. Beer is insanely expensive, roughly twice the price you pay in Denmark. At bars and such, prices are pretty similar though. Eating out is a bit cheaper in Melbourne, with lots of good food available for decent prices. And for some reason peppers are insanely expensive, but this is admittedly a minor issue
activities_available: Plenty. Especially the Melbourne University Exchange Society (MUSEX) organise lots of fun events. Lots of clubs, societies and sports, which are all introduced during the orientation period
activities_recommended: Joining a sports team is a good way of meeting people, doesn't have to be at a serious level. For example, netball is surprisingly good fun, and fairly easy to pick up
weekend_recommendations: I recommend getting into Australian Rules Football. AFL, commonly known as footy, is very entertaining and going to games at the MCG (Melbourne Cricket Ground, huge stadium) is a great experience. More importantly, it is a really good conversation topic. Absolutely everyone in Melbourne follows it and supports a team, so picking a team and knowing just the basics is very useful when getting to know locals
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Australians are incredibly open and friendly, and brilliant at making people feel welcome straight away
socializing_tips: As mentioned, footy is a great way to break the ice and start a conversation, works with almost everybody in Melbourne. Again, Australians are typically open to new people in a way we are not used to in Denmark, so approaching people in social settings is a lot easier And then living with Australians certainly helped for me as well
cultural_challenges: Acknowledgement of Aboriginal Peoples as the traditional owners of the land of Australia is very important in society. Australians are very aware that terrible atrocities were committed against indigenous people in relatively recent history, and reconciliation is a constantly ongoing process. At first, as an outsider, the constant acknowledgements of country can seem as superficial political correctness, but it really is very important to most Australians and respected by everyone. Engaging and educating yourself on the topic is a good way of feeling more connected and part of the local culture
culture_appreciated: The Australian openness and friendliness, it is great when you are adapting to a new place on the other side of the world, and helps making friends
top3_advice: Use the orientation period to get everything sorted for the start of semester. Because of the running grading system, it is good to be on it from week 1 Don't postpone starting things such as joining clubs or sports teams. Time goes by quickly, and the earlier you start, the more you will get out of it Campus is big and very nice, with lots of good spots to study. It is an enjoyable place to spend time, so make sure to explore it and find the nice spots. Lots of hidden gems around
other_useful_info: Get an Australian bank account as soon as possible. It makes things so much easier.
most_rewarding: The friendships i have made (cliche, sorry), especially with my housemates and their extended group of friends. Testing myself academically in another system and learning from a different perspective was great as well
greatest_challenge: Going back to Denmark. I really feel at home in Melbourne, and readjusting to life back in Copenhagen will be difficult
other_comments: Go for it! It's good fun

crucial_aspects: I saw it as an incredible opportunity to live in a country so far away: Australia. I chose Melbourne because I have heard that the city and university are very international, which makes it easier for an exchange student.

The reason why I am not rating my study experience as a 10 is that I was not aware of all the work I had to do before leaving regarding the exchange program both here in Copenhagen but also in Melbourne. Further, it can be difficult to study in another country, where everything is different from home, and it is therefore a challenge you need to be prepared for.

crucial_aspects: Being an Australian who grew up in Denmark, I had a personal connection to the country that I wanted to explore during my exchange. However, going to the University of Melbourne was also important to me, as I had heard that the school was a great place to study. The courses offered were exciting, and I could apply to a lot of different courses as a student of Anthropology.
info_ease: The information was fairly easy to find. Most of the info needed was provided by KU during information sessions, mails and links to info pages. UniMelb also had a good step-by-step guide on how to get my exchange in order - how to apply for courses, student cards and such. Unimelb also held an orientation session for exchange students at the beginning of the semester. I did have to do a bit of research into how to navigate the course catalogue. It was a bit tricky figuring out what courses were available to me, and which I was eligible for, as well as how to submit them for approval from KU. I feel there could be more information on that part of the process.
arrival_assistance: I recieved help from UniMelb's student service because of some confusion about getting my vaccination certificate certified. The rules were changing, so there was mixed information about what to do. I was also in touch with other Danish exchange students during the first weeks, and we helped each other out with questions and problems in a groupchat.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You have to accept your letter of offer, then complete an administrative enrolment. After your enrollment is confirmed, you can enroll in your subjects. Remember to get your subjects approved by KU so you can transfer the course credits at the end of your stay! Create your timetable before the semester starts as well (there's a guide on the page I've linked below). The timetable tool can be a bit tricky to use - I had to spend some time on it.
registration_help: UniMelb has a student service called Stop-1. The exchange coordinator from KU was also able to answer some questions for me intitally.
registration_success: I registered for all the classes I wanted successfully, and the timetable I wanted was approved as well.
registration_advice: This page was very helpful for me:
course_level: The courses were challenging, but they were at an appropriate level for me. I studied on my 5th semester, and took two Level 2 BA subjects and two Level 3 BA subjects. I could definitely tell that the Level 3 subjects were more challenging, but I also got a lot out of them.
teaching_comparison: The teaching was very engaging, and it was interesting studying with a different group of students for each course. At KU I had studied only with other antropology students during the obligatory courses. I liked getting some different perspectives on the courses. The biggest difference I think is the way the workload is distributed. You're working on assessments throughout the semester, as opposed to KU, where only the final exam is graded. This puts a lot more pressure on mid-semester assignments, and it took me a while to find a rhythm with the workload that worked for me. Checking when all the assessments are due and planning when you're going to work on them is definitely important at UniMelb if you want to avoid doing it all last minute (like me).
courses_enrolled: Indigenous Cultures and Knowledges (UNIB20022_2022_SM2) Life Writing (CWRI30013_2022_SM2) Short Fiction (CWRI20002_2022_SM2) Trans Studies: Cultures and Communities (GEND30007_2022_SM2)
recommended_courses: I enjoyed all my courses a lot, but my favourites were Life Writing and Trans Studies. They were relevant to my personal interests, but I think they would be beneficial to anthropology students generally. Life Writing is a non-fiction writing class with a focus on biography. It taught me a lot about writing about my own and other peoples' lives, and I found the in-class discussions very engaging. Trans Studies is a relatively recent field of study that focuses on transgender and genderqueer experience. The topics covered in class were varied and cover the complexity of trans experiences. To anthropology students I recommend "Indigenous Cultures and Knowledges." It's a masterclass series taught by experts in each field, and it covers many different fields of study concerning Indigenous Australian culture and knowledge. I found the class challenging, as it covers a very broad field of interest, but illuminating as well.
unexpected_costs: Rent was a lot more expensive than I'd expected. Also fees for banking, such as currency conversion fees whenever you pay for sometthing or transfer money into a foreign account.
cost_comparison: Coffee in Melbourne is cheaper than in Copenhagen, as well as some other café foods and beverages. In general restaurant foods and groceries cost about the same. The rent is what really drives up the cost of living.
activities_available: All sorts of things! There's a lot more variety than the clubs at KU. During the orientation week they hand out guides to all the clubs you can participate in.
activities_recommended: I didn't participate in any clubs, sorry! Make sure to grab a coffee with friends around the campus, though. There are a lot of coffee shops on campus.
weekend_recommendations: Melbourne is a vibrant city with tons to do. I loved the botanical gardens, museums and cafés in the center of town. The food is also excellent, but not cheap. Make sure to see some live music while you're here!
culture_adjustment: I found the culture quite easy to adjust to, as I come from Australia and have some friends here. Meeting other exchange students who were also new to the culture was very helpful in getting comfortable in Melbourne.
socializing_tips: Get to know your classmates, participate in clubs, sports, whatever you find interesting! You're sure to find likeminded people. I made a lot of great friends in my classes and at my dorm.
cultural_challenges: I'm not sure I found the culture challenging. The first few months were hard, as I had to adjust to the clock and the seasons, and form new routines. After I had gotten settled in the city I had a great time.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness of the people and the nature. Australia is just a beautiful place, and there are always more things to see.
top3_advice: 1. Keep your budget in mind - Melbourne is not a cheap city. The rent especially brings up the cost of living. 2. The courses at the University of Melbourne can be challenging depending on courses you decide on, but they are rewarding if you're prepared to put in the work. 3. Get in touch with other students! I've met so many amazing people, both Australians and exchange students. They were what made my experience amazing!
most_rewarding: Getting to know people from all over the world, living in and exploring a whole new city, and the course at UniMelb.
greatest_challenge: Homesickness and adjusting the culture at first, as well as some issues with a roommate that I had to sort out with my dorm.

crucial_aspects: Engelsktalende land, spændende by, gode rejse-muligheder og godt universitet.
overall_comments: Virkelig skønt og anderledes semester med så mange gode oplevelser!
info_ease: Ikke nogen problemer. Det kræver altid lidt tid lige at sætte sig ind i det hele, men det fungerede super fint, og informationen var tilgængelig.
arrival_assistance: Der var gode muligheder for at opsøge hjælp gennem universitetet.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Virkelig skønt og anderledes semester med så mange gode oplevelser!
registration_process: Der var god hjælp at hente ift. valg af fag. Der krævede lidt lige at få sammensat sit skema ordentligt, men det var også rart med fleksibiliteten i selv at kunne melde sig på de hold, man syntes passede bedst i ens program.
registration_help: I Melbourne havde de det, der hedder "Stop 1" tæt på universitetet, som man altid kunne gå forbi eller skrive til ved spørgsmål omkring fag, eksaminer osv. De var hjælpsomme og der var ofte gode (korte) svartider.
registration_success: Oplevede det som nemt at få de fag, jeg ønskede. Jeg lavede også lidt om i det i starten, fordi jeg fandt ud af, at jeg syntes noget andet virkede mere spændende, eller at der var en bedre eksamensform osv.
registration_advice: Det hele kan virke lidt kaotisk lige når man kommer frem, og måske endnu mere når man stadig sidder i Danmark og ikke lige forstår deres system eller lignende, men det hele løser sig og går op i sidste ende. Derudover kan det kan være rart at gå forbi "Stop 1", eller booke et møde med dem, når man kommer til byen inden studiestart, så man lige kan få styr på det hele, inden alt andet går løs.
academics_comments: Virkelig skønt og anderledes semester med så mange gode oplevelser!
course_level: Jeg var afsted på min kandidat men endte med at have to bachelor-fag og to kandidat-fag. Noget af undervisningen lå op af noget vi havde berørt tidligere på KU, og så var der også en del nyt selvfølgelig. Den kombination var ret god, synes jeg selv.
teaching_comparison: Undervisningen var mere interaktiv, ift. hvad jeg er vant til på KU. Så det blev ofte krævet, at man var mere 'på' og deltagende. Derudover var eksaminerne i høj grad afleveringer, som man afleverede i løbet af hele semesteret.
courses_enrolled: "Epidemiology 1" "Links Between Health and Learning" "Qualitative Research in Public Health" "Population and Global Mental Health"
recommended_courses: Jeg kan som udgangspunkt anbefale alle kurserne. Dog vil jeg særligt anbefale "Population and Global Mental Health", da det er et felt, jeg synes, der mangler mere om på FSV på KU, og derfor var det fedt at have i Melbourne.
unexpected_costs: Huslejen var højere end forventet. Derudover er det også fedt at have sat en del penge af til rejser.
cost_comparison: Husleje var dyrere end forventet. Vi boede et par i en etværelses til 14.000 kr., der er dog billigere alternativer, hvis man skal bo alene. Til gengæld dejligt at man ikke havde udgifter til bøger, men at det var noget man kunne hente ned gratis online.
activities_available: Alt muligt forskelligt sport, fester og forskellige 'klubber'.
activities_recommended: Fedt at være med til et eller andet, lidt ligegyldigt hvad det er, for at lære nogle andre mennesker at kende, som ikke nødvendigvis er fra Danmark.
weekend_recommendations: Mit bedste råd er at rejse så meget rundt som muligt. Kan være små ture til nationalparker tæt på, eller længere ture. Vi var i Sydney, langs østkysten (Byron Bay, Noosa osv.), en roadtrip på vestkysten fra Perth til Exmouth, en forlænget weekend til Tasmanien, besøgte Uluru (stor oplevelse) og var i Cairns. Det er selvfølgelig dyrt, men virkelig alle pengene værd! Derfor kan det også give mening at tænke over at lægge sine fag smart, sådan så man har mulighed for at tage forlængede weekender forskellige stedet hen i løbet af semesteret.
culture_adjustment: Det var nemt, ingen problemer.
socializing_tips: Udnyt at man går til undervisning med en masse, få snakket godt der og få en masse tips. Alle jeg mødte var super søde.
cultural_challenges: Ikke noget særligt.
culture_appreciated: At de fleste bare er super søde og nede på jorden.
top3_advice: Kom godt rundt i byen, den har så meget at byde på. Rejs så meget du kan (og vil). Brug tid på at søge legater inden du tager afsted - det er det værd, også selvom det er lidt uoverskueligt at skulle tænke på oveni ens igangværende semester.
other_useful_info: Tror det er nævnt andre steder
most_rewarding: Alle de oplevelser man har fået med hjemme, smukke steder man har set og dejlige mennesker man har mødt.
greatest_challenge: Boligjagten. Koldt vand i blodet, man skal nok finde noget.

crucial_aspects: I was mainly interested in English-speaking destinations. I also saw exchange as an opportunity to visit a faraway place. Another thing I prioritised was a university that would be somewhat close to the city.
info_ease: It was fairly easy. The University of Melbourne makes it very clear that you can go to Stop 1 if you need any help.
arrival_assistance: There was an introduction week where we got a lot of information and were able to seek help if we needed it.
arrival_comments: The introduction week was one week before the official start of uni so keep this in mind when booking flight tickets. You don't want to miss the introduction week both for social and practical reasons.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You choose the subjects you want. Then you can edit your schedule so it suits you.
registration_help: You can always contact stop 1.
registration_success: I ended up being pretty satisfied with the subjects I took. However, the process was a bit stressful in the beginning. It is easy to choose the subjects you want to take and to customize a schedule that suits you. But when changing some of my subjects during the first week (though it is nice that you have the opportunity to do so) I found that a lot of the subjects were full or clashed with my other subjects. You may have to compromise.
registration_advice: My advice is to check out your chosen subjects pretty thoroughly just so you have better odds at avoiding changing subjects.
course_level: I took one first-year subject, two second-year subjects and one third-year subject.
teaching_comparison: I found it pretty similar to ucph. The teaching style varied from subject to subject just like it does at ucph. I had lectures (three out of four were unfortunately online pre-recorded) and tutorials.
courses_enrolled: - Performance, Potential and Development - Diplomat, Soldier, Spy: The Deep State - Internet Communication - Marketing Communications
recommended_courses: I would recommend Diplomat, Soldier, Spy: The Deep State if you are interested in surveillance, technology and the relationship between state and citizen. It is an anthropology course so it may be a bit different compared to the courses you have been through in Communication and IT.
unexpected_costs: In most student accommodation stuff for the kitchen (plates, knives, cups, pots and pans etc.) is not included.
cost_comparison: Housing was definitely more expensive than expected. Eating out and grocery shopping was also more expensive than expected. Eating out is probably the same as in Denmark. Groceries may even be a bit more expensive compared to Denmark. Alcohol is also super expensive. Except for the wine which is very cheap.
activities_available: Almost any sports. Language specific clubs, book clubs, wine clubs, environment clubs etc.
activities_recommended: I was a part of the athletics club where we ran each Monday and Wednesday. You weren't expected to come each time, you could join as you pleased. They have different teams for different levels. I joined the development team which was both for beginners and those who join competitions. I was also a part of the wine club. I enjoyed it although there was only 1 event during the semester.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend going travelling in the mid-semester break or whenever you feel like you have time. If you are travelling around Australia I would recommend considering the weather and when it is best to visit the different places. Some places up north go into rain season and stinger season. Also highly recommend visiting Byron Bay when it is "beach weather".
culture_adjustment: It was quite easy. There were many cultural differences but non of them were of any major importance.
socializing_tips: Australians are very welcoming and friendly people. Not like danish people they don't mind speaking to strangers. Through my job working in an ice cream shop, I also met locals. I highly recommend getting a part-time job.
cultural_challenges: I hated that cafés closed at around 2 pm haha. But nothing challenging I would say.
culture_appreciated: I really appreciated that Australians are very open and approachable. I loved their day drinking and barbecue meet-ups.
top3_advice: 1. There is plenty to do and see in and around Melbourne. 2. Don't forget to bring warm clothes. My semester in Melbourne was colder than usual. But in general, the temperatures can go from 23 degrees one day to 12 degrees the next day. 3.
other_useful_info: I really enjoyed working beside my studies. It is super easy to get a job in Australia at the moment. I worked in an ice cream shop. The pay is good, you get to meet a lot of new people and you feel more like a part of the city.
most_rewarding: I have met a lot of other exchange students from Denmark and other countries who I have become great friends with.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was probably finding housing. It wasn't that I was afraid that I would end up on the streets. It was just difficult finding something that wasn't too expensive or too far away.

crucial_aspects: The subjects provided at the university, the language and opportunity to explore a completely different nature.
info_ease: University of Melbourne were really good at providing good orientation about choosing/changing subjects, the online communication platform as so forth, to have a nice and easy start at the university.
arrival_assistance: The orientation week is filled with information on different society and sports clubs and general information on how to study at UniMelb.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You register for subjects online, which is quite easy but will take some time.
registration_help: You can easily contact the university if you have any questions. They are really nice and quick to answer.
registration_success: I was able to register for all the subjects I wanted.
registration_advice: University of Melbourne offers a lot of "different" subjects, such as meditation, wine tasting etc. So if you're allowed (from the home university) to take those kind of subjects, I would really recommend. I regret not taking those, as other people I met seemed to really connect with other students through those courses. Otherwise, take a good amount of time to look through the courses. There are plenty and it will be hard to choose. However, you are allowed to change the subjects within the first couple of weeks you start.
course_level: I think the overall academic level were similar to Copenhagen university. However, the whole learning system is a bit different with many assignments during the semester that will all be a part of the overall score for the course and thus, the final grade. Therefore, I think it is easier to pass the courses compared to Copenhagen uni.
teaching_comparison: In Australia the university courses are evaluated during the whole semester. Therefore, the study load is bigger than Copenhagen uni based on assignments and quizzes. You might also have more than one exam in a particular course. On the other hand, the presssure from the final exams are less intensive, as you will already have passed part of the courses.
courses_enrolled: Medical Microbiology: Parasitology. Medical Microbiology: virology. Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques. Developmental Neurobiology.
recommended_courses: Developmental Neurobiology and Medical Microbiology: Parasitology were both courses that I really enjoyed following. The teaching and feedback is really good as well as the topics covered.
unexpected_costs: Flight tickets were more expensive than expected.
cost_comparison: Housing costs in Melbnourne depends on where you're willing to stay and how long you're willing to wait for accommodation but in general a bit more expensive than Copenhagen. Otherwise, the living costs are comparable to Copenhagen (except beers, which are really expensive ;))
activities_available: University of Melbourne has everything! All kinds of sports and social clubs!
activities_recommended: Do engage in some of the social or sports clubs. You will meet other nice people, and there is for sure one club that will fit you.
weekend_recommendations: Go around Melbourne and explore the Victoria state. There is so much beautiful and incredible nature.
culture_adjustment: Melbourne is not that different from Copenhagen in that sense, so you will easily adjust to that.
socializing_tips: Just be open and talk to the fellow student in your classes. Otherwise, engage in some sport or social club.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: Melbourne is a super cool city with a lot of social and artistic culture. There is many really good restaurants and bars and you can almost always find live music.
top3_advice: Don't worry about accommodation if you haven't figured it out from home, you will find it when you arrive. Go explore the state Victoria, it is so amazing. Do attend the orientation week as you will easily find some people to talk to, which is nice when you don't know anyone in the city.
other_useful_info: Buy a bike. It is cheap in Melbourne and you will be able to easily get around.
most_rewarding: Meeting really good people to have in the daily Melbourne life. Traveling around Melbourne during weekends to see the wild nature of Australia.
greatest_challenge: Being completely on your own at the beginning of the stay, which is something different that you need to figure out how to cope with.

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte at tage på udveksling til Australien, både for den akademiske udfordring og muligheder som universitetet tilbød. der var ble. langt flere fag at vælge imellem som var spændende og relevante for mine ønskede karrieremuligheder. Derudover kendte jeg nogle i landet, som kunne hjælpe med noget af det praktiske.
overall_comments: Det var fantastisk både at have 6 mdr. i Australien og føle sig hjemme i Melbourne, men også at få mulighed for at læse spændende fag som ikke udbydes på KU.
info_ease: Det var utroligt nemt at finde hjælp fra University of Melbournes hjemmeside og studieportal, den er koblet op på samme system som ved KU, så det var nemt at gå til.
arrival_assistance: Der var obligatorisk intromøde et par uger før studiestart og det var super informativt og relevant. Jeg modtog samtidig mails fra et udvekslings "hjælpeteam" som informerede om deadlines, sociale aktiviteter osv.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Det var fantastisk både at have 6 mdr. i Australien og føle sig hjemme i Melbourne, men også at få mulighed for at læse spændende fag som ikke udbydes på KU.
registration_process: Man valgte fag på en søgeportal, læste lidt om dem og meldte sig til på en tilmeldingsside med fagets kode. Det var ret intuitivt på deres indskrivningstjeneste og man fik hjælp til intromøde.
registration_help: Udover intromøde kunne man fysisk henvende sig på campus i en afdeling kaldet "stop 1" hvor ældre studerende og tech-folk kunne hjælpe med opsættelse af fag/ computer/ kort over campus/ alt hvad man behøvede hjælp til. Især hjælp til indskrivning af fag anvendte jeg.
registration_success: Jeg kunne tilmelde mig alle de fag jeg ønskede, mit indtryk er at det var gældende for de fleste, at der var pladser nok på de fag man helst ville. (om ikke fysisk, så online)
registration_advice: Gennemgå universitets guide/ din personlige opsætning af din account og hjemmeside grundigt før du ankommer. Der er alt den hjælp du skal bruge og det er nemt beskrevet.
academics_comments: Det var fantastisk både at have 6 mdr. i Australien og føle sig hjemme i Melbourne, men også at få mulighed for at læse spændende fag som ikke udbydes på KU.
course_level: Jeg valgte 4 fag, på et lidt "lavere" niveau. Altså tilsvarende 3-4. semester og jeg tog 5. semester. Det betød at jeg allerede havde arbejdet med lidt af pensum, hvilket var en fordel for mig, da det også tager ekstra tid når det hele skal skrives og diskuteres på engelsk. generelt var niveauet ret kompatibelt med KU vil jeg mene.
teaching_comparison: Vi havde én forelæsning i hvert fag en gang om ugen og derudover tutor undervisning i hvert fag, hvor der var mulighed for diskussion af tekster og materiale i mindre klasser.
courses_enrolled: Kurserne hed: - Avantgarde and Postmodern art - Contemporary Aboriginal Art - Street-art - Art, Market and Method
recommended_courses: Jeg vil anbefale, hvis man har muligheden for det, at læse noget om aboriginsk kunst, kultur og samfundsmæssige problematikker hvis man vælger at tage til Australien. Det var både det mest spændende fag, men derudover også en vigtig del af den australske kultur og historie at have med sig når man befinder sig generelt i landet.
unexpected_costs: Man skal både have en Bupa forsikring og almindelig rejseforsikring, hvilket var lidt dyrt. Derudover er det dyrere end i Danmark at handle ind i supermarkederne.
cost_comparison: Det er langt dyrere end i Danamrk at ryge, drikke alkohol og handle almindelige råvare ind. Det er til gengæld billigere at drikke god baristakaffe ude/ deres cafekultur er billigere og meget brugt.
activities_available: Alt var muligt - der er utallige klubber, sportshold, kaffemuligheder med andre studerende osv.
activities_recommended: Jeg vil anbefale at komme til alle introfesterne/ de sociale intro arrangementer for at møde en masse andre studerende og danne sig en venskabsgruppe.
weekend_recommendations: Rejs rundt i landet eller bliv i Melbourne, alt er en oplevelse. Man kan ikke nå det hele, så vælg nogle steder at opleve og tag god tid til at se det.
culture_adjustment: Det var nemt, nok fordi jeg også kendte nogle i forvejen, men australiere er generelt super hjælpsomme og venlige.
cultural_challenges: Der er ikke så stor kulturel forskel.
culture_appreciated: At man altid kan få hjælp af alle, folk er meget opmærksomme på hinanden og super imødekommende.
top3_advice: - Spar penge op til det. Det er altid dyrere end man forestiller sig. - Kom hurtigt ud og mød mennekser og inviter dem ud, da tiden går hurtigt og det er rart at opbygge noget socialt så hurtigt som muligt, således der er nogle potentielle rejsemakkere. - Vælg fag der knytter sig til værtslandet.
other_useful_info: Studiet kan godt blive travlt i perioder, da der er flere (men mindre) skriftlige afleveringer, så hav det in mente at du ikke laver rejseplaner/weekendplaner i eksamensperioderne, da der bliver meget at se til og korte deadlines.
most_rewarding: At bo og leve i Melbourne og få en hverdag i et andet land har været super givende.
greatest_challenge: At finde et sted at bo var det sværeste, så kig gerne efter dine muligheder inden du ankommer.

crucial_aspects: I had heard really good things about Melbourne and its student life - and besides, it was important to me that it was an English-speaking country.
info_ease: The host university had sent out a guide to the students about important information etc.
arrival_assistance: As mentioned, the university had made a thorough guide with step by step for important things for arrival and the first few days. And if you needed help with something, you could meet at "stop1", which was located at the university.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The entire registration process is sent out by e-mail - and there are simply different steps you have to follow, also in relation to important dates, e.g. with registration for subjects etc.
registration_help: You could always get help from either KU or the host university - and as mentioned, there was "Stop 1" on arrival, where there was always someone who could help, regardless of whether it was about about your subjects, bupa or something like that.
registration_success: Registering for the classes was super easy, and you could choose which times of the week you wanted the subjects - as long as you were aware of the dates for registering this.
registration_advice: There is a lot of information and registration processes you just have to go through - but it is okay easy as long as you follow what is sent to you and pay attention to the dates.
course_level: We had the opportunity to choose subjects between levels 1-3. It was very clear that level 1 was super easy and level 3 was more difficult. But in general, I would personally say that the level at home is higher - however, there is more work during the semester, as you are graded on all assignments, which end up in an overall grade.
teaching_comparison: The teaching itself is very similar to the one we know at home with lectures and practice lessons.
courses_enrolled: Principles of Management, Marketing Communication, Performance, Potential and Development, Graphic Design
recommended_courses: Marketing Communication was super nice, we also had a really good teacher. Principle of Management was also very interesting (and easy).
unexpected_costs: Wouldn't say there was anything unexpected, but just that Australia is a super expensive place to live, especially in terms of food and experiences
cost_comparison: The same as above regarding food and experiences
activities_available: The university were super good at organizing events especially for exchange students, everything from cultural to sports events, you could simply follow along on various social media and see when and where different events took place
activities_recommended: Definitely participate in the orientation week, as there are a lot of fun activities and plenty of opportunity to meet a lot of the other exchanges. In addition, I would recommend to join a club/sport - I participated in the surf club, which organized weekend trips and events occasionally
weekend_recommendations: Great Ocean Road, Surf trip to Torquay, extended weekend trip to Sydney, go to Byron Bay in mid-semester break, Mornington Peninsula, wine-tour to Yarra Valley etc.
culture_adjustment: Super easy.
socializing_tips: Definitely become part of a sport/club or find a job, it's super easy and definitely the easiest way to meet the locals
cultural_challenges: Nothing in particular
culture_appreciated: That Australians are the most open and welcoming people, so friendly and nice to be around
top3_advice: Take advantage of the weekends and go on weekend trips, enjoy all of it (time flies:)), explore Melbourne, there are so many great places to see and experience
other_useful_info: Go, you will never regret it. Melbourne is the most amazing city
most_rewarding: The whole experience - getting the opportunity to live in Australia, study at a super good university and meet so many different and nice people - as well as see and experience so many beautiful places
greatest_challenge: Be on your own and create your own everyday life in a foreign country

crucial_aspects: It was important for me that my study destination was English-speaking and had a great study life.
overall_comments: Melbourne was the perfect city for a study destination. The people were very open-minded, and the city was very vibrant and cool. The university had a lot of great events and was really welcoming. The only bad part about Melbourne was the weather. The weather changed a lot, and sometimes it felt like four different seasons in one day.
info_ease: It was pretty easy. The University of Melbourne has a lot of information on its website.
arrival_assistance: They offered to pick one up from the airport.
arrival_comments: I was delighted with the orientation and help from the University of Melbourne. It was easy to get in contact with them over the mail. The university has a help centre, which was very helpful.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Melbourne was the perfect city for a study destination. The people were very open-minded, and the city was very vibrant and cool. The university had a lot of great events and was really welcoming. The only bad part about Melbourne was the weather. The weather changed a lot, and sometimes it felt like four different seasons in one day.
registration_process: You receive a mail from the university where you have to follow some steps to get approved. It took me around a month to finish it. Remember to apply for your visa early on (some Danish students had some problems receiving it).
registration_help: You can mail the University of Melbourne, and they have a short response time.
registration_success: It was very successful. I got the classes I applied for. However, I ended up changing some of the classes.
registration_advice: Remember to make good research for the classes you want to take and remember you can always change it if you don't like it. It is a good idea to make a broad ”forhåndsgodkendelse”, so you are able to pick another class if you change your mind.
academics_comments: Melbourne was the perfect city for a study destination. The people were very open-minded, and the city was very vibrant and cool. The university had a lot of great events and was really welcoming. The only bad part about Melbourne was the weather. The weather changed a lot, and sometimes it felt like four different seasons in one day.
course_level: The level of the courses was fine, they were not too difficult. The structure of the assignments was very similar to the way you do it on UCPH.
teaching_comparison: At the University of Melbourne, my courses were more like exercise classes. Whereas at UCPH I have both lectures and exercise classes. Another difference was that the University of Melbourne had an attendance hurdle, I was only allowed to have two absent days from each class.
courses_enrolled: Graphic Design Internet communication Marketing communication Performance, potential and development
recommended_courses: In Internet communication, I had a really great teacher and you learn a lot of different topics in the course.
unexpected_costs: Travels. You travel a lot when you are on exchange and take a lot of weekend trips.
cost_comparison: More expensive than expected: house rents and food in supermarket
activities_available: There were a lot of different sports clubs, language clubs and a wine club.
activities_recommended: The running club. It is a small team and you don't have to be advanced to be part of it.
weekend_recommendations: For weekend trips, you should go to Wilsons Prom, Mornington Peninsula and Great Ocean Road. For longer trips, you should travel along the East coast.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. It's a Western culture and everyone speaks English.
socializing_tips: The easiest way to socialize with the local students is in the class. A lot of the students are very open-minded. Get a job. A lot of students have jobs next to their studies. (Bonus: the pay is pretty good in Australia).
cultural_challenges: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.
culture_appreciated: It is an English-speaking country, and the people are very welcoming.
top3_advice: - Remember that you only have to pass the subjects, so no reason to stress - It's okay not to say yes to everything - Join a sports club. Unimelb has a lot of good sport club options
other_useful_info: The weather in Melbourne changes a lot, so remember to bring both warm and cold clothes with you. Bring a backpack if you wanna travel afterwards. Housing can be expensive so it is a good idea to research housing options beforehand.
most_rewarding: All the great friends I have met in Melbourne and all the trips we went on.
greatest_challenge: To find an apartment that was affordable.

crucial_aspects: I really wanted to go to either Australia or New Zealand, so that was kin of a crucial aspect for me. But also to study in an english speaking country. I felt that that would give me the best opportunities to meet the culture and not just explore it but live in the culture. Another crucial aspect were also that it was possible to undertake more analytical subjects at the university. I wasn't really interested in finance why it was important for me to have the opportunity to undertake other subjects.

Therefore the classes isn't the best place to meet new friends. But the clubs connected to the university is a great place to meet people. I was a part of the surf club and the dive club and that was where I met all of the people I spoke with.

housing_how: I found housing on my own

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne til et engelsktalende land, så jeg nemmere kunne kommunikere med lokalbefolkningen. info_ease: University of Melbourne har et super godt system, der hjælper udvekslingsstuderende rigtig godt. Jeg er ikke selv den bedste til at få læst alle de mails, man får i forbindelse med noget som et udvekslingsophold, men de laver en pop-up, hvor man kan komme fysisk og få hjælp til alt med enrollment.
arrival_assistance: Jeg modtog hjælp i pop-up. University of Melbourne er ekstremt dygtige til at modtage udvekslingsstuderende, og man følte sig godt hjulpet på vej. housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Jeg havde ikke fået registreret mig gennem alle de mails man fik.
