registration_help: Hjemmesiden er super hjælpsom og så hjælpen i Stop 1, deres hjælpecentral, hvor ansatte ved universitetet guider dig igennem de forskellige steps.
registration_success: Jeg var heldigvis meget succesfuld i at få de fag jeg gerne ville. Der var dog nogle fag, som jeg fandt ud var online pga. corona, og det var lidt træls, men så var der heldigvis andre fag, som jeg også gerne ville have.
registration_advice: Hvis du ligesom mig er en dør til at få gjort ting som det, så gå ned i Stop 1 og få hjælp til hele processen. Det er super hjælpsomt og man er sikker på, at man har fået gjort alt det rigtige.
course_level: Niveauet var lavere end jeg har oplevet det i Danmark, men jeg havde til gengæld også flere praktiske fag. Det gjorde mig ikke som sådan noget, jeg var mere bare overrasket over det.
teaching_comparison: Undervisningen var meget mere praktisk orienteret og øvelsestimer var mere guidede af en underviser.
courses_enrolled: Australia in the Wine World Writing for Screen Introduction to Media Writing Audiovisual Communication
recommended_courses: Australia in the Wine World: Giver i princippet ingen mening for mig, fordi jeg læser film- og medievidenskab, men jeg ville gerne have et lidt anderledes og sjovt valgfag. Det er et virkelig fedt fag. Jeg tog det mest for sjov, men er endt med at lære helt vildt meget om vin og søger nu også job på vinbarer. Writing for Screen er rigtig fedt hvis man gerne vil være manuskriptforfatter eller bare er interesseret i det. Eksamen er lave et manuskript til en kortfilm og det er meget mere praktisk orienteret end KU. Desuden bestod hver forelæsning af én times klassisk forelæsning og én times oplæg fra en manuskriptforfatter i branchen, hvilket gjorde faget meget mere "tilgængeligt" i den forstand at man følte det reelt kunne bruges til noget. Og fik gode ideer til hvordan man kunne starte i branchen. Audiovisual Communication er KUN praktisk. Vi havde nogle forelæsninger på én time, men det er vitterligt at snakke lidt om forskellige doku-genrer og greb. Hele faget handlede om at vi skulle lave en 4 min lang nonfiktionsfilm og uden nogen læsninger eller noget. Så rigtig fedt, hvis man bare gerne vil arbejde praktisk.
unexpected_costs: I forbindelse med mit visum blev jeg udtaget som stikprøve og skulle undergå en "medical examination". Vi var en del der blev udtaget. I DK koster det 3500 kr. og i Australien 1700 kr. Fordi lægerne var på ferie i DK skulle jeg gøre det i Australien, men du kan ikke få et student visa uden, derfor blev jeg nødt til at søge et tourist visa først (100 kr.).
cost_comparison: Øl og alkohol generelt er virkelig dyrt, til gengæld er sushi rolls meget billigere.
activities_available: Stort set alt du kan forestille dig, der var nærmest en klub for det hele. Og de er gode til at lave dage hvor du kan besøge alle klubberne ved forskellige boder, så man nemt kan blive en del af dem.
activities_recommended: Bliv medlem af en eller anden klub bare for sjov, man kan altid melde sig ud virkelig nemt, men det er sjovt at prøve nogle ting af som du ikke kan i Danmark.
weekend_recommendations: I Victoria: Phillip Island (pingviner) og Great Ocean Road. Jeg tog med nogle venner til Vestkysten i min mid-semester break og rejste i to uger (tag nogle dage før og efter fri) og vi rejste fra Perth til Exmouth og må bare erkende at Vestkysten er det mest undervurdere sted ift Østkysten!! Jeg rejste en måned på østkysten efter semestret og anbefaler seriøst en vantur op ad vestkysten i stedet for (østkysten er meget mere turistet og mange ting ligner hinanden lidt). Desuden var jeg to uger på Tasmanien og kan ikke fortælle nok om hvor smukt og sindssygt der var der! Mange af mine venner rejste i løbet af semestret, men det er vanvittigt koldt der - rejs i december eller januar og få gode soldage imens! Og udover det - ikke kun tag en uge, det er seriøst alt for lidt tid (jeg havde to og troede det ville være alt for meget tid ift. hvad andre havde sagt, og det er seriøst næsten ikke engang nok!!)
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt, det minder ret meget om København rent kulturelt bortset fra at folk er mindre reserverede.
socializing_tips: Australiere er seriøst de sødeste mennesker så bare snak med dem, de er så easy going og spørg om de vil med ud og have øl.
cultural_challenges: Jeg synes, det var hårdt i starten at øl var så dyre og kaffebarer lukker kl.15, men ellers er der ikke rigtig nogle kulturforskelle der er svære.
culture_appreciated: Australieres mindset synes jeg godt danskere kunne lære noget af. At være super easy going og bare snakke med nye mennesker og være mere interesserede i dem end jeg oplever herhjemme.
top3_advice: Tilmeld dig Frozen Meals - så sparer man helt vildt mange penge på mad! Universitetet tilbyder frosne måltider til studerende, men man skal huske at melde sig til. Gå til alle de der ting i starten selvom nogle virker lidt spøjse, det er en super god måde at lære skolen og andre studerende at kende på og se hvilke ting der kunne være sjove at prøve. Der er så mange anderledes og sjove fag, så tag fx et fag og dediker det til noget sjovt og anderledes.
other_useful_info: Udover frozen meals kan man også tilmelde sig et program hvor man får gratis frugt og grønt, det er også rigtig fedt og man kan spare en masse penge.
most_rewarding: De venskaber og netværk jeg har fået og de perspektiver på mit liv derhjemme.
greatest_challenge: Økonomi var klart det sværeste, fordi det er vildt dyrt og der er mange udgifter ifb. et udvekslingsophold i Australien.

crucial_aspects: Besides experiencing a new culture and trying to live abroad on the other side of the world, the academic opportunities at UniMelb also appealed to me.
overall_comments: Definitely worth it. You learn a lot about yourself and you get to broaden your horizon.
info_ease: It was quite easy. You already get a lot of information through mail prior to arriving and there is a welcome day and an orientation week before the teaching period begins, where you'll get all the necessary information.
arrival_assistance: I felt like I got assistance with almost everything. There is definitely more assistance in general than at UCPH, where you are expected to complete various things more independently.
arrival_comments: I don't feel like there was anything where I didn't get the necessary help.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Definitely worth it. You learn a lot about yourself and you get to broaden your horizon.
registration_process: After getting the pre-approval from UCPH you have to check whether the specific course has pre-requisites. If it does, you have to email the professor and prove that you meet those pre-requisites. After this, you can enrol in the course. There is plenty of help how to do this at "Stop 1", which you will hear about when you get down there.
registration_help: There was plenty of help for enrolling in your courses at "Stop 1", so don't stress about it.
registration_success: I basically got all courses I wanted.
registration_advice: Again: Don't stress too much about it before getting down there as you will have plenty of time to enroll in the courses. It's a good idea to have a look in the handbook prior to arriving though and see what kind of courses are offered.
academics_comments: Definitely worth it. You learn a lot about yourself and you get to broaden your horizon.
course_level: Generally the same level as at UCPH, but of course depending on the subject. However, the workload during the semester was bigger at UniMelb since you have to hand in assignments and hold presentations which account for a certain percentage of your grade. This is very different to UCPH, where you mostly just have one big exam in the end. However, this did make the final exam period less stressful and intense than at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: Mostly the same as at UCPH with both lectures and tutorials.
courses_enrolled: Macroeconometrics (ECOM90007) Quantitative Analysis of Finance II (ECON90010) Derivative Securities (FNCE90011) Data Analysis for Finance (FNCE90083)
recommended_courses: If you're interested in learning about bayesian techniques in macroeconometrics then I'd definitely recommend Macroeconometrics (ECOM90007). As far as I know there is no course at UCPH covering bayesian econometrics, so this is quite a unique opportunity. However, the workload in this course is very big. I think I devoted around 80% of my study time to this course. The course is very rewarding though and the lecturer (Tomasz Wozniak) is great. Other than that I'd also recommend Derivative Securities (FNCE90011). It is not math heavy (compared to what we are used to at UCPH), but is rather focusing on the intuition behind pricing various derivatives.
unexpected_costs: There weren't really any unexpected cost, however the general price level was just higher than expected I guess.
cost_comparison: Rent - More expensive than in Copenhagen Groceries - Probably same price level as in Copenhagen Take away food - A bit cheaper than in Copenhagen Beer - Way more expensive than in Copenhagen Coffee - Way cheaper than in Copenhagen
activities_available: There is a club for almost anything, so there is plenty of opportunity to engage in various activities.
activities_recommended: Join the surf club and participate in one of the surf camps - you'll have a great time. Further, I could also recommend the mountaineering club as they also offer some great trips.
weekend_recommendations: Enjoy all the events in Melbourne and explore a bit of Victoria. (Great Ocean Road, Grampians National Park, Wilsons Promontory National Park)
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy as Australia obviously also is a western society and therefore not too hard to adjust to.
socializing_tips: Join one of the aforementioned clubs. You will meet a lot of the local students there.
cultural_challenges: There weren't really any differences I found challenging - just different.
culture_appreciated: Australians are very open and talkative and not as reserved as Europeans, which was really nice.
top3_advice: 1. Go travelling before and/or after the semester 2. 3. Bring warm clothes as Melbourne gets cold in the winter.
other_useful_info: Buy a bike. Public transport is quite expensive in Melbourne, but the bike lanes are pretty good actually.
most_rewarding: Making friends from all over the world and being able to perform academically in a foreign country.
greatest_challenge: Managing the big workload during the semester while also trying to have as much fun as possible.

crucial_aspects: To experience Australia has been a dream of mine for many years. Also, I find it a great advantage to visit an English-speaking country. Even though the culture is not too different from Denmark, Australia is something completely unique
overall_comments: Going on exchange is the best thing I have ever done for myself.
info_ease: All the administrative work before going on exchange is super tiring and feels very overwhelming. But studenterservice can definitely help with a lot of questions, and the exchange inbound team at UniMelb was also very helpfull. But it is a loooong process, but when you go - it is all worth it. Reach out to older students and ask for their advice.
arrival_assistance: The inbound team at Unimelb offers a lot of information and they have an office (STOP1) where you can go for assistance and easily get an appointment. Here they will help you with everything from course registration to getting your card for public transport.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Going on exchange is the best thing I have ever done for myself.
registration_process: You registrer in advance and then you are allocated through the UniMelb platform. When allocated you need to chose the specific sessions of the course that you want to join (they often have more than one) This way you can create your own schedule.
registration_help: Stop1
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted
registration_advice: If in doubt. Go to Stop1.
academics_comments: Going on exchange is the best thing I have ever done for myself.
course_level: Based on the advice from UCPH I followed third year BA courses even though I am a MA student at UCPH. I found some courses were easier and some were harder than the ones I've previously had at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: The most difficult thing about studying in Australia compared to Denmark is the continuous assessment. This means, that you have to 'earn' points during the semester that in the end accumulates to your final grade. Aka you need to perform well all the time, if you want to do well in the end. However, this style also takes a lot of pressure of the final exam that often 'only' accounts for 60% of your final grade.
courses_enrolled: Australia in the Wine World (AGRI10039) Medical and Applied Immunology (MIIM30003) Experimental Pathology (PATH20003) Frontiers In Human Disease (PATH30003)
recommended_courses: Australia in the Wine World (AGRI10039) Very fun and different. My 'non-serious course' I used my free elective course on. It is definitely work - so don't underestimate it. But we had wine tastings every week and I learnt a great deal of wine through the course and had a lot of fun. I would definitely recommend choosing at least one course outside your normal field of study to try something new and give your brain a bit of a break. This is an unique opportunity to do so. Medical and Applied Immunology (MIIM30003) Super interesting and really high quality lectures!! But SUPER difficult. Don't take this course if you haven't had any previous courses about immunology. I took 'Immunology' on my BA at UCPH and I still struggled with following the course. The requirements are super high so be prepared to work hard! However, I know that my interests lie within immunology so I definitely would have still enrolled in this course if I had to choose again. Experimental Pathology (PATH20003) Fun but quite easy lab-based course. With a background of a BA in Molekylær Biomedicin I had a clear advantage in this course compared to the Australian students. But ist was a fun way to meet a lot of local students since you are enrolled in a lab group that follows you the entire semester. We had to hand in reports every 14 days, but they were pretty straight forward. It just takes time. The work goes very in depth with a lot of fun topics like forensics pathology and looking at anatomical specimens. Frontiers In Human Disease (PATH30003) Super interesting and inspiring. A course that goes through 34 lectures basically covering a new disease every lecture. The lectures are presented by experts within each disease so there is A LOT of content to learn, but it is very interesting to learn about what is going on in research within each specific disease.
unexpected_costs: None unexpected costs
cost_comparison: We had the pleasure of being enrolled in the 'food allocation programme' were you as a student would be allocated frozen meals every week! It saved us A LOT of money of food. The initiative was started during COVID but I don't know how long it will run for unfortunately
activities_available: I joined the surf club and went to a few exchange events in the beginning. Unimelb has a exchange society called (MUSEX) that hosts a heap of events.
activities_recommended: Go to the exchange (MUSEX) events in the beginning. Reach out to the students in your classes to get in contact with Australians. If you're single - go on a few dates. It's a fun way to meet people who knows the city ;)
weekend_recommendations: Visit the nature around Melbourne but don't stress to much about needing to experiencing ALL OF AUSTRALIA. You won't have time to do it either way ;). Make peace with the fact that one of the greatest things about exchange is just experiencing actually living in a new city. Melbourne has SO much to offer so roam around the beautiful streets in the suburbs and enjoy life. Don't stress about needing to do everything all at once. And make peace with saying no.
culture_adjustment: Super easy. Everyone in Australia are SO SWEET and welcoming! You can pick up a chat almost everywhere and a lot of people a genuinely excited to get to know you.
socializing_tips: Just go up and approach them. You have nothing to loose. And everyone is so nice.
cultural_challenges: No challenges.
culture_appreciated: Just the fact that everyone is so open, kind and welcoming. It is truly inspiring and something I would wish danish people also was.
top3_advice: Make peace with the fact that you are not going to experience everything and that it's okay to say no. Don't let other people stress you out. Be prepared for the beginning being tough. I cried a lot in the first week and felt very far away from home. However, if anyone told me at that point in time that I needed to go through that one tough week to get 25 so absolutely amazing weeks I would do it again, without a doubt. Don't be afraid to take some changes and approach people. This experience is such a great change to challenge yourself.
other_useful_info: Ask the older students for advice - they have some great first-hand experience. Also. Stay at The Nunnery Hostel when you first arrive in Melbourne. The hostel is low quality and super cold in Aussie winter. But I met all of my friends at that hostel! So hang in there while you look for accommodation. BRING A LOT OF WARM CLOTHES! AND AN UMBRELLA! The weather in Melbourne is even more unreliable than in Copenhagen. And the winter is absolutely freezing - also inside the houses. I definitely underestimated the cold.
most_rewarding: Challenging myself and realising that I am fully capable of being independent and creating a network of friends and feeling safe and at home on the other side of the planet.
greatest_challenge: The first week. Where everthing was unsettled. I was struggling with finding accommodation and I felt very far away from home.
other_comments: DO IT, DO IT, DO IT! It is truly the best thing I have ever done for myself.

crucial_aspects: That I could take electives that I couldn't in my home country.
info_ease: Very easy. I've been here before.
arrival_assistance: None.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was all online.
registration_help: None.
registration_success: I got all the electives I wanted.
registration_advice: Apply in groups and help each other out.
course_level: The level of courses was as stated on the Uni Melbourne website.
teaching_comparison: Very similar to the ones in Denmark.
courses_enrolled: Foundations of Computing Graphic Design Studio Internet Communication Performance, Potential and Development
recommended_courses: Foundations of computing and graphic design were really fun!
unexpected_costs: Doctors appointments.
cost_comparison: Books were cheaper as there wasn't any.
activities_available: I don't know as I didn't go to them
activities_recommended: The national gallery of Victoria, which is free as a uni student
weekend_recommendations: Nature is beautiful.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, Melbourne has a very european feel to it.
cultural_challenges: Everything is opposite, like sidewalks, steering wheel position etc.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness
top3_advice: Engage with the bars, find a good study group, explore other campuses
other_useful_info: Most of the material is online
most_rewarding: Seeing old friends
greatest_challenge: It wasn't that challenging

crucial_aspects: That subjects were taught in English and the city had a prominent and vibrant cultural life. Also, that the weather was somewhat hot (Spoiler alert: I didn't do my research proporly).
overall_comments: Exchange has been such a fun experience! Melbourne is a fantastic city and very easy to live in. I have left the city with friends for life and a minor vape addiction.
info_ease: Very easy. Everything's in English. Signs are English. Tramp voices are in English. People are English. Amazing how all information is available in English ey?
arrival_assistance: I didn't receive any assistance. I guess the University offers some if you need it tho, they are used to babysit american exchange students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Exchange has been such a fun experience! Melbourne is a fantastic city and very easy to live in. I have left the city with friends for life and a minor vape addiction.
registration_process: The university writes e-mails every time you need to provide some information. Which ended up being a lot.
registration_help: idk. I couldn't find any. I just hoped for the best – and you know what? it turned out completely fine.
registration_success: Went great! Got all of them and it was even possible to change subjects up to 2 weeks into the semester.
registration_advice: I know it's frustrating and time-consuming with all the paper work before departing. BUT it's worth it and just like me you'll forget about it pretty quickly.
academics_comments: Exchange has been such a fun experience! Melbourne is a fantastic city and very easy to live in. I have left the city with friends for life and a minor vape addiction.
course_level: New brain level achieved! Or, idk, I learned a lot and had fun while doing it! My subjects weren't the most academic or reading heavy and teachers were very helpfull and enjoyed their field.
teaching_comparison: There were almost no reading. A lot of the subjects allowed for creative expression and hands on experience. The assignments are posted in the beginning of the semester so you can plan out everything and start early. The exams are also shorter word-wise than I'm used to in UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Chinese Music Ensamble, Light in performance, The Art of Game Music & The Business of Music, .
recommended_courses: Uff haha, all of them! Bear in mind that some of the subjects are taught online – meaning you will never meet your teacher or any students who also follows the class. It can be a bit lonesome and might not be the experience you are looking for going on exchange. I had one class on parkville campus and one on southbank and then two online. Loved all of them, and happy I got to experience both city campuses.
unexpected_costs: The house I was living in had a few things that needed to be fixed. I think it was a total of 400$. Then there's also the cost of visa, insurance and your own travel insurance(thanks for paying my travel insurance mom). Plane tickets are expensive too. And if you want to travel Aussie while you're here – you've guessed it – expensive. And you need to quit smoking since a pack of ciggies are 50$. You might think that vaping is cheaper, but you'll soon find yourself vaping on your couch, in your bed and while cooking breakfast – that cost also quickly adds up. Don't smoke kids. what else, what else, what else...... ohh yeah shows! concerts, comedy, footy, festivals – the temptations are all around you!
cost_comparison: Pricing is just like in Denmark even more expensive in some areas – this includes everything related to "fun" like grocery shopping, getting beers, gym memberships, nightlife and taking your cat to the vet. Some people will try and convince you it's cheap going out for dinner – they be lying. Bikes are cheap! but everybody hates cyclists and will try to end your life on a daily basis – especially in the CBD.
activities_available: Sooo so so many. They will let you know at orientation.
activities_recommended: There's so much happening at campus, find something that suits you! I didn't join any uni clubs, but joined a few bouldering gyms and also had a friend who I biked around Victoria with. There's such amazing nature all around Melbourne, jump on a train and go explore.
weekend_recommendations: Get a bike! I loved mine, they are cheap on Facebook marketplace or you can find one at the bike shed – which is a fun community located in Brunswick.
culture_adjustment: Extremely easy. Almost wished I would have gotten a bigger culture shock. Oh one thing! I got stood up by four different dudes who invited me out on a date – I mean the AUDACITY!
socializing_tips: Uff tough one. People are busy with their life – just like in Cph. Most people are very friendly and can easily be chat up in class and convinced to go for a beer after class. Or you can join a club! I was fortunate to live with locals, so they took me to events where I met other Aussies. But I would say that your best odds are to socialize with other exchange students since they're as eager to make new friends as you are! I would also recommend dating (haha even though you might get stood up). I made a lot of friends on dating apps and went for some super cute dates around the city.
cultural_challenges: Aussie slang. You will begin to speak English in another way – a more fun way.
culture_appreciated: People are super chill and are very friendly! Coffee and craft beer is on point. There's a thousand things going on around the city and they have lovely parks everywhere!
top3_advice: Have fun! Uni Melb and Melbourne in general provides so many opportunities it can be overwhelming. Find your own way in your exchange. Enjoy the beautiful hogwards like campus and explore the city and the great nature Victoria has to offer.
other_useful_info: Nahh you'll be fine.
most_rewarding: Awww difficult question – I appreciate everything and already miss it! Enjoy the excellent classes and the wonderful people while you can<3
greatest_challenge: Exam period. You can stay on top of the game by starting your exam writing early. I didn't. It's just my nature. So I was batteling deadlines at the end while getting ready to move out and saying goodbye to people. Don't be like me. Be better.
other_comments: If you are debating going on exchange, I hope after reading this you aren't anymore. If you want to do it, you just got to do it! For me it was worth every worry, every second, every cent!

crucial_aspects: I had never been to Australia, but I'd always wanted to go. Because of the distance I always felt that you needed atleast a few months to go there, which was never an option until I started studying and exchange became a possibility. On top of that, the University of Melbourne is highly regarded internationally, and I was curious to experience a different approach to the psychology degree. On top of that it is an english speaking country, and Melbourne is very similiar to European cities culturally, politically etc. ... And I also just really wanted to travel around Australia, which was possible during the stay, where I visited Tasmania and various locations around Victoria during the exchange and travelled the east coast of Australia for a month upon its completion.
info_ease: It was pretty straightforward, and the host university was very helpful. That being said, I did have some difficulty locating the right subjects/courses, and the University of Melbourne turned out to be very "square" with regards to the psychology degree, where it was impossible to find courses on clinical psychology as an undergraduate. Also there were alot of people wanting help, so you did have to wait for quite a bit before they got back to you.
arrival_assistance: I received some assistance regarding course planning, but not really for anything else.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I can't really remember.
registration_help: It was possible to write them regarding difficulties with this process, but I found that they took a long time getting back to you.
registration_success: I had a hard time finding substitutes for the classes at my home university. Clinical Psychology (bachelor) was impossible, but I did manage to find substitutes for my elective/valgfag and Forskningsdesign og Videnskabs teori.
registration_advice: Just make sure you have some time to really read the information and become familiarized with the different platforms.
course_level: I did Undergraduate 3 and an Honours course as a fifth/sixth semester student in Denmark.
teaching_comparison: It was quite similar with lectures and classes in most of the subjects.
courses_enrolled: Trauma, Memory, Bodies/The Psychopathology of Everyday Life and The History and Philosophy of Science
recommended_courses: I liked them all, but I'm not really sure I would recommend them.
unexpected_costs: Everything was really expensive, which was a bit unexpected.
cost_comparison: I didn't spend any money on books, which was a nice change. Food, transport and accomodation turned out to be very expensive. Activites were expensive.
activities_available: Pretty much everything. I was a member of the Mountaineering and Scuba Diving clubs, which was great
activities_recommended: Both of the above if you are into hiking or diving.
weekend_recommendations: I can recommend just walking around the city and exploring the suburbs. If you are into hiking, I really loved the Dandenong Ranges and the beach walk between Brighton and St. Kilda. I loved the Great Ocean Road, The Grampians (nationalpark) and Wilsons Promotory (nationalpark) for hikes and wildlife. I also really liked the towns of Bright and Castlemaine.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy - they are quite similar to Denmark.
socializing_tips: I found it quite hard to meet locals in Melbourne. As with any big city the residents are quite busy and most of them already have a network of friends, and don't neccessarily want to spend time with someone who is only there for a few months. You have to be very open and make an effort to meet them. I used the app MeetUp quite a bit, and found a lot of groups where I met some very nice people. I can also recommend wednesday boardgames at Fortress in CBD, as a good place to meet cool people.
cultural_challenges: None really.
culture_appreciated: Australians (overall) are very chill and laid back, and they have a great sense of humour.
top3_advice: Be ready to put in a lot of time to make the exchange happen Don't just hang out with the other danish or international students, but make an effort to socialize Don't stay in campus housing Don't spend all your time on school, but explore the city and the surrounds - it is very beautiful down there.
other_useful_info: Not that I can think of.
most_rewarding: Exploring Australia - it is a spectacular place.
greatest_challenge: Bureaucracy and housing.
other_comments: No.

crucial_aspects: Mit valg af University of Melbourne blev motiveret af universitetets akademiske anerkendelse, det brede udvalg af studiemuligheder samt beliggenheden i den pulserende by Melbourne. Derudover ønskede jeg at rejse til et engelsktalende land, idet jeg gerne ville forbedre mit akademiske engelsk.
info_ease: Det var meget let at finde information og få hjælp. På University of Melbourne findes "Stop 1", der er en slags studievejledning. De er ekstremt hjælpsomme.
arrival_assistance: Der var både et fuldt introprogram for alle udvekslingsstuderende i den første uge, da jeg kom. Derudover fik jeg også hjælp af Stop 1.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Man tilmelder sig bare de fag, man ønsker, og så skal man være opmærksom på eventuelle "prerequisites". Prerequisites er krav til specifikke fag, du skal have haft tidligere for, at kunne tage visse fag på University of Melbourne. Man kan dokumentere, at man lever op til prerequisites ved at oversætte kursusbeskrivelserne til de/det relevante fag, man tidligere har haft.
registration_help: Man kan få hjælp fra Stop 1, men man bliver også tilknyttet en kontaktperson, der specifikt har meget med udvekslingsstuderende at gøre. De svarer hurtigt og grundigt på alle ens spørgsmål.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag, jeg ønskede mig.
registration_advice: Sæt dig grundigt ind i, hvad fagene går ud på, hvordan eksamensformen er, og om der evt. er andre krav fx "hurdle-requirement", der går ud på, at du skal møde op mindst 75% af undervisningstimerne.
course_level: Post-graduate fag på University of Melbourne er på et forholdsvist højt niveau, hvorimod under-graduate fag ofte er med andre studerende, der aldrig har haft lignende fag før, da de kan komme direkte fra High School. Niveauet svinger derfor meget, og jeg vil råde fremtidige udvekslingsstuderende til at blande niveauerne lidt.
teaching_comparison: Underviserne på University of Melbourne er helt vildt engagerede, og det er virkelig inspirerende og motiverende. De forventer også, at alle de studerende deltager meget, men det bliver meget naturligt, når undervisningen er så spændende.
courses_enrolled: "Economic Analysis of Law", "Principles of Business Law", "Intellectual Property Law" og "Legal Language".
recommended_courses: Economic Analysis of Law er virkelig spændende og anderledes. Det giver et helt nyt perspektiv på jura og økonomi. Underviseren er meget engageret, så det er virkelig et fedt fag. Det afsluttes dog med en opgave på 6.000 ord, hvilket var lidt hårdt, men det hele værd!
unexpected_costs: Jeg havde ikke forberedt mig på, at University of Melbourne kræver, at du køber en privat sundhedsforsikring til ca. 3500 DKK. Derudover koster visum også ca. 3500 DKK.
cost_comparison: Husleje var klart langt dyrere end forventet.
activities_available: Der er et væld af klubber, man kan være med i på University of Melbourne, herunder en fodboldklub, Mountaineering Club, en vinklub, Taylor Swift Club mv. Der er virkelig en klub til alle interesser.
activities_recommended: Jeg vil råde fremtidige udvekslingsstuderende til at melde sig ind i surf-klubben, idet de laver rigtig mange fedt arrangementer og fester i løbet af semesteret. Derudover planlægger de selvfølgelig også en række surf camps.
weekend_recommendations: Jeg vil anbefale fremtidige udvekslingsstuderende at tage på en masse små ture ud af Melbourne. Man kan let leje en bil fx via Uber Carshare, og så køre til Grampians, Wilsons Prom eller langs Great Ocean Road. Derudover tog jeg bl.a. en tur til Tasmanien, hvilket virkelig var en oplevelse, jeg sætter pris på.
culture_adjustment: Den australske kultur minder meget om den danske, så det var virkelig let at tilpasse sig.
socializing_tips: Vær åben og smil til folk. Alle australiere er virkelig søde og vil gerne snakke i pauserne på Uni eller til andre arrangementer. Meld dig ind i en klub, da det er en super måde at mødes med andre studerende på.
cultural_challenges: Jeg har faktisk ikke fundet nogen markante kulturelle forskelle ift. den australske kultur. Man skal være opmærksom på, at mange i Melbourne, og især i CBD er asiater, og der er lidt kulturforskelle.
culture_appreciated: Jeg har virkelig værdsat australiernes åbne og venlige sind. Derudover er "no worries"-mentaliteten helt fantastisk.
top3_advice: 1) Alle ansatte på University of Melbourne er helt vildt søde og hjælpsomme. Ræk ud med alle dine bekymringer og spørgsmål. 2) Sæt dig ind i dine muligheder ift. bolig i god tid, men tag gerne afsted uden at have et fast sted at bo. Det er langt lettere at finde noget, når du er ankommet. 3) Nyd det, og skriv gerne en dagbog.
other_useful_info: Gør brug af alle de muligheder, der er via University of Melbourne. De arrangerer gratis akademisk hjælp, "coffee and catch-up" med andre udvekslingsstuderende, fitness mv.
most_rewarding: Den mest givende del af min udveksling er helt klart alle de fantastiske oplevelser, jeg har fået sammen med rigtig gode nye venner.
greatest_challenge: Jeg synes klart, at hele bolig-situationen i den første uge i Melbourne var super hård. Det er svært at komme til et nyt land på den anden side af jorden, når man er "hjemløs". Det hele løste sig dog, og jeg fortryder intet.
other_comments: Melbourne er en helt fantastisk by, og jeg er så glad for, at jeg endte med at vælge lige præcis University of Melbourne.

crucial_aspects: English-speaking country with courses that had opportunities for unique knowledge, that I wouldn't have been able to get at UCPH
info_ease: Bradley was very helpful in letting us know what we needed to do, and a lot of the other information was available on their website.
arrival_assistance: Stop1 was always realy to answer any and all questions!
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You had to fill out an excel sheet with your desired courses, and they require you to attatch a list of completed courses that would be necessary prerequisites. Be sure to check up on the prerequisites of your desired courses and have an english course description ready, so you don't get denied.
registration_help: Stop1 and Bradley (international student contact person) were very helpful!
registration_success: I got three out of foure of my top priorities; since the last was a laboratory course, it had an earlier deadline for application, which I was not made aware of. Is also had a quota and (understandably) filled up quite fast. If it's a necessary course for you to take, you are able to contact the university and ask for an exeption, which one of my friends was successful with.
registration_advice: Find more than your required number of courses, since it's not guaranteed that you can get your top priorities. Start your research early!
course_level: Generally, the academic level was a bit lower than that of UCPH (in the courses i enrolled in)
teaching_comparison: At UniMelb, it's often times not just the final exam that will constitute your final grade, but also assignments and quizzes during the semester. This forces you to keep up with the lectures and reading list, which (for me at least) proved to be quite helpful, since I fould it easy to get distracted by exploring the amazing city and surrounding areas.
courses_enrolled: Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry Frontiers in Human Disease Australia in the Wine World
recommended_courses: Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration was an overall great course! The content was interesting and the lecturers' enthusiasm within their field of research was contagious. Australia in the Wine World was a very fun elective, which allowed me (a previous wine amateur) to learn so much about wines both from Australia and the "old world" of wine production.
unexpected_costs: It's generally expensive to live in Melbourne. Remember to put aside money for weekend trips and maybe a longer trip in the mid semester break - there are so many must-see places in Australia!
cost_comparison: The visa was more expensive than anticipated.
activities_available: So many different clubs for all different interests/hobbies/sports!
activities_recommended: Surfers club!
weekend_recommendations: Phillip Island, Great Ocean Road, Yarra Valley (wineries)
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy, since Melbourne has a very westernized culture.
culture_appreciated: Greeting the tram-/busdrivers and just a general interest in strangers' lives!
top3_advice: Bring warm clothes! It gets colder than expected. Sign up for the free frozen meals offered by UniMelb. Relax and have fun; you're headed for (in my opinion) one of the best cities on earth!
most_rewarding: Forcing me out of my comfort zone, both socially and academically; gives rise to a lot of maturation and invaluable experiences!
greatest_challenge: Time zone differences to home are kind of challenging, especially in the first couple of weeks.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to a great university in an english speaking country. I have always dreamed of going to Australia so this was the perfect oppertunity.
info_ease: It was okay. I was a bit confused with the emails, receiving information from University of Melbourne sometimes through my KU mail and sometimes through my Melb mail. However, UniMelb is really good at providing all information and the student councelling (stop 1) was absolutely phenomenal.
arrival_assistance: I received help with student card, subjects, and time schedule.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: There are so many things you need to be on top of, and the whole process was just super tiring and stressful.
registration_help: The study abroad student service. They were pretty helpful.
registration_success: I got basically what I wanted.
registration_advice: Try to get things done as early as possible - because there is a lot of stuff going back and forth and every time you need a confirmation/answer/document/enrollment/etc. from either KU or the university abroad it takes time.
course_level: I had one subject that was fairly easy and two really difficult ones. The workload is huge - so although the things might be easy you just have to do a lot.
teaching_comparison: Your final grade is the result of your academic performance throughout the whole semester (all assignments and sometimes weekly multiple choice tests). Thus, the final exam might only count 50% of your grade while your work throughout the semester counts for the other 50%. Apart from that it is similar with a couple of lectures and classes every week.
courses_enrolled: Machine learning applications for health, computer vision, and algorithms for bioinformatics
recommended_courses: Computer vision! Really challenging but so much fun. I learned a lot.
unexpected_costs: VISA is about 3.200 kr., and you need and overseas student health cover which is around 1400 kr. (depending on the insurance company)
cost_comparison: Alcohol is pretty expensive apart from wine (which you can get very very cheap), cigarettes are extremely expensive (50$AUD for a pack), fruits and vegetables depends on the season but in general the super markets are like Denmark.
activities_available: I think basically anything you can imagine. However, I did not engage in too much of the uni activities.
activities_recommended: I just used to gym but if you like that, its pretty good :)
weekend_recommendations: Close to Melbourne: Phillip island, great ocean road, Mornington peninsula, the beach. In Melbourne: Night life areas; Chapel st (Prahran), Brunswick st and Smith St (Fitzroy). Check out: Naked for Satan, Revolver, Circuit, Sunday day drag show at the Osborne, Watch a footy match (a weird aussie kind of football game)
culture_adjustment: Very easy
cultural_challenges: They are more open and easy to become friends with
culture_appreciated: Their attitude towards strangers.
top3_advice: Explore the city, go travel and dont care too much about spending money. It will be expensive anyway and its worth it!
other_useful_info: Dont know
most_rewarding: The friendships I made for sure!
greatest_challenge: Being away from my partner

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne øve mit engelsk og derfor valgte jeg Australien.
overall_comments: Det var en kæmpe stor oplevelse at være på udveksling og stå fuldtændig på egne ben på den anden side af jorden. Det er dog også hårdt til tider.
info_ease: Selvom jeg fik super godt vejledning og hjælp fra både København og Melbourne, så var det for at være ærlig lidt forvirrende at finde de rette informationer, da de sommetider ikke stemte helt overens med hinanden fra land til land, og fra dokument til dokument.
arrival_assistance: Der var et sted man nærmest altid kunne gå hen og få hjælp og sparring til spørgsmål. Derudover arrangerede University of Melbourne mange både faglige og sociale arrangementer. Jeg synes universitet tog virkelig godt i mod os.
arrival_comments: Den var bare super god.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Det var en kæmpe stor oplevelse at være på udveksling og stå fuldtændig på egne ben på den anden side af jorden. Det er dog også hårdt til tider.
registration_process: Først online med en meget god og trinvis forklarende registrering. Så offline når man ankom, hvor man skulle møde op både i et informationskontor for at få sit studiekort mm., og man skulle møde op og hilse på den udvekslingsansvarlige og de andre internationale studerende.
registration_help: Man kunne altid møde op et bestemt sted på universitet og få hjælp.
registration_success: Det gik uden problemer.
registration_advice: Accepter at det er lidt forvirrende og en langsommelig process, som man ikke kan klare på en enkelt dag. En del af processen er at vente på email-svar mm., for at kunne gå videre til næste step.
academics_comments: Det var en kæmpe stor oplevelse at være på udveksling og stå fuldtændig på egne ben på den anden side af jorden. Det er dog også hårdt til tider.
course_level: I mit tilfælde blev jeg overrasket over at BA-fagene faktisk var mere krævende end MA-fagene. Jeg tror det var fordi at man i Australien ikke så tit læser en master, så dem, der starter på en, starter helt fra scratch. Hvorimod man i et BA fag kan havne sammen med nogen, der har en masse viden på forhånd, som de bygger ovenpå.
teaching_comparison: Undervisningstilen i Melbourne var meget forskellig fra den på Københavns Universitet. På University of Melbourne skulle man aflevere flere små essays og fremlægge én gang i hvert fag - alt dette talte med i ens samlede afslutningskarakter. Så mindre essays, men flere deadlines. Derudover førtes der fraværsprotokol og diskussion var en fast del af undervisningen. På nogen måder en mere deltagende undervisning. Hvilket var rigtig fedt, men som sommetider også kunne kræve lidt meget af en, når man havde mange fag.
courses_enrolled: 1) Art Cinema and the Love Story, 2) Contemporary Art, 3) Trans Studies: Cultures and Communities, 4) Cultural Complexity and Intelligence.
recommended_courses: Jeg synes helt ærligt at de alle sammen var virkelig spændende. Men det var rart at have et fag som Art cinema and the Love Story, da det var lidt mere legende og mindre teoritungt. Godt at blande det lidt.
unexpected_costs: Ture. Når man er der vil man gerne på tur, og det koster nogle penge at leje en bil og købe et telt osv.
cost_comparison: At spise og drikke var meget dyrt, meget dyrer end i dk. En øl kostede sådan der 75 kr, og tomater var helt ekstremt dyre. Tilgengæld kunne man købe en advokado for ingen penge.
activities_available: Alt mellem himmel og jord, tror nærmest ikke at der var noget, der ikke var.
activities_recommended: Vandreklubben! og Svømme og fitness faciliteterne.
weekend_recommendations: Great Ocean Road, The Grampians National Park (mega flotte vandreturer og fyldt med kænguruer), Phillip Island og meget meget mere.
culture_adjustment: Melbourne minder om Danmark på rigtig mange punkter, så overordnet synes jeg ikke at det var så svært. Men der var alligevel nogle ting, som var ret anderledes, og bare hele det at alter på en andet sprog hele tiden, så kræver lidt tilvending.
socializing_tips: Meld dig ind i klubber, og bare vær åben for at snakke med folk omkring dig. Jeg synes folk fra Melbourne generelt var rigtig søde og åbne.
cultural_challenges: Sprog.
culture_appreciated: At det var så multikulturalt.

crucial_aspects: Both academic and cultural factors were important for me in choosing my destination. I definitely had an urge to see something outside of Europe, and initially wanted to study in either Africa or South America. However, there were limited options there when I applied - and since I had always wanted to go to Australia that seemed the way to go. The fact that there would not be a language barrier for me in Australia (since I am fluent in English) was also a major contributing factor. I had heard heaps of good stuff about Melbourne. The University of Melbourne seemed like a good institution, and they offered quite a few very relevant and exciting subjects for me. There were also many exchange spots available for UCPH students, so it seemed like a safe choice.
info_ease: It found it fairly easy to figure out.
arrival_assistance: I had a few questions about enrolment in subjects and my timetable, so I contacted Stop 1 (student services). They were very helpful.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process was quite straight forward,
registration_help: The exchange coordinator at UCPH was very helpful.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Just follow the registration guide and you'll be good.
course_level: I took one first year course, one second year course and two third year courses. Generally I would say that the academic level is pretty similar to UCPH, but to be honest I wouldn't know since all of the courses I took while on exchange were elective and in a quite different field from the rest of my degree at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: Each course has one lecture and one tutorial per week (in my case). This is quite different from the style of teaching at UCPH. The lectures are more "stiff", you basically just listen to the lecturer speak for a few hours, while the tutorials are supposed to be more engaging, as there are fewer students in each "team". Officially, you are expected to actively participate in every tutorial, however many seem to be uncomfortable speaking which does sometimes make tutorials slightly awkward.
courses_enrolled: DEVT10001 The Developing World POLS20031 Political Economy ANTH30005 Anthropology of More-than-human Worlds ANTH30009 Power, Ideology and Inequality
recommended_courses: I would recommend the Anthropology course "Power, Ideology and Inequality".

cost_comparison: Food was a lot more expensive than anticipated.
activities_available: There is something for everyone at UoM.
activities_recommended: Get involved with the Environment Collective!
weekend_recommendations: Explore Melbourne's food and music scene!
culture_adjustment: Melbourne is quite similar to Copenhagen in a number of ways, so it wasn't that difficult to adjust.
socializing_tips: Join a club - I recommend getting involved with the environment collective on campus.
cultural_challenges: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.
culture_appreciated: I really appreciate how open and chatty Australians are!
top3_advice: 1. Be prepared to spend more money than you thought you would. 2. Prioritise your social life, it is really not that hard to pass your courses, and grades don't count towards your final degree. 3. Go on weekend trips!
other_useful_info: Don't stress too much about your studies. The semester goes by VERY quickly, so make the most of it while you're in Australia.
most_rewarding: Being part of the Socialist Alternative club on campus is definitely the most rewarding experience!
greatest_challenge: I found that, while meeting lots of cool people, actually establishing real friendships is not a piece of cake. I did not hang around any other exchange students (only Aussies), so the classic "you're in it together" did not apply to me in terms of making friends. However, I am really pleased that I pushed through the initial phase, because now I have a bunch of lovely Australian friends.

First you had to pick the courses that you wanted to register for and then once registrations opened you could register in that portal. Then when they made the timetables available you had to check that your classes are not overlapping and potentially switch courses if there was a clash.

registration_advice: To check for the deadlines and have a back up in case there is a clash.

teaching_comparison: At UCPH I had way more contact hours during the week. In Melbourne I had a lot of free time and many group projects. The assignments were mostly essays in Melbourne and you had quite a lot of time to write them, with longer exam periods.

course_level: I was positively surprised at the relatively high level of the courses, I took. It varied from first-year subjects to third-year but it worked pretty well having a mixture of these. I felt the ambitious level of some of the second- and third-year courses I had were specifically due to other students' engagement as well as the teacher's giant effort to make the courses exciting. I learned more than I had counted on from all my courses.
teaching_comparison: It has been quite different but a thing I really appreciated at Melbourne University was more academic freedom to write assignments within topics that I found interesting. Furthermore, I really enjoyed the amount of feedback we got which I found useful for my own academic development.
courses_enrolled: Understanding the Student as Learner (EDUC91029) Science and Pseudoscience (HPSC10002) The Politics of Sex (POLS20011) Survey Design and Analysis (SOCI30013)
recommended_courses: I highly recommend the course called The Politics of Sex as our lecturer, Lauren Rosewarne, was truly amazing at her job. The lectures were so interesting and I learned a ton from them, and as they were all recorded the course came with a great amount of flexibility. Furthermore, I found the seminars really exciting as we had a lot of great discussions on the topics from the lectures. Though the essays were challenging to write, they were also some of the most interesting. Also, I would recommend Survey Design and Analysis to anyone who finds research within the social sciences interesting. Belinda and Shaun who taught the course were so nice and helpful and every topic from statistics and graphs to survey design and administration was explained thoroughly. Furthermore, the course was very "hands-on" as we got to actually design and distribute a real survey and then analyze the results as part of our final assignment.
unexpected_costs: I guess I was surprised at the cost of visa and insurance.
cost_comparison: The rent was definitely more expensive than I'd counted on. Also, groceries were more expensive. However, coffee was cheap compared to home and that came in handy when you had long days at campus.
activities_available: There were so many different sports and social clubs at my host institution. I joined the Mountaineering Club and went on this amazing intro-trip for two straight days which was just really fun to try. Furthermore, it was a great way of meeting new people and other exchange students. Also, there was these really random, but fun clubs like a Taylor Swift Fan Society which I also joined.
activities_recommended: I would really recommend becoming a part of some sort of club as it is a great way to meet other people and make friends. Also, I recommend trying out free events at the university as there might be free food, great music or valuable information. Really, it almost doesn't matter what club you join as long as you find it interesting or you sense there's a good vibe there. Lastly, if you have the option to go on trips in your local area and around: do it! Explore the city and country and travel to see other parts of it.
weekend_recommendations: I think you should strive to find a balance between going on trips and just setting aside time to relax and possibly catch up on studying. I loved having both weekends where I went on trips around Victoria State such as going to the Grampians, Great Ocean Road and Wilson's Prom but also the weekends spent at home in Melbourne just hanging out with friends or perhaps going to a local market or going for a walk along the river. Still, I really recommend using the holidays to go on longer trips or perhaps set aside some time after exams to travel. I managed to go to Tasmania over the Easter Break and that was truly wonderful.
culture_adjustment: I found it relatively easy as it reminded me of the culture of my homeland in many ways. It reflected the Western culture that dominates a lot of media and so on which I think made it quite familiar. In that sense, the culture shock wasn't too big. Still, the time zone and seasons were the total opposite from home so that was something to get used to upon arrival.
socializing_tips: My tip is to not be too shy. Say you have a nice chat with someone from your course, I would recommend just asking them if they'd like to grab a coffee or a beer sometime. I feel that most local students would definitely be up to that if you ask. You could also ask if they wanted to study or if they could help you explain some local phenomena that you struggle to understand, e.g. Australian Football which I did not get at all. Essentially, don't be scared of rejection as they are mostly really kind and helpful. Another way is joining clubs, and societies or going to uni events and just hang out.
cultural_challenges: I don't know if it was really that challenging but I had to get used to everything being reversed in terms of traffic. Driving, walking, and biking on the left side. That was super strange in the beginning.
culture_appreciated: I really find the history and traditions of the First Nation's People both interesting and tragic. I felt it was my responsibility to get to know some of this history as it also affected the culture. In Melbourne, I sensed a deep respect towards First Nations' history, however, it seemed it wasn't the same across the whole of Australia. In general, I think Melbourne was quite a long way ahead regarding political issues and debates on human rights, racism, LGBTQIA+ etc. On a more basic level, the food culture is great. Also, coffee and brunch. I also really enjoyed watching AFL games, and in general the sports and concert culture was also really great and had a lot to offer.
top3_advice: It's worth finding a nice place to live - possibly with nice housemates - as it will be your home every day for almost half a year. Also, don't be alarmed if you find the workload at uni heavy in the beginning as it takes some time to get used to the new study settings, classes taught in another language and different ways of writing assignments. And as marks don't transfer, you need only pass your courses to have them approved back home. Lastly, remember to enjoy yourself and have fun but also reach out to people back home if you feel lonely or go through something difficult. Even if they are far away, they are still your family and friends and they can support you still.
other_useful_info: I think it's useful knowing that there are so many facilities offered that are worth exploring. Besides clubs and societies and free events, there are great study facilities and you can even apply for a food programme where you can be nominated to receive free dinners every week.
most_rewarding: I'm really grateful for all the amazing people that I've met and got to share my experience with. I've gotten new friendships that I'm able to take home with me as well as a connection to another city that I now feel is also my home. The whole experience has been equally challenging and wonderful, and I wouldn't have been without any of it.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was feeling lonely at times and missing the feeling of being deeply connected to my friends and family back home.

However, due to the fact that my first choice for Washington D.C. was cancelled the choices in the second round were generally very limited for me.

Men jeg må sige, at jeg har været en smule utilfreds med nogle af de kurser, jeg endte med at vælge (heriblandt også niveauet (for lavt) på nogle af kurserne).
registration_process: Der er en portal, hvor man skal indmelde sig. Det er også herinde, at man vælger de kurser, man gerne vil følge. Generelt er der samling på det hele, så det er relativt nemt at finde rundt i. Man får også tilsendt en guide (pdf) på mail, som hjælper en godt på vej.
registration_help: Man modtager en guide på mail, og derudover kan man kontakte Stop 1, hvis man har spørgsmål. Der ligger også rigeligt med hjælp på UniMelbs hjemmeside, så hvis man har brug for yderligere hjælp, kan man google "bla bla unimelb", så bør man blive henvist til den rette side.
registration_success: Jeg fik plads på alle de kurser, som jeg havde ansøgt om, det var intet problem.
registration_advice: Læs deres guides godt igennem og vær ikke bange for at bede om hjælp, hvis du er i tvivl om noget.
academics_comments: Jeg havde et fantastisk ophold. Skønne mennesker, skøn by, dejligt land. Personligt og socialt var udvekslingsopholdet 10/10. Men jeg må sige, at jeg har været en smule utilfreds med nogle af de kurser, jeg endte med at vælge (heriblandt også niveauet (for lavt) på nogle af kurserne).
course_level: Niveauet er klart lavere, end jeg har været vant til. Jeg tog to bachelorkurser (som var nemme, men selvfølgelig var dette forventet), et kandidatkursus (som var passende i sværhedsgrad) og et kandidatkursus som var for nemt.
teaching_comparison: Der er virkelig meget online undervisning. Alle mine forelæsninger blev optaget og livestreamet, hvilket jeg ikke er vant til hjemmefra. Jeg synes ikke, at undervisningsmaterialet var så godt, jeg havde flere fag, hvor der ikke rigtigt var noget læsestof. Dette er ok for nogle fag, men det kan være frustrerende, at man ikke kan læse op på emner, man ikke har forstået, eller hvis man leder efter en alternativ formulering ift. den, man har fået fra forelæsningen. Forelæsninger/øvelsestimer var for mit vedkommende fordelt mere ud over hele ugen end på KU.
courses_enrolled: FOOD10001 (Beer Styles and Sensory Analysis) - supersjovt og ikke særligt krævende ACTL90023 (Data Analytics in Insurance I) ACTL90010 (Actuarial Practice and Control I) ACTL30002 (Actuarial Modelling II) - ikke fedt fag
recommended_courses: Hvis man kan få lov af sit fakultet (studerende ved CSS fik det ikke godkendt), kan jeg anbefale ølkurset FOOD10001, det var sjovt, nemt, anderledes, og man lærer noget om at drikke forskellige typer af øl. Til andre aktuarstuderende vil jeg gerne anbefale Actuarial Practice and Control. Superinteressante forelæsere og forelæsninger, man lærer virkelig meget om, hvordan forsikring og pension i Aus adskiller sig fra dansk praksis.
unexpected_costs: Når man flytter ind på student accommodation skal man købe service, dyner og puder. Man skal også købe OSHC (overseas student health care) for ca. 1800 kr (så vidt jeg husker).
cost_comparison: Husleje var meget dyrere, end jeg forventede!! At spise ude er også virkelig dyrt. Lækre restauranters priser svarer til de danske, men hvis man fx bare gerne vil have en standard pizza, ville den i dk koste 65-70 kr., hvor den ville koste 100 kr. i Australien (og smage dårligere end den danske). Offentlig transport er også dyrt, man betaler 4,6 dollars hver gang, man checker ind. Ofte kan det betale sig at tage en uber i stedet (billigt, især hvis man splitter). Dagligvarer er en smule dyrere end i dk. Telefonabonnement kan være billigt. Jeg købte gennem Moose Mobile, god dækning, superbilligt. Hvad end I gør: køb ikke Vodafone!! Dårlig dækning og meget dyrt.
activities_available: Der er en så lang liste af alverdens klubber, og de bliver introduceret allerede i introdagene, hvor der bl.a. er club fair på uni, hvor alle klubber har en bod, og så kan man ellers gå rundt og lære mere om de forskellige klubber. Der er en del, der handler om fysisk aktivitet, men også mange mere "intellektuelle" klubber.
activities_recommended: Surfklubben, mountaineering-klubben og sejlklubben var meget populære blandt udvekslingsstuderende. Jeg syntes, at der generelt var flere udenlandske end australske studerende til de arrangementer, klubberne holder. Men super måde at møde nye mennesker.
weekend_recommendations: Der er mange skønne naturområder tæt på byen, det er helt klart værd at tage toget eller leje en bil for at tage ud til fx Dandenong eller Grampians. Der er Fitzroy Mills Market hver lørdag og Camberwell Market hver søndag (begge loppemarkeder). Jeg var en tur på Tasmanien også, kan virkelig anbefales, så smukt (det bliver ret koldt i vintermånederne). Generelt vil de fleste udvekslingsstuderende gerne ud at rejse og se mere af Australien, nu de er dernede.
culture_adjustment: Jeg havde med vilje valgt at tage til et "vestligt" land for at undgå for meget kulturforskel. Det var nemt at falde til, og det hjælper helt sikkert på sagerne, at man kan tale det officielle sprog. Så er sproget i hvert fald ikke en barriere.
socializing_tips: Jeg lærte ikke specielt mange lokale studerende at kende, fordi kursusdeltagerne til næsten alle mine kurser var internationale studerende. Generelt var der mange kinesere, der hovedsageligt taler mandarin sammen, så de er automatisk lidt sværere at komme ind på. Hvis man gerne vil tale med andre udvekslingsstuderende, er de sociale klubber the way to go. Generelt er australiere ret nemme at snakke med, så jeg forestiller mig også, at det er nemt at tale med dem i forbindelse med undervisning (men ikke noget jeg har erfaring med, siden der næsten kun var internationale studerende til min undervisning).
cultural_challenges: Det er normalt, at steder som caféer, restauranter, barer og natklubber lukker relativt tidligt. Det er næsten umuligt at opstøve en kop kaffe efter kl. 15, og mange natklubber lukker allerede kl. 1 eller 2. Der skal man bare lige justere sin tidsplan, så man kommer ud tidligere. Desuden er der mange klubber, hvor de spiller teknomusik. Og så er det ret almindeligt, at folk tager stoffer.
culture_appreciated: Lidt mere åbenhed generelt. Det er ikke ualmindeligt at have en lille chit chat med ekspedienten i kassen, hvilket ikke er noget man ofte opleve i større byer (heller ikke København). Der er heller ikke mange, der ryger cigaretter (en pakke koster omkring 250 kr), hvilket var rart.
top3_advice: 1: Meld dig ind i klubber for at møde andre udenlandske og lokale studerende (eller bare deltag i deres social arrangementer) 2: Sørg for at udnytte bydele uden for centrum som fx Fitzroy, Collingwood, Brunswick, St. Kilda, Clifton Hill og Abbotsford 3: Prioriter at besøge andre områder i Australien i dine ferier og tag på forlængede weekendture
other_useful_info: Nej
most_rewarding: Jeg har for det første mødt en masse skønne mennesker. Primært andre danskere men også en masse fra andre lande (og et par stykker fra Aus). Jeg har fundet ud af, at det ikke er så skræmmende endda at være hjemmefra i længere tid ad gangen, og jeg kan nu se det at bo i udlandet som en mulighed for mig i fremtiden.
greatest_challenge: At være væk fra alle de mennesker, jeg er vant til at have lige ved hånden hjemme i kbh. Og at finde en ny balance mellem uni og fritid. Det hjalp på det, at jeg havde besluttet hjemmefra, at jeg ville bruge betydeligt mindre tid på uni på udveksling. Det kan anbefales at definere ens ambitionsniveau på forhånd.
other_comments: Nyd det! Tiden går alt for hurtigt!

arrival_assistance: Needed assistances with finding one of my lecture buildings, anc everyone was very helpful.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: There is a Student service available everyday that is very helpful.
registration_success: totally succesful.

courses_enrolled: Stem Cell in Development and Regeneration Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry Microbes, Infection and Responses Protein, Structure and Function
recommended_courses: I would highly recommend doing the Stem cells in Development and Regeneration, as many other courses are building on top of your already existing knowledge, but this is all new and really interesting with top researchers presenting their work in lectures. cost_comparison: Beers are a lot more expensive than in DK. Many fruits and vegetables (like tomatoes and capsicum) are really expensive. Sushi is really cheap.
activities_available: There is a ton of social clubs and sport activities to join at UniMelb. Almost whatever you can think of, there is.
activities_recommended: Join the Mounteneering club, they organise both one-day and multi-day hiking trip to really cool places.

culture_adjustment: Very easy, Australia is very much the same in many ways.
socializing_tips: Dont be afraid to talk to your new class mates, many of them dont know each other either and they are also looking for friends and for people to look over assignments with.
cultural_challenges: I did not encounter any cultural differences.
culture_appreciated: the very laid back culture.
top3_advice: Bring more warm clothes than you think you are gonna need when arriving in Juli. It's COLD.
other_useful_info: Campus is really big, download Lost on Campus app, it tells where everything from lecture halls to microwaves and libraries are.
most_rewarding: The friendships.
greatest_challenge: When something traumativ happens and I realised how far away I was from home. Luckily, I met so many great people here, that cared for me.

crucial_aspects: Unimelb har mange gode og spændende fag for geografer med en masse feltarbejde. Udover det så starter semestret tidlige og slutter allerede i november, så man har tid til at backpacker bagefter inden man skal starte igen i februar her hjemme.
info_ease: Inden jeg kom derned syntes jeg det var svært at finde ud af. Da man var ankommet og kunne snakke med studieinformation på campus var det nemt nok at finde alle de informationer man skal bruge - der er meget hjælp at hente hos Stop One, som er studieinformation på campus, hvis man ønsker det - måske bare bestil tid i forvejen.
arrival_assistance: Der var flere oplæg fra studieinformation om ens udveksling og universitetet som var obligatoriske at deltage i den første uge. Det hjalp meget.

teaching_comparison: Det er meget gymnasie agtig, dog meget individuelt uden meget gruppe arbejde.
courses_enrolled: Environmental Change & the Human Journey Past Climates: Icehouse to Greenhouse Understanding Planet Earth Global Climate Change in Context
recommended_courses: Global Climate Change in Context og Biogeography and Ecology of Fire. Fede feltture til enten New Zealand eller Tasmanien.
unexpected_costs: Husleje er dyrt, men er meget værre på on-campus student accommodation.
cost_comparison: Øl er meget er dyrt - en billig fadøl koster nemt 60kr men kan nemt koster 100kr.
activities_available: Der er mange klubber på universitet som man kan melde sig ind i. Sport klubber, kultur klubber mm.
activities_recommended: Jeg vil anbefale Melbourne mountaineering club, som er en vandre og frilufts klub. Derudover var jeg med i dykkerklubben som er en meget aktiv social klub.
weekend_recommendations: Lej en bil ( eller få en sød aussi ven med en bil) og kør ud af Melbourne til nogle af de mange smukke nationalparker som ligger ikke særlig langt væk fra byen. ( Budj bim , grampians, Ottaway national park, Wilsons prom)
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt, aussi´erne er meget søde og nemme at være sammen med.
socializing_tips: Meld dig ind i nogle klubber og snak med dine medstuderende i timerne - ikke hold dig tilbage!
cultural_challenges: studerende på unimelb har måske lidt en gymnasie vibe en gang imellem. Men det er ikke noget rigtigt problem og ikke så kulturelt.
culture_appreciated: Aussier er meget nede på jorden og nemme at snakke med og blive venner med hvis man har lyst.
top3_advice: - Kig godt i kursus kataloget, også under andre institutter og departementer. - led efter accommodation på fairy floss real estate - Melbourne er dyre end man tror, men man skal nok klare det.
other_useful_info: Det er fedt at bo i Brunwick, Carlton, Fritroy, Collingwood.
most_rewarding: De venner man har fået er det bedste.
greatest_challenge: Nok alt det papir arbejde man skal få ordnet for at få lov til at komme afsted.

crucial_aspects: It mainly was the courses offered at the Exchange-University. I was very interested in ecosystems other than the European ones.
info_ease: It was quite easy. The University of Melbourne hosted an orientation day for exchange students prior to a full orientation week for all students and provided a lot of information and help.
arrival_assistance: How to get my public transport card, assistance with extra curricular activities, assistance with finances.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I do not remember all of it, but there was a step-to-step guide on their website available.
registration_help: The University provides all sorts of help. You can email them with any questions. There is also a step-to-step guide for registration. When your application is accepted, they send you further information and links in an email.
registration_success: Very successful. I got everything I wanted
registration_advice: Start as soon as possible, like always.
course_level: Most of the courses are mixed Bachelor's and Master's courses, and the demands are not adjusted to your level. While some Professors were very engaging and encouraging, others seemed to lack enthusiasm.
teaching_comparison: The style is quite similar. The classes are small, and everything is quite interactive, with the Professors and Lecturers encouraging discussion and being on eye level with the students. However, the assignment process is a little different. While most of the grade is based on one big assignment at the end of the Block or Semester in CPH, the courses in Melbourne have a lot of small assignments during the semester, which requires the students to work on the course constantly. With a full study load, that can get quite challenging. Also, it is mainly written assignments, hardly any oral exams.
courses_enrolled: Nature, Conservation and Society 10/10 Economic Tools for the Environment 2/10 Science Communication 9/10 Communities and Ecosystem Management 5/10
recommended_courses: I would recommend Nature, Conservation and Society and Science Communication. The Professor running NCS is enthusiastic, and her teaching style in the tutorials is excellent. We had many fruitful discussions, and the topics and assignments helped develop a deeper understanding of conservation. Although Science Communication is rather demanding because of the many assignments to hand in over the semester, it is worth it. You get an excellent insight into the different communication perspectives and can try out many things yourself. There are also fascinating people on the course, both fellow students and lecturers.
unexpected_costs: Public transport is quite expensive, and so is local produce at some times of the year. Alcohol and going out are also astonishingly expensive. Joining sport clubs is also not cheap, but that's the same in CPH
cost_comparison: Alcohol is way more expensive
activities_available: Everything, from language clubs to film clubs, food clubs and all sorts of things. A lot of sports clubs, too. You can also enter volleyball and football tournaments, that go the whole semester.
activities_recommended: The Exchange-student society was good for getting in contact with other exchange students. The film society shows a movie every Friday with free pizza. Just browse through the social clubs, I bet you find something that is in your interest.
weekend_recommendations: Get out of the city. Go to Tasmania (at least a week), Phillip Island, Wilsons Prom, the Grampians, and Great Ocean Road. Also: Ruffey Trail Suspension Bridge in the early morning or evening if you want to spot some platypuses.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy, it's just another western culture. But Melbourne is very diverse with many different nationalities coming together. Very interesting
socializing_tips: Go to the social clubs and sport events.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: Australians are very friendly and curious
top3_advice: Go to the social clubs Be prepared for bad weather Enjoy your life, don't worry too much about your grades
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Travelling the country and seeing all this amazing wildlife
greatest_challenge: Facing the cold without a heater in my room
