teaching_comparison: They have a lot less of independency, which annoyed me a lot, as I was forced to follow a tutor, while in lab. It just sent redundant and stupid. This is a general thing, where they differ a bit in mentality from DK. Besides that, it was similar.
courses_enrolled: Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration, Australia in the Wine World, Microbes, Infections and Responses, and Foundations of Computing.
recommended_courses: Australia in the Wine World is a nice and easy way to get into some Aussie culture and jargon, and also have some wonderful wine. The Stem Cell subject offers a lot more flexibility and independency compared to the other subjects. Computing is done in Pyhton and works quite well with the help of a program called Grok, but it’s only if you haven’t done coding before.
unexpected_costs: Nothing major, if you’ve done your homework.
cost_comparison: Coffee and electronics. Alcohol is more expensive tho.
activities_available: A lot. Follow UMSU and Unimelb Sport and go to intro week to see it all.
activities_recommended: Surf club and mountaineering club activities.
weekend_recommendations: Wilsons Prom (you can go on very long, isolated, and beautiful hikes there for multiple days), Philips Island (to see wildlife), Great Ocean Road (surf here e.g. in Torquay or Lorne), The Grampians, Ballarat, Yarra Valley, Mornington Peninsula, Dandenong.
culture_adjustment: Easy, but they can be difficult to understand at times.
socializing_tips: Clubs.
cultural_challenges: Not much.
culture_appreciated: Their friendly mentality and laid back style of life.
top3_advice: Don’t be too academic (choose easier subjects), go on as many trips as possible, meet some locals either via shared housing or social clubs.
other_useful_info: Find a place to live close to campus and life. I recommend Carlton, Fitzroy or Brunswick.
most_rewarding: Living there.
greatest_challenge: They have a lot of tests and quizzes that contribute to your final grade. That’s annoying.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville til et land langt væk fra mine vante omgivelser, hvor jeg kunne opleve en masse.
overall_comments: Hvis jeg skulle give det 10, skulle kvaliteten af undervisningen være bedre. Men jeg valgte også nogle nemme fag - og det var heller ikke derfor, jeg tog på udveksling.
info_ease: Jeg synes, at det var nemt. UniMelb var god til at orientere udvekslingsstuderende.
arrival_assistance: Først og fremmest var der en hel orienteringsdag for udvekslingsstuderende, hvor man fik en masse informationer. Herudover kunne man også få hjælp ved det, de kalder Stop1. Det kunne man hele semesteret. Ved ankomsten var de gode til at hjælpe, og de tog sig tid til, at man kunne logge ind på sin unimelb studiekonto og kigge tingene igennem for en ift. fag mv. De kunne dog ikke svare sikkert på, om man fik sine fag, men de kunne hjælpe med at sikre, at man havde søgt korrekt og generelt gjort tingene rigtigt. I løbet af semesteret - særligt op til eksamen - kunne man også få hjælp fra dem, men der var de mere begrænset i deres hjælp. Jeg ved ikke, om det kunne være fordi, at man læste jura, og det juridiske fakultet var for sig selv, men de henviste mig hele tiden over til studieadministrationen på jura.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Hvis jeg skulle give det 10, skulle kvaliteten af undervisningen være bedre. Men jeg valgte også nogle nemme fag - og det var heller ikke derfor, jeg tog på udveksling.
registration_process: Som jeg husker det, skulle man inden afrejse starte med at udfylde et specifikt excelark, hvor man oplistede, hvilke fag man ville have, og hvilke "prerequisites" man havde haft på KU, som kunne give en adgang til faget. Her var det lidt svært at gennemskue, hvor mange fag, man skulle skrive på, og det tog lidt tid at lave kursusbeskrivelserne fra kurserne på KU om til engelsk og udfylde hele excelarket. Herefter skulle man så ansøge rigtigt om sine fag. Jo hurtigere du fik ovenstående godkendt, jo hurtigere kunne du søge. To af de fag jeg havde oplistet i excelarket, kunne jeg ikke komme på, da pladserne allerede var fyldt op. Derfor skulle jeg så skrive til studieadministrationen hos UniMelb igen ift. at få nogle andre fag godkendt. Det var lidt meget kommunikation frem og tilbage, men de var hurtige til at svare, og der var intet bøvl overhovedet.
registration_help: Stop1/deres studieadministration.
registration_success: Se ovenstående.
registration_advice: Få udfyldt excelarket hurtigst muligt, så du har alle muligheder åbne.
academics_comments: Hvis jeg skulle give det 10, skulle kvaliteten af undervisningen være bedre. Men jeg valgte også nogle nemme fag - og det var heller ikke derfor, jeg tog på udveksling.
course_level: Jeg havde følgende fag; Free Speech and Media Law, Global Human Rights Law, AI, Ethics and the Law og Disputes and Ethics. Det sidste fag var et JD fag, som svarer til deres bachelor i Jura. Det var civilproces og advokatetik. Faget var virkelig spændende, og niveauet svarede til et almindeligt bachelorfag herhjemme. De tre øvrige fag var helt generelle bachelorfag, som jeg havde med studerende, der var i gang med at læse en bachelor i art, economic eller noget tredje. Fagene var meget(!) nemme, og der var ikke særlig meget jura i dem. Det jura man lærte var meget basic.
teaching_comparison: Det var meget ens, da der både var forelæsninger og holdundervisning. Men indholdet og hvad de ønsker fra de studerende er megt forskelligt. På UniMelb var de eksempelvis meget interesseret i vores personlige holdning.
courses_enrolled: Free Speech and Media Law, Global Human Rights Law, AI, Ethics and the Law og Disputes and Ethics.
recommended_courses: Jeg vil egentlig kun anbefale Disputes and Ethics. Det minder indholdsmæssigt om noget, man kan lære om i Danmark (særligt etik-delen), hvorfor man også kan bruge det, når man kommer hjem. Herudover var det et fag med gode undervisere! Hvis man er til menneskerettigheder, så vil jeg anbefale Global Human Rights Law, hvor du lærer om FN's Menneskerettighedserklæring. Jeg kunne personligt ikke lide faget; det interesserer mig ikke umiddelbart, og jeg synes ikke, at undervisningen og undervisningsmaterialet var særlig godt. AI, Ethics and the Law er et fint fag, hvis man vil have en introduktion til, hvordan brugen af AI kan clashe med jura. Man skal dog ikke tage faget for at lære noget, da det er et meget nemt fag, hvor problemstillingerne behandles meget overfladisk. Arbejdsbyrden er også minimal. Free Speech and Media Law vil jeg anbefale, hvis man vil lære lidt mere om den specifikke lovgivning i Victoria, og hvis man vil læse en del cases, hvor ytringsfriheden clasher med andre rettigheder. Igen er det ikke umiddelbart et fag, jeg interesserer mig for, så det sagde ikke mig så meget. Det var dog det fag (udover Disputes and Ethics), hvor man lærte om mest lovgiving, og som generelt mindede mest om noget, man ville lære på KU, fordi man i undervisningen arbejdede meget med cases.
unexpected_costs: Ingen.
cost_comparison: Priserne svarer meget til de priser, der er i Danmark - måske en lille smule billigere faktisk. Det kommer dog lidt an på, hvad man køber. Jeg synes personligt, at det var billigere at spise ude på cafeer og restauranter end herhjemme. Alkohol var samme pris. Kaffe var meget billigere. I supermarkederne var det lidt forskelligt. Mælk og avocado var eksempelvis billigere, mens ost og bær var meget dyrere end i Danmark.
activities_available: Det samme som man har på KU.
activities_recommended: Jeg deltog ikke i noget, så det ved jeg ikke.
weekend_recommendations: Lej en bil og kør til Grampians National Park, tag på en outdoor tur til den australske outback, se en footy camp på MCG eller bare slentre rundt i nogle af de mange fede forstader til Melbourne CDB (Fitzroy, Prahran, Richmond, South Yarra).
culture_adjustment: Utrolig nemt - Australien er et fantastisk land, hvor alle er meget venlige og nede på jorden.
socializing_tips: Nej - gør som du ville på KU.
cultural_challenges: Der er mange asiater i Melbourne, og deres kultur er meget anderledes end vores. Det skulle jeg lige vænne mig til.
culture_appreciated: At australiere er så søde og venlige. Der er en helt speciel vibe i Melbourne (ikke CDB!), som jeg virkelig godt kunne lide.
top3_advice: Melbourne er ikke en by med konstant sol og varme, så pak noget varmt tøj. Du skal ikke forvente at uni er som på KU - gør op med dig selv inden, hvad det er, du vil have ud af dit ophold. Nyd det og lad vær med at tænke (så meget) på økonomien! Melbourne er den fedeste by med gode cafeer og mange nice ting, man kan opleve.
other_useful_info: Nej.
most_rewarding: Jeg har udviklet mig meget personligt. Jeg tog ikke på udveksling for det faglige, og hvis jeg gjorde, havde jeg nok været skuffet. Selvom UniMelb er et meget højt rangeret universitet, synes jeg ikke, at fagligheden var særligt høj.
greatest_challenge: At alt i min hverdag blev taget fra mig, og jeg lige pludselig havde meget mere fritid. Jeg skulle ikke arbejde, bruge lige så meget tid på uni, dyrke min holdsport eller være sammen med mine venner og veninder. Det var meget anderledes, end jeg var vant til, og det var en udfordring for mig, fordi jeg elsker struktur og ikke slapper af i at lave ingenting og have så meget tid i min hverdag.
other_comments: Nej.

crucial_aspects: It had to be an english speaking country, with a similar culture to ours that could provide academic and life quality.
info_ease: I would say it was easy. The university would send emails with information and upon arrival there was people available to ask questions. They also have a student service (STOP 1) which was great for all sorts of questions (also not uni-related even)
arrival_assistance: They were good at answering all sorts of questions
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You would have to find which subjects you want to do in an online booklet that they have. I would say it is okay, however, these subjects are not always available for different reasons. The registration process itself was not so different to the one we have in KU, you have to log in into a similar site like KUNet and register the subjects you want, the order you want them and which schedule (they have to accept the subjects first but then you choose)
registration_help: STOP1 is a place where you can always go, and they will answer your questions and even help you throughout the process.
registration_success: Pretty successful. There was one subject that was already full, so I had to change it. It is always good to have second options.
registration_advice: Read carefully the instructions, and if you have any doubt contact stop1 they will help you.
course_level: The level of the courses is high, however the biggest difference is the workload (much higher in Melbourne)
teaching_comparison: I would say the style is somehow similar in most of the subjects, there is the theory part (lectures, which in my case were recordings) and then the practical part (workshops, tutorials, lab...). However, my online subject was based on podcasts, multiple choice tests and a collage.
courses_enrolled: Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry Contemporary Art and Biomedicine (online) Protein Structure and Function Techniques in Molecular Science
recommended_courses: If you want to have a hands-on and very practical subject with lots of lab, I recommend Techniques in Molecular Science. I wouldn't recommend having Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry and Protein Structure and Function at the same time, both are great subjects, however, both have lots of workload and almost weekly assignments (that are quite heavy).
unexpected_costs: Buying things for my lab subject (I forgot to bring my lab-coat) and my artistic subject. Getting a diving certificate
cost_comparison: Sushi was very cheap. Eating out in general is very affordable compared to Denmark. However, fruit and vegetables if they are not on season, they are a bit more expensive.
activities_available: Lots of language clubs, team sports, and other sports such as surf, diving, mountaineering...
activities_recommended: If you want to learn how to dive, I recommend joining the diving club, they offer a course where you can learn and then take on dives with the club.
weekend_recommendations: Travel as much as you can. Near Melbourne you can go to Phillip Island, Great Ocean Road, Mornington Peninsula, lots of hikes... It is also very easy and quite cheap to travel to Tasmania from Melbourne, which I recommend. You can also find very good deals for domestic flights around Australia.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Their culture is very open and quite similar to European culture.
socializing_tips: Join the clubs.
cultural_challenges: I didn't find any challenge culturally.
culture_appreciated: How open and helpful they are.
top3_advice: 1. Join the clubs 2. Travel as much as possible 3. Be prepared mentally that the workload might be heavier than in KU
other_useful_info: 1. Use STOP1 whenever you have a doubt or problem (even not uni related)
most_rewarding: The whole experience was rewarding. Academically it was very challenging, however rewarding. All the trip opportunities was amazing, and I really enjoyed the university clubs and social life.
greatest_challenge: The workload and the fact that I used more time doing uni work than expected.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to study in an english speaking country. I also heard about the vibrant culture in Melbourne which was important to me. And which was very accurate!
overall_comments: Best decision ever, and worth all the hard admin work!
info_ease: It was easy. The website was very helpful and had a step-by-step guide specifically to exchange students. And a checklist as well.
arrival_assistance: We had a welcome day where we were introduced to the university and the culture of Melbourne and two former exchange student talked about their experience. They also have "Stop 1" which is a building on campus. They are all very helpful! Just write them a mail or show up! They also have a welcome week, where you can participate in as much as you want. Both about academic stuff and about clubs on campus.
arrival_comments: Helpful people at stop 1
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Best decision ever, and worth all the hard admin work!
registration_process: There was a lot of steps. Get accepted by KU, then by UniMelb, then you need to get a CoE, and visa and OSHC(health). Theres is a lot of steps, but you are guided through it all by uni one by one.
registration_help: The letters/mails were helpful. Take your time and read them. Ask your supervisor or stop 1 if you're in doubt.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted. You have to decide which subject you want beforehand, but you are allowed to change them a week or two after the semester starts, which is so good! If you have regrets, you can change the subject!
registration_advice: Start as soon as possible and take your time with the process. It's not worth it to rush it neither get stressed about it last minute. Stop 1 was helpful whenever the subject registration was annoying.
academics_comments: Best decision ever, and worth all the hard admin work!
course_level: The subjects I had was on level 1 and 2 which I found was way easier than I thought. You are studying with younger people than yourself, so the teachers are often very helpful with the first year subjects (level 1)
teaching_comparison: Way more practical which was awesome. Less bound up by books and articles and so on...
courses_enrolled: Making music for film and animation The Business of Music Big Band 2 (Breadth) Shakuhachi ensemble
recommended_courses: All! Making music for film and animation was easy and had a great teacher. For the exam we did a project on a film/animation where we either could compose our own music or use other composers' music. The Business of Music had the funniest teacher. Easy subject but also learned a lot. (And Denmark doesn't have a subject like this) Big Band 2 (Breadth). Best subject ever, but I had to do an audition beforehand to get accepted into the Conservatory. High standard but doable. The conductor was amazing and the musicians were all so nice and talented!! Shakuhachi ensemble: Learn how to play the Japanese bamboo flute and learn about Japanese culture. How unique! The instrument was harder to learn than I thought, but I enjoyed the subject so much!!
unexpected_costs: Travelled more than I thought I would. Buying a bike. Buying and renting instruments.
cost_comparison: Less expensive: Eating out, public transport, (free meals from uni), coffee More expensive: Housing, insurance, visa, veggies
activities_available: All you can think of. Music, sport clubs and appreciation clubs. Just so many clubs of all sorts, I'm sure you'll find one you love. Also a great way to meet new people.
activities_recommended: Go to concerts. Eat out, Melbourne has the best food scene ever!! And omg the coffee, put it in your budget immediately!
weekend_recommendations: In Victoria: Great Ocean Road, Wilsons Prom, The Grampians, Mornington Peninsula In Australia: Tasmania to hike, Roadtrip in Western Australia, Noosa/Byron Bay to relax and surf
culture_adjustment: Very Easy! Everyone's very nice and it has a rather european vibe.
socializing_tips: Engage in your subjects. They wanna hear about your life as much as you want to hear about them.
cultural_challenges: So much slang, but honestly loved it! Btw "see you later" doesn't mean later in the day, it can also mean later in the year or next year. Cars rule the country.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness of Aussies, the coffee and the multicultural food scene!
top3_advice: 1: Priorities whether your study or exploring experience is more important. Level 1/2 if for the explorers and Level 3 is for the study people who spend a lot of time on their subjects. It can differ, but generally speaking, it's like that. Both are good I reckon. 2: Don't be scared going to the other side of the world. You'll feel more at home than you think. Enjoy the vibe, the culture and the Aussies, they are just lovely. 3: Melbourne is called "four seasons in one day". Prepare yourself for that. It's not a tropical surf city. Oh and the houses are cold! No insulation! Really :o
other_useful_info: Enjoy it while it lasts, it is over before you know it
most_rewarding: The friends I got in Melbourne means the world to me now. I am so inspired by them and the whole exchange experience which feels so rewarding!
greatest_challenge: Being away from family and friends I think.
other_comments: Go go go!

crucial_aspects: I chose to go on exchange to the University of Melbourne because I had heard great things about Melbourne. The city is a fantastic place to live. Additionally, the university is highly prestigious and ranks well in various rankings.
info_ease: It was very easy to get information about the exchange. You are guided by the University of Copenhagen. In addition, you constantly receive emails about the stay, which means you always know what to do.
arrival_assistance: Guidance from my home university and guidance from the University of Melbourne.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was very easy to register. On the website, you can see what to do step by step.
registration_help: You receive emails, they have a website, and you get guidance from your home university.
registration_success: I got all the classes I applied for.
registration_advice: You don’t need to worry about registration. It will all work out fine. The only thing you need is a bit of patience.
course_level: The teaching was satisfactory, but I consciously chose to take undergraduate courses. That made it quite a bit easier.
teaching_comparison: There was a mix of seminars and lectures, similar to what you’re used to at home. In one of my courses, I had a 75% attendance requirement, which is different from what I’m used to. The exams are quite different from those at the University of Copenhagen, with multiple exams in a single course. You also have to write quite a few essays. However, you don’t need to worry about the level - it will be fine.
courses_enrolled: Sport and the Law Legal Language Environmental Rights and Responsibilities Principles of Business Law
recommended_courses: Sport and the Law. It was a really great course. The instructors were extremely skilled, the syllabus was engaging, and the exam was a positive experience.
unexpected_costs: Travel expenses were a significant cost. Additionally, the visa cost 8,000 kroner, which was much more expensive than expected. Unfortunately, the price has increased this year.
cost_comparison: Accommodation, visa, and travel expenses
activities_available: There are many sports clubs. I was part of the football club and also participated in some of the other sports clubs.
activities_recommended: I would recommend joining some sports clubs.
weekend_recommendations: Traveling around Australia.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy.
cultural_challenges: Not much. People are really kind. If you have an open mind and are friendly, everything will be fine. Of course, there are a few things you need to get used to, but that happens gradually.
culture_appreciated: People are very friendly.
top3_advice: I would say that, first and foremost, you should get involved socially. You need to be good at being social and reach out to other exchange students. This will make your stay much better. As I mentioned, I recommend travelling to Melbourne before finding accommodation. That way, you can see the places before choosing where you’ll live. Finally, I suggest you travel around Australia a bit - maybe even arrive well before your exchange starts - so you have plenty of time to explore beautiful Australia and everything it has to offer.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: It was an amazing experience. The best part of it all was the people I met there.
greatest_challenge: You are far away from family and friends, and the time difference is also hard to get used to.

crucial_aspects: Wanted to explore Australia while also focusing on my education
overall_comments: I had an extremely good experience. I learned a lot from my classes and Melbourne is a super fun city.
info_ease: Very easy
arrival_assistance: Didn't need assistance
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had an extremely good experience. I learned a lot from my classes and Melbourne is a super fun city.
registration_process: When you apply, you have to submit an excel file listing all the subjects you wish to take that have prerequisites along with proof that you fulfil them. Be careful with your choices as getting approved for subjects with prerequisites after the application process is an extremely tedious process.
registration_help: Didn't need help so don't know
registration_success: I got all the subjects I wanted
registration_advice: The subject pages only offer limited information. Search up the subject codes online and read what other people are saying. The UniMelb page on Reddit is extremely active so chances are someone will have written something about your subject in the past
academics_comments: I had an extremely good experience. I learned a lot from my classes and Melbourne is a super fun city.
course_level: Computer Vision: very challenging, Machine Learning Applications for Health: appropriately challenging, Database Systems & Information Modelling: homework-intensive but fairly easy, Management Competencies: very easy. I spend way more time studying throughout the semester than I'd normally do at KU but I obviously wasn't working part-time like I do at home, so there's probably a bias there. I had two project-based exams that weren't too hard and two in-person no-aids exams that required A LOT of studying.
teaching_comparison: A similar format of large lecture + small tutorial classes. My tutors (TAs) were all PhD students in the field they were teaching and thus significantly better qualified than what I've experienced at KU.
courses_enrolled: COMP90086 Computer Vision, COMP90089 Machine Learning Applications for Health, INFO90002 Database Systems & Information Modelling, MGMT90140 Management Competencies
recommended_courses: The computer science/informatics subjects I did were all very very good and I can recommend all of them. The teaching quality was great, better than anything I have experienced at uni in Denmark. Management Competences wasn't uninteresting but was unfortunately taught very poorly so I can't recommend it. I can't speak for other fields but for IT-related study I really can't recommend UniMelb enough. It will make you wish you were doing your whole degree there.
unexpected_costs: Nothing that I can recall
cost_comparison: Vegetables are pretty expensive
activities_available: All sorts. Whatever you're into basically. Sports, music, cultural exchange etc. etc.
activities_recommended: The mountaineering club were a fun bunch.
weekend_recommendations: Other than exploring Melbourne, I did a three-day group trip to see Uluru which was one of the best experiences of my life. I'd also recommend renting a car and doing a weekend trip on the Great Ocean Road. If you're able to go, take a trip to see the Great Barrier Reef.
culture_adjustment: Easy
socializing_tips: Go to your tutorials and chat with your classmates. There are a lot of international full-degree students and I ended up bonding with quite a few of them. The Aussies are very friendly but generally have their own friend groups and I found it harder to bond with them.
cultural_challenges: Don't know if it can be called a cultural difference, but It's a very car-centric country in general. Public transport in Melb is okay but getting around outside of the city is hard without a car

crucial_aspects: I had originally wanted to go to a big city in the UK, but since no programmes were offered that fit my destinations and study path, I decided to do something different. I wanted to go to an English-speaking country, but didn't feel that the US would suit me at the moment. Since Australia has always intrigued me, both culturally and nature-wise, I decided to go for it - the farthest possible destination from Denmark.
info_ease: It was fairly easy to find the information. Emails, introduction information leaflets and the university-student pages provided information.
arrival_assistance: I didn't get assistance since I didn't need it, but it was available for anyone who needed it. (transport from the airport, help with accommodation and so on). I did get help with course planning during the introduction week when some of my classes clashed and other technical/IT help.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: When you make your application, you need to outline any courses with prerequisites that you plan on taking/might take. Then, as you get accepted and closer to the semester, you need to fill out course registration/study plan, which was also fairly easy.
registration_help: You could contact IT or a course admin/STOP 1 where they would be able to help with most things.
registration_success: Very successful. Only one course was unsuccessful since it was the wrong semester (I don't know if they changed the semester it was running, or if I didn't check properly)
registration_advice: Have backup courses you want to take. Take a "fun" class that isn't necessarily relevant for your degree if you have enough elective points. UniMelb offer a lot of fun breadth courses (painting, education, music, wine courses and so on) Make sure you don't mix up sem 1 and sem 2 courses as they are opposite to each other. Also, make sure you check prerequisites and really look into whether you qualify.
course_level: I took two first-year courses in physics and astronomy as part of my electives. Then I took a 2nd-year and a 3rd-year course in Geology. The geology courses were similar in difficulty level to those at UCPH. The physics course was difficult, but that could also be because it had been a very long time since I had done any physics. The astronomy class was also at a fairly okay level. The lectures clashed with my other classes though, so that made it a bit difficult to fully follow the course. (All lectures were filmed, so I could rewatch them)
teaching_comparison: It was very similar. Geology courses had the same style of lectures and practicals as I was used to from UCPH. As for the Physics and astronomy courses, I am guessing they have a similar style as UCPH as well. We had lectures and labs, as well as some calculation classes and TA hours.
courses_enrolled: ERTH20003 - Past Climates: Icehouse to Greenhouse GEOL30007 - Geobiology PHYC10003 - Physics 1 PHYC10008 - From the Solar System to the Cosmos
recommended_courses: I liked all the courses I took and would recommend them, but as I mentioned above, I would also recommend taking some courses that aren't necessarily related to your degree. UniMelb has a bunch of different courses that are good as electives and can give some "breathing room" in your week. Take a class just for fun
unexpected_costs: Not sure what was unexpected...
cost_comparison: Some groceries were cheaper while others were more expensive. Café drinks were less expensive and eating out was also a fair bit cheaper than in Copenhagen
activities_available: The university has an incredible amount of clubs, sports and other activities. During the intro week there will be stands from almost all clubs and sports.
activities_recommended: I was a part of the hiking club, astronomy society, UMSU, and others. There are definitely going to be something for everyone
weekend_recommendations: Visit different suburbs of Melbourne. Try out some of the many markets they have, go to beaches. For weekend trips, I would recommend Philip Island, Mornington Peninsula, Wilson's prom, and Great Ocean Road. For mid-semester break I roadtripped Brisbane - Gold Coast - Sunshine Coast - Noosa. I also went to Sydney and loved it. After exams, I went on a long road trip to New Zealand with friends, and it was such a good trip. Some of the things I wish I had had time to do include is Tasmania, Great Barrier Reef, Ulluru, Perth, and Byron Bay.
culture_adjustment: It was fairly easy. It is a big cultural city like many others, so it wasn't too hard
socializing_tips: Don't be shy to initiate conversation in classes with someone you're sitting beside, or initiate a study session or coffee with a classmate you're working with. It is also good to go to different club events and similar, to meet local students
cultural_challenges: Not really any as far as I remember. It took some time to get used to the different driving lane and which side to look.
culture_appreciated: I liked a lot of it. There's a big social culture and coffee/tea culture, which is great. A lot of focus on being outside, being active and social.
top3_advice: Enjoy it. Try and see as much as possible and try to take at least one class thats a "fun" class/not related to your degree/fairly easy.
other_useful_info: Not sure no...
most_rewarding: The whole overall experience, the memories, friends, and travel I got. It was incredible to try a univeristy in a different city and a different social culture.
greatest_challenge: Trying to balance the academic side while also seeing and experiencing as much as possible (also with the budget I had available).

crucial_aspects: I have always wanted to visit Australia and found exchange to be a perfect opportunity for that. I specifically chose Melbourne because I have heard that it is a very nice city to live and study in.
overall_comments: I highly recommend going on exchange! It's a great opportunity to break away from your normal everyday life and experience something new. Melbourne has been an amazing base as it is a lovely city to live in with many amazing travel destinations nearby, both within Victoria and throughout the rest of Australia.
info_ease: I found this part quite easy. The University of Melbourne was good at sending emails before arrival with all the information you needed to know.
arrival_assistance: On the 'Welcome Day' all exchange students attended a presentation where important information about studying at the University of Melbourne was provided. Additionally, you could always visit the student service 'Stop One' on campus for assistance with course planning or any other questions related to student life.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I highly recommend going on exchange! It's a great opportunity to break away from your normal everyday life and experience something new. Melbourne has been an amazing base as it is a lovely city to live in with many amazing travel destinations nearby, both within Victoria and throughout the rest of Australia.
registration_process: The first step of the process was to search the Handbook (https://handbook.unimelb.edu.au/search), which provides an overview of all the courses. Once you have accepted your spot at the University of Melbourne, you can apply for the courses you want to take. I was lucky to get all the courses I applied for, and none of them overlapped, making the process very straightforward for me.
registration_help: If you needed help, you could always email the university both before and after arrival. I remember they responded quite quickly! After arriving, you could also book an appointment at Stop One, the university's student service centre.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: The Handbook is very useful tool for exploring all the courses offered by the University of Melbourne - take some time to search through it!
academics_comments: I highly recommend going on exchange! It's a great opportunity to break away from your normal everyday life and experience something new. Melbourne has been an amazing base as it is a lovely city to live in with many amazing travel destinations nearby, both within Victoria and throughout the rest of Australia.
course_level: My courses were interesting, and I had some great lecturers, but compared to the University of Copenhagen, I would say the academic level was not as high.
teaching_comparison: My courses included a mix of lectures and tutorials with class discussions, so it was quite similar to University of Copenhagen. However, one difference was that all lectures were livestreamed, which meant that many students didn't attend lectures in person. Another difference was that most of my courses required students to attend at least 80% of their tutorials to pass the subject.
courses_enrolled: Living in a Risk Society, Melbourne: Urban Anthropology in Action, Punishment and Social Control and Street Art
recommended_courses: I found all my courses interesting! They were also quite manageable in terms of workload, as all of them had assignments during the semester instead of a final exam.
unexpected_costs: The OSHC (an obligatory health insurance) - there are different providers, and I personally chose the cheapest option, which costed 1,523 DKK.
cost_comparison: Buying food in supermarkets was more expensive than I expected, but otherwise, most other things were pretty much as I had imagined – though I did expect Australia to be expensive. I highly recommend taking advantage of the University of Melbourne's free food options! You can pick up three free frozen meals every week, enjoy free breakfast on campus a couple of days a week, and collect a free box of fruits and vegetables every other week, if I remember correctly. Traveling around Australia is also very expensive – I was especially surprised by how expensive accommodations, such as hostels, are.
activities_available: University of Melbourne offers many different clubs, such as surf club, mountaineering club, coffee club and wine society
activities_recommended: I didn't join a club, but I did attend some of the events organised by Musex (the club for exchange students), which was a great way to meet other exchange students.
weekend_recommendations: In Victoria I would recommend to visit Wilsons Prom, Great Ocean Road, Grampians and Phillip Island. Additionally I have really enjoyed visiting Tasmania, the East Coast, Northern Territory and New Zealand. I can recommend to rent a campervan - it is such a nice way to travel around in Australia and New Zealand!
culture_adjustment: Melbourne is not that different from Copenhagen, so I found it have been pretty easy
socializing_tips: I ended up getting to know most local students through my courses. However, I found it easier to become friends with other exchange students. I heard from others that joining clubs and living with Australians can be a great way to connect! :)
cultural_challenges: I didn't found any cultural differences challenging
culture_appreciated: I really enjoyed the vibe in Fitzroy, where I lived - lots of great shops, cafes and bars! And the coffee is so good - however, be prepared for most coffee shops in Australia to close around 2 pm in the afternoon :((
top3_advice: I was very happy that the courses I chose didn't have any final exams, as it gave me more time to travel after the semester. However, it did mean a slightly heavier workload during the semester, but it was still manageable. Winter in Australia can be surprisingly cold, and the weather in Melbourne is generally very unpredictable, so be sure to pack a variety of clothing. Australia is also quite expensive, so try to save up as much money as possible. I'd highly recommend starting early with scholarship applications - it's a time-consuming process, and many scholarships close for applications early. Start as soon as you've secured your spot!
other_useful_info: There are a lot of other Danes on exchange in Melbourne, and it's very easy to stay within that bubble. If you want to make more international friends, you'll need to actively seek out those opportunities, such as by joining clubs.
most_rewarding: All the great people I have met and all the amazing places I have visit both during the semester and after it ended! I've also really enjoyed having more free time and being able to be more spontaneous.
greatest_challenge: Sometimes being so far away from home, friends, and family can be challenging, but most of the time, it's absolutely worth it!
other_comments: I cannot recommend going on exchange at the University of Melbourne enough! If you're considering it - do it! Melbourne is an incredible city to live in, and Australia is an amazing country to travel around.

most_rewarding: Traveling! Seeing different parts of Australia, surfing, scuba diving, hiking!

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte Australien, da jeg tænkte at landet ville give gode muligheder for at opleve noget helt særligt, både kulturelt og ift. naturen, som man ikke kan finde indenfor Europa. Samtidig vidste jeg at landet er tilpas udviklet og har et godt uddannelsessystem med undervisning på engelsk, således at jeg ret let ville kunne indgå i undervisningen og fagene. Desuden tænkte jeg, at jeg nok ikke lige foreløbig får muligheden for at rejse til Australien, hvorfor jeg så et udvekslingsophold i lige netop Australien som en god mulighed for at besøge landet, samtidig med at jeg ville kunne komme videre med studiet.

Selve ansøgningen / tilmeldingen til fagene foregår gennem en portal ligesom KUs selvbetjening, og her kan man følge med i processen. Når du er tilmeldt fagene, skal du lave dit eget skema, hvilket er anderledes end vi kender det fra KU. På Unimelb har de et selvstændigt system til skemalægning, hvor du går ind og ønsker, hvornår du vil have dine timer. Man kan risikere at nogle timer falder sammen, og at man derfor skal skifte fag i eftertilmeldingsperioden.
registration_help: Stop 1 var til rådighed, ligesom at der var bestemte mailadresser man kunne skrive til, ved bestemte problemstillinger.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag jeg ansøgte om.
registration_advice: Vær opmærksom på, om der er prerequisites til de fag du ønsker. Hvis der er det, ligger der en lille smule mere arbejde i at ansøge om fagene. Derudover vil jeg fraråde fag som har obligatorisk fremmøde - det havde jeg i alle mine fag og det var ret træls ift. planlægning af andre aktiviteter og fungerede bare dårligt når man er vant til frihed under ansvar.
academics_comments: Jeg vil måske være opmærksom på at justere forventningerne til, hvordan et udvekslingsophold egentligt er inden afrejse - mange italesætter det som en badeferie og der findes et narrativ om, at et udvekslingsophold er mindre akademisk tungt end et semester herhjemme. Dette vil jeg dog sige kommer meget an på hvilket universitet man er på, hvilke fag man har, og hvad ens egne forventninger er til egen indsats.
course_level: Jeg synes niveauet svingede ret meget fra fag til fag, ligesom arbejdsbyrden, i hvertfald i praksis, også svingede meget. Det generelle niveau var meget ligesom herhjemme. Jeg synes dog at der var forskel på niveauet til selve timerne og så til niveuet i gradings af ens opgaver. Timerne var meget chill og lette, men underviserne var ambitiøse og forventede et ret højt niveau i de akademiske opgaver man skulle aflevere ( I hvertfald i de fire fag jeg havde).
teaching_comparison: Måden at undervise på var ret anderledes. Jeg havde næsten kun holdtimer og ingen forelæsninger, og holdtimerne var meget dialogbaserede elev til elev, med ingen eller kun en let gennemgang af stoffet fra underviserens side af. Alle mine undervisere snakkede meget overordnet om tingene og var aldrig særlig konkrekte omkring begreber, teorier mv. I timerne og forelæsningerne var det altså den lette overflyvning, og der blev sjældent italesat eller skabt overblik over, hvad det vigtigste ift. et begreb eller en teori var. Min oplevelse var dog, at det var forventet i opgaverne, og derfor var der en del mere arbejde i at skrive opgaver og forsøge at regne ud hvad underviserne ladge vægt på, eftersom de aldrig rigtig var tydelige omkring dette i undervisningen. Både undervisere og elever var dog virkelig engageret i undervisningen, hvilket skabte et mere livligt og nysgerrigt miljø end man måske er vant til herhjemmefra.
courses_enrolled: POLS90042 Latin America in the World, PPMN90031, Public Policy Lobbying Strategies POLS90016, International Organisations DEVT90043, Advocacy in Development
recommended_courses: Jeg kan anbefale alle kurserne, da de alle var spændende og lærerige. Dog var der obligatorisk fremmøde på alle fire. Hvis jeg skulle fremhæve et fag, ville det være Latin America in the World. Jeg havde ingen forventningerne eller særlig viden på området inden faget, men det var virkelig spændende og meget anderledes undervisning med gæsteforelæsere der spillede musik, fortalte historier, viste kunst ovs. Derudover var professor Adrian Hearn en virkelig god formilder og meget vidende på området, samtidig med at han var meget engareret og opmuntrende ift. bidrag i undervisningen og emner.
unexpected_costs: Jeg endte med at bruge mange penge på offentlig transport, da jeg i en periode boede udenfor byen og havde langt til universitetet, og fordi at kandidatsstuderende ikke åbenbart ikke kan få et concession card til offentlig transport i Melbourne, hvilket jeg ellers troede. Tager du offentlig transport hver eller næsten hver dag i Melbourne kommer det til at være en relativ stor post i budgettet, i hvertfald som kandidatstuderende. Før jeg ankom til byen, havde jeg tænkt at købe en cykel og bruge til transport, men det ændrede jeg holdning til, efter jeg oplevede cykelforholdene og trafikken :).
cost_comparison: Huslejeniveauet er højere end i Danmark, mad og indkøb er nogenlunde det samme. Transport er lidt billigere, men stadig dyrt. Kaffen er billigere og at gå ud og spise kan også være en del billigere alt efter hvor man spiser.
activities_available: Der var en forening til nærmest alt - sport, krea, sprog, mad, klima, osv.
activities_recommended: Jeg nåede ikke selv at prøve så meget, men jeg synes det hele virkede nice - jeg tror det bedste man kan gøre er at prøve de forskellige ting af. Der er en forening for udvekslingsstuderende som er meget god at kende til, den hedder MUSEX.
weekend_recommendations: Det hele. Hvis jeg skal fremhæve noget kunne det være byen Torquay og Bells Beach, hvis man kan lide at surfe eller at kigge på folk der surger. Derudover skal man måske være opmærksom på, at de fleste oplevelser udenfor byen kræver en bil, så man skal være glad for at køre eller alliere sig med nogen der kan og vil køre.
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt.
socializing_tips: Hvis du gerne vil i kontakt med Australiere skal du finde en anden vej end gennem universitetet - brug byen eller bo hos eller sammen med nogle australiere. De fleste på universitetet er internationale studerende.
cultural_challenges: Ingen, udover at deres kaffebarer og cafeer lukker virkelig tidligt på dagen, så det med at mødes til en eftermiddagskaffe kan godt være svært.
culture_appreciated: Den afslappet tilgang til mange ting, såsom påklædning samt den udbredte åbenhed og venlighed. Folk var meget hjælpsomme og umiddelbare.
top3_advice: 1) Giv dig selv god tid og rigeligt med penge til at skabe en god og stabil boligsituation - Det kan være ret kaotisk og udmattende i Melbourne 2) Omgiv dig selv med andre end de mange danskere der er i byen - Melb er meget multikulturel og man får virkelig meget ud af at snakke med folk fra hele verden. Og hvis du kun vil snakke med danskere, hvorfor så tage til Australien? 3) Husk at der ikke er en rigtig eller forkert måde at være på udveksling på, gør det på den måde der fungerer for dig
other_useful_info: Hvis du gerne vil udvikle dig fagligt er der rig mulighed for det på Unimelb - der er meget mere feedback fra underviserne, og de vil gerne hjælpe, sparre, diskutere osv. hvis man selv lægger en indsats.
most_rewarding: At få sat tingene i perspektiv i mødet med noget anderledes - både rent fagligt men også kulturelt og personligt.
greatest_challenge: Legatansøgningerne.
other_comments: Hvis du har muligheden for at tage afsted så gør det, og hvis du er i tvivl om, hvorvidt du har lyst eller om det bliver som du forventer, så husk at du selv former oplevelsen gennem dine forventninger. Gør opholdet til dit eget, og lad vær med passivt at indoptage andres forventninger. Opholdet er dit og du kan gøre det på den måde, du har lyst til.

crucial_aspects: 1) English speaking country 2) Far away 3) Cool city
info_ease: Very easy, everything is sent via e-mails.
arrival_assistance: Mails and I seeked out further assistance at the student help service at campus (Stop1). They're very helpful with everything both via e-mail and in person.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: After receiving your nomination from UniMelb, they send you a guide about how to apply to study there. It's just a formality; as an exchange student with a nomination from KU, you get the spot you apply for. It takes some time to have it all settled, so don't stress and just follow deadlines. During the application process, you also apply for your student visa and overseas health care (OSHC), so everything becomes settled as you move along. After applying, you get a UniMelb user and can follow their online stepwise guide for completing your enrollment (applying for subjects etc.).
registration_help: Stop1 (student help service at UniMelb)
registration_success: Not really succesful at once. 3/4 of the subjects I wanted had requirements of prerequisite subjects, so I had to document that I was eligible for the subjects by documenting the previous subjects I'd had at KU. One of my required documents was missing, so instead of Stop1 reaching out to the subject coordinators on my behalf, I just had to e-mail them myself later. It was a bit stressful, since I only received notice of this in June, but everything was settled in July before the semester started.
registration_advice: Be ahead of deadlines, make sure you submit all the required documents, and enroll in the subjects you want as soon as possible. The subjects without prerequisites needed can be applied for as soon as you get your user, and if quotas apply, they fill up somewhat fast. The 1 subject I wanted with no prerequisites and quotas was full when I wanted to enrol, but I just wrote to the subject coordinator and asked if I could get a spot anyways, and then I was approved.
course_level: There's 3 levels for BA: 1000 (1st year), 2000 (2nd year), 3000 (3rd year). 1st and 2nd year subjects have more attendance and a higher workload throughout the semester with small quizzes than what we're used to at KU. 3rd year subjects have more flexibility but not as much as we're used to at KU.
teaching_comparison: All my lectures were streamed and saved online, so I could watch them on my own time as it suited me. Otherwise, there's a lot more control around the subjects than what I've been used to. Mid-semester tests are very common, as are assignments and quizzes during the semester. They all count towards your final grade, so when you have your end of semester exam, you already have some points towards passing, if you've done some work during the semester. Normally, I prefer doing everything on my own time as we pretty much do at KU, but at UniMelb, it gave more security to know the final exam didn't count 100%, since it made it easier to pass overall (all grades are transferred as passed/not passed to KU, so your grades at the host university do not count).
courses_enrolled: AGRI10039 Australia in the Wine World PHRM20001 Pharmacology: How Drugs Work NEUR30004 Complex Functions in Neuroscience NEUR30005 Developmental Neurobiology
recommended_courses: AGRI10039: very fun and different. Each week there's a prac class with is a wine tasting where attendance is required (I believe you have to be there for 8/10, but I recommend coming as much as possible since you learn a lot). Not just for fun; there's still curriculum and lectures, exam is divided into 1 theoretical and 1 prac, so you still have to learn the theoretics. Gives knowledge on wine in general and wine regions. PHRM20001: intro subject to pharmacology. With a background in biomed, I knew a lot in advance, so it was a pretty easy subject to follow. It gives some new perspectives pharm-wise and in terms of therapies. The lecturers were very enthusiastic. A lot of repetition as well on general physiology. If you want a more academically challenging subject, I'd not recommend this. For me, it worked well with my other subjects since I had a big background knowledge so it gave me more time for exploring the city and traveling during the semester. NEUR30004: not what I expected. The first half of lectures were not so well-organized and a bit confusing as to what they wanted us to actually learn. Almost philosophical about cognition, not science-oriented in my opinion (I did not enjoy this). Last half was very well-organized and interesting to me (about nociception and pain). If you're into neuroscience, it's an alright subject, last part at least was very fun. Mid-semester test was difficult, but end of semester test went smoothly so I wouldn't worry too much. Otherwise, I've heard great things of the 3rd year stem cell subject. NEUR30005: by far my favorite subject. Well-organized, all lecturers were great, and it builds very well on Signal Transduction and other bio/pathway stuff learned with a background in biomed. 3 lectures every week, so you get a lot of knowledge, but no attendance required, so you can fit it in your schedule as you please. Lot of neuro stuff of course, but since they use research articles as the basis of the lectures, you also get are more plain biomed POV as well as cancer and what therapies/methods you in general can use.
unexpected_costs: Visa and OSHC (5000 DKK in total) and plane tickets are expensive. So is living in AUS in general.
cost_comparison: Groceries are pricy, so is alcohol, but coffee is cheap and good. You can sign up to get free frozen meals (3-4 per week) and groceries from campus each week. It's not good food, but it's edible and you can save a lot on this. Plane tickets are pretty cheap (if booked at least 2 weeks before departure), so it's easy to get around. Public transport is also cheap in Victoria if you're on your bachelor's; you can get a concession card and save 50% on all trams, busses and trains. I recommend this as it helps you get around easily, and Melbourne's a big city, if you want to go beyond inner city CBD (central business district). I think you pay a max. of 5$ a day with concession, otherwise I think it's 10$.
activities_available: I signed up for the gym at campus. Pretty cheap (less than 300DKK per month) loads of racks, machines etc., and always space if you steer clear of rush hour (5 PM ish). You also get access to their swimming pools, yoga/dance classes. Otherwise, they also have loads of clubs. I didn't sign up for any because I was plenty busy without still. But they both have sports clubs and social clubs. Before the semester starts, the uni host intro-days where you can meet all the clubs and hear about what they do. They have an exchange student society (MUSEX) as well that connects you with other exchange students.
activities_recommended: They have a mountaineering club which you can rent gear from if you join some of their trips in the beginning, pretty nice if you like hiking and have some experience. They also have a ski club where they go in trips, but you have to sign up pretty early for the good trips (already in April I think). Lastly, their surf club is very popular, too (especially for parties and stuff). All clubs have instagram, so go check them out in advance if you're curious, otherwise just show up for intro days
weekend_recommendations: Take some time to get to know Melbourne. It's a wonderful city and I loved living there. Especially the neighborhoods around CBD (Fitzroy, Collingwood, Brunswick, Carlton, South Melbourne/Yarra, St Kilda) are lovely. I lived in South Melbourne and loved it. Loads of cafés and thrift shopping in Fitzroy/Collingwood/Brunswick/Chapel Street. Victoria (the state Melbourne is located in) is beautiful and there's plenty to do on smaller trips (day/weekend). I can recommend Great Ocean Road, the Grampians, Wilsons Promontory, Camel's Hump, Hanging Rocks, Thousand Steps and Phillip Island. Otherwise, you can catch a plane and go further. Tasmania is beautiful and nearby, but a weekend is a bit too short I'd say. It's also pretty easy to get to Uluru/Ayer's Rock, but book in good time since plane tickets get expensive and before it gets too hot (October was good). Sydney is also just 1,5 h away by plane, you can also take bus/train, but it's 8-12h.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Melbourne is very European in style. People are friendlier though.
socializing_tips: The Australian students kept a lot to themselves. Few came to lectures/class in general and they're a bit younger, so I mainly socialized with other exchange/international students. Though, the few Aussies that come to class are friendly, so try and chat with them if you want (especially easy in wine class). Otherwise, the clubs are a good way to meet other students, both local and exchange. A lot of Danes were in Melbourne as well. We had messenger/Facebook groups to arrange meetings and ask questions about enrollment which was very nice.
cultural_challenges: Not really anything culturally. Only thing that was difficult was being far away from home and finding a place to live in the beginning, but I got adjusted quickly and just had a lot of fun and kept busy.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness and the good coffee. Also, being outdoors is a big part of the culture; people go a lot to the many parks, outside dining and rooftops are popular, and people are very active and do a lot of sports (bouldering, tennis courts, running etc.). We also found a paddle court in Docklands which was a chill way to hang out.
top3_advice: 1) Take your time with application for it to be less stressful 2) Enjoy the city, Melbourne is awesome 3) Travel around if you have the money/time
other_useful_info: I appreciated that my exchange wasn't too academically challenging so I had time for fun stuff and traveling as well. It can also be overwhelming to live so far away, so it was nice to not have a hard time with studies as well.
most_rewarding: The travels. Overall, with the subjects I had, UniMelb was not as academically challenging as KU, but this can maybe be modified with other subjects. I studied much less than I usually would and still passed everything, no issues there. Just don't fall too behind, otherwise the exam period will be too tight.
greatest_challenge: Finding a place to live. Afterwards, everything went smoothly.
other_comments: Best decision I made, best half year of my life. It's an amazing opportunity to try and live somewhere else than Denmark/far away, which is very fun and rewarding to try. Also a great way to see Australia/New Zealand, since it's not otherwise easy to get there and travel.

crucial_aspects: I was very interested in finding a uni abroad with good subject options and I knew i wanted to go to australia due to the weather and also the lack of language barriers.
overall_comments: It was some of the best months ever, would definitely recommend doing a semester abroad!
info_ease: It was very easy, we got loads of emails as well as had an intro day for all the exchange students where we got oriented.
arrival_assistance: There were loads of welcome emails as well as some intro meetings. I was also staying at student accommodation on campus which helped loads with the transition, the staff were so helpful and answered any questions and confusion I had.
arrival_comments: I think staying at the uni accommodation made my transition easy. The staff were helpful and being around other students who were doing the same intro days was very helpful. Other than that the uni itself also helped and had an intro meeting just for the exchange students as well as an entire intro week with tours and fairs to show which clubs the uni has to offer.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: It was some of the best months ever, would definitely recommend doing a semester abroad!
registration_process: You need to look through the handbook and choose courses that you want to take and are in the right semester and then register through their portals.
registration_help: If you were unable to register there were student hubs on campus that could help you and then also you could email the student services.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: I took four difficult courses all of which were relevant to my studies. If I did it again I would probably have taken one less serious subject so I would have been a bit less stressed.
academics_comments: It was some of the best months ever, would definitely recommend doing a semester abroad!
course_level: I think the level is similar to that of at KU but the exam format is quite different because they were all closed book and some were even non calculator.
teaching_comparison: At KU I was used to having 2 courses at a time because we do the blok struktur, but at Melbourne it was all four courses at once which took a while to adjust to the juggling of. There was also less focus on the class time and more focus on lectures. They left you to do a lot of the work in your free time. In the beginning I found it difficult because I thought you had to do all the prep work for the tutorials but as the semester went on I realised they didn't require that much prep which took some of the pressure off.
courses_enrolled: Elements of Quantum Computing, Condensed Matter Physics 3, Theoretical Physics 3, Sub-atomic Physics
recommended_courses: I would recommend Condensed Matter Physics 3 and Theoretical Physics 3 they were challenging but the professors were great and willing to answer any questions you had. I think Elements of Quantum Computing was also a good subject but as it was a second year subject it was not very challenging. Don't take Sub-atomic Physics, the professors were not good at lecturing and it was often difficult to follow their train of thought. In the final exam there were also several mistakes which students noticed and corrected. It seemed like they didn't want to teach.
unexpected_costs: I wasn't planning on living on campus to start with and that ended up being very expensive. And alcohol (other than wine) is so so so expensive, definitely more than what I was expecting.
cost_comparison: The public transport in Melbourne is very expensive like 5 AUD for one ride on the tram, but one could not tap their cards unless there were inspectors to save loads of money. You could also buy a cheap bike to get around. My food was included in the rent so I didn't have to go grocery shopping.
activities_available: I was mostly involved with the sports and social activities arranged through my accommodation, such as intercollegiate sports and culture nights and pub crawls. There was also a plethora of activities at the uni that I didn't really utilise that much because I didn't have that much time next to uni and social stuff at my college.
activities_recommended: I would recommend trying a bit of everything in the beginning and meeting people through those activities.
weekend_recommendations: I went travelling around to the big cities in some of the weekends. In our mid semester break I went to New Zealand which I would definitely recommend, lots of beautiful nature! After I finished the semester I still had two months before the semester in Denmark started so I traveled around SE Asia which is much cheaper than staying in Australia where everything is so expensive.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, there was no language barrier and the people were so friendly.
socializing_tips: I think going to clubs and societies is a great way to meet local students. The surf club has great parties and two trips during the semester, but the trips are difficult to get a place on. I met all of my close friends through the accommodation, and it was a lot of fun to live so many students together.
cultural_challenges: Not many differences
culture_appreciated: I enjoyed the australian football league.
top3_advice: The stress of planning a semester abroad is definitely worth it. I would recommend looking at accommodation a bit early then it maybe will be cheaper
other_useful_info: no
most_rewarding: The friends I met are some great people from all over the world that I can't wait to see again!

crucial_aspects: I chose Australia because I had heard great things about the country and the opportunities it offered for outdoor activities and exploration. Additionally, Australia provided excellent travel opportunities after my studies.
overall_comments: I chose Melbourne, but looking back, I think I would have preferred Sydney – it’s such a great city
info_ease: It was a very long process, and you need to be prepared for the many official documents and applications you have to keep track of. However, I found that there was good communication from both KU and Melbourne University if I needed any help.
arrival_assistance: They have an office called Stop-One that can help you with anything.
arrival_comments: There are plenty of student accommodations in Melbourne, but they are very expensive. I ended up renting an Airbnb with a friend near campus – it was cheaper, though a bit more basic compared to the pricier student housing options.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I chose Melbourne, but looking back, I think I would have preferred Sydney – it’s such a great city
registration_process: They held an online meeting where all students were informed about practical matters such as visa, course registration, health insurance, etc. Additionally, you can always contact their student support service, Stop-One, but it can take some time for them to respond, especially when things are busy just before the start of the semester.
registration_help: You can always contact them but it can take a while for them to respond.
registration_success: I was registered for most of the classes from home, but I had some issues with the portal. I was only fully registered when I arrived there and received help from Stop-One.
registration_advice: My advice would be to start early and participate in the online meetings. This will help you stay informed and prepared for the registration process.
academics_comments: I chose Melbourne, but looking back, I think I would have preferred Sydney – it’s such a great city
course_level: 2x level 1 1x level 2 1 x level 3
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching at my host institution was quite similar to that at UCPH in terms of the structure of classes with lectures and tutorials. However, a notable difference was that most lectures were recorded, allowing students to watch them remotely if they preferred. Also, they held a lot of midterm exams.
courses_enrolled: Microbes, Infections and Responses Australia in the Wine World Our Planet, Our Health Medical Microbiology: Virology
recommended_courses: The courses I would recommend depend on your interests, but if you're looking for something enjoyable, I would suggest taking the wine course. It's a fun subject where you learn about wine production, wine regions, and get to participate in various wine tastings.
unexpected_costs: Medical bills and medication also turned out to be costly, even though I had the mandatory health insurance.
cost_comparison: Food was quite expensive.
activities_available: I was very satisfied with the non-academic opportunities at my host institution. There were many engaged students and a wide range of clubs to join, including hiking, surfing, swimming, and all kinds of sports.
activities_recommended: I would recommend renting a car with some friends and going on a road trip along the Great Ocean Road. It's incredibly beautiful and a must-see experience.
weekend_recommendations: I recommend taking as many trips as possible, visiting wildlife sanctuaries, or joining some of the excursions offered by the social clubs, such as hiking, surfing, or diving trips.
culture_adjustment: t was quite easy to adjust, as I spent most of my time with other exchange students. Their society and culture are similar to our own.
socializing_tips: No, I didn’t socialize much with local students. It seemed like the majority of students were international, and I’m not sure where the Australians were.
cultural_challenges: I had hoped to experience more of the Australian culture, but Melbourne is very international and strongly influenced by students from Asian countries.
culture_appreciated: The part of the culture I appreciated the most was what I experienced during my travels along the east coast after my studies. Australians are very laid-back and friendly, they have a chill vibe. I also love their nature and all the cool activities you can do, like diving, hiking, surfing, boat trips, waterfall tours, and much more.
top3_advice: Find accommodation close to your institution. Be prepared to participate in a lot of social activities, especially at the beginning of your stay when people are forming their friend groups. It's great to know some people from home, so you have someone to hang out and participate in activities with in the beginning.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: To be honest, the most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the weekend trips and my travels along the east coast afterwards.
greatest_challenge: At KU, we have a block structure where we take 2 courses at a time and have exams at the end of each course. In Melbourne, I had 4 courses at once, each with ongoing mid-term exams that counted for a percentage of the final exam. This meant I was constantly studying for exams in one of the courses, and once that was over, I had to start studying for the next one. It was a bit of an exhausting system.
other_comments: Being on exchange is very rewarding but also quite challenging. Remember to apply for as many scholarships as possible well in advance. I would also recommend leaving some time afterward for travel.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to Australia, and when I started researching courses and universities, I realised that the University of Melbourne is highly ranked and offers the most interesting classes. Furthermore, it was important for me to be able to travel and experience the country I was in.
info_ease: Very easy. It was a bit much the first day, but then it became very easy. UniMelb's website has a lot of information, and any additional information was available at Stop 1
arrival_assistance: I had some help switching a class, but that was about it.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was a bit early you could register, but there was also a secondary period for registrering for classes. I would, however, highly recommend registrering in the first period, as each subject have multiple classes, and you can prioritise which classes (regarding time) you want. This makes it easier to make a timetable that allows time for other things, except studying.
registration_help: Stop 1 is a very helpful service. On the first couple of days in the secondary registration period, they have full days where you can come unannounced and talk to them to get help.
registration_success: I got all my classes, but ended up switching a class after I saw that it was recommended that I could speak/understand Chinese for one of my original classes. But it was easy to switch, so I ended up in all my preferred classes and my preferred timetable as well.
registration_advice: Registrer in the first period, even if it seems unmanageable. And maybe take some intense subjects? I had one that ended a month early, and one class that started a month later. It means that the teachings are going to be three hours instead of two, but I only had three weeks where I had four subjects.
course_level: I had three MA classes and one third-year BA course. But ironically, the third-year BA course was the one I found most difficult.
teaching_comparison: It is a lot more class discussions at UniMelb than what I am used to at UCPH. Which, in some cases, was good, but in some cases was bad. Especially because not all students have the same English skills. However, the level is a bit lower at UniMelb, so I found it easier to show up without necessarily having done all the readings and still be able to follow along. All my classes also had compulsory attendance, so that was different.
courses_enrolled: 1) Race, Ethnicity, and Nationalism, 2) Latin America in the World, 3) Public Policy Lobbying Strategies, 4) International Organisations.
recommended_courses: I liked all my courses, but I would definitely recommend "International Organisations" as Justin is a really good teacher, and the course is interesting. Likewise, I would recommend "Latin America in the World" as there are a lot of different kinds of teachings, and you just learn a lot about Latin America.
unexpected_costs: The visa (!!!!). It is really expensive. It cost 7.571 DKK and I also had to buy an OSCH insurance that cost 2.034 DKK.
cost_comparison: Of course, it costs something to move and get a blanket, pillows, etc., but if you go to Kmart, you can really get them cheaply. I was surprised by how cheap I found public transport, but I ended up walking most places anyway.
activities_available: There is everything. You can join sports clubs for most sports, clubs for wine drinking or chocolate eating, and cultural clubs like the French club, the German club, the Myanmar society, etc.
activities_recommended: I would recommend joining Mussex, as this society is for exchange students.
weekend_recommendations: As much as possible. I travelled the entire East Coast before the semester started and loved it. And then see if you can adjust your timetable so you can go on extended weekends to places in Australia. I also went on an Easter Holiday, so there are so many opportunities.
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: In a lot of classes, there will be a lot of exchange students, but local students are also in the classes, so it is just a matter of finding them.
cultural_challenges: I do not think I found anything particularly challenging, but it was definitely different from Denmark how outgoing Australians are, even if you are just going grocery shopping.
culture_appreciated: I actually came to really appreciate how outgoing and social Australians are.
top3_advice: 1) Remember to enjoy the social life - you just need to pass your subjects, and the level is lower 2) Enjoy what Melbourne has to offer, as well as Australia 3) It might seem like there are a lot of administrative things you need to do beforehand, but everything works out, and UniMelb is very good at helping.
other_useful_info: Not really
most_rewarding: Getting to experience Australian culture while studying at such a prestigious university. And all the international friends I made, as we are planning on visiting each other next year.
greatest_challenge: Maybe at first, being alone in such a big city, and knowing you know no one. And that you can not just call home if something happens, as the time difference is quite big.

crucial_aspects: Crucial for my choice of exchange was the fact of going somewhere english speaking so that there would not be any type of language barrier. Also, as I have lived in Sydney in my early youth, I have always felt an urge of going back to Australia as a young adult and make use of the unique opportunity of trying to live abroad and immerse myself in new cultures, ways of living and establish a new network here in Melbourne. The overall motivation included the different academic oppurtunies UniMelb offers, also with regards to Film and Media. Here I have had four creative breadth courses that all have given me a better overview and helped me narrow down my overall interests for the field of film and photography. Specifically I had a micro documentary course, a street art course and a screenprinting course that all offered me the possibility of trying out new and prevalent interests in more hands-on and practical approach to learning and studying.
overall_comments: Overall I think the semester was very well structured, however towards the end of the semester everything got a little more intense as I was doing final assignments for all four courses at once which really forced me to prioritise the amount of energy used to finish them all. E.g. the documentary course was of my biggest interest, hence I disposed my time in perfecting those assignments. As I am normally used to only having two courses pr. semester (2x 15 ECTS points), this was a little more of a challenge as I had double the amount of courses whilst also working around 24 hours a week in order to sponsor my whole exchange semester abroad.
info_ease: It was very straight forward, given the fact that the UniMelb website (University of Melbourne) was very easy to navigate and they were good and communicating all the most essential information and steps for completing the enrolment. Also they were good and quickly responding on email to any relevant questions I had to the whole process.
arrival_assistance: Help to order my student id, enrol into subjects and/or change any courses I was unsure about.
arrival_comments: Good orientation but not very personal. Very hectic, too many students. Maybe for the more social aspect of studying, each course I was studying could maybe have had a form of small introduction in order to socialise with other students. I am aware that this is costly, so all in all I think that UniMelb offered a lot of possibilites to meet other exchange students, however I had more of an idea to immerse myself and integrate myself with locals, hence the biggest network I have made from living here was through my work colleagues.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
