registration_process: I think it was pretty straightforward and the website of University of Melbourne really also made it easier. I know of people who have done exchange where it has been a lot more difficult.
registration_help: The messaging and mailing with Melbourne University and also with a contact person from my home institutition. Also zoom meetings and pdf documents sent through to assist the whole process.
registration_success: It was very smooth and my home institution also accepted the course list I sent through to them. However after arriving, within the first week of studies I ended up changing one of my courses as I found out it was planned to be active from end june till end july, which I did not realise before having spoken with a person at "Stop 1", UniMelbs study desk.
registration_advice: Have a good general idea of the courses, what the study load involves and also when the courses are planned out - what day of the week you study and when the first and final lecture is given. I had a course that I found out would run from end june till end july and immediately I wanted to change courses as the semester would only have been longer if i sticked to my initial four courses.
academics_comments: Overall I think the semester was very well structured, however towards the end of the semester everything got a little more intense as I was doing final assignments for all four courses at once which really forced me to prioritise the amount of energy used to finish them all. E.g. the documentary course was of my biggest interest, hence I disposed my time in perfecting those assignments. As I am normally used to only having two courses pr. semester (2x 15 ECTS points), this was a little more of a challenge as I had double the amount of courses whilst also working around 24 hours a week in order to sponsor my whole exchange semester abroad.
course_level: I was content with the level of courses I ended up choosing for my semester at UniMelb. Street Art was a lot more academic than I initially thought, however I really enjoyed the lectures and the classroom discussion. Making Micro Documentaries was a very nice thought, some repetition with one of my previous courses at UCPH but I had anticipated it. Screenprinting was very interesting and I really enjoyed the different techniques we learned over the course of the 6 weeks of the intensive. Electronic Arts: Vision & Sound, was really something else and I kind of missed an overall structure and more clarity in the teaching and weeks of lectures. However, this can always be the case for breadth subjects as they often are not as academic and have a likelyhood of shifting a bit over the course of the semester
teaching_comparison: The teachers were very engaging and there was generally a good balance of interactivity, guest lecturers and also some field trips to cement the teaching and different theories. In my documentary course we unfortunately were taught online through zoom which really removed the personal aspect of teachings and interactions. Throughout the 12 weeks, it was not before the final week where we showed our productions that I got to actually have a feel about the course and who was partaking. I was among one of the only students that dared to "cam on", during the lectures and show myself instead of hiding "behind a computer screen", passively engaging.
courses_enrolled: Street Art (CCDP20001) Making Micro Documentaries (FLTV10024) Introduction to Screenprinting (FINA20045) Electronic Arts: Vision & Sound (CCDP10002)
recommended_courses: Street Art and Making Micro Documentaries I would recommend for future exchange students. If you are interested in subcultures I think that Street Art is a very interesting course to parttake in. Showcasing both local and international art, our teachers were very engaging and investing in doing their teachings. Also as Melbourne is globally known as one of the biggest hubs for Street Art and graffiti, I think this course is very relevant and interesting. Making Micro Documentaries I would also recommend as it was very well structured, the teachings were interesting and the assignments were very well spaced out and also challenged me to try filming and editing a micro documentary myself. I was very happy to have done this course and finally given it a go at doing all production and post-production of a movie myself. For future scenarios I will definitely use this skillset to make more films.
unexpected_costs: Visa was a lot more expensive than what we initially thought when applying and doing research in the autumn of 2023. Back then it cost around 3500,- dkk, however due to new immigration rules we were affected by the price increasing more than 100% where we ended up having to pay 7500,- dkk.
cost_comparison: If you buy yourself a bike you can definitely save a lot of money. I did not expect the infrastructure making it able to bike around the city in a way that could relate to Copenhagen. You can save a lot of money and time by investing in a nice bike for around 120 bucks.
activities_available: Political clubs, tennis/football/gym clubs, mountaineering/bouldering clubs. Also film societies and other niche clubs that also had to do with food and cuisine.
activities_recommended: I did not end of joining any clubs, however in retrospect I would have loved to have joined the Mountaineering club. Primarily as it offered trips out of Melbourne to nature areas where you could explore and also try forces with bouldering together with other likeminded students. I have a friend that did it, and he was very satisfied with it.
weekend_recommendations: Do some trips out the city, the infrastructure is good and it is easy to go explore other areas and also refresh a bit from living the metropolitan life. Melbourne has many good beaches (Sandringham etc) and also good nature areas such as Grampians and the Mornington Peninsula.
culture_adjustment: In my own opinion, being a very sociable and open person I think it was pretty easy. Also given the fact that I found a job as a waiter at nice Bar/restaurant, it really helped me boost my goal of immersing myself in local culture and make friends with locals.
socializing_tips: Be openminded and do not stress about not having enough friends. It is a process of learning to be more in your own company combined with many repetitive conversations about yourself and your background. It is so okay to just have a small friend group of 5-10 people.
cultural_challenges: Did not really find any cultural differences compared to back home in Copenhagen. There is not really any language barrier and the cities are quite similar with regards to the gastronomy, music scene and also the love for the outdoors.
culture_appreciated: Especially the interest for music and gastronomy. Also how open and genuine Australians are. Always welcoming and asking about "how it is going". Some very friendly and polite aspects that I would love to bring back home and spread throughout Copenhagen. They are not judgy and actually put interest in learning about you.
top3_advice: 1. Be well structured and organised with regards to your courses (important dates, weekly schedule, assignments etc) 2. Do not expect uni to be as social as back home, however it really depends on the courses you take and who you are studying with 3. Stay openminded, don't be too judgy and generally take initiative
other_useful_info: Just keep an eye on your email and don't be afraid of writing too many emails.
most_rewarding: Definitely establishing a local network and having a normal looking week as back home with studies and work. Making friends with likeminded locals and also having the time to be more creative in my studies.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was probably making friends at uni in your own classes and subjects. I think because of a general age-gap I did not immerse myself as much as I initially thought. However everyone is in the same position so just be open and take initiative. I was luckily blessed with nice housemates and good friends at work so I did not feel the urge to make friends at uni
other_comments: no

academics_comments: Det har været en oplevelse jeg aldrig ville være foruden, og jeg er overordnet set så glad for, at jeg har gjort det. Jeg synes dog undervisningen har været værre end hjemme på KU, særligt at den er mindre social, hvilket trak lidt ned for mig på den front.
course_level: Jeg synes generelt jeg fik mindre læring og forståelse ud af kurserne, end hjemme. Jeg var meget forvirret over den ikke-eksisterende eller lille mængde læsestof, kombineret med forelæsninger hvor folk nærmest ikke stiller spørgsmål eller interagerer. Undervisning i mine kurser var typisk 1-2 timers forelæsning på den ene dag, og en workshop af 2-4 timer den anden dag (x4 kurser). Men jeg synes ikke rigtig folk snakkede sammen eller brugte hinanden eller underviser særlig meget. Der var lidt forskel på det punkt kurserne imellem. Den manglende arbejden med stoffet synes jeg ikke var godt for den overordnede læring.
teaching_comparison: Man skal lige vide at de på UniMelb (og måske australske universiteter i det hele taget) kører undervisning hvor folk kommer til tiden og går direkte bagefter, og hvor der ikke er indlagt pauser i forelæsninger. Så det er mest at lytte, og ikke så meget interaktion. Der er mange, mindre assignments undervejs, og så tæller en sidste eksamen eller raport måske 50%. De 10-15 mins pauser hvor man er vant til at socialisere derhjemme, eller gruppearbejde hvor man møder og lærer andre at kende, var helt fraværende. Ingen snakkede særligt med hinanden på tværs af mine 4 kurser. Snakkede også med en australsk studerende, som sagde at folk i udpræget grad slet ikke kommer til forelæsninger, fordi alt er optaget. Det kan man jo se som et + eller - efter smag, man skal bare vide at undervisningen slet ikke giver så meget socialt, som jeg i hvert fald er vant til hjemme.
courses_enrolled: Spatial Tools for Ecosystem Management Climate Science for Decision Making Environmental Geoscience Microscopy for Biological Sciences
recommended_courses: Klart Spatial Tools, da det var meget veludført, og jeg føler jeg har konkrete, nye og brugbare færdigheder. Climate Science var helt klart det mest interaktive fag af dem alle, undervisningen i sig selv var fin, men emnet og at man får lov at lære om konkret om Paris aftalen, IPCC rapporter og videnskaben om klimates påvirkning af de planetære hav- og vejrsystemer var fedt, og ikke noget jeg har fået hjemme. Microscopy var noget rod, og Environemntal Geoscience var lavt niveau

cost_comparison: Kaffe og mad er langt billigere i København, og der er rigtig mange gode restauranter, specielt meget lækker asiatisk mad. Gå til den! Offentlig transport var lidt dyrt, men sådan er det jo også i DK

Fok er meget åbne og vil gerne være venner, men man glemmer også hurtigt folk man kun har mødt kort, hvis man ikke får set hinanden noget mere snart efter
cultural_challenges: Ikke meget, det er jo en enormt vestlig kultur, og Melbourne er en progressiv by. Men pas på når du cykler, de er glade for store biler og mindre glade for at etablere brugbare cykelstier

other_comments: Overvej få et kreditkort inden du rejser, hvis du gerne vil leje biler Brug noget tid på at rejse rundt!

arrival_assistance: Free taxi-service from airport to accomodation, orientation week to meet other exchange students.

registration_help: Support was quick and fast over mail.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted
registration_advice: Just start looking at the courses early, and make sure you have the prerequisites.
course_level: I would say the level of courses are similar to KU, but as the course structure was very chaotic it was sometimes hard to know what excactly was the syllabus. Also, no courses used textbooks, but instead the lecturers own notes or just powerpoints, which was often less structured and educational than a normal textbook.
teaching_comparison: Similar lecturers. We also had tutorials (regnetimer), but it was not nearly enough time to finish the work for each week, and often only one TA for the whole class, so they didnt have enough time to help. Courses would have one hour every week or every other week, so often you could only ask one question (if you were lucky).
courses_enrolled: Theoretical Physics 3 Sub-atomic Physics Elements of Quantum Computing Electronic Dance Music Technique
recommended_courses: Theoretical Physics 3 was the best course. A fairly difficult course, but very interesting, good professors. Was the best strucured course, but still not very good as they didnt give an overview of what we where supposed to learn each lecture. Sub-atomic Physics is a horrible course, would not recommend to anyone. There was two professors, which are easily the two worst professors I have ever had. Extremely messy way of teaching, no structure whatsoever, no examples of how to do problems in lectures, no correspondance between lectures and problems in tutorials. Only one turorial every other week, which was not nearly enough. I had too learn all the syllabus by myself. It is some very interesting material, but sad it is taught in such a horrible way. Elements of Quantum Computing was very interesting. It was fairly easy, as there are a mix between physicists, mathematicians, computer scientist and finance students taking it. If you've had quantum mechanics before, the first 4 weeks is basicly recap. Then they start too teach you how the different quantum algorithms work, which I enjoyed a lot. They change professors often, and while some are good, some are pretty bad, but it was easy enough that it's possible to learn it by yourself. EDM Technique was I course I took to try something new. It's okay if you like EDM, but completalyi online so very anti-social. Would take something else if I had the chance.
unexpected_costs: Public transportation is expensive, just buy a cheap bike.
cost_comparison: University accomodation is extremaly expensive you're better off trying to find a sharehouse.
activities_available: Bunch of different clubs too join, they're all fairly cheap and good value for money, would highly recommend joining one. There is a bunch of events for exchange students, especially in the beginning, great to join too meet people. There is a gym on-campus, its very good but quite expensive
activities_recommended: Both the surfing- and boxing-club was very fun. The club for exchange students also hosts a bunch of events I would recomend going to.
weekend_recommendations: Melbourne in general has a ton of events all the time. Keep a look out for concerts, DJs, plays etc. Many nice museums. You can rent a car and take day-trips (or overnight stays) to Philip Island, Torque (surfing), Great Ocean Road, St. Kilda beach (can also do public transport). After exams I spent a bunch of time doing a road trip along the eastcoast, highlights are Cairns (Great Barrier Reef diving is awesome), Brisbane, Byron Bay, Sydney, Kosciuszko National Park. Bring a tent and enjoy;)
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy, very similar to western countries.
socializing_tips: Join clubs and events. Nobody knows anyone in the beginning, so its very easy to make friends!
cultural_challenges: Nothing really. One thing to be aware of is that there is a lot of drugs going around, and you will often be asked if you want something and you will see people openly do drugs at nightclubs etc, which can be uncomfortable.
culture_appreciated: Australians are very chill and laidback people, very friendy and generally love talking to strangers (in contrast to scandinavians). Say hi to people!
top3_advice: Spend your weekends wisely, do day-trips etc Be open and try to meet as many people as possible in the beginning so you figure out who you vibe with. Whatever you do, don't take enroll in sub-atomic physics.
other_useful_info: Dont take sub-atomic physics.
most_rewarding: Meeting new friends from all over the world, and seeing Australia, a very beatiful country.
greatest_challenge: Saying goodbye to those friends. Also, my wallet is not in the best condition, but its worth it.
other_comments: Dont take sub-atomic physics.

crucial_aspects: I've heard that Melbourne was a great city to live in, and I felt that this would be a perfect opportunity to experience a place so far away from home.
info_ease: Very easy. It is stressfull of course, but the university was very helpful in settling in.
arrival_assistance: Melbourne Universitys "Stop 1" is a perfect place to get any assistance you might need. No matter what the problem is, you can go there and they will either directly help you or quickly send you to someone who can.

housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You had to get your student card, attend an orientation day, and otherwise it's all handled before you leave on their website. It can seem a bit stressfull with the formulas, but my feeling is that it matters way less than you might think.
registration_help: Email support, in-person support and a hotline.
registration_success: I got exactly the classes I signed up for.
registration_advice: Don't worry about it!

The physics subjects were definitely difficult, but I didn't feel very prepared for the tests and assignments.
teaching_comparison: Less contact hours in general. For Physics, we had way less tutorials and lectures. Also, in experience there was a kind of performer culture where students didn't feel very comfortable asking questions.
courses_enrolled: I took the subjects: Introduction to Urban Planning - Interesting subject, has a field trip mid semester - can recommend. Subatomic Physics - Interesting subject, bad instruction. Honestly I cannot recommend. Theoretical Physics 3 - Very good instruction and interesting subject, but be prepared as it is very difficult and you might not want that level of academic stress on exchange. Language Society and Culture - Very very nice!! Good and very nice lecturer
recommended_courses: LSC is nice and maybe TP3 if you want a little challenge.
unexpected_costs: I had a very expensive scratch on a rental car :|
cost_comparison: Housing, and groceries are very expensive here. I really encourage you to make a budget, cause the spending can quickly get out of hand.
activities_available: There's free swimming every morning from 9-11, can recommend. They have their own gym also. Theres a bunch of parties directed towards internationals throughout the year, but especially in the beginning of the semester.
activities_recommended: The mountaineering club, otherwise just go on a bunch of trips! Use the weekends wisely.
weekend_recommendations: Victoria has so much beautiful nature and with pretty good train access, you can do a lot of hiking trips pretty cost effective. In the mid-semester break, a lot of people go to Tasmania, which I've heard so many good things about. The national parks around are incredible.
culture_adjustment: Easy enough. It's a former english colony, so it never strays too far from home. It's an incredibly international city, which is very nice. Honestly the academic adjusting was the most difficult.
socializing_tips: Get a share house! Otherwise you can engage in the clubs. It's more difficult to befriend locals but it can definitely be done.
cultural_challenges: Idk, spiders??
culture_appreciated: The people are so incredibly nice and caring!
top3_advice: 1. Save some money :o 2. Get a share house 3. Try to find subjects that you find interesting but don't require too much exam wise.
other_useful_info: Get a bike! It's a pretty bike-friendly city (to international standards), and you can save so much money by getting one. Theres a place called "second-chance bikes" which sells $50 bikes in Collingwood. I can very much recommend that place.
most_rewarding: Travelling with incredible people I never would have met otherwise.
greatest_challenge: Being so far away from home. It's so far away and expensive, that you can't as easily get visits from friends and family, and the time zone makes it difficult to communicate with the people at home.

crucial_aspects: I've always been fascinated by Australia and wished to have a lot of time to explore the country, its culture and history. It was also important for me to speak the language of the people of the country I was going on exchange to, so that integrating and connecting with the locals would be easier.
overall_comments: It was an incredible experience overall. a really good personal challenge and adventure.
info_ease: University of Melbourne felt a bit overwhelming at first, but they have loads of helpfull resources and staff to make it easier.
arrival_assistance: I went to Stop 1, where I was met by some very helpfull and sweet people, who could help me with receiving all the information I needed.
arrival_comments: Due to the size of the university, it did feel a bit overwhelming, and it was important to take the initiative to go to social events and onboarding. The University didn't encourage these things particularly.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It was an incredible experience overall. a really good personal challenge and adventure.
registration_process: It was easy and a smooth process
registration_help: Stop 1 can help you with everything basicly.
registration_success: I got the classes I wanted. You can also make your own schedule, which I would recommend doing as early as possible, as fewer time slots for classes are available later on.
registration_advice: You can make your own schedule, which I would recommend doing as early as possible, as fewer time slots for classes are available later on. I put all my classes on Monday and Tuesday, which was the best decision, cause it allowed me to go on longer trips. You can also watch lectures online, which gives a lot of freedom.
academics_comments: It was an incredible experience overall. a really good personal challenge and adventure.
course_level: The classes were easier than at the University of Copenhagen. Felt kinda like gymnasium classes. Exams were easy to pass, but getting good grades still took work.
teaching_comparison: It was very different from UCPH. The professors made a lot of fun (sometimes a bit strange) activities in the classes. Encouraged a lot of student participation and class discussions. Most of the time, there wasn't a PowerPoint in the class; it was just us and the professor talking. It could seem a bit unstructured and random at times.
courses_enrolled: Introductory Macroeconomics Terrorism: Shifting Paradigms (did not enjoy this one. Would not recommend) Global Intersections: Gender, Class, Race Authoritarian Politics
recommended_courses: Authoritarian politics were really interesting and relevant for current times. Global intersections gave really good perspectives, and the teaching format was very enjoyable.
unexpected_costs: I travelled a lot during my exchange and after, and did some expensive activities (diving, skydiving, Uluru trip, etc.), which I would really recommend, but it was definitely these trips that made the exchange expensive. The living cost in Melbourne was very comparable to living in Copenhagen, if anything, maybe a bit cheaper for food, transportation etc.
cost_comparison: Eating out is way cheaper than in Denmark, so that was really enjoyable. Sushi is cheap and a big part of the culture for some reason. However, alcohol (except for boxed wine) is very expensive.
activities_available: The University of Melbourne is very diverse, which is also shown in the incredible amount of student clubs available. They also have really good athletic clubs and facilities. The pool is free in the morning, and a lot of fitness classes are free as well.
activities_recommended: I joined the wine club, the underwater club (cheap diving!!) and the Arts students club. Would really recommend getting involved, as the classes themselves aren't that social unless you really try hard to make friends there.
weekend_recommendations: Go explore the different neighbourhoods of Melbourne. Drink coffee, go to cafes, little shops and museums. The city is so vibrant and has amazing vibes. I would also recommend taking some trips around the country or planning a longer trip after the semester. I went to Sydney, Cairns (Great Barrier Reef), Uluru, Great Ocean Road, Western Australia and Tasmania. I did most of the trips during the semester, and I regret not spending more time being in Melbourne, so I would recommend doing most of these things after the semester. I also joined a running club, which was a fun way to meet locals who were looking to socialise and make friends. A lot of people also went to New Zealand and Fiji (would recommend!!)
culture_adjustment: It was very easy. Australians are generally very helpfull and outgoing, so it felt very safe and welcoming when I first got to Australia.
socializing_tips: I was surprised by how few exchange students were in my classes. It was mostly just local or international students, but a lot of them had busy lives with work and didn't seem to be looking for friends in the classes. I would recommend taking a lot of initiative and being outgoing, as most people in the classes didn't really socialise. It is also fun to attend events that the clubs organise.
cultural_challenges: I honestly found it easy. Danish and Australian humour are very similar. The most challenging part was how anti-social the classes were. Most classes are 40 minutes once a week, so there is very little time for socialising and making friends. I did manage to make friends in class, but it took a lot of initiative and awkward moments being the only people talking in a classroom of 25.
culture_appreciated: Australians are very chill and laidback people, which was lovely to experience. They also love small talk in public, which felt really nice and comforting when arriving in a country alone.
top3_advice: Take initiative, use the social opportunities the university provides and don't live on campus if you want a local experience, as most of the people living on campus are first-year international students, and I heard it was surprisingly anti-social.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: It was overall the most incredible experience. I think experiencing the nature of Australia, the amazing, vibrant and diverse culture of Melbourne, and the very liberating freedom of being on exchange was extremely rewarding. Showing up alone in a new country, so far away from Denmark and building a life there felt very rewarding, freeing and of course also scary in a good way.
greatest_challenge: The amount of opportunities was a bit overwhelming at times. Deciding where to put my energy and look for friends was probably the most difficult part of the exchange, but it just took some time before it worked out.

crucial_aspects: I valued that there were some interesting subjects which is not available in Denmark - and then I always wanted to visit Australia for culture and exploring purposes
info_ease: It feels so overwhelming, but just check your email and everything will work out.
arrival_assistance: They have something called STOP1 which is students heelping you out in case you have any questions - they are both online and physical and is extremely nice and helpfull

The workload is higher, though, since you have to hand in more assignments throughout the semester instead of just having one final exam. On the other hand, this also means that the exam period itself is very chill.
teaching_comparison: Very similar with lectures and then tutorials (forelæsninger og holdundervisning).
courses_enrolled: 1. Drugs that shape society 2. Health Geography 3. Genetics, Biopower, & History 4. Dancing the Dance
recommended_courses: podcasts and speeches and so on for assignments/exam I really enjoyed all of my subjects, especially Genetics, Biopower, and History. The lecturer was incredibly good and engaging. The course focused on eugenics and on how evolutionary theory has been used to justify racial hierarchies, with a strong historical perspective, including examples such as the feebleminded, Nazi ideology, and similar cases. The lecturer is also not a big fan of traditional exams, but instead encourages creative and critical thinking. So our assignments and exams took the form of things like podcasts and speeches rather than standard sit-in exams.
unexpected_costs: Mmh I think the price of Visa surprised me (around 3000kr)
cost_comparison: I expected prices to be similar to those in Denmark, but they were actually a bit cheaper overall - not by much, but still noticeable. Meat and coffee were surprisingly cheap, while alcohol and vegetables were quite expensive.
activities_available: Everything you can imagine.
activities_recommended: I joined the running club and the wine club - highly recommend.
weekend_recommendations: There are soooo many places to go - the Great Ocean Road, the East Coast, Uluru, Tasmania, Perth/west coast, New Zealand, and so on. You’ll figure it all out once you’re there.
culture_adjustment: Aussies are extremely open, easy to talk to, and very laid-back. Culturally, it’s quite similar to Denmark, so you won’t experience much of a culture shock.
socializing_tips: Just talk to them - they are (in general) very open and happy to engage with you!
cultural_challenges: The people are much less reserved than Danes, which is really lovely when you are far away from home. Another aspect is the Aboriginal population: some communities/many people are still affected by the country’s colonial history, so it is something to approach with respect, but also incredibly interesting to learn about.
culture_appreciated: the laid-back and outgoing people—and the camping culture, which I especially enjoyed. It’s such a nice way to experience the nature and the country.
top3_advice: 1. Be open-minded and adventurous, and you’ll have such a good time. 2. Time flies sooo fast, so enjoy it while you’re there - say yes to as much as possible. 3. Make sure to have some savings. Travelling and experiences will be quite expensive, and it’s much nicer not having to worry about money while you are there.
other_useful_info: The semester starts early, but that also means you finish early, so you have 2 - 3 months afterwards to just travel around before the next semester starts in Denmark.
most_rewarding: I got to experience so much, and it was incredibly rewarding to try living on the other side of the world for half a year. The people I met and everything I experienced made it feel very wholesome, and it’s just an opportunity I think everyone should take while having no obligations at home.
greatest_challenge: I did feel homesick at times, and the 10-hour time difference means you can’t always just call home, which could be quite hard for me at least. But surround yourself with good people, you’ll be just fine.
other_comments: Gooo, you won't regret it!

Efter ankomsten oplevede jeg i høj grad selv at skulle opsøge information og tage initiativ. Undervisningen er i høj grad præget af selvstudie uden studiegrupper, hvilket gjorde studieoplevelsen mere individuel end social. En specifik introduktion til det fakultet, jeg tog fag på, kunne derfor have været givende i forhold til at møde andre studerende og have givet mulighed for at få afklaret de spørgsmål, jeg stod med i starten.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Det var relativt nemt at tilmelde sig kurser via Universitets side. Jeg kunne sagtens gøre det hjemmefra og efter tilmelding til kurserne, kunne jeg selv tilmelde mig de rigtige lektioner for at tilrettelægge mit skema. Der bliver hurtigt fyldt på kurserne, så jeg kom på venteliste til flere, men i sidste ende oplevede jeg at det hele lykkedes.
registration_help: Stop 1 ved University of Melbourne hjælper med alt administrativt i forhold til tilmelding af kurser, hvis der er problemer. Jeg var forbi dem af flere omgange og de var lige hjælpsomme og søde hver gang.
registration_success: Fordi to af mine valgfag overlappede endte jeg med at tage et andet valgfag end jeg først havde tænkt, men det var nemt at skifte rundt med hjælp fra Stop 1. Pga prerequisites havde jeg udfordringer med selv at tilmelde mig Introductory Macroeconomics. Der var det nemt at skrive til kursusprofessoren og få en skriftlig accept af, at jeg kunne tage faget. Han svarede hurtigt og var hjælpsom.
registration_advice: Hvis der er den mindst tvivl så gå forbi Stop 1 og tal med dem ansigt til ansigt. De er virkelig hjælpsomme og kan svare på de fleste adminstrative spørgsmål.
course_level: Jeg oplevede et svingende niveau. Det kan sammenlignes med niveauet på KU.
teaching_comparison: Min oplevelse af undervisningen kan i høj grad sammenlignes med den jeg oplevede i Gymnasiet i DK. Holdundervisningen foregik i mindre hold. Nogen gange var vi kun 5-10. Der var en generel forventning om, at alle bidrog aktivt til undervisningen. Ofte oplevede jeg, at den akademiske samtale var mindre målrettet end på KU. Diskussionerne havde i højere grad karakter af overordnede samfundsbetragtninger frem for den mere tekstnære og teoritunge tilgang, som jeg kender fra Statskundskab på KU. Samtidig var der lang flere assessments i løbet af semesteret end jeg har været vandt til på KU. Det afhænger i høj grad af de specifikke kurser.
courses_enrolled: Introductory Macroeconomics (ECON10003) Authoritarian Politics (POLS20033) Living in a Risk Society (SOCI30009) Terrorism: Shifting Paradigms (CRIM30015)
recommended_courses: Living in a Risk Society. Det var velstruktureret og interessant at lære om risikosamfundet fra et australsk perspektiv.
unexpected_costs: I forsikringen indgår en obligatorisk sygeforsikring som påkræves af Universitetet/Australien. Det var ca 2500 kr i alt.
cost_comparison: Visa.
activities_available: Alt man kan forestille sig lige fra dykkerklub til surf til atletik. Om formiddagen kan man gratisk gøre brug af deres svømmehal, man kan melde sig ind i deres fitnesscenter relativt billigt og gøre brug af både batminton og tennisbaner. Der er også flere gratis holdtimer såsom dans og hit, som man kan finde gennem deres sportsafdeling. I introugen kan man få en guidet tur rundt i deres sportsfaciliteter, som jeg vil anbefale.
activities_recommended: Tag på de surfture, der arrangeres af surfklubben på uni. Dér kan man møde mange søde og engagerede mennesker i et socialt studiemiljø, der minder lidt om det jeg kender fra KU.
weekend_recommendations: Rejs rejs rejs. Både i og omkring Melbourne, men også til andre steder i Australien. Man kan sagtens nå en uge eller to henover semesterbreaket og weekenderne er der også rig mulighed for at opleve. Sæt også massere tid af til at nyde Melbourne! Det er en virkelig dejlig by med dejlige parker, hyggelige kaffe- og vinbarer og god stemning. Jeg kan kun anbefale!!
culture_adjustment: Det var lidt svært at komme i kontakt med lokalbefolkningen eftersom der er et rigtig stor international tilstrømning til Univeristy of Melbourne. Dét sagt så synes jeg, at alle er enormt imødekommende og man skal ikke tøve med at spørge nogen om hjælp eller vejledning. De fleste vil gerne hjælpe og endda drikke en kop kaffe.
socializing_tips: Jeg meldte mig ind i et lokalt fitnesscenter, hvor jeg ind i mellem faldt i snak med lokale. Der er også massere af løbeklubber, hvor folk mødes med formålet at møde nye mennesker.
cultural_challenges: I dele af undervisningen oplevede jeg en betydelig sproglig barriere. En relativt stor andel af de internationale studerende havde begrænsede engelskkundskaber, hvilket til tider vanskeliggjorde den faglige dialog og samarbejdet i undervisningen.
culture_appreciated: Den australske åbenhed.
top3_advice: Alt bøvl med forhåndsgodkendelser skal nok ordne sig. Glæd dig.
other_useful_info: Der er velkomstfester for alle udvekslingsstuderende i Melbourne, som arrangeres af private aktører i Melbourne. Det er et godt sted at møde andre udvekslingsstuderende, men jeg tror jeg ville tilmelde mig én klub på uni og forsøge at tage til nogen af deres arrangementer for at møde lokale, der også læser på Uni Melb.
most_rewarding: At studere i Melbourne, rejse og møde nye mennesker.
greatest_challenge: At strukturere sin tid i eksamensperioden. Min eksamensperiode var presset på fem dage, hvilket gjorde den meget intens. Jeg tror, jeg har været uheldig og andre har haft det anerledes.

crucial_aspects: I was very interested in living in a different European culture and I've always wanted to live in Italy, which made me choose Milano.
info_ease: I found most information on my own and everything worked out fine, but I didn't find i
arrival_assistance: I didn't really receive a proper introduction, because it was cancelled due to Covid. This of course made my start a bit more confusing, stressful and hectic. Very basic stuff like finding the different campuses, classrooms, toilets etc., was difficult, and I would have been nice with a bit more information on simply getting around and being a student at Unimi. But I reached out to the Erasmus coordinator per mail whenever I had issues or questions and usually got a quick reply. In general I received all necessary information right on time, but it meant a lot of communication per mail.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I found my classes online and received an email with instructions on how to enroll a few days before the lectures started. This seemed a bit late to me, but it didn't seem important to enroll early. You write your classes in a sort of document and it was quite easy to do and to change afterwards.
registration_help: The Erasmus coordinator could help and my teachers were in general very helpful too.
registration_success: I had a bit of difficulty with choosing classes because I looked at a lot of trimester course (which are early winter/late spring), but I didn't know that from home. In the end it worked out but I had one overlap, where I just skipped lectures every second week.
registration_advice: Go to a lot of different lectures the first week before you make your final decision.
course_level: I took four course and I learned a lot from the two of them. In general the expectations seemed a lot lower than what I'm used to, which had a negative effect on the outcome of the course.
teaching_comparison: I had teachers who were very similar to what I'm familiar with: a lot of discussions and open questions. But I'm not sure if this is the general way of teaching in Italy.
courses_enrolled: English Literature British Theater Representation and Image theories The Western Tradition: Moral and Political Values
recommended_courses: 'Representation and Image theories' and 'The Western Tradition: Moral and Political Values' were taught by great teachers.
unexpected_costs: I ran out of free data because I was abroad for a long period, which I didn't expect since I was in the EU. And Milano is in general quite expensive when you go out (often you pay an entrance when going to a club), but of course you can find cheaper place to eat/drink/buy groceries.
cost_comparison: Coffee was really cheap and some bars.
activities_available: You could sign up for sports through the university or join different activities through the volunteering Erasmus group (they also arranged a welcome day).
activities_recommended: I would recommend joining a sports team through the university since it makes it easier to meet some Italien students in a different setting.
weekend_recommendations: I really recommend visiting Lake Como and hiking to some the refugios in the surrounding mountans. I joined the facebook group International Hiking Milano who arranges different trips almost every weekend. Milano has a lof of museums (PAC, Mudec, Fondazione Prada, Pirelli Hangar), that I would recommend going to - and many private collections and houses like Villa Necchi which are worth a visit.
culture_adjustment: I found most Italians friendly and talkative, but sometimes they could seem a bit cold (mostly in stores/bars). But I think it was easy - especially because the social life in Milano is very vibrant and happens in the city and outdoors. I did find it a bit difficult getting used to the school system and the way information was delievered.
socializing_tips: Join a sport activity and just talk to people in your class. In my experience my Italian classmates were very interested in meeting new people and were often good at suggesting we'd go out for a coffee or an aperitivo after classes. There are cheap bars everywhere, so it's not a big deal to set up.
cultural_challenges: Nothing
culture_appreciated: The social life in the city and all the little bars where you can buy cheap coffee and practice Italian at the counter.
top3_advice: Try to learn some basic Italian beforehand and practice in all the little bars. Most people speak English but are happy to talk Italian with you. Go hiking on the weekends and take the train to other cities. Make sure to visit the different areas in Milano (Isola, Porta Venezia, Porta Romana, Loreto etc.) and not just the city centre.
other_useful_info: Milano can be very cold and rainy during winter so bring an umbrella and winterjacket, if you're going in the spring semester.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people, being in nature and living in a very different culture and city.
greatest_challenge: The first few weeks were though because the university didn't plan any real introduction and was quite late on giving information on classes.

crucial_aspects: That is was another culture with a wide option of subjects.
overall_comments: Italy is a beautiful country, and the ESN was really good at making us feel at home! However the University lacked organising skills. The classrooms assigned were too small, it took them too long to give the class another room, some of the teachers did not follow the exam dates (chose other dates) etc. At one campus sight where we spend an entire day every week, there were not wi-fi and no heat.
info_ease: It was hard. The University really did have anything figured out before we started. There were much more classes than stated on the website. They kind of took it as it came, which was difficult for an Erasmus student to do.
arrival_assistance: The ESN helped with the social aspects. When it came to the class, we just had to figure it out on our own and help each other.
arrival_comments: The social aspect was amazing, but not the University itself.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Italy is a beautiful country, and the ESN was really good at making us feel at home! However the University lacked organising skills. The classrooms assigned were too small, it took them too long to give the class another room, some of the teachers did not follow the exam dates (chose other dates) etc. At one campus sight where we spend an entire day every week, there were not wi-fi and no heat.
registration_process: I did not really register. We just sent our Erasmus application through the platform and then an email with our name, number, address etc. and then we were giving a university card and an access to the mail and uni platform.
registration_help: Help through mail. But not a lot.
registration_success: Succesful but the process was a little forced because it only was possible to register a few days before start.
registration_advice: Do not panic when you cannot register in good time. They just do everything last minute.
academics_comments: Italy is a beautiful country, and the ESN was really good at making us feel at home! However the University lacked organising skills. The classrooms assigned were too small, it took them too long to give the class another room, some of the teachers did not follow the exam dates (chose other dates) etc. At one campus sight where we spend an entire day every week, there were not wi-fi and no heat.
course_level: It was all MA sources, but the level felt BA comparing to my home university.
teaching_comparison: There were no books everything was online which was nice. There was not as much group work as there is in UCPH which I thought was nice. Otherwise pretty much the same.
courses_enrolled: European Labour Law, Sustainable Transport, Comparative Contract Law, An Introduction to Italian Private Law in a comparative perspective, Law and Philosophy in a cross-cultural perspective
recommended_courses: Sustainable Transport was an amazing course. The teacher was really nice and his English was good. The exam was two papers through the semester which was a nice way of doing an exam. It was intersting and like nothing I learned at home. The other courses was nice as well, except European Labour Law. The workload was way to much, the teacher was not always that nice, had no structure and kept getting off topic.
unexpected_costs: Some extra things to the apartment. Otherwise I had budget for the rest.
cost_comparison: Food in the supermarked was either way less or more. Meat is more expensive the rest is cheaper. Going out to eat can be really cheap also drinks. Night clubs are really expensive. Public transportation is cheap also getting an italian number so you have free acces to data was cheap. Traviling by train/bus to other cities is also cheap.
activities_available: ESN help you meet other people - but it is outside the University
activities_recommended: ESN help you meet other people and do something - but it is outside the University
weekend_recommendations: Travel to other cities. The bus/train tickets can be cheap so it is a good possibility.
culture_adjustment: Easy with the people and culture in that way, but I did not adjust to how the University and teachers did not plan ahead. It was often a big chaos.
socializing_tips: Go to ESN activities - in that way I socialized with a lot of people. Everyone is really nice, so do not be afraid to ask people to hang out. 10/10 they say yes. If you are more people from the same country then try to talk to some people from other countries.
cultural_challenges: That Italians do not plan, think ahead or inform. That is very frustrating. Like one week before your exam, you don't know how the exam will be or your landlord removing the washer while you are away without informing of this.
culture_appreciated: That people are out a lot. Restaurants, bars and streets are always filled and there is a nice atmosphere because of this. I felt very safe in Milan even if it is a big city
top3_advice: 1. Search for a place to live in a good time. 2. Try not to panic when they don't inform you about anything. Ask and wait. They just do it in another paste. 3. Enjoy it! The time goes by so fast. Even though it is school the academic level is not as high so you will have more free time to enjoy your time in Italy.
other_useful_info: Get an Italian phone number. It is like 75kr a month and then you have free access to the data. Travel to other cities. You will not regret it. Involve yourself in the ESN. I did go to a lot of events in the beginning and found a lot of friends this way.
most_rewarding: Living in another country and figuring out things on my own, getting to know a lot of really nice people and seeing many parts of Italy.
greatest_challenge: Missing home and trying to figure out what to do, when the Italians did not provide the information as needed.
other_comments: Some people speak English but others not a lot. Knowing a bit of Italian helped me. I used Duolingo. There is also an Italian Course. I did not attend but heard from others that it was not that helpfull.

crucial_aspects: I chose my destination primarily because I speak some Italian and wanted to improve my language skills. Also I have spent longer periods of time in Italy before and wanted to go back and try to live there properly and experience every-day life there. Furthermore the University of Milan had a virology course that I really wanted to follow, which I unfortunately was not able to follow in the end.
overall_comments: I had an amazing time, and I think it was an incredible and important experience to have. I enjoyed living abroad, trying something different from what I am used to, adapting to situations that turn out different than what you expect - and of course meeting so many amazing people and exploring a wonderful culture along the way.
info_ease: Not always super easy, but when you emailed them with questions they replied very fast and was always very helpful.
arrival_assistance: I had a lot of email correspondance with different people about which couses I could follow etc. It was confusing to figure out, but they are very helpful and in the end it all worked out. They are all very available with help and answers, both in the administration and the professors.
arrival_comments: I would have liked more comprehensive information with more time before the arrival, instead of having to wait until the last minute. And it would have been nice to have more information automatically instead of having to ask for it.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had an amazing time, and I think it was an incredible and important experience to have. I enjoyed living abroad, trying something different from what I am used to, adapting to situations that turn out different than what you expect - and of course meeting so many amazing people and exploring a wonderful culture along the way.
registration_process: When you log in to your university page, there is a module where you can fill out the courses you would like to register for. Then later you get a confirmation if you ask for it. You chance your course registrations several weeks after the semester has started so you can try out different things, or change your mind if you need to.
registration_help: There was a guide document on how to register, and also the erasmus coordinator was available through email.
registration_success: Some of the classes I wanted had a lot of overlapping hours, so I was restricted in choosing certain things, but ultimately I ended up with courses I had had preapproved from home and nothing I didn't find interesting.
registration_advice: Find more courses than what you are required to take, because some of them might not be possible to follow. And if they recommend you to do something, just be insistant that you don't want to do that, and they will probably allow you to do it your way. Also, some courses are taught in italian but has english course material and will allow you to do the exam in english if you ask the professor.
academics_comments: I had an amazing time, and I think it was an incredible and important experience to have. I enjoyed living abroad, trying something different from what I am used to, adapting to situations that turn out different than what you expect - and of course meeting so many amazing people and exploring a wonderful culture along the way.
course_level: I took MA level courses to have courses taught in english instead of italian. Even though I was a BA student it was easy enough to follow the material, it was not very complicated but in some cases the curriculum was quite large.
teaching_comparison: I only had lectures, no seminars or class activities (apart from some laboratory work), and no reading material either. I mainly learn by doing, so it was very difficult for me to have no assignments or focused teaching. The material was very interesting but I missed the more involved teaching style of Copenhagen University.
courses_enrolled: Communicable and non-communicable diseases (8 ECTS) Pathogenetic basis of disease (12 ECTS) Applied Pharmacology to biotechnology (7 ECTS) Italian language course (3 ECTS)
recommended_courses: I particularly enjoyed communicable and non-communicable diseases. The communicable part had very interesting topics and competent professors.
unexpected_costs: My personal spending was quite high, but that was something that was pretty purposeful, I was there to have a good time. And this also includes a ski trip and several trips around the country.
cost_comparison: Transportation and supermarkets are very cheap, also alcohol. Restaurants were quite expensive compared to other expenses, and rent was generally very steep.
activities_available: There is a volunteer driven organisation called ESN Erasmus Student Network that organizze several activities every week, especially in the beginning. This includes city tours, italian language cafe, picnic in the park, karaoke night, volleyball, outdoor fitness, wine dinners etc. There are so many things, and I recomend going to it all - it is a great way to meet new friends and explore the city. And a great way to get reccomendations from the volunteers who are all working or studying in Milan themselves.
activities_recommended: Ski trip! It's called Erasmus Snow Week, it is super cheap and so much fun. Lots of international and italian students for the opening of the season. We went to the Dolomites for 4 days of skiing and it was so great. Also all the ESN events, so much fun and a great way to connect with people.
weekend_recommendations: Milan is exceptionally well connected to the rest of the country, so I reccomend going on trips as much as you can to different cities. There are trains to basically everywhere, all of the time. We went to the Como lake, Bergamo, Venice, Cinque Terre in Liguria, Rome and Sicily (Palermo) among others for extended weekend trips, or day trips. So easy and relatively cheap and easy, and can be planned spontaneously.
culture_adjustment: Certain things can be frustrating with the ways they do things there, but it always works out in the end - so it is a good lesson to learn, and quite in the italian spirit: just relax, everything will work out fine in the end, don't be too bothered, and take it one step at a time.
socializing_tips: Go to the ESN events and get to know the volunteers, or ask your italian classmates for help to start up the conversation. Or live in a dorm or a shared apartment with local students.
cultural_challenges: There can be a bit of a language barrier sometimes, but they always do their best to understand you, and if you do the same it will be fine. And also, the university is a lot less structured than what I was used to which can be frustrating, but again, write them an email and it will all work out just fine.
culture_appreciated: I think Italian people are generally very open and hospitable, and eager to help if you ask. Also they have wonderful food, and a beautiful country. I had an absolute pleasure staying there for a longer time, and if you have a little hedonist hidden inside you, this is the place for you.
top3_advice: 1. Don't worry if you can't find the info or haven't heard anything. Just write them an email. 2. Go see the country! Hop on a train and you can get basically anywhere in no time. 3. Go on the ski trip! Also if you are no good at skiing. Will be worth it!
other_useful_info: Speaking Italian is definitely not necessary, but learning a few words and phrases can be useful in certain situations - and they are very eager to teach you something if you ask as well!
most_rewarding: Meeting lots of wonderful friends from all over Europe, and learning to adapt to unexpected situations.
greatest_challenge: All the paperwork and emails and registrations and such takes a toll on you but are all worth it. When you are finally there you can just enjoy it.

crucial_aspects: My host country specializes in my particular field and I wanted to explore new academic opportunities.
info_ease: I thought it was quite difficult and I felt left alone by the host university.
arrival_assistance: I didn't receive a lot of assistance. I think due to the fact that my courses were all in Italian, so they aren't used to having Erasmus students, this complicated my first semester and I was very confused about a lot of things.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It's a very liberal registration proces. You can change your registrations throughout the whole semester.
registration_help: I got helped by other Erasmus students in a big WhatsApp group.
registration_success: In the end it worked out.
registration_advice: Don't do it last minute. It is a difficult system, but you'll get it eventually.
course_level: Difficult to say because the teaching styles are so different.
teaching_comparison: My host institution taught in a completely different manner. All my exams were oral and based highly on memorialization, learning by heart. It seems old fashioned and completely different from the analytical style I'm used to at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Storia Romana Letteratura Latina Storia della Filosofia Antica
recommended_courses: Archeologia e Storia dell'Arte Greca was a good course, a good introduction to archeology for someone coming with no knowledge at all. But also this was an exam of learning by heart.
unexpected_costs: I was surprised by the housing prices. Also I got my phone stolen during my stay, there are many pickpockets in Milan, be aware.
cost_comparison: Public transportation is cheaper than in DK. Food and drinks are cheaper than in DK. Housing is expensive, at the level of Copenhagen.
activities_available: There were many activities organized by ESN, both sports, cultural and just hanging out-events.
activities_recommended: I would recommend to go to those that interest you, it's a great way to meet new people.
weekend_recommendations: Go for trips around Italy!
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy. It's a bit more chaotic and the bureaucracy can be a struggle.
cultural_challenges: Bureaucracy, in general and in the pace it works.
culture_appreciated: Food, architecture, the style of going out and using the city.
top3_advice: 1 Be patient with the systems 2 Ask for help even if they tell you there is none to get 3 Adjust early on to the different teaching style, it helps towards the exams
other_useful_info: Don't be too hard on yourself if you don't have the energy to go meet new people all the time. Do it in your own pace.
most_rewarding: Learning the language Meeting really good friends
greatest_challenge: Learning the language, following the courses in Italian. In the beginning it was difficult being alone in a new country. I wish I could've been better at telling myself that it was gonna be alright. That it takes time to build a life in a new country.

crucial_aspects: The courses available, the culture of the country and what the University could offer me in terms of my career path
overall_comments: It was an amazing experience and I can highly recommend going on exchange!
info_ease: Even though the experience was unforgettable, the application process was really difficult. The lack of information and late response rate was highly critical, so this is indeed negative aspects you have to deal with during the exchange-experience.
arrival_assistance: I received assistance from my host university, and other students. My experience was that my main students were actually the ones helping me the most, since the system is not working well for the student itself, unfortunately.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It was an amazing experience and I can highly recommend going on exchange!
registration_process: Very flexible. I could sign all the courses I wanted to, and there were no sudden restrictions. However, it is more difficult on your BA to find rights courses fitting your program. But my host university was not an obstacle in this matter,
registration_help: Help from Professors and other students, also a mobility responsible person.
registration_success: In the end successful, but it took some time to get courses approved by my Home University.
registration_advice: Remember that it is very common to figure out your courses while on exchange and not before. Do not stress about this, it is much more common than you think. And also, be prepared to change courses in last minute.
academics_comments: It was an amazing experience and I can highly recommend going on exchange!
course_level: I had courses on the MA-degree, even though I was at the BA, because I found the courses more interesting. This worked for me; I liked the higher level of the courses, and I would say the Italian academic level is different than the one in Copenhagen, but very funny to explore!
teaching_comparison: Very difficult. Not as much reading as in Copenhagen, but on the other hand you were much more dependent on yourself and your own reading and knowledge.
courses_enrolled: Comparative Legal Traditions Journalism, Media and Politics Comparative Politics and Development History of Regional Integrations
recommended_courses: I can highly recommend courses with the Professor Antonia Baraggia. She is excellent and also a coordinator of the Erasmus-students, and a lot of her courses are directed towards Erasmus-students. Professor Piero Graglia is also very friendly and his course (History of Regional Integrations) was fun to be a part of.
unexpected_costs: I do not know.
cost_comparison: Books less expensive since a lot of them were online.
activities_available: A lot. Tennis, soccer, volleyball etc.
activities_recommended: Day-trips out of the city and nights out.
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips out of the city or hang around on your coffee house.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Italians are so warm and welcoming.
socializing_tips: Just be open and friendly. They are usually all very curious and friendly.
cultural_challenges: Not much.
culture_appreciated: The Italian coffee, the Italian vibe and the no strict deadlines at Uni. Of course you had deadlines, but they were not as time strict as in Denmark.
top3_advice: There are plenty of courses and it can be difficult to navigate in the catalogue. Be aware of scam posts when you search for housing on your own Have fun!
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: The personal and academic development.
greatest_challenge: Adapting to a new academic culture and way of studying.
other_comments: No.

crucial_aspects: I have lived in Italy before, but that was for work, so I wanted to go back and experience the country in an academic setting, by attending university and experience what that would be like. It was important to me that I could choose courses that were still relevant to my direction of studies (Asian Studies) in Copenhagen, to make my electives work in line with other courses I have taken in Denmark and Japan.
overall_comments: Overall I have been very pleased with the study abroad experience.
info_ease: It was very easy. Websites both of University of Copenhagen and University of Milan were easy to use regarding finding information, and the International Office/Study Abroad offices both places were very good at supporting me every step with providing the guidance and information that I needed.
arrival_assistance: There wasn't much, but this was due to Covid. However, the support online from the International Office was always there, the student cards could be picked up in an easy way, and the screens at the university and the website guided me to find classrooms, updated timetables etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Overall I have been very pleased with the study abroad experience.
registration_process: Registration was partly through Mobility Online with upload of various documents. Upon arrival I confirmed the courses I wanted to follow, and was quickly able to access the courses' different forums on Ariel, to search for readings etc. After a while, I received my student card with my Erasmus Student number.
registration_help: Through email and online, help was provided quickly and efficiently. Staff at the university campus itself was also very helpful in case I had additional doubts or questions.
registration_success: Very succesful. After the first two classes I had followed, I had two ones, where one of them I confirmed and continued with, and the other I wanted to change and replace with another. Also this process was very easy, and the host university helped me with information on how to attend the new class, so I could search for an updated pre-approval at my home university.
registration_advice: No other advice other than it is very easy and accessible. If in doubt, my experience was, that writing an email will clarify any question about the process.
academics_comments: Overall I have been very pleased with the study abroad experience.
course_level: The courses I took were mainly for MA students, but I didn't experience problems with following the courses. Some of them required a bit of basis pre-knowledge, but fortunately I had had similar contents during other courses in either Denmark or Japan.
teaching_comparison: The style is similar. I think it was a nice combination of academic but creative writing, and more standard memorizing the teaching sort of style.
courses_enrolled: I followed four courses during the semester, two in one trimester and two in another one. First I had International Relations and Language in Politics, secondly I followed Global Geopolitics and International Relations of East Asia.
recommended_courses: I think it very much depends on the person's own personal interest. I liked all of the above mentioned courses, because they involve my interest in politics, language and rhetoric, international relations and global affairs etc.
unexpected_costs: The rent was higher than what I expected to pay when I first thought of going on exchange. I also had a security deposit and service fee to pay when I moved in. I had quite a big problem with money because of my high rent, but was unable to find something else to live in, and so I had to spent some of my own, and borrow some additional money.
cost_comparison: Rent was more expensive, transportation was less expensive, the travel card I had was just 300 a month for the metro, tram and busses all over Milan. Books and readings could be found online mostly.
activities_available: There were many social and cultural activities and trips arranged for students, really a wide variety of options.
activities_recommended: Going to some of the social events organised for the Erasmus by students of the host university or other exchange students, they really aim to create a social climate, and organising trips for the students to see more of Italy, and meet new people while on exchange.
weekend_recommendations: Definitely go to see some of the near by places such as Lake Como, it's beautiful, and I was there several times. With perhaps some more time on weekends I would recommend going to other big cities such as Rome or Venice.
culture_adjustment: To me it was very easy. I have lived in Italy before and know the culture and the language, but it was also nice to experience the regional differences there are in Italy. I just to live south of Rome, which was partly why I also wanted to go to Milan, to experience a different part of Italy in a new setting.
socializing_tips: Go to the Erasmus meetings or events, I didn't attend many actually, but just attending a few made me meet people and speak to people in the local environment. Also in class it can be a good idea to say hi to the local students or maybe sometimes ask them a question you have for something regarding a course or something, instead of always writing an email to a professor or the office, in that way you help each other and start talking with the other students.
cultural_challenges: Not really many, I think Italy is a wonderful and in many ways easy accessible culture. Of course the language can be difficult when you don't know some basics, so learning some of the local language is always a good idea. The Erasmus program offered language courses based on a language placement test, which was also nice to have the possibility to attend.
culture_appreciated: Every part really. The food, the language, the beauty of the culture. The social factor, it was easy to speak to people, as has also been my previous experience in Italy.
top3_advice: Enjoy the city and also get outside the city to see some of the beautiful places around Milan. Learn some Italian, even if just 'ciao', it is a very nice way to engage with your local community also, and makes you feel more at home. Ask for help, send an email to the International Office or ask other students if you are in doubt of something. Or say hi to someone and ask what courses they attend or something. It's always nice to feel like a part of something, and usually this is how conversations, encounters and friendships start.
other_useful_info: None other than keep yourself updated on the email of both your host and home university, to make sure you know what the next step of the exchange is and so on.
most_rewarding: To be in Italy in a study setting and to see more of the country. It became of course very warm in the late spring and summer months, which can be hard to concentrate in, but I actually think it worked out well as it is a very nice place to attend university in general, and I was very pleased with the experience.
greatest_challenge: The rent. I would definitely recommend everyone to find a place where it is not too expensive if possible, apply for student housing in time, so that there is some more financial freedom to do stuff and not worry too much about economics every month.
other_comments: Go on exchange. I have done it in both Japan and Italy now, and I have loved both. It can be a challenge, but an absolutely amazing opportunity to see new places and meet new people, and I have never regretted for a minute that I decided to travel and study abroad.

crucial_aspects: language, culture, academic level, distance, weather
info_ease: not that easy, i didn't have my schedule the before i had to start..
arrival_assistance: i got a student assigend to me who could anwer me a few questions which was nice. He was not from my derpartment though..
housing_how: I found housing on my own

cultural_challenges: language
culture_appreciated: spontanity
top3_advice: Look at housing in good time (maybe choose studentsdorm), don't get so scared about university registrations etc., everything works slower but mostly works out in the end and say yes to all opportunies for meeting people or visiting new places.
other_useful_info: no

crucial_aspects: I was looking for a place where i would feel comfortable, not too different from home but still a change of scenery. Furthermore i wanted to develop my language skills so i was looking for a place where i already knew the basics at least.
overall_comments: I can only recommend to go, it was an incredible experience!!!
info_ease: It was ok. In the beginning i was a bit confused since i had some last minute problems with my registration and courses..But i think that overall it was ok, i received some emails upon arrival with the information that i needed to start at the uni.
arrival_assistance: You could write to the mobility office at the university. It seemed like there was only one guy dealing with all the problems, which meant it took a while, but he was very helpfull.
arrival_comments: Great but slow
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I can only recommend to go, it was an incredible experience!!!
registration_process: It was very simple, you just had to choose the courses that you wanted on the unimia page. They sent instructions on how.
registration_help: once again i think you could write the mobility office, but it wasn't necessary since it was very simple.
registration_success: I got all the classes that i wanted without any problems.
registration_advice: You can change your courses even after they begin, this makes it possible to try them out and see what you like. And you have to register for exams yourself, this was probably the hardest. not because it was complicated, but because the registration is only open for a few weeks.
academics_comments: I can only recommend to go, it was an incredible experience!!!
course_level: I took masters classes at the university even though i am a bachelor student. In 3/5 of the courses the level was lower than what i am used to at KU.
teaching_comparison: The lectures were more interactive. The exams were without any type of help (no books, notes or anything)
courses_enrolled: ADVANCED INDUSTRIAL ORGANIZATION (6) FINTECH INDUSTRY (6) DECISION THEORY AND BEHAVIOURAL ECONOMICS (6) PORTFOLIO OPTIMIZATION (6) GLOBAL FIRMS AND MARKETS (6) I also took the italian course that they have, this gives 3 credits if its on level A2 or above.
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed the decision theory and behavioural economics course, since it combined some thing i knew fro economics with some psychology. I also liked the fintech course, the professor was not my favourite, but the topic was really interesting.
unexpected_costs: I didn't think that i needed to get a sim-card but luckily it wasn't too expensive.
cost_comparison: Food was actually more expensive than i thought it would be. The sim-card was less expensive than i thought. And housing was more expensive than i thought.
activities_available: You could join a lot of stuff. The people from ESN arranged all sorts of things! anything from volleyball to escape rooms and wine nights. There was even a ski trip that you could go on. The possibilities were endless.
activities_recommended: I went to the intro night which was a bit overwhelming, but a nice way to get an introduction to the ESN. I also recommend going to the karaoke night. It was a lot of fun!
weekend_recommendations: I went to a lot of the cities around Milan while i was there. Milan is really well connected so this was a great opportunity to explore. I went to Monza, Bergamo, Bologna, Venice and Como. I also went on a one day ski trip with some friends in Valmalenco. There are a lot of beautiful museums in Milan too. Otherwise i recommend going to the markets that are all around town, here you can buy anything from clothes to vegetables and practise your italian ;-) And of course have aperitivo and go out with your friends, the nightlife in Milan is good!
culture_adjustment: I think it was easy since i have been in italy many times before, so nothing was completely new to me.
socializing_tips: People are so nice and open! I found that they always invite you to join them for whatever they are doing and that they are really good at including the erasmus students in the things that are happening outside of class as well. I met some italians at the hostel where i stayed in the beginning and then in class at uni and they are honestly amazing. I worked in a group with them in school so it came pretty naturally, but im sure if you just introduce yourself they will be happy to talk to you!
cultural_challenges: They are late for everything (at least my friends..)
culture_appreciated: The going out! You go out to have a coffee, you go out to study, you go out to have aperitivo, you go out to enjoy the sun, to have a gelato, to eat dinner, the list goes on... And then the openness, i really want to adopt their thing of inviting people everywhere i think it's so nice!
top3_advice: They don't turn on the heating until 15. of October so it gets a bit cold there for a few weeks. Bring sunscreen it's sunny 4/5 days. Enjoy it while you can, it flys by!!!
other_useful_info: The classes at the economics department is in trimesters. This meant that i had to do a semesters worth of classes in just a trimester. However you can do the exams many times, so i just chose to do half in december when my classes ended and the other half in January were i had more time.
most_rewarding: Meeting the best people, improving my italian and getting to know another city so well!
greatest_challenge: It was difficult being away from my family but luckily we have facetime!! I think the exam periods were the greatest challenge. You go from having so much fun everyday to just sitting in your room and reading day in and day out and being stressed by the exams, not so fun...

crucial_aspects: The city, the University and the culture of the people. In Italy I felt that all these aspects where fulfilled in regards to what I was looking for in my exchange.
info_ease: I thought it was quite easy. University of Copenhagen and University of Milan was good at communicating and gave good response.
arrival_assistance: The administration at University of Milan was very helpful. They responded quickly and gave me the necessary information when needed.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: At University of Milan you can change courses during the semester and actually up to two weeks before the exam. Because it is so different from University of Copenhagen I was very confused about it in the beginning, because I did not understand why the University did not inform anything about registration for courses until 1 week before semester start.
registration_help: The Administration at the University was very helpful and responded quickly.
registration_success: I changed many of my courses during the semester, so my first choices were actually not that successful. So in that aspect it was nice that you could change the courses during the semester if you e.g. was not happy about the course or the professor.
registration_advice: Do not stress about before you are there! You will figure it out as soon as the semester begins.
course_level: The level of the courses was very easy. There was no mandatory reading and they only demanded presence, but many of the professor's did not take attendance anyway. So I would not recommend that you go there for the academic experience, because it is quite different and easy compared to University of Copenhagen - both the level of the courses and the final exams.
teaching_comparison: It was very different. The professors chose themselves the material of the courses and how the exams should be.
courses_enrolled: European Company Law, European Labour Law, Introduction to Italian Private Law in a comparative perspective, Constitutional Challenges in the EU, Comparative Contract Law, Fundamental Rights in the EU
recommended_courses: I would recommend Comparative Contract Law, European Company Law and European Labour Law
unexpected_costs: I did not experience any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: The monthly rent costs.
activities_available: It was possible to go on a ski trip.
activities_recommended: The ski trips!!!
weekend_recommendations: It is very easy to come around in the rest of Italy from Milan. I would especially recommend trips to Como Lake, Venice, Rome, Verona and Florence. The plain tickets from Milan to Sardinia and Sicily is also very cheap (500 DKK both ways)
culture_adjustment: I thought it was quite easy. The italian people are very open-minded and generous.
socializing_tips: Go out to local restaurants, bars etc. This is the perfect place to meet local italian people - because it is a central part of their culture.
cultural_challenges: I did not find any.
culture_appreciated: The Italian people are very easy-going and relaxed and the eat and drink out a lot. There is just a really nice vibe every night in the city.
top3_advice: 1) Look for a residence in good time, 2) Save up a lot of money to experience Milan and the rest of Italy, because there is so many options 3) Be patient with the information - it will come
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: The University experience and all the nice people I meet from all around the world.
greatest_challenge: I did not have any bigger challenges during the stay, but of course it is always a big change to move to another country and find your everyday there, without your safe environment from home.
