crucial_aspects: I really wanted to go on exchange in Italy to improve my Italian. But since my Italian is not quite good enough for academic purposes I also needed there to be some courses in English that could substitute some obligatory courses at KU
info_ease: It can be quite hard to find the information you need. But the Erasmus Office in Pavia responded to all my emails and answered all my questions.
arrival_assistance: There were two welcome seminars during the welcome week, which were informative. But to be honest a lot of the time you just had to learn by doing. And take it a bit as it comes.
arrival_comments: With my specific program if was quite frustrating the lack of information - especially about the schedule, classes and so on.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I mainly found the process difficult because I had very specific courses I needed to make sure I could take. But the registration itself went very smoothly.
registration_help: The Erasmus Office was very helpful and you can also sign up for a buddy, who can help you set settled.
registration_success: I did a lot of research beforehand so I ended up getting all the classes I wanted
registration_advice: Have patience! sometimes you want things to happen a bit faster, but it is Italy! ;) And then just write to the Erasmus Office with questions.
course_level: The level was not high! I only had classes on Masterlevel and these were very easy. A lot of them very introductory.
teaching_comparison: It was primarily frontal lectures and not a single discussion or group exercise. We wrote a lot of abstracts as an exercise.
courses_enrolled: Cognitive development Experimental Psychology Neuroeconomics Neurolinguistics Psicologia della cognizione sociale
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed Psicologia della cognizione sociale, but that is mainly because of personal interest. I also joined some Practical Lab Courses from the program, which was really interesting.
unexpected_costs: Not as far as I remember
cost_comparison: Eating out was really cheap! Books from the bookstore the same. Cross-country traintickets were cheap too. The rent was actually a bit more expensive than I expected.
activities_available: There was an university sports club with all sorts of cool sports. There was an outdoor club. And then ESN had all sorts of events and trips you could sign up for.
activities_recommended: I would recommend to participate in the welcome week activities! very easy way to make friends! Also check out events outside of ESN to meet Italians and not just other exchange students.
weekend_recommendations: TRAVEL! Even though the local trains can often be late, the long-distance trains are amazing and connect all of Italy. From Milan you can reach so many places!
culture_adjustment: Very easy. The most difficult was having dinner late.
socializing_tips: Uh that is more difficult. But If you try to speak some Italian to them you are definitely one step ahead.
cultural_challenges: Actually the more laissez faire attitude to schedules, time and planning was quite hard to get used to.
culture_appreciated: The socializing, going out, meeting friends, having dinner, having drinks, drinking coffee-thing! <3
top3_advice: 1. Prepare yourself for some chaos and lack of organization 2. Everything will eventually sort itself (maybe you need to send one or two emails) out 3. Enjoy!
other_useful_info: The above.
most_rewarding: Meeting a lot of nice people, eating amazing food, traveling in Italy off-season, newfound appreciation for my home university
greatest_challenge: The lack of organization and cancelled trains
other_comments: In the end every challenging thing was worth it!

crucial_aspects: I chose Perpignan because it is in the South of France, and I love the area. I wanted to go on exchange to experience France and its culture, as well as utilising the language more. For these purposes, I felt that Southern France was perfect. So I can say that I chose my destination based on the food, culture, nature and weather.
overall_comments: My stay abroad was exceptional socially. I met some amazing people, and I got to experience some very cool and interesting things. I absolutely loved this aspect and would go back to the area in a heartbeat for this. However, my experience with the host university was not the best, but rather quite stressful. I didn't feel like I got the best reception as an Erasmus student, and the administration at the university was quite bad - I'm still having problems with attaining certain documents, and the pacing and quality of services simply don't live up to my own university. The problems I have experienced with administration have certanly tainted some aspects of my stay, so I would not recommend the univsersity itself to any future students.
info_ease: It was not very easy. I got my room and internet access easily. However, information about administrative things, such as attaining a student card, or finding out how to pay the rent was not given to me, and I had to get this information from former Erasmus students. Problems such as these also came when we had to inscribe to exams and get our grade transcripts - overall it wasn't easy, and one had to send many mails and proactively ask around a lot, to get the necessary information.
arrival_assistance: I was given a quick tour of the campus and a bunch of pamphlets about the area. Then I was given some information about what I needed to do, like getting room insurance or paying my deposit for the room. After this, not much assistance was offered.
arrival_comments: I would have loved a better introduction to practical matters, as well as any kind of social introduction for foreign students. During my stay, the university didn't host an event of any kind, and students were left to socialize themselves. This worked out fine for most people, but some sort of meeting or any event hosted by the university would have helped and made the first few weeks easier and less lonely.

registration_process: For three weeks you can visit any classes you're interested in, and then you should make a choice and let the professors know that you're joining the class. Later on, you sign up for the exams, which is a document that you fill out and get signed. You should always let professors know that you're an Erasmus student who would like to follow the class so that they can add you manually. Also, some professors may not advise Erasmus students to follow their course, si it would be best to get it out of the way.
registration_help: The necessary documentation is sent to you via email. It isn't totally clear how to fill it out, or who signs, but this can quickly be cleared up.
registration_success: I filled out the necessary documentation and got it signed. After that I was registered for my exams, which wasn't too difficult.
registration_advice: You should definitely expect your courses to change after arrival. You will need to have around 10-12 courses, so many of your pre-chosen courses are likely to overlap on the schedule. Therefore you should be prepared to make some changes, will in turn will need to be approved by your university. This will give you some extra work.
academics_comments: My stay abroad was exceptional socially. I met some amazing people, and I got to experience some very cool and interesting things. I absolutely loved this aspect and would go back to the area in a heartbeat for this. However, my experience with the host university was not the best, but rather quite stressful. I didn't feel like I got the best reception as an Erasmus student, and the administration at the university was quite bad - I'm still having problems with attaining certain documents, and the pacing and quality of services simply don't live up to my own university. The problems I have experienced with administration have certanly tainted some aspects of my stay, so I would not recommend the univsersity itself to any future students.
course_level: The level of courses is very different from universities in Denmark. Since you have 10-12 courses, they are all quite surface level. And be careful to choose the right courses upon your arrival, because not all of them can be recognised to be on a bachelor's level compared to Danish standards, which may cause you problems later on. Overall, I found that the academic level was in many ways considerably lower than Danish standards - however, this varied a lot depending on the course.
teaching_comparison: The style is completely different. You aren't given much reading material but you will need to show up for class and listen to everything that is said (and take notes!!). because that is what is used for the exams. Also, the universities in France rely heavily on memorising what the professors say, and it isn't very analytical in nature. So it is important to show up, listen well and take notes.
courses_enrolled: I was enrolled in Latin, History of Contemporary Art, Linguistics, History of Rome, Comparative Literature, History of the French Langauge, Reflective Learning of a Language, Advanced German, Techniques of Expression in English, and then two French Erasmus courses.
recommended_courses: I would recommend most literature courses, as they are easy to get approved by Danish universities, and I had some very good experiences with these courses - they had passionate teachers and interesting subject matter. However, there may be problems with getting language courses approved in Denmark, as they may not live up to the Danish standard.
unexpected_costs: I had no unexpected costs that I remember.
cost_comparison: Food is very cheap compared to Denmark. You can also often find buses and train tickets for one euro (even longer trips). However, if you buy a cheap bike you won't need public transport much in your every day.
activities_available: The university had a lot of different activities available, both creative and within sports. There were classes like pottery, sewing, drawing and singing, as well as football, volleyball, wrestling, yoga, and dancing. It was all free, you just had to sign up on a weekly basis.
activities_recommended: I would recommend yoga, it was one of the few classes that I took, and it was extremely relaxing and nice.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend visiting some of the smaller towns nearby, such as Carcasonne, Argeles-sur-mer, Banyuls-sur-mer, just generally some of the charming villages around. I would also recommend taking the two-hour bus to Barcelona, it is amazing. There are also really great hikes and cool things to see and experience in nature, such as big caves and natural hot springs.
culture_adjustment: The biggest cultural difference was the difference at the university, with classes and exams. However, you adjust quickly. Other than that I didn't find many cultural differences and absolutely love the French culture and mindset. It was easy to adjust.
socializing_tips: Don't be afraid to be the first to talk to someone. A lot of foreign students might think that the French students seem closed off or reserved, but they are extremely friendly and open to help - sometimes you just have to be the first one to talk.
cultural_challenges: I didn't find that there were any challenging cultural differences (apart from systematic differences, like administrative difficulties or differences in university).
culture_appreciated: I love the way the French know how to enjoy life and do a lot of different things on the weekends. They really know how to relax, enjoy food and enjoy life, without too much hurry and stress. I really appreciate this.
top3_advice: I would say that you should be prepared for a lot of confusion around practical and administrative matters. Therefore, it is really important that you're not afraid to ask and send a lot of emails if you're ever in doubt about something. Don't be shy on that front. Secondly, I would say that you should (probably) be prepared for a different university system than your own. At my own university class isn't mandatory, and there isn't too much time spent in class, but there is rather a lot of time spent on preparation. In France, it is mandatory to go to class, and you will most likely have a lot of classes to go to. It is really important that you go to class and listen well, as you aren't given much text or reading material, but the exams will be about what is said in class. Therefore, if you don't go to class, or you don't listen, you could lose a lot of valuable information that will be complicated to regain. Also, most exams are written exams, and they're done by hand - so you should get comfortable writing by hand for a long time. Lastly, I would advise anyone to really enjoy and explore the area. Perpignan is close to Barcelona, Marseille, Montpellier and Toulouse - all great places! It is also close to the sea and the mountains, where you can go skiing in winter. It is a really amazing placement, where you can go and explore all kinds of different nature. I would highly advise anyone to explore the areas around and take advantage and travel while you're there.
other_useful_info: France offers a lot of student discounts, so always bring your student card when you're going somewhere. Also, the university offers a "culture pass", which will give you huge discounts on events, such as movie tickets, theatre, operas and all kinds of things like that. Furthermore, the university has a lot of different free classes available. They offer a bunch of sports classes, like yoga, dancing, volleyball etc. (there are a lot!), and also a lot of creative classes, like singing, pottery, sewing and so on. Definitely take advantage of this, if you can.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part was definitely meeting so many amazing people and getting so many new friends. Throughout my stay, I also had to speak French the entire time, so it was probably the biggest improvement I have ever made with my language in such a short time.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was definitely overcoming so many difficulties administratively. The university in France simply doesn't work on the same level as in Denmark. I don't mean to make too drastic statements, but getting things done and signed generally took ages, and things often had to be done twice due to mistakes. At the same time, the university of Perpignan often lacks satisfactory official documents, such as course descriptions and such, so there were a few times when documents had to be written and signed for a small matter. I finished my exams in May, and I am still missing some key elements to finish my stay, so I recommend a lot of patience and perseverance when it comes to practical and administrative matters.

crucial_aspects: Since I am a student of French culture who never had the chance to learn French in school, I wanted to go abroad to improve my skills in oral French. I chose Perpignan because it is a rather small city, at least compared to most other opportunities I was given in choice of destination. I thought that people here would be more laid-back, have more time and patience to listen to my broken French and be less international and thus less likely to speak English. Secondly, being from Denmark and suffering from mild depression during the winter months because of the cold and the general darkness, I found the warm weather, the high number of sunshine hours and the geographical situation of the city appealing. After all, why go to Calais, Normandie or any other département that looks quite like Denmark when you can try out something completely different down South.
overall_comments: It has been great. My spoken French has improved significantly, and I have learned to not love another educational system, which really makes me appreciate where I come from. Since I am older than most of the other students here, and since I have aldready travelled a lot it has not been "the best time of my life" as some people find it, but I am fine with that and did not expect it to be otherwise. I think one thing that could have improved my stay would have been doing it outside of the last covid restrictions - wearing a mask made it difficult to bond with the French students in my class since the absence of facial expressions and the muffling of spoken words made communication difficult, but of course all that was out of the control of the host university or anyone in power.

All while trying to catch up with the missed classes I, and the rest of the Erasmus students, had to sort out the genuine ocean of administrative inscriptions, tasks and so what all on our own, while being threatened with being kicked out of our accommodations and the university for not having done things that noone had told us to do, or how to do it. With the bike I can go anywhere and often arrive earlier than my friends, I can explore town and have found amazing locations that they would never encounter, I have driven all around the area visiting small idyllic villages and historical sights, or just sped though the wineyards, feeling the warm air against my skin. Alors, students - get yourself a bike!!!!!! Secondly, although public transport within the city is not well developed, the département has bus lines that take you to most major sites for just one euro! Not that's cheap!

cultural_challenges: It seems that both "no" and "yes" means "maybe" when pronounced by someone French. And that if it is normal in your culture to be less outspoken, they will probably not understand it when you reject them or their ideas.

housing_how: I found housing on my own

crucial_aspects: For my study destination it was important for me that the destination had a rich culture, good weather and a good social life. It was also important for me to be in Europe because of the Erasmus grant but also because i would have a short way home for fx christmas. And i wanted to learn more about Europe.
overall_comments: Accommodation was great and really nice people. And the city was just so much nicer than expected.
info_ease: Very easy. The faculty administration was very good and helpful. Also had a good communication with my home university, when i wanted to change one course. It was really nice to see that the two universities had good communication. It made it more safe for me.
arrival_assistance: I received assistance with my courses, how to get the university card and the metro card for the city. I would have liked to get some information about some social life on university or something about some sport activities.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Accommodation was great and really nice people. And the city was just so much nicer than expected.
registration_process: Good information in the first days with meetings and time to meet new students. This proces kept on going for 2-3 weeks so there was a lot of time to settle in and be sure that you knew everything you should. For future development they could maybe extend the deadline for when you should have chosen the courses you wanted. Give a week more for the students to get a better feeling about changing the courses.
registration_help: They had a good administration online with one very good coordinater. I felt that it was enough and i didnt have to wait for too long. Good response time online on email and also good response time when meeting up in person. I guess they also had help with the IT-services but it wasn't necessary for me or my fellow students.
registration_success: Very succesfull. There was enough spots for all the courses i wanted, and i even wanted to change one, which i also was allowed to do.
registration_advice: My best advice is that they should start in good time. Start the registration before exploring the city. This will ease the process and make it less stressfull so that the time in the city will be more efficient and nice. Its also a good idea to just ask as much as you can. When arriving in a place for the first time its totally fair to ask "dumb" questions.
academics_comments: Accommodation was great and really nice people. And the city was just so much nicer than expected.
course_level: I had 5 courses in total. I would say that the level was good, and i learned a lot when being on exchange. They were a bit easier than at my home university because there was less math than i was used to. But this was a good thing since there were a lot of other things to get to know and a whole new way of teaching.
teaching_comparison: Smaller crowds, which made it more productive i would say. They had time for all the questions. Compared to my home university Porto had no exercise classes, which could have helped in some of the courses.
courses_enrolled: Corporate finance, international trade, economic and public finance, organizational behaviour and economic growth.
recommended_courses: Economic and public finance. good structure and useful stuff. I would also recommend international trade and coorperate finance, since they were very interesting and i learned a lot. Good teachers.
unexpected_costs: I just did a lot more trips than i expected but i dont know if that is unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: Shampoo were more expensive. Food in general were less expensive than expected. And also the beers and drinks when going out to party.
activities_available: I didn't see or hear so much. That is also what i wrote earlier that i wished for better activities there. especially with sports because that could help me with meeting locals and also just other international students.
activities_recommended: For my university i really can't recommend any since i didn't participate in any.
weekend_recommendations: I did an amazing trip to Madeira. Very beautiful and memories for life. I also did the camino from Porto to Santiago which is also something i will remember for the rest of my life. I can also recommend trips to the capital of Portugal, Lisbon. It's very cheap with bus and they arrive all the time, which makes it very easy.
culture_adjustment: It was a bit tough since i didn't speak their language and their level of english was challenged. Apart from that they were very sweet and they wanted to greet me and make me feel welcome.
socializing_tips: I can only recommend learning their language but also just approach them. Even though the maybe seem to be not interested its sometimes not the case. They are just shy sometimes.
cultural_challenges: I found the tempo a bit challenging in the start because it was a lot slower than i am used to. But after a while i really started to like how they walked slow and just took everything in a slow tempo. I actually also found their food a bit challenging since it was not as good as i expected. Only meat options as well.
culture_appreciated: As i mentioned above i learned to appreciate their tempo.
top3_advice: The three most beautiful things is the amazing city of Porto. Then it is the social life and all the good international classes on the university.
other_useful_info: No, not other than they expect you to be fluent in english and that the exams is written on paper by hand.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange was the self-realisation i had. I got to know myself a lot better in many ways, and also just got to know a new city into its core.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was to be away from family and friends back home. I really missed them and the social life in Porto wasn't as good as back home. But that is also the reason why i got to know myself a lot more.
other_comments: No.

crucial_aspects: I went to Berlin on exchange, first and foremost as I've always wanted to try to live in the city. Furthermore, I wanted to improve my German, why it was a good opportunity.
info_ease: It was quite hard to find information regarding the courses taught at the university and additionally, to understand how to apply for courses. I had to a lot of research myself to be able to understand the system.
arrival_assistance: I was a part of a Buddy-program, where I was partnered with a person studying the same major at the university. Furthermore, the university arranged information meetings.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration for courses was really difficult and not designed for international students. Few courses were provided in English and both the registration for courses, the acceptance and the registration for exams had to be done on platforms in German and by email to the professors.
registration_help: I contacted the professors a lot on email and they provided me with some necessary information, however they did not always have the answer needed as an exchange student. Furthermore, it was possible to contact the international office at the university.
registration_success: I got accepted to all of my courses after writing emails to the professors.
registration_advice: Engage with a student who attends the university, who is able to help you obtain the necessary information as it can be quite hard to figure the system out.
course_level: I had three courses at bachelor level and one at master level. Some of the courses were well-structured and informative, however some did not live up to the expected level.
teaching_comparison: The courses I was signed up to only did class-teaching once a week. Therefore, I did not have any seminars.
courses_enrolled: - Introduction to family sociology - Policy-making in the European policy cycle - Judicialization of politics from a comparative perspective - International Institutions
recommended_courses: Except for my course Judicialization, the courses were well-structured and the professors were helpful and competent.
unexpected_costs: None.
cost_comparison: Food and transport are very cheap compared to Denmark.
activities_available: It was possible to attend various clubs and sports, however due to COVID, a lot of the activities were shut down.
activities_recommended: I participated in some activities arranged by the international office in order to meet other exchange students, which is recommendable.
weekend_recommendations: Visit the different parts of the city and walk around.
culture_adjustment: Except for understanding the educational system and the structure of the university, it was easy to adjust.
socializing_tips: Due to COVID, it was difficult to meet the local students as a lot of my classes were only taught online.
cultural_challenges: The relationship between professor and student is a lot more formal and the German students were much more polite than what I am used to.
culture_appreciated: The way the people engage with each other more openly and polite.
top3_advice: Be prepared to do a lot of paperwork, contact your professors early on and attend the information meetings.
other_useful_info: None.
most_rewarding: It loved living in Berlin.
greatest_challenge: Having to figure the structure of the educational system out on my own and having to fill out a lot of paperwork.
other_comments: None.

arrival_assistance: None
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The International Office of University of Potsdam had made a folder with all necessary information upon arrival
registration_help: How to register for courses, how to register in Berlin/Potsdam, how to apply for sports courses on campus etc.
registration_success: There was one course I really wanted but did not get since too many students applied for it - you had to be the first to register to get a spot on the course
registration_advice: Register for all courses you find interestering, go to all the courses in the first week, and then withdraw from the courses you decide not to take afterwards.

recommended_courses: Women in International Relations - Very interesting course building on the IR knowledge we already have from the bachelor's degree Democracy: then and now - Very well structured Intro to R for Social Scientists - Very well structured
unexpected_costs: I had most of my meals at restaurants or cafés (and my lunch in the cheap canteen at the university)
cost_comparison: Most things are cheaper compared to Denmark, but it is especially very cheap to go the the opera, theatre, ballet etc. as a student.
activities_available: The University of Potsdam offers a lot of sports courses which are cheap and very good. Furthermore, the different faculties had barbecues throughout the summer.
activities_recommended: I would recommend the sports courses, especially the water sports - Potsdam is very beautiful with its lakes and forests, so I chose to do only outdoor sports courses
weekend_recommendations: Check out concerts or festivals in Berlin, go to the opera, go swim in the lakes of Schlachtensee/Krumme Lanke
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: I found it really easy to meet local students in my courses and in my sports courses
cultural_challenges: People are more kind than in Denmark - and you have to adjust to that to not seem rude
culture_appreciated: People were very open to talk and help, which made it easy to meet people.
top3_advice: Apply for a lot of courses and withdraw from some of them later on - Meet people on the university's sports courses - Remember to call the Professors by their last name
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: I liked everything about it
greatest_challenge: The COVID-19 restrictions

crucial_aspects: It was very close to Berlin which is a city I've always wanted to live in.
info_ease: Very easy, the international office was very helpful.
arrival_assistance: An employee of the International office sat down with me for half an hour and explained me everything I needed to know.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You get the course catalog 2 weeks before the start of the semester and then there is a week where you can attend whichever courses you find interesting and then a couple of weeks where you can deregister for the ones you don't want.
registration_help: The international office, the professors
registration_success: Very.
registration_advice: Do as many classes in the first week as you can. And look out for the exam requirements. Some have very hard exams and some are just passed by regular attendance. I think I would have preferred to take more classes and then have no exams at the end.

teaching_comparison: Very different. In some classes the professors barely participated but instead had us do many group presentations. In some cases it worked well, but generally I think I would have gained better insight into the various topics by having a professor teach me.
courses_enrolled: Regionale Integration im Internationalen Vergleich Autoritärer Föderalismus: Russland im Vergleich Forced Migration: Aufnahme und Integrationspolitik in der EU Die Erweiterungspolitik in der Europäischen Union Democracy Under Pressure
recommended_courses: Any courses with Stanislav Klimovich. I think he mostly teaches in German, but the courses are super interesting!
unexpected_costs: My German phone plan.
cost_comparison: Food is generally pretty cheap. Movie tickets too.
activities_available: Many different ones. I didn't get around to exploring any of them though.
activities_recommended: I didn't try any.
weekend_recommendations: The park Sanssouci is really beautiful. The lakes in the Potsdam area are also beautiful. Many pretty places to walk like Grunewald
culture_adjustment: Very.
socializing_tips: I found it pretty easy to just ask people about things I was unsure of in class and made friends that way. It will probably be easier if you speak German.
cultural_challenges: Not really any to be honest
culture_appreciated: It is a very flexible education system and the professors are generally really chill.
top3_advice: Take more courses than you think you need. Maybe you can avoid taking exams at the end
other_useful_info: The administration is generally very helpful and respond really quickly
most_rewarding: Getting to know a lot of new people both through uni and elsewhere.
greatest_challenge: Taking courses in German

crucial_aspects: I wanted to experience a different culture and a different education system. I chose University of Queensland because Brisbane seemed like a nice city and the academic level of the University seemed relatively high.
info_ease: The university did a great job providing all necessary information, so it was quite easy to find the needed information. There was a Zoom session prior to arrival with a lot of information and the opportunity to ask for any information not presented by the university.
arrival_assistance: I got assistance with my courses, as one of my courses got cancelled when i got there. The university was very helpful with providing a list of courses suitable for exchange students, and they helped me with enrolment in a new course.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I did most of the course registration online, and then I just had to enrol in the courses when I got there.
registration_help: There was a lot of possibility to get help available. The student central at campus offered help with course registration and enrolment as well as any other difficulties with course enrolment.
registration_success: I got the courses i registrered for except for one, which got cancelled. I got another course instead, which I really liked, so I was quite happy with my courses in general.
registration_advice: Don't stress too much about course registration. It is quite easy to change courses after arriving in Brisbane. I would just make sure to get preapproval for as many courses as possible in advance to be able to freely change courses after arrival.
course_level: The courses were not as hard and demanding as the courses from the University of Copenhagen. I didn't have to put in as much effort to succeed, as I would have at the University of Copenhagen.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching were quite different. A lot of courses were intensive and thus the teaching only lasted a few weeks. Additionally, I didn't have any regular exams, as all courses finished with a written assignment (academic paper).
courses_enrolled: Maritime Law Mediation and Conflict Management Fundamentals of the Common Law International Law and Development
recommended_courses: All my courses were good and suitable for exhange students, as they didn't require any prior knowledge to the Australian legal system and the common law system. I enjoyed Maritime Law the most, as it was the course resembling courses from the University of Copenhagen the most.
unexpected_costs: I had to go buy kitchen equipment, as it was not in my apartment, when I got it.
cost_comparison: Groceries was way more expensive than I expected. Transportation was quite cheap compared to Denmark.
activities_available: There were a lot of clubs available. They were all presenting their club at market day during orientation week. It was a great opportunity to find activities to parcipate in during the exchange.
activities_recommended: There is a lot of clubs, and I would just recommend finding a club within your area of interest. There is a club for almost everything, so there is plenty of opportunity to find something of interest.
weekend_recommendations: I would just recommend traveling a lot. Plan some longer trips during the holidays. There is a lot of places close to Brisbane, where you can go in the weekends, so there is plenty of opportunity to experience Australia.
culture_adjustment: Yes. Australia is very Western, so the it is quite easy to adjust to the local culture.
socializing_tips: There is a lot of social activities during the first couple of weeks, which I would highly recommend attending. After that I would just recommend staying in touch with the all the people you meet, as it is a lot harder to meet new people later on in the semester.
cultural_challenges: There wasn't any significant cultural differences. The most challenging differences I encountered was probably when I traveled to places with a high population of aboriginals, as their culture is quite a bit different.
culture_appreciated: Their laid back and welcoming attitude.
top3_advice: Travel a lot. There will be plenty of time, if the academics is planned well. Join some clubs. It is a good way to meet people. Attend as many social activities as possible during the first couple of weeks.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: The opportunity to travel a lot in a very nice and diverse country.
greatest_challenge: Finding the time to do everything i wanted to do while in Australia.

crucial_aspects: Courses in English and nice weather
info_ease: Very easy. UQ was super helpful with everything introductory. Though, a little confusion about which introduction "classes" to attend from time to time. It seemed crucial to attend everything, but I guess it wouldn't matter much if you were to miss something.
arrival_assistance: Different introduction seminars - both academic, social etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I'm not really sure what is meant by registration process, but getting my student card and everything was pretty smooth.
registration_help: A student central with very knowledgable students were available. And a lot of other platforms and services available for various matters.
registration_success: 4/4. I got all the classes I wished for. I changed one course for another once I got to Brisbane, as I figured it would be too much work.
registration_advice: It's easy. And UQ is happy to help.
course_level: It's a very different way of studying than what I've been used to at KU. Many assignments during the semester and a greater expectation to actively participate in the courses. I spent a lot more time on the classes than what I had anticipated before going, and it payed off (grade-wise), but don't expect it to be super easy just because the grades will be transferred to pass/failed. I guess it depends on the specific courses though.
teaching_comparison: Larger focus on active participation. More class discussions etc. The teaching style was more of a seminar than lectures.
courses_enrolled: Intercultural Communication Ethics and Human Rights International Relations in Asia-Pacific Gender, Peace and Security in Local and Global Perspective
recommended_courses: I would very much recommend the Ethics and Human Rights course. Emma was a great lecturer, super nice. The Gender, Peace and Security courses was also very interesting, and Nicole the lecturer was both inspiring and very knowledgeable. The Intercultural Communication was an easy course, but I didn't like the lecturer and the course was very focused on the gaps and differences between Australian culture and Chinese culture, as the lecturer was Chinese and 95% of the students taking the course were Chinese. International Relations was a very cool course as well, but I struggled a bit, since I didn't have any prior knowledge about the region. But very interesting course and I learned a lot.
unexpected_costs: I expected it to be expensive, so nothing really unexpected, but super cheap coffee at cafés and very expensive beers at the bottle shops. Otherwise very much as in DK in terms of supermarket costs and eating/going out etc.
cost_comparison: As mentioned above. Cheap coffee, expensive beers from bottle shop, cheaper drinks and beers at bars/clubs. A bit cheaper eating out. Cheap local transport.
activities_available: Anything you can think of!
activities_recommended: Sports clubs.
weekend_recommendations: Go see the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast - great for weekend trips. I went to Sydney for a weekend also and went on a road trip to Cairns when the semester had ended. I also wish I had more time and money to simply explore Brisbane and the food scene there.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Australians are super friendly and welcoming. Loved how they were genuinely interested in getting to know you.
socializing_tips: I didn't socialize much with my fellow local students, as I didn't have any courses with local students. Most of my courses were with other international students. I spent a lot of time with other Danes - which was also great.
cultural_challenges: Nothing really.
culture_appreciated: The hospitality
top3_advice: If you're a masters student, don't stress about everything you feel like you need to see and do when in Australia. Try also to enjoy your time at UQ. It's a great experience to study at another university, and if you, as I, spend a lot of time on your courses, it helps if you try to appreciate the opportunity in this. Enjoy Brisbane and try to make it your home. I got to see many places on the east coast, but I also wanted to spend time in Brisbane so that I actually felt it as my home. Don't try to escape Brisbane. Put in the needed work, but don't stress about the grades etc.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Many rewarding things, can't single out one. The people I met, the things I learned (from UQ and from locals), etc.
greatest_challenge: Finding accommodation and occasionally the time difference and time managing uni and fun stuff.

crucial_aspects: A crucial aspect of choosing my study destination was the culture and the city, however it was also very important for me that the university had a profile that matched my expectations, offered courses that were relevant and interesting for my education and also offered different social activities.
overall_comments: My study abroad experience was definitely one of the best experiences in my life, but sometimes it was also hard to be so far away from home. Also I didn't find accommodation before I arrived, and I had some problems with finding accommodation when I arrived, which effected the beginning of my stay.
info_ease: The information was very easy to find.
arrival_assistance: The university offered a free airport pickup, and there where a lot of assistance available in orientation week.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: My study abroad experience was definitely one of the best experiences in my life, but sometimes it was also hard to be so far away from home. Also I didn't find accommodation before I arrived, and I had some problems with finding accommodation when I arrived, which effected the beginning of my stay.
registration_process: You had to complete an application form, and upload different documents.
registration_help: I had a contact person both at my home university and my destination university, but it took a long time for them to respond.
registration_success: That was very easy and succesfull.
registration_advice: To set a lot of time aside to it.
academics_comments: My study abroad experience was definitely one of the best experiences in my life, but sometimes it was also hard to be so far away from home. Also I didn't find accommodation before I arrived, and I had some problems with finding accommodation when I arrived, which effected the beginning of my stay.
course_level: I had to take a lot of first year courses, but they were great.
teaching_comparison: In some ways it was quite similar, but it was also more practical which was quite nice. Also I didn't have any exams, but instead we were graded on participation and different assessments through the whole semester. I found this way of grading the students very meaningful, and enjoyed it more than exams. This takes away some of the pressure that exams put on students.
courses_enrolled: COMU 1052 - Intro strategic communication DRAM 1100 - The theatre experience DRAM 2025 - European theatre (1500-1800) DRAM 2030 - Experimentation in 20'th century theatre
recommended_courses: All the courses were great, but I would especially recommend "intro strategic communication" and "Experimentation in 20'th century theatre".
unexpected_costs: I had to live on a hostel for one month, and then I had to buy duvet, pillows, towels, plate, cup, cutlery etc. when I found my accommodation.
cost_comparison: Rent and alcohol
activities_available: There were a lot of different clubs and activities to be a part of, and they also had a club that planned trips and parties for exchange students which was great. There was a club for almost everything, surfing, beach volley, tennis, drama, choir, music, art etc.
activities_recommended: Definitely "Quest"(Queensland University Exchange Students Society). We were on two weekend trips, with different activities, parties etc, and then they arranged different parties throughout the semester. This was a great club to be a part of, since you could meet other exchange students
weekend_recommendations: For activities in Brisbane I recommend: City beach, Felons, Eat Street, Mt Coot-tha Lookout. For daily trips from Brisbane I would really recommend: Gold Coast, Moreton Island, North Stradbroke Island, Sunshine Coast For longer trips and holidays I recommend: Cairns, Sydney, Melbourne, Tasmania
culture_adjustment: It was quite easy.
socializing_tips: Everyone is so nice, so just be open ad welcoming and don't be afraid to approach or talk to them.
cultural_challenges: Not anything.
culture_appreciated: How welcoming, polite and helpful everyone was.
top3_advice: There is a lot of academic support available at the library. Become a part of QUEST. Make sure to look in the lake at the university - it has five turtles.
other_useful_info: no
most_rewarding: The social bond with the other exchange students.
greatest_challenge: Homesickness
other_comments: Being on exchange is not easy, everything is new, you are alone a lot, everything is in english, and you are very far away from home, family and friends but it is definitely worth it. It is a great adventure and you learn a lot from it.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to a university with good academic opportunities and still live fairly close to the water to go surfing in my free time.
info_ease: I didn't have any problems finding information I needed upon arrival.
arrival_assistance: We had an introduction lecture for exchange students get the information we needed. Also there were a day in the first week where all the societies of the university had stalls and told about what they did. It was fx the surf society, diving society or the QUEST society, which is a society for international students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You first had to enroll in courses. To be able to enroll in a course you also needed to get pre approval of the host university. It is possible to enroll in 5 courses and then later drop one of them, when you have figured out which 4 you would like. After enrolling you could choose at what time you wanted practicals and tutorials. I would recommend to do this as soon as possible to have as many options available as possible.
registration_help: There where both a consultation where staff from the different faculties helped with pre approval and the student services could also help.
registration_success: I got to register to all the 5 classes I wanted whereafter I dropped one of them.
registration_advice: It helped me to look at programs that were similar to my own to get inspiration for courses.
course_level: I took 2 second year economic courses, 1 second year math course and a first year history course.
teaching_comparison: It was very similar with 1 lecture pr week and 1-2 tutorials or practicals.
courses_enrolled: ECON2020 - Intermediate Macroeconomics ECON2300 - Introductory Econometrics MATH2504 - Programming for Mathematicians HIST1201 - The Australian Experience
recommended_courses: The Programming for Mathematicians is one of the best courses I have done so far. However it was also very challenging, especially in the start. I would also recommend The Australian Experience which was a history course about Australian history. I very much enjoyed trying a different type of course than mathematics or economics that I am used to.
unexpected_costs: I didn't find any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: Food was a lot more expensive than what I thought. Also compared to Denmark. Public transport however is very cheap in Brisbane.
activities_available: All kinds both different kind of sports, societies such as the UQ Surfers who did weekend trips and the QUEST society who arranged trips and bar nights for international students.
activities_recommended: I would recommend the QUEST society and the UQ Surfers. Also I would also recommend the UNIDIVE - The University of Queensland Underwater Club, which I didn't participate in myself. However I would very much have liked to go diving in the weekends.
weekend_recommendations: Noosa, Gold Coast and Byron Bay are great for weekend trips. Either to just go to the beach or go surfing.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy, the culture is not very different from the danish one.
socializing_tips: I mostly met local students at my classes.
cultural_challenges: I didn't find any particularly challenging.
culture_appreciated: The relaxed surfer culture here in Australia.
top3_advice: Make sure to also enjoy your freetime to go explore places in Australia. Most of the assessment is due during the semester. Don't stress about this too much. It also makes the examination period less stresfull. Look forward for your stay!
other_useful_info: No not that I can think of.
most_rewarding: Being within two hours drive of some very beautiful nature and surfspots.
greatest_challenge: The first assignment of Programming for Mathematicians, was very challenging and time consuming.

crucial_aspects: I chose Australia for its weather and natural landscapes. I was very happy to stay in the state of Queensland, which is the gateway to all of the beautiful east coast, Great Barrier Reef and is subtropically warm all year.
overall_comments: UQ offers a great academic experience, while Australia itself offers unlimited travel and adventure opportunities both for nature and city lovers
info_ease: UQ does an awesome job with providing any kind of information needed and are always proactive in supporting and being responsive to any inquiries
arrival_assistance: UQ arranges a hole week of orientation with fun events both socially and academically. Besides that they offer both mental health support, academic support, housing support and personal issues support through the student service which is available both online and onsite
arrival_comments: UQ does a far better job than KU in regard of caring for their students and being responsive and helpful.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: UQ offers a great academic experience, while Australia itself offers unlimited travel and adventure opportunities both for nature and city lovers
registration_process: I must say I forgot besides the fact that it was smooth and painless
registration_help: UQ offer online guiding session via zoom to help international students through the process
registration_success: UQ was happy to let me into any courses I wished for what so ever, but KU has some rigid rules limiting the options for master students. However UQ was very helpful in assisting me in finding other courses I was happy with choosing instead
registration_advice: Communicate with UQ try are so lovely and re-motivates you to make the exchange happen whenever KU demotivates you.
academics_comments: UQ offers a great academic experience, while Australia itself offers unlimited travel and adventure opportunities both for nature and city lovers
course_level: The level is slightly lower than that of Denmark, however language barriers and adjusting to a foreign educational system can cause some challenges to deal with instead. Totally worth it tho and great learning experience on seeing tho Mhh a from a different perspective than the Danish one
teaching_comparison: Far more hands on and career geared than the lecture heavy style of humanities in DK
courses_enrolled: Digital heritage, academic English and thesis writing for international students, museum management, visitor management
recommended_courses: Visitor management was the most engaging course I’ve ever taken. The professors do a great job making the lectures entertaining, useful and interactive always filled with practical exercises and themes to dress up as or bring cultural food for. The other happy surprise was digital heritage which was very up to date and gave invaluable applicable skills for photogrammetry, object handling, coding, podcast producing and more
unexpected_costs: Living in Brisbane is rather expensive for student accom. The food is slightly cheaper than in Denmark but eating out is the same.
cost_comparison: See the above
activities_available: Oh see the above :)
activities_recommended: Since student accom also arranges events I ended up travelling more with them, but definitely go to the free breakfast and UQ festivals plus o week - this is where to make a lot of friends and ppl are really open to chatting
weekend_recommendations: Try and get your uni work done during the week (doable) and then go on day trips or if u have a car longer trips in nature during weekends. I recommend Tallebudgera Creek on the Gold Coast and Noosa on the Sunshine Coast. For holidays snorkel the southern Great Barrier Reef at lady Musgrave island. Straddle is worth a daytrip as well
culture_adjustment: Australia has for the most part a western culture similar to the American one. They are far more chatty but on a rather superficial level tho they are very welcoming and helpful, but asking how are you going is just a greeting and not that sincere
socializing_tips: Chat to anyone - it will be so easy to make friends this way because everyone on campus is in a similar situation to yours
cultural_challenges: People don’t raise there hands when they speak in class - you just speak out loud whenever. The constant small talk with the Australians is something that Mig be challenging for a Scandinavian to keep up with, the fact that they never dive into deep convos. Conservative politics and values from the older generations.
culture_appreciated: Friendliness and openness to make new friends
top3_advice: Do it :) Brush up on your written and spoken English. Have fun with it, don’t worry too much about the grades
other_useful_info: Have fun with it, take whatever you can use from the classes and don’t worry too much besides that. You’re probably in the country more for the cultural experience than the academic one anyways.
most_rewarding: Travelling around the country, making friends with Australians to get an insight into the authentic Australian life. Experiencing how easy it is to make friends in other countries than Denmark where we tend to be more cold and closed.
greatest_challenge: It can be hard to adjust to the more laid back time perception and less timeliness when it comes to making appointments with Aussie friends, they might also cancel last minute.
other_comments: It was so worth it! Definitely go if you can and apply for grants at home beforehand - it takes you a long way

crucial_aspects: I had been in Brisbane in my gap year and really liked the city and the weather, and then I wanted to study in an english speaking country. I chose University of Queensland because of the relatively high academic level.
overall_comments: I had the best half year in my life and would recommend everyone to go on exchange.
info_ease: It was easy
arrival_assistance: The university had an orientation week where I got a lot of practical information, and information about where to get help if needed.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had the best half year in my life and would recommend everyone to go on exchange.
registration_process: I found the process very long. I had to complete a registration form and upload different documents.
registration_help: I had a contact person from KU and a contact person from UQ. They both responded quite fast and they were a big help.
registration_success: I found the course registration very confusing because i did not find the UQ webpage with courses easy to navigate.
registration_advice: I would recommend contacting your contact person from UCPH and ask for a course list from UQ.
academics_comments: I had the best half year in my life and would recommend everyone to go on exchange.
course_level: I found the courses at UQ easier than the courses at UCPH, and I generally did not put in much effort to pass my courses.
teaching_comparison: The courses were held as seminars as at UCPH, but with less student participation than at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Principles of International Law Mediation and Conflict Management International Maritime Trade Law Fundamentals of the Common Law
recommended_courses: I would really recommend the course International Maritime Trade Law. I had no expectations to the course, but I found it very interesting and the teacher of the course is really great. I would also recommend choosing intensive courses, because it gives a lot of sparetime and not much classes to attend. All of my courses were intensive courses which gave me the opportunity to plan my own days much more than if I had chosen normal courses.
unexpected_costs: I spend much more money on experiences and small trips than I had expected. I have been on so many great vacations and trips around Australia, which I would recommend to spend some money on.
cost_comparison: Food at restaurants was less expensive than in Denmark. Alcohol was a lot more expensive in Australia than in Denmark. Other items generally cost the same as in Denmark.
activities_available: There is almost a club/society for everyone (political clubs, Harry Potter, surf, sports, etc.) The club QUEST is a club for exchange students that arrange weekly pub nights and some really nice weekend trips. I would recommend following them on facebook to get updated on their events.
activities_recommended: Go to as many pub nights and weekend trips with QUEST as possible. The surf club also arranges parties and trips.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend going on roadtrips, for example Great Ocean Road or a roadtrip from Brisbane to Cairns. I would also recommend visiting Melbourne and Sydney. In Brisbane I can recommend the city beach at South Bank, shopping on Queen St., drinking a beer at Felons at sunset, hiking Mount Coot-Tha, visiting Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary and go for a walk in Roma Street Parklands.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Australians are very laid back and easy-going.
socializing_tips: Go to social events at campus.
cultural_challenges: The only big difference in the culture is the alcohol-policy. You cannot drink alcohol in most public places, so be aware of that.
culture_appreciated: The laid back culture and everyone being super nice and friendly.
top3_advice: Even though the whole process before going on exchange is very long it is all worth it when you arrive in Brisbane. Don't be nervous about the social aspect. Everyone are so friendly and just want to make new friends and experience as much as possible. There are plenty of events and parties where you can meet new friends. There are a lot of danish students in Brisbane which in my opinion is so nice because I have so many danish friends from my exchange that I can see after getting back home to Denmark. Don't stress about the academic aspect of the exchange. I honestly found the courses very easy and you will quickly get used to reading english texts.
other_useful_info: If possible I would recommend finding housing before going to Brisbane, because a lot of people found it very hard to find housing when they arrived, and some stayed at hostels for a month. But everyone found housing in the end so please don't stress too much about it, but be prepared to spend some money on hostels in the first period of time.
most_rewarding: The new friendships and all the great experiences (roadtrips, pub nights, weekend trips). Be prepared to not wanting to go back to Denmark after living in Australia. I could easily have stayed for another semester!
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was the economical aspect of the exchange. Be prepared to spend a lot of money, but it is all worth it! I would recommend to start the whole scholarship process in good time.
other_comments: I was personally doubting whether an exchange was someting for me, but I can say that it honestly have been the greatest half year of my life, so I would recommend everyone to go!

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte Australien da jeg ønskede at tage til et engelsktalende land. Derudover ænskede jeg at lære mere om Indigenous Australians og den australske kultur
overall_comments: Jeg kan kun anbefale at tage på ud udveksling
info_ease: Universitetet var rigtige gode til at sætte os ind i det, som vi skulle vide
arrival_assistance: Der blev afholdt informations-, fakultets- og institutmøder, hvor man fik indblik i universitetet.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Jeg kan kun anbefale at tage på ud udveksling
registration_process: Det var super svært at få alle de fag, som jeg havde fået forhåndsgodkendt på KU. Det var virkelig en udfordring at få avanceret metode, da alle metodefagene på UQ var begrænsede og lukkede på deres psykologiuddannelse, og jeg måtte søge om særlig tilladelse og kontakte alle mulige professorer for at høre, om jeg kunne deltage. SÅ det var forholdsvis kompliceret at få adgang og plads på en metodefag, fordi de var forbeholdt de australske studerende
registration_help: Overordnet set var de super hjælpsomme på UQ. Da jeg havde en del problemer med at få alle mine kurser, var jeg ofte i kontakt med universitetet, og de var super hjælpsomme fx Student service center. Dog oplevede jeg også at blive kastet rundt blandt alle mulige centre/administrative afdelinger, så jeg skulle i kontakt med mange før jeg fik den rette hjælp
registration_success: Jeg fik 3/4 fag som jeg ønskede. Det var super udfordrende at få et metodefag, men det lykkedes til sidst efter at have kontaktet flere professorer og bedt om særlig tilladelse
registration_advice: Det er en god ide at indstille sig på, at man ikke nødvendigvis får de fag, som jeg ansøger om, når man ansøger om optagelse. Der kan ske mange ændringer og der kan være forbehold og restriktioner.
academics_comments: Jeg kan kun anbefale at tage på ud udveksling
course_level: Jeg fik særlig tilladelse til at tage to bachelorfag (som jeg fik særlig tilladelse til at tage) og to kandidatfag
teaching_comparison: Der var flere opgaver i løbet af semestret fx quizzer, essay spørgsmål, oplæg etc. Det krævede lidt mere arbejde i løbet af semestret og man blev nødt til at læse for at følge med. Til gengæld var eksamensperioden ikke så intens, da man ikke havde nogle “rigtige eksamener” men kun afleveringer. Alle ens opgaver blev vurderet løbende, og til sidt fik man en samlet karakter ud fra de forskellige opgaver, der vægtede forskelligt. Så det var en del anderledes fra KU, hvor der ikke er så mange deadlines i løbet af semestret (dog afhænger dette af faget) og så én eksamen til sidst der udgør den endelig karakter.
courses_enrolled: "PSYC 3082 PSYCHOTHERAPIES & COUNSELLING" "SWSP 3027 FOUNDATIONS MENTAL HEALTH". "PSYC 7053 PARENTING, FAMILY INTERVENTION" "PSYC 7474 APPLIED RESEARCH METHOD"
recommended_courses: "SWSP 3027 FOUNDATIONS MENTAL HEALTH"! John er en af de mest dygtige og inspirerende forelæsere jeg nogensinde har haft. På trods af at jeg er psykologistuderende, endte jeg med at tage et fag på social work uddannelsen, der handlede om mental health. Han gav mig så mange nye perspektiver på mental sundhed. I undervisningen berørte vi emner såsom: magt ved diagnosticering, det levede liv ved psykisk sygdom og de personlige, sociale og strukturelle konsekvenser dette kan have, sorg, mental sundhed hos indigenous people og meget andet. Meget spændende perspektiv på mental sundhed og det lærte mig så meget. Der lægges vægt på at forstå den levede oplevelse af psykisk sygdom og behandlinger som udgangspunkt for at hjælpe. Det var stort fokus på psykisk sygdom som politisk spørgsmål, da diagnosen psykisk sygdom er for mange mennesker en oplevelse, der involverer stigmatisering, diskrimination, fattigdom, frihedstab, isolation, sorg, kronisk fysisk sygdom og tidlig død. Derudover lagde John enormt meget op til diskussion og deling af erfaringer. Han var virkelig god til at engagere de studerende og super faglige kompetent men virkelig ydmyg.
unexpected_costs: Man skal købe pude og dyne, da det ikke er en del af pakken, når man bor på StudentOne.
cost_comparison: Mad var generelt rigtig dyrt dernede
activities_available: Jeg var en del af volleyball klubben. Der var plads til alle niveauer og super mange internationale studerende var medlem.
activities_recommended: Meld dig ind i en klub på universitet
weekend_recommendations: Tage til Glasshouse mountains, Moreton Island, North Stradbroke Island, tage til øl- og quizaften på Felons og nyd strandene på Goldcoast (Burleigh)
culture_adjustment: Forholdsvis nemt. Australierne er super hjælpesomme
socializing_tips: De australske studerende var forholds lukkede og havde travlt med deres eget liv, men UQ var fyldt med internationale studerende og er virkelig multikulturelt, så det var super nemt at falde i snak og blive venner med andre internationale studerende
cultural_challenges: Ikke umiddelbart
culture_appreciated: Mine yndlingsting ved Brisbane/Queensland: - vanvittige solnedgange over floden hver aften - folk siger “tak” til buschaufføren, når de går ind og ud af bussen. - der er en vildt god og afslappet køkultur omkring offentlig transport. Folk står i én lige linje på helt op til 20 meter ned ad gaden og venter på bussen og tager det helt stille og roligt med at stige af og på uden af mase. - de er vildt hjælpsomme (især på uni). Hvis man går rundt og ser lidt søgende ud, er folk meget hurtige til at spørge om de kan hjælpe. - de har vildt gode acai bowls (morgenmad)
top3_advice: Forberedt dig på ikke nødvendigvis at få dine ønskede kurser Vær åben og tal til folk Meld dig ind i en klub
other_useful_info: Ved ikke
most_rewarding: At få en masse international venskaber for livet
greatest_challenge: I starten er det hårdt at skulle have styr på alt det praktiske (oprette en bank, oprette mobilnummer, få styr på alle fag, finde bolig) men lige så langsomt lander man i det og falder på plads. Man undervurderer hvor meget krudt man bruger på alle de ting i starten

teaching_comparison: Quite different in some ways. There are a lot more assesments throughout the semester instead of one big exam at the end.
courses_enrolled: Psychological Research Methodology I (PSYC1040) Introduction to Music Psychology (MUSC1300) Music, Wellbeing and Health (MUSC2310) Positive Psychology (PSYC2381)
recommended_courses: Positive Psychology was by far my favorite course. So interesting and engaging with amazing tutors and professors. But I would recommend all my courses.
unexpected_costs: The student visa is very expensive.
cost_comparison: Housing and groceries were more expensive than I thought. Public transport was cheap. It's free to enter most nationalparks and nature areas.
activities_available: Social clubs for everything you could ever want. All types of sport, crafts, music and so on.
activities_recommended: UQ Voices choir for international students. No music experience needed but a very welcoming group and great place to meet friends. The clubs and societies in general. You can absolutely find something within your interests.
weekend_recommendations: North Stradbroke Island, Moreton Island, Gold Coast hinterland, the list for amazing nature and wildlife experiences is never ending. In Brisbane the South Bank area is nice, Kangaroo Point, West End and the botanical gardens.
culture_adjustment: Quite easy. Australians are very welcoming, and there are also a lot of international students, so you absolutely won't feel like an outsider.
socializing_tips: Join the clubs and societies.
cultural_challenges: Everything closes very early.
culture_appreciated: That it's so multicultural, people are generally very open and funny. And the culture around being in nature.
top3_advice: Use sunscreen, join clubs at uni and don't worry if everything seems overwhelming in the first few weeks. It will get better.
other_useful_info: Find a place with air condition!!!! Consider renting an e-bike or something similar. Public transport is NOT as good as in Europe.
most_rewarding: Getting out of my comfort zone and exploring a new part of the world, making great friends along the way
greatest_challenge: Honestly staying in a place without AC during the summer. And also feeling a bit lonely during the first two months. Remember to stay in touch with your friends and family at home.

crucial_aspects: It was important for me to do an exchange in a country, where I normally wouldn't go on vacation. Therefore, I chose Australia, because it was a once in a lifetime opportunity to explore a country for half a year, that is far away from Denmark. Moreover, I wanted to go to a country, where it was easy to travel around during the weekends, and where the weather was good.
overall_comments: It was an unforgettable and amazing experience! I can highly recommend going on exchange in Australia - it has everything: good weather, wonderful nature and beaches, nice people and culture etc.
info_ease: It was very easy. UQ's website was very helpful, and I could easily find information about my courses and the academic calendar was very helpful to get an overview of the semester and the deadlines.
arrival_assistance: We got a lot of information from the councelors at UQ. The first day in the orientation week, we went to an oriention particurly made for exchange students, which was really helpful! Here we got useful information about enrolment of courses, deadlines etc. During the orientation week we also attended several useful seminars about safety in Australia, tour on Campus etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It was an unforgettable and amazing experience! I can highly recommend going on exchange in Australia - it has everything: good weather, wonderful nature and beaches, nice people and culture etc.
registration_process: The UQ website was easy to navigate in. I used the website to register and enrol my courses, find courses etc.
registration_help: It was possible to use the website or sent an e-mail to UQ.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted. I enrolled the courses before I came to Brisbane, and after arrival I had three weeks to change my courses, which was really nice. For example I switched one course after attending the first class.
registration_advice: It is possible to change your course after the semester has started - therefore, don't stress, if you don't like a course. You can easily change it.
academics_comments: It was an unforgettable and amazing experience! I can highly recommend going on exchange in Australia - it has everything: good weather, wonderful nature and beaches, nice people and culture etc.
course_level: As previously described the overall academic level was not that high compared to UCPH. But it also depended on the course. I took some courses in indigenous politics and international relations in Asia Pacific, which was areas/regions I didn't knew much about before going to Australia.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was very different compared to UCPH. At UQ the grade was depended on the attendence and the assigments during the semester, which is different from UCPH, where I normally have one exam in the end of the semester, that counts for the overall grade.
courses_enrolled: Indigenous Policy and Politics, International Relations in Asia-Pacific, Global Governance, Ethics and Human Rights
recommended_courses: I can highly recommend taking a course in indigenous politics! It was very interesting learning about politics, society and culture in regard to the indigenous people of Australia.
unexpected_costs: None.
cost_comparison: Buying alcohol was very expensive - especially beers. But eating take away or eating at restaurants was not as expensive as I thought.
activities_available: As previously described: UQ have so many clubs and there are a lot of opportunities when it comes to sports, social events etc.
activities_recommended: I joined QUEST (club for exchange students) and the surf club, which I would highly recommend joining! The clubs arranged several events during the semester - for example trips to Byron Bay, Noosa and other amazing places in Australia, and it was very easy to get international friends in those clubs.
weekend_recommendations: Just explore as much as Australia as possible :-) Go to Byron Bay, Sydney, Blue Mountains, Melbourne, Noosa, Sunshine Coast, Whitsundays, Cairns, Fraser Island, Uluru etc - there are lots of amazing nature, beaches, authentic surfer towns etc. to explore!
culture_adjustment: It was very easy - the Australian people are so nice and kind! And they have a very relaxed and informal tone and atmosphere.
socializing_tips: I didn't socialize much with locals. I mostly got friends from Europe and the US.
cultural_challenges: None. The Australian culture is so relaxed and informal - it is easy to navigate in the differences between the australian and danish culture.
culture_appreciated: The calm and relaxed culture.
top3_advice: 1. Explore Australia! Brisbane is well located in Australia - it is close to so many nice places. 2. Join the clubs at UQ! 3. Remember to bring factor 50 sunscreen :-)
other_useful_info: None.
most_rewarding: Having the most amazing experiences in the most amazing country and getting new international friendships!
greatest_challenge: I didn't experience many challenges.
