crucial_aspects: I wanted it to be different from Denmark so I wanted to go to some of the southern states in the US. Florida was cheaper than California so that's why i chose USF.
overall_comments: Amazing experience, it was the best five months of my life. Would recommend it everyone who has the opportunity to go.
info_ease: Very easy since a lot of people on campus are ready to help you with finding your school ID, house keys, and where to go. There was also people ready to help with any questions you may have.
arrival_assistance: I arrived at the wrong building and a very nice girl offered to drive me to the housing location since it was a long walk and super hot outside. I met some people at the key pickup place that helped me navigate to my housing.
arrival_comments: We had an orientation just for exchange students which gave a lot of useful information. However it would have been nice to get some information about the area. I found out later that one area outside USF is very unsafe and it's not recommended to walk there, and that would have been nice to know from the start.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Amazing experience, it was the best five months of my life. Would recommend it everyone who has the opportunity to go.
registration_process: When the registration opens you can go into your OASIS account (which is like KU selvbetjening) and type in the course code for the course you want and press submit. Then you are registered right away. The course code can be found on the schedule search for the current semester, where you can also see what time of day the course lectures are and how many spots are available.
registration_help: We went over the course registration at the exchange orientation.
registration_success: Quite successful, however, some of the courses I put on my application for pre-approval was not taught in my semester so I had to re-apply for pre-approval.
registration_advice: You don't have to find your final courses on the first day of class. I ended up registering for 2 more courses than necessary and then dropping the classes I didn't find interesting and adding another one. You can also register for courses in the add/drop week even though you didn't attend the first day of class.
academics_comments: Amazing experience, it was the best five months of my life. Would recommend it everyone who has the opportunity to go.
course_level: The academic level is for the most part was lower than at UCPH. Even the ones they called "high level courses" where they warned us about the amount of studying required was not very challenging and didn't really require that much studying. For the most part I just paid attention during the lectures and did my homework, and I got B's and A's.
teaching_comparison: The exams required a lot less independent thinking and much more that you remember a bunch of the material from the lecture slides. I had to get used to studying to remember and not necessarily to understand. In my courses we mostly had 75 minute lectures, and then a lot of quizzes and a few assignments. The amount of quizzes are obviously higher than UCPH and the assignments were usually less time consuming than what I am used to.
courses_enrolled: Molecular Microbiology Molecular Biology of the Gene Nutrition and Disease Introduction to Earth Science
recommended_courses: Molecular Microbiology was a great course. The professor was great at teaching and the work load was also fitting. If you've taken any microbiology courses at home this one will build on that knowledge.
unexpected_costs: The TOEFL English test for 2000 DKK and the cost of setting up my room and getting cleaning supplies for the apartment. I also had a spontaneous trip that required a plane ticket.
cost_comparison: You can get a pretty cheap phone plan through Mint Mobile with call, texts and data which is what most exchange students did (it is cheaper than going to Target/Walmart to get one). A lot of food was more expensive than expected like meat and fruit, but that wouldn't have been an issue if I had a bigger meal plan.
activities_available: If you're really good at a sport you can go to try-outs for sport clubs and maybe join a team. That is one way to make friends and be part of a team, and that way you also have the opportunity to compete outside USF. If you want to play a sport for fun you can join an intermural sport team. You also have trainings and competitions but only at USF against other intermural teams. They obviously also have football, basketball, volleyball and soccer teams where you can get free student tickets to go watch the games. If you are interested in joining any clubs they have quite a few events where you can hear all about them and other social events. USF have patio Tuesdays (first Tuesday every month) which is just a social event, and Bulls Nite Out every other Friday where they stream movies and have some activities.
activities_recommended: I personally found a lot of friends at the Bulls Nite Out events and the tailgate parties before football games. All the social event are on the app BullsConnect where you can read about them and see when and where, and there is a lot every day of the week. Just go to as many of them as you like and talk to people.
weekend_recommendations: Miami, Cocoa Beach, Clearwater Beach, Crystal River, Lettuce Lake Park, Rainbow River Springs, Downtown Tampa, Orlando and the whole Disney area (Disney Springs), Universal Studios and Busch Gardens.
culture_adjustment: It was pretty easy since I knew the language and the culture is somewhat similar to Denmark.
socializing_tips: If you initiate a conversation they are all super easy to talk to and will ask a lot of questions. Sometimes they will also start the conversation. Make plans with them to keep in touch and you will likely become friends.
cultural_challenges: Metal detectors at every event and no-bag policies.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness and how they are willing to take in foreign students. Everybody I met were so nice to me and I even got invited home at Thanksgiving.
top3_advice: Trust the process, everything will work out and you will figure everything out little by little. Be open minded to all the people you meet and you will definitely make friends. Try new things and don't be scared to push some of your limits.
other_useful_info: Take advantage of the Bull Runner busses on campus - you can use them for free if you show them your USF ID. Also the busses outside campus is free if you show them your ID. The busses are useful when you have to go to Target or Walmart the first day to get all your stuff for your room. The fifth floor of the library is the best one for a quiet study with new seating and the whole floor is quiet.
most_rewarding: How many amazing people I have met and to try the college experience in America in the American school system.
greatest_challenge: To adjust to their school system since the exams were quite different from those at UCPH and I needed to study differently than I was used to. Also, it felt lonely in the beginning when you don't know a lot of people yet. I was the only Danish student and everyone was hanging out with people from their own country in the beginning so I went to a lot of events on my own.
other_comments: No

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne opleve, hvordan det var at studere i USA, og på USF synes jeg virkelig man fik den oplevelse på en positiv måde.
overall_comments: Jeg kan klart anbefale at tage til USF, da jeg havde et så godt ophold med god vejledning undervejs, gode faciliteter dernede og mødte en masse gode mennesker på vejen, og så er Florida et fantastisk sted at tage på udveksling.
info_ease: Det var relativt nemt at finde de informationer man skulle bruge, da man i tiden op til udvekslingen var blevet informeret godt om dette fra koordinatoren fra USF af.
arrival_assistance: Man blev guidet ret godt på vej fra ankomst til hvor man skulle hen for at finde sin lejlighed, tilmelding af fag, finde rundt på campus osv. samt var der massere af ressourcer og andre hjælpemidler til dette hvis man var i tvivl om det mindste.
arrival_comments: Jeg var meget tilfreds med ankomsten, det eneste minus kunne dog være at man fik rigtig mange informationer de første dage om forskellige portaler, apps, events osv. på samme tid med at man lige skulle lære campus og alt andet at vide så man ikke lige huskede allesammen.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Jeg kan klart anbefale at tage til USF, da jeg havde et så godt ophold med god vejledning undervejs, gode faciliteter dernede og mødte en masse gode mennesker på vejen, og så er Florida et fantastisk sted at tage på udveksling.
registration_process: Op til udvekslingen blev man guidet meget i forhold til tilmelding af fag osv. fra USF, da de har en koordinator der kontakter en så snart man er godkendt til universitetet, og på den måde holder en i hånden igennem hele processen.
registration_help: De havde som sagt en koordinator fra USF af der hjælper med alt det praktiske som udvekslingsstuderende, og hvis de ikke har svaret er de gode til at sende en videre til hvem der så kan hjælpe.
registration_success: Som økonomistuderende er det lidt bøvlet med tilmelding af fag i første fase, da man skal sende syllabi (stort set kursusbeskrivelser) for alle beståede fag, samt skal disse så godkendes før man kan tilmelde sig fag, hvilken kan tage lidt længere tid end andre uddannelser som jeg forstår det, men udover det, så var det fint nok..
registration_advice: Begynd processen så snart som muligt, da det er irriterende at skulle stresse med det tæt på at man skal afsted, samt kan flere dele af processen også have ventetid, hvorfor det er meget bedre at gå i gang så snart det er muligt.
academics_comments: Jeg kan klart anbefale at tage til USF, da jeg havde et så godt ophold med god vejledning undervejs, gode faciliteter dernede og mødte en masse gode mennesker på vejen, og så er Florida et fantastisk sted at tage på udveksling.
course_level: Jeg var afsted på første år af min kandidat, så derfor kunne jeg selv vælge om jeg ville indskrives som undergrad (4 fag) eller graduate (3 fag) på USF, hvor jeg så valgte undergrad, men der tog jeg så 4. års undergraduate fag, så niveauet burde minde meget om kandidatfag, selvom de dog var lidt nemmere.
teaching_comparison: Til dels minder det om København da flere af de fag jeg havde bestod af forelæsninger, hvor man bare sidder og lytter med, men så har man også muligheden for at vælge 1 fag som foregår online, hvilket jeg synes var rart da man på den måde har lidt nemmere ved at organisere sin uge.
courses_enrolled: Economics of Business Strategy Retirement Planning Financial Institutions/Markets Advanced Corporation Finance
recommended_courses: Retirement Planning var faktisk er ret sjovt fag da man fik en anden indsigt i pensionsplaner i USA med fokus på finansieringsdelen. Dog er der en masse af disse planer samt en masse regler for hver af planerne, som gør det lidt sværere at følge med i til en start som en fra Danmark, når man ikke kender nogle af pensionsplanerne fra USA udover en klassisk 401(k).
unexpected_costs: Jeg ved ikke hvad man kan sige der var uforudsete udgifter, men man kan selv afgøre hvor meget "ekstra" man bruger alt efter hvor meget man regner med at rejse under sit udvekslingsforløb, og så løber det selvfølgelig op.
cost_comparison: Normal indkøb af dagligdagsvarer er langt dyrere end i Danmark, men dette gælder for hele USA.
activities_available: Der er muligheder for alle og enhver, fra løbeklubber, til religiøse klubber eller events, politiske debatter og demonstrationer og bare events hvor alle er velkommen. Derudover er der mange sportsfaciliteter på campus som jeg fik brugt en del, da de er så nemt tilgængelige, og der er også 2 fitnesscentre på campus som er gratis at benytte.
activities_recommended: Jeg ville anbefale at blive en del af nogle af de sportsklubber der er tilgængelige da det er en nem måde at møde nye mennesker, og når man alligevel er i USA kunne man sagtens vælge nogle af de sportsgrene som måske ikke er lige så store i Danmark som eventuelt Flag Football, Ultimate eller Basketball, men ellers så ville jeg anbefale at udnytte de faciliteter der er til rådighed fra USF af, heriblandt enten den udendørs pool ved fitness centret "The Fit" eller poolen i The Greek Village, da det jo i Florida ofte er godt vejr til at være udenfor.
weekend_recommendations: Rejs rundt i landet eller staten eller oplev i hvert fald ting når du er i Florida. Jeg kan klart anbefale at sejle kajak i Crystal River, da man sejler blandt utallige Manatees, som svømmer helt tæt på en. Og hvis man er til det kan man tage på en gunrange og skyde med store rifler. Hvis man er over 21 er bylivet i Tampa også ret godt downtown enten i Soho eller ved Ybor, samt er der også en fed rooftop bar der hedder M Bird, hvor man har udsigt over Tampas skyline.
culture_adjustment: Amerikanere er meget åbne for at tale med en og meget venlige til et punkt, hvor det næsten virker som falsk venlighed, men hvis man ikke er bleg for at snakke med fremmede skal man bare være åben for dette og så kan man sagtens vende sig til den amerikanske kultur nemt.
socializing_tips: Jeg mødte mange af de andre udvekslingsstuderende jeg snakkede med i løbet af semestret gennem orientation en af de første dage, men derudover så deltag til så mange events som muligt de første par dage (her kunne disse findes især på BullsConnect), da dette også er en god måde at møde andre amerikanere. Der var også nogle af de andre udvekslingsstuderende (briterne som dog var her 2 semestre), som tilmeldte sig frat-huse, som på den måde også er en god måde at møde en masse andre amerikanere og lokale samt holder de forskellige frats en masse events i løbet af semestret, men dette er selvfølgelig kun hvis man er til den slags.
cultural_challenges: Personligt var der ikke noget ved den amerikanske kultur som var specielt "svært" at vende sig til, da de på mange måde minder om folk fra Danmark.
culture_appreciated: Som også nævnt tidligere er det jeg nok synes var bedst ved den amerikanske kultur den venlighed som de fleste amerikanere udsteder, og især fra amerikanere i sydstaterne (der er også et udtryk for dette der kaldes southern hospitality), hvor folk i høj grad er interesseret i at høre mere når man siger at man er fra Danmark blandt andet.
top3_advice: Jeg kan i HØJ grad anbefale at tage på udveksling til USA, og hvis du tager til specifikt USF, så når du ankommer så gå til det med åbne arme og så skal du nok have et godt semester. På USF (og Florida generelt) skal man dog være opmærksom på at når man ankommer om sommeren er det ulideligt varmt og det værste er fugtigheden som i høj grad minder om at begå sig i en regnskov. Om sommeren og tidlig efterår er det også regnsæson, så man kan godt komme ud for at der på daglig basis kommer et kæmpe regnskyl og tordenvejr om eftermiddagen i små 20 minutter og så er det væk igen. Til sidst er efteråret i Florida også hurricane-season, så der er høj risiko for at man nok kommer til at opleve sådan en i sin tid på USF.
other_useful_info: Det mest skræmmende ved udvekslingen på USF var nok ideen om at tage på et universitet langt væk fra Danmark og ikke kende en eneste anden person. Men hvis man går ind til udvekslingen med troen på at man nok skal møde andre og at det nok skal gå, så skal man lige over de første uger hvor man ikke kender så mange, og derefter skal det nok gå.

greatest_challenge: Det sværeste var nok egentligt at tage beslutningen om at tage på udveksling og så alt det praktiske op til udvekslingen, men idet man kommer frem går alt sådan set godt og nemt.

Men hey, det hele flaskede sig, og det er kun nogle lidt dårlige 2 timer jeg snakker om her.

Jeg ansøgte på deadline dag og jeg er så taknemmelig for, at jeg tog afsted. Det er med høj sandsynlighed den eneste chance du får i livet for at leve i USA. Jeg kan ikke anbefale det nok.
course_level: Jeg endte mit ophold med tre A's og et enkelt B. Når man siger, at USA har et lavere niveau på universiteterne, så snakker de sandt. KU og Danmark har et højere niveau, men undervisningsformen er også bare ekstremt meget anderledes herovre. Mit cybersecurity kursus var svært og udfordrede mig en del. Mine andre 3 kurser var nice og havde en meget rolig hastighed. Hvis du blot møder op til undervisning og laver dine lektier, så kan du aldrig helt gå galt i byen uanset hvilket kursus du vælger. Deres kurser er inddelt i levels der svarer til deres sværhedsgrad og hvor langt de er på uni. Fx så er et level 3000 kursus mindre komplieret end et level 4000 kursus, og du har typisk et level 3000 kursus på tredje år. Jeg havde et enkelt level 4000 kursus, som svarer til et master kursus hjemme i Danmark. Det var virkelig ligetil, så du behøver ikke være bange for tallet.
teaching_comparison: Dette er nok det, som er mest anderledes mellem KU og USF. På KU har vi typisk en endelig eksamen som tæller for 100% af karakteren. Vi har også typisk en masse afleveringer inden, som vi skal have godkendt for at kunne gå til eksamen. Og der bliver heller ikke taget fravær. Når du tager et kursus på USF, så er det meget vigtigt, at du læser kursets syllabus først. Derinde står der alt hvad kurset indebærer, hvor det vigtigste er hvordan din karakter bliver talt. Typisk så har du en masse quizzer, der måske tæller for 15% af din karakter. Så har du afleveringer, der måske tæller for 25% af kurset. Så har du en midterm, som er en form for eksamen, der tæller for 25%, og så har du en final exam, der også tæller for sådan 30%. De sidste 5-10% er typisk for fravær. Dette eksempel er dog KUN et eksempel. Alle kurser er fuldkommen forskellige, og især på hvordan de tæller karakteren, så vær meget opmærksom på hvad du kan og ikke kan tillade dig at gøre i hver kursus. Du har typisk bestået et kursus, hvis du får over 67%. Det lyder måske en smule højt, men tro mig, det er ikke svært, hvis du blot laver dine lektier, som der jo tæller for meget af din karakter. Det betyder også, at du kan tage det lidt mere rolig til dine eksamener. Det er der ekstremt meget værdi i, da du gerne vil bruge din sidste tid sammen med dine venner og ikke foran en computer eller bog.
courses_enrolled: Foundations of Cybersecurity (CIS 3213), Intro to Computer Programming (CGS 2060), Web Systems for IT (CGS 3853) og Cloud Computing for IT (CIS 4083)
recommended_courses: Hvis du godt kan lide cyber- og informationssikkerhed så er Foundations of Cybersecurity (CIS 3213) et meget fint kursus. Kurset er online, som er en smule underligt i starten, men pensum er virkelig stort og godt. Og underviseren er mega vild med feltet, som gør at kurset er virkelig gennemtænkt.
unexpected_costs: Dit værelse har intet, så du skal købe alt til det. Det indebærer alt køkken grej og senge grej også. Bøger er også monster dyre, så find dem hellere online gratis end at købe dem. Supermarkeder er også ekstremt dyre her, så dagligvare er ligesom Danmark, hvis ikke dyrere nogle gange. Uber er også virkelig dyrt, hvis du kører alene. Hvis du kører med 2-4 andre, så er det virkelig billigt. Blev også nødt til at købe en billig windows computer, da en af mine kurser krævede det, hvor jeg personligt har MAC. Så husk at tjek efter det i kursets syllabus.
cost_comparison: Bøger og mad. At flyve rundt i selve USA er virkelig billigt, så udnyt det imens du er der.
activities_available: Mindre sportsklubber her og der.
activities_recommended: Kan ikke rigtigt anbefale noget her desværre. Måske flag football holdet, da det er det jeg har hørt mest om.
weekend_recommendations: Her er hvor det sjove begynder. Florida og USA tilbyder så mange forskellige oplevelser. Og som jeg tidligere har skrevet, så er indenrigs fly virkelig billige. Tampa som by har nogle små perler her og der, men er ellers rimelig kedelig. Hyde park er meget fin og Busch Gardens er virkelig fed. Derudover er Ybor og Soho nogle fede steder at tage i byen. Bare husk dit pas, fordi de er fuldkommen ligeglade med dit kørekort, men mest i Soho og ikke så meget i Ybor. Rundt om Tampa Bay er der Clearwater, Sarasota og St. Petersburg. Dem bliver du nødt til at se. De har alle virkelig fede og kæmpe strande, som er super nice. Clearwater er meget sådan en ferieby. Sarasota er virkelig smuk og St. Petersburg er rig med kultur og fede bysteder. Orlando er også kun 1,5 timer i bil/bus væk. Der så jeg NBA, og der kan man selvfølgelig også besøge Disneyworld, Universtal studios og alt muligt andet sjovt. Vi tog også 4 dage til Miami, og lejede et Airbnb der. Det var magisk og Miami er virkelig en speciel, magisk og underlig by. det er et MUST. Vi tog også til Puerto Rico i 4 dage, som er virkelig tæt på i fly og som byder på tropiske scener. Junglen er super fed at udforske der. Ellers så er amerikansk fodbold jo en religion herovre. Når fodboldholdet spiller, så handler ALT om den kamp. Der bliver holdt kæmpe fester uden foran stadion inden kampen, som de kalder for "tailgates". Dem SKAL du tage til, det er super sjovt. Ellers så er der basketball og hockey du kan se. I weekenderne er der fester rundt omkring du kan tage til eller bare holde din egen. Selvom Campus er alkoholfrit, så er der altid alkohol rundt omkring. Det handler mest om at kende de rigtige mennesker eller skabe dit eget.
culture_adjustment: Det var rimelig nemt. Alle er virkelig imødekommende. Du skal blot turde at snakke med folk, selvom det nogle gange kan føles lidt ubehageligt. Du skal blot vide, at det synes de ikke.
socializing_tips: Orienteringsdag er alfa/omega her. På orienteringsdag mødes du med alle andre udvekslingsstuderende og får den information i skal bruge. Snak med de andre europæere! På aller første dag, der blev vi en gruppe af 12 europæere der snakker sammen, og vi har vitterligt brugt hver eneste dag sammen siden. Vi er fuldkommen uadskillige. Gennem dem møder du dine amerikanske venner, fordi de med høj sandsynlighed vil have amerikanske roommates. Du vil typisk bo enten 2 eller 4 i en lejlighed/værelse. Giv alt hvad du har de første 2-3 uger, så du danner et virkelig godt socialt fundament. Derefter kan du slappe lidt mere af og dyrke dig selv også.
cultural_challenges: Der var ikke rigtig nogle forskelle, som endte med at have en særlig betydning for mig. Gik mest rundt sammen med europæere, og de minder bare meget om danskere, så der er intet der. Spisetider var det eneste, som vi skulle blive enige om haha. Franskmænd og spaniere kan jo godt lide at spise meget sent.
culture_appreciated: Høfligheden. Folk siger "sorry" for nærmest alting herhenne. Det bliver næsten for meget til sidst. Amerikanere vil altid høre om din kultur og især hvorfor du valgte USA.
top3_advice: 1. KOM TIL ORIENTERINGSDAG. Der vil du møde stort set alle dine venner og egentlig bare folk, som er i den præcis samme båd som dig. Bliver gode venner med dem, og brug dem til at rejse rundt med og opleve ting sammen med. Bliv gode venner med deres amerikanske roommates. 2. Husk at rolige dage også skal være en del af din rejse. Det er ikke alle dage, hvor du skal tage et specielt sted hen eller holde en fest. At være på udvekslings er dyrt, både for din pengepung, men også for dit sociale batteri. Pas på dig selv og tag en aften i sengen/sofaen en gang i mellem uden at have nogen form for dårlig samvittighed. 3. tag andre steder hen end bare Tampa Bay området. Rejs et sted hen under thanksgiving eller på andre tidspunkter. USA byder på så ekstremt meget, og det er virkelig billigt at rejse rundt i landet.
other_useful_info: Købte selv 80 meal swipes med 350 dining dollars eller noget i den retning. Brug et enkelt swipe om dagen og suppler med mindre ting du køber fra et supermarked. På den måde får du mest for pengene. Lad vær med at drikke med folk under 18 år og lad vær med at blive taget i at drikke mere end 1 gang offentligt. Du må drikke så meget du vil på dit værelse, men tag åbent alkohol ud fra lejligheden. Tag ikke i The Hub mellem 15-16 for der er de i gang med at lave nyt mad til senere. HUSK at tjekke din USF mail hver eneste dag, for der får du virkelig meget information om events og dine kurser. Husk at lave ALLE dine lektier, da det vil betyde, at du ikke behøver særlig gode resultater til eksamenerne. Lav dit værelse til et hjem. Du bor der i 4 måneder, og det er overraskende dejligt, at det er pænt at se på. Pak rigelig med shorts og T-shirts. De første 2-3 måneder er virkelig varme, hvor den første måned skildre sig meget ud. Nogle gange er det for meget. De første 2 måneder er det regnsæson og hurricane season. Nogle gange om dagen, så vil det styrtregne i 20 minutter og så være høj sol efter. Så køb en paraply. Oplevede selv ikke nogle hurricanes, men det er en reel ting herovre. Området rundt om campus er ikke så godt, så lad vær med at vandre rundt der om natten. Har selv gjort det et par gange uden nogle som helst problemer, men amerikanerne anbefaler, at du ikke gør det. Campus er dog fuldkommen sikkert at gå rundt på, så det behøver du ikke være bange for. Der er politi overalt, og USF har også deres eget politi, sjovt nok. Det siger sig selv, men en adapter er vigtig for opladning. Tag 2 kufferter med, så du kan tage en masse af dine ting med og du har rigelig med plads til nye ting, du køber hernede. Der er meget mere, men kan ikke komme i tanke om det.
most_rewarding: Mine venner. De venner jeg har mødt her er venner for livet. Vi har oplevet alt for første gang sammen, og vi har dannet et bånd som er virkelig særligt. To af europæerne bode i Kosove 521, som vi har tilbragt 80% af vores tid i. De boede med 2 amerikanere, som vi blev gode venner med. Amerikanerne introducerede os til deres venner, som vi så også blev gode venner med. Du danner også bare et tæt forhold til USF. Det er bare et fantastisk sted, som jeg ønsker alle at kunne opleve.
greatest_challenge: At styre sine penge. Alt koster penge og alt er mega spændende. Jeg kunne 100% have styret mine penge bedre, men jeg har også levet præcis som jeg ønskede, og det er meget vigtigt synes jeg. Så tag afsted med et godt økonomisk fundament. Det gavner helt ekstremt meget. At finde roen til at være i sit eget selskab var også svært nogle gange. Flere aftener havde jeg brug for at være for mig selv, men mine venner mødtes og hyggede, og det var svært i starten. Mit råd er, at du går all in de første uger, og så trapper stille og roligt ned efter. Nu kan jeg være alene, når jeg har lyst og jeg nyder stilheden. Det giver mig også lysten til at fyre den af dagen efter.
other_comments: Hvis du overvejer USF, så LÆS alle mine kommentarer. Læste selv disse rapporter grundigt, og det var derfor jeg valgte det her sted. Jeg elsker det. Jeg elsker USF. Det vil forevigt være et andet hjem for mig, og en periode af mit liv, hvor jeg aldrig har følt mig mere fri. Og det lyder måske som meget, når du læser det her hjemme i kolde Danmark og overvejer hvad du skal gøre, men jeg kan ikke sige det nok gange... Du skal vælge USF. Det er det bedste valg du tager i dit liv, hvis du bare turde gøre det. Jeg sidder alene på mit værelse i greek village og skriver dette lige nu. I morgen flyver jeg væk fra USF. Jeg vil ikke hjem. Jeg vil ikke have, at det er slut. Jeg har haft en fantastisk tid. Det er de følelser, der vil gå igennem dig, hvis du vælger USF. Hvis du gør det, så hedder jeg -NAME REDACTED, og jeg kan hjælpe dig med alle spørgsmål og udfordringer du må have. Tak for at læse min rapport.

course_level: Most of the modules were lectures and some prerecorded videos. I took a module in education, where the class was more of a seminar, which I really liked.
teaching_comparison: It was quite different, for example, there wasn't a curriculum as we know it from home, but instead a list of recommended readings. Moreover, I think the focus was more on current research and not so much on theories. Also, the final grade was made up of different things, for example, quizzes, a presentation, research participation and an essay in the exam period.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Educational Psychology Current & Emerging Issues in Psycho-Oncology & Pain Research Psychology of Attractiveness Social Justice & Inclusive Education
recommended_courses: I really liked Introduction to Educational Psychology and Social Justice & Inclusive Education, first and foremost because of the professors teaching the classes. The classes always covered intersting content, so I really liked going to them. I also liked Psychology of Attractiveness, because it was so different from the modules I have taken previously. The module covered why people fall in love, relationships, attraction etc. Also, the professor teaching the module is really great, and always included small, funny tasks for the students.
unexpected_costs: Since I received the bus card, I didn't have to spend money on transportation in Southampton. However, since I went on several trips and took the train, this was pretty expensive. Therefore, it's a good idea to buy a railcard, which gives you a discount on all your journeys. Also, I had to buy some kitchen equipment, since some were provided but not everything that I needed.
cost_comparison: Grocery shopping and going out for dinner at restaurants and pubs was cheaper than in Denmark. The train was around the same as in Denmark, while housing (at least the Uni halls) was more expensive than in Copenhagen.
activities_available: At the university, there are more than 300 clubs and societies, which mean that there is something for everybody. For example, you can find creative-, cultural-, and sports clubs. At the beginning of the semester, there was an event, where the clubs members told about their clubs, which was a good way to hear about the many opportunities.
activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend joining some societies. This is a good way to make new friends and get to know the locals. I joined a sports society, and they had a training and a social event each week (for example going to a pub together), which is very common for societies. I found it nice that you try a new sport and get to know people.
weekend_recommendations: Try the local/English food at the pubs, go to a football match, take the train and explore the cities around Southampton - Bath, Brighton, Bournemouth, Isle of Wight etc. There are so many beautiful places to go, especially by the coast, where there are some really nice walks.
culture_adjustment: Very easy! English people are very friendly and welcoming, and therefore it was easy to meet both locals and other exchange students
socializing_tips: Go to the events at school (especially in the beginning of the semester), karaoke nights at the pub at campus, and joining a society
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: People are so nice and friendly, and very easy to talk to. I think that is very different from home, where most people never get to meet and talk with exchange students.
top3_advice: 1)Enjoy the campus experience and make the most of it by joining some societies and attending events at campus. 2)I experienced the exam period to be harder than at home since the deadlines of the exams were very close to each other, so try to prepare for exams in advance to make the exam period less stressful. 3)Explore the cities and nature around Southampton, often it's only 1-2 hours by train from the city.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: To meet so many nice people, and get friends from different countries in Europe. It was also nice to try living and experiencing university in a different country.
greatest_challenge: I don't think I would say that I experienced any greater challenges during my stay, but I guess it was a bit of a challenge, in the beginning, to adjust to the way of teaching and writing assignments since it was different from home.
other_comments: no

courses_enrolled: The Exercise and Health Management. crucial_aspects: The academic opportunities were important to me. I knew from friends and research that St Andrews University had an excellent school of IR. Which I highly valued. I had learned that the teachers were very personal with their students and classes very small and intimate to improve the participation of every individual in the class. I was also very intrigued by the scenery. It is a beautiful old town with long beaches on one side and green fields on the other side of the town. Furthermore, I prioritised an English speaking destination to improve my English.
overall_comments: Overall I loved the destination and the experience. I made some great friends and was lucky to get close with many permanent students. The only downsides of my exchange were mainly due to covid.
info_ease: It was not easy to find information upon arrival, but I think this is mainly because of Covid. Because of covid, the help desk was closed - and there honestly wasn't much help to get from the school. Luckily my roommates were very friendly and helpful. The school didn't share information on the condition of our schooling before the term started, and our schedule was not ready before classes began either.
arrival_assistance: As mentioned, there wasn't any assistance upon arrival. But throughout the semester, the global office was very present and helpful. They even hosted events and socials for exchange students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Overall I loved the destination and the experience. I made some great friends and was lucky to get close with many permanent students. The only downsides of my exchange were mainly due to covid.
registration_process: I registered through an online portal and was in contact with the global office during the process. Overall it was straightforward.
registration_help: Upon registration, the global office was very helpful and quickly replied to my questions and worries.
registration_success: Yes, I was. The registration of classes happened very late. Almost only a couple of weeks before class started. Because I needed to be enrolled in the specific courses, KU asked for, the lateness of the process was a worrying factor. I was told that one of the classes was full but that I had to wait till late August to talk to my course coordinator. Obviously, this was a bit worrying, but as soon as late August came and I could talk to my coordinator, he was incredibly helpful and ensured that everything got sorted out.
registration_advice: The registration is closed over the summer, so there is no need to stress unnecessarily at that time, but make sure to contact them as soon as it opens in August, and they will be helpful.
academics_comments: Overall I loved the destination and the experience. I made some great friends and was lucky to get close with many permanent students. The only downsides of my exchange were mainly due to covid.
course_level: The levels I took was supposed to be relatively high. Courses you take on your last year of the bachelor. But I don't think the level felt necessarily more elevated than the courses I've taken at Copenhagen University. There was, of course, a language barrier at first, but I fast overcame that.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching is very different from KU. There was a lot less teaching in the classes I took and a lot more time to study yourself, but the teachers offer lots of personal office hours. Ultimately, students do have the chance to get more face to face teaching from the professors. Versus KU, which schedules a lot of in-class time with professors and older students to help one understand the course.
courses_enrolled: IR3056 Political Leadership: Theories and History IR3039 International Relations of the European Union
recommended_courses: IR3039 International Relations of the European Union
unexpected_costs: School events turned out to be rather expensive. And sports clubs was an unexpected cost as well.
cost_comparison: I got lucky with housing which could otherwise have been 8000 dkk per month. School events though where very expensive. Between 1000 and 2000 dkk per month, as every big school event was between 400 and 800 dkk and smaller events was 80 and 150 dkk.
activities_available: Very many sports clubs were available and lots of social and creative clubs as well.
activities_recommended: Join as many sports clubs as possible. They give you a chance to try new sports which is so much fun and get new friends.
weekend_recommendations: The Islands and highlands.
culture_adjustment: Easy. The Scottish culture (and British as lot's of British people study at St Andrews) is quite easy to get on with. The humour is sort of familiar to the Danish humour.
socializing_tips: Join the different clubs, and don't be afraid to talk to people.
cultural_challenges: I think it was rather the culture of the school than the actual culture that was a big change from what I'm used to. It is a culture where you either socialize or study. There is no time for a chill. But that was a part of the experience and really fun.
culture_appreciated: Most of it. The humour is great, the society and social life at St Andrews, the competitive culture that makes every student aim for the highest.
top3_advice: If the student is going on exchange from Danish university they are usually older than student living in student housing, take your time to find a good housing situation with older students. Be aware that the semester is very short. I would recommend maybe doing two semesters. It is an expensive destination.
other_useful_info: Use the facebook groups: fx find a room st andrews and contact the global office.
most_rewarding: Finding my roommates and friends. And visiting the highlands and islands. The nature in Scotland is unbelievable.
greatest_challenge: I don't think there were any great exchange related challenges. Being one of the only danish exchanges and living among permanent students, I did have to put myself out there a lot. But it was for the best and I got some great friends and the true St Andrews experience from it.

greatest_challenge: Being away from your family and friends for so long

crucial_aspects: The academic opportunities and prospects of going abroad at St Andrews seemed great, as University of St Andrews is listed as one of the most renowned universities in Great Britain. Moreover, I have British family connections and wanted to explore both Scotland and England whilst improving my written and oral English.
info_ease: I was really happy about my exchange in St Andrews, especially due to my choice of accommodation at Deans Court, which proved to be a crucial addition to my stay because I gained many friends and connections there who were current master’s and PhD students. This meant they were generally older and more on wavelength than bachelor students.
arrival_assistance: So much help. They have a great student service. I got relocated to Deans Court because I couldn’t afford DRA, and in the beginning, they said no but changed their stance. They helped me a lot getting the electives I needed and proved great support when I had a potentially unsettling situation with a future peer (which proved to be perfectly fine in the end, it was just a person I was going to live with, and the student services were invaluable and supportive). They physically helped me find my accommodation and made sure I could borrow bed linen for a few days before I sorted it out and got some for free via St and ReUse. Also, Andrew is a sweetheart, he’s the janitor at Deans and just lovely.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Everything is in-person, so quite easy actually. I was stressing a lot about it before-hand but it proved out to be quite ok. But go the the academic fayres in September (start of term), because in this way you get to chat to the teachers about their subjects etc.. It's just a lot of e-mailing and admin back and forth, honestly.
registration_help: You get appointed a personal supervisor for academic advising, who helps you choose your subjects. So its really quite practical.
registration_success: Got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Trust in the process! All the admin work will pay off and calm down - just get it over and done with, so it's not hanging over your head all the time. And ask the university for help, if you need it. They're really friendly in the adminstration.
course_level: CO4038 - Environmental Imaginations (level 4000 bachelor 4-års studerende) SA5020 - Anthropology, Art and Perception 1 (master level 5000) CO4034 - Utopia: Past, Present, Futures (level 4000 bachelor 4-års studerende)
teaching_comparison: More formal. I was not that academically challenging, honestly... It was mostly the big amount of work you had to do, which was quite stressful. At UCPH we're used to writing our exams in January, and here, the exams are written throughout the semester.
courses_enrolled: CO4038 - Environmental Imaginations (level 4000 bachelor 4-års studerende) SA5020 - Anthropology, Art and Perception 1 (master level 5000) CO4034 - Utopia: Past, Present, Futures (level 4000 bachelor 4-års studerende)
recommended_courses: I wish I had gone for some teachers I had heard good things about, or courses such as: R4572 - Economy of Anger: Marxism, Psychoanalysis and the Politics of Status and SD4118 - Extractive Environments. Because really, it's more about the teacher than the specific subject. Because they influence the subject so much Mattia is lovely in Anthropology, Art and Perception, but he's style of teaching kind of sucks and is extremely vague and fluffy. Damiano Benvegnu is also kind of Meh... But I liked Nial Sreenan (Utopia)! I would recommend 'auditing' subjects as well, which you can request to do. Basically just following a course without taking the exams and being officially inscribed.
unexpected_costs: Costs are extremely high! Cost of housing: easily 7500-10.000 - mine was 40.000 total for 3,5 months in catered accommodation :O Supermarket prices are super high Cost of balls etc are easily 50 pounds, and it's also quite expensive to join societies and activities
cost_comparison: Same as above. Everything was more expensive...
activities_available: Honestly, everything your heart desires. Huge tradition for societies and clubs at Andrews
activities_recommended: Loved "Caledonian Society" - Dancing Scottish Reels once a week Violin lessons at Laidlaw Music Centre with Gordon St Leonard's chapel choir Debate nights with the Tories Breakaway hillwalking club Mountaineering club Going to church once in a while in a cloak (sooo many beautiful churches) Clay Pigeon shooting for people watching the rich (but it's a rip-off) join the balls even if they're expensive!
weekend_recommendations: Going on trips to the highlands - Isle of Skye, Fort William, etc. Join trips via Breakaway or Mountaineering Club
culture_adjustment: Very easy, although it's quite conservative which you have to be prepared for
socializing_tips: Join everything you can, and say yes to all the possibilities in the first few weeks. And then see what you like. Most importantly, go to the academic/sports fayres, and give-it-a-go lessons at the societies.
cultural_challenges: Many Americans and many privileged people... Especially the bachelor students. Usually, the master's students are a little older (21-35 ish) and have had to work or be on fully paid scholarships in order top afford a master's, which means the master's and PhDs are usually a little older. So can actually really recommend going here as part of a master's exchange, if you're considering it.
culture_appreciated: I liked the respect for traditions, the Britishness, and observing the weird conservativeness. The cloaks! Coming from a very leftist and communal life here in Copenhagen, it was a cultural shock for sure but I really did enjoy parts of it!
top3_advice: 1) It's pricey. If you can't afford it, think whether you'd rather go to another country where you can receive Erasmus money. Even when trying to save money, with SU and scholarships (13,500) DKK) I ended up spending 25K extra. 2) Take time to find a good place to live! It matters a lot, I think... At least it did for me. 3) Join all the societies and activities you can. That's what made it worthwhile for me. And then ask for extensions for assignments, lol.
other_useful_info: Utilise StAndReuse and the charity shops to get things such as duvets, sheets, towels, plates etc.
most_rewarding: The general dedication throughout the whole campus! Everybody, from staff to students were just incredibly dedicated to making it a good and worthwhile experience both academically and socially. I think that's what you get from being at a privileged and Ivy-league-ish institution, honestly... It's both really nice and slightly depressing.
greatest_challenge: I was sick for 3 weeks during my stay and had to go to the doctor's 6 times because of different infections:// so remember to sign up for the doctor's! It's free in St Andrews, and so is prescription medicine, which is helpful. And the academic stress as well from the assignments! The best advice is to just suck it up, write them and pull and few all-nighters if you have to. There's honestly so much work and it's just part of the experience. You learn a lot from it though!

crucial_aspects: That St Andrews is a renowned university, where I knew that I could get at least as good teaching as I would have in Copenhagen. And that with St Andrews I would get to experience a wholly different university life than what we have in Denmark.
overall_comments: Overall I found the experience very satisfactory.
info_ease: Very easy. St Andrews is used to handling loads of international students. The matriculation process was quite straightforward and well communicated.
arrival_assistance: University shuttle bus from airport to St Andrews. If you stay in a hall (university accommodation), there will be people there to greet you and give you all the information needed. During matriculation week (the first week of the semester), you will be able to meet with your academic advisor if needs be to talk about your module choices. To confirm your module choices, you will get an appointment with the university where you will talk to a member of staff about your preferences. It is not possible to know for certain, that you will be able to get a spot on your preferred modules before matriculation week. Each module has a cap on the amount of students, that can take it. However I found, that they were able to be flexible, as me being able to get all 30 ECTS credits transferred depended upon getting to specific modules.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Overall I found the experience very satisfactory.
registration_process: They have a web portal, where you send your application to the university. It takes a couple of hours, but it is generally quite easy. You should be aware that you have to get a recommendation from an academic staff at UCPH (could be an instructor), and you have to take the TOEFL english proficiency test, which costs around 2000 DKK. You will receive emails from the university which will guide you through the process. You will probably feel like you'll be missing information at some points, but that's just cause it's a long process. Just trust that everything will work out if you follow the steps in the emails they send you, and that they will send you information in due time as according to their own schedule.
registration_help: Guidance on the web page was generally quite extensive.
registration_success: I ended up being successful, but at first it was declined. However, when I spoke to my academic advisor we were able to figure it out. Be aware, that you won't register for classes (called modules in st andrews) before the first week of the semester.
registration_advice: Just trust the process and the information they give you.
academics_comments: Overall I found the experience very satisfactory.
course_level: The academic level was generally similar to Copenhagen.
teaching_comparison: As an honours student (3-4th year student) in political science you will have very contact hours. For each of my two modules, I had a 1 hour lecture followed by a one hour seminar. In the seminars you will be just 6-10 students with the lecturer teaching the module, which was quite nice. This in turn means more time being spent on reading. The semesters are generally quite short (they run from mid september until Christmas, so you will be only be there for 3,5 months) but also quite intense. More emphasis is placed on essays written throughout the semester. Writing the essays were great experiences as they were a whole lot more free than what we are used to from Copenhagen. Subject, approach, theory, method etc can be chosen by yourself, and you will typically get 4-5000 words to elaborate on your thesis.

crucial_aspects: As an English student, the language spoken in the country of destination was the most crucial. My choice of university in the UK depended heavily on safety (I wanted to go somewhere were I could easily and safely get from A to B at all hours). The second other important factor for me was the reputation and high academic standard of the university. Finally, I chose the UK, because the expenses of travelling to and living are lower than what is the case for Canada, Australia and the US.
overall_comments: St Andrews is a lovely study town and the university offers an incredibly unique social life and inspiring teaching. It is also beautiful and safe. However, as a master's student who has never had any issues keeping up with the work load at Copenhagen University and who has continually received high marks, I was pushed to my absolute limit as a postgraduate at St Andrews School of English. At times, I experienced stress and anxiety symptoms due to the high pressure to meet all my deadlines. This also meant, I did not have as much time to socialise and enjoy the culture as many other exchange students. However, I also grew as an academic and achieved skills I had not expected to achieve in such a short time. Hence, I would recommend the postgraduate programme at St Andrews School of English to those of my fellow students who wishes to go on exchange for academic opportunities mostly.

It was very overwhelming trying to find a group of like-minded students the first couple of days through a WhatsApp group with hundreds of members.

However, as a master's student who has never had any issues keeping up with the work load at Copenhagen University and who has continually received high marks, I was pushed to my absolute limit as a postgraduate at St Andrews School of English. At times, I experienced stress and anxiety symptoms due to the high pressure to meet all my deadlines. This also meant, I did not have as much time to socialise and enjoy the culture as many other exchange students. However, I also grew as an academic and achieved skills I had not expected to achieve in such a short time. Hence, I would recommend the postgraduate programme at St Andrews School of English to those of my fellow students who wishes to go on exchange for academic opportunities mostly.
registration_process: Before my stay, it was quite demanding and slow. It all happened via email and it was well into June before I received a final confirmation that I was actually going which was quite stressing because it left me little time to sublet my flat and terminate my job. When I got there, it was very easy and efficient.
registration_help: A whole array of help was available and a lot of effort was put into informing us and even encouraging us to reach out for help whenever we needed it during orientation week.
registration_success: Quite succesfull. I had listed to courses back in May that I was interested in taking, but three days before departing I was asked to send a 1000 word essay so that they could decide if I was qualified. In the end, I got two other classes that I had also listed as relevant. I would just have appreciated an earlier notice for that other essay than three days before departure.
registration_advice: Be patient but make sure to follow up regularly via email so the prioritise your application.

course_level: SCQF level 11, 30 ects in total.
teaching_comparison: Very similar. Dialogue based with lots of time for class discussions.
courses_enrolled: EN5504 Reading the Modern & EN5503 Contextualising the Modern at University of St Andrews
recommended_courses: I would recommend these two courses (EN5504 Reading the Modern & EN5503 Contextualising the Modern) to any students who are passionate about literature and ready for an academic challenge. If you are looking to apply for a PhD in English Literature in the future, this is definitely the course for you.
unexpected_costs: No unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: I had almost no transportion costs because everything is within walking distance in St Andrews but travelling around Scotland can be quite expensive. Food is a little less expensive than in Denmark.
activities_available: So many clubs and opportunities to socialise if you can find the time outside your studies. The breakaway society is a great way to see more of Scotland if you are on a budget. Not a lot of socialising happened in with my classmates since we only saw each other four hours a week, so at St Andrews, it is important to be outgoing and join some of the university clubs' events and pub socials.
activities_recommended: Breakaway, yoga and book society.
weekend_recommendations: Go hiking and hang out with people from your dorm and try to reach out to some of the other students from Copenhagen Uni through the Facebook group shared by the global office.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. St Andrews is super international - 30% are American.
socializing_tips: Again, joining the pub socials for a club that catches your interest. Or ask your classmates out for a pint.
cultural_challenges: British people can be a little bit more formal, especially in class, so be conscious of how direct you are in your communication. But I would not worry about that to much. Scottish people are so kind, chatty and funny!
culture_appreciated: The Scottish humour and helpfulness as well as their folk dance and pub culture.
top3_advice: 1) If you are a postgraduate, make sure you are up for an academic challenge 2) If you want an easy way to socialise, pay for that expensive catered meal plan (those who did said it was worth it) 3) find the other few Danes in St Andrews because it is nice to have those to share your ups and downs with.
other_useful_info: Get started on your assignments in due time and try to visit your teachers during their office hours - they are among the best scholars in the world, so make use of it.
most_rewarding: St Andrews and Scotland is marvellously pretty and charming. It is like a fairytale town and the study spaces are straight out of Hogwarts.
greatest_challenge: Keeping up with the deadlines and spending so much time in my own company because class time was so sparse.

course_level: My courses were what they called third year courses

weekend_recommendations: Isle of Skye is beautiful, I mean all of Scotland is, but remember to spend some weekends at St Andrews enjoying the live music at all the local pubs.

cultural_challenges: People were less interested in talking about politics then I'm used to, especially the americans. Part of the reason might be another challenge: the fact that the other students are much younger (often 17-18 when they start uni).
culture_appreciated: The curiosity
top3_advice: Bring some fancy clothes (they like to be fancy over there, especially with wellies), explore Scotland and go to the pubs and listen to live music

crucial_aspects: The cultural aspects of an old university, it being a British university and having a good English programme
info_ease: They sent out multiple emails with the information needed and how to find additional information. Furthermore, they reiterated where and how to find it during in-person lectures etc.
arrival_assistance: Multiple emails, multiple oral descriptions during lectures etc.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You had to pre-register online before you arrived and after arrival you must register via an employee of the uni. Either via zoom or in person when you get there. You should try to do it as quickly as possible, as the spots fill up quickly.
registration_help: You get assigned an academic advisor whom you can always email or set up a meeting with. Furthermore, the university has multiple forms of assistance for free, all you need to do is reach out
registration_success: I got one of my prioritised classes and because I wanted to sign up in person, one of the classes I wanted was full. However, they have multiple
registration_advice: Do it as early as possible - that way you have as much choice as possible
course_level: I had honour classes which are quite high academic level as they are what counts for their final grade
teaching_comparison: Quite similar - especially when comparing them to electives in UCPH - mainly seminars, rarely proper lectures (at least in School of English)
courses_enrolled: Literature and Childhood in the 18th Century Celtic Modernism
recommended_courses: Celtic Modernism was extremely interesting both regarding the literature, the culture and the analysis
unexpected_costs: Most costs were expected - the price of public transport was probably what shocked me the most
cost_comparison: Public transport is quite expensive - around the same or a bit more expensive than Danish public transport.
activities_available: The very culture is based around societies and athletic clubs, which is where most people find their friends. Thus, in the orientation week, there are fayres to learn about all the different academic, hobby and sport societies. They basically had everything - soccer, polo, theatre, book clubs, individual societies for basically every academic school - whatever you like, there is a society for it.
activities_recommended: Enroll in societies, go to the pub socials, meet people - but you don't need to go to every single one, you can easily take a day of if you need it.
weekend_recommendations: You should definitely go explore the surrounding parts of Fife: Crail, Kingsbarne, the East Fife Coastal Route. If you find time, go to the Highlands. It is absolutely beautiful!
culture_adjustment: Quite easy - the culture is not that difficult from the Danish one.
socializing_tips: Be curious, be aware that if you take honour classes, you probably don't have as much to do with your classmates, as they already are part of friend groups. However, it is absolutely possible; you just have to make a bit more effort. Be aware that your main friends might become other exchange students and freshers who live in the same dorm as you
cultural_challenges: Not a lot, really. The biggest problem would probably be understanding Scottish accents.
culture_appreciated: The focus on academia, the traditions and history of the university, the smallness of the town where you often saw someone you knew in town
top3_advice: Be aware that the written assignments might be more consuming than what you're used to from UCPH You might have less actual lessons than what you're used to - be aware of learning how to construct your own routine The scale of grades makes it difficult to translate to the Danish grade system directly
other_useful_info: Enjoy it - and be aware that the semester flies by far too quickly
most_rewarding: The learning experiences, the friendships made, the experience of living alone in another country
greatest_challenge: Making a routine that worked when I only had class once a week

crucial_aspects: I decided to study in Scotland as I wanted to experience something different from Denmark. As I study English it was crucial to me to pick a country with English as its first language. As I have previously lived in England I wanted to visit Scotland as I knew it was renown for the Highlands. University of Stirling was appealing to me, as you are assessed during the course with no finals. The courses were very interesting and I had the opportunity to branch out and learn something else than possible from KU. Particularly due to the COVID-19 pandemic I felt a need to travel, and being within the European continent was nice so you're not too far away from family and friends.
overall_comments: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic all my classes were online, which (of course) was a possible outcome, but not an expected one.
info_ease: It was fairly easy. The staff at University of Stirling replied very quickly on any questions I had about arriving.
arrival_assistance: N/A
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic all my classes were online, which (of course) was a possible outcome, but not an expected one.
registration_process: You are linked to a course catalog and can basically pick and choose between all of them, if you are qualified. The catalog will state if you are qualified or not.
registration_help: I would say any help was available. The international office staff at Stirling was very nice and very helpful.
registration_success: I got 2/3 of all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Choose the classes you might find interesting! And classes you might not be able to join at your home university. If your classes are intersting they're much more fun to write essays in.
academics_comments: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic all my classes were online, which (of course) was a possible outcome, but not an expected one.
course_level: I would say my year 4 classes were at same level as KU however the work load was fairly easier.
teaching_comparison: It was far more fluent and thought through. All my classes were online and through Teams and we "only" had one hour of seminar a week per class while lectures were all pre-recorded.
courses_enrolled: Applied Digital Media: from theory to practice [CMCU9DL] Gender and Representation [FMSU9AS] Writing for Journalists 1
recommended_courses: Would absolutely recommend Gender and Representation!
unexpected_costs: N/A
cost_comparison: Eating out was way cheaper than in Denmark. A ticket to the cinema was £4.99 so I recommend going there as much as you can!
activities_available: There was clubs, the sports facility, student hub and bar was nice. As I lived off campus I didn't really use it that much.
activities_recommended: N/A
weekend_recommendations: You should definitely go travel as much as possible! Alongside a friend we went on the Highlands tour with Heartland Travel and it was amazing. You get to see all the touristy attractions and live in a really cozy house with all the other students on the tour. Nori was an amazing and entertaining tour guide with plenty of knowledge of Scottish traditions. I also recommend you go visit Glasgow and Edinburgh! Both cities were amazing in their own way. I liked Edinburgh more than Glasgow as it had a really cool old/new vibe to it. Go to Glasgow for clubs and shopping!
culture_adjustment: Fairly easy. It took some time to get used to the Scottish dialect but people were very nice and friendly. And if you needed help just ask and any lady would call you "hen" or "love" as a token of appreciation.
socializing_tips: Join any group chat for your accommodation and anyone would ask if there were any gaffs (house parties) constantly. I lived in an all girl flat with a friend, three Americans and a French-Turkish so I didn't really socialize with any locals which was a shame.
cultural_challenges: Probably only the language. And the fact that they say 'cheers' to anything: As an excuse, thanks, hello etc.
culture_appreciated: The cheap pints and cinema tickets!
top3_advice: Use the campus as much as possible! UoS has a really nice new library and newly build area to study. If you need help don't hesitate to ask the campus staff. They are there to help with anything! Go to the free fresher's events! so many free coupons and items.
other_useful_info: Save up, because you will use that for trips around Scotland!
most_rewarding: To be able to go see some of the things I've seen on film. I was lucky enough to go travel with a close friend of mine, so the shared experience of traveling together though particular cities and nature areas is just very nice to have.
greatest_challenge: N/A
other_comments: N/A

crucial_aspects: Exploring a different country and culture to my own, exciting courses, and experiencing another study environment.
overall_comments: Due to covid I did not feel I got the full study abroad experience. My classes were online and I didn't get to interact much with my fellow students. The best parts of my stay were exploring the country and Scottish nature.
info_ease: The Stirling University website offered much information, but any queries I had were quickly and easily answered by the study abroad team at Stirling.
arrival_assistance: The study abroad team emailed much useful information regularly during my stay.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Due to covid I did not feel I got the full study abroad experience. My classes were online and I didn't get to interact much with my fellow students. The best parts of my stay were exploring the country and Scottish nature.
registration_process: I found courses in the course catalogue and then I had to send my choices and reserve choices with my acceptance form, and then I would be told which of the courses I could and could not register for.
registration_help: I could email the study abroad team and the course catalogue had most information I needed when choosing courses.
registration_success: I could not register for all of my choices due to different reasons, but I was successful in registering for some of my first choices and some reserves.
registration_advice: Watch out for credits, Autumn/Spring semester, if you need to have taken another class before taking the one you want.
academics_comments: Due to covid I did not feel I got the full study abroad experience. My classes were online and I didn't get to interact much with my fellow students. The best parts of my stay were exploring the country and Scottish nature.
course_level: I found some of my classes to be challenging and others to be a bit below the level that I am used to at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: There is much fewer weekly teaching seminars and much more independent study at Stirling with only 1 hour per class per week compared to 3-6 hours per class per week at UCPH. However, the teachers at Stirling give much more personal and detailed feedback for assignments and offer more obvious help with academic issues.
courses_enrolled: FMSU9AS - Gender and Representation LINU911 - Language and Society JOUU9X1 - Introduction to Journalism Studies
recommended_courses: FMSU9AS - Gender and Representation This course was by far the most challenging and exciting of my courses. The teacher, Darren, has my full praise, he did a great job and many interesting topics were discussed during the course that enlightened me not only academically but also personally.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Basic groceries, coffee at coffee shops and drinks at pubs were quite cheap. National train tickets were a bit expensive. Rent for the housing was expensive.
activities_available: We went on a highland trip with a private company that the university collaborated with to get us a good deal.
activities_recommended: The highland trip, definitely. It was an amazing way to see loads of the Scottish highlands and nature in only three days and quite cheap compared to how much you get. The gym facilities are great, so I recommend those to anyone who wants to exercise.
weekend_recommendations: Highland trip, go on hikes (remember proper footwear), Loch Ness/Inverness, visit Glasgow and Edinburgh, cinema, The Settle Inn (oldest pub in Stirling), Stirling Castle, Wallace Monument, take the train to Aberdeen and get an amazing view of the coast.
culture_adjustment: The local community in Stirling is very nice and polite. It was quite easy to interact with people.
socializing_tips: Because of covid I didn't socialise a whole lot, but go to parties, or "gaffs" as they're called, if there are any in your accommodation area.
cultural_challenges: I can't think of any
culture_appreciated: That people always interact with you, say hiya when you enter a shop and see you when you leave, sorry if they bump into you.
top3_advice: Get the First Bus app and use the University of Stirling tickets for a discount, get to campus early if you want a study space, explore the paths on campus, they are great for a long walk.
most_rewarding: Experiencing Scottish nature.
greatest_challenge: Meeting other students due to covid.

crucial_aspects: It was important for me to have courses that matched my academic interest and the university had to be located somewhere that allowed me to travel easily.
info_ease: It was completely different from how things are done in KU, but the administrative office at Stirling was were helpful and would always answer me emails, etc.
arrival_assistance: Because of Covid, it was very restrictive, but I also arrived in July so I mostly recieved help from the people I was living with.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was fairly easy, if I had any questions I simply emailed my host university and they helped me.
registration_help: I mostly relied on the teachers I had at my host university, but you are asked if you have certain conditions that require assistance, etc. and they are very good at helping students with special needs.
registration_success: I got all the courses that I applied for.
registration_advice: Make sue to check whether it says spring or autumn.
course_level: Some of the courses were very intense with the amount of weekly reading, and it can feel overwhelming that the exam papers are written during the semester instead of after the end of the semester.
teaching_comparison: Because of Covid, everything was different from their normal teaching. Some courses were only online, some courses posted lecture videos online and had seminars at the campus.
courses_enrolled: ARTU9H5 - Death, Disease and Disability: The State and the Hazardous Working Environment 1800-1914 ENGU9EH - History of the English Language ENGU9EV - Victorian Literature and Culture
recommended_courses: If you like linguistics then the History of the English Language course is fantastic as it teaches you parts of the English language that have never been focused on at KU. However, you do need a good grammatical, phonetic, and linguistic foundation, since the course does not focus on teaching those aspects, only the different language periods.
unexpected_costs: The train tickets and the Covis test kit I had to buy when I came to the UK. I had to pay around £75 for two tests I had to take on day 2 and day 8 whilst I self-isolated for 10 days.
cost_comparison: Food is less expensive than I thought it would be when their prices are reduced.
activities_available: Because of Covid it was difficult, but the English department had an event over Halloween and over Christmas.
activities_recommended: There are a lot of clubs you can sign up for and there is something for everybody.
weekend_recommendations: Visit as many places in Scotland as you can, it is all worth a visit.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy.
socializing_tips: Just talk with them before or after class.
cultural_challenges: I did not find anything particularly difficult.
culture_appreciated: They are very friendly.
top3_advice: Bring books from previous semesters that might help you (grammar books, novels, etc.). Warm clothes and waterproof outerwear. Snacks and food to help you get through self-isolation since online orders can be very expensive.
other_useful_info: Make sure to ask the teachers about the structure of a paper since they measure word count, not anslag, and sometimes they assignments that are not traditional essays. Also, ask if you can use them as a reference on your CV.
most_rewarding: To push my academic boundaries with courses that were more specific than in KU.
greatest_challenge: The workload in the history department is very different from what I was used to at KU. Also I had to write my exam papers during the semester so the balance between doing the weekly studying and the exam papers was very difficult.
other_comments: No.

crucial_aspects: At det var en engelsksproget destination
overall_comments: Der var desværre online undervisning. Derudover var jeg den eneste kandidatudvekslingsstuderende, deres udveksling var ikke bygget op til at have kandidatstuderende hvilket gjorde at det var svært at finde rundt i det hele og at jeg ofte stod alene uden at have andre der kunne rådgive mig.
info_ease: Det var svært at finde den rette information og hjælp omkring fag, idet der står på deres hjemmeside at de kun har bachelorudvekslingsstuderende, mens mit studies aftale er for kandidatstuderende. Jeg prøvede at skrive og spørge om hjælp både hos KU og Stirling Uni, men fik ikke rigtig nogen respons, andet end at jeg blev henvist til Stirlings udvekslingskatalog for bachelorstuderende, og fik at vide at jeg måtte være lidt mere tålmodig og prøve at finde det på egen hånd... Generelt var der alt for dårlig information om hvad det betød at være kandidatudveklsingsstuderende på Stirling Uni. Idet opbygningen af kandidaten er meget anderedes i Skotland, var jeg ikke forberedt på hvad det betød. I Skotland er en kandidat kun et år og det mange kommer fra forskellige uddannelser. Dermed var det svært at finde fag, idet de ikke byggede ovenpå økonomi, men var mere grundlæggende. Det betød også at jeg blev bedt om at ankomme samtidig med bachelorstuderende selvom kandidatkurserne først startede 2 uger efter.
arrival_assistance: Generelt blev vi modtaget rigtig dårligt. Jeg fik fin hjælp over email inden jeg ankom. Da vi ankom var der 1 times online informationsmøde. Det var den eneste hjælp vi fik.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Der var desværre online undervisning. Derudover var jeg den eneste kandidatudvekslingsstuderende, deres udveksling var ikke bygget op til at have kandidatstuderende hvilket gjorde at det var svært at finde rundt i det hele og at jeg ofte stod alene uden at have andre der kunne rådgive mig.
registration_process: Udvekslingskontoret i Stirling klarede det meste af registreringen.
registration_help: Udvekslingskontoret håndterede al kursusregistrering. De hjalp også til hvis man ønskede at skifte kursus hvilket var meget nemt.
registration_success: Jeg havde en del problemer med at en del af kurserne lå tidsmæssigt oven i hinanden, men ellers fik jeg de kurser jeg gerne ville have. Jeg har ikke et indtryk af at der er begrænsning på størrelse af kurserne, så man fik dem man gerne ville have.
registration_advice: Man finder først ud af hvornår kurserne ligger tidsmæssigt et par uger inden man skal afsted. Så find en række backup kurser som og søg forhåndsgodkendelse til dem, så det er nemt at skifte kursus hvis dem du oprindeligt havde valgt ligger skemamæssigt oven i hinanden.
academics_comments: Der var desværre online undervisning. Derudover var jeg den eneste kandidatudvekslingsstuderende, deres udveksling var ikke bygget op til at have kandidatstuderende hvilket gjorde at det var svært at finde rundt i det hele og at jeg ofte stod alene uden at have andre der kunne rådgive mig.
course_level: To af mine kurser var lettere end i Danmark, det sidste kursus var på niveau med undervisningen i Danmark. Det ene kursus bestod udelukkende af internationale studerende hvor der var meget stor forskel på engelskkundskaberne blandt de studerende. I dette kursus havde jeg fremmøde 2 timer om ugen, langt størstedelen mødte ikke op eller var ikke forberedt. Kurset bestod af en del gruppearbejde hvilket kunne være ret udfordrende.
teaching_comparison: Der var forelæsning 2 timer om ugen og øvelsestime 2 timer om ugen i hver af kurserne. Det krævede at man læste hjemme. Dette var meget anderledes end Science, hvor jeg er vandt til mere fremmøde. Desuden bestod eksaminer af essays og kurserne krævede ikke de store matematiske egenskaber. Dette er meget andeledes i forhold undervisningen på JØ-studiet, hvor udregninger er en stor del af kurserne.
courses_enrolled: Industrial Organisation Behavioural Economics Business Analytics
recommended_courses: Jeg vil anbefale Industiral Organisation, her anvendte vi teorien i praksis, og generelt var det interessant at arbejde med områder af mikroøkonomi, som ikke levede om til de antagelser der bliver lavet i mikroøkonomisk teori.
unexpected_costs: Jeg havde ikke nogen uforudsete omkostninger.
cost_comparison: Fødevarer er det samme som i Danmark. Transport med tog var rigtig dyrt, et godt råd er at benytte sig af deres busser i stedet.
activities_available: Der var rigtig gode sports faciliteter, herunder et nyt bygget sportscenter og svømmehal. Stirling er Skotlands førende sportsuniversitet. Der var også mange forskellige sports foreninger man kunne være medlem af.
