crucial_aspects: I chose University of Sydney and Australia in general because I realised that I may never have the same opportunity to travel so far away for such a long period. It was crucial that it was an English speaking country as well. It can't complain about Australia also has really nice weather and beaches :-)
info_ease: Pretty easy. We were assigned a supervisor from USYD that we could contact. At times it was difficult to get ahold of her as she had annual leave.
arrival_assistance: I don't recall getting any assistance once I arrived in Sydney.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: The process is a bit confusing. You receive an e-mail with a document with a link to a spreadsheet with the courses available to exchange students. When applying for enrolment, you also put your preferences for the courses. At some point the supervisor will let you know which courses has been approved for you, and you then have to apply (as far as I remember) again for the courses. During the first week of the semester, you can drop courses and apply for new ones after having been to class. The supervisor helps with this once they've sent out an e-mail with instructions about it.
registration_help: As previously mentioned, the supervisor is very helpful with course registration. I even know that it is possible to apply for courses that are not usually available for exchange students. I did not do this myself, so I am unsure how successful such an application is.
registration_success: I got approved for all the courses (I applied to 8-10) I applied to but one.
registration_advice: When you have the option to apply for 8-10 courses, apply for all of them. This will ensure pre-approval for the course and then you don't have to worry about the classes being full.
course_level: I had tried to apply for the BA courses (they pretty much offer all courses as both BA and MA level). I was assigned only MA courses by the University.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching is a lot less case based and more lecture based. I only had seminars but it was very rare for anyone to raise their hand. Professors encouraged being active in class but it seemed that no one was interested. Some professors offer powerpoint slides, others don't. One teacher had no slides and spoke for 1 hour constantly without asking any questions for the students to answer.
courses_enrolled: Rule of Law and its Value - MA course Criminology - MA course Federal Constitutional Law - MA course Media Law: Defamation and Privacy - MA course
recommended_courses: I CANNOT recommend Federal Constitutional Law. This class was very difficult to follow as it required a lot of prerequisite knowledge, and the sit-in pen and paper exam was tough. It was interesting, though, to learn about the constitution of Australia. Criminology is very international, and so it was easy to follow as an exchange student. Media Law is very common law based, so it was interesting to learn about from a Danish perspective. The exam(s) are multiple assignments during the semester (one where you choose the topic yourself), so it is not too difficult to do during the semester. Rule of Law and Its Value was just ok. The professor is very engaged in the different theories and the exam is just two assignments (one of them with a topic you choose yourself)
unexpected_costs: There is a cleaning fee that you have to pay once you move in to the Queen Mary Building of about 126 AUD (as far as I remember). Also there is a fee for paying rent with international bank accounts (I paid an additional 44 AUD each month for this fee).
cost_comparison: Going to restaurants etc. is usually cheaper than in CPH. Groceries are somewhat cheaper than Denmark (some fresh produce is VERY expensive since it is not native to Australia and must be shipped in). Public transportation is very cheap (especially if you manage to get ahold of a student concession card).
activities_available: There a multiple clubs (I joined the run club, food adventure society). There are always different events by the clubs and the student union (USU) hosts events every week (usually for free). There are clubs for all ethnicities pretty much and for all kinds of hobbies and interests.
activities_recommended: Join the clubs!! This is a great way of meeting people, getting a free meal etc. and so much fun.
weekend_recommendations: Go travelling! It's allowed to drive with a Danish license in New South Wales, Tasmania and Queensland, and it is not very expensive to rent a car. I also loved going to the beach, walk around Sydney or going to national parks (Royal National Park, Blue Mountains etc.) to hike.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy. Australia is not exactly the same as Denmark, but it is not that different either.
socializing_tips: The Australian students are not very easy to socialise with. I mostly made friends with other exchange students and a few domestic students living at the Queen Mary Building.
cultural_challenges: N/A
culture_appreciated: Australians are quite friendly which is nice. There is a normal culture of it being allowed to bring your own drinks to restaurants which is plus!
top3_advice: Be prepared that the academic level is confusing. The professors seem to make it very very difficult, but then when you look at the requirements for the class, it does not seem that difficult. I still have not received all my grades, so I am unsure what the expectations are. Get the student concession Opal card! It makes the public transportation almost free. You apply through the opal card website. Drop courses that don't feel right within the first weeks of classes!!! You will regret not doing it :,(
other_useful_info: Can't think of any.
most_rewarding: Meeting lots of amazing people, seeing beautiful nature and the personal growth!
greatest_challenge: It is difficult being away from family, partners, friends etc. and it specially is difficult because of the time zone.

crucial_aspects: English speaking and nice weather
overall_comments: Loved it!
info_ease: My UCPH coordinator did not provide much information, and nothing was available specifically to Sydney online
arrival_assistance: We were showed around by a local USYD coordinator at the hospital which was nice
arrival_comments: My supervising doctor was not used to having exchange students, so I didn't receive any information prior to leaving Denmark, which was unfortunate.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Loved it!
registration_process: We were referred by our local UCPH coordinator to USYD, and were then contacted several months later by a USYD coordinator to apply for our desired departments. She was, however, new to the international student placements, and placed us in one department for 12 weeks, although the usual agreement is 4 weeks in 3 departments.
registration_help: We had a contact coordinator at USYD, but as I mentioned she was unfamiliar with the usual process.
registration_success: We ended up having to negotiate our way to have a placement of six weeks in two departments, which was okay, but three departments would have been ideal.
registration_advice: Advocate for having three departments placements - this is what the local med students get as well, and what the departments are geared towards.
academics_comments: Loved it!
course_level: Clinical placement in the hospital.
teaching_comparison: Similar with clinical placement combined with theoretical seminars and workshops, but we were not really encouraged to participate in the local med student classes.
courses_enrolled: Six weeks in emergency medicine and six weeks in neurology.
recommended_courses: Both departments were good! Emergency is very hands-on and you can get to see patients yourself (which is quite unusual for Australia, where even junior doctors spend their first few years just taking notes). Neurology at Concord is a very advanced department, and you can learn a lot from the very interesting specialists.
unexpected_costs: You can be randomly selected to get a health examination with a chest X Ray as part of the visa application. This is mandatory and costs 2000 DKK.
cost_comparison: Rent is super expensive, so apply for the hospital student dorm! Groceries are more expensive but eating out is cheaper than in Denmark, especially cafés and coffee. You will want to spend money on trips and tours while you are there, so set aside money for traveling.
activities_available: Sports, choir, theatre, fan clubs etc.
activities_recommended: I heard all of it is fun if you arrive early enough for orientation week!
weekend_recommendations: So much to do in Sydney - beaches, coastal walks, sightseeing, national parks, many cute cafés and shopping. We also did weekend trips to Melbourne, Noosa and Cairns, all within a 3 hour flight, which is not too expensive.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, Australian culture is very laid back and Western.
socializing_tips: Arrive early enough for orientation week in February.
cultural_challenges: Probably the hierarchy between doctors - the junior doctors in internal medicine departments only take notes and never get to examine patients, which means that medical students only get to observe. Also Sydney is an extremely multicultural city, so the language barrier between patients was quite unexpected.
culture_appreciated: Their openness, love of nature and the socializing both before and after work.
top3_advice: 1. Apply for the student housing and save so much money. It is only a 25 minute train ride outside of the city centre, and you will appreciate having that money for traveling. 2. Arrive early or leave after your placement - Australia is a once in a lifetime destination, and you will want to explore more than just Sydney while you are there. 3. Soak up the learning opportunities at Concord! You can volunteer for teaching seminars and be trained in ultrasound, emergency simulations etc.
other_useful_info: Set aside enough time for the application documents, and get started on your health examinations well in advance. Apply for scholarships.
most_rewarding: Being able to take a full consultation with a patient in English, write up a note, order the relevant workup in the local system and consult with the attending doctor.
greatest_challenge: Having to write my Master's thesis at night while being in the hospital full-time, and having my exam with a 10 hour time difference. Would not recommend!

crucial_aspects: I chose Sydney as my study destination because it offers the chance to live in a vibrant international city with stunning nature nearby and an amazing lifestyle. The University of Sydney's strong reputation for high-quality education was also a major factor, along with the opportunity to improve my English in an English-speaking environment.
info_ease: It was relatively easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. The university provided clear pre-arrival guides, and there were plenty of online resources outlining practical details like transportation, accommodation, and campus orientation.
arrival_assistance: When I arrived, I received assistance through the university's orientation program, which included campus tours, informational sessions, and social events for international students.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: The registration process at the University of Sydney was smooth and well-supported. I had a student counsellor from the university who was very informative and provided clear guidance throughout. They helped me with all the necessary steps, from course selection to understanding the requirements for registration.
registration_help: You could always email the student counsellor for assistance, but the university's website was also a valuable resource, providing detailed information. Additionally, a Google Sheet with helpful links about the courses and other relevant resources was shared, making it easy to find everything you needed.
registration_success: I found it very easy to register for the classes I wanted. The process was straightforward, and I was able to select my desired courses without any issues.
registration_advice: My advice to future exchange students would be to remember to thoroughly read the emails you receive from the student counsellor at the host university. All the information you need for registration and other important steps is included in those emails, and by doing so, you won't miss any deadlines. If you have a question, make sure to check the emails first before reaching out to the student counsellor.
course_level: The level of the courses was appropriate for all the ones I took. Some courses were more challenging than others and required more time, especially because some of the content was completely new. On the other hand, some courses involved repetition of material I had already learned, which was then built upon.
teaching_comparison: The mix of lectures and tutorials was similar to what I'm used to. There was a lot of group work in the courses I chose, just like at UCPH, which I found to be a great way to meet new people from different cultures while also strengthening my collaboration skills. However, I noticed there was a greater focus on attendance, tests, and grades, which were aspects I had to adjust to.
courses_enrolled: Responsible Design for Innovation Digital Business Innovation Marketing Principles Introduction to Interface Design
recommended_courses: I would highly recommend the courses Responsible Design for Innovation and Digital Business Innovation, as they offer insights into the intersections of communication, technology, and innovation. These courses provide valuable perspectives on how responsible design and digital innovation are shaping industries and influencing the future of business. Additionally, if you have an interest in marketing, Marketing Principles is an excellent choice. The course covers foundational marketing concepts in an engaging way, offering both theoretical and practical applications. All of these courses are supported by passionate teaching teams, making the learning experience very enjoyable!
unexpected_costs: I didn't really have any unexpected expenses.
cost_comparison: Groceries are a bit more expensive, but other than that, the prices are similar to those in Denmark.
activities_available: There were plenty of opportunities to join a club. At the beginning of the semester, they held two days with stalls where you could ask questions and learn more. There was a wide variety of societies to choose from, such as the Surfing Society, Chocolate Society, Bushwalkers, and many more. I highly recommend joining a club to meet new friends and have a break from studying all the time.
activities_recommended: Whatever sparks your interest or if you're looking to try something new. There are plenty of athletic facilities on campus, including tennis courts, a gym, and a swimming pool. It's a great way to have fun and stay active.
weekend_recommendations: Australia has so much to offer! In Sydney, make sure to check out its amazing beaches and explore the city itself. You could also take a van trip along the East Coast to visit Byron Bay and try surfing, or head north to Cairns to experience the Great Barrier Reef and the beautiful Whitsundays. For a truly unique adventure, don't miss the opportunity to visit the iconic Uluru in the Outback.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy. I didn't encounter any issues along the way.
socializing_tips: Be persistent! If making friends with local students is a goal for you, keep pursuing it. Once you get to know them, they are the nicest people, but there might be a bit of a shell to get past at first.
cultural_challenges: To be honest, there weren't many cultural differences in Australia. However, there are a lot of international students at Australian universities pursuing their full education. Sometimes, it could be a bit challenging to communicate due to a language barrier, but I wouldn't say it was a major issue.
culture_appreciated: I really appreciated the openness and kindness of the people in Australia. The locals are generally warm and welcoming, which made it easy to feel comfortable and build connections. I also loved the easygoing lifestyle outside of the university. People seem to prioritize a good work-life balance, with plenty of time for outdoor activities, socializing, and enjoying nature.
top3_advice: 1) Be prepared for a more performance-driven academic environment. The academic culture in Australia might have a stronger focus on attendance, participation, and grades compared to what you might be used to at UCPH. Stay on top of deadlines, and be ready to engage in more frequent assessments such as quizzes or participation points. 2) Explore beyond the city. Australia offers so much more than just city life. Take the time to travel around and experience different parts of the country. 3) Don't hesitate to ask for help. If you're unsure about anything, whether it's academic or personal, the support services are there for you. Whether it's the student counselor, professors, or fellow students, don't be afraid to ask questions. The academic system might be different, and getting advice early can save you time and stress.
other_useful_info: I recommend reading through these travel reports, as I found them very helpful before my exchange. They offer useful information not only about your host institution but also about other destinations in Australia, helping you prepare for what to expect.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was meeting such kind people from all over the world and connecting with locals, even though they had busy schedules and jobs. I met the locals through my courses, where we had the opportunity to be creative in our work. This not only allowed me to collaborate with others but also gave me many fresh new perspectives that I truly appreciated.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge during my exchange was juggling having fun and studying at the same time. My schedule was quite tight from Monday to Wednesday, which made it difficult to balance academic commitments with exploring and enjoying my time in the city. You want to do everything and make the most out of your exchange while you're there, but it's really important to prioritize and choose between things.

arrival_assistance: Min vejleder sendte alle deadlines og lokationer for introduktionsugen.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Det foregår ved, at man søger godkendelse direkte gennem sin vejleder, hvorefter man tilføjer fagene på universitets hjemmeside. Der er to uger "add and drop"-periode fra semesteret starter, hvor man frit kan udskifte fag. courses_enrolled: Anthropology of Gender and Sexuality Anthropology in the World Sport and Learning in Australian Culture Outdoor Education Education
recommended_courses: Jeg vil anbefale at vælge et "udvekslingsfag" såsom Sport and Learning in Australian Culture eller Outdoor Education Education, hvor der er en lav arbejdsbyrde i forhold til andre fag. unexpected_costs: Ingen uventede omkostninger.

activities_available: Der er utrolig mange foreninger, som er frit tilgængelige for de studerende at deltage i.
activities_recommended: Oplev Australien og de omkringliggende lande! Engager dig i det lokale miljø, eksempelvis brugte jeg meget tid med medstuderende fra queermiljøet,

culture_adjustment: Utrolig nemt, idet at den australske kultur minder meget om den danske.
socializing_tips: Vær åbensindet og grib de muligheder som bliver stillet til rådighed fra USYD og de sociale udvalg. Interager med lokale i din undervisning.
cultural_challenges: Jeg oplevede ingen i forhold til Australien som land eller dets indbyggere, men nok mest i forhold til andre medstuderende. Jeg har ikke haft dårlige oplevelser i forbindelse med disse forskelle, de har nærmere indbudt til dialog.
culture_appreciated: Den mere "laid-back" atmosfære samt diversiteten, både blandt det australske folk, men også i udvekslingsmiljøet.

greatest_challenge: At ikke skulle gå på kompromis med mig selv særligt i sociale sammenhænge og relationer.

crucial_aspects: - the fact that Australia is an english speaking country - the courses available at the university
overall_comments: - I was very happy with my overall experience
info_ease: - the process was quite straightforward, I received all information via E-Mail and the host university provided a lot of information
arrival_assistance: Every student was assigned to s study coordinator who we could talk to before and after arrival. We had an intro week with a couple of welcome events where we got all information and assisstance
arrival_comments: Even tough it was a lot of information and several e-mails to go through, I think the University of Sydney did a good job in providing several resources and assistance during orientation week
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: - I was very happy with my overall experience
registration_process: After being approved from UCPH I received an "unconditional offer" from Sydney University. To receive my conditional offer I needed to apply again to Sydney University, but the application was fairly easy and not extensive (no new motivation letter etc., just hand in of documents etc.). After receiving my conditional offer, course registration, visa application and things like the student health insurance followed.
registration_help: Study coordinators from Sydney University
registration_success: Despite all the help students received, the class registration was quite a mess. I study Global Health and since Sydney University has a global health masters degree I chose the university (the global health classes I found online matched my interests and I was very excited to take them). However, we only got a list with available classes after we went thourgh the entire reigstration process and it turned out that Sydney University has only very limited course availabilites for global health students. I almost dropped my entire exchange cause no classes I wanted to take were available. All exchange students from Sydney University receive a "postgraduate course list" and most of the classes are from degrees like law or engineering etc. I never understood why Sydney University didnt give us a list of available classes BEFORE the registration process so we could have made a decision based on that. It took quite a while but I finally found 4 classes that matched with my study degree and my interests from master degrees like "the sustainability masters degree" or "international relations masters degree". Once I got my classes approved from copenhagen university I thought the process is done but the worst part was yet to happen. In Sydney, you can only see the time of each class AFTER you got approved. So it turned out that 3 of my four classes take place at the same time so all my classes clashed and I couldnt take them. Process began from again and I had to find 3 other classes that took place at a different time. By the time I applied for new classes tho, most of them were already full. With a lot of effort and help of my study coordinator I finally figured out a study plan that fit my interests and worked out with the timeline but it was not what I initially wanted at all. I think as undergad students there is a lot more classes available. I was quite restricted since I also couldnt take any undergrad classes (from copenhagen university side) which made it more complicated.. But i figured it out.
registration_advice: Ask for the postgraduate / undergraduate course list and definetely have a couple of back up courses / a back-up plan in case your classes clash.
academics_comments: - I was very happy with my overall experience
course_level: More challenging than some classes I had at copenhagrn university cause the System in Sydney is quite different. Completing 30ects (which is equivalent to 4 classes in Sydney) was definetely a lot of work and my most challenging semester during my masters degree.
teaching_comparison: Sydney University is more siminlar to the american System than the european. Each course has multiple submissions (each submission counts a specific percentage to the overall grade) so students can expect around 4 submission per class. I had 17 submission in total between August and end of November. Students are more flexible with deciding essay topics and you can get simple extensions (5 days more time) if you have multiple submisison during the week. Overall, students need to reach 50% in order to pass the class so there is less pressure on each exam since multiple count towards the final grade. I liked that the professors gave extensive feedback on each assignment where as at UCPH we only get general feedback / a few comments. There was a rubrik for every assignment with a specific score you could reach so it was very clear to see where your grade was coming from. At UCPH is often seems more random. Therefore, i liked to structured approach at Sydney University and the slightly more interactive teaching style (more disucssions, seminars, tutorial papers etc.)
courses_enrolled: - Food and water security (SUST5002) - Sustainable Development and population health (SUST5004) - Globalisation and Governance (GOVT6123) - Forces of change in international relations (GOVT6137)
recommended_courses: I personally liked the globalisation and governance and forces of change course a lot, since it covered topics that I was missing within my masters. The courses were quite political but offered a good perspective about globalisation and its drawbacks / positive aspects and both classes were really interactive and discussion based.
unexpected_costs: - not a lot of unexpected costs, a lot of expenses were my personal decision and are very subjective
cost_comparison: - more expensive: groceries, public transport, gym, travel costs - less expensive: eating out in restaurants / cafes, there a are ot of things to do for free in Sydney
activities_available: Sydney University had a couple of campus festivals where they introduced clubs students can join, There is a ton of options for everyone and really cool opportunities to get involved. The university also offers a sustainability programm, volunteering opportunities and sport clubs. no complaints here.
activities_recommended: I liked to bushwalking club cause it offers a lot of cheap trips to cool places and is good for socializing. I liked joining yoga classes at the beach to get engaged in Sydney´s morning culture and I also joined a surf camp which was really fun and goof to meet people. There are so many options since Sydney is such a big city where everyone can find something to do.
weekend_recommendations: - rent a car and go down south to jervis bay / kiama / wollongong - go north with the train and visit palm beach and all other northern beaches - a lot of cool camping opportunities around the east coast and cheap camping stuff to find at k-mart (definetely make your way up to byron bay!) - I went to tasmania which was amaying and so worth it as well to the ayers rock with a company that organized four days in the outback; doing a padi diving licence at the great barrier reef was my highlight - however, if the budget is limited there are so many cool and cheap / free trips from sydney. Public transport is really good and you can just hop in the train and go to the royal nationalpark or all the way up to new castle.
culture_adjustment: - pretty easy - australians are very chatty, friendly and laid-back and the culture is very western / quite americanzed - a very easy country to adjust to
socializing_tips: - join clubs, engage in course work / group work
cultural_challenges: - personally, I didnt find cultural differences challenging it was more challenging to actually engage with australians and not only socialize with exchange students. It is very easy to get into this big international bubble and forget socializing with australians but most of them already have their established friend group etc. There are mainly asian students at the campus, so there are not a ton of options to meet a lot of australians at university (at least for the postgraduate courses)
culture_appreciated: - very laid back and chilled - very social and friendly people. I liked that everyone just starts talking to you / australians like to have small talk and I always felt very welcomed
top3_advice: - be prepared to have quite a lot of university work but also appreciate the campus life and dont get too stressed. The USYD campus is awesome and there are so many ways to engage there as a student and enjoy the cheap coffee all around campus :) - Make sure to really enjoy sydney. I know a lot of people who just went from trip to trip and lost track of how beautiful sydney is. It is such an amazing city and definetely worth to spend time there and around it (make sure to visit all the beaches!) - be prepared to have the financial resources to enjoy it. There are a lot of free things to do but Sydney is very expensive. You are allowed to work as a student so it might be worth it to look into job opportunities. Also be aware that Sydney is really big and you might spend a lot of time in public transport
other_useful_info: - I know that undergraduate students had different experiences with that but I found it hard to find "my group of people" in the beginning. Since I attended 4 different courses from 4 different master degrees where everyone already knew each other it was a bit more challenging to socialize. I love that Sydney offers a lot of opportunities to join running clubs / social clubs. I would recommend to participate in those to meet other people as well and have a good time. I also volunteered there (at an asylum seeking center) which was also a really cool experience. Also, make use of the USYD app and get the 25 dollar membership for the semester to make use of free lunch, free coffee etc.
most_rewarding: - I don´t think there was one single experience that was rewarding. I truly enjoyed studying and having a dails life / routine at a place that always feels like vacation. Sydney definetely opened a new perspecive of how I would like to live in my later life and showed me that a good work / life balance actually does exist. I loved exploring so much and I am still amazed by all the incredible places I saw.
greatest_challenge: - getting used to the different university system and the fact that I had constant submissions over a 3 month period
other_comments: - I loved going to Syndey and would absolutely recommend it. It is very hard to get a visa for australia and an exchange is a fairly easy and cool opportunity to explore the country for 6 months. I would have loved to stay longer, Sydney is such a cool place

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne møde nye mennesker og nye kulturer samt komme til et land med godt vejr. Her var Australien og især Sydney et helt perfekt valg.
overall_comments: Bedste semester i min uni tid.
info_ease: Det hele var meget nemt.
arrival_assistance: På USYD får man tildelt en study abroad advisor som står for det hele og kan svare på ens spørgsmål.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Bedste semester i min uni tid.
registration_process: Meget nemt gennem Mobility online.
registration_help: Der var en udvekslingskoordinater tilknyttet til ens udvekslingsdestination fra KU af.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de classes jeg ville have og har ikke hørt om nogen som havde problemer.
registration_advice: Overhold alle deadlines. Ellers gør man det kun svært for sig selv.
academics_comments: Bedste semester i min uni tid.
course_level: Generelt er holdningen at niveauet er lavere end på KU. Kravene for at gennemføre og bestå kurserne er lavere end på KU
teaching_comparison: Meget det samme som på KU.
courses_enrolled: DATA1001 Foundations of Data Science DATA2002 Data Analytics: Learning from Data EDUH4052 Learning in Outdoor Education EDUH4058 Sport and Learning in Australian Culture
recommended_courses: EDUH4052 Learning in Outdoor Education EDUH4058 Sport and Learning in Australian Culture 100% de her to fag. De er designet til udvekslingsstuderende og er bare virkelig fede. Man lærer meget om Australien herigennem og fagene minder ikke om andre fag som jeg har haft før. Hvis du har mulighed for at tage fagene så gør det. Hørte ikke om nogen som ikke var glade for dem. I Learning in Outdoor Education kommer man ud i den Australske natur og en del af faget inkluderer en weekendtur til the Blue Mountains National Park. Det her fag er en virkelig god måde at møde andre studerende på. Wayne som har faget er en virkelig fed underviser. I Sport and Learning in Australian Culture kommer man ud og ser sportsgrene i Australien. Man kommer ud på stadion og skal skrive nogle små opgaver om sine oplevelser i forbindelse med dette. Kurset kan godt være lidt kaotisk struktureret, men Steve som kørte faget er virkelig passioneret omkring australsk sport og elskede at lære fra sig. Hvis du kun har mulighed for at vælge et af de to fag ville jeg anbefale Learning in Outdoor Education.
unexpected_costs: Brugte mange flere penge på at rejse/små ture end jeg havde regnet med, men helt klart det hele værd!
cost_comparison: Øl i supermarkedet er dyrt ift. Danmark. Vin kan fås virkelig, virkelig billigt (Køb Golden Oak papvin(mums filibaba))
activities_available: Der blev holdt ret mange arrangementer for udvekslingsstuderende. Specielt i starten.
activities_recommended: Tage til sociale events som der bliver holdt for udvekslingsstuderende.
weekend_recommendations: Tage på stranden. Sydney har virkelig fede strande. Mine favorit strande var Manly og Coogee. Det er oplagt at tage på ture/rejser når man alligevel er så langt væk hjemmefra. Steder som jeg synes er værd at besøge er: -Blue Mountains National Park er et must og man kan komme derud på omkring 2 timer fra Sydney. -Tasmanien er en undervurderet del af Australien. Virkelig et fantastisk sted at besøge. Smuk natur og ikke proppet med mennesker. -Bali/Fiji. Mange Australiere holder ferie her og man kan få billige flybilletter. -Melbourne
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Australiere er søde og der er ikke de store kulturchok.
socializing_tips: Det er svært at komme i kontakt med de helt lokale studerende, men nogle af sociale klubber ville nok være mit bedste bud.
cultural_challenges: Der er ikke lige så meget gang i nattelivet som hjemme i København. Barer lukker typisk meget tidligere end hvad jeg var vant til hjemmefra-
culture_appreciated: Australiere er virkelig søde og imødekommende. De tager ikke tingene for seriøst og kalder en spade for en spade.
top3_advice: -Sig ja til oplevelser/ture som folk spørger om du vil med på. -Søg QMB lige så snart du kan hvis du gerne vil bo der. Kendte til mange som ventede lidt og ikke fik plads og som var trætte af at de selv skulle ud og finde noget. -Nyd det. Det går meget hurtigere end man lige tror
other_useful_info: Vær åben og imødekommende. Tag med til sociale arrangementer. Snak med nye mennesker. Drik alkohol. Alle (udvekslingsstuderende) er i samme situation med ikke at kende nogen når man kommer derned og der er det nemt at skabe venskaber.
most_rewarding: Alle de søde mennesker som jeg mødte og som endte med at tage på rejser med. At rejse rundt i Australien var en kæmpe del af min samlede oplevelse af semesteret.
greatest_challenge: Der var en del gruppe arbejde i nogle af mine fag og det var lidt op ad bakke når man endte i en dårlig gruppe. Men det er vel lidt mere et universelt problem og ikke særlig USYD specifikt. Ellers synes jeg faktisk ikke at der har været de store problemer.
other_comments: Kan kun anbefale at tage afsted. Du vil ikke komme til at fortryde det. Rejs rundt i så vidt et omfang at det er muligt. Sig ja til ting.

crucial_aspects: I chose Sydney because it was an english speaking country far away from Denmark where you don't just get to live another time.
info_ease: University of Sydney was very informative with a lot of emails from the exchange coordinator beforehand.
arrival_assistance: We had a welcome day exclusive to exchange students where we were told relevant information about everything from studying to life in Sydney.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You had to fill out personal information of different sort but the guiding was very good so it was not a problem.
registration_help: Guides with pictures and you could write the exchange coordinator if you had any doubts.
registration_success: I got all the courses i wanted - it was not a problem for any chemistry courses.
registration_advice: Get it done quickly so you don't miss out on housing offers.
course_level: I took two level 3000 courses which is 3rd year courses, but in Australia they often have minors, so the courses were a bit lower level than at home.
teaching_comparison: We didn't have any "regnetimer" where you sat with a teacher. We only had lectures and laboratory.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Programming Learning in Outdoor Education Molecular Self-Assembly Computational Chemistry
recommended_courses: Learning in Outdoor Education was an amazing course to lake off some workload while at the same time meeting a lot of people from all over the world and learning about the Australian nature.
unexpected_costs: Cleaning fees at the student accommodation.
cost_comparison: Alcohol was more expensive to buy in stores, but cheaper in bars.
activities_available: So many societies across campus which you are introduced too in the welcome week during what they call "Welcome Fest".
activities_recommended: I was a part of the yoga society which was very nice! Also the student union offered a lot of free day trips which are worth a try.
weekend_recommendations: Travel as much as possible but also enjoy your weekends getting to know Sydney. Go to Tasmania! We did it in the spring break and it was amazing.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy to adjust. Compared to it being the other side of the world it felt very european.
socializing_tips: It was hard to socialise with local students because they often just want to get home after class and the student accommodation is mostly exchange students.
cultural_challenges: It was not challenging - they are very friendly and always want to help you.
culture_appreciated: Getting to know a bit of aboriginal culture and how complex it is. Barbecues on the beach (and everywhere else) is a big thing with free places to do it, which you should definitely do!
top3_advice: Spend a lot of time socialising in the beginning! This is when you build friendships and friend groups. other_useful_info: Enjoy - time flies by!
most_rewarding: Meeting so many nice people from all around the world. It really broadens your perspective a lot.
greatest_challenge: The time difference between Australia and Denmark. It is a bit hard to coordinate phone calls with people at home.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to an English speaking country to improve my English skills and so there would not be a language barrier between me and the locals. Further I had never been to Australia before and it was a place that I really wanted to visit and I wanted to try to live here.
info_ease: It was quite easy the coordinator made some good step-by-step emails of all the things you needed to do and complete. housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

registration_help: There were a coordinator, that helped with any questions you might have and she responded to any emails within 5 days.
registration_success: I got almost all of the classes that I wanted but there were one I wanted that had some prerequisites that I didn't met and therefore I was not allowed to have this unit.
registration_advice: Make a to-do list of the things you need to do and take your time. In some periods there is quite a lot of things you need to do. course_level: At USYD you are only allowed to take BA units when you are on your BA. I felt that the academic level was quite similar to UCPH or a bit easier.
teaching_comparison: At USYD I had laboratory classes and lectures. In my units there were no theoretical exercises as I have in UCPH. Further there are many small quizzes, tests, assignments and presentations during the semester that all count as a small part of the overall grade for a unit, so the final exam only count 50-60% of the final grade. They record all lectures but watch them during the semester so you are not super busy in the study vacation.
courses_enrolled: “Microbes, Infection and immunity”, “Neuroscience in health and disease”, “Biochemistry of human disease” and “Beyond the genome”
recommended_courses: I would recommend “Beyond the genome” to exchange students because Stuart the lecturer is really good and passionate about the unit and content. Further it is very relevant and new methods that he teaches about which makes this unit very relevant for students within the biochemistry, microbiology and biomedicine field of study.
unexpected_costs: I didn't have many unexpected costs but I was a bit surprised that the prizes in the supermarket was more expensive than in Denmark. I also used more on weekendtrips and holidays during the semester than I expected to do before the exchange.
cost_comparison: The vegetables and diary products are more expensive, but bying meat and take away is generally cheaper than in Denmark.
activities_available: There are all kind of sports clubs that you can join if you have any sport that you do in Denmark or a new sport you want to try. They also have many different cultural societies, hiking societies, chocolate society and choir. They have all different societies you can imagine. I was a part of yoga society, bushwalkers, dance society and the choir, and all of them were great fun.
activities_recommended: I think the bushwalker society is a good one to join because they arrange many trips so you can go out in the nature on different hikes to places that you might no go yourself and together with people that also wants to explore more of the country and area around Sydney.
weekend_recommendations: I really recommend going for a weekend trip to Blue Mountains. You can also do canoeing in the Blue Mountains. The area south of Sydney with Royal national park and Jervis bay is also really nice. There is also many nice costal walks around Sydney. North of Sydney by New Castle is also nice and Hunter Valley is also worth a visit. It is also possible to take the plane for a weekendtrip to Brisbane and the area around or to Melbourne. There is also one week off during the semester where you can eg. can go to Tasmania or do an East Coast road trip. Also if you have the time after the semester then visit New Zealand, that is amazing!
culture_adjustment: I found it easy to adjust to the local culture because it is not so different from Danish culture and everyone speaks English.
socializing_tips: It can be a bit hard to socialize with Australian students, but the best way to do it is in the classes and if there is groupwork then try to form a group with the local students.
cultural_challenges: I had to adjust a bit to speaking English all the time and express myself in English but within the first few weeks it felt normal
culture_appreciated: I really appreciated that everyone was so helpful and kind and also very chatty.
top3_advice: Don't stress to much about socializing right in the beginning, it will come slowly and you will get friends! Take your time to explore both Sydney and the area around. The nature is so pretty and it has so much to offer. Enjoy every moment of it because time goes super fast so before you know the semester is over and you will return back home.
other_useful_info: Attend all the activities in the beginning of the semester it is a good way to meet other exchange students.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part was all the travels and small trips I was able to do in Sydney and around Sydney while I was studying. I really enjoy travelling so it was very nice to be able to combine it with studying.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge for me was the FOMO I got when I saw other people were doing fun things that I was not a part of. Sometimes it was just because I needed to relax so I chose to stay home, but I had to remind myself that they would still be my friends eventhough I was not a part of every single activity and that I couldn't see all of Australia in 5 months.

overall_comments: Studying abroad in Sydney has been one of the greatest experiences of my life. It’s a wonderful country with beautiful nature, vibrant cities, prestigious universities, and a rich culture, among many other things.
info_ease: The University of Sydney (USYD) and KU were extremely efficient in providing the necessary information, making the process very easy despite the many steps involved, such as visa application, insurance, enrolment applications, and unit selection.

registration_process: You will get in touch with a study-abroad adviser from USYD and through email correspondences they will guide you through the different processes of enrolment and time-table management.
registration_help: You have a study-abroad adviser and you can always contact this person if you have any questions and they reply relatively quick.
registration_success: I got all the units of study that I applied for and everything was possible in my time-table.
registration_advice: Read your email feed carefully and then you will be fine (-;
academics_comments: Studying abroad in Sydney has been one of the greatest experiences of my life. It’s a wonderful country with beautiful nature, vibrant cities, prestigious universities, and a rich culture, among many other things.
course_level: I think the level of the courses are similar to what I’m used to back home in Copenhagen. However, it seems more common not to read at all, as the lecture PowerPoints, workshops, lab sessions, etc., make up the course curriculum. All in all, I found it a bit less challenging, although all four units of study I participated in were within the life sciences field.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style is very similar to UCPH in terms of lectures, lab sessions, and workshops. However, the examination system differs from UCPH, as the final exam typically counts for 40-50% of the final grade. You also have midterms, which (at least for my units) accounted for 15-25% of the final grade. This means you should expect smaller quizzes and assignments, each contributing between 3-15% to the final grade. In Australia, multiple-choice questions are very popular, and they were included in all my midterms and final exams.
courses_enrolled: BCMB3003 Biochemistry of Human Disease BCMB3004 Beyond the Genome BIOS1171 Neuroscience MIMI2002 Microbes, Infection and Immunity
recommended_courses: BCMB3004 Beyond the Genome was a great unit where you learn about various methods using mass spectrometry to analyze changes in healthy and diseased cells. The lab component of this unit was very well-structured, and it was interesting to perform different mass spectrometry analyses and gain some experience in bioinformatics. Microbes, infection and immunity was also a very well structured unit with a lot of basic learning about the immune respons to pathogens and microbes.
unexpected_costs: To get a student visa, you need overseas student health coverage (OSHC), which I didn’t know beforehand (around 1900 DKK). There were also some unforeseen fees for the student accommodation.
cost_comparison: In general, prices are similar to Copenhagen, but I think groceries and alcohol are more expensive in Sydney.
activities_available: The University of Sydney Union (USU) offers a wide range of clubs and sports, and it's very affordable (tennis, surf camps, bouldering, dancing), so this opportunity should be exploited. Additionally, they provide pantries (a great opportunity to get free food), cheap coffee, and parties.
activities_recommended: I can recommend the surf-camp (weekend-trip) strongly.
weekend_recommendations: Explore Sydney in the weekends - go for a hike!!! In the holidays travel Australia (east-coast, Tasmania, Melbourne, New Zealand, Bali?)
culture_adjustment: It was very easy to adjust as the culture of Australia is very similar to Europe.
socializing_tips: Participate in some of the clubs, go to the parties on campus, talk to your mates in the classes or at your accommodation.
cultural_challenges: Nothing in particular.
culture_appreciated: The Australian people are very kind and polite, so if you're unsure about something, feel free to ask a stranger!!
top3_advice: - Remember why you decided to go on exchange and focus on that – what weighs the most, the academic experience or the travel experience? - Keep up from the start and try not to fall too far behind, because you’ll soon have a quiz or a submission that counts towards your overall grade. - Enjoy it while it lasts, because it will be over soon!!
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: To get new friends from Denmark and all around the world, and to travel one of the most beautiful countries in the world.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge during the exchange was adapting to a different academic system and finding a balance between studying and exploring the new environment. academics_comments: If you are ever in doubt about one thing in your life, please dont let it be whether to go on an exhcange program or not! Just do it! You will learn so much about yourself and grow to be a better you. You will have the hardest and the best time of your life and I promise it is worth every sad and happy tear, as you leave to go on exchange full of hope and maybe a little afraid, to crying over the assignments or due to homesickness, to having a laugh at dinner with your new friends, to finally crying in the airport (Yes, you will cry) when you eventually have to leave because you leave a piece of yourself in that place. I promise that is how much an exchange program is gonna mean to you. You will be enriched for life and when you grow old it will be hell of a story to say you lived in another city in your 20s. Not many people have that privilege to call two cities home, so use it!
course_level: The level of course was easier than or almost the same as KU I would say. It is more practical and KU is more theoretical is what I found.
teaching_comparison: Lectures are essentially the same, but be aware they start at the time advised not liek at KU where it is 15 min past. And they only hold a 5 minute break in the middle of the lecture not 15, which was really hard I thougjt. The tutorials are almost like KU too, although some of them are shorter and more compressed.
courses_enrolled: BUSS6002 Data Science in Business QBUS6810: Machine Learning for Business QBUS6840: Predictive Analytics QBUS6860: Visual Data Analytics
recommended_courses: QBUS6860: Visual Data Analytics is a really easy unit. If you make an okay effort on the assignments you dont have to attend the final exam! QBUS6810: Machine Learning for Business was one of the most interestting units I have ever taken would highly reccomend if youre into Data Science and what to work with it, it will prepare you for that.
unexpected_costs: When I moved into my student apartment I had to buy a matress, cups, utensils and so on.. which can run up in price really quickly.
cost_comparison: Transportation is really cheap. You can get a student Opal card so you will save 50% on all your trips compared to normal price. It is actually really cheap to eat out in Sydney, especially compared to Copenhagen. Groceries are more expensive here Most museums are free
activities_available: Sports (they even have their own football pitch and swimming pool) and chocolate club, book club everything you can think of there is a club for it.
activities_recommended: If you get the chance to vacation around in Australia please do it. Australia is so much more than Sydney even though it is a nice city is gets pretty boring fast. It is also relatively cheap to fly around Australia. You can go to a wilflife sanctuary if you want to pet a kangaroo (highly recommend) or just go to a nice nature walk around Bondi/Manly.
weekend_recommendations: If the weather is nice take the ferry to Manly and eat at Yochi and the fish and chips shop. Otherwise just look at tiktok/pinterest
culture_adjustment: Sydney is actually a really interesting city. It is a mix between Europe and Asia. The transition will really not be that hard as Australians are really close culturally with British/US and Western Europeans, but you can also go to Chinatown and you will literally not feel like you are in Sydney anymore bu like Hong Kong. Very multicultural, really brings out the best of the city.
socializing_tips: Expect your classes to be 95% international Chinese students and Indian students. If you want to socialise you should dare to go up and talk to them they will not come and talk to you. Also a good idea is to take a unit which contains group work that will force you to socialize which is really good, it worked for me at least.
cultural_challenges: They drive on the left hand side. I was so close to getting run over a million times until I learned to look the right way when crossing :-D A lot of the Chinese students are quite hard to understand sometimes and also it can be challenging understanding cultural differences but that is also part of the fun, and you will learn a lot about Chinese culture haha (but I mean it i a good way, it actually interesting) Each time you walk into a clothing store they are almost harrasing you and asking what they can help me so annoying.
culture_appreciated: Australians are so friendly and will talk to everyone. Honestly just go to a bar or even at the stoplight. The food culture in Sydney is propably the best in the world. They have the best European and Asian food omg, that is the one thing I am gonna miss the most about Sydney!
top3_advice: 1) Be aware of the English requirements maybe you have to take an English test! 2) Save up. Sydney is expensive 3) Have as much fun as possible, sometimes just say screw uni and go do what you want. Dont take school too seriously when youre on exchange
most_rewarding: Having to challenge myself each and every single day and getting out of my comfort zone, by socializing always trying to make frineds and cant let a rejection set you astray. I became way more confident in both myself and my English skills. Having finished all my units was really rewarding even though I didnt get perfect scores I did my best at one of the best univesities in the world.
greatest_challenge: Having to sozialise. It is hard to travel to a new country on your own without knowing noone there or have maybe never even been there before so you also have to get used to the culture. It is propably the hardest part of going on exchange.

crucial_aspects: Ville gerne til Sydney og samtidigt til et relativt anerkendt universitet
info_ease: Forholdsvis lige til. Fik den info jeg skulle bruge via infomødet og fra diverse pre-departure materialer fra USyd. Dertil er der meget brugbar info i disse rapporter
arrival_assistance: Man bliver tilknyttet en vejleder ved Usyd, som svarer hurtigt og kan hjælpe med det meste
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Man har så vidt jeg husker 14 dage fra skolestart og frem til at beslutte hvilke fag, man vil have. I de to uger kan man add/drop kurser, og fremmøde tæller ikke med i ens karakter (i de fag hvor det gør). Vær opmærksom på, at processen med at add/drop dog kan være lidt langsom, så bedst at have sendt sin endelige ansøgning efter en uge. Dertil er der stor rift om de populære kurser og de mest belejlige tidspunkter, så det en god ide at være ude i så god tid som muligt. Hvis et givet hold er fyldt op, kan man "like" den og komme på en venteliste, hvor man får lov at bytte sig ind, hvis en anden studerende ønsker det hold, som du selv har. Det fungerer rigtig godt, og hvis man er lidt tålmodig er det oftest muligt at få sine ønsker opfyldt
registration_help: Vejlederen fra Usyd
registration_success: Fik alle fag jeg ønskede. Fik også alle hold jeg ønskede efter at have lagt lidt kræfter i ventelisterne. Ved et enkelt fag måtte vi spørge forelæseren, om vi kunne komme på et andet hold - kom med en god undskyldning, og så imødekommes det formentlig
registration_advice: Vælg fag efter primært den eksamensform, der passer dig bedst (kan findes på kursussiden under assessment) og (ii) sekundært efter skemaet. Nogle fag har én stor aflevering (eller ingen) og derudover kun stederprøver (midterm og final) med lukket bog; andre fag har mange afleveringer og ingen eller én final. Jeg gik efter fag med stedprøver og så få afleveringer som muligt - det gav mest muligt ro i løbet af semesteret. Eksamenerne var nemme at læse op til, og de få gruppeafleveringer, der var, var forholdsvis smertefrie. Der er få fag, hvor du får point, som tæller lidt i din karakter (måske 5-10%) - men resten tæller ikke reelt fravær, så det ikke nødvendigt at dukke op (det har ingen konsekvenser at blive væk) - så det ikke verdens undergang, hvis du får et hold med et dårligt undervisningstidspunkt. I processen får du mail med en advarsel om maksimalt at tage ét level 6000 kursus som kandidatstuderende og vist 3000 som BA-studerende pga. arbejdsbyrden. Tag ikke dette for bogstaveligt
course_level: Niveauet var væsentligt lavere end KU (reference: polit). 2 af mine fag, som findes også på KU (FINC3014 og ECOS3006), kunne have haft væsentligt højere matematisk niveau, men forblev på et niveau med helt simple ligninger med én ubekendt (ingen calculus), men i de fleste tilfælde blev matematikken ikke engang brugt. Det var oftest blot definitioner, man skulle huske, og taksonomisk forblev niveauet meget beskrivende. Pensum kunne altså have givet anledning til et noget sværere stof - derfor kan du selvfølgelig også på eget intiativ gå dybere i materialet... Forelæserne var generelt acceptable, mens holdunderviserne var meget svingende, hvilket uddybes forneden. Niveauet blandt ens medstuderende er markant lavere end på KU og føles i en del tilfælde som dansk gymnasieniveau. Hoveddelen af ens medstuderende er kinesiske og kan ikke snakke engelsk - begge dele kan være en udfordring ved gruppearbejde. Eksamenerne (stedprøverne) er markant nemmere end på polit. Man kan nemt læse hele pensum op på én dag og få et godt resultat
teaching_comparison: Forelæserne var efter samme koncept, mens holdundervisningen var lidt mere tovejs ind KU, hvor det oftest er en monolog opgavegennemgang.
courses_enrolled: FINC3014 - Trading and Dealing in Securities Markets. God forelæser og spændende stof med stor relation til praksis. Nem eksamen. Gruppeafleveringen går ud på at udforme sin egen trading strategi og teste den med fiktive penge - fed aflevering. FINC6017 - M&A. Giver en fin intro til diverse koncepter i M&A og til værdiansættelse og kan være brugbart hvis du arbejde i den sektor. Det er et af de mere tidskrævende fag, da der er både en individuel (10 sider) og en gruppeaflevering (20 sider), som kræver noget arbejde. Fin øvelse i at få udformet en DCF. Holdundervisernes niveau var meget lavt - forelæseren var angiveligt ok. FINC6025 - Entrepreneurial Finance. Fint fag, som også giver intro til koncepter relevant for IB, PE og lignende. Niveauet er ret basalt, men du introduceres til en del interessante koncepter. Vælg en tutorial class, hvor forelæseren (Peter Pham) er underviser. Eneste fag, hvor dit fremmøde tæller med i din karakter, men kan optjene maks point ved at møde op blot fem gange og deltage aktivt. ECOS3006 - International Trade. Mere politagtigt fag, ret tungt på grafintuition; meget lidt matematik påkrævet. Fin intro til handelsteori, men mere fokus på udenadslære en egentlig intuition. 15% af karakteren er online multiple choice quiz (som laves hjemmefra med alle hjælpemidler) - resten af hhv. en midterm og final, som begge er relativt lige til. Kræver dog mere forelæsning end de andre fag, da der alligevel er en del modeller, man skal have overblik over
recommended_courses: FINC3014 og FINC6025. M&A er for tidskrævende ift. afkast; din tid er bedre tjent ved at læse koncepterne op selv (men det er dog som nævnt fin øvelse i at lave en DCF model). Trade er ok, men kurset er formentlig mere givende på KU Kombiner med et regnskabsfag, hvis du er finansinteresseret - de er nemme og regnskabsøvelse er altid brugbart. Overvej at tage et af de mere udvekslingsorienterede fag, som lærer dig om Australien; f.eks. kurser om australsk økonomi eller landets historie. Generelt: Lad være med at være for ambitiøs for dig selv, når du vælger fag; når du kommer i gang opdager du, at kvaliteten ikke er vildt god; at det påkrævede niveau er lavt; og at du kan udnytte dit udvekslingssemester på andre måder, som er mere givende for dig på lang sigt
cost_comparison: Visum var meget dyrt; husleje er virkelig dyrt; når du rejser rundt, bruger du en del penge på aktiviteter. Alkohol er virkelig dyrt at købe - en sixpack koster +80 kr og slavevodka +200 kr; med undtagelse af (australsk) vin, som er virkelig billigt. Udover ovenstående er det meste dog billigere end i Danmark. Det er billigere at handle ind; oksekød er f.eks. markant billigere. Frugtudvalget er væsentligt bedre, da de gror det meste selv - økologi er dog ikke en stor ting. Kaffe er billigere - 20-25 kr for en god kaffe. Det også lidt billigere at spise ude. Det billigt at rejse indenrigs.
activities_available: Alle former for foreninger - finans, niche-faglige, kaffe, hiking, løb, dykning osv
activities_recommended: Jeg fortryder, at jeg ikke dukkede op til foreninger, da jeg tror det er den bedste måde at møde australiere på.
weekend_recommendations: I nærheden/i Sydney: Blue Mountains, Manly Beach, 7-bridges walk (35 km gåtur, hvor du får set mange områder, du ellers ikke vil se), Hunter Valley (vinregion; super hyggeligt og billigt), Jervis Bay, Canberra (hovedstaden - fint at lave en dagstur eller maks én overnatning). Ellers: Lav roadtrip fra Cairns (hvor du ser Great Barrier Reef) til Brisbane (eller helt til Sydney); Vestaustralien roadtrip; New Zealand; Tasmanien (stor anbefaling); Melbourne (australian open hvis du er der i januar); Uluru (Ayers Rock - ikke nødvendigt med mere end én overnatning, husk insektet); Mt Kosciuszko; Vanuatu; Fiji; Bali; Darwin. Fraser Island er lidt overvurderet. Hvis du tager afsted i efterårssemesteret, så sørg for allerede at komme ud af rejse allerede i august, hvor vejret er sløjt i Sydney og dagene er korte. Lad være med at stress for meget over at rejse præcis i spring break ugen - som nævnt er dit fremmøde i skolen ikke vigtigt; og du vil alligevel opdage undervejs, at det er vigtigere at prioritere rejser + så har du bedre tid til at nyde Sydney, når sommeren indtræffer.
culture_adjustment: Nemt i hverdagslivet - folk er venlige og serviceniveauet er højt. Campusmæssigt svært, da det svært at møde australiere, med mindre du lægger en stor indsats i at opsøge det. Vi fik ikke nogen australske bekendtskaber og kender ikke nogen der gjorde i mere end i et begrænset omfang.
socializing_tips: Vil anbefale at søge ud fra din komfortzone og opsøge steder med mange lokale (sportsklubber og lignende) samt proaktivt opsøge relationer til dem
cultural_challenges: Ovenstående. Ligesom vi i Danmark sjældent snakker med udvekslingsstuderende, er cirklen også forholdvis lukket ved dem.
culture_appreciated: Den australske livsstil
top3_advice: Udnyt at du har et halvt år på den anden side af jorden - det en enestående mulighed for at udforske Australien og omkringliggende lande. Hvis du udnytter tiden, kan du nå virkelig vidt omkring. Prioriter dette over studiet. Gå efter at møde australiere - der er virkelig mange danskere i Sydney, så dem skal du alligevel nok møde (f.eks. danskerbar hver måned)
most_rewarding: Rejserne
greatest_challenge: Tidsforskellen gør det besværligt at holde kontakten til dem derhjemme

crucial_aspects: There were multiple aspects including choosing an ambitious and good university and experiencing a new country and having the opportunity to travel a lot.
info_ease: The host university was not that good at providing specifically law students the right information on study units and how we were supposed to choose and submit these in time. The proces was overwhelming and not very well guided.
arrival_assistance: There was a study counselor from the host university who was supposed to help the exchange students with questions and in choosing study units. This was in theory good, but there was limited help from the counselor who had maybe 100 other students to attend to at the same time.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The university sent detailed emails out to students with guides on registration.
registration_help: The student counselor via mail or the universities website.
registration_success: Not very successful. Speaking from a law point of view, it was impossible to get all the classes I originally had submitted because they were all full or did not fit into the timetable. There was not a lot of guidance and it was stressfull trying to make the timetable fit for all the classes. I ended up with 2/4 classes that I had originally wanted.
registration_advice: I would advise future exchange students to ask for prior approval on as many subjects as possible so the timetable process won't become as stressful.
course_level: The MA courses were of a high level and were manageable but challenging for someone studying a master in law at KU.
teaching_comparison: There is mandatory in class teaching and sometimes also mandatory participation that makes out some of your final grade.
courses_enrolled: Copyright and Designs War Law Conflict of Laws Private International Law
recommended_courses: I would recommend taking as many of the elective courses as possible rather than the mandatory courses. I would recommend war law and private international law because of the not so difficult material and easy exam forms.
unexpected_costs: Books are very expensive and I would not say they are woth buying as an exchange student. One can either borrow them in the library or find online
cost_comparison: Public transportation is very cheap in Sydney
activities_available: I did not myself participate but there were different clubs. The school also hosts a welcome party and a halloween party
activities_recommended: X
weekend_recommendations: Enjoy the city and visit some of the many beaches
culture_adjustment: It was quite easy. The language is English and the culture is similar to danish
cultural_challenges: Not any cultural differences but it was challenging at times that Australia is so far away from home
culture_appreciated: The easy way of living that is more laid back and outdoorsy
top3_advice: The courses are quite challenging so you will still have to study a lot, but remember to also enjoy free time and travel! Research and be prepared to have many different course options Try to interact with some australian students in each of your classes, it can be a big help :)
other_useful_info: X
most_rewarding: Meeting so many new friends and getting to travel around in Australia
greatest_challenge: Balancing study and freetime

crucial_aspects: I've always wanted to go to Australia and I thought: "What better way than to actually live there?"
overall_comments: I would go on exchange and also on exchange in Sydney a thousand times again. I can highly recommend it to everybody.
info_ease: University of Sydney is very informative university and provided us students with all necessary information.
arrival_assistance: At University of Sydney they provide Intro to Sydney sessions, Official Welcome session, Welcome fest, Scavenger Hunt and Campus Race on campus so that the students are fully prepared for a life in Sydney and at campus.
arrival_comments: There's so much information given that you almost drawn in it.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I would go on exchange and also on exchange in Sydney a thousand times again. I can highly recommend it to everybody.
registration_process: USYD has a shared Google Sheets showing all the units (courses), what semester they're available, amount of Credit points, and links to the University's website where you can read more about the content of each unit, prerequisites, prohibitions and so on. After deciding your units (pick more than you need since they can be turned down by USYD) you apply for enrollment on their Sydney Student Portal. On this portal you check the approval of the units. When units have been approved, you can choose to enroll or to decline.
registration_help: Students stay in close contact with the organization Sydney Global Mobility, where a exchange coordinator is at your service to help with all kinds of questions.
registration_success: I had two units declined because i didn't meet the prerequisites. I then found two new units and was enrolled in all four units I wanted. One of the units needed some evidence of my skills in a laboratory which made the enrollment a bit prolonged.
registration_advice: Apply for more units than you need. If some of them are declined then the process gets a bit longer because the new units you add have to be added manually by the exchange coordinator who is already very busy answering other mails.
academics_comments: I would go on exchange and also on exchange in Sydney a thousand times again. I can highly recommend it to everybody.
course_level: My elective units in Diet and nutrition for health and sport and Learning in outdoor education were very easy. My limited elective units in Neuroscience and Biochemistry in human diseases were more comparable with the level of my home university UCPH. But the exams were much easier.
teaching_comparison: The teachers are really eager for you to understand the content and always make a great effort by sending out a lot of information on a weekly basis, which actually turned out to be even more confusing.
courses_enrolled: Diet and nutrition for health and sport, Learning in outdoor education, Neuroscience, and Biochemistry in human diseases
recommended_courses: Every exchange student should enroll in Learning in outdoor education. It's a unit where you go on field trips to Royal National Park and Blue Mountains. There's no exam, but instead 4 blog posts that needs to be written and a media campaign to be presented. Diet and nutrition for health and sport is a very easy unit where you learn a lot about nutrition. There's no final exam, but three quizzes throughout the semester and a final report.
unexpected_costs: Learning in outdoor education costed addition 175 AUD
cost_comparison: Accommodation and grocery shopping were more expensive than expected. Public transport was cheaper than expected.
activities_available: Endless.
activities_recommended: I can recommend yoga which is really relaxing for a stressed out student.
weekend_recommendations: Travel!
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Sydney is very busy, but so is Copenhagen.
socializing_tips: Sign up for the Mates Abroad Program.
cultural_challenges: European students and Asian students don't really mix up, but instead stay separated.
culture_appreciated: Everybody is always ready to chat.
top3_advice: 1. Don't hesitate – I myself was in doubt right until i boarded the plane, but exchange is the best thing that I've ever done (and I've done a lot of stuff already). 2. Ask when in doubt – The process is long and sometimes confusing. Ask for help if you know any who has been to the same uni or get in touch with other exchange students who are going. 3. Be patient – Response times are long and the time differences doesn't make it any easier, but I promise you that all your patience will pay off, and when you arrive, it will seem to be the easiest thing ever to move to a foreign country!
other_useful_info: Attend the Scavenger Hunt and Campus Race (provided by USU). Here you get to know campus and meet a lot of other exchange students who have also just arrived.
most_rewarding: Passing my final exams and acknowledging than I'm actually also quite intelligent in a foreign country.
greatest_challenge: Balancing studies, social life and time to recover.
other_comments: Just do it.

crucial_aspects: I chose Australia since it is an English speaking country which makes it easier for me to speak with locals. I also wanted to travel further away in order to push personal boundaries.
info_ease: I found it very easy.
arrival_assistance: A lot of emails in how to settle in, get help/support, find further information, access units etc. The University of Sydney also held an orientation day for exchange students.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: After creating an account at their student portal you needed to type in the names of the units and codes. After some time my units were approved. Up to one week after semester start, you had the opportunity to change units. We got emails with step-to-step guides.
registration_help: Each of the exchange students had a student coordinator who helped with it all. We also got a lot of different emails in how to do the different things.
registration_success: Very successful. I got the units I wanted.
registration_advice: Read about the units on the university's website.
course_level: I found the level of the units the same as at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: We had lectures and tutorials which is the same as at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Fixed Income Securities Derivative Securities Financial Derivatives Learning in Outdoor Education
recommended_courses: Learning in Outdoor Education is only for exchange students. It is a good way to meet other exchange students and also learn more about Australia's nature and culture.
unexpected_costs: Nothing
cost_comparison: Rent and visa were more expensive than expected.
activities_available: The University of Sydney has a lot of different clubs.

crucial_aspects: wanted to go on an exchange in a country I had not visited before. In addition, it was important to me that it was an English-speaking country so I could communicate more easily with patients. I had also heard many positive things about exchange programs in Sydney, which played a significant role in my decision.
info_ease: The university and the hospital’s academic supervisor provided information well in advance and were very helpful in answering any questions I had prior to departure.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance beyond the information provided via email.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The academic supervisor at the hospital met us on the first day and gave us a tour of the hospital as well as the associated medical education center. Afterwards, we were assigned to the departments, where we were very well received.
registration_help: There was always the option to email or call the student advisory services to receive assistance.
registration_success: I did not have to choose classes myself; however, I was able to state my preferred hospital department, and they were very receptive to my wishes.
registration_advice: You should ask any questions you have – everyone is very kind and helpful.
course_level: The level was appropriate.
teaching_comparison: I felt that the level of teaching and clinical experience was very similar to what I experience at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: I did a clinical placement for 12 weeks at a hospital.
recommended_courses: This was the only avaliable course.
unexpected_costs: There were many expenses associated with the NSW Health requirements, which were mandatory to participate in the hospital placement.
cost_comparison: I felt that the expenses aligned well with the budget I had prepared beforehand.
activities_available: Unfortunately, I was not offered any activities by USYD, as I was doing a hospital placement and not taking courses on campus. However, I know from my roommates that they organized many fun events!
activities_recommended: Unfortunately, I was not offered any activities by USYD, as I was doing a hospital placement and not taking courses on campus. However, I know from my roommates that they organized many fun events!
weekend_recommendations: Sydney got lots to offer and I would recommend exploring all areas in the city!
culture_adjustment: I found it very easy - the aussies are very welcoming.
socializing_tips: The students at the hospital were really kind, welcoming, and interested in learning about another culture. Just go up to them and ask – I only experienced positive responses.
cultural_challenges: I didn't find anything particularly challenging.
culture_appreciated: I experienced a genuine interest in getting to know new people.
top3_advice: 1) Align your expectations with the department when you start, so you can get the most out of your placement. 2) Always speak up if there’s something you don’t understand or are unsure about – they are really good at teaching. 3) Dive in and take on patients yourself – they are often very kind and patient when you’re a foreign student.
other_useful_info: I can’t think of anything else for now.
most_rewarding: I learned a great deal about the healthcare system in a new country and how to interact with culturally diverse patients respectfully!
greatest_challenge: I think the biggest challenge at the beginning was figuring out how to express myself politely to patients from a different culture when giving difficult news or asking sensitive questions. However, I quickly learned this along the way and can take these experiences with me.
