crucial_aspects: I have also wanted to go but the nature and the people were a big part of the reason I choose Australia. Have always heard so much about the country and I thought this was the best way to experience it.
info_ease: It was preet easy. They gave you everything you needed to know in the introduction day and the persons to contact if you needed anything.
arrival_assistance: I didn't receive any as I don't think you'll need that much assistance when you arrive as most things are pretty much all done. The only thing could be classes but they are helpfull with that.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was pretty easy process as they guided you the whole way through with reminders of when you had to do certain things and what.
registration_help: We had a student coordinator who you could always contact if there was anything you neeeded or just had a question. This was really helpfull and you shoulnd't worry about contacting to much as one too much is better than one to little.
registration_success: Pretty successful as I got the classes I registered for but not necessarily the was I wanted but just try to registre for as many as you can as you can then choose the ones that sounds most interesting.
registration_advice: Just follow the instructions and it will be a walk in the park and ask questions if you have any.
course_level: I would say the level was average and you shouldn't worry about that at all. It's almost the same as UCPH.
teaching_comparison: Bit different as I'm used to more of a class were here it was big lectures. Here they are also more focused on you
courses_enrolled: Quantitative Business Analysis, Quantitative Methods in Economics, International Trade, Learning in Outdoor Education
recommended_courses: Learning in Outdoor Education would be my biggest recommendation to any student. It's a course were you learn about the outdoors in Australia and where you get to go on hikes with your class and even a weekend trip.
unexpected_costs: I wouldn't say there were any unexpedted cost. It will depend on the travels you do as they sometimes came unexpeted and suddenly as you sometimes just decided to go as there was space in your calendar.
cost_comparison: Transport was more expensive then i thought but you can get a commision card for students but it's still a bit expensive. The. food and drinks are less expensive than i thought.
activities_available: Many but the problem is that many of the outdoor sports were done for the 2 semester as they had the finals in september so you couldn't sign up for any of those which is pretty frustrating but there are still many others to choose from.
activities_recommended: Do some sports as it's a good way to learn other people and as well learn about Australian culture through sports.
weekend_recommendations: Not anything particulary but just to go on as many trips as you through out the semester even if it is just a day trip or a little week. Just go and enjoy the country as you don't have to worry about the classes as you can keep up still.

socializing_tips: Just go out and be open for anything. Go to the events at school and try to talk to them in class as most are open to talk and hear about your culture as well.
cultural_challenges: THe biggest difference is how international Sydney is compared to Copenhagen. There are so many nationalities but I wouldn't say there was anything that was challenging.
culture_appreciated: The openness from everybody. It was so easy to fit in as everybody have done the same thing and if not they know how it can be.
top3_advice: Just be open for the adventures and experiences you get along the way. Don't miss out on anything because you stress about the courses you pnly have to pass so enjoy your time there and have fun.
other_useful_info: Do your research on the courses and what are available to you before you get there as it will be much easier and less stressfull.
most_rewarding: The people you meet and get to know. I thought it would have been the things you see which have also been so rewarding but the people you meet is the most rewarding thing I would say. So you be open to meet and talk to as many as you can.
greatest_challenge: Having time to do all the things you wanted to and as well what you wanted to prioritise instead of others things.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go somewhere english-speaking, outside Europe but not the US and somewhere sunny which led me to Australia:)

housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Sydney og Australien er fuldstændig fantastisk, men de har en boligkrise lige nu, så husk at søg en masse legater og vær indstillet på at dele et værelse med anden, hvis du skal afsted
registration_process: Man har mulighed for at skifte fag i løbet af de første to uger og man kan ofte selv vælge, hvilket tidspunkt man gerne vil have sin holdundervisning, hvilket giver mulighed for et fleksibelt skema og mulighed for at rejse i løbet af semesteret.

teaching_comparison: Mindre krævende, mere holdningsbaseret, meget venstreorienteret. Til gengæld var alle underviserne meget passionerede om deres fag og ønskede virkelig, at vi studerende bidrog med vores inputs.

recommended_courses: Fantastisk underviser i det antropologiske fag "Rethinking Poverty" Underviseren i fredsfaget var ret irriterende og selvsmagende Hvis du har haft et fag om International Politik er Forces of Changes in Int Relations meget nemt og overfladisk.

activities_available: Sportsklubber, hobbyklubber, religiøse foreninger. Altså der var ALLE slags foreninger!
activities_recommended: Hike-klubben på uni er en fantastisk måde at komme ud at opleve en masse af Australiens smukke natur meget billigt
weekend_recommendations: Tag til Whitsundays - det er de lækreste bountystrande, som jeg nogensinde har været på. Når du er der bør du desuden købe en tur, hvor du overnatter på et sejlskib.
culture_adjustment: Australiere minder meget om danskere, men er lidt mere åbne og amerikanske i deres møde med fremmede.
socializing_tips: Det er svært. Regn med at komme ind i en boble med andre exchange-students. Og så undgå kun at være sammen med andre danskere - det er trods alt sjovere at møde nye mennesker fra hele verden.
cultural_challenges: De har en forholdsvis striks alkohol-lovgivning, så du kommer ikke ind på klubben, hvis du er tydeligt beruset.
culture_appreciated: Klimaet, naturen og alle de fantastiske mennesker fra hele verden, som jeg mødte.
top3_advice: Det er dyrt. Så husk at søge masser af legater og skriv dig op til kollegiet Queen Marys Building.
other_useful_info: Hvis du er i tvivl om du skal tage af sted, så gør det. Men forvent at sparegrisen er tom, når du kommer hjem igen.
most_rewarding: Alle de nye venskaber og bekendtskaber, som jeg fik. Nu har jeg et netværk i hele verden, så jeg altid har en lokal at besøge, når jeg er ude at rejse.
greatest_challenge: Savnede min kæreste og mine venner

crucial_aspects: I actually didn't intend on choosing Tasmania. I had missed the first application deadline to apply for other universities in Australia and therefor ended up being able to only choose between Tasmania or Canberra. I chose Tasmania because of the beautiful nature, the cheaper prices, the sense of community and the fact that the UTAS website was very easy to understand and use to search for subjects.
overall_comments: I was in SUCH DOUBT about whether or not to do this exchange semester. I was originally going to do it during my Bachelor's degree, but it all got cancelled due to COVID. I didn't think it would be possible to even do this during my Master's, but it all worked out in the end and I could not be more grateful for this experience. I know it's hard work putting this exchange experience together and using the time applying and planning for the semester, but it's 100 % worth it in my opinion. I also had personal reasons for doubting my choice to do this (I was worried about having to do long-distance with my partner), but this was also worth the experience in the end. I learned so much about myself and came back slightly braver and more confident than when I left. I've also experienced what's it's like to study in Australia and made so many new friends along the way. If you are wondering whether or not you should put in the work and hours to plan an exchange semester for yourself, then this is your sign to do it. I loved my life here in Denmark and couldn't really understand why I'd want to leave it all, but wow - this experience has been one of the best times of my life!
info_ease: Georgia and Patrick at UTAS' Exchange Office are delightful people that are ready to help. They sent a bunch of emails prior to arrival about enrolment and other information. They also sent out a calendar invite link to book a meeting with one of them to just say hi and get acquainted once you arrive. I definitely recommend doing this. They'll buy you coffee and give you all the info you need about orientation week, MyLo, signing up for units, changing units, enrolment deadlines, etc.
arrival_assistance: The UTAS accommodation office helped me get checked in to the Uni Apartments and the Exchange Coordinators at UTAS reached out and sent a bunch of info my way. As part of living at student accommodation, there was a whole Orientation week and even a P-week prior to that. So basically two full weeks of intro activities that provide campus tours, city tours, get-togethers and barbecues. It was very social and I felt so welcomed and received. Keep in mind I started in February, which is their semester 1.
arrival_comments: Definitely join as much O-week related stuff as possible. The accommodation had introduction activities at the same time as the exchange office did, but we kind of just picked and chose what we came to and this worked out great. There are some events that are mandatory though - so keep an eye out for those.

You might also have to swap things around if there are timetable clashes.

Also, make sure your units are actually offered in-person. I had 3 out of 4 units that were online, and this is the only reason I rated my overall experience a 9 out of 10 instead of a 10 out of 10.

teaching_comparison: They put a lot of emphasis on being able to argument for the points you make in class and in assignments, so be prepared for this. Also, the reading lists (altså pensumlister) for the units are merely suggestions of what to read. It's assumed that you read more or broader than just this list when completing an assignment, so remember to include a bunch of self-found literature! This seems very opposite to KU, so I figured it might be worth mentioning.
courses_enrolled: CAM720 - Health research methods HEJ509 - Strategic Digital Media KHA619 - Relationship counselling KHA609 - Counselling Skills
recommended_courses: I took HEJ509 as a valgfag / elective unit and this was such a blast! It's a hands-on and creative class that doesn't involve much reading, so I really enjoyed the break from heavy academia and the very collaborative classes.
unexpected_costs: We rented a car for the duration of our stay from a rental company in Hobart and even though this cost 600 DKK per person (we were 6) per month, it was a GAME CHANGER and almost a MUST in order to explore all the nature and beautiful surroundings around Hobart. Seriously do this. It made the biggest difference. We also had friends that bought a car and sold it before they left for the same price. This also worked out great for them.
cost_comparison: Less - Tasmania is so much cheaper than for example Sydney and Melbourne, so I think you save quite a lot of money by going here instead. I'm going to miss the coffees for 25 kroner!
activities_available: The first intro / orientation week had PLENTY of social activities and if you live at one of the colleges (or the university apartments at College Road), there will be plenty of parties and social events throughout the semester as well.
activities_recommended: See Tasmania! Rent a car and go drive! Our favourite hikes were just 1,5 hours away from Hobart - Cape Hauy and Cape Raoul. Also, there's the Rivulet Track at the base of Mount Wellington which is literally 8 minutes from Hobart. Also, make sure to go camping before the weather gets cold.
weekend_recommendations: - All the beautiful nature (Cradle Mountain, Mount Wellington, Mount Field, Cape Hauy, Tasman Peninsula, Maria Island, Bruny Island, King Solomon's Cave). - Historical & Cultural Sites (Port Arthur, Mona) - Wildlife Sanctuaries (UnZoo or Bonorong) - During winter: Dark Mofo in Hobart
culture_adjustment: Very easy. People are so genuinely friendly and welcoming.
socializing_tips: Attend the barbecues at the start of the semester! I know it's a lot of sausages, but it's a great way to meet new people.
cultural_challenges: In the start I was a little shocked at the "style". It's a lot of bare feet, oversized t shirts, mustaches and mullets. But you get used to it, and people are so friendly, even though they look a little rugged.
culture_appreciated: The openness, the respect for nature and wildlife, the fact that everybody is so outdoorsy and active in their freetime (rock climbing, mountain biking, bushwalking, hiking, swimming, etc).
top3_advice: 1. Get a car when you arrive (either rent or buy) - this gives you so much freedom and allows you to see 100 times more then if you didn't have one 2. Reach out to the exchange office or accommodation office if you have questions - they are really there to help you! 3. Explore as much of the nature as you can. Tasmania really is STUNNING and there will be so much to see. 4. Don't overpack, but if you do, you can always go down to the post office in Battery point (much better service then in sandy bay) and send some clothes home. I sent a box with 15 kg of clothes for 1200 DKK - which was far cheaper than having an extra suitcase on the flights home. 5. Double check that your units are available for in-person teaching. Almost all my classes were online and this was not very fun at all.
other_useful_info: Bus: The UniHopper is great to get around if you don't have a car and find yourself living at College Road. Gym: There is a UniGym at the Sandy Bay campus which is a very basic but effective gym to stay active :) Bedding: if you book a room at the College Road Uni apartments, there most likely won't be any bedding when you arrive. I was lucky enough to be provided sheets and a duvet by accommodation, but if not, try go over to the laundry room and check the closets! Other exchange students usually leave their bedding in these. I'd recommend not arriving at night, so that you have time to go to K-mart or Target in town to by bedding and sheets before your first night. Doctor's and Insurance: It's compulsory to get a MediBank insurance, but I actually only used my Danish insurance when claiming doctor's visits and blood tests. They reimbursed 100% (I used Europæiske) and this worked much better for me then having to claim via MediBank. Also, if you do get sick, I can recommend the Private Doctor's Clinic at Sandy bay - the appointments are expensive, but if your insurance covers it, then it's worth it! If not, urgent care in Hobart is free (but there's always a 2-4 hour wait).
most_rewarding: The fact that I have been dreaming of doing this for so long and finally got to do it. Also the fact that I'm coming home with so many new friendships and life experiences that have matured me as a person.
greatest_challenge: The fact that most of my classes were online. The units I took had quite a heavy workload and I often felt I was juggling a lot of school work compared to at KU. I often felt stressed about having to uphold my life in Denmark by catching up and facetiming with friends and family while also having time and energy to meet the new people around me in Tassie.
other_comments: I really hope this has helped you decide to go to UTAS in Tasmania. It really really really was the experience of a lifetime and well-worth applying for.

crucial_aspects: I chose Tasmania as my preferred destination due to the similarities between the Danish and Australian health care systems and because of the language. Also I was very interested in exploring the beautiful nature in Tasmania.
overall_comments: I will highly recommend going on exchange to Tasmania if you want to experience parts of the Australian nature and culture in small and a safe environment.
info_ease: I received information via email from a contact person at University of Tasmania and found the rest of the information on their website and with the help from other students who had been on exchange. In the beginning, it was a bit overwhelming with all the new information but it was manageable.
arrival_assistance: My contact person at University of Tasmania met me one of the first days upon my arrival which was a great help. She showed me the hospital and made sure that all my registrations, IT logins ect. were ok.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I will highly recommend going on exchange to Tasmania if you want to experience parts of the Australian nature and culture in small and a safe environment.
registration_process: For the registration you'll have to send a lot of documents, fill out forms from the university and hospital and send a photo. I was very surprised that your ID-documents needed to be signed by an Australian Notary. It is quite expensive but needs to be done.
registration_help: I received most of the information via email from a contact person at University of Tasmania. It explained most of the process but I also needed help from other students who have been on exchange.
registration_success: Very successful! I was able to do the clinical rotation as I wished for.
registration_advice: The registration process may seem a bit overwhelming in the beginning. Break it down step by step and ask for help a the host university, your own university or ask other students who have been on exchange. Even though it'll take quite some time and money, it is definitely worth all the work!
academics_comments: I will highly recommend going on exchange to Tasmania if you want to experience parts of the Australian nature and culture in small and a safe environment.
course_level: I did a 3-month clinical rotation at Department of General Surgery at Royal Hobart Hospital as a part of my 11th semester of the master of Medicine.
teaching_comparison: As a medical student, be aware that the way of teaching in Australia is slightly different that in the Danish health care system. The students in Australia is a bit more passive at the ward and spend a lot of the time observing. As always you'll need to reach out to get involved and to get an opportunity to improve your pratical skills - this is even more important as an exchange student. Except this, the style of teaching resembles the style at the Danish hospitals.
courses_enrolled: 3-month clinical rotation at Department of General Surgery at Royal Hobart Hospital
recommended_courses: I would recommend spending a part of your clinical rotation at the Emergency Department. My experience is that you'll be able to practice your clinical skills better here since the students in the Emergency Department often get the opportunity to see their own patients. The other part of the rotation, I would spend on one or more of the different wards at the hospital. Here you get the opportunity to learn more about a specific department and experience how the doctors work at the ward.
unexpected_costs: The Australian Notary who had to approve my ID-documents for the registration process (2000 DKK)
cost_comparison: The "cost of living" is much comparable to Denmark.
activities_available: Cooking classes, sports classes, day trips in the weekend, a dinner for all the students living on campus ever 14th day.
activities_recommended: I would highly recommend participating in as many activities arranged by the university as possible. It is a great way to meet other students and to experience Tasmania.
weekend_recommendations: Especially the day trips arranged by the student organization TUSA are a great way to meet new friends and explore Tasmania in a cheaper way.
culture_adjustment: Very easy - the culture is not very different from back home. Australians are very friendly and openminded.
socializing_tips: Be open minded and catch all opportunities to participate in social events.
cultural_challenges: I did not experience any challenging cultural differences.
culture_appreciated: How friendly and open minded Australians are.
top3_advice: Reach out for every opportunity to learn at the hospital. Participate in the social events arranged by the university. Explore the stunning nature in your weekends.
other_useful_info: It can be difficult to connect with the other medical exchange students at the hospital. Ask your contact person at the hospital or the other students. If possible, try to start your exchange in the beginning of July to make sure that you're a part of the introduction week at the university. Here you'll receive good information and meet a lot of people.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange was to live 3 months in a country so far away from home. It is a great way to gain more self-confidence and to get a new perspective on yourself and your everyday life back home. Also it has been very interesting to experience another health care system and compare it to the Danish health care system. Last, it has improved my skills in professional communication in English.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was to get used to being far away from family and friends for a decent amount of time. Make sure to participate in social events, meet other students and make new friendships!
other_comments: I highly recommend going on exchange and studying a semester abroad. It'll be an experience of a lifetime! :)

crucial_aspects: One of the key factors in choosing my study destination was Australia’s unique and diverse agriculture. The country has completely different climatic conditions, crops, and production systems compared to what I’m familiar with in Denmark, which provides me with a new and valuable perspective for my studies. Additionally, it was important for me to experience a different culture and the distinctive wildlife, which have both played a significant role in my academic and personal development.
overall_comments: I truly enjoyed my time abroad, and I would highly recommend the experience to others. It has helped me build a broad network and gain a wider perspective on environmental issues, sustainability, and cultural challenges—both globally and locally.
info_ease: It has been relatively easy.
arrival_assistance: I received a lot of help from the Learning Abroad team. They were able to assist with everything from housing and jobs to course selection and even the small details.
arrival_comments: I have been very satisfied. I felt safe and supported throughout the entire process. In addition, there were some great activities organized by the Learning Abroad team that made it easy to meet both other exchange students and local students.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I truly enjoyed my time abroad, and I would highly recommend the experience to others. It has helped me build a broad network and gain a wider perspective on environmental issues, sustainability, and cultural challenges—both globally and locally.
registration_process: It was simple and easy to navigate.
registration_help: The Learning Abroad team was extremely supportive.

I spent about an hour with someone from the Learning Abroad team to sort out my courses, as several of them were in the same schedule group.
registration_advice: Use the Learning Abroad team. If they can’t help you, they know who else you should get in touch with.
academics_comments: I truly enjoyed my time abroad, and I would highly recommend the experience to others. It has helped me build a broad network and gain a wider perspective on environmental issues, sustainability, and cultural challenges—both globally and locally.
course_level: I took 2 first-year courses and 2 second-year courses.
teaching_comparison: The teaching involved a lot of online material and few hours of physical attendance in some courses. Often consisted of recorded PowerPoint presentations and discussions or exercises related to the material when meeting physically. In courses with laboratory and fieldwork, there were more in-person sessions where attendance was required. I think it worked quite well.
courses_enrolled: KLA115 Sustainable Resource Management KLA255 Introductory Entomology and Plant Pathology KPA214 Plants in Action KSA101 Introduction to Marine and Antarctic Science A
recommended_courses: I would recommend the course KLA115 Sustainable Resource Management, as it is a very broad course that covers many of the sustainability and environmental challenges Australia faces, while also providing a global perspective. The courses Plants in Action and Introductory Entomology and Plant Pathology were also very good, with many practical exercises such as insect collection and nutrient experiments with various plants.
unexpected_costs: I chose to buy a car while I was there, so I had quite a few expenses related to that. Additionally, I also had to purchase a lab coat.
cost_comparison: Vegetables were a bit more expensive than expected, but otherwise most things were priced about the same or slightly higher than in Denmark.
activities_available: Almost everything you could think of.
activities_recommended: Going on many excursions. There are great opportunities for camping and hiking, which allow you to get out into nature and experience Tasmania’s wild landscapes.
weekend_recommendations: Going on many excursions. There are great opportunities for camping and hiking, which allow you to get out into nature and experience Tasmania’s wild landscapes.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy to adapt. People are very hospitable and have a great understanding of exchange students.
socializing_tips: Just be yourself!
cultural_challenges: Mostly the language, as there was a bit of slang.
culture_appreciated: That it is a country area, so it was great to see rodeo and the Australian style of agriculture.
top3_advice: Consider getting a car, as there are no trains or buses that go out to the beautiful nature areas. It gives you great freedom to explore the whole island during holidays and weekends. I really enjoyed living in a 6-person apartment because there was plenty of space, and you get to know the people you live with. Be patient when learning their school system, and everything will work out.
other_useful_info: Definitely live on campus. It’s very social, and it’s easier.
most_rewarding: The nature, the people, and diving – I got my diving certification there, which I highly recommend because of the beautiful marine life.
greatest_challenge: I had some difficulty understanding everything because my English wasn’t very strong, but it got better and better.
other_comments: I am very grateful for my stay and will definitely visit Tasmania again. It is the most beautiful place I have ever been.

crucial_aspects: The opportunity for more practical application of theory especially within my chosen field. As some who wants to work in conservation I found that Australia possesses a higher degree of expertise.
info_ease: The people at UTAS were extremely helpful and accommodating making the whole process very straightforward even before arrival. They were also quick to answer questions over email.
arrival_assistance: There were multiple introduction seminars and events specifically targeted at exchange and study abroad students which were very informative.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You send a priority list to the echange coordinator and they have to do the registration for you. If you wanna change your courses you have to contact them again later either by email or (better) in person. It's pretty easy though.
registration_help: UTAS website and the exhange coordinators (they were pretty easy to contact)
registration_success: It was fine, didn't get all my top priority courses since some of them ended up clashing and others got filled but that's how it goes.
registration_advice: Make sure to research some backup courses incase you don't get the exct ones you had planned. You can always ask the exchange coordinators for recommendations.
course_level: Good level to the courses, matches what I found back home for the most part. Be aware that taking second year courses is an option, but might mean they have more expectations that you've had certain first year courses.
teaching_comparison: Depends on the course, but generally a lot of practical exercises including field and lab work in my case which was great this also included data collection and analysis for use in report writing. Be prepared that assignments are a big part of the assessment, depending on your courses you may not have any exams.
courses_enrolled: Antarctic Ecology Biodiversity conservation Fauna of Tasmania Marine Resource Management and Conservation
recommended_courses: Biodiversity conservation was great with some great opportunites for field excursions Fauna of Tasmania gave a really good insight of both theory and how it could be applied Antarctic ecology had an awsome teacher and offered great insight into scientific practice with some reall cool prac classes.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: I found meat to be fairly expensive. The visa was also quite expensive at around 8000 dkk, last I heard this might go up again in the coming years.
activities_available: Loads of clubs for basically all interests. They have a clubs and societies event where you get to meet bunch of them. A lot of good opportunities if you like to be active or outdoors. The student association (TUSA) also orgnised a bunch of trips you could sign up for.
activities_recommended: I took my open water diver certificate which was awsome (though also kinda cold in winter) - I actually found it to be cheaper than at home which was surprising but great since Tassie offers some georgeous diving.
weekend_recommendations: Go hiking, it is beautiful, wish I had gone out more. Also go on the public transport ferry, it is dirt cheap but a beutiful short ride, and you can explore around a new area for the day.
culture_adjustment: Really easy, no real language barrier helps a lot. Very similar culture to Europe.
socializing_tips: Most of them are really friendly. Obviously many already have esstblished friends, but just jump in and don't be afraid to approach people, especially in class.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: There is some effort at acknowleding the traditional owners of the land which I really appreciated. otherwise just really enjoyed the outdoor culture.
top3_advice: This will depend on what you are studying and what you are used to. Personally, as someone studying biology, I was not used to the amount and quality of assignments we had to do, as such i would advise: 1. Get an idea EARLY of the kind of assignments (e.g. how many words and references you need) and when they are do. Research takes time and will slow down writing, plan for this 2. Try to plan out you assignments, don't count on being able to finish all of them the week before they are do, they Will pile up. 3. Remember to have fun, don't spend all your time studying, grade are likely to be converted to pass/fail
other_useful_info: Take advantage of the TUSA food bank for cheap food.
most_rewarding: I feel much stronger academically than before I went. I got a lot more opportunities to practise research and do data analysis than back home, not to mention all the practical work and awesome field excursions. Also meeting all the new people was great. Made some really solid friends and felt really welcome which was so nice.
greatest_challenge: Time management. I really underestimated the number of assignments and how much time they would take. I feel I spent way to much time at the library.

culture_adjustment: Australians are generally very outgoing and happy to engage with "strangers". Be open and join when it is possible. They are easy to be around and I felt good being here culturally right away.
socializing_tips: Join UTS clubs, go to the parties, chat with your study group members outside uni.
cultural_challenges: Australian accents can be challenging to understand, but it's generally not a problem.
culture_appreciated: People in Sydney are very outdoorsy and active which I really liked. Also, their coffee culture is next level (and half the price of coffee in CPH). The weather is generally very sunny as well.
top3_advice: Be open to new experiences and people It can be difficult and stressful to get everything organised in the beginning, but it will be all worth it! Explore everything Sydney (and Australia) has to offer when you can
other_useful_info: UTS is in the center of Sydney and easy to get to no matter which suburb you stay in.
most_rewarding: To experience living in another city far away from home, and learn the language even more fluently. Also, all the people that I have met and the opportunities I have gotten.
greatest_challenge: The first four weeks were quite challenging. Finding a place to live, setting up phone, getting an Australian bank, etc. can be stressful. But it all works out!

recommended_courses: All classes - except Trade Marks Law. The others were easy to understand and with very sweet and motivating teachers. Trade Marks Law required some pre-knowledge and all the other students were professionals so the academic level was much higher.
unexpected_costs: I did not encounter any.

activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend showing up on Orientation Day to hear from all the clubs and get a feeling of what you find exciting. Personally, I found the hangout spot to be quite fun.
weekend_recommendations: Either do a roadtrip up the East or West Coast in a van. It is a bit expensive but so worth it.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy due to it being a Western culture as well.
socializing_tips: Come to the introductory arrangements as they will also be attending.
cultural_challenges: There was not really anything that was difficult. However, I quickly learned that Australians are much in debate about the Aborigines and their legal standing and, therefore, it was important to learn about the issues as it came up in most discussions.
culture_appreciated: They were super laid back, welcoming and positive.
top3_advice: 1. To show up for orientation events to get to know a lot of other students. 2. There are surprisingly many exchange students (especially from Denmark). 3. It is very modern and situated in the city which is super nice for sightseeing in breaks.

crucial_aspects: I chose Sydney as destination because Australia has a different legal system than Denmark. I have no doubt that this aspect will benefit me in my future career. In addition to the professional aspect, Australia as a country offers a lot of experiences that are not found elsewhere in the world. By choosing Sydney as my destination, I knew that I would not only experience living in a "real" metropolis but also have ample opportunities for enjoying nature. Furthermore, Australia was a perfect choice for me because I wanted to be out on my own. The time difference between Australia and Denmark automatically forces you to be more present and figure things out for yourself.
overall_comments: No.
info_ease: I found that the university in the host country had prepared me well for my arrival in Australia. Australia has specific requirements and procedures for entry, so it was helpful that the university had provided various materials to read through before I departed.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance when I arrived at my study destination.
arrival_comments: No.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: No.
registration_process: It was a very confusing process, but luckily the university has an entire department dedicated to assisting exchange students, making it easy to get help and resolve any issues that arose.
registration_help: The university has a dedicated department ready to assist.
registration_success: Some of the courses I wanted to take were never offered, which was unfortunate. However, I ended up with some courses that I still found satisfactory.
registration_advice: Be prepared for it to be a difficult process and have plenty of alternative courses ready in case the ones you prefer are not offered.
academics_comments: No.
course_level: The level varied significantly from course to course. In courses where there were primarily exchange students, I found the level to be low. In courses with Australian students, I perceived the level to be higher but still lower than in Denmark.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was very different from that at UCPH. Class participation often contributed to one's grade, so the students were much more active than back home. Additionally, we had a lot of supplementary online teaching material, which was helpful. Furthermore, all the teaching was in the form of seminars, and we did not have any lectures.
courses_enrolled: Justice Principles of Public International Law Dispute Resolution Trade Marks Law
recommended_courses: Justice was completely different from any other legal course I have experienced at UCPH. Trade Marks Law was a challenging but fun course, and the instructors were really excellent.
unexpected_costs: The weather in Australia changed towards the end, so it was necessary to purchase warmer clothing.
cost_comparison: It is significantly more expensive to go shopping in Sydney compared to Copenhagen.
activities_available: At the university, there were all kinds of associations and activities.
activities_recommended: UTS Law Students' Society, UTS Tennis Club, UTS Build (Global leadership program). I personally benefitted from these associations as they provided a network within the university.
weekend_recommendations: Australia has a lot to offer. Personally, I visited Melbourne and went on a road trip down the Great Ocean Road as well as a road trip up the East Coast.
culture_adjustment: There are plenty of things happening in Sydney, and there are ample opportunities to be part of various sports clubs, and more. Therefore, I found it easy to adapt as there were constantly new experiences to be had.
socializing_tips: I personally joined two running clubs where there were only Australians. It was the best way for me to make friends with people from Australia.
cultural_challenges: I did not find any.
culture_appreciated: Australians are very open and helpful.
top3_advice: 1. Sign up for all sorts of events during the first few weeks to get to know people from different fields of study. 2. Take the time to plan your assignements and deadlines, so you know when you can travel. 3. Be open to different cultures.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: The entire experience was incredibly rewarding, both academically and personally.
greatest_challenge: Being so far away from home has its ups and downs.
other_comments: No.

Dette var en smule tidskrævende, og gjorde det mere besværligt at ansøge om fag. Derudover var mange af fagene hurtigt fyldt op, hvilket gjorde at man var nødt til at gå en del på kompromis med, hvilke fag man ville have, for at få sit skema til at gå op.

recommended_courses: Jeg vil anbefale alle de kurser jeg havde: Intellectual Property Commercialisation International Commercial Transactions Law of the Sea Marketing Law Jeg synes det var en god blanding af fag om international ret og fag om australsk ret. Det gav derfor både en større indsigt i den international regulering, men også en indsigt i forskelle og ligheder mellem dansk og australsk ret.
unexpected_costs: Der var en del omkostninger i starten af opholdet forbundet med at etablere sig, herunder omkostninger til dyne, hovedpude, håndklæder, tallerkener, bestik, pander og øvrige køkkenredskaber.
cost_comparison: Det overraskede mig, at priserne på dagligvarer og restaurantbesøg var mere eller mindre på samme niveau som i Danmark. Til gengæld er omkostningerne forbundet med at bo på kollegie en del dyrere i Sydney end i Danmark.
activities_available: UTS har klubber inden for stort set alle interesseområder, herunder fodbold, håndbold, tennis, musik, adventure aktiviteter og meget mere.
activities_recommended: Jeg deltog ikke i nogle af de non-academic activities, som UTS udbød udover O-Day. Jeg kan dog anbefale at deltage i O-Day, hvor man får et indblik i hvad der foregår på universitetet både socialt og fagligt.

Derudover vil jeg anbefale at besøge en masse af de forskellige strande i Sydney, herunder både de mere kendte strande som Bondi og Manly, men også f.eks. Red Leaf Pool og Castle Rock Beach. Derudover vil jeg anbefale, at man prøver en masse af de forskellige spændende restauranter, som Sydney har at byde på og får smagt en açaí bowl.
culture_adjustment: Jeg synes hurtigt, at jeg blev vant til livet i Sydney, som i høj grad byder på en aktiv livstil med coastal walks, ligesom at alle de lokale er super søde og imødekommende.
cultural_challenges: Jeg føler ikke som som sådan, at der var nogle af de kulturelle forskelle, som var udfordrende.
culture_appreciated: Jeg værdsatte i høj grad, at (stort set) alle australiere er så åbne og imødekommende.
top3_advice: De tre vigtigste ting vil være følgende: 1. Det er normalt, at det hele føles meget overvældende i starten af udvekslingsopholdet, og at man bliver i tvivl, om hvorvidt ens udvekslingsophold nu også kommer til at blive, som man håber. Hvis bare man sørger for at være opsøgende i forhold til at møde nye mennesker, så skal det hele nok gå, og der er mange forskellige måder at møde nye mennesker på, som har de samme interesser som en selv. 2. Sørg for at spare nok penge sammen og få søgt relevante legater, så det ikke skal holde dig tilbage i forhold til at deltage i sociale aktiviteter, som også kan koste penge. Dog er en luksus ved Sydney, at der er så mange aktiviteter, som stort set er gratis udover betaling til transport, såsom at besøge strandene, national parker og lign. 3. Sørg for hurtigt at finde ud af hvordan biblioteket på universitetet fungerer, hvis du ved, at du får brug for det til de fag, som du skal have. Det var super nemt at finde ud af på UTS, og viste sig, at de bøger, som jeg skulle bruge til undervisningen var gratis. Derudover var det deres digitale database, som jeg i høj grad brugte til kildesøgning til 3 ud af 4 af mine eksamener.
other_useful_info: UTS er generelt meget hjælpsomme på alle fronter, og det gælder bare om at række ud eller søge efter hjælp på deres hjemmeside, såfremt man har brug herfor.
most_rewarding: Jeg føler at det største udbytte jeg har fået af opholdet er alle de oplevelser jeg har fået i den smukkeste natur med søde mennesker.
greatest_challenge: Den største udfordring var klart den overvældende følelse, som de fleste får, når man er landet i Sydney og skal til at etablere sig i forhold til social omgangskreds og bolig.

crucial_aspects: Min primære motivation for at vælge Australien har primært været at styrke sproglige og kulturelle kompetencer. Mit ønske har været at blive bedre til engelsk, hvor Australien er et perfekt valg. Derudover har Australien også en vildt imødekommende kultur, hvilket er perfekt, når man kommer fra - til tider - indelukkede Danmark. Rejsemulighederne indenrigs og i de omkringliggende områder er ligeledes virkelig gode.
info_ease: Universitetet gav løbende vejledning om, hvad jeg skulle gøre og hvornår, herunder information om det obligatoriske orienteringsmøde. Derudover havde de guides til forskellige aspekter af studielivet, såsom fagvalg. Studieadministrationen på værtsuniversitetet var også meget effektiv og hurtig til at besvare henvendelser, så jeg vil anbefale at tage kontakt, hvis der er behov for hjælp.
arrival_assistance: Jeg kontaktede studieadministrationen vedrørende valg af fag, hvor jeg ret hurtigt fik svar.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Registreringen hos værtsuniversitetet var enkel. De krævede blot nogle grundlæggende oplysninger, bl.a. til studiekortet, men også til registrering til diverse, obligatoriske ting til administration. Hele processen blev forklaret via mail, og det tog højst en til to timer at få det ordnet, efter jeg blev kontaktet over mail.
registration_help: Studieadministrationen er god. Skriv en besked til dem over deres portal, hvis der er problemer. De er hurtige og effektive til at svare.
registration_success: Der var flere udfordringer med fagvalg, da alle fag først skulle godkendes af værtsuniversitetets studieadministration. Afhængigt af faget krævedes der opfyldelse af visse forudsætninger (prerequisites), hvilket betød, at man skulle søge dispensation. Man kunne dog kun søge dispensation for ét fag ad gangen, hvilket gjorde processen besværlig. Først efter opnået dispensation kunne man se, om der var ledige pladser på holdet. Selvom et fag fremgår af kursuskataloget, er det ikke ensbetydende med, at det rent faktisk udbydes. Hvis det udbydes, kan det stadig være fyldt, da pladserne fordeles efter først-til-mølle-princippet. Det betyder, at selv med dispensation er man ikke garanteret en plads. I så fald skal man søge dispensation til et nyt fag og eventuelt også ansøge om ny forhåndsmerit på KU. Derfor giver det bedre mening at vælge fag på værtsuniversitetet først og derefter søge forhåndsmerit.
registration_advice: Studieadministrationen er som nævnt ret god. Giv det et skud, hvis der er problemer, og ellers orienter dig på værtsuniversitetets hjemmeside for andre midler, som kan hjælpe. Alt plejer typisk at stå der
course_level: Jeg havde følgende kurser, som alle både blev forhåndsgodkendt, og som jeg fik efterfølgende merit for: Competition Law in a Global Context Contemporary Business Law International Business Transactions and the Law (undergrad, BA) Introduction to Law (undergrad, BA) Alle fagene udgjorde 6 credits svarende til 7,5 ECTS.
teaching_comparison: Karaktergivningen følger et pointsystem, hvor man maksimalt kan opnå 100 point pr. fag. Eksempelvis kan mundtlig deltagelse give op til 20 point, skriftlige opgaver op til 40 point og eksamen op til 40 point. Hvis man er aktiv i undervisningen og scorer mindst 51 point gennem opgaver og mundtlighed, behøver man i princippet ikke at tage eksamen seriøst for at bestå. Underviseren giver karakterer for både mundtlighed, opgaver og eksamen, og der er ingen anonymitet i bedømmelsen.
courses_enrolled: Competition Law in a Global Context Contemporary Business Law International Business Transactions and the Law (undergrad, BA) Introduction to Law (undergrad, BA) Alle fagene udgjorde 6 credits svarende til 7,5 ECTS.
recommended_courses: Introduction to Law og Contemporary Business Law er en god kombination, fordi det er det samme man lærer i begge fag. Der er således mindre at læse. International Business Transactions and the Law er god for dem, som kan lide obligationsret og shipping. Spændende fag. Jeg havde en underviser, der hed Paddy i både Contemporary Business Law og International Business Transactions and the Law. Hun var virkelig god og det kan anbefales at tage kurserne, hvis det udbydes med hende.
unexpected_costs: Food, Personal spending og Other fees er arbitrært sat til 5.000 kr., da jeg ikke har udregnet, hvor meget jeg faktisk har brugt. Men regn med at bruge lidt penge på rejser og husk at nyde livet :))
cost_comparison: Visum er pisse dyrt. Kostede 6.000 kr. for mit studievisum. Se alternativt om det er muligt at søge det billigere working holiday visum, hvor man også kan studere samtidig. Endnu mere alternativt og billigere, så er der mængderabat, hvis flere søger visum på samme tid. Mobilabonnement kostede mindre end forventet. Mange abonnementer tilbyder for meget data til en for høj pris. Kig efter billigere abonnementer, som ikke er fra de store udbydere som Telstra. Jeg fandt et abonnemnt fra TPG til 10 AUD (45 kr.) om måneden Det er generelt billigere at spise ude
activities_available: Fester, fredagsbar, fitness, gaming, kajak, skydiving
activities_recommended: Universitetets aktiviteter er en oplagt mulighed for at møde andre udvekslingsstuderende - derudover er det pisse grineren at skydive
weekend_recommendations: Spise, shopping og fest: Spice Alley, El Loco (stedet for Frederik mødte Mary), Coogee Pavilion, Glebe Market, The Caterpillar, ivy, Oplevelser og natur: Blue Mountains, Vivid Sydney, alt ved Circular Quay, hesteløb ved Randwick, Royal National Park, Grand Pacific Drive,
culture_adjustment: Australierne er meget åbne og imødekommende, og det er meget nemt at hoppe med på deres kultur. Der er lighedspunkter med det danske, bortset fra at australierne generelt er mere imødekommende
socializing_tips: Hav ja-hatten på og vær imødekommende og nysgerrig :)
cultural_challenges: Sproget kan være lidt svært at forstå til tider, men ellers fungerer det perfekt
culture_appreciated: Alle australiere jeg har mødt har været pisse flinke og mega imødekommende. Sproget er derudover også virkelig fedt
top3_advice: 1. Opholdet er dyrt, men det er pengene værd 2. Husk også at møde andet end danskere 3. Nyd opholdet mens du kan og giv den gas. Hav ja-hatten på!!!! Husk at alt ikke handler om studiet. Det er meget nemt at bestå
other_useful_info: Mange af de bekymringer, man har inden afrejse, viser sig ofte at være ubegrundede og løser sig helt naturligt, når man først er afsted. Selvom det kan føles overvældende at rejse langt væk til ukendte omgivelser uden familie og venner, så hav is i maven – alt falder på plads Det er helt normalt at være nervøs, men du vil hurtigt opleve, at du tilpasser dig og møder nye mennesker, både gennem studiet og sociale aktiviteter. Husk at alle udvekslingsstuderende er i samme situation som dig - alle er uden relationer i et land, de (måske) aldrig har været i før, hvilket kan være nervepirrende, men de er klar til at skabe nye venskaber Udveksling er en fantastisk mulighed for personlig og faglig udvikling. Du vil lære at stå på egne ben, opleve en ny kultur og styrke dine sproglige og akademiske kompetencer. Så tag springet og nyd oplevelsen – det bliver uden tvivl en af de mest givende perioder i dit liv!
most_rewarding: Den mest givende oplevelse på udveksling har været at møde nye mennesker og rejse. Jeg har fået venskaber på tværs af kulturer, oplevet Australien på tæt hold og forbedret mit engelsk markant – både akademisk og i hverdagen
greatest_challenge: Den største udfordring på udveksling har været kontakt med familien og savn. Tidsforskellen på 8-10 timer gjorde det svært at finde gode tidspunkter for videoopkald, så kontakten var begrænset. Det krævede tilvænning, men hverdagen og nye oplevelser hjalp med at håndtere savnet.

crucial_aspects: I have always wanted to travel to and live in Australia, and Sydney stood out because of its strong academic reputation, English-speaking environment, and unique location where the city life and beaches are closely connected. Australia offers a different academic and cultural perspective compared to Europe and Sydney in particular combines a city with easy access to nature and outdoor activities. The University of Technology Sydney (UTS) offered courses that aligned well with my degree, and the opportunity to experience a new education system while developing both academically and personally was an important in my decision.
info_ease: Overall, the information provided prior to arrival was clear and well structured. The application process is quite long and requires attention to detail, as there are several steps and deadlines to keep track of. However, both UCPH and UTS provided thorough and helpful information throughout the process, and there was plenty of time to complete all requirements. The host institution shared detailed guides and I received all essential information regarding enrollment, courses, and housing through emails, which made the transition to studying and living in Sydney very smooth.
arrival_assistance: Upon arrival, I received support through orientation programs and detailed information from UTS via email. The university organized welcome activities such as an introduction meeting and a campus tour, which were very helpful in getting familiar with the campus and academic environment. In addition, there were social events for exchange and international students, including a pub crawl, which was a fun and effective way to meet other students on exchange. Staff members and student ambassadors were available to answer questions, assist with practical matters, and provide guidance on campus facilities and student services.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process was generally straightforward, although it required some planning and the completion of various forms and documents. Course registration was done through an online system where we could browse available courses and register during a designated period. I had already decided which courses I wanted in advance, which I would strongly recommend, as UTS follows a first-come, first-served principle and it is important to register quickly once the system opens.
registration_help: I did not personally use much of the available support, as the guides and instructions provided were sufficient. However, the international student office and various online support resources were available to assist us with course selection, registration and any other questions throughout the process.
registration_success: I was able to register for my preferred courses, as I already knew which ones I wanted to apply for in advance. The system also allowed me to choose preferred days and times for my classes. If a class time was full, it was possible to join a waitlist and be enrolled if a spot became available later.
registration_advice: I would recommend reviewing all available courses in advance and deciding which ones you prefer before registration opens. Make sure to register as early as possible, and always have backup course options in case your first choices fill up quickly.
course_level: The courses were generally comparable in level to my studies at KU, although some courses felt slightly less advanced. Overall, the academic level was appropriate and well suited for exchange students.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style was more interactive and continuous, with regular assignments, group work and active participation throughout the semester. I really appreciated this approach, as it allowed me to work steadily with the course material and complete a significant portion of the assessment during the semester. Many courses were assessed through three to four assignments, which together made up the final grade, rather than relying solely on one final exam.
courses_enrolled: 52703 - Media Influence 52661 - Strategic Communication in Society 52718 - The Social Life of Technology 52681 - Understanding Digital Audiences
recommended_courses: I would highly recommend Understanding Digital Audiences, as it was very relevant to my studies at home and covered similar concepts, but from a different and international perspective. The course provided valuable insights and practical understanding that complemented my academic background well. Media Influence is also a course I would recommend, as it addresses highly relevant and contemporary topics and offers a great deal of freedom in how assignments are approached, allowing students to tailor their work to their own interests. Strategic Communication was a more demanding course with several assignments and a strong focus on the Australian media landscape, including topics related to Indigenous issues. While this can be somewhat challenging for exchange students who are less familiar with the local context, it was still a very interesting and educational course. Overall, I was very satisfied with my course choices and found them both academically rewarding and relevant.
unexpected_costs: I traveled quite a lot during my exchange and was surprised by how expensive it is to travel within Australia. Australia is generally not a cheap country, so I would strongly recommend having some savings, as most students will want to explore and travel while they are there. Planning trips well in advance can help secure better prices. I was also surprised by the high cost of renting an apartment. Housing in Sydney is significantly more expensive than in Denmark, and many students choose to share rooms in order to reduce costs. Even then, rent often ends up around 7000 - 8000 DKK per person per month. On-campus accommodation may be slightly more affordable and is worth considering.
cost_comparison: I was surprised by how expensive local transportation in Sydney was, especially buses and trains. There are no particularly student-friendly options or monthly passes, and you pay per trip, which adds up quickly. As a result, we often used Uber or DiDi, as the price was frequently similar. Food, coffee, alcohol, and eating out were roughly the same price level as in Denmark, which was less surprising and made budgeting easier than expected.

activities_recommended: Joining student societies and sports clubs is a great way to meet people and feel integrated quickly.
weekend_recommendations: Explore Sydney’s beaches, drink coffee and go to the parks, go shopping, coastal walks, and take trips to places like the Blue Mountains or along travel a few weeks down the East Coast.
culture_adjustment: Adjusting was relatively easy. Australians are open, friendly and welcoming which made it easy to settle in.
socializing_tips: Be active and open, join clubs, attend the social events and don’t be afraid to start conversations.
cultural_challenges: The main challenges were mostly practical, such as adjusting to the cost of living and learning how to navigate a new city. It was also an adjustment to communicate exclusively in English on a daily basis, both socially and academically, and to have all courses and interactions conducted in English. However, this quickly became easier over time and was also a valuable part of the experience.
culture_appreciated: The relaxed lifestyle, the nice weather, outdoor culture, friendliness, and emphasis on work–life balance.
top3_advice: 1. Plan ahead, especially when it comes to course registration and housing. Registration follows a first-come, first-served system, so knowing your preferred courses in advance is important. 2. Be active by joining clubs or social events early on. It makes a big difference in meeting both local and international students. 3. Make the most of the experience outside academics. Sydney and Australia have so much to offer, so take time to explore, travel and enjoy the lifestyle alongside your studies. And have the money for it :)
other_useful_info: Sydney is an amazing city to live in, but it is important to be prepared for the high cost of living. Budgeting in advance and planning trips early can help manage expenses. The academic system at UTS is more continuous than at UCPH, with several assignments throughout the semester, so staying organized from the beginning is key. Overall, the university provides good support for international students, and taking advantage of the resources and activities offered makes the transition much easier.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the growth that came from living in a completely new environment. I gained greater confidence and adaptability, while forming close friendships with people from many different countries, many of whom I will stay in touch with and bring back into my life in Copenhagen. Experiencing an entirely new country, culture, academic system and lifestyle in Sydney was incredibly enriching and motivating. The exchange inspired me both academically and personally, and it is an experience that I will carry with me long into the future.
greatest_challenge: A little challenge was studying and communicating exclusively in English every day, but it quickly became more comfortable and ultimately strengthened my academic and language skills.

crucial_aspects: It was important for me to study in an English-speaking country that offered exciting opportunities to experience both nature and culture. I have always wanted to visit Australia, and because it is so far away from Denmark, I saw the exchange as a unique and once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to live there for half a year.
info_ease: Overall, it was not difficult to find the required information upon arrival. However, the process is quite long and involves many deadlines that need to be met. I would therefore strongly recommend creating a clear overview of all important deadlines and ensuring that the necessary documents are prepared in advance. Despite the length of the process, it is absolutely worth it in the end.
arrival_assistance: The university had organized an orientation week upon arrival. This included a mandatory introductory session as well as a variety of social activities, such as a campus tour, tastings of Australian specialties, and speed-friending events. I did not know anyone before arriving, and although it was sometimes a bit outside my comfort zone, I made an effort to participate in many of the activities at the beginning. This turned out to be a great way to build a network early on while being far from home, as everyone is eager to meet new people.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process was generally straightforward. Before course registration opened, I had already decided which courses I wanted to enroll in, which I would strongly recommend, as UTS operates on a first-come, first-served basis. I therefore set an alarm in the middle of the night when registration opened to ensure that I secured my preferred courses. Registration was completed through an online system where students could select courses from a list of available options. The system also provided detailed timetables for each course, making it possible to choose specific class times. Many students aimed to concentrate their classes into as few days on campus as possible, allowing for greater flexibility during the week.
registration_help: UTS had provided a course catalogue with pre-approved courses that all exchange students could choose from without any issues. There was a wide selection of courses available, and many of them aligned well with my degree program.
registration_success: I was successful in registering for all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: It is important to be aware of which courses you want and to be prepared when registration opens for enrollment.
course_level: Overall, I found the academic level at KU to be somewhat higher than at UTS. However, I was surprised by the continuous assessment structure at UTS, as there were many assignments throughout the semester. Grading is handled differently, with each assignment or presentation contributing a specific percentage to the final grade. For example, in one course I had two major written assignments during the semester, each accounting for 35% of the final grade, followed by an oral exam worth the remaining 30%. This structure required consistent effort throughout the semester rather than focusing solely on a final exam.
teaching_comparison: All of our lectures were held online, and many of them were pre-recorded. Personally, I prefer in-person teaching; however, the pre-recorded lectures offered a high degree of flexibility, as long as they were watched before the scheduled tutorials. This allowed students to engage with the material at a time that suited them best. Overall, the tutorial sessions were largely comparable to those at KU, although the level of preparation among tutors varied considerably. In several of my courses, attendance at tutorials was mandatory and absences were recorded, with only two absences permitted throughout the semester. In one of my courses, 20% of the final grade was based on active participation, which encouraged all students to contribute actively to class discussions.
courses_enrolled: Project Management Career and Portfolio Planning Event Creation Workshop IT Professional and Society
recommended_courses: Career and Portfolio Planning was a very valuable and useful course. As I am currently pursuing my Master’s degree and will soon be entering the job market, the course encouraged meaningful self-reflection by focusing on identifying professional strengths as well as areas for improvement. The final oral examination was designed as a simulated job interview, which made the course particularly relevant and practical.
unexpected_costs: I was surprised by how expensive it was to live in Sydney. I lived in a shared house with 11 other people and paid over DKK 7,000 per month for a single room.
cost_comparison: The visa for Australia is very expensive. I paid over DKK 7,000 for my visa. In addition, traveling within Australia is very expensive. I would therefore recommend allocating sufficient time before departure to apply for scholarships and to travel with some personal savings.
activities_available: There was a wide range of student clubs and societies, including surfing, running, tennis, dance, martial arts, hiking, camping, women in Business, theatre, IT clubs, and there even was a society for swifties. During the orientation week, there was a dedicated day where students could walk around and learn more about the different clubs. There was something for everyone.
activities_recommended: Coastal walks, blue mountains, surf-camp, visiting the opera house, and generally just travelling around Australia, there are so many nice places to visit.
weekend_recommendations: Uluru! It is located in the middle of Australia, and I have never seen anything like it. We slept in swags, which are a type of sleeping bag, and it was one of the greatest experiences.
culture_adjustment: It was pretty easy.
cultural_challenges: I did not encounter many cultural differences that I found challenging. The biggest challenge was probably establishing a daily routine in a new country, but even that became manageable relatively quickly.
culture_appreciated: The relaxed lifestyle and how open and chill Australians are.
top3_advice: 1. Make sure to set aside plenty of time to apply for scholarships before departure. 2. Be active in the social events organized by the university at the beginning, as they are a great way to build a strong network. 3. Travel – there are so many exciting places to explore in Australia!
other_useful_info: Going on exchange requires a significant amount of work, especially before departure, but it is all worth it in the end.
most_rewarding: I went on some incredible trips with the most wonderful people I met during my exchange.
greatest_challenge: The time difference can be challenging when you have family, friends, and a partner back home.

crucial_aspects: Academic opportunities and hearing good things about the city and the study environment.
info_ease: Easy. UT Law is very good at communicating.
arrival_assistance: The international office at UT Law helped with course registration etc.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You register during the first week in an online system. There is an add/ drop period where you can change your courses in the same system. Don't worry about the process at all - UT Law will guide you through it.
registration_help: Lots of help form the international office at UT Law. They guide you through the process and answer any questions you have.
registration_success: I got most of the classes I wanted (4 out of 5) but I dropped one of my classes and had trouble finding a replacement during the add/ drop period.
registration_advice: Don't worry about it, and use the add/ drop period if you change your mind.
course_level: Challenging courses, but the workload was mostly appropriate.
teaching_comparison: At UT Law they use the socratic method in many courses where they cold-call students. Generally, you are expected to be well prepared for class and to participate.
courses_enrolled: U.S. Constitutional Law for Foreign Lawyers Antitrust Wall Street Regulation Corporations and the Constitution Directed Research and Study
recommended_courses: Wall Street Regulation was a fun class and the workload was very light. The professor specifically tries to make it a low stress class. I also really enjoyed Corporations and the Constitution which is a seminar class with Prof. Sepper who is a very good teacher. However, I would only recommend taking seminar classes if you are actually interested in the topic because it's pretty time consuming to write a seminar paper.
unexpected_costs: If you live at a co-op, food is included in the rent, but I bought some additional groceries because depending on the co-op there won't be ingredients for personal cooking etc.
cost_comparison: Books cost about 3000 kr. for the semester even though I bought as much as possible used which was more than I expected. Insurance is very expensive.
activities_available: All kinds! There are a lot of opportunities if you look for them.
activities_recommended: I didn't really use the clubs, but there are free gyms on campus. Greg Gym has a great recreational pool, and it is free to use it as a student. I would also recommend going to as many sports events as possible. Football is a big event and you should experience it at least once. Basketball is also fun, and the women's volleyball team is really good.
weekend_recommendations: Go on trips, both in Texas and in other states. We went hiking in Big Bend National Park in Texas, visited Houston, New Orleans, Chicago etc. Domestic flights are expensive, but you can really get a lot out of a weekend/ holiday.
culture_adjustment: I think it's very easy to adjust to the U.S., but Texas can be a pretty special state in some way.
socializing_tips: Talk to the people you live with and have classes with! People are very friendly and are happy to show you fun things to do in Austin.
cultural_challenges: Texas is built for driving, and the locals pretty much drive to everything. That can be challenging if you don't have a car but want to join an event, but people are happy to give you a ride if you ask.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness! Texans are generally very good at talking with strangers.
top3_advice: 1. Keep an open mind 2. Travel as much a possible 3. Go dancing on a traditional Texas dance bar! (White Horse was our favorite!)
other_useful_info: The busses are free for UT students. They are unreliable, but they can take you most places on campus and downtown when it is too hot to walk (which it pretty much is from August to November...)
most_rewarding: Travelling and meeting new people from around the world.
greatest_challenge: Accepting the poor housing conditions.

crucial_aspects: I've always been pretty determined to study abroad in America, and crucial aspects to choosing the exact destination were definitely the courses offered and the accessibility to information about international students.
info_ease: Upon arrival everything was very easy for me. I had gotten all of the information in emails weeks before arriving. I also knew who to contact if I needed additional assistance or info.
arrival_assistance: I got some help with an immigration practicality.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: You need to know the unique number for every course to register for them. The system in which you do it, seems a little old fashioned, but it works. You put in the unique number and add yourself to the courses individually. You are provided with a certain time slot with access to the registration website, and you need to add the courses fast, because a lot of other people are doing it at the same time. It works on a first come first served basis. If you don't get into the classes you want, you can add yourself to a waitlist and see if room becomes available.
registration_help: Tutorials on how to use the course registration website were provided and we also went over it during an orientation for international students over zoom.
registration_success: I had to register for 4 courses but I tried to get into 5 so that I could try them all before dropping 1. However, there was one class that was full when I tried to register for it, so I put myself on the waiting list. The next day I got lucky and got an email saying that I got in. I ended up will all of the classes I hoped for and got to drop one that I didn't like.
registration_advice: Spend time making a good plan for the class schedule you want and then be ready with the unique numbers when its your time slot.
course_level: One of my classes was upper division and the level here was higher and more was expected of you. I would compare this upper level class to the ones that I've had at UCPH. My other classes were not very hard to get good results in - coming from a student with 2 years of university experience of course.
teaching_comparison: Much was the same. One of my classes was only online lectures, one was in-person lectures and labs, and my other two classes were smaller in-person classes.
courses_enrolled: 1. Biological anthropology 2. Introduction to psychology 3. Shakespeare 4. Women, gender, literature, culture.
recommended_courses: I would recommend all of them. I really enjoyed them because they are very different from each other, and I got to explore new interests.
unexpected_costs: Being forced to set money aside to use at on-campus facilities
cost_comparison: I think housing and insurance were more expensive than I expected. Housing is expensive because it includes the meal plan, but still a lot of money pr. month.
activities_available: A LOT of student organizations and clubs are available for all sorts of culture, interests, sports, etc. There is also museums on campus as well an a giant gym, shopping facilities, and coffee shops.
activities_recommended: I would recommend getting out and exploring the city.
weekend_recommendations: Go to museums, go shopping, go outside of campus, go to sports games.
culture_adjustment: I think it was very easy. Very few differences.
socializing_tips: The locals are extremely open here, and if you just push yourself a little and get out there, it is easy to get a friend group.
cultural_challenges: The education system and the expectation to get good grades in everything is different from home. I could see this affecting mostly local students, but some internationals might get sucked into the performance culture.
culture_appreciated: I mostly appreciated the openness of the locals.
top3_advice: Take fun courses that aren't available at home, prioritize going to games and experiencing the school spirit, remember to have fun outside of campus and enjoy that you get to study in and experience another culture.
other_useful_info: There is always help if you need it, and though the process for all the practical stuff you need to do before going is hard, you can do it.
most_rewarding: My new friendships
greatest_challenge: My greatest challenge during the exchange had more to do with my home university. There is not really any communication and most of the time you are left to figure everything out yourself. My challenge was to plan my next semester at home while help was hard to get, and no one reminded me to do anything. I mean in regards to registering for courses and finding an advisor for my BA project, etc.
