Når man kom ind i registreringssystemet var kurser som lige havde været tilgængelige kun mulige for venteliste. Der sker meget i de uger som tilmeldingsperioden er igang, så man kan også få kurser senere. Jeg fik fra start kun et af de tre kurser jeg havde brug for, men fik hjælp både fra forelæsere og advisors med at tilmelde mig de andre fag. En af de forelæsere jeg havde sagde også at hvis det var kunne han måske også hæve antallet pladser til kurset. Jeg hørte også om andre udvekslingsstuderende som var gået til sin advisor og fået hjælp med at få en plads på et kursus selvom der ikke var flere i systemet. Så selvom der ligner det er umuligt, er der mange muligheder hvis man bare skriver/mødes med de rigtige mennesker.
registration_advice: Jeg havde ikke særlig mange alternativer fordi kravene fra KU var meget hårde, men endte med at være meget heldig. Men mange alternativer for forskellige kurser gør det nok lidt nemmere for at kunne have en mindre stressende registrering end jeg havde.
course_level: Generelt er niveauet lavere i USA, selvom der er meget mere at lave i løbet af semestret. Det er måske hellere ikke kun at niveauet er lavere, men også at man ikke har lige så meget fokus på analytiske evner som i DK. Fordi jeg var nødt til at læse et fag indenfor komparativ politik, og det eneste kursus UT havde indenfor det felt var på graduate niveau, læste jeg også et fag på højere niveau end bachelor. Man skal have tilladelse fra både forelæsere og administration for sådan noget, men det var ikke særligt svært i mit tilfælde. Niveauet i det fag var meget højere end i de andre, og de studerende var blandet mellem forskellige folk der lige var startet på graduate programmet, og dem der allerede havde sin master og var på vej mod PhD. Selvom det var meget skræmmende fra start, og at det fag krævede virkelig meget af min tid, er det generelt meget nemmere at få gode karakterer i USA end det er i DK, så det endte med at gå helt fint også i det fag.
teaching_comparison: Det var meget mere personligt at studere i USA. Undervisere er meget mere interesserede i faglig og personlig dialog, og forelæsningsgrupperne er meget mindre. Hvor jeg i DK har haft oplevelsen af at office hours er tilgængeligt men ikke rigtigt bliver opfordret til eller brugt, så bruger folk virkelig den tid i USA. Forelæserere var virkelig kede af det hvis folk ikke kom til office hours. Man får også virkelig meget feedback på opgaver, hvilket er godt når man har mange opgaver i løbet af semestret og gerne vil vide hvordan man skal gøre noget bedre.
courses_enrolled: EUS 305 - Introduction to European Studies EUS 348 - The Comprehensive Notion of European Security GOV 310L - American and Texas Government GOV 390K - Comparative Study of Political Systems
recommended_courses: Selvom det er lidt mærkeligt at skulle læse om Europa i USA, kan jeg virkelig anbefale både Introduction to European Studies og Comprehensive Notion of European Security. Det er meget spændende at lære om Europa fra et andet perspektiv. Om du kan læse kurser indenfor government eller europæiske studier, tag et fag med Michael Mosser! Han er fantastisk!
unexpected_costs: Visumafgifter var virkelig høje, og det er VIRKELIG dyrt med den sundhedsforsikring som er obligatorisk hvis man er udvekslingsstuderende på UT (og generelt i USA som jeg forstår det). Jeg havde også min egen forsikring som jeg var meget glad for, fordi jeg fik akut tandpine hvilket ikke var inkluderet i UT-forsikringen.
cost_comparison: Alle fødevarer og alkohol er virkelig dyre. Den offentlige transport er gratis for studerende når man fået sit UT ID. Var heldig og fandt bøger online eller gennem soeg.
activities_available: Virkelig meget, der er alle mulige typer af organisationer på uni. Der er adgang til fitness center og en pool på campus for alle studerende.
activities_recommended: Virkelig gode museum i Austin! 6th street er fedt men tag også ud til East Austin hvis du skal i byen.
weekend_recommendations: Jeg tog til Los Angeles og Oklahoma i weekender og ferier. Desuden rejste jeg rundt i USA både før og efter semestret startede. Texas er virkelig fedt, så tag ud og se mere end bare Austin.
culture_adjustment: Det var ret nemt at tilpasse sig, selvom der er stor forskel på alder på universitetet. Folk er generelt virkelig unge, ofte 18-19.
socializing_tips: Gå med i en eller flere clubs, altså en studentorganisation. Tag til begivenheder for udvekslingsstuderende i starten.
cultural_challenges: Jeg synes amerikanere var virkelig søde til at starte med, men sværere på længere sigt.
culture_appreciated: Folk er virkelig åbne for at snakke, og det er virkelig nemt at snakke med folk til forelæsninger og sådan noget.
top3_advice: Hold styr på al den information UT vil have før du tager af sted. Find mange alternativ (hvis muligt) for kurser. Skriv til UT (gerne det internationale kontor og Kelli Weaver), de er virkelig søde og hurtige til at svare.
other_useful_info: Var tidligt ude med at finde bolig, selvom det er muligt også senere er det godt for at finde de billigere alternativer. Jeg ville bo på en co-op igen, fordi du kan bo så tæt på uni og stadig få en okay husleje OG mad inkluderet i prisen.
most_rewarding: Studierne! Det var meget sjovere og meget mere rewarding at studere på UT.
greatest_challenge: Jeg er 25 og følt mig nogle gange lidt gammel, folk var meget søde men det var også meget stor forskel på 18 år gamle amerikanere og mig.

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte at tage til et engelsktalende land, så jeg kunne snakke med lokalbefolkningen.
info_ease: Universitetet sendte mange e-mails med al den nødvendige information.
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik mails og kontaktoplysninger på vejledere.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Registrering til fag for udvekslingsstuderende åbnede først op fem dage inden studiestart, hvilket betyd at mange fag var fyldt op. Ved tilmeldingen kan man sige at et lukket fag skal erstatte et åbent fag, hvis der skulle opstå ledige pladser, så man skal løbende holde øje med fagene. Nogle fag har krav man skal opfylde for at kunne tilmelde sig, i de tilfælde så skriv til professoren.
registration_help: Både professorer og studievejleder var meget villige til at hjælpe og svarede hurtigt på ens henvendelser.
registration_success: Jeg endte med at få alle de fag jeg skulle have.
registration_advice: Jeg vil anbefale at have flere mulige fagkombinationer, så du ikke er låst til at du skal have fire specifikke fag. Det gør det lettere hvis du fra ku's side ikke skal have obligatoriske fag.
course_level: Jeg havde to upper-division fag, et introduktions-fag og et kandidat fag.
teaching_comparison: Vi var ca. 40 studerende og en professor det for det meste holdt et oplæg. Professoren stillede spørgsmål undervejs og engagerede de studerende. De fleste fag endte med at vi skulle holde en fremlæggelse foran hele holdet.
courses_enrolled: EUS 305 Introduction to European Studies, GOV 365V Comprehensive Notions of European Security, GOV 360G Causes of War, GOV 290K Comparative Study of Political Systems
recommended_courses: Jeg vil anbefale at tage Comprehensive Notions of European Security, hvor du får et indblik i europæiske sikkerhed ud fra et amerikansk perspektiv. Du vil få en bedre forståelse for både NATO og OSCE. Dr. Mosser er super dygtig og engageret. Han har fuldstændig styr på hvad der foregår i verden og kan sætte det i perspektiv til det vi lærer om.
unexpected_costs: Der er mange gebyrer, der samlet var på 7.200 kr. for administration og visum. Gebyrer for bare universitets administration, når man er i Texas løb op i 1.800 kr.
cost_comparison: Jeg fandt alle bøger online gennem sorg.kb eller på universitetsbiblioteket. Jeg blev overrasket over at busserne i Austin var gratis med studiekort.
activities_available: Alt tænkeligt.
activities_recommended: Jeg vil opfordrer til at prøve at blive en del af en gruppe eller to og gøre brug af de mange de akademiske oplæg der løbende er der og alle de gratis arrangementer for studerende.
weekend_recommendations: Tag rundt i byen og oplev de forskellige bydele, besøg museerne og naturstederne.
culture_adjustment: Overraskende nemt
socializing_tips: Tag til undervisning i god tid og snak med folk omkring dig, blev en del af nogle grupper.
cultural_challenges: Amerikansk høflighedsfraser.
culture_appreciated: Deres åbenhed overfor at snakke med fremmede og inviterer en med.
top3_advice: Drik en masse vand, der er varmt i Texas om efteråret. Tag amerikanerne på ordet og aftal et tidspunkt, hvor I mødes. Vær åben for at snakke med folk, du normalt ikke ville opsøge.
other_useful_info: Der er mange små opgaver hver uge i ens fag, så du bliver nødt til ugentligt at sætte timer af til at få læst pensum og lavet opgaverne.
most_rewarding: Venskaberne.
greatest_challenge: Vende sig til varmen.
other_comments: Det er fagligt lettere, men arbejdsbyrden er større. Det er det hele værd.

overall_comments: Would be a 10 if it wasnt so expensive
info_ease: It was pretty easy

housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Would be a 10 if it wasnt so expensive

registration_advice: Have a lot of backup plans ready

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte at studere i Austin, fordi jeg fik anbefalet deres retorik-afdeling af min professor. Det var vigtigt for mig at komme på udveksling i et engelsktalende land, fordi jeg gerne ville have nemt ved at snakke med de lokale.
info_ease: Det føltes meget overvældende at holde styr på det hele, men så vidt jeg husker, var det meste vidst faldet på plads, da jeg ankom til USA. Universitetet var super gode til at række ud med oplysninger og hjælp.
arrival_assistance: Jeg fik en masse tilbud om sociale arrangementer. Der var også et intro-møde, jeg desværre ikke nåede at være med til. Desuden havde universitetet et kontor for deres globale arbejde, hvor jeg henvendte mig og fik hjælp til, hvad jeg skulle gøre og hvor jeg kunne gå videre hen.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Man kan først registrere, når man er ankommet. Du får tilegnet et tidspunkt, hvor du kan registrere kurser, hvilket er meget som at købe koncertbilletter til noget populært. Det er vildt uigennemskueligt, hvem der kan registrere på hvilket tidspunkt. Jeg kom på venteliste på 3/4 kurser, men endte med at få dem alle. Der var god information om det, men måske er oplevelsen anderlederes, hvis man søger mere populære fag.
registration_help: En masse online information. Man skal mange steps igennem for at være erklæret klar til registration. Nogle kan laves hjemmefra, og andre kan først fikses derovre. Det er nemt nok at se, hvad der skal gøres, der er bare mange steps i det.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle mine ønskede kurser efter 1-2 dage på ventelisten.
registration_advice: Lav så meget af forarbejdet hjemmefra som muligt. Det er det, de kalder registration-holds.
course_level: Niveauet var væsentligt lavere end derhjemme, men jeg er alligevel godt tilfreds med det faglige udbytte. Tilgangen til akademia er helt anderledes, så du vil opleve, at man læser langt mindre og langt mindre komplekst. Der er mindre fokus på kritisk tænkning og analyse. Til gengæld er der flere praktiske opgaver, og dem er der mange af, så der er konstant små deadlines. De store teoretiske indsigter om retorikkens tradition og væsen udeblev, men til gengæld fik jeg en masse faglig udfordring, fordi det hele foregik på engelsk og fordi jeg pludselig skulle producere meget mere. Vælg så højt fagligt niveau som du kan, og forbered dig på, at dine medstuderende ikke er lige så solidt teoretisk funderede som du selv er. Til gengæld skriver de sindssygt godt, og det må du så også lære.
teaching_comparison: Mindre teoretisk, mere praktisk. Det var klasseundervisning, hvor man gerne måtte stille spørgsmål og ofte skulle svare på ting, men det var ikke teoretiske diskussioner og kritiske spørgsmål, som vi kender dem hjemmefra. Man læser næsten ingen primærlitteratur, hvilket både er en befrielse og en begrænsning. Du skal lave små opgaver konstant, og din karakter i sidste ende er baseret på, hvordan du løser dem.
courses_enrolled: Advanced Writing (Rhetoric) Advanced Presentation (Communication) Magazine (Rhetoric) Principles of Rhetoric (Rhetoric)
recommended_courses: Magasin-faget var klart det mest lærerige. Underviseren stillede fuldstændigt vanvittige krav, og jeg blev helt slået ud af det i starten. Men det var så motiverende, fordi han samtidig var sindssygt dygtig. Det var fedt at skulle gøre sig så umage, fordi de andre fag til gengæld var lette for mig. Måske er han gået på pension nu - han hedder Tom Buckley. Principles of Rhetoric bliver alt for nemt for dig, så lad være med at tage det.
unexpected_costs: Udvidet rejseforsikring fra min forsikring hjemme i Danmark. Det koste vist 4000 kr., og jeg tror primært det var nødvendigt, fordi jeg resjte videre i USA og Mexico efterfølgende. UT har også en obligatorisk forsikring, men den er vist kun til sundhed.
cost_comparison: UT's forsikring er obligatorisk - og det mener de - og den koster ca. 10.000 kr. Min bolig og mad var billigere end forventet, fordi jeg boede i co-op, hvor begge dele var inkluderet i huslejen på 6.200 kr. Desuden skulle jeg kun betale for halvdelen af maj, hvilket også gav en god besparelse.
activities_available: Der er mange ting arrangeret for udvekslingsstuderende. Det kan være rigtig fedt, for der er en hel flok, der heller ikke har nogen venner endnu. Til gengæld er det også værd at søge mod klubberne, hvis du gerne vil have amerikanske venner, men her skal du altså være tidligt ude, hvis det skal nå at give mening.
activities_recommended: Jeg gentager lidt mig selv, men jeg vil bare sige co-ops. Du får så sindssygt meget forærende ved at bo et socialt sted.
weekend_recommendations: Nyd at Austin er en fantastisk fed by!
culture_adjustment: Det syntes jeg egentlig var relativt nemt. Altså det er jo maks presset lige pludselig ikke at kende nogen omkring dig, men det skal man nok klare.
socializing_tips: Bo i et co-op :)
cultural_challenges: Jeg ved ikke, om det tæller her, men folk er væsentligt yngre på amerikanske universiteter. Det tager lige lidt tid at finde ud af, hvilke mennesker man mærker det tydligt på, og hvilke man slet ikke bemærker det hos.
culture_appreciated: Folk er jo bare sindssygt åbne og imødekommende i USA. Det er en kæmpe fordel, når du kommer som ny.
top3_advice: 1. Bo i et co-op. 2. Brug de andre danskere som en ventil. Undgå at bo sammen, men tag på bar og snak om, hvor skøre amerikanerne er. 3. Det er både okay at dyrke de andre udvekslingsstuderende og at lade være.
other_useful_info: Formelt set skal du være i USA inden dit program begynder (5.-6. januar-ish). Vi fandt ud af det, da vi havde købt billetter, så de fleste af os danskere ankom efter det. Vi havde ingen problemer, men det kan man vist i princippet risikere. Desuden - lad være med at vente med at købe flybilletter!!! Køb nogle tidligt, der kan ændres. Jeg gav 7000 kr. den ene vej, og det kunne have været langt billigere, hvis jeg havde købt tidligere.
most_rewarding: Det var vildt fedt at få venner, der er amerikanere. Det giver et helt nyt perspektiv, og så er de bare vildt søde.
greatest_challenge: Man starter fra nul med alle relationer. Det er jo helt naturligt, men det kræver virkelig tålmodighed, når alle i ens hverdag er nogen, man har kendt i en måned. Det bliver bedre, men man må også affinde sig med at det tager tid.
other_comments: Jeg var vildt glad for at have taget nogle relativt overskuelige fag i efteråret inden min udveksling. Der er bare virkelig meget administrativt arbejde, der følger med. Det skal ikke stoppe dig, men du skal nok tage det alvorligt, når nogen siger, at det er som at have et ekstra fag.

crucial_aspects: The weather, the academic reputation of the university, that rent would not be over 6.500 dkk and that it was outside of the EU

housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: meeting with advisor, which is also required to take the courses

registration_advice: Take it easy! relax, it seems quite overwhelming but you don't know till you know, and waitlists do work!

courses_enrolled: Cognition psychology of consciousness adolescent development intro to develoopmental psy
recommended_courses: I would very much recommend everything apart from adolescent development, the other 3 were pretty engaging and hard good professors, a different way of seeing things, dev psy was online but one of the best online classes i have had, very nicely designed with breakout discussions and interactive polls

culture_adjustment: extremely easy, but i am also half american. Even with that, I needed to get used to the how are you's and the very polite culture
socializing_tips: Be friendly and open, most people i met were very interested and open with me, and that is different than DK, embrace it!
cultural_challenges: I did find the chattyness and the southern hospitality a bit startling at first, but you might grow to love the little chats with strangers and saying thank you to the bus driver
culture_appreciated: see above
top3_advice: Don't stress too much before going, it will work out with the classes. don't just hang out with fellow exchange students as many do, take this oppurtunity to immerse yourself in the culture and see what a weird and wonderful place the US can be
other_useful_info: It can be hard to make friends who you don't live with, so join an org or a club
most_rewarding: The people I met, feeling closer to my heritage, the absolute immersion and openness i experience, austin is a beautiful place and the people are very warm mostly
greatest_challenge: Not having a car, do rent one if you can, there is so much to see and do that is just not accessible without a car, i was lucky enough to have friends to drive me places, but it's hard in the beginning

crucial_aspects: I chose the U.S. because of my heritage. Within the U.S., I wanted to experience the college culture while also staying in a city which has more to offer than just the college
info_ease: A little difficult. I had received all the necessary information, but the amount of information made it difficult to sort through to find the relevant information.
arrival_assistance: We were greeted and provided with all necessary information as well as informed about the office for international students, which was very helpful.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: We were provided with information from the office for international students. You choose the courses you want and then you prioritise these courses. They are not allowed to overlap.
registration_help: I found it to be a pretty easy process, but you can always ask the office for international students for help.
registration_success: I was very successful. I got four very interesting courses and I only had classes from monday to Wednesday.
registration_advice: Spend some time looking through the course catalog beforehand so you have an idea which courses you are interested in. Also, spend some time thinking about the course composition that you want - classes are not allowed to overlap, so you can try to use a calendar to out together different class schedules depending on which courses you end up getting. Also, there is quite a large difference between professors, so ask around about other people's experiences with professors.
course_level: I thought the level was very fitting. It varied depending on the course and professor, but I found it to be well balanced between easy enough to follow along without too much time spent preparing but also challenging enough that I ended up learning quite a lot.
teaching_comparison: In the US in general, they are very fond of the socratic method, whereby the professors ask students questions in order to arrive at an answer to a legal issue, even if the student does not raise their hand. It can seem intimidating, but I found it to be quite enjoyable. I didn't spend too much time preparing for classes, but I still felt prepared for questions. Also, it varies from professor to professor how much they use this method of teaching, so I wouldn't be worried about it.
courses_enrolled: U.S. law, an introduction (professor Haynes), Business Associations (professor Damman), Negotiation (professor Jury) and Venture Transactions (professor Vela)
recommended_courses: I enjoyed all the courses. U.S law was a good and rather light introduction to the U.S. legal system. Business Associations with professor Damman was one of the most rewarding courses I have had, as you learn an incredible amount about U.S. corporate law, M&A, economic theory and business acumen. Negotiation with professor Jury was not a very legal-heavy course, but Jury created a very comfortable atmosphere with fun exercises throughout the course. Venture Transactions with Vela is the best course I have had during my time as a law student. It was definitely challenging, but I learned so much about venture capital since the course encompassed both general concepts within venture, fund structure, tax benefits, negotiation, math in relation to ownership stakes through different financing rounds and in-depth analysis of the contracts used within venture capital.
unexpected_costs: Nothing too unexpected, mostly just travelling and cultural experiences. You can always adjust the amount you spend on this based on your available finances though.
cost_comparison: Housing was very expensive. The coop was one of the cheapest housing options I could find in Austin but I still came out to more than DKK 8.000 pr. month. However, food was included in the rent, so this was cheaper than I expected for me.
activities_available: There are endless opportunities for cultural, athletic and social activities through UT. There are multiple gyms, pools, indoor tracks, basketball courts, volleyball courts etc. available to students for free. Other than that, there are a ton of athletic clubs within different sports that you can join. This is the case for other types of cultural and social activities as well. I would highly recommend making use of some of these opportunities.
activities_recommended: College sports are a huge part of college life, especially college football. I would highly recommend getting the big ticket and going to some of the college football games, basketball games, volleyball games etc. Austin nightlife is also very fun, so I would recommend going out quite a bit as well to experience this.
weekend_recommendations: I enjoy going out, so I would recommend experiencing Austins nightlife or spending time canoeing on lady bird lake, Other than that, the U.S. has plenty of destinations to visit for weekend or holiday trips, especially if you are willing to travel a bit to destinations such as New Orleans, Nashville, California etc.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. The culture is different, but in a way that is easy to adjust to for Europeans.
socializing_tips: Say yes to as many things as you can in the beginning. I found some of my closest friends during the first day in Austin because someone suggested that the exchange students in the law school go out to dinner. I also found some very good friends at the coop, so think about placing yourself in as many situations as you can where you get to meet other people, whether it be through your living situation, classes, exchange program, sports programs etc.
cultural_challenges: None. I enjoyed the american culture quite a bit. People are very open and friendly - it takes some getting used to, but it is also a very welcome change when you are looking for friends.
culture_appreciated: The openness amongst americans and the focus on enjoying yourself and having a good time. There was such a great atmosphere and an interest in meeting new people, which is exactly what you want as an exchange student.
top3_advice: 1. Find some good friends as soon as possible, they were without a doubt the most important part of my exchange. 2. Bring as much money as you can through your own savings and through grants - even if you don't intend on spending it all, it is always great to have the opportunity to go travelling or go out with friends without having to worry about your finances. 3. Make a list of all the things you want to do during your exchange, such as local attractions and travel destinations. Be realistic though, because a big part of being on exchange is just enjoying life in a new city, so you want to find a good balance between spending your time on trips and attractions and spending your time getting to know the city and being with friends.
other_useful_info: Start as early as you can with all the requirements for your exchange, such as TOEFL tests, visa applications etc. Especially the TOEFL test was quite expensive and not as easy as one might think, and the deadline for when you have to document having taken the test is very early, so you need to start this process early so you don't end up missing the deadline.
most_rewarding: The friendships I made during the semester, having a more chill semester where enjoying life was more important than studying and creating a bond to a new city.
greatest_challenge: All the hours spent preparing. It was worth it though - the more you prepare, the less you have to worry about when you arrive, leaving more time to enjoy your exchange.

crucial_aspects: The fact that I got to have the proper college experience which did not fail! UT Austin is a lot like you see on the movies, in a very good way! You get too meet so many new people from all over the world, whilst also experiencing texas. Even though Austin is very democratic you can still get a feel for the proper texan lifestyle. The academics was honestly very good too, way more practical than what is was used to back home which I really liked.
info_ease: Very easy, either visit their website texas global (https://global.utexas.edu/) or attend the virtual seminars they have to prepare you for exchange, they will go over everything you need and you can ask questions.
arrival_assistance: There are multiple lectures and welcome meetings to prepare you for the following semester (they usually start 1,5 weeks before the actual semester starts and the rest of the UT students arrive at campus).
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You will get a date and a time where the registration is opened to all exchange/international students, and it is first come first serve. Make sure to write down all the courses you want and their unique number beforehand in excel so you can copy paste easily so you get the courses you want. Also make sure you have gotten approval from your study counsellor for the courses you want beforehand or it will not let you register for the course (this might change depending on major)
registration_help: For my major I had a virtual meeting with a study counsellor from that major, here I told him which courses I would like to do and he “pre-approved” me for those courses. Make sure to get the pre approval for all the courses you might take even your second choices as some courses might get filled up fast. (Note that not all courses need pre-approval, but check it in advance).
registration_success: I got all my courses in the end. At first I did not get one of my courses but I signed up for the waiting list for the course, and during drop week (a week where you can try and change courses as much as you want, enough people dropped the course and I was admitted).
registration_advice: Do research on the courses beforehand, download UT registration plus (chrome plugin), and talk to a study counsellor.
course_level: I did mostly upper level undergraduate courses, it is pretty hard to get approval for graduate courses. The workload is a bit bigger than back home (granted I also did an extra course), but every single assignment during the semester will likely count toward your final grade so you cannot just slack for half the semester.
teaching_comparison: Mostly lectures, but much smaller classes with room for questions. Also some group work, but be aware that Americans (at least in my experience, and other exchange students’ experience) are quite bad a doing group work so if the final product matters to you, you might need to take on a leadership role early in the process.

recommended_courses: PSY 355N - Cognitive Neuroscience EDP 387 - Sports/Performance Psychology CLD 360 - Communication for executive leadership Really fun courses and great teachers!

The big ticket (entry to all sports, which you should really buy) 200 dollars and an extra 150 dollars with longhorns foundations pass, which I can also recommend, then you are guaranteed tickets to all the football games. cost_comparison: Food was not that bad if you buy it and make it yourself from HEB or Walmart.
activities_available: There are so many clubs/orgs that are absolutely awesome! They will all have stalls on speedway the first couple of weeks of fall semester, go talk to them and figure out what you like.
activities_recommended: Join the wakeboard club it is an incredible experience! You will get to go on a boat every other week and wakeboard/wakesurf, you will meet great people and likely also attend some great parties/formals.
weekend_recommendations: Travel around the US, go to football games, ask local families to join them for holidays if you can befriend some.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, people are very accommodating!
socializing_tips: Just talk to people, they are pretty open. Go to parties. Join a club/org. (People usually have back to back classes so they have to hurry, therefore it is pretty hard to socialise in the classrooms).
cultural_challenges: Nothing really, only the fact that you can’t address the professors by their first name.
culture_appreciated: The unity around all the college sports (especially american football, which is only in the fall semester) The fact that people actually wear boots and hats, and not as a costume The fact the everything is so over the top compared to Denmark, in a very good way. The openness of people
top3_advice: Be open to experience, and talk to as many people as you can, you won’t regret it. It will be very expensive no matter how you do it so make sure to save/apply for scholarships ahead of time so you won’t have to worry too much about financials. All the issues you have beforehand will likely resolve themselves, and it is way easier to solve them once you are actually In texas.
other_useful_info: You get so much free stuff with your UT (E)ID. NY times, Public transport, Amazon prime, Uber one, Canva. Use it.
most_rewarding: The Unity around campus, especially regarding the college sports. The new friends. Experiencing Texas and US culture first hand.
greatest_challenge: Balancing having fun/experiencing things and academic work.

overall_comments: I really enjoyed my exchange stay in Austin, which is a very lively and active city with plenty of things to do. I was positively surprised by the food culture, especially the strong Mexican influence and the excellent barbecue scene. Campus life at University of Texas at Austin was also a highlight for me, with many opportunities to attend basketball, football, and volleyball games. In addition, there were great options for staying active, and I especially enjoyed swimming in the outdoor pool. One downside of Austin is its location within Texas, as distances are very large, which makes it harder to travel to other parts of the United States. The city is also very car-oriented, meaning that simple tasks like grocery shopping can be inconvenient without a car. However, renting a bike worked well for everyday transportation, and the Orange Bike Project was a great and affordable option, costing only $50 for an entire semester.

crucial_aspects: Being able to take courses that I couldn't take at home, and getting an interesting cultural experience.
info_ease: Very easy, the International Student and Scholar Services had put great effort into holding zoom lectures and giving us relevant information. They are also very responsive throughout the semester if you need any help.
arrival_assistance: I had trouble paying for the mandatory health insurance, as their system did not support all the characters in my name, leading to my card constantly being declined. So I needed help figuring out how to pay in person.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: For CS students, once accepted for the exchange program you have to apply to have CS as your major. The CS department only guarantees you to have 2 CS courses, and you need to send them a list of courses you are interested in taking. Shortly before the registration opens you will have a zoom meeting with your academic advisor, who will tell you which 2 CS courses you will get, and then you talk about what other courses you want. I took Electrical and Computer Engineering courses, even though they are often restricted to engineering students, I solved this by my advisor giving me the email address for the ECE department advisor, who then gave me the courses I was interested in.
registration_help: Your advisor can help you figure out which courses you can take, and explain how to register for courses.
registration_success: I was very successful. I got all of the courses I was interested in, even managing to circumvent the restrictions on engineering courses, by just asking the relevant advisor.
registration_advice: Talk with your assigned advisor, and if you want to take courses in other departments, get the relevant advisors email address from your advisor.
course_level: I found that the courses were a similar difficulty as courses at UCPH. I have heard from other exchange students in law, business and humanities, that they have found the courses here to be quite easy. But I found that science and engineering courses were about the same difficulty as at home.
teaching_comparison: Quite similar with two lectures a week and assignments every week or every other week, depending on the course. There were two major differences from UCPH. The first being that we here have 4 courses at a time, while the block schedule at UCPH means we only have 2 courses at a time. The other major difference is that the US university system has midterm exams in all courses, and quite a lot of them. One of the courses I had, had 3 midterms and one final exam, meaning one exam every month.
courses_enrolled: C S 360V Virtualization, C S 358H Introduction to Quantum Information Science, ECE 302 Introduction to Electrical Engineering, ECE 316 Digital Logic Design.
recommended_courses: C S 360V I found to be quite easy and straightforward, and reasonably interesting, I think it is a good course that also allows you to have free time. C S 358H I found to be quite difficult to understand, and not as interesting as I had hoped. If you want to take it, you should definitely prepare by doing linear algebra and getting comfortable with calculating with complex numbers. ECE 302 is notoriously difficult, and definitely not a course you want to take with other difficult courses. But if you are interested in learning about circuits and transistors it is a great course. ECE 316 is awesome. I thought it was a straightforward course that wasn't too difficult, and also quite interesting. For the lab assignments you get to program FPGA's.
unexpected_costs: None.
cost_comparison: Nothing, I think on average things are about as expensive as in Denmark.
activities_available: There are lots of recreational sports and cultural clubs on campus. There are sports games in different sports, most notably of course being the American football games. The RecSports Outdoors Center also organizes hiking/biking/canoeing trips to different parts of Texas and neighboring states.
activities_recommended: Go on trips with the Outdoors Center, it is a great opportunity to meet other exchange- and local- students, as well as getting to explore Texas.
weekend_recommendations: There are quite a few museums on campus that you have free access to with your student ID if you've got nothing else planned. Barton Springs Creek, Zilker Park, and the trails around Lady Bird Lake, in downtown, are also all great places to go hang out or go for a walk. The Texas capitol building is also pretty cool to see, and it is free to visit.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy, UT and Austin are both quite cosmopolitan, so if you know how things work in America I don't think there will be much of a shock.
socializing_tips: Talk with the people you have courses with.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: I don't know, it's America, so I think it's pretty similar to most western countries in many ways.
top3_advice: 1. Go on tours with the outdoors center. 2. Don't take too difficult courses so you can have time to go explore. 3. Explore campus and all the different events happening on and around it.
other_useful_info: If you are in humanities, depending on your specific field of study, or if you are LGBTQ, you might want to reconsider going to UT. As the newly appointed president of the university is kind of a political appointee, and has previously worked for the republican party in Texas. There currently rumors that the humanities are going to be heavily limited, with some fields of study expected to be scrapped, and a lot of courses no longer being offered going forward. Additionally, while I was here, fall 2025, the Trump administration invited a number of universities to sign a "compact" that would effectively put the university under the presidents control, and UT was the only university to not reject the compact. At time of writing, the deadline for signing the compact has passed, with UT neither accepting or rejecting it.
most_rewarding: Getting to take courses I can't take at home.
greatest_challenge: The constant midterms.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go somewhere in the US where I could potentially see myself live in the future. This included appealing culture, good weather and a not too small city. Also, the fact that UT Austin is well-ranked university in the world on many measures.
info_ease: Very easy. UT does a great job arranging events in the first few weeks and sending out information and hosting live webinars in advance.
arrival_assistance: I attended many intro events called "orientations".
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration platform opens up first at a certain date and time "normal" full-degree students. Then, after they have registered for courses, it opens up for international students at a later point. Then courses are filled up on a first-come-first-served basis. It is fairly simple, but be sure to have done your research in advance so that you are ready to find and type in your preferred course titles and code numbers in a split second when the registration opens. Otherwise all spots on some popular courses might get taken in quickly. Importantly, there is a so-called "add-n-drop" period in the first week or two of the semester where students can drop out of their registered courses and register for new ones if vacant spot. Thus, there is a waitlist function you can use, in case someone drops a course that you want.
registration_help: Live Zoom meeting running in the meantime with advisors for pop-in questions.
registration_success: Managed to register for all my three required courses in the end, one or two by waitlist, and got two additional elective courses.
registration_advice: Do your research, be ready on time when registration opens, have backups ready, and use the waitlist function in case your preferred courses are filled up.
course_level: One introductory "lower division" course and four "upper division" courses. Lower division more lecture hall style with many people and less interaction with professor (like BA psychology at KU). Upper division much smaller classes with more interaction.
teaching_comparison: Similarly informal, but with more respectfulness towards professors. Also much more interaction and the opportunity to make a personal impression and get a relation to your professor.
courses_enrolled: Intro to Cognitive Psychology (PSY 305) Cognitive Neuroscience (PSY 355N) Psychopathology (PSY 352P) The Art and Science of Negotiation (MAN 372T) THe Psychology of Persuasion and Influence (BGS 372T)
recommended_courses: The Art and Science of Negotiation (MAN 372T) The Psychology of Persuasion and Influence (BGS 372T) Extremely useful and interesting with professors making learning engaging and even fun at times.
unexpected_costs: Not many apart from an occasional small fee for stuff like learning software or an ID card at UT.
cost_comparison: Depending on where you buy your household items; "Target" at campus pretty expensive, Walmart much cheaper.
activities_available: Many kinds of sports (volleyball, ultimate, swimming, soccer, football, basketball etc) and political and social activities.
activities_recommended: Go to as many intro events as possible in the beginning. Specifically the walking tour: excellent way to meet new friends and get better at finding your way around campus. I met one friend who made the rest of my semester so much better.
weekend_recommendations: For Austin: Zilker Park, Barton Springs, downtown, the Texas Capitol, the UT museums. For weekends: find a car and go to Fort Worth, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio or Enchanted Rock. For fall or winter break: go to Big Bend National Park or other states.
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: Be open, say hi, and ask questions about American/Texan/Austin culture.
cultural_challenges: None really.
culture_appreciated: The whole UT culture. It is just something completely different from anything you find back in Denmark or maybe even Europe. Great in so many ways, making you feel like a part of a distinct community with its history, traditions, events and everything in a matter of weeks (much more than KU does).
top3_advice: Courses: Do your research and get the courses you need/want. Housing: Find a place where you are not isolated, but live with a mix of Americans and international students (like a co-op). Balance: Find your own balance of studying vs socializing vs exploring. Some people are there only to have fun and party every weekend, some people are there to ace their grades for career purposes, and some people are everywhere in between.
other_useful_info: A note on the observation that many Danish people seem to have some preconceived negative beliefs about Texas culture. For instance, in terms of conservative politics and ideology. In fact, Austin and UT are democratic hot spots (like all major cities in Texas) and in my experience, it seems in many ways just, or even more, as progressive a as Copenhagen and KU.
most_rewarding: Experiencing the combination of the UT and Texas culture and all of the Americans and international students infused in it all together.
greatest_challenge: All the research and preperation leadning up to it. During the stay itself, it was probably prioritizing studying vs exploring/socializing.
other_comments: Do it. Going on exchange at UT has been so extremely enriching and probably one of the best experiences of my life. Even if you don't go to to UT, or Texas or the US, go somewhere. I would say people who don't exploit this opportunity are seriously missing out on so much. It might change your outlook on the the whole world or your own life. See it as a phenomenal investment in yourself.

arrival_assistance: In the week before the classes started you had two online info meetings and an in-person campus tour.
arrival_comments: It was good. The info was pretty clear and well-prepared for the students, even though most of it were online.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Overall I would say that the experience was good, however, getting the courses I had hoped for, unfortunately, turned out to be challenging. The Covid situation also made stuff a bit challenging since most of my classes turned out to be online.
registration_process: They had two different portals to apply for courses through depending on possible course restrictions.
registration_help: You could ask for help over e-mail or through a Teams groups that was created for the international coordinators and the students. This worked well, and the coordinators answered fast.

recommended_courses: I would recommend them all depending on your specific interests. They all had interesting elements. Particularly did I enjoy the populism course due to an excellent visiting professor from Canada.
unexpected_costs: Nothing that I can think of.
cost_comparison: Colombia is pretty cheap, so nothing. Prices are good. Especially cabs and food are cheap.
activities_available: They have a lot to offer in every sense, however, some natural restrictions due to covid.
activities_recommended: I did not participate regularly on anything and was little on campus due to the covid situation and most of my classes being online.
weekend_recommendations: Bogota has a lot to offer for everyone. Many great restaurants, hikes in the mountains around, etc. Monserrate is a must.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy, but I had also been in the city on several occasions before doing my exchange semester in Bogota. I guess it depends on how much experience you have from Latin American countries and big cities before coming.
socializing_tips: Be active and get engaged in activities that are offered through the university. There was also a group of local students that helped organizing trips and activities of different kinds for exchange students. However, some stuff was obviously restricted due to the covid situation.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: How friendly and overall helpful the locals are. Food is also great.
top3_advice: Be as open and adaptable as possible, and do not expect things to be done the same ways that you might be used to from DK.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: Getting to know new people, experience the Colombian way of doing thing in general, and also, and especially, getting a different perspective on academic stuff.
greatest_challenge: Covid. I barely had classes on campus and most of my classes were online.
other_comments: No.

crucial_aspects: I have previously traveled in Latin America, and since I study spanish language and culture it made great sense to go back here.
info_ease: Not too easy. I had to contact the supervisor various times, before she got back to me. Since there was a delay in the application process that I had not been informed about, It was pretty stressful at first, cause I had to insist on getting the information.
arrival_assistance: There was 3 introduction days for all exchange students at Uniandes, and we could contact an employee at the uni, who always replied fast.
arrival_comments: There was a lot of information, which I understand is necessary to some extent, but some of the info felt irrelevant, like e.g. the presentation about the security system on campus.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was pretty stressful because you get told on beforehand that you have to be ready cause there at limited spots. However I got all the courses I wanted and more.
registration_help: The same employee who was available at all the time responded within minutes to any e-mail.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Do good research about the classes and take advantage of the fact that you can create "wish-schedules" before registering. Because you have to figure out yourself which classes you can take that don't overlap, the system will just reject you if you apply for to classes at the same time. I had 4 different templates of schedules, and itreally helped me get an overview.
course_level: My courses where interesting and challenging, I really improved my painting and drawing skills and learned a lot. Sometimes it was challenging since I don't normally study art, but the professors were really helpful. If you don't speak good spanish it could be a really big challenge, I'm fluent and I often misunderstood assignments.
teaching_comparison: It's very different from the danish university. There are many test and many assignments. Much more like Gymnasie than university, so it can feel like much more work, in some ways.
courses_enrolled: Painting bodies Basic painting Basic drawing Drawing space
recommended_courses: If you are artistic, this is an amazing opportunity for you. I got to spend 5 months painting and drawing and the facilities at Uniandes' art department are amazing. You get to learn from professors who all work currently as artists. I really recommend studying art courses here. But there are a bunch of materials that you have to buy, so it's a bit more expensive, but totally worth it.
unexpected_costs: Everything is quite cheap in Colombia. Only thing could be that somethings might not be AS cheap as you expect, but it's still cheaper than DK.
cost_comparison: Transportation. It's cheap but since you take a lot of cars around you end up spendig more than you might think at first. Food delivery is really really cheap though.
activities_available: There were sport classes, dance lessons and events for exchange students.
activities_recommended: I didn't participate in any so I don't know.
weekend_recommendations: Go out of the city! There are plenty of lovely villages and places in nature to see. Or book flights to further away in the country - if you do it a few weeks in advance the tickets to e.g. the caribbean coast could be like 300 dkk for the round trip.
culture_adjustment: It's very different here. To me it was easy cause I adjust well to Latin american culture, since I'm and open person and I speak spanish. You should know that Colombians are much better at small talking than danes, so you can get friends while waiting in line for your lunch.
socializing_tips: Don't be shy. Speak spanish with them, and invite them to hang out. Then it's not difficult at all.
cultural_challenges: The fact that people in Bogota don't move when you need to get on the Transmilenio (the metro) so you have to push them. And the fact that you can't walk in the streets at night.
culture_appreciated: The heartwarming people. It's very easy to befriend a colombian. And the parties are amazing here, lots of dancing and much better night clubs than in DK.
top3_advice: 1 If you want and ID card to access uni, you should start insisting on it early on. I never got mine, and had to enter everyday with my admission-letter. Not a big deal, but still annoying. 2 People in Colombia a usually much younger when they start university (around 16-17 yrs old) So if you're a bit older like me when you go (26) you might find it challenging to bond with fellow students. Be patient with the colombian bureaucracy. There are a lot of forms to fill out, and the processes are slower than we are used to in DK.
other_useful_info: Bogota can be pretty cold, and none of the houses are isolated. So bring warm socks and sweaters for the nights. And it also rains, but so much that you just use an umbrella, so no need to bring all your danish rain-gear. Some people bike, but the distances are way longer that in CPH and the traffic is like freeways (pretty crazy) in many places, so I don't recommend it. Always have cash on you, but not too much.
most_rewarding: I got a bunch of great friends that I will always want to come back to and visit.
greatest_challenge: Sometimes it's hard to be so far away from your family.
other_comments: Don't let you scare away from people saying that Colombia is dangerous. Just don't be irresponsible and have fun, Bogota is an incredible city!

crucial_aspects: My main goal of studying abroad was to be able to learn in Spanish again and pick up this language in an academic setting. So I explored different universities across South America. I chose Universidad de Los Andes because it is the best university in Colombia and had a really good interdisciplinary program involving environmental and social issues. Also have always wanted to visit Colombia, a country with a lot of diversity within its culture, people and landscapes.
info_ease: The Exchange Office at Universidad de los Andes is extremely prepared and attentive to the needs of the incoming students. The main point of contact, Anderson, was always fast to respond through email with any questions we had. Before arrival we had some online talks and received a checklist of the documents we need to have to pass migration procedures
arrival_assistance: The first week upon arrival there were many intro talks and activities hosted for exchange students specifically. About the university, teaching style in UniAndes, life in Bogotá, code of conduct, safety, local customs and other general advice. This was really insightful and good way to start the term. We also were introduced to a group of volunteering local students called 'Hermanos Sin Fronteras' that guided us the whole semester and were in contact with us through a WhatsApp groupchat. They planned events, gave us advice, traveled with us and answered smaller questions (eg. where to get a SIM card, restaurant recommendations, transport information, etc)
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: - I received access to a course catalogue from UCPH but it was outdated by 2 years. So when I had to sign up to course at UniAndes I could not find the courses I had previously seen on the catalogue. That was a bit tricky because I had to go through the pre-approval UCPH process again which takes up to 6 weeks. The course registration at UniAndes is a bit messy because since we are exchange students we go through a separate portal from home students to sign up to courses. You are advised to sign up to as many courses as possible because quite a lot are rejected depending on access requirements and availability. Also the website is a bit glitchy and outdated. Just be prepared to deal with this.
registration_help: - Anderson from the UniAndes exchange office is really understanding and warned us about the trickiness of this process. Although he is not a specialist in each course he can help you with the course registration portal
registration_success: - I managed to register to 2 out of the 3 courses I wanted. And then for the third course, I picked another one that was also interesting and told UCPH again to go through the course pre-approval.
registration_advice: It is a bit like UCPH course registration portal so you won't be too surprised. Always tricky with these online sign up portals because everyone is on it at the same time due to the limited window and the server crashes from time to time. Just be patient and keep an open mind when signing up to courses. Choose a wide range of them so you don't get disappointed that you did not get into some.
course_level: - I managed to register to 2 out of the 3 courses I wanted. And then for the third course, I picked another one that was also interesting and told UCPH again to go through the course pre-approval.
teaching_comparison: - It was pretty similar to the style of teaching masters at UCPH. We had to do 3-4 readings/ class and then talk about them in class discussions and relate it to other literature and current issues. A different thing was that most class discussions were related to local context so I had to do extra research and readings to prepare for class. The class discussions involved the whole class rather than small working groups like it's normally done at UCPH. Then lastly, we were graded on our class participation and attendance 10-20% of our total grade. - I know for bachelors it was different teaching style to that of UCPH involving more weekly homework that is more “high-school” like
courses_enrolled: I took 3 courses in total. All in Spanish. All worth 10 ECTS or 4 créditos in Colombia. - Ecologia Politica y Justicia Ambiental - Teorias Feministas y Cambio Social - Debates Contemporaneos del Desarollo
recommended_courses: - I really liked all 3. They were courses that are also offered in UCPH or at least similar concepts. - I loved learning about political ecology from a latin American perspective and reading local literature. - Teorias Feministas was an eye-opener about how feminism is lived in other parts of the world and the whole academic history and progress of it. Also related the assignments to films and current issues like the new left-wing Colombian government - Maybe I would say that Debates Contemporaneos del Desarollo was the most difficult one because it had a lot of Colombian public policy context and harder to get engaged with. It was also 80% online and post-Covid it is not ideal cause I wanted to interact more with other students in person
unexpected_costs: To visit some places you have to pay "foreign" fees like museums, clubs, outdoor activities and sightseeing places while the local students paid less. It wasn't a lot of money but just something to keep in mind so it doesn't shock you - a very normal thing in Latin America and has a reason behind it. For example, a really beautiful national park by the Caribbean coast called Tayrona National Park the entry fee for locals was around 35000 COP while for foreigners it was over 50000 COP.
cost_comparison: Food is extremely affordable. Did not spend as much money as expected on it as I had predicted. Even when I ate out and more "pricey" meals Also accommodations for when I was travelling. Would be able to pay 30000-70000 COP for a night at a decent hostel. Sometimes even sleeping in hammocks would be great if you don't mind that - 20000 COP / night
activities_available: UniAndes is a private university so the extra curricular activities are incredible. There was all kinds of sports and installations: swimming pool, football fields, tennis and squash courts, a fully equipped gym(with machines, classes, weights). Also golf and horseback riding fields (not in the campus but part of the university and accessible through private university transport). I was personally part of a sewing class elective and the dance classes such as salsa, bachata and merengue and loved every minute.
activities_recommended: Some of the above!
weekend_recommendations: Travel! Get to know Colombia! This country is so diverse it could be a continent. There are so many regions to visit. These are some I visited:
culture_adjustment: For me that was one of the main priorities to fit in. You have to adapt a bit to the normal customs: people socialize differently. Bars and clubs are less about drinking and more about dancing. Be open to ask questions. Colombians were so welcoming and loved when I are curious about their country and their traditions. There is a number of festivos / national days that happen all year around so I tried to join and be a part of those.
socializing_tips: In class just talk and chat to the person sitting next to you and ask questions. Otherwise attend events and try to meet as many locals as possible. Be a part of their daily lives, follow the routine! Go to campus events! Ask questions
cultural_challenges: The haggling culture is REAL. Not neccesarily a challenge just to have to adapt to it fast once they see you are a foreigner otherwise you can get scammed really easily. Don't be shy and haggle for the prices in taxis, markets, tours, etc. Also a really famous saying there: 'No des papaya' which translates to Don't Give Papaya. This means don't flaunt yourself to much in a way you could expose yourself - just a warning to be Be careful with your jewellery, phone, money and your expensive items.
culture_appreciated: Colombians are so proud of their food, their culture and have a really strong sense of place that I have not seen in many other parts of the world. They know a lot about where they live specially in rural and nature regions. They want to show you Colombia and they appreciate when you enjoy it.
top3_advice: 1. Adapt - try to speak spanish and to the locals as much as possible. Also outside university. The university is a bubble culture since it's private so talk to people outside of it. 2. Go to the salsa dance classes at UniAndes with prof. Mauricio. He is a pro and makes them so fun 3. Explore the whole university and all the events it has. Way more social and campus life than that at UCPH
other_useful_info: Good to have a go-to cross-body bag for when you travel and carry important stuff there. Don't carry a lot of cash on you - just what you need that day. There are more and more places that take in card as payment so I recommend you get a travel debit card. Safest to do this. I even had it on my phone as Apple Pay so didn't have to take out my whole wallet to pay. Some places charge commissions when you pay by card so have that in mind as well
most_rewarding: Travelling and visiting all the regions outside of Colombia. I learned the most this way.
greatest_challenge: Time difference and being hard from "home" but easy to adapt once you just accept that it's your life. Also sometimes it was hard that life became some different after it turned dark at 6pm and it was not as recommended to walk around freely.
other_comments: Once in a lifetime experience to do 5 months abroad. Would do it 10 times again

cultural_challenges: Maybe the food... It is allright, but im not a huge fan.
culture_appreciated: The nature and the people.
