Likewise, it was free to choose and participate in sport courses. The campus is extremely beautiful with a lot of outdoor areas connecting the different lines of study. There was a lot of outdoor cafe and food options and the university arranged many social activities for all of the students.
overall_comments: I had an absolutely amazing experience and I truly wish that I could come back for another semester.
info_ease: Pretty easy. There was a one week orientation before classes started and we were also connected to a student organization called Hermanos sin fronteras who helped us with any social and travel related issues. We also had a contact person from the international office who we could contact any time concerning any issues related to visa or the university.
arrival_assistance: I arrived a week before orientation and had a hard time finding my way around and socializing.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I had an absolutely amazing experience and I truly wish that I could come back for another semester.
registration_process: Very confusing. They have two systems depending on wether the course you want to register has any requirements. If not, you get signed into the course as soon as you register. Otherwise, you'll be put on pending and can see the result after 1-2 weeks. There's no was to prioritize so you have to register subjects in the order you want them. Also, registration starts only 3 weeks before classes start which I found very stressful prior to registering. Some of my subjects was first accepted in the system a few days before class started.
registration_help: I could contact Anderson (the contact person from the international office). He created a Team group where we could talk with him and the other exchange students.
registration_success: I got the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: A danish saying: Hav is i maven.
academics_comments: I had an absolutely amazing experience and I truly wish that I could come back for another semester.
course_level: Too easy
teaching_comparison: In KU I have lectures and seminar classes. Attendance is voluntary and our grades are decided on one single exam on the end of the semester. In UniAndes we only had interactive seminar classes. A lot of presentations and in-class quizzes, mid-term exams and assignments, so the final exam was only 20-40% of my final grade.
courses_enrolled: Ética professional, derecho internacional II (ingles), contratos internacionales and criminología. Also salsa and bachata básico and Escalada en muro intermedio.
recommended_courses: Contratos internacionales was a great and practical course. They take you through every step of a contract and give you recommendations throughout the course on how to improve, as well as take you through arbitration steps. I also really liked criminología. It's a smaller course and you get a good understanding of the different theories from a teacher that is really interested in the subject.
unexpected_costs: I travelled a lot more than I had expected which was very expensive
cost_comparison: transportation was very cheap. Also eating out costed more or less the same as making food at home, so I ate out a lot.
activities_available: A wide range of sport classes (dance, ball-games, martial arts, fitness etc.) Many different student unions and clubs (book, pride, biodiversity, sport, cars, debate clubs etc.)
activities_recommended: Take part in the Hermanos sin Fronteras activities. They throw fun parties and arrange great trips around Colombia.
weekend_recommendations: Travel as much as you can. Colombia is so beautiful! I would highly recommend these cities: Medellin, Cartagena, Villa de Leyva, Santa Marta, Barranquilla, Neiva (to see the Tatacoa Dessert), Leticia (to see the Amazon). In and around Bogotá I can recommend going to Gringo Tuesday (a language exchange that occurs every Tuesday of the year) and Andrés Carne de Res in Chia, which is the biggest one.
culture_adjustment: It took me a good 2 months to get accustomed. I had a lot of problems with culture shock, home sickness and language barriers in the beginning, but halfway through I get way better and had the time of my life.
socializing_tips: Colombians are very open and warm people but you might have to initiate friendships. But as soon as you have made a friend they're very loyal and love to share their culture and traditions with you.
cultural_challenges: I looked very foreign (tall, pale, blonde, blue eyes) so I experienced a lot of staring and comments on my appearance. The meat tastes very strong and the food in general is very different. There was always latin music playing and people talk a lot especially gossip about other people.
culture_appreciated: The open and warmness that I was met with everywhere. People are extremely nice and curious about you. There was a more relaxed attitude towards time, we were more spontaneous and didn't necessarily meet on time. It was also great that everyone could dance without having to get drunk, the parties and socials were so much fun. Christmas traditions were also great, I can recommend going out with some local at la noche de las velitas.
top3_advice: Be social. It helps a lot on culture shock. Live in the moment. The exchange year passes by way too quickly. Say yes. Every day is an adventure in this country.
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: I had a presentation in spanish for my final exam in criminology and I succeeded with really good grades.
greatest_challenge: The language barrier. My spanish is fairly good, however legal spanish was something else and if I zoned out in class I would be completely lost in translation.
other_comments: The only danger of going to Colombia is not wanting to leave. In all seriousness, fantastic country and amazing experience. Have a wonderful exchange!

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne hen et sted, hvor man kunne opleve en anden kultur, og hvor leveomkostningerne var lave nok til, at man havde muligheden for også at udforske landet.
info_ease: Det var okay let. Jeg syntes stadig det var lidt overvældende, men det er vel uundgåeligt.
arrival_assistance: Vi havde et møde med udvekslingskoordinatoren i løbet af den første uge og derefter et opfølgende møde efter tre uger. De arrangerede workshops for at hjælpe med at tilmelde os kurser, og der var et kontor kun dedikeret til at hjælpe udvekslingsstuderende. Det varierede, hvor dygtige medarbejderne var. Derudover var der en hel uge med introdage for udvekslingsstuderende, der blev styret af en studenterforening, der havde ansvaret for at integrere udvekslingsstuderende. De hedder Hermanos sin Fronteras og man kan følge dem på Instagram.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Som jeg husker det, åbner tilmeldingen for udvekslingsstuderende 48 timer før de normale studerende på Uniandes. Det skar ca. en uge før semesterstart. Først når den åbner (eller ugen før?), kan man se hvilke kurser, der rent faktisk bliver udbudt. Kursuskataloget indeholder MANGE flere kurser, end de rent faktisk udbyder. Det var en ret stor udfordring for mig. Desuden har man 30 credits at tilmelde sig kurser for, og 12 credits svarer til 30 ECTS. Derfor tilmelder man sig mange kurser, da det ikke er sikkert der er plads på kurserne, man bliver godkendt eller om de overhovedet optager udvekslingsstuderende (det var mest et problem på kandidatkurser). Man kan ikke tilmelde sig to fag der overlapper bare ét minut skemamæssigt. Derudover skal man også tilmelde sig sport (som fag) i denne proces. Man kan også gå til uforpligtigende sport, der ikke er et fag. Derefter venter man på at underviseren godkender at man er kvalificeret til kurset, og om man nåede det før alle pladser blev fyldt op. ELlers må man søge igen om noget andet. Forrsten søger man både en plads på faget (forelæsninger) og SKAL også ansøge og godkendes til de tilhørende "klassetimer/arebejdshold".
registration_help: De lavede en workshop, og dem fra udvekslingskontoret, stod klar til at hjælpe i de efterfølgende dage.
registration_success: Jeg fik dem jeg søgte om (og 4 ekstra jeg droppede efter den første uge), men de udbød ikke et eneste af de fag jeg havde planlagt at tage ud fra kursuskataloget.
registration_advice: Lad være med at stresse over, at alle de relevante informationer kommer meget sent. Derfor kan msn ligeså godt bruge et gammelt kursuskatalog til at orientere sig om mulige kurser. Søg merit for så meget du kan på forhånd, men husk, at man kan søge merit helt frem til november, så man kan godt tilmelde sig kurser, man endnu ikke har merit for. Vær åben overfor ændringer i dine kursusvalg, da de ofte overlapper skemamæssigt, og så kan man kun følge ét af kurserne.
course_level: Jeg troede jeg skulle have nogle 1. semester fag fra andre uddannelser (introduktion til molekylærbiomedicin e.lign.), men droppede dem alle. Nogle forelæsere var rigtig gode, andre var frygtelige til at formidle, hvad de gerne ville have man skulle lære.
teaching_comparison: Meget forskellig. Der var mødepligt, og hvis man missede mere end 20% af et fag, dumpede man automatisk. Der er sjældent man har en afsluttende eksamen i faget, man tager små quizzer hver uge, der tæller en eller anden procentdel. Andre vurderingskriterier er: Mindre eksamener, fremlæggelser, deltagelse i undervisning mm. Det er meget gymnasie-agtigt. Man kan af og til tjene ekstra point ved at svare på spørgsmål eller melde sig frivilligt til et eller andet.
courses_enrolled: ADMI 3133 MANAGEMENT FOR CIRCULAR ECONOMY MUSI 1820 CORO UNIANDES QUIM 4300 SINTESIS DE COMPUESTOS HETEROCICLICOS LENG 1572 ESPAÑOL LENGUA EXTRANJERA 2
recommended_courses: Det tre uger lange spanskkursus, Uniandes tilbyder før semesterstart, er det hele værd. Man ankommer 4 uger før, og når at finde sig tilrette før det hele går løs. Vi var også kun 13 studerende, så vi blev hurtigt tætte og tog ud at rejse sammen i friugen mellem kurset var slut og semesterstart. Derudover kunne jeg få det godkendt som kursus til 7,5 ECTS point i DK, så jeg kun skulle følge 22,5 ECTS i løbet af semesteret. Resten af kurserne var ok.
unexpected_costs: Jeg rejste rundt i Colombia meget mere end jeg havde regnet med. Jeg tog Uber hjem meget oftere end jeg havde regnet med, da jeg havde undervisning til sent to gange om ugen.
cost_comparison: Æg var billige og frokost meget billig! Jeg spiste næsten altid Almuerza del día, og fik så meget mad, at jeg kunne tage det med, og også spise det til aftensmad. Kaffe var okay billigt, men ikke vanvittigt, medmindre det var dårlig kaffe. Ost var virkelig dyrt og de ingredienser, vi er vant til at bruge i vores madlavning i DK, er også ret dyre. Det var lidt svært at opfinde nye retter baseret på de dagligvarer, der var billige i Colombia. Vegansk mad var overraskende let at få fat i (jeg havde en del veganske venner).
activities_available: Sport, kreative fag og ture/arrangementer arrangeret af Hermanos sin Fronteras. Lidt sport: Dans, tennis, volleyball, boksning, fodbold, spinning, bordtennis, billiard, svømning, basketball mm. Kreative fag: keramik, kor, tegning og sikkert mange flere
activities_recommended: Lær at danske salsa! og engagér dig i et eller andet efter skoletid, enten sport eller kreativt. Det er den letteste måde at møde colombianere på. Desuden er det hyggeligt at deltage i arrangementer og ture som Hermanos sin Fronteras står for især i starten af semesteret.
weekend_recommendations: Jeg var væk næsten hver weekenden (jeg havde fri torsdag-søndag). Jeg var i San Agustín, Popayan, Villa de Leyva, Salento, Tatacoaørkenen, Medellín, Guatavita, Barichara, Bucaramanga, El Camino del Rey, og mange små dagsture fra Bogotá bl.a. til paramos. I efterårsferien var jeg i Guatemala og jeg rejste rundt i det nordlige Colombia i en måned efter vores studier endte. Jeg anbefaler alle stederne, men specifik vil jeg tilføje at Cabonera Valley er meget smuk og et lidt usædvanligt turistmål. Man skal selvfølgelig se en Paramo mens man er i Colombia. San Agustín er en virkelig fantastisk og billig destination.
culture_adjustment: Meget let. Det var overraskende let at vænne sig til ikke at gå rundt efter mørkets frembrud. Colombianere er enormt søde og udadvendte, og mange af dem er meget nysgerrige efter at lære fremmede at kende. Tag imod det, det bliver helt sikkert en masse uforglemmelige oplevelser!
socializing_tips: Deltag i en aktivitet efter skole og vær åben, hvis nogen opsøger dig mens du fx. spiser frokost. Hvis du først lærer én at kende, præsenterer de dig garanteret for resten af deres venner, der også er interesserede. Hvis du er heldig, tager de dig også med hjem til deres familie.
cultural_challenges: De studerer rigtig meget ift udvekslingsstuderende, så de har ikke helt så meget tid. Desuden tilbringer de fleste hver søndag med familien.
culture_appreciated: Der åbenhed og imødekommenhed.
top3_advice: Lad være med at stresse over alt det bureaukratiske. Det er mega hårdt, men det skal nok gå. Snak med colombianere, de er enormt søde. Forvent at rejse en hel del i løbet af weekenderne. Prøv at finde bolig udenfor et af de store amerikanskejede lejlighedskomplekser. Lad være med at gøre noget dumt, bare fordi du ikke orkede/gad passe på.
other_useful_info: Ja, men jeg tror jeg er kommet ind på det meste
most_rewarding: Min veninde Juliana jeg fik gennem kor, og alle de fantastiske oplevelser jeg fik på mine rejser.
greatest_challenge: Jeg havde lagt al undervisning mandag-onsdag, så det var nogle meget lange dage. Desuden fungerede deres vurderingssystem ikke for mig. Jeg blev meget udmattet af at skulle være på god for med underviserne og hele tiden have en tests. Desuden var det hårdt ikke at være ligestillet med underviseren, så det var sværere at give konstruktiv kritik.
other_comments: Colombia virker måske farligt, når man kigger på udenrigsministeriets hjemmeside, men det er på størrelse med Frankrig og Spanien tilsammen. Et område på størrelse med Frankrig er vurderet gult, hvilket svarer til den rating de giver Paris. Bussystemet er meget velfungerende, så det er super let og billigt at komme rundt. Derfor anbefaler jeg, at man skal få det bedste ud af at opleve landet!

crucial_aspects: Jeg ønskede at studere i et spansk talende land og gerne så anderledes som muligt fra vores almindelige liv i Danmark. Jeg ville gerne udfordre mig selv og opleve noget jeg ellers aldrig ville komme til.
overall_comments: Det var hårdt at komme afsted mht. papirarbejdet men oplevelsen var det hele værd.
info_ease: Det var ikke let men det skyldtes særligt en sprogbarrier. Alt stod på spansk men universitet i Colombia hjælp så godt de kunne når man spurgte om hjælp.
arrival_assistance: Der var en klar og grundig introduktion og som udvekslingselev bliver man guidet gennem systemet.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Det var hårdt at komme afsted mht. papirarbejdet men oplevelsen var det hele værd.
registration_process: De har en portal hvor man kan se alle kurser og så får man som udvekslingselev lov til at melde sig til før alle andre. Det er en kæmpe hjælp da kurserne er først til mølle og det ikke altid er lige let at finde kurser særligt ikke hvis man gerne vil have en godt skema og nogle af sine kurser på engelsk. Man kan melde sig til flere kurser end man har brug for til en start så man senere kan fravælge nogle hvis de ikke er så spændende alligevel. Dette gælder også sports fag som også kræver at du er meldt til kurset.
registration_help: Anderson var meget behjælpelig og lavede en session hvor alle udvekslingselever sad og meldte os til vores fag sammen.
registration_success: Det gik perfekt. Igen jeg havde lavet meget forarbejde og havde endda lavet en plan A, B og C men det endte med at jeg fik alle de kurser jeg ville uden problemer.
registration_advice: Sørg for at søge forhåndsgodkendelse i goooood tid da det på SAMF kan tage lang tid og det er ikke fedt at melde sig til kurser man ikke engang ved om man må tage. På Science er de hurtigere til at svarer så der er det ikke så problematisk.
academics_comments: Det var hårdt at komme afsted mht. papirarbejdet men oplevelsen var det hele værd.
course_level: Jeg tog et MA kursus og det var mega godt. BA kurserne var mere gymnasie agtige hvor MA var mere universitets agtigt.
teaching_comparison: Som nævnt ovenfor afhang det af niveauet på kurset og også rigtig meget af læren men generelt er det mere som vi kender undervisningen for gymnasiet.
courses_enrolled: Sustainability issues in Latin America Circular Economy Python Workshop Financial Planning Financial Economy
recommended_courses: Sustainability issues in Latin America var det bedste fag jeg havde. Mega fedt underviser og emnerne er super interessante. Circular Economy er et hyggeligt fag. Ikke super lærerigt men givet et nyt perspektiv på hvordan man optager viden og så er læreren hyggelig og tager en med på flied trips.
unexpected_costs: Husket ikke nogle overraskelser men det at få fat i SIM til telefon kan godt være lidt besværligt første gang da man skal ned og vise sit pas og registrer sig i eksempelvis CLARO.
cost_comparison: Alt der importeres er vildt dyrt. Køb lokalt ellers er det urimeligt dyrt.
activities_available: Næsten al form for sport heriblandt salsa, storskærms arrangementer for eksempel fodboldkampe, koncerter, brætspil og mange andre klubber.
activities_recommended: Salsa, fodboldkampe og billiard.
weekend_recommendations: HELE COLOMBIA. Eller rettere de gule område ifølge udenrigsministeriet. Der er kæmpe dele af colombia som er helt sikkert at besøge heriblandt alle turist stederne mod nord men også mere syd såsom San Agustin som jeg personligt elskede.
culture_adjustment: Det var ikke svært for mig men tror det afhænger af hvor meget man har rejst og hvem man er. Kulturchokket man får i Colombia er ikke som i Asien. I Colombia bliver man mest af alt overrasket over hvor åbne og imødekommende mennesker/fremmede kan være.
socializing_tips: Meld dig til en masse sports kurser og snak spansk så godt du kan. De er simpelthen så åbne så vær ikke bange de skal nok kontakte dig hvis du gør dig selv tilgængelig.
cultural_challenges: Folk er åbne uden at have en bagtanke meeeeen vær ikke naiv. Kriminalitet er en ting i Bogota man på Universitet kan man være helt tryg.
culture_appreciated: Deres åbenhed og deres markeder med friske råvarer, friskpressede juice og særligt almuerzo del dia. (Dagens frokost til omkring 25-30 kr)
top3_advice: 1) Gør dit forarbejde mht. kurser og bolig det giver det en meget bedre start. 2) Rejs og se landet så sørg for at ligge dit skema så du minimum har enten mandag eller fredag fri. Evt. tjek helligdagene da det også kan have ret stor betydning. 3) Tag og meld dig til en masse sports kurser og lær folk at kende. Det var her jeg lærte flest Colombianere at kende.
other_useful_info: Husk at have styrt på spansk kravene før du søger og hvis du ikke er virkelig god til spansk så tjek at du kan få nogle relevante kurser på engelsk. Økonomi og Management er let at få på engelsk men alt andet er meget begrænset.
most_rewarding: Oplevelsen af at have en hverdag som er så forskellig fra den jeg har i Danmark.
greatest_challenge: Spansk niveauet gør at du ikke kun skal fokusere på at lære et fagligt emne men også forstå hvad der overhovedet bliver sagt til en start.
other_comments: Tag på udveksling og gør det her. Det er en oplevelse for livet.

crucial_aspects: It has been my dream for 5 years to go to Colombia, because I wanted to improve my spanish, and for me Colombia represents a country full of diversity (cultural, landscapes, nature, ethnic), and I think that is very beautiful
info_ease: More or less, some things were a bit confusing, but everything got sorted out, and I think it's part of the experience that things are a bit confusing to begin with.
arrival_assistance: Unfortunately I missed the introduction week because of exams, and during that week the other students got a lot of information and met each other. So I really recommend to go to the introduction week if you can.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was a messy and very confusing to understand how it works. I found it frustrating. And then I ended up with almost all the courses I wanted to, which was nice, but the process was annoying. So just be prepare for that, but don't worry as it will be sorted out. For example my llast course got approved the week the courses started.
registration_help: Yes you could easily ask the persons in charge of the mobility program.
registration_success: I got 2 out of 3 courses I wanted.
registration_advice: You can sign up for more credits than you need, so do that, because it's nice to try the course and afterwards drop it. And sign up for sports clases- salsa bachata beginner is awesome!
course_level: You have to attend classes and there is quite a lot of work during the semester, assignments, test, stuff like that. I wouldn't say it's super difficult, I think the level some times may be a bit lower than UCPH (depends on the course).
teaching_comparison: A lot of the master courses are hibrid but more online. It was a bit disapointing and not very motivating. Furthermore there are either in the morning like 7-9 or afternoon 15-19 because the colombians that are enrolled in their master are working full time.
courses_enrolled: - Género e interdisciplinariedad - Teorías de desarollo - Teorías de relaciones internationales Ekstra credit - Espanol lengua extranjera - Salsa bachata
recommended_courses: I wouldn't recommend the courses I had.
unexpected_costs: You use a lot of uber
cost_comparison: In general Colombia is a lot cheaper than Denmark
activities_available: Many sports clases but also creative classes.
activities_recommended: I already said bachata salsa haha And if I could do it again, I would have chosen an art course.
weekend_recommendations: There is a loooooot. I can't list everything here, you'll figure it out ;)
culture_adjustment: Easy, colombians are really nice
socializing_tips: Do sports classes and other activites.
cultural_challenges: Nothing, I have also travelled in south america before.
culture_appreciated: Everything I love Colombia. The culture, the people, the street food, the landscape, the openness, the salsa culture in bars.
top3_advice: 1. Even though the course registration is annoying, don't worry you'll be fine 2. Be open to all the different exchange students, don't stay in a european bobble, take initiative, organize a barbecue or something 3. Don't worry about housing, some of my friends even change accomodations during the stay, there are many places available.
other_useful_info: Don't worry if your spanish isn't perfect, mine is neither, and you don't need perfect spanish to pass the courses. Take extra spanish class at the university.
most_rewarding: The people I met.
greatest_challenge: It was a challenge with the online classes and not being there at the introduction week. I feel like I missed out on some relations.
other_comments: No

crucial_aspects: I really wanted to learn/improve my spanish level, and Uniandes offers a free spanish summer course, along with spanish course during the real semester. Plus colombian spanish is easier than a lot of other dialects. Bogotá also seemed like a really interesting city.
overall_comments: I highly highly recommend going to Uniandes, it's really nice for a bunch of reasons: - Colombians are great and hospitibal people and are easy to make friends with. I knew close to no one who didn't make colombian friends to some degree - The spanish summer course offers you a chance to create a social circle before starting starting the semester. Everyone there is looking for new friends in a foreign place, so it's very social. - Bogotá is located super central, so plenty of fun weekend trips to be had - Bogotá in itself is really a fun city, there's sooo much culture and it's a melting pot of the country's cultures. Plus the climate is like danish april/may weather all year - The flights are expensive, but living there can be really cheap if you want it to. - At uniandes there's a group of local students in charge of integrating the exchange students, meaning there's a lot of events and opportunities to meet other exchange students. - Colombia really has a strong beating heart, it's one of those countries you can't help but fall in love with - People who choose Colombia as an exhange destionation rather than something more conventional are often quite fun and interesting. Plus there's a good age-mix since many also go during their masters. I'm 25 and didn't feel too old. If you want to go to Rosklide and it overlaps with the first days of the summer course you can skip a couple of days (but not something like a week), attendance is registered and mandatory like in gymnasiet. Safety wise Bogotá is mared strongly by armed robberies, it happens a lot. I was robbed four times. But everytime it happened close to a park called Parque de los periodistas, so stay away from there and that helps alot. Also, there's a culture of almost only robbing men, i know maybe 20 men (local and foreign) who've been robbed, and only one woman. One the plus side, robbery is more or less the only danger in Bogotá itself, and it really rarely turns violent, so just consider it part of your travel budget. Ask locals how to take precautions. To stay safe in the rest of the country, avoid the guerilla controled areas (see british foreign travel advice and ask locals), and be aware of robberies in all big cities. Besides that it's no worries.

registration_process: The portal opens for one day a week-ish before classes start. Anderson's there to help physically on the day.
registration_help: Anderson
registration_success: Got all the ones i wanted.
registration_advice: No clue. Find the list of last semesters courses somewhere online.
academics_comments: I highly highly recommend going to Uniandes, it's really nice for a bunch of reasons: - Colombians are great and hospitibal people and are easy to make friends with. I knew close to no one who didn't make colombian friends to some degree - The spanish summer course offers you a chance to create a social circle before starting starting the semester. Everyone there is looking for new friends in a foreign place, so it's very social. - Bogotá is located super central, so plenty of fun weekend trips to be had - Bogotá in itself is really a fun city, there's sooo much culture and it's a melting pot of the country's cultures. Plus the climate is like danish april/may weather all year - The flights are expensive, but living there can be really cheap if you want it to. - At uniandes there's a group of local students in charge of integrating the exchange students, meaning there's a lot of events and opportunities to meet other exchange students. - Colombia really has a strong beating heart, it's one of those countries you can't help but fall in love with - People who choose Colombia as an exhange destionation rather than something more conventional are often quite fun and interesting. Plus there's a good age-mix since many also go during their masters. I'm 25 and didn't feel too old. If you want to go to Rosklide and it overlaps with the first days of the summer course you can skip a couple of days (but not something like a week), attendance is registered and mandatory like in gymnasiet. Safety wise Bogotá is mared strongly by armed robberies, it happens a lot. I was robbed four times. But everytime it happened close to a park called Parque de los periodistas, so stay away from there and that helps alot. Also, there's a culture of almost only robbing men, i know maybe 20 men (local and foreign) who've been robbed, and only one woman. One the plus side, robbery is more or less the only danger in Bogotá itself, and it really rarely turns violent, so just consider it part of your travel budget. Ask locals how to take precautions. To stay safe in the rest of the country, avoid the guerilla controled areas (see british foreign travel advice and ask locals), and be aware of robberies in all big cities. Besides that it's no worries.
teaching_comparison: Super different. Classes have frequent hand-ins and are way smallers (often 20 ppl or the like). Attendance is mandatory, but how mandatory depends on the professor. Often you can skip up to 15%.
courses_enrolled: - Summer spanish (ELE 2) - Semester spanish (ELE 3) - Ceramicá Basica Take ceramics!! It's really nice (10 ects) and you only have to pay for clay. - Taller de dibujar basica Really fun drawing course, you don't need any previous drawing experince to do it (same with ceramics) - Escalar Climbing course, okay but the facilies are not that good - Billar Fun course, but they play a colombian version of billard and it's very technique oriented but you always play - ECOPOLÍTICA Y POÉTICA DE LOS PENSAMIENTOS INDÍGENAS LATINOAMERICANOS-PROBLEMAS ANTROPOL. CONTEMP Super interesting, but attended it as assistant because the workload is insane.
recommended_courses: See above.
unexpected_costs: I travelled around a lot, so that got somewhat expensive. The semester ends start december, so you can travel for two months before your next semester at KU if you want and can afford it. Using Uber daily (kind of) is necessary due to security, but it's really cheap. Motorbike ubers are cheaper and more fun but also kind of dangerous (a lot of crashes). NEVER HAUL A TAXI!
cost_comparison: Eating out is super cheap.
activities_available: Hermanos sin fronteras.
activities_recommended: Go to parties at Uni Nacional, it's great Check out La Mechanica and Matik Matik for concerts, and Cinemateca for interesting movies.
weekend_recommendations: If you wanna see somewhere that no other people go, Gachalá is really nice for a weekendtrip. Good for hiking, and there's a direct local bus leaving from somewhere in Chapinero. Other than that there's a million options, but you'll learn about them when u arrive.
culture_adjustment: People are super welcoming, so don't worry about it. My spanish was quite basic when i arrived, but locals are happy to talk to you anyway. Most young uni people know english, but will address you in spanish anyway unless you insist or really struggle in spanish.
socializing_tips: People in class will often want to make friends with you, so just be open to it. Creative classes can be great because you have time to hang out it class.
cultural_challenges: The language, it's tiring but super rewarding. Plus there's sometime a toxic vibe amoung young local people that it's looking down on a bit to go home early from a party.
culture_appreciated: The love and warth of the people, hard to find better anywhere in the world. Plus the cultural diversity of the country is breathtaking. About 70 indiginous language still get spoken.
top3_advice: Do it!!!! I was scared before going too, trust me it's the right decision!!
other_useful_info: For brushing up your spanish (or learning it) before going, i recommend getting a language exchange partner in Copenhagen, it's the best way to improve. You might find one through Studieskolen or the app Hello Talk.
most_rewarding: The time during the spanish summer course was really magical.
greatest_challenge: Improving my spanish.
other_comments: Do it!!

crucial_aspects: First of all I was intrigued by the program: "Construcción de Paz", and I always wanted to go back to South America with my studies. Prior to the exchange I did not have any personal ties to Colombia, but many people around the world had recommended me to go. In addition, I was curious to delve into the anthropological discipline and hoped to find a place and a theme for my Master's Project, which I think I did.
overall_comments: Demanding, but excellent professors! I absolutely loved the content of the program, and the study environment was also vibrant with dedicated students who were more than willing to share their experiences and perspectives on the subjects as well as on life. Bogota was an interesting city with a lot of culture, but leaving the capital to undertake some preliminary fieldwork after the exams Colombia opened itself to me. I definitely hope to go back sooner rather than later!
info_ease: The staff at the the international office was very attentive to our needs. All international students received all the information regarding inscription, visa regulations, housing, etc. in due time. They even managed to respond to e-mails within 48 hours, and also opened a live chat where we could raise any concerns both prior and during our stay.
arrival_assistance: Introductory weekend arranged by the international office together with the various student clubs. Again, all information was presented in a comprehensible and well organized manner.
arrival_comments: Simply always attentive to their students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

Bogota was an interesting city with a lot of culture, but leaving the capital to undertake some preliminary fieldwork after the exams Colombia opened itself to me. I definitely hope to go back sooner rather than later!
registration_process: First come first serve. In theory international students were allowed to enter the platform before the other students, but more than a few had issues with the platform not working. In that case one had to apply through another platform that for some strange reason allowed all the courses to fill up, which in a lot of cases resulted in people not getting the courses they needed.
registration_help: In person, e-mail, or online call. Very service minded and helpful indeed.
registration_success: First I had issues with the first platform, but I managed to convince two professors to open their class when the system would not let me register. Others were less fortunate and had to settle with something else.
registration_advice: Identify all the courses of your interest which could be approved at KU, ask the responsible professor to share the course description, and finally consider to apply for fewer courses with more credits in order to make your week more manageable.

Bogota was an interesting city with a lot of culture, but leaving the capital to undertake some preliminary fieldwork after the exams Colombia opened itself to me. I definitely hope to go back sooner rather than later!
course_level: High expectations. Not an awful lot of reading (80-100p per week per class), but compared to KU I had to write a lot of papers: In one course I had to hand in 3-4 pages every class, other than that each class had a midterm paper and a final paper of approximately 10p each. Finally, all my courses had an oral component which could for instance be a group presentation.
teaching_comparison: I followed three courses which all took shape of seminars.
courses_enrolled: CISO 4043 ; CISO 4029; CISO 4640. Two anthropological courses and a political economics class
recommended_courses: All the anthropological courses were extremely interesting. Not only did the teachers have a lot of experience they also invited guest lecturers to join our conversations.
unexpected_costs: Taxis and robbers
cost_comparison: Transportation (taxi) was cheaper than in Denmark, but Bogota is a big city where you do not want to walk after dark.
activities_available: Dance, museums, concerts, city-walks (!), cooking classes, and all sorts of clubs!
activities_recommended: Use the facilities! - sign up for a free dance class or learn to swim.
weekend_recommendations: Casa de la Paz in Bogota, graffiti tour, street rap, salsa clubs in Bogota... Go explore, but remember that you have time after the study program ends ! Some students seemed to burn out towards the end because they had not taken time to study.
culture_adjustment: Somewhat difficult to asses the safety situation to be honest, but besides from that people were extremely helpful and fun.
socializing_tips: Participate in class! Ask them out or join a student club.
cultural_challenges: Safety
culture_appreciated: People seemed genuinely curious!
top3_advice: Do not stress but take your time to plan your study. And do not be shy to ask for help!
other_useful_info: Uniandes is the most expensive private university in Colombia, which is reflected in the demography of the people attending class. Some would rightfully claim that it is an elitist upper class institution, so do not expect an alternative school with progressive student politics, etc. Teachers and students seem open to critical discussions and I did not experience any political dogmatism, nonetheless, I do recommend to visit 'La Nacional' to not leave Colombia...
most_rewarding: School ! No doubt.
greatest_challenge: Personal relationships in Denmark

crucial_aspects: That the destination was within Central or South America. Also the subjects’ relevance to my studies.
info_ease: I think it was a bit difficult. The university itself did not do much for the exchange student community in my opinion.
arrival_assistance: We had three orientation days as exchange students prior to the semester start.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: There were two portals and some things you could only register in one of them. The portals would close down every few minutes, so it was difficult to research the courses, also because there weren’t any descriptions of the courses in the portals.
registration_help: A contact person in the exchange department on campus, who you could also contact through teams.
registration_success: Somewhat successful. Except for the fact that I couldn’t change one of the courses.
registration_advice: Research it thoroughly beforehand. But it is a bit difficult to do on their website.
course_level: The whole system is quite different to KU. There were a lot more smaller tests and a lot of group work. I would say the level is lower.
teaching_comparison: A lot more interactive teaching through tests, projects, group work etc.
courses_enrolled: Música en America latina Los animales en la historia Contextos de America latina y Colombia Arqueología de Colombia Arte en Colombia Art and travel
recommended_courses: All of them, except contextos de America latina y Colombia, because I think it was a bit too difficult to follow in Spanish, unless you speak and understand it perfectly. The other subjects were very interesting and easier to follow.
unexpected_costs: None really
cost_comparison: Groceries were more expensive than I expected. Rent was also a bit higher than expected.
activities_available: You could go to sports classes of all sorts, and there were Japanese clubs, cultural exchange club, volunteering for animals club etc.
activities_recommended: The sports and dance classes. They were great!
weekend_recommendations: Travel the country, especially to the Caribbean coast of Colombia.
culture_adjustment: At first it was very difficult but once you made friends it was much better.
socializing_tips: Living off campus so you’re forced to speak Spanish with local students. On campus housing was mostly exchange students.
cultural_challenges: Punctuality was very different (it was normal to be late).
culture_appreciated: The way they value social life very highly, and how easy it is to become part of a big friend group. Their dance culture is very rich too. They are also very helpful.
top3_advice: To make sure to show up and socialize on the intro days. To travel a lot while you can and also research a lot on the university’s website beforehand.
other_useful_info: That you can’t switch your courses once you’ve chosen them. Also that the university only arrange one thing for exchange students, so don’t rely on them to create a space for the exchange community - it can get very lonely.

greatest_challenge: Being very lonely and feeling that it was impossible to meet people and make friends. Also feeling unsafe and being robbed.

crucial_aspects: Oppurtunity to learn spanish and going to a culturally very different part of the world.
info_ease: Fairly easy, the office at uniandes that helps exchange students is very good, and whenever there was something i couldn't figure out on my own i went to them, and they solved it or pointed me in the right direction.
arrival_assistance: Read the above
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I honestly don´t remember
registration_success: I got all the classed i wanted.
registration_advice: Sign up for more classes than you need, you can drop the ones you have extra up until sometime in october. (So either take an extra few fun classes, or do it because you are in doubt which to choose)
course_level: I study anthropology but didn't do any anthropologycourses at uniandes, so i don't really know to be honest.
teaching_comparison: Many of the courses have smaller classes, which means its often more dialog teaching (which i really liked) but I think it depends a lot on the subject. In general columbian students spend a lot of time on uni, and the culture is to be on campus most days and for many hours.
courses_enrolled: ARTE 1151 ACUARELA ARTE 1244 CINE - COLOMBIANO DEPO 1010 VOLEIBOL ARENA DEPO 1256 SALSA BÁSICA LENG 1573 ESPAÑOL LENGUA EXTRANJERA 3 LENG 1577 ESPAÑOL INTENSIVO 2
recommended_courses: The spanish classes are great. I would especially recommend the intersemestrial one from start of juli that goes for a month. Its a great introduction to the uni, some of your new exchangemates, and the city in general. Even if you cant get credits for it, i would really recommend it! The salsa classes are very fun (but you can also show up without being inscribed (shhhh))
unexpected_costs: All the traveling :))
cost_comparison: Groceries are more expensive than i would have thought, but going out to eat (especially lunch menues) is cheap, and often cheaper than cooking on your own. Uber/Indrive or whatever ride-app is very cheap, but you also probably need to use it a lot, and will be a decent part of your expenses.
activities_available: Dosens, but I never joined any of them.
activities_recommended: Salsa/dancing classes, also so that you dare to go out on salsabars (Columbians are mostly very good, but its still very fun and a good way to meet new people whos not from uni)
weekend_recommendations: Travel as much as you can around in Columbia, its the greatest. My favorite place was the pacific coast, we went on the 1-week holiday in october and prolonged or vacation a bit :)) I would recommend to fly to Nuquí and visit towns from there, its the greatest. But do many weekendtrips! Go to Tatacoa-dessert, to Bucharamanga, to Los Llanos, Cali, Chiquinquirá, Villa de Leyva, Santander, places on the northcoast (you'll need more than a weekend), and the Amazon!! There are also so many great places to hike in and near bogotá!
culture_adjustment: Bogotá is a very big and very busy city, with a lot of stuff going on everywhere. You will spend a lot of time in traffic, and you will probably think more about your security than you are used to in Europe. But the Colombians are great and helpful and friendly. And they love to party and to meet new people, so if you want you can easily make a lot of friends while you are there (especially if you speak some spanish).
socializing_tips: Uniandes is the most expensive uni in the country, so most students come from very wealthy backgrounds. This often means that they like stuff like going to malls, and in general behaving a bit like they think american youth act. (and you usually starts uni when you are 17, so most people are quite young). But you can definetly find people that stick out, you'll just have to approach them in your classes.
cultural_challenges: Colombians don't usually make plans far out in the future, and if you made one you will have to confirm with them if its still there haha. And they will often invite you to stuff, and then never follow up on it (unless you ask them later), but don't be offended, if you like them just ask them again. But yeah a lot of them will probably cancel on you once in a while. Most plans are made on the day it happens.
culture_appreciated: As i said before, extremely sweet, funny, helpful, festive, open, and in general very curious about other cultures.
top3_advice: Try to avoid courses monday/friday, so its easier to go on long weekend trips :)) Bring extra credit card / phone from home. Its quite likely that you will lose it (stolen) at one point. Its very much worth it to go, even though its a bit unsafe and very different!!
most_rewarding: Learning to talk with so many people in their native language made traveling a very different (and much better) experience.
greatest_challenge: The city of Bogotá will never be a place where i feel that much at home. Its to unsafe, noisy and grey. But the people make up for it of course.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to improve my spanish and Colombia is an incredible country, which I wanted to get to know better
overall_comments: It's "easy" to do an exchange at Uniandes (Bogotá) because they are so used to having exchange students, so they are super good at helping with whatever question you might have. I love Colombia. The reason why it's not a 10 is just that Bogotá is a super intense city and the uni is located in a rather unsafe area, but if just don't walk alone at night and then you will be fine:)
info_ease: Rather easy, the Uni in Colombia is quick to answer questions over e-mail, but I mostly asked my friend who had done an exchange there before, who helped me a lot - so if you need assistance just ask in the "KU South America" facebook group if you can talk to someone who has been at the destination you're going to
arrival_assistance: There is an exchange office at Uniandes which I visited frecuently in the beginning of my stay, especially in the course selection period
housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: The people from the exchange office walked around and helped the exchange students to choose courses in their online registration program
registration_success: Exchange students can choose courses first so it went easy for me, I had 30 "free" ECTS which also helped. If you have problems go as soon as possible to the exchange office so they can help you
registration_advice: It's a super nice Uni to have "free" ECTS points at because they have a big sports center so you can also get ECTS points for participating in sports!! I love Colombia. The reason why it's not a 10 is just that Bogotá is a super intense city and the uni is located in a rather unsafe area, but if just don't walk alone at night and then you will be fine:)
course_level: It's the most expensive uni in Colombia (maybe south america) so crazy good facilities. The students are in general super young though and a bit boring, but the teaching is good.
teaching_comparison: I did a lot of courses I can't do at UCPH, like arts and sports, so very nice to have the opportunity to try subjects that is not part of your usual carreer.
courses_enrolled: Colombia (espacio, tiempo, diferencia), Salsa & Bachata, Spanish course level 2 & 3, Dibujo basicó
recommended_courses: Do sports courses and art classes:)
unexpected_costs: The everyday life is not that expensive, you can buy nice ok cheap lunch close to uni. The expensive costs are the weekend trips (not super expensive to travel in bus, but if you do it a lot with friends it always adds up!)
cost_comparison: In general a nice and cheap everyday life
activities_available: All sports you can think off! Take dance classes !!
activities_recommended: Go on a lot of weekend trips (in bus ofc;) - try to plan your subjects so you don't have classes monday or friday (or both) so you have long weekends to do stuff!!
weekend_recommendations: The pacific coast (also the carribbean - but the pacific is extraordinary) - you can see whales there! The area around Salento (the national park Sierra Nevada), 3-day hike in Santander (Camino Real hedder selve hiken), visit the Amazonas !!! (Leticia - from Leticia go to Puerto Nariño and take a 4-day slow boat to Iquitos in Peru). Visit "los llanos" region (western-vibe region east for Bogota), Caribbean coast (Minka and Tayrona nacional Park)
culture_adjustment: Colombian people are the sweetest and most welcoming, love to party and chat, also if you don't know a lot of spanish
socializing_tips: Don't worry if you don't make a lot of friends at Uniandes, the people studying there are super young and rich, you can find friends outside. Go to "La Casa de la Paz" in Chapinero area, very sweet people there.
cultural_challenges: Difference in time management, you have to check in some times if you meet up with a colombian person to know if it's actually happening and a lot of people cancel on the day haha
culture_appreciated: Everyone loves to dance, to talk and to get to know you. Super heart warming, curious and welcoming people
top3_advice: 1) Take sports classes or art classes 2) plan your schedule so you have multiple days off 3) remember that it's the most expensive univeristy in Colombia so people going there are just more reserved 4) Eat lunch at "mi Caserito" close to uni!!

Watch out at night though in Bogotá, especially in the center, always take a Uber or Indrive home (also don't trust regular cab drivers). Bring an extra phone just in case it gets stolen.
most_rewarding: Improving my spanish, getting to know a beautiful country and getting a lot of good friends to visit in Europe (from exchange)
greatest_challenge: Accepting that learning a language takes super long time but that you're improving each day also without knowing it:)
other_comments: Enjoy!!

crucial_aspects: I'd lived in South America before so I wanted to go back to be able to enjoy more of the language, culture and beautiful nature there:)
overall_comments: I had an amazing trip overall! A few reasons why it isn't a 10 is that Bogotá is a huge and overwhelming city + there's a lot of insecurity that you need to consider.
info_ease: Pretty easy! Not all of it made sense immediately, but -NAME REDACTED- is the person in charge of the exchange program, and any question or doubt I had I'd just ask him, and he'd help me figure it out.
arrival_assistance: -NAME REDACTED- - he was pretty quick at responding and would help out with any doubts you had.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I had an amazing trip overall! A few reasons why it isn't a 10 is that Bogotá is a huge and overwhelming city + there's a lot of insecurity that you need to consider.
registration_process: Courses are first come, first served so you should sign up as soon as the sign up-process opens - though it opens up for exchange students and first year students a bit earlier than for everyone else. The course registration happened online in two separate programs (which was a bit confusing). They explained it multiple times, but I never really understood how it worked hahah. I did the summer spanish course tho which means I was already in Bogotá when we had to sign up for courses, and they hosted a session where we could show up and get help. -NAME REDACTED- helped me then and honestly I don't know if I would've figured it out on my own...
registration_help: -NAME REDACTED- is the main help available in general! If you're already in Bogotá you can show up to the session they host, and if you're not I think there was a teams chat where you could ask questions and then -NAME REDACTED- would reply pretty quickly.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted!
registration_advice: You can't apply for courses that happen at the same time, so having planned out what courses you want to apply to and alternatives if you don't get these courses is a good idea + apply for more courses than you need cause you can always drop them later!
academics_comments: I had an amazing trip overall! A few reasons why it isn't a 10 is that Bogotá is a huge and overwhelming city + there's a lot of insecurity that you need to consider.
course_level: I found the level to be quite low compared to UCPH and the contents of the classes weren't very complicated. The only thing that surprised me was how much time a had to spend doing various assignment during the semester - it's definitely a lot more work, although then there's barely an exam period then, which makes it kinda worth it.
teaching_comparison: Usually at UCPH I have a mix of seminars and larger lectures (all voluntary) and what is being taught is based on a book. At UniAndes they only have more seminar style classes (where you can't have more than 20% absence), and the courses mainly center around what the professor says. In some of the classes there was external material but I didn't find it super relevant to the classes, so I didn't really read it. The exams and general evaluation (spread between many different assignments) are all elaborated and evaluated by the professor.
courses_enrolled: Propiedad Industrial, Derecho e Industria Cultural, Ética Profesional and Derecho Internacional II
recommended_courses: I liked Derecho e Industria Cultural + it didn't demand too much during the semester.
unexpected_costs: Travelling can be pretty expensive! I'm used to Copenhagen being more expensive than the rest of Denmark, but Bogotá isn't super touristy, so the more touristy places (e.g. Medellín and Cartagena) are a lot more expensive! Flights can also be pretty expensive, and it's not always advised to take the bus (both with regards to time and security).
cost_comparison: I mainly used Uber/InDrive to get around - it's very cheap, but since it's the main form of transportation it adds up. If you want to buy any food that's not typically colombian (e.g. tinned tomatoes or coconut milk) it's super expensive! Eating out is really cheap though.
activities_available: There were lots of clubs, sports classes and general activities. I didn't join a club, but I used the pool quite a bit + did salsa and yoga classes.
activities_recommended: Have a look at what's there and maybe try something new! Try the salsa class (also just to get to experience Mauricio hahah:))
weekend_recommendations: I'd never been to Colombia before so I did kind of a classic tourist route (with a few not so touristy places); Cartagena, Medellín, Cali, Desierto de Tatacoa, Villa de Leyva. Some of my friends, that had already been, went less well-known places and had a great time. I also went to Peru and saw Machu Picchu over the longer break:)
culture_adjustment: Colombian people are super welcoming which helps with the culture shock, but I still struggled a bit with the things that are just inherently different - just a matter of getting used to it tho:)
socializing_tips: Talk to people in your classes! People are really super nice and open + there's a lot of group work where so it's nice to know some people, and if you don't you'll get to meet them there!
cultural_challenges: I look very european so people would stare a lot, point at me and talk to me on the street. Sometimes I'd have nice chats with people, but sometimes I just wanted to be anonymous and be left alone hahah
culture_appreciated: How lovely the people are! They are so proud of their country, and they want to share the best parts of their culture, like food, music, dance, with you.
top3_advice: 1. Travel! Colombia has so much to offer, and one semester is not enough to get to see everything. I feel like I've only seen a small part of the country, but my most important take away is that I'll definitely come back 2. Do the 3 week summer spanish course! We were around 30 people, whereas there are like 250-300 people starting when the semester starts so it's a bit easier to get to know people. I met my closest friends there:) 3. Be aware, but don't be afraid. You definitely need to consider security, but I made it through without anything happening, so it is possible!
other_useful_info: It's useful to know at least a bit of spanish before going. I spoke pretty fluently and still struggled sometimes - both at uni and out in the real world. If you study law, there are also barely any classes in english, which means you might have to do classes in spanish. Other than that speaking spanish just opens so many doors to be able to get to know Colombia and Colombians:)
most_rewarding: Getting to know Colombia - beautiful country with lovely lovely people! Also the friends I made on exchange, very excited to hang out with them again in Europe!
greatest_challenge: Probably always feeling like (and being treated like) a foreigner because of how different I look and act
other_comments: Go - you're not going to regret it!

crucial_aspects: Spanish speaking, non touristy compared to bigger cities and it being on the partner list.
overall_comments: In general Bilbao is a great place for exchange. The city is both small enough to walk around without a map within a couple of weeks, but large enough to feel metropolitan. It offers everything other cities have wrt. eating, partying and culturally. Furthermore, as it is located in the mountains, hiking trails are endless and start right outside your doorstep. It is also 30 min. away from the beach where you can surf. Culturally the Basque country is distinct and different from the rest of Spain. This is nice as an exchange student, as you feel immersed in something most people (me included) didn't know exist (the strong basque culture).

crucial_aspects: I was specifically looking for an exchange opportunity in Spain to improve my Spanish. For me i chose Bilbao because i find the Basque history and culture very interesting, but i also liked the fact that it is less visited than Barcelona or Madrid. I also really liked the fact that it was a smaller city close to nature allowing for hiking. Besides that i had heard a lot about the gastronomical scene in the basque country.
overall_comments: I think Bilbao as a city is very nice and you definitely get to feel the very special atmosphere and culture in the Basque Country. I really liked the basque people i met on the way, and they were very welcoming towards me and i had some spots around the city where i could feel like a local/regular. On the other hand the study environment is in my opinion not the best. There are not a lot of events or student organizations within the University of the Basque Country. This makes it harder to meet local students, and compared to University of Copenhagen, it would've been nice with friday bars on campus, different events and talks either for the social aspects or as a supplement to the studies. At least for me the only negative part of my experience is that you as a student are left with events coordinated by ESN or Happy Erasmus, so you only really meet other Erasmus students.
info_ease: I think information in regards to UPV (University of the Basque Country) was a bit sparse, but with a buddy student this helped a lot. Although this was only the first few days. I was also lucky enough to have a landlord that was able to help me with finding information.
arrival_assistance: I got a lot of assistance from Maitane the international student coordinator at UPV, she has been a great help and done a really good job.

teaching_comparison: The style of teaching is very different, it's mainly lectures but with emphasis on participation. I found it to be more similar to that of danish high schools than of lectures and then lab/instructor classes.

recommended_courses: I would recommen all of the courses i took, besides ecodesign and circular economy. The course i took were fairly easy to participate in for exchange students. I did not like the attitude of the lecturer/professor in ecodesign and circular economy though. The classes was also friday from 16-21 and saturdays.

activities_recommended: I don't know which non-academic activities exist
weekend_recommendations: I would definitely recommend to visit the coast of Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa, Vitoria and San Sebastian. It is also really nice visiting Cantabria and Asturias. Some towns outside of Bilbao would be Lekeitoa, El Antxobe, Gernika and Bermeo/Mundaka in the Bizkaia region. Santoña in Cantabria is also really nice. I also like San Francisco and Bilbao la Vieja. Visit the cafe Bihotz, the wine bar Taska Beltz, the pizzeria Demaio and the restaurant Kimtxu. And don't forget to try a menu del dia at midday.
culture_adjustment: I found it a bit hard, with different times for eating out and with the stores being closed between 14 and 17. It is also difficult if you don't speak any spanish. But i managed to speak to some locals by being a regular at a few bars and cafes.
socializing_tips: It is very difficult because a lot of students being uncomfortable speaking English or non-English speakers, they also tend to be younger than scandinavian students. But if you speak some spanish or have the courage to do courses in spanish it is definitely easier to meet local students as you will most of the time be the only or one few exchange students in the class.
cultural_challenges: As i only speak some spanish it was difficult that a big part of the population speaks only Spanish or Spanish and Basque, but it is also a great opportunity for improving spanish proficiency.
culture_appreciated: The pride in the Basque heritage was really interesting, people were very nice and really wanted to show why Bilbao and the Basque Country is such a great place. I liked the pintxos, kalimotxo, the food in general and the vibrant city.
top3_advice: - Really try to learn spanish - Visit the different regions, cities and nature of the Basque Country instead of spending all weekends in all of the other cities in spain. - Don't get to caught up in the Happy Erasmus parties, but it is a great way to find likeminded exchange students
other_useful_info: Don't stress to much about school, if you attend classes and do all assignments you're gonna be fine.
most_rewarding: Learning about the culture of the basque country and having the experience of living outside of Denmark. I also met a lot of great people.
greatest_challenge: Getting to know local people.

crucial_aspects: My main objective of going on exchange was to explore new cultures and experiencing what it was like living abroad.
info_ease: Quite easy I would say. I received info on mail in good time before arrival, and the host university were quick to respond if I had any questions.
arrival_assistance: There were an introduction day for incoming exchange students the week before semester start. Everything about your courses and exchange-related activities were explained, along with a tour of the campus. You also get assigned a "buddy", who you can contact if you have further questions.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I found the courses on the website after a good amount of looking. The courses are split up into 5 blocks to avoid overlapping between the courses you pick.
registration_help: Once again the help was good. I asked them if the courses I found were the correct ones, because it looked like it was the previous year. But they confirmed it was the correct courses I was picking from.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted but one, which was cancelled for some reason. That meant I had to pick another course and since I couldn't get any other courses from that block pre approved by UCPH, I had to pick a course that overlapped with another course.
registration_advice: Make sure to get your pre approval from UCPH in good time to be sure you can get a course from each block approved, to avoid overlapping.
course_level: The level varied quite a lot from course to course. Some were really easy, partly because I was a masters student and some parts of the courses were closely related to something I had learned earlier. Others were quite hard, especially because the exam is without any notes and has to be handwritten.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching almost felt closer to high school than university since a minimum attendance were required for each course to be approved for the continuous evaluation. However, it is possible to decide not to take part in the continuous evaluation and only be evaluated on your exam. I wouldn't recommend this, since I failed my first try at both exams where I hadn't been attending the course regularly.
courses_enrolled: Urban Economics Economics of Development Public Sector Economics - Spending Financial Accounting Applications of Marketing Research
recommended_courses: For academic reasons I would recommend Economics of Development, for a more chilled and easy (but still interesting) course I would recommend Urban Economics.
unexpected_costs: I wouldn't say I experienced any major unexpected costs
cost_comparison: Eating and drinking at bars and restaurants were cheaper relatively to grocery shopping compared to Denmark.
activities_available: There were some activities, but they weren't organised by the university but by some exchange student organizations like ESN or Happy Erasmus. I didn't really attend it though.
activities_recommended: Go out and eat some pintxos and drink a glass of txakoli at some of the local taberna, especially in Casco Viejo. Visit Guggenheim.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend going to watch a game at San Mames if you're interested in football. Also go out explore the nature and the other cities of the Basque Country and maybe even walk a couple days on the Camino. Busses to other cities like Santander or San Sebastian are fairly cheap.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy. Only thing was that they eat a lot later then in Denmark, so many restaurants aren't open until 20 or later. Also a lot of shops, including supermarkets, are closed on sundays. So you need to prepare for that.
socializing_tips: Not really.
cultural_challenges: Not really that much to be honest, the only thing would be that language barrier. But most of them spoke a little bit of English and I spoke some Spanish so it was not a problem.
culture_appreciated: I love that they use the city a lot. There are always people in the street and they love to go out for just a little bit of food or a glass of wine.
top3_advice: The choices of courses isn't the greatest if you are a masters student since a lot of them cant be approved by UCPH. Bilbao is a lovely and cheap city to live in. Go to the classes, or the exams will be very hard. You don't get access to previous exam sets and solutions.
other_useful_info: Not that I can think of.
most_rewarding: Just the experience of living abroad and getting to explore Bilbao and the rest of the Basque Country.
greatest_challenge: The exams for the courses that I hadn't been attending.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne til USA for at opleve kulturen derovre på en dagligdagsbasis. Konkret var mit største ønske at komme til Californien for at opleve kulturen her og se staten. Jeg valgte McGeorge pga. det havde fået gode anmeldelser førhen og lokationen var virkelig god til at opleve Californien.
overall_comments: Først og fremmest var mit ophold på McGeorge virkelig godt. Folk er søde og rare. Særligt Mary, Adriana og Clemence er helt fantastiske til at tage imod dig. Selvfølgelig er der altid plads til forbedring på stedet, men jeg oplevede så meget på min tur og lærte så meget om mig selv, at opholdet var næsten perfekt i mine øjne. Ift. McGeorge som skole er det en lille skole. Der er ca. 1000 elever vil jeg tro og campus er småt sammenlignet med andre campus. Under mit ophold var faciliteterne sgu ikke state of the art, men det fungerer. Ift. det sociale, så er det lidt som at komme ind i en lille familie. Men det vil kun føles som en lille familie, hvis du selv sørger for at opsøge venskaber, deltage i arrangementer og generelt ikke er bange for at tage en snak med hver og en du møder på din vej. Det er en oplagt mulighed for at komme ud af din komfort zone of være den mest ekstroverte version af dig selv. For giver du den en skalle med at være udadvendt og smilende skal du nok få godt med venner. Jeg havde succes med denne tilgang og endte med at få en masse amerikanske venner, men jeg havde også venner, der var internationale studerende, som var lidt for generte og ikke fik opbygget venskaber med amerikanere. For mit vedkommende vægtede jeg det højt at interagere med alle, men særligt prøve at opbygge venskaber med amerikanere, for at lære kulturen bedre at kende. I hele denne proces fandt jeg det vigtigt altid at have ja-hatten på, men det fandt jeg også rimelig nemt at have, da jeg ikke synes det var så slemt at følge med i løbet af semesteret. Jeg kom godt ud af starthullerne med at lave de opgaver jeg kunne så tidligt som muligt og så var mit valg af fag også helt perfekt ift. hvad det krævede af mig og hvornår undervisningen lå.
