crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte University of Toronto da jeg havde obligatoriske fag på KU, som blev udbudt lignende på UofT.
info_ease: Det var relativt nemt at finde fag osv inden ankomst, men man kan ikke nødvendigvis regne med at komme ind på fagene, man havde forestillet sig.
arrival_assistance: Ingen. Jeg søgte alle fag inden ankomst.
arrival_comments: Der var ingen orientation, men vi var heldigvis mange fra KU, som kunne hjælpe hinanden med fag og andre praktiske ting.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Man blev indstillet af KU og gennem deres portal udfyldte man det step for step, meget nemt og overskueligt.
registration_help: Man kunne kontakte exchange office på mail og telefon, de svarede hurtigt.
registration_success: Jeg fik 3/4 fag, når der ansøges på Google Forms så husk at skrive dine fag fra KU med, da jeg i første runde blev afvist, men fik fag i anden runde pga jeg skrev mine KU-fag på efterfølgende.
registration_advice: Søg mange fag og søg forhåndsgodkendelse hos KU så snart du kan.
course_level: Jeg havde to 3. års fag og to 4. års fag.
teaching_comparison: Jeg havde meget små hold og der var ingen forelæsninger men kun holdundervisning, så man er meget mere aktiv end på KU.
courses_enrolled: African Cultures and Development Global Environmental Politics Special Topics in European Affairs: European Union Topics in Comparative Politics I
recommended_courses: Ingen grund til at søge hårde og svære 4. års fag hvis man er bachelor på KU, arbejdsmængden er meget større og man får samme credit på KU uafhængigt af niveauet.
unexpected_costs: Inge umiddelbart, men det var dyrere end forventet generelt.
cost_comparison: Alt er meget dyrere i Toronto end i Danmark, men kan spise relativt billigt ude, men det løber op hvis man skal have alle måltider ude.
activities_available: Se en masse sport, det er gratis for studerende at se UofT's egne hold.
activities_recommended: Se sport, gratis for studerende.
weekend_recommendations: Rejs lidt rundt, der er Flixbus og billige flyafgange hele tiden.
culture_adjustment: Relativt nemt, folk er åbne og imødekommende, men det hjalp helt sikkert at have mange andre danske studerende også.
socializing_tips: Engager dig i klubberne og til sport, ellers mød folk i byen og til undervisning.
cultural_challenges: Der er meget mere diversitet blandt de studerende og mange studerende holder sig til deres egen kultur, hvilket er uvant for mig som dansk studerende. Meget opdelt efter kultur og etnicitet, svært at trænge igennem som udvekslingsstuderende.
culture_appreciated: Man mødte i undervisning enormt meget diversitet, som gav nogle gode indspark til undervisningen og det sociale.
top3_advice: 1) Søg forhåndsgodkendelse i god tid og søg til mange fag 2) Husk det sociale, undervisningen er ikke alt på udveksling 3) Sig ja til alt, tiden flyver afsted
other_useful_info: Insister på at komme ind på fag selvom der er venteliste, professoren kan prioritere dig over andre. Lav en Facebook-gruppe med alle danskere på fra UofT, York og TMU.
most_rewarding: At udvikle sig og møde mange nye mennesker.
greatest_challenge: At balancere studie og det sociale, man vil gerne opleve det hele, men uni fylder også meget selvom man er på udveksling.

crucial_aspects: Det virkede umuligt at vælge udveksling i Europa, idet udvalget af engelske fag var meget begrænset for mig. Jeg ville derfor gerne til et engelsk talende land. England var ikke en mulighed pga Brexit, jeg har boet i Oceanien og ville gerne prøve noget nyt, men ville ikke til USA. Dermed var Canada tilbage på listen over mulige destinationer.
overall_comments: Udvekslingsopholdet har været meget anderledes end forventet, men stadig godt. Jeg regnede fx med at møde mange andre udvekslingsstuderende som ikke var danskere, da det er det man hører meget om. Det var dog nær umuligt grundet ingen hjælp fra U of T. Jeg har dog fået andre gode relationer.
info_ease: Det var nemt at finde information om kurser og tilmeldning hos U of T. Vi fik dog ingen information fra U of T om social sammenvær, hvilket resulterede i at vi ofte først fandt ud af sociale arrangementer dagen efter de var sket eller efter endt tilmeldning. Det gjorde opstarten på opholdet meget hårdt.
arrival_assistance: Jeg modtog svar på emails om ting som forsøg på tilmeldning af volleyball hold, men ellers ingen hjælp.
arrival_comments: U of T skylder deres udvekslingsstuderende mere end aflyste arrangementer og halvhjertede begivenheder midt i semesteret hvor man har fået en hverdag op at køre.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Udvekslingsopholdet har været meget anderledes end forventet, men stadig godt. Jeg regnede fx med at møde mange andre udvekslingsstuderende som ikke var danskere, da det er det man hører meget om. Det var dog nær umuligt grundet ingen hjælp fra U of T. Jeg har dog fået andre gode relationer.
registration_process: I sin optagelsesmail modtager man link til et google sheet (det er sådan man tilmelder sig som udvekslingstuderende, andre er gældende for normale studerende). Man indsender derefter én besvarelse per fag man ønsker sammen med sine forudsætninger hvis sådanne er nødvendige. Man kan tilmelde sig op til 5 fag, som nemt kan droppes efterfølgende hvis man fx kun skal have 3 fag. Der er 3 af disse runder, hvor pladserne på fagene bliver fyldt op. Det er rart med 3 runder når man fx venter på lange svar tider fra KU. Derudover skal man også anskaffe sig et T-card. Jeg fik først registreret mig, da jeg var ankommet til Toronto. Det var dog ikke noget problem. Jeg fik blot mit studiekort én uge senere end de andre.
registration_help: Det har ikke været nødvendigt at få hjælp til tilmelding af fag. U of T afholdte et zoom møde ved ankomst (dog først efter 2. runde) hvor de gennemgik alle de tekniske ting i forbindelse med opstart på universitet.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag jeg ønskede.
registration_advice: Forhåndsgodkendelser fra KU langt fra ligeså nemt som det blev fremlagt af den ansvarshavende fra KU. Til trods for fuld valgfrihed på alle mine 30 ECTS opstod der stadig forvirring fra KU omkring omregning af ECTS var korrekt. Dette kom først efter det var for sent at rette mine fag på U of T. Det ordnede sig tilsidst, men var en stor stress faktor da det har afgørende betydning for hvorvidt man kan blive bachelor til rette tid. Man skal selvfølgelig ansøge og håbe på det bedste. Men vær forberedt på at det langt fra er en selvfølge at få godkendt fag til rette point og indhold fra KU.
academics_comments: Udvekslingsopholdet har været meget anderledes end forventet, men stadig godt. Jeg regnede fx med at møde mange andre udvekslingsstuderende som ikke var danskere, da det er det man hører meget om. Det var dog nær umuligt grundet ingen hjælp fra U of T. Jeg har dog fået andre gode relationer.
course_level: Jeg ville gerne prøve nogle helt andre discipliner så jeg tog to introduktionsfag i filosofi og ét introduktionsfag i genderstudiet, hvilket har været meget givende.
teaching_comparison: Alle mine fag har bestået af løbende evaluering i form af afleveringer og participation marks. Mine filosofi fag forgik i store forlæsningssale hvor professoren blot snakkede og ellers skrev på tavle. Mit genderstudies fag forgik med slides og multimedie indslag. I mit ene filosofi fag og i mit genderstudies fag havde vi også øvelsestimer hvor ens deltagelse indgik i den samlede karakter. Eksamen har karakter af udenadslære.
courses_enrolled: PHL232H1 Knowledge and Reality PHL244H1 Human Nature SDS255H1 Histories of Sexuality
recommended_courses: Jeg vil klart anbefale PHL232H1 Knowledge and Reality til alle, især science studerende. Faget giver et indgående indblik i hvordan vi forstår den verden vi lever i, samt hvordan vi anerkender viden hos os selv og hinanden. Mange science (og filosofi) studerende tager det på U of T. Derudover er faget et introduktionsfag så man behøver ingen forudsætninger på forhånd.
unexpected_costs: Det har generelt været overdrevet dyrt at bo og leve i Canada. Både mad i supermarkeder og på restauranter er dyrt.
cost_comparison: Mad i supermarket har været overraskende dyrt.
activities_available: Sportshold, flere fitness faciliteter, klatre klub, Outdoor klub, faglige klubber. Men som sagt krævede det mere energi at opsøge det sociale og klubber end opstart af det faglige.
activities_recommended: Jeg meldte mig ind i Outdoor klubben (25$ medlemskab) og vil klart anbefale! Jeg har været med på hytte tur og de skriver nyhedsbrev hver måned med aktiviteter. Derudover er der mange gratis drop in fitness classes så som zumba, aquafit, volleyball etc. Det er godt at have nogen man mødes fast med. Det kan fx være til strikkeklub, Aquavit eller lignende, så man også får pause fra læsning i hverdagen.
weekend_recommendations: Tag ud af byen og se den smukke natur! Vi var 6 udvekslingstuderende på en uges roadtrip i Nova Scotia. Det var billigt og har virkelig flot natur. Muskoka, Algonquin park, Blue Mountains er lidt tættere på byen. Tag ud på Toronto Island mens været er godt. Tag ind og se U of T sport! Det er gratis og en hyggelig aktivitet. Generelt være opsøgende i alt det U of T tilbyder. Tag til Montreal og Quebec. Tag op i CN tower når været er godt, det er mange penge men det værd. Sjovt at gøre når man kender byen.
culture_adjustment: Nemt
socializing_tips: Min oplevelse var at mange lokale studerende kun er på U of T for at læse og derfor ikke har venner på universitetet. Jeg vil dog klart anbefale at aktivt tage kontakt til nogen til de første forlæsninger. De kender højst sandsynligvis heller ikke andre og bliver ligeså glade for at få et velkendt ansigt til forelæsninger. Man er ikke enrolled på et studie på samme måde som i DK og de studerende er derfor meget mere "alene" i deres studie. Det har været rigtig rart at kende nogle fra sine fag også selvom det mest bare har været snak før og efter forelæsninger.
cultural_challenges: Mit studie derhjemme består også af meget løbende evaluering, så det har ikke været den store udfordring for mig. Men man skal vende sig til at få mark for participation som man gjorde i gymnasiet.
culture_appreciated: De mange officielle sports begivenheder har været afgørende for at få et tilknytningsforhold til universitet. Derudover er der rigtig mange med forskellige kulturer på U of T så der er rig mulighed for at lære om forskellige baggrunde.
top3_advice: Tag et SU lån Prioriter at komme ud af byen og se natur (Det faglige optager alt den tid du tillader) Prøv at lade vær med at stresse over at udveksling skal være det bedste halve år i dit liv (Det bliver bedre nu mere du slapper af) og det kommer helt sikkert til at blive godt også selvom du ikke var i byen 3 gange om ugen.
other_useful_info: Gode cafeer at læse på: Balzac ved St. Lawrence, Carbonic coffee, Coffee Island.
most_rewarding: Klart det faglige jeg har fået med ved at prøve nogle helt andre discipliner. Prøve at bo midt i en storby som Toronto.
greatest_challenge: Opsøge det sociale og få godkendt ting af KU.
other_comments: På trods af udfordringer vil jeg klart anbefale at tage afsted! Det har været det hele værd.

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte et land jeg aldrig har været før, samt så langt væk som muligt for at udfordre mig selv og se en anden kultur. Canada har altid været på min Bucket list, så det var oplagt at kombinere studie med rejse.
overall_comments: Generelt har det været en hel fantastisk oplevelse, mødt en masse nye mennesker, samt skabt connections med danskerne hjemmefra KU. Udover nogle udfordringer med forhåndsgodkendelse og bolig herover, har det været en oplevelse jeg ikke ville være foruden.
info_ease: Jeg synes det var svært og det var vi alle enige om som var afsted. Hvor man skulle tilmelde sig kurser, lokaler og generelt info om hvad der skulle til at ske. Orientering blev vi aldrig en del af da vi ikke vidste hvor vi skulle finde informationer om det, men da vi kun var der i 4 måneder var det ikke noget vi mærkede til manglede.
arrival_assistance: Vi fik nogle "abroad" mails om ting der skete på campus, men brugte vi ikke så meget. Udover det var det muligt at få møder med fakulteterne om evn spørgsmål om studiet og tilmelding af fag.
arrival_comments: Vi fik ingen info om orientering, og fik af vide man skulle finde det selv enten på UofT eller facebookgrupper hvor ting blev slået op.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Generelt har det været en hel fantastisk oplevelse, mødt en masse nye mennesker, samt skabt connections med danskerne hjemmefra KU. Udover nogle udfordringer med forhåndsgodkendelse og bolig herover, har det været en oplevelse jeg ikke ville være foruden.
registration_process: Jeg benyttede websiden ACORN som er den webside hvor min fakultet skulle tilmelde sig fag og betale for health insuance. Det fungerede super fint og meget enkelt at til/framelde sig fag.
registration_help: Jeg mener der var en information/question side hvor man kunne søge hjælp. Min fakultet var meget søde til at mødes med mig og forklare om fagene og hvordan ventelister fungerede.
registration_success: Det gik lige som jeg ville have det. Fagene der blev tilbudt fall 2022 var ikke lige dem jeg havde tænkt, men udover det fik jeg de fag jeg ville.
registration_advice: Undersøg hvilke dag der kan blive tilbudt hver sæson og vær' ud i god tid når man skal tilmelde sig - hvis der er specifikke kurser man særligt ønsker sig. Er man i tvivl er det en mega god ide at tilmelde sig flere fag og afprøve dem i den første uge af studie, høre om strukturen, se professoren og om indholdet er dig. Man kan afmelde sig helt frem til nov, mener jeg, men sidste tilmelding er et par uger efter start.
academics_comments: Generelt har det været en hel fantastisk oplevelse, mødt en masse nye mennesker, samt skabt connections med danskerne hjemmefra KU. Udover nogle udfordringer med forhåndsgodkendelse og bolig herover, har det været en oplevelse jeg ikke ville være foruden.
course_level: Niveauet var meget passende synes jeg. Til at følge med i, men med plads til at have nogle sygedage eller bare slappe. Mine fag lå kun på 3 ud af 5 hverdage så de andre dage kunne jeg udforske byen eller læse op. Meget passende level lift bachelorfag.
teaching_comparison: Holdene herover kan spænde fra 20 studerende til 200, hvilket ændre pettingen lidt ift at interagere med underviseren. Udover det var det meget ligende KU med forelæsninger og evt tutorials.
courses_enrolled: KPE329 - Developing Physical Literacy Foundations in the Early Years KPE 328 - Exercise and Nutrition for Health and Performance KPE368 - Sport Concussion
recommended_courses: KPE329 var mega fedt hvis du er interesseret i undervisning og børn. Så hyggeligt at se de små udvikle sig og lave noget fysisk når man læser idræt. Det fag har dog ikke "deltagelse" karakter, dvs man ikke bliver bedømt på hvordan man underviste eller kom til timerne, hvilket jeg synes var underligt.
unexpected_costs: Da vi blev scammet ved vores Airbnb og skulle betale lidt mere om måneden for bolig da vi stod uden. Udover det så var mad bare generelt dyrt. Taxes skal man være opmærksom på ikke står inkluderet i prisen, samt drikkepenge som er en stor ting herover, også selvom det er en kaffe på en café. Altid rund op ift hvad du tror du skal betale, så er du på den sikre side.
cost_comparison: Kaffe er billigere de rigtige steder, hvilket var rart så man kunne komme ud af lejligheden når man skulle læse og ikke bruge kassen hver gang. 14-15 kr for en normal filterkaffe.
activities_available: Abroad sendte mails ud om evn aktiviteter man kunne deltage i, fx udskæring af græskar eller football på storskærm.
activities_recommended: AGO har fri adgang for studerende i et helt år, hvilket var hyggeligt på en regnvejrsdag. Vi lavede derudover også en strikkeklub, hvor vi mødtes og drak kaffe.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på ture. Tag til Montreal, Quebec som er en mega hyggelig fransk del af Canada. Oplev Toronto Island når det er godt vejr, hvor man kan tage på stranden, stå på paddelboard eller bare gå en tur rundt om. CN-tower er et must, selvom det er lidt turistet, men når man bor der i 4 måneder bliver man nødt til det. Planlæg på en skyfri dag i løbet af ugedagene eller til solnedgang - mega flot.
culture_adjustment: Efter 2 uger havde man styr på hvor man havde kurser og hvor ting lå. Det kan betale sig at tage nogle dage hvor man bare går rundt og kigger. Toronto er stort i starten, men bliver genkendeligt når man har været der i nogle uger.
socializing_tips: Selvom det kan være nervepirrende så bare sæt sig vedsiden af en til timerne og sig "Hej". Mange kender ikke alle på kurserne og vil derfor ikke vide at du ikke er derfra. Mange på UofT er fra andre lande eller universiteter så man møder mange andre udveksling. Deltag i klubber er også en god ide, eller bo på kollegier giver jo også god mening hvis det er muligt.
cultural_challenges: Når de starter på Uni herover er det lige efter High School, så de er meget unge ift hvad man er vant til derhjemme fra. Det kan derfor være svært men også sjovt at snakke og udveksle erfaringer. Mange herover skal bruge høje karakter til at komme videre, hvor vi blot får overført bestået eller ik-bestået, så tiden man bruger på studiet er meget forskelligt.
culture_appreciated: De er meget åbne når man først kommer i snak med dem og vil meget gerne høre om ens liv og hvad man har oplevet. Meget hjælpsomme.
top3_advice: Vær forberedt på at undersøge ting på egen hånd. Der er facebookgrupper og hjemmesider man kan finde info og invitationer til ting, men dem skal man selv finde. Tag dig tid til at tage på tur, enten med fly eller leje en bil og kør nord-på. Man er der kun i kort tid så benyt lejligheden på at få set og oplevet så meget som muligt. Afprøv alle deres faciliteter, fitness, svømmehal, drop-in sport og hold - du kan blive overrasket og møde nye mennesker.
other_useful_info: Få styr på din forhåndsgodkendelse i god tid!. Ventetiden på svar er +6 uger, hvilket gør det meget vanskeligt for os studerende der er 6 timer bagud i tid og kun er afsted i 3-4 måneder. Undersøg hvor mange kurser du skal have, om de vil godkende kurserne og få sendt den hurtigt afsted. Generelt forvent lang responstid fra KU. Søg SU-lån hvis ikke du får legater. Det har givet så meget frihed ikke at skulle tænke på at spare op eller leve på havregryn. Du er jo kun afsted i kort tid og det er det hele værd.
most_rewarding: Personlig udvikling. Igennem dette ophold har vi oplevet mange uforudsigelige ting fra scam til Subway breakdown inden eksamen, så man er blevet meget god til at fikse og finde en løsning på ting. Hvile i sig selv og det at få en hverdag op og køre herover.
greatest_challenge: At få fat i KU var utroligt vanskeligt og tog meget energi og tid. Finder det underligt der ikke er en form for særlig undtagelse for studerende der på udvekling langt væk, da det allerede er svær at falde til og få styr på uni-hverdagen.
other_comments: Tag til Toronto hvis du er til bylivet med fuld fart på, er klar på udfordringer og være selvstændig. Lav en gruppe med de andre danskere der skal derover, de bliver nogle skide gode venner og støtte gemmen denne fantastiske men også underlige oplevelse. Det er jo dem du kommer til at se derhjemme.

crucial_aspects: I really wanted a University that was strong in my field of study (Biology and Pharmacology)
overall_comments: Very much as inspected and one of the best 4 months of my life! I cannot recommend this enough. A semester at any foreign university would be exciting but I have been really happy with my 4 months at UofT.
info_ease: Fairly easy if you could find it on your own, but if not you needed help it wasnt easy to get.
arrival_assistance: None
arrival_comments: No assistance was issued to exchange students upon arrival.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Very much as inspected and one of the best 4 months of my life! I cannot recommend this enough. A semester at any foreign university would be exciting but I have been really happy with my 4 months at UofT.
registration_process: You get a T-card (studiekort) once you arrive on campus and this is one you need to identify yourself when taking exams. There wasnt any other kind of registration other than registrering for courses on their university portal.
registration_help: None
registration_success: With a bit of persistence I got the ones that I wanted - even if they say that you dont have the prerequisites for a course, you can more often than not convince them that you do by showing them transcripts froom your courses at UCPH.
registration_advice: They are very strict on the registration deadlines so be aware of those!
academics_comments: Very much as inspected and one of the best 4 months of my life! I cannot recommend this enough. A semester at any foreign university would be exciting but I have been really happy with my 4 months at UofT.
course_level: Course are in either on these levels: 100: 1st year 200: 2nd year. 300: 3rd year 400: 4th year. As a bachelor you can take courses from either category.
teaching_comparison: More lectures but less reading than UCPH.
courses_enrolled: CSC108: Introduction to Computer Programming PCL200: Drugs and the Brain HMB300: Neurobiology of behaviour PCL475: Neuropsychopharmacology
recommended_courses: Both of these were very interesting and had very competente professors being the best in their field: HMB300: Neurobiology of behaviour PCL475: Neuropsychopharmacology
unexpected_costs: Winter clothing - and the metro and food being more expensive than I had anticipated
cost_comparison: Everything is more expensive than in Denmark!
activities_available: Everything you can imagine
activities_recommended: I enjoyed the rural running club!
weekend_recommendations: Weekend trip to Montreal and a walk through the Distillery District in Toronto
culture_adjustment: Easy - much like europe
socializing_tips: Just talk with the ones you are sitting with at lectures! People are usually very nice.
cultural_challenges: not really
culture_appreciated: Canadians are very nice!
top3_advice: 1) Remember to use the city as you are living in a real city and things happen all the time around you. Just taking a stroll in the different neighborhoods of Toronto (or down by the water) is amazing through the different seasons. Also, try attending a fratparty - that is part of the culture. 2) Dont bring a lot of clothes! The rumor is really true - your wardrobe triples when being on exchange! Especially because UofT has a sick merchstore where you can buy everything imagineable. 3) Get a ESTA so you can go on a weekend trip to New York! It is very close by and quite cheap as well.
other_useful_info: Have fun, remember to socialize with fellow students and be conscious of the different papers needing to get into the country. You need a visa and maybe a study permit as well as being able to prove vaccination.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people and have lectures with some of the wisest people in my field of research.
greatest_challenge: The cold!! - even though it has been unusually nice weather, it really gets cold during the winter in Canada! But the winter is beautiful as well - just remember a sweater.

crucial_aspects: A highly esteemed university with courses that are relevant to my education. A destination with an interesting culture. An English-speaking country
info_ease: Quite easy. I was a bit confused though, because I thought there were many different channels where information was given, eg. KUmail, Quercus, UofT mail, etc. and you had to check them all to make sure you didn't miss anything.
arrival_assistance: None.
arrival_comments: There was only an online orientation. It would have been nice with a physical one.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You can begin checking out courses early, but be aware that they may change from year to year. Mine were pretty much the same as last year though. Then when the final course list is pusblished, you sign up for a lecture period and possibly a lab class, depending on the course. You are responsible for ensuring your courses don't overlap.
registration_help: I believe there was an e-mail you could contact, though I didn't need any help.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: You should sign up early to avoid getting waitlisted. You can sign up for 1 or 2 more courses than you want, either as back-up or if you want to check them out before deciding, because the deadline for dropping a courses is after the first week of classes,
course_level: Around the same level of difficulty.
teaching_comparison: Lectures were kind of the same, but there were a lot more assignments and tests. The grade for each course is split over multiple assignments, mid-term exams and a final exam or assignment. My exams were all written in hand, with a lot of memorization required.
courses_enrolled: GGR334H1: Water Resource Management, GGR347H1: Efficient Use of Energy, GGR375H1: Introduction to Programming in GIS, GGR415H1: Advanced Remote Sensing
recommended_courses: All my courses were pretty great, but especially GGR334H1 and GGR347H1 (though there was a lot of memorization for the tests)
unexpected_costs: Taxes on food.
cost_comparison: Groceries were more expensive than in DK. Clothes and other stuff were a bit less expensive.
activities_available: Clubs (creative, sport clubs, language and culture clubs), fitness classes, gyms, pool, skating rink.
activities_recommended: The fitness classes, especially barre. The outdoor club goes on trips about every other weekend and has some other activities that were very nice.
weekend_recommendations: Algonquin National Park - rent a car and stay at Wolfden Hostel, one of the nicest and coziest hostels I've ever stayed at. Fly to Nova Scotia - has beautiful, rugged nature. Take the train to Montreal.
culture_adjustment: They were more outgoing and extrovert than in Denmark. It took some getting used to, but was actually quite nice. Most Canadians are quite friendly.
socializing_tips: Join some clubs. It is quite difficult making friends in class, especially if you are taking higher-level courses, since most other students already have a social circle by then.
cultural_challenges: Not really anything.
culture_appreciated: Their friendliness. That the city was very multicultural with lots of different things to do including foods to try.
top3_advice: Look for housing early, there are a couple of off-campus colleges you can apply to. Join some of the clubs early on. Attend all lectures and take good notes.
other_useful_info: Grocieries are expensive, but you can get vegetables and fruits for cheap in some of the Asian supermarkets. Bulk Barn is another great shop to check out.
most_rewarding: Improving my English, adapting to another culture, great courses.
greatest_challenge: Finding housing.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to try experiencing what it's like to live in a really big city - and preferably in an English-speaking location. I visited Toronto once and thought it seemed like a really cool place. The university also has a great reputation and they offered some really cool courses within my field.
overall_comments: It was a great experience, and I would highly recommend going on exchange in Toronto!
info_ease: It was easy to find information regarding academics and we were sent a few emails explaining everything we needed to do. There was no planned orientation for exchange students (besides an informational zoom session) and we were not informed about any regular orientation events at the university which was a bit disappointing.
arrival_assistance: None.
arrival_comments: I think they could arrange more social/orientation events for exchange students - it was difficult to meet other exchange students if you did not live in a student residence.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It was a great experience, and I would highly recommend going on exchange in Toronto!
registration_process: You just had to fill out a Google Form for each course you wanted to register for. Be sure to write the names of your courses in the course prerequisites field in the form. Although they receive a description of all of the courses you have previously taken, it's as if they forget this document exists once you have to apply. I was denied a course because I did not fill it out (because I assumed they had a list of my old courses) - when I applied a second time and filled it out they approved me on the course.
registration_help: You could email the inbound exchange office.
registration_success: I got all of the classes I applied for - but I was on a waitlist for one of them until 2 days before classes started.
registration_advice: Get pre-approval of your courses as early as possible, and get it for many courses so you have the option to switch around if you end up not liking it. If you are on the waitlist you will most likely still get into the class - a lot of students "shop around" and try out a bunch of courses at the start, and then drop out of them.
academics_comments: It was a great experience, and I would highly recommend going on exchange in Toronto!
course_level: I originally applied to be enrolled in the Graduate School, but for my specific area they did not take exchange students, so I ended up being enrolled as an Undergraduate. I took 3rd and 4th year (level 300 and 400) courses and it was pretty similar in level to UCPH - maybe a bit lower level (but I think this depends on the course).
teaching_comparison: At the University of Toronto your final grade depends on many aspects (and not just the final exam). This includes getting graded for presentations, midterms, assignments/essays, and your final exam. This means that there is a bigger workload (because you have more deadlines than at UCPH), but I would say it takes some of the stress away from the exam period. The style of teaching is pretty similar to the one at UCPH. My classes only had lectures (no tutorials/practical classes).
courses_enrolled: HMB300 - Neurobiology of Behaviour HMB303 - Global Health and Human Rights PCL482 - Biomedical Toxicology
recommended_courses: HMB303 - Global Health and Human Rights was a course that was super interesting! It covered a lot of aspects of Global Health and Politics. It was really cool to get a different perspective on science and health care. It is definitely very different from all the other courses I have had during university, but it taught me a lot. The workload is quite intense (you have to submit 7 essays during the semester, and do a presentation - but no exam), but I would still recommend it. The teacher was really excellent and we had some great discussions. I would also recommend the other 2, but they did not really stand out to me specifically.
unexpected_costs: Rent was very expensive (but this was expected). Everything in Toronto is expensive, especially groceries!
cost_comparison: Drinks out could sometimes be cheaper than in DK. Everywhere you would have to add taxes and tips on top of the price, so most things ended up being similar to Danish prices or more expensive. Fast food is less expensive than in DK.
activities_available: Clubs of any kind, tons of sports (free gym and workout classes).
activities_recommended: Join the Outdoor Club! They arrange fun events where you get to see some nature close to the city. Many exchange students also join the outdoor club, so it is a good opportunity to meet other exchange students. I also very much utilised the free gym, pool, and workout classes.
weekend_recommendations: Travel around! I went to Montreal, Nova Scotia, and New York - but there are many other cool places to go (Vancouver, Miami, Cuba, Chicago, Algonquin National Park). It's nice to get out of the city every now and then and people are often down to join! Otherwise I definitely recommend going to see a sport event (at the University it's free, but it's also a great experience to see a real NHL match!). Kensington Market is a great area, and Toronto has thousands of cute coffee shops. Go to the bar "2 Cats" on Thursdays - they have a great happy hour deal, and you might run into Shawn Mendes ;)
culture_adjustment: I think it was quite easy - Canada is pretty similar to Denmark.
socializing_tips: It was a bit difficult to socialise with the local students - they are often quite young, and since UofT is quite academically rigororous a lot of them seem to not be super interested in socializing/meeting new people. But I would recommend just speaking to whoever you sit next to in class - due to the way their teaching is structured they most likely also do not know anyone in their class, and it is nice to have a friendly face you can chat with before class starts.
cultural_challenges: I can't really think of any.
culture_appreciated: Toronto is very diverse which was cool to experience!
top3_advice: I think it is important to take it slow and not put too much pressure on yourself to make your exchange "the best time of your life". Figure out what you enjoy to do and there is no need to feel like you have to be doing something cool or go out at all times - the experience of moving somewhere completely new and having to adapt to a new life is a great experience in itself. Try to not focus that much on school (it can be easy to be stressed out because it is quite an academically intense environment at UofT) - but you will definitely pass your classes! Prioritise going on trips and meeting new people! Bring a winter jacket and buy Uniqlo Heattech ;) - it will get cold.
other_useful_info: Phone plans are ridiculously expensive in Canada. I recommend using CBB World (but you need to get a SIM-card and activate it while you're still in DK). Apply for scholarships or take an SU loan - Toronto is expensive and you might as well get the best out of it while you're there instead of stressing out about money.
most_rewarding: Meeting all the lovely people from all around the world (and also meeting all the other Danes). It was nice to focus on socialising and experiencing the neighbourhood, instead of worrying about grades or work and other responsibilities at home in DK.
greatest_challenge: Being on your own in a foreign country - it is a challenge, but it is very empowering!
other_comments: No :)

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go somewhere outside Europe to an English-speaking country. Also, Toronto being a big city and UofT being a good university had a big impact on my decision.
overall_comments: The only downside to choosing Toronto is that it's an expensive city to live in. But with a little bit of savings four months is completely fine.
info_ease: It was very easy for the most part. As long as you check your email and make the necessary 'university-profiles' you will be fine. Also, join the Facebook group created from UofT as soon as it's available for you - they also provide some information regarding the arrival here. If there's something you're uncertain about it also helps to ask other students from UCPH going to your university.
arrival_assistance: Not very much (some emails) - most of the information we got before arriving.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: The only downside to choosing Toronto is that it's an expensive city to live in. But with a little bit of savings four months is completely fine.
registration_process: It was very easy. We looked at the different courses in the course catalogue and then we had to fill out a Google Forms. Also, I think we chose courses before "their own students" so you have a good chance of getting the courses that you want - and they have multiple rounds where you can apply and drop courses.
registration_help: You could write and email to the registration office. They were very helpful and responded fast.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted. (If this is relevant for you: At first I was told we weren't able to take laboratory courses, but then I wrote an email to the registration office and was allowed on the course anyway)
registration_advice: Check the course catalogue before registration opens so that you know kinda which courses you would like to take (they have a lot to choose from).
academics_comments: The only downside to choosing Toronto is that it's an expensive city to live in. But with a little bit of savings four months is completely fine.
course_level: The academic levels wasn't very different from classes at UCPH but their courses are build around a very different structure than at home.
teaching_comparison: Their grade from the courses is not just based on one final exam (as we know it from Copenhagen) but it consists of various assignments, midterms, participation and quizzes in addition to the final exam (different from every course how many of these the grade is based on) so you have a little more work to do during the semester but each part is "less important" compared to the single exam we have at home. Also, most midterms and final exams are multiple choice!
courses_enrolled: CSC108: Introduction to Computer Programming HMB300: Neurobiology of Behaviour HMB310: Laboratory in Neuroscience PCL475: Neuropsychopharmacology 1
recommended_courses: Introduction to Computer Programming: Gives a good introduction to programming in Python. Workload: Weekly quizzes and three assignments in addition to a midterm and a final exam. Neurobiology of Behaviour: Probably the "easiest" course regarding the workload. Gave a very interesting view into different neurological and psychological diseases/disorders. Workload: Weekly quizzes (however with unlimited tries) and two assignments in addition to a midterm and a final exam (however both of these two were online). HMB310: Laboratory in Neuroscience: Very nice course with a smaller class size - and a nice break from "normal" classes with being in the lab (we had both wet lab and dry lab experiments). However, a bigger workload: Four assignments (however could drop one of them), quizzes weekly/every other week and one in-class presentation. However, no midterm and the final exam was a presentation of our project we worked on in the lab (was before the actual 'exam period' which was nice!). PCL475: Neuropsychopharmacology 1: Gave an introduction to different brain diseases and how we treat them - also with a more psychological aspect. You could feel that it was a pharmacology course given that they talked a lot about different drugs (both medications and 'abuse' drugs) and how we use/used them. However very little workload with only one assignment and one midterm and final exam. Interesting to see diseases from another aspect compared to what we usually learn about in our degree at home and learn more about the different drugs we use to treat these diseases.
unexpected_costs: Because Canada usually is not included in different packages for insurance and phone services it can get a little bit more expensive. I can recommend getting a travel insurance through IDA and phone service from CBB - however, these might be a problem if you're away for more than four months. Another unexpected cost was that we had to pay to get our transcript (which is required to get your courses transferred to your degree at UCPH) - however it's not that expensive.
cost_comparison: Groceries (and alcohol) and public transportation was way more expensive than I imagined. However, most things cost approximately the same as in Copenhagen. Take away and coffee (Tim Hortons!!) can be way cheaper than at home.
activities_available: The gym was free for all students and they offered a lot of different workout classes which was very nice! They also had different cultural clubs you could join and offered different social activities for students.
activities_recommended: Participate in the introduction events hosted by the university as this will be a good chance to meet other exchange students. Also, going to different workout classes and events at Hart House. And frat parties!
weekend_recommendations: There are a lot of different things to do in and around Toronto. Here are some daytrips you can take: Visit Niagara Falls or rent a car (very nice if one in your group is 25 or older - then it's way cheaper!) and go to a lake or park around Toronto - for instance Algonquin National Park is very nice especially in fall with the different coloured leaves!! You can also rent a cabin or an AirBnb and stay for the weekend. In Toronto I would really recommend Toronto Islands (!!!) especially going there to see the sunset. Also, Distillery District (especially for their Christmas market!), Eaton centre, walk along the habour front, and just in general walk around in the very nice city. Also, for going out: Definitely check out 'Pizza, Wine, Disco'! Also, going to other places in Canada. I went with friends to Montreal and Vancouver - and especially Vancouver was really amazing!
culture_adjustment: Very easy - not very different from Copenhagen/Denmark. However, the students at the university is a little younger and at little less social than we're used to from home.
socializing_tips: Talk to them in the lectures and say that you're an exchange student - they don't really have that very much so many people will be interested to hear about your experiences in Toronto and where you're from. Or go to frat parties.
cultural_challenges: They are less social/used to going out than we're used to - most bars/discos close at 2/3 and are kinda empty around 1.
culture_appreciated: The culture is not that different from at home but being in a bigger city is very nice.
top3_advice: Participate in all the events/parties you're offered in the beginning so that you already make some friends from start and try to get a room in at student residence/live with other students! Also, know that it will take a little time to fully adjust and being away from home will be difficult - but it will be harder to say goodbye at the end :))
other_useful_info: In the beginning we were "offered" to buy tickets to welcome parties. However, most of these were very expensive and were either rescheduled or cancelled without us getting our money back. So I don't know if I would recommend buying these tickets. Most clubs/bars are free (at least for girls - and also guys for the most part as long as you get a free ticket and go there before midnight) - @uoftparties provides link/tickets to the free clubs/bars every week and is a great place to start).
most_rewarding: Making friends from all over the world and just being 'on your own' in another country without having any responsibilities other than taking care of yourself. Also, it was very nice that we just need to pass our courses and not depend on getting good grades (as most people do at home) - I know some of my friends from other countries felt like they spend too much time studying instead of exploring the city because they needed the grades (UofT is a hard university when you need to get good grades!).
greatest_challenge: Adjusting to the life at start - but it will not take long :))
other_comments: Go, go, go!! It's the most amazing experience and something you will always remember - with great friends and a lot of fantastic memories!

crucial_aspects: English as the first language, multiculturality, bigger city. On top of that, wanted to understand what American/Canadian culture is about.
overall_comments: The university is great but the workload is way higher than at KU, students have to memorize quite a lot for exams and 90% of them are handwritten. The university has a lot to offer ranging from different clubs to the coolest sports center I've ever seen. This exchange could really be anything from a 1 to a 10, it all depends on how much effort you put in to socialize, as the university doesn't really arrange many events for you. The city has a lot of great food and cultural activities! In addition, it's really affordable to visit other cities in Canada
info_ease: Fairly easy it's mostly on the website + the emails sent out are by UoT are rather informative, however, a lot of back-and-forths information emails with the inbound exchange office as the university is insanely strict about which courses you can take; course prerequisites are not flexible and if there is no overlap with their descriptions you can end up with no courses at all. In my case, it was fairly hard as I'm studying Social Data Science which is a new degree.
arrival_assistance: When the university is starting, there wasn't much information presented yet most of it could be found on the website. My advice is to get really familiar with the study portal. The university could have done a better job by creating guides for incoming exchange students, it took me a lot of time to find info on the website. Once again it stems down to how motivated you are to find the info.
arrival_comments: Not many orientation events, most of them were booked out once I opened the emails. In my opinion, this shouldn't be the case, it doesn't make an inbound orientation activity limited in space. Your social life mostly depends on various events organized by other exchange students. Once again it is all in your hands, hence emphasizing that the experience of going to this exchange can vary a lot.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

The university has a lot to offer ranging from different clubs to the coolest sports center I've ever seen. This exchange could really be anything from a 1 to a 10, it all depends on how much effort you put in to socialize, as the university doesn't really arrange many events for you. The city has a lot of great food and cultural activities! In addition, it's really affordable to visit other cities in Canada
registration_process: The system is rather outdated and takes a lot of time, they were using google forms instead of the normal registration process for exchange students, I submitted several of these forms and got into some courses in the last round
registration_help: You could write an email from Europe. Once you are there; you could call or book the inbound exchange office through zoom.
registration_success: Completely unsuccessful and did not get (almost) any classes I wanted to take, there is no flexibility!
registration_advice: Make your research about prerequisites and stick to them. The university is run by bureaucrats so they don't understand that people in Europe have a hard time getting exactly the same courses they have in prerequisites.
academics_comments: The university is great but the workload is way higher than at KU, students have to memorize quite a lot for exams and 90% of them are handwritten. The university has a lot to offer ranging from different clubs to the coolest sports center I've ever seen. This exchange could really be anything from a 1 to a 10, it all depends on how much effort you put in to socialize, as the university doesn't really arrange many events for you. The city has a lot of great food and cultural activities! In addition, it's really affordable to visit other cities in Canada
course_level: As described above, the courses are tough yet rewarding, especially computer science.
teaching_comparison: The style is different, there are weekly assignments for most subjects, a mid-term exam, and a final exam. Some courses are taught in smaller classes. In contrast, the computer science course I took is taught in a large auditorium.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Databases Special Topics in Economics with Data Analytics Special Topics in Economics
recommended_courses: Introduction to Databases; Although it's the hardest course, you are learning a lot. It's the most useful course out of the three I took as it teaches how to design a database and use SQL. On top of that, the lectures are entertaining.
unexpected_costs: CN tower was quite expensive, but if you go during sunset it's worth it!
cost_comparison: Eating out is less expensive, and mobile providers are more expensive. Public transport can be fairly cheap using city bikes.
activities_available: Free gym center with a swimming pool. Free university sports events (as a spectator). Social activities by clubs, there is a club for everyone!
activities_recommended: different clubs, everyone is into something else. I would recommend attending the club fair in the beginning of the semester.
weekend_recommendations: CN tower, Toronto Islands, Niagara falls, NYC, Washington or any other cities in the US
culture_adjustment: fairly easy, it's very similar to Europe (and so is the metric system). Though there were a few cultural shocks (such as raccoons on the streets)
socializing_tips: Go to bars, and university events. Just go out and talk to people. Canadians are one of the friendliest people!
cultural_challenges: wild animals in the streets
culture_appreciated: friendliness and genuine interest of Canadians
top3_advice: 1. Be ready to socialize and seek those events 2. Make your weekly assignments, they can save your grade 3. Travel in your free time, really recommend NYC and Washington it's fairly closeby
other_useful_info: nothing on top of my mind
most_rewarding: traveling, meeting new people, studying
greatest_challenge: course selection, that period was insanely stressful, they should really be more transparent with their processes.

crucial_aspects: Big english speaking city that i didn't know
overall_comments: Well, every experience abroad is also contingent on the specifics of the person abroad's life and i think my experiences on the trip abroad was fine, but i was unlucky and didn't meet anyone i wanted to spend a lot of time with during the trip. This is a big part of what is bringing the score down. Another aspect bringing the score down is how bad the courses were and the general very low academic level the university operates on. While Toronto ranks very high in the world rankings, i found it quite unacademic. The culture around education is very different abroad compared to Denmark, i had the same experience when studying at Sorbonne in Paris previously. My beef is that they do not foster autonomous or critical thinking at U of T, which i think is the main goal of Danish education, at least at HUM and SAMF (less so, but still). I really do not think that the courses i followed in Toronto live up to what I think makes an endeavour academic, which to me is sober investigation of an object(s) of interest supported by a multitude of different perspectives, methodologies and theoretical backgrounds engaged on a highly detailed level through primary texts. I.E. it needs to be 1. sober (nøgternt), 2. present multiple perspectives on the same object of interest and 3. be detailed and served through primary texts. While it might be difficult to "prove" that a course does not live up to 1 and 2, it's very easy to prove that it does not live up to 3, which none of my courses except "moral thought and behaviour" did. In my course "Introduction to sociology", a first year course we had no curriculum, the only thing that was expected of us between lectures was to watch a youtube playlist comprised of pop-cultural/scientific clips such as sketches from the talk show "last week tonight with John Oliver" or ted-talks. this course does obviously not live up to point 3. (i know I've created these criteria, but I would be surprised if anyone disagreed with them, except for them not being exhaustive), and it did also not really live up to criterias 1 & 2. Due to the lack of curricula and primary texts, every lecture felt like being taken along the professors train of thought, which was interesting, but in my eyes highly unacademic. There were few references to theories and if there was it was a reference to general theories (Weber's theory of Bureaucracy) and not a specific text. It all seemed as academic as a google search or a wikipedia page. The assessments were multiple choice questions about lecture content as we did not have any curricula. This results in the assessments being unacademic as they test us in content that didnt live up to the craft of academia. I remember a question from the final being "Is professor McIvor a part of the proletariat?" McIvor being our professor, and several questions about game of thrones in relation to some quasi-presentation of a sociological theory. One refutation of my critique could be that this is normal for a first year course in north america, to which i would point out that this is exactly the problem. Cause in DK we dont have levels of difficulty throughout the bachelor, we have different content, but all courses including first year are academically sound and serious. My view is that courses like this should not be possible to follow as substitutions for courses at KU, it's simply not academically a high enough level. In another course "Introduction to developmental Psychology," a second year course, we did have a curricula, but largely of secondary texts. Our main text book was "Twenty studies that revolutionised child psychology" in which the context and content of twenty studies is recounted. This book is valuable in that it places the studies in an academic context but very invaluable in that it was written in a style that dumbs the science of it down "to accommodate students". It's written in a convivial style, which comes of as "the professor that wants to be cool," phrases like "This sounds boring right?" were pretty common. I specifically remember when the methodology of a study by Diana Baumrind related to parenting styles one study was presented the author simply stated that the details of the methodology were too boring and complex and would therefore not be reported on in full. This is most definitely a failure to live up to my 3rd criteria of detailed primary texts and i really think this is a disservice to us students who rather than being bombarded with a vast amount of low quality secondary texts should be offered the time to actually read and understand primary texts. The course was also fully quantitatively based with no qualitative methodology, no socio-historical perspectives, and I've never felt so far away from what we studied (child psychology) as when reviewing secondary texts about only experiments in this classroom. I do not think this course lives up to criteria 2 at all. Studies were presented as truth, and the methodology of experimentation was never questioned. The only critique "allowed" was one that already had accepted the premises of experimentation as a process of engaging truth. It was not discussed how this whole academic tradition is critiqued, how the replication crisis renders it if not invalid then at least a bit doubtful. This course also felt like being taken along the professors train of thoughts or peeping inside her brain, which could be fine it there were multiple perspectives in there, but it was more so one long argument for one specific approach. Philosophy of science does not really seems to exist in Toronto, which is a shame and a horror as this will result in a headless science charging ahead without consideration or self-reflection. Exams were also multiple choice questions, but related to curriculum or to lectures that was very closely based on curriculum. This is an improvement from Introduction to sociology. In the course "language Acquisition", a third year course, our curriculum was also a secondary text book, but as this is within linguistics it was all very new to me, and I do not feel in a position to crtique it as with the courses above. That being said, one does not need to know the content of an academic field to be aware that the lack of primary texts and of non-experimental approaches or at least of multiple diverse approaches is needed and would improve the course. The final course i took lives up to all criteria; "Moral thought and Behaviour" was both sober, it presented multiple perspectives, most weeks the two texts we read disagreed with each-other and they were all primary texts. This felt like a rare gem, which is horrifying as this should be the standard, as it is in copenhagen, at least at HUM, less so at Samf. the course was a seminar, so 2,5 hours out of 3 were in class discussion where we were able to ask questions, raise critiques, connect the content with out of class ideas etc. fostering autonomy and critical thinking. Some of the multiple perspectives were perspectives you would not really find in KU e.g. ethological perspectives. This specific perspective i do not really care much for, but the course really lived up to my second criteria of multiple perspectives, it was presented very soberly, and the professor was very good at accommodating and welcoming points that contradicted both him and the texts. 10/10 course

In my course "Introduction to sociology", a first year course we had no curriculum, the only thing that was expected of us between lectures was to watch a youtube playlist comprised of pop-cultural/scientific clips such as sketches from the talk show "last week tonight with John Oliver" or ted-talks. this course does obviously not live up to point 3. (i know I've created these criteria, but I would be surprised if anyone disagreed with them, except for them not being exhaustive), and it did also not really live up to criterias 1 & 2. Due to the lack of curricula and primary texts, every lecture felt like being taken along the professors train of thought, which was interesting, but in my eyes highly unacademic. There were few references to theories and if there was it was a reference to general theories (Weber's theory of Bureaucracy) and not a specific text. It all seemed as academic as a google search or a wikipedia page. The assessments were multiple choice questions about lecture content as we did not have any curricula. This results in the assessments being unacademic as they test us in content that didnt live up to the craft of academia. I remember a question from the final being "Is professor McIvor a part of the proletariat?" McIvor being our professor, and several questions about game of thrones in relation to some quasi-presentation of a sociological theory. One refutation of my critique could be that this is normal for a first year course in north america, to which i would point out that this is exactly the problem. Cause in DK we dont have levels of difficulty throughout the bachelor, we have different content, but all courses including first year are academically sound and serious. My view is that courses like this should not be possible to follow as substitutions for courses at KU, it's simply not academically a high enough level. In another course "Introduction to developmental Psychology," a second year course, we did have a curricula, but largely of secondary texts. Our main text book was "Twenty studies that revolutionised child psychology" in which the context and content of twenty studies is recounted. This book is valuable in that it places the studies in an academic context but very invaluable in that it was written in a style that dumbs the science of it down "to accommodate students". It's written in a convivial style, which comes of as "the professor that wants to be cool," phrases like "This sounds boring right?" were pretty common. I specifically remember when the methodology of a study by Diana Baumrind related to parenting styles one study was presented the author simply stated that the details of the methodology were too boring and complex and would therefore not be reported on in full. I do not think this course lives up to criteria 2 at all. Studies were presented as truth, and the methodology of experimentation was never questioned. The only critique "allowed" was one that already had accepted the premises of experimentation as a process of engaging truth. It was not discussed how this whole academic tradition is critiqued, how the replication crisis renders it if not invalid then at least a bit doubtful. This course also felt like being taken along the professors train of thoughts or peeping inside her brain, which could be fine it there were multiple perspectives in there, but it was more so one long argument for one specific approach. The final course i took lives up to all criteria; "Moral thought and Behaviour" was both sober, it presented multiple perspectives, most weeks the two texts we read disagreed with each-other and they were all primary texts. This felt like a rare gem, which is horrifying as this should be the standard, as it is in copenhagen, at least at HUM, less so at Samf. the course was a seminar, so 2,5 hours out of 3 were in class discussion where we were able to ask questions, raise critiques, connect the content with out of class ideas etc. fostering autonomy and critical thinking. Some of the multiple perspectives were perspectives you would not really find in KU e.g. ethological perspectives. This specific perspective i do not really care much for, but the course really lived up to my second criteria of multiple perspectives, it was presented very soberly, and the professor was very good at accommodating and welcoming points that contradicted both him and the texts. 10/10 course

crucial_aspects: As my exchange was in spring 2023, I had to apply already in October 2021 where COVID-19 was still very much on everybody's mind, so although it's quite boring reason to choose your study destination I wanted to choose a country that I hoped would deal with a new wave/break out of covid well including having a decent health care system. Other factors that were important to me were that I could speak the language kind of coherently and that I hadn't visited the country before.
overall_comments: Overall, I had a good experience, and I'm really happy that I went, because I had a few personal issues to work out. However, I started classes on January 7th, and was finished with exams and everything April 15th which means I only had school for three months and a week which, to me, was timeframe I would have wished was longer, as I hadn't properly settled in and made friends until around the two month mark (leaving not that long to fully enjoy that studying abroad life). I'm a bit introverted though, so might not be a problem if you're more extroverted / quicker at making friends :) The upside of this short term is that I had an amazing long summer break to go explore the remaining parts of Toronto and Canada :)
info_ease: Most information was sent to me through the UofT email system, and I highly recommend reading them and reading them THOUROUGHLY. The UofT inbound site was also so so helpful. Generally speaking, you're kind on your own in figuring everything out :)
arrival_assistance: After the first week of class there was a meeting for inbound (and outbound?) exchange students. The meeting mostly focused on stuff that I was already aware of such as the mandatory healthcare plan (what it covers, how it's paid) and telling students to make sure that they're getting the right credits to be able to graduate....so like very practical / technical stuff and not anything about how to adjust to UofT as an academic institution.
arrival_comments: I wish it had been maybe the day before classes started, and maybe could also have included a tour of campus or like some info on how to get help for papers and stuff (like information about the amazing writing centers) or anything that has an impact on day to day living as a student.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

I'm a bit introverted though, so might not be a problem if you're more extroverted / quicker at making friends :) The upside of this short term is that I had an amazing long summer break to go explore the remaining parts of Toronto and Canada :)
registration_process: After receiving a spot through the KU exchange program, I received a mail to UofT's inbound application website where I had to go through most of the steps of the KU application again (which classes do you expect to be taking, personal information and so on). When UofT then approved my application, I had to convert my application login to a UofT student login and login to all their portals and email system. Then I had to apply to classes through a google forms. The form itself was easy to fill out and the explaining email on how to do it was pretty detailed, but figuring out was classes I could apply to (most have prerequisites) and ensuring that they don't overlap took a long, long time...like i spend maybe a week figuring it out. Lastly I had to apply for the health insurance, and then I think I was good to go :)
registration_help: Emails being sent to my UofT email, and then sending emails with questions if I had any.
registration_success: A lot of the classes I originally wanted, I couldn't take because of prerequisites, but all the classes I applied to I got into :) But I also applied in application round 2 I think? There are 5 total as far as I remember, so being quick can definitely be smart, because popular classes fill up pretty fast! (This meant I applied for classes in July/August 2022 even though my stay didn't start till January)
registration_advice: Learn what the different aspects of the course codes means quickly, and take your time looking through the course catalogue. And check your emails. Seriously. Each course application round only had a week to do it in, so it's pretty easy to miss a round if you aren't checking your UofT email frequently :)
