activities_available: There were too many to list. Check out the University's website, they have so many!
activities_recommended: They have 4 excellent gyms scattered around campus:)
weekend_recommendations: Visit Niagara falls and plan a trip to Montreal.
culture_adjustment: Easy enough
cultural_challenges: There were no particularly challenging cultural differences.
culture_appreciated: The architecture was quite nice. I found Robarts library to be super cozy.
top3_advice: Beware of prerequisites for courses. Try to find a student co-op for housing. I wasn't able to myself, but some of my friends lived in one and that was amazing for them. Good luck!
other_useful_info: Scotty Bons makes wonderful jerk chicken. Huge recommendation! I ate there at least once a week:)
most_rewarding: Meeting wonderful people and simply overcoming the challenge of moving to a foreign country all by myself.
greatest_challenge: Moving to a foreign country all by myself.

crucial_aspects: I wanted the destination to be mainly English-speaking and wanted to go outside of Europe. I also wanted to take courses relevant for my area of studies, preferably courses not otherwise available at my home institution.
overall_comments: It was a really great experience, and I would highly recommend anyone considering going to go. I met so many nice and friendly people and got to experience a completely different way of attending university as well as a new culture.
info_ease: Mostly it was easy to find. Sometimes you did, however, need to dig a bit on different websites to understand the system properly and get all the necessary information.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any specific assistance. The University did not arrange any meet-ups or social gatherings, but my fellow exchange students managed to arrange picnics and other get-togethers, which was a great way of meeting other newcomers.
arrival_comments: I received some information emails and an invitation to a party, but the latter very much appeared to be a scam, so I did not try to attend it. There was a short presentation for exchange students, but it was pretty much the same information as in the emails, so it felt like a waste of time.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It was a really great experience, and I would highly recommend anyone considering going to go. I met so many nice and friendly people and got to experience a completely different way of attending university as well as a new culture.
registration_process: I sent my application, and later accepted an offer of admission. Gradually, I sent my documents and grades to the Mobility Online platform. I only got into contact with my host institution after they officially sent me a letter of acceptance, which was a few months before the semester.
registration_help: I received powerpoints and documents with information.
registration_success: Very successful. I got all the classes I wanted in the first round of applications.
registration_advice: Make sure to have your documents ready and checked well before they are needed. Some classes are very hard to get into (e.g. computer science), while others are a lot easier to get a place in. Remember to have a backup plan and watch out for different deadlines.
academics_comments: It was a really great experience, and I would highly recommend anyone considering going to go. I met so many nice and friendly people and got to experience a completely different way of attending university as well as a new culture.
course_level: I took one 300 course and three 400 courses. I found that they were not that different in difficulty, but the 300 level course definitely felt more like a high school class during lectures, while the 400 level courses had lectures more like the ones at my home institution.
teaching_comparison: The workload varies a lot throughout the semester, and the final grades are based upon your work throughout the entire semester instead of just a final exam. There were generally fewer lectures and rarely any tutorials. In general, we were not informed of which pages of the books to read for a given lecture, so you have to be able to figure that out yourself, as well as how to solve the assignments.
courses_enrolled: CHM338, CHM423, CHM455, CHM457
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed the CHM338 course which had both a theoretical and practical part. Working in the lab was a lot different than at home, and we were able to do analyses and procedures otherwise not possible at UCPH. CHM455 was also a great course where the focus was on current research and thinking outside the box based on the knowledge you already have. Very different from anything I've tried before, but also very inspiring!
unexpected_costs: The university has a mandatory health insurance that all students must pay for. It is not too expensive, and I heard it works just fine. Most prices are indicated without taxes, and some places expect tips.
cost_comparison: Groceries are generally really expensive, while eating out is often cheaper than in Denmark. Otherwise the prices are quite similar.
activities_available: A very large variety of clubs were available, and those I attended were very friendly and open to new people. The two run clubs were my favorites! There were several athletic centres with fitness areas, swimming pools, indoor and outdoor tracks, and different types of classes were available. Pretty much everything was included in the tuition price. There were also frat parties close to campus, but I chose not to go as I heard a few bad rumours about them.
activities_recommended: Try out as many clubs and activities as you can! I met so many nice people and also got to talk to a lot of local students which can otherwise be hard as people are not very social at lectures and tutorials. Definitely go for something you are interested in, but also try something you might not do at home. Attend some of the varsity blues games, they are free for students and a great experience!
weekend_recommendations: Niagara Falls, Scarborough Bluffs, the CN Tower, Toronto Islands, Distillery District, High Park, Algonquin Provincial Park, Bruce Peninsula National Park.
culture_adjustment: It was pretty easy. It took a few weeks for my English to fully catch up and understand some of the local phrases, but the culture is a mix of a ton of international cultures, so accents etc. are not unusual.
socializing_tips: Go to social clubs and remember to exchange something like instagram tags to stay in touch! Most are pretty busy but also open to meeting up. I also studied with a lot of people at the library even though our courses were different. It was a nice way of spending a bit of time together without compromising our studies during exam season:)
cultural_challenges: None in particular. Usually when people say sorry a lot, you are expected to reply with "sorry", which I found confusing at first, but it is seen as being polite.
culture_appreciated: Everyone were really open and friendly. I was invited to Friendsgiving and birthdays by locals although we had only been talking a few times. Although the locals may not be super interested in talking about culture differences, I had some really nice conversations with them about everyday life and had lots of fun.
top3_advice: Make sure to keep track of important dates and deadlines. Try to plan out a few trips/things you want to see before arriving - time flies once you get there! Tough days will come, but talking to others (both people at home and new friends) can help a lot. It will get better:)
other_useful_info: Do not underestimate the distances in the country. It may look small on a map, but even travelling from Toronto to Montréal takes at least five hours by train/car!
most_rewarding: Getting to experience life in a completely different culture and attending a university with a large campus filled with students and different opportunities was really great.
greatest_challenge: Missing people at home. I definitely underestimated how much the time difference affects calls and texts with people at home, and I missed out on several larger events which I was a bit sad about.

crucial_aspects: I decided course selection would be my priority number one, besides the fact I knew I would pick either Canada or USA (and to a lesser extent Australia or New Zealand) due to my specific topics of interest in Indigenous peoples in settler colonial nations.
info_ease: Most often I would just look in my mail, but finding information wasn't the trickiest part, more so it was feeling I knew all the things I had to or had done all I had to.
arrival_assistance: Firstly, there was an orientation about two weeks in where they told you everything, but almost all of it had been told to you before arriving. Was an opportunity to meet more exchange students, though. You get frequent mail from University of Toronto about opportunities for meeting other exchange students at certain events and the first couple weeks there are some booths around campus where they give flyers for the same type of thing. I did not go to any, however, as it was unnecessary for me.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You just fill out a google form for each course you want to apply to and you can apply to 5 if you want and drop one later. In the google form you just write the course you want and what courses you have taken previously that should grant you access (fulfil prerequisite requirements).
registration_help: You can always write them an email. I did so when I didn't know how to read the course codes and found out Y courses were for the full year (2 semesters) so I could not take them as I was there for one semester.
registration_success: I got all the courses I applied for.
registration_advice: Remember to also ask for permission from UCPH for more than just what you need so you have options if there are many you are interested in.
course_level: It can feel very unclear what is required to pass a class, but in the end it wasn't too bad and I was nowhere near not passing in any of my courses. Even after subpar performances in some assignments or midterm tests. This does not mean they won't be complicated as I had one course where the professor kept using the most unusual words instead of more normal synonyms. I spoke to the Canadian students and even they had to google most of the words from the readings and lectures.
teaching_comparison: There are grand auditorium lectures as well as smaller 20-person classes so it's a mix of things most have tried before. In some courses they offer a lot more freedom than others like one course where the assignments were in a topic of your own choosing, disconnected from the lecture topics. Another class didn't have any exams because the teacher didn't believe exams were beneficial.
courses_enrolled: ANT318H1 - The Preindustrial City and Urban Social Theory LIN202H1 - Introduction to Indigenous Languages of the Americas JPI201H1 - Indigenous Politics in Canada FAH255H1: Art of Indigenous North America
recommended_courses: I would wholeheartedly recommend JPI201 - Indigenous Politics in Canada as it very much shaped my experience and my relation to Canada and to a lesser extent Denmark as well. When speaking to Canadians it is very obvious the Indigenous peoples are not given much thought from day to day and their suffering is ignored and ignorance is uncontested. I believe anyone studying in Canada should take this course or one like it to understand the country they are studying in. It is also quite entry-level I would say as you do not need to know the name of a singly Indigenous group or anything about Political Science theory. + no exams!
unexpected_costs: My costs ^ are not necessarily super accurate, but I paid more than necessary for food because I ordered out a lot because of 1) my kitchen was in poor condition and 2) food opportunities in Toronto are very tasty.
cost_comparison: Prices aren't so different from Denmark. If you go watch varsity matches it is entirely free for students so it was a frequent way to meetup with other exchange students.
activities_available: There are a lot of different clubs you can be a part of and most don't even require you to sign up, you just show up. I spoke to some who went on camping trips and I went to board game club every Wednesday evening.
activities_recommended: If you have any hobbies at home in Denmark I recommend you check if they have a club for it as it's likely they do and if you don't have a lot of roommates or travelled with someone the social activities really feel so refreshing. I felt so much lighter and better after board game club (GLG). A lot of people there weren't board game nerds or playing big complex board games, it was mostly party game type games and social games. I made a lot of friends there and the friends I made outside of it I would bring so we could hang out there.
weekend_recommendations: I went to Houston and Dallas in the reading week which should just be treated as a vacation week. This does not mean I recommend Texas, just to say it makes sense to visit other spots in North America now that you're so close. If you haven't been you should visit Niagara Falls and most Canadians recommended people visit Banff and Halifax.
culture_adjustment: Took a couple weeks to get used to the baffling amount of homeless people, but just don't interact and they are harmless.
socializing_tips: In class they often sit with people they already know, so it is most easy to seek out the other exchange students. In clubs, however, it is easy to socialize with locals as they are most of the attendants. There they are also more welcoming.
cultural_challenges: It wasn't very challenging. If anything, when they get angry they often end sentences in "eh?" which can be hard not to laugh at in serious situations.
culture_appreciated: I found a lot of people really liked that you were from somewhere else even if their parents were 1st generation immigrants. It was fun to feel special for something completely out of your control.
top3_advice: Go to a club, interact with Indigenous opportunities like Native Canadian Centre of Toronto just off campus, and relax - enjoy your stay you will pass just focus on learning and getting something out of it, and not being perfect in your classes.
other_useful_info: Robarts Library is a great study space. In the evenings you can find raccoons around campus and in Queen's Park just off campus.
most_rewarding: I loved my courses.
greatest_challenge: Just getting used to my housing.

crucial_aspects: I really wanted to experience living in a big city, and go outside of Europe. Furthermore, I thought it was a bonus, that English was an official language.
overall_comments: It is really an amazing experience to live and study abroad. You learn to build a life for yourself in another city and get a whole new perspective on your life in Denmark. However, it can also be quite hard and feel a little lonely at times, but you just have to lean into it.
info_ease: You can just do research on the UofT website, and if you need more information you can always call or email the office or professors of specific courses. UofT also host some zoom-meetings for incoming exchange students with information.
arrival_assistance: When I first arrived at the airport, there was a booth with UofT students. They gave you maps of the campus and information. In the days around school start, there are also plenty of booths around campus handing out different flyers and information, and UofT host an information meeting in the first week of classes.
arrival_comments: UofT didn't really do anything to get the exchange students together socially, so you had to do that on your own initiative. Furthermore, there were no tours of campus, so before school starts, you should check out where your courses are, and do your own little orientation tour of the campus to find the right buildings and rooms.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It is really an amazing experience to live and study abroad. You learn to build a life for yourself in another city and get a whole new perspective on your life in Denmark. However, it can also be quite hard and feel a little lonely at times, but you just have to lean into it.
registration_process: You have to apply for courses through a google sheet in end may/start June. It is really important that you list all the courses you've already taken at UCPH, otherwise you won't get in. If you don't get in to enough courses you have to try again in the 2nd round, and then apply for courses with available spots.
registration_help: You can just do research on the website, or call/email the office or professors. After arrival you can also show top at the offices for late registry.
registration_success: First I applied for 5 courses and got in to 4. I then dropped one, and applied for another two in the 2nd round. I got into both of them and then dropped one of them later. I think in general, they are pretty nice at letting exchange students into courses, and if you are not sure, it would be a good idea to email the professor of the specific course before registration starts, to ask if you can join their course.
registration_advice: You can apply for a maximum of 5 courses. even though you only need four, it's a good idea to apply for 5 just to be sure, and then you can always just drop one course. -And also email the professors for help and information. A lot of them are helpfull.
academics_comments: It is really an amazing experience to live and study abroad. You learn to build a life for yourself in another city and get a whole new perspective on your life in Denmark. However, it can also be quite hard and feel a little lonely at times, but you just have to lean into it.
course_level: I took 3 300-level courses and 1 400-level course. However, I think the difficulty of a course depends more on the subject and the professor than on the actual level.
teaching_comparison: It is a bit more like high school. You have to show up to class and actively participate, as this will most likely affect your grades. This also means that the other student are way more active in class than at UCPH. Furthermore, the workload throughout the term is also bigger, due to assignments etc that will affect your final grade. However, the content of the work is a bit easier, as it is not as theoretical as at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: POL301H1 Colonial legacies and post-independence African Politics (valgfag) POL380H1 Topics in international politics: Gender and intersectionality in Global Politics (Valgfag) POL378H1 Topics in Comparative Politics: Law and Political Development (DAK3) EUR498H1 Special Topics in European affairs: European Union (EP)
recommended_courses: It really depends on what you're into. I really like critical theory and therefore chose courses about post colonialism and intersectionalism, as UofT offers a broad range of courses on critical theory and diversity. However, you can take courses within almost every faculty, so it is also a great opportunity to explore new fields such as media, law, history etc. As for the style of studying, you won't really know if it works for you, until you've tried it.
unexpected_costs: All international students in Toronto are obliged to pay for a health insurance called UHIP. It's around 1200 dkk and then you can go to the hospital and doctor for free without any worry or hassle, if an accident happens. It's really nice.
cost_comparison: The only thing that's cheaper in Toronto compared to Denmark is to-go coffee and 2nd hand stores. Groceries and alcohol is quite expensive, but you can get some relatively cheap meals, when you eat out actually.
activities_available: There are a lot of sport teams. Some of them require try-outs and some of them has a fee. However, there are a lot of sportfacilities around campus that all students can use for free. I my self swam three times a week, but you can also go ice skating, play tennis, basket or squat with your friends completely free. There are also a lot of clubs. In the weekend before school starts, there's a clubs fair, where you can walk around and see if there's something for you. A lot of clubs, you don't even have to be a part of to show up to their events. it's just all about following the right instagrams and mailing lists to know what going on.
activities_recommended: Definetly go see some uni-sports games!! It's completely free for students and a good way to get some school spirit. The center for international experience also regularly hosts get togethers where you can meet fellow international students.
weekend_recommendations: If you have the time (eg. during reading week) definetly go to Banff! It's really beautiful. I also went to Montreal and really loved it. There are lot of great places and cities in Ontario and the east of Canada, that you can reach in a few hours with bus or a rented car. If you go to Algonquin, try to go in the middle of October to see the beutifull colors of the leafs just before they fall off.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy. It's basically what you expect from watching american movies.
socializing_tips: Live with them. That's what I did, and it was really nice. Otherwise, just talk to them in classes. People don't talk much to each other in classes, but I promise you, if you start a conversation, they will be very nice and welcoming.
cultural_challenges: The style of teaching and the way the school work was probably the most different, but also the poverty rates. There's a lot of homelessness in Toronto, but I did not feel unsafe at any point.
culture_appreciated: Canadian people are definetly the most nice and welcoming people I have ever met, and you will smalltalk a lot with strangers. Also, the fact that Toronto is too international and multicultural. It literally feels like the whole world is gathered in one place, which also means that there isn't really one specific local culture.
top3_advice: Live at campus coop Say yes to everything Don't be afraid to take initiative and write in the exchange group chats. Everybody just wants to meet people.
other_useful_info: no
most_rewarding: Meeting so many new friends, and getting a whole new perspective on my life in Denmark.
greatest_challenge: Being so far away from everyone I know and love. At first it is really hard that every time you go out, it's almost like 'friend-dating' and getting to know people, and you don't really have anyone who really knows you, but you'll get there, and it will be sooo fun in the end.

crucial_aspects: At det var et engelsk talende land.
overall_comments: Det var en virkelig fed oplevelse. Anbefaler det virkeligt! Det eneste der var svært var at balancere skole med det sociale.
info_ease: Meget nemt
arrival_assistance: Kan jeg ikke huske.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Det var en virkelig fed oplevelse. Anbefaler det virkeligt! Det eneste der var svært var at balancere skole med det sociale.
registration_process: Man får en Google Form tilsendt af universitetet, som man skal udfylde med de ønskede kurser. Der er flere runder, man kan søge i. Husk at tjekke, hvornår de finder sted.
registration_help: Man kan stille spørgsmål til UofTs internationale kontor.
registration_success: Alle de kurser, jeg oprindeligt gerne ville have, blev ikke tilbudt i efteråret. Derfor var jeg nødt til at finde nye kurser. Jeg var uheldig i første runde, hvor jeg kun fik ét fag ud af fem ønskede. I næste runde valgte jeg mere strategisk ud fra, hvad jeg troede, jeg kunne komme ind på, og fik tre ud af fire kurser. Mit råd vil være at søge flere kurser, end du har brug for, fordi du altid kan droppe et eller flere senere.
registration_advice: Mit råd ville være at være strategisk i valget af kurser - vælg nogle som du ved du opfylder kravene for og har en god chance for at komme ind på. Et andet råd er at huske at tage det roligt, det skal nok løse sig.
academics_comments: Det var en virkelig fed oplevelse. Anbefaler det virkeligt! Det eneste der var svært var at balancere skole med det sociale.
course_level: Niveauet er på samme måde som på KU.
teaching_comparison: Der er mange opgaver, læsninger osv. i løbet af semesteret, som tæller med i ens karakter. Hvorimod på KU er det kun den endelige eksamen mod slutningen af semesteret, der tæller. Derfor vil jeg sige, at arbejdsbyrden var større i Canada, men indholdet var ikke nødvendigvis sværere.
courses_enrolled: BMS420H1 F: Bookbinding Then and Now BPM438H1 F: Mindfulness Meditation: Science and Research BMS431H1 F: Media and Environmental Justice NMC472H1 F: Theory & Method in Middle East Studies
recommended_courses: "Bookbinding Then and Now" var et super hyggeligt fag! Med en super sød underviser, så det ville jeg anbefale!
unexpected_costs: Ikke rigtigt noget uventet.
cost_comparison: Det er generelt omkring samme pris som i DK.
activities_available: Der var mange forskellige klubber, som arrangerede forskellige events, man kunne deltage i. Der var også en del sportsbegivenheder som amerikansk fodbold, hockey osv., hvilket var rigtig fedt.
activities_recommended: Der er forskellige grupper på sociale medier for udvekslingsstuderende, jeg vil anbefale at tage med til de arrangementer, der bliver planlagt der.
weekend_recommendations: Rejs i det, der hedder ‘Reading Week’. Jeg tog selv til New York, men man kan også tage til andre steder i Canada, som Vancouver.
culture_adjustment: Virkelig nemt. Canadierne er meget åbne og venlige. Derudover er der også enormt meget diversitet, hvilket jeg satte stor pris på.
socializing_tips: Canadierne kan godt lide at small talk, så sig hej til personen, der sidder ved siden af dig i timen. Jeg mødte en af mine gode venner på den måde.
cultural_challenges: Syntes ikke rigtigt der var noget.
culture_appreciated: Diversiteten og hvordan folk var imødekommende.
top3_advice: Ikke brug for meget tid på at studere. Opsøg fællesskaber, tag kontakt til folk du har mødt. Der er en del planlægning og udfordringer, men vær tålmodig, alt skal nok gå i sidste ende.
other_useful_info: Kulden i Canada er ikke nogen joke, så husk en god vinterjakke. Det starter rigtigt i begyndelsen af december, og så bliver det bare værre i januar.
most_rewarding: At møde en masse nye mennesker fra forskellige steder i verdenen og skabe minder med dem. Jeg værdsatte også bare at have en helt ny hverdag.
greatest_challenge: Kursustilmeldingen og tidsforskellen mellem Canada og DK var udfordrende.

crucial_aspects: Reccomendations from professors and friends, number and variety of courses at host university, interest in the country/city of stay.
info_ease: Quite easy, good information from the host university provided. I would've liked more information about student societies and social events.
arrival_assistance: Orientation tour, emails.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Google form to be filled out in three (or four) rounds prior to arrival. Courses were often filled up after the first round. Information about courses would sometimes come quite late (3rd or 4th round) making it difficult to know what you signed up for. I changed two or three courses in the last round and didn't get all the ones I was hoping for.
registration_help: Emails with information.
registration_success: Semi-succesful. See above.
registration_advice: Sign up early if you can.
course_level: Took two at 200-level, one at 300 and one at 400. Level does not always reflect complexity or difficulty.
teaching_comparison: Larger lectures, less contact with professors during lectures, meanwhile more opportunities to meet with professors outside of class (office hours)
courses_enrolled: Aesthetics Seminar in Continental Philosophy (Reading Capital by Marx) Social research methods Topics in environmental geography (Urban climate justice)
recommended_courses: Seminar's in philosophy are very fruitful.
unexpected_costs: Groceries are very expensive in Canada.
cost_comparison: Groceries: more Coffee (at café): less Drinks: similar to Denmark Transport: a little less
activities_available: all kinds, but not widely shared in an accessible way/place. I had to look around on different sites/social media profiles to find
activities_recommended: sports clubs, language clubs, meeting up with exchange students and locals
weekend_recommendations: Montreal, natural parks around Ontario, Niagara falls.
culture_adjustment: Toronto is more american than I expected. But all in all not too dissimilar to northern europe.
socializing_tips: Be brave, you often have to be the one to take the first step, but canadians are generally quite open - be honest: say you're on exchange and want to hang out
cultural_challenges: Cannabis culture: canadians smoke a lot making them (in my opinion) less sociable, more introverted. Bars close early (2am) so you have to look around for places to go out.
culture_appreciated: General openness, easy to talk to strangers.
top3_advice: Sign up early for courses Say yes to everything! (social events) Go to Future Bistro
other_useful_info: Download Resident Advisor if you want to go out dancing.

greatest_challenge: Making friends with other students.

crucial_aspects: Courses relevant for my studies
info_ease: not very intuitive. Lecture about housing being held, after all affordable housing had been filled/the deadline had passed. No introduction to exchange students about the practicalities until 1,2 weeks after arrival.
arrival_assistance: Not a lot. Again any assistance was given way after it was actually needed.
arrival_comments: Assistance was available and very helpfull but only after arrival. Any assistance prior or any type of orientation was not available or only given after it was needed.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: an individual google application form for each course. Very easy to fill out and understand.
registration_help: I don't now
registration_success: I got 3/4 courses, that I wanted. The last was unavailable for me due to waitlist.
registration_advice: Have backups for your backups.
course_level: Bachelor courses are quite easy. I would recommend doing master courses along with bachelor courses. (400 = masters)
teaching_comparison: Very different, many powerpoints and "lectures" compared to practical and blackboard lectures at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Chemistry of environmental change (200 course), Applied quantum mechanics (400 course), Advanced materials chemistry (400 course), Polymer chemistry (400 course).
recommended_courses: Depends on their field. I would recommend Materials chemistry because the professor is very engaged and engaging.
unexpected_costs: Housing was way more expensive than I had planned more, because I hadn't been told I wasn't admitted to the dorm I had applied for, and assumed I had gotten, until very close to my moving date and by then all affordable options had been taken.
cost_comparison: all housing is expensive. Generally everything is expensive compared to DK.
activities_available: almost everything. A lot of clubs and athletics.
activities_recommended: Clubs or workout classes to make friends.
weekend_recommendations: Local nature areas and trips to national parks.

most_rewarding: Culture and personal development.

crucial_aspects: Som statskundskabsstuderende er det ganske få universiteter man kan komme på udveksling på uden for Europa på bacheloren. Canada var et af de steder, og jeg synes det kunne være mega fedt at opleve den nordamerikanske kultur og natur!
overall_comments: Det har været en KÆMPE oplevelse, der har rummet alle følelser - men hvor er jeg glad for at jeg tog afsted!
info_ease: Man blev ikke per automatik taget i hånden af universitetet, men hvis man var proaktiv, var der meget hjælp at hente! Inden jeg tog afsted fik jeg en masse informationsmails, der ledte videre til steder man kunne få svar på sine spørgsmål - f.eks. et center dedikeret udelukkende til udvekslingselever, hvor der var en studieordning, der kunne hjælpe med stort og småt.
arrival_assistance: Da jeg ankom i lufthavnen var der en designeret UofT-bud med studerende, der kunne svare på spørgsmål ift. campus og hvor man skulle afhente til studiekort, kunne finde trænings- og aktivitetscentre, studiecenter, bibliotek mv. Man fik desuden en mail fra universitetet, med trin til hvordan og hvor man skulle hente sit studiekort. Men hvor ens undervisning skulle finde sted mv. måtte man selv undersøge. I den første uge, var der dog en bod ved hovedindgangen på uni, hvor man kunne stille spørgsmål til at finde rundt. VIGTIGST: Der var en campus dag den første fredag inden studie startede - her kunne man få introduktion til diverse foreninger, klubber og aktivitetscentre på campus. Kæmpe anbefaling at tage til dette, hvis man gerne vil komme ind på det sociale foreningsliv på campus!
arrival_comments: Praktiske information var de sådan set gode nok til at assistere med, men universitetet satte ikke nogen rammer ift. at samle de udvekslingsstuderende socialt. Vi havde en enkelt forelæsning på en time, hvor udvekslingsstuderende kom ind i 'slots' og fik en hurtig introduktion til, hvor de kunne søge hjælp, hvis de oplevede noget under deres udveksling eller havde spørgsmål. Men så finder man det sociale af andre veje! Og alle studerende på udveksling er selvfølgelig interesseret i at etablere sig socialt, så det kommer:)
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Det har været en KÆMPE oplevelse, der har rummet alle følelser - men hvor er jeg glad for at jeg tog afsted!
registration_process: Generelt tager det bare noget tid, at skulle ansøge om at komme på udveksling. Toronto krævede måske en anelse mere som statskundskabsstuderende, fordi det kan være svært at finde kurser, der matcher EP og DAK3 (de obligatoriske fag) + man skal dokumentere diverse fag man har haft på studiet og deres relevans ift. de kruser man søger + tage en sprogprøve, for at dokumentere ens engelskkundskaber (det klarer du let). Det er okay sent i processen, at man finder ud af, om ens kruser bliver udbudt, det skal man lige være forberedt på, MEN det skal nok gå op til sidst og det er tiden værd;) Ift. fysisk registrering, når man kommer til uni, Man skulle tage til en bygning der hedder "Exam Center", hvor man skulle hente sit studiekort (TCard). Det var egentlig meget nemt.
registration_help: Hmm synes KU var rigtig god til at informere om processen tidligt, så man vidste hvad man skulle have for øje, diverse deadlines osv.
registration_success: Jeg fik godkendt min to obligatoriske fag (!). EP gik igennem første gang, men DAK3 skulle der to forsøg til, da jeg ikke blev optaget på mit forhåndsgodkendte kursus, fordi man ikke måtte tage det som udvekslingsstuderende. Jeg endte med at finde en erstatning, så det gik op. Der var ingen problemer ift. mine to valgfag - hverken fra KU eller UofT's side. Udnyt muligheden for at prøve alle de spændende og anderledes kurser af!
registration_advice: Tjek kursuskataloget igennem og forsøg så vidt muligt, at have flere bud på dine obligatoriske kurser, da man ikke kan være sikker på, at kursuskataloget fra sidste år, er det samme som for det nye semester.
academics_comments: Det har været en KÆMPE oplevelse, der har rummet alle følelser - men hvor er jeg glad for at jeg tog afsted!
course_level: Alle mine kurser var på 0,5 Credits. Det føltes som om, at der var et ok højt forventningsniveau fra UofT side ift. de studerende, men i virkeligheden har det nok været lige så højt som KU, man har bare langt mere autonomi/selvstændighed på KU. Jeg tror ikke det bliver noget problem at følge med i kruserne, man skal nok bare lægge lidt mere tid i sine studier, fordi der er flere prøver, afleveringer og fremlæggelser undervejs (i modsætning til KU, hvor der kun er én eksamen til sidst i semesteret).
teaching_comparison: Kurserne var væssentligt mere 'aktiverende'. Med undtagelse af ét kursus, var alle mine kurser holdtimebaserede, hvor der var en forventning om at man deltagede mundtligt og også blev vurderet på sin aktivitet i timerne. Det er væssentligt anderledes fra KU, hvor man i højere grad kan være 'tilskuer'. På den måde var det nok lidt mere 'gymnasie-agtigt'. Samtidig virkede den der mundligt deltagelse også lidt 'pro-forma', man skulle bare sige et eller andet og så havde man deltaget.
courses_enrolled: Obligatoriske fag: - Law and Political Development (DAK3) - Special Topics in European Affairs: European Union (EP) Valgfalg - Energy Policy and Environment (forelæsningsbaseret) - International Environmental Policy
recommended_courses: Jeg var enormt glad for Energy Policy and Environement! Det var foreslæsningsbaseret - så på den måde mindede det mere om KU-formatet - og så var det et kursus med både ingeniører (for dem var det obligatorisk) og political science studerende. Det var en mega fed dynamik at begå sig i krydsfeltet mellem teknik og policy - undervisningen var tilrettelagt på en måde, hvor det var let at følge med som political science studerende, samtidig med at man fik et indblik i den energi-tekniske verden. Samtidig fik jeg et virkelig godt kendskab til Canada og public policy i Canada! Både ift. dets føderale indretning, provinsernes historie og kultur, Canada som en kolonimagt, dets energi forsyning og meget andet.
unexpected_costs: Jeg var heldig med min husleje, men ellers er det nok den udgiftspost, der trækker mest. Ift. forsikring er det obligatorisk at have forsikring igennem universitetet, men den dækker kun nogle poster (bl.a dækker den kun i Ontario), hvorfor det er godt at have sin egen rejseforsikring også. På den måde er man måske lidt dobbeltforsikret, men sådan er det.
cost_comparison: Generelt husleje, men der var jeg jo heldig. Ellers er indkøb nok ret dyrt. Der er ret billigt at spise ude, men var nok mindst lige så dyrt at købe ind som i DK.
activities_available: Der var virkelig et solidt socialt campusliv, hvis man opsøgte det. Diverse foreninger og klubber, alt lige fra foreninger om salsa til foreninger om undervandsdykning til foreninger som frivillig for pakning af nødpakker til hjemløse til foreningen for political science studerende. Der er så meget man kan kaste sig over, man skal bare ikke være bange for at opsøge det! og så skal man huske, at alle studerende er lidt 'on their own', fordi de skifter kurser hvert semester og dermed ikke på samme måde har et stamhold de går på. Det betyder også, at det sociale liv udfolder sig i sports og foreningslommerne.
activities_recommended: Sporthold og foreningerne i Hart House var virkelig fede. Det var bare generelt et dejligt sted at være. Der var også ture og ekskursioner med bl.a. outdoor foreningen.
weekend_recommendations: Jeg brugte selv meget af min tid (og mit budget) på at rejse rundt i de forskellige provinser. Det er ret nemt at tage offentlig transport til bl.a. Montreal og Quebeck City, det tager bare lidt tid og koster lidt penge, men det er bestemt det værd at komme ud. I efterårs(læse)ferien tog jeg til Novo Scotia og lejede en bil der, med en anden dansk udvekslingstuderende jeg var afsted med - det var mega fedt! Vi to besøgte også diverse nationalparker (gør det!) og rejste vestpå (Calgary, Banff, Jasper, Vancouver, Vancouver Island) efter vores semester var slut. Synes selv det er oplagt at rejse rundt i landet, når nu man er der, for nøj hvor har det meget at byde på og hvor er det smukt.
culture_adjustment: Det var meget lige til - folk er enormt venligt og imødekommende. Canada er genrelt et enormt mulitkulturelt land og Toronto i endnu højere grad.
socializing_tips: Vær ikke bange for at tale med folk i undervisningen og spørge om I skal hænge ud, spise frokost eller læse sammen efter skole - og spørg ind til hvad de synes om at gå på UofT, evt. om de har nogle gode tips. Mit indtryk var klart, at langt de fleste studerende fandt det mega fedt, når man 1) var udvekslingsstuderende og 2) opsøgte dem socialt, fordi de er så vant til at skifte kurser og dermed ikke rigtig bygger sociale stamhold op.
cultural_challenges: Ærligt, synes jeg ikke rigtig der var nogen. Som sagt, Canadierne er enormt venlig og åbentsindede - langt mere end i vi er DK, efter min mening.
culture_appreciated: Hvor imødekommende folk var, hvor bredt kulturen favnede (måske netop fordi der ikke var én dominerende kultur), hvor åbne folk var overfor forskelligheder og generelt hvor divers befolkningen var!
top3_advice: 1) Selvom der er flere test, fremlæggelser og prøver undervejs, skal du bare bestå og det klarer du let:) 2) Brug tiden til at gå op opdagelse i byen, tal med lokale, find dit yndlingskaffested, spis mad fra alle de geniale kulturer der findes i byen, vær nysgerrig og opsøgende og folk vil gribe dig 3) Benyt muligheden til at rejse rundt - Canada har så meget at byde på
other_useful_info: Toronto er en meget spændende by - særligt relativt til USA - den formår virkelig at favne mange kulturer på en meningsfuld måde. Gå på opdagelse i det.
most_rewarding: Jeg boede med nogle virkelig dejlige mennesker hos Campus Coop - det var en lidt mere afdæmpet version af et kollektiv. Desuden kulturen, det var helt utroligt at opleve en by (og et land), hvor der er plads til og respekt for så mange forskellige kulturer.
greatest_challenge: Når man er langt væk fra sin sædvanlige hverdag skal man (selvfølgelig) bruge mere energi på at finde ud af hvad man gerne vil, på at opsøge det og på at skabe nogle rammer for sig selv, som man føler sig tilpas i, selvom alting føles nyt og anderledes. Men det kommer! Og der vil altid være gode og dårlige dage - ligesom derhjemme. Man finder ud af hvad man savner derhjemme, men også hvad man gerne vil have mere af derhjemme!

crucial_aspects: For mig var det vigtigt at tage til et engelsktalende sted, hvor jeg ikke samtidig med at skulle lære en masse nyt, også skulle lære et helt nyt sprog. Desuden var det vigtigt for mig at finde nogle fag, som er helt umulige at få derhjemme, og idet jeg læser film- og medievidenskab, var UofT det perfekte valg, da deres Cinema Institute har så meget spændende at vælge imellem.
overall_comments: På godt og ondt var semesteret kort.
info_ease: I starten syntes jeg at UofT's egen hjemmeside var lidt svær at finde rundt i, især da jeg skulle til at vælge mine fag. Men alt vigtig information som man skal tage stilling til kommer også ind på mail, det vidste jeg bare ikke før jeg så jeg havde over 100 mails liggende fra universitetet. Når det er tid til at vælge kurser, modtager man også en mail med deadlines og links til katalog, så det er nemt at finde ud af. Mit tip er at sætte sig ned en dag eller to og gå UofT's hjemmeside igennem for udvekslingsstuderende, og så notere dig alle de ting, der er vigtige at vide på forhånd, fx at man skal købe sig en ETA inden afrejse osv. Når du får adgang til universitets egen intranet, ACORN, så finder du også nogle gode informationer der, fx at mn skal betale en obligatorisk sundhedsforsikring.
arrival_assistance: Der sidder både studieopholdskoordinatorer på KU og UofT som meget gerne vil hjælpe. Jeg fik hjælp fra begge, da jeg blev i tvivl om nogle detaljer vedr. mine fag, så det er en god ide altid at række ud til dem, hvis du er i det mindste i tvivl.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: På godt og ondt var semesteret kort.
registration_process: Jeg syntes i starten det var lidt mange ting at have styr på 1 år før min udvekslings, fordi UofT kræver at man allerede en år før sit ophold registerer sig. Der er nogle vigtige ting at få styr på, blandt andet at man skal tage en sprogtest, før de optager dig. Jeg tog Duolingos sprogtest. Det er den billigeste, og den godtager de heldigvis. Men det er en meget nøgtern test, hvor den mindste form for mistanke om snyd, og så skal man tage den om. Jeg bestod heldigvis i første forsøg.
registration_help: Skrive til studieopholdskoordinatorerne. De er hjælpsomme.
registration_success: Umiddelbart fik jeg alle de fag jeg oprindeligt havde tænkt jeg gerne ville have. Så det var fedt. Men jeg havde misforstået, og troede jeg skulle have 5 fag, hvor jeg kun behøvede 4. Mit 5. fag var jeg på venteliste til, og det stressede mig lidt, indtil en anden udvekslingsstuderende fra KU fortalte mig vi kun behøvede 4 fag. Så kunne jeg nemt droppe det fag jeg var på venteliste til.
registration_advice: Hold øje med dine mails, det er der du får besked, når du kan begynde at skrive dig op til fag. Og så hver ude i rigtig god tid med din forhåndsgodkendelse, så godt du kan, så du kan melde dig på lige de fag du har lyst. Jeg måtte melde mig på fag uden jeg havde fået den forhåndsgodkendt, fordi jeg var lidt for sent ude (eller måske mere fordi det tager dem op til 7 uger at svare dig). Jeg fik heldigvis godkendt alle mine fag.
academics_comments: På godt og ondt var semesteret kort.
course_level: Jeg tog kun 200 level kurser, og det syntes jeg var helt passende for det niveau jeg er vant til på KU. Arbejdsmængden er dog noget større, også selvom det kun er et 200 level fag, så hver forberedt på en del afleveringer og tests i løbet af semesteret. God ide at følge godt med, også selvom du "bare skal bestå".
teaching_comparison: På UofT bliver din karakter vurderet på en samling af flere ting og ikke kun din endelige eksamen. Det er både afleveringer, test og din deltagelse i undervisningen der tæller med i din karakter, så du ikke bare kan "slagge" hele semesteret og så gå til eksamen og få din karakter. Her tæller alt med. God ide at læse dine ting og lave dine afleveringer, og så række hånden op en gang imellem i timen, selvom det kan være grænseoverskridende. Det er hårdt arbejde på UofT, men det er virkelig også belønnende. Man lærer meget mere end hvad jeg er vant til på KU, fordi undervisningen ofte er passiv.
courses_enrolled: CIN211H1 Science Fiction Film CIN220H1 Special Topics in Cinematic: The Cinematic City CIN230H1 Business of Film CIN260H1 Selected Topics: The Hollywood Renaissance
recommended_courses: Jeg var rigtig glad for alle mine fag, men især Business of Film syntes jeg var super spændende, og underviseren var rigtig god og inspirerende. Det er nok det fag jeg har fået mest ud af. Anbefaler alle fagene for en filmnørd, men især Business of Film.
unexpected_costs: Mastercard gebyrer overraskede mig. Det er mine ekstra 150kr om måneden i gennemsnit. Og desuden at alle priser ikke er inklusiv skat, så det også lige bliver lagt oveni prisen, når man skal betale. At handle ind kan også være lidt en dyr omgang, især i den første måned. Hos det supermarked, der hedder Metro kan man få studierabat (10%). Jeg boede lige ved siden af campus, så det tog mig ikke mere end 5-10 min at gå i skole hver dag, derfor er min transport-udgift ikke så høj.
cost_comparison: Jeg havde godt regnet med at fødevarer osv. ville være lidt dyrere end hvad jeg var vant til. Det er okay pris at spise ude. Der er massere af god mad at prøve. Husk at nyd dit ophold.
activities_available: Der er rigtig mange forskellige tilbud, det er overvældende. Der er klubber til enhver smag. Der er gratis fitnesscentre og svømmehalle. Der er fitnesstider, hvor det kun er kvinder tilladt i centrene. Der er teater, musik, film, natur/udendørsklubber, skak, mad, yoga osv, you name it, så er det der.
activities_recommended: Igen, jeg har ikke deltaget i noget af det. Jeg havde travlt med at udforske byen og være sammen med de mennesker, jeg mødte på kollegiet. Hver tirsdag kl. 19 tog jeg til pubquiz på den lokale pub (The Madison), som ligger en spytklat fra Tartu. Det er en klar anbefaling og en rigtig god måde at lære nye venner at kende på.
weekend_recommendations: Tag en tur til Niagara Falls. Man kan et weekend pass til Transit GO-togene for kun 10CAD og så varer det 24 timer. Tag en tur til Banff med de andre udvekslingsstuderende, selvom det er en længere rejse og kræver mere planlægning. Det vil du ikke misse. Tag til Montreal, selvom det er en længere togtur. Tag et fly, hvis du har samvittighed til det. Udforsk byens rigtig mange forskellige kvarterer. Jeg anbefaler Little Italy, Kensington Market og The Beaches. Også Toronto Islands, men udenfor sæson er alt på øerne lukket, så det bliver en lang gåtur uden mad eller drikke.
culture_adjustment: Jeg havde rigtig svært ved almindelige høflighedsfraser på engelsk. Hver gang du møder nogen er det "hi, how are you" og de forventer du svarer noget ala "i'm good, how are you". Det havde jeg svært ved at vænne mig til. Har stadig udfordringer med det, men det er blevet nemmere. En stor ting er også at holde døren for andre. Vænner du dig hurtigt til. Du kommer til at støde ind på hjemløse, tiggere og stofmisbrugere på din vej. Det kan være lidt overvældende. Gå over på den anden side af gaden, hvis det er ubehageligt for dig. Eller mix dig ind i en stor mængde mennesker for at undgå dem. Jeg havde ikke nogle problemer med dem, men syntes da heller ikke de var rare til at starte med.
socializing_tips: Min oplevelse med de lokale studerende herovre er, at de er mere interesserede i at være venlige overfor dig, end venskabelige med dig. Jeg er ikke blevet venner med nogle af de studerende fra mine hold. Til gengæld er jeg blevet rigtig gode venner med de andre udvekslingsstuderende på mit kollegie. Måske min oplevelse havde været anderledes, havde jeg ikke boet på kollegiet. Det kan jeg ikke sige. Desuden er de studerende herovre meget afhængige af ChatGPT og de er unge (jeg er 25, de er måske 19-20), så der er også en aldersforskel, der gør det svært at socialisere med dem. Måske jeg bare er snobbet. Men jeg fik altså nogle rigtig gode venner blandt de andre udvekslingsstuderende. De er nemmere at imødekomme, fordi man alle er i samme båd.
cultural_challenges: Har allerede lidt besvaret det her. De hjemløse og stofmisbrugerne. Jeg ville heller ikke gå udenfor alene om aften. På UofT tilbyder de en følessvend/vagt, som man kan følges med på campus, hvis man ikke er tryg ved at gå alene. Det får du mere at vide om når du lander herovre og skal til orienteringsmøde herovre.
culture_appreciated: De har en rigtig god madscene herovre i Toronto, så der er massere af god mad at udforske.
top3_advice: 1. Søg ind på Tartu kollegiet. 2. Husk, du skal "bare" bestå dine fag, men du får også rigtig meget ud af at gå lidt op i det du lærer 3. Udnyt at du er i Canada, og tag rundt og se nogle ting i fx din reading week eller efter dine eksamener (april måned er en eksamenmåned, der har du ingen fag)
other_useful_info: Jeg landende herovre en 1,5 uge før jeg skulle starte på uni, og det syntes jeg var rigtig godt, fordi det tillod mig at vænne mig til at være alene og komme mig over jetlag. Bare husk at nyd det. Jeg har været her i 5 måneder nu, og jeg kan slet ikke forstå, at det bare er fløjet afsted.
most_rewarding: At jeg har gennemført det.
greatest_challenge: At skulle være helt alene i et fremmed land

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go somewhere where they offered in depth courses for my field of interest.
info_ease: The university was slow to send out information regarding like place and time to meet,what material to get and so on. I found this to be super confusing in the beginning, as it was very different from what I'm used to at University of Copenhagen.
arrival_assistance: An orientation tour the week after the beginning of the semester.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You choose courses later than you do in Denmark, and you have a much longer period, where you can drop them without further notice. Be aware that not all the courses you see on the UofT will be available for you as it changes from semester to semester.
registration_help: I contacted the registrars office if I felt unsure of anything in the course.
registration_success: I got some pretty neat classes, but the one I wanted the most, I didn't get because it wasn't offered in the semester I was going abroad. I would've wished I had known that earlier on.
registration_advice: Don't stress if it takes time to get the confirmation and all of that. I can be a bit of a process, but the professors know that people changes courses quite a bit in the first few weeks, and they do take this into account in their planning of the course material.
course_level: The course material itself is easier compared to university of copenhagen, but the workburden is a lot greater due to many, many assignments, presentations and quizzes that you need to participate in throughout the semester. Also there's both a midterm and an exam, which also increases the workload and restricts the flexibility.
teaching_comparison: It was in many was like that of UCPH, with the exception of the workload from the constant assessment.
courses_enrolled: CSB328H1 F Animal Developmental Biology, HMB300H1 F Neurobiology of Behaviour, HMB360H1 F Neurogenomics and HMB310H1 F Laboratory in Neuroscience
recommended_courses: I enjoyed all my courses, but I will say that Neurogenomics definitely stood out the most. It was absolute amazing, with a great prof as well. The Laboratory in Neuroscience was super exciting and the prof was nice, but the workload was crazy. Even the Canadians complained about the amount of work being like way to great for the amount of credits.
unexpected_costs: You need to pay a mandatory health fee called UHIP.
cost_comparison: Grocery are really expensive. Going out to eat is a bit less than in Denmark.
activities_available: There lots of sport facilites and a bunch of club.
activities_recommended: Use all the amazing sport facilities, and many of the outdoor clubs are great as well.
weekend_recommendations: NY is close, and also you can take the train to see other beautiful cities like Ottowa.
culture_adjustment: Super easy.
cultural_challenges: None really.
culture_appreciated: Canadians are as friendly as the stereotype.
top3_advice: Find housing in due time, don't make a lot of plans outside of uni before you get an idea of the scheduele - uni is not very flexible like in Denmark and lastly sit next to people sitting alone in class and make small talk. It's super easy to gets friends here.
most_rewarding: New friends and new exciting academic challenges.
greatest_challenge: The work burden and the fixed scheduele. I was not pleased about that.

crucial_aspects: I knew that I wanted to go outside of Europe, and I wanted a university that was in either a really big city or in beautiful nature. Toronto definitely offered the big city.
info_ease: There wasn't really a whole lot of information to find. University of Toronto uses the same system as Absalon, and the small bit of information needed was on there. When I had questions, the Centre for International Experience at UofT was very helpful.
arrival_assistance: Unfortunately, the Faculty of Arts and Science did not do any real introduction week (but I believe that other faculties do). This meant that there was no form of introduction before classes started. The Centre for International Experience offered some exchange-events and campus tours later in the school year, but it would have been nice if there was something before classes started.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Once the course catalog was ready they opened up for course registration. For the fall-2025 semester they opened for course registration June 6th. There were three rounds where you could apply for five courses each round (KU students need 4 courses to reach 30ects).
registration_help: The course platform was very helpful once it was updated with what courses were actually available and they also had a few guides online. Centre for International Experience was helpful as well
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted except for one in round 1, and then I got the last one I needed in round 2. No issues really.
registration_advice: Apply for everything that sounds remotely relevant in round 1 cause most fill up quickly. You can always drop courses if you have too many or you find something more exciting.
course_level: BA courses were a bit easier than at KU. Took a 200 course (2nd year) which was extremely easy, while 300 & 400 courses were probably about the same level as back home with way higher expectations than the 200 course. The one MA course I took was extremely high level, but it was also a boutique course with only 20 students from a special IR program.
teaching_comparison: You are expected to participate in class, and you are graded based on your oral participation. Also way more assignments and midterm exams. Actually it feels a bit like gymnasiet, but it makes you participate more. About the same amount of reading at home as at KU, but fewer hours of classes throughout the week (I had 9 hours in class every week)
courses_enrolled: POL218H1 F (Fall) State, Society and Power in Comparative Perspective. POL311H1 F (Fall) Law and Political Development. POL358H1 F (Fall) Conflicts, Minority Rights and Para-States in Europe. POL466H1 F (Fall) Topics in International Politics III - Dealing with dictators.
recommended_courses: POL218H1 F (Fall) State, Society and Power in Comparative Perspective was an extremely boring and overly easy courses with a bad professor. Only took it cause it was the only course KU would pre-approve, but it was a waste of time. The other courses were amazing, and I can't recommend the professors enough. If in any way possible, take a course with Professor-NAME REDACTED-, a UofT legend who is so different from any other teaching professionals I have ever met. Professor -NAME REDACTED- (Topics in International Politics III - Dealing with dictators) is also a rock star in the IR field, so try to take her courses if possible if you like IR. Law and Political Development was a little too law-based for me, but professor -NAME REDACTED- was extremely nice and talented. Also the tests and exams were really easy so it wasn't that stressful.
unexpected_costs: On top of your own health insurance you have to purchase the UHIP one from the university. However it's money well spent. They paid for everything when I broke my wrist.
cost_comparison: Going out to eat is cheaper than in Copenhagen and beers and also way cheaper. However, groceries are extremely expensive.
activities_available: You can participate in multiple sports leagues at UofT (Varsity, tri-campus & intramural). However, I did not get any information about this from UofT and had to do all of the research myself. Make sure to do this as you have to sign up essentially right when you get there. I did not participate throughout the semester as I broke my wrist during tri-campus tryouts, but it seems like a great way to make friends. There is also a club for literally everything. I did not sign up for any, but did participate at a food-event with the Georgian society club.
activities_recommended: Would recommend trying everything! Why not?
weekend_recommendations: Toronto is massive, so you can visit new places every week. Would definitely recommend going to Banff.
culture_adjustment: Extremely easy do to the many cultures in Toronto. It really is the melting pot of the world! However, there are so many exchange students at UofT that you're not special, so don't expect any free points for being an exchange student (About 30% of the students at UofT are international students). You have to actively do something to make friends and meet people.
socializing_tips: The other KU students and I always joke about not having made a single Canadian friend. The other exchange students are generally more outgoing. Try to join the events set up by the Centre for International Experience and join a sports team.
cultural_challenges: Nothing really
culture_appreciated: No matter which cuisine you want on any given day, you can definitely find it in Toronto. Also a great shopping culture if you want to spend all of your money late at night with all clothing stores staying open till 9pm.
top3_advice: Get a Bike Share Toronto membership! Toronto is a fairly good biking city, and you can get unlimited bike rentals for a year for 300kr. as a UofT student. Try to be social in the beginning - It's probably the most overwhelming time, but it's when everybody are looking for friends. It might look cool, but don't live down by the water. It's really boring when it gets cold.
other_useful_info: UofT publishes their exam dates extremely late (2-3 weeks before the actual exams). Don't wait for this to buy your plane ticket home unless you want to spend 10000kr on a one-way home for Christmas. Just look up the last possible exam date and work from there.
most_rewarding: First of all I thought that the professors were amazing and that the academic experience was extremely rewarding. Also, Toronto is an amazing city to live in, and you will never get bored. It is crazy but so much fun! I can't recommend it enough.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge before and during was trying to get KU to pre-approve courses and everything else. It felt like they worked against us and not with us. Felt like giving up on the whole thing multiple times because the process was so frustrating. The people at KU-abroad were very nice, but the whole process was insane. It killed the excitement and even 2 months before the start of the semester I wasn't sure if I would be able to go. Once here, there were no great challenges (other than missing my mom of course).
other_comments: Something has to be done about the process leading up to exchange. Do your exchange at The University of Toronto (St. George). I can't think of a better city/university combination. 10/10

crucial_aspects: I wanted to experience a big city like Toronto to see what it was like. I wanted a diverse international environment. Furthermore, the academic opportunities were excellent and were a significant factor in choosing my exchange.
info_ease: It was easy. There was a lot of information about it online on UofT's website.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive assistance.
arrival_comments: The university did not have an intro week for the exchange students, so it was hard for us to organize ourselves. We did manage to create our own group chat and make arrangements.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was easy to register; I just had to be early.
registration_help: I don't know.
registration_success: I got into every class I wanted.
registration_advice: Apply early and be ready to have backup classes if there is a change in schedules.
course_level: I took level 200, 300, and 400 classes. The 400-level class was registered as a master's course at my home university.
teaching_comparison: I liked it a lot. It was much more intimate, and you could build personal relationships with the professors.
courses_enrolled: POL218H1 F (Fall) State, Society and Power in Comparative Perspective POL311H1 F (Fall) Law and Political Development POL358H1 F (Fall) Conflicts, Minority Rights and Para-States in Europe POL466H1 F (Fall) Topics in International Politics III
recommended_courses: POL358H1 F (Fall) Conflicts, Minority Rights and Para-States in Europe - Robert Austin is a great professor who takes his time to get to know most of his students.
unexpected_costs: I did not expect to travel as much as I did, and that was a high cost I had not expected. I do recommend travelling as much as possible and experiencing all that Canada has to offer.
cost_comparison: Groceries in the supermarkets. They are more expensive than in Denmark.
activities_available: A lot of athletic and social activities. I personally played a little football and attended many of the social gatherings.
activities_recommended: Go to the sports events. It is great fun to watch the varsity team play against other teams from other universities.
weekend_recommendations: Go to Banff. Banff was the single most incredible place I have ever been to. It is so beautiful, and there is a lot to do there.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy. People are from all over the world, so there is not a single "local" culture.
socializing_tips: Join the clubs and social gatherings happening at the school.
cultural_challenges: The cafe culture is very different. No one is sitting outside and drinking coffee.
culture_appreciated: How friendly people are towards others. People small-talk all the time. It took some time to get used to talking to strangers in that way, but it is a pleasant experience.
top3_advice: 1. Say yes to everything - there is a lot to experience. 2. Be initiative. Go up to people. Talk to people. Make friends. 3. Be prepared actually to study.
other_useful_info: Download WhatsApp. Everyone uses WhatsApp.
most_rewarding: My friend group I made in Toronto. I will for sure see them again when I get back.
greatest_challenge: The exam period. Very stressful, and there was a lot to study.

crucial_aspects: English speaking, good university, far from Europe.
overall_comments: Toronto in the fall is great - you get a long summer, beautiful fall and taste of the snow in december.
info_ease: Okay. UofT has a lot of websides so it can take som time to find the information. But most of it is at the webside and otherwise you can always email them (then they answer pretty quickly)
arrival_assistance: There was a welcome event in the first week - and then I was lucky to have a house with housemates who helped me with all my small questions.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Toronto in the fall is great - you get a long summer, beautiful fall and taste of the snow in december.
registration_process: You apply and then you have to upload a language test around March. You can not choose courses before May/June, so when you aplly for the "forhåndsgodkendelse" you just have to checkout the courses from former years. When you apply for courses, you do it through a google survey link.
registration_help: You could email them and there was some Q&A websides
registration_success: I got 3/5 at first round. Some of the 4th year courses I applied for had a limited amount of spots so I did not get them. But you can also get bachelor credits for 200 and 300 level courses (and they are often easier). So in 2nd round, i found some other good courses. There is also a 3rd round of course choosing.
registration_advice: Just relax - they always find a solution with KU. Perhaps email UofT directly after you have filled out the google survey link; that helped me once.
academics_comments: Toronto in the fall is great - you get a long summer, beautiful fall and taste of the snow in december.
course_level: I had 3 bachelor courses and one course that I got credited as a Master course.
teaching_comparison: Way more like a danish "gymnasie" with participation grades and smaller assignments through the semester. The grading scale goes from 1-100 and you need 50 to pass. So you can check out in the syllabus how many points, each category counts.
courses_enrolled: POL358H-F: Conflicts, Minority Rights and Para-States in Europe (valgfag) POL 311 – Law and Political Development (DAK3/valgfag) POL 218H1F - State, Society, and Power in Comparative Perspective (DAK3/valgfag) POL354 - POLITICS AND SOCIETY IN RUSSIA (Valgfag/MA credit)
recommended_courses: POL354 and POL358H was great as they were way more in detail (more practical politics and less theories) with a topic than the ones we usually have at KU.
unexpected_costs: Bike annual plan (able to use all the tourist bikes around the city) for 80CAD as a student - saved me a lot on public transport.
cost_comparison: Cheaper to get coffees and eat out. Grocery stores are almost the same as Denmark. Fruit and greens are cheap in Chinatown
activities_available: Outdoor club, lots of different sport activities (you can join for free)
activities_recommended: Use the Varsity centre run track and athletic centre swim pool
weekend_recommendations: Travel a lot. Algonquin national park can be done as a long daytrip in the fall (so beautiful, but rent a car with other people). Ottawa and Montreal as a combined weekend trip with bus/Via rail. Vancouver and Whistler in the holidays. And then USA is so close with 1,5 hour planes to NYC and Washington. Of course also Niagara Falls as a day trip with bus/train (pretty cheap).
culture_adjustment: no problems - the Canadians are friendly
socializing_tips: Get to join events that are not just for exchange students. Find a community; like a university club or a church (they are so friendly) and introduce yourself, then they will give you a warm welcome
cultural_challenges: In class people do not know each other as well as in Denmark. So it can be a bit silent. But if you talk to people, they will most likely respond kindly and engage in conversations.
culture_appreciated: The Canadian kindness
top3_advice: 1. Campus Coop for housing 2. Try to meet local canadian people 2,5. Travel a lot - get to see the American continent, as it will never be as easy as now 3. Buy fruit and greens in Chinatown (saves money for travels;))
other_useful_info: There is a lot of courses, so you will no matter what find something that is interesting (even if you do not get your 1st priority)
most_rewarding: Improved my English and got to travel a lot - and have the opportunity to be at a top25 University with a lot of good professors and cool buildings.
greatest_challenge: Not that many challenges. But perhaps the time before travelling without knowing what it would be like.

crucial_aspects: I’ve always wanted to live in an English-speaking country outside of Europe for some time. I had been to Canada before and really liked the nature, as well as the friendliness of the people. Further, the University of Toronto has a good reputation and Toronto, being a big and very diverse city, seemed like a cool city to live in for a few months.
overall_comments: I really loved the vibe of the city, I found some really nice friends and went on some cool trips; however, I did not like the university system very much, as uni involved a lot of homework, quizzes, and mandatory attendance – which reminded me too much of highschool.
info_ease: Relatively easy, I would say. I found everything I needed to know regarding arrival on the university website, and the international office even held 2 online information meetings for exchange students (I think one about housing and one about general information about the exchange) before arrival. There was another information meeting in person after arrival organized by the international student office.
arrival_assistance: I did not need any assistance, but you could always email the international office or stop by in person if you have questions or need help.
arrival_comments: I did a 2-month internship (in July & August) in Toronto before the start of the exchange semester. For that period of time I found a room via a Facebook housing group. For the period of the exchange semester I rented an Airbnb with another exchange student that I met through a Facebook group.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I really loved the vibe of the city, I found some really nice friends and went on some cool trips; however, I did not like the university system very much, as uni involved a lot of homework, quizzes, and mandatory attendance – which reminded me too much of highschool.
registration_process: Please check my answer for question 9:)
registration_help: You can write emails if you have any questions and, as mentioned before, the course registration emails contained detailed instructions on how to fill out the course registration forms.
registration_success: I got all 4 courses I wanted!
registration_advice: I would register for all courses you want in the first round since courses may already be full in later registration rounds.
academics_comments: I really loved the vibe of the city, I found some really nice friends and went on some cool trips; however, I did not like the university system very much, as uni involved a lot of homework, quizzes, and mandatory attendance – which reminded me too much of highschool.
course_level: 2 of the courses I took (ECO310 and ECO439) were comparable to the level at UCPH. The other 2 courses were easier, especially since they did not involve many models or (complicated) math and focused more on just learning by heart.
teaching_comparison: In Toronto I had mandatory attendance, regular quizzes, homework, and assignments. Your final grade didn’t just depend on one exam at the end of the semester (like at UCPH), but also on things like assignments, quizzes, homework, attendance, and a midterm. Because of that, the workload during the semester was higher, but the pressure at the end was lower since the final exam didn’t count for your entire grade.
courses_enrolled: ECO 310 Empirical Industrial Organization / ECO333 Urban Economics / ECO369 Health Economics / ECO439 Empirical Methods in Microeconomics
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed ECO310. It is a great course if you are into industrial organization, because you learn the theory and then actually apply it using datasets and STATA. The professor also gives you past exams and assignments (with solutions), which makes studying for the midterm, final, and the 2 assignments much easier. I would also recommend ECO333 if you are looking for a relatively easy course. The lecturer was really nice and easy to follow. Even though the professor for ECO369 was very good – she is really good at presenting and the content was interesting – I did not like the course that much. It was mostly about learning by heart, and I personally prefer courses with more models and calculations. ECO439 had really interesting content and the professor was nice, but the slides were very theoretical and sometimes hard to understand. There were no regular problem sets (just two assignments), and we only got one past exam without solutions to prepare for the final, which made studying quite difficult.
unexpected_costs: Maybe that I had to buy a book for one of my courses (&textbooks are usually quite expensive!)
cost_comparison: Phone plans are quite expensive. Getting a coffee is quite cheap (which is why often went to cafes).
activities_available: Many! As mentioned before, there are many student clubs you can join. Also, the international office organized a few social events for exchange students, such as watching a varsity American football game, a trivia night or pumpkin carving.
activities_recommended: I would go watch a varsity game (I went to an American football game as well as an ice hockey game) and I liked the run club where you get to go for a run and socialize with other students.
weekend_recommendations: Visit the Niagara falls (it’ll be easy to find other exchange students to go with, as everyone wants to visit the falls). Further, I went on a roadtrip to the Algonquin Provincial park; the nature is absoluteliy worth a visit! You could also do trips to Alberta (visit the Rocky Mountains, Banff etc.) or Montreal and Quebec city. I also went to St. John’s in Newfoundland with a friend for a couple of days (very cute town and pretty nature but very rainy!!). There is so much to see in Canada!! You also get a week off from uni in October (“reading week”) which you can use for traveling; I used it to travel to Cancun in Mexico, which I can recommend as well! In general, there are many cheap flights from Toronto to destinations in the US or Mexico.
culture_adjustment: Quite easy; it’s very similar to European culture.
socializing_tips: Speak to students in your classes and join student clubs. Canadians are generally very open:)
cultural_challenges: Canada/generally North America is made for cars! Compared to other North American cities, the public transport system (you have TTC in Toronto and GO Transit in the Greater Toronto Area) in Toronto is well developed and relatively reliable, however, if you would like to visit provincial parks or smaller towns outside of Toronto it can get tricky or even impossible to get there without a car.
culture_appreciated: I felt very welcome! Canadians are very friendly:)
top3_advice: 1. Join the UofT Facebook group for exchange students as well as Whatsapp groups. Exchange students will use these groups to organize events:) 2. Register for the courses you want in the first registration round! 3. Visit some nature!
other_useful_info: Like I said before, join Facebook and Whatsapp groups! That helps a lot to meet people!
most_rewarding: Finding nice friends and visiting pretty parks near Toronto!
greatest_challenge: Finding housing, I would say?
other_comments: noo

courses_enrolled: - ANT366H1: Anthropology of Activism and Social Justice - INS390H1: Research and Ethics in Indigenous Studies - WGS390H1: Land-ing: Indigenous and Black Futurist Spaces - CRI364H1: Indigenous Peoples & Criminal Justice

top3_advice: Find a place to stay at campus or rent something in the outer suburbs of town. Engage with fellow exchange students. Engage with the Indigenous People and learn from them.
other_useful_info: Find events that interrests you at Folio which is the place where you find most of the events at the U of T, also be up to date on the U of T website as there can be other relevent event there that are not on Folio.
most_rewarding: Meeting fellow Indigenous Students and people from all around the world and to be able to talk about our studies with especially fellow Indigenous Students and professors/lectors

crucial_aspects: French people had told me a lot of good things about Tours + affordable living costs + I wanted to speak French, so I didn't want a big, international city
overall_comments: Amazing. So many new impressions, nice people and great things to do, I really needed that after almost two years of covid
info_ease: I arrived a couple of weeks before the semester started, so I had a lot of time to figure it all out. It was quite easy to find information, the university of Tours sent out emails with the most basic stuff and adresses, deadlines etc.
arrival_assistance: I didn't have any assistance from the university, but my housemates in Tours picked me up at the train station and helped me a lot in the beginning
arrival_comments: The whole uni inscription, welcome meetings etc were a bit chaotic and many informations at once. A lot of paperwork and it took a few hours a couple of times (also keeping in mind documents and signatures for KU), but it worked out fine in the end
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Amazing. So many new impressions, nice people and great things to do, I really needed that after almost two years of covid
registration_process: See above
registration_help: I had a lovely coordinator, Carine, who helped me a lot
registration_success: Somewhat succesful. I couldn't make it work with all of the classes that I wanted, but I found good replacements
registration_advice: It's normal if the registration process is chaotic and takes a lot of time, it's the same for all the exchange students. Don't worry if you don't get all the courses you want and be prepared to change classes.The university administration in Tours is generally helpful and patient.
