crucial_aspects: I wanted to get far away from Denmark, to explore new cultures. I wanted an English speaking country, to not make it too difficult for myself, since I'm not that great in other foreign languages.
overall_comments: It would have been a 10, if it wasn't for the stress of applying to a new university and getting the courses I wanted to take approved by my host uni and KU
info_ease: It became easy to get help with stuff once I arrived, they had a great team helping international students
arrival_assistance: They had a great team that provided a lot of help and that you could text or talk to if any help was necessary.
arrival_comments: They also did a full week of welcome activities, so you quickly find friends that are in the same situation as you, that you can get help from
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It would have been a 10, if it wasn't for the stress of applying to a new university and getting the courses I wanted to take approved by my host uni and KU
registration_process: There's a website, where you can match your courses and make sure they don't overlap, use that!! If something happens, you still have like a month from when you start, where you can change courses, but you have to have the new courses approved by KU as well, so make sure you apply for a lot of courses before you go.
registration_help: You can e-mail (takes a little while to get an answer back), call them or go talk with them, they are very helpfull
registration_success: There was 1 course i was really hoping I would get, but I didn't get approved for it. other than that it was fine, and they have a lot of different options
registration_advice: Join some of their clubs, they have a lot, from sports to book clubs, they have sooo much, and it's a great way to make friends.
academics_comments: It would have been a 10, if it wasn't for the stress of applying to a new university and getting the courses I wanted to take approved by my host uni and KU
course_level: It's alot like "gymnasiet" in DK, with a lot of assignments, that all count for a small percentage of your final grade, which is a bit anoying. But I just needed to pass my classes, so when the final exams came, I had no stress, because I knew I already was going to pass. You can read about the classes and what the expectations are, so you can do whatever you want, but I recommend you take easy classes, so you can enjoy the free time with your new friends and nature
teaching_comparison: Depends on the courses you take, you can choose what you want
courses_enrolled: Geography for today: Geography of food Our digital earth Coastal Geography AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Technique
recommended_courses: AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Technique. You do pottery!! I was really bad at it, which was kind of scary, because the rest of the class was pretty good. But you have to remember it's an introductory class, so the bar is very low. You basically just have to hand in whatever and you will pass. One annoying thing though, was all the deadlines you have in that class, so you end up spending quite some time there, if you wanna make your stuff kinda pretty
unexpected_costs: UVic have their own insurance mandatory insurance that you need to pay.
cost_comparison: Housing prices is about the same as in copenhagen, but not as bad as in Vancouver. Food is expensive
activities_available: Everything.. all the clubs you can think of, and they have an orientation day, where you can go talk with them all. Every week they have some service dogs come visit the campus, that are there for you to pet and play with - great if you're feeling home sick or just want some love.
activities_recommended: Victoria has some quite okay nightlife, although most stuff closes between 12 and 02. But you should definetely focus on renting cars and drive out into the wilderness! Go surfing at Tofino, climb mountains, go skiing, go see whales, orcas and sea otters
weekend_recommendations: Rent a car and explore the island - it's way bigger than you think. You can also visit Vancouver about 5 hours away with public transport, less with a car. You can visit some of all the ski resorts. I Went to Cypress mountain for a day, near Vancouver and also took a bus to revelstoke (best skiing place in the world) during christmas to go ski there for a week. Visit Seattle for a weekend. fly or drive to Banff - can't recommend this enough. INSANE nature!! There's an airport in victoria that can take you there. Other trips a lot of exchange students and myself went from that airport include Mexico, Hawaii, LA, and Las Vegas. Flights to and from the states directly can be crazy cheap.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. I think Canada in general is a lot like DK. They are very polite and you will get used to thanking the bus driver before leaving busses. One bad thing is the number of homeless people in cities. I've grown up in Vesterbro, but still got a bit shocked about how bad the opiod crisis is and how vissible the homeless are in the cities. But I never ran into an actual problem with the homeless, it's just different.
socializing_tips: Join a club!! It can be hard to socialize in class, because most people just leave straight after class to go to a new one. UVic do invite all the exchange students to do a lot of socializing the week before school starts, so that helps you meet like minded people, that like yourself, will be trying to make new friends.
cultural_challenges: Tipping! Just prepare yourself to be paying 15-20% more than advertised.
culture_appreciated: Their friendliness!! Such great people and they have also started preaching a lot about the first nation history (indigenous).
top3_advice: Go with an open mind and be preparred to make friends. Make sure your social battery is charged! although, you of course decide for yourself, if you need a break. You might feel overwelmed with all the assignments, but the level isn't too bad and you will find yourself stress free at the final exams. Focus on making friends and exploring the wonderfull Vancouver island!
other_useful_info: Don't stress too much, they are very nice and everything is going to work out fine
most_rewarding: The friends I made, and the nature I explored with them
greatest_challenge: Getting the right courses and getting them approved
other_comments: Enjoy - you're gonna love it!!!

crucial_aspects: the language spoken in the country of exchange, proximity to nature and outdoor activities
info_ease: The exchange office at the University of Victoria was easily located on campus and the staff was incredibly kind and helpful. The only hard aspect was that the time change to the office in Denmark made it a little hard to communicate efficiently, but all was solved in the end.
arrival_assistance: Upon arrival (in late august) I had not been enrolled in the classes that I needed yet, and the exchange office helped me understand the enrollment online system, find classes that I could enroll in, contact professors that had initially denied my application to be in their class, and helped me understand the way the class syllabus worked at UVIC
arrival_comments: Orientation week at UVIC was helpful both academically and socially.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: There were online seminars hosted that told you about the different things you needed to in the semester before arriving. There was an access link that was sent to you sometime during mid-june to late-june, and this gave you access to the online sign up for classes. Here you had to look up classes and sign up for them - this was a bit confusing for me, because I couldn't find all the classes that I wanted, but also didn't just want to sign up for whatever. (But apparently you can sign up for a bunch and then you can drop the classes even after the semester abroad has started). I was nervous about this whole thing all summer, but it all turned out okay once I was at UVIC and the same goes for every other exchange student I knew at UVIC.
registration_help: In the time before arrival you were able to email the office at UVIC, but this wasn't very helpful to me because of the 9 hour time difference. What was most helpful was actually arriving in Victoria and visiting the exchange office in the week before classes officially started.
registration_success: I didn't register for the classes that I initially wanted, but upon arrival I was able to enroll in classes that fulfilled the requirements I had for classes at UCPH.
registration_advice: The exchange office at UVIC is very helpful and if I was to redo it, I would maybe ask them if they would be available to do a teams-call with me, instead of emailing back and forth. Otherwise, try your best in the online system (UVIC will send information about how it works) and then if all else fails, just wait until you arrive and they will help you.
course_level: All of my courses were 2nd-year level courses (and this you can tell by the number at the beginning of the course number, eg 220, 281)
teaching_comparison: Class 1: lectures with a professor (200 students) + seminars with a teachers assistant (30 students) Class 2: lectures with a professor (200 students) Class 3: seminars with a professor (20 students) Class 4: seminars with a professor (50 students) Class 5: seminars with an Indigenous knowledge keeper (6 students)
courses_enrolled: COM220 Organizational Behavior SOCI281 Sociology of Gender ED-D219 Introduction to Indigenous Approaches to Helping and Healing ED-D203 Leadership Theory and Practice PSYC201 Research Methods in Psychology
recommended_courses: I recommend any courses on Indigenous teachings and history (these can be found in a variety of faculties). These classes are incredibly unique, as they aren't taught globally, and the land on which the University of Victoria stands is connected deeply to Indigenous history and present time. There is a First Nations House in which most of these classes are taught, and it is one of the most beautiful places on campus. The teachers and professors that are teaching these classes are knowledgeable, kind and engaged, and I can't recommend it enough!
unexpected_costs: My rent was 880CAD, but every month there was a wifi+hydro+gas bill added, which was unpredictable. I also paid for membership in clubs at UVIC (climbing, kayaking, surfing, spinning etc.), as well as trips to other places in Canada, such as ski, camping and surf trips (which I couldn't budget for before, because I didn't know what trips I would go on).
cost_comparison: Groceries were way more expensive than I had accounted for. And the books and bus-pass were more expensive as well, but I was able to find used books/online versions and I had access to a bike (which meant I didn't want to buy the semester bus-pass, but paid pr bus ride).
activities_available: The clubs at UVIC are such a good opportunity to be social, go on trips and be active. I highly recommend joining the UVIC whitewater rafting kayak club, they did fun trips and social events. There was also a climbing club (with climbing once a week) that was fun. There was a surf club that did trips, but the sign up for these was hard and they sort of expected you to be a little better than just a beginner (but it was fun to go on the trip anyways). There is also a ski club, but it only does trips in the spring semester. There was a bunch of intramural teams (football, volleyball, basketball, ultimate frisbee, handball) that are fun to join. There is also the university gym (CARSA) that has good training facilities, and offers team training sessions such as spinning (really fun!).
activities_recommended: The clubs at UVIC are such a good opportunity to be social, go on trips and be active. I highly recommend joining the UVIC whitewater rafting kayak club, they did fun trips and social events. There was also a climbing club (with climbing once a week) that was fun. There was a surf club that did trips, but the sign up for these was hard and they sort of expected you to be a little better than just a beginner (but it was fun to go on the trip anyways). There is also a ski club, but it only does trips in the spring semester. There was a bunch of intramural teams (football, volleyball, basketball, ultimate frisbee, handball) that are fun to join. There is also the university gym (CARSA) that has good training facilities, and offers team training sessions such as spinning (really fun!).
weekend_recommendations: I recommend going to Tofino to camp with friends and surf or kayak, as well as do some hikes. I also recommend going to Strathcona Nationalpark, especially in late-spring to early-fall. I also recommend going to the Islands around Victoria, such as Hornby, Denman, Saltspring. It is pretty easy as well to do weekend trips to Seattle and Vancouver, which are accessible by ferry. There are also day trips from Victoria, such as Goldstream Provincial Park, Sooke Potholes and East Sooke Regional Park, and then the Juan De Fuca Coastline is amazing, with beaches such as China Beach, Botanical Beach, Sombrio, and Mystic Beach.
culture_adjustment: It was fairly easy, because there was no language barrier. My roommates were good at explaining things and answering any questions I had, and the Canadians are super nice!
socializing_tips: I would join clubs at UVIC, they are usually run by local students, and they are very social students.
cultural_challenges: I would say the only challenging thing to me, was that the students were generally very young, because they start university at an earlier age than Danish students usually do. This meant that I could have classes with 17 year-olds.
culture_appreciated: Canadians are nice and genuinely show interest in you, if you show interest in them. Bus drivers are kind and let everyone on the bus, all the staff at the university wanted to help you always, baristas at coffee shops talked to you about your day. If you meet someone you would love to get to know better, invite them for a coffee, a walk, a cold dip and they will most likely say yes! I have met some wonderful Canadian friends this way:)
top3_advice: The exchange office will help you, they are super nice! Sign up for clubs and extracurricular activities (especially if you don't live with canadian roommates)! And lastly, try your best to find off-campus housing with roommates, this will help you socially <3
other_useful_info: most clubs "operate" on instagram, it can be a good idea to already look through UVIC's instagram to find clubs that you are interested in and keep up with their activities.
most_rewarding: Meeting wonderful people, genuine people that are my good friends now, and experiencing the beautiful nature in Canada. Victoria and Vancouver Island are exceptional!
greatest_challenge: the biggest challenge was actually before, because I couldn't get my classes to workout, I was very very very nervous about this all summer. But everything worked out in the end, especially once I arrived in Victoria and could ask the exchange office for help.
other_comments: In Victoria you need two pieces of ID when you are buying alcoholic beverages in a bar/store/restaurant. This has to be one picture ID (passport, drivers license) and the second piece just needs your name (credit card, UVIC student card). The legal drinking age is 19.

crucial_aspects: I have always wanted to go on an exchange. I went to Vancouver a few years ago and fell in love with the city, so when I had the opportunity to study and live on Vancouver island so close to the nature and the surroundings I knew I had to go.
info_ease: University of Victoria was great about introducing all of the exchange students and we were given a lot of information and help if needed in the first couple days.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any. I found the most difficult thing to be the pre requisite applications for applying for different courses as they were often denied on small things.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Almost all courses have prerequisites (at least the science ones I had).
registration_help: Emails to the exchange team at UVic.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Look into all the prerequisites and be prepared to argue that you do have the right qualifications lining up with these.
course_level: They were maybe comparative to first or second year courses at KU. (I took third and fourth year UVic courses)
teaching_comparison: Almost all the focus was on the lectures. Not a lot of reading material prior to lectures, if any. And they focused a lot on attendance. As in it would be difficult to pass the class if not show up, as most of the material would be the lecture slide and information said in class. Even to a point where one of the lectures would leave out words on the slide so you would only get the information if you showed up to class.
courses_enrolled: MICR303 - Immunology BIOL459 - Human microbial diseases BIOL465 - The Molecular basis of cancer ANTH358 - Biology of human skeletal variability
recommended_courses: Human microbial diseases was a super interesting course, but the professor was a bit confusing and the slides very overwhelming. But if you are able to overlook this, the professor is super motivated to teach this information.
unexpected_costs: The cost of food. The food prices in Canada are extremely high at the moment.
cost_comparison: Groceries were very expensive.
activities_available: A lot of different options.
activities_recommended: I didn't really participate in any non-academic activities the university did. I went to a few smaller events they planned, but did not participate in any clubs or such.
weekend_recommendations: Hiking and enjoying the nature. UVic is the perfect place to go if you love nature and the outdoors, just a short walk from the beach and beautiful scenery.
culture_adjustment: Easy, Canadians are super friendly and are happy to include you in stuff.
socializing_tips: Go to the local pubs. I met one of my best friends from the exchange just a random night at the pub. He's Canadian and then showed us all the hidden local spots and hikes. Just be open when meeting new people, Canadians are the friendliest people ever!
cultural_challenges: Not really anything.
culture_appreciated: The openness and friendliness of Canadian people. Always happy to help and be there if you need anything.
top3_advice: 1) Be open the first couple of introduction days, join everything you have the energy for. The people you bond with these days are likely to be your friends the rest of the exchange. 2) Enjoy the nature, get to know someone with a car and go see stuff beyond Victoria on the island. 3) Be prepared for the course selection, make sure you can argue that you have qualifications for the courses you want.
other_useful_info: Just enjoy it and take every opportunity that comes your way.
most_rewarding: The friends I made. And getting to go outside of my comfort zone being entirely on my own like this for the first time.
greatest_challenge: Having to get through everything on my own, challenging and rewarding.

crucial_aspects: Opleve Canada og naturen der.
info_ease: Det var nemt nok.
arrival_assistance: Der var nogle intro-dage for udvekslingsstuderende som var gode og oplysende.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: De fag jeg havde fået forhåndsgodkendt fra KU fik jeg på UVIC. Jeg valgte dem, hvor skemaet hang bedst sammen, og sørgede for at have fri om fredagen. Vær obs på at alle udvekslingsstuderende bliver indskrevet på Social Science fakultet uanset studieretning, men det har intet at gøre med hvilke fag du kan vælge. Der kan man frit vælge fra alle fakulteter.
registration_help: De har en enhed på UVIC der kun står for udvekslingsstuderende, og de er super hjælpsomme og svarer hurtigt på mails.
registration_success: Jeg fik dem alle. I starten havde jeg 5 kurser af 1,5 unit pr. kursus (7,5 ects), og så prøvede jeg dem alle af i den første uge, og droppede derefter 1, så jeg kun havde 4 kurser tilbage (i alt 30 ects). Det vil jeg klart anbefale at gøre. Registrér for lidt ekstra kurser og prøv dem af og se hvad de kræver, derefter hop af nogle af dem. Det er meget normalt at gøre derovre inden for den første måned.
registration_advice: Søg om forhåndsgodkendelse hos KU tidligt, så du har god tid til at søge videre, hvis der skulle være nogle komplikationer eller du har brug for at indhente dokumentation.
course_level: Havde tre 1. års kurser og et 3. års kursus.
teaching_comparison: Meget det samme. En del forelæsninger og nogle fag med labs (øvelsestimer). Største forskel er, at de har midterms og flere afleveringer løbende som også tæller for den endelige karakter. Dermed er final exam ikke nødvendigvis afgørende for om man består faget.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Health Information Science Introduction to Nutrition: Concepts and Controversies Social Determinants of Health Personal Health, Wellness and Potential
recommended_courses: De var alle fine nok. Social Determinants of Health var et online fag, som gjorde at jeg kun havde 2,5 dage på skolen, hvilket gjorde mit skema rimelig fleksibelt og mulighed for masser af fritid.
unexpected_costs: Ikke rigtig nogle. Man får af vide på forhånd, at man SKAL have en sundhedsforsikring igennem uni, så den betaler man for når man kommer derover.
cost_comparison: Ture/oplevelser - her sparede jeg ikke! Det er klar der jeg brugte flest penge. Det er lidt dyrere at handle i supermarkeder ift. i DK, men hvis man handler i Walmart, kan man stadig leve nogenlunde billigt.
activities_available: Der findes alle slags clubs på UVIC. Det er bare med at undersøge og deltage i noget der interesserer en.
activities_recommended: Tag på ture, meld dig ind i nogle clubs.
weekend_recommendations: Udforsk øen. Lej en bil på Turo og kør rundt på øen og de omkringliggende øer og byer.
culture_adjustment: Ret nemt, de er søde.
socializing_tips: Vær åben og nysgerrig.
cultural_challenges: Canadiere er enormt søde, åbne og hjælpsomme. En stor kontrast til det danske folkefærd.
culture_appreciated: Venlighed og naturen.
top3_advice: 1. Lad vær med at spare på oplevelser og ture. 2. Tag det semi chill med skolen. Canadiere er generelt ret seriøse omkring deres skole og læser meget, men de har også nogle andre forudsætninger. Så lad vær med at blive skræmt af det. Lav tingene, men husk og slappe af og nyde alt det rundt om i stedet. 3. Bo tæt på uni frem for tæt på downtown. Der er masser af smuk natur og strande omkring uni, og downtown er kun en bustur væk, så det er nemt at komme derind.
other_useful_info: Spar penge op, så du ikke skal sige nej til ture og oplevelser. En bil er nærmest et must for at rejse rundt på øen og andre steder i Canada, så lej en igennem Turo eller Evo (begge billige), eller køb en billig en selv. Evt. connect med andre danskere der også skal afsted til samme universitet og snak med dem omkring diverse ting inden afrejse.
most_rewarding: At opleve de forskellige årstider i Canada og bare deres natur. Canada har ALT!
greatest_challenge: Helt klart at tage kurser på engelsk. Det var godt for mig at forbedre mit engelsk. Og selvfølgelig at være væk fra familie og venner derhjemme.

crucial_aspects: I høj grad naturen i Canada og på øen, men også at det var et engelsk talende land
info_ease: Ja, der var rigtig mange online info møder inden ankomst
arrival_assistance: Jeg missede desværre intro dagene, men de holder en del intro arrangementer for udvekslingsstuderende. Jeg var heldigvis kommet i kontant udvekslingsstuderende som hjalp mig de første par dag med at finde rundt osv
arrival_comments: Tror det var godt. Som sagt missede jeg selv intro, men vil anbefale folk at tage til det for både at få info om skolen og for at møde andre
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Man skal først få godkendt af universitetet om du lever op til kravene til faget før du overhovedet kan søge det. Det kan godt tage lidt tid at samle al den nødvendige info. Derefter får man en dato og et tidspunkt for hvornår man skal søge selve fagene. Synes det var lidt forvirrende at finde rundt i, men endte med at få alle de fag jeg gerne vil have.
registration_help: Der er en kontakt person på universitet som svarede godt og hurtigt
registration_success: Der var mange af de kurser jeg gerne ville have som jeg opdagede kun var i forårs semesteret, eller foregik på Bamfield Marine Science Centre som ligger en sjat timer væk fra universitet, og som krævede at man tog alle 5 kurser som de udbød på samme tid. Dog fik jeg alle de kurser som jeg gerne ville have i efterårs semesteret.
registration_advice: Brug tid på at gennemskue systemet, danne sig et overblik over hvornår kurserne bliver udbudt og finde vigtige deadlines.
course_level: Jeg havde 3 kurser som var relativt nemme, med en overskuelig arbejdsbyrde. Dog havde jeg et fag, animal behaviour, som var meget krævende og var et rigtig højt niveau. Derudover var professorens undevisningstil ikke lige min kop te, da der var rigtig meget hurtig og mumlende oplæsning af abstracts fra videskabelige artikler.
teaching_comparison: Jeg havde mange forelæsninger med tilhørende laboratorie timer. En del opgaver og midterms undervejs som også talte med i den afsluttende karakter, så mine eksamener talte imellem 35-50% af min afsluttende karakter. Havde et online fag, som jeg både kunne se live eller efter, som jeg var rigtig glad for.
courses_enrolled: Whale conservation and ecology, biodiversity of BC, Animal Behaviour og Ocean and atmosphere
recommended_courses: Whale conservation and ecology og Ocean and atmosphere var begge virkelig spændende fag, og som var nemme at følge med i. Jeg havde en rigtig fed lærer i biodiversity of BC, men selve faget var lidt rodet og dårligt struktureret, men er stadig glad for den viden jeg fik omkring øen og hele BC.
unexpected_costs: Ingen. Brugte generelt mange penge på at leje bil, surfboards, camping osv.
cost_comparison: At handle ind er dyrt, og biler er billige at leje
activities_available: Der er rigtig mange klubber og sports tilbud på skolen, som er en god måde at møde nye mennesker på og komme på eventyr.
activities_recommended: Climbing club, outdoor club og camping shenanigans
weekend_recommendations: Camping, surfe i Tofino, som kan gøres hele året rundt. Tage på vandreture. Whale watching, kan både gøre fra Victoria og andre steder på øen. Generelt udforske hele øen, der er så meget smuk natur overalt, og vil virkelig anbefale at leje bil igennem Turo. Derudover tag i biffen på Uvic, brætspils cafe i downtown, svømmehal og drik en øl på nogle af de hyggelige barer med live musik i byen.
culture_adjustment: Alle lokale er rigtig søde og meget høflige. Synes det tog lidt tid at føle sig hjemme, men synes generet at det var nemt at tilpasse sig til kulturen.
socializing_tips: Meld dig ind i klubber, og bo med lokale. Tag til forskellige arrangementer på skolen eller i klubberne. Synes det var svært at blive venner med folk til forelæsninger.
cultural_challenges: Synes ikke der var en bestemt udfordring. Man skal huske høfligheden, og at man ikke må drikke alkohol i offentligheden.
culture_appreciated: At canadiere er så søde og høflige, og deres kærlighed til naturen
top3_advice: Midterms og afleveringer, generelt skolen, fyldte en del mere end jeg lige var forberedt på. Jeg ville i høj grad tage til intro dagene, da jeg synes det var lidt svært at komme ind i det hele fordi jeg havde misset dem. Heldigvis var jeg kommet med i en Facebook gruppe hjemmefra med en gruppe andre danske udvekslingstuderende, som jeg endte med at blive rigtig gode venner med, og nogle venskaber som fortsætter derhjemme. Meld dig ind i klubberne på skolen. Det er en genial måde at møde folk på, både lokale og andre udvekslingstuderende. De planlægger også tit arrangementer eller ture man kan deltage i.
other_useful_info: nej
most_rewarding: De søde menneske som jeg har mødt, og alle de vilde ture vi tog på.
greatest_challenge: At rejse til et nyt land langt væk fra ens venner og familie, og få skabt sig en hverdag. Det kan godt føles en smule ensomt og svært specielt i starten. Derudover synes jeg det var lidt svært at jonglere skolen og alle de ting jeg gerne ville opleve.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to a place with easy access to nature where i could hike, camp and surf. I wanted to go to a university that had access to the ocean with good marine and ocean courses.
info_ease: It was pretty easy. The university keeps you updated on deadines and information through emails on your university profil on the website.
arrival_assistance: There are multiple info sessions and campus tours to give you information about the campus and the resources available on campus and events to mingle with other exchange students
arrival_comments: Go the the events in the beginning - it is a great place to meet new friends.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You received an email with a timeslot and date for registration and then you received an email and link to a thorough guide on how to register.
registration_help: Emails with reminders and guides on how to.
registration_success: I found out quite late that a lot of the marine courses that I wanted to take, could not be taken on the campus in Victoria but only as part of a bigger program in Bamfield and the rest of the marine courses were in the spring. After finding the new classes I wanted, I could get into all my classes.
registration_advice: Make sure to sign up for your classes in your given timeslot to make sure to get at spot on the classes you want. Sign up for 1 or 2 extra classes if you end up changing your mind or want to try out some different classes the first weeks of class and then decide after trying them out. Most students do this, as you freely can drop courses for the first few weeks of classes.
course_level: I only took 300-level courses. The level of the courses I took were quite easy, although this really depends on the course and is not the same for every course.
teaching_comparison: You are graded and evaluated throughout the semester. I liked it this way, as you were forced to participate along the way and the load during the exams in the end was therefore much smaller.
courses_enrolled: AE303 Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques. ES 361 The Biodiversity of British Columbia. EOS 350 Understanding the Oceans.
recommended_courses: My favourite course was definitely EOS 350: Understanding the Oceans! In general UVic has a really good Earth and Ocean science program and I believe and have heard that many of their other courses in this field are also good at UVic. EOS 350 was both new stuff to me as a biologist because is started with ocean earth science and later a good blend with biology. The whole course was really interesting to me and the workload was not to big. The exams were all open book, take home exams. ES 361 The Biodiversity of British Columbia was a quite fluffy course as it is not a science course. The professor is really nice! The lectures were mostly just talk about different species on a fluffy basis. There was some really interesting stuff as well, but it was mostly just scrapping the surface. It is a smaller class(30-40 people I think) with some cool group projects which included data collection through inaturalist outside of class which I enjoyed a lot! AE303 Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques The course load on this one was bigger than I thought. You can tell that this is a university course with deadlines and requirements. There a quite a few assignments and if you have never done much ceramics like I hadn’t, then be prepared to spend maaany hours in the studio outside of class to practice wheeling and to finish assignments. It ended up being my most stressfull course at times, but also a nice place to be able to go anytime of day to work on your projects and zone out.
unexpected_costs: Groceries were expensive
cost_comparison: Groceries were more expensive. A lot of sweet treats were cheaper than in Copenhagen. Coffee at cafes was cheaper than in Copenhagen.
activities_available: There are all the clubs you could possibly imagine. They have a club for everything!
activities_recommended: Climbing club! It is a great way to meet people and make new friends. Camping Shenanigans - camping club that goes on trips - great people! Surf club - they do fun trips to Tofino (hard to get onto a trip, but keep trying - we found that the trips later in the semester were easier to get a spot on)
weekend_recommendations: Explore the island - it has so much to offer! Go hiking and camping! There are so many amazing hikes and mountains on the island. Go surfing in Tofino and by Jordan River or Sombrio. Go see a hockey game. Go tidepooling (the club: UVic rockhoppers goes sometimes). Lucky bar on Mondays.
culture_adjustment: It felt quite easy, people are really friendly and very open, even just strangers you meet on the street.
socializing_tips: Join some clubs and join some club trips - great place to meet local students. I met some good friends through the climbing club.
cultural_challenges: There is more homelessness.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness and openness of everyone. People are very inclusive. The outdoors/nature mindset that everyone has.
top3_advice: 1. If you have the possibility to come before and travel a bit - do it! 2. Join a club, go on a club trip 3. Look into the courses, check what others think of the courses(here on mobility) and take a few ekstra courses from the start so you can test them out a little before being stuck with them.
other_useful_info: Get Revolut to avoid the fee normal banks have for every purchase. Tips for car rental: the app Turo works well and is cheap. The same with EVO carshare: Get an EVO account early - it takes some time to process your drivers licens, but it is good to have.
most_rewarding: The friends I made and the nature: insane views and hiking/camping trips that I went on with friends.
greatest_challenge: Especially early in the semester: Not having the people around me that know me and that I would usually go to when having a hard time.

crucial_aspects: The Subjects that UVIC offered were very interesting, and opened new oppertunities to try different areas of my study. The location also played a big part. As well as it being an English speaking country
overall_comments: It was amazing!! i recommend it to everyone, even just victoria as a city to visit on Vacation.
info_ease: quite easy. you get a Schedule for the International welcome and i suggest you take part in as much as you think is relevant. some of it is very repetetive but you meet the international students who end up becoming your friends.
arrival_assistance: They have a Center for internal students on campus who are really sweet and ready to help!
arrival_comments: I did not need any help but they were available!
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It was amazing!! i recommend it to everyone, even just victoria as a city to visit on Vacation.
registration_process: all is online, where you can create a mock schedule and plan it out. You then get a Time slot where you can registrer. this time slot is over 2 weeks so you might be lucky to get an earlier date or a later one, and this also influences if you get on the waiting list for some courses. HOWEVER... it is not impossible to get off the waiting lists as a lot of people drop courses.
registration_help: you can mail the international center (i think) but a lot of people send mails, so it takes some time to get a reply.
registration_success: I was very successfull i got all the courses i wanted. i Also had a very early registration date, so none of the courses were filled up when i registered.
registration_advice: If there is a course you REALLY want, then send en email to the professor directly, they have the power to overwrite the prerqruisites.
academics_comments: It was amazing!! i recommend it to everyone, even just victoria as a city to visit on Vacation.
course_level: I had 1 x 200 Level, 2 x 300 level and 1 x 400 Level. the 200-300 were good. the 400 was difficult. However... if i had really wanted a good grade in the 400 i could have done it, but i prioriticed other things. The level of difficultness in generel i would say is a bit easier than copenhagen, but not so much that you can relax completely.
teaching_comparison: there is more lectures, where someone speaks for 1,5 hours and you write notes. There is A LOT of midterm and quizes during the semester that count for 15-25% of your grade, so you dont just have a final exam that counts 100% of your grade. This means also that when you reach the final quiz/project or whatever you already know if you have passed 75% of the course. A lot of the finals were online as well. Handing in an online presentation or an essay or a quiz.
courses_enrolled: "AE303A Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques" & "AE307 Printmaking" & "BIOC403 Biochemistry of Signal Transduction" & "ENSH240 Introduction to a Major Author: Taylor Swift"
recommended_courses: The ceramics was super fun and casual, but requires a lot of extra time and work. This was probably my most demanding course during my semester. Printmaking was also fun but kind of difficult if you cannot draw and it also requires extra time outside of class but not as much as Ceramics. ENSH240 was a phenomenal course, even if you are not a taylor swift fan. The course is analysing lyrics and talking about references to old litterature, poems and songs! (Name redacted) is the best professor i have ever had! so i highly recommend this course! BIOC403 was very difficult. and the teacher speaks very fast. i also dont have a background in biochemistry so it was even more difficult. I also had "natural hazards" course but dropped it in September. Be aware there are classes with up to 300 people in it. it is not the greatest.
unexpected_costs: Tipping and taxes are added AFTER the you see the price.
cost_comparison: the groceries are SO expensive. Even more expensive than copenhagen!! so expensive! especially the fruit and vegetable. eating out is also cheaper than CPH. there are a lot of cafes on campus but their stuff is quite expensive. go to the Grad House (even if you are not a Grad student) and get cheap (ish) food there! they also have board games and beer.
activities_available: All kinds of sports, intermurals, clubs for everyone! check out their list of clubs online.
activities_recommended: I found it difficult to find time for all the clubs, but go to the clubs and unions days!
weekend_recommendations: Visit all over the island! Tofino, port alberni, strathcona, campbell river! also the golf islands are amazing for a day trip! Saturna, salt spring, pender and galliano! but you need to rent car! i Went to vancouver for a couple of days and it was Not as cozy and fun as Victoria. I recommend spending all your time on the Island while you are there. as there is so much to see! Be aware that some things are better during specific months. you can see the salmon jumping in the rivers in November and going to campell river around the same time then you might see a bear grabbing the salmon!
culture_adjustment: It was kind of easy. The small talk is a big change. It is in generel very different but also kind of the same. it is good to talk to other Danes about the experience because it is a little weird, but everyone is very friendly
socializing_tips: Small talk is big, but that does not mean that you are friends. People might say "lets get coffee" but you will not actually get the coffee unless you really arrange it on purpose.
cultural_challenges: The small talk, it is very shallow and strange. There are A LOT of homeless and drug addicts downtown! it was very shocking the first couple of times going downtown after dark, it felt very unsafe. but just try not to be around Pandora Avenue after dark and then nothing will happen, i have not heard of anyone who had a bad experience with the homeless or addicts, so just leave them alone and then they leave you alone.
culture_appreciated: The coffee culture. there are many cafes and going for coffee is a big thing! the coffee is cheaper than CPH as well. How easy it is to start a conversation with random people. people are super interested in talking. also saying hello and thank you to the bus driver is very nice. Their thrift stores are REALLY nice! and cheap! so if this is something you like to do in CPH, you can look forward to it in Victoria. i recommend Value village, Broad view united, Beacon hill and WIN. aswell as going to Sydney and brentwood bay they have a lot.
top3_advice: GET A CREDIT CARD! otherwise you cannot rent a car! and if you want to go on a trip you NEED a car! The busses only take EXACT cash or UMO buss card! in the first couple of days make sure you have coins on you! Get Rain pants, Rain coats and Rain boots! IT RAINS!!!
other_useful_info: The full time canadian students pay for their buss passes in the tuition but i think 75% of all student have a car, so they dont use it. if you can find a canadian student who havent activated their buss pass you can pay them 50$ or something for it. then you dont have to pay 130$ for it as it costs for international students.
most_rewarding: Meeting the people and experiences the nature. The nature is HUGE. you know that before you go but it is crazy to see in real life! it is so beautiful and there are deer everywhere! in the gardens and on campus, everywhere! It was so much fun!
greatest_challenge: adjusting to the culture. but after 3 months everything becomes natural, so it is sad to go home after 4 months.
other_comments: GO! DO IT! it was so much fun! it was wonderfull and the people were amazing. the food was not the greates but it does not matter. go try all the things you want to do before November/december as it RAINS! it rains so much! 10x as much as Denmark! dont be fooled, i thought it would not be that bad and they were dramatic as we come from a rainy country, But this is on another level! they get asmospheric rivers, which is crazy!

crucial_aspects: I have some Canadian friends who recommended BC for the nature
info_ease: Easy! Uvic sends out a really helpful email with all the information needed.
arrival_assistance: The university is really good at providing help when you arrive. There are tutors and guides, and welcome events with tours of the school. Everything is very straightforward.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The process is really easy and you'll get an email from UVic with all the information
registration_help: ICS exchange team, tutors and informationcenter - all really helpfuld and friendly
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted without any problems. During the first week I wanted to change some of my courses, and it was super quick and easy. I emailed the professors of the courses I wanted to switch to, and they handled the rest for me. Even for courses I didn’t have the prerequisites for, I just wrote that I was interested in joining, and I was given a spot
registration_advice: Send emails! All the professors are super kind and helpful.
course_level: The courses are definitely easier than what I’m used to at the UCPH. I didn’t go for the academic challenge, and I chose my classes based on wanting a lot of free time to travel. So I chose online courses or courses that were recorded, so I could watch the lectures whenever I wanted. However, I do know that a few of my friends chose courses that were much more demanding than what they were used to.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style is quite different from UCPH. I’m used to attending lectures, keeping up, and then only stressing during the exam period, where I basically shut myself in and study nonstop. At UVic, the structure is very different, with lots of assignments and midterms throughout the semester that count toward a large part of the final grade. At first, I found it a bit annoying, but I actually ended up liking it because it took a lot of pressure off the final exam, which was really nice. I had completed so much of the required work during the semester that technically, I didn’t even need to pass my final exams to pass the courses
courses_enrolled: ES 361 The Biodiversity of British Columbia AE 303A Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques ENSH 240 Introduction to a Major Author GEOG 303 Conservation and ecology of Whales
recommended_courses: I was really burnt out from studying when I left, so I ended up switching to courses that weren’t very related to my degree - which was amazing! Ceramics turned out to be my most demanding course because I had to spend a lot of time in the studio working on assignments, but it was an incredible creative break and I highly recommend it. I also took an English course, and I’ve never experienced anything like it. My professor was absolutely phenomenal, and I wish everyone could take a class with him! In general, UVic offers a lot of courses outside the usual academic fields, and I definitely recommend taking advantage of that
unexpected_costs: The mandatory university insurance is expensive, and it’s a struggle to get money refunded if you don’t have a Canadian bank account
cost_comparison: Food is more expensive than what I thought
activities_available: As stereotypical as it sounds, there’s a club for absolutely everything.
activities_recommended: I bought a car in the first week, and that’s definitely my biggest recommendation! While it’s possible to get around by bike or bus, I found it to be a bit tricky and honestly, biking can be pretty scary in Victoria at times. Having a car made life so much easier. We used it for everything: grocery shopping (which is a bit far by bike or bus), exploring the island, and even heading to the mainland. Used cars are really cheap on Marketplace, so in the end, three of us bought one each for our whole group of friends, making it much easier to go on trips together. It turned out to be a big win for the clubs at UVic as well, since we could contribute by providing transportation for surf trips and other group activities.
weekend_recommendations: An absolute must is the trip to the mainland, driving from Banff to Jasper! It’s hands down one of the most beautiful journeys I’ve ever taken. Make sure to take a weekend trip to Salt Spring Island - don’t miss the Saturday market. Tofino is a top spot for surfing! It’s pricey, but definitely worth it. While you're there, also check out Ucluelet, which is nearby and equally amazing. Strathcona National Park is stunning! If you’re into hiking, tackle either King’s Peak or the Landslide Trail. On the way back, be sure to stop at Campbell River to swim with the salmon during salmon season - it’s a pretty unique experience. Telegraph Cove, located on the northern part of Vancouver Island, is a tiny, picturesque town. The waters around there are preserved for whales and orcas, so there’s an abundance of marine life. I spent a month driving around the island before the semester started, and while it was beautiful, I wouldn’t recommend going farther north than Port McNeill - there’s not much to do beyond that point. Victoria itself has a bunch of cozy bars and cool hangouts. We loved the board game café, and when we went out, we went to Darcies or Lucky’s (they’ve got the best music on Mondays, which is when everyone goes out).
culture_adjustment: As soon as you get used to everyone wanting to small talk, it's really easy.
socializing_tips: Canadians are very inviting, so don't hesitate to say yes - they do actually mean it
cultural_challenges: Around Pandora Avenue, there are quite a few homeless people, which can be a bit shocking at first. However, I never had any uncomfortable experiences with anyone - it was more the initial surprise of seeing so many in one area.
culture_appreciated: The Canadian openness <3 Everyone is kind and friendly
top3_advice: Get a place to live as soon as possible! Take every opportunity to get out of the city and into nature - it’s absolutely incomparable. When I started my exchange, my goal was to meet people from outside of Denmark. We had a group of 16 Danes at UVic, and honestly, the best thing that happened to me was meeting them. I met so many amazing Canadians and exchange students from around the world, but I’m incredibly grateful for the friendships I made with fellow Danes.
other_useful_info: Don't be afraid to ask
most_rewarding: Exchange can be tough - so much fun, but also really challenging at times. That’s why having friends who speak the same language and understand exactly what you’re going through is so valuable. The fact that we can reunite back in Denmark and relive all those memories together is, without a doubt, the highlight of this journey for me.
greatest_challenge: Something personal happened in my family back home. It was really difficult not being there, and not being able to help or talk about it with an ocean and a nine-hour time difference between us. I’m very grateful that I had a strong support network during the exchange who helped me through it.

crucial_aspects: The fact that the university is known for having a good environmental studies programme and the amount of interesting classes I could take there. It was also important for me to be able to experience and explore another kind of nature than I'm used to and the possibilities for that are many on Vancouver Island!
info_ease: It was easy. They provide you with all the information in e-mails well in time and if you're in doubt about something they will answer fairly quickly.
arrival_assistance: I received e-mails also after my arrival. Apart from that I joined the welcome activities for international students, that was very helpful! They show you around and make sure to facilitate meetings between between students which in my opinion is important for a good exchange stay.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I filled out a registration form in spring (spring right before the autumn of my exchange) and got my Letter of Acceptance in May. Then I could start looking for classes. Registration for classes was in start/mid June.
registration_help: Zoom-meetings, e-mailing and a website that provides step-by-step guides for registration.
registration_success: I had some trouble getting the classes I wanted because I had to replace some compulsory classes in my home university. It ended up working out, and I got some other classes instead.
registration_advice: Be patient! And take it one step at a time.
course_level: My impression was that the level of the courses was generally lower than in my home university. We worked differently though, there was a lot of small assignments throughout the semester, so I'd say that the effort it takes is about the same.
teaching_comparison: More work throughout the semester and more focus on details and remembering a lot of texts at the same time.
courses_enrolled: Biodiversity and Conservation Biology, Environmental Management, Ethnoecology and Introduction to Ceramics Wheels and Hand Techniques
recommended_courses: Ethnoecology was great! You learn a lot about the First Nations of Canada and the way they have stewarded and taken care of the land. Environmental management was also great, the professor is super nice and the class is very broad and comes around many interesting topics.
unexpected_costs: Groceries are quite expensive on the island
cost_comparison: A bit more expensive
activities_available: All kinds of clubs ranging from sports clubs, craft clubs, hiking/outdoor clubs, academic clubs, religious clubs, etc.
activities_recommended: Join Clubs and Unions Day at the beginning of the semester. That's a great way to experience just how many clubs there actually are and also to meet the people behind the clubs. I joined the Ecological Restoration club and went a trip with them and met the nicest people. The outdoor club is also cool!
weekend_recommendations: Rent a car and go out to explore the island! It's cheap to rent a car and easy to get around. Join clubs and be open to meeting new people! Don't go alone! Nature is different over there.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, Canadians are super welcoming and kind.
socializing_tips: Be brave and open. It's a cliché but it works: Put yourself out there!
cultural_challenges: Only small differences as the humor. But you will quickly adjust.
culture_appreciated: The openness and that they're always willing to help you. I experienced this throughout my whole stay.
top3_advice: Participate in the welcoming activities for international students! Remember to relax sometimes :)
other_useful_info: Not other that the above mentioned.
most_rewarding: The people I met there! Will cherish that forever
greatest_challenge: Balancing resting and exploring and academic work.

crucial_aspects: I sought a combination of interesting academic opportunities and a location that excited me. Victoria in Canada definitely worked for me in that regard.
overall_comments: More details below. In short - it was fantastic.
info_ease: The social elements of the introduction were really good, with lots of opportunities to connect and make friends. There were these intro days where there were presentations, icebreaker events, and so on. When it came to actually going to school, that was a bit trickier. We didn't get an introduction to the platforms we were going to use to find information on classes and how attending classes actually worked. Weirdly the international student center weren't really able to help with school technical stuff, like changing classes, but could instead only help with visa stuff and social arrangements.
arrival_assistance: I just got the emails and then we figured stuff out as it came.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: More details below. In short - it was fantastic.
registration_process: UVIC will send you some emails that guide you on how to register. It's important to send the registration application for every course - even the ones that you think you should be able to get based on what you are studying. If it's not a first year course, i'd send an application to take that course just to be sure.
registration_help: I made a mistake in one of my registrations and over the summer it took really long for them to get back to me about the issue.
registration_success: I ended up getting all the courses i wanted, but it was a lot of work.
registration_advice: In the full list of courses, some are only available in fall and some only in spring. Also take 5 courses even though you just need 4, and drop the course you like the least. I took one online course - ecology and conservation of whales, and while online courses rarely work, this one was actually really good.
academics_comments: More details below. In short - it was fantastic.
course_level: Course levels are similar or maybe a little lower than Uni of CPH, but structurally very different. You have a lot more homework and stuff to turn in, all of it being graded. You can end up having grades from all the stuff you turned in is good enough for you to be able to skip the final exams.
teaching_comparison: Generally, you are guided much more through the course material, being quizzed and tested, so they know that you are doing readings and homework. UVIC has a super cool Indigenous programme that I recommend. Just be aware that you are not taught in a conventional western way - and while it can be difficult to wrap your head around, I found it super valuable.
courses_enrolled: Biodiversity of BC Geography of BC Indigenous Studies 101 Ecology and Conservation of Whales
recommended_courses: I recommend all my courses. Biodiversity of BC - great professor with some really fun projects throughout the course. One being that you have to collect iNaturalist observations. Was an easy course to get through and attending lectures was not mandatory. Geography of BC - This course with -Name Redacted- was the closest to a Danish uni course of the courses I had. There was a lot of reading and high expectations for you to understand the course material. Great course if you want to understand BC as a place. Indigenous Studies 101 - Fantastic course that challenged you to consider your privileges, perspectives, history and your role as someone contributing to science. The course is taught by -Name Redacted-, who is an Indigenous woman and matriarch. Ecology and Conservation of Whales - Fun, easy and interesting course that happened online.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Groceries are generally as expensive or more compared to Denmark. Traveling on Vancouver Island in the summer - super expensive, book stuff as far in advance as you can. Traveling in the off-season is significantly cheaper, and you don't have to book stuff way ahead of time. Do it a week or two before, ideally.
activities_available: There is pretty much everything. Taylor Swift club, Clubs for people from different countries, diving, caving, reading, knitting, dog petting, idk you name it.
activities_recommended: Bad weather: Go to downtown for: board game cafe (amazing place), axe throwing, Lucky Mondays (the night to go out in Victoria - no joke at Lucky Bar), Darcys for live music, haunted mini golf. Browse outdoor stores (MEC is the best). Boulderhouse is fun for climbing and much better than CARSA (campus climbing). You can go to the movies on Campus or downtown. Munro's books is great too. Browse Market Square. Good weather: Go to Mt. Douglas (panorama view of the city), go swimming (it's cold but safe and amazing all year), or go to East Sooke Regional Park or Goldstream (has salmon run and Indigenous traditional fishing). Run around Elk/Beaver Lake. Go on a whale watching trip (expensive but worth it 100%). Join social/sports events on campus - like frisbee on the lawn. Go surfing at Sombrio.
weekend_recommendations: Here's my priority list 1. Tofino - go surfing and camp there. Book everything (camping spot, surfboards, tours) well in advance. Ideally, 6 months before or as soon as you have a group of friends to join you. There are also group trips arranged by UVIC that go here. 2. Port Renfrew - you can go on a day trip or sleep there a couple of nights. This is where i saw a black bear and it was amazing. 3. Mt. Washington and Strathcona - Bring your best hiking gear and go on the most amazing mountainous hikes. Lots of trails starting at Strathcona Park Wilderness Centre. If you sleep out here, be experienced or bring someone who is. There are bears and mountain lions here and weather that can turn dangerous. Bring bearspray. 4. Cape Scott - super far away from Victoria, but so wild and untouched. You can surf and hike here. 5. East Sooke - close to Victoria. It's generally hard to go somewhere on that island that isn't pretty amazing. Get a car and go!!
culture_adjustment: As everyone speaks English here and are generally very friendly and helpful, I don't think you're ever going to find yourself in a bad situation here. Some things work differently, like buying alcohol or having a campfire. You'll figure it out - nothing to be stressed about.
socializing_tips: Join clubs and be open, but don't force yourself or push yourself too far. Almost every single one of my friends were exchange students or not locals and I had a fantastic time socially. Every time I felt like doing something, there was always someone who wanted to join, or there was an invite open for something. Being back home, things are much slower.
cultural_challenges: Canadians can sometimes over-promise in order to be polite and friendly. They might say we'll do this or that, but when it really comes to it, they might just have said it to be polite. So don't stress about it if it falls through
culture_appreciated: Canadians were unrelenting in their friendliness. We had someone fix a road for us on the way to Cape Scott, people sharing stories at bars, people offering to help in all kinds of ways, and actually following through. We met an older couple on a mountain, and she let us see the mountain cabin she was staying in and left beer for us + invited us to visit her home. The most extreme cases of Canadians being friendly happened when we were on trips to remote little towns, where people were eager to give tips, share stories, and help out. Be ready for friendly small talk everywhere and just embrace it and learn new things and meet people.
top3_advice: Get a car or some way to transport yourself and your friends. I bought a car after two weeks and sold it a week before I went home. It's a pretty simple process. You need a driver's license (Danish is ok - I brought an international license too, but never used it) and either CAD cash or a way to transfer money relatively quickly (I got a Canadian bank account ahead of time to make it easier). Then you find a car on FB marketplace or wherever, check the car, and go to an ICBC (state car insurance office), and they handle the transfer from the previous owner to you. You have to pay tax based on the price you pay for the car, but you can agree on a lower official sale price with the seller. I paid 5000 CAD for my car, about 1100 for taxes and insurance for 6 months, and I sold the car for 4000 CAD. You can also use Turo (private rental program) or register with EVO (do it through UVIC booths if you can and get a discount) Having a car opens up the island and lets you explore more easily.
other_useful_info: I focused on enjoying my courses, focusing on topics I enjoyed and spending less time on stuff I didn't find interesting. I got good grades with this strategy and avoided feeling stressed out and kept my energy for going on super fun group trips.
most_rewarding: Having amazing outdoor experiences with great new friends while studying unique courses in a new way.
greatest_challenge: I had 1 week where I had several projects due at the same time and was a little stressed due to that. The biggest challenge was perhaps the FOMO from all the amazing opportunities that there were too many of. Reflecting on the trip, I'm very satisfied with the things I did. So know you can't do everything and that's ok.
other_comments: All the work with signing up for courses, application processes, expensive plane tickets, and tricky housing stuff - getting through that will reward you with months of amazing experiences. I can't recommend going to Victoria enough.

crucial_aspects: I was very interested in the courses at the university’s. The location was also important to me, since I wanted to be close to nature. Then I also chose actually based on the universities webpage. I wanted to go somewhere where they were prepared for exchange students and the information was easy to find and understand.
overall_comments: I was so happy with the university, the nature around it and the many danish people I met. I really prioritised getting to know danish people, so that I would have friends to share the experience with, when I got home. This is probably the thing that I’m most grateful for.
info_ease: I think it was very easy. We got a lot of emails from the school, and I feel like we where well informed and in time.
arrival_assistance: Many information emails and meet ups with all the exchange students. So many gatherings of different kinds, so that we could get to know each other.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I was so happy with the university, the nature around it and the many danish people I met. I really prioritised getting to know danish people, so that I would have friends to share the experience with, when I got home. This is probably the thing that I’m most grateful for.
registration_process: After acceptance by Copenhagen University, we waited until May when the registration opened at the host University. Then we applied and shortly after received an email with the acceptance letter. It was very easy.
registration_help: We where in contact with the help centre for international students, and they where very helpful and quick to reply.
registration_success: I was very successful. I got all the courses that I wanted. They give you a date and time for when the registration opens, and then we were quick to sign up for the courses we wanted. We didn’t even need to hurry that much, we all got the courses we wanted.
registration_advice: Really look at the schedules for the courses before registering. In their system they have a function, where you can create your own schedules, and that was very helpful. Also, if you want as few hours a week as possible, don’t choose courses that has laboratory work. You can find all this information at Uvics website under courses.
academics_comments: I was so happy with the university, the nature around it and the many danish people I met. I really prioritised getting to know danish people, so that I would have friends to share the experience with, when I got home. This is probably the thing that I’m most grateful for.
course_level: I took third and fourth year courses. None of them were that difficult, and I was really happy with the teaching method and the material.
teaching_comparison: My courses were only based on learning from the lectures, and we had no reading homework. I was really fond of this method. Also, we had midterms and reports which was grated and counted in the final grade. This was an amazing experience. The final exam usually counted for between 30-40% of the final grade, which took a lot of pressure off us. Also, we learned everything way better, since we had to do a lot of work along the way, which also made me rember everything way better. I would hope that Copenhagen University will do it like this one day.
courses_enrolled: MICR410 - Microbiota and Human Health ES361 - The Biodiversity of British Columbia BIOL388 - Applied Molecular Biology AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics and wheel techniques
recommended_courses: Microbiota and human health were very well structured, and amazing teacher and very interesting topics. The midterms are two tat home quizzes with all aids allows, very easy. And the we had to do a research paper, which was very cool to try. Ceramics was fun and it was nice to have something different. It is a lot of work though, so don’t expect it to be easy and quickly over with.
unexpected_costs: It was really easy and cheap to rent cars for going on trips, so we ended up doing that a lot. I also feel in love with surfing, and that is a bit expensive.
cost_comparison: Grocery’s were more expensive. Takeout where less. Uber and car rentals was also cheaper than expected.
activities_available: So many clubs, you could choose every sport and every hobby. They had everything from sailing, climbing, river rafting, surfing, baking, Taylor swift, book clubs, outdoor club.
activities_recommended: Join a club, any club! It was a cool way to get to know the locals and your fellow exchange students. Especially the outdoor club did some fun stuff, but it is very popular, so don’t hesitate to sign up!
weekend_recommendations: Go around the island! Go surfing and hiking in Torino. Visit telegraph cove and Strathcona National Park in the summer. Go to salts spring island. Go to whistler and Squamish. Go to Banff National park!!! Amazing experience. Just really get around and see stuff, that is so fun. Visit Vancouver one day. Go whalewhatching!
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: Join clubs! Go to Lucky Mondays:))
cultural_challenges: They students are in general younger when they start Univeristy, so sometimes I felt a bit of an age barrier.
culture_appreciated: How respectful they were about the indigenous people and their heritage. They are very friendly and genuinely interested in what you are telling them. People are very sweet.
top3_advice: Research housing as early as possible. Do courses that has the workload that you can manage when living abroad, it can be overwhelming. Do a fun course that only exists at Uvic, that is so fun to try.
other_useful_info: You will spend more money than you think, but don’t let it put limits on you! This is a once in a lifetime experience, so do it just they way you want to!
most_rewarding: Exploring the nature of Canada and meeting my now really close danish friends.
greatest_challenge: Dealing with all your problems in a whole new setting with all new people. You will have tough days and it is really important to find someone you trust and can share with.

crucial_aspects: As I am studying biology, it was important for me to be close to nature and Vancouver Island seemed like the perfect place.
info_ease: UVic sends out tons of information, which can feel overwhelming, but in the end it was pretty easy.
arrival_assistance: Whenever I needed assistance, I just contacted the exchange team, and they responded super quickly.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: From what I understood, exchange students have priority, so you are nearly guaranteed to get the courses you want. You are given a date, after which you sign up on their website.
registration_help: Email the exchange team if you have any questions. There is a limited amount of information about the courses, so it can be a good idea to sign up for more than you need, as you can drop courses during the first two weeks
registration_success: Got everything i signed up for
registration_advice: Be more bold when picking courses. Don’t limit yourself to what you are studying at home. I loved GEOG 303 – Conservation and Ecology of Whales and ES 361 – Biodiversity of British Columbia. I also took BIOL 418 – Forest Ecology, which I loved and hated at the same time, as it was a lot of work.
course_level: I took Immunology and Forest Ecology. Both courses had a high workload, especially Forest Ecology, where there were continuous assignments and ongoing tasks throughout the term. The academic level itself was not overly difficult, but the courses required consistent effort and regular work to keep up. Conservation and Ecology of Whales and Biodiversity of British Columbia were both very fun courses and had exactly the kind of workload you want on exchange, as they allowed time to explore while still being interesting classes.
teaching_comparison: It is different because of midterms and many assignments. So even if the overall level is lower, it can still feel like a lot, as you constantly have to hand something in.
courses_enrolled: BIOL 418 – Forest Ecology MICR 303 - Immunology GEOG 303 – Conservation and Ecology of Whales ES 361 – Biodiversity of British Columbia
recommended_courses: Geog 303, ES 361
unexpected_costs: Food is really expensive, and Walmart is the only affordable grocery store.
cost_comparison: Eating out is relatively cheap compared to Denmark.
activities_available: There are many clubs, and they all seemed super fun, but I didn’t sign up for any, as they require a lot of commitment and I preferred to spend my free time exploring the island on my days off.
activities_recommended: Hiking, surfing and road trips. I spent a lot of time surfing at Jordan River, which is about an hour outside of town.
weekend_recommendations: Get lost, the island is amazing.
culture_adjustment: Canadians are very friendly and welcoming but in school it can be hard to make new local friends
socializing_tips: I joined the Fernwood run club, which is not part of the university, but people were very welcoming.
cultural_challenges: It’s not really a cultural difference, but you need a car if you want to get around the island. So try to find some friends who want to rent a car with you, or consider buying one.
culture_appreciated: People are very friendly when you’re exploring the island.
top3_advice: Joining a club makes it super easy to make friends. Don’t pick very demanding classes. You want to spend your time exploring the island. Choose classes that help you learn about the culture and nature of the island.
other_useful_info: Take advantage of the fact that you can switch classes during the first two weeks. It makes choosing classes with limited information less stressful.
most_rewarding: Being able to combine studying with experiencing a new country.
greatest_challenge: Balancing studying and exploring, especially as I picked two very demanding classes.
other_comments: Enjoy

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne finde et sted hvor jeg kunne komme ud i naturen stå på ski og surfe indenfor rimelig afstand.
info_ease: Uvic var egetnlig ret gode til at give informationer via mail, den skal man huske og tjekke løbende, hvis man har spørgsmål så er det en god ide at ringe de sidder klar i alle dagtimerne til at tage telefonen og svare på spørgsmål
arrival_assistance: Vi havde nogle introdage for international studerende, de var lidt kedelige men meget gode til lige at komme rundt og se skolen og møde nogle mennesker
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Når du er blevet optaget foregår processen over mail, du skal lige tjekke du får en officiel "du er optaget" mail, det gjorde jeg ikke, så skrev jeg bare til dem og det blev fikset hurtigt. Du skal herefter anmode om de fag du gerne vil have, det er lidt en proces. Jeg brugte chatgpt til at tjekke, hvilke fag jeg kunne få adgang til at tage på baggrunde af de fag jeg havde med hjemmefra.
registration_help: Du kan altid ringe eller skrive til dem. Jeg vil altid anbefale at ringe, der får du svar hurtigt.
registration_success: Jeg fik stort set mulighed for at tage alle de fag jeg gerne ville have. Der var et enkelt der blev afvist, men så sendte jeg bare noget ekstra dokumentation og så lykkedes det.
registration_advice: Jeg vil egentlig bare sige at man skal prøve at læse de mails der bliver sendt i god tid og have styr på deadlines, det afhjælper meget af stresset der kan være i forbindelse med processen, der godt kan være lidt bøvlet.
course_level: I de fag jeg tog var niveauet væsentlig under hvad det er herhjemme, det er langt mere redegørende og mindre analytisk og matematisk.
teaching_comparison: Det føltes lidt mere som at gå på gym, jeg havde løbende midterm eksaminer og opgaver der alt sammen talte i den endelige karakter. Den sidste eksamen talte maks 50% af ens karakter og for det meste under.
courses_enrolled: ECON 383 - Climate Economics ECON 329 - Development and Economics ECON - 325 Public Economics ECON ??? - International Economics
recommended_courses: Jeg vil anbefale climate economics. Det er en dygtig underviser der er god til at variere undervisningen og så synes jeg det er et spændene emne. Det kan blive godkendt som det prioriterede klimaøkonomi valgfag fra KU, hvilket også er meget lækkert
unexpected_costs: Man bliver tvunget til at købe skolens sundhedsforsikring som koster en sjat.
cost_comparison: Dagligvarer var egentlig dyrere end forventet, medmindre du går i Walmart.
activities_available: Der er en klub til det hele på UVIC. Det gælder de fleste sportsgrene, sociale aktiviteter, politiske organisationer. Det er helt klart noget jeg vil anbefale man engagerer sig i. Ved siden af klubberne er der det her "Intramurals" system. Du tilmelder dig et sportshold online (enten et random eller nogle du har mødt som har et hold) og så kører der en tunering i løbet af hele semesteret, hvor du spiller en kamp om ugen. Det hele er organiseret af uni, og det er virkelig sjovt at være en del af. Der er fodbold, basket, volley, ultimate og mange andre sportsgrene der er dækket af intramurals systemet.
activities_recommended: Ud i naturen! Det er simpelthen den flotteste ø, så du skal ud og se så meget af den som muligt. Der er en stor vandrekultur på uni, og der er mange virkelig flotte gåturer. Derudover er en personlig anbefaling at tage ud og surfe. Start med at tage en tur op til Tofino som er surfcentralen på øen, herefter kan du tage til jordan river og sombrio, hvis du er blevet lidt mere ruti surfer.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på ture ud i naturen. Lej en bil og kør rundt på øen, det er billigt og nemt at leje bil på en app der hedder turo.
culture_adjustment: Det er egentlig meget fint, canadiere er meget flinke og åbne, de kan finde på at snakke til dig i offentlig transport, hvilket man lige skal vende sig til.
socializing_tips: Brug klubberne på skolen og lær folk at kende igennem en aktivitet. Hvis man har mod på det så bare tag kontakt til personer man har timer med, de er meget åbne og flinke i ni ud af ti tilfælde.
cultural_challenges: Canadiere kan finde på at starte en samtale på ethvert tidspunkt om du er ude og handle, står i bussen eller løber en tur. Det skal man lige vende sig til, men på et tidspunkt lære man at omfavne det.
culture_appreciated: De er meget hjælpsomme, åbne og virkelig nemme at snakke med, hvilket gør det relativt nemt at skabe et netværk.
top3_advice: Forbered dig på at det er en stor udfordring, især oppe i hovedet, det er okay at føle sig presset og ikke orke alle sociale aktiviteter. Du skal lytte til dig selv så meget som du kan og tage tingene i eget tempo. Prøv at være i god tid med alt det praktiske hjemmefra (det var jeg ikke) det tager meget af stresset væk fra hovedet og gør det nemmere at overskue. SURF!
other_useful_info: Vil anbefale at man skaffer sig en cykel, fordi der er lidt langt til indkøb og andre ærinder.
most_rewarding: Få nye venskaber med hjem til Danmark. De andre danskere der er afsted får man et ret tæt bånd til fordi alle står med de samme udfordringer og det er vigtigt at få sagt det højt, hvad end man lige bokser med fordi min erfaring er, at de andre bokser med helt de samme ting.
greatest_challenge: Det er en stor social udfordring at tage på udveksling, mit sociale batteri var ikke lige så holdbart som det plejer at være og det lader langsommere op når det er nye mennesker hele tiden.
