crucial_aspects: Fordi Wien er en del af det tysksprogede område
overall_comments: Universitetet i Wien og at den studerende skal lære at kende til et nyt universitets system, samtidig med at deadlines på hjemme universitetet også skal overholdes kan ikke anbefales.
info_ease: Svært! Hverken studievejledningen eller lektorer på KU gav konkret udtryk for at have kendskab til Universität Wien og dets fordele og ulemper. Det hele er op til den studerende selv, at finde informationer om det kommende ophold. Hvilket kan føles meget uoverskueligt.
arrival_assistance: Ingen! Erasmus koordinatoren i Wien har jeg aldrig mødt f.eks. Det eneste var et online introduktions møde med over 500 andre studerende. Men personlig vejledning i forhold til valg af fag eller aktiviteter på universitetet eksisterede ikke.
arrival_comments: Hjælp er svært at finde på Universität Wien. Skriver man en Mail til dem, bliver man henvist til en hjemmeside. Men kender man ikke systemet eller reglerne for Erasmus studerende, så er det ikke en hjælp. Universitetet er så stort og der er så mange studerende, så er den enkelte studerende er bare et nummer i rækken. Man kan let føle sig overset.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Universitetet i Wien og at den studerende skal lære at kende til et nyt universitets system, samtidig med at deadlines på hjemme universitetet også skal overholdes kan ikke anbefales.
registration_process: Meget nemt i forhold til ind registrering.
registration_help: I forhold til registerering af, at man var ankommet var det meget nemt. Fordi man bare skulle møde op på "International Office" i deres åbningstider. I forhold til valg af fag, hvilke fag der var gode for Erasmus studerende, hvilke krav der var til den studerende så var der ingen hjælp. Vidste man ikke hvad man skulle vælge, så var den eneste hjælp "Det er op til dig selv". Så mangel på vejledning generelt og personlig interaktion med en vejleder eksisterede heller ikke. Meget koldt atmosfære.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag jeg ville have. Men ønsk altid flere fag end man egentlig behøver så kan man selv vælge fag fra senere og andre til.
registration_advice: Vælg kun fag på 1 institut, maks 1 fag på et andet.
academics_comments: Universitetet i Wien og at den studerende skal lære at kende til et nyt universitets system, samtidig med at deadlines på hjemme universitetet også skal overholdes kan ikke anbefales.
course_level: Passende, men meget materiale for få ECTS point.
teaching_comparison: I Wien er læringsstilen meget upersonligt. Om de studerende er til stede eller ej er egentlig ligegyldigt. Hvem man er, hvor man kommer fra, hvorfor man er der er lektorerne fuldstændig ligeglade med. De fleste studerende møder ikke op til undervisning, først til eksamen. Så den der følelse af at være en del af en klasse og et hold eksistere ikke. Hvor på KU, efter hvad jeg har prøvet, så mødes de studerende med interesse og nærvær. Det har stor betydning.

recommended_courses: 100198-1DaF/Z:Intersektionelle Perspektiven auf die mehrsprachige Migrationsgesellschaf (4 ECTS) 100034-1 DaF/Z: Deutsch in der Migrationsgesellschaft (4 ECTS) 040108 - Interkulturelle Kompetenz in Unternehmen (4 ECTS) 00031-1 DaF/Z: Einführung in DaF/Z (4 ECTS) De her fag var virkelig interessante. De gav et nyt syn på Germanistik, samt sprogets indflydelse på det enkelte menneske. Kan virkelig anbefales.
unexpected_costs: Ikke rigtig nogen.
cost_comparison: Ikke rigtig noget.
activities_available: Mange. Men jeg havde ikke tid til at deltage i det.
activities_recommended: Det ved jeg ikke. Evt. et sportshold. Men hver klar på tasterne, når tilmeldingen starter, ellers er der ikke plads.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på ski eller besøg et af nabolandene. Det er nemt og billigt at komme rundt med tog fra Wien.
culture_adjustment: Svært. Fordi de lokale studerende ikke mødte op til undervisning. Samt der var ingen pauser i en lektion, så der var ikke mulighed for at snakke med folk. Kom de studerende til undervisning, så mødte de op og gik hjem igen efter undervisningen.
socializing_tips: Ikke rigtig. De fleste jeg mødte var også Erasmus studerende.
cultural_challenges: Universitets systemet, det var så anderledes og så tydeligt at se. Det er en kæmpe indsigt at opleve, trods den store kulturelle forskel.
culture_appreciated: At der var så mange studerende fra hele verden. Især fra Østeuropa. Det gav et helt nyt perspektiv på at være studerende. Fordi for mange studerende er et udlandsophold den eneste mulighed, for at opleve et andet land men også en mulighed for at forbedre deres chancer i livet. Hvor mange danske studerende og studerende fra vesteuropa er super priviligeret uden at vide det. Det er sætter virkelig perspektiv på tilværelsen.
top3_advice: Mødet med ikke bare et land, men flere lande, kulturer og mennesker. Det er så givende. Samt det giver ens fag og studie et helt nyt perspektiv og betydning.
other_useful_info: Gør det, selvom universitets systemet i Wien ikke forløber efter danske standarder. Det kan virke skræmmende, men at semestret har en slutning, gør at man kan se enden på det.
most_rewarding: At se og mærke hvordan en anden offentlig institution fungere.
greatest_challenge: At opleve sig selv være på dybt vand.
other_comments: Nej

registration_help: I contcated the Erasmus coordinator at my institute via e-mail.
registration_success: One course was cancelled entirely with short notice before the start of the semester. Aside from that, I was allowed to attend all the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: You can register for any number of courses, in case you do not get a space in all your desired courses, and then deregister once spaces have been allocated.
academics_comments: Covid naturally had an impact but I still enjoyed my stay and had a lot of great experiences
course_level: I followed mostly BA courses and found the teaching slightly more demanding than at UCPH though the exams were more forgiving.
teaching_comparison: The biggest difference is that in most courses, you are graded for your participation in exercise classes where you will usually be required to succesfully present a few exercises per course.
courses_enrolled: Complex Analysis, Numeric Mathematics, Introduction to Mathematical Logic (MA course), Mathematics Meets Philosophy, and Gender Aspects of Mathematics.
recommended_courses: Complex Analysis was my favorite course. Introduction to Mathematical Logic was very interesting but also incredibly challenging - however, the lecturers/teachers for this course were great. Mathematics Meets Philosophy is too easy (compared to VtMat at UCPH) and Gender Aspects of Mathematics was unfortunately also a somewhat disappointing course.
unexpected_costs: None, really
cost_comparison: Most courses do not require the purchase of any books. Public transportation is really cheap (75 euro per semester). Cinemas are cheap!
activities_available: All kinds of sports as well as some music and performance classes offered by the university sports institute.
activities_recommended: I did not personally attend any uni sports but it sounded great
weekend_recommendations: Go hiking on the Stadtwanderwege. Get very cheap tickets (~90% discount if you're <27 years old) for operas with the app Gretchen and go to concerts and plays. Go to museums; buy an annual ticket for Kunsthistorisches Museum (which is worth several visits by itself) which also gives access to a few small museums. The Ephesos Museum is great for ancient history. MUMOK, Albertina (main one as well as Albertina Modern) and Upper Belvedere were my favorite art museums. The 7th district in particular has a LOT of nice cafés and bars. It'es easy to go on trips to for example Budapest or other towns in Austria. Schneeberg is a nice place to go hiking, easily reached by train.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, I didn't really experience any culture clash
cultural_challenges: Stores are closed on Sundays
culture_appreciated: Sitting in a café for hours (while studying, for example)
top3_advice: 1) It is very easy to meet other Erasmus students. Sign up for welcome events and WhatsApp group chats with other students in order to meet people 2) Do seek out as many cultural experiences as you have the time for (they are endless) 3) If you want to meet local people, seek them out through hobbies and such
other_useful_info: You can get by in the city without speaking particularly good German
most_rewarding: Making friends with other Erasmus students
greatest_challenge: Finding for both studying, social events as well as pursuing hobbies Also, practicing German rather than defaulting to speaking in English.

crucial_aspects: In Vienna there are two options for studying psychology; Wien Universität (WU) and the private university Sigmund Freud University. I choose WU for academic reasons, since it's the superior university in this regard. Also the main building is one of the most beautiful buildings you'll ever see, and to get to study in that place.... What an experience.
info_ease: The international office at the main building was very qualified in helping with whatever problem you could think of. I didn't really reach out to them before getting the certificate of departure, but everyone I know got the help they needed.
arrival_assistance: As mentioned before, I didn't need help in the beginning of my stay.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Oh wow, what a stressful event. Before departing from home, you'll have to register for every course you just have the slightest interest in, because you aren't secured a spot on any of the courses before the deadline of registration. So you'll need registration on backup-courses in the case - and this WILL happen - you don't get offered a spot on the ones you have made the "forhåndsgodkendelse" for. Another problem is that the courses for the semester are only made visible very close to the day of departure from home, so the hole thing seems very confusing. BUT everything will work out in the end, it's just not a very intelligent registration process as far as I'm concerned.
registration_help: Everyone says the same thing, just register for a lot of different courses!
registration_success: I would say around 50% of the courses I took was in alignment with courses I had planned on taking beforehand.
registration_advice: Have patience and always a large cup of coffee close at hand.
course_level: A very wide range of good and bad courses; as you can expect from taking around 6-8 different courses.
teaching_comparison: Some matched, others didn't.
courses_enrolled: 1) Economic Psychology - Motivation in Work and Occupation, 2) Economic Psychology (another focus in this course), 3) Psychology of Work and Labour, 4) Environmental Psychology, 5) Slavoj Zizek and the Arts, and 6) SE Advanced Seminar: Mind and Brain - Meta-psychology.
recommended_courses: The teacher Filip Melinšcak is a champ, and gives very good lectures in generel. I took his course Meta-psychology which was awesome.
unexpected_costs: The prices of domestic train commutes. You'll have to buy a student reduction card, where you get a huge discount on every ticket.
cost_comparison: The prices aren't that much lower than in Copenhagen.
activities_available: Many activities I believe, but I didn't really use them.
activities_recommended: Too many things to write about here. The city offers everything, and you need a least six months to get to experience just a fraction.
weekend_recommendations: Too many things to write about here. The city offers everything, and you need a least six months to get to experience just a fraction.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, the people of Vienna are warm and welcoming.
socializing_tips: Hmm, you'll probably socialize primarily with other Erasmus students.
cultural_challenges: Only the language, which I really can't complain about.
culture_appreciated: Its richness.
top3_advice: 1) the city brewery Ottakringer makes a zwickl beer that is just out of this world, 2) if you like history and are culturally aware, then this is the city for you, and 3) you won't regret going here.
other_useful_info: Not really, just leave already.
most_rewarding: To end up being mistaken for a local myself.
greatest_challenge: To get time to try everything.
other_comments: Not really.

crucial_aspects: The cultural and language oppotunitites of my destination were a major factor when I chose Vienna.
info_ease: It was not very easy and the overall initial assistance regarding course registration, etc., was very poor. I had a single conversation with my receiving coordinator which did help out a lot, however, many important details regarding deadlines and especially my e-mail account linked to the university, were not explained to me before it was too late. This resulted in me not being able to take a full worth of ECTS points for the semester, which in hindsight was actually not too bad of a situation. The Erasmus team of students linked to the host university were very helpful and a big Erasmus Whatsapp group really helped a lot when one had a small, quick question.
arrival_assistance: Assistance was not very elaborate. It would have been nice with a quick overview of course registration mechanics, your university e-mail adress and other minor stuff such as grading scales, etc. Primarily, the help I received was when I asked my fellow native students for assistance, which usually is also the best way to be introduced to a new system. My receiving coordinator was very helpful, although not very elaborate, and one could tell that she had a lot of other stuff going on, which one must respect of course, this, however, sometimes left me hanging for days waiting for e-mail replies and not fulfilling deadlines due to lack of awareness.
arrival_comments: All in all it was fine but it took a lot of effort and time to get just minor information.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: One has to puzzle together each and every course, juggling with courses worth only 2 ECTS points sometimes, and try to put together a program for the semester. Many course will overlap and one needs to either chose to find another course or just accept that you will miss a bunch of lectures. After finding the courses you wanna pick, you have to allocate points as a priority measure; each student has 1000 points and the more points you allocate to a course, the higher you prioritize it. Very confusing. Then, you have three different kind of courses, seminars, lectures, and übung, all of which will most of the time follow their own registration systems - some without points, some with points. I received almost no strategic advice on how to approach this system, so I had a very hard time figuring out what would be smartest to do.
registration_help: None - except for a quick meeting with your receiving coordinator.
registration_success: I managed, only after missing a few deadlines, to put together a program of 21 ECTS points, which my home university did not appreciate.
registration_advice: You need to be aware that course registration is an extremely time consuming process and you should start in good time.
course_level: The level was perfect, however, sometimes the workload did not match the ECTS points granted. 2 points for 15 lectures and 10 points for 45 lectures did not seem very rational to me in the long run, comparing to my home university.
teaching_comparison: Pretty much the same
courses_enrolled: Signalling in the Immune system Immunology and cellular microbiology, part A + B Basics of Neuroscience Laboratory Course II - Biochemistry German language course at Sprachenzentrum, level A1.2
recommended_courses: The immunology course were excellent and can be recommended
unexpected_costs: none
cost_comparison: none
activities_available: Orchestras and voice club were available but they were not too keen on taking in Erasmus students who were only there for 1 semester.
activities_recommended: Concerts, operas and museums - it's just really good in Vienna.
weekend_recommendations: Go skiing or hiking in the hills outside the city. Travel to Budapest for weekend or visit the balkan coastline.
culture_adjustment: As a Dane it was rather easy - the food is equally as disgusting as in Denmark so I had no struggle with that and the amount of beer being drunk is somewhat also similar.
socializing_tips: Nope - I did not succeed very well in that due to Covid19 lockdown... Just talk with people, anyone you meet at your course, what other advice do you need?
cultural_challenges: No sink by the toilet... rather disgusting sometimes.
culture_appreciated: The fact that shopkeepers actually say 'hello' and 'goodbye' when you enter and leave a store makes you feel appreciated and welcome when shopping. It's a small thing but I already miss it. Also the coffee houses are brilliant - bring a book and just sit there for 3 hours drinking coffee and eating cake.
top3_advice: 1. Be VERY thourough with your course registration and start in good time 2. Go to language school, even just for a few weeks, it is really, really worth it and you will make good friends there 3. Participate in the initial Erasmus events - pretty basic advice but it is also really worth it
other_useful_info: Remember to buy a 'Semester Ticket' for the public transport. It is only €78 and you can ride the tram, bus and U-bahn anywhere in the city for the whole semester. Also, consider buying a 'Vorteilskart' with the ÖBB - it is very cheap, valid for a year and will save you up to 50% on train tickets if you feel like going skiing for visiting Salzburg for example.
most_rewarding: I really can't say - so many things happened during my 6 months stay, I can't possibly pick one single experience.
greatest_challenge: The course registration and generally just being thrown into a completely new university system with barely any introduction.
other_comments: No.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to go to a German-speaking country and to a larger city, because I wanted to connect with people fast. Therefore I considered Vienna a cool opportunity - also getting to know Austria!
info_ease: The international office of the university was always ready to help. I stayed in a WG with other students, who could help me, so I didn´t need much information from the office - but I´m sure, they are always ready to help.
arrival_assistance: I didn´t get any help from the university.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I went to the International Office to pick up a document - there were a lot of time slots and it was very easy and convenient.
registration_help: I don´t know, since I didn´t ask for help.
registration_success: I got all of the classes, that I wanted to take. Dont forget the rating - the system with the 1000 points, with which you can be sure to get at least some of the courses you want to take!
registration_advice: Its´s not at all complicated! Just read your emails and go pick up the document. And ask for help if you have any questions!
course_level: It differed a lot. I took 2 Pro-Seminar Course, which were very good and one Einführung in die Literaturwissenschaft Course, which was less challenging, but also because it was really just an introduction.

And I can definitely recommend the Proseminar Course, which is always offered in the Spring Semester (if you study literature) with an excursion to the Rauriser Literaturtage - it was a very nice opportunity to get to know other students better and see other areas of Austria. cost_comparison: The USI (Uni Sport Courses) were not as expensive as I thought, so I signed up for a couple of courses.
activities_available: There was a free concert with Musik Verein in the Arkadenhof. I also went on two excursions with the courses I signed up for - the university payed for transport and hotel and it was a very interesting, cultural experience. I went to Burgtheater a couple of times, because you only pay 10 euros as a student. The erasmus-team was also very kind and answered so many questions in the group chat.
activities_recommended: Burgtheater - generally going in the theater, tickets are very cheap for students. I also went to Musik Verein and bought a membership to a couple of museums, because it already after the second visit was cheaper. During summer the festival season is so crazy - so many events and concerts for free in the city. I also went to a couple of readings with various authors - also a very nice kind of event, if you´re interested in literature.
weekend_recommendations: I went to Budapest, Bratislava, Brno, Graz, Klagenfurt and Innsbruck. And went hiking at the Schneeberg, went to visit a couple of "Heurigen" at Kahlenberg.
culture_adjustment: Very easy!
socializing_tips: Join the courses with excursions!
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: Vienna has culturally so much to offer! And the people I met at university were also very friendly and open-minded!
top3_advice: Enjoy the beautiful sorroundings - both the university and the city! It was in the beginning very overwhelming, but I slowly got used to studying in what would have been worthy of housing some monarch! Pick some of the courses with excursion and find a WG where you can get to know locals!
other_useful_info: Even though you have a lot of small courses or at least courses which only give you 3-4 ECTS points and it can be hard to keep track of the many courses, it will be all right in the end. Maybe if possible start writing some of your papers so that you can also enjoy the summer outside of the reading rooms (MAK has a good one! you can enter for free)
most_rewarding: Improving my german skills and getting to know very nice and kind people - and experiencing that my work payed of and I managed to get through all of my courses - even though it was hard to keep track in the beginning!
greatest_challenge: The many (6) courses, because we rather have to larger courses in Copenhagen.

crucial_aspects: Even though my main purpose of going on exchange was to get to explore a new culture and to gain new perspectives, it was also important for me, that my university of choice offered interesting and relevant courses, that would fit with the rest of my education. Due to Covid-19, it was also important to me, that the university was in Europe. It was also crucial to me, that the courses at the destination were offered in English.
info_ease: Overall, it was pretty easy to find most information needed upon arrival. We had a really great coordinator at the Department of Sociology at the University of Vienna, who was always ready to answer questions quickly. The process of choosing and applying for the different courses could have been easier and better explained, as that was a bit stressful. Also, the process of applying for an address in Austria could have been a bit better supported. However, in my experience, everything worked out fine and overall there was always information to be found, and people to ask for help.
arrival_assistance: We were offered an online meeting before arrival, with practical information, which was really great, as it fixed some concerns and we also got to talk to some of the other exchange students. I was also offered to be teamed up with a local student upon arrival. Furthermore, we had a coordinator at the specific department at the University of Vienna, who helped with a lot of the practical stuff, especially in the beginning. I was lucky to live with local flatmates, who could also help me with most of my questions.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration itself was pretty easy and explained along the way. The process of choosing courses however, was confusing and stressful.
registration_help: There is a lot of information on the website, and I was also e-mailed a lot of information along the way. There was also help to be found by asking the coordinators both at my home university and Uni Wien.
registration_success: I was succesful, and got most of the ones I wanted - I think that differs a lot though, depending on the department. It was also difficult to get exactly 30 ECTS, as Uni Wien generally offers less points per course, compared to my home university.
registration_advice: Just follow the instructions offered along the way, and don't panic about the course selection. If you want to follow a course from another department than your own, it's best to know a bit earlier, as you need a signature from the specific apartment, and not just your own coordinator.
course_level: I was a BA student, but I was also allowed to do MA courses at my stay. Furthermore, I did a German language course, which is linked to Uni Wien, but not specifically BA or MA level.
teaching_comparison: Most of my courses were lectures, so they were very similar to the ones at UCPH. There was less group work, but that is solely due to the courses I chose, and not the University itself.
courses_enrolled: Sustainable Solutions for Planetary Health (2 ECTS). German Course (8 ECTS). Introduction to Cultural Theories (5 ECTS). Climate Change and Climate Crisis - Transformative Concepts and Innovations Gruppemerit (5 ECTS). Approaching Cultural Studies (5 ECTS). Culture, Society and the Media (5 ECTS).
recommended_courses: I would recommend a language course, if you're interested in German (you can also do less than 8 ECTS, or do it before the semester start). It's a different type of learning, and links you to the country you're on exchange in. The course "Culture, Society and the Media" was really interesting. It's about representations of nature and nonhuman bodies in media and culture, and offers a lot of alternative perspectives and ways of thinking about the world we live in, than any course I've ever had. "Climate Change and Climate Crisis" was really interesting, as it was a collaboration between the university and Fridays for Future. Every time, there was a new speaker, specialized in their own field, guesting and teaching the lectures. This was a new and inspiring way to do a course.
unexpected_costs: There is a student ticket for the public transportation in Wien - however it's much more expensive, if you only set your Vienna address as "secondary". Furthermore, I struggled a lot to access the ticket in the beginning, and eventually just bought a regular one, as it was easier. I ended up using way more than expected on transportation.
cost_comparison: Housing is generally less expensive in Wien than in CPH. Most groceries, food and drinks are also less expensive in Wien, but not by a lot.
activities_available: Different sports, debate club, choir etc.
activities_recommended: I would recommend researching the stuff offered, but I would also recommend searching for stuff outside uni. I ended up joining a local fitness boxing club (Backyard Vienna), and I was also in a WhatsApp Chat about bouldering, where it was easy to just meet up with others at the different climbing gyms.
weekend_recommendations: There is A LOT to do in Wien, but it's also easy to travel to other parts of Austria by train or bus. There is a lot of beautiful nature, even just on the border of Vienna. It's also easy and quick to get to e.g. Bratislava, Budapest or Prague for getaways.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy in my experience, but I was also lucky to share a flat with two locals, so I was introduced to many of their Austrian friends. For me, that was the perfect combination - living with locals and getting to know their network, and on the other hand meeting a lot of international students through the Erasmus Network.
socializing_tips: Practice German. Join social events or a sports club. Choose courses with group projects.
cultural_challenges: The waiters of Vienna are known to be a bit rude - which in some cases is true. You just need to learn not to take it personally. Furthermore, Austrian humor is often sarcastic and dark, and locals will respect you more when you can also make fun of yourself, and not be offended by them joking with you.
culture_appreciated: They have a lot of very strong traditions, and they use a lot of energy and ressources, going out of their way to make a big deal out of Christmas decorations and ice skating arenas fx. That is pretty cool. All the Austrians I've met are very welcoming and including, and ready to help with whatever, if you ask for it.
top3_advice: Remember to fill out the "Meldezettel" upon arrival in Austria, stating that you moved there. Take part in the WhatsApp groups provided in the beginning - then it's really easy to meet other exchange students. Use your mobility coordinator - they are there to help you.
other_useful_info: It's nice to know, that you can do a language course before the semester, if you want to. The exams are quite different than in DK - most of them are very short, and you don't get to apply your knowledge as much. In my experience, they were more about "repeating" what we had learned.
most_rewarding: Wien is such a nice, beautiful and great city. I felt very "at home" there, almost from the beginning, and most of my friends felt the same way. The social exchange and meeting so many great people (both locals and other international students) was very rewarding. It was also great to be able to try out some other courses, than those offered at UCPH, and also just actually completing a whole semester in a foreign country and to pass the exams is a big victory.
greatest_challenge: There was a lockdown and some of the courses were online due to Covid, which was a bit of a challenge. The exam period was also intense, as it was different than at UCPH, and all the courses are taught until the date of the exam.
other_comments: Wien is a perfect place to live, I'm sure you will love it!!

most_rewarding: Experiencing the city and meeting new friends from all around the world.
greatest_challenge: The practical stuff in the beginning/before the semester.

crucial_aspects: Jeg valgte at tage på udveksling, da jeg havde et ønske om at opleve andre kulturer samt at få en international vinkel på min uddannelse. Jeg havde Wien som min 5. prioritet, men jeg ville ikke have været andre steder henne. Wien er en fantastisk by. Grunden til at jeg havde Wien på min liste, var at en af min kærestes venner, som også har læst jura, havde været i Wien på udveksling og havde været virkelig glad for det. Jeg havde aldrig selv været i Wien før, men da jeg begyndte at læse om byen lød den helt fantastisk. Wien har også et anerkendt juridisk fakultet, samt det faktum at et af FN's hovedkontorer ligger i Wien. Dette var med til at få mig til at vælge Wien.
overall_comments: Mit udvekslingsophold var helt fantastisk. Jeg har ikke en finger at sætte på det.

arrival_assistance: Jeg var til et orienteringsmøde på universitetet, hvor vi fik basis ting at vide
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Mit udvekslingsophold var helt fantastisk. Jeg har ikke en finger at sætte på det.
registration_process: Man har en periode hvor man kan registerer fag inde på u:space. I denne periode kan man tilmelde sig alle de fag man har lyst til. Det er vigtigt at tilmelde sig for mange fag/ECTS, da man ikke er sikker på at få alle sine fag eller få fag nok til at have et fuldt semester. Efterfølgende er der en afmeldingsperiode, hvor man kan afmelde sig de fag man er blevet tildelt, men ikke ønsker at have. Afmeldingsperioden er efter den første uge, så man har mulighed for at prøve fagene af inden man endeligt afmelder sig fagene og beslutter hvilke man gerne vil følge
registration_help: Der var ikke noget hjælp
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag som jeg gerne ville have. Mange af de engelske fag vælges kun af udvekslingsstuderende og derfor er det nemt at få en plads
registration_advice: Registerer dig på alle de fag du overvejer at have også selvom du er registeret til 100 ECTS. Lav så et skema over dem du gerne vil prøve af, og tag til undervisning i dem den første uge. Så får man en følelse af faget og finder ud af om det er noget man har lyst til at deltage i. Så kan man afmelde sig de fag man ikke ønsker at følge
academics_comments: Mit udvekslingsophold var helt fantastisk. Jeg har ikke en finger at sætte på det.
course_level: Kurserne var ret små 3 eller 4 ECTS, hvilket gjorde at arbejdsbyrden for de enkelte fag ikke var så stor, men sammenlagt var den større. Dog var niveauet generelt lavere end på KU
teaching_comparison: I Wien var det op til de enkelte professorer at tilrettelægge faget. Det vil sige at nogle fag mindede meget om dansk undervisning, med en professor der står og underviser ud fra et powerpoint og så kan de studerende svare på spørgsmål/stille spørgsmål. Andre havde undervisningen bygget op med oplæg fra de studerende og en professor der underviser om et emne. Andre igen havde mest studerende der holdte oplæg og så var underviseren der til at supervisere det. Der var også et enkelt fag, hvor der var rollespil om medieringssituationer.

unexpected_costs: Jeg rejste meget mere rundt end jeg tænkte at jeg ville gøre, hvilket selvfølgelig koster penge. Men det er rimelig billigt at komme fra Wien og rundt til det meste af Østeuropa.
cost_comparison: Generelt er prisniveauet lavere end i Danmark. Det var især take-away mad, mad I supermarkeder, øl/andre drikkevarer og restaurantbesøg samt caféer og kaffe der var billigere end herhjemme. De har et studiependlerkort, hvor man betaler 75 euro for hele semesteret, og så må man bruge alt offentlig transport i Wien
activities_available: Der var en sportsforening, hvor man billigt kun tilmelde sig alverdens forskellige sportshold for studerende. Jeg gik selv til ballet, volleyball og yoga. På Wien Universitet er der en studenterorganisation kaldes European Student Network (ESN), som arrangerer arrangementer for udvekslingsstuderende. Dem deltog jeg meget i i starten. Det var her jeg mødte en masse andre udvekslingsstuderende som jeg blev venner med.
activities_recommended: Wien er generelt en meget kulturel by. Her er alverdens spændende muséer om mange forskellige ting og en masse smukke bygninger at kigge på. Der er også en masse ting der omhandler musik, opera, ballet og skuespil. Man keder sig aldrig i Wien.
weekend_recommendations: Jeg vil anbefale at rejse rundt og se resten af Østrig og de omkringliggende lande, da der er gode transportmuligheder. I Wien vil jeg anbefale at man ser alle de store monumenter omkring Ringstrasse, at man går på museum, ser tingene omkring kejserfamilien, besøger nogle af de smukke parker (især om sommeren), gå i operaen/nogle af teatrene (man får rabat som studerende), spis en Wiener schnitzel på Figelmüller og kage på Café Central. Deltag i studenteridræt og i de aktiviteter der arrangeres af ESN.
culture_adjustment: Det var virkelig nemt. Wien er super nem at bo i og minder på mange måder om København. Det eneste man skal være opmærksom på er at supermarkeder (og alle andre butikker) lukker tidligt og har lukket om søndagen
socializing_tips: Nej, jeg talte mest med andre udvekslingsstuderende
cultural_challenges: Det eneste jeg skulle venne mig til, er at de er meget mere analog end vi er herhjemme. Det er en god ide altid at have kontanter med, da man ikke kan betale med kort alle steder. Alle eksamener var også i hånden, hvilket var en udfordring.
culture_appreciated: Jeg var især glad for deres kultur om at gå på café og spise små fine kager. Østrigere er en perfekt kombination mellem de strukturerede tyskere og de mere loose italienere.
top3_advice: 1. Husk at nyde tiden, det går virkelig stærkt 2. Få en masse gode oplevelser. Sig ja til alle de muligheder du kommer i nærheden af. Her var ESN særligt vigtige i starten, da de arrangerer en masse ting 3. Skriv direkte til professorerne hvis der er problemer, det bliver løst hurtigere end at skrive til universitetet
other_useful_info: Husk at udfylde din "meldezettel" og aflevere den på magistratkontoret. Der står det skal gøres indenfor tre dage, men de er ikke så strenge med det
most_rewarding: Det mest givende ved mit udvekslingsophold var at møde en masse forskellige mennesker fra hele Europa, samt at få et internationalt perspektiv på min uddannelse. Det gav mig meget at se hvordan der bliver undervist i andre lande.
greatest_challenge: Det er svært at svare på. Jeg havde ikke nogen store problemer på min udveksling
other_comments: Tag afsted! Det bliver det bedste semester nogensiden!

crucial_aspects: The availability of behavioral and experimental economics courses
info_ease: Very easy - the exchange arrival team was very helpful
arrival_assistance: The exchange arrival team provides all details
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: So there are two systems of point allocation and preference ranking depending on the faculty you are in. I was in the Economics and business faculty which had the complicated point allocation system. Also while the courses themselves aren't at a high level as KU, the ECTS number allocated for each course is lower so people have to do at least 4-6 courses if they want 30 ECTS and that can get hectic.
registration_help: Looking into the University's webpages, I found an explanation of the system. I asked my assigned buddy for help on what strategy to use.
registration_success: I was successful in getting the courses I got the pre-approval for
registration_advice: The strategy is that two hours before the Registeration closes, it is recommended to go and allocate maximum points to the courses where there is demand (>500 points) and almost none (i.e. between 1-10 points) to courses were there are still empty places. Since all students do this, ensure that you aren't doing it in the last minute as the system is widely-known to crash. Also unlike KU, you can actually go to the first class and then drop it if not interested. This means you can sign up for more classes than required.
course_level: I'm on my final year of Masters - by the time I went to University of Vienna, I only had my Master thesis left to do back in KU.
teaching_comparison: Entirely dependent on the professor - some of them are chill and interactive while some others are formal. You can get the vibe from the course description and first day of class.
courses_enrolled: Topics in Behavioural Economics - a Seminar VCEE seminar series International negotiations
recommended_courses: The international negotiations is hands-down the best course I have attended - the professor was extremely interactive and insightful and we did case studies and role-playing of practical scenarios like job negotiations which is useful outside of the university. Will also recommend the other courses I took as they were also interesting and provided additional perspective to what I have learnt at KU.
unexpected_costs: I was fined once 50 euros in public transport for having my mask in my hand and not wearing it as soon as I entered. So be prepared to follow the rules to the letter
cost_comparison: Generally, food and other items are less expensive than here. However there are so many interesting museums and arts and culture so do budget for that :D
activities_available: It is extremely competitive to get into the sports classes at University. However there are plenty more opportunities apart from sports. I was in a book club and the university poetry writing club and made some great friends via it
activities_recommended: There are so many activities being conducted by the exchange team so definitely look out for that. To meet local students, recommend joining some club of interest like mentioned above
weekend_recommendations: There are so many arts and culture activities happening throughout the city which are still accessible to students on a budget
culture_adjustment: it was fairly easy
socializing_tips: There are no concepts of study groups. However people are generally friendly if you take the first step to go talk to them.
cultural_challenges: Outside of University and tourist areas, people don't know as much English and hence learning some basic German is recommended. People of color might also face some looks in some areas so do check the route in advance to wherever you are going.
culture_appreciated: People are very relaxed - they read newspapers and physical books in the trams and take long coffee breaks
top3_advice: Everything mentioned above - I think it's a great city to live in both in summer and winter and offers a different culture while still providing the same infrastructure as Copenhagen: perhaps one will miss biking as Vienna is a bigger city
other_useful_info: Everything mentioned above
most_rewarding: The culture of the city and classes at university and the discussions in it
greatest_challenge: Nothing much really - everything fairly runs smoothly like here. If you are vegetarian or vegan then there might be difficulties as not many places have the option like here. Also if you are super environmentally-conscious then you would be appalled by the lack of recycling available there

crucial_aspects: I had not been to Vienna before but always wanted to go. The University of Vienna also had interesting courses for me to attend.
overall_comments: The semester in Vienna overlapped with my semester in Copenhagen, which was a bit stressful.
info_ease: It was very easy to find the necessary information for incoming exchange students at the University of Vienna. Most information could be found of the webpage of International Office.
arrival_assistance: I did not need any assistance.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: The semester in Vienna overlapped with my semester in Copenhagen, which was a bit stressful.
registration_process: You register for courses and exams in the online platform U:Find. It is very simple and easy to use. You can chose between different kinds of course; either seminars and lecture series. They are graded differently and the exams are different as well. You can read about grading, exams, and expectations in the course description on U:Find as well.
registration_help: You can always contact the International Office or the Erasmus coordinators at your institute. They can be a great help.
registration_success: I registered for all the courses I wanted. Remember to check the dates and times for your chosen courses, as they can overlap. Also check the webpage of the International Office for information about course registration.
registration_advice: Remember to check dates, times, and exams for your courses! You must register for exams for lecture-series courses separately. Furthermore, I would recommend choosing a mix of seminar and lecture-series courses.
academics_comments: The semester in Vienna overlapped with my semester in Copenhagen, which was a bit stressful.
course_level: I attended mostly Master-courses, which was not a problem. The academic level is very dependent on the specific course instructor as they choose the reading and lead the discussion. I did not feel a big difference between the level of BA-courses and Master-courses.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was very similar to UCPH with regard to both seminars (student presentations and so forth) and lectures.
courses_enrolled: 070187 Introduction to Digital Humanities 070294 Guided Reading Medieval History - The Crusades in History and Memory 070118 Guided Reading Global History - Histo- ry of Humanitarian Aid 240518 ‘The Pale Horse' - Introduction to the Anthropology of War and Warfare 240519 Machine vision: images, operations, and the (post)human 240524 Digital identities
recommended_courses: If you are interested in history then I would strongly recommend any course with John Giebfried. He is one of the best instructors I have ever had making class interesting, fun, and entertaining.
unexpected_costs: I did not experience any unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: The price of groceries and the prices at restaurants/bars were pretty much the same as in Copenhagen.
activities_available: The Erasmus Student Network facilitated a lot of activities. I attended some in the beginning but not all, however I played handball at the University Sports Institute which was super great! I can highly recommend playing at the Sports Institute as you meet other students from other universities as well.
activities_recommended: Playing a sport at the Univeristy Sports Institute - it is for all students in Vienna not just for students at Universiat Wien. It was a great way to meet new people and friends.
weekend_recommendations: It is easy to travel to other parts of Europe by bus from Vienna. Weekend trips into Europe or the Alps were super nice! You can also hike in the hills surrounding Vienna. That is super nice if the weather allows it.
culture_adjustment: The culture was very similar to Copenhagen, but people from Vienna can be very annoyed in traffic - that is just how it is.
socializing_tips: Attend some of the events made by the Erasmus Student Network in the start of your semester - everybody wants to meet other exchange students, so it is very easy to socialize with new people at the ESN-events.
cultural_challenges: People being angry and annoyed in traffic - a lot of honking.
culture_appreciated: The café-culture was super nice. Always great to grab a cup of tea after a long day.
top3_advice: Remember to register for exams in your lecture-courses! Enjoy the beautiful city - explore the museums and the concert halls. Use Vienna as a starting point for weekend trips to other parts of Europe.
other_useful_info: You do not need to speak German to live in the city - almost everyone speaks decent English.
most_rewarding: Meeting wonderful friends from all over Europe. The academic leaning was nice - but the people were the best!
greatest_challenge: The end of my semester in Vienna overlapped with the beginning of my semester in Copenhagen. That was stressful but I was aware of the overlap in good time so I could plan my exams well in advance. It was nonetheless stressful.
other_comments: Universität Wien is a fantastic place to study and Vienna is wonderful. I can only recommend it!
