crucial_aspects: I wanted to go somewhere where they spoke English and where I would feel like I could challenge myself socially and academically and experience a new part of the world.
overall_comments: My stay in Seattle was an amazing experience for me. It is a very easy city to like and has a very European vibe to it. The people are so kind and helpful and there is plenty of amazing things to do both in the city and in the nature around the city. UW is a really good university and I was very overwhelmed by the academic and personal engagement from my peers and professors.
info_ease: Very hard. The Danish system for going abroad overseas is complicated to understand and the other Danes going to Seattle and I were constantly met with either lack of help or differing responses to the same question. The host institution however was very helpful at all hours and gave more than sufficient information upon arrival.
arrival_assistance: FIUTS the international student organization, sent me many emails and a woman named Sarah Berryman was a significant help whenever something was confusing or challenging.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: My stay in Seattle was an amazing experience for me. It is a very easy city to like and has a very European vibe to it. The people are so kind and helpful and there is plenty of amazing things to do both in the city and in the nature around the city. UW is a really good university and I was very overwhelmed by the academic and personal engagement from my peers and professors.
registration_process: You add classes on their "my plan" page and then you attend them for the first week and maybe drop or change a class if it's not for you.
registration_help: A lot a the international student's service office. Again, Sarah Berryman was my hero.
registration_success: Very successful. I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Think twice about taking graduate courses. It is a great way to learn, but watch the workload, cause it's basically PHD classes, so maybe mix graduate and undergrad classes and prioritize one class more than the other.
academics_comments: My stay in Seattle was an amazing experience for me. It is a very easy city to like and has a very European vibe to it. The people are so kind and helpful and there is plenty of amazing things to do both in the city and in the nature around the city. UW is a really good university and I was very overwhelmed by the academic and personal engagement from my peers and professors.
course_level: The workload is higher but the expectations for your work are not the same as at KU. They do not expect you to break your neck like a 72-hour exam at KU. The level is a bit lower all depending on the class you choose. Graduate was hard and very high level, but Undergrad was easy but with more papers.
teaching_comparison: It's way more engaging and fun. The professors care a lot about creating a talkative and discussion-based learning environment. I felt like I learned a lot more this way than at KU.
courses_enrolled: In the first quarter I had African American Political Theory, African American Politics: How Does it Feel to Be a Problem? and Ethnic Politics in the US and Beyond. In the second I had Middle East in the Modern World and Social Reproductive Theory
recommended_courses: I strongly recommend taking classes with Oliver Rollins, Jonathan Warren, and Jey Saung. Both are amazing teachers of critical race theory and feminist theory. In general, they are experts on anti-capitalist works and anti-colonialism. UW has some amazing classes on critical theory that KU would never even consider having, so diving into that was an incredible learning experience.
unexpected_costs: Doctor's bills. Even though you are ensured it still costs money to go to the doctor.
cost_comparison: UW provides a Husky Card which gives you free rides on all public transport in Seattle. So that was nice. Food is so so expensive though. It's delicious but expensive. Particularly groceries.
activities_available: There was a club for everything, all kinds of sports clubs, movie clubs, heritage clubs, hiking clubs etc. etc. FIUTS did a lot of social events.
activities_recommended: Hiking, kayaking, concerts, eating Asian food and fish, the cinema, and bouldering. Also biking the Burke Gilman Trail.
weekend_recommendations: Go on a trip to the mountains. It is so beautiful out in nature. I also went to Portland and Vancouver BC (both 4 hours bus ride away), which was a lot of fun.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Americans (and Pacific North Westeners) are very easy-going and kind to you.
socializing_tips: Ask them out for coffee. You have to push yourself a lot to do those things where you just ask people out in the first while and then suddenly you have great friends. If you find it hard to find friends at uni, you can also use Bumble Friends to find friends.
cultural_challenges: Not really any. Seattle people are very easy people.
culture_appreciated: The openness and kindness Americans show to strangers like yourself.
top3_advice: Don't be afraid to be vulnerable in terms of approaching new people, remember to get out into nature, and remember that once you return you will have forgotten your grades from class but the time you spent exploring.
other_useful_info: Apply for scholarships. It's an expensive time.
most_rewarding: Meeting and getting to know my American friends, experiencing nature and academic learnings.
greatest_challenge: Being so far away from home with such a big time difference.

crucial_aspects: I chose University of Washington in Seattle because it has a very acknowledged creative writing program and because Seattle is known as a liberal city with lots of culture so I figured that I would have fun there. And I had!
overall_comments: A semester as an exchange student not only makes you grow as a person and become very independent, it also pushes you to handle difficult and unforeseen situations all the time, and you experience new things everyday. I would recommend it to anyone who have the opportunity!
info_ease: The information and help from that students receive from KU is very criticizable. I felt very on my own and I got the sense that the people who are hired to help were bothered by my questions and lacked basic information. I know that many of the other students share my experience. I have ideas to how the process can be improved, and would love to talk with someone about it. Please feel free to contact me if you want me to elaborate further on my experience.
arrival_assistance: The people who are hired at UW to help the exchange students settle did not do their job. They misinformed me about my tuition which left me with a fee, and they did not answer any emails or questions. I believe that they have found a new system to integrate the exchange students after the summerbreak so hopefully it will be better in the future.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: A semester as an exchange student not only makes you grow as a person and become very independent, it also pushes you to handle difficult and unforeseen situations all the time, and you experience new things everyday. I would recommend it to anyone who have the opportunity!
registration_process: I felt that I had some trouble filling out my application and that it was difficult to get help from the UW because the application needed to be filled out during the summer vacation. We also needed to pay 100 dollars in order to get a paper that we needed to apply for a visa. They said that the money covered the costs of an express mail but it took a month before they sent it anyway.
registration_help: They answered by mail but very slowly.
registration_success: I could only apply for one creative writing class which was very disappointing but the classes that I got were very very good. Exchange students are not prioritized but that I think that is pretty fair because the exchange semester is about so much more than the academia.
registration_advice: Students who apply to UW must be aware that the application shall be sent during KU's summer vacation. KU did not inform us about this the first time I applied and I almost missed the deadline. We were specifically told that there would be no deadlines before the new semester started and I only realized it because I got a mail from UW. The people who were supposed to help us from KU were on vacation and we needed some papers from them. It was very criticizable.
academics_comments: A semester as an exchange student not only makes you grow as a person and become very independent, it also pushes you to handle difficult and unforeseen situations all the time, and you experience new things everyday. I would recommend it to anyone who have the opportunity!
course_level: I was a MA student at KU but took BA classes at UW.
teaching_comparison: There is so much more homework during the semester than at KU, and attendance is also very common. The final exams are shorter though. The grading system was also very different.
courses_enrolled: I took three literature courses my first quarter. One about modernism, one about surrealism and one about the reader as a participant in meaning creation. My las quarter I had a creative writing course and a literature course about the printing press. They were all so good and I have learned so much!
recommended_courses: I only had good experiences with my courses and teachers. All the professors were so nice and helpful and the classes were so intersting. I guess people just need to apply for courses that seem interesting to them!
unexpected_costs: Food was more expensive than I expected. I had lived in the US before but the prices were so high now. I guess Seattle is an expensive city. I spent a lot of money on traveling. We flew out two times to visit other states. I would recommend to save some money up for this.
cost_comparison: Food was more expensive but transportation in Seattle is only about a 50 dollars pr quarter (3 months) if you are a student so I saved a lot of money on that.
activities_available: I guess you can do anything a UW. They offer so many clubs and activities.
activities_recommended: We went line dancing on a country bar once a week. That was very fun. I know that some people did Salsa and rock climbing too. You can do any type of sport.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend that you rent a car and drive out to see some of the nature surrounding Seattle. It is so beautiful. There is a company called ScanDesign who arrange events for danish exchange students. New students must get in touch with them! They are so nice and everything is free!
culture_adjustment: It is difficult to say. I guess you never really get used to a culture that is so different from your own. Things and people kept surprising me but that is the fun of a exchange semester. And I settled pretty quickly. I guess you do that when you know that you only have 6 months in the new place.
socializing_tips: My classmates were not so open to be friends so I guess the best way would be to join a club or a sport.
cultural_challenges: I guess one of the biggest cultural differences is the gun law. I never felt unsafe because of it but it is wired that people there have such a fundamental different view. Seattle is pretty liberal but there are still some political differences as well. And I hate that every time you need help from a company you must talk to a robot or like three different people. It is so difficult to just solve basic problems with for instance an internet provider. New students must be aware of this!
culture_appreciated: I love the English language and I really like how there are so many different cultures in Seattle. And the nature there is so beautiful. I am a huge fan of the US, and this exchange semester has only made me more of a fan!
top3_advice: 1. Bring a mastercard. We had so much trouble paying with our danish cards. You must bring a master card and get an american card. Chase was not a good bank, I have heard good things about American Express. And bring a second danish card to keep in your house if you loose your wallet (that happened to me and it sucked). 2. You must pick a housing that already has internet because it was so difficult to find a provider who would give internet to a non US citizen (I do not know why but it was). 3. Don't bring so much stuff or clothes. You can buy it when you are there and you want to be able to bring a lot of things home. 4. Travel as much as you can. You have such a great opportunity to see the country and in country flights are pretty cheap.
other_useful_info: See my answer above
most_rewarding: All the travling that I got to do. And also that I got to experience college life. Overall I just had a great time and I am so grateful that I got the opportunity to do this!
greatest_challenge: We had so much trouble with things such as getting internet access and renting cars. I do not know why it is so difficult to be a foreigner in the US, but you must be aware of this. I guess it helps if you have a mastercard and an American Express card.

crucial_aspects: A range of factors were important to me when choosing my destination. First of all, I was interested in trying to live in a non-European country, as I expected the culture to be different, but I was at the same time determined to attend a well renowned university. I ended up in Seattle as the Northwest Pacific is known to be absolutely beautiful nature wise, but also because I could choose to stay for two quarters, which gave me the opportunity to become familiar with the university, and make lasting friendships. The amazing campus didn't hurt either.
info_ease: I had done a lot (a lot..) of emailing beforehand, so I had some good contacts when getting there. The university staff is extremely fast at getting back to you, which is pretty useful as a new student - we're talking the same or next day. The more difficult part might be figuring out where to look for the information you're in need of. The FIUTS is a nonprofit organization founded on campus which focuses on international relationships, and besides arranging events, they can often point you in the direction needed, whether regarding housing, how to get around, or suggestions on cool hangout spots. If you need information on specific courses, you can email the professor directly.
arrival_assistance: As an international student, you'll have to attend an obligatory FIUTS event where you're provided some useful information and welcomed. If you don't need further information during your stay, you can in theory leave it at that. The professors will introduce you to your courses, and most courses will spend a lecture or two on getting you settled with any program you might be required to download.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration is easy when you've become familiar with UW's MyPlan page. You'll get a UW netID when accepted at the university, that you need in order to register for courses online. When browsing through courses you can add them to your MyPlan and register from there. It's not the easiest system at first, but when you become a bit acquainted with it, it is actually quite helpful.
registration_help: Some courses require a system key in order to register, which a professor or the faculty can provide. System keys aren't needed that often though, so most of the time you'll be able to register easily when your registration period begins. If you have any questions regarding the course or if the level is of any concern to you, the professors and TA's are really helpful, and usually get back to you pretty fast.
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted, so my main issue was that many courses were scheduled at the same time, requiring me to prioritize. That was honestly a bit annoying, but that way I had an opportunity to sign up for some classes I didn't think of originally.
registration_advice: I would recommend spending some time deciding on courses prior to the registration period, as some are filled rather quickly. In my case it wasn't an issue, but depending on your field, it might be to you. UW offers a lot of courses though, so you should be able to get something that interests you, even if your first choice fills up faster than expected.
course_level: Please don't worry about the academic level. If you spend as much time on your studies as in Denmark, you'll do absolutely fine, and if you spend less, you'll also get by. As long as you make sure of handing stuff in on time, you won't run into any trouble. I studied at UW as an undergrad student, but ended up taking some master courses, and the level was still suitable. If you do have some concerns though, you can always contact the professor, and they'll be able to guide you.
teaching_comparison: The teacher-student tone is overall as you're used to in Denmark: down to earth, usually first name based, nothing to worry about. Some teachers might prefer being addressed as professor, but they will make that clear early on. The style of teaching is quite different in a number of ways. For instance, you'll be expected to be doing assignments, exercises, quizzes, and post on discussion boards during the quarters, where the amount obviously differs. It can feel a bit overwhelming at first, so if you, like me, prefer your workload presented in an easy and clear way, I found an Excel sheet containing all my tasks a very useful tool.
courses_enrolled: - Introduction to Geographic Information Systems in Forest Resources - Rivers and Beaches - Remote Sensing of the Environment
recommended_courses: If you like me haven't had remote sensing, I would recommend ‘Remote Sensing of the Environment'. Monika Moskal is an amazing teacher, and the course provides a broad idea of the applications of remote sensing in earth sciences, including some LiDAR and general classification. I also enjoyed ‘The Global Carbon Cycle And Climate', which introduces Python in an manageable way, if you're new to programming.
unexpected_costs: Concerts, theatres, and such are pretty similar to Danish prices, but food and bars were definitely more expensive than what I expected. For some reason vegetables especially were expensive, so I had some rather unsatisfying meals once in a while, when feeling a bit cheap.
cost_comparison: I had expected to buy a bicycle to save money on transportation, but you'll automatically get charged for the so-called ‘UPass' which provides you with free public transportation in Seattle. The UPass is a bit expensive ($92 pr quarter), but once paid, it's very convenient to have. Tipping is always expected and is usually around $15-$20. Taxes are not included in the prices you see in stores or restaurants, and you can always pay with card - cash is rarely necessary unless having to pay for the bus.
activities_available: The organizations FIUTS and Circle, both located at campus, offer international students an array of social, get-to-know-each-other activities which are especially nice to attend in the beginning. The IMA has some fitness classes you can sign up for, and then there are the student led clubs that you can join.
activities_recommended: While in Seattle I ended up taking sailing lessons, which I absolutely loved! Seattle has some big lakes, so if you're looking to get into sailing, I would recommend that! At The Little Red Hen they have free linedance every Monday night, and a number of bars have trivia nights which are a lot of fun too! Seattle is also known for its grunge music, so if you enjoy concerts that's a must. If you like cats you could also check out Neko Cat Café. Their Instagram is cute.
weekend_recommendations: If someone were to visit Seattle, I would recommend some of the parks such as Discovery Park (especially the lighthouse), Golden Gardens (where you if lucky can see sealions), Union Bay Natural Area, and the Arboretum Waterfront Trail. If going out, The Mountaineering Club is a cool rooftop bar with fancy cocktails at the University Avenue which is definitely worth a visit. Seattle also has a number of farmers markets whereof I especially liked the one in Ballard, open Sunday mornings. Another site worth mentioning is the Ballard Locks where you can also see the fish ladders. If you're going in December, you should visit Candy Cane Lane, which is a cute, tiny street in Ravenna decorated with Christmas lights.
culture_adjustment: Supermarkets are bigger and further apart, the houses are bigger, the measurements are all different to the ones you're used to, and you need a car if leaving the city, but other than that Seattle isn't that odd. The jetlag probably caused the biggest disturbance, but that will wear off quickly.
socializing_tips: As an international student, you'll more easily interact with other international students, as they are the ones in search of new friends. The American friends I made were housemates, friends' housemates, FIUTS staff, or people I met rather randomly when going out. If being open and taking initiative, it will happen naturally.
cultural_challenges: I found it a bit annoying that not having a car would sometimes pose an issue, which is why it's clever to joining a club or rent a car with friends, when going somewhere.
culture_appreciated: I really liked the American openness and being greeted whenever entering a store or paying for something. I find myself in need of a Danish equivalent of “How're you?” now..
top3_advice: - Rain clothes - Hiking boots - Slippers
other_useful_info: The campus has a lot of great study spaces to discover if you prefer studying at campus. You can even reserve a private study room if in need, but this usually requires you to do so a day or two in advance.
most_rewarding: I really enjoyed having an actual campus, as it somehow makes you feel as a part of a large community. Also, I generally just loved getting to know so many amazing and lovely people from all over, as I have developed a better understanding of a lot of countries, as well as now having the option to visit people from here and there.
greatest_challenge: I had some personal challenges in the very beginning, as my partner and I broke up, making me considering going home for a few weeks - but I'm so glad I didn't! If you come across something similar, let your housemates know so they can look out for you, keep yourself busy with fun stuff, and call your friends and family back home. Don't let it ruin your exchange, because you rock for doing it in the first place!
other_comments: Enjoy! Time passes so quickly and before you know it, you're back home missing all your new friends. Have fun, make friends, and challenge yourself.

crucial_aspects: In my choice of University of Washington (UW) academic opportunities were the most important thing. There was a highly esteemed Department of Communication at UW which intrigued me a lot as I sat at home and researched among different universities. But the beautiful and vibrant surroundings of Seattle and Washington State was also an essential contributing factor to the final choice.
overall_comments: I has been the most wonderful experience full of tackled challanges and personal growth. The only reson i dot credit this bullet with the highest mark is due to the turbulent application process and the many misunderstandings between me, KU and UW. Also, there were Covid restrictions in Washington at the beginning of 2022 which restricted the first two months of my stay a lot.
info_ease: Very easy. UW is a large university and they are very used to having international students. UW Study Abroad, FUITS and ISS were organizations that helped out a lot in the beginning.
arrival_assistance: FIUTS (Foundation for International Understanding Through Students) was a great help. The did an emboark-session on Zoom within the first 1-2 weeks. Also, we received several emails from Study Abroad in the first few weeks with important information regarding our visa status, special opportunities as international students etc.
arrival_comments: I think they did their job to perfection, honestly. It all seemed very professional and they always replied fast when one had questions or inquiries.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I has been the most wonderful experience full of tackled challanges and personal growth. The only reson i dot credit this bullet with the highest mark is due to the turbulent application process and the many misunderstandings between me, KU and UW. Also, there were Covid restrictions in Washington at the beginning of 2022 which restricted the first two months of my stay a lot.
registration_process: There was a lot of misunderstandings and complications with me registering as an international graduate student at University of Washington, Seattle, which in the end costed me a lot of frustration, time and money. In the end I had to apply as an undergraduate student to be accepted and enrolled, which was less than ideal. Honestly, though, I think the fault was more at poor information I received from UCPH Abroad which in the end caused me to miss deadlines. The hos institution, UW Study Abroad was actually pretty reliant in the registration process.
registration_help: UW Study Abroad gave us an email address where many of us exchange students had success getting help.
registration_success: Once I was finally accepted, registration for classes was fairly decent. Because I wanted to take graduate courses but was enrolled in their system as an undergraduate, I had to communicate back and forth with all the professors to explain that I was academically skilled enough to take the classes. Again, this would have been easier if my graduate application had worked out. But I got all the courses that I hoped for except for one.
registration_advice: Be willing to fight a bit for the classes you want. Often a few emails to the right professors or a talk after class can get you far. The professors tend to reward academic interest as well as persistence.
academics_comments: I has been the most wonderful experience full of tackled challanges and personal growth. The only reson i dot credit this bullet with the highest mark is due to the turbulent application process and the many misunderstandings between me, KU and UW. Also, there were Covid restrictions in Washington at the beginning of 2022 which restricted the first two months of my stay a lot.
course_level: my impression was that there were plenty of relevant classes to choose from. Each class differ a lot from the other and it is my impression that the professors have more independence in how to structure curriculum and tests than in DK. Regarding level: If you choose 400 and 500-point classes, you can get them merited as MA classes. 300 and below are merited as BA classes.
teaching_comparison: As said above, the professors at UW had more freedom was my impression. I had five different classes in 2 quarters and each was unique. They grade differently though. They accumulate grades the same way we do in DK in High school. Attendance, discussions, presentations and final exams accumulate your grade in the of the quarter on the 4.0 GPA scale.
courses_enrolled: Rhetoric of Science (5 credits) Literature and Science (5 credits) Rhetorical Field Methods (5 credits) Class, Labor and American Capitalism (5 credits) Contemporary American Public Address (5 credits)
recommended_courses: Class, Labor and American Capitalism (5 credits) was a beautiful course for me, even though it was not within my original department (Communication). I would recommend diving into any kind of classes which would give you background knowledge of the American culture, in which you find yourself at your exchange.
unexpected_costs: Seattle was just in general very expensive. Compared to my original budget food prices went through the roof in 2022. Especially if you also want to visit local restaurants, food markets etc.
cost_comparison: Food! Concerts! Going out! Almost everything, honestly, were more expensive than expected - maybe also due to the sudden inflation in the US in the beginning of 2022. Transport was all right since you can bye a U-pass through the university which gives you total access to all public transport in Seattle (including several ferries!).
activities_available: Everything. I did mostly climbing, yoga and tennis but there were a plethora of social, cultural and sports opportunities.
activities_recommended: The organization FIUTS is a good way to meet other exchange students. Also, often the independent Scan Design Foundation will have some cool free events for Danish exchange students.
weekend_recommendations: Try to see some of the nature outside of Seattle. If you team up with locals with a car (or rent one) Mount Ranier, Olympic and North Cascades national park are only a few hours away. If you come in the winter/fall then I would recommend all the ski opportunities, eg Crystal Mountain, which was frequently frequented by my roommates.
culture_adjustment: It was fine, but of course, one has to be prepared that adjusting and adapting takes time - and it does not happen if you do not actively engage. I would say it took me three months to feel at home in Seattle.
socializing_tips: Meetup was an app I used to schedule hikes and events with local people from Seattle. It is a good way to meet people outside of the university environment.
cultural_challenges: The US is not too bad. But the language barrier of course was difficult in the beginning.
culture_appreciated: Their relationship with nature. Everyone I met was pretty outdoorsy and was always on their way to summit some mountain or on their way skiing. A wonderful way to live.
top3_advice: Team up with other exchange students from KU beforehand. The application process at KU is ridiculous and you risk being faulty advised, but it is all easier if you help each other out. Be persistent in communicating with home and host universities. As soon as you are in the States, everything will work itself out. :-)
other_useful_info: Be prepared to study a lot too as UW require you to "overload" compared to what you will be merited for by KU. I had 25 credits completing five classes, which in total which equals 50 ECTS. Though, I will only be merited for 30 ECTS from KU (three of the classes). The Winter quarter starts in early January.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people.
greatest_challenge: Getting there in the first place. The application process took a lot of (unnecessary) effort.

crucial_aspects: It was crucial to me that the institution had a lot of opportunities for extra curricular activities and beautiful surroundings and nature. Furthermore, it was very important to me that the destination that I chose had a big international environment and was rich on culture. Lastly, I found it very important that the institution offered classes in my area of studies that I found interesting.
overall_comments: The application process is very confusing and difficult to navigate in, especially working with UCPH administration, but hang in there, it is a lot easier when you arrive in the UW and the administration at UW are always ready to help.
info_ease: Somewhat easy. If in doubt you can always email the office of international students at UW and they will help you out,
arrival_assistance: The school have different organisations that help new international students and organize events so you can meet other international students.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: The application process is very confusing and difficult to navigate in, especially working with UCPH administration, but hang in there, it is a lot easier when you arrive in the UW and the administration at UW are always ready to help.
registration_process: It is a very easy step by step process and if you are ever in doubt you can ask and UW will help you
registration_help: ISS - international student services are always very helpfull
registration_success: I got all the classes that I wanted
registration_advice: Register for more classes than you need to take. Do this because in the first week you can drop classes you do not want, but then you have the opportunity to decide instead of ending in the situation where all the classes you want are fully booked.
academics_comments: The application process is very confusing and difficult to navigate in, especially working with UCPH administration, but hang in there, it is a lot easier when you arrive in the UW and the administration at UW are always ready to help.
course_level: The level of courses are very reasonable.
teaching_comparison: There are a lot more assignments in the classes that I took at UW then at UCPH. However, the difficultness level is a bit lower and the assignments are also smaller.
courses_enrolled: Environmental Health In Media (ENV H) Managing the Health Risks of Climate Change (GH / ENV H) Contemporary Social Movements (SOC) Media and Society (SOC) Comparative Politics (POL S) Race, Identity, And The Ancient Mediterranean World (CLAS)
recommended_courses: Race, Identity, And The Ancient Mediterranean World (CLAS) - If you like the classical world and critical thinking about race, identity and how we see and understand the world today. Contemporary Social Movements (SOC) - This class is really interesting if you are interested in social movements, how they are formed and how they affect political systems. Comparative Politics (POL S) - This class goes really well with the class Contemporary Social Movements. In this class you cover the various political systems and how they work and how they affect culture and society. Media and Society (SOC) - This class is really interesting if you are curious about how media affect society, but also how society affect media and how everything is intertwined.
unexpected_costs: Insurance, transportation card, emergency backpack etc. that you have to buy when you live on campus
cost_comparison: The food and housing is very expensive in Seattle. I lived in the on campus housing, which is not much cheeper than finding your own housing off campus.
activities_available: Almost all sports you can think of is available at UW. Other than that there is a big gym with basketball courts, climbing walls, a pool etc. You can also rent gear from the gym like for example tennis rackets, kayaks, bikes, or even skiing gear.
activities_recommended: Go to the IMA and do whatever sport you like or registrer for classes at the IMA like yoga. I would also recommend UWild Adventures if you like hiking or signing up for a team like the volleyball team.
weekend_recommendations: FUITS and other organisations arrange a lot of different trips and hikes in the weekends that you can sign up for. I also recommend going out and seeing the beautiful nature in Washington State, you can for example take the ferry to Bainbridge Island or rent a car and go to Forks, Hoh Rainforrest, La push, the Olympics, the North Cascades etc.
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: Talk to your classmates. People are always very friendly and keen on meeting new people, sometimes you just have to take the first step.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: People are very talkative and friendly.
top3_advice: 1. Keep an open mind and interact with your peers 2. Sometimes it can be difficult to adjust a new culture and city, but it will quickly get better 3. Bring a raincoat and hiking boots
other_useful_info: Use www.ratemyprofessors.com before choosing classes if you want to look at reviews of the professor whose class you are thinking of choosing.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people and making friends from all over the world and learning and living in another cultural setting.
greatest_challenge: Adapting the new settings and way of studying

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne læse på et engelsksproget universitet. Jeg var især interesseret i PNW på grund af min studieretning og det plantesamfund, der er i PNW. Derudover er Washington en af de mest liberale stater i USA. Jeg ville især også gerne opleve et af de store amerikanske universiteter og det campusliv der følger med her. Jeg synes især Seattle er attraktivt fordi der er let mulighed for at komme ud af byen og opleve nationalparker/natur mm.
overall_comments: Det er svært at forestille sig hvad det er man kommer til og uanset destinationen er jeg sikker på det ville være en fed oplevelse.
info_ease: Jeg synes det var svært at få ordenligt kontakt og information fra KU. Især fordi jeg ikke havde mulighed for at deltage i informationsmødet pga en eksamen og KU ikke gjorde noget for at hjælpe. Processen med at få DS 2019 formen var meget lang og meget svært at få information omkring. Især på grund af covid 19. Det sværeste i processen var at jeg er kandidatstuderende på KU, men Ku anbefalede mig at søge ind på bachelorniveau i USA, fordi det er lettere og der ikke er så mange krav/dokumenter man skal udfylde. Jeg mødte efterfølgende mange andre danske og europæiske studerende, som godt havde fået det til at lykkedes. Jeg føler mig derfor lidt vildledt af KU, og tror umiddelbart løsningen bare var lettere for KU.
arrival_assistance: Der var et velkomstmøde for internationale studerende et par dage efter ankomst. Jeg synes UW var gode til at sende information ud via mail og der er masser af kontaktsider/telefonnumre, hvis man var i tvivl om noget. Der er nogle ting ved tilmeldning af fag som er lidt lettere, hvis man har et amerikansk telefonnummer fra starten.
arrival_comments: Professorerne var meget hurtige til at svare. Generelt tror jeg det handler om at finde fag der passer til en studieretning og niveau og så skrive til professoren, hvis man ikke kan tilmelde sig faget umiddelbart via deres Myplan. Der er prerequireties til mange af fagene, men jeg havde ikke problemer, hvis jeg sendte en mail og mit cv/fag fra DK, så kunne de se at faget var indenfor mit kompetenceområde.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Det er svært at forestille sig hvad det er man kommer til og uanset destinationen er jeg sikker på det ville være en fed oplevelse.
registration_process: Man tilmelder sig fag online på MyPlan, hvor man også kan lave et fiktivt skema, for at sikre, der ikke er overlab imellem fag. Man skal være sikker på at man kan nå at gå fra det ene lokale til det andet. Er der langt imellem kan det godt tage 10-20 min at gå igennem campus. I den første uge kan man tilmelde/afmelde sig fag, så man kan godt overveje at vælge ekstra mange credits i starten og så droppe et fag indenfor den første uges tid. Der er let tilgængelig information om reglerne for at droppe/tilmelde sig fag (skal ske indenfor den første/anden undervisningsuge). Som undergraduate skulle jeg have 12 credits pr quarter. Jeg havde 14 credits i første quarter, hvilket gjorde det muligt kun at have 10 i andet quarter. Det var dejligt at have lidt mere fritid i 2. quarter, hvor man kendte alt meget bedre og derfor naturligt havde mange flere fritidsinteresser mm. Man skal have 24 credits på 2 quarters. Første quarter skal man minumum læse 12 credits. hvis man som jeg ønsker nedsat credits i 2. quarter, skal man søge herom ved den Internationale Student Services - da der er krav om fuldtidsstudie for at ens visum kan bibeholdes!
registration_help: Der var alt den hjælp man havde brug for. Nogle gange var det lettere at ringe studenterservice op. Jeg vil derfor anbefale at få et amerikansk nummer hurtigst muligt. Jeg havde mintmobile, som umiddelbart var den billigeste løsning, hvis man vælger Esimkort, kan man få sit nummer med det samme.
registration_success: Der var flere fag, som jeg var interesseret i, der blev fyldt op inden jeg kunne registrere fag. Jeg skrev dog til professoren. Nogle gange åbner de op for et par ekstrapladser eller man kan komme på venteliste og blive optaget på faget indenfor 1.-2. uge. Hvis der er fag man er meget interesseret i, vil jeg anbefale at skrive til professoren og få oplysninger om undervisningslokale mm, så man evt kan komme til undervisningen fra starten, selvom man måske først bliver officielt optaget senere. Mange fag har dog discussion sessions/lab hvor man skal arbejde i grupper osv, så det kommer meget an på om det passer alt.
registration_advice: Vær hurtigt ude med at tilmelde sig fag og skriv til professoren. Der er mange pladser som bliver frigivet indenfor de 2 første uger, så det er bare med at holde øje. Har man amerikansk mobilnummer kan man også tilmelde sig en service, så man får en sms, når der er ledige pladser, som åbner op, men man skal skynde sig, da det er først til mølle. Jeg vil også anbefalde at tage et par credits i et nyt felt, gerne et lidt mere kreativt fag end ens uddannelse. jeg læste for eksempel spansk i 2. quarter.
academics_comments: Det er svært at forestille sig hvad det er man kommer til og uanset destinationen er jeg sikker på det ville være en fed oplevelse.
course_level: Der er generelt mere arbejde/forberedelse til fag på grad niveau, men er man registreret på gradniveau skal man til gengæld kun lave 10 credits pr quarter. Jeg læste fag på niveau 300-500. Jeg var indskrevet som undergraduate på UW, men havde ikke problemer med at tilmelde mig gradniveau, når jeg sendte mine oplysninger fra DK til professoren.
teaching_comparison: Der er generelt meget mere test og deltagelse i løbet af quarteret. I mit ene fag skulle jeg oploade et spørgsmål/undren til undervisningen og artiklerne vi havde læst til ugen. Derudover skulle jeg komme med svar til de andre studerende. I et andet fag havde vi 5 rapporter, der skulle laves i grupper i løbet af de 10 undervisningsuger. Jeg oplevede at der enten kun var en skriftlig mindre sluteksamen eller ingen i de fleste fag, fordi man netop deltager mere aktivt undervejs.
courses_enrolled: International trade, marketing and environment (ESRM 423) (3 credits) Wildlife Ecology and Conservation (ESRM 450) (5 credits) Fundamentals of Plant-Soil Interactions (SEFS 510) (3 credits Pacific Tourism (SMEA 485) (3 credits)
recommended_courses: Jeg lærte meget i Wildlife Ecology and Conservation, men det var også et fag der krævede at man deltog i undervisning og besvarede quiz og læste artikler til hver uge. Derudover var faget i tourisme meget interessant og åbnede nye vinkler op ang. tourisme. Professoren havde en meget anden tilgang til undervisningen og det var meget samtale blandt os alle og handlede meget om at finde citater i teksterne. Jeg synes faget Arctic Literature var rigtig godt. Det var meget interessant at lære om nordisk/arktisk kultur fra en usa vinkel. Spændende bøger og tekter og en fantastisk underviser. Generelt havde jeg fag med aktiv deltagelse og jeg har ikke haft fag med forelæsninger, hvor der sad flere 100 studerende.
unexpected_costs: Jeg var overrasket over hvor dyrt det er at købe mad. Derudover brugte jeg mange penge på frokost på campus, café og kaffe med mine venner. Man bruger mange flere penge end man umiddelbart tror, der er meget inflation og høj dollarkurs mm og nok også prisstigninger efter covid. Dertil var dollarkursen meget høj (1 $= 7 kroner), hvilket gør at alt bare er dyrt. Man skal regne med at en kaffe, en øl, frokost salt mm er ligeså dyrt, hvis ikke dyrere end i DK.
cost_comparison: Det var meget dyrt at handle i supermarkeder, alkohol er også dyrt. Man skal virkelig tænke sig om inden man signer en lease om bolig, så man ikke sætter sig for dyrt, da man ofte binder sig for 6 måneder. Der er ca 10% taxes på alt man køber!
activities_available: Der var nærmest alt slags sport. Jeg spillede lidt fodbold og tennis, men brugte mest fitnesscenteret og betalte også 50$ for et quarter, hvor jeg så kunne deltage i alle deres holdtræninger (zumba, dans, træning, yoga mm)
activities_recommended: Alle sportsgrene i IMA. Det er et fedt sted at hænge ud med sine venner. Derudover deltog jeg oftest i Pubquiz på College In Pub eller Big Time Brewery med mine venner. Vi tog også til Line Dance på Little Red Hen ved Greenlake. Green Lake og Gas Works Park er skønne parker at gå tur i eller se view over skyline.
weekend_recommendations: Sørg for at tage på ture til fx Vancouver, San Francisco og Olympic NP i weekenderne, men nyd også bare weekender i Seattle og dagshike lige udenfor byen. Jeg vil anbefale at invistere i et skipass (EPIC eller ICON) hvis man vil stå meget på ski. Det er virkelig dyrt at stå på ski, op mod 1000 kr pr dag, hvis man ikke har skipass. Det er også lettest, hvis man kender nogle der har bil tilrådighed. Jeg meldte mig ind i Snowklubben, da der oftest var folk der kørte til skisportsstederne.
culture_adjustment: Det var meget let at tilpasse sig kulturen. Seattle er meget moderne.
socializing_tips: Man kan prøve at bo med amerikanere, men ellers møder man dem i fagene (med mindre der er covid og alt er online). Generelt skal man bare være nysgerrig og spørge folk om de vil mødes/lave noget.
cultural_challenges: Jeg synes ikke der var noget som var svært generelt. Jeg var meget sammen med mange andre internationale studerende, da det generelt er dem, der har tid og er i samme situation som en selv. Bonus ved det er at man får kontakter rundt i verdenen.
culture_appreciated: Jeg synes virkelig at amerikanerne er god til at skabe et godt studiemiljø med gode fritidsaktiviteter sport med mere.
top3_advice: Deltag i alle arrangementer i begyndelsen (selvom det måske er lidt overvældende) Tilmeld dig en klub eller sport fra starten i IMA bygningen. Inviter folk til fest eller aktivitet, så du lærer folk at kende.
other_useful_info: Hvis man ønsker at leje en bil, skal man have et creditkort (de godtager ikke debitcard) derudover skal man have en amerikansk bankkonto, det kan anbeales at bruge den til alle ens køb, da der ofte er gebyr på danske kort.
most_rewarding: Jeg har fået nogle rigtig gode venner, udviklet mit sprog og fået et meget bedre indblik i hvor komplekst et land USA er.
greatest_challenge: Man skal måske forberede sig på at man er lidt alene i starten, men det er okay, det tager lidt tid at få dannet sig en vennegruppe netværk. Derfor skal man bare være åben og deltage i alle arrangementer.
other_comments: Gør det. Jeg ville ønske jeg havde taget afsted før i mit uddannelseforløb. Vil klart anbefale at tage afsted på ens bachelor. De fleste studerende er imellem 21-25 år.

crucial_aspects: At studere i et engelsktalende land på et godt universitet, prøve storbylivet kombineret med storslået natur og prøve mig af i en akademisk akademisk miljø og dermed komme meget ud af min komfort zone
overall_comments: Opholdet i Seattle var generelt rigtigt godt og lærerigt. Prøvede at gå fantastisk smukt og godt universitet, hvor jeg havde nogle spændende fag. Mødte en masse søde mennesker fra hele verden og fik nogle gode venner og udforsket den smukke natur omkring Seattle, som gør byen så unik
info_ease: Generelt synes jeg kommunikation fra UW Seattle var ganske fin, og man relativt nemt komme i kontakt med de ansatte for udviklingsprogrammet. Dog virker det kontor til at være lidt underbemandet, men de gør deres bedste
arrival_assistance: Fik løbende information fra de studiekoordinatorer og tilsendt intro-program og lignende, hvor vi mødte de andre udvekslingsstuderende, så det var ganske fint og informativt
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Opholdet i Seattle var generelt rigtigt godt og lærerigt. Prøvede at gå fantastisk smukt og godt universitet, hvor jeg havde nogle spændende fag. Mødte en masse søde mennesker fra hele verden og fik nogle gode venner og udforsket den smukke natur omkring Seattle, som gør byen så unik
registration_process: Man skal tilmelde sig fag inde på noget, der hedder MyPlan i UW's system, og det er nogenlunde til at finde ud af. Man kan også bruge fagets "SLN kode" til at tilføje det til sin plan
registration_help: Der var noget info på MyPlan omkring, hvordan man gør, og studiekoordinatorerne stod også klar til at hjælpe samt ansatte fra det enkelte fakultet. Dem kunne man booke møder med, hvis man ønskede at snakke med dem om de forskellige fagmuligheder. Jeg benyttede mig dog ikke af denne mulighed
registration_success: Jeg fik egentligt mere eller mindre de fag, som jeg havde ønsket, så det var meget tilfredsstillende
registration_advice: Vælg så hurtigst muligt de fag, som du finder spændende og tilmeld hellere et fag for meget end for lidt, da man kan droppe fagene i de første uger, efter man er startet. Så kan man lige se, om faget er det rigtige for en
academics_comments: Opholdet i Seattle var generelt rigtigt godt og lærerigt. Prøvede at gå fantastisk smukt og godt universitet, hvor jeg havde nogle spændende fag. course_level: Synes egentligt undervisningen var god, og at underviserne var yderst kompetente, men det er mit indtryk, at det var klart nemmere at få højere karakterer og vel nærmest umuligt at dumpe et fag, da de fleste af de andre udvekslingsstuderende også scorede rigtigt høje karakterer, selvom vi også brugte tiden på meget andet ift. hvordan jeg ville studere hjemme i Danmark
teaching_comparison: Det er en noget anderledes akademisk kultur med mange flere tests og små ugentlige afleveringer, participation points på holdtimer (ikke tilhænger af denne tilgang) - man får point for at sige noget, men ikke specifikt kvaliteten af, hvad man siger. Den helt store forskel jeg oplevede var, at det tilsyneladende er langt mere normalt på et amerikansk universitet som UW at komme med sin egen mening uden at underbygge det ligeså grundigt fagligt, så meget: "I think that..., "I feel like" Havde også et seminar om Klimakrisen, som var rigtigt spændende og langt mere interaktivt end andre fag, jeg har prøvet i DK. Det var mere som et bogklub, hvor professoren faciliterede undervisningen, og os studerende så skulle diskutere og holde oplæg på skift
courses_enrolled: POL S 307 RELIGION & WORLD POLITICS POL S 401 POLITICAL THEORY ADVANCED SEMINAR: CLIMATE CRISIS POL S 371 GLOBAL CRIME & CORRUPTION POL S 442 GOVERNMENT & POLITICS OF CHINA
recommended_courses: Jeg synes særligt seminaret om klimakrisen var meget spændende og gav mig mange spændende indsigter i vores hold-disskusioner. Særligt at høre unge amerikaneres perspektiv på klimapolitik, og hvilket ansvar USA har / ikke har, var rigtigt spændende. Kurset om Kina og landets politiske system var også rigtigt lærerigt og spændende pga. der var mange amerikanske og også kinesiske studerende på det kursus
unexpected_costs: Madvarer er rigtigt dyre i Seattle, især grøntsager, kød og brød. Generelt er leveomkosninger bare rigtigt høje i Seattle, særligt husleje og gå ud og spise
cost_comparison: Alt var egentligt dyrere, end jeg havde regnet med. Havde aldrig troet det ville blive dyrere end at bo i Kbh, men det kunne det, så søg en masse legater eller spar op/tag nogle SU lån med eller lignende
activities_available: Jeg spillede badminton med nogle af de udvekslingsstuderende og tog på adskillige ski- og vandreture, men det var primært noget, vi selv arrangerede og mødte derigennem også amerikanske studerende (fx hinandens roomies eller studievenner)
activities_recommended: Der er masser af forskellige klubber, som man kan engagere sig i, fx skiklub, hiking clubs, dansehold og meget andet, så hvis du har interesse indenfor det, så prøv det af!
weekend_recommendations: Udforsk Washington State, det er er den smukkeste, storslåede og meget diverse natur, særligt regnskoven i Olympic National Park, bjergene i North Cascades og vandre rundt om vulkanen Mount Rainier var fantastisk. Kan virkeligt også anbefale at tage på skiture i de kolde vintermåneder, der er gode steder som Stevens Pass kun et par timers kørsel fra byen (ikke vælge Snoqualmie, Stevens Pass og Crystal Mountain er langt bedre steder med bedre sne). Besøg Vancouver, San Francisco, lav et roadtrip igennem nogle stater, som vi gjorde, da vi var færdige i juni 2023 (Colorado, Utah og New Mexico)
culture_adjustment: Forholdsvist nemt ift. de andre udvekslingsstuderende og også med amerikanerne, de fleste er unge, progressive mennesker med et internationalt udsyn, så på den måde er vi meget ens. Jeg kunne godt mærke, at den danske humor nogle gange er lidt anderledes ift. vi bruger mere ironi og nok har en mere mørk humor, men sådanne kultursammenstød er også sjove at opleve
socializing_tips: Jeg mødte de fleste igennem udvekslingsprogrammet og ellers på vandreture, skiture, strandture eller byture mv.
cultural_challenges: Måske ikke en kulturel forskel, men en systemisk forskel: der er mange hjemløse i Seattle og folk med psykiske problemer, og det vænnede jeg mig aldrig til at se alt det armod i gadebilledet, selvom nogle områder er meget værre end andre. Kontrasten mellem rig og fattig var til at få øje på, og det kunne godt påvirke mit humør og sætte pris på det mere lige samfund, jeg kom fra
culture_appreciated: Amerikaneres gæstfrihed og nysgerrighed på os europæere og måske særligt skandinavere. Jeg kunne godt mærke, at der er meget skandinavisk historie i Pacific Northwest området
top3_advice: Læg et realistisk budget og regn med, at alt bliver dyrere end ventet Tag det hele i dit tempo og sig ja og nej til de tilbud om aktiviteter du får, alt efter hvad du selv har lyst til Forbered dig på, at vejret er meget som herhjemme med en del regn (medbring praktisk tøj). Dog er forårs- og sommermånederne ret magiske i Seattle, når det hele springer ud og bliver grønt
other_useful_info: Udforsk Seattles mange sjove nabolog og fantastisk smukke sites, det er en helt særlig by ift. samspillet mellem det urbane og naturen
most_rewarding: Personlig udvikling og naturoplevelser
greatest_challenge: De første par måneder (januar/februar), hvor det hele var mørkt, regnfuldt og koldt. Derefter blev det hele kun federe i takt med vejret blev godt, og alle var ude og nyde byen eller naturen

crucial_aspects: The academic aspect of exploring a country, where the school system differed from the Danish way of teaching and also differed in what was being teached. Also, I was really interested in experiencing the american culture more in depth rather than just what you could learn from a 3 weeks holiday there. I feel that the american culture is something which most be experienced through living in the country for a longer time to also be able to meet people and learn about their impressions of their own country. Furthermore I chose Seattle do to its placing in Washington State by the pacific northwest and its beautiful surrounding nature which was perfect for hiking and skiing combined with a vibrant city.
info_ease: It was very easy to get into the country and the visa proces after arriving at the airport was much less frightening than I had imagined. I had a family friend, who I lived with for the first 2 weeks, so he picked me up and showed me everything I needed to know, therefor I don't really know how easy it is to find information, if you don't know anybody in the country beforehand.
arrival_assistance: There was introduction days at the university three days before school started, which was a helpful way of getting to know the university, which is very big compared to CSS. They also had an orientation day for all the new international students, where they told os all the relevant information regarding how to sign up for classes, what we needed to know about health insurance, who to contact regarding this and that and so on, which was very helpful. But still, it is a very big institution and there were still, after does days and in the beginning of the first quarter, a lot of things we didn't know about, that we learnt along the way
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Course registration opened to students to months before school started and therefor also 1.5 months before I got to the college. I found the online proces of registrering very difficult, since you had to show that you had the right prerequisites to be able to take courses higher than level 100-200, since they didn't know your prerequisites as an international student. This meant, that I had to write to each professor and ask, if I could take their course, and often times I could not. But then when I arrived at the university and could talk to the professors myself everything was much easier. So therefor I didn't sign up for any classes besides one before I arrived. This also meant, that a lot of the classes that I wanted was already filled up, unfortunately.
registration_help: I had an online zoom-session with the psychology department and their study guide before I arrived, because I was a little stressed about waiting to sign up for courses. They were really helpfull and gave me names of different people I could reach out to to get further help, which was a big help. They were also my primary contact when I had to register when I came to the country
registration_success: Semi - I got some classes, but unfortunately there was also a lot of classes that I would have preferred that I couldn't do to either the classes being sparred for national, american students only or because classes were already full when I got there.
registration_advice: Keep calm and be patient in the proces of registrating for classes. It takes time, and there isn't much you can do before you arrive in the country, where you can meet with people in person and get help. So even though I was a little stressed about not having signed up for classes before I arrived, I ended up getting some interesting courses that I was happy about.
course_level: The levels were lower than in Denmark, I would say. There is much more day-to-day work than I have been used to from Denmark, so I spent a lot more time on homeworks, but the level of these assignments wasn't that high, and they only read secondary texts and textbooks, which also meant that the level of the reading wasn't that difficult. Also, I had no final exams in any of my courses since they grade you through out the quarter, so you get a combined grate in the end, which meant, that I didn't have a stressed exam period as I normally would have in Denmark.
teaching_comparison: It was much more personal with a lot of back and forth between the teacher and the students, and often we also as students had to teach each other in what we had read for todays class.

recommended_courses: I really liked health disparities

culture_appreciated: That they are a very friendly culture.

crucial_aspects: I chose UW, Seattle because I had previously visited the West Coast (Berkeley, California) and was interested in college-culture and loved the nature. Also, I wanted to attend a good university, but not on Lars tyndskids mark. I study psychology where we dont have a lot of electives, and UW also had the right courses for me, which is probably the real reason why I chose it :)
overall_comments: KNOW that UW has quarters! I did fall+winter (october to late march), which doesnt allign well with the danish system. I struggeled a lot with coming home mid-march and starting school.
info_ease: Not easy. You have to figure it out yourself, and KU cannot help you.
arrival_assistance: None. If you have 'a major' (mine was psychology) you can speak to the advisers, they will tell you something about the programmes and help you. You have to contact them yourself. If you live in the dorms (which I do not recommend) you will be in contact with volunteers, but they'll just hand you the key. If you start in fall, there will be all kinds of activities, but they arent mandatory and there will be different people attending everything. The intro is mostly for freshmen, so as a 25 year old senior I felt pretty out of place.
arrival_comments: You will not be helped at UW, you need to do everything yourself. I was fine with it, but it's a steep learning curve.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: KNOW that UW has quarters! I did fall+winter (october to late march), which doesnt allign well with the danish system. I struggeled a lot with coming home mid-march and starting school.
registration_process: You get a date for your registration, and then your registration opens at 6am. Find your courses at myplan.uw.edu. 100 and 200 level courses are often work-load heavy because they are introduction courses. Expect to feel like you're in highschool but learn a lot!
registration_help: You can contact your majors advisor (or any advisor really)
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted, but it was blood, sweat and tears. UW has tons of rules for who can register for what. You can easily get around prerequisites if you email the professor. Check your professor and your courses on ratemyprofessor.com. UW has so many courses, so you can spend ages looking at courses. If your professor doesn't answer or the advisers tell you that you can't register for a course, just go to the first class and talk to the professor. They have the final power, and most of them are so sweet and willing to help. Just remember to call them prof. xx and not their first name !
registration_advice: KU is not going to help you. Go talk to professors. You can apply for reduced course load on 2nd quarter. As a 25 year old, I really enjoyed talking graduate courses the most, because people were more similar to my age and the content was so much more interesting! It's more work, but if you want to get something out of your time on UW academically - I would say its your best bet :) Also, take advantage of the possibility to enroll en all kinds of courses! I really enjoyed being able to choose so freely, and can recommend the gender studies and music department!
academics_comments: KNOW that UW has quarters! I did fall+winter (october to late march), which doesnt allign well with the danish system. I struggeled a lot with coming home mid-march and starting school.
course_level: 100-, 200- level are workload/deadline heavy and has final exams, where 300-, 400-, 500- have more reading but less deadlines. If you want an easy time (and prob a more interesting time) I suggest picking higher level courses. Also, then you won't be in class with 400 freshmen. I recommend the dinosaur class though! And the Marx course!
teaching_comparison: As a psychology student, I was afraid that UW would have a very empirical/neuroscience/data-driven psychology program, because it's very competitive and that's what I heard about the US. Have been so pleasantly surprised! So many professors who do interesting personality-, social psychology research! They love if your interested in research, and will enroll you in their lab if your interested.
courses_enrolled: PSYCH 209 - Fundamentals of Psychological Research (not recommend) MGMT 311 - Introduction to Strategic Human Resources Management GWSS 500 - Social Feminist Theory (HIGHLY RECOMMEND) MUSEN 300 - UW Symphony Orchestra
recommended_courses: If your an psychology student, I would recommend looking into the first-year graduate program if you would like a bang for your buck academically. Professors and student are highly skilled, and are interested in the same critiques as we are having at home (aka alternative forelæsningsrække) and it meant a lot to me, that a top 10 US university were also having these conversations. I also recommend prof Chandan Reddy if you're interested in feminism and neoliberalism and prof Eve Weinbaum if you're interested in marxism. Lastly, UW has a notorious Computer Science program. Don't choose courses from that department unless you really want a steep learning curve. I think future student should think about what they want from their exchange. It's difficult to not use a lot of time in school in the US, because there are so many deadlines.
unexpected_costs: I was surprised that on-campus housing was so expensive. Also comes without anything, so you have to buy pots and pans, linen, fridge, microwave - therefore I do not recommend it. Also, you can easily waive the insurance at UW with your own travel-insurance.
cost_comparison: Seattle is very expensive. Eating out is easily 20-30 dollars everywhere (but food on the Ave is really shitty, go somewhere else). Groceries are also expensive, but Trader Joes is okay. Get a friend who has a car or use Turo to rent cars fairly cheap for trips.
activities_available: I have been very disappointed in the social aspects of UWs exchange program. It's called CIRCLE and they do events. No one shows up and its awkward. Unite UW is a very intensive social program, some international students like it and I didn't do it so I won't be the judge - but it's a lot about telling stories and sharing insecurities, and it seemed a bit too intense for me - I suggest to go to the intro and see for yourself :) As a danish student, you should apply for the Scandesign grant. They will invite you to events where you meet americans who went on exchange in DK - there I met some of my American friends. I mostly made friends in higher-level classes.
activities_recommended: I recommend going on trips with the hiking/climbing club! The area around Seattle is amazing all time of year, and I've had the best experiences and met the nicest people in long early car-rides, doing long hikes, and climbing. Also, just rent cars with other exchange students and get out there! Seattle has three mountain ranges (Olympics, Cascades and Rainier) close, and all of them are stunning. Twillight is filmed in Forks, and Twin Peaks is filmed in North Bend (the diner is still there!), Greys Anatomy and Ten Things I Hate About You is also from Seattle, so movie scene hunting!
weekend_recommendations: Seatle has lot of good music venues
culture_adjustment: Seattle is an interesting city. Used to be a little city known for grunge (Nirvana, Pearl Jam, etc.etc.), but is now a booming tech-city. It has grown a lot in the last 10 years, and gotten waaay more expensive. Big homelessness problem. Not as bad as San Fransisco, but very close. I'm a tough cookie, but I do not always feel safe on the streets. Choose Seattle because you can easily feel like you're a resident, a part of the city, and live in the middle of it - That would be too expensive in San Fransisco. Seattle is a smaller city than San Fransisco, and doesn't have the same 'big city feel'. It's more dirty than Vancouver, but to me also feels more authentic. Seattle has lots of good dive bars, and a lot of young people (most of them work for amazon though <3).
socializing_tips: Be open to having friends than are younger than you :) Seattle has a big scandinavian population, so tell them you're scandinavian and they will love you <3
cultural_challenges: Living in the US, especially on the West Coast, you will be shocked about the homelessness. Seattle is expensive, so don't go if you don't feel like you have the funds. It's really no fun to be here if you're stressing about money and can't go on trips/go to concerts/etc.
culture_appreciated: Seattle has a lot of people moving in and out of the city - people are used to having friends for a short amount of time, and a lot of people are looking for friends(!) I have honestly found a lot of friends on Hinge and Feeld - it has been a good way to find people who were more my age, if I got a bit tired of college-kids and gave me a feeling of actually moving to another country and not 'just' being in an exchange program.
top3_advice: 1. Don't live on campus 2. Talk to your professors 3. If you don't like the outdoors, you're going to be bored with Seattle.
other_useful_info: You can get Amazon Prime for free for 6 month as a UW student. Seattle public library is very good, and you can get free museum tickets. Ballard is cozy! I loved having a bike and biking on the Burke Gilman Trail to Fremont and Ballard, North Seattle is young and cute!
most_rewarding: I did two weeks on the Pacific Crest Trail before starting school in October, and it was such an experience to be Pacific Northwest nature - I can really recommend doing Snoqualmie Pass to Stevens Pass! After spending 6 month in Seattle, it is a city dear to my heart - but if you're used to living in Copenhagen, Seattle has some lacks city-wise. Everything closes early (5pm) and the culture-scene (museums, theaters, galleries) is quite lacking. But the mountains are beautiful!
greatest_challenge: Obviously moving across the world is challenging. There is a lot of practical stuff that will take a lot of your energy the first month. UW does not help you, so be sure to ask for help when you need it. Seek out other exchange students first. If you feel lonely, I garentee you that you're not the only one. Americans are very friendly, so get used to small-talking yourself through your day. A lot of people in Seattle are looking for friends, so just start conversation! In Seattle people come from all over the world, and I've found it surprisingly difficult to meet people from so diverse backgrounds - this means people are used to different ways of life and have different ideas of right and wrong. Stick to your values, and make sure to set boundaries (especially if you're dating)!

crucial_aspects: - the high global rank of the University of Washington - the research opportunities at the University of Washington - the opportunity to interact with the US culture as a whole and visit various places across US
info_ease: The accommodation upon arrival process was smooth and the administrative staff and fellow colleagues were very helpful.
arrival_assistance: - someone was waiting for us in the parking lot to help us find our dorm room - there were various meetings for international students were I was able to meet other exchange students and find out useful information
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was very hard to register to the desired subjects at the University of Washington. As an exchange student, I was considered university-wide exchange student so I had no major (even if at KU, I am Computer Science Master student). 80% of the classes are majors only, so if you don't have any major you can apply for a class but you will have lower priority and since Computer Science is a very competitive subject at UW, me and my friend were able to get into only one Computer Science class. The other two classes we got into were some generic first or second year subjects (one was Leadership) which were going to be very dull and boring.
registration_help: The administrative people were very helpful as much as they could, but since we had no major it was very hard for us to get into any kind of classes.
registration_success: Me and my friend got extremely lucky because I have received an email from a UW computer science professor in which he was advertising a research project. Since we had a couple of years working as professional ML engineers, we were able to get into this research project for which we have received a lot of credits (17 UW credits = ~22 ECTS). Given this, we could drop most of the useless classes that we got into and work on the research project.
registration_advice: If you just want to spend one or two quarters at a US university, I would say that UW is way to expensive and very hard to find classes (you can get on some first year generic economics classes or leadership which are totally useless). If you want to get into top of the world research and have a chance of publishing into an international journal, UW is your chance. I would totally advise master students that want to go for an exchange at UW to directly write emails to teachers and ask them for temporary research positions in the laboratories they lead. If there is someone interested in computer science/machine learning research, they can contact me on linked-in (username: "Filip Tasadan") and I can help them with useful advices and even direct them to some of the laboratories that I have collaborated with.
course_level: I had taken only two classes (since I was mostly doing research). One class was first year (bachelors) leadership, which was quite boring but I was able to talk to some students that otherwise I would have never met. Since the leadership class had a lot of social activities (group projects, group discussions, etc.) it was very easy to talk to other people that had very different majors (it was a non-major class). The other class was Introduction to Human Computer Interaction, which was one of the best university classes I have ever attended. The level of commitment from the teacher and TAs was incredible, and the subjects presented were very actual. The HCI class has broadened my perspective on human centered design, and I am very satisfied that I have attended this class.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was more focused on the student and there were more discussions between us and the teachers compared to UCPH.
courses_enrolled: - Leadership - Introduction to Human Computer Interaction - Research
recommended_courses: - Research
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Food was very expensive on campus and the quality was very low.
activities_available: At UW there is the Intramural Activities Building (IMA) which has all the imaginable sports (from athletics at the top floor with the view of the bay to basketball, volleyball, soccer, gym, swimming pool) and for each sport there a a lot of classes that you can take. There is even a sauna. I was spending my evenings and weekends there either in the gym or at some class (classes are very cheap, around 10$ / class).
activities_recommended: - search of the UW hiking club, they have 1 or 2 activates every weekend and it's a very nice way to meet people and explore the Washington state - there are ethnic clubs (I was able to find a Romanian club) in which you can meet very nice people and go to parties together
weekend_recommendations: I would explore as much as possible of the US if you have the money to do it. Below I will list some of the places that I liked the most: - Vancouver, Canada (you can go by bus, 3h from Seattle) - Las Vegas, Nevada (you must rent a car and go into the desert and at Hoover dam, it's an incredible experience) - San Francisco, California (it is 20% more expensive than Seattle but I would go anytime again there for a long weekend) - Austin, Texas (vibrant city with a lot of social activates)
culture_adjustment: It was very easy, Americans are great at feeling everyone welcomed and they are very helpful
cultural_challenges: There were no particular cultural differences that I have found challenging
culture_appreciated: The friendliness and helpfulness of the people
top3_advice: - plan your budget very carefully and make sure you have all the money to cover any emergencies - try to get in touch to teachers directly through email or go and knock on their office. Most of them are going to be helpful and try to help you
most_rewarding: Doing top level research which colleagues from all over the world (China, Middle East, India) into one of the best NLP laboratories in the US.
greatest_challenge: The housing and food, I was barely coping with the low quality of both the living space and of everyday meals.
