crucial_aspects: My primary motivation for choosing the University of Western Australia (UWA) was the strong academic profile within climate change, environmental science, and sustainability, which aligns directly with my MSc Climate Change programme at the University of Copenhagen (UCPH). Australia is at the forefront of climate-related challenges such as droughts, heatwaves, biodiversity loss, and coastal vulnerability, making it an exceptionally relevant context for studying climate impacts and adaptation. Beyond academics, I have a long-standing personal connection to Australia. I have previously visited the country three times and this exchange represents my second exchange experience in Australia. Each visit strengthened my appreciation for the country’s culture, lifestyle, and academic environment. I feel that Australia suits me both personally and academically, particularly due to its applied, solution-oriented approach to climate and environmental challenges.
overall_comments: Overall, my exchange experience at UWA was extremely positive. I gained valuable academic knowledge, international experience, and personal growth. The combination of high-quality teaching, a supportive campus environment, and living in Western Australia made the exchange both academically rewarding and personally enriching.
info_ease: The information was generally easy to find. UWA provided clear pre-arrival emails, online guides, and checklists covering enrolment, orientation, housing, and practical matters such as student cards and transport.
arrival_assistance: Upon arrival, I participated in orientation activities specifically designed for international and exchange students. These included campus tours, information sessions, academic advising, and social events. There were also staff and student ambassadors available to answer questions and provide guidance.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: Overall, my exchange experience at UWA was extremely positive. I gained valuable academic knowledge, international experience, and personal growth. The combination of high-quality teaching, a supportive campus environment, and living in Western Australia made the exchange both academically rewarding and personally enriching.
registration_process: Course registration was done online through UWA’s student system. Exchange students submit preferred courses in advance, which are then assessed for eligibility and availability. Final confirmation occurred shortly before the semester started.
registration_help: Academic advisors and the international office were available via email and during orientation. Course coordinators were also approachable and willing to discuss course content and prerequisites.
registration_success: I was largely successful in registering for my preferred courses, particularly those related to climate change and environmental science. Though be aware that different course do clash, making it a bit hard to create good schedule. Something both universities should consider.
registration_advice: Start the registration process early, be flexible with course choices, and communicate clearly with both UWA and UCPH regarding credit transfer and course approval.
academics_comments: Overall, my exchange experience at UWA was extremely positive. I gained valuable academic knowledge, international experience, and personal growth. The combination of high-quality teaching, a supportive campus environment, and living in Western Australia made the exchange both academically rewarding and personally enriching.
course_level: The courses were at a Master’s level and comparable to UCPH in academic depth, with a slightly more applied and interdisciplinary focus.
teaching_comparison: Teaching at UWA was more continuous and assessment-based, with regular assignments, group work, and participation. Compared to UCPH’s exam-focused structure, UWA placed greater emphasis on ongoing evaluation and practical application.
courses_enrolled: During my exchange at the University of Western Australia, I was enrolled in the following courses: Marine Conservation and Fisheries Management (BIOL4407) Assessing Environmental Quality (ENVT4461) Marine Ecosystems (ENVT4413) Managing Threatened Species and Ecological Communities (BIOL5502) These courses covered a broad range of topics within climate change, marine science, conservation biology, and environmental management, and complemented my MSc Climate Change studies at the University of Copenhagen very well.
recommended_courses: I would highly recommend all of the courses I took, particularly for students studying climate change, environmental science, marine biology, ecology, or sustainability. Marine Conservation and Fisheries Management (BIOL4407) provides a strong understanding of how marine resources are managed under increasing pressure from climate change, overfishing, and human activities. The course combines ecological theory with real-world management and policy perspectives, making it especially relevant for students interested in applied conservation and sustainable resource use. Assessing Environmental Quality (ENVT4461) is highly relevant for students with an interest in environmental monitoring, pollution, and impact assessment. The course focuses on practical methods for assessing environmental stressors and interpreting environmental data, which is directly applicable to climate impact studies and environmental management. Marine Ecosystems (ENVT4413) offers a comprehensive overview of marine ecosystem structure and function, with strong links to climate-driven changes in ocean systems. Studying marine ecosystems in the Australian context adds unique value due to the country’s biodiversity and exposure to climate extremes. Managing Threatened Species and Ecological Communities (BIOL5502) is particularly valuable for students interested in biodiversity conservation, climate adaptation, and ecological management. The course emphasizes real-world conservation challenges, management strategies, and decision-making under uncertainty, which closely aligns with global climate and biodiversity policy discussions. Overall, these courses stand out for their applied focus, strong scientific grounding, and clear relevance to current and future environmental and climate challenges.
unexpected_costs: Some upfront costs related to housing and initial setup. Even fully furnished apartments are not fully stocked with everything you need, so you need to put something money into getting housing stuff.
cost_comparison: Groceries and eating out were more expensive than expected, while public transportation was relatively affordable with a student discount. Shop in Aldi, woolies for cheapest groceries.
activities_available: There are numerous clubs, sports teams, and student-led initiatives that make it easy to stay active, meet people, and become part of the campus community. The strong student culture and focus on well-being created a balanced exchange experience beyond academics.
activities_recommended: A wide variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities were available to students. These included organised sports clubs at different levels, outdoor and adventure-based activities, academic and interest-based student societies, cultural and international student events, volunteering opportunities, and regular social gatherings. UWA’s campus also hosts events throughout the semester that encourage student engagement. Also go to different sporting events as this is a big part of the Aussie culture. And read books on Australian and First Nation people. I recommend the book, Tracks by Robyn Davidson
weekend_recommendations: Explore Western Australia’s nature, beaches, national parks, and nearby destinations such as Rottnest Island. Do a roadtrip to Exmouth and Esperance, amazing drive.
culture_adjustment: Adjusting to the local culture was relatively easy. Australians are generally open, relaxed, and welcoming, which made it straightforward to feel comfortable both on campus and in everyday life. Having previously spent time in Australia also helped, but even without that background, the environment at UWA made the transition smooth and inclusive.
socializing_tips: A key tip is just to be open and curious which will be one of the best ways to meet local students as they are interested in your story. Participating actively in group work and tutorials also creates natural opportunities for social interaction. Attending social events early on is particularly important, as many friendships form at the start of the semester. Being open, proactive, and willing to take initiative makes a significant difference.
cultural_challenges: The main challenge was adjusting to the academic structure, particularly the continuous assessment system and different academic calendar compared to UCPH. The workload was spread more evenly throughout the semester, with frequent assignments and deadlines, which required good time management and planning.
culture_appreciated: I especially appreciated the strong outdoor lifestyle and close connection to nature, which is deeply embedded in Australian culture. There is a clear emphasis on spending time outdoors, whether through sports, beach activities, or exploring natural areas. In addition, the friendliness and openness of people made everyday interactions pleasant. I also valued the strong awareness of environmental and climate-related issues, which was reflected both in academic discussions and in broader societal attitudes.
top3_advice: Take full advantage of the applied and climate-related courses, as they offer practical insights and real-world perspectives that complement the more theory-driven approach at UCPH. Engage in student life early, by joining clubs, societies, or sports teams, as this is the easiest way to build a social network and integrate with local students. Explore Western Australia beyond campus, as the region offers unique natural environments that greatly enhance the overall exchange experience.
other_useful_info: Future exchange students should plan housing well in advance and be proactive when it comes to course approvals and registration. Being organised early reduces stress upon arrival and allows more time to focus on academics and social life once the semester begins.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the combination of high-quality education within climate and environmental sciences and the opportunity to live in a country I feel a strong personal connection to. Studying climate-related topics in an Australian context provided valuable academic perspectives while also being personally meaningful.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge was balancing the continuous assessment workload while adapting to a new academic system. Managing multiple deadlines alongside adjusting to a new environment required strong time management, particularly during the first part of the semester.
other_comments: Enjoy this beautiful country! Australia has so much to offer, so be curious, stay open, and make the most of every opportunity both on and off campus. To finish, I was inspired by a quote from Greenlights by Matthew McConaughey, which I read during my time here and feel captures the spirit of studying abroad well: “Life is not about avoiding the red lights, but learning how to turn them green.” This exchange was exactly that for me, an opportunity to grow, challenge myself, and move forward both academically and personally.

crucial_aspects: Madison has some really interesting courses and professors in my field of study. The town of Madison is almost exclusively college students, I really wanted to be part of that kind of college experience.
info_ease: It takes time but it's not that bad and when you're here all of that work is over.
arrival_assistance: I got assistance from the danish/american fellowship, scandesign. They have a storage unit filled with loaners items and bikes.
arrival_comments: There's a lot of international students and a lot of events for international students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Theres a lot of waiting for responses and a lot of making sure you know all of the deadlines. But after that you're all good.
registration_help: I emailed different professors, course administrators and international advisers in the process and all responded with kindness.
registration_success: There was only one class that I didn't get - but I got another one that was interesting too. (I really recommend Film Comedy Com arts 300, if you happen to be studying film and media studies, or English).
registration_advice: Be patient.
course_level: A lot of small assignments during the semester.
teaching_comparison: There's less of a direct connecting with the professors, but you have TA's for that). And there's designated office hours if you're interested.
courses_enrolled: CA300 film comedy , CA351 television industries, CA 325 media and human behavior , GEN&WS 101 introduction to gender and women's studies.
recommended_courses: I recommend taking som gender and women's studies since that isn't possible at home. Film comedy was very cool and professional. The discussion sections was a really nice room to talk to other students. CA 325 was a bit disappointing. Also try and avoid friday classes. Thursday is thirsty Thursday.
unexpected_costs: Travelling by plane within the United States is expensive. I knew that but I kind of forgot. I recommend book trips a bit in advance. I have spent most of money on social activities - I recommend saving up for this. I've travelled multiple times and done weekend trips.
cost_comparison: Fresh groceries are expensive. It's not necessarily cheaper than Denmark to go out and eat, but if you want something with fresh veggies it costs the same to make it at home.
activities_available: There's so much sport. I played some badminton at the gym. The gym is easily the size of all Copenhagen fitness centers in one. There's a track on the top floor and an olympic swimming pool in the center.
weekend_recommendations: Book a lodge up north and rent cars, go to Chicago, travel to New England for the weekend, take part in different student organized parties (eg. mifflin street block party). Watch sports! the college sport culture is insane!!
culture_adjustment: Just talk to other students and exchange students.
socializing_tips: I have two American roommates which is my no 1 tip.
cultural_challenges: Americans aren't as easy to make arrangements with - they're way more spontaneous than I find Danes to be.
culture_appreciated: All of my new friendships.
top3_advice: 1. You're going to have so much fun - it will be worth all the hard work. 2. be prepared to buy new clothes for this weird climate. 3. Save up to have fuuuun
most_rewarding: getting to experience american (college) culture - good and bad.
greatest_challenge: Sometimes you can be filled up with new impressions - it can be hard to say; ok, now I'll take a break and not experience anything the rest of the day.

crucial_aspects: I didn't have that many preferences as to where I wanted to go, but I knew I wanted to go to the US. The midwest, and especially Wisconsin turned out to really be a great place. This is, from my understanding especially true when coming from Denmark, since there is a lot of scandinavian heritage in the midwest area.
overall_comments: I would definitely recommend going to UW-Madison since it is a really nice place to both explore academic opportunities, socialise with other students and explore midwestern America.
info_ease: It was super easy. The university really does a lot for you to feel welcome, and there was even a fair which introduced international students to all the different things on campus.
arrival_assistance: The university does also send out a lot of emails with useful information once you get here.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I would definitely recommend going to UW-Madison since it is a really nice place to both explore academic opportunities, socialise with other students and explore midwestern America.
registration_process: It can be a bit tricky to choose courses and to know which courses are good, but as long as you look out for emails from the university you should be all good.
registration_help: Looking up the professors online and seeing what other students thought of them.
registration_success: If you take the time and sit down at look properly at it, you should be just fine.
registration_advice: Don't be afraid that you picked the wrong course. Within the first two weeks, you can change your courses, if you regret choosing one. As long as you report if back to KU.
academics_comments: I would definitely recommend going to UW-Madison since it is a really nice place to both explore academic opportunities, socialise with other students and explore midwestern America.
course_level: Some of the lower-level courses can seem a bit too easy since people are a bit younger when starting university (18-19). Most of the courses have some really great professors who are really committed to your learning. Be sure to tell them that you're not from the U.S., they will love it.
teaching_comparison: Most classes are divided into lectures with the professor and discussion sections with a TA (teaching assistant, who is usually a student themselves or recently graduated). You go to the lectures and listen and go to the discussion section and discuss what the professor said.
courses_enrolled: EDPSYCH301: How People Learn (003) SP22 FOLKLORE100: Introduction to Folklore (001) SP22 SCANDST432: History of Scandinavia Since 1815 (001) SP22 SLAVIC245: Topics in Slavic Literatures
recommended_courses: Slavic245 is really great if you're interested in post-communism cultures! SCANDST432 is a really really great course. Basically all courses with professor Dean Krouk.
unexpected_costs: Social events
cost_comparison: Food was a bit more expensive, because of the inflation.
activities_available: There are almost 900 different clubs to be a part of! all from cheese tasting to skiing. There is basically a club for everyone.
activities_recommended: Be a part of hoffers! It's an outdoor club which does sailing, swimming, hiking etc.
weekend_recommendations: Go see "The house on the rock". It's a crazy house outside of the city.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, since the culture is very Western.
socializing_tips: Americans are really good at socializing, so just go up to someone and say you're from Denmark and enjoy your new friends!
cultural_challenges: The food is not that great honestly. You will have a hard time eating healthy. If you like enormous amounts of cheese, you will be in heaven.
culture_appreciated: Everyone is super helpful and approachable!
top3_advice: Be prepared to socialize! Americans love to talk, so don't be worried if you'll make new friends. Be prepared to do many more small assignments. IF you are used to doing 1-2 big assignments at the end of the semester, you will be surprised. There are many more small assignments and quizzes throughout the semester. This can be tricky, but it makes the exam period a lot less struggling. Be open to new things!
other_useful_info: I would definitely recommend the ScanDesign foundation, which is a fellowship with other Scandinavian students. For me, it was a really big part of the exchange and made sure you also had some fellow Scandinavians to discuss problems with or go to social events together. You will have to apply to be a part of it, and a scholarship also comes along! Look it up online.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding thing was also the most challenging. The progress of being alone and figuring out a lot of things on your own felt really good, and really helps making you a better student and person.
greatest_challenge: Being away from your friends and danish food.

crucial_aspects: Location and infrastructure -- Madison has a lot of bike baths, a nice winter with lots of snow, etc. Also academics --- they have good engineering and comp sci departments with lots of courses to choose from. I also had friends and family in the area that I wanted to see and visit.
info_ease: Not that easy. I needed help with finding the right courses and figuring out alternatives to the courses I was waitlisted for, and it took a lot of back and forth until I found the right advisor for that. Other more practical things were easier to get help for.
arrival_assistance: Got help from International Student Services for practical stuff and from the office of Study Abroad for academic advising.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Getting all you info in MyUW and Terra Dotta, completing an introductory little course in Canvas.
registration_help: Detailed instructions
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted, but I was waitlisted for them and was not sure until the end that it would be possible. But in general it seems like most classes have a high turnover and you have a good chance of making it from the waitlist.
registration_advice: Don't be afraid of the waitlists -- your chances are good.
course_level: PSYCH 711 definitely felt like a masters-level course, very good level and very research-focused ECE 539 and 532 are more like BA-courses if you already have a technical background, but for IT and Cognition students like me, who don't all have that background, the level felt quite appropriate. I was definitely challenged and didn't do that well on all the tests. However, the grading is based on a lot of other coursework as well, so you can make up for it.
teaching_comparison: The main difference for me was the grading, since I'm used to one project or exam making up the whole grade. Here we had midterms, or multiple tests and/or projects, so there was a lot of "making up for" a bad grade, and just doing the homework basically puts at "passed" level. But there really is a lot of homework and I did feel busier than in UCPH on a daily basis.
courses_enrolled: PSYCH 711 Advanced Topics in Psychology (Language Comprehension in Adults and Children) ECE 532 Matrix Methods in Machine Learning ECE 539 Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks
recommended_courses: PSYCH 711 with Maryellen Macdonald was EXCELLENT, but the topics and instructor change, so I'm not sure it will be available in the same form going forward. ECE 532 was a great foundation for machine learning that I really needed, and the instruction was very clear and helpful. ECE 539 was a confusing and frustrating course that I don't recommend. Teaching style very dull and and not paedagogical, very difficult tests and lots of work.
unexpected_costs: Clothing! The winter is MUCH colder than in Denmark, and I needed new gloves, coats, etc.
cost_comparison: I didn't pay anything for books, as none of my courses had textbooks, it was all online material.
activities_available: Lots, sports, gym, libraries, events....
activities_recommended: Football games! Hike around the area, maybe water sports
weekend_recommendations: Go down to Chicago or Milwaukee
culture_adjustment: easy
socializing_tips: go to the international student events
cultural_challenges: none
culture_appreciated: friendliness, food
top3_advice: go there early and get everything in order, get advising and ask others about good courses!
other_useful_info: I can't think of any!
most_rewarding: Good instructors, good food and new friends
greatest_challenge: Keeping up with academics
other_comments: No

arrival_assistance: The Scan Design Foundation (SDF) was a big help and the University provided a guided tour for international students.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was quite easy to follow the guide.
registration_help: You could send an email and they would respond pretty fast.
registration_success: I didnøt have any problems at all.

courses_enrolled: 303 Biology of Microorganisms 528 Immunology 640 General Virology-Multiplication of Viruses 703 Carcinogenesis and Tumor Cell Biology
recommended_courses: 703 - very relevant assignments, no exam, pretty chill. 528 - learned a lot, multiple choice exams 640 - probably the most interesting in my opinion (the exams were however more difficult than the others) 303 - probably my least favorite because it was too easy, but good if you want a lot of freedom and still pass
unexpected_costs: Visa was more expensive than expected.
cost_comparison: In general, things were more expensive because of the exchange rate at the time I arrived. More specifically I would say groceries. Going out is less expensive (note: Whiskey Jack's have 25-cent rail drinks every Thursday)
activities_available: There were over a hundred clubs with whatever you can imagine. Almost every day the university also had events, often with free food included.
activities_recommended: Go to a football game to get the experience.
weekend_recommendations: Plan trips to Devil's Lake, Minneapolis, Chicago etc.
culture_adjustment: It was not too difficult.
socializing_tips: Get a buddy through the SDF programme, join a club or socialize with people in class.
cultural_challenges: Not anything specific. People wore a lot of gym clothes to school. Also, remember tipping.
culture_appreciated: I enjoyed game days a lot. Football is a big part of the culture and not just watching the sport but also tailgating before.
top3_advice: 1. Bring a warm winter jacket and thermal underwear to keep warm during winter 2. Attend as many events as possible (mainly at the beggining) 3. Plan trips to explore more of the US.
other_useful_info: Bring a lot of rye bread and put it in your freezer.
most_rewarding: Making new international friends and going on self-arranged trips with other students.
greatest_challenge: I shared my bedroom with another international exchange student and even though we got along very well, sometimes I needed a private space that I didn't have.

housing_how: I found housing on my own

registration_help: Professors were very responsive when one wrote them.
registration_success: I was able to get into every class I wanted
registration_advice: Write the professors early enough. Classes can fill up and if you get permission after too many students have registered it is too late.

unexpected_costs: Cant think of anything

activities_available: At the beginning of the semester there is a student organisation fair where organisation present themselves and recruit new participants. I joined the triathlon and hunting club
activities_recommended: Go to a Badgers american football and women's volleyball games.

cultural_challenges: Nothing was particularly challenging.

other_useful_info: Madison is a small college town, meaning that a majority of people living around campus are undergrad students (18 - 22 years old)
most_rewarding: Turning in a research proposal as part of one class that I had been working on throughout the semester and getting overwhelmingly positive feedback.

crucial_aspects: Jeg læser i København normalt jordbrugsøkonomi. I kraft af at Wisconsin er en landbrugsstat, er de ret gode inde for det område. Samtidig er Wisconsin en stat som ikke er oplagt at tage til som turist. Derfor lød netop Wisconsin tiltalende for mig
info_ease: Det var relativt nemt. Man får ret meget information i starten, men hvis man bare læser og forholder sig til de mails man får, så er man nogenlunde kørende
arrival_assistance: Der var en række introarrangementer som man havde mulighed for at deltage i
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Man skal godkendes til at tage kurser af forskellige professorer, for at tage forskellige kurser. Det skal man have styr på inden tilmeldingen åbner, hvis man gerne vil have de fag som man har udset sig. Jeg synes personligt ikke at det fungerede så godt.
registration_help: Jeg synes at det var ret uklart. Det afhang af hvilke kurser man vil have osv.
registration_success: Jeg endte med at få nogle fag som jeg var glad for. På forhånd kan det dog godt være svært at vurdere, da det ikke er ret mange linjer de bruger på at beskrive de enkelte fag
registration_advice: Tilmeld dig alle de fag som du kunne forestille dig at have. Du kan nå at framelde dig i den første uge af semesteret, hvor du så endeligt kan vurdere, hvilke fag du ender med at ville tage
course_level: Jeg vil vurdere niveauet som værende sammenligneligt med det danske
teaching_comparison: Der er mange løbende tests som tæller med i din karakter. Når man ikke er vant til det, kan det godt virke lidt stressende. Det endte med at gå fint. Hvis man bare følger med og laver de obligatoriske ting der kræves, så er de fleste fag til at have med at gøre
courses_enrolled: Bank Management, Animal Welfare, Issues in food systems, Energy and Ressource Economics
recommended_courses: Jeg vil anbefale dem alle 4. Bank Management er lidt svært, fordi der er nogle ting i deres banksystem som ikke er som i det danske. Det var umiddelbart det kursus jeg fandt mest udfordrende. Animal Welfare er et fag om dyrevelfærd. Hvis man interesserer sig for produktionsdyr, kan faget være meget givende, da dyrevelfærden er på et væsentligt andet niveau i US. Faget handler meget om dyrevelfærd fra et videnskabeligt perspektiv og iscenesatte blandt andet, hvordan det kan skille sig ud fra vores mennekselige opfattelse af, hvad vi opfatter som god dyrevelfærd. Issues in food systems var et sociologisk kursus. Jeg ville normalvis aldrig tage et kursus om sociologi, men det var egentlig meget spændende at høre om, hvordan forskellige minoriteter særligt i USA har sværere ved at have adgang til mad. Jeg blev personligt mødt af nogle problemstillinger man har i US, som man altid blot har taget for givet i Danmark. Energy and Ressource Economics var et økonomikursus som blandt andet gav indsigt i prisdannelsen på elnettet. Tilsvarende kiggede vi på, hvad der driver olieprisen op og ned fra et økonomisk perspektiv
unexpected_costs: Der er mange små ting som visum osv. der er dyrt. Ovenstående er et slag på tasken, men turen har for mig samlet set kostet ca 70.000 DKK inkl. fornøjelse. Hvis man ikke er villig til at bruge nogen penge på oplevelser osv. imens man er afsted, så vil jeg anbefale at man bliver hjemme.
cost_comparison: Husleje er cirka lige så dyrt som i København
activities_available: Der er rigtig meget sport forbundet med universitetet. Hvis man er der i efteråret, så skal man sørge for at tage afsted til fodboldkampene og tailgates inden fodboldkampene. Tailgates er en form for forfest, som der afholdes alle steder i byen på de dage hvor der er hjemmekamp. Det er en fantastisk oplevelse at prøve at være en del af
activities_recommended: Lej en bil og kør på roadtrip væk fra Madison. Dem som lever i Madison er ikke repræsentative for alle amerikanere - de har flere penge og minder mere om danskere. Kom ud på landet, snak med nogle lokale, vær nysgerrig, besøg en skydebane, kør ind til en våbenforhandler, osv. Personligt var jeg med på en tur, hvor de havde våben til salg hængende i en alkoholforrenting
weekend_recommendations: Kør ud af byen. Inde i Madison møder du kun nogen som tænker og er som dig selv
culture_adjustment: Folk i Wisconsin er meget imødekommende. Det var nemt
socializing_tips: Nyd en øl på en bar. Spørg ind. Folk kigger ikke mærkeligt på dig, hvis du spørger en tilfældig om anbefalinger til turistattraktioner e.lign.
cultural_challenges: Amerikanere er utrolig søde, men også lidt overfladiske på samme tid. Danskere kan godt være lidt sværere at komme ind på, men når man kender en dansker, så kan man dele alt med hinanden. Det er selvfølgelig lidt sat på spidsen, men det er min analyse af det
culture_appreciated: De er meget imødekommende. Hvis man blot opsøger det en lille smule, kan man få rigtig mange gode samtaler med amerikanere, som man aldrig har mødt før.
top3_advice: Der er et program som hedder Scan Design. Det vil jeg anbefale at man bliver en del af. Jeg var ikke selv en del af det, da jeg synes at det lød som en gruppe, hvor det hele handlede om miljø og klima. Gruppen danner grundlag for rigtig meget socialt, og jeg vil anbefale alle at ansøge om at blive en del af det
other_useful_info: Der er nem adgang til Madison fra lufthavnen i Chicago. Busselskabet Coach USA kører fra en terminal i lufthavnen, med afgange det meste af døgnet. Man køber en billet som skal bruges inden for 365 dage fra købstidspunktet, hvorefter man blot hopper på bussen når man ankommer
most_rewarding: Det kulturelle. Derudover har jeg aldrig været så stærk til engelsk. Jeg føler at min evne til at kommunikere på engelsk er blevet forbedret væsentligt
greatest_challenge: Jeg havde svært ved at vurdere, hvor meget der skulle til for at bestå mine fag. Hvis man blot følger med og laver de obligatoriske ting, vil jeg dog ikke sige at det er noget som man skal være bekymret for

housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I am so happy that I finally got to try the american college life as it has always been a dream of mine. I think that I just realized that living in the US isn't for me.
registration_process: Upload transcript and request the courses that you want. Then the host institution considers whether you have the right prerequisites for those courses.
registration_help: The different department are very good at assisting you with course requirements, credits, prerequisites etc. I recommend writing to them for help.
registration_success: I got the classes I wanted. I missed out on one class because it filled up too fast, but just found something else.
registration_advice: Sign up for classes as soon as course registration is open.
academics_comments: I am so happy that I finally got to try the american college life as it has always been a dream of mine. I think that I just realized that living in the US isn't for me.
course_level: I took 3 BA courses and 1 that's for both BA and MA.
teaching_comparison: In the beginning it was all very exciting, but by the end I really missed the way it's done at UCPH. Some of the professors in the US just seem like they do it for the status of being a professor and not because they actually want to teach the students. The grading system is so weird. Most of your work is graded based on a curved grading system which means that ex. 15% get A, 15% get B etc. This means that even if you did very poorly, but better than the rest, you get an A. Or, if you do very well but everyone else does better, you get a B or C. You're essentially being judged on how your classmates are doing, not yourself. Midterms/exams are very poorly set up. You sit in a regular class room with pen, paper and calculator like it's the 1980's. Two of my classes were completely based on the use of excel and yet we used a calculator in the exams. Some of the classrooms are designed so you sit in a row with a TINY pull out desk in front of you which means that when people leave during the exam, you have to stand up, stop what you're doing and let them out. Exams are noisy because of the scribbling and turning of pages and overall very bad.
courses_enrolled: ECON 521 - Game Theory and Economic Analysis (Difficult) ECON 306 - The Real Estate Process (Easiest A) FIN 330 - Derivative Securities (Interesting) ECON/FIN 320 - Investment Theory (Bit boring at times)
recommended_courses: FIN 330 - Derivative Securities was the best course. It was interesting, fun and the professor(s) was good. I liked the weekly assignment because it gave a good understanding of the material. ECON 306 - The Real Estate Process was the easiest course I have ever taken. I attended maybe 4 lectures and got an A. ECON/FIN 320 - Investment Theory was okay but sometimes a bit boring. I really didn't like professor Roberto. ECON 521 - Game Theory and Economic Analysis was really interesting but super difficult. In the beginning I thought that it was fairly easy to keep up and I really liked it. By the end I was so done with it. I spent probably 8-10 hours on the weekly assignments. If you're taking the semester for experiences more than the learning outcomes - do not take this course.
unexpected_costs: Surprised at the price of food, it's so expensive. I spent around 1000 DKK a week on groceries. Tips, tax on goods, service charges etc. are all added on top of the price you see. It quickly adds up.
cost_comparison: Food was more expensive.
activities_available: Don't know.
activities_recommended: Try to go a hockey game or basketball game. It was cool to see. Join the Scan Design Foundation to get even more experiences. I think it's a must.
weekend_recommendations: In the Scan Design Foundation some weekends are used for trips. In the holidays I recommend going on a roadtrip.
culture_adjustment: More difficult than expected.
cultural_challenges: Americans wear grey sweatpants, a hoodie and slippers to school. When they go out they wear a t-shirt, sweatpants or jeans and a backwards cap. As a dane I can't go out without dressing up a little bit (also to school) and you definitely stand out in the crowd - apparently not in a good way. For some reason americans look down on wearing a shirt when going out, and I probably looked down on them for dressing so badly. When they go out drinking they don't talk about anything. If they do, it's just empty words. I feel like I am very good at having conversations with people but over there it's so different. They talk about how drunk they were at that one party 8 months ago whereas I would try to ask about what they're studying, what they plan to do after finishing school, what job do they have etc. Their tipping culture is absolutely insane. When you are at a bar/club and order a beer, they ask you for a tip and it's expected to give between 15-20%. Even at the hairdresser where you literally paid for their service you're expected to tip.
culture_appreciated: How grand everything is. I love the american culture with big cars, large supermarkets, going out shooting etc. I have just come to understand that it's cool for two or three weeks on a vacation but not after 4 months.
top3_advice: 1. If you have been wanting to go to the US so that you can experience the college life, then you should definitely go. Despite my criticism of the strange things they do in the US, I am so happy that I went. 2. Don't go in the spring semester. Much less is going on in the 3 first months and fewer students choose to go abroad to Madison. Go in the summer time. 3. Join the Scan Design Foundation so you have some danish friends when you're there. You also get some great experiences.
other_useful_info: No.
most_rewarding: Getting to experience the college life - it's really cool.
greatest_challenge: Being away from my girlfriend, friends and family.
other_comments: You should go if you have a dream about experiencing the US college life. If you do, go in the summer, join the Stan Design Foundation and then I am certain you're gonna have a great time.

crucial_aspects: I knew that I wanted to go to the US during my bachelors and wanted a "real American travel experience". I narrowed down my search to good schools in the US and since one of my best friends went to UW and loved it the choice was easy.
overall_comments: I absolutely loved studying abroad. I made really good friends in the US and had interesting courses. I am not giving a score of 10 since one of the courses was really bad.
info_ease: It was fairly easy since UW made an effort to be welcoming towards incoming students.
arrival_assistance: I went to a campus tour and received my bus pass and student ID upon arrival. Other than that I didn't receive that much assistance, but further assistance would have been accessible if needed.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I absolutely loved studying abroad. I made really good friends in the US and had interesting courses. I am not giving a score of 10 since one of the courses was really bad.
registration_process: You had to send in your financial statements, transcripts, passport and other administrative stuff. They will tell you if something is missing and will give you a chance to send in any missing documents even after the deadline.
registration_help: The UW exchange team is really helpful and will answer your question really fast if you send them an email.
registration_success: I was successful in getting all of my wanted classes in the end. I was waitlisted for one of them and didn't get in until two weeks before departure from Denmark, which was super stressful.
registration_advice: Get your pre approvals as early as possible as the course registration is super competitive.
academics_comments: I absolutely loved studying abroad. I made really good friends in the US and had interesting courses. I am not giving a score of 10 since one of the courses was really bad.
course_level: I took one 300 level, which was too easy in comparison to KU. One of the courses was a 400 level, which was easier than KU courses, but I still learned something. The last course was a 500 level and super difficult, it is comparable to the harder courses at KU.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style was pretty similar to KU. I had two lectures and one discussion in each course each week and one assignment in each course per week. The biggest difference was that assignments and midterms were graded and one exam was multiple choice.
courses_enrolled: ECON330 - Money and Banking with Steven Rick ECON461- International Macroeconomics with Stella Chan ECON521 - Game theory and economic analysis with Benjamin Bernard
recommended_courses: I would recommend both ECON461 and ECON521. Both courses have good professors and are really interesting. ECON521 is hard, but you can get it approved as Micro III which is super neat.
unexpected_costs: UW has its own insurance policy (SHIP) for International students. It is mandatory and more expensive than if you just had gotten a normal travel insurance.
cost_comparison: Food prices are comparable to Denmark and sometimes a bit more expensive. Going out to bars is way cheaper than Copenhagen. The books are super expensive, but you can usually find them used or as a pdf online.
activities_available: There were both language clubs and different academic clubs. The campus gyms are amazing and free for students!! The new gym is huge and has amazing amenities like a swimming pool and an ice rink.
activities_recommended: The cheese club is so fun! Also go to the gyms if you like working out. It is also highly recommended to apply to ScanDesign as they help a lot with socializing with other Danes.
weekend_recommendations: I went on a road trip with a close friend of mine before the semester started, which I highly recommend doing! We took the east coast route and went to Michigan, Canada, the Niagara Falls, Boston and New York City. Some of my other friends flew to LA where they bought a car and went all the way down Route 66. If you have time and money I highly encourage a road trip. Things that you can do near Madison are going to Milwaukee or Chicago or walking around the Picnic Point if its just for a day.
culture_adjustment: It was super easy. Madison is a really nice city and the culture is not that different to Denmark, so you won't be experiencing a culture shock per se.
socializing_tips: I met my American friends through ScanDesign, clubs and classes.
cultural_challenges: I didn't really find anything challenging.
culture_appreciated: Kindness. People are so welcoming and it is super easy to build up profound friendships. It is so much easier to make friends in the US than in Denmark.
top3_advice: Find accommodation early, sign up for ScanDesign and try to not have any classes on Fridays.
other_useful_info: Find your classes before the first day of school. The campus is really big and some buildings are confusing.
most_rewarding: I went to my friends parents house in Michigan for Thanksgiving. We stayed there for a week and I just had the most wonderful time.
greatest_challenge: Sometimes the work load of homework was a bit high, but I'm also an overachiever, so you will probably be fine.

teaching_comparison: Personligt er jeg mere fan af KU's store fokus på eksamen fremfor alt der bliver micromanaged på amerikanske universiteter. For mig fungerer det ikke at blive bedømt på mit fremmøde og mit aktivitetsniveau i undervisningen.

weekend_recommendations: Tag rundt og oplev området omkring byen. Madison er ikke en voldsomt stor by, så man kan godt løbe tør for ting at lave. Man har heldigvis mest af alt Chicago tæt på, men også Milwaukee og Green Bay. Naturen omkring byen (særligt vestpå) er også vær at besøge. Lej en bil nogle weekender og tag et lille roadtrip.

cultural_challenges: Husk ikke at drik på gaden, man kan blive arresteret for det (hæld øl i en kaffekop, så fanger de dig ikke).
culture_appreciated: Madison som college by er fyldt med festglade unge på en mere afslappet måde end i Danmark. Nyd det og involver dig i festerne så skal det nok blive en fed tur.
top3_advice: -30 grader er ikke en unormal temperatur i januar, så tag sydpå hvis du bliver i USA efter semesteret. Hvis du får chancen for at komme med til et tailgate, så tag med, det er fedt. Søg Scan Design legatet, de udlodder 20.000 kr. til studerende fra Danmark der tager til UW.

most_rewarding: Nye venner og sindssygt mange oplevelser. Ny påskønnelse af KU's måde at undervise på.
greatest_challenge: Det er lang tid at være væk fra venner og familie, men det er det værd og man kan overleve med facetime i 5 måneder.
other_comments: Tag afsted! Det er sk*dedyrt og stressende at planlægge op mod afgang, men når man er der er det den fedeste tid.

crucial_aspects: Jeg har haft et stort både akademisk og personligt ønske om at prøve at læse og bo i USA. Jeg søgte et universitet med en god School of Public Health af akademiske årsager. Jeg søgte UW Madison, idet det levede op til førstående, men også fordi det var et af de universiteter i USA, hvor KU havde flere pladser, og jeg vidste derfor, jeg ikke ville være den eneste danske studerende afsted. Jeg valgte også universitetet, idet jeg ikke kendte andre, der skulle samme sted hen, hvilket jeg så som en fordel, da jeg så ville blive personligt og akademisk udfordret ved at skulle stå på egne ben. Desuden har jeg rejst før i USA, men jeg har aldrig besøgt Midvesten, og jeg ønskede derfor også at vælge en destination, jeg ikke havde et forhold til på forhånd, og som jeg om muligt nok aldrig ville besøge, hvis ikke det var for mit udvekslingsophold.
info_ease: Der var meget der skulle holdes styr på, og jeg syntes, det var ret uoverskueligt. Der var et stort stykke forarbjede inden afrejse.
arrival_assistance: Universitetet har fra start til slut af opholdet været gode til at holde arrangementer, sende løbende e-mails og holde åbne telefon- og mødetider, hvor man kunne komme og få hjælp til, hvad man nu havde brug for hjælp til. Helt i begyndelsen blev der afholdt et Zoom-møde, hvor udvekslingsafdelingen introducerede én til alt det praktiske. Der blev også holdt et fysisk møde/event, hvor sociale og akademiske klubber blev præsenteret.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Jeg kunne ikke tilmelde mig kurser i begyndelsen, idet alle kurserne krævede, man var registreret forskelligt. Jeg blev derfor nødt til at kontakte hver enkel professor for at spørge om lov til tilmelding, hvor jeg skrev om mig selv og min faglige profil og medsendte mit bachelorbevis.
registration_help: Selvom jeg blev nødt til at skrive til rigtig mange for at kunne blive tilmeldt kurser var alle, jeg var i kontakt med meget søde og behjælpelige.
registration_success: Jeg tog tre kurser, som alle var nogen, jeg havde ønsket at tage.
registration_advice: Skriv til underviserne og spørg om du må tage kurserne. Man får en skabelon af universitet, som man med fordel kan anvende i sin mail. Alle underviserne synes det er dejligt med interesse for deres fag fra udvekslingsstuderende. Skriv hvilke kurser, du har taget på KU, som du mener kvalificerer dig til kurset og skriv om dine egne faglige interesser, og hvorfor de relaterer sig til dit ønske om at tage netop deres kursus.
course_level: Jeg tog to graduate kurser, der var en del af Masters of Public Health programmet. Derudover tog jeg et enkelt kursus, der var for undergrad studerende på 4. år.
teaching_comparison: Det var meget forskelligt fra, hvad man kender fra KU. På nogle måder var det mere som det, man kender fra gymnasiet. Man blev bedømt på flere ting, og der var mange små og store afleveringer i løbet af semesteret. Undervisningen var mere case-baseret og ikke altid ligeså teori-og metodetungt, som man kender det fra KU.
courses_enrolled: Planning and Management to Promote Health Public Health and Health Care systems Stress and Resilience in Families across the Lifespan
recommended_courses: Tag kurser, som du ikke kan tage i Danmark, og som styrker din faglige profil indenfor det område, du finder spændende og interresant.
unexpected_costs: De mange udgifter, der ligger forud for opholdet (visum, forsikring, ansøgningsgebyrer osv.)
cost_comparison: Mad, kaffe og at gå i byen var generelt billigere end i Danmark. Shampoo og andre produkter til personlig pleje var generelt dyrere.
activities_available: Der var flere forskellige klubber, men jeg undersøgte dem ikke så grundigt.
activities_recommended: At tage til sportskampe.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på små ture og oplev natur og kultur.
culture_adjustment: Jeg faldt meget hurtigt til.
socializing_tips: De amerikanske studerende er meget åbne og søde. Vær initiativrig og grib de muligheder, der kommer din vej.
cultural_challenges: Jeg fik oplevelsen af, at man ikke talte politik eller om verdenssituationen, idet de var meget respektfulde overfor, at andre nok har en anden holdning end dem selv. Samtalerne er derfor mere personlige, hvilket kan være lidt uvant som dansker.
culture_appreciated: Åbenheden, venligheden og gæstfriheden!
top3_advice: Find ud af din boligsituation og telefoni, inden du tager afsted. Vejret kan skifte med mere end 20 grader dag til dag, så pak til alle årstider.
other_useful_info: Ikke umiddelbart.
most_rewarding: Menneskerne, jeg mødte!
greatest_challenge: At være helt alene og selv måtte finde ud af, at få alle puslespilsbrikkerne til at falde på plads.

crucial_aspects: The destination was never the most important aspect of studying abroad, but UW-Madison had a lot of advantages. It was in an English-speaking country with a somewhat familiar culture, that was still interesting to experience first hand. The city itself, Madison, felt were average for a university city, which allowed me to experience a more representative university experience than in a bigger city. I would also not travel there as a turist, so I would have missed out on it, had I not gone there.
info_ease: Very easy. The university has a very informative website for exchange students, though transportation to and from the airport may not be as easy as they claim.
arrival_assistance: We had an exchange student orientation shortly after. I was also part of the Scan Design foundation, which helped me getting my free bus pass, bank account, and student id.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: Apply special permission for each class incl. discussion section. The method of applying for permission depends on the faculty. This can first be done after the American students have applied for classes, so you also have to make sure, that there is actually room for you. When permission is granted, you can enroll into the class or onto a waitlist.
registration_help: You could write to a service specifically for International Students or the faculty itself. They were quick to answer and usually helpfull.
registration_success: I got some of the classes I originally wanted. Some I didn't get because the process of getting acceptance from both UW-Madison and KU was too slow compared to the deadline, and some I didn't get because there was no more room in the class. I still had good classes though.
registration_advice: Apply for permission from KU as fast as possible. And if the professors at UW don't answer emails then follow up quickly.
course_level: I thought my classes were MA, as KU said they would be. Turns out they were kind of a mix. But the level in general for those courses (and others I've heard about) was far below BA courses at KU.
teaching_comparison: The classes were shorter (an hour and 15 min.), they were more focused on class participation, assignments took up a lot of the time, and many classes were more relaxed. Some classes micro managed, in the sense that our grade was affected by how we took notes.
courses_enrolled: Investment Theory, Behavioral Economics, Economics of Health Care, and Population Economics.
recommended_courses: Economics of Health Care was really interesting and the professor was passionate and made a great effort. Just be prepared for a big workload. Population Economics was also really interesting, though the econometrics requirements were quite low for an applied Econ class.
unexpected_costs: Nothing really comes to mind.
cost_comparison: Can't think of anything.
activities_available: Sports clubs for all sorts, clubs based on identity and activism, you could go to games like ice hockey or basket ball.
activities_recommended: I can definitely recommend watching a game and going to the Union Terrace while it's still warm.
weekend_recommendations: The same as the exchange students. Also, there is a lot of nature which is great for hikes.
culture_adjustment: It took some time, but it happened eventually.
socializing_tips: Just listen to yourself and what feels right.
cultural_challenges: I sometimes felt that conversations and relations were superficial.
culture_appreciated: I appreciated the ease with which they invited you to things despite having just met you. This, at least for me, made it way easier to meet new people and experience American traditions.
top3_advice: 1. There is a lot of school work (not necessarily difficult though) depending on the classes you choose. So consider that before enrolling. 2. Consider joining Scan Design. It has both a scholar ship and a buddy program with activities. Both really helped me during my stay. 3. But if you do travel, Chicago and Milwaukee are relatively close by, which I can recommend.
other_useful_info: It's really cold in the winter time, so pack a lot of warm clothing and good boots.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part was to experience being a part of a completely different culture.
greatest_challenge: Though I really enjoyed being part of the American culture, I still felt more at home in the Danish and sometimes just felt very foreign.

crucial_aspects: The university having a good reputation and courses that interest me.
info_ease: It was relatively easy. The university will frequently email you on your university account about any useful information.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance apart from attending the required orientation meetings.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The university has its own website where you can register for courses when it opens up in April. However you need certain requirements to be able to register for courses, which is why you need to email the professors of the courses you want to take before the course registrations open up.
registration_help: The course registration process was confusing at first, as I was not aware that I had to email professors to be able to take their courses.
registration_success: I only emailed them after it opened up so there were a few courses that I would've liked to have taken that got filled up quick. There were also some Computer Science courses that I would've liked to have taken that were not available for exchange students, and some Computer Science classes also get filled up quickly. However the university offer so many courses that I did not have a problem finding other courses that I was interested in. I also got permission by the professors to enroll in all the courses I wanted to enroll in.
registration_advice: Find out which courses you want to take early, and email professors before course registration opens up. Also be aware that not all courses on their course catalog list will be available for you to take as some of them are only available in specific semesters. Only on the course registration website can you see which ones are available to you.
course_level: I was taking a mix of undergraduate (BA) and graduate (MA) level courses. Classes closer to level 300 might be for early undergraduates but that does not necessarily mean that they will be easier than courses with a higher course number.
teaching_comparison: A lot of classes only have 50 minute lectures (no discussion class and no breaks during lecture), which means you're not going to be meeting a lot of people in your classes. The amount of coursework varies from class to class (some had very little while other courses felt like 20 ECTS worth of coursework). Overall I found the workload to be very high compared to KU, and at times very overwhelming, especially with weekly assignments and weekly quizzes in multiple courses + midterms and larger projects as well. However, actually passing a course felt less stressful than at KU because your grade is not dependent on the final exam only, but on all the coursework throughout the semester. American students are also going to be a lot more determined to come to class and do well, compared to in Denmark, probably because they paid a lot of money to go to university.
courses_enrolled: COMP SCI 300, COMP SCI 639.1 (Data Mgmt for Data Science), POLI SCI 305, I SY E 649
recommended_courses: I would recommend all of them except for COMP SCI 300, unless you have good Java skills, as it is a very intensive and time consuming course otherwise.
unexpected_costs: A lot of fees to the university.
cost_comparison: Lunch options at the university were a lot more expensive than i expected ($9-$14). Clothes, electronics and other personal stuff was a lot cheaper than i expected (maybe 20-40% cheaper than in DK)
activities_available: A lot of sports games happen all the time. Getting student tickets was impossible and very expensive to buy through resellers though.
activities_recommended: Go to an american football game at Camp Randall just for the vibes, even if you don't know anything about the sport. I would also recommend seeing women's volleyball and men's basketball.
weekend_recommendations: There are a lot of bars downtown and the alcohol is cheap. Otherwise there are a lot of free options in Madison (e.g. Arboretum, Zoo). I would also recommend going to Chicago, Devils Lake, or the beach in Milwaukee when the weather is nice.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. People in Wisconsin are very talkative and hospitable, and it's not significantly different from anything in Denmark.
socializing_tips: Don't be afraid to talk to strangers.
cultural_challenges: For a lot of American undergraduates, university is basically their whole life. It seems to be more normal for them to spend all their time on university-related stuff, both academic and non-academic. I was not used to having so much of my time be devoted to the university.
culture_appreciated: That people were so friendly and hospitable.
top3_advice: Find housing early. Don't take multiple difficult courses. Bring warm clothes.
other_useful_info: Look up your courses and professors on sites like ratemyprofessor. It can be extremely important for determining whether or not you should take a course.
most_rewarding: Meeting and living with Americans, and experiencing their culture first-hand.
greatest_challenge: The coursework was often overwhelming.
other_comments: Try Culver's and get their concrete mixer as well. Possibly the best fast food in the US.

crucial_aspects: I chose the University of Wisconsin–Madison because I wanted to experience a different study environment and an educational approach that is significantly different from the one I am used to in Denmark. I was motivated by the more interactive and discussion-based classroom culture, as well as the strong sense of campus life, which I believe will challenge me both academically and personally and give me a broader perspective on higher education.
info_ease: t was easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. There was a well-organized welcome, and we had a Zoom meeting shortly after arriving that provided important and helpful information. Additionally, it was easy to get in contact with the International Student Office in Madison whenever questions came up, which made the transition much smoother.
arrival_assistance: Upon arrival, I received support through a Zoom meeting that provided essential practical information, as well as a guided campus walk that helped us get familiar with the university and its facilities. There were also small social events at the beginning of the semester, which made it easier to meet other exchange students and feel welcomed into the community.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process was different from what I was used to, as the system at the host institution works differently than in Denmark. It took some time to get used to, but once I understood the structure, the process became manageable and worked well.
registration_help: Help was readily available through the International Student Office in Madison, who were very helpful and quick to respond to emails, both before departure and after arrival, whenever questions came up.
registration_success: I was very successful in registering for the classes I wanted and was able to enroll in all the courses I had planned to take.
registration_advice: I would recommend that future exchange students stay in close contact with the International Student Office and do not hesitate to reach out by email if they have questions about registration. They are very helpful and responsive, and contacting them early can make the registration process much smoother.
course_level: The level of the courses was appropriate and well-matched to my academic background. There were many assignments and frequent quizzes for each class, which required continuous engagement, but this is part of a different educational system and teaching approach than what I am used to.
teaching_comparison: The teaching style was very different from that at UCPH, with mandatory lectures and a strong focus on continuous participation. The instructors were highly engaged, approachable, and supportive, which created a motivating and positive learning environment.
courses_enrolled: COMARTS200: Introduction to Digital Communication COMARTS260: Communication and Human Behavior COMARTS266: Theory and Practice of Group Discussion COMARTS345: Online Communication & Personal Relationships
recommended_courses: I would highly recommend COMARTS200: Introduction to Digital Communication and COMARTS345: Online Communication & Personal Relationships. Both courses had excellent instructors and were closely connected to real-world examples, which made the content easy to relate to and engaging. The assignments throughout the semester were interesting and relevant, encouraging reflection on everyday digital communication and personal experiences, which made the courses both motivating and rewarding.
unexpected_costs: One unexpected cost was the tipping culture, as tips are expected in many situations and quickly add up. Additionally, sales tax is added to most purchases, which increased everyday expenses. I also encountered extra fees when using my Danish card abroad, which made transactions more expensive than anticipated.
cost_comparison: Groceries were much more expensive than I expected, especially if you want to eat something other than fast food. Fresh and healthier food options in particular were significantly more costly, which made everyday grocery shopping more expensive than anticipated.
activities_available: There was a wide range of cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students. The school spirit was very strong, inclusive, and engaging, creating a strong sense of community on campus. There were many sports activities and long-standing athletic traditions, which played a big role in student life and made it easy to get involved and feel connected.
activities_recommended: I would highly recommend attending sports events, especially football games and other major matches. They are a big part of campus culture and school spirit and are a great way to experience American college traditions. These events are very social, energetic, and inclusive, making them an excellent opportunity to meet other students and feel part of the campus community.

culture_adjustment: t was relatively easy to adjust to the local culture. People were very open, welcoming, and helpful, which made it easy to feel comfortable and included. Although there were cultural differences, they were easy to adapt to and became a positive part of the exchange experience.

culture_appreciated: I especially appreciated how welcoming and approachable people were, which made it easy to feel included and at home. I also greatly valued the strong school spirit, which created a sense of community and made campus life engaging and enjoyable.

other_useful_info: Future exchange students should be prepared for a more structured and demanding study system with continuous assignments and mandatory attendance, which can be different from what they are used to. most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was becoming part of a very welcoming and engaged campus community. Experiencing a different study culture with strong school spirit, supportive instructors, and close interaction with other students broadened my perspective both academically and personally and made the exchange experience truly memorable.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge during the exchange was finding housing for only one semester, as most off-campus options require a full-year lease. The process was stressful and time-consuming and required a lot of flexibility and early planning.

crucial_aspects: One of the most crucial aspects in choosing my study destination was the strong school spirit and campus culture in the United States. registration_help: Help was mainly available via email. They were good at responding to questions, although it was important to keep the time difference in mind when waiting for replies.
registration_success: I was very successful in registering for the classes I wanted, as I was able to enroll in all the courses I applied for.
registration_advice: My advice to future exchange students would be to be patient and allow some time to understand the registration system, as it may be different from what you are used to. Once you become familiar with the system, the registration process works well.
course_level: The level of the courses was appropriate and well-structured. However, the teaching and learning approach was quite different from what I was used to, so it took some time to adjust. teaching_comparison: The style of teaching at my host institution was quite different from that at UCPH. There was a much stronger focus on student interaction and participation in class. unexpected_costs: While not entirely unexpected, both insurance and housing turned out to be more expensive than I had anticipated. These costs were higher than expected and became a significant part of my overall expenses.

A wide range of sports events, such as football games, ice hockey, and volleyball matches, were especially popular and created a great atmosphere on campus. In addition, the International Student Office was very good at bringing exchange students together by organizing various social events, which made it easy to meet new people and feel part of the community.
activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend attending sports events. They are a very American experience and a lot of fun, and they offer a great opportunity to experience the strong school spirit and sense of community on campus.
weekend_recommendations: I would recommend exploring the city and seeing what is going on, especially on weekends. Spending time with American friends is also a great way to experience the local culture. culture_adjustment: It was quite easy to adjust to the local culture at my exchange site.
socializing_tips: My main tip would be to be open and not be afraid to take initiative and approach people. In addition, joining different clubs or student organizations at the university is a great way to meet new people and socialize with local students.
cultural_challenges: One cultural difference I found challenging was the tipping culture, as this is quite different from what I was used to. Additionally, it took some time to adjust to the fact that class attendance was mandatory and that there were more weekly academic requirements compared to the University of Copenhagen.
culture_appreciated: I especially appreciated the strong school spirit and the feeling of being part of a large and engaged community. You could really feel that people value the social aspect of university life, for example through the strong sense of togetherness at sports events.
top3_advice: First, be open and proactive when it comes to socializing. Taking initiative and joining clubs or attending events makes it much easier to meet people and feel part of the community. most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was being part of the strong campus community and school spirit, while also experiencing a different academic system and way of university life. It was both personally and academically enriching and gave me valuable new perspectives.
greatest_challenge: The greatest challenge during my exchange was definitely housing and visa-related matters. The visa process was especially challenging because parts of it were shut down over the summer just before my departure, which made the situation more stressful and difficult to manage.

cultural_challenges: Vegemite and vapes.

Australia is also a great place to do some solo travelling and you meet some many nice people at hostels.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy. Australians are really open and welcoming. They are also very interested in people from other countries.
socializing_tips: Join some clubs at uni!
cultural_challenges: The part days in NSW is Wednesday and Sunday. This was a really bad fit with my school schedule and it felt pretty weird to me to go out on weekdays.

top3_advice: Take advantage of the great lokation of Wollongong! your weekends can be filled with: 1. Hikes in the Royal National Park 2. City get away to Sydney 3. Beach days in one of the beaches in Wollongong

weekend_recommendations: Sydney ligger en togtur væk, ca. 1-1,5 time. Meget nemt. Ellers er der meget natur omkring Wollongong, så der er masser at udforske. Wollongong er ikke den største by, men har stadig et stor shoppingcenter.
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt.
socializing_tips: Mine fag var 99.9% udvekslingsstudenter, så jeg var mest sammen med andre study abroad studerende. Ellers er der mange cafeer og restauranter på campus, så det er nemt at møde andre.
cultural_challenges: Mest undervisningsstilen.
culture_appreciated: Menneskenes imødekommenhed og åbenhed på gaden.
top3_advice: 1) For mig, på kandidaten/MA, var niveauet højere end hvad jeg har været vant til. Overvej derfor dette. Andre danskere var kun på BA niveau og sagde at de intet undervisning havde nærmest, og at det var nemt. Der er derfor stor forskel! 2) Wollongong er nemt fordi det er meget billigere end Sydney, men samtidig er det stadig nemt at komme til Sydney hvis man begynder at få økuller. 3) Jeg boede på Campus East, og kan godt anbefale det, men vælg self-catered, for lejlighederne er så meget bedre.
other_useful_info: De er virkelig gode til at hjælpe deres studerende, så der er altid hjælp at hente, og de er så søde.
most_rewarding: De søde mennesker jeg mødte og havde nogle fantastiske oplevelser med.
greatest_challenge: At tilpasse mig det faglige niveau. Jeg havde undervisning hver dag, og om onsdagen havde jeg undervisning fra 08.30 til 20.30 (dog med pauser), men jeg kom fra at være vant til undervisning 2-3 gange om ugen, så det var virkelig en voldsom omvæltning.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville meget gerne til New Zealand eller Australien, fordi naturen her nede er helt fantastisk, og kulturen inspirerer mig.
overall_comments: Australien er et fantastisk land at være på udveksling i. Jeg kan varmt anbefale at tage her til.
info_ease: Jeg følte mig godt informeret fra KU's og mit værtsuniversitets side.
arrival_assistance: Vi havde introdage, hvor vi blev klædt på til det nye semester. Vi fik information om alt fra fagtilmeldning til kulturelle forskelligheder og muligheder for surfcamps og andre ture.
arrival_comments: Det var rart at blive "holdt i hånden" i begyndelsen, da man var helt ny her på den anden side af jorden.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Australien er et fantastisk land at være på udveksling i. Jeg kan varmt anbefale at tage her til.
registration_process: UOW har en trin-for-trin-guide til processen på deres hjemmeside, som bl.a. forklarer, hvordan man søger om endelig optagelse, hvordan man søger fag, hvordan man søger accommodation, osv.
registration_help: Jeg har mailet en del med administrationen, som har været en stor hjælp undervejs. De har altid svaret inden for 24 timer, hvilket har været virkelig skønt!
registration_success: Jeg synes, at processen med fagtilmelding var en smule besværlig, fordi det var svært at gennemskue, hvornår hvilke fag blev udbudt her nede (om det var i spring semester eller fall semester). Men takket være hjælp fra administrationen lykkedes det.
registration_advice: Følg deres guides på universitetets hjemmeside og ræk endelig ud til dem over mail, hvis der skulle opstå spørgsmål undervejs.
academics_comments: Australien er et fantastisk land at være på udveksling i. Jeg kan varmt anbefale at tage her til.
course_level: I og med, at mange fag har "prerequisites", har det været nemmest at søge om BA-fag. Fordelen ved det er også, at hele det australske retssystem jo er noget anderledes end det danske, og at man på BA-fagene stadig forklarer lidt om dette.
teaching_comparison: Ingen forelæsninger - kun seminarer på hold af 30-40 studerende.
courses_enrolled: Children and the Law, Intellectual Property Law, Contemporary Issues in Criminal Justice, Environmental Law.
recommended_courses: Children and the Law er et af de fedeste fag, jeg nogensinde har haft.
unexpected_costs: Det er generelt dyrt at tage på udveksling, og ønsker man at rejse og tage på udflugter med venner (som jeg har gjort meget), skal man være indstillet på at komme til at bruge en del penge. Men for mig har det været de bedst brugte penge nogensinde, for jeg har fået oplevelser for livet.
cost_comparison: Madindkøb er en lille smule billigere end i Danmark, kaffe er billigere (og mega lækkert!), benzin er billigere, flybilletter er billigere. For mig har husleje dog været dyrere end i Danmark.
activities_available: Rigtig mange. UOW har holdt internationale markeder, osv., og lært os om aboriginsk kultur.
activities_recommended: Australien er et fantastisk land at rejse i, og området omkring Wollongong er enormt smukt! Vi har både bjerge og turkisblå strande. Jeg vil helt klart anbefale at rejse rundt i landet i det omfang, det økonomisk kan lade sig gøre.
weekend_recommendations: Tage på ture i området med venner.
culture_adjustment: Jeg elsker at rejse og lære nye kulturer at kende, så jeg tilpassede mig hurtigt det nye. UOW har en linje, man kan ringe til, hvis man føler sig overvældet over det nye - og det virker til, at de tager virkelig godt hånd om en, hvis man har brug for hjælp eller støtte.
socializing_tips: Jeg har haft held med bare at tale til min sidemakker i de seminarer, jeg har haft. Det er sådan, jeg har mødt alle de australiere, som jeg i dag kvalificerer som nogle af mine gode venner.
cultural_challenges: Man skal altid tilpasse sig, når man kommer til en ny kultur. Dog synes jeg virkelig, at Australien er et "welcoming" land, der får én til at føle sig velkommen fra start.
culture_appreciated: At Australien er et meget multikulturelt samfund, og at folk er åbne og enormt søde.
top3_advice: Wollongong North Beach er virkelig dejlig og har hyggelige små strandcaféer, en togbillet til Sydney er billig, og sørg for at få rejst rundt i Australien, hvis du har råd til det!
other_useful_info: Du må ikke være bange for at spørge om hjælp, hvis du har brug for noget. Uni staff er vildt søde og altid klar på at hjælpe!
most_rewarding: Mine australske venner og de rejseoplevelser, jeg har fået i Oceanien!
greatest_challenge: Jeg har følt et stort socialt pres under mit udvekslingsophold. Men jeg valgte fra start at prioritere de australske venner, jeg havde mødt - og det er jeg så glad for i dag, hvor vi er blevet meget tætte venner!
other_comments: Glæd dig til at komme til Australien!

socializing_tips: Live on campus, go to surf-camp, join for 0-week and the parties, join some local activities like the run clubs, Wednesday uni nights in the bouldering centre etc.

most_rewarding: Learning to surf and meeting friends here, along with being at a university that was very invested in everyones' well-being and accommodating that

courses_enrolled: BIOL103 - Molecules, Cells and Organisms CAVA125 - Introduction to Photography 2 INDS130 - Indigenous Knowledge in Global Contexts SOC 347 - Sociology of Health, Illness and Medicine
recommended_courses: BIOL103 var nemt og helt fint at få opfrisket noget af ens viden. CAVA125 er ret hyggeligt, især hvis man har en ven at gøre det med. unexpected_costs: Potter, pander, bestik, glas osv Sengetøj, vasketøjskurv, håndklæder mm
cost_comparison: Visum var 3.373kr Acceptance fee var 2370kr Havde håbet på de ikke var så høje igen. Uber rundt i byen samt tog til sydney var heldigvis "billigt" Indkøb er nogle ting billigere mens andre dyre end i DK. Tøj er billigt og super sødt, så pak let!
activities_available: Alt muligt forskelligt.
activities_recommended: Deltag til så meget som muligt de første par uger. Så kan man se om der noget som er sjovt samt møde andre
weekend_recommendations: Jeg tog med nogle veninder på en weekend tur til Jervis bay, hvor vi lejede en bil og overnattede i en "hytte" tæt på stranden. Her så vi vilde kænguruer, delfiner, hvaler og en af de hvideste strande. Det klart et besøg hver. Ellers tog vi ofte dags turer om lørdagen eller søndagen til Sydney (specielt til Manly) og tilbragte en dag. Andre weekender blev brugt på at surfe eller slappe af ved standene i Wollongong. Det også muligt at hike på bjergene lige bag ved uni. I ferien er der mange muligheder, jeg fik selv besøg af min familie og rejste rundt i to uger med dem. Men flere af mine venner planlagde forskellige ture bla til tasmanien, fiji, melbourne osv

socializing_tips: Vær åben og snak med folk hvis du fx bliver sat i gruppe med ikke udvekslingsstuderende. Jeg mødte en pige som inviterende mig med ud at snorkle med hende og hendes veninder.
