culture_appreciated: Folk er åbne og søde.
top3_advice: Spar en masse sammen, så det ikke begrænser dig. Brugte nok omkring 100.000 i alt med rejse osv Ikke vær for bange hvis der går et par uger før du finder de rette venner. Lad vær med at vælge Wollongong hvis du kun kommer for at feste.
other_useful_info: Wollongong er en super hyggelig by og du får rig mulighed for at opleve andre dele af Australien. Så ikke vælg den fra blot fordi det ikke er en storby man kender. most_rewarding: De mennesker jeg mødte og alle de nye oplevelser jeg fik. Blandt andet har man rig mulighed for at rejse rundt efter eksamener i start november. Her oplevede jeg både noget af Australien i en van men også som backbacker
greatest_challenge: Håndtere jetlag ugen op til studiestart hvor der er en masse sociale aktiviteter som man gerne vil være på til. Vil klart anbefalde at komme mindst et par dage før alle aktivteter mm starter

crucial_aspects: I wanted to get to know British politics and culture better and was recommended University of York (UoY).
info_ease: Pretty easy. The university reached out to me with information and held some online seminars where we could ask questions about everything pre-arrival.
arrival_assistance: I was picked up at the airport and taken to college I was staying at. There were some students to guide us to get our keys and stuff.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Depends on your department. For politics, they reached out via email around the beginning of September and asked which classes I would like to take.
registration_help: You can always email them or ask questions about it in the pre-arrival seminars.
registration_success: Very successful, I got the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Be patient – the process might take place a lot later than at KU. However, within the first two weeks it is also possible to change classes, so if you do not get your preferred ones at first you might be able to get them then.
course_level: The courses vary a lot in difficulty. The first year course was very easy, but the second and third year couses were similar in level to KU. Maybe slightly fewer readings compared to KU.
teaching_comparison: Very similar – 1 lecture and 1 seminar per class per week. During the lectures you mostly listen and take notes, and they are recorded and uploaded online which is very convenient. The seminars are very interactive and usually only around 10 people with a professor, so I learnt a lot during them.
courses_enrolled: POL00013C: Introduction to Comparative Politics (first year module) POL00079I: European Union Politics (second year module) POL00068H: Politics of Peace after Civil War (third year module)
recommended_courses: Politics of Peace after Civil War was absolutely incredible – very interesting course materials and great professors! European Union Politics was taught by a quite fun professor, so if you're interested in the EU it is a good course, but it can be a bit heavy with the readings sometimes.
unexpected_costs: You have to pay a fee to join sports and societies. Sports were around 20-40 pounds I believe, while societies were only a couple of pounds.
cost_comparison: Trains in the UK are expensive. However, grocery shopping is significantly cheaper than in Denmark, especially if you go to Aldi or Lidl.
activities_available: So many options, literally societies for every niche theme. Also loads of sports teams, music, theatre etc.
activities_recommended: Whatever your heart desires honestly – joining societies and clubs is a great way to meet people. I did the choir, football and roller-blading and would recommend all three.
weekend_recommendations: York is such a lovely city, so make sure to make time to explore it! Go see the Minster (free for students at UoY), walk along the rivers and visit some cute cafés. York is also the UK's most haunted city, so go for a ghost tour if you're into that. For pubs, go to the Phoenix for jazz-night and the golden ball for folk music. York is also a great location for exploring the UK – around 2 hours to London and 2,5 hours to Edinburgh via train. For nearby day-trips I would recommend Leeds, Whitby (very cheap with the bus and so pretty), Knaresborough and Newcastle.
culture_adjustment: Easy, culturally the UK is quite similar to Denmark
socializing_tips: Join clubs, societies etc! And go to the international socializers in the first week.
cultural_challenges: Nothing really.
culture_appreciated: Locals are generally pretty welcoming and open, especially in the Northern parts of the UK.
top3_advice: Be patient with the application process, join societies/sports and explore the UK!
most_rewarding: Meeting new people and experiencing a different university life.
greatest_challenge: Being ill and dealing with the NHS – they're were not very helpful and I had be quite insistent in order to see a doctor at the local GP.

crucial_aspects: I always really liked traveling to England and wanted to experience what it would be like to live there. I chose York specifically because I thought both the city as well as Yorkshire in general looked really pretty.
overall_comments: I couldn't have had a better semester abroad. York is such a lovely city :)
info_ease: It was very easy. The university sent a bunch of emails with information, and the visiting students team also hosted a pre-arrival Zoom meeting where we were told everything we would need to know before arriving.
arrival_assistance: I signed up for the university's airport collection service, so when I arrived in Manchester, I was picked up at the airport and driven all the way to the university. At the university there were volunteers who showed us around and helped us get checked into our student accommodation. Throughout the welcome week there were also a bunch of talks and events to help us get settled. The visiting students team also hosted a few socials during the semester.
arrival_comments: Everyone at the university is really friendly and helpful. If you have any issues, just contact them. I originally misunderstood the English requirements and didn't know that the Politics course specifically requires visiting students to provide an IELTS-test. I called and emailed with the university, and in the end they accepted my English A from STX combined with a language document from KU, and I was able to save a lot of time and money by not having to take the IELTS-test.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I couldn't have had a better semester abroad. York is such a lovely city :)
registration_process: A few weeks after completing my online enrollment and getting my York-email address, I was contacted by the Politics department who asked for my module choices. I sent them an email with the modules I wished to take, and then they made sure I was registered for those modules.
registration_help: I was told I could contact the department if I had any questions.
registration_success: I was very successful. I sent them a list of three modules, and then they registered me for those three modules.
registration_advice: Don’t worry if they don’t tell you that you got the modules you asked for. I was confused at first, because I never got an email back, but then I saw on the website that the registration was already in the system, they just didn’t email to let me know that it had gone through.
academics_comments: I couldn't have had a better semester abroad. York is such a lovely city :)
course_level: I took a first-year module, a second-year module, and a third-year module. The second and third-year modules felt similar to the level of difficulty at KU, but the first-year module was very easy and a bit like being back in Gymnasiet.
teaching_comparison: The seminar groups are a lot smaller - about 10-12 people per seminar group. I was surprised by how much I liked having a smaller group. It meant that instead of the same couple of people raising their hand, everyone was engaged in the discussions. There was also a lot more interaction with the lecturers as they were often also the ones teaching during the seminars.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Comparative Politics - POL00013C (10 ECTS) European Union Politics - POL00079I (10 ECTS) Politics of Peace after Civil War - POL00068H (10 ECTS)
recommended_courses: I combined Introduction to Comparative Politics and Politics of Peace after Civil War to get DAK3 approved and took European Union Politics as EP. European Union Politics and Politics of Peace after Civil War were both really interesting. Introduction to Comparative Politics I wouldn’t have taken if I didn’t need to in order to get DAK3 approved. It was like DAK1, DAK2, and DAK3 combined into a single course, so a lot of the things we covered, I had already learned at KU.
unexpected_costs: There were a lot of expenses in the first month buying stuff for my room and the kitchen. I really hated the mattress, so I ended up ordering a mattress topper from Jysk. It was money I did not expect to spend, but I really did not regret it as I slept very comfortably for the rest of the semester and was able to bring it home to Denmark in a vacuum bag.
cost_comparison: Public transport. I thought I would be taking the bus into the city, but instead I just walked everywhere.
activities_available: They had a lot of different sports and societies. Whatever hobby you have, they probably have a society for it.
activities_recommended: I didn’t end up joining any societies, but I would probably just recommend going to the welcome fair and seeing if anything interests you.
weekend_recommendations: Travel! York is the perfect location for a bunch of different day-trips. A few of the places I went and really loved were the Lake District, Knaresborough, Staithes, Robin Hood’s Bay, Whitby, and Durham. Yorkshire also has a lot of great spots for hiking. For longer trips I can also recommend going to London and Edinburgh. Also - buy a railcard! It saves you a lot of money on train tickets.
culture_adjustment: It was pretty easy. British culture is relatively similar to Danish culture.
socializing_tips: In England they start university at 18, so all the local students were very young. I small-talked with the people I had seminars with as well as with some of my housemates, but other than that I didn’t really have that much contact with the British students. Pretty much all my friends were other exchange students. I did enter the university’s “buddy scheme”, where they matched new international students with student volunteers, and made friends with the buddy I was assigned. However, most of the students that sign up to be a buddy are second or third-year international students that study full-time in York.
cultural_challenges: The age gap made it difficult to get to know that many British people, but I just spent my time with the other exchange students instead, so it wasn’t really that big of a problem.
culture_appreciated: The friendliness. People in England, especially in the North, are a lot more friendly and less reserved towards strangers than in Denmark.
top3_advice: 1. York is such a lovely city! I had never been there before going on exchange, and it truly exceeded all my expectations. The streets are very charming and filled with cute cafes and shops. I can also really recommend buying a 1£ coffee from Pret and taking a walk in the museum gardens or by the river. The Minster Gate Bookshop also has a lot of really cheap books. Also, visiting the Minster is free for all York residents. You have to pay to go up into the tower, but the view from there is really nice. The city walls have some great views as well. In general, I found the city to be a really nice size. There were plenty of things to do, but it was also small enough that you could just walk instead of having to take public transport. 2. The campus looks a lot nicer in person than in pictures. I thought it would be kind of ugly, because a lot of the buildings aren’t that pretty, but the lakes, trees, and wildlife make it feel like you’re walking through a park. Especially in autumn, it was very pretty. 3. Just reach out to the university if you have any issues. They are really nice and always happy to help.
other_useful_info: Buy a railcard and download the UniDays app - it has a bunch of different student discounts. Also, when the university invites you to a visa registration event, you still have to go, even if you’re not there on a visa. We were given a bit of conflicting information about it, but you just have to book a time slot and show them your ETA instead of a visa. The bagels at the library café are also really good :)
most_rewarding: Moving to a different country all by myself. Building a whole life in a different country and meeting people from all over the world was such a fun and fulfilling experience.
greatest_challenge: The age gap between me and my housemates. I was lucky that my room was next to another exchange student who was my age, but everyone else in the house was significantly younger than us. I think it might have been less of an issue, if a lot of them weren’t also pretty inconsiderate when it came to cleaning up after themselves and quieting down at night.

crucial_aspects: I chose UZH as the academic opportunities for economics students are very broad. I got introduced to academic research on a very high level. In addition I chose Zürich because of the surrounding nature. I love to spend my weekends travelling or hiking in the mountains.
overall_comments: The only minus in the hygiene in my student house, and the covid restrictions in the beginning. Otherwise its been amazing!
info_ease: Very easy. The university provided me with any information I needed, and they are very good at remembering you about deadlines etc.
arrival_assistance: My ESN buddy picked me up in the airport and we travelled together to my student house. After this I primarily used the student service at UZH for help. They are super nice and helpful. The easiest way to contract them is to go to their office at the university site.
arrival_comments: UZH also offered several welcome events with information about life in Switzerland, city tours, speed-friending etc. which was very helpful in the beginning.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: The only minus in the hygiene in my student house, and the covid restrictions in the beginning. Otherwise its been amazing!
registration_process: You have to register within the registration period. The only thing that was challenging was that the information sheet about course registration provided by the university was in German (hello google translate).
registration_help: The university provided all the information I needed.
registration_success: Pretty successful. I only had a seminar that I didn't get into. Otherwise I got all the courses I wanted. In general I think that most people get the courses they sign up for.
registration_advice: In the first two weeks you can try several courses and then drop those who you don't like, as the registration is open in these weeks. I used this opportunity to try different courses, and I got surprised by the content. Therefore is was very happy that I signed up for several courses and thereby could choose between those.
academics_comments: The only minus in the hygiene in my student house, and the covid restrictions in the beginning. Otherwise its been amazing!
course_level: The level is quite similar to UCPH, however the teaching style and the exams are different. I read less books and papers here but wrote more assignments and had to make more group work and presentations. In general I would say that I spend way more time on my studies here during the semester, but less time before the exams.
teaching_comparison: Usually the courses consist of lectures, excise classes, presentations and/or assignments. In most courses the assignments and presentations also count towards your final grad, why the exam only counts for maybe 50%.
courses_enrolled: Sustainable Investing (3 ECTS), Advanced Banking (6 ECTS), Experimental Economics (6 ECTS), Econometrics for Policy Analysts (6 ECTS), Global Switzerland (6 ECTS), Blockchain (3 ECTS).
recommended_courses: I can really reccomend Econometrics for Policy Analysts if you want to learn how to interpret on economic analyses. It is a professor from Harvard (his name is David) that teaches in this course and he is really good. Also the Sustainable Investing course, here I learned a lot about ESG ratings. Be careful when you choose your courses. I chose Blockchain, which was a very interesting course, but it is only 3 ECTS and the workload was approximately the same as the 7.5 ECTS courses at UCPH.
unexpected_costs: In the beginning there is a lot of administrative stuff that cost you a lot of money. For example when have to register at the Kreisbüro (corresponding to our kommunekontor) it costs 40-80 chf.
cost_comparison: The transportation in Switzerland is very costfull. However the train system is super efficient. You can buy a half fare travel card for 120 chf (900 dkk) and thereby get discounts, which I will definitely reccomend. I also bought a monthly pass for zone 110 which cost 64 chf/month (450 dkk), and then if you want to travel you can buy day passes which is around 40-60 chf per day (250-500 dkk). Also meat is very expensive to buy. I will definitely reccomend you to eat lunch at the Mensa/cafeteria at UZH as it is cheap and good food, and cook dinner yourself in the evening.
activities_available: A lot of welcome events where you can meet new students. Finance Club provide lunch every Thursday during the semester. Many parties and social activities.
activities_recommended: The university provide the ASVZ app, which is the student sport association, Here you can enroll in different sports for free. I used it a lot to try out different sports.
weekend_recommendations: Travel as much as you can in the beginning. Make sure to go on day trips to different parts of Switzerland before the exam period starts. In the winter season you can go skiing and in the summer season you can go hiking and camping in the mountains. The nature is amazing!
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy as the culture is quite similar to the Danish culture. The Swiss people are quite reserved and are proud of their country. One of the things that I had to adjust to: the trains and trams are on time always. If you come 1 minute late you can be sure that it already left (and they excuse a lot for a couple of minutes delay).
socializing_tips: It can be hard to socialise with swiss students as they already have their friends. I recommend you to socialize with the exchange students and attend university events if you want to socialize with the swiss students.
cultural_challenges: Some people cannot speak English (for example the employees in the Mensa/canteen at UZH), and unless you are really good at speaking German they can be really hard to understand. The swiss-german language is not the same as high-german as we learn in Denmark!
culture_appreciated: I really appreciate how polite and helpful the swiss people are. They are always ready to help you if you need anything. It is also very safe. I went home alone in the night several times, and it has never been an issue. We also went swimming in the lake several times leaving our phones/keys/etc. on the grass and nothing will ever happen.
top3_advice: 1. make sure to make enough money (in total I spent around 100,000 dkk), 2. reach out to new people (you need to be very openminded in the beginning, but it pays off afterwards), 3. remember to enjoy it, because time flies by so quickly!
other_useful_info: I attended the German course in the first two weeks, which I will really recommend. It is a nice way to meet a lot of people, and to get to know the city before the semester starts.
most_rewarding: I learned a lot about myself and my boundaries. I am better at speaking to new people without any prejudices, and I also learned when I want to be social and when I need some time alone.
greatest_challenge: The hygiene and the fact that I had to accept the risk of being sick.
other_comments: No.

crucial_aspects: Location, culture
overall_comments: Great experience! I enjoyed every day in Switzerland and felt very much at home.
info_ease: I was a bit unsure about a couple of things since I did not receive anything on mail but only on Mobility Online, and I was not aware of that in the start of the proces. As soon as I realized, it was super easy to gather all important information in order to be prepared for my stay. The communication with the Swiss University was great and they provided me with all the information I needed.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any from the university, but I had a feeling that I could contact the International Office to get support in case I would need it at some point. I lived with a lot of other exchange students in a student housing which meant that we supported each other and shared information about the different processes of moving to another country, getting to know the university and so on.
arrival_comments: I am not fully aware of the different options available and therefore I do not think that I am the right one to answer this question. Overall I am happy with the orientation even though I would have liked to have understood the structures at the university a bit earlier. However, I think it might have been my own responsibility and therefore mistake.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Great experience! I enjoyed every day in Switzerland and felt very much at home.
registration_process: I uploaded the documents needed and afterwards received a letter of admission. Afterwards I received a lot of different information about registration in home commune and immigration office, health insurance and so on.
registration_help: I could e-mail the office of international affairs at any time if needed. I did however no use their offers.
registration_success: Very. It was super easy to do online. However, non-german speakers might face a challenge when registering since a larger part of the information is only available in German.
registration_advice: At UZH you can change your courses within the first two weeks of the semester. This allows you to try out all the courses you find interesting and then pick the ones you like the most in the end. You can for example sign up for 45 ECTS, attend them all for the first week and then pick the ones you like the most/change them all completely. I was not 100% sure about how this worked at first and would have liked a bit more information about this, but it worked out well and I was very happy for this system. Note that in some faculties the courses are rather small (2-6 ECTS) and therefore you'd have to pick a lot of different courses to reach the right number of credits. This requires you to check all class times AND locations carefully, since courses can overlap and/or be held in completely different campuses in the city making it impossible to get to class in time/attend the whole class. Some courses are live online, some are recorded and some required physical attendance - check it out before signing up.
academics_comments: Great experience! I enjoyed every day in Switzerland and felt very much at home.
course_level: I studied with both BA and MA students. The level was fine all over and I am very satisfied. However, spending the first 1-2 weeks of the semester finding out which courses suit you best is a good idea. I for example found that some courses required way more preparation than others even though the number of credits was the same. Some are passed through a multiple choice test and others require you to write a 5 page essay to the texts of the week every week the whole semester. In one case I changed subject because the level was too high and the field was new to me.
teaching_comparison: I experienced several teaching styles, but the biggest difference was that I did not have any group work in my courses. This was nice, because it gave me flexibility to explore the country, but it also made it very hard to meet local students from the host country. I expected the instructors to be more authoritarian, but they were all very kind, open and inclusive.
courses_enrolled: - Animal Ethics - Media Management - Communication, Technology and Urban Life - Digital Well-Being - Global Switzerland: From Early Globalizer to International Geneva - Summer School: What defines a country's succes? - German Courses (B1 Diskutieren + B2 Lesen & Schreiben)
recommended_courses: Animal ethics was great and a very special course for people from many different fields. Here we discussed literature and philosophy on animal ethics. The learning environment was very comfortable and we all learned from each other when discussing different aspects of animal rights. Digital Well-being taught me a lot about the significance of creating healthy frames around the use of digitized solutions, products and platforms. Since this is expected to increase in importance in the future, it is very interesting to learn about. Unfortunately, it was a bit far from my study since it also includes big data and the like, which I have never worked with as a language and communication science student. I can also recommend Global Switzerland and the summer school. These courses are made for exchange students and students from many different fields can participate. It is multidisciplinary and they also work as an academic introduction to the country you'll live in (historically, socially, economically, politically).
unexpected_costs: It is obligatory to have a private health insurance. They pay almost all expenses to doctors and so on. However, if you do not work in Switzerland and you are covered by the common European health insurance, you can get an exemption from the insurance. This is nice, but it means that you have to pay all doctor bills at first and then send it to the organization afterwards. I think it is a good option to get a private health insurance which covers everything, because EU do not pay everything, but it is expensive and therefore it might make more sense for some to get an insurance through a Danish company while still getting the exemption from a Swiss insurance. Also, several companies offer cheap additional health insurances, but these are usually not good and it has proven to be very hard to get money back from them. Therefore it is important to fix these things in time.
cost_comparison: Food is incredibly expensive. I spent approximately 40% more on food than I do when I am in Denmark. Also, public transportation is expensive especially if you are over 25 years old. SBB has good offers making it more affordable to travel by train, but normal tickets for people who do not use these offers (Snow25, half fare and more) are super super expensive if you travel out of the city of Zürich.
activities_available: Zürich and the surrounding unis has the best student sports association! All sports from pilates to hiking, biking, football, strengt training, climbing, ski touring and to sailing and surfing are included (100+!). Most are free and there is hundreds of activities to sign up for every day. There is also great facilities such as sport halls, gym, sauna and more. This is the greatest and I can only recommend! Weekly bars and coffee clubs at uni were harder to get to know since they are located in many different areas. If you do not know local students well, you probably wont go. The big shared bar BKVM is however a great place for everyone to meet. Erasmus also arranges tons of activities, which is also a great way to meet new people and explore new places.
activities_recommended: All ASVZ activities!
weekend_recommendations: Go to the mountains! Skiing in winter and hiking in summer. The nature is amazing! SBB and the local ski resorts have a lot of different offers (such as Snow25) for students and young people, so you can go skiing at a reasonable price. Also, the Half Fare train card gives you half price of all travels in Switzerland for 1 year - if you intend on exploring the country, this is usually worth it!
culture_adjustment: Very easy! City reminded me a bit of home and I felt at home very fast.
socializing_tips: Go to ASVZ sport activities.
cultural_challenges: Everything is closed on Sundays. Besides of that, no challenges.
culture_appreciated: Everything is very clean, well-maintained and punctual. Also, the Swiss really appreciate the nature which means that they 1) clean up after themselves 2) love going on trips and adventures and 3) they adapt to the weather and have fun activities to do all year. The people respect each other and each other's privacy, but if you initiates contact, they are very friendly and helpful!
top3_advice: Buy yourself some good hiking boots. Bring more money than you think you'll need. Do not forget swimsuit and a rain jacket - they are equally important!
other_useful_info: Information about insurance and in particular private health insurance is important. Also, do not forget to apply for scholarships beforehand - the country is so expensive for foreigners that extra finances can be ver helpful.
most_rewarding: Exploring the culture and in particular the nature.
greatest_challenge: Learning and writing in academic English took a bit of getting-used-to.
other_comments: Go to Switzerland!

crucial_aspects: I wanted to improve my German skills and I knew that the University of Zurich had a very good reputation. Also, I wanted to explore the Swiss nature.
overall_comments: Overall, I had a very good experience. The university was great, the professors too and I lived with amazing people from all over the world.
info_ease: It was super easy, the departmental coordinators from UZH did an amazing job in providing the exchange students with all necessary information.
arrival_assistance: I received information about the university, the city and the different student offers.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Overall, I had a very good experience. The university was great, the professors too and I lived with amazing people from all over the world.
registration_process: It was a really great process. Of course it is always a bit challenging to navigate in a new system, but the departmental coordinators of UZH gave us the opportunity to pre sign up for course enrollment. So we could basically be ensured that we would get all the courses we wanted - really a great option.
registration_help: I had a lot of contact back and forth with the coordinators, and they were always super helpful and usually replied in one or two days.
registration_success: As described before, I could get all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Do a proper research before course enrollment. I could only take seminars with a lot of requirements during the semester and I would maybe have preferred to do some lectures too.
academics_comments: Overall, I had a very good experience. The university was great, the professors too and I lived with amazing people from all over the world.
course_level: The level was quite high, but since I did the first semester of my masters here, I can only compare the level to the bachelor level in Copenhagen - so I guess the level must be equivalent to the level in Denmark.
teaching_comparison: It was a bit different from Copenhagen and the style also varied in the different classes. But usually my classes were quite small and we had a lot of student interaction which I found really rewarding. We had a lot of activity during the semester, for example response papers and mid-terms. I was not really used to this, and sometimes it could be a bit stressful. But in the end it also gave me a lot of experience, so I am happy with the outcome.
courses_enrolled: Switzerland for Incomings (course for exchange students) Globalization as a new challenge to global governance Margaret Cavendish - Feminism, utopia or enlightenment Post-Industrial Transformations: Cleavages, Policy and Politics I also enrolled at two different German courses: One intensive course before the semester and one during the semester.
recommended_courses: I would recommend all of them! My professors were amazing and I have definitely gained a lot from taking the courses.
unexpected_costs: I paid 1200 DKK for a half-tax (a travel card that gives 50% discount on all travels in Switzerland). I also paid for the membership in the Opera. And then I just travelled a lot around in general.
cost_comparison: Everything is expensive in Switzerland but it is definitely possible to save some money. Just do grocery shopping in cheaper places like Lidl or Aldi or eat in the canteen at uni. Buy the half-tax and month card if you want to travel a lot. The university offers a whole range of student sports (for free!) through the ASVZ community - so enjoy that. And you can get free entrance at many clubs on Thursdays (which is usually the party day of the week).
activities_available: All sorts of sports (ASVZ!) and many different student associations. Also, the ESN (Erasmus Student Network) arranges a lot of different trips etc. You will receive all information about the different activities per mail from UZH.
activities_recommended: Just do a lot of sports, it is so much fun and you can try anything there - the ASVZ system offered more than 100 different classes - ranging from football to sailing etc.
weekend_recommendations: The Swiss nature is amazing, so please make use of it. We went on so many hikes and if you are into skiing, Switzerland is the place to be. Also, visit other cities, for example in the Italian or French parts of the country. Because of Switzerland's central location, it is super convenient to travel to places outside the country's borders, for example Germany or Italy. Zurich is a nice city also, where you can visit a lot of museums, swim in the Zurich lake or in the river, hike up the mountain Uetliberg, visit cafés or eat fondue or raclette (Swiss specialities).
culture_adjustment: It was pretty simple to be honest. (Most) Swiss people speak English very well and the infrastructure is great which makes it easy to get around. The Swiss people are not the most extroverted but they are always polite and willing to help.
socializing_tips: Talk to people in your class, do sports, sign up for a buddy through the mentor program (also provided by the university).
cultural_challenges: Swiss people are always on time, so be sure to adapt or it will seem offensive.
culture_appreciated: The decency of Swiss people
top3_advice: 1) Explore the nature 2) Learn a bit of German 3) Bring money
other_useful_info: Do not hesitate to reach out to your professors - they were always really helpful.
most_rewarding: Living in an international community, getting new friends from all over the world and practicing my academic English and German.
greatest_challenge: The courses were quite challenging in the beginning. But just focus on all the rewarding parts you get out of it.
other_comments: ENJOY!

crucial_aspects: Good university, option to have classes in English, country within Europe (convenient because of Covid in case anything happens), good options to explore nature by skiing and hiking. I have a friend who had a really good experience at UZH.
info_ease: Very easy. UZH had an info meeting and were also answering very quickly by e-mail.
arrival_assistance: No specific assistance
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: There was a special process for exchange students. Registration is online. Option to attend courses and assess whether you would like to registrate before actually having to decide.
registration_help: Info meeting and option to write e-mail. They usually answer very fast.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Be aware that some classes have limited capacity.
course_level: I only attended MA courses at UZH, and they seemed to be very much aligned w. the level at UCPH.
teaching_comparison: It is more formal than we are used to in Denmark in terms of addressing the professors.
courses_enrolled: Contract Design I, International Organisations, Comparative Constitutional Law, Introduction to Swiss Law and Current Issues in International Law.
recommended_courses: Current Issues in International Law. Professor Kaufmann taught the class, and she was such a kind and skilled professor. The topic of the course was digitalisation and it was super interesting. Introduction to Swiss Law is fun in terms of getting to know the Swiss legal system better.
unexpected_costs: Public transportation
cost_comparison: Everything was more than expected, Zürich is quite expensive. Especially public transportation + eating out.
activities_available: Free gym ASVZ through the uni.
activities_recommended: Enjoy the Swiss nature by skiing, hiking etc.
weekend_recommendations: Skiing, hiking and snow shoe hiking. Go to Zermatt.
culture_adjustment: Easy
socializing_tips: I had a very positive experience - the more you challenge yourself to go beyond your boundaries in terms of
cultural_challenges: Swiss people tend to be quite difficult to get to know (maybe even more than Scandinavians)
culture_appreciated: Openness when you try to practice your speaken German.
top3_advice: Attend a German course in the beginning of the term, you will meet so many new people. Super good start.
other_useful_info: If you attend courses in German, be aware that it is not Swiss German.
most_rewarding: Spending time with the other students
greatest_challenge: Everything was quite smooth.

crucial_aspects: The language was definitely a crucial part of my choice, as well as the fantastic nature and culture.
info_ease: It was quite easy, there were many info events.
arrival_assistance: The University held information events and other exchange students were also of great help.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was quite easy since the platform was similar to the one use by KU. It uses the same setup with a checklist of different things you need to do and when you need to do them by.
registration_help: UZH was very quick to respond to any questions I had through their contact form.
registration_success: This was a very pleasant experience as UZH informed the students about when and how to do what.
registration_advice: Stay informed, especially look out for the registration dates for classes with a maximum number of students. These are often popular.
course_level: I took master courses as they were in English. This was not a problem as a BA student.
teaching_comparison: The materials for the courses were different from what I was used to in Copenhagen. At UZH they use many different ways of communication of knowledge such as videos, podcasts, seminars and so on instead of books sometimes.
courses_enrolled: - Contract Design I - Workshop & Lecture Series on the Law & Economics of Innovation - German intensive language course certificate (C1) - European Tax Law - International Sales Law (CISG) - The Art and Science of Negotiations
recommended_courses: - Contract Design I - International Sales Law (CISG) - The Art and Science of Negotiations
unexpected_costs: Meat is very expensive in Switzerland, we are talking 150 Dkk per kg chicken breast. You should budget for traveling on the weekends, this is easily between 200-1000 per weekend depending on where you go.
cost_comparison: Meat definitely more expensive. Cell service was not very expensive. Look up Swype, they cost 15-20 chf per month and with the coupon "helloneptun" I got 60 chf for free.
activities_available: A VERY wide range of sports and activities using the ASVZ app. They were almost all free.
activities_recommended: Definitely hiking and skiing. It might be expensive, but since you are already there on an exchange it is the cheapest it will every be in Switzerland.
weekend_recommendations: Matterhorn (Zermatt) Lausanne Luzern Geneva Flumserbeg Arosa Davos
culture_adjustment: Since it is very similar to danish culture I would not worry about it as a problem.
socializing_tips: You have to really be make sure to try and speak to the local students and suggest doing stuff together. Many exchange students will tend to hang around other exchange students as this is very easy.
cultural_challenges: Not really, it is quite similar.
culture_appreciated: The politeness and the importance of being on time.
top3_advice: The written exams are hand written, no computers allowed at all. When that is said it is very different and not something UCPH students are used to, but it is possible and should not discourage anyone from picking UZH.
other_useful_info: Take the Polybahn sometime, it is an experience in it of itself. Also the "Mensa" cafeterias are very reasonable priced with very nice food.
most_rewarding: The friendships I have made along the way as well as the nature I have had the privilege of experiencing.
greatest_challenge: Definitely the fact that the written exams were hand written, however it is very possible and should not discourage anyone from choosing UZH.
other_comments: Go to Switzerland, you will not regret it!

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne til et tysksproget universitet. Jeg valgte Zürich, fordi jeg havde et indtryk af, at de havde flere relevante kurser for mig og mine faglige interesser end Hamborg eller Berlin. I retrospekt tror jeg blot at Zürichs kursuskatalog var nemmere at navigere i. Derudover lød Zürich mere 'eksotisk' end Hamborg og Berlin.
info_ease: Da jeg først kom til Zürich, synes jeg at det var rimelig nemt at finde den information jeg havde brug for. Det var også nemt at få kontakt til udvekslingskontoret, når jeg havde brug for deres hjælp.
arrival_assistance: Der var et infoarrangement i starten af opholdet. Derudover fik jeg tildelt en fagkoordinator, som var behjælpelig i spørgsmål om fagvalg, learning agreement og hverdagen på universitetet. Jeg havde et møde med ham kort efter min ankomst, hvilket var godt til at få styr på det praktiske.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Kursustilmeldingen foregik online og fungerede fint. Der skelnedes mellem pladsbegrænsede og ikke-pladsbegrænsede kurser, hvor de pladsbegrænsede kurser havde deadline for til- og afmelding inden studiestart. Dette gav mig problemer, da jeg efter semesterstart ville udskifte to kurser, der viste sig ikke at passe til min uddannelse. Men derudover virkede tilmeldingen helt fint.
registration_help: Jeg talte med min fagkoordinator om kursusvalg og fik hjælp af udvekslingskontoret ifm. de kurser jeg ville udskifte efter til- og afmeldingsfristen var overskredet. Derudover var der ikke brug for den store hjælp.
registration_success: Jeg fik de kurser jeg gerne ville have. Dog måtte jeg overbooke mig, da jeg ikke kunne afmeldes to kurser, som jeg fortrød. Jeg endte altså med stadig at være tilmeldt de to kurser og blot udeblive fra undervisning og eksamen i de to fag. Dvs. jeg tog på papiret 39 ECTS, men dumpede med overlæg 9 af dem.
registration_advice: Søg de kurser du gerne vil have, og hvis du får brug for at lave ændringer senere, så skal der nok findes en løsning. Den største udfordring er, at det tager lang tid og er besværligt at få forhåndsgodkendt alting, men det har som sådan ikke noget med Zürich at gøre.
course_level: Niveauet var lidt svingende fra kursus til kursus. Der var fin mulighed for at dykke mere i dybden i alle kurser, men jeg synes generelt ikke at niveauet blandt de studerende var højt. Forventningerne til de studerende virkede heller ikke til at være særlig højt. Kurserne var spændende, og jeg har bestemt lært en hel del af dem.
teaching_comparison: Mange kurser bestod af seminarer, hvor der kun blev givet meget lidt oplæg fra underviserens side. Dette blev nogle gange lidt for løst og gjorde at diskussionen tit ikke kom op på nogete særlig højt niveau. I nogle seminarer var der dog studenteroplæg til hver undervisningsgang, hvilket fungerede godt. Derudover havde jeg et forelæsningsfag, som blot var forelæsning uden tilhørende undervisning eller seminar.
courses_enrolled: Jeg havde følgende kurser: – Kulturanalyse Jetzt! – Kulturtheoretische Grundlagen – Identität, Differenz und Wiederholung in Theorie und Literatur – Judith Butler: Die Macht der Gewaltlosigkeit – Ökologische Literaturwissenschaft
recommended_courses: Jeg var særligt glad for faget Judith Butler: Die Macht der Gewaltlosigkeit. Det var et godt, fokuseret fordybelseskursus i et enkelt teoretisk værk. Det var særligt godt, at vi brugte de første undervisningsgange på at få en ordentlig indføring i Butlers begrebsapparat, hvilket hjalp til læsningen af Die Macht der Gewaltlosigkeit.
unexpected_costs: Det kostede cirka 70 CHF at blive registreret på borgerkontoret. Derudover endte jeg med at bruge penge på viskestykker og små håndklæder, og en wifirouter.
cost_comparison: Lange togture er meget dyre, hvis man er over 25 år. Man kan dog spare en del, hvis man køber et halvtakstkort i begyndelsen af opholdet.
activities_available: Det var gratis at være med i universitetets sportsforening, ASVZ, hvilket var superfedt. Der kunne man deltage i mange forskellige sportsgrene.
activities_recommended: ESN students club arrangerede nogle ret billige skiture, som jeg godt kan anbefale.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på ski- eller vandretur i bjergene. Sejl på Zürichsee – det kræver kun en almindelig busbillet. OG stor anbefaling: bad i floden ved Untere Letten. Det er et badeanlæg, hvor man kan flyde med strømmen og det er super sjovt.
culture_adjustment: Jeg synes kulturen var ligesom i DK, så det var ikke det store problem. Den største udfordring var den sproglige barriere.
socializing_tips: Gør det! De fleste jeg mødte var rigtig søde og det var fedt at få insidertips. Jeg ved ikke om jeg har så mange tips desværre. Jeg var heldig, at der var nogle lokale studerende på mit kursus, der rakte ud til mig, og som jeg blev gode venner med uden at gøre den store indsats.
cultural_challenges: Jeg synes ikke der var nogen specielt udfordrende kulturforskelle. Det er kotyme, at man banker i bordet efter hver forelæsning/undervisning, hvilket jeg stadig finder undeerligt.
culture_appreciated: Det var rart at det var så nemt at omstille sig til, og jeg synes generelt folk var meget søde og imødekommende.
top3_advice: Der var ikke mange engelsksprogede kurser inden for uddannelse og jeg vil råde andre til at sørge for at man 1) enten på forhånd sikrer sig at der er engelsksprogede kurser nok inden for ens studiefelt eller 2) er i stand til at tage kurser på tysk.
other_useful_info: Jeg kan kun anbefale UZH, jeg har været rigtig glad for det.
most_rewarding: Det bedste har helt bestemt været at lære lokale studerende at kende og få tips og anbefalinger af dem til fede steder i byen. Derudover har det været fedt at forbedre mit tyske.
greatest_challenge: At al undervisning var på tysk. Det var lidt en udfordring i starten – især at skulle holde mundtligt oplæg –, men det blev bedre hen ad vejen.

crucial_aspects: Reflecting on my recent exchange experience in Zürich, several factors were instrumental in my decision to choose this destination for my studies. Foremost among these was the exceptional academic reputation of both the University of Zürich and ETH Zürich. These institutions are renowned for their rigorous academic standards and pioneering research, which aligned perfectly with my educational aspirations. Additionally, Switzerland's breathtaking landscapes offered endless opportunities for hiking and outdoor adventures, providing a much-needed balance to my academic pursuits. Moreover, I found Switzerland's culture to be surprisingly reminiscent of Denmark's, which brought a comforting sense of familiarity to my experience abroad. This cultural similarity made the transition smoother and enriched my stay, making it an invaluable part of my academic and personal growth.
overall_comments: The courses I followed was very good and insightful, but in the exam period, some of the exams were too short compared to the questions asked in the exam. Which led to a very stressful exam period.

The students from Zürich are not commonly taking 30 credits each semester, but this was not told to us. Therefore we had a lot of studying compared to the local students.
