arrival_assistance: I received a presentation from a teacher and got emails containing information about the place and who to contact if needed.
arrival_comments: Everything was okay simpel and people were helpfull.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Amazing student city and talented teachers.
registration_process: It was complicated and i was in contact with many different people. I succeeded in the end.
registration_help: Email.
registration_success: I got all the courses i wanted in the end, but the way there was horrible and very long.
registration_advice: Call them and ask for an explanation in how their courses works (if they are different from your own home university).
academics_comments: Amazing student city and talented teachers.
course_level: I had 3 courses with 7, 10 and 15 ECTS.
teaching_comparison: It was very different and much more physical than i was used to. Many excursions and changes in teaching methods.
courses_enrolled: Marine biology 15 ECTS Natural science and religion 7 ECTS Faunistics vertebrates 10 ECTS
recommended_courses: Marine biology 15 ECTS and Faunistics vertebrates 10 ECTS. For someone interested in the zoology part of biology, these courses were absolutely brilliant and with talented teachers. The teaching methods were mixed and there was a lot of excursions and practicals.
unexpected_costs: Buying a bike and a couple of things for the housing. Very expensive alcohol.
cost_comparison: Vegetables are incredible expensive, together with alcohol.
activities_available: A lot of student nations with a vast variation of activities.
activities_recommended: Working in a student nation (for the social connections). Going on hikes in the nature (there are cabins all around that people can sleep in for free). Try to learn the language.
weekend_recommendations: Hiking, working in student nations, visit cities nearby and take advantage of the many activities in student nations.
culture_adjustment: Very easy.
socializing_tips: Socializing with sweds is not as easy as internationals. They are very private, but working at student nations is a good way to socialize.
cultural_challenges: Sweds are very private and afraid of conflicst - and can be very rude to Danish people.
culture_appreciated: Politeness and the acceptance of different sexualities.
top3_advice: Don't be afraid to ask someone if you can join an activity. Ask people out on fika as much as possible and take advantage of the activities in the student nations.
other_useful_info: Do not take to many courses if possible and especially be sure to look at the percentage of the course that you have chosen. Figuring out the courses can be tricky, but it is good to take some interesting courses, but on 50% or 33%. The social activites every week can be very hard to balance with courses that are on 100%.
most_rewarding: Making friends for life, learning about independence and evolving my skills within zoology.
greatest_challenge: Learning to listen to when I needed a break from the social activities and to balance studying with the social student life.
other_comments: Uppsala is a perfect and amazing city to be a student in.

crucial_aspects: As I live in Copenhagen, I had a wish to study in a smaller city and thus be closer to the nature that I am studying and reading about every day. Furthermore, Uppsala has a long history of botanic which is what I am interested in.
info_ease: It was easy to get information, and I had all information that I needed when I left for Sweden.
arrival_assistance: I didn't receive any assistance, because I didn't arrive on the official welcome day.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was easy and they were very helpful. I got all information at the service desk in one of the university buildings.
registration_help: They helped me both changing subjects but also just the first sign up when arriving. The first time was online due to covid, so I needed a Studium account to attend the classes, which was easy to figure out.
registration_success: I was registered for the classes I wished automatically by the university.
registration_advice: It is easy to figure out, and most is done automatically when you wish for classes when applying to the university. It is, however, important to remember to sign up for the exams in time.
course_level: The level was the same as at my home university. However, it was challenging in other ways that I am used to. The exams were easier, I would say, but the courses were challenging in other ways and it was necessary to attend and be well prepared.
teaching_comparison: There were much more classes, and a lot more components to each course. This I really liked. Instead of the exam being the most important, there were many different parts to attend in order to pass the course. Also there were literature and ethics seminars which were very enlightening, and something that is not usually a part of the course at my home university.
courses_enrolled: Plant Structure and Function (15 ECTS) Evolution of Life in the History of Earth (7.5 ECTS) Marine Biology (15 ECTS)
recommended_courses: Marine biology had a 3 weeks field course on the West coast which was amazing. Here you really get experience and get to see what you are otherwise learning about. Also, Evolution of Life in the History of Earth, which is an evening course was very interesting. I would definitely recommend it!
unexpected_costs: Not really any.
cost_comparison: The prices were very similar to the danish prices in general.
activities_available: Many different things, it is just to find the right student nation and then you can find people who share your interests or learn something new.
activities_recommended: I joined the sewing club and the painting club at my student nation. In general I would just recommend you to join a student nation.
weekend_recommendations: Go on a hike in the area, go see the botanical garden or the tropical green house. Also the museum at Evolutions Biologisk Centrum (EBC) is nice and free if you are a student.
culture_adjustment: It was easy, especially as Denmark and Sweden are quite similar.
socializing_tips: Join the student nations and some activities in the welcome weeks where there is a lot planned. Don't be afraid to attend activities alone as everyone are joining to meet new people and find friends.
cultural_challenges: Not any in particular.
culture_appreciated: Very sweet and caring people and society in general.
top3_advice: Use the nature around you! It is amazing (I even saw northern lights in Uppsala). Join a student nation! Try the different reading halls in both libraries and university buildings. They are beautiful and very different.
other_useful_info: Importance of signing up for the exam in the right time. As this is your own responsibility, you are not able to attend the exam if you forget.
most_rewarding: I enjoyed meeting a lot of sweet people, and having great talks and discussions about our cultural differences. The nature around Uppsala was beautiful and I really enjoyed hiking and spending time outside.
greatest_challenge: Attending social activities alone was very challenging in the beginning, however it was also a very empowering feeling when it was a good experience.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to find a good university with classes that was not offered at my home university. Furthermore, I looked for a university town where there were good opportunities to meet new people and with good study facilities.
info_ease: Very easy. Everything was communicated well - absolutely nothing wrong with Erasmus and communication from them!
arrival_assistance: There was a welcome centre where I got all the assistance I needed. I chose to live in Stockholm and organise that myself which went well.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You applied through a link they sent via e-mail, and then you just chose the courses you would like. Luckily, I got the courses that I wanted.
registration_help: They sent reminders via e-mail, the website was very easy and helpful. If I had any issues, I just sent an e-mail to the Mobility-office, and would receive a reply very quick.
registration_success: I got the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Look into classes that are not offered at your home university. I thought it was a nice opportunity to learn something which would normally not be accessible to me.
course_level: I had one BA-level course, which turned out to be the most difficult course. It was very interesting and I learned a lot, however, there was a much too large work load packed into this course (which was only a 7.5 ects point course) - this course was called 'Investigating the Structure of English then and now'. I had three other courses that were a part of the 'English Linguistics' Master's programme. I thought the work load and level of these were appropriate.
teaching_comparison: I would say it was a bit more disorganised than that of UCPH. Some teachers were really great and had planned their course great, however, the others were either ambiguous or had been teaching for way too many years to care about their course. I think Engerom at UCPH is much better at creating a fun environment with new and exciting teaching methods.
courses_enrolled: 5EN445: From Project to Paper: Writing about Linguistic Research. 5EN490: Language in Society: Theory, Analysis and Interpretation. 5EN491: Introduction to Corpus Linguistics. 5EN165: Investigating the Structure of English then and now: From 'elne mycle' to 'with great zeal'.
recommended_courses: 'Language in Society' and 'Introduction to Corpus Linguistics' were great course with great teachers. Especially the Corpus Linguistics course was very interesting and I have learned a lot about that methodology which I will be using for my thesis.
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: Everything was as I expected.
activities_available: There are the so-called 'Nations' which are sororities/fraternities (although not divided by gender) with a lot of activities for students. Their bars and clubs were fun to visit.
activities_recommended: Definitely join a nation. I was not there as much, but if I had lived in Uppsala (not Stockholm), I would have used the nations a lot more. They seem like good places to meet friends and party. They also have study cafés with student pricing.
weekend_recommendations: Stockholm is a must. I've heard it's nice up north as well. A lot of students went camping, which looked great.
culture_adjustment: Very easy since Denmark and Sweden are so alike.
socializing_tips: I would say, join a nation and participate in all the activities. I met friends on the intro day. Also, the Goin' app is really great to find others with similar interests as you.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The local, Uppsala culture is very student-oriented (since it is a student town). The nations were cool to experience.
top3_advice: 1. Live in Uppsala if you want to make friends, 2. Join a nation, 3. Look into the difficulty of the course before you go according to how much time you want to spent on classes and exams.
other_useful_info: I was a bit disappointment that the department I had classes in was so small. If you want to meet a lot of people, maybe look into how big the departments are.
most_rewarding: Interesting courses that I would not have had in Copenhagen.
greatest_challenge: Definitely that I lived in Stockholm and was so far away from the other exchange students. Generally, I did not make that many friends because I was not able to go out every weekend in Uppsala. Furthermore, the classes I were in were really small.
other_comments: No

crucial_aspects: Peace and conflict courses not available in UCPH (I'm a pacifist). This is my 2. exchange so I got my 4. priority. Academic and teaching quality at least on par with UCPH/not significantly lower (I looked at all the rankings and student reports I could find while staying inside Erasmus grant eligible destinations).
overall_comments: Very good academically, but quite boring housing/city especially during winter time so if possible come here during the Spring semester as I did (don't be discouraged by my experience).
info_ease: Quite OK, but always a lot of things to get to know.
arrival_assistance: Everything was communicated by e-mail.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Very good academically, but quite boring housing/city especially during winter time so if possible come here during the Spring semester as I did (don't be discouraged by my experience).
registration_process: Online
registration_help: I don't remember
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted and that seemed to be the case for everyone. There were more spots than students in all my courses so no full classes.
registration_advice: You'll get what you pick so no stress about that but on the downside they really don't offer a lot of courses for statskundskabs student from UCPH unlike Sciences Po Paris (my previous Erasmus exchange).
academics_comments: Very good academically, but quite boring housing/city especially during winter time so if possible come here during the Spring semester as I did (don't be discouraged by my experience).
course_level: Approximately around the same level as UCPH (that is quite good) and also similar in the focus on the theories but not as good as Sciences Po Paris that was a lot more practical (I prefer more practical so I'm biased).
teaching_comparison: A lot more reading whole books, doing written book review assignments and seminar discussions of those read books so you can't just skip the readings the same way as you can at UCPH. A lot smaller classes than UCPH (2 classes of between 15-20) and 1 larger class with around 25-30 students. Seminars being even smaller with 8-15 students (half the class). A lot more resources per student compared to UCPH and the teachers always give quite thorough feedback during all your hand-ins and even after you get your final grade compared to UCPH where you just get a grade. Be aware that some courses only have very limited classes/lectures and require mostly readings or independent research. Also the exams are usually spread out where the book reviews, seminars, participation all count towards to final grade. Also the courses are one after the other with no overlapping courses (this being quite unique and a reason I chose Uppsala to try it). There deadlines are also more flexible (you can ask the teacher for extensions) and the grading is also just 3 possibilities: failed, passed and passed with distinction. Also if you have special needs you can even ask for a difference style of examination such as oral exams which I did instead of the normal one for 2 of the courses.
courses_enrolled: Comparative Politics 15 ECTS, Negotiation and Mediation in Practice 7,5 ECTS, Causes of Peace 7,5 ECTS
recommended_courses: Negotiation and Mediation in Practice: if you like a very practical approach, a lot of teaching hours which I loved instead of just reading but also with a huge workload for only 7,5 ECTS. The workload was equal to or greater than Comparative Politics 15 ECTS. The teacher Isak was also a brilliant teacher. The other 2 courses were also OK, Causes of Peace was a personal choice since I'm a pacifist and Comparative Politics had some interesting perspectives of European History and Chinese politics so not a lot of overlap with DAK1+2 (I had DAK3 at Sciences Po Paris) or Comparative Politics at Sciences Po Paris.
unexpected_costs: Moving out fees of 1650 SEK...
cost_comparison: There was no cheap public transport for short distances so I just walked everywhere. I wished they had Swapfiets like in Paris but no. Some students bought a bike 2nd hand on Whatsapp groups. Supermarkets in the city center are more expensive so I walked to Lidl which was cheapest but also checked etilbudsavis for discount on eggs (there are eggs for 2 SEK/egg every other week at some supermarket). Fresh fruit and vegetables are way more expensive except bananas, onions, potatoes and oranges when on discount. All other food items are cheaper than Denmark especially chocolate, nuts, milk and fil (Swedish yoghurt, but much better than yoghurt!). In total I've probably spent 20 % less on groceries (around 1500 DKK per month when buying the cheapest food in Lidl and eggs for 2 SEK/egg) than in Copenhagen. Normal people would probably spend 2000-2500 DKK in Lidl if not always eating the cheapest and if buying from the nearest ICA city probably have to spend 3000-4000 DKK for the same goods as the 2000-2500 DKK in Lidl. Like in Paris the ICA city (nearest supermarket) is equivalent to Carrefour city and unlike in Denmark where a Lidl or Netto in the city center has the same prices as those in the countryside/suburbs, in Uppsala and Paris they are around 50 % more expensive than Lidl. So if I bought the same groceries as I did in Lidl in the local ICA city nearby for convenience I would have spent MORE than back home in Copenhagen. Systembolaget is more expensive than Danish alcohol. A lot of the Uppsala museums are free for Uppsala University students! I didn't eat out a lot but the prices were quite cheaper than in Copenhagen. Clothes, glasses, eye laser operations, dentists and fish oil are a lot cheaper than in Denmark so I e.g. bought a lot of clothes from H&M and Alewalds, but also check the numerous 2nd hand shops. Also remember to join Mecenat where you'll have access to all the discounts which are way more comprehensive and numerous compared to Copenhagen's student discounts. Especially join Lidl's student discount through Mecenat. Also join the different supermarket's memberships for free such as Lidl Plus, ICA and Hemköp for weekly member discounts. Buy your scent free 1L hand soap refill from Normal. You can use your Danish phone plan in Sweden even though it is for 5 months (I didn't encounter any issues from Telmore) (the price of 200 DKK is thus the price of my Danish phone plan from back home. Internet (no WiFi in the rooms, only ethernet cable port), water, heating, electricity, waste disposal are all included in the rent. Notice that not all books are provided for free by Uppsala University, but if you search on Google or ask some of the other students you'll probably be able to get the PDF from them or else borrow the book for free from the library if you plan ahead. But if you don't do that you'll most probably have to budget some hundred DKK for buying books for each course. Uppsala University has a free comprehensive health insurance that has you covered on top the EU health insurance card so you won't need to buy a separate health insurance even including stuff like emergency dental care. https://www.uu.se/en/study/exchange-studies/living-in-sweden/insurance
activities_available: Most were organized by the nations but there where also an international social club at the Department of Government. If you come during the Spring Semester "Valborg" is the greatest celebration and highly recommended. Join the Buddy program.
activities_recommended: Ask someone in your housing or join a nation or join a club at your department. One could also take free Swedish lessons offered by Uppsala University at 7,5 ECTS (that don't count as ECTS points at UCPH since UCPH doesn't acknowledge language courses as valid MA courses for statskundskab). Join the Buddy program. Join the hiking group on Whatsapp that does hiking once in a while. Watch Northern lights from your Northwards facing window or go to nearby Gamla Uppsala to watch it (remember to install an Aurora app for monitering+alterting you when there are high chances for Northern lights).
weekend_recommendations: Take the train up north to Lapland, Kiruna or Narvik in Norway (the final station) to e.g. see Northern lights. Or take a day trip skiing (quite cheap). Or take a day trip to Stockholm (cheap). Or take a day trip to Åland (quite cheap). Or visit some of the free museums/gardens/greenhouse/orangery. Also if you're a nationalistic Dane go to Uppsala Cathedral to see Margrete I's red silk dress that the Swedes stole from Roskilde Cathedral...
culture_adjustment: Quite easy. The Swedes were more quiet and introverted than the Danes. Less drinking. Also Swedes just walk across the road even if the light is red if there are no cars (but not as blunt as the French that totally disregard traffic lights).
socializing_tips: Talk to students from your courses and ask them about any events they know about.
cultural_challenges: Swedes eat so much (ultra)processed food such as ready to eat frozen dishes e.g. meatballs. Less cycling and more cars. The Swedes apparently love old USA muscle cars that pollute and are noisy. The Swedish superior-ness about their way of life, democracy, human rights, that they know how to solve other countries problems. Also the shootings and violent crime in general even though I FELT a lot more safe than in Paris. Just don't be unlucky I guess since Sweden I think is the number 1 of shootings/killings per capita in Europe besides wartime Ukraine+Russia. One day when I was in the city 3 people where killed in a hairdresser which I walked by every week on my way to and from Lidl... This shooting even appeared in Danish news: https://nyheder.tv2.dk/live/udland/2025-04-29-tre-draebt-i-skyderi-i-svensk-by https://www.dr.dk/nyheder/udland/tre-personer-draebt-efter-brutal-voldshandling-i-stor-svensk
culture_appreciated: Swedes are very open to foreign cultures and they feel a bit more open to the world than Danes. In general just nice people.
top3_advice: 1. UCPH only has 1 exchange spot at Uppsala University so you're going alone as I did which can be quite lonely if you're depressed and don't have energy for socializing. If possible choose a housing that doesn't have private kitchens but shared ones even though they aren't in the city center since you'll always have people to talk to then when you are at home. 2. Don't stress over housing or courses, you'll get them. 3. Don't come here to drink alcohol but to appreciate the low population density and lots of nature. 4. Appreciate a quite different way of teaching.
other_useful_info: You don't need cash. I recommend using Revolut for 7500 DKK free exchange to SEK each month. Remember to buy your train tickets to and from Uppsala as early as possible for the cheapest price (become a SJ member helps since they regularly send you newsletters with time limited discounts such as extra points or 20 % off all journeys in a time period so remember to become a member some months in advance) but also remember that you only can get student discounts on the way back since you don't have a Mecenat card yet on the way up. Uppsala isn't a place to wear fancy or business clothes and has a more outdoor-ish vibe in stark contrast to Paris. Remember to bring your warmest outdoor clothes for the long winter period, where Spring arrives at least a month later than in Copenhagen and you can still experience nights with negative temperatures in April/May. Check Weatherspark: https://weatherspark.com/compare/y/74001~82852/Comparison-of-the-Average-Weather-in-Copenhagen-and-Uppsala
most_rewarding: Learning to cook and feed myself, to go on a hermit-ish slow retreat for mental cleansing and detoxing myself from all the dopamine addicting activities and in general high speed in Copenhagen where there is always something to do (FOMO). Quite comparable as to going to your summer house in Denmark for ½ a year. Appreciating the grandness of nature and the earth with the Northern lights every once in a while and feeling tiny compared to Copenhagen where there are people everywhere. My favorite activity of watching from my 5th floor (highest floor), Northward facing window with no other tall buildings blocking the view, watching the street life, the suns movement across the sky, Northern lights, birds, and when reaching summer the sky that nearly doesn't darken because Uppsala is so close to the polar circle. Appreciating that humans can survive in such cold, dark and much more hostile environment compared to Copenhagen and even built Universities and live their whole lives here which requires quite some resilience with winter temperatures going below -10 degrees celsius with wind chill on top.
greatest_challenge: Loneliness and I missed human touch (but I was also quite depressed so I didn't have the energy to go out and socialize and having private kitchens at Klostergatan also removed the social aspect of shared kitchens, therefore if possible don't choose Klostergatan but one of the housings with shared kitchens e.g. on the same floor). Craving fresh fruits and vegetables.
other_comments: Good luck, I'm sure you'll have a better experience than me. In total I personally preferred Sciences Po Paris over Uppsala, but they are very, very different exchanges, one could say polar opposites.

crucial_aspects: It wasn't too far from home and that the city was a bit smaller.
info_ease: Very easy, there is a lot of information to find on the university website and also intro meetings.
arrival_assistance: During the arrivall days, it was possible to get the shuttle bus from the airport to the university building, I know a lot of people that did that, and also there was people to ask questions to etc.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was very easy, a lot of information was available on their website as well. I received emails about what I had to do in good time. Didn't have any issues I can recall.
registration_help: The website has a lot of information, and I know that the International office has some drop-in session every week on zoom I think, but you can also just write an email, they respond very quickly.
registration_success: I got the courses I applied for, so very successful. Their course catalogue has a lot of information.
registration_advice: If you are in unsure about something or have a question, just send them an email, the mobility office is very helpful.
course_level: The overall level was fine, but I did find some of the courses a bit too easy compared to home. But then I also had some courses on another faculty than I'm usually on, which then on the other hand was quite challenging for me. So overall it was fine.
teaching_comparison: They differed between seminars and lectures, and on my faculty at home we do not have seminars, so this was another kind of teaching than I am used to, which I learned a lot from. Also, I had my courses one at a time, or two at once on half time, which is another way they do the semester in Sweden, and that was very interesting to try.
courses_enrolled: Introduction to Development studies 7,5 ects Development and Political Institutions 7,5 ects War and Peace one Film 7,5 ects Environmental Ethnography 7,5 ects
recommended_courses: The course on Development and Political Institutions was very interesting and I learned a lot, but I think the Introduction course to Development studies was a bit boring. The course War and Peace on Film was nice to try, because it was very different and fun, it however was very easy also. The course Environmental Ethnography was very good, I learned new stuff as well, despite it being an introduction course.
unexpected_costs: If my deposit for my accommodation is not covering the final cleaning, that would become an unexpected cost.
cost_comparison: Alcohol is very expensive in Sweden, especially from Systembolaget.
activities_available: The nations in Uppsala hold a lot of activities and events and cultural Swedish parties that is called gasques, where you dress up really nice and is a lot of fun and social experience.
activities_recommended: Becoming a part of a nation is a must in Uppsala, really nice to go with your friends or meet new people.
weekend_recommendations: Would recommend to visit Stockholm. I also went to Kiruna in northern Sweden, which is very beautiful.
culture_adjustment: Very easy, it is easy to meet new people and other exchange students, especially if you live with them.
socializing_tips: Choose student accommodation through Uppsala University with roommates! The best way to meet new people. Also, go to the nations, they do a lot of events.
cultural_challenges: Being in a new city where you don't know anyone was a challenging the first days, but then I met so many people, so I didn't miss home so much.
culture_appreciated: The nations are very unique and special. Also, the parties/gasques were so much fun and is something completely different than I have tried before.
top3_advice: In Uppsala the nations make the student life so special and fun, and it is very easy to meet new people and socialize. In the arrival days you can get a temporary nations card so you can try it out. Get student accommodation with roommates (if you like to live with other people), my roommates ended up becoming some of my closest friends. Go to at least one gasque at one of the nations, it is a very cultural traditional experience and a good way to meet new people also.
other_useful_info: There is a lot of libraries in Uppsala and they are quite beautiful inside, so you should definitely check them out.
most_rewarding: Becoming friends with other exchange student from so many different countries and cultures.
greatest_challenge: Being away from home for so long, missing my friends and family.

crucial_aspects: It was very important to me that Uppsala was a very student friendly city especially the 'sorority' houses and the nice cafées was a big part of my experience.
overall_comments: I thought it was really hard to take courses that is not in my field of study. The exams were difficult because of the formalities - but it was good to try something very different.
info_ease: Uppsala campus is really big, but it did not feel so big at any time. There was a nice introduction and a tour upon arrival.
arrival_assistance: I wanted to get my student id, and the reception was very helpfull. Maybe they are used to mecenat app, so they thought it was very sweet that i wanted a campus card.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I thought it was really hard to take courses that is not in my field of study. The exams were difficult because of the formalities - but it was good to try something very different.
registration_process: It was fairly easy. Much like in Denmark
registration_help: Students and Erasmus
registration_success: I got some of the classes i wanted, but i would have liked to have attended some of the ethnology classes i applied for.
registration_advice: Pick the destination and the student environment first, and then the classes.
academics_comments: I thought it was really hard to take courses that is not in my field of study. The exams were difficult because of the formalities - but it was good to try something very different.
course_level: BA level 'Nordiska Språk'
teaching_comparison: All of my teachers were really nice, but more distanced from the class that i am used to. But to be fair, that might have reflected more on the students attendance. We did not really get to know the professors that much (except for Lisa Hansen, a danish professor that helped me a lot during my exams and frustrations)
courses_enrolled: Isländska, Språkstruktur, Svenskan i tid och rum, Dansk/Norsk (30ects)
recommended_courses: I would recommend Svenskan i tid och rum and Dansk/Norsk, if you are coming from a nordic country. The Isländska, Språkstruktur was too difficult to follow as a foreigner
unexpected_costs: No unexpected costs
cost_comparison: Books were cheaper, but if you buy second hand like i did, make sure to have cash if you dont have Swish
activities_available: Lots. The 'sorority houses' hosts a lot of events. I have been to several dance nights at V-dalarna on Eptu.
activities_recommended: Make sure to sign up for choir!
weekend_recommendations: Hang at the 'sorority' bars and drink coffee.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. I love Sweden.
socializing_tips: Swedes are in my opinion either very shy or very outgoing (mostly in groups), much like the danes. So just be yourself and try to ask some questions for example when working in groups.
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The language and the costs of everything :)
top3_advice: Bring warm clothes, get in a 'sorority' and spot the nice cafées (Uno, Queen beans)
other_useful_info: Try to speak swedish - they do not understand danish :-)
most_rewarding: There is a lot to choose from. But it really felt like the world was opening up to me - in a different way than if you are traveling or visiting.. living in another country by yourself gives you some chest hair
greatest_challenge: Exams. Without a doubt. They where different, and much more old fashioned than i am used to. Sitting four hours with nothing but a piece of paper and your water bottle is very different from writing at home/library/etc over several weeks.
other_comments: It was great.. but i failed two of my courses, and i had not failed anything before that.. so that was a tough thing to experience for the first time, and also feeling like you took someones money for granted..

crucial_aspects: Location as my family is from Sweden as well as the history of Uppsala University
info_ease: It was pretty easy and the mobility office was very helpful
arrival_assistance: Initial orientations and tips and tricks from fellow exchange students in my accomodation
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

registration_help: The mobility office was very helpful in this regard tho and writing them to get suggestions on courses worked very well as well as them being open to changes.
registration_success: Quite succesful. I got what I wanted and even got to change a course.
registration_advice: Write the mobility office with questions and be sure to take your time.

teaching_comparison: I felt again that the teaching style was not as in depth as I was used to.
courses_enrolled: Culture and War The craft of public speaking Forestillingsverdener War and Peace on Film
recommended_courses: Culture and War as the structure of reading a whole book a week was very interesting and gave me a lot. Also Sverker is very knowledgable and passionate in his field. Forestillingsverdener as Birgitta is a very good teacher as well and you really get a lot of information in the relatively short duration of the course.
unexpected_costs: The buying of a bike and an internet router for my room
cost_comparison: Food
activities_available: A gym with different sports offers, climbing gym. There was some different things, but a lot of them you kind of forgot about. And the nations of course.
activities_recommended: The Gasques, nations, sports
weekend_recommendations: Go travelling around the nordics. There's not a lot to do in Uppsala.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy as I'm danish, but swedish people are kind of closed off.
cultural_challenges: The swedish people being kind of closed off
culture_appreciated: The 'cleanliness' and structure.
top3_advice: Go in with an open heart and be ready to really emerge yourself in the experience (don't do it halfway). Do your homework/emerge yourself in the studies and social life around that - especially if you go by yourself.

greatest_challenge: The darkness and social life.

crucial_aspects: A strong student-body along with good courses available.
info_ease: Quite easy - The university is very informative upon arrival and very helpful in case of needing further assistance
arrival_assistance: There was multiple seminars where we were introduced to a number of people to contact in case we needed help or information, along with plenty resources on how to get settled abroad, what was required and recommended.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: After admittance through erasmus+, you are given an email on the UU portal. Through this you gain acces to most of the registration sites, although they themselves enlist you in your selected courses.
registration_help: Plenty - service desks, open hours, different emails for different problems. Easy to find, as long as you know what your problem is.
registration_success: It was done for me before I arrived by the host institution
registration_advice: Their portal for courses is quite confusing an often not up to date or plainly in dutch. There is a ton of options, but I would recommend setting up a phonecall or digital meeting with someone to guide you through what might be available to you.
course_level: I had one entry-level class that was a lot of reading, but otherwise quite simple. Three "informatica" courses with a very high expectation and complex curriculum. The courses are seldom "easy" and require more time than I initially expected.
teaching_comparison: Less mathematical, more practical, and a steep learning curve.
courses_enrolled: Cognition and emotion Image processing Concurrency and Parallelism Language and Compilers
recommended_courses: Concurrency and Parallelism Language and Compilers - These were the most instructive and constructive courses I had. They are very technical, so a student should have a interest in the complex workings of computers and machines.
unexpected_costs: Although it is recommended beforehand, getting a dutch bank account and transfering money around was quite the hassle, and cost a bit if done haphassardly. Kitchen utensils - had to buy everything. Pots and pans, cutlery, knives, plates, cups, cutting-board ect.
cost_comparison: Grocery shopping was quite costly unless you went out of your way to find a "jumbo" instead of a "albert heijn"
activities_available: There is a great sport center on campus named "olympos" that is affordable and offers all kinds of athletic and social activities. BuddyGoDutch was available for a great many social experiences and meeting exchange students and dutchies alike.
activities_recommended: BuddyGoDutch
weekend_recommendations: All the different cities of the netherlands. Den Haag, Rotterdam, Amsterdam, Leiden. Even belgium with Ghent, Brussels, Antwerp ect. There are beautiful forests, long lovely beaches and every city has its own feel and plenty to explore. There is a thing called "free walking tour" that is available in every city and I would strongly recommend it. No place in the netherlands is more than 1.5-2 hours by train from Utrecht.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. The dutch people are very much like danes. Theres a exciting vibe amongst the exchange students, but I think anyone going on exchange are in part also looking for / enjoying that vibe.
socializing_tips: Again - BuddyGoDutch, and meeting people in bars and parks
cultural_challenges: Young dutch people are very loud. And self-centered at first glance, it is therefore important that you don't judge them harsly on first impressions
culture_appreciated: The friendlyness and light-hearted conversation - even with complete strangers
top3_advice: Utilize buddy go dutch Travel on weekends Study from 9-17 in week-days, that should be plenty to follow the courses, and it leaves a lot of spare-time to enjoy socializing and day-travels
other_useful_info: The grading system is quite strange. Theres a narrow range from "passed" to "best in class" that is difficult to decipher. Talk to a dutch student about it, as to get a grasp on it - then it wont seem so scary. Get (if possible) student housing through UU/SSH, having roommates and an extended social circle is crucial
most_rewarding: The people I met and the places we travelled.
greatest_challenge: Keeping up with the level of the courses

crucial_aspects: The fact that Utrecht has a big hospital for companion animals, and that the veterinary school in Utrecht is very well recommended internationally.
overall_comments: The administration part of my exchange was not the best, for my first 4-6 weeks (out of 12 weeks) I was “rejected” every Monday morning when I showed up in the department/service my schedule said. They were not expecting any students, or did not have room for me, and I was therefore told to find another place to be by myself. I did not feel like the administration did much to help me to get to know any of the local students by always sending me to departments where I was the only student (without any local student). Besides that, I was only together with the same group of local students for one day, and the next they were all new, so I did not really get the chance to make a deeper connection with any local students through school. Although most of the students and vets/educators were very kind to me and did not have a problem of switching to English even though I was the only non-Dutch speaking person in the room.
info_ease: Very easy, I got a contact person who was very kind and answered all my questions. I got my full schedule for the three months of exchange prior to my arrival.
arrival_assistance: I was told to be at the hospital at a certain time and call my contact person within the hospital when I got there, but unfortunately, she was on vacation during my first week, so she was not there. The reception did not really know what to with me, but after some confusion a person came to pick me up and gave me a short tour around the hospital and showed me where I should be the first week (the department I was supposed to be in the first week did not expect to have any students that week, and especially not an exchange student, but they were very adaptable and kind to me even though they were not prepared for my arrival). The administration helped me a little to find new departments to be in for the first 4-6 weeks, when the department I was supposed to be in “rejected” me.

course_level: The level was more or less the same as it is in Copenhagen.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was much alike the style of teaching in Copenhagen, you are in small groups of students who do the anamnesis and the general clinical examination, and afterwards the students discuss their findings and the treatment plan with the responsible veterinarian.
courses_enrolled: I was only there for three months (not a full semester), and I had 12 weeks of clinical rotations at the companion animal hospital.
recommended_courses: I had a very kind and helpful vet in neurology, but most of the vets and departments are very kind and really experienced and at the top of their league within their field, so just go for whatever you like and are interested in.
unexpected_costs: You need to bring cash, most supermarkets (and other places) do not accept visa cards (at least not Danish visa cards).
cost_comparison: The prices are more or less as in Denmark.
activities_available: Sports, food, social, and creativity clubs, there were a lot of opportunities.
activities_recommended: I joined a sports club, they have a big sports facility called “Olympus sportscentrum” where you can join most sports.
weekend_recommendations: Go visit Amsterdam, watch a football match either Ajax or Utrecht's local football team, walk along the canals in Utrecht city and visit some of the parks around Utrecht.
culture_adjustment: Not a problem, the Dutch culture are much alike the danish culture.
socializing_tips: Be open minded and say “yes” to everything in the beginning, it might be exhausting, but it is worth it in the end. The Dutch people are (much like the danish people) a little closed/private, so in most cases you must be a bit extrovert and go look for friends yourself.
cultural_challenges: None really, besides the Dutch people being a little difficult to get to know, so you have to invest some time and energy.
culture_appreciated: That everyone speaks English.
top3_advice: Bring cash (most supermarkets do not accept card), bring a rain clothing (it rains A LOT), I would recommend to rent a bike (swapfiets) down there to get around, and if you need anything you can get it down there (there is a big shopping mall in the center of the city).
other_useful_info: I would highly recommend renting a bike (Swapfiets) down there to get around.
most_rewarding: Getting taught by some of the best vets in the world, they are very experienced and helpful.
greatest_challenge: The administration in the beginning, that I was “rejected” every Monday morning at the department I was supposed to be in for 4-6 weeks and having to find another department/service to be in by myself. It made me feel quite unwelcome and alone.

crucial_aspects: Good English skills in the Netherlands. Nice infrastructure to travel to other countries easily. A language I didn't know so I could feel like I was far away (even though I could take a flight back in less than 2 hours)
overall_comments: My student housing was really bad, but overall I really enjoyed both the Dutch and the friends I made. And the university, of course.
info_ease: Very easy. And people are very helpful and effective, so emails are responded to fast.
arrival_assistance: The university provided a Welcome program with all information needed. The orientation was both socially and educationally super good.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: My student housing was really bad, but overall I really enjoyed both the Dutch and the friends I made. And the university, of course.
registration_process: It was easy to contact the International Office and I was able to change courses the day before my arrival without further problems.

registration_success: Very much indeed, it was easy and also to change if necessary. I had to change because my number 1 priority unluckily got fully booked.

academics_comments: My student housing was really bad, but overall I really enjoyed both the Dutch and the friends I made. And the university, of course.
course_level: Very high. But more like in high school with emphasis on tutorials and mandatory presence. I did not really like that since I'm used to schedule my time on my own and be responsible myself for my learning.
teaching_comparison: Very different, as mentioned, as in high school with teachers pointing at us if no one speaks up.
courses_enrolled: Criminal Behavior during the Lifecourse Health in Society Science of Happiness Youth Culture in a Digital would
recommended_courses: Youth Culture and Criminal Behavior were very interesting.
unexpected_costs: Paying for bedsheets when I came.
cost_comparison: Everything is cheaper than in DK
activities_available: Everything basically
activities_recommended: I recommend the gym, making friends in the Orientation Week and of course if you live in a student housing - you will never be alone. Remember to breathe sometimes and go for a walk alone as well.
weekend_recommendations: Travel to Paris, Berlin, Luxemburg, etc.! The opportunities are so good and trains are super fast and accessible.
culture_adjustment: Very easy indeed, basically the Dutch are like Danes, though we are a bit more relaxed I would say. The Dutch are super productive
socializing_tips: Orientation Week was the bomb!
cultural_challenges: The local students are not really interested in internationals.
culture_appreciated: The canals, the big windows, the Christmas traditions!
top3_advice: Vær opmærksom på, at SSH udbyder rimelig hæslige værelser. Jeg boede som sagt i De Sterren og vores toiletter stoppede ofte så meget, at vi havde kloakvand til anklerne (seriøst). Jeg havde også skimmel på mit værelse og kunne høre ALT fra de andres værelser og fra stuen. Så hvis du elsker konstant stimuli og at bo med +10 mennesker, go for it! Jeg var selv bare virkelig blevet for gammel til dét og ville så gerne være alene bare nogle gange (er tidligere højskoleelev og har været på Roskilde seks gange, dette var klart hårdere) og have en "voksen", der kunne hjælpe med alt det, der virkede uoverskueligt, f.eks. skimmelsvampen. Jeg ville ønske jeg havde haft mere rene faciliteter, der var virkelig klamt ofte. Jo flere, du bor med, jo mindre gider de at rydde op efter sig selv. Men men men - jeg er selvfølgelig mega glad for, at jeg fik 10 virkelig gode venner, da det hele var overstået, så det var jo klart fordelen. Jeg ved fra andre, at det kan være ensomt kun at bo med 1-2 andre, fordi man ikke nødvendigvis kommer hjem til nogen hver dag. Og det er især vigtigt i starten, hvor alt er lidt overvældende. Jeg ville have boet i Johanna Building eller privat (dog røvdyrt), hvis jeg kunne lave det om.
other_useful_info: Vær opmærksom på, at det faglige niveau er højt, og det forventes, at du aktivt deltager flere gange i hver time. Så man kan altså ikke tage en slapper, selvom man (læs: jeg) ellers havde håbet på dét.
most_rewarding: Engelskkundskaber, fantastiske venner, fantastisk by. En masse rejseminder. At jeg gjorde det! Der var mange nedture, men på den anden side har jeg lært SÅ meget om mig selv og om, hvad jeg ønsker for fremtiden. Det har været alle tudeturene værd.
greatest_challenge: My student housing
other_comments: Enjoy it, relax, go for it. Remember to take care of yourself.

cost_comparison: Going out for coffee or food is cheaper than Denmark. Travelling with train is expensive unless you order a personalized student OV-chipkaart to get 40% off trainrides outside of peak hours.
activities_available: Loads of sports, ESN organises stuff, great places in the city of Utrecht
activities_recommended: Join the ultimate frisbee club UTKA! Even if you have no experience with ultimate, I would recommend UTKA. Go cannoying, have a walk in the forrest, check out all the great caffé's and bars around town, go to the flower market, eat waffles, enjoy the grey weather.

socializing_tips: Join the ultimate frisbee club UTKA!

culture_appreciated: People bike slowly

crucial_aspects: It was important for me that it was a destination where English was spoken on a high level so there was a good communication. Besides that, I wanted a destination that encountered a similar ethics standard as the one we have in Denmark.
info_ease: Not very easy. By the time I needed to find information upon my arrival Utrecht University site was under construction so there was minimal information to get. All my information upon arrival I received from my student counselor. You get very little information before the exchange begins, so you need to find or contact people yourself to get it.
arrival_assistance: The location and arrival time of the first day of my exchange I received by e-mail from my student counselor at Utrecht University. Before arrival, I also received my schedule for my entire exchange. On the first day, I was greeted by a woman who gave me a quick tour and showed/explained the hospital to me. Unfortunately, it was a very short tour (about 5-10min). The tour did not encounter any information about the routines of the hospital or my role as a student. All that I had to learn from the students over time. So it was very limited assistance I got on my first day.
arrival_comments: A folder over the normal workflow as a student and an overview of the system would have been a great help to receive on the first day.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was very confusing. I didn't get an overview of things. I just got e-mailed when I should upload documents to the mobility service. The host institution was also very hard to get in contact with during the registration process.
registration_help: I could always write to my student counselor at my host university if I had some questions. But the reply time was sometimes long.
registration_success: Very successful.
registration_advice: It can be a little chaotic. But just follow the instruction you get from your own institution and the host institution and it will be fine. And don't be afraid to contact people with questions.
course_level: The courses were of very high quality. The teaching is very evidence-based and you work with specialists in every department.
teaching_comparison: It is very similar. The student gets to receive the anamnesis and perform the exam on every patient. Thereby you discuss the patient with the specialist and together make a plan for further exams and/or therapeutic plans.
courses_enrolled: Companion animal hospital for 10 weeks.
recommended_courses: I can fully recommend the companion animal hospital. You get to perform a lot of hands-on examinations and diagnostics methods. Besides that, you also get to see a lot of different cases which you discuss very thoroughly with the specialist.
unexpected_costs: No one
cost_comparison: Housing is very expensive.
activities_available: There were a lot of activities planned by the student associations club (D.S.K).
activities_recommended: Definitely go to the student associations club. They know all the activities who is going on.
weekend_recommendations: Ask the Dutch students what to do on the weekend. The Netherlands has a lot of festivals and events on the weekend to experience. I myself went to some of the many events in Utrecht, explored the city of Utrecht, and visit other cities in the Netherlands on the weekends.
culture_adjustment: Very easily, Netherland and Denmarks have a lot of similarities.
socializing_tips: Just be very positive and outgoing on campus. Many of the Dutch students are very friendly and welcoming.
cultural_challenges: Nothing I can recall now.
culture_appreciated: I spend a lot of time with the local Dutch students who showed me their culture. So I most appreciate the Dutch people being so friendly and welcoming.
top3_advice: I know it is hard to find accommodation but keep on seeking it is definitely the time worth it. If you have any academic questions, just ask the students you work with. Just jump out into it. You need to seek some things yourself in the beginning, but 9/10 times it gives a very positive response/experience.
other_useful_info: There are not many exchange students at Utrecht University. I, therefore, recommend spending time with the Dutch students.
most_rewarding: To learn from all the specialists and all the nice experiences I had with the Dutch students.
greatest_challenge: To find accommodation

crucial_aspects: The reason for choosing Utrecht University was the high level of education you receive at UU. They had an interesting European and International programme in Law, and UU have received lots of appreciation from former students.
overall_comments: It is an amazing experience, and I would encourage everybody to take the opportunity to study abroad. It is a learning experience, and you really get to know yourself better and improve your english skills.
info_ease: It was quite easy. UU has a great office that can respond on every question within short time. They are very warm, and you receive many information about the University.
arrival_assistance: I had many questions regarding the grading system, which is quite different in the Netherlands.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: It is an amazing experience, and I would encourage everybody to take the opportunity to study abroad. It is a learning experience, and you really get to know yourself better and improve your english skills.
registration_process: The process is easy to follow. You get much help from your own institution and the host institution. You need to provide some information, but nothing to be worried about.
registration_help: You can easily get help through both your own institution and the host institution.
registration_success: I got all the courses I applied for.
registration_advice: Text them if you are in doubt. They are very helpful.
academics_comments: It is an amazing experience, and I would encourage everybody to take the opportunity to study abroad. It is a learning experience, and you really get to know yourself better and improve your english skills.
course_level: The level is high. But it is what you can expect from a course at MA level. You really have to keep up with the reading list, because there is a lot of reading and very little time to prepare.
teaching_comparison: I would describe UU as an institution whose style of teaching is more on the theoretical level, where UCPH is focusing more practice. You have a short period to prepare for the exam, which is quite different from UCPH. Your grade is also not just associated with the final exam, but here at UU you have 2-3 "exams", where you have to hand in a paper or make an oral presentation. These may between 10-50% of your final grade.
courses_enrolled: Judicial Protection and Enforcement of EU Law International Security Law Constitutional Law of the European Union International Humanitarian Law
recommended_courses: I would definitely recommend all courses, but especially the courses of International Security Law and International Humanitarian Law. These are the best courses I have ever had. Great teachers, exiting discussions, great way of structuring the seminars.
unexpected_costs: No unexpected costs.
cost_comparison: somewhat same prices in DK. Maybe a bit cheaper though.
activities_available: I participated in the UU Welcome Week. Many students also joins other things, but I chose to focus on Uni.
activities_recommended: ESN, Buddy-go Dutch, UU Welcome.
weekend_recommendations: There is not far to anywhere in the Netherlands. You have to visit Amsterdam, Den Haag and Maastricht. Wonderful cities.
culture_adjustment: Very easy. Dutch people are very good at english.
socializing_tips: Be open-minded. The dutch student on the international programmes speak english nearly all the time. They are very friendly!
cultural_challenges: Dutch people can be very direct. Be aware of that and don't take anything to personal :-)
culture_appreciated: Their open-mindedness.
top3_advice: Be prepared for the time you have to spent on studying. It is more extensive down here. Read everything on time. The lectures and seminars are important to pass the exams. And prepared for many various 'exams.' Spent time with the other international (or dutch) students. A social network is important in a new country.
other_useful_info: Get a Swapfiets. Very cheap and biking is by far the easiest way of transport in Utrecht. Get a tripkey card, which you can travel on within netherlands. Be aware that not all stores take VISA cards. Albert Heijn, the biggest supermarket, do not use VISA. Remember your raincoat. It is raining a lot ;-)
most_rewarding: The level of education. What an amazing experience. UU have some of the best teachers. I have really enjoyed my courses.
greatest_challenge: the greatest challenge has also been the most rewarding part. The level of education. You are expected to read a lot, and they keep you on your toes with assignments and oral presentations, so you don't just have a final exam.
other_comments: Utrecht University, the place you have to go study.

crucial_aspects: having a big exchange student culture as well as accessibility and relevance. My institute had allocated spots which made the chance of me getting in bigger. I also wanted to go somewhere where i already knew somethings about the country as well as knowing that i could easily communicate with other students.
info_ease: Pretty easy. Train strikes made it harder, but the university had warned me about this beforehand.
arrival_assistance: The university had arranged for students to me available in the airport to show new arrivals to the correct train, but due to train strikes they couldnt be there. This was communicated in advance and other options had been presented by the university.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: In the initial description of the University they link to their website where they have the courses available listed. Very easy to see what the possibilities are.
registration_help: They have a great and helpful international student center which you can email with questions and they will help you.
registration_success: Very. I experienced no cancellations. I wanted to change course once i got there but i was too late. I think it would have been easily possible if i were quicker.
registration_advice: Check the requirements for each course in the course catalog so you know what kind of pre-knowledge is expected and you wont be overwhelmed. If the course is not for you when you get there, be quick to email the international student office and inquire about a change.
course_level: 3rd year BA courses,
teaching_comparison: Somewhat different grading criteria and focus than what im used to. More closed-book and focus on remembering specific terms/formulas
courses_enrolled: Introduction to functional programming Data analytics Introduction to financial mathematics Introduction to machine learning
recommended_courses: I would recommend data analytics, as they are a pretty new course and doesnt rely on any other course at the university. I would recommend functional programming if you are a data science student or programmer and want to expand you codeing skills. Would not recommend if you just want to learn to code. I would not recommend Introduction to machine learning or Introduction to financial mathematics unless a math student and really interested in the mathematical formulas behind both concepts. They build upon theory that i dont think ive been exposed to before even though i thought i had the prerequisites necessary.
unexpected_costs: Because of the inflation, electricity was way more expensive.
cost_comparison: Transport were more expensive than i thought. I think there was some ways to save on that, but not too easy to figure out. Wine very cheap
activities_available: buddygodutch is an association that helps putting internationals in contact with duchies and host cheap social activities. Not always successful but a good way meet new people. Have an academic counterpart as well. They also have student associations connected to almost every course direction as well as dance clubs mm.
activities_recommended: Would recommend joining ESN and/or buddyGoDutch to meet other international students.
weekend_recommendations: Very easy to get around the netherlands, so could visit other cities such as amsterdam, ammersford or rotterdam. There are also lots of museums. If going in the summer/spring, canal tours are also available.
culture_adjustment: very easy, although the Dutch can be a bit hard to become close with
socializing_tips: Join a student association, but be aware that few international students show up
cultural_challenges: Dutch students seem to stick to themselves which makes it hard to get to know locals. And although they bike a lot, the attitude towards bicyclist is a bit different and the biketracks are often both ways
culture_appreciated: Beautiful cities with canals running through.
top3_advice: Be on the lookout for accommodations from the beginning and be sure to have somewhere to go when you arrive. Will recommend stayokay hostle in the middle of Utrecht center. Bike paths are often two-ways so be sure to look both ways before crossing. Also bikes will not stop for pedestrians. Find a bike. Bike rental is pretty easy and often other students will have a voucher.
other_useful_info: Not all places take foreign cards, and some of these places dont take cash either so make sure to check. You can get a maestro card (which they take everywhere they take cards) through revolut even if you dont want to open a dutch bank account
most_rewarding: Being on your own and learning new things about yourself and get the chance to immerse yourself in an other culture and city.
greatest_challenge: Finding people to meet with on a regular basis while also making sure to meeting new people and try new things. I think this will be easier if living in a student dorm. (also housing is very very difficult)

crucial_aspects: Appropriate courses available. The student climbing club.
overall_comments: I'm glad i went on exchange and experienced living in a new place. I feel I didn't manage to get the most out of the opportunity, though. Having chosen difficult courses, I didn't manage to invest much time into getting to know Dutch students. Even then, I would advise others to give it a go!
info_ease: Easy. Almost everything was automatically sent to me by email, or written on websites linked to in those emails. While it was easy, it did end up taking me a lot of time.
arrival_assistance: A bunch of useful emails. And there were some informational intro days.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: I'm glad i went on exchange and experienced living in a new place. I feel I didn't manage to get the most out of the opportunity, though. Having chosen difficult courses, I didn't manage to invest much time into getting to know Dutch students. Even then, I would advise others to give it a go!
registration_process: UU has a website where you can look up courses. The Dutch universities have united to offer shared master-level courses in Mathematics. Those courses use another website, elo.mastermath.nl. It was a combination of using those websites and using the Erasmus websites (linked to and explained in the automatic emails). I made a priority list of courses on the Erasmus website and someone from UU signed me up.
registration_help: Someone at UU replied to my emails, when I was in doubt of anything. You will be given a contact automatically.
registration_success: Successful.
registration_advice: Expect it to take some time to sort through the possible courses and fill out the documents.
academics_comments: I'm glad i went on exchange and experienced living in a new place. I feel I didn't manage to get the most out of the opportunity, though. Having chosen difficult courses, I didn't manage to invest much time into getting to know Dutch students. Even then, I would advise others to give it a go!
course_level: I took two BA courses and two MA courses.
teaching_comparison: It was very similar, actually. In the masters courses, the exercise sessions didn't have time for working on the problems.
courses_enrolled: BA: Analysis on Manifolds BA: Concurrency MA: Commutative Algebra MA: Algebraic Geometry 1
recommended_courses: Analysis on Manifolds was fun. Algebraic Geometry was quite fun. All the courses were fun. My lecturers were well qualified and gave good lectures. Maybe especially good lecturers in Algebraic Geometry 1 and Analysis on Manifolds.
unexpected_costs: I had to buy a bunch of kitchen equipment, as not all of the basic things were present.
cost_comparison: Their standard supermarkets are a bit more expensive than what I'm used to. If you are willing to travel outside the city center, you can find cheaper options like LIDL/ALDI.
activities_available: They have multiple student sports associations. Student associations are taken much more seriously down here compared to Denmark. They also have some kind of semi-academic student associations, which I never really figured out.
activities_recommended: I participated in the student climbing/alpine club, USAC. That was fantastic. They gave every member a group and a mentor, so we could easily get to know some people. Almost everyone was Dutch, but they were willing to speak English in my group. They also took us on an outdoor climbing trip, which was definitely one of the best experiences of my exchange.
weekend_recommendations: - Go on a bike trip to the northern outskirts of Utrecht. You will see the famous very flat fields, and how they drain them. Maybe some old windmills. - Utrecht has a beautiful old city center. Go for a walk along the canals. - Take a day-trip by train (or overnight by bike!) to Amsterdam. It's way more touristy, but also interesting. The van Gogh Museum was a memorable experience.
culture_adjustment: The culture is not that different from the Danish culture. Much like in Denmark, most people are not very outgoing, so it's mostly on you, to get to know people. That was difficult for me. There were some funny differences, which I felt no need to adjust to. Like people feeling embarrassed about wearing rain jackets/pants. And almost no dutchies wearing bicycle helmets.
socializing_tips: Try to find a sports club. That was where I had most success. On campus, they have no obvious shared place where math students like to go to. After lectures, people dissipate in every direction with each of their little friend groups. You might need to be really proactive, if you want to talk to your fellow students. If you like partying, then join Erasmus Student Network (ESN) which is very active in Utrecht.
cultural_challenges: Not sure if it's cultural, but I had a hard time with the lack of someplace specific, I could go, to find other math students.
culture_appreciated: Biking is in their blood. And they can be very direct.
top3_advice: Time will go by quickly. Choose interesting courses, but don't give yourself too much work to do. With all the practical things to figure out, you will probably feel like you have less time than back home, not more. It's important to give yourself time and a surplus of energy, to reach out to new people. And to go explore your host country. I truly enjoy my study, and like working on hard courses. But on an exchange stay like this, the social experiences are more important. They are what you are going to treasure most, when your stay is over. I've never heard anyone complain about choosing courses that were too easy, during their exchange. I've had multiple people advise me, to prioritize time towards social experiences. I wish I had listened even more! Go make the most of it. Do the things you can't do at home, with the people you won't meet at home. Enjoy your stay. Grab the it with both hands!
other_useful_info: Just really spend the time to make sure you will have housing.
most_rewarding: The climbing club. Trying to live in a different country.
greatest_challenge: Meeting new people.
other_comments: You should go :) Go make the most of it. Do the things you can't do at home, with the people you won't meet at home. Enjoy your stay. Grab it with both hands!

crucial_aspects: Within Europe, good academic standing and a nice city to live in as a student.
overall_comments: Much better than I had ever hoped.
info_ease: Pretty easy. There are student organisations such as the Erasmus Student Network and the school's International Office which offer assistance and help you get settled and start your semester without any stress.
arrival_assistance: I received assistance with my registration, transportation and finding student accommodation on campus.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Much better than I had ever hoped.
registration_process: UU has its own portal for exchange applications and it guides you through your application.
registration_help: You could call the school and ask questions but the portal itself was so easy to figure out, so you didn't need too much help.
registration_success: It was quite easy. I had to change classes a few times and the student office was so helpful. It was not any issue for me to change, as long as I did it in the first teaching week.
registration_advice: Make sure to do everything on time.
academics_comments: Much better than I had ever hoped.
course_level: I did level 3 courses, meaning they were meant for third year BA students.
teaching_comparison: UU was similar to UCPH as they also have a block structure, at least in science. The exams were slightly different but it was not too foreign.
courses_enrolled: "Nanomaterials", "Making modern science: a history of Chemistry", "Organometallic Chemistry" and "Persuasive Technologies"
recommended_courses: I enjoyed the "Making modern science: a history of Chemistry" course, as it was not my usual chemistry course. There was focus on the history of chemistry and not the theoretical, experimental and calculation aspects.
unexpected_costs: I had to pay for some medication when I was sick and my insurance here in Denmark did not cover it, which was a bit annoying.
cost_comparison: The Netherlands is cheaper than Denmark in a lot of aspects, so it was nice to spend slightly less money on things I needed.
activities_available: ESN, BuddyGoDutch, School-led initiatives such as the Wellness week, the sports arena which offered several sports activities for students at a decent price.
activities_recommended: There is an app called UniLife, which shows all the different events happening in the city for students and it's a great way to get out there and try things. Additionally, make sure to join the events held by the student organisations as they are a great way to meet people.
weekend_recommendations: See another city! NL is so small and their trains are convenient to get around. If you travel in groups, you get a discount as well. I also highly recommend to just explore and get to know the city you will be living in for the next few months.
culture_adjustment: It was pretty easy. I never really felt homesick but having nice roommates and forcing yourself to try new things really helped with this.
socializing_tips: Join events and if you live on campus, go for dancing and drinks at Cambrigdebar! I don't drink myself but their drink selection and pricing was student friendly and they had good sodas.
cultural_challenges: Not many because the Netherlands reminds me a lot of Denmark.
culture_appreciated: The nature, canals, flowers, etc.
top3_advice: 1. Housing 2. Join events 3. Explore the city
other_useful_info: The SSH is the housing portal for students coming to study in the Netherlands.
most_rewarding: Meeting new people, exploring a new city, learning to live on my own and trying new things.
greatest_challenge: Living away from home (in the start) as I had never lived away from my parents.

crucial_aspects: That the culture was not too different from Copenhagen and that I had good experiences with the Netherlands beforehand
overall_comments: There was a lot of administrative stuff with courses that was hard to decipher, both before and after the exchange which takes the rating down from 10-ish to 8.
info_ease: A bit difficult to navigate the different websites: welcome week, myuu, osiris, mastermath etc. and having a lot of different passwords and authenticators for each website.
arrival_assistance: There was a welcome week from Utrecht University and there was a welcome lunch for the Faculty of Science. But no assistance before the welcome week, which was placed quite late (from 28. August).
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: There was a lot of administrative stuff with courses that was hard to decipher, both before and after the exchange which takes the rating down from 10-ish to 8.
registration_process: You find courses on UU course website or Mastermath and then you send the international office an email with the courses that you want and they will let you know if you can get them or not.
registration_help: You can ask the international office.
registration_success: I couldn't take one of my wanted classes because of a prerequisite which was not listed, and I couldn't take another two because they were not for exchange students. But the rest was succesful and I was allowed to switch courses after trying one I didn't enjoy.
registration_advice: Start early and ask about if the courses are for exchange students
academics_comments: There was a lot of administrative stuff with courses that was hard to decipher, both before and after the exchange which takes the rating down from 10-ish to 8.
course_level: I took only Mastermath courses
teaching_comparison: Very similar, although there was a lot less classes, only 3 hours per course per week. And there was a lot more assignments compared to math at KU. Also, almost all exams are closed book which was difficult when used to KU standards where almost everything is open book
courses_enrolled: Systems and Control (Mastermath, UU) Forensic Probability and Statistics (Mastermath, VU) Asymptotic Statistics (Mastermath, VU) Statistical Mechanics (Mastermath, UU)
recommended_courses: I really enjoyed the Forensic and the Asymptotic Statistics courses. The first one was quite hands-on, looking at court cases and calculating probabilities, likelihood ratios etc., and the asymptotic statistics was quite theoretical but a good continuation of the course Stok2 from KU, where we considered types of convergence of random variables, estimators and consistency of estimators etc. The systems and control course was very applied mathematics (probably more engineering) and I didn't like that. When you have primarily taken theoretical maths courses, it was hard to have to calculate matrices, solve differential equations and think in a very different way than normal. Also most people taking that course were Applied Maths students. Statistical Mechanics I only took for about 2 weeks, when I had to do the first assignment I realized it was way too demanding and complex, so I dropped out of the course. The lectures I went to were interesting but prepare to do a LOT of work in this course!
unexpected_costs: Parties cost more than you expect and public transport is actually more expensive than Denmark
cost_comparison: As stated before. Groceries and eating/drinking out were a bit less expensive though
activities_available: Olympos sports association and a bunch of other clubs, but I only really know about that. Also there was indepedently the ESN association, BuddyGoDutch.
activities_recommended: I would definitely recommend being a part of ESN and joining their introduction week, I met quite a few friends there and it was fun! I have also heard good stuff about Olympos but I never did it
weekend_recommendations: Go and explore the nature around Utrecht, the other cities of the Netherlands or go to parties/gatherings and have fun :)
culture_adjustment: Quite easy, very similar to Denmark. However it was a bit hard to find things in the supermarkets sometimes because things are sometimes not called what you think they are in Dutch or are placed other places than you are used to
socializing_tips: I didnt meet a lot of Dutch students, but the ones I met was in BuddyGoDutch and in ESN, so probably do that if you wanna meet Dutchies :)

housing_how: I found housing on my own

unexpected_costs: I rent a bike, which I was really glad I did. cost 22 euros pr month
cost_comparison: Housing less expensive than I expected, but living cost is the same as in Denmark.
activities_available: There are so many opportunities for clubs, sports and activities. This also applies in Utrecht in general. A lot of students have different clubs and activities that are available.
activities_recommended: There is a big sport center at science campus called Olympos. Very good facilities with a lot of sports clubs to register for. This opens new opportunities to meet local people and other exchange students out of class.
weekend_recommendations: Explore the Netherlands and its beautiful cities. Furthermore, ESN plans a lot of different and nice trips to other cities. The Netherlands location makes it easy to travel around Europe yourself with friends.
culture_adjustment: It was very easy to adjust to the culture. It seems a lot like Denmark.
socializing_tips: Sign up as a member in different clubs and activities. Additionally, the Dutch people talk very easily to you.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: The Dutch people really want to talk to you and are welcoming but direct.
top3_advice: Find housing before coming, look at courses before going, but do not expect you will get them alle. Lastly, rent a bike, it makes it easy to go around.
