most_rewarding: The personal experience and growth, and improving my English a lot.
greatest_challenge: Finding new friends and be in another country just yourself. It was nice to speak a lot of English and improve the language.

crucial_aspects: A big motivation for me going on exchange was to meet a ton of people with different backgrounds and nationalities. The oppurtunity to put myself in a situation that would force me to seek out new friendships in a foreign setting, seemed like a fantastic way to grow as a person. Since it can be incredibly demanding to venture out on your own to study for a semester, my goal was to find a highly international country but with a culture that is not too different from my own.
overall_comments: My exchange stay was interesting and exciting but I unfortunately did not get all the courses that I had wished for and my housing was located too far from campus. This resulted in me having to spend a lot of time commuting and studying subjects that I found incredibly challenging.
info_ease: It was very straight forward. All the information that I need was sent by mail in due time. Whenever I had a question for either my home or host university, they would quickly reply to my mails.
arrival_assistance: My host university had arranged a Welcome Week with various informative events. It all began with a welcome show that was composed of a concert by students and an informational presentation by the International Office at Utrecht University.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_comments: My exchange stay was interesting and exciting but I unfortunately did not get all the courses that I had wished for and my housing was located too far from campus. This resulted in me having to spend a lot of time commuting and studying subjects that I found incredibly challenging.
registration_process: All I had to do was specify my first and second priorities for each block of the semester.
registration_help: The instructions for the registration were clear and when I after one lecture contacted the administration because I could tell I did not meet the prerequisites for a course, they were kind and immediately transferred me to another.
registration_success: I unfortunately did not end up getting my preffered courses but like I described in the prevoius question, they were very helpful and transfered me from one course to another after I requested it.
registration_advice: Make sure to double check the prerequisites. I officially met the prerequisites based on courses that I had completed, but I still did not possess the proficiency needed to participate in one of the courses. I identified this after the first lecture and luckily got transferred to another course that I really enjoyed. Another point to make is that some courses will have prerequisites that you do not officially comply with. If you are confident that you have the neccesary knowledge to participate in some of those courses anyway, it is well worth your time to describe the situation. I ended up not getting some of my first priorities because I did not meet the prerequisites based on courses completed. If I had explained that I had adeqate knowledge of the subject anyway, I might have ended up participating in the course.
academics_comments: My exchange stay was interesting and exciting but I unfortunately did not get all the courses that I had wished for and my housing was located too far from campus. This resulted in me having to spend a lot of time commuting and studying subjects that I found incredibly challenging.
course_level: I only participated in BA courses. The academic level was comparable to that of UCPH's courses.
teaching_comparison: It was the exact same style and structure of teaching. Each course was composed of lectures and exercise classes. During the exercise classes we would work individually or in groups on exercises related to the lecture that had happened beforehand.
courses_enrolled: - Image Processing - Data Analytics - Intro to Machine Learning - Functional Analysis
recommended_courses: I highly reccomend Data Analytics and Image Processing.
unexpected_costs: I ended up paying a lot of money for public transportation. This was a natural consequence of finding housing far from campus.
cost_comparison: All my expenses were similar to the ones I have in Denmark except for the price of public transportation.
activities_available: It is very common for dutch students to be members of student associations. There are both student associations based on study programme and student associations based on hobbies. I ended up signing up for a general student association that hosted a weekly event every Tuesday. This was a great way to ensure that I socialised with people outside of class.
activities_recommended: Sign up for a student association that focuses on a hobby or a more general one were the focus is being social and where the activities differ from week to week.
weekend_recommendations: The number one priority after getting settled in your hosuing situation should be to aquire a bike. A bike will enable your to get around Utrecht faster and much cheaper than any other method. Utrecht is a lovely city to spend your weekends hanging out in. The Netherlands has a lot of stunning and charming old cities and since the public transportation network is well structured and effective, you can easily visit a new wonderful city every week.
culture_adjustment: The culture in the Netherlands is very simlar to that of Denmark's.
socializing_tips: Most local students are already a part of "estabilshed" friend groups and thus it can be intimidating to approach them. Using group projects as opportunities to get to know people and potentially befriend them, I found to be a good idea.
cultural_challenges: I can't think of any cultural differences when it comes to behaviour but I generally found the cities to be more chaotic, more lively and less clean.
culture_appreciated: I loved the Dutch market culture. Twice a week I would bike to a market in Haarlem (the city I lived in) to buy a bite to eat or a bouquet of flowers to bring home to my appartment. The weekly markets where always buzling with people and they always gave me a wonderful sensation of being in some medieval marketplace.
top3_advice: 1) Make sure that find courses that you are passionate about and do what you can to guarantee that you get them. 2) Find housing as close to the campus or Utrecht city as possible. 3) Sign up for a student association.
other_useful_info: The housing crisis in the Netherlands is very severe. Make sure to start looking for housing early.
most_rewarding: The most rewarding part of my exchange stay was getting to meet curious and ambitious people from all around the world who had come to Utrecht to widen their horizons and meet new people.
greatest_challenge: My greatest challenge was living way too far away from Utrecht which made it incredibly hard for me to find the time and energy to participate in social activities happening in Utrecht.

crucial_aspects: I chose Utrecht due to its strong international reputation within veterinary medicine and its practical approach to teaching. The university is known for its high level of English and the close collaboration between students and teachers.
info_ease: I was a little difficult, I got all the information straight from my contact person. However, I received some information very late, and only when I asked for it from the student counselor.
arrival_assistance: On my first day, I was welcomed by a staff member who showed me around and helped me settle in. However, I did not receive any information about what is expected of the students, what we are allowed to do, or the routines of the hospital. I had to ask the other students about all of this, but they were all very helpful and understanding
arrival_comments: I was warmly welcomed by a staff member and met with the coordinator responsible for exchange students during the first week, who answered all my questions. However, I received the information about where to arrive on my first day rather late, which meant I had to send several emails to obtain the necessary details.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: It was a bit confusing. I received an email confirming my exchange spot and asking about my preferred subject, as well as instructions on uploading documents to the mobility service. However, there were issues getting the online Learning Agreement accepted because my start date didn’t match the regular semester dates. I had to contact them to find out what to do instead
registration_help: Both the Danish and the people from Utrecht were very good at answering any questions. However, the reply time was long.
registration_success: The university was very accommodating, and upon my request, I was allowed to switch one week to another specialty that I found more interesting
registration_advice: Just follow the instructions, and don't be afraid to ask for help.
course_level: It was a clinical rotation, with a high quality. You get to work with a lot of specialists.
teaching_comparison: It is very similar, but is still done a little differently
courses_enrolled: Companion animal hospital for 10 weeks, where I did: Diagnostic Imaging, Anesthesiology, soft tissue surgery, Cardiology, Emergency, Neurology, Internal ward, ophthalmology
recommended_courses: Anesthesiology, Soft tissue surgery, Emergency, Ophthalmology. It was the rotation I got to do the most and learned the most.
unexpected_costs: Housing is very expensive
cost_comparison: Housing is very expensive, otherwise close to the Danish prices
activities_available: I did not join any non-academic opportunities at the university, but I do know that the student association club plans a lot of activities.
activities_recommended: Go to the student associations club, they know what is going on, and can help you with recommendations
weekend_recommendations: Utrecht is a beautiful city with a lot of life, cafés, and activities to enjoy. I would also definitely recommend visiting Den Haag and Rotterdam, which are both really beautiful and easy to reach by train, making them perfect for a one-day trip. In most major cities in the Netherlands, you can join free walking tours, which is a great way to explore and get to know the city
culture_adjustment: Very easy, as it is quite similar to Danish culture
socializing_tips: They are very nice and helpful; you just have to be open and not afraid to be the one starting the conversation.
cultural_challenges: The language. The teachers and students are very good at English, though you need to remind them to speak English. It was a bit more challenging with the owners, but most of them were fine speaking English during the anamnesis
culture_appreciated: There is a very good work ethic, and people were generally very nice and helpful
top3_advice: 1. Don’t be afraid to ask for help. 2. Choose the rotations you find most interesting, but keep in mind that in those with more owner contact, you might miss some of it because it is in Dutch. 3. There are a lot of cool procedures and things we don’t see as much in Denmark, so don’t be afraid to say that you want to participate or ask if you can try.
other_useful_info: It can seem a bit intimidating in the beginning, and sometimes they might discuss things that we in Denmark haven’t been taught much. Other times, there are topics we have studied in more depth than they have. So don’t be afraid to say that you’re not sure about something and ask them to explain it to you
most_rewarding: Getting to see different ways of doing things and experiencing procedures I haven’t seen in Denmark, as well as learning from specialists and meeting the Dutch students
greatest_challenge: Getting information about where I should meet and how to arrange my credit transfer

Man skal huske, at man har ok meget tid når man er på udveksling fordi man ikke arbejder. Eksamenerne på UU er som oftest et essay på 700-1200 ord (NEMT), en fremlæggelse (NEMT) og ender som oftest i en multiple choice uden hjælpemidler på 2 timer - så man skal lære udenad (og derfor læse), hvor man på KU kan slippe afsted med at læse det pensum man skal bruge når man skrive eksamen (ish). Nogle fag var nemmere end andre - men man skal virkelig læse op. Sidenote, og ikke for at skræmme, men dumpede en eksamen og fik 5.0/10 - så skulle tilbage til re-eksamen. Så det er vigtigt at læse meget op...

For de fleste er der en uges fri mellem de to blokke omkring slut oktober/start november, hvor man fx kan rejse eller hygge sig. Forelæsningerne var meget som på KU, med alt fra 50-250 elever og 1 forelæser. Øvelsestimerne var dog meget gymnasie-agtige (med fravær), men samtidig også meget lavt niveau.

Lærte ikke så meget nyt her, men de bedte karakterer jeg har fået (for både essay og multiple choice) - Risk behavior and addiction in adolescence. Psyk-fag. Det fag jeg har fået mest ud af! Så spændende. Kan virkelig anbefale <33 Men, desværre med en ret høj dumpe-%. Men hvis man læser godt op er alt okay. I anden blok havde jeg: - Science of happiness. Fjollet, men nemt fag, hvor man skulle lave en happiness-intervention på sig selv. Dog det fag jeg dumpede... crucial_aspects: I have family living in the U.S. and I wanted to be closer to them. Additionally, Vermont Law and Graduate School (VLGS) had an interesting environmental profile that offered some academic opportunities.
overall_comments: Overall, I enjoyed my time in Vermont, as I got to experience living in a completely different environment than I am used to. Small town life is slow and sometimes I got bored, but it can be cute too, and it made me focus on my academics. I also got to experience other places in the US, like Boston (MA), Miami (FL), NYC (NY), and Portland (ME) - places I'd never been to. If I had planned better, I could've definitely planned more trips.
info_ease: Very easy thanks to the international admissions counselor at VLGS. She helped me with everything and even checked up on me on her own initiative. Since the school is small, the staff is always available to help out. If you're considering going on exchange at VLGS, I recommend contacting their admissions office, as they will be happy to help you with any questions, you might have.
arrival_assistance: I was picked up at Burlington Airport by a staff member and he drove me to my housing, which was very nice. When we arrived at my housing, he made sure that I had everything I needed, and even got me a shower curtain and some pots and pans. You can either fly to Burlington which is closer, or Boston and then take the Dartmouth Coach to Lebanon. A staff member can pick you up in either Burlington or Lebanon.
arrival_comments: The school had an international orientation before the orientation week, which meant that I met the other international students before everyone else. Knowing some students already made it easier going into the orientation week. The first week of the semester is fully dedicated to orientation, and all the new law and graduate students are there to meet each other. There are people from all over the country and no one knows each other. It was a nice and mostly informal week, where I met a lot of new people in a relaxed and non-academic setting.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

registration_process: I e-mailed the registrar's office and they assigned me to the courses that I wanted.
registration_help: The registrar's helped me answer questions before and after my arrival. After my arrival, I booked a meeting with the Vice Dean for Faculty and she talked with me about the courses I had chosen.
registration_success: I was unsuccessful in registering for Constitutional Law, as it is a JD class, but othr than that i got all the courses I wanted.
registration_advice: Look into the possibility of taking first year JD classes, as you will be able to spend much more time with your friends. Don't take the first no as an answer and maybe ask UCPH for a letter of approval of your legal ability.

I also got to experience other places in the US, like Boston (MA), Miami (FL), NYC (NY), and Portland (ME) - places I'd never been to. If I had planned better, I could've definitely planned more trips.
course_level: The courses were more or less the same level as those in Denmark, of course with the added challenge of having a class in english. The courses was not a law-heavy as in Denmark.
teaching_comparison: Most of my classes were small with less that ten students. These classes were generally focused around a class discussion where all students were able to equally contribute and asks questions. My larger classes were much like what I remember high school being like with rows of table and a professor going through the topic of the day. In all my classes, I was partially graded on my performance in class.
courses_enrolled: - Energy Law & Policy in a Carbon Constrained World (ENG5226 01 E) 3 credits - Negotiation (ADR6420) 2 credits - Climate Change: Power of Taxes (CLM5365 01) 2 credits - International Climate Change Law (ENV5218 01) 3 credits - International & Comparative Environmental Law (INT7444 01) 2 credits
recommended_courses: Negotiation! The professors are great, and the course is fun and different, as it mostly consists of simulations of negotiations. Climate Change: Power of Taxes was my absolute favorite course. Professor Milne is and expert in this field, and it was obvious that the course was well thought-out.
unexpected_costs: Housing costs above is excluding utilities which ranged from 400 DKK to 900 DKK depending on the month. Utilities can be expensive during winter month because of heating costs. The local transportation covers the Dartmouth Coach which I took when traveling to Boston or NYC. My friends would never ask me for gas money when I drove with them.
cost_comparison: Books. I was able to lend all the books from the on-campus library. Some of my courses didn't have any required books and instead all readings were available on Canva.
activities_available: There are a lot of community dinners during the semester where you can come and eat with your friends often for free.
activities_recommended: In summer, enjoy the warm weather and take a swim in the river. Go hiking, and explore the beautiful nature. Go to Fable Farm Fermentory every Thursday and enjoy the food, wine, music, camp fires, and starlit sky - it is the nicest way to spend your Thursday evening. Go skiing, ice skating, snow tubing, and any other winter activity you might find.
weekend_recommendations: Visit big cities like Boston, NYC, Montreal, or fly out to any place in the country from Boston Airport. Definitely go to Portland, Maine, on a day trip! Coziest city ever. I went in September and loved it. Try a Maine lobster roll. Don't miss out on the Tunbridge Fair! So much fun and a true American experience.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy, americans are welcoming, friendly, and easy to get to know.
socializing_tips: Invite yourself if you hear of something you'd like to join! During orientation, this is how I met my friends, and since everyone is new, they won't mind you joining, they'll think it's nice to get to know you.
cultural_challenges: Though I enjoyed the friendliness of Americans, it did make it a bit harder figuring out who actually wanted to be friends, and who was just being overly nice. You'll figure it out, just give it time. I expected the tipping culture to be different, but still had to adjust and ask my friends what was expected.
culture_appreciated: Vermont is a relatively progressive state, and I felt very safe there considering the current political climate. Generally, the Americans students that I befriended were nothing like the stereotypical American.
top3_advice: - Consider getting or leasing a car. As a minimum, make sure that you have an international license - maybe a friend will let you borrow their car. - Enjoy and explore the nature. - Use the professor's and TA's office hours.
other_useful_info: I can't stress enough that you should reach out to VLGS with any questions you might have whether you have accepted a spot or not. They are very helpful and made my stay there so much easier.
most_rewarding: The feeling of completing a semester on exchange and the independence it brought me. I also felt very accomplished academically, as attendance is mandatory, and I really got to focus on my courses.
greatest_challenge: I was homesick, and sometimes felt lonely. Looking back, I wish I would've reached out more to my friends at the school and asked them to hang out, as I later found out that many of my friends were lonely too. The lack of public transportation was a challenge too, as I couldn't really go anywhere without a friend or a student ambassador to drive me. I wish I would've had a car to go explore by myself.
other_comments: This is not the classic exchange experience like in a big city where there is something new to do every day. The town is small, and you will be seeing the same people, but take it as an experience and just be sure to be proactive in planning activities. The people there are lovely and very open to getting to know you. The outdoors in Vermont are something special and definitely something you won't experience anywhere else. If you're not into the outdoors, then take as many trips to the surrounding big cities as possible. It's easy to get to Boston Airport.

crucial_aspects: The fact that I had never been there before and that it seemed to have lots of beautiful nature. Also the fact that it was an English speaking country, as I thought this would make it easier to connect with people.
overall_comments: Overall, I am very glad that I went on the exchange as I have had some great experiences traveling around the country and experiencing the culture. However, I experienced a lot of difficulties leading up to the exchange; for instance with having my courses pre-approved by KU and receiving wrongful information and documentation from KU. Altogether, this meant that the months leading up to the exchange were pretty stressful for me. Of course this was not a part of my exchange per se, but it nonetheless affected my overall experience.
info_ease: I did find the whole proces of getting admitted into the courses I needed etc. quite confusing and VUW were often slow in responding to my e-mails. However, when I arrived and was able to visit the Student Administration Office in person, they were very keen to help me out.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any assistance per se, besides from the help I received when visiting the Student Administration Office and the information I got during the orientation week.
arrival_comments: The staff were definitely very keen to help, though they were sometimes a bit hard to get in touch with. The orientation week was not all that good in my opinion; the program was the same for all students (international students, exchange students, undergraduate students and graduate students) and thus it was not all that relevant for me as an exchange student.
housing_how: I found housing on my own

However, I experienced a lot of difficulties leading up to the exchange; for instance with having my courses pre-approved by KU and receiving wrongful information and documentation from KU. Altogether, this meant that the months leading up to the exchange were pretty stressful for me. Of course this was not a part of my exchange per se, but it nonetheless affected my overall experience.
registration_process: I applied for courses in an online portal and after some time was admitted into a number of courses. In contrast to at KU, at VUW you do not submit different "course wishes" for the same course, you are simply admitted into all the courses you applied for with space and then you drop the courses you don't want to take.
registration_help: You can get help by contacting your "Student Success Adviser". I also recommend contacting the lecturers of the courses you are interested in taking, they are very helpful in answering questions.
registration_success: I registered for 2/3 of the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Definitely contacting the lecturers of the courses you are interested in taking if you have any course specific questions.
academics_comments: Overall, I am very glad that I went on the exchange as I have had some great experiences traveling around the country and experiencing the culture. However, I experienced a lot of difficulties leading up to the exchange; for instance with having my courses pre-approved by KU and receiving wrongful information and documentation from KU. Altogether, this meant that the months leading up to the exchange were pretty stressful for me. Of course this was not a part of my exchange per se, but it nonetheless affected my overall experience.
course_level: I wouldn't say that the courses were harder than courses at KU, but they certainly required a lot more work during the course period, i.e. due to having a lot of group work, weekly assignments, oral presentations etc.
teaching_comparison: All my classes at VUW were discussion based and quite small with around 15 people or less. The style of teaching varied quite a lot between the classes; some of them involved lots of group work, others involved more full class discussions.
courses_enrolled: PSYC434 - Conduction Research across Cultures PSYC412 - The Psychology of Criminal Conduct PSYC437 - Advanced Human Memory
recommended_courses: I would recommend PSYC412 (The Psychology of Criminal Psychology) as the classes were very interesting and quite thought provoking. Also, the lecturers were very engaging and knowledgeable.
unexpected_costs: I did not expect food and housing to be quite as expensive as it was.
cost_comparison: Food is very expensive, especially vegetables and fresh food in general (a "cheap" cucumber would cost $6!). Also, housing is expensive. Coffee is probably the only thing that is cheaper in NZ than in Denmark.
activities_available: There were quite a lot of clubs and athletic and social opportunities; everything from international clubs to football clubs etc.
activities_recommended: I actually did not engage in any non-academic activities at VUW.
weekend_recommendations: There is so much to see in New Zealand! I recommend going tramping at the Tongariro Crossing, taking the train to Auckland from Wellington (goes through beautiful scenery), going on a whale trip in beautiful Kaikoura and visiting Wanaka.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy; kiwis are quite like Danes and generally very kind and open.
socializing_tips: Joining clubs or going to the orientation week. Since I was at the graduate level, people were generally quite "set" socially, i.e. not all that open to meeting new people at uni. Nonetheless, people were very friendly!
cultural_challenges: I did not find any cultural differences to be challenging.
culture_appreciated: People are genuinely so kind and helpful in New Zealand and I always felt very safe traveling around in the country.
top3_advice: 1. Pack warm clothes! Wellington quite often gets cold, windy and wet. 2. Pack you hiking boots; there is so much beautiful nature to explore. 3. Save up enough money; living costs in NZ are high.
other_useful_info: Just that I would really recommend going on exchange in spite of all the hard work with applying, getting scholarships etc. - it is so worth it!
most_rewarding: Definitely traveling around. New Zealand is such a beautiful country.
greatest_challenge: Probably the fact that uni was so "hands on" and required so much work; I had expected it to be more easy going, but I had a lot of assignments, presentations etc. and was required to participate in all my courses. I had hoped for uni to be a bit more "lose" so I could go on more spontaneous trips etc.

crucial_aspects: It was important for me to experience a new culture different from what we are used to in Denmark. I wanted to visit a country with the possibility to travel during my free time but also be enrolled in a high-ranked university to achieve the highest possible learning outcome combined with my cultural experiences.

arrival_assistance: Got relevant e-mails, brochures etc.
arrival_comments: Could have been more events just for exchange students since we had orientation with all new uni students as well
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process was easy since you can find all relevant courses on the university webpage before you are enrolled but I remember it was a bit late in the process that you could choose the courses.
registration_help: Contact with the faculty but was a bit hard being abroad. Good that you are able to change your courses during the first week so you are sure to make the right choice. However, a lot of the courses were full so better to choose the right courses upon registration.
registration_success: I got all of them but some teaching time tables changes which led to overlapping courses. I ended up changing one course after trying it the first week which was a good option. registration_advice: Try to choose the courses you like the most in the beginning because it can be hard to change if they are full afterwards. If courses are overlapping, maybe contact the course coordinator to ask if it will be available as a recording. Be aware of any overlapping exams. It was possible to find student comments about the courses in their Facebook group which could have been nice to see before choosing the courses. It was called VUWLSS for law students.
course_level: High level
teaching_comparison: A mixture of seminars and lectures, pretty similar to law courses in Copenhagen. However, the exams and essays were different from what we are used to but you can take optional workshops to learn more.
courses_enrolled: LAWS 334 - Ethics and the law LAWS 340 - International law LAWS 380 - Evidence LAWS 394 - Special Topic: The Treaty of Waitangi in New Zealand Law
recommended_courses: LAWS 380 - Evidence was an interesting class for people interested in criminal law. LAWS 340 - International law had a level too high for the credits provided and too much reading but a really interesting course.
unexpected_costs: Establishment costs
cost_comparison: Grocery stores, rent, and food was very expensive in general. You didn't really have to buy books since the material was also provided online.
activities_available: Different social and athletic clubs - a long list can be found on the website. I joined the international leadership programme and the international buddy programme which I can recommend,
activities_recommended: International buddy programme so you can meet other international students and have a buddy to ask for advice
weekend_recommendations: Try traveling as much as you can around the country before/after your stay or during the break. Wellington is located far away from other big cities but you can do hikes or activities in the city. I really enjoyed Somes island on a sunny day.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy
socializing_tips: Sign up for events
cultural_challenges: Their accent
culture_appreciated: The openness
top3_advice: 1) research your causes before signing up, 2) buy a car and sell it again before you leave if you can stay at a place with parking to do roadtrips, 3) book your flights early since they can be expensive and also the ferry ticket to the South Island if you plan on going by car
other_useful_info: Use book.me to get cheap experiences
most_rewarding: Learning to live in a different country, embracing their culture, and making new connections
greatest_challenge: Being far away from friends and family

crucial_aspects: Interesting courses offered, English language, and a country with a nature and activities I can explore
info_ease: Quite easy, during the international orientation week we received a folder and had a lot of information lectures with the necessary information.
arrival_assistance: I arrived a few weeks before the semester started and I didn't receive any assistance then. However, we received a lot of information during the international orientation week. I rented a room in a flat privately, so it might be different if you stay at a hall of residence.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: I had to register for courses through an online form on VUW's student portal. I was able to do that after I received pre-approval for courses by UCPH. You had to fill in different courses you wanted and they would decide which ones you were eligible for and enrol you in them. I was enrolled in a few wrong ones because you couldn't specify which you would like to replace others. After applying for changes to the enrolment, I received an email from the Student Success Advisor who helped me finalise the process by enrolling me in courses that still had spots left.
registration_help: You had to do the research on which courses you'd be able to take, based on pre-requisites at the host university and whether the courses could be approved as the compulsory courses you would have needed to take at your home university in that semester.
registration_success: It was a long process but I ended up with the courses I wanted and needed.
registration_advice: Make sure you have as many courses as possible pre-approved by your home university, it makes the process a lot easier.
course_level: Most of the courses I took consisted of the students discussing their own opinions on the course readings, rather than learning theories and the application of them. 3 out of 4 of the courses was mostly comprised of 40-minute presentations on course readings by student peers followed by class discussions. It would have been nice if the lecturers taught the class more. We also had many small assignments, I think I had 2-3 assignments each week, which took up a lot my time.
teaching_comparison: At Vic Uni, there was a lot of focus on the students expressing their opinions on theories, rather than diving into their meaning and how to use them practically. At UCPH, we focus a lot more on the latter.
courses_enrolled: PSYC405: Environmental Psychology PSYC411: Behavioural Analysis: Translating from Experiment to Analysis PSYC423: Culture and Social Behaviour PSYC431: Culture and Human Development
recommended_courses: I think all of the courses were worth it, e.g. learning about cultures when you're experiencing a new culture was very fitting. However, my favourite course was PSYC411: Behavioural Analysis: Translating from Experiment to Analysis, as the class had the Department of Conservation (DOC) as a partner and had to help solve a human behaviour problem they faced. In the beginning we were presented with different behaviour theories but we were free to identify theories and models that could help solve the problem. It was a very collaboratively based class as we were divided into groups, and felt a lot like an actual work project you could have as a psychologist working with behaviour change projects.
unexpected_costs: I bought a used car and had to pay an insurance excess when I reversed into a fence one time, haha. But other than that, I didn't really have any unexpected costs. But if you buy a used car, make sure you buy excess-free insurance, 5 dollars extra every second week is worth not having to pay unexpected excesses. Also, it was very easy to resell the car when you have to leave - I sold it on Facebook Marketplace.
cost_comparison: Vegetables are expensive! However, there is a market on the waterfront every Sunday where vegetables are slightly cheaper.
activities_available: There is a recreational centre with a lot of different clubs and sports you can try. I didn't sign up for it since the gym was a bit too small for me. I became a member of CityFitness instead, which is a big gym chain in New Zealand.
activities_recommended: I also signed up for Wellington Boxing Gym in town. It has such a cool vibe, and you can either get a 10 training pass or sign up for 3 months. Every Monday you could also go there for free. One of the best things I did! I hadn't tried boxing before but the Boxfit class was more a combination between boxing and fitness and it was a lot of fun and the 45-minutes went by very fast.
weekend_recommendations: To be honest, there is so much to see around New Zealand. Here is a few highlights: Around Wellington: - Go to Mt Vic lookout - Visit some of the local breweries! - Concerts at the San Fran venue on Cuba St - Walk the Skyline track (or at least some of it) Around NZ: - Definitely Queenstown on the South Island, it's a town full of different adventure activities, fx bungy jump, white water rafting, canyoning, mountain biking, wine tours - If you can go on a road trip by either renting or buying a camper van, do that! - Skiing during the NZ winter! Either Mt Ruapehu (North Island) or around Queenstown (South Island) - Rotorua: Geysers! - Hobbiton - Waitomo glowworm caves- I tried blackwater rafting here! - West Coast (driving along the coast!) - Fiordland: either Milford Sound or if you have time: Doubtful Sound (accessible by ferry) - Mt Cook (try the Hooker Valley Track on a good day for incredible views of mountains, glaciers, a lake and a river! Unreal!)
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: Rent a room privately! The exchange students staying in the halls mostly socialised with other exchange students. But if you want to get to know locals, a great way is to live with them. You can talk to some of them in class, but it will be hard to socialise with them outside of classes.
cultural_challenges: Not really anything - the culture is quite similar to the Danish culture. Also remember to indicate to the bus that you want to get on by holding out your arm and remember to say thank you to the driver when leaving the bus.
culture_appreciated: That they are more open to different cultures due to their bicultural heritage.
top3_advice: Remember to see more of the country than just Wellington! Have access to a car! Be ready for the weather to change from sunny to basically a storm in 5 minutes!
other_useful_info: Do some research about what you want to see and do in New Zealand. The months fly by so fast!
most_rewarding: Getting to know my flatmates and experiencing what New Zealand has to offer
greatest_challenge: The time difference to back home. You feel very distant from Denmark when people are mostly sleeping when you are awake. But it's fine when you're keeping busy!

crucial_aspects: A good film programme, an interesting destination, and having formerly studied at a high school in New Zealand
info_ease: Very easy
arrival_assistance: Orientation week was fine, felt a little bit condescending and childish at times, but I suppose some people need more support when abroad than I did.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Don't really recall the exact process at this point. I know there were a bunch of registration forms and I had to go get my passport and other documents verified by a lawyer and the Danish ministry of foreign affairs, which is fine I guess, since I live in Copenhagen, but it's a lot of paperwork. Which makes sense of course.
registration_help: Don't know
registration_success: I got exactly the ones I asked for.
registration_advice: Just follow the instructions and it's pretty straightforward.
course_level: Lower than Copenhagen standards for the 100 and 200 level courses I took. However, the 300 level course, current issues in film studies, was super interesting, and the level was higher (again, makes sense). I was very impressed with that course and its teacher.
teaching_comparison: Slightly different. I haven't had tutorials at UCPH before, where the course is divided into smaller groups and we do little assignments. It seemed a little high school-y to me. Also, the amount of assignments was way higher than in Copenhagen. I had one every few weeks and with 3 courses at once that made for a lot of writing assignments and not a lot of time to actually study the subject.
courses_enrolled: Current issues in film studies, gender and genre, and Mental Health and Disorder: Inter-disciplinary Perspectives
recommended_courses: Current issues in film studies - or any courses taught by Dr Tim Groves for that matter.
unexpected_costs: None, as I recall.
cost_comparison: Rent and groceries. They were about the same as Copenhagen prices which surprised me. Especially because the housing is as sad as it is, I am surprised they charge the same as Copenhagen.
activities_available: A LOT. All sorts of sport clubs, language clubs, film clubs, cultural clubs, poetry, music... you name it, they had a club.
activities_recommended: I did a lot of hiking and travelling around the rest of the country, which I highly recommend.
weekend_recommendations: Hiking and travelling.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy, I think. It's different from Denmark, for sure, but the kiwis are a very welcoming people and want to help out where they can. It is a more sociable culture, where it is common to talk to people you don't know at pubs or other places in public. Colonization means that they have very European sensibilities and it doesn't feel that far from home. Meanwhile, Maori culture is super interesting and welcoming.
socializing_tips: Just be open and friendly. Try and talk to people, they're not as closed off as Danes are. Go out and have some beers with people, if you drink. Or join one of the many many clubs as a way to meet people over a common interest.
cultural_challenges: I had to overcome my instinct of not talking to strangers.
culture_appreciated: Their humour, their openness, and of course the Maori culture which is so different from any European culture and something I think we can learn a lot from.
top3_advice: Be open to new experiences, get out of the flat and see what the city and the rest of the country has to offer, and make friends and make plans, because before you know it, you're out of time and headed back home.
other_useful_info: Not that I can think of
most_rewarding: I think I rediscovered my love for film studies thanks to the course Current issues in film studies and Tim Groves' teaching. I was so impressed and interested in that course.
greatest_challenge: Staying active and interested after a few months when the novelty had worn off.

crucial_aspects: My interest in getting to learn about the culture and that there was a good study friendly environment in the city.

arrival_assistance: I emailed a coordinator of the international student program who was very helpful in regards to student accommodation and classes.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

registration_help: You could text them. Otherwise, the website had a lot of information.

cultural_challenges: Dating...
culture_appreciated: People are really friendly and helpful.
top3_advice: 1. Make sure to plan a good schedule so that you have room to write your assignments 2. They do not have power sockets for you to charge your computers in the lecture halls, so charge your computer from home 3. You are in a country where many different cultures and ethnicities meet - be respectful and open to seeing them expressed in your everyday life
other_useful_info: There are three different campus'. Kelburn is really cool and where I had all my classes. Te Aro is in the CBD, and Pipitea is closer to the stadium.
most_rewarding: I have gotten a unique insight to a different culture consisting of many cultures, which I have enjoyed immensely.
greatest_challenge: Balancing learning about an indigenous culture and understanding the responsibility I have to support them.

crucial_aspects: Jeg ville gerne langt væk, men et sted, hvor jeg var sikker på, at undervisningen ville foregå på engelsk. Jeg har altid gerne villet til New Zealand og tænkte, at et udvekslingsophold ville være den perfekte mulighed for at besøge landet.
info_ease: Det var relativt nemt, men det tog selvfølgelig noget tid at finde rundt på deres forskellige hjemmesider. Heldigvis brugte de også Absalon, kaldet Nuku, til at give information om kurserne og til at aflevere opgaver osv.
arrival_assistance: Jeg blev hentet i lufthavnen, hvilket var super rart, da jeg landede midt om natten. Derudover gav de mig også et SIM-kort, så jeg hurtigt kunne få data på min telefon.
arrival_comments: Den første uge var orientering, hvor ikke alle dage var lige relevante, men det var en god mulighed for at møde de andre udvekslingsstuderende.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Man fik en mail med al information og et link til den hjemmeside, hvor man skulle søge kurser. Jeg lavede ikke nok prioriteter i første omgang, fordi jeg troede, man kun skulle søge det præcise antal points. De skrev så til mig og spurgte, om jeg havde nogle backup-kurser, jeg kunne tænke mig, i tilfælde af at jeg ikke kunne få dem, jeg helst ville have.
registration_help: De havde en mail, man kunne stille spørgsmål til, og de var relativt hurtige til at svare. Det var for det meste kun tidsforskellen, der gjorde, at man ventede længe.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle mine første prioriteter, så det var ret succesfuldt.
registration_advice: Læs de mails, der bliver sendt. Ja, der kommer mange, og de gentager sig selv meget, men det er der, al informationen kommer fra. Jeg gav dem min private mail i stedet for min KU-mail, hvilket gjorde, at jeg fik læst og gjort det, jeg skulle, til tiden.
course_level: Jeg havde to 300-niveau-kurser og et 200-niveau-kursus, hvilket svarer til to tredjeårs- og et andetårs-kursus.
teaching_comparison: Undervisningsformen minder overordnet meget om den på KU. Jeg havde forelæsninger og laboratorier, men jeg havde ikke regne- eller øvelsestimer i alle kurserne, hvilket gjorde, at man ikke arbejdede så meget med materialet. Derudover dukkede folk ikke altid op til forelæsningerne, da de blev optaget, og man kunne se dem på Nuku, når man ville. I forhold til eksamener er det ikke på samme måde som på KU, da de ikke har én endelig eksamen, der tæller 100% af ens karakter. Der var løbende bedømmelse, så hver gang man afleverede en opgave, talte den en vis procentdel af ens endelige karakter.
courses_enrolled: BMSC354 Pharmacology CHEM309 Chemical Biology and Medicinal Chemistry CHEM207 Experimental Chemistry and Spectroscopy
recommended_courses: Jeg ville anbefale de to CHEM-kurser, hvor underviserne var meget engagerede og dygtige til at undervise. CHEM309 var et helt nyt kursus, så der var lidt forvirring, men indholdet var meget godt. Der var dog en del overlap fra tidligere kurser, jeg har haft på KU, men det gjorde det egentlig nemmere, da vi ikke havde en bog at læse i. CHEM207 var også et nyt kursus, hvor de havde lagt to tidligere kurser sammen, men det var superfed, fordi man havde en hel dag i lab om ugen, hvor man helt selv skulle gennemføre alle forsøgene. Her lavede vi forsøg både i organisk og uorganisk kemi, så det var dejligt med en blanding og lidt selvstændighed.
unexpected_costs: Jeg var både forsikret af universitetet og af min egen rejseforsikring, så det kan være en god idé at tjekke, om du har mulighed for kun at bruge din egen forsikring.
cost_comparison: Udover de udgifter, jeg har noteret ovenfor, betalte jeg selvfølgelig også for visum (1.800), flybilletter (16.500) og rejser (???).
activities_available: n/a
activities_recommended: Recreation Center er fitness på campus, som man selv skulle betale for. Det var lidt gammeldags, men det var ret fedt, at det var der.
weekend_recommendations: Bare rejs rundt i hele New Zealand og se så meget du kan af både Nord- og Sydøen. Det er virkelig et smukt land, som man bare skal opleve.
culture_adjustment: Det var virkelig nemt.
socializing_tips: Man har helt klart mest at gøre med de andre udvekslingsstuderende, men snak med dem, du bor med, eller dem, du har undervisning med. Alle er virkelig søde og vil gerne snakke med dig.
cultural_challenges: n/a
culture_appreciated: Maori-kulturen var ret fedt at høre om i samspil med hele New Zealands historie.
top3_advice: Wellington var virkelig en dejlig by, men det bliver ikke kaldt "Windy Welly" uden grund. Udnyt, at der er rigtig mange dejlige steder i byen og smukke gåture i lokalområdet. 6. sal på biblioteket har den smukkeste udsigt over byen, så det var virkelig et dejligt sted at lave opgaver.
other_useful_info: Bare hav is i maven gennem hele ansøgningsprocessen, for den kunne til tider godt trække tænder ud.
most_rewarding: Det mest givende var at møde en masse nye mennesker, men også at finde noget styrke i, at man selv har gjort det. Altså, at man har rejst hele vejen til den anden side af jorden for at studere, selvom det kun var for et semester.
greatest_challenge: At ens venner og familie var så langt væk, og at tidsforskellen var stor, var noget, man skulle vænne sig til.
other_comments: Der var et superfedt veggie market hver søndag på havnefronten.

crucial_aspects: I've always wanted to explore nz both in terms of culture and especially (!!) in terms of the nature. Since nz is literally on the other side of the world, and you can't naturally just pass by + considering the environment, I wanted to stay for a longer period of time and an exchange seemed like the perfect opportunity:) Also, I really wanted to go to an english-speaking country, so there wouldn't be a language barrier and I could easily communicate with the locals.
overall_comments: Nz is literally the most amazing and beautiful place on earth. I wish for everyone to go there and I can't believe I had the privilege to live there and get to experience their culture:') GO!
info_ease: In general, vuw's website is extremely helpful and if in doubt about anything, they respond really fast on their email. They have an entire team only focusing on their international students and they guide you through most. That said, there's a ton of things that you need to have taken care of before arriving, but it's definitely manageable and you can always email them.
arrival_assistance: As I lived in a campus dorm, there's a lot of extra assistance and guidance. I was picked up in the airport, had a welcome team, there were events and food in the first week (and the rest of the trimester) and I feel like if I had any requests, my RA or head of hall would do anything to help me:)
arrival_comments: There were so many events, also specifically directed towards international students - Nz get a lot of internationals and vuw were generally really aware of us and our well-being, KU take notes<3
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Nz is literally the most amazing and beautiful place on earth. I wish for everyone to go there and I can't believe I had the privilege to live there and get to experience their culture:') GO!
registration_process: You need to register as a student and then apply for courses after. I honestly don't remember the process in detail, but there were quite a few things you needed to do, but I had no issues at all.
registration_help: EMAIL! They are so good at replying and helping.
registration_success: I got all my first choices, but know of people who had to re-apply.
registration_advice: Do it fairly quickly so you know early if you have any issues or need to change courses.
academics_comments: Nz is literally the most amazing and beautiful place on earth. I wish for everyone to go there and I can't believe I had the privilege to live there and get to experience their culture:') GO!
course_level: I had heard that the courses were really easy compared to KU, but that was not necessarily my experience lol. It is definitely different and you don't have 1 big project by the end of the trimester, like I've had in DK, but a lot (!!) of smaller assignments. I feel like it really depends on your lecturer and their style. I had two first year courses and one second year course, and while one course was extremely easy, the other two were quite rough due to my lecturers and their expectations:))
teaching_comparison: Like I mentioned, vuw tend to have a lot of smaller assignments/quizzes spread out over the tri, kinda like gymnasiet. It was rough getting used to, as there are many assignments due at the same time and you don't really know what the level is or what your lecturer expects. In hindsight I could've relaxed a lot more, as it is pass/fail when you're on exchange..
courses_enrolled: Film206: Hollywood Cinema (I took this course because I read that Tim Groves was amazing. I really didn't think so, but it was honestly a refreshing course as it was contemporary films) Film102: Film movements (As much as I disliked Tim Groves, I loooved this lecturer Missy Molloy - a feminist icon<3) Maor123: Te Iwi Māori me āna Tikanga/Māori Society and Culture
recommended_courses: Maor123: Te Iwi Māori me āna Tikanga/Māori Society and Culture!!! This course was amazing. When in nz, I encourage everyone to learn about the maori culture and potentially learn a bit of te reo. It was a tricky course in the beginning, as you need to figure out what all the different words mean and learn about a complex history and culture. But it was sooo rewarding and interesting and honestly added so much more to my exchange and relation to nz<3
unexpected_costs: I drank a lot more than I expected haha. Going out every weekend wasn't on my to-do list in nz, but it was fun and a nice way of relaxing after a busy week.
cost_comparison: Coffee and eating out is a looot cheaper. Groceries are the same or a bit more expensive than dk. Vegetables were quite expensive in the beginning (july/august) but as summer came closer, the price dropped. Also, there's a vegetable market every sunday by the waterfront, and there, there's money to save.
activities_available: There's literally so many clubs and an expo in the beginning of the tri, where you can meet them all and join.
activities_recommended: Welly is a really cultural city and there are a ton of nice shops and cafes, so I spent a lot of time just hanging out and exploring the city. It is fairly walkable, the streets are just steeeep and it is windy;)
weekend_recommendations: I wish I spent more time going on smaller trips outside of welly in the weekends, because everytime I did, it was the best thing ever. My flatmate invited me to stay with her and her family in Whanganui for a weekend, which was niicee. We went on a hike to the escarpment track (1-day hike), went to a rugby match (that's a must-do), visited Zealandia, and I spent a lot of time in the botanical garden which is just by Kelburn Campus.
culture_adjustment: Really easy. Kiwis are so freaking nice and easy-going + so open and interested<3 And Welly is just an amazing city, by far the nicest in nz (no bias), but nz is known for its shitty cities, and Welly is NOT one of them - it's full of culture and good vibes, though the cafes close at 15 (??)
socializing_tips: honestly, as I took two first year courses, the students were usually 18/19, so I didn't really hang with them. I was lucky to live with older local students so I spent time with them, but mostly I got international friends.
cultural_challenges: As mentioned, the cafes close early and so do the clubs. Also, you can't really go anywhere without a car, as the public transportation is quite shit. So either buy one (they're cheap), rent one, or team up with someone who has a car, if you feel like exploring the country.
culture_appreciated: The natureeeee!!! so freaking beautiful. Their appreciation of their ancestry - Maori, their consideration of other people and the environment<3
top3_advice: 1. The preparation is a lot, but definitely worth it. I was so stressed in the spring, but it all worked out. 2. The tri (tri 2) usually finish mid/end october, and I ended up staying until beginning of Jan, as I wanted to travel further, and it was the best decision ever. 3. Don't stress about the academics. I def stressed way too much and that took away a lot of my time in Welly. It doesn't matter if you get an A+ or C-
other_useful_info: I worked for a month at an orchard close to queenstown after I finished my time at vuw, and it was amazing BUT I had to apply for a holiday working visa and that ended up costing a lot, cause I had to get a chest x-ray.. just worth thinking about if that is the plan, cause I really didn't know I had to do that.
most_rewarding: ah everything.. the people, the nature, the culture. It was freaking amazing and I really hope i get to go back at some point. it was a solid 10/10 and the perfect mix between living in a smaller big city, studying and learning about the culture, and then travelling and really experiencing amazing nature afterwards<3
greatest_challenge: I left 30/6, just before the summer break and therefore didn't have any break before starting a new trimester. All of my friends back home were at festivals and enjoying their summer, while it was winter in nz and I just started school again. That was tough, but finishing in october and travelling for two months during nz summer made up for it x100.
other_comments: GO TO NEW ZEALAND!!! It is expensive and faaar away, but sooo worth it.

crucial_aspects: That it was a good university with courses that aligned with my interests. A full and lively study environment, with social clubs, and recreational sport.
info_ease: I had no trouble whatsoever finding the information I needed. The University staff and other students where immensely helpfull
arrival_assistance: Maps over the campus Clubs expo, to hear about what they were offering. Help settling in to my new surroundings
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: You sign up trough Nuku, their student platform.
registration_help: Student advisors and technical support, both online and in person
registration_success: Completly successful
registration_advice: Be in good time, and just ask the advisor if you need help
course_level: Two level 200 courses and one 100 course
teaching_comparison: It was different, we had more assignments to hand in, and the total grade is based on those and the exam, and not just the exam as it is a UCPH
courses_enrolled: Introductory Marine Ecology Māori Culuture and Society Geographical Information Systems and science
recommended_courses: Definitely the Māori Society one! Such an interesting course, and really gives you a perspective on everything that has taken place to make Aotearoa into the country it is today. 10/10
unexpected_costs: If you want to stay here longer than a month after ended studies, ypu have to get a visitors Visa which is 433 NZD
cost_comparison: Avocados and Coffee was cheaper, everything fresh is kind of expensive
activities_available: Gym Language club Tramping club Sailing club All kinds of sports clubs
activities_recommended: Go tramping, it's fun
weekend_recommendations: Mount Taranaki Red Rocks
culture_adjustment: Very simple, mostly time difference
cultural_challenges: Driving on the left side of the road
culture_appreciated: The indigenous Māori people's culture and history.
top3_advice: Wellington is windy, be prepared Kiwi's are friendly and talkative, chat with them! Join a lot of clubs, you'll make some cool friends
other_useful_info: No
most_rewarding: Meeting people from all over the world, who became friends
greatest_challenge: Being far away from family

crucial_aspects: Et sted, hvor jeg kunne se mig selv bo i et halvt år. Samtidig skulle jeg afsted med obligatoriske fag, så det var essentielt at jeg fandt et sted, hvor de tilbød fag der svarede til det jeg skulle have derhjemme.
overall_comments: Bare gør det! Ansøgningsprocessen kan være lang og besværlig, men det er virkelig det hele værd!
info_ease: Rimelig nemt. Jeg blev hentet i lufthavnen af personale for universitetet og kørt til der, hvor jeg skulle bo da jeg havde valgt at ansøge om at bo i student accommodation.
arrival_assistance: Som sagt blev jeg hentet og det hele, så det var super.
arrival_comments: Orienteringsforløbet den første uge var sådan lidt meh. Noget information var godt at få og f.eks. det med at gå rundt på universitetet så man kunne finde sine lokaler og blive vist rundt i byen, men der var også meget information som var sådan lidt ligemeget. Jeg havde selv valgt at droppe nogle sociale arrangementer derhjemme for at komme til orienteringsugen i NZ og det kan jeg godt fortryde lidt jeg gjorde. Så jeg vil sige, hvis du/I har mulighed for at tage til orientering så gør det, men hvis der foregår ting hjemme i DK som gør du/I måske misser orienteringen så don't stress it.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Bare gør det! Ansøgningsprocessen kan være lang og besværlig, men det er virkelig det hele værd!
registration_process: Efter at ha fået forhåndsgodkendt kurser hos KU skulle jeg bare søge dem hos VUW. Jeg fik først tilbudt et forkert kursus så det ikke svarede til de kurser jeg skulle have haft herhjemme, men så skrev jeg en mail til dem og blev sat på et andet kursus som jeg kunne bruge og havde fået forhåndsgodkendt, så super fint og god hjælp.
registration_help: Der er nogle mails man kan skrive til ift. hvad det er man har brug for og overordnet set er de rimelig hurtige til at svare.
registration_success: Som sagt først et forkert kursus, men så rykket til det jeg skulle bruge.
registration_advice: Bare skriv til dem, hvis I har spørgsmål, super søde og gode til at hjælpe.
academics_comments: Bare gør det! Ansøgningsprocessen kan være lang og besværlig, men det er virkelig det hele værd!
course_level: Jeg havde et 100, et 200 og to 300 level kurser. Så det svare til 1., 2. og 3. års hold på BA.
teaching_comparison: Jeg havde forelæsninger og holdundervisning, så meget lig det jeg ville have haft hjemme. Holdundervisningen var obligatorisk i en sådan grad at man skulle møde op til x gange ud af det samlede antal holdundervisninger, hvilket er anderledes end hvad jeg er vant til fra KU. Derudover var forelæsningerne kun en time i stedet for to.
courses_enrolled: 101 Introduction to Management, HRER301 Workplace Wellbeing, PSYC231 Cognitive Psychology, PSYC327 Cognitive Neuroscience.
recommended_courses: Hvis du/I tager afsted med fag der ikke er obligatoriske vil jeg anbefale også at kigge lidt ind i de kurser de tilbyder som har med Maori kulturen at gøre. Et par andre udvekslingsstuderende havde Maori fag og de lød virkelig interessante (hvis man er til sådan noget selvfølgelig).
unexpected_costs: Indkøb er overraskende dyrt. Særligt frugt og grønt om vinteren, men et hack er at tage til deres sunday market som er hver søndag, hvor der bliver solgt friskt frugt og grønt, hvilket er billigere end i supermarkederne.
cost_comparison: Som sagt, frugt og grønt. Til gengæld var kaffe overraskende billigt på cafeer.
activities_available: Alt muligt. Både forskellige kulturelle grupper, men også sportsklubber osv.
activities_recommended: Jeg meldte mig ind i deres tramping club som laver forskellige kortere og længere vandreture + en ugentlig bouldering tur. Jeg fik ikke brugt det helt lige så meget som jeg havde håbet, men en god måde at connecte med andre studerende og komme ud og hike, hvis man er til det.
weekend_recommendations: I mid-tri-break lejede jeg en van med nogle andre og kørte rundt på nordøen, det vil jeg klart anbefale! En van er den nemmeste og billigste måde at komme rundt og se landet på - camping mulighederne er virkelig fine og gode i NZ både med campingpladser og freedom camping. Find en campervan på Camplify.com - lidt ligesom airBNB, men for vans og markant billigere end alle de større firmaer der lejer ud.
culture_adjustment: Så fint. På nogle punkter med Kiwi kulturen ikke så anderledes fra derhjemme. Maori er selvfølgelig en del anderledes, men det er ikke en kultur man oplever i sin daglige gang i NZ vil jeg sige.
socializing_tips: Jeg var så heldig at komme i flat med en lokal studerende som så introducerede mig til flere af hendes venner osv. Derudover vil jeg sige at de klubber man kan melde sig ind i og holdundervisningen nok er de bedste steder til at falde i snak med folk, da der ikke er mulighed for at snakke med folk til forelæsningerne. Jeg meldte mig også ind i det træningscenter der var på campus, hvor jeg også endte med at snakke med lidt forskellige studerende. Men vil generelt sige det er rimelig svært som udvekslingsstuderene at snakke med de lokale både i form af Kiwi, Maori og Polynesiske studerende, da folk holder sig lidt i grupper på campus.
cultural_challenges: Ikke rigtig noget.
culture_appreciated: Den lille smule jeg blev introduceret til Maori kulturen var virkelig smuk og interessant - også derfor jeg vil anbefale evt. at tage kurser om Maori, hvis man er interesseret i sådan noget. Jeg vil sige generelt er folk i NZ virkelig søde, venlige og snaksagelige. De er meget åbne og nemme og snakke med (modsat hvordan det kan være i DK nogle gange), så det var virkelig skønt og dejligt. Så hvis du/I vil snakke med nogen vil jeg sige bare gå op og snak med dem.
top3_advice: 1. Bare gør det, det er mega fedt! 2. Tag tiden til at udforske NZ enten før eller efter dit ophold, der er så skønt og smukt 3. Spar op, NZ er ikke billigt
other_useful_info: Overvej om du/I synes det er det værd at købe en bil/van. Man kan ende med at bruge mange penge på at leje transportmidler.
most_rewarding: Nye venner, oplevelser og generelt en fantastisk rejse
greatest_challenge: At være væk hjemmefra og tage afsted til noget man ikke ved hvad er kan være svært, men vil klart sige at hvis man har smag for at rejse og møde nye mennesker og kulture er udveksling en optimal måde at gøre det på. Ansøgningsprocessen i sig selv kan være meget langhåret og ærligt få en til at overveje om det er det værd, men det vil jeg klart sige det er!

crucial_aspects: Jeg havde mulighed for at tage nogle virkelig spændende kurser på VUW. Engelsktalende land og undervisning på engelsk. Jeg havde hørt meget godt om New Zealand, bl.a. at naturen skulle være virkelig smuk og at folk skulle være søde - begge dele passede!
overall_comments: Helt fantastisk. VUW er et virkelig godt universitet, der er meget langt fremme i forhold til inklusion, og de har mange forskellige tiltag, der skal styrke de studerendes trivsel og få alle til at føle sig velkomne.
info_ease: Meget nemt. Jeg havde fået en masse brugbar information fra både VUW og Independent Living (universitetets boligtilbud)
arrival_assistance: Fordi jeg havde fundet accommodation gennem universitetet, havde jeg mulighed for at blive hentet i lufthavnen og kørt ind til byen.
arrival_comments: Jeg blev taget virkelig godt i hånden, og der var planlagt en masse spændende aktiviteter, både på uni og gennem IL (Independent Living), hvor jeg havde mulighed for at møde en masse andre studerende. Der var næsten planlagt lidt for meget (når man er sådan en som mig, der har svært ved at sige nej - men det er jo mit eget ansvar).
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Helt fantastisk. VUW er et virkelig godt universitet, der er meget langt fremme i forhold til inklusion, og de har mange forskellige tiltag, der skal styrke de studerendes trivsel og få alle til at føle sig velkomne.
registration_process: Kursusregistreringsprocessen er lidt forvirrende og foregår af to omgange. Først skal man søge om at blive godkendt til at tage kurset, og så skal man søge om en plads på kurset.
registration_help: VUW var virkelig søde til at hjælpe med spørgsmål og tekniske udfordringer. Man kan bare ringe eller sende dem en mail, så svarer de rimelig hurtigt.
registration_success: Jeg fik plads på alle de kurser, jeg gerne ville have.
registration_advice: Endelig skriv til VUW og spørg om hjælp, hvis du er i tvivl om det mindste! Vær ude i god tid, for processen tager ret lang tid og det kan være stressende ikke at vide, hvilke kurser man skal have lige op til studiestart.
academics_comments: Helt fantastisk. VUW er et virkelig godt universitet, der er meget langt fremme i forhold til inklusion, og de har mange forskellige tiltag, der skal styrke de studerendes trivsel og få alle til at føle sig velkomne.
course_level: Det er, hvad man gør det til. Jeg havde fx et kursus, hvor der var meget læsestof, men jeg klarede mig godt igennem med ikke at læse overhovedet og bare komme til forelæsningerne og undervisningen - så var der selvfølgelig en masse viden, jeg gik glip af, men havde ikke overskud til andet. Der er altså god mulighed for at lære rigtig meget, og der er også mulighed for at tage den lidt med ro, hvis det er det, man har brug for - alle mine undervisere var også søde til at udskyde deadlines, da jeg fortalte dem, at jeg var lidt presset.
teaching_comparison: Det var meget forskelligt fra kursus til kursus. På ART101 var der klassiske forelæsninger med slideshows og så obligatoriske tutorials, en slags holdundervisning i mindre grupper/klasser. På CMPO186 var der forelæsninger og frivillige tutorials, hvor det mest handlede om at komme og få hjælp til afleveringerne, og man lærer at bruge programmet Ableton fra bunden. På SARC360 var der ren praktisk tegneundervisning, hvor vi tog ud forskellige steder i byen og tegnede og fik hjælp og feedback på stedet.
courses_enrolled: ART101 - Art, Creativity and Identity SARC360 - Drawing CMPO186 - Audio Production and Music Technology Foundations
recommended_courses: Alle sammen! Det har været så fedt at have nogle lidt mere kreative kurser end jeg er vant til fra KU, lidt mindre læsning. Og så har jeg bare lært en hel masse om kunsthistorie og praktiske færdigheder i forhold til tegning og lydproduktion.
unexpected_costs: Jeg havde ikke tænkt, at jeg ville rejse så meget rundt, som jeg gjorde, og at det ville være så dyrt - men det er jo mit eget valg.
cost_comparison: Grøntsager i supermarkedet er generelt dyrere end i DK, en agurk koster fx 20 kr. - Men veggie market på Wellington waterfront i weekenden er et kæmpe hack! Det er billigere at spise ude end i DK, et måltid på restaurant koster omkring 100 kr. og en god kop barista-kaffe koster kun 20 kr. Offentlig transport er billigt, og hvis man har undervisning på to forskellige fakulteter på samme dag, kan man få gratis busture mellem fakulteterne. Det er også ok billigt at leje bil, hvis man er ude i god tid (kan anbefale Apex). Accommodation var dyrere, end jeg havde regnet med, men jeg tror, det er muligt at finde noget billigere, hvis man ikke lejer gennem uni.
activities_available: VUW's recreation center er virkelig godt, der er både fitness center og holdundervisning, det ligger på Kelburn campus og det er ikke super dyrt. Der er vildt mange forskellige klubber, man kan melde sig ind i, som fx holder fester og tager på ture sammen.
activities_recommended: Helt klart bliv medlem af Recreation Center. Det er så fedt at kunne gå hen og lave yoga eller tage en tur på løbebåndet efter undervisningen eller mellem timerne - til den smukkeste udsigt, man kan nemlig se ud over hele byen fra den store sal.
weekend_recommendations: Tag på tur! Der er SÅ mange utroligt smukke steder i New Zealand, og så mange fantastiske hikes og roadtrips man kan tage på. Te Papa, nationalmuseet, er virkelig godt, og der er gratis adgang, hvis man bor i New Zealand. Der er rigtig mange små kunstgallerier og caféer og spillesteder i Wellington og ofte også nice festivaller og events - hold øje med theimage04 på insta.
culture_adjustment: Nemt, det minder meget om Europa.
socializing_tips: Måske meld dig ind i en klub. Min oplevelse er, at det er sværere at socialisere med de lokale, fordi de allerede har en masse venner. Det er nemmere at blive venner med andre udvekslingsstuderende, der er i samme situation som en selv.
cultural_challenges: Syntes accenten var svær at forstå, især i starten.
culture_appreciated: Kiwis er generelt virkelig søde og imødekommende og oprigtigt interesserede. Jeg følte mig meget velkommen. OG det er supernemt at være glutenallergiker i New Zealand, der er næsten altid en glutenfri option
top3_advice: Hvor er du heldig, nyd det! Tag ud og oplev landet og den fantastiske natur. Vær åben og snak med de søde kiwis.
other_useful_info: Solen er virkelig stærk i New Zealand, fordi ozonlaget er tyndere, så husk solcreme:)
most_rewarding: At være så meget ude i de mest fantastiske landskaber, møde så mange søde mennesker og lære så meget nyt og spændende. Føler mig meget heldig over at have fået lov at opleve, hvordan en hverdag som studerende i Wellington kan se ud.
greatest_challenge: At jeg ofte havde svært ved at forstå, hvad folk sagde - især hvis jeg befandt mig i en gruppesamtale med flere kiwis, så går det altså bare stærkt.
other_comments: Gør det, gør det, gør det

arrival_assistance: Pick-up from the airport
arrival_comments: Some of the events overlapped
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution

registration_help: Basically any kind

teaching_comparison: they do exams rather differently

activities_recommended: the buddy programme go to the club expo
