crucial_aspects: I prioritized finding an english-speaking country, while I also wanted to do my exchange in a country far away from Denmark, as these countries are more difficult to travel to
info_ease: Very easy
arrival_assistance: There was a pick-up option from the airport. In the first week there was orientation days and welcome nights.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: It was kind of annoying with a lot to fill out, but overall fine.
registration_help: I could email the administration of student exchange, they helped a lot
registration_success: I got the classes I applied for, but I know other people had trouble applying for postgrad courses as undergrad students
registration_advice: Just do it as soon as possible
course_level: I took only 3 level courses, corresponding to 3rd year courses in the Denmark, but I wish I had taken more 1 level courses as this was possible and the work-load was much smaller on these. The 3 level courses can have a lot of workload during the course: tests, papers and so, that are mandatory and count towards your final grade. The level of the courses was a bit lower than in Denmark, as I had already learned some of the content in the courses in courses I had in first and seconds year at home.
teaching_comparison: Teaching was both lectures, tutorials and laboratory work
courses_enrolled: Pharmacology, Cell- and Immunobiology, and Cellular Regulation
recommended_courses: My favorite of the three courses I had was definitely Cell- and Immunobiology, I found it very interesting with good teachers Pharmacology I would not recommend, unless you like chemistry
unexpected_costs: None
cost_comparison: I expected food to be expensive, which it was :) especially vegetables and fruit that are not in season. So buy what is in season, thats the cheapest way to eat in NZ
activities_available: A lot
activities_recommended: Did not join any clubs
weekend_recommendations: We are multiple exchange students who bought a used car together, so we would travel around the north island in weekends and holidays. We got to see A LOT of the north island while on exchange which was really nice!!
culture_adjustment: Very easy
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: They locals are very nice and welcoming
top3_advice: Take more lower-level courses if you want more free time. Apply for student accommodation if you want to get to know other exchange students. Use your free time on exploring the country, it is beautiful (both north and south)
most_rewarding: Getting to know other exchange student and exploring New Zealand was amazing
greatest_challenge: Workload on 3 level courses was a bit much as you dont really want to spend all your time studying while in New Zealand, so learning to prioritizing also exploring the country

crucial_aspects: Det var vigtigt for mig at vælge et engelsktalende land, som også var naturskønt. Derudover synes jeg, at det var fedt at komme langt væk fra Danmark og ikke bare have muligheden for at tage hjem i ny og næ, men ægte føle, at man var på udveksling og dyrke relationerne der.
info_ease: Det var ret nemt at navigere på hjemmesiden https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/, her kan du både finde "key dates", kursus-oversigt og beskrivelser fra studerende. Vær dog opmærksom på, at du ikke er en International Student, men en Exchange Student. Der er forskel :)
arrival_assistance: I lufthavnen stod der nogle søde frivillige studerende fra universitetet og tog imod os. Vi fik en lille goodiebag og blev kørt til vores bolig med et gratis kørselstilbud, som man skulle melde sig på på forhånd.
arrival_comments: Der var introuge, som man egentlig godt kan skippe, men som er god at deltage i, hvis man har mulighed for det. Her blev vi introduceret til Wellington på en byvandring, hørte om New Zealandsk kultur og om sikkerhed i byen. Meget informativt og fint til at danne relationer inden skolen startede.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Da jeg endelig havde fået forhåndsgodkendt kurser hos KU skulle jeg bare søge de samme kurser hos VUW. Det var ret nemt, fordi man fik et link til registrerings-siden.
registration_help: Der var en masse webinarer op til starten på trimestret. Jeg blev fx. inviteret til et "Pre-Departure Seminar", hvor man får svar på en masse spørgsmål. Desuden kunne man altid spørge på disse mails: international@vuw.ac.nz og info@vuw.ac.nz.
registration_success: Alt med registrering gik fint.
registration_advice: Start med processen ret tidligt og spørg, hvis du undrer dig over noget.
course_level: Jeg havde et 100, et 200 og to 300 level kurser. Så det svare til 1., 2. og 3. års hold på BA. Jeg vil klart anbefale at tage 100-level kurser, da de er nemmest og frigør mere tid til at opleve landet og være sammen med sine venner.
teaching_comparison: Jeg havde forelæsninger og holdundervisning, som egentlig mindede meget om KU. Holdundervisningen i et af mine fag fungerede sådan, at man skulle sige noget og tage initiativ i selve undervisningen, og blev bedømt ud fra det. Lidt skræmmende, men man vænnede sig til det. I de andre fag var det super afslappende.
courses_enrolled: HLWB 103 Human Biology for Health, HRER 301 Workplace Wellbeing, MGMT 210 Ethical Leadership, PSYC 202 Culture in Psychology
recommended_courses: Jeg vil klart anbefale Culture in Psychology hvor man får indblik i Maori-kulturen og andre Indigenous kulturer. Ethical Leadership var 100% online fag, som ikke krævede alverden.
unexpected_costs: Vi købte to biler, som selvfølgelig endte med at koste i brændstof osv. Til gengæld har vi fået dem begge solgt igen. Vi endte med at miste ca. 2000 kr., hvilket sagtens kan betale sig ift. at leje biler af flere omgange.
cost_comparison: Nogle madvarer var ret dyre. Særligt importerede madvarer. Vi troede at frugt og grønt var billigere på sunday market, men fandt ud af, at det var ca. samme pris som i supermarkedet. Men det er stadig hyggeligt at gå på marked hver søndag:)
activities_available: Der var et bredt udvalg af forskellige klubber. Jeg endte med at melde mig ind sejlklubben, styrketræningsklubben og yogaklubben. Allesammen anbefalelsesværdige.
activities_recommended: Jeg kan virkelig anbefale at melde sig ind i træningscenteret på universitetet. Det er ret billigt og man får også afgang til holdtimer, og Særligt -NAME REDACTED- yogatimer er fantastiske. Hun spiller harpe og er så dygtig:)
weekend_recommendations: Jeg vil klart anbefale at købe en bil så hurtigt som muligt, så man kan tage på weekendture. Man kan gå i genbrugsbutikker og finde outdoor-gear og købe en sovepose i Mountain Warehouse, og så bare ud i naturen:) I mid-tri break tog mine veninder og jeg til Fiji, som kun ligger fire timer væk i fly. Det er en kæææmpe anbefaling. Den bedste ferie jeg nogensinde har været på og en perfekt sæson der i august. Det kan også anbefales at tage til Sydøen i campervan, men vent gerne til efter udvekslingsforløbet, da vejret på det tidspunkt er blevet en del varmere. Jeg hørte om nogle hvis olivenolie frøs til is i deres campervan, da de var afsted i mid-tri break...
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Det største kulturchok var nærmest, at jeg ikke fik noget kulturchok. Kiwi'er og vejret minder ret meget om Danmark. Maori-kulturen er en del anderledes, men det er ikke rigtig noget, man bliver eksponeret for dagligt.
socializing_tips: Jeg fik to venner i forelæsningssalen i den første uge. Mit største tip er bare at tale med folk, være åben og interesseret. De fleste kiwi'er synes at udvekslingsstuderende er ret spændende, og beundrer at man kommer helt fra den anden side af jorden. Mange kiwi'er har ikke forladt New Zealand.
cultural_challenges: Mange i Wellington starter uni, når de er 18 år, dvs. de er færdige som 21-årige, fordi de færreste tager masters. Man skal lige vænne sig til, at alle er ret unge. Det er ikke rigtig kulturelt, men Wellington er den mest blæsende by i verden. Det var til tider hammerkoldt.
culture_appreciated: Jeg nød virkelig at Wellington var så divers og accepterende for alle. Folk i New Zealand er rigtig gæstfri og enormt søde. Jeg holdt meget af den afslappede u-prætentiøse kultur som de har. Det handler mere om at have en god fleecetrøje, der holder længe end at gå i fast fashion og se godt ud.
top3_advice: 1. Tag afsted! Og tag til Sydøen mens du er dernede 2. Benyt dig af de forskellige clubs, det er en god måde at møde lokale studerende. 3. Spar op i god tid, så du ikke får økonomisk stress når du er afsted
other_useful_info: Overvej om du/I synes det er det værd at købe en bil. Man kan ende med at bruge mange penge på at leje transportmidler.
most_rewarding: Nye fantastiske relationer, personlig udvikling og empowerment i at tage så langt væk helt alene.
greatest_challenge: Det var mest udfordrende at være væk fra min familie i så lang tid. Jeg valgte at rejse i to måneder efter mit udvekslingsophold, så jeg endte med at være afsted i et halvt år. Det var utrolig lang tid, og jeg savnede familie og venner helt vildt.
other_comments: Hvis du står mellem at vælge Nord- eller Sydøen, vil jeg sige, at Nordøen er fedest at bo på, mens Sydøen er fedest at rejse rundt på.

crucial_aspects: Location was one of the biggest aspects when choosing a destination. I wanted to get as far away as possible.
overall_comments: New Zealand is a amazing place would highly recommend. Pro tip: buy a car it makes everything easier
info_ease: Easy much of what you needed was online and the rest you picked up along the way.
arrival_assistance: There was a orientation week but youcould also find all the info online
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: New Zealand is a amazing place would highly recommend. Pro tip: buy a car it makes everything easier
registration_process: As far as I remember, you apply for approval to register because you’re an exchange student, and then after that you can register. Everything happens online. But note your prefered courses have to be approved by the faculty which can take some time.
registration_help: There is a student support team to assist you in the process.
registration_success: A solid 6/10. Took med about 2-3 month from start to finish to get my courses due to me insisting on getting masters courses while on the bachelor. And then when classes where about to start one of them got canceled so I had to find a new one.
registration_advice: Start early, and if they don’t want to approve your courses, talk to your head of studies and name-drop them in your emails that should get things moving. If they really don’t want to give you your preferred courses, ask them what you should take instead; they usually comply.”
academics_comments: New Zealand is a amazing place would highly recommend. Pro tip: buy a car it makes everything easier
course_level: I had two MA courses and two BA courses
teaching_comparison: It’s much more American-style, with midterms, and the final exam often only counts for 50% of your grade, with assignments and tests making up the rest. Lectures are either 50 minutes or two hours long, and not all courses have tutorial classes. It’s very different from UOCH, where I take two 8-week courses at a time. You have more free time, and in some cases, when the exam counts for less than 50%, you might not even need to take it.
courses_enrolled: MATH 361 Graph Theory PAAH 101 He Tīmatanga Kōrero mō te Kori Tinana me te Hauora / Introduction to Physical Activity and Wellbeing PHYS 412 Theoretical Physics PHYS 417 Astrophysics
recommended_courses: PAAH 101 He Tīmatanga Kōrero mō te Kori Tinana me te Hauora / Introduction to Physical Activity and Wellbeing Is a good and fun course and you learn a lot about New Zealand history and culture. PHYS 412 Theoretical Physics Just a great course on the theory of many body quantum physics
unexpected_costs: not many and nothing to big
cost_comparison: public transport is super cheap, cars are also cheaper. Eating out is cheaper. And buying food is about the same.
activities_available: A lot of activities if you wanted to join.
activities_recommended: Hiking, camping, snorkling, roadtrips. It's just a very beatiful country that makes you wanna be outside. It turns you into a vegetarian outdoor person. I also did a internship with a pro football club which was setup through the host uni
weekend_recommendations: I spent almost every weedend or holiday hiking, and roadtrip'ing. Had a ski holiday which was nice and spent most of the free time exploring.
culture_adjustment: Pretty easy the biggest problem was the jetlag.
socializing_tips: Just talk and be nice to your fellow students during class or lecture usally does the job
cultural_challenges: none that spring to mind
culture_appreciated: The Māori parts of the new zealand culture is a highlight giving a inside into the history of the country.
top3_advice: Enjoy your classes, and remember not to take studying too seriously — the real magic is in the new places you go and the friends you make along the way.
other_useful_info: Independent living means something else in New Zealand, so if you want truly independent living, choose the Kelburn option if finding housing via the host uni.
most_rewarding: Going on holiday in the mid-term break with friends you did not know a few months earlier and making a ton of good memories
greatest_challenge: Packing your bags and leaving the place you have called home for a semester and saying goodbye to friends who live across the world
other_comments: Just enjoy yourself and have fun They only transfer the credits not the grade

crucial_aspects: Det var essentielt for mig, at der var interessant natur at udforske og fedt at komme langt væk fra Danmark, så man ikke nemt kunne tage hjem - man var virkelig afsted. Samtidig ville jeg gerne bo et sted, hvor modersmålet er engelsk, så man ikke på den korte tid man er der, også skulle lære et nyt sprog. Det er nice at øve sit engelske:) Derudover synes jeg det var spændende at komme et sted hen med en særlig historie!
overall_comments: Selvfølgelig var der op- og nedture (som der jo opstår), men samlet set har det været én af de største og mest udviklende perioder af mit liv. Og så er Wellington vildt hyggelig!
info_ease: Det var nogenlunde nemt at finde rundt på hjemmesiden, men alting bliver nemmere, når man så er dernede og kan spørge et fysisk menneske om hjælp.
arrival_assistance: I lufthavnen blev vi modtaget af en lille gruppe fra vic uni, som kunne køre os til vores boliger
arrival_comments: Der var en introuge med masser af aktiviteter, rundvisninger og mulighed for at stille spørgsmål. Der var også en dag, hvor man kunne komme rundt til alle klubberne på universitetet, så man kunne finde nogle fritidsaktiviteter! Det var selvfølgelig lidt overvældende og vildt, men det var meget fint arrangeret.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Selvfølgelig var der op- og nedture (som der jo opstår), men samlet set har det været én af de største og mest udviklende perioder af mit liv. Og så er Wellington vildt hyggelig!
registration_process: Søg først forhåndsgodkendelse fra KU, derefter søg på vic uni gennem Puaha (universitetets portal). Husk at tjekke, om der er specifikke fag, du skal have haft i forvejen. Jeg søgte fx musikfag og skulle indsende en lille portfolio med musik, jeg havde komponeret
registration_help: Man kan altid skrive til deres support mail og få relativt hurtigt svar
registration_success: Jeg endte med at få alle de fag, jeg havde søgt, men det tog noget tid at få godkendt musikfagene, da de skulle tjekke mine egne kompositioner først. Det var også kun valgfag, så derfor har det nok været en anelse nemmere ift. KU.
registration_advice: Gå i gang tidligt!
academics_comments: Selvfølgelig var der op- og nedture (som der jo opstår), men samlet set har det været én af de største og mest udviklende perioder af mit liv. Og så er Wellington vildt hyggelig!
course_level: Jeg tog fag på 100 eller 200 level, hvilket var godt, når jeg havde så mange. Det var stadig tilpas udfordrende, og workload kan godt være lidt heftig. Man vil også gerne have tid til at opleve landet ved siden af;)
teaching_comparison: Det var ret anderledes. På musikvidenskab (KU) er jeg vant til at have få opgaver i løbet af semesteret, som man ikke får karakter for, og så en afsluttende eksamen, som er karakteren for hele faget. I Wellington oplevede jeg, at der var mange opgaver i løbet af semesteret, som man fik karakterer for, hvilket blev regnet sammen til sidst. Det kan der være fordele og ulemper ved - synes selv, det var lidt hårdt at blive målt og vejet hele tiden, men til gengæld behøvede man ikke stresse voldsomt over eksamen.
courses_enrolled: PSYC122 – Foundations in Psychology 2 ANTH208 – Human Rights and Development CMPO201 – Projects in Composition CMPO286 – Audio Production and Recording
recommended_courses: Var rigtig glad for ANTH208! Det handlede rigtig meget om kolonialisme og arbejdede med meget konkrete eksempler fra hele verdenen. Det her fag vendte hele mit perspektiv:)
unexpected_costs: Købte 2 biler med en gruppe venner, som vi købte for cirka 40.000kr, og vi endte med kun at tabe 1800kr på det, da vi solgte dem til sidst. Kan virkelig betale sig, fordi fleksibiliteten i at have bil, når man skal på tur i weekenden er meget fed. Vi lagde hver 5000kr ud for at kunne købe dem, og gik jo så med til, at vi måske ikke så de penge igen.
cost_comparison: Madvarer er meget sæsonbaserede, så det er ret forskelligt, hvad der er dyrt. Men mad er generelt ikke vildt billigt. Kaffe er billigt! Og oplevelser er der tit student discount på
activities_available: En masse outdoor, en masse sport, lidt musik, sprog, aktivisme og politiske klubber
activities_recommended: Kajak var virkelig sjovt og nogle rigtig søde mennesker! Det er sådan noget whitewater kayak, så det er ret vildt
weekend_recommendations: Tag ud og hike eller campe! Man skal ikke køre vanvittigt langt for at finde smuk natur, og så er det en billig måde at rejse på. Midt i semesteret er der et 2 ugers break, hvor det er virkelig fedt at planlægge en større tur. Jeg campede med nogle venner rundt på nordøen, andre tog til Fiji eller Australien, og så var der en del, der besøgte sydøen.
culture_adjustment: Kulturen i Wellington er jo ret vestlig, så på den front var det virkelig nemt at falde til. Det er heller ikke den største by, så man bliver hurtigt tryg i byen. Maori kulturen er noget helt andet, end hvad man er vant til, men jeg synes det er enormt vigtigt, at man sætter sig ind i den og er nysgerrig! Det er en meget smuk kultur, som vi kunne lære en del af.
socializing_tips: Vær med i klubberne på universitetet. Der er det rigtig nemt
cultural_challenges: Man skal vænne sig til en masse smalltalk:) Men de er for det meste virkelig søde at snakke med - ikke overfladiske. Og husk at bilerne køre i venstre side, når du går over vejen
culture_appreciated: Helt sikkert deres forhold til naturen. De har et meget større fokus på at bevare den, sandsynligvis også pga Maori kulturen. Og så er de enormt venlige mennesker! Alle smiler til hinanden
top3_advice: 1. Hav tålmodighed med dit sociale overskud i starten - det ER hårdt, men det BLIVER godt 2. Vær klar på at bruge nogle penge... 3. Glæd dig<3 Det er en fantastisk by og et fantastisk land!
other_useful_info: Wellington er en blæsende by. Det er ik for sjov! Men man vænner sig til det. Og du skal gå meget op ad bakker
most_rewarding: Den natur jeg fik lov at opleve, men allermest de mennesker jeg mødte!
greatest_challenge: At balancere uni og fritid. Husk at leve;)
other_comments: Hvis du tager til Wellington, håber jeg du får den allerbedste tid!<3

crucial_aspects: De havde et stort udvalg af spændende fag, og jeg har hørt godt om New Zealand fra andre, der har været der.
info_ease: VUW er ret gode til at sende mails, der er lette at forstå, og som indeholder forskellige tjeklister til, hvad man skal gøre. Derudover har jeg et par gange ringet til deres hotline, som også er meget behjælpelige.
arrival_assistance: Der var en slags introuge, hvor vinklen vist rundt, og fik forklaret de forskellige tilbud, herunder at blive tilmeldt skolens sygeforsikring.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_process: Det var let nok at udfylde ansøgningen, men man skal sørge for, at alle ens dokumenter bliver underskrevet og stemplet af officielle personer, hvilket tog lidt tid med mails frem og tilbage.
registration_help: Man kunne ringe til deres hotline, og det var meget hjælpsomme.
registration_success: Jeg fik alle de fag jeg ville have.
registration_advice: Jeg ville anbefale, at man gør det i så god tid som muligt, så man ikke bliver tidspresset, hvis man mangler et dokument der så også lige skulle være stemplet og underskrevet af en person fra KU.
course_level: Jeg tog andensårs- og tredjeårsfag på VUW, fordi det svarede til de obligatoriske fag herhjemme. Niveauet var meget lavere end jeg er vant til fra KU.
teaching_comparison: På VUW er forelæsningerne meget vigtigere end på KU, og de varer typisk kun en time. Derudover er der også holdumdervisning, hvor ens akademiske performance kan blive noteret og indgår i ens karakter. Der er mange fag som ikke har en eksamen, eller som kun tæller en vis procentdel, så det handler om at læse tingene gennem semesteret.
courses_enrolled: PSYC202 Culture in Psychology PSYC2014 Psychology and Law MGMT2010 Ethical leadership HRER 301 Workplace Wellbeing
recommended_courses: Alle sammen, men særligt Psychology and Law var spændende for mig, og jeg tror ikke der er et fag på KU som minder om. Faget handler meget om kriminalpsykologi og rehabilitering.
unexpected_costs: Jeg kan ikke huske, at jeg havde nogle uforudsete udgifter.
cost_comparison: Jeg købte et par biler sammen med andre danske udvekslingsstuderende, og de var meget billigere, end jeg havde troet. Vi betalte ca. 5000 kr pr. person for to store biler (vi var otte personer i alt)
activities_available: Der var en masse klubber man kunne melde sig ind i. Alt fra sportsklubber til sprogklubber til faglige klubber til filmklubber osv.
activities_recommended: At dyrke sport, fordi man møder flere af de lokale, som gerne vil vise landet og traditionerne frem, samtidig med at man laver noget sjovt og bevæger sig.
weekend_recommendations: Jeg købte i fællesskab med andre danske udvekslingsstuderende to biler, og vi tog næsten hver weekend ud på forskellige vandreture. Det kan jeg klart anbefale.
culture_adjustment: Det var virkelig nemt. Jeg kan også anbefale at må med en eller flere roomies, fordi det gør processen nemmere at have nogen at tale med om det.
socializing_tips: Man kan dukke op til forelæsningerne og forsøge at snakke med nogen der, men ellers ville jeg melde mig ind i en klub.
cultural_challenges: Det sværeste var nok måden folk gik klædt. Det er meget normalt at have joggingbukser og hættetrøje på til forelæsning, eller at gå ned og handle i nattøj. Det skulle jeg lige vænne mig til.
culture_appreciated: New Zealand er et meget åbent og venligt land, og jeg oplevede de lokale som meget hjælpsomme og flinke til at hjælpe en. De har også en rig Maori kultur, som anerkendes tydeligt, hvilket var godt at se og spændende at lære om.
top3_advice: Husk praktisk tøj (vandresko, regnjakke) Vær nysgerrig på de lokale og den lokale kultur Se dig omkring - der er så meget fantastisk natur i New Zealand
other_useful_info: Man skal i mange tilfælde selv tilmelde sig holdundervisning (underviserne sendte en mail ud eller nævnte på forelæsningerne, hvornår tilmeldingen åbnede). Men jeg ville tilmelde mig hurtigt, så man kan ligge sine timer på en god måde. Jeg havde for eksempel fri om fredagen, hvilket gjorde, at jeg kunne tage på mange forlængede weekendsture.
most_rewarding: Det er helt klart de mennesker jeg har mødt. Min roomie, som er fra New Zealand, er blevet en af mine tætteste venner, og jeg har allerede besøgt mange af mine andre venner i deres respektive hjemlande efter udvekslingsopholdet.
greatest_challenge: Der er ret mange dokumenter og frister man skal have styr på, samt mange mails frem og tilbage med underskrifter etc. Derudover må man ikke arbejde i New Zealand, når man kun er på udveksling på et semester. Derfor kunne det til tider være lidt stressende at se kontoen blive mindre og mindre, fordi New Zealand er et dyrt land at bo i.

crucial_aspects: First of all, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam had specific courses about Neurobiology which I was very interested in. Second, I always wanted to live in Amsterdam since I find the city very interesting.
overall_comments: I had an amazing experience. I was lucky with the university, the city and especially the people I met.
info_ease: I would say it was pretty easy. Check your mails and reach out to people if you are in doubt.
arrival_assistance: There was a very nice introduction-week where it was possible to ask all the questions one might have. Very helpful.
arrival_comments: VU is a very well-organized University. I found it easy to access the information I needed.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I had an amazing experience. I was lucky with the university, the city and especially the people I met.
registration_process: I found the courses on their website and applied through a guide I found there (along with a guide from KU). I would say that it was pretty intuitive.
registration_help: I contacted some people through e-mail if I needed answers to my questions. I think it is also possible to call someone? In general, most information can be found on the websites of KU and the host university (VU)
registration_success: Very successful - it was easy and I registered for the courses I wanted
registration_advice: Look at the websites, don't feel too scared to ask for help.
academics_comments: I had an amazing experience. I was lucky with the university, the city and especially the people I met.
course_level: I would say the academic level is pretty high. Maybe similar to KU.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was pretty different, which took me a while to get used to. There is way more group-work at VU, weekly assignments, and everything is more "scheduled" and mandatory. On the other hand, there was a bigger division between school-days and weekends, meaning that the weekends were mostly without any school-work on my behalf. In comparison, I think UCPH is based more on individual responsibility and planning (eg. catching up with lost work on the weekends)
courses_enrolled: I took the minor Brain and Mind with 5 courses of 6 ECTS points each
recommended_courses: I think choosing courses is based mainly on interest of the student applying, and therefore I cannot recommend specific courses. I personally did though really enjoy the courses: Brain in Trouble and Developing Brain (each is 6 ETCS)
unexpected_costs: Hmm partying maybe. Also, if you go to Amsterdam you should really rent/buy a bike
cost_comparison: In general living is cheaper, but not that much. Public transport is pretty expensive unfortunately - therefore I recommend getting a bike
activities_available: I think there was many, although I didn't really apply to any. I mainly spend time in the city or with friends
activities_recommended: Biking around the city! Also - Amsterdam has a lot of nice museums and outdoor green areas (parks, the forest, etc). Cinemas and bars are very nice also. Good fleamarkets for shopping
weekend_recommendations: Museums (I loved Foam, Stedelijk, the Eye, Anne Frank), green areas; Amsterdam Bos, Vondelpark etc, second-hand shopping at Mevius or Waterlooplein Fleamarket, trying out food at Albert Cuypmarkt, idk - explore! And GET A BIKE
culture_adjustment: I would say it was pretty easy. Amsterdam is not that different from Copenhagen.
socializing_tips: I honestly didnt socialize with locals - all the friends I got was also foreigners on exchanges or similar. I think this is very common, and I personally don't care if my friends are from London or Serbia or The Netherlands... So maybe just accept that the chances of befriending dutch people are pretty low
cultural_challenges: The language a bit. But people are very good at english, fortunately. Also - they bike like crazy compared to Copenhagen, so be aware of that. Also, dutch food is not that interesting
culture_appreciated: Amsterdam is beautiful. I love the bars and the museums, and I honestly loved everything about living there (but I also think that I was very lucky).
top3_advice: 1) be open, and try to socialize with new people even though they might not look as someone you would normally befriend. 2) get a bike and go exploring! 3) dont be to anxious about school and filling out official stuff and all that - everything always work out in the end, and you should really try to enjoy and have fun whilst being abroad
other_useful_info: Ask questions. Have some good rain-clothes. Dont plan too much - you'll have no idea how things end up anyways. And just GO!
most_rewarding: The people I met, without a doubt. I've gotten some very close friends from all around the world.
greatest_challenge: Being on my own - especially in the beginning. It felt scary and overwhelming and uncomfortable. But as time passed, I met some really good people and everything fell into place.
other_comments: Dont take it all to seriously - pick some interesting courses, follow them, but also enjoy life and have fun! I think going to Amsterdam will be a great experience, especially if you are open and not too afraid to talk to new people

crucial_aspects: I chose my destination on the basis of course selection and for economic reasons. In Amsterdam I had the opportunity to follow a very specific minor within the area of my academic interests. Furthermore it was an affordable destination with many social and cultural offers.
overall_comments: Overall the exchange experience was amazing! But unfortunately the Netherlands had heavy corona restrictions, which affected the last two months of my stay quite a bit.
info_ease: Very easy! The university is very organized and everything you need to now will be send to you by email. In addition they are very easy to contact and they respond quickly.
arrival_assistance: Someone waited for me at my building to give my keys and show me around. Otherwise I didn't get any assistance at the arrival but I was assigned a dutch buddy after a few days, who was super nice and ready to answer all questions. But in general everything I needed to know was provided by email.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Overall the exchange experience was amazing! But unfortunately the Netherlands had heavy corona restrictions, which affected the last two months of my stay quite a bit.
registration_process: I followed courses offered by the faculty of medicine, which meant that they did the registration for me, so the only thing I had to do was to email them. The application deadline for medical minors is very early compared to the other faculties, so be aware.
registration_help: An exchange coordinator was available via email - very helpful!
registration_success: I got all the courses I wanted even though the exchange agreement was restricted to another faculty (science).
registration_advice: Don't worry too much about the faculty restriction.
academics_comments: Overall the exchange experience was amazing! But unfortunately the Netherlands had heavy corona restrictions, which affected the last two months of my stay quite a bit.
course_level: The level of teaching is more or less the same as in my home studies at KU. But the level of the other students was lower than I am used to.
teaching_comparison: In my class we were 27 students and most of our classes were lecture-based. But in general the lectures were more interactive and they took place in a normal class room. In addition to lectures I also had practicals, site visits, two debate clubs and one journal club. The practicals included one time looking at bacteria cultures/bacteria techniques, MRI computer practical and scientific reading. The site visits were mostly at the hospital located next to campus. But we didn't have any lab in the courses I followed.
courses_enrolled: Minor Cancer - Immunity - Personalized therapies (24 ECTS) Minor Literature essay (6 ECTS)
recommended_courses: I would recommend my entire minor! I am very interested in immunology, cancer biology and genetics and these elements were the core of my minor. The level of details was lower than I am used to but the minor covered many topics which gave me a broader understanding. In addition to the previously mentioned topics, the minor also included virology, microbiology, neurodegenerative diseases, advanced diagnostics, imaging and therapies. Of course it was a medical minor, which meant that some lectures were a bit too clinical.
unexpected_costs: Trash tax
cost_comparison: I rented my bike through swapfiets which was very cheap (150 kr per month). Public transport is more expensive than I expected, but most of the time I just used my bike.
activities_available: There were many different activities offered to students. A big gym with lots of different activities like fitness, different ball games, dance, yoga etc. They also had a cultural club with classes in drawing, mindfullness, acting etc. I joined a gym that was not associated with the university, because I specifically wanted to do crossfit.
activities_recommended: I bought a museum card which gave me access to a lot of the museums in Amsterdam. The gym I joined was amazing, but also quite expensive.
weekend_recommendations: Amsterdam has a lot to offer with museums, restaurants, shopping etc. But a lot of the cities in close to Amsterdam are worth a visit as well! Many students also go to the southern part of the Netherlands, Bruxelles or Paris.
culture_adjustment: Easy. The culture is not that different from Denmark.
socializing_tips: Talk to the dutch people in your class!
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: The canals are absolutely amazing for the atmosphere. I also really enjoyed the going out culture in Amsterdam! The restaurants and the cafes are always full (so remember to make a reservation).
top3_advice: - Get a bike! - Be open and spontaneous - Enjoy your time there! Time flies...
other_useful_info: Many of the smaller stores they don't accept mastercard or creditcard, so you should consider to get a dutch bank account.
most_rewarding: I feel more independent and confident after my exchange. I got amazing friends and a second home for life (luckily not that far away).
greatest_challenge: Living alone in a new country during corona with many restrictions.

crucial_aspects: That it was a big city in Europe and that I could go with my friend from back home.
info_ease: Quite easy, I had no problems with arrival.
arrival_assistance: I did not receive any because of covid, but it would definitely have been nice.
arrival_comments: Because of covid there only was an 2 hour online introduction, but it was very unstructured and I did not get anything from it besides extra confusion.
housing_how: I found housing on my own
registration_process: The registration process at VU was easy and I got all the information I needed.
registration_help: You could send an e-mail to the institution at any time and they were super fast at replying.
registration_success: I got all the classes I wanted.
registration_advice: Apply for more courses than you actually need, because some of them might overlap, and then you do not need to apply/register all over but just de-register for those you do not want in the end.
course_level: There was a lot of presentations and papers during the semester and therefore it got quite busy. Also, the expectations from the teachers and ambitions of the other students were quite high, but I really liked it because it was in a good and motivating way.
teaching_comparison: The students had more responsibility and in general more work to do, but they also participated more.
courses_enrolled: Humanity and Climate Modern Philosophy: Mind and Body Neurophilosophy and Psychiatry Neuroethics and Society Randomized Controlled Trials of Psychology
recommended_courses: Neuroethics and Society Humanity and Climate
unexpected_costs: I had to pay a lot to do laundry.
cost_comparison: We did not have to buy any books as all of the literature was online and provided by the university
activities_available: There were some activities available, but I dod not make use of any.
activities_recommended: Open mics and festivals.
weekend_recommendations: The museums in Amsterdam, they are great! But also, go to the beach!
culture_adjustment: Very easy, Denmark and The Netherlands are quite similar.
socializing_tips: Go to open mics and festivals.
cultural_challenges: Dutch people can be a bit more direct compared to Danish people.
culture_appreciated: The openness towards individual differences.
top3_advice: Bring a raincoat, an analogue camera and say yes to all the invitations to out.
other_useful_info: It can be easier to become friends with other exchange students than the locals, but the locals are also super kind once you get to know them.
most_rewarding: I learned that I cannot plan everything down to the smallest detail as life is unpredictable, but is also leaves room for more surprises.
greatest_challenge: People on the masters are often quite settled, so it was a bit hard to become friends with them as they were quite busy and already had a lot of friends.

crucial_aspects: Upon choosing my study abroad, it was crucial for me that I chose a contry where the education and local community were good at english. This was due to the fact that I did not want to be educationally or socially limited by not knowing the local language. Further, I wanted to choose a study destination where I could take upon the last 4 courses I had left of my Bachelors, which was challenging enough in itself. Luckily, VU did offer exactly the Clinical Psychology courses I needed. Further, I naturally wanted to choose a place in which I knew I wanted to explore the cities, nature and environment of the country, since this is an important part of exchange to me.
overall_comments: My stomach hurts just thinking about if I hadn't gone. Go!
info_ease: Very easy. There were advisors standing at both the student accomodation and at uni.
arrival_assistance: DUWO (accomodation) councelors gave me my key and pointed me to my dorm. The student office helped me with my student ID, getting access to the student library and finding my books.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: My stomach hurts just thinking about if I hadn't gone. Go!
registration_process: It's hard to rate, because my process was complicated. I found the perfect minor of 30 ECTS which fit my last courses at UCPH perfectly. However, two months before going abroad, VU told me that I could not get my minor anyway and should choose other courses. However, there were no other matching courses, i.e. my study abroad would just be straight up cancelled. This was very stressing and upsetting of course, as I had planned everything, found someone to lease my home in CPH, signed off courses in UCPH etc. However, the reason why I don't give them a 1, is that after contacting them over and over again, VU did let me into the minor. This was only because I was so insistent, so had it been a nicer (lol) person than me, they would have just been forced to give up, and that is not okay from VU's side according to me.
registration_help: I reached out to the incoming office and they were always quick at replying, but the whole process was still very stressful and felt unsecure.
registration_success: 10/10 ended up getting the one's I wanted but only because I was super insistent and the VU made an exception.
registration_advice: Reach out and ask whether the minor or courses you want will be offered to exchange student before you get your hopes up - and make them put it in writing, if they say it will be available to exchange students.
academics_comments: My stomach hurts just thinking about if I hadn't gone. Go!
course_level: The level is higher than at UCPH, but not unbearable or more time-demanding necessarily, if you just keep up from the beginning.
teaching_comparison: There's more weekly assignments and exams every 7th weeks. This was a bit intense to adjust to in the beginning, but it also means that the curriculum for each exam is way smaller along with lower expactations, which is what I mean by the workload not necessarily being rougher, because you do remember stuff when the periods are so short.
courses_enrolled: Minor of 5 courses (minor called Psychopathology, Health and Prevention 30 ECTS): Psychopathology and Prevention Assessment and Coaching Skills Diversity in Clinical Practice Research Toolkit Psychopharmacology
recommended_courses: All 5, they were amazing. There was a lot of practical knowledge and exercises, so you'd never feel like anything was irrelevant for your education, as I've sometimes suffered a bit with at UCPH. The professors are extremely passionate and interactive with the students about the topics, and the whole study-mentality and passion is just higher at the VU. People really wish to learn.
unexpected_costs: None. Everything was cheaper than expected.
cost_comparison: Housing, food, social stuff, going out etc. was cheaper. Public transport (I biked everywhere but when going on day trips for larger citites, e.g. Rotterdam, Hague, Utrecht, Brussels, Paris) was more expensive.
activities_available: Lots of sport activities, lots of social events, debate clubs, pub quizzes etc. were available - all with a cost naturally.
activities_recommended: Find a nice friend group and with them: Go on weekend trips by flixbus: paris, brussels, rotterdam, utrech, hague, antwerp Go biking on the country side Organize your own food- and pub-crawls Attend gym classes in the parks (often free trials;))
weekend_recommendations: Travel travel travel and explore the NL by bus and train
culture_adjustment: Very easy
socializing_tips: It will come naturally, first in introduction week, but also via ESN and via the place you live (especially if you live at Uilenstede)
cultural_challenges: None
culture_appreciated: More extrovert than danish people
top3_advice: 1: Be open and social from the beginning so that you interact and create some lovely friendgroups 2: Go exploring on the weekends, all of a sudden, its over :( 3: Even though there's not a lot of hours of teaching, try to make your own everyday schedule (e.g. 9-16) at uni - that way, even with all the assignments, you're free on nights and weekends
other_useful_info: Uilenstede is a great student accomodation if you want the full social exchange experience
most_rewarding: The social life and getting a feeling of re-inventing myself in new wonderful surroundings
greatest_challenge: None

crucial_aspects: At bo i en multikulturel by, at studere på et universitet som tilbød spændende, anderledes kurser end hvad KU kan tilbyde og at finde et universitet med et lovende udvekslingsprogram og hvor jeg ikke ville være den eneste udvekslingsstuderende. Alt dette kunne Amsterdam og Vrije Universiteit tilbyde
overall_comments: Jeg elskede mit ophold i Amsterdam og min studietid på Vrije Universiteit! Udvekslingsprogrammet var lovende, men rundet corona blev der desværre sat en stopper for de fleste planlagte arrangementer. Der var dog stadig masser socialt at hente ved at bo i student housing, og kurserne på VU inkluderer desuden en del gruppearbejde, hvorfor jeg fik mit sociale behov fint dækket på anden vis
info_ease: Meget nemt. VU Incoming Student Exchange stod altid hurtigt klar med svar på de spørgsmål jeg havde, hvilket dog ikke var mange, da de var virkelig gode til at formidle information om ansøgningsfrister, arrangementer og diverse andre oplysninger
arrival_assistance: Ved ankomst til mit værelse blev jeg modtaget med nøgler og oplysninger af andre studerende bosiddende i området, som også fungerede som kontaktpersoner under mit ophold
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Jeg elskede mit ophold i Amsterdam og min studietid på Vrije Universiteit! Udvekslingsprogrammet var lovende, men rundet corona blev der desværre sat en stopper for de fleste planlagte arrangementer. Der var dog stadig masser socialt at hente ved at bo i student housing, og kurserne på VU inkluderer desuden en del gruppearbejde, hvorfor jeg fik mit sociale behov fint dækket på anden vis
registration_process: Efter godkendt ansøgning sendte VU mail ud hvor de beskrev den kommende registreringsproces og login til deres platform. Alt fra værelsessøgning til kursustilmelding foregår derinde, hvilket er meget ligetil
registration_help: Man kunne altid skrive til enten VU's hovedkontor eller VU Incoming Student Exchange som begge var hurtige til at svare på spørgsmål
registration_success: Da jeg søgte en minor, og dermed fem allerede sammensatte fag, fik jeg alle de fag jeg søgte. Hørte dog om andre der søgte fag individuelt, som ikke fik alle deres ønskede fag, da nogle har stor forespørgsel
registration_advice: Det kan være en super idé at søge en minor, da du derved er sikret, at du ikke søger fag der overlapper hinanden (skemaerne for de enkelte fag kommer nemlig før ud efterfølgende), og sandsynligheden for at få godkendt sin minor er stor, da det er en sammensat pakke. På den måde er man også sikker på, at man får det antal ECTS man skal have
academics_comments: Jeg elskede mit ophold i Amsterdam og min studietid på Vrije Universiteit! Udvekslingsprogrammet var lovende, men rundet corona blev der desværre sat en stopper for de fleste planlagte arrangementer. Der var dog stadig masser socialt at hente ved at bo i student housing, og kurserne på VU inkluderer desuden en del gruppearbejde, hvorfor jeg fik mit sociale behov fint dækket på anden vis
course_level: Forskellen på niveauerne på de forskellige fag skyldes hovedsageligt, at jeg tog både antropologiske, sociologiske og økonomiske fag, hvilket gjorde, at nogle af fagene var uden for mit vante akademiske felt, hvilket til tider var udfordrende. Til gengæld var der en sammenhæng mellem alle fagene, fordi de var sat sammen til en minor, hvilket kun gjorde det nemmere med tiden, når man allerede havde haft undervisning i noget af det
teaching_comparison: Undervisningmetoden er meget anderledes end på KU. For det første bliver man ofte bedømt ud fra mange forskellige kriterier såsom skriftlige afleveringer, gruppearbejde, peer feedback, fremlæggelser, aktiv deltagelse og endelige eksaminer. Det er ikke unormalt, at din karakter i ét fag udgør summen af din samlede præstation i fem forskellige elementer. Dette medfører ligeledes, at der ofte var flere deadlines og generelt mere arbejde i løbet af et kursus, modsat på KU, hvor det meste arbejde ofte ligger til sidst, udmundet af en eksamen. Slutteligt kører VU et såkaldt periodesystem, som betyder, at man har to-tre fag på én gang, som du så afslutter efter ca. to måneder, hvor du derefter starter to-tre nye fag. Dette betyder, at man aldrig har alle sine fag på én gang og at eksaminerne/arbejdsopgaverne er mere ligeligt fordelt over hele semestret, og altså ikke ligger lige inden jul, men fem eksaminer på kort tid. Dette gav virkelig mulighed for at fordybe sig mere i de få fag man nu engang havde, men til gengæld var der mere pres på ift. at få læst og udført arbejdet løbende, da der kun var otte uger til at færdiggøre et helt fag
courses_enrolled: Minor: Development and global challenges 1. Development and globalisation 2. Environment and development 3. Identity, diversity and inclusion 4. Global political economy 5. Urban studies
recommended_courses: Hvis man er interesseret i ulighed, mangfoldighed og identitet, er Identity, diversitym and inclusion et virkelig spændende fag med fantastiske undervisere og virkelig givende gæsteforelæsere. Desuden er Urban studies et fedt fag, hvis man interesserer sig for byplanlægning og har lyst til at udarbejde et større feltarbejde i Amsterdam
unexpected_costs: Museumspas (alle pengene værd!) Cykelreparationer (ikke pengene værd..)
cost_comparison: Togtransport ud af Amsterdam er til den dyre side, minder ret meget om togpriserne i DK
activities_available: Alle tænklige sportsklubber, akademiske klubber, middage for udvekslingsstuderende, museumture, fester
activities_recommended: Deltag generelt i velkomstprogrammet, som tilbydes for udvekslingsstuderende ugen op til uni-start. Det er en rigtig god måde at møde nye mennesker og lære byen at kende
weekend_recommendations: I Amsterdam skal du spise og drikke dig igennem det hele, tage på museum, besøge de mange genbrugsbutikker og smukke parker og ikke mindst tage færgen til NDSM værftet, hvor der er god stemning og sjove events. Derudover er der altid et marked åbent et eller andet sted i byen, som er værd at besøge. Uden for Amsterdam kan jeg anbefale Harlem, Rotterdam, Zandvoort, Utrecht og The Hague
culture_adjustment: Meget nemt. Den hollandske kultur minder egentlig meget om den danske, og fordi Amsterdam - og Holland generelt - er et meget mangfoldigt sted, føler man sig velkommen uanset hvor man er
socializing_tips: Bo på værelse med andre studerende, f.eks. på kollegie i Uilenstede. På den måde er der altid folk omkring dig og du møder folk som ikke læser det samme som dig og som kommer fra hele verden
cultural_challenges: Hollændere er kendt for at være meget ekspressive og de er generelt ikke bange for at sige deres mening eller måske endda snakke lidt hårdt, hvilket er godt at vide på forhånd, da de bestemt ikke gør det af ond mening - de er nemlig SÅ søde!
culture_appreciated: Egentlig synes jeg, at ovenstående har sin charme, ligeså vel som jeg elsker, at hollændere er super hjælpsomme og venlige
top3_advice: 1. Få fat i en cykel og tag ud og oplev Amsterdam og alt det skønne den har at tilbyde 2. Prioriter tid på sociale arrangementer og nye venner, i stedet for at sidde derhjemme og studere 3. Have fun, for pokker! Det bliver uden tvivl fantastisk
other_useful_info: Hele ansøgningsprocessen kan godt virke uoverskuelig og meget formel ved første øjekast, men jeg lover, at det virkelig ikke er sådan i realiteten. Og har du spørgsmål, så er både VU og KU behjælpelige. Det skal i hvert fald ikke holde dig fra at søge
most_rewarding: At møde venner for livet, at lære utrolig meget om andre kulturer og at lære Amsterdam at kende som var det København
greatest_challenge: At bevare fokus på studiet med alle de spændende ting og søde mennesker omkring en ;)
other_comments: Er du i tvivl, så spring ud i det! Du kommer ikke til at fortryde det

crucial_aspects: Because of Covid, I was obligated to find an exchange destination in Europe. I was sure I would like to go to a bigger city. I never went to Amsterdam before, but the city has such a good reputation and I really liked that the exchange program is 5 fixed courses. The minor I choose also consisted of a lot of laboratory work, which was important to me both because of the upcoming bachelor project, but also because the chances for online teaching was still big and with laboratory courses I was sure I would still get the opportunity to go to uni, as these courses can't be held online.
overall_comments: Overall I had an amazing exchange! But arriving at a different country is a lot of work. I did not expect it to be so time consuming studying in a different country, mostly because the things excepted of you is different than what I was used to.
info_ease: Very easy. Vrije Universitet sends out emails with timelines showing when to do what. I remember thinking it was a bit late to find housing and get information, but I think it is just how it is when going abroad. In general they also responded very quickly to e-mails and was always very helpful.
arrival_assistance: The first week was introduction, which was very useful. There was a scavenger hunt on campus and different other activities to navigate on campus, in the city, in your neighborhood and lots of other stuff.
arrival_comments: The introduction week was the best! I met most of my friends in this week and everyone is so open in the beginning of the semester, making it a lot easier to connect compared to a couple of months into the exchange. The introduction program is for all exchange students and master students which makes it possible to meet so many people! In the Netherlands they also have a huge student organization called ESN, that makes a ton of different activities in the introduction week and during the entire year.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Overall I had an amazing exchange! But arriving at a different country is a lot of work. I did not expect it to be so time consuming studying in a different country, mostly because the things excepted of you is different than what I was used to.
registration_process: You register for a minor or you choose your courses yourself. They don't recommend choosing you own, but I would say you can do it anyways. After you register you still have to register for each course in the beginning of each period. The incoming team will help you with it.
registration_help: Incoming team helps with everything regarding exchange, and they replied very quick.
registration_success: I got all the classes I applied for.
registration_advice: After the first registration it said that my courses was not available and I couldn't register. This apparently just because I choose I minor. I just had to write to the incoming team and they would register me manually for each course.
academics_comments: Overall I had an amazing exchange! But arriving at a different country is a lot of work. I did not expect it to be so time consuming studying in a different country, mostly because the things excepted of you is different than what I was used to.
course_level: As mentioned, the first two courses was a bit basic. The 3 other courses was more similar to the danish level.
teaching_comparison: They have a lot more to do during the course. In each course we had to hand in at least one report and do one presentation and also have a written exam. It means you have to keep up and follow the course. I only had one course at a time, so I felt like a had to go to the exam all the time (once a month) The exams are not as stressfull as at UCPH. You have plenty of time to answer their questions. They give very good feedback on reports, which I was very happy with, since you spend a lot of time making the reports, and then you don't make the same mistake through all the courses. A lot of the presentations and reports are made in groups, which is also different from what I was used to at UCPH.
courses_enrolled: Experimental Cell Biology I Experimental Cell Biology II Protein to Cell Molecular Cell Biology Molecular Microbiology
recommended_courses: I especially liked Molecular Microbiology. I have never enjoyed microbiology, but through the minor I really learned to love it and this course is so well structured. The course coordinator is a very good teacher. The course has a theoretical part and a practical part. The practicals is helping the molecular microbiology department of VU with a research project, which is so cool! We were divided in small groups of 10 people and with one professor and two student assistens in the lab the practicals were so well structured and you could get as much help as you needed with you project.
unexpected_costs: When living with own bathroom and kitchen you have to pay a trash tax to the municipality which was around 100-120€ for half a year - but then remember to apply for housing benefit.
cost_comparison: Public transport in the Netherlands was very expensive. I was surprised in the beginning of how much money I spend in general because it is expensive to buy all the stuff I needed for the apartment, such as a broom, kitchen stuff, food and so on.
activities_available: You can sign up for a lot of different stuff and they also have very cheap VU gym with many different sports such as kickboxing, spinning, soccer, basket and so on. You could sign up for a buddy group, where you were a couple of exchange students together with one dutch student. There was supposed to be one event each month with the buddy group, but because of covid it was limited. However, we went bowling, to dutch quiz night and for walks in the city.
activities_recommended: I enjoyed the gym classes with my friends, and also recommend signing up for the buddy group. But most important is the introduction week, it is where everyone meets.
weekend_recommendations: Buy a museums card, so you can visit all the cool museums in ams. I would also recommend traveling around in the netherlands before uni starts (we had one week between introduction and start of classes). This is when the weather is still nice and a lot of the dutch cities just look better when the sun is shining haha
culture_adjustment: The dutch culture is very much like the danish
socializing_tips: It was more difficult to socialize with dutch students, as they already have their study groups and are well established. Also many of them don't live in Ams but in smaller towns around the city. I would say, don't be disappointed with only getting exchange friends, as it is a lot easier because everyone is open and ready to make new friends.
cultural_challenges: All letters you receive from the municipality is in dutch, which can be challenging and frustrating. You need a DigiD (like NemID) to pay stuff like taxes and fines. They do a lot of communication by mail (not email) which takes forever and seems very old school.
culture_appreciated: Everyone speaks English and it is such an International city with so many different cultures. They really enjoy parks and outdoor life, which I think really brings the city to live even though it is winter. They also bike everywhere, and 7km to Uilenstede is not far:)
top3_advice: Make as many friends in the beginning before classes starts. ENJOY! It is over before you know The destination is really not that important, you will have a great time no matter where you are.
other_useful_info: If you want the dorm felling while on exchange I would try getting a room at Uilenstede. However, I really enjoyed being able to close my door and have friends and family over in my own apartment.

crucial_aspects: I wanted to visit a city with a high educational standard but also have a rich cultural life. I wanted to go to Europe because it was easier with the application and it also helps a lot with the Erasmus gran. Amsterdam perfectly fits all these criteria.
overall_comments: Of course, Covid-19 was still happening and there was also a lockdown while I was in Amsterdam. However, I still had a great time and made new friends and enjoyed my courses.
info_ease: It was very easy. Vrije University contacts you several times to remind of the important dates and give great advice. It could not have been any easier.
arrival_assistance: A student helper waited for me at the dorm and showed me around. There were also many tutors in bright blue t-shirts guiding us into the auditorium on the very first day of school.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: Of course, Covid-19 was still happening and there was also a lockdown while I was in Amsterdam. However, I still had a great time and made new friends and enjoyed my courses.
registration_process: I applied for merit for the chosen courses at my host university. When it was time for course registration (it was quite late), Vrije University sent out a notification for course registration. You have a lot of time to apply. I was notified that I was not able to register some of the courses because it was not applicable for exchange students. I ended up finding other courses by myself and registered for them. It was quite easy.
registration_help: The VU International team replied very quickly, but it was also possible to e-mail the course coordinators. They were also very helpful.
registration_success: I ended up registering for 2 out of the 5 courses that I initially had merit for because I did not see that some of the courses had pre-requisties or were not offered to exchange students.
registration_advice: Try to find something (a little bit) outside your track/major but is still relevant. Take advantage of the fact that you are offered some courses that your home university does not have. And do not stress too much about the planned courses because you will probably change them anyways due to different unforeseen circumstances. But it is not difficult at all.
academics_comments: Of course, Covid-19 was still happening and there was also a lockdown while I was in Amsterdam. However, I still had a great time and made new friends and enjoyed my courses.
course_level: The academia level is very high but it is possible to follow along AND have some free time for going out or do some cultural activities.
teaching_comparison: It is not much one-on-one with the lecturers. It is mostly lectures and and work groups/classroom teaching. Each course had 1-3 assignments. They are very much focused on research so you will gain insight into many pharmaceutical methods.
courses_enrolled: 1) ADMET 2) Advanced Molecular Immunology and Cell Biology 3) Drug Target Biochemistry and Signaling 4) Human Cells in Culture 5) Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Development
recommended_courses: Drug Target Biochemistry and Signaling and Human Cells in Culture are very useful and relevant if you study Pharmacy/Pharmaceutical Sciences at KU. The lecturers are passionate and skilled.
unexpected_costs: I got a waste disposal tax of 100 €. I also bought a used bike at Waterlooplein for 80 euro (highly recommended!) I also ended up getting a museum card where you get free access to several museums in NL. If you visit 3-4 museums the museum card is a good deal.
cost_comparison: The generel cost of living is cheaper in Amsterdam compared to Copenhagen. It is cheaper to eat out but also general grocery shopping in the super markets.
activities_available: There is a cinema at Vrije University and there a so many student associations. I recommend 3D (look it up on Instagram). They are especially perfect for international students. I also recommend joining the sports activities. You can do try outs in the first weeks and sometimes Vrije University also offer some free sports classes because they have health weeks etc :D
activities_recommended: Get yourself a museum card
weekend_recommendations: - visit Albert Cyup market - visit Brouwerij 't IJ in East/Oost - attend Amsterdam wine festival - go to the museumplein - visit Vondelpark with friend
culture_adjustment: Very easy. The NL is not much different from Denmark.
socializing_tips: It is quite difficult because they tend to talk to other Dutch students. But if you want to get in contact with Dutch students you can join the groups with Dutch-sounding names when you make the groups for the assignments.
cultural_challenges: None.
culture_appreciated: There are so many cultural activities and Amsterdam also offer a lot of excellent restaurants and cafes.
top3_advice: 1) Apply for rent allowance if you can. 2) Don't stress out because there WILL be a lot to study, many assignments etc. Make room for having fun also. 3) Get a bike.
other_useful_info: The university is very big, try to find good study places a part from the Main Building and New Building.
most_rewarding: Gaining insight into many new cultures. I got to know many new international students and it is very fun to experience the cultural differences. This whole experience also made me appreciate the Danish educational system. We have a big safety net and we do not have to worry as many students from other countries.
greatest_challenge: I had to present in front of many people. However, this also made me more comfortable speaking in English now when I am back at KU again and is a part of a research team.

crucial_aspects: I chose to study in the Netherlands and Amsterdam specifically to take part in the culture and to experience to the life abroad. I also found that the courses at the university were fitting quite well with my program and even gave some opportunities that were not offered at my home university.
overall_comments: I throughly enjoyed my studies at VU and the life outside of the study. However my visit was affected by the COVID-19 and limited some of the culture aspects and social activities.
info_ease: I think the VU were excellent in giving the information needed by incoming students and also aided by the introduction days at campus.
arrival_assistance: The information given through mails and at the campus introduction days were extensive and helpful. Beside from that I did not receive any assistance, but I also did not have a need.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I throughly enjoyed my studies at VU and the life outside of the study. However my visit was affected by the COVID-19 and limited some of the culture aspects and social activities.
registration_process: The first registration is made before the schedule is released which means that schedule clashes might mean you have to alter your choices later on. It was annoying to read up on the courses you were interested in chosing what to register for and then later on to find out the combination of courses were never possible. However besides from that the course information was easy to get and the process was no problem.
registration_help: I register for a course were I found out that the prerequisites were not met from my previous studying. So I had to change to course for another. This could have been bad, but the course coordinator in the first selected course helped me and I also was enrolled in a new course without any big issues due to the help from a course coordinator at the new course. This was despite the fact that the deadline was already expired and I really got the help I needed to find the right course.
registration_success: I was successful, but had to change a course for a new one due to the prerequesites not being met and it being too difficult for that reason. I luckily was able to change without any problems
registration_advice: Do not underestimate the requirements of the courses, but even if you do there is always something to be done if you ask for help.
academics_comments: I throughly enjoyed my studies at VU and the life outside of the study. However my visit was affected by the COVID-19 and limited some of the culture aspects and social activities.
course_level: I found the level aprrioate for most of the courses however the ADMET courses was closer to bachelor level if compared with my studies of pharmacy in my home university. I chose a course of Computer-aided drug design and virtual screening out of interest, but the found the level unsuitable for me, with my background in pharmacy and not really any previous knowledge with the computational modelling. The course was interesting though, but I had to change it due to it being too difficult.
teaching_comparison: The style of teaching was generally relying on lectures and group work with assignments, with not much classroom teaching besides from the Advanced Molecular Immunology course. The teaching were also online for a lot of the semester due to COVID-19, this might be affected by that.
courses_enrolled: ADMET Advanced Molecular Immunology Drug Target Biochemistry and Signalling Human Cells in Culture Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Development
recommended_courses: Advanced Molecular Immunology - gives a in depth knowledge of the immune system and techniques with the field. However the other students generally have a background in the immunology field, so prepare for catching up if you dont. Drug Target Biochemistry and Signalling - Interesting course with great teachers. The course has new technologies in the field of drug targets has cool components with give insight in the field of drug target and the life of a researcher. The assignment was to make a research proposal, which was not overwhelming. but made the group work interesting for anyone interested in research. Human Cells in Culture - Really usable if want to work with cell culturing and cell methods. The course introduces to techniques, so you dont need to know about cells culturing beforehand since the course covers everything in an approachable way
unexpected_costs: My bike broke down so I subscribed to a bike service with monthly payments, which were more expensive, but a much better and safer bike.
cost_comparison: Housing were less expensive than expected due to rent allowance providing around 2200 DKK per month to help pay the rent.
activities_available: It was not very active due to COVID-19 and I was at the one Friday bar, but the information on social activities were either not there in english or not at all. I think more activities are held normally when there is not lock down though. Introduction days were a nice start and also made it possible to make new friends with the other exchange students. Most of my friends were made it the introduction days, and we kept contact throughout-
activities_recommended: Introduction days
weekend_recommendations: So many museums are available in Amsterdam, I are really cool to experience. Rijkmuseum, Van Gogh, Anne Frank House if you get a museum card (BSN needed) you can visit 600 museums free of charge after the one time purchase. Well worth it in my mind.
culture_adjustment: I think the culture shock was limited because the danish culture are similar in a lot of ways with the dutch. The directness can be wrongly interpreted as being rude, but as a danish person that is perfect. Howevever
socializing_tips: I heard joining the clubs at campus are a good way to meet local students but did not have the upportunity due to lockdown (COVID-19). I personally made a post on reddit to find local people to hang out with through my hobby, which made me make some friends. So social media can be a way to might somebody of the locals who have similar interests as you.
cultural_challenges: I think dutch culture is not always so approachable, which makes it a bit harder to make friends. But if you do it is well worth it. In my experience they generally do not go out of their way to invite you in, so you definitely have to make the effort of you want to engange with them. However Vrije has
culture_appreciated: The informal way the dutch communicate which makes it easy to say what you mean and limits risk of misunderstandings. Some might consider it rude, but I really like it.
top3_advice: See the city of Amsterdam and do all the touristy stuff while you are there. The exchange is also for you to experience the city. Museum cards make it cheaper on maybe also motivates you to see more than you would otherwise. Get a bike ASAP while you are there. It is nice to get around plus you get to see much more while you travel. However beware that the dutch, not unlike bikers in Copenhagen drive fast and stops for no one. But if you want to understand the dutch you need to live like the dutch and the bike is a must. Chose different courses that have your interests covers. You get the opportunity to chose from a variety of different course that maybe your own program does not include. Use this to expand for academic horizon and also get the perspective of student and lecturers outside for track. Once your education is over you will probably work with people with different academic background anyways and this is a great way see interdisciplinary cooperation and is really useful
other_useful_info: You dont need to learn dutch of you are there for one semester only, but it is fun to learn anyways at least to read, since you will be able to pick up a lot quickly if you know English, Danish and German. Get an BSN (citizen service number) as quick as you can. The process of getting one is kind of slow so start early so you can get a dutch bank account to get a Maestro card many places do not accept Mastercard or Visa, so the Maestro card help a lot in the everyday.
most_rewarding: The friends I made with the other exchange students, since it was both open my horison to new culture and just a lot of fun. I hope I will be able to maintain the relations and create new experiences with them in the future.
greatest_challenge: The lockdown was the biggest challenge, but hopefully that will not be an issue going forward.

crucial_aspects: I had both academic and personal reasons for going on exchange. Academically I thought it would give me the opportunity to be taught in a different way than I'm used to, furthering my academic experience and abilities. Personally, exchange is a wonderful way to get out of your comfort zone and meet a bunch of new people from all over the world.
overall_comments: I had a really good experience both academically and personally, although balancing both having a full-time study, finding yourself in a new country/city, and finding new friends, was a challenge. Definitely worth it though!
info_ease: VU Amsterdam was very good at providing relatively timely information about almost everything. And if you still lack information on something they were really quick to respond per mail.
arrival_assistance: VU had some tutors we could ask questions during most of the intro days. We did have to do a self-guided tour around campus, which felt kind of pointless. Especially since it was self-guided.
arrival_comments: We had a two week introduction period where we had a bunch of events offered to us, both academically and socially oriented. Most of the things were really fun, and it was a good way of having something to do the first couple of weeks after your arrival, and a wonderful way of getting to meet a bunch of really great people. I made a bunch of friends during these weeks.
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
registration_comments: I had a really good experience both academically and personally, although balancing both having a full-time study, finding yourself in a new country/city, and finding new friends, was a challenge. Definitely worth it though!
registration_process: VU sent various links to forms we had to fill in regarding which semester you were registering for, what kind of exchange student you were (semester/full year), passport information etc.
registration_help: They answer relatively fast per email!
registration_success: I got to register for all the classes I wanted. They did however have to change one of the courses in the minor to another, that they registered me for instead, which was fine with me as it fitted pretty well into what the minor was about (Gender and Diversity)
registration_advice: Don't hesitate to send a bunch of emails, even if you think they are dumb questions. Also, talk with your friends if you know people who are going to the same place as you. It helped me a lot to do the more important forms etc. with someone.
academics_comments: I had a really good experience both academically and personally, although balancing both having a full-time study, finding yourself in a new country/city, and finding new friends, was a challenge. Definitely worth it though!
course_level: I took 30 ECTS as electives, and I chose a minor programme called 'Gender and Diversity'. I took 5 courses (6ECTS each) all but one, were 300 points/level and the last one was 200.
teaching_comparison: The semester was from the beginning of September till the end of January/beginning of February depending on exams. At VU they split the semester up into three periods: P1 = 2 months; P2 = 2 months; P3 = 1 month, and typically you will have two courses in each P1 and P2 and one course in P3
courses_enrolled: Identity, Diversity and Inclusion; Religions and Gender; Sexual Health: Threats and Opportunities for minor GAD; Theorizing Gender and Intersectionality; Diversifying Philosophy
recommended_courses: Identity, Diversity and Inclusion was a really cool course! The professors were super nice and very good at engaging the students. The contents of the course were also incredibly interesting - The course focused in particular on contemporary issues concerning processes of inclusion and exclusion in the Dutch/European context. The central questions in this course were: 1. How and why are identities based on ethnicity, gender, class and sexuality constructed by both insiders and outsiders? 2. How do (groups within) European/Dutch societies respond to diversity? 3. What are the relevant mechanisms of inclusion or exclusion? 4. How should we contextualize current debates and practices related to inclusion/exclusion processes in relation to Dutch/European historical developments?
unexpected_costs: If you live in private housing as I did, they have taxes on trash, which is pretty expensive!! I had to pay around 100 Euros from august til January, and it is really difficult because you have to have a dutch bank account. and do it through their municipality website with a special login (similar to MitID/NemID), which. took a while to sort out.
cost_comparison: I feel like it is pretty much the same as in DK
activities_available: During the introduction period, they had classes you could sign up with, like yoga, football/soccer, various dance classes etc. Most of these classes were also available after the introduction period through memberships.
activities_recommended: Explore the city! Amsterdam is BEAUTIFUL, and it has so many attractions to visit. If you plan to visit more than 4 of the big museums, I would recommend buying a 'museum card'. It is super worth it for the price and you get access to A LOT of museums all over The Netherlands.
weekend_recommendations: Museums, visiting other cities (Den Haag, Utrecht, Rotterdam, Delft...), just walking around enjoying the city!!
culture_adjustment: Easy. I feel Dutch people a very similar to Danes.
socializing_tips: Some say they can be quite direct, which can come as a shock to people, so this is maybe something to be aware of. I didn't find them overly direct though.
cultural_challenges: Don't have any
culture_appreciated: The architecture
top3_advice: 1) Read the course manuals very well 2) BE PREPARED FOR THE HOUSING SITUATION 3) Join as many introduction events as possible - even though it is overwhelming in the beginning, it pays off socially in the end
other_useful_info: Nope
most_rewarding: The friends I have made <3
greatest_challenge: Balancing both wanting to have fun, travel, explore, party etc. and having a full-time study.

crucial_aspects: The city, the culture, having the possibility to speak English and have English-spoken classes as well as the university not being considered academically bad.
overall_comments: In general, I had a really good experience with my exchange. I liked my classes, the level of teaching and workload was similar to KU. I felt that the university and teachers were very helpful if I had any issues. I had a few issues with the place I was staying at, but it got solved.
info_ease: VU was good at sending out information (emails) and they were good at helping one upon arrival. There were also always people at the university ready to help you with any questions including directions around campus.
arrival_assistance: See comment above
arrival_comments: Some things could have been done a bit better on the introduction day, but they were all very helpful
housing_how: I found housing through my host institution
